(4) Rule (a)'s path check reads the whole docs set, deployed content included, and another project's path is written with a placeholder (`<clone>/…`, `<project>/…`), never an ignore marker (plan D12, D26, D27).

**Consequences:** `internal/check` is a new package importing the standard library, `internal/trail` and `internal/brain` (for `ReadTrail` only); it opens no SQLite database and imports no driver itself (the driver reaches it only through `internal/brain`), so R4's list of the driver's users does not grow. `cmd/fyr` builds the vocabulary from its own verb table and `recordFlags`, so a doc naming a verb of a newer binary is a finding. A refactor that changes no behaviour still marks its spec stale; the remedy is a re-read and `fyr record edit <ID> --status current`, never a change to the rule. Deployed content's other-project paths are reworded to placeholders (plan Phase 3). Rejected: going through the brain store (writes `brain.db`, refuses unmigrated projects), a per-spec `Code:` field, comparing `updated` with commit times (never converges), an ignore marker, `--json`, auto-fix.

title: `fyr eval` — the Antigravity run kit as a verb, and the second thing that leaves the machine
body:
## ADR-065: `fyr eval` — the Antigravity run kit as a verb, and the second thing that leaves the machine     (2026-10-26) — Accepted

**Context:** Roadmap item 4 asks for the Antigravity run kit (`.agents/kit/agy-rel/run.sh` and `kit-preamble.sh`) moved into `fyr`, runnable on any project, its results stored as records and compared over time; R0 says fyr grows to evaluate projects. The kit runs only in this checkout, against one fixture and a hard-coded row list, stores nothing, and its safety checks are bash with Linux-only tools. Each run sends a sandboxed clone's prompts, and the files its agent reads, to the model of the CLI: until now R8 named the nightly dreamer's redacted prompt as the one thing that leaves the machine, and the kit's runs were outside the harness. Plan: `PLAN-2026-10-26-0659-plan-fyr-eval-the-antigravity-run-kit-as-a-verb`, cold read `REVIEW-2026-10-26-0708-review-cold-read-of-the-fyr-eval-plan-2026-10-26`, approved by the operator 2026-10-26 (D31), the R8 and Non-goals texts with it (D4, D4b).

**Decision:** (1) A new verb, `fyr eval [--fixture DIR] <row>...` and `fyr eval --list`, in a new package `internal/eval` wired from `cmd/fyr/eval.go`. It runs each named row in its own sandbox under `<home>/.config/fyr/eval/<stamp>/<row>/` (a clone of the fixture and a throwaway HOME with the harness installed as `fyr install` would give a place, plan D16), with every check the kit's preamble made: refused roots, outside every checkout, the real config unchanged, no new credentials against a baseline, no processes left, and the agent invoked. Only the operator starts it; no gate and no timer runs it (R3). (2) The suite is one `guide` record per project, `GUIDE-eval`, holding a seven-column table (plan D2); a new record kind or files under `.agents/evals/` were rejected. (3) eval reads `GUIDE-eval` from the project's `.agents/trail.jsonl`, not from the brain store, and refuses when its body or `updated` differs from HEAD's copy, read with the new `brain.ParseTrail` (plan D3, D28): a run always names the commit its scenarios came from, and a testing record an earlier run wrote does not block the next. (4) Results are one `testing` record per invocation in the evaluated project's scope, and each sandbox ingested into the metrics store with label `eval=<row>` and the final verdict as outcome, only after the verdict (plan D6, D22); comparison over time is `fyr metrics show --label eval=<row>` and `fyr record list --kind testing`, with no compare verb (plan D7). (5) R8 now names two things that leave the machine, both to the model of the CLI the machine already uses: the dreamer's redacted prompt and `fyr eval`'s runs, which send a sandboxed clone's prompts and the files its agent reads unredacted, as any session of that CLI does (plan D4). The Non-goal on vendor settings now says the one vendor file `fyr` writes is a sandbox's `settings.json`, never the operator's (plan D4b).

**Consequences:** R0 needs no edit: its "nothing in fyr acts on the CLI between its turns" concerns the operator's session, and eval drives a separate CLI process in a sandbox HOME. R3 needs no edit: its exception governs what runs on a timer, and eval runs only when typed. ADR-056 and ADR-056a forbid permission keys in what the harness installs; a sandbox's grants are the operator's permission mode for that sandbox, written by eval from the suite the operator committed. `internal/eval` imports no SQLite driver (plan D10): its agent check is a bytes search, and its stores are reached through `brain` and `metrics` from `cmd/fyr`, so R4's list of the driver's users does not grow. A suite's `setup` and `check` are bash that runs as the operator, so running `fyr eval` trusts the project as much as running its tests does (plan D30). The README map gains an `eval` node with a dashed olive line to the model provider, which, like the dreamer's, never turns solid (AGENTS.md rule 4). On macOS the leftover-process check does not run and says so (plan O1). The kit stays until the plan's Phase 3 moves its consumers and deletes it. Rejected: redacting what eval sends (the point is an agent working on the fixture as any session does), running rows in parallel, a `--history` verb, in-process install (it skips the rebuild a checkout place gets).

title: Code modularity is the harness's third always-on rule
body:
## ADR-066: Code modularity is the harness's third always-on rule     (2026-10-26) — Accepted
**Context:** On 2026-10-26 the operator asked, in their own turn: "This needs to be added to the harness right away as a global rule or context and we need to run this ASAP on this project right now", followed by the rule's text. The text sets file and function size limits, a pre-edit split check, paradigm-aware splitting, no dumping-ground files, an acyclic import graph, and an audit-then-approve protocol for files over 600 LOC. `context/AGENTS.md` (the hand-written part) stood at 14,814 bytes against its 15,000 target. The Antigravity rules block stood at 18,491 of 22,000.
**Decision:** `rules/code-modularity.md` holds the operator's text verbatim, under a title and the `trigger: always_on` frontmatter of the other two rules (`critical-thinking.md`, ADR-050; `session-sizing.md`, ADR-058). It deploys verbatim to `~/.gemini/config/rules/` like them. It is a file drop with no code change (AGENTS.md § Rules for working here).
**Consequences:**
- The rules block is 20,945 of 22,000 bytes (`TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock`). That leaves 1,055 bytes for every future rule and context line together.
- The cyclomatic-complexity limit (10) has no tool here. The Go code is stdlib-only and there is no CI, so the limit holds only by reading, like the rest of the context.
- The rule exempts machine-generated files but does not name vendored ones. AGENTS.md's rule that vendored skills and the catalog are never edited still governs them.
- Files already over the ceilings get the rule's item-5 audit table before anything moves. The audit of this checkout ran on 2026-10-26, in the session that added the rule.
- Work in flight on files over 600 LOC waits for that audit's approval, since item 2 requires extracting the touched cluster first. The open case is the `fyr eval` plan's Done-section fixes in `internal/eval/run.go`.
- The rule reaches a machine only through `fyr install` or `fyr update` there. No behavioural Antigravity run of it exists yet, so it is a release-gate item (AGENTS.md § Release).
**Amended (2026-10-26, same day):** the operator approved the audit's item 12 ("go all approved as plan"), so item 1's exemption now also names vendored third-party files. The audit's items 2–8 are `PLAN-2026-10-26-modularity`, one phase per file. Item 1, `internal/eval/run.go`, was split at 52259a5 before the `fyr eval` Done-section fixes landed. Item 11 stays a reading-only limit.

title: A child process that reads untrusted input gets an allow-listed environment
body:
## ADR-067: A child process that reads untrusted input gets an allow-listed environment     (2026-10-28) — Accepted
**Context:** `fyr dream` runs `agy` over text it did not write: project trails, memory, feedback and Antigravity transcripts, any of which may carry a planted instruction (prompt injection). Until now the child got fyr's whole environment with only `HOME` replaced (`withHome(os.Environ(), …)`). The ledger's dream sandbox showed the cost at ade98e8 (`PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` § The dream sandbox, finding 2; audit finding SD25): every `agy` call received 50 variables, the canary values of `GEMINI_API_KEY` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` among them. The child runs with no tools granted, so the credentials are only one injection or one `agy` bug away from use. The operator approved the allow-list's contents on 2026-10-27 (audit-choices row 4, D8), and asked for the dream to be verified in a sandbox before it is built on (D46).
**Decision:**
- A child process that reads input fyr did not write gets its environment from an allow-list, never from `os.Environ()` minus a deny-list. A deny-list fails open for every credential variable nobody named; an allow-list fails closed, and its failure is visible (the child cannot log in or reach the network).
- One helper filters such a list out of fyr's own environment: `trail.AllowEnv(env []string, names ...string) []string` keeps the entries whose name is listed, a name ending in `*` being a prefix, in the input's order (choices D6, D20). `internal/trail` already has no SQLite and is imported by every package that runs a child into a project.
- The dreamer's `agy` gets `AllowEnv(os.Environ(), PATH, LANG, the thirteen locale category names (LC_ALL, LC_CTYPE, LC_COLLATE, LC_MESSAGES, LC_MONETARY, LC_NUMERIC, LC_TIME, LC_ADDRESS, LC_IDENTIFICATION, LC_MEASUREMENT, LC_NAME, LC_PAPER, LC_TELEPHONE), TERM, TMPDIR, TZ, the proxy variables in both cases, SSL_CERT_FILE, SSL_CERT_DIR)`, then `HOME` set to its private login copy (choices D8, § Interfaces "Child environments"). The locale names replace D8's `LC_*`, because Debian's sshd accepts any `LC_` variable a client sends, so the prefix carries arbitrary values (ledger D10, from the Phase 1 security review).
- A name joins the dreamer's list only after a run shows `agy` needs it, and only by the operator (`USER`, `LOGNAME`, `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` are the named candidates, D8).
**Consequences:**
- No variable outside the list reaches the model's process, so a credential exported in the operator's shell (an API key, a cloud secret) stays out. A listed variable passes as it is: a proxy URL in `https_proxy` that embeds a user name and password still reaches `agy`. The private `HOME` keeps `agy` from loading the operator's own config and settings; it does not stop a read by absolute path, which only the run's no-tools setting refuses.
- `agy` on Linux was verified with this list by one real run in the ledger's sandbox (run R1). macOS cannot be verified from the Linux box: its login reads the Keychain, which may need `USER` or `LOGNAME`. The macOS `fyr dream --all` run is a release obligation, and the release is NO-SHIP until it passes; if it fails, a fix or a revert lands first (choices D27, ledger A2).
- When the list drops something `agy` needs, the dream fails with its existing `not logged in` or `invalid output` hint in `dream.log`, and widening the list is the operator's call.
- `trail.Command`'s git keeps its SD24 deny-list (`repoVars`): its allow-list half was struck because the deny-list already drops every locating variable (choices D40). git reads repository config, not prose, so it is not a child of this decision; a later change that makes git or any other child read untrusted text brings it under this ADR.
- `fyr eval`'s `agy` already gets an allow-list that predates this ADR: a constructed one, where eval names every variable, copying `PATH` (its sandbox `bin` first), `TERM`, `LANG`, `USER` and `LOGNAME` from its own environment and setting the rest (`(*row).agyEnv` in `internal/eval/row_env.go`, `SPEC-fyr-eval` § One row, step 10). It meets this decision as built and stays as it is; it is not rebuilt on `AllowEnv`.

title: A project reaches the cross-project consumers only by the operator's registration
body:
## ADR-068: A project reaches the cross-project consumers only by the operator's registration     (2026-10-28) — Accepted
**Context:** Until now a checkout registered itself in the global search index whenever `fyr search` or `fyr index` ran in it and it held a `.agents/docs/` directory, and a checkout whose trail is records reached the brain store's scopes whenever any `fyr record` or `fyr search` call ran in it. Every cross-project consumer reads those two lists: `fyr dream --all` (whose redacted prompt leaves the machine, R3, R8), `fyr search --global`, `fyr record import --global` and the metrics trail join. A clone of someone else's harness-scaffolded repository therefore became a dream target and a `--global` source the first time a command ran in it, without the operator ever saying so. The ledger's dream sandbox showed it at ade98e8 (`PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` § The dream sandbox, finding 1; audit finding SD19): one `fyr search` in a foreign clone, a search that itself failed, made it a brain scope; `fyr dream --all` then sent its bug record, a canary string and a planted instruction included, to `agy`. The operator approved opt-in registration and its R3 wording on 2026-10-27 (audit-choices row 1, O1, D32).
**Decision:**
- A checkout is registered only by the operator's act: `fyr index --register`, run in it. It writes the marker, the regular file `fyr-registered` (mode 0600, one line `registered <YYYY-MM-DD>`) in the checkout's git common directory, then indexes as a plain `fyr index` does (choices D2, D19).
- The marker sits inside `.git/` (the common directory, so every linked worktree of one repository shares it), because git never copies `.git/` files: a clone, a fork or an unpacked archive is never registered, whatever it carries in its tree. Only the marker's existence is read, and only a regular file counts: `trail.Registered` reads a symlink, a directory or any stat error as not registered, and `trail.Register` refuses to write through a symlink or over a non-regular file.
- The marker is checked at every cross-project consumer, not only where a checkout joins the global search index (choices D3, D15): the dream's `--all` targets, `reconcileGlobal`, the `--global` record hits, `brain.ImportGlobal` and `brain.ForMetrics`. `ListProjects` and `brain.Scopes` stay raw lists of what the index and the store hold. `fyr dream --project <dir>` needs no marker: naming the directory is the same explicit act (choices D16).
- The file index registers a checkout only when it carries the marker; the `.agents/docs` condition goes (ledger Phase 2). The consumers' filters land in ledger Phase 3.
- Today's registrations are not carried over (choices D4): every one came from the automatic registration this ADR removes. The operator re-registers their own projects, listed by `fyr dream --dry-run --all`'s `skip not registered` lines (choices D17).
- There is no `--unregister`: deleting the marker file is the opt-out (choices D5). `init-project` does not register what it scaffolds (choices D18).
**Consequences:**
- REQUIREMENTS.md R3's exception narrows to the projects the operator registered, in choices D32's words. R0's one store still holds every project's records: only the cross-project consumers narrow, and a project's own `fyr search` and `fyr record` are unchanged.
- After the upgrade nothing is registered: the first `fyr dream --all` skips every former target and `fyr search --global` answers only from `~/.config/fyr` until the operator runs `fyr index --register` in each project they want back (Phase 3's handoff tells them).
- The marker is local state the trail does not hold: a fresh clone of the operator's own repository, or a new machine, must be registered again. It is lost with a re-clone and survives `git gc`, a branch switch and a worktree prune.
- Registration is consent, not a trust check of the content: a registered project's records still pass through the redactor and reach the dream's prompt as text.

title: Addendum to ADR-068: the marker is sealed to its checkout and its home; the file index keeps .agents/docs; Phases 2 and 3 ship together
body:
## ADR-068a: Addendum to ADR-068 — the marker is sealed to its checkout and its home, the file index keeps its `.agents/docs` condition, and Phases 2 and 3 ship together     (2026-10-28) — Accepted
**Context:** ADR-068's fourth decision bullet says "the file index registers a checkout only when it carries the marker; the `.agents/docs` condition goes (ledger Phase 2)". Building Phase 2 showed that the global search index's reconcile (`dropReason`, `internal/search/global.go`) drops every registration without `.agents/docs`, because a plain `docs/` is never served in its place (security review rounds 2-3). Phase 2's review (`reviewer`, 2026-10-28) found the ADR stating the opposite of the code, the spec and `TestRegistersOnlyHarnessProjects`, and found that REQUIREMENTS.md R3, as edited with ADR-068, is not yet true of the dreamer: until ledger Phase 3, `fyr dream --all` still takes every file-index row and every brain scope. The Phase 2 security review (2026-10-28) reproduced two ways a third party's tree read as registered without the operator's act, both of them with an existence-only marker: (1) a tree whose `.git` file names a registered repository's git dir (`gitdir: <a>/.git`) resolves to that repository's marker; (2) any tree that carries `.git/` itself — an archive of a working directory, `cp -a`, rsync, or a tarball built to carry the marker, whose name README publishes — brings the marker with it, so ADR-068's "an unpacked archive is never registered" was false. One `fyr search` in either then put the tree's own `.agents/docs` into `--global`. An ADR is never rewritten, so this addendum corrects it.
**Decision:**
- The marker is sealed. Its body is `registered <YYYY-MM-DD>` and `seal <hex>`, the HMAC-SHA256 (Go's `crypto/hmac`) of the checkout's main top level under a random key kept in the fyr state directory, `~/.config/fyr/registration.key` (0600, `crypto/rand.Text()`, created by the first `fyr index --register`, hard-linked into place so two first registrations agree on one key, and never followed through a link). `trail.Registered(stateDir, root)` counts the marker only when its seal matches this checkout's main root under that home's key, so a redirect tree, a copy at another path, a moved checkout, a planted marker and another home all read as unregistered; the consumers pass the state directory beside the root. Only existence was read before (audit-choices D2's "only its existence is read" is superseded).
- The file index registers a checkout when it carries the marker AND has `.agents/docs`, the one trail the global search index reads (ledger D11). A registered checkout without it, such as a project whose trail is records, is not added only to be dropped by the next `--global`; it reaches the cross-project consumers through its brain scope once Phase 3 filters them.
- Ledger Phases 2 and 3 ship as one: no tag is cut between them (none is cut before the ledger's Done in any case, ledger § Session order). ADR-068's consequences ("after the upgrade nothing is registered") describe the release that carries both.
**Consequences:**
- ADR-068 stands, with its fourth bullet read as above.
- At the Phase 2 commit, R3's "over the projects the operator registered" is a requirement the dreamer meets only after Phase 3; `--global` also still serves rows registered before ADR-068 until Phase 3's reconcile checks the marker (`SPEC-fyr-search` says so). Phase 3's Kickoff names the restatements to bring in line then (`README.md`'s dream row, the dream lines of `cmd/fyr/main.go`'s usage, the `dream` flag help in `cmd/fyr/ctx_verbs.go`, `SPEC-fyr-dream`'s target list, `internal/search/dream.go`'s doc comments).
- A moved checkout, a restored backup at another path and a new machine must run `fyr index --register` again; so must a home whose `registration.key` was deleted (deleting it unregisters every checkout of that home at once). The key is a local secret of the same kind as the stores beside it; it never leaves the machine and `uninstall` leaves it with them.
- `fyr index --register` run inside a redirect tree writes the shared git dir's one marker sealed for that tree, so the repository the tree borrows from reads as unregistered until it is registered again: it fails closed, and it takes the operator's own act (security review finding 4, accepted).

title: The dream cap drops news newest first, and the watermark stops before what it dropped
body:
## ADR-069: The dream cap drops news newest first, and the watermark stops before what it dropped     (2026-10-28) — Accepted, amends ADR-055a
**Context:** `fyr dream` caps each project's prompt at 256 KB. ADR-055a fixed the metrics summary as the first input dropped over the cap; the dream plan's D21 then dropped transcripts oldest first, then trail files oldest first, then feedback, then skills, with memory always whole. After a successful run the project's watermark moved to the run's start, so an input dropped to fit the cap was older than the next run's watermark and was never sent. The ledger's dream sandbox showed it at ade98e8 (`PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` § The dream sandbox, finding 3; audit finding SD28): of nine ~40 KB change records, the first run sent six, named the three oldest as left out, and the second run logged `unchanged` and made no call. The operator approved the mechanism on 2026-10-27 (`PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-choices` § Interfaces "The dream cap", O2 answered by D33; D24).
**Decision:**
- The dated kinds — transcripts, trail and feedback — are dropped together, newest first, after the metrics summary and before the skills. What a capped run sends is the oldest news, so everything older than what it dropped has been sent. Two inputs of the same time drop transcript first, then trail, then feedback.
- `Collected.Through` is the instant just before the oldest dated input dropped this way, or zero when none was. A successful run stores it as the project's watermark when it is non-zero and before the run's start, else the run's start, as before. The next run reads the dropped inputs again, because they are newer than the watermark.
- A dated input too big to be sent beside memory and the skills under the cap is dropped first, named `(too big for the <n> KB cap beside memory and skills)`, and does not hold the watermark (D33): the budget is the cap less the prompt's head, memory and the skills, not the cap alone, or memory and skills that nearly fill the cap would drop every dated input every night and the watermark would never move. A drop holds the watermark only while an input strictly older than it is kept. One of the oldest time left — the last dated input when the left-out line beside it leaves no room, or part of a group of one time (a batch of records from one commit) bigger than the room — is dropped for good and named `(dropped to fit the <n> KB cap; not sent again)`: a time watermark cannot split a group of one time, so holding it there would re-read the same group and drop the same part every night (the Phase 4 code review). So a run always advances.
- The metrics summary and the skills are undated and never hold the watermark. Memory is never dropped; a project whose memory alone passes the cap still fails.
**Consequences:**
- Nothing dated that fits is lost: a backlog larger than the cap is sent over consecutive runs, oldest first. Only an input too big to fit beside memory and the skills is lost, named in the prompt, the proposal body and the dry run, as before this ADR.
- Inside one capped run, a new trail record now gives way to an older transcript: the kinds' order (transcripts before trail before feedback) holds only between inputs of the same time. Dropping each kind in turn, as D21 did, would let a kept new input sit above a dropped old one, so the watermark could not advance past that old one while the kinds above it always filled the cap: a run that never moves on.
- Lost besides a too-big input: the part of a group of one time that does not fit beside memory, the skills and the left-out line, named as not sent again. A cursor finer than a time (a time and a label) would lose nothing, at the cost of a new `dream-state.json` shape; not built.
- An input of the same time as the oldest held-back one may be sent twice, once kept and once with its group the next run; a re-sent input may give a duplicate global `proposal`, which `/retro` drops by hand (D33). Two inputs of one time and kind drop the later label first, so a rerun drops the same ones.
- A watermark is now any instant, not only a run's start; `dream-state.json` stores it at nanosecond precision, as it stores every time.

title: Experience reaches the harness checkout only through /retro --harness; retro and distill from another project queue a global proposal
body:
## ADR-070: Experience reaches the harness checkout only through `/retro --harness`; `retro` and `distill` run from another project queue a global `proposal`     (2026-10-28) — Accepted, amends ADR-062

**Context:** AGENTS.md rule 1 (and ADR-062) says experience does not come back to the harness by any path but one: a harness-target proposal reaches this checkout only through `/retro --harness`, run by the operator on that machine. Two skills still wrote the checkout from another project (audit finding WS40): `skills/retro/SKILL.md` Step 6 let a retro run elsewhere locate the checkout and apply a harness proposal there "when the user asks in the same turn to apply now", and `skills/distill/SKILL.md`'s `--global` wrote `<harness-repo>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, installed it and committed in the harness repo, or ran `fyr adopt` on a project-local draft. The operator approved striking both (`PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-choices` row 6 and D39, carried as `PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` items 14 and 15, D8). The same audit found the `dreamer` dispatch written out in full in both skills (WS-S5), so a change to it had two places to drift.

**Decision:**
- A `retro` run from any project but the harness checkout gives every harness-scope proposal the status `queued`, always; the same-turn "apply now" branch is struck. The harness checkout's own `/retro` and `/retro --harness` are the only runs that apply a harness proposal.
- `distill --global` from another project stores the drafted skill, in full, as one global `proposal` record (`fyr record add proposal --global --project <root>`), status `queued`, and writes nothing under the harness checkout: no `skills/<name>/`, no `fyr install`, no `fyr adopt`, no commit there. Run in the harness checkout itself, `--global` writes `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` there under that repo's own rules, as a retro there applies a harness proposal. `/retro --harness` applies a queued distill proposal as a new `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`.
- The `dreamer` dispatch is written out once, in `retro` Step 1 source 8; `distill` Step 1 points at it and names its one difference (`Promoted: none`).

**Consequences:**
- A harness skill or rule drafted in a project waits for the operator's `/retro --harness` in the checkout, where the harness's own Definition of Done (install, eval, review, change record, release) runs on it; nothing lands in the checkout from a session whose checks and trail belong to another repository.
- Experience still stays on the machine that logged it (rule 1): the proposal is a global record in that machine's `~/.config/fyr/brain.db`, never exported. A checkout on another machine sees it only when the operator runs `/retro --harness` on this one.
- Not changed: `fyr adopt` itself (the operator's verb for a skill installed by another tool, run in the checkout), and `skills/discover-skills/SKILL.md:113`, which suggests where a new global skill belongs without writing it.
- No test pins the new branch: the `retro` and `distill` eval rows run project-scope paths only. The skill text is pinned by `git grep` in the ledger's Phase 5 box.

title: The map's experience node names the brain store; the old logs are what import --global migrates, not what stays
body:
## ADR-071: The map's experience node names the brain store; the old logs are what `import --global` migrates, not what stays (2026-10-28) — Accepted, amends ADR-062's map **Context:** AGENTS.md rule 3 makes the README map the contract for what reaches a machine and what stays on one. Its experience node still read `~/.config/fyr/ feedback.jsonl, retros.jsonl, proposals/, state.json, search.db, metrics.db — stays on this machine`, and `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § What stays on the machine named the same three logs as a place's experience (audit finding C37, `PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` item 32). Since ADR-063 the experience is in the brain store, `~/.config/fyr/brain.db`: every project's trail records and the global `feedback`, `retro` and `proposal` records, which the `feedback-log` skill, `/retro` and `fyr dream` write. The map never named `brain.db`. The three logs are the shape from before the store: `fyr record import --global` reads them into it and lists them for the operator to remove; `fyr dream` and `fyr metrics` still read a `feedback.jsonl` where one is left. The dreamer's harness-target proposals are global `proposal` records, not files under `proposals/dream/harness/`; only its draft skills are files, under `proposals/dream/drafts/`, which a record names (`DEPLOY-local` keeps that path, because it is true). **Decision:** - The node becomes `~/.config/fyr/
brain.db, metrics.db, search.db, state.json
stays on this machine`. No line on the map moves: `sessions -- "logs" --> configDir`, the dreamer's `proposal records, metrics.db` and eval's `testing record, metrics.db` already point at it, and they now point at the store their labels name. - `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § What stays on the machine names the same four files, says the old logs are migrated by `import --global` and left in place for the operator to remove, and names a harness-target proposal as a global `proposal` record that `/retro` or the dreamer queued. - One commit holds this ADR, the map and the spec (rule 3); rule 6's one home for the delivery claim is unchanged, because which place gets what from a tag does not move. **Consequences:** - The map now says where the experience actually is, so a reader looking for a place's corrections or proposals is sent to `fyr record list --global`, not to files that may never exist on a place installed after v3.0.0. - Not a new path: a project's own records are also exported to its committed `.agents/trail.jsonl`, which travels with that project's repository when the operator pushes it. That is the project's git, not a harness path, and the map draws no line for it, as before. - Not changed: `TestHarnessMap` checks verbs and the report path, not node labels, so the node's text rests on this ADR and on the item's `git grep` (no `feedback.jsonl`, `retros.jsonl` or `proposals/` in README.md). - The interactive page of the map is a view (rule 5) and is updated from it by the operator (ledger item 38).

title: What ADR-062 reversed in ADR-003 and ADR-006
body:
## ADR-072: What ADR-062 reversed in ADR-003 and ADR-006     (2026-10-28) — Accepted, amends ADR-003 and ADR-006

**Context:** ADR-003 and ADR-006 still read `accepted` and state facts that ADR-062 (fyr: the Antigravity CLI only, renamed) reversed, and neither carries a pointer to it (audit finding C44; `PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` item 33). An ADR is never rewritten and a status cannot say "in part" (`PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-choices` D10, after the audit fix's D23), so the correction is this record. ADR-003 and ADR-006 are left as written.

**Decision:** read ADR-003 and ADR-006 through this list. What ADR-062 reversed:
- **ADR-003, derived agents.** `agents/` is no longer in Claude Code format, and nothing is translated at install: an agent is authored natively as `agents/<name>/agent.md` in Antigravity's format and installed as written (ADR-062 decision 1; project AGENTS.md § Layout). `derive.go`, `toolMap` and `modelMap` are gone; the one place a vendor constraint lives is `knownTools` in `internal/harness/inventory.go`, where an unknown tool still fails the install, because Antigravity hangs a subagent that names one. The verb is `fyr install`, not `styrman install`.
- **ADR-006, the name.** The binary is `fyr`, not `sh-agent`; its state directory is `~/.config/fyr` (`fyr install` migrates `~/.config/sh-agent`); its environment variables are `FYR_*` (`FYR_REPO`, not `SH_AGENT_REPO`); its marker is `.fyr-noindex`, with `.sh-agent-noindex` still honoured (`trail.NoIndexMarkers`) (ADR-062 decision 3).

What still stands:
- ADR-003: `context/`, `agents/` and `skills/` (with `commands/` and `rules/`) are the only sources; `fyr install` assembles the context (AGENTS.md, dev-setup.md and the generated inventory); nothing generated is committed.
- ADR-006: GCP defaults are asked for before the first GCP action and never assumed.

Also out of date in ADR-006, and not ADR-062's reversal (this record does not trace which decision changed them): the defaults are now recorded in the project's `DEPLOY-gcp` record, not its `AGENTS.md` (`context/dev-setup.md`); and the repository holds shell scripts again (`skills/handoff/scripts/check-trailers.sh`, the `google-catalog` refresh script, the vendored catalog's own).

**Consequences:** A reader of ADR-003 or ADR-006 who finds this record by `fyr search --refs ADR-003` (or `ADR-006`) gets the current facts; the two records' bodies and statuses are unchanged. ADR-002's name, superseded by ADR-006, is superseded again by ADR-062's.

title: The visible dream
body:
## ADR-073: The visible dream     (2026-10-28) — Accepted, amends ADR-047a and ADR-067

**Context:** The operator wants to see the dream. Their words (`PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` D32 3, 2026-10-28): "If antigravity is open and there are idle/stale projects. Dream is allowed to run by it self as a agy conversation that would be visible to the user." Today `fyr dream --all` runs nightly at 03:00, when no one is at the machine, and runs `agy` in a private HOME that fyr deletes, so nothing it did is listed anywhere the operator looks. That conflicts with R0 ("nothing in `fyr` acts on the CLI between its turns") and with R3's one exception (the nightly timer, a CLI with no tools), and it moves a line on the map (AGENTS.md rule 3). Phase 8a of the ledger researched what agy 1.4.9 allows (ledger D35: its help, changelog and web docs, and one sandbox dream): agy has no no-tools flag and no per-run permission file, a conversation is listed by `/resume` from the home it was written in, and print mode reports the effective permission state through `/permissions` and `/config` without starting a turn. The operator approved the seven-row proposal, "Approve recommendations (Recommended)" (ledger D36), and the plan that builds it, `PLAN-2026-10-28-1510-plan-the-visible-dream-2026-10-28`, after its cold read ("Approve all (Recommended)", that plan's D17).

**Decision:**
- **R0 and R3 change** to the texts quoted in the plan's D1 (ledger D36 1 and 3), and R8's "the nightly dreamer's redacted prompt" loses "nightly" (approved by the operator, "Approve drop 'nightly' (Recommended)", 2026-10-28; the plan's D19). The one conversation `fyr` starts is the visible dream, a conversation of its own that no session is sent into; R3's exception becomes an hourly user timer that acts only while an Antigravity CLI process of the operator's runs, and runs the CLI headless in plan mode with no tools.
- **Where the CLI runs** (ledger D36 2; plan D3, D6, D11, D12): in the operator's own Antigravity home — `--home`, by default `$HOME`, never `$HOME` when they differ — from the empty `~/.config/fyr/dream-work`, when that home grants no tool without review, so each project's dream stays as a conversation `/resume` lists. "Grants no tool without review" is what `agy -p "/permissions"` and `agy -p "/config"` (`--output-format json`) report, asked before each project's call, failing closed: a report fyr cannot read, an allow rule from any source, a review mode that auto-approves, a grant outside the workspace, a non-empty working directory or a missing login sends that project to a private home as today. Never `--dangerously-skip-permissions`. Settings files are not parsed by hand.
- **When it runs** (ledger D36 4; plan D2, D9, D10): the timer fires hourly; `--all` first checks for an interactive `agy` session of the operator's uid (Linux `/proc`, macOS `ps`; a `-p` run or a subcommand such as `remote-control` does not count) and, without one, prints one line, creates nothing and exits 0; a check that errors exits 2 and creates nothing. Each project is attempted at most once per 24 hours under `--all`, success or failure (`dream-state.json` `attempts`). `--project` never checks and ignores the cooldown.
- **What the conversation looks like** (ledger D36 5; plan D14): no pinned title; the prompt's first line reads `dreaming: <project>`.
- **The dream reads no dream** (plan D5, D15): a conversation whose workspace is `dream-work` (as written or through its symlinks) is no project's: not ingested into the metrics store, not read by any project's dream or its in-use check.
- **The map** (ledger D36 6; plan D16): the dreamer node reads "hourly user timer, while agy runs"; a new olive line `dreamer` → `sessions`, "one conversation per project, in /resume", is drawn DASHED until the build works end to end (the plan's V1 and ledger A2), then solid, per AGENTS.md rule 4; the dashed line to the model provider is unchanged.
- **Amends** ADR-047a (the schedule, and where the CLI runs) and ADR-067 (in the visible branch the child's `HOME` is `--home`, not a private login copy; the allow-list itself is unchanged). Neither record is edited.

**Consequences:**
- In the visible branch the no-tools guarantee rests on agy's own report of the home's settings, not on isolation; the window between the report and the call is a Known limit (`SPEC-fyr-dream`).
- The redacted prompt and the model's answer persist in the operator's Antigravity store, where until now they were deleted with the private HOME; what leaves the machine is unchanged (R8).
- The operator's MCP servers, plugins and hooks load in a visible dream as in any session they start (plan D8, accepted by the operator as a Known limit); the model still has no tool it may use without review.
- The dream spends the operator's quota while they work: at most one attempt per registered project per day, the same ceiling as the nightly run. The oracle adds two print-mode calls per project, which start no turn.
- An installed nightly unit is not rewritten by `install`, `update` or `--install-timer`; the operator runs `fyr dream --remove-timer`, then `fyr dream --install-timer`, and `fyr status` names a unit of the older schedule (plan D4, D13).
- The macOS process check is verified only by the operator's Mac run (ledger A2). Until the plan's Phase 5 the binary still runs nightly and privately; the specs say so in one sentence each, and no tag is cut while the plan is open (plan D16).

title: `status` reported the installed binary as stale right after `install`
body:
# BUG-001: `status` reported the installed binary as stale right after `install`

## Prevention
A path that install writes but status cannot compare must be excluded from drift explicitly, and the exclusion needs a test. Before adding a new managed path, decide how status compares it.

title: `sh-agent adopt <path> --home DIR` failed with a usage error
body:
# BUG-002: `sh-agent adopt <path> --home DIR` failed with a usage error

## Prevention
When a command takes positionals, test it with flags after the positional; the stdlib parser does not interleave.

title: two scratch rules in the deployed context contradicted each other
body:
# BUG-003: two scratch rules in the deployed context contradicted each other

## Prevention
When a rule changes, run `sh-agent render | grep -n <keyword>` before deploying and read every hit; the deployed file is the concatenation, not one source file.

title: Antigravity silently dropped the `bug` and `feature` skills
body:
# BUG-004: Antigravity silently dropped the `bug` and `feature` skills

## Prevention
The lenient parser is not the reference; the vendors' strict parsers are. After any frontmatter change, install into the sandbox home, run each CLI once, and grep its log for parse errors — `sh-agent status` says the files match, not that the vendor read them.

title: `verifier` ran in a fresh worktree and could not see uncommitted work
body:
# BUG-005: `verifier` ran in a fresh worktree and could not see uncommitted work

## Prevention
A Claude-only agent key is not free: `isolation: worktree` is only right for an agent that must work on a committed base, never for one that judges uncommitted work. Any change to an agent's frontmatter is followed by one dispatch in the sandbox on an uncommitted change.

title: `sh-agent install` kept the operator's real `~/.local/bin/sh-agent` stuck on the 2026-09-03 build
body:
# BUG-006: `sh-agent install` kept the operator's real `~/.local/bin/sh-agent` stuck on the 2026-09-03 build

## Prevention
A self-updating tool that copies "itself" runs its OLD code on the very tick meant to install the change — the same shape as styrman-crew's BUG-035 and the review-standards §2 "installers count as callers" paragraph. Any installer that copies its own running binary must instead build from source, and `status` must compare the running build's stamp against the repo. After any change to `cmd/` or `internal/`, run `sh-agent status` from the real home and read the `binary` line before calling the install done.

title: repo docs told tests to use /tmp while the deployed hard rule forbids it
body:
# BUG-007: repo docs told tests to use /tmp while the deployed hard rule forbids it

## Prevention
Widen BUG-003's rule: when a global rule changes, `git grep -n '<old
wording>'` across the WHOLE repo, not only `context/` — the repo's own
`AGENTS.md`/`README.md` count as context because the global context is
deployed from here.

title: five retro commits changed context/agents/skills with no trail
body:
# BUG-008: five retro commits changed context/agents/skills with no trail

## Prevention
A change to another repo made from inside a project session is a task IN
THAT REPO — its own AGENTS.md rules (here: sandbox start of each CLI, changes
entry) and the Definition of Done apply there before the push; the retro
skill must say so explicitly.

title: `TestRunInstallStatusUninstall` asserted uninstall removes `~/.claude` itself
body:
# BUG-009: `TestRunInstallStatusUninstall` asserted uninstall removes `~/.claude` itself

## Prevention
Before asserting that something is removed, read the code's documented stop/keep list first (here `pruneEmptyDirs`'s comment) and assert on what it actually says it removes, not on an assumption. A test that fails on its first run for a reason other than the change under test is itself a recorded failure, per the global context's "every failure gets a number" rule.

title: Python batch-edit script silently left later files unedited after an assert failed on an earlier one
body:
# BUG-010: Python batch-edit script silently left later files unedited after an assert failed on an earlier one

## Prevention
Before writing any file, check every `old` string against every target file in a first pass (or process one file
per script invocation) so a stale assumption fails before anything is written. Have the script print a
"written: <file>" line per file so success/failure is legible from output, not inferred. After any batch edit,
run `git status --short` and `git diff --stat` against the list of files the edit was supposed to touch, before
trusting the change is complete.

title: commit message described 60 files, commit contained one
body:
# BUG-011: commit message described 60 files, commit contained one

## Prevention
Staging is a verification step like a test run: run `git add` bare, read its
exit status and `git diff --cached --stat`, then commit in a separate call —
never `git add … ; git commit` or `… && git commit`. A path list saved
earlier is stale after any delete or rename in the same session; regenerate
it from `git status --porcelain` immediately before staging, don't reuse it.

Graduated to: `context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules, "A verification command is never piped into a filter inside a `&&` chain" bullet ("Staging is a verification step too: … never `add … ; commit`")

title: explorer claims a written brief that does not exist on disk
body:
# BUG-012: explorer claims a written brief that does not exist on disk

## Prevention
A user's "change nothing" scopes source, never the trail — `context/AGENTS.md`
now says so explicitly; an agent names an artifact only after its write
succeeded (never report a file you did not write); a dispatcher that needs an
artifact checks the path exists (already the pattern in `/review`).

title: main agent cited a headless run's output tail as evidence without reading its own exit-status file first
body:
# BUG-013: main agent cited a headless run's output tail as evidence without reading its own exit-status file first

## Prevention
Every headless run cited as evidence is read from its exit status first (`<name> exit N`),
then its artifacts; a non-zero or missing status line is a FAIL of the evidence, whatever
the output tail says. A run that fans out to several subagents gets a budget beyond the
tool's ten-minute limit by running detached (`setsid nohup … &`) with its own status file.

title: verifier installed its scratch home under /tmp instead of .agents/scratch/
body:
# BUG-014: verifier installed its scratch home under /tmp instead of .agents/scratch/

## Prevention
An agent definition must restate the global rules that govern its own side effects
(where it writes, what it never touches) — a global rule alone does not reach a
subagent reliably. Before writing or editing an `agents/*.md` file, check it names
its own scratch/output location explicitly rather than relying on the global context
being read.

title: install rebuilds from source even in a read-only, git-less copy of the tree
body:
# BUG-015: install rebuilds from source even in a read-only, git-less copy of the tree

## Prevention
A behavior that depends on the environment the binary runs in (toolchain on
PATH, writable tree, git present) must be designed against every deployment
shape the trail names — `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md § Downstream mirrors`
lists both consumers and their call sites. A change to `install` is not done
until that section has been re-read and those call sites traced, not just
the sandbox scratch-home path this repo tests against itself.

title: TestDryRunNeverBuilds asserted a checkout-only message from a test that never built a checkout
body:
# BUG-016: TestDryRunNeverBuilds asserted a checkout-only message from a test that never built a checkout

## Prevention
A test that asserts a shape-dependent path (checkout vs. plain copy) builds
that shape itself in a temp dir; `../..` in a test is the shape of wherever
the tree happens to sit, which a downstream mirror changes. Same family as
BUG-015's "designed against every deployment shape the trail names" —
`.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md § Downstream mirrors` — but this is a test
fixture, not the production code path, so recheck test fixtures too, not
just `install`/`status`, whenever a change touches `IsCheckout`.

title: Workflow resumeFromRunId re-ran finished proposer agents live instead of replaying them from cache
body:
# BUG-017: Workflow resumeFromRunId re-ran finished proposer agents live instead of replaying them from cache

## Prevention
Before resuming a Workflow run whose earlier stage used concurrent/pipelined agent() calls, assume `resumeFromRunId` cannot guarantee a stable prefix — completion-order-dependent stages break the replay even with unchanged prompts. To reuse finished agents after a failure, write their outputs to scratch files (`.agents/scratch/`) and start a new run that reads them by path instead of resuming. On any long-running workflow, pin `model` on every agent explicitly, since the session model can change mid-run and pinning only the failed calls does not protect calls not yet started. Always access hyphenated object keys with bracket notation, never dot notation.

title: the bug skill's missing-repro gate no longer holds against an "autonomous" instruction
body:
# BUG-018: the bug skill's missing-repro gate no longer holds against an "autonomous" instruction

## Prevention
A change that trims or moves instructions lists each removed rule with its new home (file:line) or with why it was dropped, and a reviewer checks that list against the diff — do not rely on a line-count target ("under 70 lines") as the sole acceptance criterion for a trim.

title: skill texts and references instruct against the global hard rules
body:
# BUG-019: skill texts and references instruct against the global hard rules

## Prevention
A change to a global hard rule greps `skills/*/SKILL.md` **and**
`skills/*/references/` for guidance that contradicts it. Graduated:
`TestNoTmpInHarnessProse` — its prevention rule is now a test, not prose.

Graduated to: `TestNoTmpInHarnessProse` (walks every non-vendored skill's `references/`, `commands/`, `rules/`) and the corrected reference files

title: cloud-run-deploy skill's own triggers bypass the /preflight gate
body:
# BUG-020: cloud-run-deploy skill's own triggers bypass the /preflight gate

## Prevention
A skill whose triggers overlap a gated command names that gate as the entry
point rather than restating the trigger words itself. Graduated:
`skills/cloud-run-deploy/SKILL.md` description.

Graduated to: `skills/cloud-run-deploy/SKILL.md` description (defers to `/preflight`)

title: distill's feedback.jsonl entry omits the `project` field, breaking retro's cross-project filter
body:
# BUG-021: distill's feedback.jsonl entry omits the `project` field, breaking retro's cross-project filter

## Prevention
Every writer of `~/.config/sh-agent/feedback.jsonl` uses the `feedback`
skill's entry shape rather than a locally drafted example. Graduated:
`skills/distill/SKILL.md`.

Graduated to: `skills/distill/SKILL.md` (defers to `skills/feedback/SKILL.md` entry shape)

title: golang-ecosystem reference tells agents to register private code with third-party indexers
body:
# BUG-022: golang-ecosystem reference tells agents to register private code with third-party indexers

## Prevention
Imported skill text is checked for steps that send code or data to an
external service before it is vendored or kept; a step that "registers" or
"publishes" project content to a third party is scoped to public/OSS work
only. Graduated: `skills/golang/references/golang-ecosystem.md`.

Graduated to: `skills/VENDORED.md` (opening paragraph: imported skill text checked for register/publish/telemetry steps)

title: preflight's security trigger list omits crypto, so a crypto-only release skips security review
body:
# BUG-023: preflight's security trigger list omits crypto, so a crypto-only release skips security review

## Prevention
A trigger-list change greps every restatement of it (here, `context/AGENTS.md`, `agents/security.md`, and `skills/preflight/SKILL.md` all needed the same edit); a restated list should instead point at the canonical source.
Graduated: this rule has lived in `skills/review-standards/SKILL.md` § 3's
last bullet ("a rule, ban, threshold or trigger the diff changes has every
other restatement of it in the repository changed too...") since the
2026-09-16 commit applying Proposal 5 of `retros/2026-09-16-retro.md`.

Graduated to: `skills/review-standards/SKILL.md` § 3 (every other restatement of a changed rule is changed with it)

title: `explorer` and `init-deploy` rows failed the matrix although the run did what the row asks
body:
# BUG-024: `explorer` and `init-deploy` rows failed the matrix although the run did what the row asks

## Prevention
A kit built from a Markdown table unescapes `\|` in code spans before running it as shell. Before
trusting a check's FAIL, run the check once against a state where it must pass — a must-fail control
alone cannot catch a check that fails on everything.

title: init-project's "keep content, add `@AGENTS.md`" edit left CLAUDE.md not a one-line import
body:
# BUG-025: init-project's "keep content, add `@AGENTS.md`" edit left CLAUDE.md not a one-line import

## Prevention
A plan's cold-reader check and rehearsal compare every edit against `REQUIREMENTS.md`; an edit that
changes a requirement's invariant stops at the operator before it lands.

title: Step 4 docs-freshness routing patched twice, each patch introducing new defects
body:
# BUG-026: Step 4 docs-freshness routing patched twice, each patch introducing new defects

## Prevention
When one mechanism draws findings in two consecutive rounds — a cold read or a review — stop patching
and settle its purpose with the operator before a third change.

title: plan's describing-text check missed restatements in other words
body:
# BUG-027: plan's describing-text check missed restatements in other words

## Prevention
A rule change greps the rule's subject nouns — "deferred work", "Antigravity", "graduat", "`documentation`
when" — not only its old wording.

title: docs-lens finding applied without checking a recorded decision that already set the threshold
body:
# BUG-028: docs-lens finding applied without checking a recorded decision that already set the threshold

## Prevention
Before applying a review finding, grep `DECISIONS.md` and the active plan's decision rows for the rule
it changes. A recorded decision makes the finding a rebuttal, not a fix.

title: five checks and guards in scratch scripts matched the wrong state
body:
# BUG-029: five checks and guards in scratch scripts matched the wrong state

## Prevention
Before a check or guard gates anything, run it once where it must pass and once where it must fail.
Read a failing control's exit status for its reason: 126, 127 and 2 (not executable, not found,
usage) are not a failing check. A pattern that searches process lists or files must not be able to
match its own invocation or a quotation of its target.

Graduated to: `context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules, "Silence from your own instrumentation" bullet

title: Phase 6.4 comparison's first launch died at its base install
body:
# BUG-030: Phase 6.4 comparison's first launch died at its base install

## Prevention
Run a detached script's setup steps once in the foreground before launching it, or give it a dry-run
mode. A script that installs a second tree into a home passes `--repo` on every install and status
call for that tree.

title: a print-mode run ends its turn while a dispatched agent is still running
body:
# BUG-031: a print-mode run ends its turn while a dispatched agent is still running

## Prevention
A headless run waits for every agent it dispatched to return before it ends
its turn, and says so in its output when one has not. Graduated:
`context/AGENTS.md`, next to "Unattended runs on Claude Code set a `/goal`
naming the check that must pass."

Graduated to: `context/AGENTS.md` (a headless run waits for its dispatched agents)

title: a changed status message shipped without a covering test, behind a coverage claim that named one test for two strings
body:
# BUG-032: a changed status message shipped without a covering test, behind a coverage claim that named one test for two strings

## Prevention
When one change edits the same message or rule in more than one file, each edited file gets its own assertion, and the coverage claim names the covering test per file plus what is left uncovered — the global hard rule "Claims of test COVERAGE are the sharpest case: name what is not covered." A reviewer checks a per-file coverage map, not one failable test standing for the whole diff.

title: agent-name shadowing defeats the independent review rows
body:
# BUG-033: agent-name shadowing defeats the independent review rows

## Prevention
Before dispatching `reviewer`, `security`, `verifier`, or `explorer` for an independent judgement, list `.claude/agents/` and `.agents/agents/` (and the diff's changed paths there) for a name clash with a harness review agent; a clash stops the dispatch and is blocking in `/preflight` Step 5, not just Step 2.

title: the release gate's blocking list fails open on an incomplete security row
body:
# BUG-034: the release gate's blocking list fails open on an incomplete security row

## Prevention
Before trusting a preflight VERDICT: SHIP, check that every dispatch Step 2 required actually produced a complete artifact — a report a dispatcher decided not to write is not distinguishable, at the gate, from one that found nothing.

title: installer and status advise moving a hand-written CLAUDE.md into rules/, which ships everywhere
body:
# BUG-035: installer and status advise moving a hand-written CLAUDE.md into rules/, which ships everywhere

## Prevention
Guidance text that tells a user to move content into a harness-managed, deployed-everywhere path (`rules/`, `context/`, `skills/`) states what must never go there (credentials, personal/host-specific notes) in the same sentence, not as a separate caveat a reader can miss.

title: the symlink refusal is incomplete
body:
# BUG-036: the symlink refusal is incomplete

## Prevention
A security fix scoped to "the reader that was flagged" is incomplete by default; when a review finds one unsafe reader of a file class (here: symlinks under harness-managed directories), grep every other reader of that same class in the same change, not just the one cited.

title: `sh-agent adopt --force` can delete the harness checkout
body:
# BUG-037: `sh-agent adopt --force` can delete the harness checkout

## Prevention
A command that composes a deletion path from user-typed input validates the resolved path is inside its intended subtree and distinct from any ancestor of the deletion root before calling `RemoveAll` — `.` and `..` are not edge cases to special-case after the fact, they are the default inputs `EvalSymlinks` passes through unchanged.

title: a read-only agent ran a destructive git command against the tracked working tree
body:
# BUG-038: a read-only agent ran a destructive git command against the tracked working tree

## Prevention
An agent that does not own the working tree never runs a git command that changes
it — `checkout --`, `restore`, `stash`, `clean`, `reset`, `apply` — even to reproduce
a prior state. To compare against another revision it copies what it needs into
`.agents/scratch/` and reverts the copy, or reads old content with
`git show <rev>:<path>`. Reading commands (`status`, `diff`, `log`, `show`, `grep`)
stay allowed. This belongs in each read-only agent definition (`verifier`,
`reviewer`, `security`, `explorer`) and is a candidate for `context/AGENTS.md` where
it describes what a subagent may do.

title: Claude Code headless commits carried a Co-Authored-By trailer despite the no-attribution rule
body:
# BUG-039: Claude Code headless commits carried a Co-Authored-By trailer despite the no-attribution rule

## Prevention
A rule that overrides a CLI's built-in behaviour must name the CLI's own setting for it and the command
that reports the setting missing — prose alone does not hold against a vendor-injected reminder. Before
writing a "never do X" rule about agent-emitted output, check whether X is actually a tool/vendor default
rather than a choice the agent is making.

title: init-project's deploy/local.md template shipped invented facts for a project that didn't exist yet
body:
# BUG-040: init-project's deploy/local.md template shipped invented facts for a project that didn't exist yet

## Prevention
A template ships no value that could be mistaken for a fact: an example is either a `<placeholder>`
or wrapped in a comment, and the filling instruction states explicitly what happens to a placeholder
the answers don't cover (delete it, don't invent a value).

Graduated to: `skills/init-project/SKILL.md` Step 4 and `skills/init-project/assets/agents-tree/docs/deploy/local.md`

title: security agent graded stdlib crypto/rand UUID generation as hand-rolled cryptography
body:
# BUG-041: security agent graded stdlib crypto/rand UUID generation as hand-rolled cryptography

## Prevention
A ban must name the thing banned precisely enough that its stdlib counterpart is not caught by it.
When two harness agents contradict each other on the same mechanism in the same round, the rule is the
defect, not the code — fix the rule before trusting either report.

title: feature skill's cold-read cap, scope rule and decision rows all had gaps the simulation exposed
body:
# BUG-042: feature skill's cold-read cap, scope rule and decision rows all had gaps the simulation exposed

## Prevention
A gate must count something a print-mode (headless) run cannot argue its way around — reports, not
subjective "convergence". A design ambiguity is resolved by one recorded, named choice, never left open
for the agent to build every candidate under "simplest reading". A decision row that a later fix
reverses is updated in the same change that reverses it, not left standing as stale description.

title: verifier skipped the first-use guide and let a cached Go test result hide an e2e regression
body:
# BUG-043: verifier skipped the first-use guide and let a cached Go test result hide an e2e regression

## Prevention
An agent's "first time" duty is keyed to whether a specific file exists, never to a judgement call about whether another file "describes" the same thing. A verifier's counted test run is never a cached one — always force `-count=1` on the counts command, in this repo and in any project's own verification guide.

Graduated to: `agents/verifier.md` § What to run (`-count=1` always) and § Records (guide sentence)

title: security agent's crafted-input probes landed as untracked files in the repo root
body:
# BUG-044: security agent's crafted-input probes landed as untracked files in the repo root

## Prevention
Before writing ad hoc probe inputs, a review or verification agent puts
them under `.agents/scratch/<slug>/` with names it chooses itself, never
derived from the input content and never in the working directory — this
is already the agent's own stated rule (`agents/security.md:77`,
mirrored in `agents/verifier.md`), so the gap here is that it was not
followed, not that it was missing.
Second rule, new: after any dispatch that ran probes or crafted-input
tests, the main agent runs `git status --short --untracked-files=all` and
treats an untracked path outside `.agents/docs/` as a stop sign — the same
posture the hard rules already require for an unexplained `D` on tree
changes.

Graduated to: `context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules, "Ask git what actually changed before committing" bullet (sentence beginning "After any dispatch that can write")

title: failed probe-repo init fell through to the real checkout
body:
# BUG-045: failed probe-repo init fell through to the real checkout

## Prevention
Both halves written in the same commit as this record:
`context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules, "Ask git what actually changed" bullet
now also runs `git log --oneline @{u}..HEAD` and `git tag` after any
dispatch that can write, treating a commit or tag the dispatch did not
name as a stop sign; `agents/security.md` now says a probe repository is
created with `git init <dir>` whose exit status is read, and every later
command names that directory (`git -C <dir>`).

Graduated to: `context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules ("Ask git what actually changed" bullet, `git log`/`git tag` check) and `agents/security.md` (probe repo bound with `git init <dir>` / `git -C <dir>`)

title: `sh-agent update` reinstalled an uncommitted, dirty checkout
body:
# BUG-046: `sh-agent update` reinstalled an uncommitted, dirty checkout

## Prevention
`update` refuses a dirty checkout on every path, not just "behind
upstream" — graduated into `cmd/sh-agent/main.go`, `ADR-027`, and
`REQUIREMENTS.md` R4. Before relying on `sh-agent update` on a checkout used
for active development, confirm the dirty check itself is pinned (see
BUG-049): a guard that trusts git's configurable default can still pass a
dirty-looking-clean tree.

Graduated to: `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` `update()` (refuses a dirty checkout on every path); ADR-027; `REQUIREMENTS.md` R4

title: signed-tag release check compared a placeholder to itself
body:
# BUG-047: signed-tag release check compared a placeholder to itself

## Prevention
A check's expected value never comes from the same hand-substituted
input as the thing it checks — bind it to something produced elsewhere
(HEAD, a prior gate report), never a placeholder threaded through both
sides. A must-fail case is validated only in a state the real flow can
actually produce, or it validates nothing.

Graduated to: `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` § Releases (tag sits on HEAD; checks bind to HEAD and the gate report's `Range reviewed:` head)

title: the documented gate `gofmt -l .` fails on junk left in `.agents/scratch`
body:
# BUG-048: the documented gate `gofmt -l .` fails on junk left in `.agents/scratch`

## Prevention
A verification command that walks the whole tree is scoped to the source
directories on any project that keeps generated files under
`.agents/scratch/`; `agents/verifier.md` § What to run now names this caveat
for its Go auto-detect so the rule reaches every project, not just this one.

Graduated to: `agents/verifier.md` § What to run, plus `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md`, `.agents/docs/testing/sh-agent/guide.md` (`gofmt -l cmd internal`)

title: the BUG-046 dirty-checkout guard trusted git's configurable default
body:
# BUG-049: the BUG-046 dirty-checkout guard trusted git's configurable default

## Prevention
A guard never trusts a git command's default when a config key can change
it — pass the flag that pins the behaviour, and test with that key set
against you.

Graduated to: `internal/harness/repo.go` (`--untracked-files=all`) and `TestInspectCountsUntrackedFiles`

title: the install walk copied secret-shaped files into every vendor directory
body:
# BUG-050: the install walk copied secret-shaped files into every vendor directory

## Prevention
The same secret shapes that stop a commit (`context/AGENTS.md` § Hard
rules, "Ask git what actually changed" bullet) stop a deploy too: any step
that copies project files outward applies that list, not just the commit
step.

Graduated to: `internal/harness/plan.go` (`secretShaped`) and `TestPlanRefusesSecretShapedFiles`

title: `git init --bare` failed with "GIT_WORK_TREE not allowed without GIT_DIR" inside an isolated test
body:
# BUG-051: `git init --bare` failed with "GIT_WORK_TREE not allowed without GIT_DIR" inside an isolated test

## Prevention
Before isolating git (or any tool with "empty means set" semantics) from the
environment in a test, unset variables with `os.Unsetenv` after
`t.Setenv(k, "")`, not `t.Setenv(k, "")` alone; a blank string is not an unset
variable.

title: rejected-push case of `TestSendReport` returned nil error, no rejection
body:
# BUG-052: rejected-push case of `TestSendReport` returned nil error, no rejection

## Prevention
A test asserting a git conflict (rejected push, merge conflict, divergent
history) must make the competing commits differ in content, not just in
timing or checkout path; a fixed clock combined with otherwise-identical
inputs produces byte-identical, same-hash commits, which git treats as
already-applied rather than conflicting.

title: `sh-agent report`'s redaction needles missed most real credential shapes, and `--dry-run` could not reveal the miss
body:
# BUG-053: `sh-agent report`'s redaction needles missed most real credential shapes, and `--dry-run` could not reveal the miss

## Prevention
Before shipping a redaction or secret-detection feature, build adversarial fixtures of the realistic shapes it must catch (case variants, env-var prefixes, common vendor formats) — not only the shapes named in the design doc — and run them as must-fail tests against the shipped matcher. A safeguard the docs recommend to catch a failure mode must itself be tested against that failure mode (does `--dry-run` show a miss, not just a hit) before the docs claim it.

title: a secret in a JSON key was written verbatim into `report.json` as the redaction's recorded path
body:
# BUG-054: a secret in a JSON key was written verbatim into `report.json` as the redaction's recorded path

## Prevention
A test that verifies redaction correctness must assert on content (the marshalled/sent bytes contain no secret), not just record count — `len(recs) == 1` proves a record was made, not that it is safe. When a field is meant to carry metadata only (a path, a location), assert directly that it never carries the value it points at.

title: `sh-agent report` pushed to whatever remote its checkout resolved to, with no check that it was the feedback repository
body:
# BUG-055: `sh-agent report` pushed to whatever remote its checkout resolved to, with no check that it was the feedback repository

## Prevention
A tool that commits and pushes to a repository resolved from a flag, default, or the environment must verify the resolved remote matches the expected target before writing anything — not just that a `.git` exists. Refuse (do not silently follow) redirect-shaped environment variables (`GIT_DIR` and siblings) in any tool that shells out to git.

title: `sh-agent report`'s redaction had four structural gaps where a needle was present but content was still sent and the run reported success
body:
# BUG-056: `sh-agent report`'s redaction had four structural gaps where a needle was present but content was still sent and the run reported success

## Prevention
A text-processing redaction pipeline needs fixtures for malformed/adversarial structure, not just malformed *content*: duplicate keys, multi-marker lines, altered delimiters, and a structure that satisfies one parser (JSON) while defeating another (block scanning) in the same pipeline. When two matching strategies (JSON walk, line/block scan) can each individually "succeed" on the same input, test what happens when one finds nothing but the raw text still contains the needle — it must fall through, not be treated as clean.

title: a file-editing tool converted a JSON escape into its literal character, so a test named for that escape never exercised it
body:
# BUG-057: a file-editing tool converted a JSON escape into its literal character, so a test named for that escape never exercised it

## Prevention
After writing any fixture or text containing an escape sequence (`\u`, `\n` inside a string literal meant to stay literal, etc.) via an editing tool, check the actual bytes (`grep -n` / `od -c`) before trusting the file. A test's name is not evidence that it exercises the path it names — run a mutant that removes the path under test and confirm the test fails.

Graduated to: `context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules, "Ask git what actually changed" bullet

title: a review Outcome marked a finding "fixed by deleting the mechanism" while one of the finding's two triggers still leaked
body:
# BUG-058: a review Outcome marked a finding "fixed by deleting the mechanism" while one of the finding's two triggers still leaked

## Prevention
When a review Outcome marks a finding fixed, check every trigger the finding names — not only the headline reproduction — against a must-fail test before recording "fixed". "Fixed by deleting the mechanism" is only true if the deletion removes every path the finding described.

Graduated to: `context/AGENTS.md` § Definition of Done, step 2

title: replacing a matcher and a decoder each introduced a regression the old implementation had handled
body:
# BUG-059: replacing a matcher and a decoder each introduced a regression the old implementation had handled

## Prevention
When replacing a decoder or a matcher, run the old implementation's already-accepted inputs (edge-case numbers, quoting styles, encodings it previously handled) as must-pass cases against the new one before deleting the old code — a swap is a regression risk even when it targets a real, named defect.

title: code comments and docs claimed a push "cannot be redirected" without naming the redirect mechanisms actually checked
body:
# BUG-060: code comments and docs claimed a push "cannot be redirected" without naming the redirect mechanisms actually checked

## Prevention
A claim that a destination "cannot be redirected" or "never goes to X" names the specific redirect mechanisms it was checked against, not an unscoped guarantee — the next round otherwise finds the mechanism nobody tried. When a review finding lands a second consecutive round on the same mechanism (here: the push target, three rounds running), stop patching and take it to the operator for what it must guarantee, per the project's own review-convergence rule.

title: changelog agent's ADR-031 draft asserted facts not in its dispatch or the diff
body:
# BUG-061: changelog agent's ADR-031 draft asserted facts not in its dispatch or the diff

## Prevention
An ADR or changes entry states only what its dispatch and the diff say — every factual claim traceable to one of the two, no fill-in from memory of older ADRs or other repos. The main agent reads an agent-written ADR against the diff itself before committing it, not only via the reviewer. A claim about another project's use of the harness never enters a decision record (R8); this is the second time R8's no-consumer-naming rule was violated by a subagent (see BUG-015 for the installer-side case) and reinforces graduating a "no consumer names in this repo" check into the `changelog` agent definition or a `.agents/rules/` file, plus a citation rule (name sections, never line numbers, since lines drift).

Graduated to: `feature § Decisions (the main agent writes ADRs; changelog refuses them) and context § Definition of Done step 4`

title: Claude Code's verifier resolved `<app>` to the repo directory name, Antigravity to `cmd/<app>`
body:
# BUG-062: Claude Code's verifier resolved `<app>` to the repo directory name, Antigravity to `cmd/<app>`

## Prevention
An ordered resolution rule names the check for its first branch, not only the outcome, so an agent cannot silently fall through; the artifact records which branch fired, making a wrong resolution visible without a repro.

Addendum (2026-09-17): the b093fd6 fix was not reliable — repro-8 (`.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-17-bug-063-adr-032-repro.md`, 1 of 5 runs with it) never ran `ls -d cmd/*/` and named the guide `demo` again. The operator then chose to delete the `<app>` level for testing guides (ADR-032): one guide per project at `testing/guide.md`, so nothing needs resolving. Status stays fixed, now by removing the mechanism rather than patching the rule; the fix commit carries ADR-032 and the `agents/verifier.md`/`agents/documentation.md` update. When a prose rule is followed in most but not all runs, prefer deleting the decision it asks the agent to make over rewording it — three defects on `<app>` resolution (G20, BUG-062, the b093fd6 miss).

title: verifier's log said `Scope: complete` while a required testing guide was never written
body:
# BUG-063: verifier's log said `Scope: complete` while a required testing guide was never written

## Prevention
A duty an agent must perform is a numbered step it runs, not a paragraph beside the steps; "complete" is defined by the artifacts it owes, not only the commands it ran.

title: verifier's guide duty still not reliably performed on Claude Code after BUG-063's fix
body:
# BUG-064: verifier's guide duty still not reliably performed on Claude Code after BUG-063's fix

## Prevention
A duty a subagent must not skip goes in the dispatch text the main agent writes, not only in the subagent's own definition: rules inside `agents/verifier.md` itself were followed intermittently on Claude Code, while the same instruction placed in the dispatch prompt held in every run today.

title: `/feedback` loaded the harness skill instead of Claude Code's built-in
body:
# BUG-065: `/feedback` loaded the harness skill instead of Claude Code's built-in

## Prevention
A skill, agent, or command in this harness never takes the name of a built-in
slash command of either target CLI; check the CLI's built-in command list
before adding or renaming one. This is the same class of clash one level up
from `AGENTS.md` (project) § Rules for working here, which already forbids a
project skill reusing a harness name — that rule should be read as covering
vendor built-ins too, or a matching check added alongside it.

title: `go:embed all:` compiles untracked or gitignored files into the release binary
body:
# BUG-066: `go:embed all:` compiles untracked or gitignored files into the release binary

## Prevention
A test that a generated or embedded artifact matches a source must assert BOTH directions — extra content is as much a defect as missing content. An artifact built from the working tree, not from git, must be pinned to what git tracks, not just checked for completeness.

Graduated to: `skills/review-standards/SKILL.md` § 2 (generated-counterpart checklist item); one-line version in `context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules

title: `knownCheckout` resolved an `embedded:vX.Y.Z` manifest value as a filesystem path
body:
# BUG-067: `knownCheckout` resolved an `embedded:vX.Y.Z` manifest value as a filesystem path

## Prevention
When one field gains a value of a new kind, grep every reader of that field in the same change — guarding only the reader that prompted the change is half a fix. Same shape as BUG-036.

title: a must-fail mutation anchored on non-unique text hit the wrong site and its restore didn't undo the damage
body:
# BUG-068: a must-fail mutation anchored on non-unique text hit the wrong site and its restore didn't undo the damage

## Prevention
A must-fail mutation asserts its target is unique before writing (count occurrences, fail if not exactly one). Undo it by restoring the saved copy of the file, never by a reverse text replacement. After restoring, read `git diff` to confirm nothing else changed.

Graduated to: `skills/review-standards/SKILL.md` § 2 (mutation checklist item), cited from `skills/bug/SKILL.md` Step 3 and `skills/feature/SKILL.md` Step 4

title: `RemoveKeptClone`'s unpushed-commit guard fails open, deleting the operator's only copy
body:
# BUG-069: `RemoveKeptClone`'s unpushed-commit guard fails open, deleting the operator's only copy

## Prevention
A guard standing in front of a destructive action is written so that an
ERROR from the check keeps the data — `if err != nil` leaves, never falls
through to the delete — and its test suite includes the case where the check
itself cannot run, not only the cases where it runs and answers.

Graduated to: one-line form in `context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules; `err == nil && somethingToLose` example in `skills/golang/SKILL.md` § Error Handling

title: `sh-agent update --check` deleted files despite its read-only contract
body:
# BUG-070: `sh-agent update --check` deleted files despite its read-only contract

## Prevention
When adding a side effect to a command that has a read-only or dry-run mode,
