find that mode's early returns first and place the effect below them — and
the test for the effect asserts the read-only mode does NOT perform it, not
only that the normal mode does.

Graduated to: `context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules, "When a command has a read-only mode" bullet

title: two Phase 3 tests set up conditions that did not hold, so they passed or failed for the wrong reason
body:
# BUG-071: two Phase 3 tests set up conditions that did not hold, so they passed or failed for the wrong reason

## Prevention
Before trusting a test that sets up an unusual condition, prove the
condition actually holds — run the command by hand in a scratch fixture and
read its output — because a premise that silently does not hold produces a
test that passes or fails for the wrong reason. This is BUG-024's rule
("validate a check against a must-pass state, not only a must-fail one"),
applied to test setup rather than to the assertion; it did not generalize on
its own and needed re-recording here for the setup case specifically.

Graduated to: `context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules, "A test that sets up an unusual condition proves the condition HOLDS" clause

title: verifier dispatched against a tree the main agent kept editing
body:
# BUG-072: verifier dispatched against a tree the main agent kept editing

## Prevention
While a `verifier` dispatch is in flight, do not edit any file in its scope — keep
the tree frozen until the artifact lands; note anything found meanwhile and apply
it after. When a fix cannot wait, stop the run (TaskStop) rather than let it verify
a moving tree, then dispatch again after committing.

Graduated to: `context/AGENTS.md` § Definition of Done, step 1, "While that dispatch is IN FLIGHT the tree stays frozen" sentence

title: new retro record overwrote an existing same-day retro instead of taking the next free suffix
body:
# BUG-073: new retro record overwrote an existing same-day retro instead of taking the next free suffix

## Prevention
Before writing any DATED trail artifact whose name may already be taken (retro, handoff, changes entry, testing log, review), `ls` the target directory in the same turn as the write and pick the next free suffix from what is there, never from what this session remembers writing — an in-context directory listing goes stale the moment another session commits. When a write meant to create a file instead shows as MODIFIED in `git status`, that is read before staging, per BUG-011.

title: RemoveKeptClone reported "unpushed commits" for commits already on the remote
body:
# BUG-074: RemoveKeptClone reported "unpushed commits" for commits already on the remote

## Prevention
A message that reports a count names what the count was measured against whenever that basis can be stale or indirect, and never restates it as a stronger conclusion than the measurement supports — "N commits no remote-tracking ref holds" is what `--not --remotes` establishes; "N unpushed commits" is not. When the difference affects a decision the reader will make (here: delete a directory or not), the message also gives the command that settles it.

title: documented `go install` line for v1.1.0 fails without an SSH rewrite the reader was never told to add
body:
# BUG-075: documented `go install` line for v1.1.0 fails without an SSH rewrite the reader was never told to add

## Prevention
A command a doc tells the reader to RUN is executed as written, from the state the reader will be in, before the release that documents it — never approximated with different flags or read against the code instead. When it cannot be run before the release because it needs the tag the release itself creates, the release's Done row runs it immediately after and the doc is corrected in that same task; a docs review that can only read such a command says so under `## Not examined` rather than passing it.

title: `ResolveSource`'s not-found error hid the real precondition (no harness built in)
body:
# BUG-076: `ResolveSource`'s not-found error hid the real precondition (no harness built in)

## Prevention
When a fallback or guard refuses because a precondition failed, the error names the precondition that failed, not only the alternatives the reader might try. "X not found: try A, B or C" is right only when X's absence is the whole story; when the code knows something more specific — this build cannot do it at all, this file is the wrong kind, this mode forbids it — say that first, since the reader's next action depends on which it is.

title: release binary silently installed a stale plain-copy tree instead of its embedded harness
body:
# BUG-077: release binary silently installed a stale plain-copy tree instead of its embedded harness

## Prevention
When a program can obtain the same input from several sources, decide the order per KIND of
build, not once for all of them — an artifact that ships its own copy of an input must never
silently prefer a copy it found on the machine, and a source that cannot be updated (a plain
copy) is never preferred over one that can. State which source won whenever more than one was
possible and the choice changes what the tool then deploys.

title: verified v1.2.1 release binary installed to /usr/local/bin, but an earlier PATH entry kept running a stale (devel) build
body:
# BUG-078: verified v1.2.1 release binary installed to /usr/local/bin, but an earlier PATH entry kept running a stale (devel) build

## Prevention
Candidate rule (not yet written into any file — proposing, not applying): after installing or replacing the `sh-agent` binary, run `which -a sh-agent` and compare every match against the binary just installed; a "verified install" claim is only true once `sh-agent version` (run through the shell, unqualified — not by absolute path) reports the expected version. Separately: a downloaded release artifact is run (`version`) and checksum-verified before being moved into a system path, and the download step uses `--clobber` so a stale file at the download path can't be silently reused.

Graduated to: `context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules, "A claim that something works states HOW it was verified" bullet

title: `sh-agent update` reported success but left the running binary stale (bash hash cache)
body:
# BUG-079: `sh-agent update` reported success but left the running binary stale (bash hash cache)

## Prevention
Before shipping a fix, `update`/`install` should compare the running binary's path (`os.Executable()`, resolved) via `os.SameFile` against the file it just wrote; when they differ, the output should say the running binary was not replaced and is stale, and name the remedy (`hash -r` in bash, `rehash` in zsh). Docs (README / `remote.md`) should add `type sh-agent` (or `hash -r` before `which -a`) to the post-install/update verification steps, since `which -a` cannot see a shell's hash cache. Now also in `testing/guide.md` § 5's post-update check (a doc, not yet a formal graduation target — see Related for the recommendation).

Graduated to: `context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules, "A claim that something works states HOW it was verified" bullet; § Definition of Done, step 2

title: relative `--home` resolved against the repo directory on a real install, against cwd on `--dry-run`
body:
# BUG-080: relative `--home` resolved against the repo directory on a real install, against cwd on `--dry-run`

## Prevention
A path handed to a child process started with a different working directory (`cmd.Dir`) is made absolute before the handoff — the child cannot know the parent's cwd. This is also an instance of the `context/AGENTS.md` read-only-mode rule: `--dry-run` must resolve paths exactly as the real run does, or it is not a dry run of the real run.

Graduated to: `context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules, "When a command has a read-only mode" bullet

title: three fixes each passed their own test and the next review round found the same mechanism still broken
body:
# BUG-081: three fixes each passed their own test and the next review round found the same mechanism still broken

## Prevention
`context/AGENTS.md` § Definition of Done, step 2 already states: a fix's test builds the arrangement the finding measured — the pre-existing loose directory, the branch that installs nothing, the symlinked path — not a fresh fixture where the fix cannot lose. This rule was added as part of the session that produced this bug and covers it going forward.

Graduated to: `context/AGENTS.md` § Definition of Done, step 2 ("that test builds the ARRANGEMENT the finding measured" clause)

title: four must-fail mutations printed "fails as it must" when `go test` had failed at the build, so no test ever ran
body:
# BUG-082: four must-fail mutations printed "fails as it must" when `go test` had failed at the build, so no test ever ran

## Prevention
`context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules, the mutation clause already states: a must-fail mutation "counts as a verdict only when the mutated code COMPILED and a named test failed — a build failure … is printed as such and is no evidence". This rule was added as part of the session that produced this bug and covers it going forward.

Graduated to: `skills/review-standards/SKILL.md` § 2 (mutation checklist item, names BUG-082)

title: rewritten "write the artifact EARLY" rule in verifier.md followed in only 1 of 3 runs
body:
# BUG-083: rewritten "write the artifact EARLY" rule in verifier.md followed in only 1 of 3 runs

## Prevention
A change to an agent definition is verified by runs whose dispatch does NOT repeat the changed rule, and the count is reported as n of N, never "works". The sentence that must hold every run goes in the dispatch text (BUG-064) — the definition alone is not reliable enforcement on Claude Code.
`Diagnosis missed:` n/a.

Graduated to: `guide.md § 4 § Behavioural runs (n of N, never "works")`

title: retro-applied edits left a vocabulary enumerated in one place stale in another
body:
# BUG-084: retro-applied edits left a vocabulary enumerated in one place stale in another

## Prevention
When a value joins a vocabulary (a signal, a status, a category), grep the file and its consumers for every enumeration of that vocabulary — schema lines, templates, tables — and change them in the same edit. A rule that names an ordinal step ("the first command") is read against the agent's own step order before it is written.

Graduated to: `context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules, "A behaviour change includes the text that DESCRIBES it" bullet ("Two shapes hide best: a value joining a VOCABULARY …")

title: Antigravity loads only the first 24,000 bytes of the deployed global context
body:
# BUG-085: Antigravity loads only the first 24,000 bytes of the deployed global context

## Prevention
A deployed file that a vendor caps is pinned by a test that renders it from the real repo against the observed cap with a margin. Every smoke check asks one question answerable ONLY from the file's last section — never a question (like a skill count) the CLI can answer from its own internal listing, because that gives a false pass on a truncated file.

title: installer piped into `head` was killed by SIGPIPE, leaving files with no manifest
body:
# BUG-086: installer piped into `head` was killed by SIGPIPE, leaving files with no manifest

## Prevention
Never pipe a command that has side effects (install, update, report, a git write) into a filter that can exit before consuming its output (`head`, `grep -q`, `grep -m1`, `sed q`); run it bare, redirect its output to a file under `.agents/scratch/` if it must be shortened, and read that file. Recommend widening the existing `context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules sentence "A verification command is never piped into a filter inside a `&&` chain that leads to a commit…" with one clause covering a side-effecting command piped into an early-exiting filter, rather than a new bullet — the rendered context is size-pinned at 22,000 bytes (ADR-035, `TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock`).

Graduated to: `review-standards § 8 (code-shape rules; the reviewer's criterion, and golang/typescript/bash point at it)`

title: a behavioural-run fixture did not hold the condition its dispatch claimed, twice
body:
# BUG-087: a behavioural-run fixture did not hold the condition its dispatch claimed, twice

## Prevention
Before a behavioural run, prove the fixture's claimed state with the same command the agent will use (e.g. `git log -1 --format=%B | grep -c <line>` → 1), and choose the repository kind in which the changed rule can actually fire — a rule about the global context runs in a clone of the harness, not of a project.

Graduated to: `GUIDE-testing` § 4 § Behavioural runs + `fyr eval` (a `GUIDE-eval` row's setup asserts its fixture and a failed setup fails the row; the sandbox's `settings.json` is written for each row, `internal/eval/run.go` step 8) (the run kit's preamble until plan `PLAN-2026-10-26-0659-plan-fyr-eval-the-antigravity-run-kit-as-a-verb` Phase 3 deleted it)

title: cross-project survey findings landed in this repo's trail and issue lists
body:
# BUG-088: cross-project survey findings landed in this repo's trail and issue lists

## Prevention
A finding about another project is not recorded in this project's trail,
handoff Next Steps, or issue lists; a cross-project survey records only the
answer to the question it was run for. Before listing an issue, check which
repository it lives in.

Graduated to: `skills/research/SKILL.md` § Step 1: Discovery

title: changelog agent's date rule named a command it has no Bash to run
body:
# BUG-089: changelog agent's date rule named a command it has no Bash to run

## Prevention
An instruction in an agent or skill that names a command is checked against that agent's `tools:` list before it ships; an agent without Bash receives the command's output in its dispatch text instead of an instruction to run it.

title: changelog-agent behavioural fixture did not hold the state its dispatch claimed
body:
# BUG-090: changelog-agent behavioural fixture did not hold the state its dispatch claimed

## Prevention
A behavioural-run fixture is built to hold every fact its dispatch states, and the run script asserts each such fact (a grep for the line, a git log for the commit) before the CLI starts; a fixture fact with no assertion is not trusted.

Graduated to: `GUIDE-testing` § 4 § Behavioural runs + `fyr eval` (a `GUIDE-eval` row's setup asserts its fixture and a failed setup fails the row; the sandbox's `settings.json` is written for each row, `internal/eval/run.go` step 8) (the run kit's preamble until plan `PLAN-2026-10-26-0659-plan-fyr-eval-the-antigravity-run-kit-as-a-verb` Phase 3 deleted it)

title: first E2E 1 attempt invalid — headless agy auto-denied, control run couldn't isolate context
body:
# BUG-091: first E2E 1 attempt invalid — headless agy auto-denied, control run couldn't isolate context

## Prevention
A sandbox home for headless agy runs gets the real home's
`~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json` (no credential in it) copied in beside the copied token; a run
that uses tools is checked for the "auto-denied" stderr line before its output is read. A control for a
context change runs in a project that does not contain the harness source, never in a clone of
styrman-harness.

Graduated to: `GUIDE-testing` § 4 § Behavioural runs + `fyr eval` (a `GUIDE-eval` row's setup asserts its fixture and a failed setup fails the row; the sandbox's `settings.json` is written for each row and an `auto-denied` line fails it, `internal/eval/run.go` steps 8 and 12) (the run kit's preamble until plan `PLAN-2026-10-26-0659-plan-fyr-eval-the-antigravity-run-kit-as-a-verb` Phase 3 deleted it)

title: behavioural probe's truncated fixture left `claude -p` running inside the harness checkout, one run wrote a fake change entry
body:
# BUG-092: behavioural probe's truncated fixture left `claude -p` running inside the harness checkout, one run wrote a fake change entry

## Prevention
A probe script never extracts shell code from another file with a line-range pattern (a `}` inside a heredoc ends the range early); shared fixture code lives in its own file and is sourced whole. Every `cd` into a fixture directory is `cd <dir> || exit 1`, preceded by the fixture assertion that the graduated `AGENTS.md` § Testing rule ("a behavioural or sandbox run proves its setup before its output counts") already requires.

title: a refused `--from-zip` still created `~/.config/sh-agent`
body:
# BUG-093: a refused `--from-zip` still created `~/.config/sh-agent`

## Prevention
A command that can refuse its input creates nothing before the refusal
point; its test for the refused case asserts the whole target is
unchanged (an empty home stays empty), not only that the obvious
temporary artifact is absent.

title: A red test run pushed a real report to the feedback repository
body:
# BUG-094: A red test run pushed a real report to the feedback repository

## Prevention
A test for a command with an outward-facing side effect (report, download, push, deploy) cuts that reach first — empty `PATH`, no reachable credentials — before the command can run, and above all when the test is written ahead of the refusal or guard it checks: the red run executes the real thing. `--home` pointing at scratch does not isolate credentials that live elsewhere (`~/.ssh`, `gh` auth).

title: retro-applied rule text contradicted its own neighbors twice; verify log counted refused calls as executed
body:
# BUG-095: retro-applied rule text contradicted its own neighbors twice; verify log counted refused calls as executed

## Prevention
Before inserting a rule from a retro proposal, grep the target file for the mechanism's key words and
read every hit, not just the insertion point. A rule that changes a gate updates every sentence in that
file that lists the gate, in the same edit. A behavioural or verify log's call count reads each tool
result's error/refusal flag and states executed and refused as separate numbers, never one combined
count.

title: `skills/retro/SKILL.md` cited `dream`'s step numbers wrong, twice
body:
# BUG-096: `skills/retro/SKILL.md` cited `dream`'s step numbers wrong, twice

## Prevention
Before writing a sentence that cites another file's numbered steps or sections, run `grep -n "^## Step"` (or the equivalent heading pattern) on the target file and keep it on screen while writing the citation; name what the step does, not only its number. This is a specific case of `review-standards` § 3 ("every other restatement of a changed rule is changed with it") — extend it, or the project `AGENTS.md`, to cover cross-file numeric citations specifically, since three records now share this shape (BUG-027, BUG-032, BUG-096 all involve stale/wrong restatements caught only by grepping the subject, not the old wording).

title: verifier grep needle didn't match the sentence it was checking
body:
# BUG-097: verifier grep needle didn't match the sentence it was checking

## Prevention
Before dispatching a verifier check built on a grep, the main agent runs that grep bare on the working tree in the must-pass state first — this is the existing global rule ("a check is validated once in the must-pass and once in the must-fail state before its verdict is cited") applied to the dispatch-authoring step, which was skipped here. This is a test failing for a reason other than the change under test and cost one extra verifier round.

title: nine `/dream` probe runs measured the installed skill, not the working-tree edit
body:
# BUG-098: nine `/dream` probe runs measured the installed skill, not the working-tree edit

## Prevention
Already written: `AGENTS.md` § Testing — "a headless probe of a working-tree skill passes `--setting-sources project,local`, or first shows the real home has no installed copy of that name."

title: `/retro --dry-run` skipped the dreamer dispatch it was supposed to include
body:
# BUG-099: `/retro --dry-run` skipped the dreamer dispatch it was supposed to include

## Prevention
A skill that gains a dispatch under a read-only mode states in the same sentence that the dispatched agent's artifact is exempt from that mode — do not rely on the reader inferring the trail/change distinction from elsewhere.

title: dreamer sampled `bugs/INDEX.md` and missed the newest rows
body:
# BUG-100: dreamer sampled `bugs/INDEX.md` and missed the newest rows

## Prevention
An agent told to read an index states the bound explicitly (a date, or "all") and says "every row", never "recent rows" — an unbounded instruction over a growing table is read as a sample.

title: memory migration trusted an `autoMemoryDirectory` value that could come from a tracked file
body:
# BUG-101: memory migration trusted an `autoMemoryDirectory` value that could come from a tracked file

## Prevention
A step that derives a filesystem destination from a project-supplied setting checks whether that setting's source file is tracked before trusting its value for a write or move; a tracked source is reported, never acted on.

title: `/dream` Step 1 read the committed settings file with no trust gate
body:
# BUG-102: `/dream` Step 1 read the committed settings file with no trust gate

## Prevention
Same rule as BUG-101: a step that derives a filesystem destination from a project-supplied setting checks the source file's tracked status before trusting it, and constrains the resolved path to a known-owned directory tree regardless of source.

title: an empty slug from a failed `git rev-parse` made the store the shared root, and migration ran even when the settings write was refused
body:
# BUG-103: an empty slug from a failed `git rev-parse` made the store the shared root, and migration ran even when the settings write was refused

## Prevention
A step that derives a path from a project file or a command's output checks the result (non-empty, well-formed) before any move; a step that depends on a prior write's success checks that write succeeded before acting on its result, never assuming order implies success.

title: `TestReinstallBuildsAndInstalls` flaked under a concurrent `go test`
body:
# BUG-104: `TestReinstallBuildsAndInstalls` flaked under a concurrent `go test`

## Prevention
A test that asserts a shared directory is clean names the exact path its
own run created, never a glob over a directory other processes also write
to.

title: gate report's VERDICT: SHIP contradicted its own "What was not checked" section
body:
# BUG-105: gate report's VERDICT: SHIP contradicted its own "What was not checked" section

## Prevention
Before writing a VERDICT line, read every item in "What was not checked" against every blocking condition (including project-added ones like `AGENTS.md` § Release's Antigravity-run rule); an item a condition names forces NO-SHIP. Write the verdict last, after that section is final, never before it. Candidate home: `skills/preflight/SKILL.md` Step 5.

Graduated to: `skills/preflight/SKILL.md` Step 5 ("Write the verdict line LAST … an item a condition names makes the verdict NO-SHIP whatever the rows above say (BUG-105)")

title: headless fixture clones placed inside the harness checkout wrote to its own trail
body:
# BUG-106: headless fixture clones placed inside the harness checkout wrote to its own trail

## Prevention
A fixture clone for a headless run must live outside every git checkout the
agent works in (never under `.agents/scratch/` of this repo), and the run
script asserts it before starting the CLI: `git -C "$(dirname <clone>)"
rev-parse` must fail. This is a specific instance of `AGENTS.md` § Testing's
existing sentence that a must-fail control "runs in a project that does not
contain the harness source" — that clause did not name fixture placement for
ordinary (must-pass) runs too, and the main agent did not extend it on its
own while the risk was visible.

Graduated to: `fyr eval` safety check b (`internal/eval/guard.go`, `TestGuardOutsideCheckout`, `TestGuardPreflight`: a sandbox root or clone inside a checkout is refused) (the run kit's preamble until plan `PLAN-2026-10-26-0659-plan-fyr-eval-the-antigravity-run-kit-as-a-verb` Phase 3 deleted it)

title: `sh-agent search` inside headless fixture clones wrote the real home's global search index
body:
# BUG-107: `sh-agent search` inside headless fixture clones wrote the real home's global search index

## Prevention
A behavioural run in which the agent under test may itself invoke `sh-agent` puts a wrapper
first on PATH that pins `--home` to a scratch home (not only the kit's own calls); the run
script then asserts afterward that the real `~/.config/sh-agent/` gained no file.

Graduated to: `fyr eval` (the sandbox's `fyr` wrapper first on PATH pins `--home` to the sandbox and refuses an agent's own `--home`, `internal/eval/run.go` step 7, `TestRunWrapperPinsHome`; safety check c fingerprints the real `~/.config/fyr`, `~/.config/sh-agent`, `~/.gemini/config` and the CLI's `settings.json` before and after each row, `TestGuardFingerprint`) (the run kit's preamble until plan `PLAN-2026-10-26-0659-plan-fyr-eval-the-antigravity-run-kit-as-a-verb` Phase 3 deleted it)

title: `gitView` read a work-tree rename's source path outside the checkout
body:
# BUG-108: `gitView` read a work-tree rename's source path outside the checkout

## Prevention
Parse a tool's output only in the shape a flag pins (`--no-renames`, `-z`, `--porcelain=v1` here), never a shape the tool may vary by its own heuristics (git's rename detection). Before recording a mutation as "equivalent" in a plan, re-examine it for the input shape that would make it live — a mutation judged equivalent deserves the same adversarial-input scrutiny as a live finding, not less.

title: `update` swept leftover release directories with a glob built from the home path
body:
# BUG-109: `update` swept leftover release directories with a glob built from the home path

## Prevention
A path built from the home directory or any operator-supplied path is never
passed to `filepath.Glob`; list the parent with `ReadDir` and match by name.
When a class of defect is fixed at one call site, `git grep -n
'filepath.Glob' | grep -v _test` before closing the fix, to find the other
call sites of the same class.

Graduated to: `skills/golang/SKILL.md` (no `filepath.Glob` on an operator path) and `skills/bug/SKILL.md` Step 4 (a class fix covers every site)

title: report redaction deny-list missed common credential shapes, then missed escaped/underscored tokens
body:
# BUG-110: report redaction deny-list missed common credential shapes, then missed escaped/underscored tokens

## Prevention
A deny-list of credential-shape instances never converges — when a review
names more shapes for the third time on the same mechanism, put a per-kind
generalized rule to the operator instead of writing a fourth batch of
literal prefixes (done here: Outcome item 4, `delivery.md` § report notes
redaction is a safety net, not a guarantee). A needle matched against raw
text never carries a leading `\b`, because escapes and underscores are word
characters. Every added needle gets a benign near-miss case in the same
test.

Graduated to: project `AGENTS.md` § Rules for working here (needles grow by kind; no leading `\b`)

title: two vendored skills carried no source, pin or digest, and rewritten local text was indistinguishable from upstream
body:
# BUG-111: two vendored skills carried no source, pin or digest, and rewritten local text was indistinguishable from upstream

## Prevention
A provenance pin is verified by `git archive <pin> <path> | tar -x` and
`diff -r` against the vendored directory before it is written, not inferred
from a commit date or message; the diff itself is recorded as the row's
"Local changes". "Vendored" means verbatim; anything with local edits is a
fork, and it says so in the manifest, with its own pin and diff record.

Graduated to: project `AGENTS.md` § Rules for working here (the pin verified by an upstream diff; an edited copy is a fork)

title: consolidating the settings writer onto WriteAtomic dropped a diagnostic, then reordered close and rename
body:
# BUG-112: consolidating the settings writer onto WriteAtomic dropped a diagnostic, then reordered close and rename

## Prevention
When a refactor merges or consolidates a sequence whose ORDER is the
contract (write, sync, close, rename; or any lock/unlock, open/close
pairing), diff the merged sequence against each original line by line before
dispatching it for review, not just its net effect. Any such ordering that
no behavioural test can observe gets its own source-level pin test in the
same change, not added later after a regression.

Graduated to: `skills/review-standards/SKILL.md` § 2 (a source pin for an unobservable order; a consolidation keeps each original's order)

title: /init-project writes .claude/ on an Antigravity-only machine
body:
# BUG-113: /init-project writes .claude/ on an Antigravity-only machine

## Prevention
A harness step that writes a vendor's own path (`.claude/`, `.gemini/`, a vendor settings file) runs only when that vendor is installed: read the install manifest's vendor, never assume both CLIs. A reader of that path has a fallback for the machine where it was never written.

title: the context clause for BUG-113 overflowed the Antigravity rules block
body:
# BUG-114: the context clause for BUG-113 overflowed the Antigravity rules block

## Prevention
An edit to `context/AGENTS.md` runs `go test ./internal/harness -run TestRenderedContext -v` and reads the byte count before any dispatch; with a few bytes of headroom, every added word is paid for by a cut in the same edit. The size rule already existed as a test (BUG-085); it was not run, so it was not followed.

title: first agy-only sandbox runs for BUG-113 used a copy of the real home's Antigravity settings
body:
# BUG-115: first agy-only sandbox runs for BUG-113 used a copy of the real home's Antigravity settings

## Prevention
1. Before building any sandbox home, read AGENTS.md § Testing and the skill-matrix agy settings line and write the settings file from them, never from the real home.
2. An agy scenario whose skill runs compound shell scripts (/init-project, /dream) needs `--dangerously-skip-permissions` in its throwaway clone, decided before the run.
The first rule already existed in AGENTS.md § Testing; it was not followed.

title: the agy tool-free probe used a toy prompt, so D7a declared an invocation that failed on the real prompt
body:
# BUG-116: the agy tool-free probe used a toy prompt, so D7a declared an invocation that failed on the real prompt

## Prevention
A probe that decides an invocation runs with the real payload's size and shape, never a toy one; read the flags' own stderr warnings before recording a probe as a pass.

title: the agy prompt went on argv, over the 131072-byte execve argument limit
body:
# BUG-117: the agy prompt went on argv, over the 131072-byte execve argument limit

## Prevention
Large or private data to a child process goes on stdin or in a file, never as one argument; check the payload cap against the OS per-argument limit.

title: pid-file locks raced and could lose an index line or stop the nightly job
body:
# BUG-118: pid-file locks raced and could lose an index line or stop the nightly job

## Prevention
A lock between processes on one machine is a flock, never a pid file with staleness rules.

title: the headless agy child inherited the operator's permissions
body:
# BUG-119: the headless agy child inherited the operator's permissions

## Prevention
An unattended child CLI fed untrusted text runs with a configuration that grants nothing, built by the caller, never with the operator's own.

title: a stale "Claude Code loads" line survived Phase 2
body:
# BUG-120: a stale "Claude Code loads" line survived Phase 2

## Prevention
Before calling a claim reversed, grep its key words across every living file, not only the setting's name (the global context's describing-text rule, applied).

title: a read-only path and a cleanup path wrote to the home
body:
# BUG-121: a read-only path and a cleanup path wrote to the home

## Prevention
A read-only or dry-run path gets a test that lists the directory before and after; cleanup order lives in one deferred function.

title: a commit went through after a secret scan that reported hits
body:
# BUG-122: a commit went through after a secret scan that reported hits

## Prevention
The global rule already covers this: a verification step and the commit are separate calls, and the verification's result is read first. This was a failure to follow it.

Graduated to: `review-standards § 8 (code-shape rules; the reviewer's criterion, and golang/typescript/bash point at it)`

title: a real-home gate run of /distill wrote test lines into the real ~/.config/sh-agent logs
body:
# BUG-123: a real-home gate run of /distill wrote test lines into the real ~/.config/sh-agent logs

## Prevention
A gate run of a skill that writes `~/.config/sh-agent` (feedback-log, retro without `--dry-run`, distill) runs in a sandbox home, never the real one. The kit lists `~/.config/sh-agent` before and after every real-home batch and reads any change before the log is written.

Graduated to: `fyr eval` safety check c (the real `~/.config/fyr` and `~/.config/sh-agent` fingerprinted around every row, `internal/eval/guard.go`, `TestGuardFingerprint`; `GUIDE-testing` § 4 § Behavioural runs) (the run kit's preamble until plan `PLAN-2026-10-26-0659-plan-fyr-eval-the-antigravity-run-kit-as-a-verb` Phase 3 deleted it)

title: a tool call's arguments in a string-only protobuf sub-message reached the dreamer's prompt (SD1)
body:
# BUG-124: a tool call's arguments in a string-only protobuf sub-message reached the dreamer's prompt (SD1)

## Prevention
A schemaless decoder tries the structured parse before the text reading. A corpus measurement ("0 of 971") is evidence about one corpus, never a structural guarantee: the structural case gets its own unit fixture.

title: `search: 2 hits ..., 1 with every word` printed the same chunk twice (SD2)
body:
# BUG-125: `search: 2 hits ..., 1 with every word` printed the same chunk twice (SD2)

## Prevention
A dedup key names the entity (the chunk), never a derived display value (the printed line).

title: data strings could forge a proposal section or a prompt data block (SD3, SD8)
body:
# BUG-126: data strings could forge a proposal section or a prompt data block (SD3, SD8)

## Prevention
Every string that comes from data and lands beside a delimiter (heading marker, fence, label) is escaped for that delimiter, labels and summary lines included. The test forges each delimiter from each position.

title: report redaction hit ordinary prose, then after the first fix kept short real secrets (IN1)
body:
# BUG-127: report redaction hit ordinary prose, then after the first fix kept short real secrets (IN1)

## Prevention
A needle that judges a value states its rule in one comment and pins BOTH a benign near-miss and a must-redact shape per clause in the same commit. A fix that narrows a needle gets security review in the same round, since the safe direction is over-redaction.

title: a write that failed midway through `install` left files no manifest listed (IN2)
body:
# BUG-128: a write that failed midway through `install` left files no manifest listed (IN2)

## Prevention
In a function that writes several files and records them, every return after the first write goes through the one path that saves the record. Grep the function for `return` before calling the fix done.

title: install, status, diff and uninstall followed symlinks under the home (IN3)
body:
# BUG-129: install, status, diff and uninstall followed symlinks under the home (IN3)

## Prevention
Every file operation under a home directory the operator may have linked `Lstat`s the path AND its components, in every verb that touches it (install, status, diff, uninstall, resync). The test links a directory, not only a file.

title: `update --check` / `--dry-run` on a dirty checkout reported success where the real run refuses (IN4)
body:
# BUG-130: `update --check` / `--dry-run` on a dirty checkout reported success where the real run refuses (IN4)

## Prevention
A test of every read-only mode runs it in the state the real run refuses and asserts the same refusal.

title: after a clone every trail record looked new and the size cap dropped the transcripts
body:
# BUG-131: after a clone every trail record looked new and the size cap dropped the transcripts

## Prevention
"Changed since" for a file git tracks comes from git, never from the filesystem's mtime, which a clone resets.

title: one extra JSON key in the model's answer failed the run every night
body:
# BUG-132: one extra JSON key in the model's answer failed the run every night

## Prevention
A decoder of a model's free-form JSON ignores unknown keys and validates the fields it uses; strict decoding of model output is a nightly failure loop.

title: a conversation database copied mid-checkpoint failed the project (a torn global-index copy failed the whole run)
body:
# BUG-133: a conversation database copied mid-checkpoint failed the project (a torn global-index copy failed the whole run)

## Prevention
A read of a live SQLite database is a copy, retried once. A test of an open failure forces a read, since `sql.Open` does not touch the file; the fixture proves its condition in a subtest before the retry test is trusted.

title: harness-generated user content reached the dreamer's prompt
body:
# BUG-134: harness-generated user content reached the dreamer's prompt

## Prevention
A transcript reader lists the harness's own line shapes (meta flag, injected tag prefixes) and drops them; a new tag the harness starts writing is added to that list, with a test line per prefix.

title: dream verb inconsistencies, and a git option placed after the verb that silently emptied the modified-file set
body:
# BUG-135: dream verb inconsistencies, and a git option placed after the verb that silently emptied the modified-file set

## Prevention
A command line built in code gets a test that runs it (an exec of the real binary against an empty directory), since git rejects a global option after the verb with an exit status the caller may swallow. Every usage refusal of one verb exits with the same code and writes to the caller's writer.

title: change entry named with a guessed time stamp
body:
# BUG-136: change entry named with a guessed time stamp

## Prevention
A time-stamped file name is produced by running `date +%F-%H%M` in the same tool call that writes the file, never typed.

title: a 0755 script under an embedded tree failed TestEmbeddedPlanEqualsCheckout
body:
# BUG-137: a 0755 script under an embedded tree failed TestEmbeddedPlanEqualsCheckout

## Prevention
A file under the five embedded trees is a source change for the embed tests whatever its extension: run guide § 1 on every change, never skipped for "no .go file in the diff". Never give a file in those trees an exec bit; invoke scripts as `bash <path>`.

title: restatement-grep.sh exits 1 with no output in any project but the harness checkout
body:
# BUG-138: restatement-grep.sh exits 1 with no output in any project but the harness checkout

## Prevention
1. A script a skill ships for every project is tested in a fixture that is NOT the harness checkout (a temp git repo with none of the harness's files), in both the hit and no-hit state, asserting exit code and output shape; the harness tree makes every optional input present, so a run there proves nothing about other projects.
2. Under `set -e -o pipefail`, a command substitution whose pipeline may legitimately produce nothing ends in `|| true` on the whole group, never only on its first stage. Parent rule: "silence from your own instrumentation is not evidence" (review-standards § 2) was not applied to this script.

title: `documentation` agent's "ROADMAP.md is not yours" lane held in 5 of 6 behavioural runs
body:
# BUG-139: `documentation` agent's "ROADMAP.md is not yours" lane held in 5 of 6 behavioural runs

## Prevention
- Report a lane rule's result as n of N runs, never "holds".
- A dispatch to `documentation`, `changelog` or `bugs` never names `ROADMAP.md` or `TODO.md` as a file to edit; the definition's refusal is the weaker guard.

title: three of five matrix kit processes ended without their result line or EXIT-trap listing
body:
# BUG-140: three of five matrix kit processes ended without their result line or EXIT-trap listing

## Prevention
1. A run kit separates RUN from CHECK: the check is a second script (or a `--check-only` mode) that re-reads the clone and transcript and can be re-run after the driver finishes; a result line is derived from state on disk, not from the process that produced it.
2. `grep ... | wc -l || echo 0` under `pipefail` prints two zeros (grep's exit 1 fails the pipeline, so the `||` also fires; the kit's `cloud_cmds` field shows it). Use `grep -c ... || true` for a count.

Graduated to: true`), written 2026-10-01; cause of the lost lines still unknown

title: headless Antigravity rows died "auto-denied" for a shell command the per-name grant list could not express
body:
# BUG-141: headless Antigravity rows died "auto-denied" for a shell command the per-name grant list could not express

## Prevention
A headless Antigravity row that dies "auto-denied" is diagnosed from its conversation database (last `CommandLine`) and `cli.log` (`invalid allow entry`) BEFORE any grant is widened. A grant is one of the four actions the store knows; a skill whose text holds a shell construct (loop, heredoc) is run with `command(*)` in a sandbox clone, never with a longer name list.

title: working tree edited while the verifier ran; its log ended BLOCKED
body:
# BUG-142: working tree edited while the verifier ran; its log ended BLOCKED

## Prevention
Before dispatching `verifier`, empty your own edit queue: make every fix still intended, read `git status --short`, then dispatch. While the dispatch is in flight do only reads (`Read`, `grep`, `git log`); a fix that cannot wait stops the run (`TaskStop`), is committed, and the verifier is re-dispatched. A "docs-only" edit is not exempt: in this repository the test suite reads `skills/`, `agents/` and `context/`.
The rule already exists (`context/AGENTS.md` § Definition of Done, step 1), so it was not followed.

Graduated to: `context/AGENTS.md` § Definition of Done step 1 ("the tree stays frozen while it runs … a fix that cannot wait stops the run (`TaskStop`), commits, then re-dispatches"); held through all five v2.1.0 gate verifier runs

title: skills shipped `allowed-tools: Bash` and unverified install fetches (`curl | sh`), missed by four reviews
body:
# BUG-143: skills shipped `allowed-tools: Bash` and unverified install fetches (`curl | sh`), missed by four reviews

## Prevention
- A skill's frontmatter is a permission surface: `allowed-tools` is never set in a harness skill (the operator's permission mode decides). Graduated: `LoadSkills` in `internal/harness/inventory.go` refuses any skill whose frontmatter sets it ("allowed-tools is never set in a harness skill; the operator's permission mode decides (BUG-143)"), pinned by `TestLintRefusesAllowedTools` in `internal/harness/harness_test.go`.
- Every install instruction in a skill fetches a pinned artifact and verifies a checksum or signature before running it; `curl | sh`, `wget -O- | bash` and unpinned `npx -y` are findings. The security reviewer's brief for skill assets names them. Not yet mechanised: stays a review rule. Graduation target: `review-standards` § 8 or the security agent's definition.

Graduated to: `internal/harness/inventory.go` `LoadSkills` (refuses `allowed-tools`) and `TestLintRefusesAllowedTools` in `internal/harness/harness_test.go`; the pinned-install-artifact half stays a review rule

title: `--home <scratch>` timer commands drove the operator's real service-manager unit
body:
# BUG-144: `--home <scratch>` timer commands drove the operator's real service-manager unit

## Prevention
Anything a `--home`-scoped command touches OUTSIDE the home (a service manager's unit namespace, a PATH entry, a global cache) is named or keyed by the home as well, and its test asserts the name the manager receives, not only the files under the home.

title: the escaped-secret redaction test passed with its fix reverted, then failed with the fix present
body:
# BUG-145: the escaped-secret redaction test passed with its fix reverted, then failed with the fix present

## Prevention
- A test that sets up an unusual condition proves the condition holds first: for an escape, `grep -n` the written file for the escape itself, as the hard rule says.
- A must-fail control that PASSES means the fixture, not the code, is wrong: fix the fixture before touching the implementation. Choose the needle from the measured shape, not from a guess.

title: refresh-catalog.sh with a relative --dest/--work cloned for 3m32s, then exited 1 "the catalog is empty"
body:
# BUG-146: refresh-catalog.sh with a relative --dest/--work cloned for 3m32s, then exited 1 "the catalog is empty"

## Prevention
A script that takes a path flag and starts a child with another working directory (a `cd`, a `go test`, a `git -C`) makes the path absolute at parse time, and its test passes at least one RELATIVE path from a directory that is not the repository root.
The rule already existed (`review-standards` § 8): it was not followed.

title: refresh-catalog.sh's swap ran rm -rf on every directory under --dest, whatever --dest was
body:
# BUG-147: refresh-catalog.sh's swap ran rm -rf on every directory under --dest, whatever --dest was

## Prevention
A script that deletes under a path it was given deletes only what its own manifest names there, refuses an empty value and the places that can never be the target (`/`, home, the checkout, their ancestors), and its test asserts that a bystander directory survives. A guard backed by a second check gets a test on the guard's own message, or removing the guard fails nothing.

title: refresh-catalog.sh's swap loop exited 1 silently half way, leaving the destination with no entries
body:
# BUG-148: refresh-catalog.sh's swap loop exited 1 silently half way, leaving the destination with no entries

## Prevention
In a bash script under `set -euo pipefail`, a loop body or pipeline stage never ends in `test && command` or a bare `grep`: write `if ...; then ...; fi` and `{ grep ... || true; }`. A destructive loop is tested with its input in the state a half-done earlier run leaves behind.

title: the timer's "real home" was read from `$HOME`, which a sandbox run overrides
body:
# BUG-149: the timer's "real home" was read from `$HOME`, which a sandbox run overrides

## Prevention
Never decide "the operator's own" from an environment variable a sandbox sets (`HOME`, `XDG_*`, `PATH`): ask the account database or the service itself. A fix for an isolation bug is tested in the isolation setup the project really uses (here `HOME` overridden AND `--home` passed), not only through a seam that replaces the lookup.

title: the red run of a guard test wrote into the real checkout
body:
# BUG-150: the red run of a guard test wrote into the real checkout

## Prevention
A test for a guard is written so that the guard's ABSENCE is harmless, because red-first runs it without the guard: the forbidden place is a stand-in under the test's temporary directory (copy the script or point it at a fake root) and the sources cannot run; never the real checkout, home or `/` with working inputs. After any red run of such a test, `git status --short --untracked-files=all` before the next edit.
The first half already existed (review R3-4), so it was not carried over: the rule was followed for `--dest` and missed for `--work`.

title: the frontmatter reader closed a block at a fence followed by two carriage returns
body:
# BUG-151: the frontmatter reader closed a block at a fence followed by two carriage returns

## Prevention
A check that decides where untrusted text ends compares the exact shape, never a trimmed one: trim one known terminator, not a set of characters, and test the neighbour shapes (two of the terminator, another space character, a byte-order mark) as must-refuse cases.

title: search output filtered a list of characters, not Unicode's format class
body:
# BUG-152: search output filtered a list of characters, not Unicode's format class

## Prevention
Text shown to a terminal or handed to a model is filtered by Unicode class (`unicode.Cc`, `Cf`, `Zl`, `Zp`), not by a list of code points; a second report against one list is the signal to switch to the class.

title: two frontmatter shapes hid a permission key from the installer's lint while a YAML reader still reads it
body:
# BUG-153: two frontmatter shapes hid a permission key from the installer's lint while a YAML reader still reads it

## Prevention
A lint that guards against what ANOTHER parser will read must refuse everything it cannot itself read the same way: whatever it skips as harmless (indentation, a character it does not treat as a line break, a line it calls a continuation) is a place the other parser may find a key. For each skip rule, write the must-refuse case in which the skipped text holds the forbidden key, in every kind the lint covers.

title: the verifier followed the dispatch's description of its log over its own template (file name, status line)
body:
# BUG-154: the verifier followed the dispatch's description of its log over its own template (file name, status line)

## Prevention
An agent's artifact has parts a program reads (file name, status line): the definition names them and says they hold against the dispatch, and a dispatch never re-describes an agent's artifact format: it names the slug and the duties, the definition owns the shape. A kit's `pass=0` is read from the saved run before it is called a failure or a pass.

title: the refresh ended with exit 141 and no message when an entry held very many files of a refused kind
body:
# BUG-155: the refresh ended with exit 141 and no message when an entry held very many files of a refused kind

## Prevention
Under `pipefail`, never `producer | head -N` in a command substitution or as a statement: the producer's SIGPIPE ends the script with 141 and no message once the output outgrows a pipe. Make the producer stop itself (`find -quit`, `awk '{...; exit}'`), and test each refusal with enough input to fill a pipe. The fail-open form: the same pipe in a condition (`producer | grep -q x || refuse`) does not end the script, it takes the wrong branch, because 141 reads as "no match" (BUG-157); ask the tool directly or feed the consumer a here-string.

Graduated to: `TestScriptsHaveNoEarlyExitPipe` in `internal/harness/scripts_pipe_test.go` (fails on an unguarded pipe into `head`, `grep -q`, `grep -m` or `sed ...q` in any tracked `skills/*/scripts/*.sh` or `.agents/docs/testing/*.sh` that sets `pipefail`)

title: `git remote set-url` showed a source override's value on failure
body:
# BUG-156: `git remote set-url` showed a source override's value on failure

## Prevention
A value that must never be shown is tracked by where it FLOWS, not by which call was seen to print it: list every command that receives it and silence or wrap each. The test plants a marker in the value and greps the whole output for it on each failure path. This is `AGENTS.md`'s "needles grow by KIND" rule applied to call sites.

title: a kit asserting a commit that IS in a long-history clone was refused
body:
# BUG-157: a kit asserting a commit that IS in a long-history clone was refused

## Prevention
Under `pipefail` a pipeline into a consumer that exits early is wrong in a condition too (`if`, `||`, `&&`): status 141 reads as "no match". Ask the tool directly, or feed the consumer a here-string. Graduated: pinned by `TestScriptsHaveNoEarlyExitPipe` in `internal/harness/catalog_test.go`.

Graduated to: `TestScriptsHaveNoEarlyExitPipe` in `internal/harness/catalog_test.go` (same test as BUG-155)

title: the kit preamble ended with exit 2 and no message when `~/.config/sh-agent` did not exist
body:
# BUG-158: the kit preamble ended with exit 2 and no message when `~/.config/sh-agent` did not exist

## Prevention
A script that every kit sources gets a behaviour test under a temporary home before it is trusted, with the unusual states as cases (the directory absent, the tool missing). A check whose two readings can be the same empty value is proven once in its must-fail state (`review-standards` § 2).

title: TestRefreshCatalogScript failed once with no code change when a run crossed midnight
body:
# BUG-159: TestRefreshCatalogScript failed once with no code change when a run crossed midnight

## Prevention
A test that compares two runs of something that stamps the date either fixes the date or does not straddle midnight. A one-off red run gets its cause found before it is called a flake.

title: live credentials left in scratch homes while the records said they were deleted
body:
# BUG-160: live credentials left in scratch homes while the records said they were deleted

## Prevention
Before a kit copies any credential into a sandbox home, it records every path it copies and deletes exactly those, then proves none is left with a `find` over the home for the credential names (`id_ed25519*`, `.credentials.json`, `application_default_credentials.json`, `credentials.db`, `*oauth-token*`); that `find` is run once against a home that still holds a planted credential (must-fail seen) before its empty result is cited. A record or handoff never says "credentials deleted" without that find's output.
Mechanism now enforces this: `fyr eval` safety check d, a credential scan of every sandbox directory (the clone, the CLI's output, the logs and the sandbox home) against a baseline taken before the token is linked (`internal/eval/creds.go`; `TestCredsLeftovers`, `TestCredsNotCredentials`, `TestCredsBaseline`; mutation-checked in plan Phase 1). A row with a new credential FAILs with that reason. Until 2026-10-26 it was the run kit's preamble (`kit_credential_leftovers`) and `TestKitPreambleRefusesLeftoverCredentials`, both deleted with the kit.

Graduated to: `fyr eval` safety check d (`internal/eval/creds.go`, `TestCredsLeftovers`, `TestCredsBaseline`) (the run kit's preamble until plan `PLAN-2026-10-26-0659-plan-fyr-eval-the-antigravity-run-kit-as-a-verb` Phase 3 deleted it); first graduated to the preamble's `kit_credential_leftovers` at commit ee28fe3

title: v2.4.1 was cut right after the v2.4.0 bridge, stranding a binary-only place
body:
# BUG-161: v2.4.1 was cut right after the v2.4.0 bridge, stranding a binary-only place

## Prevention
Rule: after a release that bridges a trust or format change (one older binaries need in order to move forward), the next release is not cut until the operator confirms every binary-only place has crossed.
Graduated 2026-10-06 into a mechanism: `skills/preflight/SKILL.md` Step 6, the paragraph "Then the bridge check." (after "Before item 1"): /preflight names the bridge and asks, in the operator's own turn, whether every place has crossed it; without a yes it stops before item 1, and an unattended run never tags past a bridge. Project `AGENTS.md` § Release carries the one-clause pointer ("a release right after a bridge release waits for the operator's word that every place has crossed it (preflight Step 6, BUG-161)"). Both read and confirmed. The changed skill ships in the next release, which owes its Antigravity run (AGENTS.md § Release); until then the rule is prose, not yet exercised on either CLI.

Graduated to: `skills/preflight/SKILL.md` Step 6 "Then the bridge check." (names the bridge, asks the operator before item 1, never tags past one unattended) and the pointer in project `AGENTS.md` § Release; ships in the next release, which owes its Antigravity run

title: the A/B kit's harness runs registered scratch apps in the real global search index
body:
# BUG-162: the A/B kit's harness runs registered scratch apps in the real global search index

## Prevention
Any headless run of a harness-loaded CLI goes through `fyr eval`, whose sandbox puts a `fyr` wrapper pinning `--home <sandbox>` first on `PATH`; a headless run outside it puts such a wrapper first on `PATH` itself. Isolating `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` alone isolates the CLI, not the harness.

title: an A/B kit run left an agent-written server listening on every interface for four hours
body:
# BUG-163: an A/B kit run left an agent-written server listening on every interface for four hours

## Prevention
A kit that runs an agent checks, after the run, for processes it left behind (cwd or executable under the clone or `KIT_HOME`, or `HOME=$KIT_HOME`), kills them, and fails the run; from 2026-10-08 the run kit's exit trap did it for every kit, and since 2026-10-26 `fyr eval`'s safety check e does it for every row (`internal/eval/procs_linux.go`; `TestProcsLeftovers`, `TestRunExitChecks`). A residual a review names as "survives" gets a check, not a header note.

title: `git log` in a project root ran that repository's `gpg.program`
body:
# BUG-164: `git log` in a project root ran that repository's `gpg.program`

## Prevention
A git call into a directory the operator did not just choose (a project root taken from the index or a transcript) goes through `internal/trail.Command`, and nothing else. Only object- and file-reading commands run there: `log`, `ls-tree`, `ls-files`, `hash-object --no-filters`, `rev-parse`, `check-ignore`, `config --get` (BUG-165 added the search and memory ones). A new git command there gets a marker test against a repository whose config or attributes would run a program. Not covered: config keys that make other git commands run programs (`diff.external`, textconv, `core.pager` on a tty, hooks). Today the harness runs none of those commands in a project root.

title: `sh-agent search` runs an unhardened `git status` in the checkout it indexes
body:
# BUG-165: `sh-agent search` runs an unhardened `git status` in the checkout it indexes

## Prevention
As BUG-164: every git call into a project repository goes through `internal/trail.Command` and only reads objects and files (never `status`). A new git command there gets a marker test against a repository whose config or attributes would start a program. `internal/harness` is the exception: it runs git only in the harness's own checkout.

**Partial clones (security review finding 3, closed 2026-10-09):** search refuses a partial clone only when this machine's git is older than 2.44 (`trail.LazyFetchSafe`); a newer git honours `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH` and searches it. Pinned by `TestGitViewPartialCloneNeedsNewGit` (red before the fix) and `TestVersionAtLeast`.

title: `sh-agent dream` cannot log in to Antigravity on macOS
body:
# BUG-166: `sh-agent dream` cannot log in to Antigravity on macOS

## Prevention
How agy finds its login differs per OS: a file on Linux, the Keychain through `$HOME/Library/Keychains` on macOS. Any change to `agyHome` or to the private HOME owes one real `sh-agent dream --all` on a macOS place before the release (`testing/guide.md` § 3e). A fake CLI cannot show where the real one looks.

title: the delivery claim's one home named v2.4.1 and no `metrics` at v2.6.2
body:
# BUG-167: the delivery claim's one home named v2.4.1 and no `metrics` at v2.6.2

## Prevention
A doc that restates a fact the tree holds elsewhere (a version, a verb list, a count) is pinned to that fact by a test that reads both, or carries no number. The release commit updates `delivery.md` § Where things stand together with the release entry; `TestDeliverySpecCurrent` in the release procedure refuses the tag otherwise.

title: six usage errors exited 1 on stderr while the docs promised exit 2
body:
# BUG-168: six usage errors exited 1 on stderr while the docs promised exit 2

## Prevention
A convention that spans verbs is pinned by one table test over every site, and a new usage refusal adds its row there. In `cmd/sh-agent`, a usage refusal is `fmt.Fprintln(c.out, ...)` then `return exitCode(2)`; an `errors.New` for a usage message is the review's finding.

title: a grandchild of the dream CLI could hold the run, and the lock, past the deadline
body:
# BUG-169: a grandchild of the dream CLI could hold the run, and the lock, past the deadline

## Prevention
Every `exec` with a deadline whose output goes through pipes sets `WaitDelay`, and one that may start helpers kills its process group; its test runs a fake command that backgrounds a pipe holder and asserts the call returns. The dream call is the only deadline-bounded exec in the tree today (`grep -rn CommandContext cmd internal`).

title: an ignored hangup or interrupt killed the dream CLI's group and left sh-agent running
body:
# BUG-170: an ignored hangup or interrupt killed the dream CLI's group and left sh-agent running

## Prevention
A process that relays a signal checks `signal.Ignored` first: `signal.Notify` overrides an ignore the parent set on purpose (nohup, a background job), and `signal.Reset` brings the ignore back, so a re-raise after Reset cannot kill the process. A test for a signal path starts the child with the signal ignored (`trap '' SIG; exec`) as well as with it at default.

title: `update --vendor bogus` pulled the checkout before refusing, and other verbs exited 1 or 0
body:
# BUG-171: `update --vendor bogus` pulled the checkout before refusing, and other verbs exited 1 or 0

## Prevention
A flag registered on every verb is validated once, before the verb dispatch, not where each verb first reads it. A usage check that sits after a side effect (a fetch, a pull, a write) is a bug even when its exit code is right, and the read-only mode of a verb resolves the same check (review-standards § 8).

title: Claude Code 2.1.309 replaces the sandbox's credential symlink with a file, so a token refresh in a sandbox run would not reach the real login
body:
# BUG-172: Claude Code 2.1.309 replaces the sandbox's credential symlink with a file, so a token refresh in a sandbox run would not reach the real login

## Prevention
A kit's guarantee about a vendor's file handling is re-checked when the vendor's version changes: the kit asserts the link survived (it does) and the log records the WARNING count per run as a row, never as noise. A WARNING a kit prints on every run is a finding, not a warning.

title: the committed Antigravity kit passes `--vendor agy`, which Phase 2 made a usage error, so every row dies at its install
body:
# BUG-173: the committed Antigravity kit passes `--vendor agy`, which Phase 2 made a usage error, so every row dies at its install

## Prevention
A flag or verb removed from the binary is grepped for in every committed script (`git grep -n -- '--<flag>' -- '*.sh'`), not only in Go and the docs, and the removing phase runs one row of each committed kit that calls the binary before its checkpoint.

title: on agy 1.4.6 the main agent chains the context's post-dispatch check into one command, the grant store denies it, and the run fails or idles to its print timeout
body:
# BUG-174: on agy 1.4.6 the main agent chains the context's post-dispatch check into one command, the grant store denies it, and the run fails or idles to its print timeout

## Prevention
An instruction that names several shell commands says that each is its own call, because the grant store allows simple commands only. A kit's auto-deny count is read per attempt and diagnosed from the conversation database before any grant is widened (BUG-141).

title: on agy 1.4.7 the model saves a memory through a `$(date +%F)` substitution, the grant store refuses it, and nothing is saved
body:
# BUG-175: on agy 1.4.7 the model saves a memory through a `$(date +%F)` substitution, the grant store refuses it, and nothing is saved

A skill that tells the agent to compute a value says to run that command as its own call and write the value in by hand; a command a skill names is run once under the kit's real grants before it ships.

title: `skills/bug/SKILL.md:55` kept "a tool-call budget below the agent's `maxTurns`" past Phase 3b
body:
