A sweep that removes a concept greps for the concept's own name (the key, the flag, the verb) across the living tree, not for one phrasing of the sentence that used it; the sweep's verification line is that grep, empty.

title: the Phase 4a rename commit was first written with a `Claude-Session:` trailer
body:
# BUG-177: the Phase 4a rename commit was first written with a `Claude-Session:` trailer

## Prevention
Before every push, `git log --format=%B --branches --not --remotes` is read for `Claude-Session:` and `Co-Authored-By:` lines, and a hit is amended before the push. A commit message is written from the context's § Git, never from a CLI's reminder.

Graduated 2026-10-25 (plan `plans/2026-10-25-harness-audit-fix.md` D4, D13): the read is the script `skills/handoff/scripts/check-trailers.sh`, which `handoff` Step 6 and `preflight` Step 6.4 run before the push. It exits non-zero on a `Claude-Session:` or `Co-Authored-By:` line in `git log @{u}..HEAD --format=%B`, and a Go test runs it against a fixture that must fail and one that must pass. It is a script a skill runs, not a git hook (R3).

Graduated to: `skills/handoff/scripts/check-trailers.sh`, run before the push by `handoff` Step 6 and `preflight` Step 6.4 (exits non-zero on a `Claude-Session:` or `Co-Authored-By:` line in `git log @{u}..HEAD --format=%B`), and the Go test that runs it on a must-fail and a must-pass fixture (plan audit-fix D4, D13)

title: the kit move shipped in an unrelated commit with the preamble's checkout guard pointing at the repo's parent
body:
# the kit move shipped in an unrelated commit with the preamble's checkout guard pointing at the repo's parent

## Symptom
`git mv` staged the move of `.agents/docs/testing/{kit-preamble.sh,agy-rel/run.sh}` to `.agents/kit/` (brain plan D17). The next commit, `f28e8bc` (the Phase 1 review round-2 fixes), staged three other paths by name and carried the two renames with them, pushed. In that commit the preamble still located the harness checkout as `$(dirname BASH_SOURCE)/../../..`, right from `.agents/docs/testing/` but the checkout's PARENT from `.agents/kit/`; `run.sh` likewise (`$KIT/../../../..`), and the tests still sourced the old path. A local run of the kit tests on the edited tree then accepted `KIT_HOME=<the harness checkout>`: the stub `bin/fyr` was written into the repository, and the preamble's exit trap sent SIGTERM to every process under that "kit root" — the test run itself (exit 143). Fixed in `726138d` before any kit run with credentials.

## Root cause
Two things. The commit's `git diff --cached --stat` listed the two renames and was read, but not against the list of paths meant for that commit. And a script that finds its checkout by relative depth was moved without grepping it for `BASH_SOURCE`/`..`.

## Fix
`726138d`: `../..` in the preamble (both places) and `../../..` in `run.sh`, the test paths updated, the stray `bin/fyr` removed by name. Mutation: with `../../..` restored, `TestKitPreambleKillsLeftoverProcesses` (case "KIT_HOME is the harness checkout") does not pass — the run is killed.

## Recurrence
`921fcfc` (the Phase 2 checkpoint, the same session): the init-project templates' `git mv` and `git rm`, staged during Phase 3, rode along in a commit that named only `.agents/trail.jsonl`; the `git diff --cached --stat` that listed them was chained into the commit's call, against the context's § Git (read it, then commit in a separate call). `2a158b3` restored the skill. Since then the staged set is checked against the staged list in its own call: `diff <(git diff --cached --name-only | sort) <(sort <list>)`, empty or no commit.

## Prevention
Read `git diff --cached --stat` against the path list you staged by name: a path you did not name in that `git add` (a rename `git mv` staged earlier included) is a stop sign. Moving a script that locates its checkout by a relative path is not done until the tests that source it ran at the new place.

title: a dispatched verifier ran fyr without --home and moved the real ~/.config/sh-agent to ~/.config/fyr
body:
# a dispatched verifier ran fyr without --home and moved the real ~/.config/sh-agent to ~/.config/fyr

## Symptom
The verifier dispatched on ddaa522 (brain Phase 1 checkpoint) ran one `fyr record` call in its clone without `--home` and printed `migrated ~/.config/sh-agent → ~/.config/fyr` (its log, step 4, "Side effect to report"). After it, the operator's real home has `~/.config/fyr` and no `~/.config/sh-agent`; at 14:18 the handoff recorded `~/.config/sh-agent` untouched, kept so until the operator's own crossing (fyr plan Phase 6). The operator's live tools on this box — the v2.7.0 `sh-agent` binary and both CLIs' deployed context (`~/.config/sh-agent/feedback.jsonl`, `proposals/`, `search.db`, `metrics.db`) — still read the old path, so the next `sh-agent` write starts an empty `~/.config/sh-agent` beside the moved one.

## Repro
A clone of 6000815 or later, `go run ./cmd/fyr record list` (any writing verb) with `HOME` the real home and no `--home`: `MigrateStateDir` renames the old directory on a box that has not crossed.

## Root cause
The dispatch told the verifier to use a scratch `--home` for the install and the brain verbs, but not that EVERY `fyr` call must carry it; a help-shaped call without it is a writing verb's path through `MigrateStateDir`. The 14:18 handoff's rule ("audit agents were told not to run `fyr`, so the real ~/.config/sh-agent would not migrate") lived only in a handoff, not in the dispatch.

## Fix
Not fixed in the repository: the real home is outside this session's approval. The operator restores it with `test -e ~/.config/sh-agent || mv ~/.config/fyr ~/.config/sh-agent` (contents intact: feedback.jsonl, retros.jsonl, proposals/, metrics.db, search.db, state.json, reports/).

## Resolution
Obsolete 2026-10-26 23:37, by the crossing, not by a code change. Every place has crossed to fyr (TEST-2026-10-26-2233, CHANGE-2026-10-26-2308), and on this box `~/.config/sh-agent` is absent and `~/.config/fyr` present (checked 23:37). The harm needs a box that has not crossed: on a crossed box, where both directories exist (for example after a Claude Code session's v2.7.0 `feedback-log` recreated `~/.config/sh-agent`, D32), `MigrateStateDir` moves nothing and prints the both-directories notice (`internal/harness/migrate.go:48`). The prevention rule stays a dispatch rule: a sandbox `--home` on every `fyr` call keeps a dispatched agent out of the operator's real state.

## Prevention
Until this box has crossed to fyr, every dispatch that may run `fyr` says: "every `fyr` call carries `--home <scratch home>`; a `fyr` call without it moves the operator's real state directory". The same sentence goes into the verifier and security dispatches of this plan's remaining checkpoints.

title: the import's removal list told the caller to run git rm --literal-pathspecs, which git refuses
body:
# the import's removal list told the caller to run `git rm --literal-pathspecs --`, which git refuses

## Symptom
`fyr record import` (since 76327b8) printed "remove with git rm --literal-pathspecs -- and these paths"; run as printed, `git rm` exits with `error: unknown option 'literal-pathspecs'` and removes nothing. Found on the first real use, this repository's migration (brain plan Phase 2).

## Root cause
`--literal-pathspecs` is a global git option (`git --literal-pathspecs rm …`), not one of `git rm`'s. The round-2 security fix (literal pathspecs) was written from memory and its test asserted the printed text, not that the printed command runs.

## Fix
The heading and `SPEC-fyr-record` say `git --literal-pathspecs rm --`; `TestRecordImport` asserts that text. This repository's removal ran as `git --literal-pathspecs rm -q --pathspec-from-file=<list>`.

## Prevention
A command a tool prints for its caller to run is run once, as printed, in a fixture before the change is called done; a test that pins the printed text pins the command that works.

title: an Antigravity conversation whose summary time is the zero time is stored with ended_at -62135596800000
body:
# an Antigravity conversation whose summary time is the zero time is stored with ended_at -62135596800000

owner: main

## Symptom
A copy of this box's `~/.config/fyr/metrics.db` (`.agents/scratch/m2/metrics.db`, 2026-10-25) holds one Antigravity session, `5ee7d42d-7e39-45ea-b352-93e592efbfad`, with 0 steps, `started_at` NULL and `ended_at` -62135596800000 (Go's zero time, 0001-01-01, in unix milliseconds). The store's invariant is a real time or NULL (`SPEC-fyr-metrics` § Data); a reader that takes `ended_at` without `started_at` (wall time, window filters) sees a time 2,000 years in the past.

## Repro
Read-only on this box: `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversation_summaries.db` row `5ee7d42d…` has `last_modified_time` = the text `0001-01-01 00:00:00+00:00`; `fyr metrics ingest` (any home holding that file) stores the session as above.

## Root cause
`internal/metrics/agy.go:112-113` takes `search.AgyTime(modified)` as valid whenever it parses, and the zero time parses; the session insert (`agy.go:187-196`) guards the value with `NULLIF(?, 0)`, which catches 0 but not the zero time's negative milliseconds. The same value is written to `ingest_state.mtime` (`agy.go:244`). The conversation has no steps, so no step time ever replaces it.

## Fix
Fixed 2026-10-26 under the `bug` skill. The class is the parser, not the one insert: `agyTime` (`internal/search/dream.go:154`) now returns no time for anything before 1970, so both of its callers are covered: the metrics ingest (`internal/metrics/agy.go:114`, whose `NULLIF(?, 0)` now sees 0) and the dream job's conversation list (`internal/search/dream.go:133`). Migration 3 (`internal/metrics/store.go`) sets a negative `started_at` or `ended_at` to NULL and a negative `ingest_state.mtime` to 0, so the stored row is repaired forward (R4: no rebuild) and the conversation is not re-read into a zero end time. Tests: `TestAgyTime` (zero time, its text form, 1969), `TestAgyZeroTimeIsNoTime`, `TestMigrationRepairsZeroTimes`; each failed before the fix. The repro on a copy of the 2026-10-25 store: session `5ee7d42d…` went from `ended_at` -62135596800000 to NULL, schema 2 to 3.

## Prevention
A time read from another program's store is checked for the zero value before it is stored (`t.IsZero()`, never only `!= 0` on its milliseconds); every guard on a time column fed from another program's store has a test with Go's zero time as input.

title: the session ran fyr record get without --home, copied from the Kickoff, and wrote the real ~/.config/fyr/brain.db
body:
# the session ran fyr record get without --home, copied from the Kickoff, and wrote the real ~/.config/fyr/brain.db

## Symptom
At the start of the fyr check Phase 1 session (2026-10-25), the main agent ran `go run ./cmd/fyr record get <id>` twice with no `--home`, as the Kickoff of `HANDOFF-2026-10-25-2037-handoff-2026-10-25-roadmap-item-3-fyr-check-plann` wrote those lines. The real `~/.config/fyr/brain.db` was opened and refreshed from this project's trail (mtime 2026-10-25 20:54). Nothing migrated, because `~/.config/sh-agent` was already gone, and no content was lost; the store took this project's own records.

## Repro
In this checkout, `go run ./cmd/fyr record get <any id>` with `HOME` the real home and no `--home`: the brain verbs open `~/.config/fyr/brain.db` and import `.agents/trail.jsonl` into it.

## Root cause
BUG-179's prevention sentence lives in dispatches only ("every dispatch that may run `fyr` says…"). A Kickoff is the next session's first instruction, and it named `fyr record get` without `--home`, so the session copied the command as written. Nothing checks a Kickoff, and the main thread had no rule of its own beyond AGENTS.md's installer sentence.

## Fix
None needed in the repository. The real home is not restored: `brain.db` holds the same records it would after the operator's own next `fyr record` call. Every later call in that session carried `--home .agents/scratch/home-trail`, and `HANDOFF-2026-10-25-2113` writes `--home` on each `fyr` line of its Kickoff.

## Prevention
Every `fyr` command a Kickoff, a handoff, a plan box or a dispatch names, in this repository, is written with `--home .agents/scratch/<name>`, and the main agent adds it when a copied command lacks it. A third recurrence graduates the rule into AGENTS.md § Rules for working here (a sentence beside the installer's) or a test over handoff records.

Graduated to: AGENTS.md § Rules for working here, the state-writing `--home` rule (2026-10-27 audit, TR16; commit e0915fa).

title: a GUIDE-eval edit was committed without go test, and TestSuiteHarness's pinned row count failed
body:
owner: main

## Symptom
`go test ./internal/eval` fails at f12f499 on `main` (committed, not pushed): `TestSuiteHarness`: `suite_test.go:169: 59 rows, want 56` (60 with the `rule-code-modularity` row of the followups branch). Found by the bare `go test -race ./...` of the followups branch, 2026-10-26.

## Repro
At f12f499: `go test -count=1 -run TestSuiteHarness ./internal/eval`.

## Root cause
The session added three rows to `GUIDE-eval` (a record, not code), validated each row's check against reference builds, and committed with no `go test`: a record edit felt like data. `TestSuiteHarness` pins every row of the suite by id, agent and grant, so a new row is a test change too.

## Fix
`internal/eval/suite_test.go`: the `want` map holds `build-cli`, `build-api`, `build-fullstack` and `rule-code-modularity` (wide, no agent); `TestSuiteHarness` passes. Landed on the followups branch before f12f499 was pushed.

## Prevention
A `GUIDE-eval` row is added together with its `want` entry in `TestSuiteHarness`, and the commit that adds it runs `go test ./internal/eval` first: an edit to `.agents/trail.jsonl` is a change under test like any other (the setup commands of AGENTS.md run before every commit, not only before one that touches Go).

## Graduated
2026-10-28, ledger Phase 6 (item 20, D5): `AGENTS.md` § Testing now says a `GUIDE-eval` edit is a test change: `TestSuiteHarness` (`internal/eval/suite_test.go`) pins every row by id, agent and grant, so a row added or changed changes its `want` entry in the same commit, and `go test ./internal/eval` runs before that commit. `TestSuiteHarness` is the mechanism; the AGENTS.md line makes running it the rule a session reads before editing the suite.

title: agy 1.4.7's read_file, write_file and edit_file are stored as agy: names, and no path key but AbsolutePath is read, so skill loads and trail kinds go missing
body:
owner: main

## Symptom
In the eval metrics store (`~/sandbox/fyr-eval/home/.config/fyr/metrics.db`, a copy read 2026-10-27), agy 1.4.7's file tools are stored as unmapped names: `agy:read_file` 589 steps in 77 sessions, `agy:write_file` 118, `agy:edit_file` 30. A SKILL.md read through `read_file` records no skill: `build-fullstack` (TEST-2026-10-26-2357) followed the frontend skill and its session shows no `frontend` read. Raised as an unverified agent note in HANDOFF-2026-10-27-0044.

## Repro
Copy `conversation_summaries.db` and `conversations/` of `~/sandbox/fyr-eval/home/.config/fyr/eval/2026-10-26-232943/build-fullstack/home/.gemini/antigravity-cli` into a scratch source, then `fyr metrics ingest --home <scratch> --source <copy> --label eval=repro`: before the fix, the Read steps carry no skill and the file tools are `agy:*`.

## Root cause
Two gaps in one place, the argument reader of `internal/metrics/agy.go`. The tool map knew only the names of the plan D35 spike (`view_file`, `write_to_file`, `replace_file_content`), and agy 1.4.7 also sends `read_file`, `write_file` and `edit_file`. And `agyArgs` read the path only under `AbsolutePath`, `view_file`'s key. The argument keys over all 340 conversation databases on this box (keys only, from copies) show `Path` for the three 1.4.7 tools and `TargetFile` for `write_to_file` and `replace_file_content`. So no Write or Edit step had ever stored a trail kind, even under the old names.

## Fix
`internal/metrics/agy_tools.go` (new: the vocabulary moved out of `agy.go`, which was past 400 lines) maps `read_file`→Read, `write_file`→Write and `edit_file`→Edit. `agyArgs.path()` reads `AbsolutePath`, `Path` or `TargetFile`, and `agy.go` `agyTool` uses it for both the skill and the trail kind. `manage_subagents` stays `agy:manage_subagents`, as `SPEC-fyr-metrics` § Shared tool vocabulary decides. The spec's table and its § Where the shape is read now name the new tools and the keys. Tests: `TestAgyToolVocabulary` (three new rows, plus `manage_subagents` pinned unmapped) and `TestAgyPathKeys` (each tool's key gives the skill and the trail kind); both failed before the fix. On the repro copy after the fix: 9 skills recorded (`frontend` among them), every Read and Write with a trail kind.

Not repaired: rows already stored stay `agy:read_file` etc. with no skill, since the arguments were never stored (R4: no rebuild). A conversation is re-read only when it changes. The operator decided against a renaming migration (2026-10-27, "Go all approved" on HANDOFF-2026-10-27-0646 Next Step 4).

## Prevention
When the Antigravity CLI's version changes, list the tool names and argument KEYS of a fresh conversation, from a copy, keys only, before trusting metrics built on them (`agy:` rows in `fyr metrics show` are the signal). Every name added to `agyTools` gets its path key in `TestAgyPathKeys`.

title: fyr eval's credential scan reads an installed node_modules, and prettier's AKIA-shaped literal FAILs build-fullstack
body:
owner: main

## Symptom
`fyr eval build-fullstack` (TEST-2026-10-26-2357) FAILed on check d, "a new credential", though the app passed its own check. The path was `web/node_modules/prettier/plugins/flow.js (aws-key)`, and `flow.mjs` too.

## Repro
Run `scanCreds` over `~/sandbox/fyr-eval/home/.config/fyr/eval/2026-10-26-232943/build-fullstack/app` against an empty baseline. Before the fix it reports the two prettier files; after it, nothing.

## Root cause
Check d reads every file in the sandbox for credential shapes, and an app build installs third-party packages (`npm install` into `web/node_modules`) whose code holds credential-shaped strings of its own. prettier's flow plugin holds an AKIA-shaped literal that is not AWS's published example key, the only one set aside. A new path with an `aws-key` count fails the row.

## Fix
`internal/eval/creds.go` `scanCreds` marks a `node_modules` directory as a locked install when a regular lockfile sits beside it (`lockedModules`: `package-lock.json`, `npm-shrinkwrap.json`, `yarn.lock`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `bun.lock`, `bun.lockb`). `scanEntry` then checks the files under it by name, path, link and readability (an `os.Open`), and never reads them. A link that resolves outside the scanned tree is read even there, and the scan root itself is never an install (both from REVIEW-2026-10-27-0635 and its security pass). A `node_modules` with no lockfile, the lockfile itself, and a plain file named `node_modules` are read as before. This is the operator's choice (HANDOFF-2026-10-27-0044 Next Step 3, approved 2026-10-27): skip the lockfile-backed install in the content scan, keep the name scan. It is generalised from `web/node_modules` to any directory with a lockfile beside it, so a `ui/` frontend gets the same treatment. `SPEC-fyr-eval` check d and § Known limits say so. Test: `TestCredsLockedModules`, which failed before the fix. Seven must-fail mutations each turn it red: the outside-link read, the readability check, the root exclusion, the trailing separator, `Lstat` of the lockfile, a dropped lockfile name, and the skip removed.

## Prevention
A content check that runs over a tree an agent may fill with third-party packages names those package trees and decides for them explicitly, by name or by a skip the spec states. It never answers a false positive by weakening the patterns themselves.

title: the session recommended removing the ~/.claude harness on dave against the project memory keep-claude-files-on-dave, which it had not read
body:
owner: main

## Symptom
The session's report recommended removing the sh-agent harness from `~/.claude` on dave twice: row 3 of the first report, then HANDOFF-2026-10-27-0646 and HANDOFF-2026-10-27-0722 Next Step 1. The operator corrected it (2026-10-27): "1 i Said should stay while we are using Claude."

## Repro
Resume from HANDOFF-2026-10-27-0044 without running `fyr memory show`. Its Next Step 1 recommends removal, and nothing in the handoff, the plan or ROADMAP contradicts it.

## Root cause
The project memory `keep-claude-files-on-dave` (operator, 2026-10-25) already decides this: the Claude Code skills and context on dave stay, and fyr never removes them. The session skipped the resume order's last step, `fyr memory show`. It read only AGENTS.md and the handoff, as the Kickoff named them. It then carried the earlier handoff's recommendation forward unchecked. HANDOFF-2026-10-27-0044 had written that Next Step against the same memory.

## Fix
The recommendation is struck: HANDOFF-2026-10-27-0722's Next Step 1 is superseded by the next handoff, which names this record. Nothing on the machine was changed, and `~/.claude` was never touched.

## Prevention
A Next Step that removes, rewrites or moves anything on a machine is checked against `fyr memory show` before it is recommended or carried forward. A Kickoff that names only AGENTS.md and the handoff still implies the full resume order, memory included.

title: two first opens of a new SQLite index or metrics store at once fail busy at once, past the 10 s busy timeout (TestConcurrentReconcile flake)
body:
owner: main

## Symptom
`TestConcurrentReconcile` (internal/search/open_test.go) failed intermittently: one of its two helper processes failed after 0.01 s with `search: index busy (another fyr is indexing); retry, or use grep`, well inside the 10 s busy timeout. Rates: about 1 in 9 serial runs of the package and 1 in 4 under parallel load (funclen Phase 4, 2026-10-27); 1 in 100 runs of the test alone under CPU load. Two real `fyr search` or `fyr index` runs started together on a checkout with no index yet would fail the same way.

## Repro
`go test -c ./internal/search/`, then run the binary with `-test.run '^TestConcurrentReconcile$' -test.count 100`, three copies at once beside twelve busy loops: 2 failures in 900 runs (`.agents/scratch/bug-busy/`). Deterministic: a connection holds `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` on a new file that is not yet in WAL mode, and `openStore` on that path fails within 0.3 ms. That is `TestFirstOpenWaitsForALock` in internal/search/open_test.go, and the same test in internal/metrics/store_test.go for `metrics.Open`.

## Root cause
The first open of a new database switches it to WAL (`_pragma=journal_mode(WAL)` in `search.DSN`). SQLite does that switch by opening a read transaction and upgrading it to a write. When another connection holds a lock at that moment, SQLite answers the upgrade `SQLITE_BUSY` at once and never calls the busy handler, because waiting while holding a read lock could deadlock. So `busy_timeout(10000)` does not apply. `openStore` (internal/search/store.go) mapped that error straight to `errBusy`. The metrics store's `Open` returned it as `database is locked`. Instrumented runs showed the extended code was plain 5 (SQLITE_BUSY, not 517 BUSY_SNAPSHOT), from the first statement on a fresh connection, inside `openStore`'s first `tryOpen`. The brain store had the same exposure and was written with a retry loop for it (internal/brain/store.go:85-101, plan brain Phase 1), but the loop and its reason were never carried to the two older stores.

## Fix
- `internal/search/store.go`: `tryOpenWaiting` retries `tryOpen` while it fails busy, for up to the busy timeout, every 50 ms. `openStore` uses it at both of its opens.
- `internal/search/store.go`: `IsBusy` exports `isBusy` for the metrics store.
- `internal/metrics/store.go`: `Open` retries a new `open` (one attempt) the same way, for `openWait` (10 s).

The two SQLite stores outside `internal/brain` are the whole class: `git grep journal_mode` names only `search.DSN`, and the three stores open through it.

## Prevention
A SQLite store that opens through `search.DSN` (WAL) retries its whole open while it fails busy, for as long as the busy timeout. `busy_timeout` does not cover the first open's switch to WAL. A new store copies that loop, as brain, search and metrics now do, and gets a test that holds a write lock on a fresh, non-WAL file across its open.

## Diagnosis
The goldfish explorer ranked "pragma order in the DSN" first, as did my own hypothesis. The driver's source falsified it: modernc.org/sqlite runs `busy_timeout` first whatever the order. Its second candidate, BUSY_SNAPSHOT in `ensureSchema`, was falsified by the extended code, 5. The cause found, the WAL switch's lock upgrade, was in neither list.
Diagnosis missed: the WAL switch's lock upgrade at connection setup. The brief's "Investigate the codebase" read only this module. A line asking to check how the driver and SQLite apply the busy timeout to the failing statement would have led there, as would "look for the same failure handled elsewhere in the repo" (internal/brain/store.go:85-101 names it).

title: trail.Dirty is fooled by a tracked name opening with a double quote: hash-object --stdin-paths unquotes it and hashes another path (false clean, a read outside the checkout)
body:
owner: main

## Symptom
`trail.Dirty` (internal/trail/dirty.go) answered "clean" for a tree where `git status --porcelain` shows ` M "\"x\""`: a committed file whose name opens with `"` had been modified. It could also hash a file beside the repository, outside the checkout that the code's comments say `os.Root` confines it to. Its two callers rely on the answer: `fyr record import` refuses a tree with uncommitted changes (internal/brain/import.go:126), and `fyr eval` labels its install source `(dirty)` (cmd/fyr/eval.go:293). The same `hashesDiffer` serves `trail.Dates` (internal/trail/trail.go:118), which dates a project's trail files for the dream: a quoted name under the docs root could keep a modified record on its commit date. Found by the v3.1.0 release gate's security review, part B (`REVIEW-2026-10-27-1556-security-review-v3-1-0-gate-part-b-metrics-redac`), medium, high confidence. `trail.Dirty` came in with the 2026-10-27 audit fix (SD38, ce4f977) and was never in a release.

## Repro
A repository with `a` and `"a"` committed, both holding the same bytes. Modify `"a"`. `Dirty(root)` returns `false, nil`. That is `TestDirtyCannotAnswerQuotedName` in internal/trail/dirty_test.go. The security agent's probes are under `.agents/scratch/sec-B-probe/` (`repo`: false clean; `repo2`: a tracked file named `"../outside.txt"`, which git unquotes to `../outside.txt` and reads outside the checkout).

## Root cause
`hashesDiffer` feeds tracked names, one per line, to `git hash-object --no-filters --stdin-paths`. git reads a stdin line that opens with `"` as a C-quoted string and unquotes it, so `"a"` is hashed as `a`, and a name `"../outside.txt"` as `../outside.txt`, outside the tree. The guard refused only `\n` and `\r`. The same class was found and closed in `internal/search` by an earlier security review: `git_view.go:193-196` hashes a file's own bytes and never calls `--stdin-paths`. The rule was not carried to `trail.Dirty` when it was written.

## Fix
`internal/trail/dirty.go`, `hashesDiffer`: a path that opens with `"` is refused with `errUnhashable`, as a newline or CR already was, so `Dirty` says it cannot answer instead of guessing. Every caller already handles the error safely: `record import` refuses with "checking for uncommitted changes: …", `eval` labels the source `(dirty: unknown, …)`, and `trail.Dates` treats every record as modified, keeping its mtime. `errUnhashable`'s text names the new case.

Class check: `git grep -e '--stdin' -e 'stdin-paths' -e 'cmd.Stdin = '` over the non-test Go code finds two other git calls fed on stdin. `internal/check/docs.go:262` runs `check-ignore -z --stdin`, NUL-separated, which does no unquoting. `internal/search/git_view.go` hashes in Go. `hashesDiffer`, shared by `trail.Dirty` and `trail.Dates`, was the only site.

## Prevention
Never pass a path to git on a line-oriented stdin (`--stdin-paths`, `--stdin` without `-z`): git C-unquotes a line that opens with `"` and strips a trailing CR, so the name git acts on can differ from the one meant. Use `-z` where the command has it; otherwise hash or read the file in Go through `os.Root` (as `internal/search/git_view.go` does), or refuse such a name and say the answer is unknown.

## Diagnosis
The location was given by the security agent's reproduced probe, so Step 2's explorer dispatch was skipped as mechanically obvious. My hypothesis matched the probe: `--stdin-paths` unquoting.

title: fyr install's directory-in-the-way refusal names no alternative, and the real run fails with a bare rename error
body:
owner: main

## Symptom
`fyr install --dry-run` into a home where a directory sits at a managed file's path refused with `writing …: a directory is in the way; the install cannot replace it`, naming the cause but no alternative. The real `fyr install` into the same home failed with a bare `writing …: rename …/.fyr-NNN …: file exists`. GUIDE-testing § 3c passes a refused cell only when its message names both the cause and the alternative. Found by the v3.1.0 gate's § 3c matrix run (`TEST-2026-10-27-1619-verification-v3-1-0-gate-3c-matrix-v3-0-0-31de61`), FAIL. The dry-run refusal came in with the 2026-10-27 audit fix (IN41, 5f2b941) and was never in a release. The real run's bare rename error is older: a v3.0.0 build gives the same.

## Repro
`mkdir -p <home>/.gemini/config/rules/AGENTS.md`, then `fyr install --dry-run --home <home>` and `fyr install --home <home>` (the matrix's cell). In a test: `TestDryRunRefusesADirectoryAtAFilePath` (internal/harness/dryrun_dir_test.go), which now also requires the cause, "move or remove it" and "fyr install" in both runs' errors.

## Root cause
`dirInTheWay` (internal/harness/apply_guard.go) was written as the dry run's copy of the real write's failure (IN41). Its message carried only the cause, and the real run never called it: it reached `WriteAtomic`, whose rename error names neither the cause in words nor a way out.

## Fix
- `internal/harness/apply_guard.go`: the message ends `: move or remove it, then run fyr install again`.
- `internal/harness/apply_steps.go`, `installRun.write`: both runs call `dirInTheWay` before writing. The real run returns through `saveOnError`, as a failed write already did, so the files written before it stay in the manifest.

## Prevention
A refusal names the cause and the alternative, and a dry run's guard is the real run's guard: one function that both runs call before acting, never a dry-run copy of an error the real run meets later (review-standards § 8). The matrix (GUIDE-testing § 3c) checks the message's two halves.

## Diagnosis
The location was named by the matrix cell and the guard's own comment, so Step 2's explorer dispatch was skipped. Not fixed here: the real install still writes the files before the one in the way (nine in the matrix's home) before it stops. `saveOnError` records them, so `status` and a later install see them, and the behaviour is unchanged since v3.0.0.

title: the release gate's verifier opened the operator's live Antigravity conversation_summaries.db instead of a copy (copies-only rule, GUIDE-testing § 3g)
body:
owner: main

## Symptom
During the `/preflight v3.1.0` gate, the first `verifier` run (`TEST-2026-10-27-1619-verification-v3-1-0-gate-v1-v3-0-0-31de61a-fail`, § 3g and the audit-fix E2E 2 setup) opened the operator's LIVE `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversation_summaries.db` with Python's `sqlite3`. Its log says: "(I also read the live conversation_summaries.db once with python sqlite3, read-only, before building the E2E fixture: a read of the real home, no write.)" GUIDE-testing § 3g allows real data from copies only, and the dispatch said so in capitals ("a real-data check from COPIES only"). `sqlite3.connect` opens read-write, so "read-only" is the agent's claim, not a mode it set. Found by the gate's security read of its own records (`REVIEW-2026-10-27-1809-security-review-v3-1-0-gate-trail-records-31de61`, low, medium confidence).

## What was checked afterwards
The database's mtime is still 2026-10-26 21:53:22, and there is no `-wal`, `-shm` or `-journal` beside it, so the file itself was not written. The directory `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli` has an mtime of 2026-10-27 16:11:35, within the verifier's run, so an entry was added, removed or renamed then. The cause is not determined: Antigravity rewriting its token by rename is one candidate. The token's own mtime is 17:21, from the eval run's refresh through its link.

## Root cause
The verifier's definition (agents/verifier/agent.md) has no rule against opening the operator's real Antigravity or fyr data. The copies-only rule lives in GUIDE-testing § 3g and the dispatch, and the agent read the live file to learn the table's schema before it built a fixture.

## Fix
None in this change. The record is written so the rule is known. The graduation below changes an agent definition, which owes `GUIDE-eval` rows and a review, so it is left to `PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-cleanup`.

## Prevention
An agent never opens a file under the operator's real `~/.gemini/` or `~/.config/fyr/` in place, read-only or not. It copies the file into `.agents/scratch/` first (`cp -p`), reads the copy, and deletes the copy by name. A schema is learned from a copy, or from the code that reads it. Graduation target: a sentence in `agents/verifier/agent.md` (and `security`, which also probes), with an `inject`/`lane` row in `GUIDE-eval`.

## Graduated
2026-10-28, ledger Phase 6 (item 17): the prevention rule is the "Copies only (BUG-190)" bullet under § Records in `agents/verifier/agent.md` and `agents/security/agent.md`, with two carve-outs the rule above did not state: the installed harness text under `~/.gemini/config/` (both agents read `init-project/references/trail.md` there) and the `fyr` verbs each definition names (which open `~/.config/fyr/brain.db` as its own reader). Behavioural runs on that text: `TEST-2026-10-28-1127-eval-2-of-2-pass-at-bfb4329` (`agent-verifier`, `agents-security`). The proving `GUIDE-eval` row stays deferred (ledger item 18).

title: the v3.1.0 gate added GUIDE-eval's smoke row without TestSuiteHarness's want entry and committed it without go test (BUG-183 again)
body:
owner: main

## Symptom
At 8bfd2bc on `main` (committed, not pushed), `go test ./internal/eval` fails: `TestSuiteHarness`: `suite_test.go:171: 61 rows, want 60`. The v3.1.0 gate added the `smoke` row to `GUIDE-eval` and committed it without running `go test`. The main agent caught it before the verifier's test step reached the package: the verifier was stopped, and its partial run is in `.agents/scratch/v310-v1c/`.

## Repro
At 8bfd2bc: `go test -count=1 -run TestSuiteHarness ./internal/eval`.

## Root cause
The same as BUG-183. The row's check was validated by hand, in must-pass and must-fail states, against a kept eval sandbox and a fake store. A record edit felt like data, so `go test` did not run before the commit. `TestSuiteHarness` pins every row by id, agent and grant. BUG-183's prevention rule is a sentence in that bug record and nowhere a session reads before editing `GUIDE-eval`, so it did not fire.

## Fix
`internal/eval/suite_test.go`: `want` holds `"smoke": {"", false}`, and `TestSuiteHarness` passes. Without the entry it fails with "61 rows, want 60" (checked with `git stash`). Landed before 8bfd2bc was pushed.

## Prevention
The rule is BUG-183's: a `GUIDE-eval` row is added together with its `want` entry, and the commit runs `go test ./internal/eval` first. It has now recurred, so it graduates into a mechanism, filed as a PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-cleanup Follow-up. Candidates: `fyr record edit GUIDE-eval` (or any edit of a record a Go test reads) prints the test to run, or the note in GUIDE-eval § Columns names `TestSuiteHarness`. This record's status becomes `graduated` when one lands.

## Graduated
2026-10-28, ledger Phase 6 (item 20, D5): `AGENTS.md` § Testing now says a `GUIDE-eval` edit is a test change: `TestSuiteHarness` (`internal/eval/suite_test.go`) pins every row by id, agent and grant, so a row added or changed changes its `want` entry in the same commit, and `go test ./internal/eval` runs before that commit. `TestSuiteHarness` is the mechanism; the AGENTS.md line makes running it the rule a session reads before editing the suite.

title: the ledger Phase 7a checkpoint commit was pushed with a Claude-Session trailer (BUG-177 again, on a checkpoint push)
body:
# BUG-192: the ledger Phase 7a checkpoint commit was pushed with a `Claude-Session:` trailer (BUG-177 again, on a checkpoint push)

## Symptom
97cf077 ("Ledger Phase 7a: Slack handling removed from the redactor (D32 1)") is on `origin/main` with a `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_…` line. The context's § Git forbids it: "no session links … and not the trailer a CLI's own reminder asks for". The commit before it, 296cc0d, carries none. Published history is never rewritten, so the trailer stays.

## Repro
`git log -1 --format=%B 97cf077`.

## Root cause
The main agent wrote the message from the CLI's attribution reminder instead of from § Git, as BUG-177 did. BUG-177's mechanism, `skills/handoff/scripts/check-trailers.sh`, runs only before the handoff skill's push (Step 6) and preflight's (Step 6.4). A plan phase's checkpoint commits and pushes at step 10 before the handoff is written, and that push runs no check. The script reads `@{u}..HEAD`, so once the handoff runs, an already-pushed commit is never seen.

## Fix
None possible for 97cf077 without a force-push, which the context forbids. The handoff commit of this session was checked with `check-trailers.sh` before its push.

## Prevention
Every push runs `check-trailers.sh` first, not only the handoff and preflight pushes. Two candidates: § Git in `context/AGENTS.md` names the script ("before any push, run the handoff skill's `check-trailers.sh`"), or the checkpoint step of the feature skill and the plan template names it before its push. Either one is a harness change for the operator to approve. The first landed in ledger Phase 9 (§ Graduated).

## Graduated
2026-10-28, ledger Phase 9 (D33 2): `context/AGENTS.md` § Git now says "Before any push, run the handoff skill's `check-trailers.sh`.", after the trailer rule, so every push a session makes, a plan phase's checkpoint push included, runs the script first, not only the handoff's and preflight's. `skills/handoff/scripts/check-trailers.sh` is the mechanism; the context line makes running it the rule every session reads. Inside both size pins (`TestRenderedContextUnderTarget`: 14,876 of 15,000 bytes).

# Rebuild: single-source harness with the `styrman` installer     (date: 2026-09-03)

## Summary

Rebuilt the harness after the hook-driven design was reverted (09fc5cc, 20a5abd). The harness is now context + skills + subagents only, installed by a small Go binary. Twelve design questions were put to the operator first; the answers are recorded in `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-03-rebuild.md`.

- **Layout:** `shared/`, `claude/`, `antigravity/` collapsed into `context/`, `agents/`, `skills/`. No generated copies committed. `.agents/skills -> ../skills` so `npx skills add` from the repo root lands in `skills/`.
- **Context:** `context/AGENTS.md` rewritten without the binary, dispatch rows, scope digests, or hooks. Definition of Done is prose: tests, changelog, reviewer on 50+ lines / 5+ files, security on sensitive paths, docs on behavior change, commit and push. `context/dev-setup.md` holds the environment, stack, and GCP defaults (two placeholders to confirm).
- **Agents:** all six rewritten. `verifier` now runs the project's tests itself. Frontmatter is `owner:` + `date:`; descriptions are single-line and quoted.
- **Skills:** `audit`, `preflight`, `init-project`, `retro` rewritten; `handoff`, `distill`, `feedback`, `find-skills`, `VENDORED.md` edited to drop the binary. `init-project` now ships its templates in `assets/` and creates the `.claude/` symlinks and `CLAUDE.md` import. The other 19 skills are unchanged.
- **Binary:** `cmd/styrman` + `internal/harness` (stdlib only): install/sync, status, diff, update (`git fetch`, `pull --ff-only`, rebuild, reinstall), uninstall (manifest-only), list, render, adopt. Self-installs to `~/.local/bin/styrman`. Foreign `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` is never overwritten.
- **Repo docs:** README, AGENTS.md, REQUIREMENTS.md (R1–R6), TODO, ROADMAP, ADR-001..005, this entry, and the rebuild checklist.

task

## Files changed

- `context/AGENTS.md`, `context/dev-setup.md` — the global context, agents.md standard
- `agents/*.md` — six subagents
- `skills/{audit,preflight,init-project,retro,handoff,distill,feedback,find-skills}/SKILL.md`, `skills/VENDORED.md`, `skills/init-project/assets/**` — skills without binary references; templates moved in
- `cmd/styrman/main.go`, `internal/harness/*.go`, `internal/harness/harness_test.go`, `go.mod` — the installer
- `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `TODO.md`, `.gitignore`, `.agents/**` — repo docs and trail
- removed: `claude/`, `antigravity/`, `shared/`, all `.DS_Store`

## Verification

`gofmt -l .` empty, `go vet ./...` clean, `go test -race ./...` passes (frontmatter, derive, inventory, install/status/resync/uninstall, adopt, find-repo, git behind/pull). # Harness practices Phase 4: agents and records (G07, G16 verifier half, G17, G18, G23, G24)     (2026-09-15)

## Summary

The verifier runs every command on its own, records test counts against the previous log, marks inherited failures and lists added suppressions. The agents that can be cut off count a cut tool result as not reached, and the reviewer, security and verifier templates carry a Not examined section. A bug record can carry a `Diagnosis missed:` line that the retro reads. A bug's index row moves to a Graduated table when its prevention rule graduates.

## Type

task

## Files changed

- `agents/verifier.md` — I-16a–d and I-17b. What to run gains four rules. Every command on its own: a chain is split into its commands, each run in the directory the chain would run it in, and `gofmt -l` fails by printing. Test counts: each Go test command runs once with `-v`, its output saved under `.agents/scratch/verify-<slug>/`, and the log writes a `counts:` line and a `vs previous:` line against the newest earlier log with counts; a fall in pass or a rise in skip is a FAIL unless the diff or the environment explains it. Inherited failures: a failing test the change set did not touch is marked `pre-existing?` and Status stays FAIL. Suppressions added: every added suppression, skip or `.only` is listed as file:line, and an added `.only(` or a suppression with no reason is a FAIL. The log template's Go line records exit status, counts and vs previous, and the template gains `## Not examined`. A cut tool result counts as not reached.
- `agents/reviewer.md` — I-17a and I-17e: a cut tool result (a preview, a saved-output path, a line limit) counts as not reached until the rest is read; the report template gains `## Not examined` for files, criteria and commits, or `nothing`.
- `agents/security.md` — I-17c and I-17f: the same sentence; the findings template gains `## Not examined` for paths, surfaces and tools, or `nothing`.
- `agents/explorer.md` — I-17d: the same sentence.
- `agents/bugs.md` — I-18a–g: it keeps both tables of `INDEX.md`, and a new id is the highest in either table plus one; a record carries a `Diagnosis missed:` line when the dispatch names one; when a dispatch says a prevention rule graduated in this repository, the bug's row moves to a `## Graduated` table (`| ID | Area | Graduated to |`) and the record file stays untouched, while a rule promoted from a project to the harness leaves the project's row in place; the prevention recommendation says whether the rule is actionable and generalizable, as information and never a filter; moving a row edits the index, not a record.
- `skills/bug/SKILL.md` — I-18h: when Step 2 ran and the reviewer, the verifier or the fix surfaced a cause the diagnosis did not rank, the `bugs` dispatch carries a `Diagnosis missed:` line naming the line of the Step 2 brief that would have found it.
- `skills/retro/SKILL.md` — I-18i–k: the retro reads `Diagnosis missed:` lines in bug records dated on or after the newest retro record; a bug-derived proposal that targets an `AGENTS.md` says whether its rule is actionable and generalizable; when an applied rule is a bug's prevention rule, `bugs` moves that bug's row to the Graduated table in the same task.
- `context/AGENTS.md` — I-18l: a recurring rule can also graduate into a skill or an agent definition, and the commit that writes it has `bugs` move the matching index rows to the Graduated table. The rendered context stays at 93 lines.
- `.agents/docs/bugs/INDEX.md` and `skills/init-project/assets/agents-tree/docs/bugs/INDEX.md` — I-18m and I-18n: the header says a row lives in the main table, or in the Graduated table once its prevention rule lives in an `AGENTS.md`, a rule, a skill, an agent definition or a test.
- `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` — ADR-021, "Bug index rows move to a Graduated table when their rule graduates" (task 4.4).
- `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-15-harness-practices-g01-g26.md` — boxes 4.1–4.5 and the Phase 4 checkpoint ticked with evidence; task 4.3's label corrected from I-18a–l to I-18a–n, since I-18m and I-18n are the index edits its check already covered.

# `sh-agent install` writes Claude Code's attribution setting when absent     (date: 2026-09-16)

## Summary
Implements ADR-025 to resolve BUG-039: `sh-agent install` (and its alias `sync`, for vendor `all` or `claude` only) now writes `"attribution": {"commit": "", "pr": ""}` to `~/.claude/settings.json` when the `attribution` key is absent, creating the file if missing. A present key of any value is left alone and the advisory note stays. File edits use textual insertion re-parsed before writing so the operator's other keys and formatting remain byte-identical. `--dry-run` reports and writes nothing. No state of the file fails install; the setting is advisory (R4). `uninstall` leaves the key (the trailer must stay off with or without the harness). Supersedes ADR-010's "never touch vendor settings" clause on this one point only; the permission-write refusal it stated still stands.

## Type
feature

## Files changed
- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` — `attributionSet` (file creation, textual insertion, Lstat guard, size/format checks, Sync before rename), `readSettings` (shared helper for `attributionSet` and `attributionOff`), `abandonTemp` (temp-file cleanup with error reporting), `attributionOff` refactored to use `readSettings`, install/sync case wired to call `attributionSet` before `attributionHint`
- `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` — `TestAttributionSet` (14 subtests: missing file, other keys with formatting/mode preservation, CRLF, empty object, off/custom value, malformed, non-object JSON, null, >1 MiB bound, symlink guard, dry-run, vendor-agy no-op), `TestAttributionNote` cases `no settings file` and `other settings only` updated for new order (install leg expects `settings:` line and no note; status leg has no note because key now present); new case `status alone on a home without the key` keeps the note
- `REQUIREMENTS.md` — R4 sentence approved 2026-09-16: "`install` also sets one key in the operator's `~/.claude/settings.json`, `attribution` (commit and PR trailers off), only when the key is absent; it never changes or removes another key, and `uninstall` leaves it."; § Non-goals exception approved 2026-09-16: narrowed "Editing `settings.json` or any vendor setting" to name the exception and ADR-025
- `context/AGENTS.md` § Git — "`sh-agent install` sets it when absent; `status` says when a different value is set"
- `README.md` — § Install: attribution sentence and line reworded to "the installer touches no vendor setting except the attribution key (ADR-025)"; `status` row updated for the absent-file note-firing condition

# Release binary — Phase 2 of the release-binary plan: the embedded source     (2026-09-17)

## Summary

The harness's own files now live inside the binary, and every reader reaches them through one abstraction. `embed.go` (package `styrman`, module root) embeds `context/`, `skills/`, `agents/`, `commands/` and `rules/` with `//go:embed all:…`, so the 15 `.gitkeep` files come along. `Source{FS, Dir, Version}` replaces the `repo string` every reader took: `Dir` is a checkout or plain copy (`FS` is `os.DirFS(Dir)`), and an empty `Dir` with a `Version` is the files built into a release binary. The symlink refusals of BUG-036 run when `Dir` is set — `embed` cannot hold a link — and are unchanged in meaning for a tree on disk. `ResolveSource` replaces `FindRepo` and adds one last candidate after today's four: the embedded files, but only when the running binary's version is a `vX.Y.Z` tag (D14), so a development build outside a tree keeps today's error instead of installing a stale copy. An explicit `--repo` or `$SH_AGENT_REPO` naming something that is not a harness tree is still refused, never replaced by the embedded files (D15). With an embedded source, install copies the running binary and never builds (D13), `state.json` records `"repo": "embedded:vX.Y.Z"` with no commit, `status` prints a `source     embedded vX.Y.Z` line instead of the `repo` line, `diff`, `list` and `render` read the embedded files, `adopt` and `update` refuse with a message naming the release, the report record carries a new `harness_version` field with `harness_commit` null, and no git helper is called with an empty path (D17). Phase 4 replaces `update`'s refusal with the release flow (D22).

## Type

task

## Files changed

- `embed.go` (new, committed in 7f3c0f9) — package `styrman`, `//go:embed all:context all:skills all:agents all:commands all:rules`
- `embed_test.go` — `TestFilesMatchTree` (disk ⊆ embed, `.gitkeep` included); `TestEmbedHoldsOnlyTrackedFiles` (embed = `git ls-files`, both directions) from the security review's finding 1
- `plan_test.go` (new, package `styrman_test`) — `TestEmbeddedPlanEqualsCheckout`: the embedded plan equals the checkout plan in paths, bytes, modes and KeepForeign, for all three vendors
- `internal/harness/source.go` (new) — `Source`, `DirSource`, `EmbeddedSource`, `EmbeddedPrefix`, `IsReleaseVersion`, `Source.path`, `Source.readRegular`
- `internal/harness/source_test.go` (new) — MapFS plan, nine refusals from a MapFS, non-regular `SKILL.md`, DirSource = MapFS, a linked `skills/<name>` followed and a dangling one refused, embedded install state and report record
- `internal/harness/inventory.go`, `render.go`, `plan.go` — every reader takes a `Source`; `fs.ReadDir`/`fs.Glob`/`fs.ReadFile`/`fs.WalkDir` in place of the `os`/`filepath` calls; `checkManagedTree` runs only for `Dir != ""`
- `internal/harness/repo.go` — `ResolveSource` replaces `FindRepo`; `absSource`
- `internal/harness/apply.go` — `Install` takes a `Source` and records `embedded:<version>` with no commit for one
- `internal/harness/report.go` — `ReportRun.Source`, `BuildRecord(home, Source, …)`, `Record.HarnessVersion` (`harness_version`)
- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` — `var version` (release `-ldflags`), `ResolveSource`, `installFiles`, the per-command embedded branches, `releaseFromInfo`, `knownCheckout` refuses an `embedded:` manifest, usage text names the new source
- `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` — `TestReleaseBinaryWithoutCheckout`, `TestReleaseFromInfo`, `TestKnownCheckoutRefusesEmbeddedManifest`
- `internal/harness/harness_test.go`, `pathguard_test.go`, `report_test.go` — calls moved to `DirSource(repo)`, assertions unchanged; `TestFindRepo`/`TestFindRepoRefusesNamedNonRepo` became `TestResolveSource`/`TestResolveSourceRefusesNamedNonRepo`
- `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-17-release-binary.md` — Phase 2 boxes ticked with evidence; D19–D23; one new Phase 5 box (preflight refuses untracked or ignored files under the five directories) and one for the `AGENTS.md` `govulncheck` call-path note

## Agents dispatched

- `verifier` — PASS, `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-17-release-binary-phase-2.md`
- `reviewer` — APPROVE, 0 findings, `.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-17-review-f7ee817-21ba8dc-code.md`
- `security` — 1 medium, 6 low, `.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-17-security-f7ee817-21ba8dc.md`; three fixed, five rebutted in its `## Outcome`, one raised to the operator

## Verification

`gofmt -l cmd internal *.go` silent, `go vet ./...` clean, `go test -race -count=1 ./...` green (verifier: 81 pass, 0 fail, 0 skip — the one former skip, `TestFindRepo`, became `TestResolveSource`, which moves to a temporary working directory and always runs). Each guard was seen failing before it was trusted, then restored: the link refusals disabled → four symlink tests fail; `skills` embedded without `all:` → 52 files planned from the tree only; a skill file made 0755 → a mode mismatch on both vendors; the release-version gate removed → `TestResolveSource` and `TestReleaseBinaryWithoutCheckout` fail; the `embedded:` skip removed → `TestResolveSource` fails; an explicit non-tree falling through → two tests fail; an ignored `rules/.env` → `TestEmbedHoldsOnlyTrackedFiles` fails while every other test stays green; `knownCheckout`'s new guard removed → its test fails. title: `sh-agent report` keeps nothing — Phase 3 of the release-binary plan (2026-09-17)
body:
# `sh-agent report` keeps nothing — Phase 3 of the release-binary plan     (2026-09-17)

## Summary

`sh-agent report` no longer keeps a clone of the private feedback repository on every machine, which is what let each place read every other place's reports ("But why can I see dave reports?"). Without `--feedback-repo`, a run now clones `~/.config/sh-agent/report-<pid>` with `--filter=blob:none --no-checkout --depth 1`, limits it with `git sparse-checkout set --no-cone reports/<host>/`, writes its run directory, commits, pushes to the feedback URL, and removes that directory on every path out — a failed push, a refusal and an early return included. No other machine's report content is fetched to the disk; this machine's own earlier runs do come along, which is what lets the `-2` suffix pick a free directory name. A server that does not support the filter makes git warn and send everything: slower, still correct. Because a throwaway clone has nowhere to keep a rejected commit, a non-fast-forward push is retried once from a fresh clone; a second rejection says `push rejected twice; re-run sh-agent report — nothing is kept locally` and leaves nothing behind. `--feedback-repo DIR` is unchanged in every respect: that checkout is the operator's, so it is written into and never removed, a stray file in it is named and left alone, and a rejected push leaves the commit there with today's `pull --rebase` message. `sh-agent update` removes the clone earlier versions kept at `~/.config/sh-agent/feedback`, but only when it is that clone, clean, and not ahead of its upstream; anything else is left in place with the reason named.

## Type

task

## Files changed

- `internal/harness/report.go` — `ResolveFeedback` reduced to the `--feedback-repo` resolver; new `throwawayDir`, `cloneThrowaway`, `sweepInterruptedClones`, `alive`, `RemoveKeptClone`, `writeAndPush`, `scrubCredentials`, `errPushRejected` and the `testHooks` pair; `SendReport` split into the dry-run, named-checkout and throwaway paths, the last a two-attempt loop with removal deferred inside each attempt; `commitAndPush` returns the rejection sentinel so each caller words it
- `internal/harness/report_test.go` — `TestSendReport` rewritten for the default path (reads what was sent from the origin, `assertKeepsNothing` after each run); new `TestSendReportNamedCheckout`, `TestSendReportThrowawayClone`, `TestSendReportRetriesRejectedPush`, `TestRemoveKeptClone` (nine subtests), `TestSendReportSweepsInterruptedClones`, `TestCloneFailureDoesNotPrintCredentials`; `TestResolveFeedbackFailures` rewritten for the new signature plus the unreachable-URL case; helpers `seedFeedback`, `localBlobHolds`, `configDir`
- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` — `update` calls `harness.RemoveKeptClone` below every `--check` return, reported and never fatal; usage text and the command comment describe the throwaway clone
- `internal/harness/repo.go` — `gitOut` split so `gitOutC` can run one call with `LC_ALL=C`: the push whose rejection message the retry has to recognise
- `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` — `TestUpdateKeptCloneCleanupOnlyWhenUpdating`
- `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md` — § Report back rewritten: a new "Nothing is kept here" bullet, both rejection paths, and what `update` does with an old kept clone
- `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-17-release-binary.md` — Phase 3's three task boxes ticked with evidence; the partial-clone assumption marked settled; D25

## Agents dispatched

- `verifier` — PASS, `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-17-release-binary-phase-3.md` (87 pass, 0 fail, 0 skip at 83f3cf6)
- `security` — 2 medium, 6 low, `.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-17-security-73f2c36-83f3cf6.md`; five fixed with tests, three rebutted in its `## Outcome`. The two mediums were real defects in this phase's own code: `RemoveKeptClone`'s unpushed-commit guard failed OPEN when the count could not be taken (a branch with no upstream), and the cleanup call sat above `update --check`'s returns, so the read-only mode deleted the clone. Both now have a test that fails without the fix, and the function additionally refuses a symlink at that path, treats a stash and ignored files as work, and resolves a relative `--home`. Also fixed: an interrupted run's `report-<pid>` is swept by the next run (a deferred removal cannot cover a signal), git's clone error no longer repeats a URL a rewrite can fill with a token, and the one push whose message the retry must recognise runs with `LC_ALL=C`.

## Verification

`gofmt`, `go vet` and `go test -race -count=1 ./...` clean at each commit. The git mechanics were settled before any code was written (`.agents/scratch/p3-probe/probe.sh`), which caught two things that would have made the isolation check vacuous: a `file://` remote ignores `--filter` unless it sets `uploadpack.allowFilter`, and `git cat-file` on a promised object lazily FETCHES it, so a naive check answers yes about a blob the clone never held. The tests therefore seed `uploadpack.allowFilter` and read with `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`. `TestSendReportThrowawayClone` inspects the clone through `testHooks.beforeRemove`: the other host's directory is never checked out and its canary is in no local blob, the run lands on the remote, and afterwards there is no kept checkout and no `report-*`. Must-fail: every new and rewritten test failed to BUILD against the old `ResolveFeedback`, so the guards were mutated one at a time instead (`.agents/scratch/p3-mustfail/mutate.py`, which asserts each target text is unique and restores from a saved copy, per BUG-068) — removal not deferred, `--filter` dropped, `sparse-checkout` dropped, the retry removed, and the dirty check dropped each failed exactly the test that covers it, and the file was restored. One real run against GitHub, authorised by the operator (D25) and logged in `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-17-release-binary-phase-3-real-report.md`, settled the last assumption: the blob-less shallow clone over SSH succeeded, the push landed as `09586ff`, and nothing was left in `~/.config/sh-agent/`. The security review then found two real defects in this phase's own code (see § Agents dispatched); each was reproduced, fixed, and covered by a test seen failing without the fix, and the suite ended at 90 top-level tests and 73 subtests, none failing or skipped. Not exercised: what the real clone contained (it is removed by design, so only the tests can show that), the retry against the real remote, `RemoveKeptClone` against this box's own kept clone (which is `sh-agent update`'s job in the operator's home), and a pid collision between two runs in separate pid namespaces (rebutted in the review's `## Outcome`).

## Docs

title: `update` from a signed release — Phase 4 of the release-binary plan (2026-09-17)
body:
# `update` from a signed release — Phase 4 of the release-binary plan     (2026-09-17)

## Summary

`sh-agent update` on a place with no harness checkout now moves that place forward from a GitHub release instead of refusing. `gh release view` gives the newest tag; the tag must parse as `vX.Y.Z` and be numerically newer than the running binary, or nothing is downloaded and the reason is printed. `gh release download` fetches this platform's `sh-agent-<goos>-<goarch>`, `SHA256SUMS` and `SHA256SUMS.sig` into a random `~/.config/sh-agent/release-*` directory that is removed on every path out. Verification is two checks and a third fact: `ssh-keygen -Y verify` checks the signature over `SHA256SUMS` against an allowed-signers line compiled into the binary, in the namespace `sh-agent-release`; the downloaded binary's SHA-256 must equal its line in that file; and the file must name the release it belongs to, `# styrman-harness vX.Y.Z`, matching the tag — so the version is part of what was signed (D26). Only then is `~/.local/bin/sh-agent` replaced through a temp file and a rename, and the NEW binary runs its own install, which deploys the harness built into it. `--check` stops after the tag comparison: `up to date (vX.Y.Z)`, or `newer release vA.B.C available` and exit 2. A development build is never overwritten from a release; it is told to download one by hand.

## Type

feature

## Files changed

- `internal/harness/release.go` (new) — `ReleaseRepo`, `ReleaseNamespace`, `releaseSigner`, `sumsVersionMarker`, `ErrNewerRelease`, `AssetName`, `LatestRelease`, `UpdateFromRelease`, `downloadRelease`, `verifyRelease`, `checksumFor`, `compareRelease`, `releaseParts`, `sshKeygen`, `sshKeygenSystemPaths`, `readCapped`, `maxAssetBytes`, `maxSumsBytes`
- `internal/harness/release_test.go` (new) — a fake `gh` and real `ssh-keygen` signatures from a test key, on a PATH holding nothing else: the good path, both up-to-date modes, `--check`, twelve refusals, the downgrade and bad-tag cases, `TestChecksumFor`, `TestCompareRelease`, `TestSSHKeygenPrefersASystemPath`, `TestReleaseSignerMatchesTheDeployGuide`
- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` — `update` with an embedded source routes to `UpdateFromRelease`, mapping `ErrNewerRelease` to exit 2; `installPassArgs` extracted and shared with the checkout path; usage text and the command comment describe both kinds of update
- `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` — `TestReleaseBinaryUpdateCheckExitsTwo`; `TestReleaseBinaryWithoutCheckout`'s update leg rewritten for the release flow with PATH emptied
- `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-17-release-binary.md` — Phase 4's two boxes ticked with evidence; D26, D27, D28; D22 marked superseded; Phase 5's release-procedure box now also requires the `SHA256SUMS` version marker and a rehearsal

## Agents dispatched

- `verifier` — PASS at 4d45155, `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-17-release-binary-phase-4.md` (96 pass, 0 fail, 0 skip). That run predates the security fixes below; the counts at 40bf2db are 99 top-level tests and 85 subtests, none failing or skipped, with `gofmt`, `go vet`, `go test -race` and `govulncheck` clean, re-run by the main agent.
- `security` — 1 medium, 6 low, `.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-17-security-dab2565-4d45155.md`; six fixed, two rebutted in its `## Outcome`. The medium was real and load-bearing: `tag == version` was an equality test and the signed bytes did not name the version, so a genuinely signed OLDER release would install, and one release's signed checksums verified under another release's tag. It found the signature chain otherwise sound — signer, namespace, identity and asset name compiled in or from `runtime`, nothing in a release able to redirect them, nothing outside the download directory written before both checks pass.

## Verification

Measured before any code: `ssh-keygen -Y verify` exits 0 on a good signature and 255 for a wrong key, a wrong namespace and altered content (OpenSSH 10.0p2). Twelve refusals are covered, each asserting the installed binary is byte-identical afterwards, no install ran, and no download directory is left: `gh` missing, `gh` unable to reach the repository, no verifier anywhere, no asset for this platform, a signature from another key, `SHA256SUMS` altered after signing, a checksum mismatch, a release shipping its own allowed-signers line under the compiled-in identity, signed checksums naming another version, signed checksums naming no version, no `.sig`, no `SHA256SUMS`. Must-fail by mutation (`.agents/scratch/p4-mustfail/mutate.py`, which asserts each target is unique, restores from a saved copy and reports a stale mutation as a failure, per BUG-068): all twelve mutations fail the tests that cover them — signature unchecked, checksum uncompared, verification skipped, no verifier required, verifier taken from PATH first, `gh` unchecked, namespace unpinned, signer taken from the release, downgrade allowed, tag unvalidated, the signed version marker unchecked, and a development build overwritten. Two mistakes of the session's own making, both caught by running rather than assuming: a test reached the REAL `gh` and the real repository because `/usr/bin` was on its PATH for `ssh-keygen` (PATH is now a single controlled directory, with `ssh-keygen` linked in), and a generated Go literal had its `\n` escapes turned into newlines, breaking the build (BUG-057's hazard; repaired and then verified by grepping for the escape itself). Not exercised: no real release exists yet, so every download is against the fake `gh`; the three-platform cross-compilation and the real `gh release create` are Phase 5; `darwin/arm64` behaviour is untested on this Linux box.

## Docs

`cmd/sh-agent/main.go`'s usage text and package comment describe both kinds of `update`. `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md` § Update still describes only the checkout kind, and `README.md`, the map, `AGENTS.md` rules 1 and 2, `REQUIREMENTS.md` R8/R9 and `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md` still describe the unpacked bundle; all of them land in Phase 5's single commit to `main` (D11, R9). Phase 5 must also write the `SHA256SUMS` version marker into `/preflight` Step 6 and `remote.md` § Releases — until it does, no release this code will accept can be cut (D26), which is stated in that box.

## Requirements

R4 holds: stdlib only, `gh` and `ssh-keygen` shelled out, no dependency added. R8 and R9 gain the release-binary way in, in Phase 5's commit, with the operator's approved text. The signer line is the same operator key `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` § Releases gives `git verify-tag`, pinned by a test so the two copies cannot drift.

title: BUG-078 — a verified release binary shadowed by an earlier PATH entry (2026-09-18)
body:
# BUG-078 — a verified release binary shadowed by an earlier PATH entry     (2026-09-18)

## Summary

On devbox the operator downloaded v1.2.1, verified its signature and checksum, saw `./sh-agent-linux-amd64 version` print `v1.2.1`, moved it to `/usr/local/bin` — and `sh-agent` kept running a stale `(devel)` build from `/opt/devbox/bin`, which installed an old tree and reported `drift none`. Two PATH entries sat ahead of the new binary and nothing said so. This change makes `install` and `status` say so, and makes both install guides verify the *file* before it moves and the *shell's resolution* after. Unreleased: it reaches binary-only places at the next release.

## Type

bugfix

## What changed

- **`internal/harness/pathguard.go`** (new): `PathShadows(pathEnv, binPath) (shadows []string, onPath bool)` walks PATH as a shell does. `onPath` is true when the walk reaches an executable that `os.SameFile`s the installed file — through its own directory, a symlinked directory, a symlink or a hard link; there is no lexical directory comparison anywhere. `shadows` are the executables of that name found before it, in order, without repeats; an empty PATH entry prints as `./sh-agent`. `executableAt` is what it calls a binary (`os.Stat`, not a directory, execute bit set).
- **`cmd/sh-agent/main.go`**: `install` prints `warning: <path> comes before <installed> on PATH, so `sh-agent` runs that one` when PATH reaches the installed file but only after an earlier entry; when PATH does not reach it and something else answers, the old "not on PATH" note names it instead (`… so `sh-agent` runs <path> instead; put <bin dir> ahead of it`). `status` gains a `shadowed   <path> comes first on PATH, so `sh-agent` runs that, not the binary above` line under the same condition. `install --dry-run` prints no PATH claim: it wrote no binary. One `PathShadows` call feeds each; there is no second definition of "on PATH".
- **README § Install without cloning**: the `gh` route is one `&&` chain — download into `mktemp -d` with `--clobber`, the real signer line written to `allowed_signers`, `ssh-keygen -Y verify`, `sha256sum -c`, `./<asset> version` on the file, then the one `mv` and the scratch dir removed — so a failed check stops the move and no checksum or signer file lands in a PATH directory. The `go install` route says what it trusts (SSH to GitHub and git's hashes; no checksum database, no release signature) and the browser route is the same chain over the files in `~/Downloads`; each route is its own fence, so a paste runs one route. Then: `sh-agent version` *unqualified* first, with the sentence that it tells stale from fresh and never genuine from forged.
- **`.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` § First install**: the same procedure as one chained block for a release-binary machine; § Verify asks for the unqualified `version` and no `shadowed` line. **`local.md` § Verify** says the same for a checkout place.
- **`.agents/docs/bugs/BUG-078-…`** and `INDEX.md`: `fixed`, with what the code half does *not* catch stated plainly (below).

## What it does not do

On devbox as it happened, the wrong binary ran the install and wrote itself to `~/.local/bin`, first on PATH — from its own point of view nothing was shadowed, so no in-binary check could have fired. The doc half catches that ordering: `sh-agent version` unqualified and `which -a`. The code half catches the other ordering, where `/usr/local/bin`, `/opt/…` or a Homebrew dir precedes `~/.local/bin`, which is common on a Mac.

## Tests

`TestPathShadows` (14 cases over real temp files: installed dir first, earlier entry, order and later entries, symlink, hard link, symlinked directory before and after a shadow, repeated entry, empty directory, non-executable, missing installed dir, `//`, `/.`, empty entry via `t.Chdir`, missing installed file), `TestExecutableAt`, `TestInstallAndStatusNameAPathShadow` (warning, `shadowed`, both quiet after a symlink to the installed binary), `TestOffPathInstallNamesWhatAnswersAndDoesNotWarnTwice` (the off-PATH note names what answers; no double warning; `--dry-run` makes no PATH claim). Ten must-fail mutations in `.agents/scratch/bug078-mustfail/mutate.py`, each failing as a test failure — three first attempts did not compile (an unused variable each) and were redone, since a build failure proves nothing.

## Definition of Done

Four review rounds, because two landed on one mechanism and the context rule then sends the mechanism to the operator:

- Round 1 (`52574a0`): `verifier` PASS (`testing/2026-09-18-verify-bug078-path-shadow.md`); `reviewer` REQUEST CHANGES — high: `binOnPath` (string compare) and `PathShadows` (`Clean`) disagreed on `.local/bin//`, hiding a real shadow; medium: a hard link reported as a shadow; low: an unbacked "for an hour" in README. `security` 1 medium (README's signer line a placeholder, the file left in a PATH dir) + 6 low. `/review --docs` APPROVE, 2 low (`local.md` narrowed; no changes entry). All fixed except two lows rebutted (`reviews/…-4cdc0b5-52574a0*.md` § Outcome).
- Round 2 (`8ce58a0`): `verifier` PASS; `reviewer` REQUEST CHANGES — the same mechanism again, lexical `onPath` vs `SameFile` on a symlinked directory. `security`: two mediums, both docs (`remote.md`'s block a sketch with `$D` unassigned; README unchained at the verify), plus the rebuttal reasons corrected. **Stopped here and asked the operator what the gate was for**; their choice: "on PATH" is the identity walk reaching the file, nothing lexical.
- Round 3 (`b029ea1`): `verifier` PASS, the alias repro run by hand; `reviewer` APPROVE; `security` all low. The three-round cap; the operator granted one bounded extra round for the cheap fixes.
- Round 4 (`28e4747`): `verifier` PASS (215 tests/subtests, unchanged; a fresh-home `--dry-run` printed no PATH line); `security` four lows, no high — it validated the dry-run gate in both states itself. One low was a docs-only edit made in the closing commit (the browser fence became the same `&&` chain as the `gh` route); the others corrected two `left` reasons and confirmed the hung-mount reason (`reviews/2026-09-18-security-4cdc0b5-28e4747.md` § Outcome).
- `documentation` for `local.md` § Verify; `bugs` for the record and its `fixed` status, read against the diff and corrected (a mistyped SHA and `os.SameFile` attributed to the wrong commit).
- Every round's findings have a `## Outcome` line: fixed with file:line, rebutted with a checkable reason, or `left` with an owner.

## Where it stops

Unreleased. `context/AGENTS.md` does not yet carry the rule ("a verified install is what the shell resolves, not what was moved into place"); the bug record marks it a graduation candidate.

title: install names every file it changes (2026-09-18)

# install names every file it changes     (2026-09-18)

## Summary

`sh-agent install` (and the install `update` runs) prints one line per file it adds, updates, corrects the mode of, or removes, on every run — not only under `--dry-run`, which used to be the only run that listed anything. Unchanged files stay a count. The operator asked for it ("more info … It should be clear what is installed new or things like that. Go with 1", 2026-09-18). Phase 1 of `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-18-sh-agent-works-everywhere.md`. Unreleased.

## Type

feature (output), phase checkpoint

## What changed

- **`internal/harness/apply.go` `Install`**: `add     ~/<rel>` when no previous file existed; `update  ~/<rel>` when the bytes differed; `update  ~/<rel> (previous file unreadable: <err>)` when the previous file could not be read — written over as before, the line says why (D6); `mode    ~/<rel> (0666 -> 0644)` when only the permission differed — the probe runs on a dry run too, only the `chmod` is gated (D7, D8), and the file stays in the `unchanged` count; `remove  ~/<rel> (no longer in the source)` on the real run as on the dry run (it was dry-run only). The line for a written file prints after the write succeeds, so a write that fails — a directory at the path, which the rename cannot replace (`EISDIR`) — leaves no line claiming a change (Phase 1 review). The summary line's shape is unchanged; `written` = add + update.
- **README § Daily commands** (`install` row) and **`specs/sh-agent/delivery.md`** say so.

## Tests

`TestInstallNamesEveryChange`: first install lists every managed file as `add` and nothing else; an identical install lists nothing; a changed source file lists exactly its deployed copies as `update`; a removed source file lists `remove … (no longer in the source)`; a mode-only drift lists one `mode` line and is counted unchanged; a `0000` previous file (D9) lists `update … (previous file unreadable: …)` and is written; `--dry-run` lists the same `update` and `mode` lines and leaves bytes and modes as they were; a directory at a destination fails the install with no line for it. Eight must-fail mutations in `.agents/scratch/phase1-mustfail/mutate.py`, each failing as a test failure. Live: 260 `add` lines then none; a touched skill in a scratch clone → its two vendor copies as `update`; a chmodded file under `--dry-run` → one `mode` line, mode untouched.

## Definition of Done

`verifier` PASS (`testing/2026-09-18-verify-sh-agent-works-everywhere-phase-1.md`, 227/0/0, all four checkpoint legs live — the agent hit its turn limit once with an empty log and finished on a continuation; and `…-phase-1-2.md` over the final range); `reviewer` APPROVE WITH NITS (`reviews/2026-09-18-review-b393525-028a43b.md`, one low fixed — the line now prints after the write); `/review --docs` APPROVE (`…-docs.md`); the docs clause done in the same change. Found on the way, filed as Phase 2 boxes: a relative `--home` with `--repo` resolves differently on a real install and a dry run (the verifier's observation); the recon's four coverage gaps.

## Type

release (patch)

## What ships

- `2026-09-18-install-names-every-change.md` — `add`/`update`/`mode`/`remove`/`keep` lines on every run; `--dry-run` the same lines and no writes; a failed write claims nothing.

## Gate

`.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-18-preflight-v1.2.3.md` — VERDICT: SHIP over `v1.2.2..30f7488`. Verifier PASS (250/0/0, cross-builds, matrix tier re-run: 53 cells); reviewer APPROVE (every slice covered, the post-cap commit on opus); security six lows, none reopening, 80 paths read; docs lens APPROVE. ## Release
