body:
# Retro 2026-09-18 applied: seven harness-scope proposals     (2026-09-18)

## Summary

The seven proposals of `retros/2026-09-18-retro.md` (queued in `~/.config/sh-agent/proposals/2026-09-18-retro.md`) are applied on the operator's "apply all": four sentences in `context/AGENTS.md`, two triggers in `feedback-log`, the verifier's early-log rule, and one clause in the feature skill's cold-reader brief. The three bugs whose rules graduated — BUG-078, BUG-079, BUG-080 — move to the Graduated table, and the two events the retro found without numbers get theirs (BUG-081, BUG-082), graduated on arrival because their rules land in this same commit. Every other place picks the change up with `sh-agent update`.

## Type

context, skills, agents (harness rules)

## Files

- `context/AGENTS.md` — § Definition of Done step 2: a fix's test builds the ARRANGEMENT the finding measured (BUG-081). § Hard rules: an installed COMMAND is verified by the shell that will run it (BUG-078, BUG-079); the read-only mode resolves paths as the real run does, a child-cwd path is made absolute first (BUG-080); a must-fail mutation counts only when the mutated code compiled and a named test failed (BUG-082). § Work: the dispatch sentence a `verifier` gets is spelled out ("after the FIRST command, Status IN PROGRESS, update after every one") — the one edit beyond the seven proposals, from the behavioural runs below (BUG-083).
- `skills/feedback-log/SKILL.md` — triggers 6 Redirection (signal `redirection`, new table row) and 7 A missed filing (signal `restatement`).
- `agents/verifier.md` — the log is written after the FIRST command with `IN PROGRESS`, updated after EVERY command; a log still in progress at cutoff is a failed dispatch.
- `skills/feature/SKILL.md` — the cold-reader brief asks whether each test fixture in a verify clause produces the condition it claims.
- `.agents/docs/bugs/INDEX.md`, `BUG-078…080` (Related lines), `BUG-081`, `BUG-082` — graduation; `BUG-083` — recorded, open.

## Verification

- `go run ./cmd/sh-agent install --home .agents/scratch/retro-home` → 260 written; `status` → drift none, 259 files match; `list` ok; `gofmt -l cmd internal` empty; `go test ./...` ok (the Go code is untouched; `TestHarnessMap` and the inventory tests read the changed files).
- Context change, behavioural: `claude -p --append-system-prompt "<the new Hard-rules bullet>"` from a scratch directory quoted the new sentence verbatim and named BUG-078 and BUG-079 — the text given, not the installed file, so it proves the wording reads as intended, not the install.
- Verifier change, behavioural: `claude -p --agents <json built from the working-tree agents/verifier.md>` in a scratch clone (`.agents/scratch/verifier-run`). First run: every subagent Bash and Write call hit the permission gate, no agent ran, no log — not evidence either way. Three runs with `--allowedTools` for the verifier's tools and a dispatch that did NOT repeat the early-write sentence: 1 of 3 wrote the log with `IN PROGRESS` after the first command and updated it after the second; 2 of 3 ran every command and wrote once at the end (tool-call order read from each subagent transcript). The definition alone does not bind — BUG-083, the class of BUG-062/063/064; the dispatch text remains the enforcement and now says "after the FIRST command, IN PROGRESS, then after every command". The proposal stays applied: the wording is what the dispatch repeats.

title: The sh-agent audit: every verb on every kind of place (2026-09-18)

# The sh-agent audit: every verb on every kind of place     (2026-09-18)

## Summary

Phase 2 of `plans/2026-09-18-sh-agent-works-everywhere.md` — the operator's Definition of Done for this session: "work until the delivery mechanism sh-agent is flawless". Five review lenses read `cmd/sh-agent` and `internal/harness` whole, an explorer mapped every verb × place-kind cell, and everything they found was fixed with a test that failed first or rebutted in writing; three review rounds of the fixes followed, two of them stopped at the operator's door because a fix had introduced the next round's defect. Phase 3, the matrix on this box, ran on the result: 53 cells, none silent. Unreleased.

## Type

fix (audit); phase checkpoint

## What changed

Behaviour a user of `sh-agent` sees:

- **Release tags are canonical.** `v1.02.2`, `v01.2.2`, `v1.2.02` and a component that does not fit an int are not release tags: `IsReleaseVersion` refuses them, so `update` never downloads such a tag, and a tag that is not newer than the running binary is refused with "the newest release X is not newer than this binary Y; nothing installed".
- **Refusals name the alternative.** `update` on a plain copy: "not its own git checkout; a plain copy cannot be updated with git — `install` still deploys it as it is; to move forward, use a checkout (`git clone …`) or a release binary (README § Install without cloning)". `adopt` on a release binary names the checkout to clone; on a plain copy its "next:" line says to copy the skill into a checkout and commit there, not "commit and push" a tree with no repository.
- **The BUG-079 note** prints only for the user's real home (never under `--home` elsewhere), identity by `os.SameFile` so a symlinked `$HOME` counts, and offers `ln -sfn` only when the file's directory is the caller's — otherwise "it is not yours to relink — remove it, with the rights that own its directory, or leave it and run the installed one by its path".
- **`~/.config/sh-agent` is private.** Created 0700; an existing looser one is tightened by `install` before it writes anything, with `mode    ~/.config/sh-agent (0755 -> 0700)`; a dry run names it and touches nothing; a symlinked directory and one the caller does not own are left alone; a failed `chmod` is a note. `diff` and `report` create it private and never change an existing one.
- **A relative `--home` beside `--repo`** lands under the invoking directory on a real install as on a dry run (BUG-080).
- **`adopt`** strips group/other write bits like `install` does. **`diff`** renders under `~/.config/sh-agent/`, never `/tmp`, and removes its temp file on every path. **`install`/`status`** report an oversized `settings.json` with one note. A description with a control character renders as valid YAML for Antigravity; a table cell never cuts a multi-byte character.
- **Docs**: the `keep` line, the `knownCheckout` refusal (README's "works from anywhere" qualified), `report: --repo is not used here`, and every changed message quoted where it is described.

Not changed, by decision: the ~220-line `settings.json` editor stays in `main.go` (a Follow-up); `LoadState` does not sanitise `Repo` (reason narrowed in the record); loose modes inside the runtime dir; ownership as the proxy for relinkability.

## Tests

`internal/harness/audit_test.go` (11 tests, one per finding) and `owned_unix_test.go`; eight tests in `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` (plain-copy `update`/`adopt`/`status` through the CLI, `adopt` on a release binary, `sync`, `diff` with drift, the relative `--home`, the oversized settings). Nineteen must-fail mutations in `.agents/scratch/phase2-mustfail/mutate.py`, each failing as a test failure; the ones that could not compile or could not be reached were redone or dropped and say so in the reports. Suite 250, `govulncheck` clean, `GOOS=windows` and `darwin/arm64` builds clean.

## Definition of Done

- **Audit** (`reviews/2026-09-18-review-harness-merged.md`, 19 findings, `## Outcome`): code lens APPROVE WITH NITS; security (opus) 1 medium + 7 low; simplify 1 medium + 3 low; docs 2 medium + 1 low; tests PASS with 2 gaps. Explorer recon `plans/2026-09-18-recon-sh-agent-audit.md`: no silent cell, four coverage gaps.
- **Round 1** (`3209cf3`): verifier PASS (244); reviewer (opus) APPROVE WITH NITS, 3 low; security 1 medium (the 0700 was a no-op after `SaveState`'s 0755) + 2 low; docs lens APPROVE.
- **Round 2** (`e7fec88`): verifier PASS (248, cross-builds); reviewer APPROVE WITH NITS — two mediums on the new `ConfigDir` (symlink followed; `EPERM` fails the run); security 1 medium — the same mechanism, worse (an install aborted after every write, no manifest). **The operator's call** (option 1): tighten as a `mode` line at the top of `install`, never fail.
- **Round 3** (`42840fb`): verifier PASS (250; four live legs quoted, the `mode` line before the first `add`); reviewer APPROVE, one low/low (README's overpromise); security four lows, no high, the medium closed structurally. After the cap, in the checkpoint commit: the two skips print a `note:` (the symlink one pinned by a test), README's clause corrected; Phase 4's gate reviews those lines.
- `documentation` ×3 (audit docs findings; the Phase 2 messages; the runtime-dir mode line); `bugs` for BUG-080.

## Where it stops

Unreleased; Phase 4 of the plan is the release. The Follow-ups are in the plan.

# `sh-agent update --from-zip`: a third way in, the zip place     (date: 2026-09-28)

## Summary
A machine that can hold neither the operator's SSH key nor `gh` can now take the harness from a repository zip downloaded by hand. `sh-agent update --from-zip <file>`:
- reads the zip once, hashes it, and checks every entry before writing anything;
- unpacks only the five harness trees under `~/.config/sh-agent/zip-*`;
- installs them with the running binary, and deletes the unpacked copy.

Nothing is fetched, and the output flags the zip as `UNVERIFIED`. The manifest records `zip:sha256:<hex>`, and `status` and `diff` say that a zip install is not compared.

REQUIREMENTS R8/R9 carry the operator-approved text ("approve as written"), with the zip place nested under Update (D9: "Go with your recommendations"). ADR-038 supersedes ADR-034 in part. `AGENTS.md` rule 1, `delivery.md` § The model, the README map (drawn dashed, because a zip is fetched by hand) and the deploy guides all say three ways.

**Also in this change:**
- `update --dry-run` is now read-only on both paths; it used to act.
- `diff` has a zip branch.
- Leftover `zip-*` directories are swept after a successful run.
- `secretShaped` and `.gitignore` cover `*oauth-token*`.
- `testing/skill-matrix.md` takes matrix option 1: the lists the scenarios need, with the statement that the allowlist is not a security boundary.
- `skills/VENDORED.md` records that the `find-skills` Step 6 edit is not verbatim.

feature

# Release v1.9.0     (date: 2026-09-28)

## Summary
v1.9.0 is gated SHIP over `v1.8.0..b5d4cb3` (`reviews/2026-09-28-preflight-v1.9.0.md`).

## Type
release

## Release notes
## New features
- **Signed release zip.** Each release now publishes `styrman-harness-vX.Y.Z.zip`, a `git archive` of the tag, under the signed `SHA256SUMS`.
  - `sh-agent update --from-zip <file>` verifies the zip when `SHA256SUMS` and `SHA256SUMS.sig` sit beside it, and prints `VERIFIED against the signed SHA256SUMS of release vX.Y.Z`.
  - It refuses the zip on any failed check, and nothing is written.
  - A zip with neither file beside it (a `main` zip) still installs, marked `UNVERIFIED` (ADR-039).
## Improvements and optimisation
- **The zip verdict is kept.** An install from a zip records in its manifest whether the zip was verified, and `sh-agent status` shows `(verified vX.Y.Z)` or `(unverified)`.
- **Refusals name the right file.** When the zip is not the one the release published, for example GitHub's automatic "Source code" archive, the refusal names the zip that release does publish.
## Fixes
- **The report sweep no longer builds a glob from the home path**, so a home containing glob characters cannot reach another home's clones.
- **Tests can no longer run the real `sh-agent report`:** they cut `PATH` first, so none can push to the feedback repository (BUG-094). The report a test pushed during v1.8.0 has been removed.
- **The pid in the sweep test is now deterministic**, so the test can no longer fail by chance.
## Other updates
- **`find-skills` is vendored verbatim again.** Its routing (a found skill goes into the harness checkout's `skills/`, then `sh-agent install`) now lives in the global context, including `npx skills add … -y`.
- **R9 wording:** "nothing in the zip replaces the binary".
- **The skill matrix drops `curl`.**
- **The README map** draws the release zip and the Releases → zip place path (by hand, verified).
## Install
- **Download:** see README § Install without cloning. Existing binary-only places: `sh-agent update`.
- **Zip place:** download `styrman-harness-v1.9.0.zip`, `SHA256SUMS` and `SHA256SUMS.sig` from this release into one folder, then run `sh-agent update --from-zip styrman-harness-v1.9.0.zip`. The output must say `VERIFIED`.

## Agents dispatched

- **Gate fixes:** `reviewer`.

# 2026-10-01-1247 — v2.0.0 gate fix: the memory store's git call runs no project hook

From the gate's security code slice (`reviews/2026-10-01-security-v1.16.2-0b1b5b8-code.md`, medium/high): `internal/memory` asked `git ls-files -- .agents/memory` with none of the guards the dream's status call has, so the nightly dream, which resolves every indexed project's store through it, ran a project's `core.fsmonitor` hook at 03:00 — the agent's scratch probe showed the hook firing on `ls-files` and not on the hardened `status`. Fix: `storeTrackedArgs(root)` in `internal/memory/memory.go` builds the call with `--no-optional-locks -c core.fsmonitor=false`, mirroring `trailStatusArgs`; `TestStoreTrackedArgs` pins the argument list and failed red against a nil body before the fix (`go test ./internal/memory -run TestStoreTrackedArgs`: FAIL, then ok). Reviewer and security Outcome named in the gate report; the verifier's r2 log (PASS at 89f3308) predates this commit, so r3 runs over the new head.

# Release signer rotated; the release key signs through the SSH agent (ADR-052)

## Summary

`a0a54b4`. The previous release key's private half was pasted into a chat session (exposed; no known misuse), and it doubled as dave's GitHub login key. # v2.7.0 gate fixes: BUG-171, the dream signal relay, the timer's home, redaction kinds, disallowedTools off the allow-list     (2026-10-12)

## Summary
The release gate's reviewer and security agents reviewed v2.6.2..13c5bde. Nothing blocked; every finding was low. The operator chose what went in. Round 1 fixes:
- **BUG-171:** a bad `--vendor` is a usage error, exit 2, for every verb before the verb does anything. Before, `update` fetched and pulled the checkout first and exited 1, `--dry-run` never checked the value, `status` exited 1, and `uninstall` and `report` took any word.
- **The dream signal relay:** `relay()` still takes a signal already queued when the CLI ends, and `callWithin` waits for it before the next project.
- **The timer:** it checks the home as given, not only through the cleaned binary path.
- **The command-line credential rule, three more shapes (operator's choice):**
  - an escaped `\n`, `\r` or `\t` written out before the flag;
  - a quote around the user and the password;
  - six clients' password flags: mongosh/mongo and sqlcmd `-p`/`-P`, an LDAP tool's `-w`, OpenSSL's `pass:`, keytool's `-storepass`/`-keypass` and lftp's `-u user,password`.

Round 2 verified all six fixes and reached the review cap. The operator chose "Fix small ones, no round 3":
- OpenSSL's `pass:` is caught inside quotes too.
- Five harmless over-redactions are pinned.
- README and the local deploy guide now say `update --vendor all` widens a single-vendor install.
- `disallowedTools` leaves the agent allow-list (ADR-056a), because Antigravity's derived agent drops it.

task (gate fixes; one bug record, one ADR amendment)

Every fix had its test red first:

A symlink, or a path under a linked directory, stays, and `~/.claude` itself stays in `pruneEmptyDirs`' stop map. `memory show` prints the index only. `dream` always runs `agy`, reads skills from `~/.gemini/config/skills` and reads transcripts from Antigravity's conversations only. `metrics ingest` reads Antigravity only. `show`, `report` and the dream summary have one `agy` column. A second column, `claude (historical)`, appears only when the window holds rows an older ingest stored (D7). Nothing deletes those rows, and `export` writes them as before.

## Type
task (plan phase)

## Files changed
from `git diff --numstat` (+1,172 −1,784 in the working tree, deleted files included)
- Deleted: `internal/harness/settings.go`, `internal/harness/settings_test.go`, `cmd/sh-agent/settings_test.go`, `internal/metrics/claude.go`, `internal/metrics/claude_test.go`
- `internal/harness/plan.go`: one target. `VendorAll`, `VendorClaude`, `NormalizeVendor`, `KeepForeign`, `IsOurs` and `ClaudeRoot` are gone. `VendorAntigravity` stays, so the manifest still records it.
- `internal/harness/apply.go`: `Install(src, home, files, dryRun, out)`. The foreign-file branches are gone. The stop map names `~/.claude` as a literal, with the reason beside it.
- `internal/harness/{render,state,adopt,inventory,frontmatter}.go`: the stub constant goes. The manifest's `Vendor` is written `antigravity`, and an old value is read and ignored. `adopt` no longer looks in `~/.claude/skills`. Comments changed.
- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go`: the `--vendor` flag, `resolveVendor`, `ctx.vendor`, the settings calls, the foreign-`CLAUDE.md` note and the `claude` status line are gone. `installPassArgs` forwards `--home` alone. Usage text changed.
- `internal/memory/memory.go`: `Show(dir)`. The native-memory hint and `nativeOn` are gone.
- `internal/dream/{dream,collect,run,metrics,timer}.go`: `command()` is agy-only, and the private HOME and the stream-json stdin are unconditional. `answer(stdout)`. The Claude transcript reader is gone. The summary counts sessions over every column.
- `internal/metrics`: `writer.go` is new and holds the writer helpers `agy.go` shares, moved verbatim from `claude.go`. `ingest.go` reads agy only. `show.go` has `Columns` and the `historical` column, with lazily made count maps. `numbers.go` and `report.go` follow the columns; the report's series and tables are built per summary, and Antigravity keeps colour slot 2. `store.go` and `agy.go` comments changed.
- `internal/search/dream.go`: one comment.
- Tests, new: `TestPlanAntigravityOnly`, `TestResyncShedsOldClaudeFiles`, `TestInstallLeavesClaudeCodeAlone`, `TestUpdateRefusesTheVendorFlagFirst` (BUG-171's rule, kept for the flag that no longer exists), `TestInstallPassArgsForwardsTheHomeOnly`, the six `--vendor agy` rows of `TestUsageErrorsExit2`, `TestShowHistoricalColumn`, `TestShowAgyOnly`, `TestReportAgyOnly`, `TestAgyIdentifiersAreNameShaped`, `TestIngestPrintsNoControlOrFormatCharacters`.
- Tests, moved onto Antigravity fixtures: `TestSourceLabelAndOutcome`, `TestOutcomeStampedAfterTheRun`, `TestMetricsVerb` (with a decoy `HOME`, for R6), every dream run test (`fakeAgy`), and the dream collect tests (`agyConversations`, whose schema both readers accept).
- Tests, historical: `historical_test.go`'s `historicalRows` inserts what an old ingest stored, for the show, report and numbers tests.
- Tests, deleted: the Claude transcript, settings, stub, foreign-`CLAUDE.md`, vendor-selection and native-memory-hint tests.
- Docs (the `documentation` agent): `README.md`, `specs/sh-agent/{metrics,memory-loop,dream}.md`, `deploy/{local,remote}.md`, `testing/guide.md`. `memory-loop.md` § Known differences is retired. Main agent: `AGENTS.md` lines 7, 39 and 44, and one `memory-loop.md` phrase.
- Plan: Phase 2's two work boxes are ticked. The checkpoint stays open (below).

## Deviations from the plan's box
- **The checkpoint's grep is met in part.** `git grep -il claude -- 'cmd' 'internal' '*.go'` lists 17 files. Expected among them: the stop-map entry (`apply.go`, with the resync comment of `Install`), the historical column (`main.go:65` and `internal/metrics/{ingest,report,show,store}.go` with their tests) and the stop-map tests. Not expected:
  - the Claude Code agent format: `derive.go`, `inventory.go` lines 23, 225 and 234, and `harness_test.go` lines 43, 155, 2351–2371 and 2439. Phase 3a deletes it (D3, D17).
  - the listing-budget comments: `catalog_test.go:671` and `size_test.go:90`. The 19,500-byte budget rests on Claude Code's listing; Antigravity's is about 44,000.
  - `internal/search/testdata/recall.tsv` rows 19 and 39 (D20).
  The box stays open until Phase 3a lands or the operator amends it.
- The "tests first" red was a build failure of the old tests against the new API in six packages, not a test-by-test red. Each removed symbol appears in `.agents/scratch/fyr/go-test-phase2-red.txt`.
- `State.Vendor` is still written, as `antigravity`, rather than dropped. `skills/init-project` and `skills/dream` grep for it until Phase 3b removes the check.
- `metrics.DefaultContextTarget` keeps 300,000. Its other half, the auto-compact window, went with `settings.go`, and so did `TestAutoCompactWindowIsTheContextTarget`.
- The `testing/guide.md` three-sandbox kit (§ 4, Claude Code runs) is left for Phase 3b. `memory-loop.md`'s `/init-project` rows are the skill's, also Phase 3b.

## Agents dispatched
- `documentation`: the README, specs, deploy and testing-guide edits. Its diff was read against the code by the main agent. One claim it kept ("Antigravity prompts … for paths outside the workspace") was already in the old text.
- The plan's Phase 5 holds the Definition of Done over the whole feature: the `verifier` log, `reviewer --code --docs` and `security`. This phase's code diff was read by the main agent only.

## Verification

It ran on go1.24.4 (`~/.local/bin/go` still dangles). `govulncheck` reports the same 15 standard-library advisories as Phase 1, all fixed in later Go (`.agents/scratch/fyr/govulncheck-p2.txt`).
- Fresh scratch home (`.agents/scratch/fyr/home-p2`): `go run ./cmd/sh-agent install --home …` exit 0, 896 files, and no `.claude` directory. The installed binary's `status` exits 0 with `drift none — 895 files match the repo`, and the `binary` line has no warning. The `installed` line no longer prints a vendor.
- Crossing, local half (`.agents/scratch/fyr/home-p2-old`):
  - The `HEAD` build (from `git archive a60f83a`) installed 897 files under `.claude`, 896 of them in its manifest, and created `settings.json`.

  - `~/.claude` and `settings.json` stayed, untouched. The new manifest has vendor `antigravity` and no `.claude` entry, and `status` reports `drift none`.
- The usage rows prove that `--vendor agy` exits 2 with `flag provided but not defined: -vendor` on install, status, uninstall, dream, memory show, metrics ingest and update (checkout, dry run, zip). No checkout moved.

Every file above. The map's node labels changed text only: no line or node was added, removed or rerouted (rule 3), and `TestHarnessMap` passes. The ADR is ADR-062.

# fyr Phase 3a: agents native, the lint, the context and rules     (date: 2026-10-24)

## Summary
Agents are authored as `agents/<name>/agent.md` in Antigravity's format and installed as written; `derive.go` is gone (ADR-062, plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md` Phase 3a, D3, D17, F6). Each of the eight files is `DeriveAgy`'s output at the phase's base commit `a2e6a5a`, generated into `.agents/scratch/fyr/derived/` before the derivation was deleted and compared with `cmp`. The lint keeps both allow-lists: `agentKeys` is now the derived keys (`name`, `description`, `subagent`, `mainAgent`, `model`, `tools`), so an old-format key such as `maxTurns` or `effort` is refused; `knownTools` is the six names the old `toolMap` produced; a harness agent sets `subagent: true` and `mainAgent: false`; a flat `agents/<name>.md`, an agent directory with no `agent.md`, and a symlinked `agent.md` are refused with the file named. The inventory prints an agent's `model` key as written, and nothing when it is absent. The global context and the two rules name one CLI: the `/goal` and `claude -p` clause, the `.claude/*` links, the `CLAUDE.md` stub and both `TaskStop` mentions are gone, and "a budget below the agent's `maxTurns`" is now "a tool-call budget" (D17). `# Compact instructions` is kept as prose. BUG-173: the committed `agy-rel` kit still passed `--vendor agy`, a usage error since Phase 2, and is fixed.

## Type
task (plan phase)

## Files changed
From `git diff HEAD -M --numstat` over the working tree:
- Agents: `agents/<name>.md` → `agents/<name>/agent.md` for all eight, each the derived file byte for byte. Git sees them as renames (−3/+4 lines each: the format keys).
- Deleted: `internal/harness/derive.go`; `yamlQuote` in `frontmatter.go` (its only caller was `DeriveAgy`).
- `internal/harness/inventory.go`: `LoadAgents` reads `agents/<name>/agent.md` through `readRegular` (a symlinked `agent.md` is refused). New: `agentKeys`, `knownTools`, the subagent and mainAgent check, and the refusals of a flat file and a missing `agent.md`. `RenderInventory` and `RenderInventoryCompact` print the model as written.
- `internal/harness/plan.go`: an agent is copied from `a.Raw`.
- Tests: `agents_test.go` is new. `harness_test.go`, `pathguard_test.go`, `source_test.go` and `zip_test.go` moved to native fixtures. `TestDeriveAgy`, `TestDeriveAgyRealReviewer` and `TestYamlQuoteEscapesControlCharacters` are deleted.
- `context/AGENTS.md`: lines 3, 15, 31, 35, 39 and 64.
- Docs: `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `specs/sh-agent/delivery.md` (§ Antigravity derivation becomes § Agents), `specs/sh-agent/memory-loop.md`, `testing/guide.md`.
- Fixture: `internal/search/testdata/recall.tsv` gold paths.
- Kit: `testing/agy-rel/run.sh` (BUG-173).
- Trail: BUG-173, BUG-174 and the INDEX rows; `testing/2026-10-24-verify-fyr-agents.md`; the plan's ticks.

## Deviations from the plan's box
- **Byte-equality is a one-time `cmp`, not a standing test.** The derived files live in gitignored scratch, so a test that read them would fail on every other checkout. `TestCheckoutAgentsAreNative` and the lint pin the shape that stays: the keys, `subagent`/`mainAgent`, the known tools, and the reviewer's skill path.
- **No standing check of an agent body's skill path.** The derivation rewrote `~/.claude/skills/` in bodies. Nothing is rewritten now, and a lint for that string would name the old CLI in the code. The reviewer's Antigravity path is pinned by `TestCheckoutAgentsAreNative`, and every other agent names no skill path.
- **Lint wording.** The lint and its tests name "the format before ADR-062", never the old CLI, so Phase 2's checkpoint grep lists only its expected hits plus D24's exemptions. That box is ticked.

- **`recall.tsv` was edited before Phase 4a.** `TestRecallQuestionsAreWellFormed` stats every gold path, and the moved agents and the deleted `derive.go` broke it. Row 39 waits for Phase 4a.
- **The behavioural log's status is FAIL.** Every row is stated as n of N, and the cause is BUG-174, which predates this phase (base-tree control 0/2). Its fix is the operator's call.

None. The main agent read the diff itself (about 200 lines in 27 files). The plan's Phase 5 holds the `reviewer --code --docs` and `security` dispatches over the whole feature, as Phase 2 did.

Every file above. No path on the README map changed (rule 3).

# fyr Phase 4a: the rename in the tree, mechanical     (date: 2026-10-25)

## Summary
The tree is `fyr` (plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md` Phase 4a, D12, D15, D22):
- module `github.com/kesokaj/fyr`, root package `fyr`, the binary at `cmd/fyr`;
- every path into the state directory reads `harness.StateDir` (`.config/fyr`);
- search honours `.fyr-noindex` and still honours the old `.sh-agent-noindex`;
- `fyr` reads `FYR_*` only, and names each set `SH_AGENT_*` variable once on stderr.

The living text says `fyr`. A scratch-home install from this tree is `fyr`: `~/.local/bin/fyr`, `~/.config/fyr/state.json`, `drift none` (§ 3 and § 3a). No migration exists yet. That is Phase 4b's, along with the release names, the dream unit names and `deploy/remote.md`.

## Type
task (plan phase)

## Files changed
From `git show --stat c565b27` (117 files, +1147 −918; Go: 70 files, +758 −531):
- **Moves (`git mv`):**

## Left for Phase 4b, and kept as history
The Phase 4a grep (`git grep -n 'sh-agent'` over the living files) lists these, each kept on purpose:
- **The old marker** and its test: `reconcile.go`, `search_test.go` (`TestOldNoIndexMarkerStillCounts`), `specs/fyr/search.md` (D12).
- **The env notice:** `main.go`, `usage_test.go`, `harness_test.go`, in upper case (`SH_AGENT_`), so the lower-case grep does not list them (D15).

# fyr Phase 4b: migration, timers, release, the crossing guide     (date: 2026-10-25)

## Summary
A home on v2.7.0 now crosses to `fyr` with one `fyr install` (plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md` Phase 4b, D13, D14, D29, D30):
- **The state directory moves first.** Every verb that writes under it renames `~/.config/sh-agent` to `~/.config/fyr` before anything opens it, and says `migrated ~/.config/sh-agent → ~/.config/fyr`.
  - Both present: neither is touched, and one line says fyr reads the new one (F3).
  - A symlinked old dir: the writing verb is refused (D30).
  - Read-only verbs and modes never migrate. They name the old dir once on stderr and read nothing from it.
- **The resync removes the old files.** It reads the old manifest from the moved dir and removes the `~/.claude` files and `~/.local/bin/sh-agent` by today's rule. A symlinked entry stays (F2).
- **The dream timer is renamed** `fyr-dream` / `com.fyr.dream`. `install` replaces this home's unit under the old name, installing the new unit first and removing the old one after.
- **The release names are fyr's.** Asset `fyr-<os>-<arch>`, `ReleaseRepo = "github.com/kesokaj/fyr"`, and one sums marker, `# fyr vX.Y.Z`. The old `# styrman-harness` marker is refused.
- **`deploy/remote.md` has § Crossing to fyr**, and its release step names `fyr-*`, `fyr-vX.Y.Z.zip` and the one marker.
- **The kit preamble watches both real state dirs** until every place has crossed.
- **BUG-176 and BUG-177 are recorded**, and BUG-176's line is fixed.

## Type
task (plan phase)

## Files changed
- **Go, new:**
  - `internal/harness/migrate.go`: `OldStateDir`, `MigrateStateDir`, `StateDirNotice`.
  - `internal/harness/migrate_test.go`: the four cases, plus the notice.
  - `cmd/fyr/migrate_test.go`: 11 writing and 16 read-only invocations, plus the symlink refusal stopping `install` before any write.
  - `cmd/fyr/crossing_test.go`: `TestCrossingFromV270`, which builds v2.7.0 from `git archive v2.7.0` and installs it with a dream unit, then runs one `fyr install` (D14). It skips without the tag, `go`, `git` or `tar`, and under `-short`.
- **Go, changed:**
  - `cmd/fyr/main.go`: `writesState` and `migrateStateDir` run before the source is resolved and on the `--from-zip` branch, after its refusals. `installFiles` calls `dream.ReplaceOldTimer` after the install. `stderr` is a test seam.
  - `internal/dream/timer.go`:
    - the new names, with `oldUnitName`/`oldPlistName`;
    - `namesFor` behind `UnitFor` and `oldUnitFor`;
    - `timerUnit` (`unitOn`, `present`, `remove`), shared by `RemoveTimer` and the new `ReplaceOldTimer`;
    - `LegacyTimerFiles` and its notice now name the old bare names.
  - `internal/harness/release.go`: the asset name, `ReleaseRepo` and the marker.
  - `statedir_test.go`: exempts the `OldStateDir` constant's line.
- **Tests renamed or extended:**
  - `timer_test.go` (new names; `TestReplaceOldTimer`, seven cases);
  - `release_test.go` (`fyr-*`, `# fyr`, the old-marker refusal, `TestReleaseNames`);
  - `zip_test.go`, `cmd/fyr/zip_test.go` (release zips `fyr-vX.Y.Z.zip`);
  - `catalog_test.go` (the guard cases for `~/.config/sh-agent`).
- **Content:**
  - `skills/bug/SKILL.md:55` (BUG-176);
  - `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:31` ("an installed command that changes its name" is a MAJOR).
- **Docs:**
  - `deploy/remote.md` (§ Crossing to fyr; every living command, asset, marker and `--repo`; the timer example `fyr-update.service`; v3.0.0 as a MAJOR);
  - `specs/fyr/delivery.md` § The model (the crossing claim, two sentences);
  - `README.md` § Install without cloning and § Install from a zip;
  - `deploy/local.md:69`, `specs/fyr/dream.md:49` (the timer names and the replacement);
  - `testing/kit-preamble.sh`, `testing/guide.md` § 4 (the guard).
- **Trail:**
  - `bugs/BUG-176-*.md`, `bugs/BUG-177-*.md` and their `INDEX.md` rows;
  - the plan (D30, Phase 4b ticked);
  - `testing/2026-10-25-verify-fyr-crossing-local.md`.

## Agents dispatched
- **`documentation`**: `remote.md`, `delivery.md`, README and the two timer docs.
  - The main agent read its diff and changed two things in `remote.md` § Crossing to fyr. The opening restated part of the delivery claim, so it now points at it in one sentence (project `AGENTS.md` rule 6).
  - The checkout place's `go run ./cmd/fyr install` gained `--repo "$PWD"`. Without it, the dev box's home, last installed by the v2.7.0 release binary, is refused by `knownCheckout`.
- **No review dispatches**, as in Phases 2 to 4a: Phase 5 holds `verifier`, `reviewer --code --docs` and `security` over the whole feature. The main agent read its own diff.

`testing/2026-10-25-verify-fyr-crossing-local.md`: PASS. In short:
- **Red first.** The new tests failed to compile, and with the migration test set aside, seven release and zip tests failed on behaviour.
- **Mutations.** Dropping `dream` from the writing verbs fails `TestStateDirMigrationByVerb`. Skipping `ReplaceOldTimer` fails `TestCrossingFromV270`. The preamble at HEAD fails the three new guard cases.
- **Full suite** under `-race`: exit 0.
- **The checkpoint crossing.** A scratch home was installed by a release-built v2.7.0 with a dream unit, behind a recording fake `systemctl`, then migrated by one `go run ./cmd/fyr install`. Result: 897 old files removed, the timer replaced, `fyr status` clean with `drift none`.

Recorded as plan D30 (by: implementer, open to the operator's veto):

- **`LegacyTimerFiles` looks for the old bare names only.**
- **The bug-skill line says "names a tool-call budget"**, not the box's "a tool-call budget the dispatch names", which would repeat its subject.
- **The global preflight skill names the rule, not the tag.** `v3.0.0` is named in `deploy/remote.md` § Releases. Step 6's bridge check had no `sh-agent` wording to drop.

## Not built, named for Phase 5
- **`uninstall` and `dream --remove-timer` leave an old-named unit.** Before a crossing install it is named nowhere.
- **F4:** `status` does not name a leftover `sh-agent` on PATH. § Crossing to fyr checks it with `ls`.
- **No Antigravity behavioural run** of the changed skills (`bug`, `preflight`). Phase 5 and preflight's rule owe it.

# fyr Phase 5b: the old `~/.claude` files stay     (date: 2026-10-25)

## Summary
Plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md` Phase 5b, D32. The operator said, in their own turn: "dont remove the claude skills and context on this machine. That should still be left on dave. But in the project we will only focus on antigravity going forward." Asked how, they chose "fyr never removes them". So:
- **The crossing keeps Claude Code's files.** Every `~/.claude` entry of a pre-fyr manifest that is still on disk stays as it is: the context, the `CLAUDE.md` stub, skills, agents, commands and rules.
  - The entries leave fyr's manifest, and install says so in one line: `keep    ~/.claude: <n> files an install before fyr wrote for Claude Code; fyr never removes them, and they leave its manifest`.
  - `~/.local/bin/sh-agent` still goes by the resync.
- **Uninstall keeps them too**, even when it runs straight after the migration, over the old manifest.
- **A failed install keeps them out of the manifest** it saves (the IN2 union skips them).
- **An unclean manifest entry is judged as the path it removes:** cleaned, with the first element compared without case.
- The project itself stays Antigravity-only. No Claude Code support returns; the files are frozen at v2.7.0's text.

## Type
task (plan phase; amends D2's stated consequence and D14's sweep)

- `internal/harness/apply.go`:

`reviewer` (`--code --docs`, working tree), `security` (working tree), `verifier` (last).

# Metrics Phase 1: one reference per trail item     (date: 2026-10-25)

## Summary
Phase 1 of `PLAN-2026-10-25-1754-plan-metrics-fed-at-every-checkpoint-joined-to-r`. A `handoff`, `verifier` or `review` event's `ref` is now the trail item's record ID. For a file, that is the ID `fyr record import` gives it: `brain.ImportedID(kind, stem)`, the kind's prefix, a dash, `slugOf(stem)`; the import's classify now calls the same function. Every ingest first rewrites, inside the join's transaction, the file-name refs an older ingest stored (`*.md`) to that ID form, and deletes a row whose ID form the session already holds. A ref already in ID form is left alone, even one ending in `.md`. No schema change (D10). Phase 2 (the join reads records) builds on this.

## Type
task

## Files changed
from git diff --numstat
- internal/brain/import.go — `ImportedID`, used by classify
- internal/brain/import_test.go — `TestImportedID`: five stems (space, `+`, upper case, trailing `.`), each against both the literal ID and the ID a dry-run import gives the file
- internal/metrics/events.go — `fileRef`, `rewriteFileRefs`; the file join writes ID-form refs; metrics now imports `internal/brain`
- internal/metrics/events_test.go — `TestJoinEvents` wants ID-form refs; `TestJoinFilesRefs`, `TestRefRewrite` new
- .agents/trail.jsonl — SPEC-fyr-metrics: the `events` payload table and a "One reference per trail item" invariant with its two known limits

## Agents dispatched
none. The plan puts reviewer, security and verifier at Done, over the whole feature. I read this phase's diff myself.

## Verification
- Unit: `go test -race -run TestImportedID ./internal/brain/`, `go test -race -run 'TestJoinEvents|TestRefRewrite|TestJoinFilesRefs' ./internal/metrics/` pass. Mutations each caught, then restored: `ImportedID` without the slug (TestImportedID), no rewrite call (TestRefRewrite), basename refs (TestJoinFilesRefs, TestRefRewrite), no duplicate delete (TestRefRewrite).
- Full suite: `gofmt -l cmd internal && go vet ./... && go test -race -timeout 30m ./...` exit 0, every package ok (2026-10-25). govulncheck not re-run: no module was added (metrics now imports internal/brain, already in the module graph).
- E2E criterion 2 on copies (`.agents/scratch/e2e2-home`, this box's `metrics.db` and `brain.db`, read through a read-only query tool in scratch whose slug rule is a separate copy): before, 276 trail events with a `.md` ref and 0 items held twice. After one ingest by the new binary (exit 0, 6 events added): 0 `.md` refs, 0 held twice, trail events 276 → 278 (none lost). A second ingest: 0 events added, same counts. Must-fail check: on another copy with one ID-form duplicate injected, the check reported 1; after one ingest it reported 0. So the duplicate delete also ran on real data.

## Deviations
- Reading my own diff, I found that a ref already in ID form and ending in `.md` (`HANDOFF-notes.md`, from a file `notes.md.md`) would be rewritten again on the next ingest (`HANDOFF-handoff-notes`), which broke idempotence. I wrote the failing case into `TestRefRewrite`, then made the fix (skip ID-form refs; `GLOB` instead of the case-insensitive `LIKE`) before the commit. Accepted limit, in the spec: an old file whose name is itself ID-shaped (`HANDOFF-x.md`) keeps its file-name ref.
- The plan's interface comment on `ImportedID` mentions a `-N` collision suffix. The import itself refuses two files that slug alike (classify); the `-N` is what `slugOf` leaves room for. The doc comment says it is not reproduced, as the plan does.

## Requirements
R4 (no schema change; the store's rows rewritten in place, none rebuilt), R6 (every test and run on a scratch home).

# Metrics Phase 2: the join reads records     (date: 2026-10-25)

## Summary
Phase 2 of `PLAN-2026-10-25-1754-plan-metrics-fed-at-every-checkpoint-joined-to-r`. A migrated project's handoff, verifier, review and bug events now come from its records, not its files (D4). task

# Metrics feature Done: review, security, verification     (date: 2026-10-25)

## Summary
The Done section of `PLAN-2026-10-25-1754-plan-metrics-fed-at-every-checkpoint-joined-to-r` (roadmap item 2). It covers the whole feature, 811442c..33c652a: Phase 1 (68870aa), Phase 2 (000233f), Phase 3 (a225df7) and Phase 4 (33c652a), with their handoff commits. A reviewer (code and docs lenses) and a security review each read that range, one fix landed, and the verifier ran after it. The fix: the metrics store now opens every transaction `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. The join's transaction begins with reads (the two ref rewrites from Phases 1 and 2). As a deferred transaction, a concurrent ingest's commit would make its first write fail at once with SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT, without waiting out the busy timeout. Ingests at every handoff and `/retro` make that concurrency routine. The plan is closed and leaves ROADMAP Now.

## Type
task

## Files changed
from git diff --numstat (this change only; the feature's own files are in the four phase change records)

- `TestTxTakesWriteLockAtBegin` FAILED before the fix ("a second connection wrote while the store's transaction was open") and passes after it. `go test -race ./internal/metrics/ ./internal/dream/` exit 0 after the fix.

Every `Log` caller gets it. `--no-ext-diff`, added in round 1, was removed after round 2: `git log` runs an external diff only with `--ext-diff` (checked on git 2.47.3). Tests: `TestLogRunsNoTextconv`, `TestSpecRuleRunsNoTextconv`.
- **Rule (b)** (`internal/check/specs.go`): the `-G` pattern quotes the ID and the stamp with `regexp.QuoteMeta`, because `-G` compiles an extended regex, so a `+02:00` stamp is literal (`breQuote` removed; both reviews). A failed `git log` or `git rev-list` for a spec is now a `note: <ID>: git … failed: spec not checked`, not a silent pass. Tests: `TestSpecRuleOffsetStamp`, `TestSpecRuleGitFailureIsANote`.

- **Scanner** (`internal/check/scan.go`): `spans` indexes a line's backtick runs once, so the scan is linear. Its output matched the old scanner on 200,000 random lines. Test: `TestSpansLinearOnUnclosedRuns`: 0.07 s, against 5.8 s for the old scanner.

  - after 4c07410: 1 finding, `SPEC-fyr-metrics spec-stale` (1 commit since 0e643fd to its code paths, `internal/harness` among them).
  - **Re-read and re-stamp (D8).** The spec's one `internal/harness` claim is its Verification row "`uninstall` keeps the store | `internal/harness` `-run TestUninstallKeepsMetricsStore`". It names a package and a `-run` filter, not a file; the test now lives in `links_test.go:161` and PASSes by name. No edit was due. Re-stamped with `fyr record edit SPEC-fyr-metrics --status current`; the trail diff is its `updated` field only (checked by diffing the two lines with `updated` stripped). Committed alone as 2eafdc5.
  - after 2eafdc5: 0 findings, exit 0.

## Agents dispatched

# Release v3.0.0 (2026-10-26-2218)

## Type
release

## Summary
v3.0.0, the first release named `fyr`, for the Antigravity CLI only. It is MAJOR because the installed command changes name. Gate: `REVIEW-2026-10-26-preflight-v3-0-0`, SHIP over v2.7.0..1acfc6c. The tag sits on this release commit, whose parent is 1acfc6c.

## Agents dispatched
- reviewer on opus, twice: the ten uncovered commits, then round 2 over e53a7cb.
- security, twice: the same two scopes.
- verifier, four times: d341d8f FAIL (fyr check), then d15d0a2 PASS, then at 1acfc6c both § 1/§ 3/§ 3a PASS and § 2/§ 3b–3h PASS.
- `fyr eval`: 35 rows on Antigravity, 34 + 1 PASS. The main agent ran this box's crossing and the real-home smoke.

## Gate fixes in the range
e53a7cb, 74ecdda, c92219f, d15d0a2 and 1acfc6c (the gate report lists each).

## Release notes
**fyr v3.0.0: the harness is renamed `fyr` and serves the Antigravity CLI only.** This is a MAJOR release because the installed command changes name. A place on v2.7.0 or earlier does not move forward by its own `update`: cross it by hand once, following `DEPLOY-remote` § Crossing to fyr (summary under Install below).

## New features
- fyr check, Phase 1: the verb and rule (a). `fyr check` is a read-only drift check of a checkout's docs against the binary and the tree (BUG-179).
- fyr check, Phase 2: rule (b) checks the specs, and rule (c) the requirements.
- fyr eval, Phase 1: `internal/eval`, with the suite, the sandbox, safety checks a–f, the runner, and `GUIDE-eval`.
- fyr eval, Phase 2: the verb, plus ADR-065, R8 and the map. Behavioural rows run against the real Antigravity CLI, each in its own sandbox, and every run leaves a `testing` record and labelled metrics.
- Brain Phases 3 to 5: the harness speaks records, and the dream reads and writes them. `fyr record` and the brain store at `~/.config/fyr/brain.db` hold every project's trail as records, exported to `.agents/trail.jsonl` (BUG-178).
- Brain Phase 1 checkpoint and Phase 2: the import (`fyr record import`) and the memory alias.
- Session-sized work, Phase 1: the session-sizing rule and the handoff Kickoff.
- The peak-context metric: sessions over the context target.

## Improvements and optimisation
- fyr Phase 1: the report path leaves, and the redactor moves to `internal/redact`.
- fyr Phase 2: Claude Code leaves the binary.
- fyr Phase 3a: agents are authored natively in Antigravity's `agent.md`; the lint, the context and the rules follow (BUG-173).
- fyr Phase 4a: the rename in the tree (module, `cmd/fyr`, `~/.config/fyr`, `.fyr-noindex`, `FYR_*`).
- fyr Phase 4b: the state-dir migration, the dream timer renamed `fyr-dream`, and the release assets named `fyr-*`.
- fyr Phase 5b: the old `~/.claude` files stay where they are at the crossing, and leave fyr's manifest.
- Metrics Phases 1 to 4: one reference per trail item, the join reads records, first reads see record verbs, and metrics are fed at every checkpoint.
- fyr check Phase 3: the consumers and the guides use it, and this repository is clean under it.
- fyr eval Phase 3: the consumers point at `fyr eval`, and the run kit is deleted.
- Modularity Phases 1 to 7e: the large source and test files are split by whole-declaration moves, under the code-modularity rule (ADR-066).
- The v3.0.0 gate's fixes: the memory import skips a file the store refuses; a future-dated record is no dream news; eval's credential scan counts a directory link that leads out of the sandbox; a relative worktree `gitdir` resolves.

## Fixes
- BUG-175 fixed: project-memory's date line uses no command substitution.
- fyr Phase 3b: the skills, kits and content name one CLI (BUG-174).
- Audit fix closed: `memory.Root` refuses an unregistered linked worktree, along with the audit's other fixes.

## Other updates
- Rules: `code-modularity.md`, the third always-on rule (ADR-066), and `session-sizing.md`.
- The `sh-agent kickoff` verb was removed (ADR-058a). The `report` verb and the `styrman-harness-feedback` path are gone (ADR-062).
- Requirements were rewritten for one CLI (ADR-062), and the repository was renamed `kesokaj/fyr`.
- Specs and guides are records: `SPEC-fyr-*`, `GUIDE-*`, `DEPLOY-*`.

## Install
- **New place:** see README § Install without cloning (`ASSET=fyr-<os>-<arch>`, `V=v3.0.0`, marker `# fyr v3.0.0`, `--repo github.com/kesokaj/fyr`).
- **A place on v2.7.0 or earlier:** follow `DEPLOY-remote` § Crossing to fyr, v3.0.0 only.
  1. First disable any unit or profile line of your own that names `sh-agent`, such as `sh-agent-update.timer`.
  2. Do not run `sh-agent uninstall`.
  3. Then, by kind of place:
     - **Release binary:** download `fyr-<os>-<arch>`, check it against `SHA256SUMS`, move it to `~/.local/bin/fyr`, then `hash -r && fyr install`.
     - **Checkout:** `git remote set-url origin git@github.com:kesokaj/fyr.git && git pull --ff-only && go run ./cmd/fyr install --repo "$PWD"`.
     - **Zip place:** download the `fyr-<os>-<arch>` binary by hand, then `./fyr update --from-zip fyr-v3.0.0.zip`.
  4. `fyr install` moves `~/.config/sh-agent` to `~/.config/fyr`, removes `~/.local/bin/sh-agent`, and replaces the dream timer.
- **Existing fyr places, after this release:** `fyr update`.

After review, three more tests were added in the checkpoint commit, each one killed by its mutation (3 of 3): `TestImportFailsClosedWhenTheDirtyCheckFails`, `TestReadMemoryStoreFailsClosedOnACorruptIndex` and `TestOwnHitsQueryError`.

`PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-choices` cited `internal/brain/import_global.go:152` (the `ListProjects` call). The citation was repointed to `:192` (`readMemories`) by procedure step 7.

## Evidence

- **Mutations:** 49, one per uncovered block the tests target. Each was applied to the code at 91e9d01 and its test run, and every one was killed. The list and the runner are in `.agents/scratch/funclen-p2/` (`mutations.tsv`, `run-mutations.sh`, output `mutations-before.txt`). Two kills were spot-checked to be assertion failures, not build failures. `git diff` was empty after the run.

The three files were rebuilt from their scratch sources, and `git diff 91e9d01` of each was byte-identical to the diff the reviewer read (`cmp`). ## Evidence

The check was validated in the must-fail state: a mutant row-name pad in `textWriter.row` and a mutant end-label gap in `placeEndLabels` each changed the output. A third mutant, `textWriter`'s minimum width 14 to 15, did not: a column label is wider than 15, so that mutant is equivalent.

Two open plans cited `internal/metrics/events.go:118-121` and `:118-130`, the records read and the corrections loop, now in `joinRoot`: `PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-choices` now cites `internal/metrics/events_join.go:56-58`, and `PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-cleanup` `internal/metrics/events_join.go:56-68`. `PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-choices`' `internal/metrics/agy.go:76-90` is above the split and unchanged. owner: main

# Change — funclen Phase 4: internal/search (PLAN-2026-10-27-funclen)

## What changed

The 9 `internal/search` functions over 50 lines were split by extract-function, inside the package. Every function in the package is now at most 50 lines. The 9 `longFuncs` rows are gone from `funclen_test.go`, leaving 25.

| Function | Was | Split into |
|---|---|---|
| `gitView` (git_view.go) | 165 | `trackedView` (the `ls-files -s` parse), `dropGoneMarkers`, `refreshTracked` (the stat fast path and the hash), `addUntracked`, `markedDirs`, `keptEntries` (the `noIndex` closure stays in it), `leftOutDirs`. The `os.Root`, its defer and both git calls stay in `gitView` |
| `refs` (search_refs.go) | 137 | `refsWhere`, `recordLine`, `pathLine`, `refRows` (with the `refRow` type, the old local `row`), `groupRefs` (with `refGroup`, the old local `group`). `refRows` closes its rows before it returns, and `groupRefs`, which queries again through `recordAt`, carries the one-connection comment (D10) |
| `reconcileGlobal` (global.go) | 88 | `rebuildGlobal`, `registrations` (with `registration`, the old local `reg`), `reconcileRegistered` (drop, skip, `gitView` and `apply` for one checkout). The two `.agents/docs` literals became one unexported const, `globalDocsRoot` |
| `prepare` (scope_prepare.go) | 69 | `scope.prepareProject` (the checkout's own index and its registration), with each close on an error path as before |
| `applyLocked` (reconcile.go) | 67 | `indexBlobs`, which now opens and defers the `os.Root` and the inserter it uses, and `writeFiles`. The two closes run when `indexBlobs` returns, not at the end of `applyLocked`: nothing after uses them, and the inserter's `close` only closes prepared statements |
| `AgyConversationText` (dream.go) | 60 | `listConversations` (the copied list's open, query and scan). The one deferred cleanup, and its comment, stay in `AgyConversationText` (D10) |
| `find` (search_query.go) | 59 | `chunkIDs` (with the keyed-by-chunk comment), `scope.snippets` |
| `indexStats` (git_indexstat.go) | 56 | `parseIndexStats` |
| `walk` (dream.go) | 54 | `skipScalar` (wire types 0, 1, 5 and the refusal of the rest), `lengthDelimited` (with the SD1 comment) |

- No file was over 400 lines before the phase. `dream.go` was 391, and its two splits would have pushed it past 400. So the protobuf step decoder (`maxDepth`, `proseLeaves`, `walk` and its helpers, `textField`, `prose`) moved whole to the new `dream_proto.go` (124 lines) (D7). `dream.go` is now 300.
- Every file in the package is at most 308 lines.
- No exported name, signature, SQL text, output or error text changed. The package's import set is unchanged; `dream.go` lost `encoding/binary` and `unicode/utf8` to `dream_proto.go`.

Characterization tests (D13) were committed first, in 5294170, before any split:

- `reconcile_arms_test.go`:
  - `applyLocked`'s failing blob, chunk and files writes (insert, delete, state update), made by schema triggers, not seams (D12);
  - an unopenable project directory;
  - an inserter that cannot prepare: a records table with only `oid`, so `gc` still runs;
  - `gitView`'s unmerged path (three stages, with "theirs" in the work tree);
  - an unreadable tracked file and an unreadable untracked file (mode 000; skipped as root);
  - the index-stat fast path, with a pinned mtime. The suite had reached it only by timing: it was covered in one run and not in the next.
- `global_arms_test.go`:
  - `reconcileGlobal`'s `--rebuild` over a non-empty directory;
  - the projects table dropped, or a row with a NULL docs root;
  - a gone registration whose drop a trigger refuses;
  - a registered checkout with a corrupt `.git/index`;
  - a registered checkout whose rows a trigger refuses;
  - `prepare`'s `index --rebuild` of the checkout's own index, and over a non-empty directory;
  - a partial clone on an old git (the existing `lazyFetchSafe` variable);
  - a global index that cannot be opened at registration.
- `refs_arms_test.go`:
  - `refs`' docs-relative directory match;
  - the records table dropped;
  - a record, a file state and a reference that do not scan (NULLs);
  - a LIKE pattern over SQLite's 50,000-byte limit, both in the same-name hint and in the references query;
  - `find`'s snippet read of a chunk whose body is NULL.
- `dream_arms_test.go`:
  - `AgyConversationText`'s list that is not a regular file, has no table, or has a NULL id, each checked to leave no state directory behind;
  - `walk`'s short varint, short 64-bit and short 32-bit fields, and a whole 32-bit field before prose.

After review, tests were added in the checkpoint commit, each killed by its mutation (3 of 3):

- `TestWalkFixedAndVarintFields` gains "64-bit then prose".
- `TestApplyLockedWriteErrors` gains the last-seen update and the touched mark.

## Evidence

- **Mutations before the split:** 37, at least one per targeted block, applied to the code at 5294170. All 37 were killed, one of them only after its test was tightened. The mutant that skipped the inserter's error first survived: `gc` then failed on the same dropped table with the same message. The test now keeps `oid` in the table so that only the inserter can fail, and the mutant is killed. The list, the runner and its output are in `.agents/scratch/funclen-p4/` (`mutations.txt`, `run-mutations.sh`, `mutations-before.txt`). The runner restores each file from a backup copy, and `git diff` was empty after the run.
- **Mutations after the split:** the same 37, adapted to the moved code (`mutations-after.txt` and `mutations-after2.txt`, five of them rewritten by hand where the text had moved), all killed. Two adapted mutants first survived: `return msg, true` in `skipScalar` is equivalent, because `walk` parses the same bytes again and refuses them. The real counterpart, `return nil, true`, which makes `walk` accept the message, is killed.
- **`walk`, old against new:** a temporary differential test (not committed) ran the 5294170 `walk` and the new one on 300,000 inputs, random bytes and generated wire messages. Results and leaves were equal on all of them, and 1,351 of the inputs yielded prose. The test failed under a mutant in `skipScalar` (32-bit step) and one in `lengthDelimited` (text guard).
- **Byte-for-byte CLI output:** `fyr` built at 5294170 and from the split tree ran the same 15 commands, each in its own clone of this repository with its own scratch home:
  - `search` (words and `--kind`), five `--refs` forms (an ID, a directory, a docs directory, a path, a bare name), `--open`, `--global` words and `--refs`;
  - `index`, `index --rebuild` and `index --global --rebuild`.

  Their output, with paths and timings masked, was identical: 426 lines. The comparison was validated in the must-fail state: a binary with a mutant `pathLine` format differed on the two lines that print it.
- **Coverage of `internal/search`** (`go test -coverprofile`, package-only): 83.6% before; 88.5% with the tests, before the splits; 89.0% after the splits; 89.2% on the final tree, with the review-fix tests.
- **Re-count after:** the lister prints nothing for the package's non-test files, tracked or not.
- **`TestFunctionLength`** passed after every split.
- **Step 7:** no tracked file cites a moved line. These were repointed:
  - `PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-choices`:
    - `scope_prepare.go:91-99` is now `:118-126`;
    - `register` `:122` is now `:132`;
    - the "registrations dropped" comment, `global.go:27`, is now `:80`, in `rebuildGlobal`; this citation appeared twice;
    - `dream.go:49` (`ListProjects`) is now `:47`, after two import lines left the file.
  - `PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-cleanup`: SD-S3's walker, `dream.go:230-305`, is now `dream_proto.go:23-98`.
  - `GUIDE-testing`: the corpus measurement's trigger was "a change to `internal/search/dream.go`". It now also names `dream_proto.go`, the decoder.

  `SPEC-fyr-dream` names `internal/search/dream.go` for the conversation read, which stays there.
- **Checks:**
  - `gofmt -l cmd internal *.go`: no output, exit 0.
  - `go vet ./...`: exit 0.
  - `go test -race -timeout 30m ./...`: exit 0, 12 packages ok. It ran on the split tree, and again on the final tree after the review-fix tests. On the final tree, `internal/search`, `cmd/fyr`, `internal/harness` and the root package ran again; the other eight packages had not changed since the first run and were served from Go's test cache.

## Exempt arms (D12)

- **`refRows`' `rows.Err()` arm** (search_refs.go; was `refs`, search_refs.go:105). The reviewer refuted the first reason given for this, and the corrected one is:
  - The plan is a partial sort (`USE TEMP B-TREE FOR LAST TERM OF ORDER BY`), so rows stream one file at a time.
  - A data-dependent error, the LIKE limit among them, still surfaces at `Query`. Every refs row is evaluated in the first file's inner scan, before the sorter emits anything.
  - A probe test checked this. Its first file's only reference matched the exact target, and a later file's reference forced the over-long LIKE. The error came from `Query`, with 0 coverage in the loop.
  - A mid-stream error needs an I/O failure or a corrupted page.

Blocks still uncovered that did not move stay in their function and are not owed a test: `AgyConversationText`'s `MkdirAll`, `MkdirTemp` and per-conversation text errors; `walk`'s depth limit and bad key; `indexStats`' two git errors; `gitView`'s `OpenRoot` and second `ls-files` errors; `reconcileGlobal`'s `configView` and config `apply` errors; `applyLocked`'s `current` and `gc` errors; `prepare`'s file-count error; `find`'s query, scan and `rows.Err` errors.

## Agents

- `reviewer`: `REVIEW-2026-10-27-1323-review-funclen-p4-internal-search-2026-10-27`, APPROVE WITH NITS. It verified every split line by line against 1a228b5 and ran its own 37 mutations.
  - Finding 1, the exemption's reason, was right; the reason is corrected above, and the arm stays exempt.
  - Findings 2 and 3 were fixed with tests. No source changed after the reviewer read the diff.
  - Its info points: the early close (`applyLocked` row above), and the redundant `delete` in `keptEntries`, which predates the range and stays.
  - Its `## Outcome` is written.
  - There was no second round: the fixes are tests only, and the main thread read their diff.
- No `security`: none of Phase 4's functions is in D19's table.
- No `verifier`: it runs once, at Done (D11).

## Not covered

- Coverage is per package. `cmd/fyr`'s tests reaching `internal/search` are not counted.
- **The Antigravity reader's corpus measurement (`TestAgyCorpusLeaves`) was not run.** `GUIDE-testing` asks for it after a change to the reader, and `walk` changed. It needs copies of real Antigravity conversation databases from outside this repository, which the Kickoff excluded. The evidence in its place is the differential test (300,000 inputs) and `TestProseLeaves`; neither is the box's real corpus.
- The CLI comparison covers the 15 commands it ran on this repository, not every input.
- Nothing was run on macOS.
- **A flake, found at the phase's start and not fixed.** `TestConcurrentReconcile` (open_test.go) failed once in 1 + 8 serial runs of the unchanged package, and once in 4 parallel runs. It passed 60 of 60 runs alone. A helper process gets `search: index busy` after 0.01 s, well inside the 10 s busy timeout, so SQLite's busy handler is not being waited on. That is consistent with an immediate SQLITE_BUSY that does not invoke the busy handler (for example, during WAL setup); the cause is not verified. It predates this phase and is left to the operator.

owner: main

# Change — funclen Phase 5: internal/harness (PLAN-2026-10-27-funclen)

## What changed

The 8 `internal/harness` functions over 50 lines were split by extract-function, inside the package. Every function in the package is now at most 50 lines. The 8 `longFuncs` rows are gone from `funclen_test.go`, leaving 17.

| Function | Was | Split into |
|---|---|---|
| `Install` (apply.go) | 170 | the new `apply_steps.go`: `installRun`, a run-state struct (home, dry run, output, the old manifest, the manifest so far, the counts) whose methods are `saveOnError` (the closure of the same name, with its IN2 comment), `writeFile` (one planned file: the link check, then unchanged or written), `correctMode` (an unchanged file's mode, with its comment), `write` (`add`/`update` line, the write or the dry run's `dirInTheWay`), `resync` (stale removal) and `record` (the commit annotation and `SaveState`). `Install` keeps `LoadState`, `tightenConfigDir` and the summary line |

The NO-defer comment stays in `Adopt`, after `stageAdopt` returns: `Adopt` holds `staging` across `swapIn`, whose failure paths are the ones the comment means (D10) |
| `Plan` (plan.go) | 89 | `skillFiles` (the walk of one skill, with the link and secret refusals) and `skillFile` (one file's read and mode mask) |

| `UnpackZip` (zip.go) | 75 | `planZip` (parse, entry count, names, root, `checkZipTrees`) and `writeZipPlan` (the write loop and the harness-tree check). Hash, then `check`, then parse, as ADR-039 requires; the named-`err` cleanup defer stays in `UnpackZip`, which owns `tmp` (D10) |
| `loadAgents` (inventory.go) | 73 | the new `inventory_load.go`: `readAgent` (read, frontmatter, name) and `checkAgent` (the lint after the name: description, one line, allowed keys, the two banned phrases, subagent, tools) |

The package's import set is unchanged; `apply.go` lost `sort` and `time` to `apply_steps.go`, and `inventory.go` lost `slices` to `inventory_load.go`. `WriteAtomic` stays in `apply.go` (`TestWriteAtomicClosesBeforeRename` reads it there by name).

Characterization tests (D13) were committed first, in d2078f4, before any split:

## Evidence

- **Mutations before the split:** 29, at least one per targeted block, applied to the code at d2078f4: 29 of 29 killed. One mutant (#20) first did not apply, because the runner turned the `\n` inside its format string into a newline; it was re-anchored and killed. Among them, a `defer os.RemoveAll(staging)` added to `Adopt`, killed by the test that checks the prepared copy survives. The list, the runner and the outputs are in `.agents/scratch/funclen-p5/` (`mutations.txt`, `run-mutations.sh`, `mutations-before.out`, `m20.txt`). The runner restores each file from a backup copy.

The output, plus every resulting tree hashed file by file (2,669 hashes) with its modes and manifest, was identical over 13,732 lines once three things were masked: the timestamps, the binary's version stamp (`+dirty` on the split build), and the zip's sha256 (Python stamps file mtimes into the archive). The comparison was validated in the must-fail state: a build with the `add` line's spacing changed in `write` differed on 7,128 lines, and one with `skillFile`'s mode mask changed differed on 5,264.
- **Coverage of `internal/harness`** (`go test -coverprofile`, package-only): 89.8% before; 92.7% after the splits, and on the final tree. Per function before: `Adopt` 76.8, `Install` 92.0, `loadSkills` 92.3, `loadAgents` 89.4, `Plan` 93.0, `UpdateFromRelease` 88.4, `ResolveSource` 100, `UnpackZip` 80.4.
- **Re-count after:** the lister prints nothing for the package's non-test files, tracked or not.
- **`TestFunctionLength`** passed after every split.
- **Step 7:** no tracked file cites a moved line (the two `repo.go:12` hits in `internal/search/query_test.go` are parser fixtures). Repointed: `PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-cleanup` IN40, whose `inventory.go:145` and `:49, 70, 101` moved up one line with the `slices` import and are now `:144` and `:48, 69, 100`. The funclen plan's own Phase 5 header keeps the as-planned locations, as Phases 2–4's do. Name citations (ADR-012 `Install`/`Plan`, ADR-033/034 `ResolveSource`, ADR-039 `UnpackZip`, AGENTS.md's `inventory.go` as the lint and `plan.go` as what goes where) stay valid under D8: each function keeps its name, and the cited behaviour stays in it or a helper it calls.

  - `go vet ./...`: exit 0.
  - `go test -race -timeout 30m ./...`: exit 0, 12 packages ok, on the split tree. It ran again on the final tree, after the review-fix test: exit 0, 12 packages ok. That run executed the root package, `cmd/fyr`, `internal/eval` and `internal/harness`; the other eight packages had not changed and were served from Go's test cache.
- **E2E criterion 5**, on the committed split, a674612:
  - `go run ./cmd/fyr install --home .agents/scratch/home`: exit 0, `1 written, 889 unchanged, 0 removed, 0 kept — 890 files managed`.
  - `fyr status` from that home's own binary: exit 0, `binary a674612058c8` with no warning, `drift none — 889 files match the repo`.

title: Change — BUG-187: first open of a new SQLite store waits (2026-10-27)
body:
owner: main

# Change — BUG-187: the first open of a new SQLite store waits (2026-10-27)

## What changed
- `internal/search/store.go`: `tryOpenWaiting` retries `tryOpen` while it fails busy, for up to the busy timeout, every 50 ms. `openStore` uses it for both of its opens. `IsBusy` exports `isBusy` for the metrics store.
- `internal/metrics/store.go`: `Open` retries `open` (one attempt, the former body) the same way, for `openWait` (10 s).
- Tests: `TestFirstOpenWaitsForALock` in `internal/search/open_test.go` and `internal/metrics/store_test.go`. Each holds `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` on a new, non-WAL file, releases it after 300 ms, and requires the open to succeed. Before the fix, both failed within 0.3 ms.

Root cause, repro and prevention rule: BUG-187. In short: SQLite's switch of a new file to WAL upgrades a read transaction and skips the busy handler, so `busy_timeout` never applied to the first open. The brain store already retried; search and metrics now do too.

## Evidence
- The original flake: `TestConcurrentReconcile`, 3 rounds × 3 parallel × 100 runs under 12 busy loops. Fixed build: 900 of 900 PASS. Unfixed: 2 failures in 900 (and 1 run in 9 for the plain package run, Phase 4).
- The verifier at 075cbbe: `TESTING` record of 2026-10-27, PASS. `gofmt` empty, `go vet` 0, `go test -race -timeout 30m ./...` all 13 packages ok (1151 pass, 6 skips none new), the two new tests, and `TestConcurrentReconcile` 20 of 20.

## Agents
- `explorer` (goldfish diagnosis): ranked the DSN's pragma order first, as the main thread did. The driver's source falsified it. Its second candidate (BUSY_SNAPSHOT) was falsified by the extended code. The cause was in neither list (BUG-187 § Diagnosis).
- `reviewer`: `REVIEW-2026-10-27-1408-review-index-busy-on-first-open-bug-fix-2026-10`, APPROVE WITH NITS. Two lows rebutted (the about-20 s worst case matches brain's and the spec's "past 10 s"; the duplicate predicate predates the fix).
- `verifier`: PASS at 075cbbe.

## Not covered
- macOS.
- The about-20 s worst case is not tested.

- **BUG-188** (security review part B, medium): `internal/trail/dirty.go` `hashesDiffer` refuses a tracked name opening with `"`, which `git hash-object --stdin-paths` C-unquotes into another path. Before the fix a modified `"a"` read clean beside an unchanged `a`, and a name `"../outside.txt"` was hashed outside the checkout. `Dirty` now says it cannot answer: `record import` refuses, and `eval` labels its source `(dirty: unknown, …)`. - **internal/check's TestMain** (security review part C, medium): `internal/check/testmain_test.go` drops `GIT_*` before the package's tests, as every other git-running test package does. With `GIT_DIR=/nonexistent` exported, `go test ./internal/check` failed before and passes after. The root package's new `TestGitTestPackagesDropGitVariables` (testmain_test.go) fails on a package whose test files name the git binary without such a TestMain. # Release v3.1.0 (2026-10-27-2117)

## Type
release

## Summary
v3.1.0, a MINOR: new behaviour (the build evals, `fyr check`'s tracked-file rule, the function-length guard) and fixes, nothing an existing place must react to. Gate: `REVIEW-2026-10-27-2117-preflight-v3-1-0-2026-10-27-resumed-final-ship-o`, SHIP over v3.0.0..835a990, after two NO-SHIP reports (`REVIEW-2026-10-27-1809-…`, `REVIEW-2026-10-27-2055-…`). The tag sits on this release commit, whose parent is 835a990. v3.0.0 was a bridge; the operator confirmed in their own turn that every place has crossed it.

## Agents dispatched
- reviewer: over the four uncovered code commits with the docs lens, round 2 over the gate fixes, BUG-189's fix, and two rounds over the gate delta (98ed6b3..48ee381); every report APPROVE or APPROVE WITH NITS.
- security: parts A–D over the code, the trail records in parts through 3cd0b48, two rounds over the gate fixes, and a last read over the records after 3cd0b48 (this run).
- verifier: v1 (FAIL, then FAIL on timing only), § 3c (FAIL BUG-189, then PASS), § 3d timings PASS, the final run at 3cd0b48 PASS.
- `fyr eval` on Antigravity: 15 of 15 changed skill and agent rows after one timeout re-run, the sandbox smoke 3 of 3.
- The main agent: the § 3e corpus measurement (K = 0) and the real-home smoke on dave, 3 of 3 (`TEST-2026-10-27-2113-…`).

## Gate fixes in the range
31de61a (BUG-188, security part C), d8c2129 (BUG-189), 75453d1 (specs re-read), 8bfd2bc (§ 3d bound, on the operator's delegation), ff4c959 (BUG-191), 48ee381 and 0594905 (the smoke row's check), 4fe0bb6 (SPEC-fyr-eval re-stamp).

## Release notes
### New features
- Sandbox app-building evals and the carried follow-ups: three `build-*` rows (a Go CLI, a Go JSON API, a Go plus TanStack Start app) built from an empty repository, the `rule-code-modularity` row, and `fyr check`'s rule that a Go file a current spec's Verification section names must be a tracked file.
- Funclen Phase 1, the length guard: `TestFunctionLength` fails on any non-test function over 50 lines; its allowlist has been empty since the funclen plan closed.

### Improvements and optimisation
- Audit fix Phase 1, trust boundaries in the binary: the dirty-tree check uses git plumbing only and never runs a repository's own clean filter; conversation files are opened non-blocking and no-follow, and a non-regular file is refused.
- Audit fix Phase 2, dream: `--install-timer`/`--remove-timer` with `--all` or `--project` is a usage error, labels are redacted like the texts, the run's clock reaches every input, and an input left out says it was dropped to fit the 256 KB cap.
- Audit fix Phase 3, brain, search, memory, metrics, redact: a query no longer writes to the project database; the metrics report renders before it creates its file; heredoc handling covers `<<-`; the redactor's needles are pinned shape by shape.
- Audit fix Phase 4, cmd/fyr, harness, eval, check: an install dry run refuses a directory at a planned file path; `adopt` compares resolved paths; the state file is read plain only; `record import --dry-run` leaves the old state directory alone; eval fingerprints the real config before a row's setup; `fyr check` notes skipped files and resolves an `enforced by:` path only when it is tracked.
- Audit fix Phase 5, the re-audit fixes and the close: docs, records and agent definitions brought in line with the code.
- Funclen Phases 2–10 and Done: every function over 50 lines split, in internal/brain, internal/metrics, internal/search, internal/harness, cmd/fyr, internal/dream, internal/eval and internal/check, plus the catalog refresh test. No behaviour change.

### Fixes
- First open of a new SQLite index or metrics store waits instead of failing busy (BUG-187).
- agy 1.4.7's file tools are counted in metrics, and eval's credential scan no longer reads an installed node_modules (BUG-184, BUG-185).
- An Antigravity conversation whose summary time is zero is no longer stored with a negative end time (BUG-181).
- A tracked name opening with a double quote can no longer fool the dirty-tree and dates checks (BUG-188).
- `fyr install`'s refusal for a directory in the way names the way out, and the real run meets the same guard instead of a bare rename error (BUG-189).
- A GUIDE-eval row lands together with its test entry (BUG-183, BUG-191).

### Other updates
- The v3.0.0 crossing finished at every place, and the old feedback repository was deleted.
- From the v3.1.0 gate's verification: GUIDE-testing § 3d's warm records-and-files search bound is now 400 ms, and GUIDE-eval has a `smoke` row, the sandbox form of the real-home context check.

### Install
Download: see README § Install without cloning. Existing places, checkout or binary-only: `fyr update`. A place on v2.7.0 or earlier: `DEPLOY-remote` § Crossing to fyr (v3.0.0) first.

After updating, on each machine: `hash -r` (or `rehash` in zsh), `fyr version` (expect v3.1.0), `fyr status` (no drift, no `shadowed` line), then the three smoke checks of `TEST-2026-09-03-verify-real-home` on Antigravity. On a Mac, also run `fyr dream --all` once and check `~/.config/fyr/dream.log` for "not logged in" (BUG-166): v3.1.0 was gated without a macOS dream run.

## Not checked
A real `fyr dream --all` on macOS, lifted by the operator for this release; every Mac place runs it after updating, as the notes say.

## Records in the release commit
This record, the gate report, `REVIEW-2026-10-27-2116-security-review-v3-1-0-gate-records-3cd0b48-work`, `TEST-2026-10-27-2113-verify-v3-1-0-gate-the-real-home-smoke-on-dave-a`, and `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § Where things stand naming v3.1.0.
