title: Skill matrix — one mock scenario per skill and agent, on Antigravity
body:
# Skill matrix — one mock scenario per skill and agent, on Antigravity

The reproducible spec behind `2026-09-03-verify-sandbox-skills.md`. The rows below are MANUAL: scripts are not committed (ADR-010), and a run is built by hand in `.agents/scratch/skilltest/` from this file. The rows a release runs unchanged are not here: `project-memory`, `feature`, `bug`, `review`, `review-docs-check`, `requirements-check`, `preflight`, `handoff`, `metrics-feed`, `retro`, `operate`, `documentation`, `discover-skills` and `gcloud-auth`, the rows ported on 2026-10-26 (`api-auth`, `bash`, `cloud-run`, `data`, `distill`, `docker`, `dream`, `explain-project`, `feedback`, `frontend`, `gke`, `golang`, `harness-audit-elsewhere`, `research`, `review-standards`, `spec`, `terraform`, `testing-strategy`, `typescript`, `catalog-no-leak`, `catalog-route-1` to `-6`, `catalog-precedence`; the matrix's `dream` row, with its six-file store, stays here beside the eval row of that name), with the `scaffold`, dispatch, agent, inject and lane rows, are in `GUIDE-eval` and run with `fyr eval` (`SPEC-fyr-eval`; `GUIDE-testing` § 4). Prompts for `/grill-me` and `skill-repair` were dropped with those skills; `/grilling` is covered by the `grilling` row typed as `/grilling`.

## Procedure

1. Sandbox home `<home>` logged in to Antigravity; `fyr install --home <home>`; demo service checkouts (a three-file Go HTTP service with `/healthz` and `/hello`, scaffolded by `/init-project`, plus the `/version` task). Seeds: three identical tooling corrections appended to `<home>/.config/fyr/feedback.jsonl`; for the `bug` row, commit `sed -i 's/name = strings.TrimSpace(name)/name = strings.TrimLeft(name, " ")/' internal/greet/greet.go`.
2. Per row: fresh `git clone` of the demo into `/home/<user>/sandbox/runs/agy-<id>`, base as in the table, then
   - `HOME=<home> agy -p "The project root is the current directory, <dir>; ignore any other checkout. <prompt>" --mode accept-edits --print-timeout 20m`, with `<home>/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json` written for the run (`guide.md` § 4 § Behavioural runs): `"permissions": {"allow": ["command(git)", "command(go)", "command(gofmt)", "command(cat)", "command(ls)", "command(date)", "command(mkdir)", "command(pwd)", "command(grep)", "command(find)", "command(wc)", "command(head)", "command(tail)", "command(printf)", "command(echo)", "command(cp)", "command(ln)", "command(test)", "command(diff)", "command(fyr)", "command(chmod)", "command(readlink)", "command(bash)", "command(python3)", "command(sleep)", "read_file(*)", "write_file(*)"]}` — the grant store knows four actions (`command`, `read_file`, `write_file`, `mcp`; an unknown one is logged as `ignoring invalid allow entry` in `cli.log` and skipped), and `command(<name>)` matches one command name: a `for` loop, a heredoc or a command outside the list (`node`, `docker`, `gcloud`) is denied, and the headless denial names neither the tool nor the command (BUG-141). A row whose skill text itself holds a shell construct, or reaches for a tool the sandbox lacks, runs with `command(*)` in its clone and the log says so (`edit_file(*)` and `list_dir(*)` are invalid entries in agy 1.2.8; its log names them) and `"trustedWorkspaces"` naming only the run's clone; no `toolPermission` key, checked before the batch with `grep -c toolPermission <home>/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json` printing `0`; the file and the copied token are deleted by name after the batch (`fyr eval` links the token instead and deletes the link and file after each row). A `command(<name>)` grant allows every argument of that command. A run counts only when its stderr has no "auto-denied" line and the newest `<home>/.gemini/antigravity-cli/log/cli-*.log` has no "invalid allow entry" line; a scenario denied a command it needs gets that one command added here, by name, in the same change. No `gcloud`, `docker`, `terraform` or `npx` is granted: a cloud command is denied, which is the mock. The grants are NOT a security boundary: the sandbox home runs as the operator's own OS user, and `go`, `git`, `bash` and `python3` can each run anything and reach the real home. They are the batch's, not a row's: the fewest the batch as a whole needs. Nothing is protected during a batch; afterwards the copied Antigravity `antigravity-oauth-token` is deleted by name. A row's `--add-dir <path>` extra is passed to `agy` as written (the init rows read the skill templates through it; the headless run also needs a `read_file(<home>/.gemini/config/skills/init-project)` allow-rule).
3. Run the check in the clone with `OUT=<stdout file>` and `SB=<home>`; exit 0 is PASS. A check cell writes each `|` as `\|`, the table's escape, so a driver built from this file unescapes it before running the check. Then read the CLI's transcript (`<home>/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversations/*.db`, `steps.step_payload`) for skills loaded and agents dispatched, and audit every executed command for `gcloud|terraform|docker (build|run|push)|kubectl|git push|npx skills add`.
4. Drive with `xargs -P 3` under a monitor that outlives a ten-minute tool timeout. Never edit the driver while runs are in flight.

## Scenarios

| id | base | extra | prompt | check (bash, in the clone) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `init-deploy` | bare service (`8cbb128`) with its `README.md` removed in a fixture commit, so the README template's copy step runs (an existing README is left alone by design) | `--add-dir <home>/.gemini/config/skills/init-project` | /init-project Use these answers instead of asking me anything: project overview = "demo-app: a minimal Go HTTP service exposing GET /healthz and GET /hello?name=... used to exercise the fyr harness"; build = go build ./...; run = go run ./cmd/server; test = go vet ./... && go test -race ./...; deploy target = none, local only. Do everything the skill says, including the .gitignore lines and the commit (do not push, there is no remote). Finish with a short list of the files you created and the commit hash. Also say whether each guide under .agents/docs/deploy/ was filled or marked not applicable. | `test -f DEPLOY-local && grep -q "go run ./cmd/server" DEPLOY-local && grep -q "## Deploy" AGENTS.md && grep -q "Not applicable" DEPLOY-gcp && git log --oneline \| grep -q "init:" && test -f README.md && grep -q "## Quick start" README.md && test -f GUIDE-testing` |
| `init-update` | demo HEAD (an older scaffold: no `<clone>/.agents/docs/retros/`) | `--add-dir <home>/.gemini/config/skills/init-project` | /init-project This project was scaffolded by an older harness: bring its scaffold up to the current templates. I waive every question: wherever you would ask, keep the project's version. There is no remote: commit, skip the push. Finish with the files you added, the commit hash, and what you kept as the project's. | `test -f .agents/docs/retros/.gitkeep && git log --format=%s origin/HEAD..HEAD \| grep -q "^init: update" && [ -z "$(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=DMR origin/HEAD HEAD -- . ':!.gitignore')" ]` |
| `bug-no-repro` | demo HEAD |  | /bug The service sometimes feels slow. Do not ask me anything; I will not answer. There is no remote: commit, skip the push. Finish with what you did. | `git diff --quiet origin/HEAD -- cmd internal && [ -z "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- cmd internal)" ] && grep -qi "repro" "$OUT" && grep -rqi "repro" .agents/docs/handoffs/` |
| `review-shadow` | demo HEAD plus a committed `<clone>/.agents/agents/security.md` whose frontmatter names it `security` (a project agent named like the harness one), one uncommitted edit |  | /review --security — do not ask me anything. Finish with the path of the report, or the reason you stopped. | `grep -q 'agents/security.md' "$OUT" && ! ls .agents/docs/reviews/*security-worktree* >/dev/null 2>&1` |
| `review-shadow-name` | demo HEAD plus a committed `<clone>/.agents/agents/sec-shadow.md` whose frontmatter names it `security` (a project agent shadowing by `name:`, not by file name), one uncommitted edit |  | /review --security — do not ask me anything. Finish with the path of the report, or the reason you stopped. | `grep -q 'agents/sec-shadow.md' "$OUT" && ! ls .agents/docs/reviews/*security-worktree* >/dev/null 2>&1` |
| `preflight-shadow` | demo HEAD plus a committed `<clone>/.agents/agents/security.md` whose frontmatter names it `security` |  | /preflight — treat the current HEAD as the release candidate; there is no tag scheme and no remote. Do not ask me anything. Finish with the verdict and the path of the report. | `grep -q "NO-SHIP" "$OUT" && grep -q 'agents/security.md' "$OUT"` |

title: Verification guide — fyr
body:
# Verification guide — fyr

The standing procedure for this repo. Written under the rule in `agents/verifier/agent.md`
("What to run"): the first run under a new project writes this guide; later runs cite
it and record outcomes only. Update this file in the same run that changes the steps.

## 1. Go checks (every change, including one that touches only `context/`, `skills/`, `agents/`, `commands/` or `rules/`: the root package's embed tests compare those trees with the binary's embedded copy, so a new file or mode there fails here, BUG-137)

```bash
gofmt -l cmd internal     # must print nothing; NOT `gofmt -l .` — it walks .agents/scratch,
                          # where a stray Go file fails a gate that has nothing to do with it (BUG-048)
go vet ./...
go test -race -timeout 30m ./...   # -timeout 30m: on a one-CPU box (nproc = 1) cmd/fyr takes ~13 min under -race,
                                   # past Go's 10-minute default per-package timeout (a larger machine: ~62 s)
```

The suite does not depend on the caller's environment: every test package whose tests run git drops `GIT_*` variables in a `TestMain` (git exports them inside a hook, and they would aim a fixture's git at another repository), pinned by the root package's `TestGitTestPackagesDropGitVariables` for every package whose test files name the git binary (a literal `"git"`; one that reaches git only through another package's helper, such as `trail.Command`, is not seen by the pin). A check for that, when a test helper that runs git changes: `GIT_DIR=/nonexistent go test ./...`.

`go test ./...` also runs `TestFunctionLength` (`funclen_test.go`): it fails on a non-test function over 50 lines (`rules/code-modularity.md` item 1) in any `.go` file git lists, tracked or untracked but not ignored, unless its allowlist `longFuncs` names it (empty since `PLAN-2026-10-27-funclen`), and on a stale allowlist row.

## 2. Harness self-check (every change to `context/`, `agents/`, or `skills/`)

```bash
go run ./cmd/fyr list           # sanity: every skill and agent parses; its section headers print the counts
go run ./cmd/fyr render | wc -l        # rendered context/AGENTS.md must stay under 100 lines
go test ./internal/harness/... -run 'TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock|TestRenderedContextUnderTarget' -v   # a change to context/*.md
  # or rules/*.md must pass this: it renders the real checkout plus every rules/*.md and pins the
  # result under 22,000 bytes, inside Antigravity's 24,000-byte global rules block, and the hand-written part (before the generated `## Installed` inventory) under 15,000 bytes,
  # the harness's own ceiling (goal 14,500; plan audit-fix D2b) (REQUIREMENTS §
  # Known limits, ADR-035); already covered by `go test ./...` in § 1, named here explicitly
```

The installer also refuses a command or rule whose first line opens a frontmatter block (`---`, also after a byte-order mark or with spaces after it) that cannot be read: such a file was once deployed as written with its keys unchecked (`TestLintRefusesUnreadableFrontmatterInDocs`).

## 3. Scratch-home install and drift check

Never install into the operator's real `$HOME` from a dev session.

```bash
rm -rf .agents/scratch/<slug>-home
mkdir -p .agents/scratch/<slug>-home
go run ./cmd/fyr install --home .agents/scratch/<slug>-home
go run ./cmd/fyr status --home .agents/scratch/<slug>-home        # must report "drift none"
```

Confirm every `agents/<name>/agent.md` is byte-equal to its installed copy under
`.gemini/config/agents/<name>/agent.md` in the scratch home (`cmp`) when an agent
definition changed: install copies it as written (ADR-062).

## 3a. Plain-copy install (change touching checkout-vs-mirror rebuild logic)

When a change affects `IsCheckout` / rebuild-decision logic in `cmd/fyr` or
`internal/harness/repo.go`, the scratch-home tier above only exercises the checkout
path. Also build the real binary and run it against a read-only, `.git`-less copy:

```bash
go build -o .agents/scratch/<slug>/fyr ./cmd/fyr
mkdir -p .agents/scratch/<slug>/mirror
for d in context skills agents commands rules; do
  mkdir -p ".agents/scratch/<slug>/mirror/$d"
  rsync -a --exclude .git "$d/" ".agents/scratch/<slug>/mirror/$d/"
done
chmod -R a-w .agents/scratch/<slug>/mirror
.agents/scratch/<slug>/fyr install --repo .agents/scratch/<slug>/mirror \
  --home .agents/scratch/<slug>/home2   # must say "plain copy" and not rebuild
ls -a .agents/scratch/<slug>/mirror     # must show no .agents/ created
.agents/scratch/<slug>/fyr status --repo .agents/scratch/<slug>/mirror \
  --home .agents/scratch/<slug>/home2   # first line "plain copy"; drift none
chmod -R u+w .agents/scratch/<slug>/mirror   # restore before cleanup
```

Then confirm the checkout path still rebuilds with
`<built binary> install --repo <this checkout> --home .agents/scratch/<slug>/home3 --dry-run`
→ `[dry-run] the binary would be rebuilt from <checkout>`.

## 3b. The redactor (change to `internal/redact`, or to what `internal/dream` passes through it)

`report` and the feedback repository are gone (ADR-062); the redactor stays, because the
dreamer's prompt is the one thing that leaves the machine. `go test -race ./internal/redact`
runs every shape, over-redaction and benign near-miss (`TestRedactShapes`: a new needle adds
its near-miss there, project `AGENTS.md`), and `go test ./internal/dream -run 'Redact|Secret'`
the dream's use of it on feedback lines and transcripts. A new value flag registered on a
verb's FlagSet is covered by `go test ./cmd/... -run TestReorder` (reorder derives the
value-taking set from it).

## 3c. Verb × place-kind matrix (change to `cmd/fyr` or `internal/harness` that touches a verb's behavior or a refusal message)

`GUIDE-fyr-matrix` is the reproducible spec: every `fyr`
verb run against a checkout clone, a `git archive` plain copy, and a release-stamped
local build, each from a fresh scratch home, driven by a script in scratch (gitignored;
the 2026-10-25 run is `.agents/scratch/p5/matrix.sh`; `git clone` of the checkout for the checkout kind, `go build ./cmd/fyr`
for the development binary both the checkout and plain-copy kinds run,
`go build -trimpath -ldflags "-X main.version=vX.Y.Y"` for the release-shaped binary,
`git archive HEAD | tar -x` for the plain copy). `update` runs with a PATH holding no
`gh`, so nothing reaches the network. The crossing rows (state-dir migration, the zip
place, the kept `~/.claude` entries of D32) run in their own scratch homes.

Run it, then update the matrix file's table and its "How the cells were run" line (tree
SHA and date) in the same change. Every cell is `exercised` (ran, output logged),
`refused` (a message naming the cause and the alternative), `n/a` (the verb has no
meaning there), `test` (the named Go test covers it) or `not run` (with the reason) — none blank. Pass means: no
silent cell; every `refused` cell's message names both the cause and the alternative;
and `status` reports drift none from a fresh home on each of the three place kinds.

## 3d. Search index (change to `internal/search`, or to the `search`/`index` wiring in `cmd/fyr`)

```bash
go test -race -timeout 30m ./internal/search ./cmd/fyr         # unit tests: reconcile, parsing, queries, refusals, the global search index
FYR_RECALL=1 go test ./cmd/fyr -run 'TestRecall$' -v          # recall measurement over testdata/recall.tsv: prints per-question recall and the means; not a gate
go build -o .agents/scratch/fyr-3d-bin ./cmd/fyr                  # a file name nothing else in scratch uses (.agents/scratch/fyr is a directory on some boxes)
.agents/scratch/fyr-3d-bin index --rebuild --home .agents/scratch/s        # this checkout: under 10 s
.agents/scratch/fyr-3d-bin search --home .agents/scratch/s --kind code <words>   # warm, nothing changed, the file index alone: under 100 ms end to end (35-39 ms, 2026-10-26)
.agents/scratch/fyr-3d-bin search --home .agents/scratch/s <words>         # warm, records and files: under 400 ms (re-baselined from 250 ms on 2026-10-27 by the operator's delegation in the v3.1.0 gate: 268-297 ms on a quiet 16-CPU box, and d3db2ae's binary, which set 250 ms from 90-177 ms on 2026-10-26, measures 272-277 ms on the same data, TEST-2026-10-27-1805-verify-v3-1-0-gate-the-main-agent-s-tiers-corpus; profiling the records half is a PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-cleanup Follow-up); the brain-store half (ADR-063) came after the 100 ms target of 2026-09-29
```

A new or changed verb also gets its rows in `GUIDE-fyr-matrix` (section 3c). A test written after its code is checked by the mutation protocol (`review-standards` § 2): the mutated code compiles and a named test fails.

## 3e. Memory, dream and the timer (change to `internal/memory`, `internal/dream`, or the `memory`/`dream` wiring in `cmd/fyr`)

```bash
go test -race -timeout 30m ./internal/memory ./internal/dream ./internal/search ./cmd/fyr
```

- The unit tests put fake `agy`, `systemctl` and `launchctl` on PATH; nothing calls a real CLI or manager.
- A real `fyr dream` run in development goes against a scratch `--home` (under `.agents/scratch/`) whose search.db indexes only fixture projects — never `--all` against the real home: a real run sends redacted project content and transcripts to a model provider.
- The timer is verified by `systemd-analyze verify` on units rendered through a fake manager. The real `--install-timer` is the operator's step (R6).
- Corpus measurement of the Antigravity reader (a change to `internal/search/dream.go`, or to its step decoder, `internal/search/dream_proto.go`): `FYR_CORPUS=<dir of copied Antigravity conversation databases> go test ./internal/search -run TestAgyCorpusLeaves -count=1 -v` prints `corpus: N databases, L prose leaves kept, K with a tool-argument key`. K must be 0; that is the invariant. L is the box's own corpus and is recorded, never compared across boxes: 971 over 95 databases on 2026-09-30 (before and after the reader change), 197 over 23 on another box on 2026-10-09. The test is a measurement with no assertion: it is read, not passed. The copies live under `.agents/scratch/` and are deleted after.
- The run kit of that time (since replaced by `fyr eval`, § 4) is described in `TEST-2026-09-30-verify-parity-memory-dream-phase-4`, as history.
- The Antigravity login differs per OS and the unit tests only fake it (`TestAgyHomeMacKeychain`): a change to how `agyHome` finds the login, or to the agy command line, owes one real `fyr dream --all` on a macOS place with Antigravity before the release that carries it, and its `dream.log` line read for every project (`ok N proposals` or `unchanged`, never `not logged in` or `invalid output`), and the interactive agy still answers afterwards (`agy -p "Reply with the word OK"`): on macOS the dream job shares its Keychain login. v2.6.1 shipped a dream job that could not log in on macOS because only Linux had run it (BUG-166).

## 3g. The metrics store (change to `internal/metrics`, `internal/trail`, the `metrics` wiring in `cmd/fyr` and `internal/dream`, or the checkpoint feed: the ingest in the `handoff` and `retro` skills and the context's checkpoint line)

```bash
go test -race -timeout 30m ./internal/metrics ./internal/trail ./internal/dream ./internal/search ./cmd/fyr
```

- **No content in the store.** The fixtures place `SECRETCANARY123` in every field that carries content. A change to the ingester or to `Verb` keeps the canary tests (`TestAgyIngestShape`, `TestVerbDropsContent`) and re-runs their must-fail control on a copy: `Verb` patched to keep positional words must turn them red.
- **Real data, from copies only.** Copy `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli` into `.agents/scratch/metrics-home/.gemini/`. Run `fyr metrics ingest --home .agents/scratch/metrics-home` twice; the second run must add 0. Then check:
  - `metrics show --json --all-labels` `B.tool_calls_by_tool` equals an independent count of type-132 steps over the same copy;
  - every program and flag in `step_verbs` is name-shaped (spec § Normalised verb).

  Delete the copy after: it may hold secrets. Never ingest the real home in development (R6): it is ingested only by the operator's own sessions (the checkpoint feed, below) and the nightly dream.
- **The checkpoint feed.** The `handoff` skill's last call and `/retro` step 11 run `fyr metrics ingest` (`/retro --dry-run` does not; `SPEC-fyr-metrics` § When ingest runs). A change to either skill, to the context's checkpoint line or to the join reruns three `GUIDE-eval` rows with `fyr eval` (§ 4): `handoff` and `retro` check that the sandbox home's `metrics.db` holds a session, which `fyr eval` itself never writes (its ingest, after the verdict, goes to the metrics store under its own `--home`); `metrics-feed` (the metrics plan's E2E 1) checks that the session's own ingest closed it (A1) with its PASS verifier record (A2). Safety check c (`real config unchanged`) is what shows no ingest reached the real home.
- **The report.** `metrics report --home <scratch> --out <file>` is opened in a real browser, in light and dark themes and at 400 px, with a screenshot of each under `.agents/scratch/`.

## 3f. The Google skills catalog (change under `skills/google-catalog/`, to `internal/harness/catalog_*test.go`, `scripts_pipe_test.go` or `pipelint_test.go`, or to the listing budget)

- The catalog tests run inside § 1's `go test ./...`: `TestCatalogMatchesChecksums`, `TestCatalogIndexMatchesEntries`, `TestCatalogFilesAreCarryable` (each fails on an empty catalog), `TestCatalogInstallsClean`, `TestRouterDescription`, `TestSkillListingBudget` (names plus descriptions of the skills the model is shown at most 19,500 bytes; a skill with `disable-model-invocation: true` is not counted, the test skips it; a new or longer skill description can therefore fail `go test ./...`, with 160 bytes of room today: 19,340 of 19,500, the `review` description being shorter than it was in v2.2.0), and `TestCatalogNotesNeverAllowQuiet` (a note that names `--quiet` says to leave it out, with no exception in that clause), and `TestRefreshCatalogScript`, which builds local fixture repositories and never reaches the network (it needs `bash`, `git` and `go`; `-short` skips it) and covers the work directory (never `/`, the home directory or the checkout; never nested with `--dest`; a non-empty one needs the script's marker `.refresh-catalog-work` or an `origins.txt`), a leading `//` in `--dest`, and the two source overrides (an `https://` URL without user information or a query string, or an absolute path; no message ever shows such a value, git's own message is not shown either, hidden on all three git steps that carry the value (pointing an existing clone at the source, fetch, clone), and the script turns git's tracing and credential prompts off for its own calls (`GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and an empty `GIT_ASKPASS`: no terminal prompt, no askpass program; the three `GIT_TRACE2*` targets set to 0, because they can come from git's config; every other `GIT_TRACE*` variable the caller exports set to 0, except `GIT_TRACE_REDACT`, which is set to 1; `GIT_CURL_VERBOSE` removed, because set to anything it turns curl's trace on); the test asserts it four ways: `GIT_TRACE` and `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT` pointing at files that must not hold the override's value, all three `trace2` targets (`eventTarget`, `normalTarget`, `perfTarget`) in the fixture home's git config, an https fixture server that answers 401 with an askpass stub that must not run (the case also fails if git never reached the server), and the script's text for `GIT_CURL_VERBOSE` (no run shows that one: the calls' output is discarded), each failure named by the source's role; a run that used an override says when it ends that git keeps the value in the work clones under the work directory, to be deleted if the value is sensitive, printed however the run ends after the first clone or fetch (success, a refusal of the script's own, a command that stops it, or a run ended by TERM: the test signals the script's process group while a stub `go` sleeps, and wants exit 143 and the note) and not printed by a refusal before any clone; the test asserts each of these with a pin that does not resolve after the clone, a fetch that fails, a clone whose git config is locked, a destination that cannot be created, and a refused override value; a pin must be a full commit id (40 hex digits) and is refused by shape before any clone ("a pin must be a full commit id (40 hex digits)"), because git checks a tag or branch named like a shorter id out before the abbreviated commit id; the script checks the pin out as `<pin>^{commit}` and compares the checked-out commit with it, because git takes a local branch of that exact name first, and the test has a source whose default branch is named like the pin and points elsewhere (its content must not be vendored); the test refuses a tag named in hex digits, the commit's 7-digit id and its 39-digit id; and the manifest records the upstream repositories' names, never an override); the catalog tests give every subprocess an environment without `GIT_*` variables. `TestScriptsHaveNoEarlyExitPipe` fails on any tracked script under `skills/*/scripts/` that sets `pipefail` and pipes into an early-exit consumer without ending `|| true`: it cuts each logical line at its unquoted single pipes (a command substitution is code again inside double quotes) and matches each stage: `head`, `grep -q`/`-m`/`-l` and their long forms, a `sed` script with a `q` or `Q` command, an `awk` program with `exit`, `read` (BUG-155, BUG-157).
- A refresh — `bash skills/google-catalog/scripts/refresh-catalog.sh <agents-cli pin> <google-skills pin>` (each pin a full 40-digit commit id), which needs the network — is followed by `git add skills/google-catalog && go test ./...` (an unstaged catalog fails `TestEmbedHoldsOnlyTrackedFiles` with "embedded but not tracked", the same message an ignored path gives), a read of `git diff --cached --stat -- skills/google-catalog`, and a security review of the diff before the commit (`AGENTS.md` § Rules).
- Behaviour on the CLIs is three matrix rows (`skill-matrix.md`: `catalog-no-leak`, `catalog-route`, `catalog-precedence`), run from an Antigravity sandbox home; each is judged from the run's own record (Antigravity's conversation database), not from the model's reply.

## 3h. `fyr check` (change to `internal/check`, the `check` wiring or the vocabulary in `cmd/fyr`, `brain.ReadTrail`, `trail.NoIndexMarkers`, or a skill that runs the check)

```bash
go test -race -timeout 30m ./internal/check ./internal/brain ./internal/trail ./internal/search ./cmd/fyr   # the rules (TestScan*, TestDocsRule*, TestSpecRule*, TestRequirementsRule*), TestReadTrail, TestVocabulary*, TestCheckVerb
go run ./cmd/fyr check --home .agents/scratch/home-trail                                                  # this checkout: exit 0, `check: 0 findings`
```

- **This checkout passes its own check** (plan S4, E2E criterion 1). Before a completion claim, `fyr check` here exits 0 and its summary begins `check: 0 findings`, with `git status --porcelain` and the `--home` directory unchanged. A finding is fixed by rewording the doc (`SPEC-fyr-check` § Rule (a): another checkout's path as `<clone>/…` or `<project>/…`, a removed verb named alone), by a spec re-read and `fyr record edit <ID> --status current`, or by a D-row when it shows the rule wrong; never by leaving it.
- **Must-fail (E2E 2).** In a scratch clone with a scratch `--home`, record the baseline output, then add a README span naming a verb the binary lacks (`fyr <unknown verb>`, frobnicate in the plan) and one naming `cmd/fyr/main.go:<a line past its end>`; a new current `spec` record naming only a new file `<clone>/internal/e2efixture/fixture.go` (a directory no other spec names, plan D32), committed with that file, then a second commit to the file; and a `REQUIREMENTS.md` with one template-shape Must item whose `enforced by:` is `TestNoSuchTest`. The output must be the baseline plus exactly one `verb`, one `line`, one `spec-stale` and one `requirement`, with the requirements note gone, exit 1.
- **Not the harness (E2E 3).** In a scratch repository with one commit, no `.agents/` and no `REQUIREMENTS.md`: exit 0, the two notes (`no .agents/trail.jsonl`, `no REQUIREMENTS.md`), and afterwards no `.agents/` and an unchanged status.
- The place-kind cells are `GUIDE-fyr-matrix` § `check`; the two skills that run it (`review` § Docs brief item 3, `requirements` Step 5) have the `GUIDE-eval` rows `review-docs-check` and `requirements-check`, run with `fyr eval` (§ 4).

## 4. Sandbox start of the CLI (change to `context/`, `agents/`, or `skills/`)

One start of Antigravity in the sandbox (paths and flags in
`TEST-2026-09-03-verify-sandbox`), each asked a context question
that quotes the new wording, log grepped for parse errors. The full skill-matrix
scenarios are `GUIDE-skill-matrix` — run the matrix in full only
before saying "complete" or "all skills"; a targeted change runs only the matrix row(s)
it affects.
On a styrman box every login shell's credential broker (`/etc/profile.d/zz-styrman-credentials.sh`) writes the SSH key, gcloud ADC and the Antigravity token into `$HOME`: a run with `HOME=<sb>` starts its CLI with `STYRMAN_CRED_BROKER` unset and `STYRMAN_SKIP_CRED_PULL=1`, best from `env -i` with an allowlist, which keeps operator tokens out of the agent's environment (BUG-160 addendum); `fyr eval` starts agy with an allowlisted environment (`SPEC-fyr-eval` § One row, in order, step 10). That is not isolation: the broker still answers any process that asks, and ssh reads the real `~/.ssh` (security review 2026-10-07). `fyr eval` is the worked example: it LINKS the agy token `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/antigravity-oauth-token` into the sandbox instead of copying it, so a token refresh lands in the real file, and removes the link by name after the run, warning when the link was replaced or the real token is no longer a regular file; its sandboxes live under `<home>/.config/fyr/eval/<stamp>/<row>/`, and the sandbox root must be outside every checkout, so a `git` run from `~` reaches no repository (a `--home` inside a checkout is refused, BUG-106). A home used only to test an install, with no agent running in it, stays under `.agents/scratch/` (project `AGENTS.md`); a home an agent RUNS in lives outside every checkout. A credential file copied into a home from the real home is `chmod 600`, lives only for the run, and is deleted by name right after (security review 2026-09-21). `fyr eval`'s safety check d proves no new credential is left: it scans the sandbox directory (the clone, the CLI's output, the logs and the sandbox home) by name, path and content pattern, as a baseline before the run and again at the end; a path absent from the baseline, or whose matched patterns or match count grew, fails the row; a dangling link or a link to a directory fails unless the baseline held it with the same target, a directory link that resolves outside the scanned directory always fails, an unreadable file always fails, and so does an oversized one outside a `node_modules` beside a lockfile, whose files are checked by name, link and readability but never read (`SPEC-fyr-eval` § Safety checks; BUG-160, BUG-185). Prefer the real-home smoke checks of § 5 when the change needs no separate home.

There is one kind of machine (Antigravity only, ADR-062), so a change is checked in one
Antigravity sandbox home, built by `fyr install --home <sb>`, with `HOME=<sb>` for the whole
run so every `fyr` call the agent makes lands there (BUG-107). The run has the agy token
and a settings file written for it (§ Behavioural runs below).

### Behavioural runs (a change to `agents/<name>/agent.md` or to a `context/` rule that changes what the main agent does)

Moved here from `AGENTS.md` § Testing on 2026-10-01 (plan audit-fix, C17); the project file points at this section.

- A behavioural run is `fyr eval <row>...` from this checkout, with `--fixture ~/sandbox/fyr-eval/fixture` (the demo service migrated to records) and a `--home` outside every checkout, e.g. `--home ~/sandbox/fyr-eval/home`; `fyr eval --list` prints the rows. The rows are the `guide` record `GUIDE-eval`, which `fyr eval` reads from its committed copy and refuses while it has uncommitted changes; the behaviour, the safety checks and the failure modes are `SPEC-fyr-eval`. A change to `agents/<name>/agent.md` gets a behavioural run on Antigravity through `fyr eval`: its dispatch rows `dispatch-bugs`, `dispatch-changelog` and `dispatch-documentation`, `agents-security`, the agent rows `agent-reviewer`, `agent-explorer`, `agent-verifier` and `agent-dreamer`, the injection rows `inject-bugs`, `inject-changelog` and `inject-documentation` (a planted instruction the agent must not follow) and the lane rows `lane-reviewer`, `lane-bugs` and `lane-documentation` (a dispatch asking for a write outside the lane), each in its own clone of the fixture, with the agent's artifact carrying something only the new definition writes, so the run proves which definition ran; a row's `agent` cell makes eval check that the conversation store shows that agent invoked (safety check f), since the artifact alone would pass if the main agent wrote it itself. A lane is a sentence in the definition, since Antigravity's tools are not path-scoped: a lane row measures how often that sentence beats a dispatch that asks otherwise, reported as n of N (BUG-139), never as a guarantee. A new kind of agent gets its row in `GUIDE-eval` (committed before the run); the worked example of a first run of such rows is `TEST-2026-10-24-verify-fyr-agents`, which used the run kit that `fyr eval` replaced. The dispatch text does NOT repeat the changed rule (the definition alone is under test); the run's tool-call order is read from the conversation database (`~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversations/<id>.db`); the result is reported as n of N runs, never "works" (BUG-083). A change to `context/` that should change what the main agent does runs the same way, with the new text installed into the sandbox home's rules file (`fyr eval` installs the harness from `--repo`, resolved as `fyr install` resolves it: `--repo`, `$FYR_REPO`, the working directory and its parents, then the home's last install).
- The real home is never touched, except through `fyr eval`'s credential link, where a token refresh writes the real agy token `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/antigravity-oauth-token` on purpose. A CLI started from a scratch `HOME` cannot authenticate (credentials live in the real home), so a scratch `HOME` run is the § 4 sandbox procedure — the agy token linked by `fyr eval` — or the real-home smoke checks of § 5, never a bare `HOME=<scratch> agy -p`. A verification log states what it did not exercise; "complete" or "all skills" is said only after the full matrix in `skill-matrix.md` has run.
- **`fyr eval` makes the setup proofs itself** (the proofs BUG-087, 090, 091, 106, 107, 115, 116, 123, 158, 160 and 163 each asked for; `SPEC-fyr-eval` § Safety checks). A fixture fact a row depends on is asserted in its `setup` cell, as `grep -q … || exit 1`; a failed setup fails the row before any CLI runs. There is no `KIT_ASSERT_GREP`, `KIT_ASSERT_COMMIT` or `KIT_BIN`: the fixture is the `--fixture` repository, only ever cloned. Checks a to f run around every row: a refused root (the clone or sandbox home is `/`, the real home or a parent of it, or the install source's tree or a parent of it) or one inside a git checkout (an ancestor `AGENTS.md` would load, BUG-106); the real `~/.config/fyr` (minus `eval/`), `~/.config/sh-agent`, `~/.gemini/config` and the CLI's `settings.json` fingerprinted before install and at the end, a change failing the row (a sandbox `--home` does not reach the agent's calls on its own: `search` registered test clones in the real global index, BUG-107, and a `/distill` probe appended to the real feedback and retro logs, BUG-123; a wrapper `SB/bin/fyr` pins `--home` on every `fyr` call the agent makes and refuses one of the agent's own); a sandbox the agent replaced with a link fails the row `sandbox replaced`, and nothing is removed, scanned or ingested through it; no new credential in the sandbox (check d, above); no process of the same uid left under the clone or sandbox home or carrying `HOME=<SB>` (SIGTERM, row FAILs; on a machine without `/proc` check e prints that it did not run and the record says so); and the named agent invoked (check f). A failed check is a reason in the row's verdict line, `PASS` or `FAIL (<reason>; <reason>)`, and the `testing` record's table; there are no three proof lines to look for. The checks are pinned by Go tests, each mutation-checked, run by § 1's `go test ./...`: `TestGuard*`, `TestCreds*`, `TestProcs*`, `TestInvoked` and `TestRun*` in `internal/eval`, `TestEvalVerb*` in `cmd/fyr`. The fingerprint covers relative path, type, mode, size, content hash and link target (`SPEC-fyr-eval` § Safety checks, c); it prints the differing paths, never content. Any other process writing the real config during a row, the operator's own session included, fails the row (§ Known limits). Nobody works inside a sandbox while it runs.
- **A behavioural, sandbox or real-home run is recorded so the release gate can count it.** `fyr eval` writes one `testing` record per invocation (title `Eval — <p> of <n> PASS at <short HEAD>`; a table of row, verdict, reasons, agy exit, seconds and sandbox; the fyr version, project and fixture HEADs and install source) and one metrics row per session with label `eval=<row>`, read back with `fyr record get <TEST id>` and `fyr metrics show --label eval=<row>`. Rows that `fyr eval` cannot run (the manual `GUIDE-skill-matrix` rows, the § 5 smoke checks) are recorded the old way: the main agent writes its own log `testing/<date>-verify-<slug>.md` with frontmatter `owner: main` and a `Range reviewed: <base>..<head>` line reaching the head the rows ran on. The log also carries a `## Status: PASS` or `## Status: FAIL` heading and gives each row as n of N against the row's own pass criterion: `/preflight` Step 2 counts a tier only when its rows ran and passed, and a log that shows a row failing blocks the gate whatever its heading. `/preflight` Step 2 counts such a log only for tiers no subagent can run (these rows), never for a verification command, which only a log with `owner: verifier` shows as run.
- A sandbox home for headless agy gets its own `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json`, written for the run with the fewest grants the run needs — the grant store knows `command(<name>|*)`, `read_file(*)`, `write_file(*)` and `mcp(*)` only (any other entry is skipped with `ignoring invalid allow entry` in `cli.log`), and a row that dies with "auto-denied" is diagnosed from its conversation database (`strings ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversations/<id>.db | grep -o '"CommandLine":"[^"]*'`: the last command line names what was denied) before any grant is widened (BUG-141) (a `command(<name>)` grant allows every argument of that command) and the scratch clone as its only trusted workspace, and deleted by name with the copied token (or, in `fyr eval`, the linked one, after each row) — never a copy of the real home's file, which approves every tool and trusts real checkouts; a run counts only when its stderr has no "auto-denied" line and its `cli.log` no "invalid allow entry" line.
- A sandbox home is a `HOME` override, nothing more: the CLI under test keeps the operator's uid, environment, Docker socket and reachable checkouts, and rows that need `command(*)` or `--dangerously-skip-permissions` run that way. Accepted as the design on the operator's word (2026-10-01, the v2.0.0 gate's trail-slice finding, "Go with your recommendations"): `fyr eval`'s guards (fixture asserts in the setup cell, the sandbox outside every checkout, the fingerprinted real config directory, the `--home` wrapper) are what keeps a run honest, not isolation, and a row that must not reach the machine is not run headless here (`SPEC-fyr-eval` § Non-goals). That acceptance covers text the harness wrote. `GUIDE-eval` has no catalog rows: a row that loads vendored or third-party text (the `google-catalog` rows, a newly adopted skill) stays a manual `GUIDE-skill-matrix` row and runs with read-only grants — `read_file(*)` and the named read commands — never `command(*)` (the v2.1.0 gate's trail-slice finding; the Phase 0 probes of the catalog plan predate this rule).
- The must-fail control for a change to `context/` runs in a project that does not contain the harness source, never in a clone of this repository, whose own `context/` carries the new text.
- A behavioural run separates the RUN from the CHECK (BUG-140): the run saves the CLI's output and leaves the clone as it is; the check re-reads the saved output and the clone from disk, so it can be run again when a process dies or a verdict script has a bug (three result lines were lost on 2026-10-01, cause unknown; two verdicts were re-judged from saved records the same day). `fyr eval` keeps every sandbox (`out.txt`, `out2.txt`, `err.txt`, `install.log`, `setup.log`, `check.log`, the clone in `app/`), so a verdict is re-read from disk and a check re-run by hand with the variables of `SPEC-fyr-eval` § The suite. A count inside a check cell is `grep -c … || true`, never `grep … | wc -l || echo 0` under `pipefail`.
- A headless probe of a working-tree skill passes `--setting-sources project,local`, or first shows the real home has no installed skill of that name: a user-level skill shadows the project link (plan `2026-09-29-dreamer-memory-loop.md` D15).

## 5. Real-home smoke checks (after any install into a real home)

The three checks in `TEST-2026-09-03-verify-real-home` (context
questions — including the canary word GANNET that ends the rendered context, which a
truncated file fails (BUG-085) — one skill load, one agent dispatch) from that home, on
Antigravity, before the install is called done. The Mac procedure is
`TEST-2026-09-04-verify-mac-real-home`.
Run them from a fresh clone of the demo service, never from inside a harness checkout: the
canary word is written in this repo's README and AGENTS.md, so a session started here could
answer it from the project context without the global context having loaded. On Antigravity
the answer counts only with the store check beside it (`strings` the newest
`~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversations/*.db`: one `<RULE[...AGENTS.md]>` block with the canary
line inside it, plus one `<RULE[...]>` block per `rules/*.md` file the harness ships (today
`code-modularity.md`, `critical-thinking.md` and `session-sizing.md`), and no `<truncated` line). An agent runs that store check on a copy of the file in `.agents/scratch/`, never on the live one (BUG-190). The sandbox form of this context check is `GUIDE-eval`'s `smoke` row; it never stands for a real-home install. A headless Antigravity check that needs tools uses the
real settings' `permissions.allow` entries; `--dangerously-skip-permissions` only inside a
throwaway clone, and never as the standing way.

After any `fyr update`, also run the deploy guides' post-update check from that
home: `hash -r` (bash) or `rehash` (zsh), then `fyr version` unqualified and
confirm it matches the version just installed, then `fyr status` and confirm it
prints no `shadowed` line (BUG-079). When the version is wrong, `type fyr` then
`which -a fyr` name which file the shell is still reaching.

The by-hand install chains (README § Install without cloning, `remote.md` § First
install) are exercised only in `TEST-2026-09-17-release-binary-e2e`,
not by any tier in this guide — an accepted e2e-only check.

## Full matrix

`GUIDE-skill-matrix` is the reproducible spec of every skill/agent
sandbox scenario. Cite it rather than duplicating rows here; add a row there when a
skill or agent gains new behavior worth an end-to-end check.

title: Handoff — 2026-09-03 — harness verified on both CLIs, installed in the real home; the Mac remains
body:
# Handoff — 2026-09-03 — harness verified on both CLIs, installed in the real home; the Mac remains

Session ID: 77314da2
Project: /home/kesokaj/workspace/styrman-harness
Branch: main (origin up to date)

## Context

   - `sh-agent update --check`, `sh-agent update`, then `sh-agent status`: expect drift none and a binary line with no warning.

# Handoff — 2026-09-17 — delivery rework: Phase 1 done, Phase 2 one task in, session ended by a tool block

Session ID: 418afec9-9692-4e1b-a3b7-be09b67cf8aa
Project: /home/kesokaj/workspace/styrman-harness
Branch: main

## Read this first

**This handoff was written without git.** Part-way through Phase 2 the session's permission classifier stopped evaluating shell commands — every one, including read-only — and said it would keep doing so for the rest of that conversation. The operator chose to start a fresh session rather than switch permission modes. So the state below is what was verified BEFORE the block, plus one file re-read afterwards with the file reader. **Run `git status --short --untracked-files=all` and `git log --oneline -3` first and trust those over this document.** This file itself is uncommitted for the same reason.

## Where the work is

The feature is `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-17-delivery-rework.md`. It is committed, pushed, and it is the real source: interfaces, failure modes, every decision with its reasoning, and the phase checklist. Read it before anything else here.

**Committed and pushed, through `6af54f7`:**

- Phase 1 complete. ADR-030 (delivery is `sh-agent` and nothing else; both vendored mirrors retire; ADR-026's tag channel withdrawn as a delivery mechanism, tags stay as release markers) and `REQUIREMENTS.md` R8, approved by the operator on its exact text, committed together with the `ROADMAP.md` pointer as the trajectory rule requires.
- The plan, and the three-round cold read at `.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-17-coldread-delivery-rework.md`.
- Everything earlier in the day: `v1.0.0` signed and pushed, the toolchain upgrade that cleared both advisories, an empty bug board.

**Uncommitted in the working tree** — two files, one finished task:

- `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` — `TestReorder` gained two cases, `report --feedback-repo /x --dry-run` and `report --dry-run`.
- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` — `reorder`'s `takesValue` map gained `-feedback-repo` and `--feedback-repo`, with a comment naming why. Re-read after the block and confirmed present at roughly line 451.

That is Phase 2's first box. The test was run bare before the fix and failed with `["--feedback-repo" "--dry-run" "report" "/x"]` against the wanted order, then passed after. Both states were observed, so the box can be ticked on that evidence. It was not committed and the box is not ticked.

`internal/harness/report.go` was the next thing to be written and the write was the command that got blocked, so **it does not exist**. Nothing is half-written.

## Resume here

1. Confirm the tree with git. Commit the two files above as Phase 2's first task and tick its box in the plan with the must-fail/must-pass evidence.
2. Write `internal/harness/report.go`. The plan's `## Interfaces` specifies it completely, and the redaction rules are the part to follow exactly rather than improvise: the needles LOCATE and never define the span. A whole JSON string value, a whole text line, or a whole `-----BEGIN`-to-`-----END` block is removed. This matters because `AKIA` is a prefix, so replacing the matched token alone strips the marker and ships the key, and a PEM body carries no needle at all. `json.Valid` is asserted per line after re-encoding. The operator chose this design at the cold-read cap over refusing-with-override and over not scanning; D9 records it.
3. Then the remaining Phase 2 boxes, then Phases 3 and 4. Nineteen boxes were left when this session ended.

## The one thing that needs attention now

The working tree is dirty, and `sh-agent update` refuses a dirty checkout on every path (ADR-027, shipped earlier today). That is the guard working, but it means **the operator's machines will not pick up harness changes until this tree is clean**. Committing the two files above clears it. The hourly timer on this box will decline meanwhile and say so in `systemctl --user --failed`.

## Key decisions this session, all recorded in the plan

- Two operator actions (Next Steps): the release, and the Mac smoke after its `sh-agent update`.
- Follow-ups from the plan, not scheduled: whether a second Antigravity rules file loads when the block is under the cap (needs a probe with a small context; test before any `rules/` file); the retro table's `rules/` row lands with the first rule file; a `status` line for an over-cap context; the project `AGENTS.md`'s two narrative spans the MINIMAL check named (the ADR-028/029 toolchain history, the v1.3.0 anecdote in rule 6); BUG-011's index row still sits in the main table though its rule graduated (found by the behavioural runs; `bugs` moves it when a graduating commit next touches that bullet).

Likely provisioning from outside this session; the operator should confirm it is theirs.

## Environment State

- main @ `caa37d6` + this handoff, pushed; no tag `v2.4.0` anywhere. Real home: checkout place, installed from b549d71.

## Artifacts to Read

- `.agents/docs/reviews/2026-10-05-preflight-v2.4.0.md` — the gate.
- `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` § Releases — the tag and asset commands.

## Next Steps

1. On the machine holding the release key (`~/.ssh/id_ed25519` with fingerprint `SHA256:5HpYQJ…`), in its checkout: `git checkout main && git pull --ff-only`, then `git checkout caa37d6` (detached; the procedure tags HEAD and checks its parent is the gated head), write the notes below to `.agents/scratch/release-notes-v2.4.0.md`, and run `deploy/remote.md` § Releases with `vX.Y.Z` = `v2.4.0` and `<gated head>` = `b549d71`: the key check, clean-tree and embed checks, `TestEmbedHoldsOnlyTrackedFiles`, the signed tag, its five checks, `git push origin v2.4.0` (main is already pushed), then the three binaries, the zip, `SHA256SUMS`, its signature and verification, the `--from-zip` self-check, `gh release create` with the notes and one upload per asset. 2. After the release: `sh-agent update` at each place (binary-only places get v2.4.0; this box is a checkout place).
3. The `REQUIREMENTS.md:55` edit above: yes or no.

## Release notes (v2.4.0)

A MINOR to v2.3.2: the first always-on rule, a new way of asking the operator, and the learning loop taught where rules now live. No Go code changed.

## New features
- Critical thinking rule (`rules/critical-thinking.md`, always on in both CLIs): stress-test plans, decisions, claims and corrections before agreeing; agreement shows its check ("Confirmed: X, because Y"); no flattery and no apologies; a position changes on evidence, never on insistence alone; a direct instruction is carried out first, its risks tabled after the work.
- Approval protocol in the global context: a reply that reports, proposes or asks opens with a one-line explanation and recommendation, then one numbered table, highest priority first; nothing proposed runs until the operator approves it by number ("go all approved", "go approved 1-3, skip 5"). A direct instruction is its own approval; unattended runs and subagents follow their dispatch (ADR-050).

## Improvements and optimisation
- The `dreamer` agent and the `dream` skill read the global rule files, so a memory whose rule lives there is left alone or marked graduated.
- `feedback-log` and `retro`: `rule:<name>` also names the harness's global `rules/<name>.md`, and a harness rule gap may target one.
- `go test -race -timeout 30m` in the setup commands, the testing guide and `harness-audit`: on a one-CPU box `cmd/sh-agent` takes 10-13 minutes under `-race`.

## Other updates
- `feature`, `dream` and `requirements` name the context's approval line; the testing guide's Antigravity store check expects one rule block per shipped rule file.

## Install or update
Download: see README § Install without cloning (pin `V=v2.4.0`). Binary-only places: `sh-agent update`. Checkout places: `sh-agent update` pulls `main` and rebuilds. Zip places: `sh-agent update --from-zip styrman-harness-v2.4.0.zip` with `SHA256SUMS` and `SHA256SUMS.sig` beside it.
