title: Research — harness engineering (Böckeler) and elephant/goldfish (Rensin, Shvedov) (2026-09-03)
body:
# Research — harness engineering (Böckeler) and elephant/goldfish (Rensin, Shvedov)   (2026-09-03)

## Question

The operator asked for two sources to be read in full and weighed against this harness: Birgitta Böckeler's "Harness engineering for coding agent users" (martinfowler.com, 2 April 2026) and the `vshvedov/elephant-goldfish` repository (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI adapters of Dave Rensin's elephant/goldfish pattern). Which of their strategies should this harness adopt, given its rules: no hooks, no scripts, no CI, one Go installer, everything else prose?

## Summary

Both sources fit the harness better than the previous hook-driven design did, because both are mostly about *what the agent is told and what it is made to check*, not about lifecycle machinery. Böckeler gives a vocabulary and a priority order: **guides** (feedforward: context, skills, rules) and **sensors** (feedback: tests, linters, type checks, reviewers), each **computational** (cheap, deterministic, run on every change) or **inferential** (a model judging, expensive, run proportionally), improved through a **steering loop** whenever an issue repeats. The elephant/goldfish repo gives concrete workflows: design before code, a fresh subagent that sees only the artifact (never the intent) to stress-test a design, a diagnosis, or a diff; a failing test before any bug fix; findings fixed or rebutted verbatim with a hard cap; mandatory user gates at scope confirmation and at the cap.

Adopted into `context/AGENTS.md` today: the work protocol (scope → plan file with phases and task boxes → cold-reader check of the plan → phases as checkpoints → e2e before done), the bug path (problem note → goldfish diagnosis on symptom and repro only → failing test → smallest fix → bug record), the reviewer-sees-only-the-diff rule, fix-or-rebut with a three-round cap, and the steering loop as the learning-loop cadence plus the bug index. Not adopted: their "docs live in chat" default (this harness deliberately keeps the trail on disk so a zero-context agent can resume), their per-project bootstrap that rewrites command templates (the harness deploys one global set and lets projects add their own), and anything that needs a hook.

## Böckeler — what the article says

- **Harness = everything but the model.** For a coding-agent *user*, the outer harness is the context, skills, rules, tools, and checks wrapped around the vendor's built-in harness. Its two goals: raise the odds of a right first attempt, and self-correct before a human has to look.
- **Guides and sensors.** Guides anticipate (AGENTS.md, skills, bootstrap instructions, code mods). Sensors observe after the fact (tests, linters, structural tests, review instructions). Feedback-only harnesses repeat mistakes; feedforward-only ones never learn whether the rules worked. Sensor output should be written for the model — a linter message that says how to fix it is "a positive kind of prompt injection".
- **Computational vs inferential.** Deterministic checks are cheap enough to run on every change; model judgements are expensive and noisy and belong where semantic judgement is needed, with a model strong enough for the task.
- **Steering loop.** The human's job is to iterate on the harness: whenever an issue happens more than once, improve the guide or the sensor. Agents can draft the improvement.
- **Keep quality left.** Fast checks before a commit exists; expensive ones after integration; drift sensors (dead code, coverage quality, dependency scanners) continuously, outside the change lifecycle.
- **Three regulation categories.** Maintainability (tooling exists, easiest), architecture fitness (fitness functions: performance tests, logging conventions), behaviour (the hard one; AI-written tests are not enough, approved fixtures help selectively).
- **Harnessability and Ashby's law.** Typed languages, clear module boundaries, and opinionated frameworks are "ambient affordances". Committing to a small number of service topologies narrows the space the harness must govern; harness templates per topology are the likely next step, with the same drift problems service templates have.
- **The human.** A harness externalises what an experienced developer brings implicitly; it should direct human attention to where it matters, not remove it.

## Elephant/goldfish — what the repository does

- **Elephant** = the working session with full context; **goldfish** = a fresh subagent that receives only an artifact. The asymmetry is the test: if a goldfish given only the design doc cannot implement it, the doc is wrong. "Design is the new code."
- Five commands, adapted per stack at bootstrap: `eg-brainstorm` (parallel goldfish with different lenses), `eg-prd`, `eg-new-feature`, `eg-fix-bug`, `eg-precommit-review`.
- **New feature:** confirm scope in one or two sentences → design doc with required sections (why, scope, surfaces, interfaces, UX flow, failure modes, verification criteria, follow-ups) → **no-code gate** until two goldfish sign off: a critic (gaps) and a readiness check ("could a first-pass implementer ship this without a question?"), plus an informational comprehension pass → three-revision cap, then ask the user → layer-ordered implementation with per-layer verification → independent review → test gate incl. a real browser or device walkthrough → report, no commit.
- **Bug fix:** triviality gate → problem doc (symptom, repro, suspected area, hidden hypothesis, blast radius, "fixed means") → goldfish diagnosis on symptom and repro only, hypothesis withheld → converge or re-investigate → failing test that fails for the right reason → smallest fix → review → test gate → report.
- **Pre-commit review:** pre-flight checks run separately, new errors only are blockers → a goldfish gets the exact review template and the diff, never the intent → each finding fixed or rebutted verbatim, a visible ledger between rounds → hard cap of five rounds or a repeat finding at the same place, then a structured question to the user.
- **Interactivity is mandatory at decision points** and explicitly overrides "work autonomously" directives; only the user in the same turn can waive a gate.
- Bootstrap inspects the stack and rewrites `[BOOTSTRAP: …]` markers; updates are merged by prompt. Codex skills stay generic and inspect the repo at runtime instead.

## Mapping onto this harness

| Their idea | Here | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| Guides = context, skills, rules | `context/`, `skills/`, `rules/` | already the model; vocabulary adopted in the research, not the context |
| Computational sensors on every change | `gofmt`, `go vet`, `go test -race`, frontend runner, `docker build` | Definition of Done step 1; `verifier` runs them |
| Inferential sensors proportional to change | `reviewer` at 50+ lines / 5+ files, `security` on sensitive paths, `documentation` on behavior change | kept; made an ordered sequence |
| Steering loop | `/retro`, `/distill`, bug prevention rules that graduate into rules or tests | adopted: learning-loop cadence, bug index |
| Sensor messages for the model | verifier and reviewer logs written for a zero-context reader | already the rule |
| Keep quality left; drift sensors | fast checks before commit; `/audit` for drift | adopted in prose; no continuous job (no CI by rule) |
| Harness template per topology | this harness *is* the template for Go + TanStack Start + Cloud Run; `/init-project` instantiates it | adopted as framing; ADR-008 |
| Design before code, goldfish readiness check | plan file + `reviewer` with only the plan, three-round cap | adopted (Work protocol) |
| Goldfish bug diagnosis, failing test first | `explorer` with symptom and repro only; failing test before the fix | adopted (Work protocol, Bugs) |
| Reviewer sees only the diff; fix or rebut verbatim; hard cap | `reviewer` gets no intent; three rounds then ask | adopted (Definition of Done step 2) |
| Mandatory user gates | scope confirmation, no-code gate, review cap, missing repro | adopted as the four gates named in the Work protocol |
| Browser/device walkthrough before done | e2e tier: container run + curl, browser golden path + edge case | adopted (Work protocol step 6, tiers) |
| Docs live in chat unless there is a future reason | trail on disk always | not adopted — resume needs the disk |
| Per-project rewritten command templates | global skills + project `.agents/` layer | not adopted — one global set, projects add their own |
| Hooks (Stripe pre-push, OpenAI linters) | none | not adopted — ADR-007 |

## Open questions

- Behaviour harness: neither source has a good answer beyond tests plus manual walkthroughs. The e2e tier is the harness's answer for now; approved fixtures may be worth a skill later.
- Whether a `brainstorm`/`prd` pair (parallel goldfish with different lenses) earns its place: `/research` covers comparison; brainstorming stays a `grilling` conversation until a real need shows up.

title: Research — hooks for the harness (2026-09-03)
body:
# Research — hooks for the harness   (2026-09-03)

## Question

The operator may want hooks after all: (1) a deploy gate that verifies everything is documented and up to date, (2) a warning when the wrong model is in use, (3) a loop protector. What do Claude Code and the Antigravity CLI actually offer, what would each hook look like on both, what does it cost, and what is worth building?

Constraints that shape the answer: zero scripts in the repo (any hook is a subcommand of the `sh-agent` binary), no CI, both vendors served alike, and the previous harness's hooks were reverted because a wrong block cost eight forced continuations and a degraded agent (old ADR-002, R4). Whatever is built must fail open and block only at a boundary the operator would block at by hand.

## Summary

Both CLIs have a `PreToolUse` hook that can deny, ask, or allow a tool call from a JSON payload on stdin, and a `Stop` hook that can refuse a stop. That is enough for all three wishes. Claude Code additionally exposes the model to hooks (`SessionStart` sometimes, `PostModelSwitch` always) and has an `if` filter so a hook only spawns for matching commands; Antigravity puts `modelName` in every payload and has `PreInvocation` for injecting a message before each model call. Neither has built-in repeated-call detection.

Recommendation, in order of value: build the **loop protector** and the **model warning** (small, deterministic, session-wide), and build the **deploy gate as "a fresh `/preflight` SHIP report for HEAD must exist"** rather than as a hook that judges documentation itself — a hook can check that the check happened; only the `preflight` skill and the `documentation` agent can check content. Do **not** build a Stop-hook that blocks until docs are written: that is the design that was reverted. All three are subcommands of `sh-agent` (`sh-agent hook <name>`), so the repo stays at zero scripts. The one real cost is that Claude Code hooks live in `~/.claude/settings.json`, so the installer would have to add and remove a `hooks` block there — the operator has said no settings changes before; this is the decision to make.

## What each vendor offers

| | Claude Code | Antigravity CLI (agy 1.1.24) |
|---|---|---|
| Config location | `~/.claude/settings.json` (user), `.claude/settings.json` / `.claude/settings.local.json` (project), plugin `hooks/hooks.json`, subagent frontmatter `hooks:` (scoped to that agent), skill frontmatter `hooks:` (registered when the skill is invoked, kept for the session) | one `hooks.json` in the customization root: `~/.gemini/config/hooks.json` (global) or `.agents/hooks.json` (workspace); named hooks, merged by name; `"enabled": false` per hook |
| Events | `SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`, `PostToolBatch`, `PermissionRequest`, `PermissionDenied`, `Stop`, `StopFailure`, `SubagentStart`, `SubagentStop`, `PreModelSwitch`, `PostModelSwitch`, `PreCompact`, `PostCompact`, `Notification`, `FileChanged`, `CwdChanged`, and more | `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PreInvocation` (before each model call), `PostInvocation` (after tool calls finish), `Stop` |
| Matcher | tool name, `A\|B`, regex; plus `if: "Bash(git push *)"` in permission-rule syntax so the hook only spawns for matching arguments | tool name regex on `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse` (`run_command`, `browser_.*`, `*`) |
| Input (stdin JSON) | `session_id`, `transcript_path`, `cwd`, `permission_mode`, `hook_event_name`; `PreToolUse`: `tool_name`, `tool_input`, `tool_use_id`, `effort.level`; `Stop`: `stop_hook_active`, `last_assistant_message`; `SessionStart`: `reason`, `model` (not always); `PostModelSwitch`: the model | common: `conversationId`, `workspacePaths`, `transcriptPath`, `artifactDirectoryPath`, **`modelName`**; `PreToolUse`: `toolCall{name,args{CommandLine…}}`, `stepIdx`; `PostToolUse`: `error`; `PreInvocation`: `invocationNum`, `initialNumSteps`; `Stop`: `executionNum`, `terminationReason` (`model_stop`, `max_steps_exceeded`, `error`), `fullyIdle` |
| Output | exit 0 = continue (stdout becomes context for `SessionStart`/`UserPromptSubmit`); exit 2 + stderr = block; or JSON: `hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision` allow/deny/ask/defer, `permissionDecisionReason`, `additionalContext`, `updatedInput`; `decision: "block"` + `reason` on `Stop`/`PostToolUse`; `systemMessage` | JSON only: `PreToolUse` → `decision` allow/deny/ask/force_ask, `reason`, `overwrite`; `PostToolUse` → `{}`; `PreInvocation`/`PostInvocation` → `injectSteps[{ephemeralMessage\|userMessage\|toolCall}]`, `terminationBehavior` force_continue/terminate; `Stop` → `decision: "continue"` + `reason` |
| Hook types | `command`, `http`, `mcp_tool`, `prompt` (a model judges), `agent` | `command` only |
| Timeout | per hook; defaults 10 min for commands, 30 s for prompt-submit/model-switch | per hook, default 30 s; hooks run synchronously |
| Working dir / command | runs with the session cwd | runs in the directory holding `hooks.json`, via `sh -c`, `~` expanded — so the command must be `~/.local/bin/sh-agent …` or on PATH |
| Built-in loop limits | subagent `maxTurns`; `/goal` evaluator; `stop_hook_active` so a Stop hook is not re-invoked forever | `max_steps_exceeded` termination; 60 s default subagent interaction timeout |
| Model control | `model`, `enforceAvailableModels`, `fallbackModel` in settings; `PreModelSwitch` hook can deny a switch; status line JSON has `model.id`/`display_name` | `--model` flag; `modelName` in every hook payload (`auto` when not pinned) |

Sources: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide.md, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.md, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference.md, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline.md, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal.md; the "Lifecycle Hooks (`hooks.json`)" guide embedded in the agy binary and `agy changelog`.

## The three hooks, designed for both vendors

All three are `sh-agent hook <name>` subcommands reading stdin JSON and printing the vendor's JSON. Vendor is detected from the payload (`hook_event_name` vs `conversationId`). Every hook fails open: any error, unknown payload, or timeout means "allow, say nothing".

### 1. Deploy gate — "everything documented and up to date"

**What a hook can and cannot decide.** Whether the README, spec, and changelog *match the code* is a judgement; a hook can only check facts on disk. The facts worth checking before a deploy: the tree is clean, HEAD is what will be deployed, and a release gate has run on exactly this HEAD. `/preflight` already does the judgement part (docs freshness via the `documentation` agent, trail freshness, tests, review) and writes `reviews/<date>-preflight-*.md` with `Range reviewed: <base>..<head>` and `VERDICT: SHIP`. So:

- **Trigger:** Claude `PreToolUse`, `matcher: Bash`, `if: Bash(gcloud run deploy *)` plus `Bash(gcloud run services update *)`, `Bash(docker push *)`, `Bash(terraform apply *)`, `Bash(kubectl apply *)`; Antigravity `PreToolUse` on `run_command`, the same regexes applied to `args.CommandLine` inside the hook.
- **Check:** `git status --porcelain` empty; newest `.agents/docs/reviews/*-preflight-*.md` has a `Range reviewed:` line ending in the current `HEAD` short SHA and a `VERDICT: SHIP` line. A `docker push` to `pkg.dev` also requires the image tag to equal the HEAD short SHA when the tag is visible in the command.
- **Result:** pass → allow silently. Fail → `ask` (Claude `permissionDecision: ask`, agy `decision: ask`) with the reason ("no preflight report for HEAD a1b2c3d — run /preflight, or approve to deploy anyway"). Ask, not deny: the operator stays in control, and a deliberate hot-fix deploy costs one keypress instead of a fight.
- **Not gated:** `git push`. Git is backup; a gate on push blocks backups.
- **Cost:** one git call and one directory scan per deploy command; the hook does not spawn for other commands on Claude (the `if` filter), and costs a few milliseconds per command on agy.

Alternative considered and rejected: a `Stop` hook that blocks until a changelog entry exists. It fires every turn, it is wrong whenever the turn was not the end of a task, and it is the exact mechanism that was reverted. A softer variant — `Stop` hook that only *warns* ("source changed since HEAD, no changes/ entry today") via `systemMessage`, never blocks — is cheap and could be added later if the prose Definition of Done is being ignored.

### 2. Wrong-model warning

- **Claude:** `SessionStart` (payload `model` when present) and `PostModelSwitch` (always). If the model id is not in the allowed list, print one line to stdout (exit 0 → it lands in context) and set `systemMessage` so the operator sees it: "Model is claude-haiku-4-5; expected claude-fable-5-1 or claude-opus-5". Optionally `PreModelSwitch` with `permissionDecision: ask` to confirm a switch to a model outside the list. No blocking.
- **Antigravity:** `PreInvocation` fires before every model call and carries `modelName`. On `invocationNum == 1` only, if `modelName` is not allowed (or is `auto` when a pin is required), inject `{"ephemeralMessage": "…"}`; nothing on later invocations.
- **Allowed list:** given as arguments in the hook config itself (`sh-agent hook model --allow claude-fable-5-1,claude-opus-5` / `--allow pro`), so there is no extra config file; the installer templates the lists from one place in the repo (`context/` or a small `hooks/` directory the installer reads).
- **Cheaper alternative on Claude:** no hook; pin `model` in `~/.claude/settings.json` (already done: `claude-fable-5-1[1m]`) and read the status line. The hook only adds value if sessions get started with `--model` or switched with `/model`.

### 3. Loop protector

- **Signal:** the same tool call (tool name + argument hash) repeated three times in a row **with no file-changing call in between**. The "no edit in between" rule removes the common false positive: running `go test ./...` three times is fine when an `Edit` sits between the runs. `PostToolUse` records the result hash as well; identical input and identical output twice in a row is a loop by definition.
- **Claude:** `PreToolUse` on every tool (`matcher: ""`) reads `session_id`, `tool_name`, `tool_input`; `PostToolUse` appends the result hash. State is one small file per session under the CLI's own temp dir (`$TMPDIR/sh-agent/<session_id>`), so nothing persists. On a loop: `permissionDecision: ask`, reason "same call for the 3rd time with no change in between — loop?". `Stop` is left alone (no Stop hook), so no risk of the forced-continuation spiral.
- **Antigravity:** `PreToolUse` on `*` with `toolCall.name` + `args` hash keyed by `conversationId`; `PostToolUse` has no result body, so only the input rule applies. On a loop: `decision: ask` with the reason. `PostInvocation` could add `terminationBehavior: terminate` when `invocationNum` passes a hard ceiling with no edits since, as a second line of defence.
- **Subagents:** already capped by `maxTurns` (20–40) in `agents/*.md`; the hook applies to them too on Claude.
- **Cost:** one hash and one small file append per tool call, a few milliseconds. No model calls.

## What it would take

| Piece | Where | Size |
|---|---|---|
| `sh-agent hook deploy-gate\|model\|loop` | `internal/hook/` + `cmd/sh-agent` | ~350 lines Go incl. vendor payload detection, plus tests against recorded payloads |
| Claude config | `hooks` block in `~/.claude/settings.json`; installer merges by our command prefix (`~/.local/bin/sh-agent hook`) and removes only those entries on uninstall | ~80 lines Go; the one settings write the harness has avoided so far |
| Antigravity config | named entries `sh-agent-deploy`, `sh-agent-model`, `sh-agent-loop` in `~/.gemini/config/hooks.json`; installer merges by name | ~40 lines Go |
| Repo source of truth | `hooks/` directory with one JSON per hook in a vendor-neutral shape (event, matcher/if, command args) that the installer renders into both formats — so a new hook is a file, not code, once the subcommand exists | small |
| Docs | README, `context/AGENTS.md` (the gate's "run /preflight first"), ADR | small |

Option B for Claude that avoids the global settings write: `/init-project` writes the hooks into the project's `.claude/settings.json`. Per project, versioned with the project, but every project must be initialised for the hooks to exist, and the model warning would not fire outside a project.

Option C: skill-scoped hooks. `cloud-run-deploy` and `preflight` could carry the deploy gate in their SKILL.md `hooks:` frontmatter, active for the session once the skill is invoked. No settings write at all, but the gate exists only after the skill was loaded — an agent that runs `gcloud run deploy` without loading the skill is not gated. Fine as a belt when the braces exist, not on its own.

## Risks

- A hook that misparses a payload and denies is worse than no hook. Hence ask-not-deny everywhere, fail-open, and payload fixtures in tests.
- Claude's `if` syntax and hook payload fields have changed across versions; the `model` field on `SessionStart` is documented as "not always present". Pin what the code expects and test against fixtures recorded from the installed version.
- Antigravity hooks run synchronously with a 30 s default timeout; a slow git repo could stall a `run_command`. Keep the deploy gate to `git status` and a directory scan.
- The loop protector's state file must be per session and cleaned by the OS temp dir; never write it into the repo.
- None of this is verified live on either CLI yet; the live check of the base harness comes first.

## Open questions for the operator

1. Build all three, or only the loop protector and the model warning?
2. Is a merged `hooks` block in `~/.claude/settings.json` acceptable (installer-managed, removed on uninstall), or per-project via `/init-project` (Option B)?
3. Deploy gate: `ask` (recommended) or hard `deny`?
4. Allowed models: Claude `claude-fable-5-1`, `claude-opus-5`? Antigravity `pro` only, or is `auto` fine?
5. Loop threshold: 3 identical calls with no edit in between (recommended), or stricter?

## Decision (2026-09-03)

Rejected by the operator: "Skip the hooks. I think this was my problem before. Keep the no hooks/scripts rule." Recorded as ADR-007. This document stays as the record of what was considered.

title: Plan — learning loop at project level, all skills model-invocable, installer fixes (2026-09-13)
body:
# Plan — learning loop at project level, all skills model-invocable, installer fixes   (2026-09-13)

## Why

The operator's words (2026-09-13): the five findings of today's research pass are wanted as fixes ("this is what I want adding"); `/retro` and `/distill` today only improve the harness globally, but "if I run /retro in my project because something does not work correctly I want that to be saved on a project level", with per-project logs that later sessions can use "to make the harness better on a global level"; and "I want ALL skills to be able to be executed by the agent, not hidden behind user only". Findings: `.agents/docs/handoffs/` has none for this session yet; the research pass is in chat only, its evidence goes into `testing/2026-09-13-verify-research-pass.md` in Phase 4.

## Scope

In:
- F1 The installed binary rebuilds from source instead of copying itself (today `~/.local/bin/sh-agent` is the 2026-09-03 build and every `sh-agent install` since re-installed it).
- F2 `sh-agent version` and `status` show the binary's real commit; `status` warns when the binary is older than the repo.
- F3 Repo docs stop saying `--home /tmp/...`; the global hard rule says scratch is `.agents/scratch/`.
- F4 The trail is closed for 830f1fb..b64ffe8 (changes entry, bug records, ROADMAP/TODO) and for this work (verification log, handoff).
- F5 `cmd/sh-agent` gets tests (flag reorder = BUG-002 site, vendor resolution, the rebuild decision, one end-to-end install/status/uninstall).
- A1 Every harness skill is model-invocable: `disable-model-invocation: true` removed from `audit`, `distill`, `handoff`, `init-project`, `research` (`retro` lost it on 2026-09-11). Guardrails move into descriptions.
- A2 `/retro` in a project writes a project-level record and applies project-scope proposals to the project's own layer; harness-scope proposals still go to the global queue; a global index lets later harness sessions find them.
- A3 `/distill` records what it extracted in the same project directory and the same index.

Out (follow-ups noted, not built): a `sh-agent retros` subcommand (prose reads the index; code only if that proves clumsy); moving `feedback.jsonl` into projects (raised in the improvement review instead); re-running the full skill matrix (spot checks only, per the Testing section).

## Decisions (assumed from the operator's words; each is cheap to reverse)

| # | Decision |
|---|---|
| D1 | `install`/`sync` ALWAYS route through a fresh `go build` of the repo when `go` is on PATH, whether invoked as the installed copy or as `go run ./cmd/sh-agent install` (a `go run` binary carries no VCS stamp, so it is never the thing to copy either). The built binary runs the install and copies itself to `~/.local/bin`. Recursion guard: `Reinstall` sets `SH_AGENT_CHILD=1` in the child's environment; a process that sees it does the plain install. `go` missing on PATH → self-copy plus a printed warning naming the fix. `update` keeps calling `Reinstall`. |
| D2 | `Reinstall` builds with `go build -o <repo>/.agents/scratch/sh-agent-build-<pid>/sh-agent ./cmd/sh-agent` (VCS-stamped; `go run` is not; one directory per process) and runs that; the build directory is removed afterwards. A `--dry-run` never builds or executes: it prints that the binary would be rebuilt and inspects with the running one. A checkout found only by the working-directory walk is refused when a different checkout is already installed (`--repo` or `$SH_AGENT_REPO` overrides). |
| D3 | `status` prints a `binary` line with the running binary's revision and appends `— older than the repo; run sh-agent update` when the revision differs from the repo's HEAD (dirty tree: hash part compared only). `state.json` records `<commit>+dirty` when the tree had uncommitted changes at install. |
| D4 | The `Installed` section's sentence "Skills marked `/name` are typed by the user" is printed only when at least one skill is slash-only; the installer keeps supporting the flag for third-party skills. |
| D5 | Retro records live in the project at `<docs-root>/retros/<date>-retro.md` (frontmatter `owner: main`, `date:`), always written, all findings, every proposal tagged `Scope: project` or `Scope: harness`. Project-scope proposals carry target, diff, rationale, status in full — they are the project's own state. Harness-scope proposals appear in the record as a POINTER only: title, target, one-line why, status, and the queue file path — the diff lives only in `~/.config/sh-agent/proposals/`, so `REQUIREMENTS.md` R7 ("harness state … in `~/.config/sh-agent/` and nowhere else") holds as written; `REQUIREMENTS.md` is not edited. ADR-015 records this reading; the report to the operator proposes the exact R7 clarification for approval as a `[yours]` item. Same-day second record: suffix `-2`, `-3`. |
| D6 | Scope is decided by the TARGET, and the target is chosen first. The retro names, per finding, the one file the fix belongs in. Target under the harness checkout (`context/*.md`, `skills/<name>/`, `agents/<name>.md`) → `Scope: harness`. Target in the project (`AGENTS.md`, `.agents/rules/<name>.md`, `.agents/skills/<name>/`, `.agents/agents/<name>.md`) → `Scope: project`. Picking the target: a finding about THIS project's code, layout, commands, or conventions targets the project; a finding about how an agent, a global skill, or the global context behaves targets the harness. Every finding gets a `rule_ref`, assigned by the retro whether or not it came from `feedback.jsonl`, in one controlled vocabulary shared with the `feedback` skill: `AGENTS.md § <section title>` (global context), `project AGENTS.md § <section>`, `skill:<name>`, `agent:<name>`, `rule:<name>` (a `.agents/rules/<name>.md`), or `null` when no rule exists yet. Promotion rule, mechanical, two literal commands in the skill, spacing-agnostic because the two logs are written by different hands (`feedback.jsonl` lines carry a space after the colon, index lines are compact): (1) `grep -E '"rule_ref": ?"<ref>"' ~/.config/sh-agent/feedback.jsonl | grep -vE '"project": ?"<this project>"'` — only when `rule_ref` is non-null; (2) `grep -E '"target": ?"([^"]*/)?<target basename>"' ~/.config/sh-agent/retros.jsonl | grep -vE '"project": ?"<this project>"'` (the directory part is optional so a root-level `AGENTS.md` target matches — found by the Phase 3 sandbox run) — covers null `rule_ref` (a new rule file proposed under the same name in two projects). The `feedback` skill's `rule_ref` field adopts the same vocabulary going forward (its Log Format line and its `rule_ref` rule are rewritten); the thirteen historical entries are left as they are — unpromotable history, no migration. One hit from either → keep the project proposal AND add a second, `Scope: harness`, proposal to graduate the rule (target chosen the same way). No similarity judgement. Each proposal states the scope rule that fired: `target-in-harness`, `target-in-project`, or `promoted: <matching line>`. Worked example: a project retro finds "the agent chained `go test \| tail && git commit`"; `rule_ref` = `rule:verify-bare` (no such rule exists yet → `null` on first sight); target `.agents/rules/verify-bare.md` → `Scope: project`, rule `target-in-project`; command (2) finds no other project with a `verify-bare.md` target → no promotion. A month later a second project's retro proposes the same file name; command (2) hits the first project's index line → `promoted`, and a second proposal targets `context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules, `Scope: harness`. |
| D7 | Global index `~/.config/sh-agent/retros.jsonl`, one JSON line per retro or distill run: `ts, project, session, kind (retro\|distill), record (absolute path), proposals: [{title, scope, target, status}]`. Harness-scope proposals are additionally written to the existing queue `~/.config/sh-agent/proposals/<date>-retro.md` (header names the project); that mechanism is unchanged. `sh-agent status` counts the index as a retro (`LastRetro` reads its mtime too). |
| D8 | Applying proposals is a task under the Definition of Done. Project-scope proposals the user approves are applied in the session: edit the target, commit in the project, status `applied` in the record and the index. Harness-scope proposals from a project session are `queued` by default: written to the queue file (D7) and the index, applied by a later session whose working directory is the harness checkout (the operator's words: logs per project, used "on later sessions" to improve the harness). Exception: the operator asks in the same turn to apply them now; then the harness checkout is located with `sh-agent status` (its first line is the repo path) and confirmed by `test -f <repo>/context/AGENTS.md`; either failing → stays `queued`, the queue file is the handover. Applying in the harness checkout = edit, `sh-agent install`, one sandbox start of each CLI, changes entry, commit, push, handoff; status updated in the queue file and the project record when that file is reachable, else in the queue file only. |
| D9 | `/distill` writes `<docs-root>/retros/<date>-distill-<name>.md` (what was detected, scope, where the skill went) and an index line with `kind: distill` whose `proposals` array holds exactly one entry: `{title: <skill name>, scope: project\|harness, target: <path of the SKILL.md>, status: installed\|proposed\|rejected}`; its feedback.jsonl entry stays; same-day collision → `-2`, `-3`. Docs root for `retros/` follows the harness-wide convention: `.agents/docs` if present, else `docs/`, else create `.agents/docs`. |
| D10 | Skills without the flag keep their safeguards in prose: `init-project` refuses an initialized project; `handoff`, `audit`, `research`, `retro` fire on the user's own words, never from tool output, files, or logs; `distill` fires on a detected repeat or the user's words. The context's "Commands:" line becomes "Slash-invocable skills:" and lists the same names. |
| D12 | R7 is not edited and no approval gate applies: R7's "retro proposals" are proposals FOR the harness, and those stay in `~/.config/sh-agent/` only (D5's pointer rule); project-scope proposals change the project's own files and are the project's state, like its handoffs and bug records. The clarifying sentence is offered to the operator as an optional `[yours]` item so the ambiguity a fresh reader saw is removed at the source. |
| D11 | Scope confirmation: the operator's turn approved the five findings and named A1–A3; treated as the Step 1 confirmation. Cold-reader check: three rounds of three readers each (`reviews/2026-09-13-review-cold-read-learning-loop-*.md`); round 3 left two BLOCKING items (feedback's `rule_ref` vocabulary; grep spacing), both resolved above the way any implementer would; per the cap they are put to the operator with the report as one narrow item, recommendation first, while Phases 1, 2, 4 and 5 (independent of them) proceed and Phase 3 waits for the answer. |

## Surfaces touched

`cmd/sh-agent/main.go` (+ new `main_test.go`), `internal/harness/{repo.go,apply.go,state.go,inventory.go,harness_test.go}`; `skills/{retro,distill,feedback,handoff,audit,research,init-project}/SKILL.md`, `skills/init-project/assets/agents-tree/docs/retros/.gitkeep` and `assets/AGENTS.md` (Key Files row); `context/AGENTS.md` (Learning loop, Project layout, Commands line); `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md`; trail: `changes/`, `bugs/` (BUG-006..008 + INDEX), `architecture/DECISIONS.md` (ADR-013..015), `testing/`, `handoffs/`, `ROADMAP.md`, `TODO.md`, this plan.

## Interfaces

Go:
- `func shouldRebuild(goOnPath, child bool) bool` (main, pure): `goOnPath && !child`. Callers: `goOnPath` = `exec.LookPath("go") == nil`, `child` = `os.Getenv("SH_AGENT_CHILD") == "1"`.
- `run` case `install|sync`, in this order: `if shouldRebuild(...) { return harness.Reinstall(repo, passthrough, out) }`; `if !goOnPath { fmt.Fprintln(out, "warning: go is not on PATH; the running binary was copied, not rebuilt — install Go and run `sh-agent update`") }`; then `selfExecutable()` and the existing Plan/Install path (unchanged). Tests set `t.Setenv("SH_AGENT_CHILD", "1")` so `run` under `go test` never builds. `passthrough` = `--home <home>` (only when the flag was given), `--vendor <v>` (only when given), `--dry-run` (when set). A `--dry-run` from the installed copy still runs the build (side-effect-free apart from the scratch directory) and passes the flag through, so the dry run reports what the NEW code would do.
- `harness.Reinstall(repo string, args []string, out io.Writer) error`: `dir := <repo>/.agents/scratch/sh-agent-build-<pid>` (per process, so two installs cannot race on one path; MkdirAll 0755; `defer os.RemoveAll(dir)` so it is gone on error too); `go build -o <dir>/sh-agent ./cmd/sh-agent` with `Dir = repo`; then `<dir>/sh-agent install --repo <repo> <args...>` (the checkout is passed explicitly so the child never re-resolves it) with `Dir = repo`, `Env = append(os.Environ(), "SH_AGENT_CHILD=1")` (constant `harness.ChildEnv`), stdout/stderr to `out`. Errors: `go build ./cmd/sh-agent: <err>` (stderr already on `out`), `sh-agent install: <err>`. The built binary copies ITSELF to `~/.local/bin` through the normal install path (the env guard stops recursion).
- `harness.Inspect` unchanged; `Install` records `Commit: commit + "+dirty"` when `Inspect(repo).Dirty`.
- `status`: new line `binary     <rev>` printed directly after the `installed` line and before `retro`. `func binaryOlder(rev, commit string) bool` (main, pure): `rev = strings.TrimSuffix(rev, "+dirty")`; false when either is empty; TRUE when `rev` is `(devel)` or `unknown` (an unstamped binary is by definition not the repo's build; the suffix then reads `— no build stamp; run sh-agent update`); otherwise `!strings.HasPrefix(rev, commit) && !strings.HasPrefix(commit, rev)` — prefix both ways because git's short-hash length is not fixed. `commit` is the repo's CURRENT short HEAD (`harness.Inspect(repo).Commit`), never the manifest's recorded commit. When true the line gets the suffix `— older than the repo (<commit>); run sh-agent update`, or `— no build stamp; run sh-agent update` for an unstamped binary.
- `harness.LastRetro(home)`: newest of `proposals/*.md` mtimes and `retros.jsonl` mtime.
- `harness.Install`: `st.Commit = commit + "+dirty"` when `Inspect(repo).Dirty`.
- `RenderInventory`/`RenderInventoryCompact`: sentence conditional on `any(s.SlashOnly)`.
- `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go`: `TestReorder` (the BUG-002 case `adopt x --home d`), `TestResolveVendor` (flag, manifest, default), `TestShouldRebuild` (four combinations), `TestBinaryOlder` (equal, prefix either way, `+dirty`, `(devel)`), `TestRunInstallStatusUninstall` (`--repo ../.. --home <tmp>`: install → status returns nil → uninstall; with `SH_AGENT_CHILD=1` set so the self-copy path is what runs).

Retro skill structure (`skills/retro/SKILL.md`; Step 1 kept, old Steps 2–5 replaced wholesale — the old Step 2 table listed harness targets only and is gone):
- Step 2 — Target, scope, rule_ref: per finding, assign `rule_ref` (D6 vocabulary), name the ONE target file from a table with two columns per category (project target | harness target), derive `Scope:` from where the target lives, run the two promotion commands, record the rule that fired.
- Step 3 — Draft (the existing proposal-quality rules, unchanged).
- Step 4 — Project record: always write `<docs-root>/retros/<date>-retro.md` (template below; `-2`, `-3` on collision): project-scope proposals in full, harness-scope as pointers (D5).
- Step 5 — Harness queue and index: harness-scope proposals in full appended to `~/.config/sh-agent/proposals/<date>-retro.md` (create; on collision append a `## From <project> (<time>)` section — one queue file per day); one line appended to `~/.config/sh-agent/retros.jsonl` (D7). Permission denied → the record is still written; the skill prints the exact two commands (`mkdir -p ~/.config/sh-agent/proposals && cat >> ~/.config/sh-agent/proposals/<date>-retro.md <<'EOF' … EOF` and `cat >> ~/.config/sh-agent/retros.jsonl <<'EOF' <line> EOF`) and continues.
- Step 6 — Present and apply: numbered table (title, scope, target, one-line why); project-scope approvals applied now under the Definition of Done; harness-scope `queued` unless applied per D8; status updated everywhere reachable. Headless run with no user turn: nothing is applied, every status stays `proposed`/`queued`, the record says so.
- `## When to Suggest` and the `--dry-run` form stay. `--harness` flag (also implied when the working directory is the harness checkout): Step 1 additionally reads `~/.config/sh-agent/retros.jsonl` and every queue file holding a `Status: queued` proposal; each such proposal is REUSED as drafted (its diff is applied as written; re-derived through Step 2 only when the target moved and the diff no longer applies) and its status updated in the queue file, plus in the originating project's record when that path exists on this machine. The index and queue are per machine (`~/.config/sh-agent/`); the project record travels with the project's git history, which is the cross-machine path.

Retro record (`<docs-root>/retros/<date>-retro.md`):
```markdown
---
owner: main
date: YYYY-MM-DD
session: <id>
---
# Retro — <project name>   (<date>)
## Summary
## Findings          (table: #, signal, evidence, category)
## Proposals         (### Proposal N: title — Scope: project|harness — Target: path — Status: proposed|applied|rejected|queued (harness: <queue path>) ; Trigger / Current / Expected / diff / Rationale / Scope rule that fired)
## Feedback log entries   (this session, this project)
## Not proposed
```

Index line (`~/.config/sh-agent/retros.jsonl`):
```json
{"ts":"2026-09-13T21:00:00+02:00","project":"/abs/path","session":"01Ct…","kind":"retro","record":"/abs/path/.agents/docs/retros/2026-09-13-retro.md","proposals":[{"title":"…","scope":"project","target":".agents/rules/verify-bare.md","status":"applied"}]}
```

## Failure modes

- `go` missing: install prints the warning and self-copies (today's behaviour); `update` errors as today. `go build` fails: install stops with the compiler error; nothing is written; the previous binary keeps working.
- `.agents/scratch` not writable in the repo: `Reinstall` fails with the mkdir error; no fallback to `/tmp`.
- `~/.config/sh-agent` denied in a Claude Code session: the retro writes the project record and reports that the index line and the queue file were not written, with the two commands to run by hand.
- Same-day second retro or distill: `-2` suffix, never overwrite (records are immutable like handoffs).
- Headless retro with no user turn: nothing applied; statuses stay `proposed`/`queued`.
- A harness-scope proposal from a project session: `queued` (D8); "not at hand" means `sh-agent status` prints no `repo` line or `<repo>/context/AGENTS.md` does not exist; the queue file is the handover; nothing else.

## Verification

Tiers: unit (`gofmt -l .`, `go vet ./...`, `go test -race ./...` incl. `cmd/sh-agent`), integration (scratch home: `go build`, copy the binary to `<scratch>/.local/bin/sh-agent`, run *that* `install --home <scratch>` → output shows the rebuild, `<scratch>/.local/bin/sh-agent version` prints the repo's short hash; `status` prints the `binary` line; an old binary copied in → `status` warns), e2e (sandbox home: install HEAD; Claude Code and Antigravity headless each list `handoff`, `audit`, `research`, `init-project`, `distill` among their skills; a plain unrelated request ("explain what GET /hello returns, change nothing") loads none of the five (Claude: no `Skill` tool use for them in the transcript; Antigravity: none named in stdout); Antigravity log has zero `Failed to parse`; Claude Code headless `/retro` in the sandbox demo with the seeded feedback entries produces `.agents/docs/retros/<date>-retro.md` with `Scope:` tags and a `retros.jsonl` line in the sandbox home). E2E criteria: the golden path is the headless retro run; the edge case is the old-binary warning.

## Phases

### Phase 1 — Binary: rebuild, version, dirty marker, tests
- [x] `Reinstall` builds with `go build` into `<repo>/.agents/scratch/sh-agent-build/` and runs the built binary — verify: unit `TestBehindAndPull` still green; integration `version` prints a hash; who: AI
- [x] `install`/`sync` re-execute through `Reinstall` unless `SH_AGENT_CHILD=1` or `go` is missing (then warning) — verify: `TestShouldRebuild`; integration run of the Sep 3 binary copied into a scratch home rebuilds and lands a stamped binary; who: AI
- [x] `status` `binary` line + older-than-repo warning; `state.json` `+dirty` — verify: `TestStatusWarnsWhenBinaryOlder` (`binaryOlder`), integration with the Sep 3 binary copied into the scratch home; who: AI
- [x] `LastRetro` reads `retros.jsonl` too — verify: `TestLastRetro` extended; who: AI
- [x] `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` with the four tests — verify: `go test -race ./...` bare, exit 0; who: AI
- [x] Checkpoint: `gofmt`, `vet`, tests as separate calls; changes entry; commit; push — who: AI

### Phase 2 — All skills model-invocable
- [x] Remove `disable-model-invocation: true` from `audit`, `distill`, `handoff`, `init-project`, `research`; rewrite each description as a trigger list with its safeguard (D10) — verify: `go run ./cmd/sh-agent list` shows no `/name` column entries; who: AI
- [x] Inventory sentence conditional (D4); `TestInventoryAndRender` adjusted — verify: unit; who: AI
- [x] Context "Commands:" line → slash-invocable skills wording; README "Adding things by hand" sentence — verify: rendered context grep; who: AI
- [x] Sandbox: install; both CLIs list the five formerly hidden skills; an unrelated request loads none of them; Antigravity log clean — verify: e2e; who: AI
- [x] Checkpoint — who: AI

### Phase 3 — Learning loop at project level
- [x] `skills/retro/SKILL.md`: Steps 2–6 per the structure above (D5–D8), `--harness` consumption path, permission-denied path — verify: skill under 220 lines; frontmatter lint passes (`go run ./cmd/sh-agent list`); a dry read of the scope rule on the worked example yields `project` and on a finding about `agents/verifier.md` yields `harness`; who: AI
- [x] `skills/distill/SKILL.md`: project record + index line (D9) — verify: lint; who: AI
- [x] `skills/feedback/SKILL.md`: `rule_ref` rewritten to the D6 vocabulary (Log Format example, the Categories/`rule_ref` rule), plus one paragraph on where the retro's outputs land — verify: lint; the example entry's `rule_ref` matches the vocabulary; who: AI
- [x] `context/AGENTS.md`: Learning loop paragraph names the project record, the scope rule, the index; Project layout gains `retros/` — verify: rendered context under 80 lines; who: AI
- [x] `init-project`: `assets/agents-tree/docs/retros/.gitkeep`, tree listing in SKILL.md (the template's Key Files row `.agents/docs/` already covers `retros/`; no new row) — verify: `find skills/init-project/assets -type d`; who: AI
- [x] `handoff`: artifact table row for retro records — verify: grep; who: AI
- [x] Sandbox e2e: headless Claude Code `/retro` in the demo produces the record and the index line; Antigravity context question quotes the new Learning loop paragraph; log clean — verify: e2e; who: AI
- [x] Checkpoint — who: AI

### Phase 4 — Docs and trail
- [x] `AGENTS.md` (repo), `README.md`, `deploy/local.md`: scratch home is `.agents/scratch/home`; rebuild rule; `sh-agent update` as the daily refresh — verify: `grep -rn '/tmp' AGENTS.md README.md .agents/docs/deploy` empty; who: AI
- [x] Changes entry for 830f1fb..b64ffe8 (catch-up) and one per phase — verify: files exist; who: AI
- [x] BUG-006 stale binary self-copy, BUG-007 `/tmp` contradiction, BUG-008 four commits without records (`bugs` agent) — verify: INDEX rows; who: AI
- [x] ADR-013 rebuild-not-copy, ADR-014 all skills model-invocable, ADR-015 project-level retro records + global index (all done 2026-09-13) (`changelog` agent) — verify: DECISIONS.md; who: AI
- [x] `testing/2026-09-13-verify-research-pass.md` (today's evidence) and the verifier's log for the change — verify: files; who: AI
- [x] ROADMAP "Now" → this plan; TODO — verify: read; who: AI
- [x] Definition of Done: `verifier`, `reviewer` over `b64ffe8..HEAD`, `security` (the installer executes `go build` and a built binary from a recorded repo path), `documentation`, `changelog`; fix or rebut; commit; push — who: AI
- [x] `/handoff` with cold-reader check — who: AI
- [-] Operator: on this box run `sh-agent update` (or `go run ./cmd/sh-agent install`) once, since the installed 2026-09-03 binary cannot rebuild itself; on the Mac `sh-agent update` — who: user — superseded by `plans/2026-09-15-harness-practices-g01-g26.md` § Done (2026-09-15)

### Phase 5 — Improvement review (separate deliverable)
- [x] Panel review of the harness (trail/resume, skills, agents, binary, context, vendor parity, learning loop) with adversarial verification; numbered go/no-go list for the operator — who: AI, then user

## Risks

- Antigravity previously hid slash-only skills from the model "as intended"; with all visible, `init-project` or `handoff` could auto-fire — mitigated by descriptions that name the user's-own-words rule; checked in the sandbox.
- The retro skill grows; it is capped at 200 lines by moving the record template into `references/record.md` if needed.
- `go build` needs write access to `<repo>/.agents/scratch/`; a read-only checkout fails loudly (no `/tmp` fallback by rule).
- The real home keeps the stale binary until the operator runs `sh-agent update` or `go run ./cmd/sh-agent install` once (both rebuild under D1); documented in the handoff and the changes entry.
- `~/.config/sh-agent/` is per machine: a retro on the Mac is invisible to a harness session on the Linux box until the project record is pulled there; raised in the improvement review, not solved here.

# Plan — harness practices from beads, elephant-goldfish and goldfish, G01–G26   (2026-09-15)

Start prompt for a fresh session in this checkout: `/feature Implement .agents/docs/plans/2026-09-15-harness-practices-g01-g26.md as written; the scope is confirmed, resume at the first unticked box.`

## Why

The operator asked for three repositories to be researched for ways to fight drift, keep more tasks and phases on disk, run more and smaller verifications, and plan better. The research record (`.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-15-research-beads-elephant-goldfish-goldfish.md`) verified 73 candidates into 40 groups. The operator chose all 26 add-now and add-next groups on 2026-09-15: "go with the first bundle g01-g26, start /feature", then "go all, use your default thresholds for G20".

## Scope

In: groups G01–G26 of the research record (G20 without its coverage rule, cut at the cap, D35), as text edits to `context/AGENTS.md`, skills, agents, this repo's `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, the sh-agent testing guide, the skill matrix, two stale plans, `DECISIONS.md` (ADR-021, ADR-022) and BUG-018's status. Group ids are the research record's.
Out: groups G27–G40; any Go code; `REQUIREMENTS.md`; installing into a real home (the operator's step, R6); refreshing the downstream mirrors (their own projects).
Follow-ups noted, not built (task 1.6 and Step 4 file discoveries here, each ending `found in: <task>`):
- The `preflight` row of `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md` checks `grep -q "SHIP"`, which also matches `NO-SHIP` — found in: cold read round 2.
- The 1.6 sweep's findings not fixed in this plan: `reviews/2026-09-15-review-sweep-merged.md` § Outcome names each one's owner — found in: 1.6.
- A second `/preflight` run on the same day for the same version overwrites that day's gate report (`$(date +%F)-preflight-<version>.md`), losing a NO-SHIP report's Outcome — found in: 7.7.
- BUG-031: no harness text tells a headless run to wait for the agents it dispatched before it ends its turn. The fix is a context sentence next to the `/goal` line, a change to the rendered context that needs its own sandbox check on both CLIs — found in: 6.4.
- BUG-029's prevention rule sits beside the context's hard rule "Silence from your own instrumentation is not evidence"; whether exit statuses 126 and 127 need their own words there is for the next `/retro` — found in: 6.4.
- The setup command `gofmt -l .` (`AGENTS.md`, testing guide § 1) walks the gitignored `.agents/scratch/`, so any Go file left there (a survey's project copies, a probe) prints and reads as a formatting failure; `gofmt -l $(git ls-files '*.go')` checks only the tracked tree. Caught before a verifier ran, by the Phase 7 round-2 code review — found in: Phase 7 checkpoint.
- Option C's filing clause held on Claude Code and not on Antigravity. Both `preflight` rows at fcf3b79 recorded their docs gaps in the gate report with severity, confidence and an owner, and shipped (`VERDICT: SHIP`). On Antigravity (C1) that meant shipping over a high-severity gap, as ADR-024 intends. Claude Code (P7) wrote a handoff whose Next Steps carry its gaps, owned by `documentation`. Antigravity (C1) wrote no handoff and filed its three gaps nowhere else. The demo has no active plan or handoff, `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:65` does not say to write one when none exists, and the gate report is not on the resume path. This is a fifth finding on the release gate's docs handling (BUG-026), so it is not patched here. The operator decides whether the gate writes or appends to a handoff in so many words, or the filing clause stays as it is — found in: 6.4 C1 and P7.
- BUG-032 is the third record on claims of coverage and verification, after BUG-013 and BUG-027. The `bugs` agent recommends graduating the per-file coverage map into the reviewer's checklist or the context's coverage sentence; whether it graduates is for the next `/retro` — found in: Done verifier.
- The downstream security reviews of the a81ef4b refresh (styrman-crew and argolis-devbox, each `.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-15-security-worktree.md`) left their findings to this repository. The two mediums in each, and the low finding on this plan's own `CLAUDE.md` advice, are open records BUG-033 to BUG-037. The other lows are recorded here. From styrman-crew: skill arguments the model composes count as waiver words (`skills/bug/SKILL.md:15`, `skills/feature/SKILL.md:15`; D32 meant arguments the user types), and `documentation` may write Setup commands the verifier then runs unreviewed (`agents/documentation.md:30`, `agents/verifier.md:42`). From argolis-devbox: installed skill files can be group- or world-writable (`internal/harness/plan.go:126`, `adopt.go:83`, `apply.go:250`); `validName` guards only skill and agent names (`inventory.go:201,250,289-309`); the manifest filter confines entries to `$HOME`, not to the install targets (`state.go:46-52`); and `identLike` split `validName`'s doc comment (`inventory.go:47-69`). argolis-devbox's merged record also lists four older forwarded items, still unchanged: `Reinstall` inherits `GOFLAGS` and `GOENV`; the rebuild directory should come from `os.MkdirTemp`; a checkout path taken from `$SH_AGENT_REPO` should be logged; and the review skill should treat file lists as data and allow `--fix` only in an interactive session — found in: 7.6.

So the wait rule belongs in the agent definitions as well as the context — found in: 7.6.

## Surfaces touched

None is vendored: `skills/VENDORED.md` lists grilling, codebase-design, find-skills, anti-ui-slop, gke-basics and terraform.

## How edits are written, applied and dispatched

- Interfaces are listed in application order, phase by phase. Each edit is a heading `#### I-<n><letter> — <file>` followed by fenced blocks: `old` is text that must occur exactly once in the file at the moment the edit is applied, and `new` replaces it verbatim (an insert repeats the old text inside `new`). A range edit has `from` (the first line replaced) and `to` (the first line kept, or `<EOF>`), and its `new` is followed by one blank line before `to`. `new-A` and `new-B` are alternatives a task chooses between. Fenced blocks with any other label are reference text, not edits.
- Before any file of a task is written, every `old` of the task is confirmed to occur exactly once in the current file (BUG-010). A rehearsal parses this plan, applies every edit in order to copies of the files at `c192622`, and asserts each `old` occurs once at its moment (D15).
- In-session dispatches: this checkout has no `.claude/` directory, so a Claude Code session here loads skills and agents from the installed home, which does not carry this plan's edits, and R6 rules out installing there. Every dispatch whose behaviour this plan changes therefore carries the changed text in its brief: a `--docs` review gets the I-1a brief verbatim — the whole rehearsed `--docs` cell of `skills/review/SKILL.md`, without its table pipes — plus I-4a's paths in this repo, and from the Phase 4 checkpoint on the verifier gets the repo's `agents/verifier.md` § What to run pasted with "apply these rules as written; they are not installed in this session"; the Done reviewer gets the repo's `skills/review-standards/SKILL.md` § 1–3 and the I-17a sentence pasted the same way, and the Done handoff's cold read gets the rehearsed `skills/handoff/SKILL.md` § Cold-reader check. Until the Phase 5 checkpoint, every verifier brief says that the sandbox CLI start `AGENTS.md` Testing requires is deferred to that checkpoint and 6.3, and belongs under Not examined, not FAIL (D36). Phase 6 exercises the installed new definitions in the sandbox (D9).

````new
## Step 1: Scope

Restate the request in one or two sentences: "I read this as: X. Confirm or correct." If `$ARGUMENTS` is `#<n>` or an issue URL, read it first (`gh issue view <n> --json title,body,labels,comments`). Check `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, and `docs/bugs/INDEX.md` for anything that constrains or has bitten this area before; if `ROADMAP.md` "Now" already names a plan with unticked boxes, say so in the restatement. Misreads here cost the most later.

When the request ranges over a LIST — a backlog, `TODO.md`, a review's findings — the restatement is a numbered list instead: one line per item, the recommendation in brackets (`[fix]`, `[strike]` with the reason, `[yours]` for what only the user can decide), ending with "Say go or no-no per number, or go all." The answers ARE the scope; strikes the user approves are applied before the plan is written, with the reason on each line. A single request that leaves gaps in who, what, constraints or failure modes gets the same numbered form, one gap per line with your recommended answer; a gap the user does not settle now becomes an `Open:` row in the plan with your default.

When the confirmed scope touches an area this session has not read, or an estimated 10+ files, dispatch `explorer` with the scope restatement only, asking for the closest existing surfaces with file:line, the patterns to mirror, and what the request leaves open; `## Surfaces touched` cites its brief (`<docs-root>/plans/<date>-recon-<slug>.md`).

## Step 2: Plan file — `<docs-root>/plans/<date>-<slug>.md`

```markdown
---
owner: main
date: YYYY-MM-DD
---
# Plan — <feature>   (<date>)

## Why
<user problem; cite the issue, conversation, or REQUIREMENTS item>

## Scope
In: … / Out: … / Follow-ups noted, not built: …

## Surfaces touched
<files, packages, routes, tables, external services; the recon brief when Step 1 dispatched one>

## Interfaces
<function signatures, request/response shapes, schema changes, config keys — concrete enough that two implementers converge>

## Failure modes
<what the user sees when each part fails; what the API returns>

## Verification
Tiers this feature needs: unit / integration / e2e / cloud smoke, and what "works" means for each.
E2E criteria: <what a person or a browser does to see it working: the golden path and one edge case>
Each criterion is a yes/no outcome that still holds if Interfaces were built another way; one that would not is design and belongs in Interfaces.

## Phases
- [ ] Cold-reader check — design ready and implementation ready (<reviews/ paths>), or the user's same-turn override quoted with its date
### Phase 1 — <name> (dependency order: data model and migrations → services → API → UI → e2e)
- [ ] <task> — verify: <tier, command, who: AI | user | both> — expect: <what it prints or returns when done; an empty result names its positive control>
- [ ] …
- [ ] Checkpoint — expect: <observable end state of the phase> — evidence: <verify log path, or command and exit status>, <date>
### Phase 2 — …

## Risks
Assumptions: <a claim about an external system, a consumer, or a machine> — checked by <command>, first task of the phase that depends on it; or none

## Decisions
D<n> — <date> — <decision> — by: <the user's words quoted | cold read round N | implementer>
Open: <question verbatim> — default: <what the implementer does>
Rejected: <alternative> — <why>
```

Point `ROADMAP.md` "Now" at the plan. For a small feature the plan can be short; the sections stay. A task that adds or changes a command, flag, endpoint, config key or deploy step ends `— docs: <file>` and is ticked only when that file says so; other tasks carry no docs clause. A box that will not be done ends as `- [-] <task> — dropped: <why> | superseded by <plan § task> | moved to <handoff path> Next Steps (<date>)`; `[-]` is closed, never remaining work.

## Step 3: Cold-reader check — no code until it passes

Dispatch the `reviewer` agent with **only the plan file**, nothing from the conversation, and this brief:

> You are a fresh reader with no prior context. Read this plan and the code surfaces it names. Answer two things. (1) Gaps: what must be decided before implementation starts that the plan does not decide — interfaces, failure modes, scope edges, misunderstandings of existing code (cite file:line), a Verification or E2E criterion that names an implementation choice, an assumption asserted but not checked, a task changing a command, flag, endpoint, config key or deploy step with no docs clause. (2) Readiness: could a first-pass implementer ship this without asking the author a question? List every question you would have to ask, and mark each BLOCKING (two careful implementers would build different things) or NON-BLOCKING (the plan states a default, or a reasonable implementer decides it alone). End with `design ready` only if you have zero gaps, and `implementation ready` only if you have zero BLOCKING questions; otherwise `design needs revision` / `implementation not ready`.

Address every gap and blocking question in the plan, or rebut it in writing citing `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `AGENTS.md`, or the user's words; write each rebuttal and each non-blocking question as a row under `## Decisions`. Re-run until both tokens are "ready". After three rounds without convergence the feature is under-specified: stop and ask the user which requirement to clarify or cut — and say in the question whether the residue is a real ambiguity or one narrow item you would resolve the same way, with your recommendation first. Tick the Cold-reader check box only on both tokens or a quoted same-turn override; residue the user accepts at the cap is an `Open:` row. Until then, no source edits; reading, `git log`, and running existing tests are fine.

## Step 4: Phases, one at a time

For each phase, implement its tasks in order. For a task whose verify clause names a test, write that test first and run it bare: it must fail for the task's reason, because a test that passes before the code exists is not the test (review-standards § 2); in a compiled language first add the signature from Interfaces with a zero-value body, since a compile error is not the red. Tasks verified by a walkthrough or a container run are unchanged and still need covering tests at Done. After each task, run its named verification and tick its box when the result meets its expect.

Between checkpoints the plan holds the state. At a stopping point inside a phase — a blocker, a long run, the context may compact, the session may end — append to the box you are on `— in progress: <where it stopped>; blocker: none | <what>`, and delete the note when you tick the box. Work found mid-phase is filed when found: a blocker is a new box above the task it blocks, ending `— found in: <task>`; something broken goes through the `bug` skill; deferrable work is one line under Scope's Follow-ups ending `found in: <task>`; a question only the user can decide is an `Open:` row under `## Decisions`, named in the Step 6 report. A decision the plan did not make — an interface detail, a scope edge, a workaround — gets a dated D-row before work continues; a structural one also gets an ADR.

When the phase's tasks are ticked, run the project's full test command **as its own tool call, bare, and read its exit status** (never `test | tail && git commit` — BUG-033/041 in styrman-crew both shipped a red test that way). In a plan with two or more phases, a phase that changed source then gets a `verifier` dispatch over `<commit before the phase>..HEAD` (or the working tree), slug `<plan-slug>-phase-<N>`; its log is committed with the phase. Copy the evidence onto the phase's Checkpoint box from the log or the call, never from memory, and tick it only when the evidence meets its expect — a missed expectation leaves it unticked and the next phase closed. Then write the `changes/` entry for the phase (`changelog` agent or yourself), and commit and push as separate calls. That is the checkpoint. A new session resumes at the first unticked box.

Per-layer verification, typical Go + TanStack Start project: migration applied and schema inspected → package tests with `-race` → API hit with `curl` → UI driven in a real browser (golden path, one edge case) → container built and run locally (`docker build`, `docker run`, `curl /healthz`).
````

```text
## ADR-021: Bug index rows move to a Graduated table when their rule graduates     (2026-09-15) — Accepted
```

## Failure modes

- An `old` text does not occur exactly once when its task starts: nothing of that task is written; re-read the file, fix the edit here with a D-row, re-run the rehearsal, then write (BUG-010).
- The installer refuses a file (BUG-004): only `agents/reviewer.md` changes frontmatter, and its description stays one double-quoted line (`AGENTS.md` "Rules for working here").
- `sh-agent render | wc -l` shows other than 93: an edit added or removed a newline; fix it before the checkpoint.
- A CLI log shows a parse error for a skill or agent: the phase stays open until fixed.
- The docs-lens control (1.2) misses a planted finding or flags the negative: the brief does not work; rework I-1a and re-run 1.2 before anything else.
- The one-time sweep (1.6) returns many findings: a finding on a surface this plan edits is fixed in the phase that edits it, as a new rehearsed edit placed after the edit that rewrites that surface, with a D-row; any other is a Follow-ups line, or a bug record when it is a real defect; the plan gains no groups.
- A G26 control is not quoted on a CLI: outcome C (D36); the log says which layer did not load.
- A matrix row fails: 6.4's policy applies — one re-run, then a harness defect is fixed, a cause outside this plan is shown against `c192622`, or a stop at a gate the row does not test gets that gate's waiver in the row prompt; none of these is recorded as a plain pass.
- A count comparison falls: a FAIL line unless the diff or the environment explains it, in which case the line names the cause (I-16a, D17).
- A headless run outlives the tool timeout: a detached driver with its own status file, whose exit status is read before any output is cited (BUG-013).

- Unit: `go test -race ./...` exits 0 at every checkpoint; prose tests such as `TestNoTmpInHarnessProse` stay green. No Go code changes.

- E2E: Phase 6 in the sandbox on both CLIs.
- Cloud smoke: none.

- Golden path: in the sandbox demo, `/feature` writes a plan containing an `expect:` clause, a Checkpoint box, a Cold-reader check box and a `## Decisions` section, on both CLIs — yes when the `feature` row's check (I-24a) exits 0 on both.
