D45 — 2026-09-15 — R2 stays: a project's `CLAUDE.md` is the single line `@AGENTS.md` and content belongs in `AGENTS.md`; `/init-project` leaves a kept `CLAUDE.md` untouched and says what it means for each CLI (merged review R2-3), and README's note on an existing `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` follows R2 — by: the operator, "Yes. We should keep the AGENTS.md style. Do your recommendation."
D46 — 2026-09-15 — the release gate records each Step 4 docs finding with severity like a Step 2 finding; one the newest prior gate report's Outcome rebutted, same statement at the same file:line, is cited and not raised again; only a Step 4 REQUEST CHANGES verdict or high-severity finding blocks, and the rest are `left` with an owner; this fixes R2-1 and R2-2 and closes BUG-026 (ADR-023) — by: the operator, "Do your recommendation."
D47 — 2026-09-15 — `/init-project` updates a scaffold an older harness wrote: when `.agents/docs/changes/` has entries it adds only missing template files and directories, missing `.claude` links and missing `.gitignore` lines, and never rewrites or deletes what the project wrote (`REQUIREMENTS.md`, an existing `AGENTS.md` except the R2 fold, `DECISIONS.md`, existing deploy guides, trail files, `INDEX.md` rows, project rules, skills and agents); a note under a title that differs from the template's is shown and replaced only on the user's yes; a kept deploy guide's missing template headings are named in the summary, not added; a bare `docs/` trail with no `.agents/docs/` stops for the user; one commit, `init: update scaffold to current templates`, or none when nothing changed. A read-only survey of seven older scaffolds (the sandbox demo, argolis-devbox, homey-troubleshooting, ranta-rankare, styrman-crew, unifi-home-network, valkompass) shaped it; its designed rewrite of openings from an asset of earlier template text, and its automatic deploy sections, were dropped after the critique found they rewrite an append-only `DECISIONS.md` and misfire on renamed headings, for this shorter show-and-ask rule — by: the operator, "Make sure the ./init-project skill can be run to \"update\" the harness in projects that have used the olderharness."
D48 — 2026-09-15 — the harness is installed into this box's real home once every change is committed; the operator installs on the Mac later; the two downstream mirrors of this harness, styrman-crew `image/harness/` and argolis-devbox `deploy/harness/` (read as the "styrman-harness and argolis-devbox" of the request), are refreshed and committed locally but not pushed, because an argolis-devbox push deploys to its VM and styrman-crew ships a mirror only through a release — by: the operator, "Install on this box. I will install on my mac later. --- Also prepare styrman-harness and argolis-devbox with the updates."
D49 — 2026-09-15 — the release gate's docs review is advisory: `/preflight` Step 4 still runs the `--docs` lens over `<base>..HEAD` and records each docs gap in the gate report with severity, confidence and an owner, but no docs gap blocks, because the Definition of Done's task-time `/review --docs` is where a docs finding blocks; Step 5's docs clause, D46's rebuttal carry-forward and the coverage rule tried in its place are gone. The Phase 7 reviews' three findings on the carry-forward and the coverage review's four, among them a gate that could ship unresolved docs findings, were the third and fourth rounds on this mechanism (BUG-026); ADR-024 supersedes ADR-023 — by: the operator, "Everything is approved. Go go go.", approving the recommended option C
D50 — 2026-09-15 — 6.4's comparison did not show an outside cause: `bug`, `review-project` and `preflight` on Antigravity passed at c192622 in 230–504 s, where each of this tree's two attempts ran into the 20-minute print timeout. Passes 1 and 2 ran five CLI processes at once (Claude Code at `-P 3` beside Antigravity at `-P 2`); the comparison ran three Antigravity rows at once and nothing else, later in the evening. Load and hour differ between the two sides, so before a row is called a harness defect the same four rows run once more at this tree's HEAD exactly as the comparison ran them (`run-one-v2.sh`, `xargs -P 3`, label C1, after the reinstall is checked for rc=0 and drift none). A row C1 passes is recorded as caused outside this plan, the load or the service at that hour, with a1, a2, B1 and C1 as its evidence, and it is not counted as a pass. A row C1 fails the same way is a harness defect under the `bug` skill — by: implementer, under the operator's "Everything is approved. Go go go."
D51 — 2026-09-16 — the two downstream mirrors are refreshed from a81ef4b, the last commit before the plan closes. Each recipe starts from a clean checkout, and nothing is pushed, because an argolis-devbox push deploys (D48). Among the paths a mirror copies, the closing commit changes only `ROADMAP.md`'s "Now" line. Each mirror's `COMMIT` therefore names a harness commit whose installed files and code are the final ones. The operator's refresh for a release re-runs the recipe at that day's harness HEAD — by: implementer, from D48 and the recipes in styrman-crew `image/harness/VENDORED.md` and argolis-devbox `deploy/harness/VENDORED.md`
D52 — 2026-09-16 — BUG-034 narrowly reverses D35 for one row: a security report that `/preflight` Step 2 owes and that is missing, has no `## Not examined` section, or names a path from the release diff under it blocks the release; every other row keeps D35's cut. BUG-033 adds the shadowing agent to the same list — by: the operator, "Security row only" and "Refuse to dispatch on a clash"
Open: G26 outcome A, B or C — default: decided by 5.1; an unquoted control means C (D36)
Rejected: several smaller plans — the order constraints (G02 before G03, G06 before G21, G22's four lines in one commit) belong in one place
Rejected: a per-phase `documentation` dispatch for docs clauses — the main agent ticks docs clauses, and `documentation` runs at Done

title: Research — beads, elephant-goldfish and goldfish against this harness (2026-09-15)
body:
# Research — beads, elephant-goldfish and goldfish against this harness   (2026-09-15)

## Question

The operator asked for three repositories to be researched in full and weighed against this harness: `gastownhall/beads`, `vshvedov/elephant-goldfish` and `lukacf/goldfish`. Can their skills and ways of working merge into what the harness already has? The interests named were drift, more tasks and phases, more and smaller verifications, and planning. The deliverable is a table of add or not, each row with a short explanation, a recommendation, and what the change would do.

## Method

- Shallow clones in `.agents/scratch/research/` (gitignored): beads `f56632a` (2026-09-12), elephant-goldfish `b8ebb3d` (2026-05-12), goldfish `5dbe820` (2026-07-08).
- Six read-only readers: two for beads, one for elephant-goldfish, two for goldfish, one mapping the harness. One proposer per repo then wrote twenty add, adapt or skip candidates each, sixty in all.
- Three independent skeptics checked every candidate, each prompted to refute. The harness lens asked whether the harness already does it. The source lens asked whether the repo really does it and what it needs. The fit lens checked R1 to R7, the non-goals and the ADR-009 context budget. A completeness critic, a second round for uncovered mechanisms and one judge of the whole set followed.
- The critic named eight mechanisms no candidate covered. A second round wrote thirteen more candidates, eight from beads and five from goldfish, and the same three lenses checked them. A set judge then merged all seventy-three into forty groups, measured the cumulative cost per file, listed conflicts and ordered a first bundle.
- The first run's verification stage failed on a model usage limit. A resume re-ran finished agents, so it was stopped, and a new run read the cached candidates from files; the failure is recorded as BUG-017. Readers and first-round proposers ran on Fable 5.1; everything after ran on Opus 5.
- The main agent spot-checked the footprint facts below against the clones, and the harness findings under "Drift found in the harness itself" against git history.

## The three repositories

**beads (`bd`), MIT.** A Go CLI issue tracker for coding agents. Every unit of work is an issue in a Dolt SQL database under `.beads/`; typed dependency edges form a graph; `bd ready` returns the claimable frontier; agents claim, close, and file `discovered-from` work. Agent behaviour is injected by `bd prime` at session start and after compaction, through a `SessionStart` hook that `bd setup claude` writes into `.claude/settings.json` (`cmd/bd/setup/claude.go:63,279-287`). Embedded Dolt needs a CGO build (`beads_nocgo.go:45`), Dolt is the only backend (`docs/cli-reference/init.md:13`), and `bd init` manages five git hooks (`cmd/bd/hooks.go:24`). Its agent skill (`plugins/beads/skills/beads/`) carries practices that work without the tool: the two-week test (`SKILL.md:23`), overwrite-only handoff notes (`resources/WORKFLOWS.md:368`), and ready fronts instead of phases (`resources/WORKFLOWS.md:147`).

**elephant-goldfish, MIT.** Prose only: 31 markdown and yaml files, no script and no hook (`git ls-files`). Five commands per vendor implement the elephant and goldfish pattern: brainstorm, prd, new-feature, fix-bug and precommit-review. The elephant is the full-context session; a goldfish is a fresh subagent given only an artifact. Its core was researched and largely adopted on 2026-09-03 (`.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-03-research-harness-strategies.md`). This second read looked for what the first one missed. The repo states its own cost: "The price is the higher token consumption and longer irrational work. Be warned." (`README.md:17`).

**goldfish (`goldfish-ml`), AGPL-3.0.** Not an elephant and goldfish kit: a Python MCP server for agentic machine-learning research. It exposes 43 MCP tools (`@mcp.tool` in `src/goldfish/server_tools/`) and keeps SQLite inside a hidden sibling git repository, run by a daemon with Docker or GCP execution. Runs are contracts: `results_spec` before, `finalize_run` after, and a gate that blocks new runs while a finished run is unfinalized (`src/goldfish/experiment_model/records.py:1778`). A regenerated `STATE.md` is "Claude's primary context recovery mechanism after compaction" (`src/goldfish/state/state_md.py:1-4`). Its AI pre-run review approves on timeout or error (`src/goldfish/pre_run_review.py:340,351`). None of the machinery transfers. Its process ideas do, mostly from its own `CLAUDE.md` (test-first, "No exceptions", `CLAUDE.md:25,50`) and the historical plans in `docs/archive/`.

Licensing: every adopted idea is restated in the harness's own words. MIT text copied verbatim would need its notice; AGPL text is not copied.

## The harness today, where the candidates land

- The rendered global context is 93 of its 100-line budget (`.agents/docs/retros/2026-09-14-retro.md:44`), and ADR-009 keeps procedures in skills. A candidate that can live in a skill or an agent file does not go in the context.
- Checkpoints happen per plan phase (`context/AGENTS.md:11`); a task line carries a verify clause (`skills/feature/SKILL.md:53`); the verifier runs once per task at Done (`context/AGENTS.md:15,21`).
- The cold-reader check is one reviewer dispatch with two questions (`skills/feature/SKILL.md:64-68`); `/review --fix` re-dispatches up to three rounds (`skills/review/SKILL.md:60`).
- Recurring failures the candidates target: describing text that outlived a moved rule (BUG-003, BUG-007), the Definition of Done skipped mid-session (BUG-008), verification cited without reading its status (BUG-011, BUG-013), and environment assumptions found late (BUG-015, BUG-016).

## Recommendation table

Forty groups cover all seventy-three candidates. **Add now** is a file-drop edit with verified value and no rule conflict. **Add next** is worth doing but costs a dispatch, grows a file every feature fills, or needs an operator decision. **Later** names its trigger. **Skip** conflicts with a requirement or is already present. Each row states the change as corrected by the verification lenses. Candidate ids point at `.agents/scratch/research/` (scratch, not committed).

### Add now

| # | Change | From | What the change would do | Where | Candidates |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| G01 | The trail outranks the compaction summary and the CLI's own memory | beads | After a compaction the agent re-reads the active plan and `git status` and restates status and next step before editing. A fact the next session needs goes to the trail file that owns it, never only to the CLI's per-machine memory. Both edits land on line 11; the first sentence of line 71 is cut to offset the words, so no rendered line is added. | `context/AGENTS.md:11`, `:71` | BD-01, BD-14 |
| G02 | Each task and phase states its expected result and closes on evidence | goldfish, beads | A task's verify clause says what the command prints when the task is done; an empty result names its positive control. Each phase ends with a Checkpoint box holding the expected end state and the evidence (log path, or command and exit status). A miss leaves it unticked, so the next phase cannot start. Verification criteria are yes/no outcomes that survive a different implementation. | `skills/feature/SKILL.md` | GF-01, GF-02, BD-08 |
| G03 | Mid-phase progress and discovered work live in the plan | beads | A task box is ticked when its verification meets its expectation, so a resume lands on the task actually in progress. At a stopping point the open box carries where work stopped and any blocker. Work found mid-phase is filed when found: a blocker as a box above the task it blocks, deferrable work as a Follow-ups line naming where it was found. Handoff, changelog and the bug skill point at the plan instead of TODO.md or the transcript. | `skills/feature`, `skills/bug`, `skills/handoff`, `agents/changelog.md`, `context/AGENTS.md:11` | BD-02, BD-04 |
| G04 | One Decisions section and a cold-reader box in the plan | goldfish, elephant-goldfish | The template gains `## Decisions`: decisions as they are taken, open questions with the implementer's default, cold-read rebuttals and rejected alternatives. The first box under Phases is the cold-reader check, so the no-code gate survives a resume until both tokens are ready or a same-turn override is quoted on it. Step 1 asks one numbered round when a request leaves gaps. Four existing plans already carry a Decisions section by hand. | `skills/feature/SKILL.md`, `skills/handoff/SKILL.md` | GF-05, GF-06, EG-06, EG-10 |
| G05 | Plans close explicitly; the handoff cold read catches trail drift | beads, goldfish | A box that will not be done becomes `[-]` with dropped, superseded or moved-to-handoff and a date; closing a plan turns every `[ ]` into `[x]` or `[-]`. The handoff's cold reader names any plan with open boxes that ROADMAP does not name, and any source commit without a `changes/` entry. The seven open operator boxes in two finished plans are closed once. | `skills/feature`, `skills/handoff`, two plan files | BD-06, BD-R2-03, GF-14 |
| G06 | The docs lens hunts old wording and dropped rules | beads, goldfish | For each rule the scope changes or removes, `/review --docs` greps its old wording in living docs and reports each stale hit with both file:line, plus a `dropped:` row for a rule that left with no new home. Under `--project` it lists stale references and ends with the greps that re-check them. The same change restores the clause the 87a862d trim dropped from the missing-repro gate. | `skills/review`, `AGENTS.md`, `skills/retro`, `skills/bug` | BD-09, GF-10, BD-R2-02, BD-13 |
| G07 | The verifier runs every command on its own | elephant-goldfish | Each command runs as its own call with its own exit status; a chained setup line is split, and `gofmt -l` is judged by its output. Every outcome is logged even after an earlier failure. A failing test the change never touched is marked `pre-existing?`; Status stays FAIL and the main agent records a bug. | `agents/verifier.md` | EG-04 |
| G08 | Hand-typed inventory counts become pointers | beads | README, the repo AGENTS.md and the testing guide stop typing skill and agent counts; `sh-agent list` and the generated inventory carry them. A trivial docs-only edit. | `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, testing guide | BD-R2-05 |
| G09 | Test first on feature tasks | goldfish | A task whose verify clause names a test gets that test written and seen failing for the task's reason before the code; in a compiled language a zero-value signature lands first, because a compile error is not the red. | `skills/feature/SKILL.md` | GF-04 |
| G10 | Review rounds keep a ledger and hand over the fix list | elephant-goldfish | Before each `/review --fix` re-dispatch the record gains `## Round N`, one line per finding: fixed, rebutted or left. The re-dispatched reviewer receives only the fixed lines and "verify each fix; look for defects the fixes introduced". Rebuttal reasons stay out of the dispatch, so no author intent reaches the reviewer. | `skills/review/SKILL.md` | EG-01, EG-02 |
| G11 | A rebuttal needs a checkable reason | elephant-goldfish, goldfish | An Outcome `rebutted` line cites file:line, an ADR or an AGENTS.md section, or the user's quoted words; intent is not a reason. An out-of-scope finding becomes `left` with an owner. A command that exited non-zero is never rebutted. | `skills/review`, `skills/preflight` | EG-05, GF-07 |

### Add next

| # | Change | From | What the change would do, and why it waits | Candidates |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| G12 | A verifier log per phase | goldfish | In a plan with two or more phases, each phase that changed source gets its own verifier run as its Checkpoint evidence. One Sonnet dispatch per phase; land after G02 shows the Checkpoint box is filled honestly. | GF-03 |
| G13 | Recon before the plan | elephant-goldfish | For an unread area or about ten files, `explorer` maps the closest surfaces first and the plan cites its brief. One dispatch per larger feature. | EG-09 |
| G14 | Environment assumptions and required docs in the plan | goldfish, beads | Risks lists each assumption about an external system with the command that checks it in Phase 1. A task changing a command, flag, endpoint, config key or deploy step names its doc file and stays unticked until that file is updated. Grows the template right after G02 and G04. | GF-08, BD-07 |
| G15 | Reviewer hunt items | elephant-goldfish | Review standards gain leftover debug output, masked fallbacks and partial writes, missing regenerated files, and stale comments and test names. Read on every review; no incident recorded yet. | EG-14 |
| G16 | Silenced checks become visible | elephant-goldfish, goldfish | A changed assertion with no source change, and a new skip, `.only`, `//nolint` or `eslint-disable` without a reason, become review findings; the verifier lists suppressions the diff adds. No incident recorded yet. | EG-03, GF-R2-02, GF-R2-03, GF-R2-05 |
| G17 | Test counts compared with the previous log | goldfish | Verifier logs record pass, fail and skip counts at a commit and flag a fall the diff does not explain. False alarms across machines are likely until real logs carry counts; land after G07. | GF-R2-01 |
| G18 | A cut tool result counts as not examined | beads | Reviewer, security, verifier and explorer treat a truncated output as unread until they read the rest. The one recorded near-miss would not have been caught by it. | BD-R2-01 |
| G19 | A Task that outgrows one sitting becomes a Feature | beads | The remainder moves into a plan under the feature gates. About eighteen words in every session, and the feature skill's description already triggers on design questions. | BD-03 |
| G20 | The release gate fails closed | goldfish | A report covers a path only if its Not examined section leaves it out; a gap gets one re-dispatch, then NO-SHIP. "Blocking" is defined from verdict and severity fields, with thresholds the operator picks. | GF-13, GF-17 |
| G21 | Same gate wording in feature, bug and review | elephant-goldfish | Each skill names its gates; a waiver is the user's words in the same turn; a cap offers clarify or cut, proceed with residue, or abandon; a headless run stops and writes the question into the handoff. Effort M plus matrix re-runs on both CLIs. | EG-07 |
| G22 | Every bug fix gets the reviewer | elephant-goldfish | Amends the 50-line threshold for bug-skill work: four files and an ADR in one commit, one Sonnet dispatch per bug. | EG-19 |
| G23 | Diagnosis misses and graduation tests | elephant-goldfish, goldfish | Bug records name causes the goldfish diagnosis missed; a proposed prevention rule states whether it is actionable and general. Rarely fires: one of sixteen records ran a diagnosis. | EG-13, GF-09 |
| G24 | Bug index rows shrink when their rule graduates | beads | A graduated rule's row moves to a short table naming its new home. Reopens the approved 2026-09-13 refusal to cap the index. | BD-11 |
| G25 | `/init-project` derives commands and folds CLAUDE.md | elephant-goldfish, beads | Derived build, run and test commands are confirmed before they replace template defaults; an existing CLAUDE.md is folded into AGENTS.md instead of skipped. Fires only at init. | EG-18, BD-20 |
| G26 | A project skill never reuses a harness name | beads | Replaces the line-37 claim that the project layer has priority on both vendors, which Claude Code's docs report as untrue for skills. Test how each CLI resolves a same-named project skill in the sandbox first. | BD-R2-06 |

### Later

| # | Change | From | Trigger | Candidates |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| G27 | A comprehension paraphrase in the cold read | elephant-goldfish | A plan misread that the Gaps question missed. | EG-08 |
| G28 | No runnable destructive one-liner in a handoff's Next Steps | beads | A destructive step executed from the trail. Only ever in the handoff Writing Rules: in the context it would contradict `context/dev-setup.md:8`. | BD-10 |
| G29 | A cross-vendor second opinion on reviews | goldfish | A review missing what the other vendor's model catches. | GF-19 |
| G30 | An upgrade test from an older manifest shape | beads | A binary change breaking a home installed by an earlier commit. The plain-copy leg is already covered. | BD-R2-04 |
| G31 | The verifier names stale generated output | elephant-goldfish | A consumer shipping stale generated files, and a decision on who runs the generator. | EG-15 |
| G32 | Plan template extras: surface obligations, a Flow section, an ordering check | elephant-goldfish, beads | Trail evidence for any of them; the template already takes about sixteen lines from this set. | EG-16, EG-17, BD-05 |

### Skip

| # | Mechanism | Why not | Candidates |
|---|---|---|---|
| G33 | Adopting `bd` or goldfish as tools | `bd` needs a Dolt database per project, git hooks and a settings.json hook, and its `bd prime` forbids markdown plans. Goldfish is an AGPL Python MCP server with SQLite and a daemon. Both conflict with R3, R5, R7, ADR-007 and the settings non-goal. | BD-16, GF-11 |
| G34 | Anything that needs a hook, CI job, daemon or clock | R3, ADR-007 and the hooks and settings non-goals; the prose halves are in G01 and G05. | BD-15, GF-12, GF-20, BD-R2-07 |
| G35 | Already present | The close protocol is Definition of Done step 5; bug records plus `changes/` entries already carry what goldfish's changelog does. | BD-18, GF-18 |
| G36 | Concurrency primitives and execution hints | No concurrent writers to the trail; model hints cannot be honoured on Antigravity. | BD-17, BD-19 |
| G37 | Contradicts a recorded decision | Stopping before commit (the commit is the checkpoint, ADR-008), per-project template rewriting (ADR-008, R4), uncapped unanimous panels (the three-round cap). | EG-12, EG-20, GF-15 |
| G38 | Ceremony with no recorded need | A brainstorm lens panel costs three to six dispatches per use; mandatory reason strings cannot be enforced as prose and would leak intent to reviewers. | EG-11, GF-16 |
| G39 | Declared baselines and trend alerts | Test counts are exact, so the previous log is the right reference (G17). | GF-R2-04 |
| G40 | Version stamps on skills or handoffs | Skills and binary ship from one commit; `sh-agent status` and each mirror's COMMIT file already show staleness. | BD-12, BD-R2-08 |

## Suggested first bundle, in order

1. G06 first, because it reviews the edits that follow and restores the lost repro clause.
2. G01, before G03, since both edit `context/AGENTS.md:11`.
3. G02, the Checkpoint box that G03 and G05 build on.
4. G03 and G04 in the same pass as G02, so feature Step 4 is rewritten once.
5. G05, after G02 defines the box states.
6. G07, the prerequisite for G17.
7. G08, which removes text and can ride along in any commit.
8. Then G09, and G10 with G11 as one review-skill change.

## Drift found in the harness itself

- The 2026-09-03 context trim (87a862d) removed "never skipped on the strength of an 'autonomous' instruction" from the missing-repro gate. `skills/bug/SKILL.md:29` still asks for a repro but no longer says an autonomy instruction cannot skip it. Verified with `git show`.
- Seven operator boxes remain unticked in two finished plans: six in `2026-09-03-rebuild.md`, one in `2026-09-13-learning-loop-project-level.md`, while ROADMAP "Now" is empty. Verified with `grep`.
- `context/AGENTS.md:37` says the project layer has priority on both vendors. A verification lens reports that Claude Code's documentation resolves skills personal-over-project; this was not tested.
- The repo's own setup line (`AGENTS.md:12`) chains `gofmt -l`, `go vet` and `go test` with `&&`. `gofmt -l` exits 0 while listing unformatted files, and a vet failure hides the test result.
- Claude Code's per-machine memory for this repo holds a status fact about a downstream mirror that lives nowhere in the trail.
- Skill and agent counts are typed by hand in README, the repo AGENTS.md and the testing guide, while the deployed inventory is generated.

## Cost of the set

- `context/AGENTS.md` stays at 93 rendered lines: every edit lands on an existing line. Words are the real cost. G01's words are offset by the line-71 cut; G19, G22 and G26 would add about seventy words and stay add next.
- `skills/feature/SKILL.md` grows from 82 to about 98 lines, and Step 4 passes 300 words; split it into short paragraphs when G02, G03, G04 and G09 land.
- `skills/review/SKILL.md` stays near 64 lines, but three long lines grow by about 180 words together.
- `skills/review-standards/SKILL.md` is preloaded into every reviewer dispatch, so G15 and G16 stay compact.
- No group needs code, a hook, a settings edit, a dependency or a new agent. An agent body change is verified with one sandbox dispatch; G22's description change needs one too.

## Conflicts to respect when implementing

- G02 lands before G03, and the line-11 parenthesis becomes "tick its Checkpoint box", or "tick its tasks" contradicts per-task ticking.
- G10 pastes only the fixed lines into a re-dispatch, never rebuttal reasons, to keep the reviewer diff-only.
- G11 limits "never rebutted" to a command that exited non-zero; a coverage finding stays rebuttable, as `/review --tests` allows.
- Every widening of the cold-reader brief folds into its Gaps question, so "two questions" stays true in `skills/feature/SKILL.md:66` and `agents/reviewer.md:28`.
- G21 states that a headless stop at a cap wins over "a headless run with --fix applies".
- G22's four line edits and its ADR land in one commit, or the four lines contradict each other.
- G24 reopens an operator-approved decision; G26 waits for a sandbox test of vendor precedence.

## Corrections from verification

The lenses changed these facts; the tables use the corrected versions.

- **goldfish history, not practice.** The per-phase gate checklists, "Done when" boxes, the five-agent Ralph loop, the documentation audit, the contract tests and the failure-pattern graduation criteria live only in `docs/archive/`. The shipped pattern store has no inclusion criteria, and nothing reads approved patterns.
- **goldfish memory.** `log_thought` writes a database row at once; the line reaches `STATE.md` only at the next regeneration, and `## Active Goal` has no caller that sets it. A reason is optional on `run()`. `vs_previous` subtracts raw values without checking that the metric matches.
- **goldfish suppressions.** No linter configuration enforces "never suppress"; the rule is text, and its forty suppressions carry codes but no reasons.
- **beads enforces less than its docs suggest.** Quality-gate labels are a documentation example that `bd close` never checks. The `bd swarm validate` direction check is a title-keyword heuristic. Compaction has one tier and targets database size. Version awareness is a one-shot `.beads/.local_version` check. `bd defer` is a snooze, not a terminal state; only closed is terminal. The upgrade gate runs six scenarios against one previous version in CI, not the documented matrix.
- **beads truncation notice.** It prefixes `bd prime`'s three built-in outputs only; extending it to diffs and logs is the harness's own generalization.
- **beads contradicts itself on markdown.** The plugin skill's two-week test allows a TodoWrite list for short work; every `bd prime` output forbids TodoWrite, TaskCreate and markdown files for task tracking.
- **elephant-goldfish scripts.** The lint baseline never checks out main, `git stash create` ignores `--include-untracked` so `git clean -fd` can delete untracked files, and it writes to `/tmp`. Its codegen step runs after the tests in every adapter, and no stale-output check exists. The headless outcome in G21 has no source precedent.
- **The harness has more than the proposals credited.** The cold-reader check already runs three readers per round in practice. The 2026-09-13 improvement review already refused capping the bug index. ROADMAP "Now" is not a phase marker. No explicit one-active-plan rule exists. Appending to a context line adds words, not rendered lines.

## Not verified

- Nothing here is implemented or tested; every "what the change would do" is a prediction from the text of the change.
- Claude Code's skill precedence behind G26 comes from a documentation summary, not a live test.
- The 60-row styrman-crew bug index behind G24 comes from a verifier's count and was not re-checked.
- Dave Rensin's article behind elephant-goldfish was not read; the repo's paraphrase was taken as stated.
- Not read in full: beads `docs/reference/`, `docs/architecture/` and most of the generated CLI reference; goldfish `cloud/`, `infra/`, `io/`, `metrics/`, `datasets/` and its web dashboard.

title: Plan — `sh-agent install` switches Claude Code's commit attribution off (2026-09-16)
body:
# Plan — `sh-agent install` switches Claude Code's commit attribution off   (2026-09-16)

## Why
BUG-039: the context's Git rule forbids the `Co-Authored-By` trailer, yet three of three headless Claude Code commits carried it, because the trailer is the CLI's own attribution setting and prose does not switch a setting off. Since 7b8743f `install` and `status` print a note asking the operator to add the setting by hand. The operator asked for the installer to write it instead ("Add this to the installer? … so when I install it fixes this?") and approved the one-sentence change to R4 that this needs (2026-09-16, both AskUserQuestion answers: "Leave it, print the note (Recommended)" and "Approve as written (Recommended)").

## Scope
In: `install` (and its alias `sync`, the same switch arm; vendor all or claude) sets `"attribution": {"commit": "", "pr": ""}` in `<home>/.claude/settings.json` when the `attribution` key is absent, creating the file when it is missing; every other byte of the file stays; `--dry-run` reports and writes nothing; the existing note stays for a key that is present with any other value; R4 gains the approved sentence and the Non-goals bullet on vendor settings gains the approved exception, both in one commit with ADR-025, which supersedes ADR-010's "never touch vendor settings" clause on this one point (ADR-010's other decisions stand); README § Install (both the attribution sentence and the line "the installer never touches vendor settings (ADR-010)") and the deploy guides say `install` does it.
Out: `uninstall` leaves the key (documented, not built); Antigravity has no such setting; the Mac (the operator runs `sh-agent update` there); forcing a value over one the operator set.
Follow-ups noted, not built:
- `internal/harness/apply.go:240-263` writes managed files through a temp file and rename without `Sync`, the pattern the security review flagged on this change; add the `Sync` there in its own task — found in: security review finding 2
- `abandonTemp`'s write-error paths and `readSettings`'s open failure have no test that forces them (the verifier's coverage gap) — found in: verifier log
- a SIGTERM between `CreateTemp` and the rename (argolis runs install under `timeout 60`) orphans `~/.claude/.settings-*.json`, which nothing removes: use one fixed temp name that the next run replaces — found in: argolis-devbox security review of the 4aa19be refresh, finding 2
- `attributionOff` reports a valid settings.json larger than 1 MiB as "is not valid JSON" (the bounded read truncates it) while `attributionSet` names the size; check the size once, before either reads — found in: the same review, finding 3
- a settings.json its owner made read-only (mode 444) is still replaced by the rename, since the rename needs only directory write: refuse a file without owner write permission with an advisory line — found in: styrman-crew security review of the 4aa19be refresh, finding 3

## Surfaces touched
`cmd/sh-agent/main.go` (the install case, `attributionHint`, `attributionOff`), `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` (`TestAttributionNote`), `REQUIREMENTS.md` R4 and § Non-goals line 43, `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` (ADR-025; ADR-010's heading marked "Superseded in part by ADR-025"), `context/AGENTS.md` § Git (the sentence that says the note is printed "while it is missing"), `README.md` § Install (the attribution sentence and line 16's "the installer never touches vendor settings (ADR-010)") and the `status` row, `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md` § Verify, `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` § First install.

## Interfaces
`func attributionSet(home string, dryRun bool, out io.Writer) error` in `cmd/sh-agent/main.go`, called from the install case for vendor all or claude, before `attributionHint`. Path `filepath.Join(home, harness.ClaudeRoot, "settings.json")`.
- File missing: write `{\n  "attribution": {"commit": "", "pr": ""}\n}\n` with mode 0o644 through `O_CREATE|O_EXCL` (the directory is created if needed; a symlink at the path is refused by `Lstat` first); print `settings: <path> created with "attribution": {"commit": "", "pr": ""} — Claude Code's commit and PR trailers are off`.
- File present, regular, at most 1 MiB, valid JSON object, no `attribution` key: insert the fragment textually before the object's closing brace — `,\n  "attribution": {"commit": "", "pr": ""}\n` after the last non-whitespace byte inside the object, or `\n  "attribution": {"commit": "", "pr": ""}\n` when the object is empty — then `json.Valid` on the result, then write through a temp file in the same directory and `os.Rename`, keeping the original mode; print `settings: <path> — "attribution": {"commit": "", "pr": ""} added; other keys untouched`. If `json.Valid` fails, write nothing and print `settings: <path> could not be edited safely (the result would not parse); add the key by hand`.
- File present with an `attribution` key of any value: write nothing, print nothing here (`attributionHint` prints the note unless the value is `""` or `false`).
- Not a regular file, unreadable, malformed, or over 1 MiB: write nothing; `attributionHint`'s advisory note is the only output.
- `dryRun`: no filesystem change; print `[dry-run] would create <path> with …` or `[dry-run] would add "attribution": {"commit": "", "pr": ""} to <path>`.
- Signature without an error return: `func attributionSet(home string, dryRun bool, out io.Writer)`; write errors on `out` are ignored as `attributionHint` ignores them (D8). No state of the file fails install (advisory file, R4).
- A file that parses as JSON but is not an object (`[]`, `"x"`, `null`): nothing written; `attributionHint` prints the one advisory line (D7).
Rest of the CLI unchanged. `attributionOff` is reused for the "present" check via a new small helper `attributionKeyPresent(path) (present bool, problem string)` or by extending `attributionOff` to return three states — implementer's choice, recorded as a D-row.

## Failure modes
Malformed or non-regular file → nothing written, the advisory note names it. A write error (disk full, permission) → the temp file is removed, the line `settings: <path> could not be written (<err>); add the key by hand` is printed, install still exits 0 (the deployment itself succeeded). The operator's custom trailer value → untouched, the note says the trailer is on.

## Verification
Tiers: unit (`go test -race -count=1 ./cmd/sh-agent`), install into a scratch home (the e2e for this binary), a start of each CLI in the sandbox after `sh-agent install --home /home/kesokaj/sandbox/home` (no frontmatter changes, so the parse grep is a control).
E2E criteria: a scratch home with no `.claude/settings.json` ends `install` with a valid settings.json holding only the attribution key and `status` printing no note; a scratch home whose settings.json holds other keys ends with those keys byte-identical and the attribution key added; a second `install` writes nothing more (idempotent) and prints no settings line.

## Phases
- [x] Cold-reader check — three rounds (`reviews/2026-09-16-cold-read-attribution-write.md`, `…-round2.md`, `…-round3.md`); round 3: `implementation ready`, `design needs revision` on one doc-line residue; the operator's same-turn override at the cap, 2026-09-16: "Proceed, residue as Open rows (Recommended)" — the residue is `deploy/local.md:37` (added to the docs task) and two implementer choices (Open rows below)
### Phase 1 — the write, its tests, the requirement and the docs
- [x] `TestAttributionSet` written first and red: missing file created; other keys and formatting preserved (non-ASCII, odd indentation, an empty object); key present with a custom value untouched plus the note; key present `""` untouched, no note; malformed and FIFO untouched; `--dry-run` writes nothing and prints the dry-run line; `--vendor agy` writes nothing; a second install is a no-op — verify: unit, `go test -race -count=1 ./cmd/sh-agent -run TestAttributionSet`, who: AI — expect: FAIL for "settings line missing / file not created" before the code, PASS after — done 2026-09-16: 8 subtests red on the stub, green on the code
- [x] `TestAttributionNote` cases `no settings file` and `other settings only` updated for the new order: the `install` leg expects the `settings:` line (created / added) and NO note, the `status` leg that follows expects no note because the key is now there; the `custom trailer`, `malformed`, `directory`, `fifo` and `--vendor agy` cases keep their expectations (nothing is written in those states); a new case `status alone on a home without the key` keeps the note on `status` — verify: unit — expect: PASS only with `attributionSet` in place
- [x] `attributionSet` implemented and wired into the install case — verify: the same test, then `go run ./cmd/sh-agent install --home .agents/scratch/attr-e2e` twice — expect: first run prints the `settings:` line and `status` prints no note; second run prints no `settings:` line — done 2026-09-16 on `.agents/scratch/attr-e2e` (`created with …`, 0 note lines, second install 0 settings lines)
- [x] Two cases shown to fail with their code reverted (the preservation case and the custom-value case) — verify: `=== RUN` and `--- FAIL` lines in the log — expect: both fail without the fix — done 2026-09-16: `custom_value`/`off_value` fail with the present-key check removed; `missing_file`/`other_keys` fail with the write disabled
- [x] R4 sentence and the Non-goals exception added verbatim as approved, in one commit with ADR-025 (context: BUG-039 and the cold read's finding; decision: the exception; consequences: ADR-010's clause superseded on this point, the permission write stays refused) and ADR-010's heading marked superseded in part; `ROADMAP.md` Now names this plan during the work and is empty at Done — docs: `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `architecture/DECISIONS.md` — done 2026-09-16: R4 and Non-goals edited, ADR-025 at `DECISIONS.md` line 197, ADR-010's heading marked superseded in part
- [x] `context/AGENTS.md` § Git: "`sh-agent install` sets it when absent; `status` says when a different value is set" (render stays 93 lines); README § Install (attribution sentence, and line 16 reworded to "the installer touches no vendor setting except the attribution key (ADR-025)") and `status` row; `deploy/local.md` § Verify and § First session after install (line 37's "the installer never edits vendor settings (ADR-010)" reworded the same way), `deploy/remote.md` — docs: those files — done 2026-09-16 by the documentation agent (README.md, deploy/local.md, deploy/remote.md; context/AGENTS.md is out of this agent's lane — confirm separately)
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: verifier PASS with the new test counted; reviewer and security over the diff; docs lens; sandbox install plus one start per CLI; this box reinstalled — evidence: `testing/2026-09-16-verify-attribution-write.md` (PASS, counts pass 79, fail 0, skip 1), `reviews/2026-09-16-review-attribution-write.md`, `…-security-attribution-write.md`, `…-review-worktree-docs-attribution.md` (all with Outcome), commit 42ba2f5; this box and the sandbox installed from 42ba2f5 with `drift none`; sandbox e2e: settings.json removed, `install` created it (`settings: … created with …`), `status` 0 notes, a headless Claude Code commit (`c00a8a1`) with no trailer, one no-tools start per CLI, Antigravity log `cli-20260916_112445.log` 0 parse errors, 2026-09-16

## Risks
Assumptions: Claude Code reads `attribution.commit` from the user-scope settings.json — checked by the `attribution-off` sandbox row of 2026-09-16 (a headless commit with the key present carried no trailer) and by this session's own reminder switching off when the key was added to this box. Textual insertion before the closing brace assumes the file is one JSON object — checked by `json.Valid` on the result before writing.

## Decisions
D1 — 2026-09-16 — an absent key is written; a present key of any value is left alone and the note stays — by: the operator, "Leave it, print the note (Recommended)"
D2 — 2026-09-16 — R4 gains the sentence "`install` also sets one key in the operator's `~/.claude/settings.json`, `attribution` (commit and PR trailers off), only when the key is absent; it never changes or removes another key, and `uninstall` leaves it." — by: the operator, "Approve as written (Recommended)"
D3 — 2026-09-16 — the write is a textual insertion re-parsed before landing, not a decode-and-re-encode, because Go's `encoding/json` reorders keys and would rewrite the operator's file — by: implementer
D4 — 2026-09-16 — no state of settings.json fails `install`; the deployment already succeeded and the file is advisory — by: implementer (R4, BUG-039's security review)
D5 — 2026-09-16 — the Non-goals bullet is narrowed by the approved sentence: "Editing `settings.json` or any vendor setting: the harness is files in the customization directories, nothing else — with one exception, R4's `attribution` key, which `install` writes only when absent because that setting exists solely to switch off a vendor behaviour the context's Git rule forbids; never a permission, never another key." ADR-025 supersedes ADR-010 on that clause only — by: the operator, "Approve as written (Recommended)" (cold read round 1, BLOCKING 1 and 2)
D7 — 2026-09-16 — a valid JSON value that is not an object is left alone; `attributionHint` prints the one line "is not a JSON object, so the attribution setting could not be checked …" (revised from a `settings:` line after the security review found two lines for one file) — by: cold read rounds 1–2, NON-BLOCKING; security review finding 3
D8 — 2026-09-16 — `attributionSet` has no error return and ignores `out` write errors, matching `attributionHint` — by: cold read round 2, NON-BLOCKING
D9 — 2026-09-16 — `install`'s note for an absent key disappears by design (the key is written instead, the `settings:` line says so); `status` alone keeps the note — by: cold read round 2, BLOCKING
D6 — 2026-09-16 — `sync` is covered by the same code path as `install` and named in Scope; no separate behaviour — by: cold read round 1, NON-BLOCKING
Open: helper shape — default: a shared bounded reader `readSettings(path) ([]byte, string)` used by `attributionOff` and `attributionSet`, no three-state return
Open: does `TestAttributionSet` drive `attributionSet` directly or through `run()` — default: through `run([]string{"install", …})`, as `TestAttributionNote` does, so the wiring is tested too
Rejected: forcing `""` over a custom value on every install — silently overrides a deliberate setting (the operator's first answer).
Rejected: removing the key on `uninstall` — the harness's Git rule wants the trailer off with or without the harness installed; the key is the operator's from the moment it is written (R4 sentence).

# Plan — linkshelf simulation: both CLIs build one project under the harness   (2026-09-16)

## Why
The harness has been verified one skill at a time (`testing/skill-matrix.md`). Nobody has watched it carry a project from an empty repository through `/init-project` and `/feature` to the Definition of Done on both CLIs and compared the results against its own rules. The operator asked for that simulation, every gap turned into a harness fix under the bug skill or a Follow-up here, then `/retro`, a reinstall into this box and `/handoff`.

## Scope
In: two empty repositories under the sandbox, one per CLI; `/init-project` then `/feature` headless with the brief below; a comparison of both results against `context/AGENTS.md`, the `feature`, `init-project` and `golang` skills; a fix or a Follow-up per gap; `/retro` (harness scope); install into this box; `/handoff`.
Out: the Mac, the two mirrors, GCP anything.
Follow-ups noted, not built:
- G4 — Claude Code's headless permission classifier refuses the init-project skill's `for … $d` loops (`Contains simple_expansion`) and its `cp -n` chain (multiple operations), so the agent re-did the copies with Write; outcome equal. Note the refusal next to the `.claude` guard remark in the skill's Step 2/5 when the skill is next touched — found in: init run, Claude Code
- G5 — Antigravity's scaffold left `AGENTS.md` § Testing as the template's two comment lines and restated the overview under § Architecture; the skill's "fill the sections" does not say what an empty section becomes — found in: init run, Antigravity
- G10 — a `store.Store` interface stayed exported with no caller after the reviewer had it declared in the consumer; the one-round review after fixes (ADR-022) does not re-read — found in: feature run, Antigravity
- G11 — the golang skill's reference table was not consulted headless (only `SKILL.md` read; `golang-io-web.md` names method-pattern routing, `DisallowUnknownFields`, timeouts); consider naming the two files every HTTP service needs in `SKILL.md` — found in: feature run, Antigravity
- G12 — default data path `data/links.json` inside the repository and not gitignored; a plain `go run` dirties the tree; no harness rule names runtime files — found in: feature run, Antigravity
- G20 — the verifier's `testing/<app>/guide.md` leaves `<app>` unresolved when the binary (`cmd/server`) and the repository (`demo-app`) are named differently: one of three runs at BUG-043's second wording wrote `testing/guide.md`; define `<app>` in the verifier (the `cmd/<app>` name; the repository name when there is none) — found in: real-home check 3b, Claude Code
- G13 — `AGENTS.md` § Setup Commands grew from one test command to a six-tier list (`go test -cover`, `bash scripts/e2e_test.sh`); the documentation agent's lane allows it, no rule bounds it — found in: feature run, Antigravity

Brief given to both CLIs, verbatim: *a local-only Go HTTP service, linkshelf, that stores bookmarks — POST, GET and DELETE /links, JSON, an in-memory store saved to a file — with tests and the deploy guide filled in.*

## Surfaces touched
Sandbox home `/home/kesokaj/sandbox/home` (installed at HEAD before the runs); run repositories `/home/kesokaj/sandbox/runs/sim-<cli>-linkshelf` with bare remotes `/home/kesokaj/sandbox/runs/sim-remotes/`; driver kit `.agents/scratch/sim-kit/` (not committed, ADR-010); this repository's `context/`, `skills/`, `agents/` for the fixes.

## Interfaces
Kit: `setup.sh` (empty repos and remotes), `run.sh <cli> <init|feature>` (one headless run, status and artifacts under `sim-kit/results/<cli>-<step>/`), `drive.sh` (both lanes: init then feature, detached, status file per lane), `compare.sh` (the checklist below, run in each repo, one line per check).

## Failure modes
A run hits a skill gate (three-round cold read, review cap): the run ends with a handoff and that is itself a comparison finding, not a kit failure. A run exceeds its timeout: exit 124, recorded as such, never cited as a result (BUG-013). A tool denial ends an Antigravity run with empty stdout: the stderr notice is the record.

## Verification
Tiers: kit dry run against a throwaway repo (setup, one no-op run) before the real runs; the runs themselves; the comparison checklist; each harness fix under the bug skill carries its own failing test or reproduction and verifier log.
E2E criteria: both repositories hold a service that answers POST, GET and DELETE on /links and survives a restart, built without a human reply; the comparison log names, per CLI, every harness rule the result kept or broke, with the file that shows it.

## Phases
- [x] Cold-reader check — not dispatched: a testing plan the operator specified in one turn; every task here is a run or a read, and the fixes it produces go through the bug skill's own review (2026-09-16)
### Phase 0 — Sandbox at HEAD and the kit
- [x] `sh-agent install --home /home/kesokaj/sandbox/home` at HEAD — verify: `sh-agent status --home …` — expect: `binary cad463d…`, `drift none` — done 2026-09-16 (1 written, 259 unchanged)

### Phase 2 — Comparison
- [x] Checklist run in both repos: layout, tests, logging, deps, docs trail, review and verifier artifacts, git hygiene — verify: `compare.sh` output saved — expect: one PASS/FAIL line per check per CLI — done 2026-09-16: `sim-kit/results/{claude,agy}-feature/compare.txt`, 90/101 and 94/101
- [x] Code read of both services against the golang skill and review-standards; an independent `reviewer` dispatch per repository — verify: reports under `reviews/` — expect: severity-ranked findings per CLI — done 2026-09-16: `reviews/2026-09-16-review-linkshelf-claude-code.md` (APPROVE), `…-agy-code.md` (APPROVE WITH NITS)

### Phase 3 — Fixes

### Phase 4 — Close
- [x] `/retro` at harness scope — expect: a record in `retros/` and a line in `~/.config/sh-agent/retros.jsonl` — done 2026-09-16: `retros/2026-09-16-retro.md`, eight proposals queued in `~/.config/sh-agent/proposals/2026-09-16-retro.md`, index line appended; applying them is the gate this session stops at

- [x] Checkpoint — expect: pushed, trail closed — evidence: `git status` clean after the handoff commit; the retro's eight proposals are the one open gate, 2026-09-16

## Risks
Assumptions: the sandbox home is still logged in to both CLIs — checked by the dry run, first task of Phase 0. A full feature run may exceed an hour on either CLI — the driver is detached with `setsid nohup` and a status file (BUG-013).

## Decisions
D1 — 2026-09-16 — one empty repository per CLI, each with a bare local `origin`, so the Definition of Done's push can succeed — by: implementer (the brief says "from an empty repository"; a push target is part of the harness's git workflow)

# Recon — coldread-handoff-harness-practices-done   (2026-09-16)

## Question
Cold-read the 2026-09-16 handoff (`.agents/docs/handoffs/2026-09-16-harness-practices-done.md`) against `AGENTS.md`, `TODO.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, the active plan, the three newest `changes/` entries and `bugs/INDEX.md`; answer six specific checks.

## Summary
The trail is internally consistent: the plan `2026-09-15-harness-practices-g01-g26.md` is fully ticked including its Done list, `ROADMAP.md` "Now"/"Next" and `TODO.md` are empty (matching the handoff's claim), and every artifact the handoff names exists. No contradictions found between handoff, ROADMAP, TODO and the plan. The fence-aware awk check finds zero unticked boxes outside fenced blocks in any plan file. All commits since the previous handoff (88f9771..HEAD) that touch paths outside `.agents/docs/` are covered by named `changes/` entries per phase (phase1–phase5, done-review, phase7-decisions/init-update/gate-docs-advisory, phase6-e2e, close). Both mirror repos (styrman-crew, argolis-devbox) exist locally with the exact commits the handoff names, unpushed as stated. Nothing is left to guess beyond what the handoff itself flags as open (BUG-031, the option-C filing clause, operator-only Next Steps 1–3).

## Relevant files
- `.agents/docs/handoffs/2026-09-16-harness-practices-done.md` — the handoff under cold read.
- `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-15-harness-practices-g01-g26.md` — closed plan; Phases 1–7 and Done list all `[x]`, evidence inline, 51 Decisions (D1–D51).
- `ROADMAP.md`, `TODO.md` — both empty (headers/no "Now" line), consistent with handoff.
- `.agents/docs/bugs/INDEX.md` — BUG-001..037; open rows BUG-019..023, BUG-031, BUG-033..037 match what the handoff lists as open.
- `.agents/docs/changes/2026-09-16-harness-practices-close.md` and the other 9 phase/close entries — cover all 13 commits from cec4d4e through a81ef4b (88f9771 is the prior handoff commit, d1ff612 is the plan-cap commit before it).
- `/home/kesokaj/workspace/styrman-crew` (HEAD 4957dfe, local commit 5418f19) and `/home/kesokaj/workspace/argolis-devbox` (HEAD 2d83282, local commit 9380a63) — both mirrors exist, both hold exactly the commits the handoff names, both unpushed.

## Flows
Resume order followed as instructed: AGENTS.md → TODO.md (empty) → handoff → ROADMAP.md Now (empty) → plan's unticked boxes (none) → three newest changes entries → bugs/INDEX.md. No missing link in the chain.

## Conventions
n/a for this recon — no code was read.

## Answers to the six questions

1. **Status / next step, as the trail states them:** the plan is closed, Done list fully ticked, main box of work finished. The single next step per the handoff's own framing is operator action: Next Steps 1–3 (Mac install/mirror pushes) are explicitly "operator" work; the first thing an AI resuming this session could act on unprompted is Next Step 4, the harness security session over BUG-033–037 (starting with the `adopt --force` deletion bug), since 5–8 are lower priority/recommendations.

2. **Files named that do not exist:** none found. Checked all testing/, changes/, reviews/, DECISIONS.md (ADR-024 at line 189) paths named in the handoff's "Artifacts to Read" list plus both mirror repos — all present with the exact commits cited.

3. **Contradictions among handoff / ROADMAP / TODO / plan:** none found. ROADMAP "Now" and "Next" are empty, TODO is headers-only, the plan's Done list closing box confirms both are empty as of 2026-09-16 — all three agree with each other and with the handoff.

4. **Plans with an unticked box outside fenced blocks not named by ROADMAP "Now":** the awk check returns no output — zero unticked boxes outside fenced blocks across all 21 files in `.agents/docs/plans/*.md`. (ROADMAP "Now" being empty is therefore consistent, not a gap.)

5. **Commits since 88f9771 touching paths outside `.agents/docs/` with no covering changes entry:** none. All 13 commits (cec4d4e, 32c8427, f3013a6, b43dde1, 22c106c, 641eccd, fe21671, c514936, e31c3a2, fcf3b79, 2a2e6a1, a33978d, 8202d6a, a81ef4b) touching `agents/`, `context/`, `skills/`, `cmd/sh-agent/`, `internal/harness/`, `AGENTS.md`, `README.md` are each covered by name in the handoff's Completed section and by one of: phase1–phase5, done-review, phase7-decisions, phase7-init-update, phase7-gate-docs-advisory, phase6-e2e, or the uncommitted close entry.

6. **Left to guess:** nothing beyond what the handoff itself already flags as open/unverified — specifically (a) whether the four Antigravity timeouts (D50) are load-caused, called "unverified" by the handoff's own Agent notes; (b) BUG-031's headless-run-ends-early mechanism, open; (c) option C's filing clause (Next Step 6), explicitly deferred to the operator; (d) whether BUG-029/032's prevention rules graduate (Next Step 8), explicitly deferred to the next `/retro`.

## Risks
None found in the trail itself. Operationally: Next Step 4 warns that `sh-agent adopt --force` can delete `skills/` or the whole checkout including `.git` and unpushed work (BUG-037) — worth flagging loudly to whoever picks up next if `adopt` is used before that fix lands.

## Open questions
None outstanding from this recon — all six checks resolved cleanly against the working tree as found.

## Not examined
- Contents of styrman-crew's and argolis-devbox's own handoffs/changes entries beyond the `git log` one-liners shown above (not needed to answer the six questions).
- The full text of every `changes/` entry body (only newest-3 plus existence/coverage-by-commit was checked, per the dispatch's scope).
- `~/.config/sh-agent/proposals/2026-09-14-retro.md` in full (only tail read, to confirm it exists and holds the two queued proposals the handoff cites).

title: Plan — delivery through `sh-agent` only, with a feedback loop back (2026-09-17)
body:
# Plan — delivery through `sh-agent` only, with a feedback loop back   (2026-09-17)

## Why

The operator, in their own words on 2026-09-17: "I want the delivery to be around the sh-agent only. Nothing else. I'm the sole user of this harness and decide everything but I install it on multiple places and when I decide to update the repo I want a smart way to push any updates to places where I use it." Four places: the work Mac (Antigravity only), the home Mac (both CLIs), argolis-devbox (both), styrman-crew (both). The normal flow is the operator updating this repository, then running `sh-agent update` at each place.

Two things stand in the way today. The two downstream projects do not use `sh-agent update` at all — they vendor a `.git`-less copy of this repository that is refreshed by hand, which is why a mirror refresh keeps appearing as a task in three repositories at once. And a signed-tag channel was designed yesterday (ADR-026) for styrman-crew's host, which this supersedes: it existed to give that host a trust root, and the operator's own credentials are already on every machine, so it solves a problem that is not there.

The operator also asked for a loop back: "Some sort of feedback function from each place installed reporting back to the main is good for a feedback loop so we can take experiences from each installed place to use to make the harness better."

## Scope

In, this repository only: a decision record superseding ADR-026's delivery half; `REQUIREMENTS.md` R8; a new `sh-agent report` command with its tests; the deploy guides rewritten around the four places and around the release bundle; the mirror sections retired.

Out: the changes each consumer needs in its own repository, which are their own sessions under their own Definition of Done — styrman-crew retires `image/harness/` and keeps a checkout, argolis-devbox retires `deploy/harness/`. This plan names what they must end up with and nothing more, because the operator's rule is that this repository is not connected to any project.

Out: the webservice the operator floated. Assessed and struck — git already carries both halves, a service adds hosting, per-machine auth and an attack surface for one user, and it contradicts R3 (no pipelines), R4 (one stdlib binary) and the local-by-default rule. A dashboard over collected data stays possible later without changing how any machine reports.

Follow-ups noted, not built:
- **Versioned release bundles** (the operator: "Maybe we should release the agent as a package on GitHub that is versioned?"). Worth doing and formalises the zip path they already use for major remodelling, but it is a second feature with its own plan — found in: scope, 2026-09-17. Assessment in `## Decisions` D6.
- Chaining `report` onto a timer, once it has proved itself by hand — found in: scope. Condition (security review round 2, finding 6): every run sends the whole of `feedback.jsonl`, `retros.jsonl` and `proposals/`, and the docs rely on the operator reading what was added since the last report, so a timed `report` sends content nobody read; the follow-up plan closes that first.
- `sh-agent update --require-signed`, if a host ever needs a trust root that is not the operator's credential — found in: ADR-026 superseded.

## Surfaces touched

`cmd/sh-agent/main.go` (the `report` verb, its flags, its help), `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go`; `internal/harness/report.go` (new) and `report_test.go` (new); not `state.go`, which D7 took out of scope — the first draft recorded the feedback path there; `REQUIREMENTS.md` (R8); `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` (ADR-030); `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md` and `remote.md`; `README.md`; `AGENTS.md`.

Found in Phase 3, same describing-text rule: the `install`/`status` note that `rules/` "ships to every install and mirror" (`cmd/sh-agent/main.go`, `internal/harness/apply.go`, asserted in `main_test.go`), three code comments calling a plain copy a mirror, and the stale `govulncheck` notes in `AGENTS.md` and `README.md`.

`skills/retro/SKILL.md` (its harness-scope bullet ends "name the downstream mirrors its `deploy/remote.md` lists as the next task in their projects" — with no mirrors, that instruction has no referent) and `AGENTS.md`'s Key-files row for `deploy/remote.md`.

The first draft of this plan claimed `skills/` was untouched and that this was "not a behaviour change for any agent". The cold read proved that false at `skills/retro/SKILL.md:132`. Not touched, and checked: `context/` and `agents/`.

## Interfaces

```
sh-agent report [--dry-run] [--feedback-repo DIR] [--home DIR]
```

- **Runs before `FindRepo`.** `main.go:105` calls `FindRepo` for every verb except `version` and `uninstall`, and it hard-errors when there is no checkout. `report` joins that early switch, because a machine that installed from an unpacked bundle has no checkout and must still be able to report. Every repo-derived field is then optional, not fatal.
- **Resolves the feedback checkout** two ways and no more: `--feedback-repo`, else `~/.config/sh-agent/feedback/`. When that default path does not exist, `report` clones `git@github.com:kesokaj/styrman-harness-feedback.git` into it — SSH, the same transport and the same credential the operator already uses for this repository, named as a constant in `report.go` and changed by editing that constant. A path given with `--feedback-repo` is never cloned into: if it is not a git repository, that is an error, because the flag exists for tests and for a checkout the operator placed deliberately. NOT `state.json` — `apply.go:106` rebuilds `State` wholesale on every install, so a path recorded there is erased by the next `sh-agent install` and the following `report` would silently clone a second checkout. NOT an environment variable, which would be a third mechanism for a value that never varies. `--feedback-repo` is added to `reorder`'s `takesValue` map (`main.go:447`) in the same task as the flag, or `report --feedback-repo X --dry-run` swallows `--dry-run` and pushes when a dry run was asked — BUG-002's exact shape, measured by the cold read.
- **Collects**, read-only, from `~/.config/sh-agent/`: `feedback.jsonl`, `retros.jsonl`, `proposals/*.md`, `state.json`. Each absent file is skipped and named in the output.
- **Redacts content before sending, structurally, and never refuses over it.** `secretShaped` (`plan.go:206`) matches a FILENAME and none of the collected names can match it, so reusing it here would be a check that cannot fire. Refusing on a match is worse than useless: this repository's own `skills/terraform/references/security-compliance.md:290-291` documents `password="secret123"` and `AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE`, so a proposal quoting that rule would jam the loop. And a needle-span replacement is worse still — `AKIA` is a PREFIX, so replacing the matched token strips the marker and ships the key, and `-----BEGIN` matches a PEM's header line while its body carries no needle at all, which would ship the key and report it redacted. The needles locate; they never define the span. The span is structural:

  **Needles** — first draft: the seven shapes the harness's Git rule stops a commit for (`-----BEGIN`, `PRIVATE KEY`, `AKIA`, `AIza`, `ya29.`, `token=`, `password=`), matched case-sensitively. Replaced by D11: vendor prefixes as written, plus case-insensitive secret assignments, bearer headers and URL credentials; the list lives in `report.go` and `deploy/local.md` § Report back.

  **`feedback.jsonl` and `retros.jsonl`, line-delimited JSON.** Each line is unmarshalled into `any`. A line that does not parse is not dropped and not crashed on — it falls through to the text rule below. Every STRING value is walked recursively, through objects and arrays. A string containing any needle is replaced WHOLE by `[redacted by sh-agent report]` — the whole value, never a span inside it, which is exactly what makes a PEM pasted into a `user_quote` leave entirely rather than headless. The line is re-marshalled and `json.Valid` asserted on the result before it is written; a line that would not be valid JSON is a bug and fails the run loudly rather than shipping. Replaced by D13: a line carrying any needle — in its raw text or its decoded text — is replaced whole by a JSON marker object, and a key block is found first; there is no walk.

  **`state.json`, one JSON document.** The same walk over the whole document. Replaced by D13: any needle anywhere replaces the whole document with the JSON marker.

  **`proposals/*.md` and any other text.** A line containing `-----BEGIN` opens a block: that line through the matching `-----END` line inclusive becomes one `[redacted by sh-agent report: N lines]`. With no `-----END` before the end of file, redaction runs to the end and the record says `unterminated`. Any other line containing a needle is replaced whole.

  The original files are never modified; redaction happens in the copy being sent. Every redaction is recorded in `report.json` as file, line, the JSON key path when there is one, and which needle fired — never the text. D13 dropped the key path with the walk. `--dry-run` prints the same list. The record's location and needle name leak nothing: the needle is a source constant and the location is already marked in the shipped copy.

- **Generates** one metrics record, `report.json`. Fields from a checkout are `null` when there is none:

```json
{
  "ts": "2026-09-17T09:00:00+02:00",
  "host": "dave", "os": "linux", "arch": "amd64",
  "vendor": "all", "files": 260,
  "harness_commit": "c7af0de", "installed_at": "2026-09-16T21:59:15+02:00",
  "drift": 0, "skills": 27, "agents": 7,
  "go": "go1.27.1",
  "redactions": [{"file": "feedback.jsonl", "line": 12, "pattern": "secret assignment"}]
}
```

`go` is `runtime.Version()` of the RUNNING `sh-agent` binary, which is what built it — not `go version` from PATH, which can be a different toolchain entirely and is why `Reinstall` pins `GOTOOLCHAIN=local` (`repo.go:170`). `redactions` is `[]` when nothing fired.


- **Writes** to `<feedback>/reports/<host>/<date>-<HHMMSS>/`, one directory per run, never overwriting. Stages **by name** — the paths it just wrote, never `git add -A` — reads `git diff --cached --stat`, then commits and pushes as separate calls, exactly as the harness's own Git rule requires of everyone else. A pre-existing dirty file in the feedback checkout is left alone and named in the output; the first draft said it would be "committed along with the run", which would have routed around both the staging rule and the content scan.
- `--dry-run` prints the destination and every file it would write, runs the content scan, and writes nothing.
- `report` never writes to the harness repository and runs no git command there beyond `Inspect`.

No change to `install`, `update`, `status`, `uninstall`, `list`, `render`, `adopt` or `version`. `--message` was in the first draft and is dropped: it is a field the request never asked for, and it was the flag that triggered the `takesValue` defect.

## Failure modes

| What fails | What the operator sees |
|---|---|
| No feedback checkout and the clone fails | `report: could not reach <url>: <git's message>; clone it by hand or pass --feedback-repo`, exit 1. Nothing written. |
| `~/.config/sh-agent/` has nothing to report | `report: nothing to send from <path>` and the metrics record still goes, because "this machine is alive and at commit X" is itself the signal. Exit 0. |
| A collected file's CONTENT matches a credential shape | The token is replaced by `[redacted by sh-agent report]` in the sent copy, the original is untouched, and `report.json` lists file, line and pattern. The run continues, exit 0. Printed as `report: redacted 2 token(s) — see report.json`. |
| The push is rejected (someone else pushed first) | `report: push rejected; run `git -C <feedback> pull --rebase` and re-run`, exit 1. The commit stays local, so nothing is lost. |
| The feedback checkout is dirty | Untouched. `report` stages only the paths it wrote, so a stray file stays stray and is named in the output. |
| Run with no harness checkout at all | Works, because `report` runs before `FindRepo`. `harness_commit`, `drift`, `skills` and `agents` are `null`, and the output says which. |

## Verification

Tiers: unit for the collection, redaction and record shape; integration for the git side against a local bare repository; e2e for one real run from this box to the real feedback repository.

E2E criteria:
- Golden path: on this box, `sh-agent report` creates `reports/dave/<date>-<time>/` in the feedback repository with `report.json` plus the three collected files, commits, pushes, and a fresh clone elsewhere shows them.
- Edge case: a second run the same day creates a second directory and does not overwrite the first.
- Edge case: `--dry-run` against a real feedback checkout leaves `git status` clean.

Delivery is verified separately and needs no new code: `sh-agent update` on a checkout, and `sh-agent install` from an unzipped plain copy, both already measured on 2026-09-17 (plain copy installs with the running binary, `status` names it a plain copy, `update` refuses it).

## Phases

- [x] Cold-reader check — three rounds, `reviews/2026-09-17-coldread-delivery-rework.md`. Never reached both tokens; ended at the cap as the workflow prescribes. Twelve blocking findings over three rounds, each verified against the code before being accepted, and four changed the design materially: `report` runs before `FindRepo`, the feedback path is not kept in `state.json`, the redaction is structural rather than needle-span, and `skills/` is a touched surface. The one ambiguity that changes what gets built was put to the operator, who chose JSON-aware redaction (D9). The remainder is resolved in D9 and D10, 2026-09-17

### Phase 1 — The decision and the requirement (no code)

- [x] ADR-030 written, D1 to D6 in the file's own style; ADR-026's heading marked "Superseded in part by ADR-030". Verified append-only: one deleted line in `DECISIONS.md` and it is that heading, 2026-09-17
- [x] `REQUIREMENTS.md` R8 applied on the operator's approval of its exact text, given 2026-09-17 in reply to that text quoted in full. R7 unchanged; R8's closing sentence carries the reconciliation. `ROADMAP.md` Now points at this plan, 2026-09-17
- [x] Checkpoint — ADR-030, R8 and the ROADMAP pointer committed together as the trajectory rule requires; `git show --stat 9222762`: 3 files, 16 insertions, 2 deletions; pushed. The staged diff's one credential-shape hit was a context line of ADR-026's own prose about armor headers, zero added lines, 2026-09-17

### Phase 2 — `sh-agent report`

- [x] `--feedback-repo` added to `reorder`'s `takesValue` map, and `TestReorder` gains `report --feedback-repo /x --dry-run` — verify: unit, `go test ./cmd/... -run TestReorder`, who: AI — expect: the case fails before the map entry exists and passes after; `--dry-run` survives as a flag rather than becoming the value of `--feedback-repo`. Must-fail observed before the entry (`["--feedback-repo" "--dry-run" "report" "/x"]`, recorded in `handoffs/2026-09-17-delivery-rework-phase-2-resume.md`); must-pass re-run bare at `c22cad0`, `go test -count=1 ./cmd/... -run TestReorder` exit 0, 2026-09-17
- [x] `report` joins the pre-`FindRepo` switch beside `version` and `uninstall` — verify: unit, run `report --dry-run` with `--repo` pointing at a directory that is not a checkout, who: AI — expect: it reports rather than erroring; the repo-derived fields are `null`. Evidence: `TestReportWithoutCheckout` (cmd) passes; must-fail observed by renaming the early `case "report"`, which failed with `… is not a harness checkout`, 2026-09-17
- [x] `internal/harness/report.go`: collect, redact, render the record — verify: unit, `go test ./internal/... -run TestReport`, who: AI — expect: absent files skipped and named; a JSONL fixture whose `user_quote` holds a full PEM has that whole value replaced and the line still satisfies `json.Valid`; a JSONL fixture with `AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE` mid-sentence has the whole value replaced, not the prefix; a malformed JSONL line falls through to the text rule instead of crashing; a markdown fixture with a BEGIN/END block collapses to one marker line; a fixture with none of them is sent byte-identical; every case continues to a written record and exit 0. Evidence: `TestReportRedactJSONL`, `TestReportRedactCleanIsByteIdentical`, `TestReportRedactText`, `TestReportRedactDocument`, `TestReportCollect` pass; must-fail observed by swapping in the needle-span replacement D9 rejects, which leaked `IOSFODNN7EXAMPLE` and the PEM body and failed five assertions. Beyond the expect: a needle in a JSON KEY replaces the whole value with the marker as a JSON string (still valid); a symlinked proposal is skipped and named, never followed (BUG-036), 2026-09-17
- [x] The git side: resolve, write the run directory, stage by name, read `--cached --stat`, commit and push as separate calls — verify: integration against a local bare repository under `.agents/scratch/`, who: AI — expect: two runs the same day make two directories; a pre-existing dirty file in the checkout is not staged; a rejected push leaves the commit local and says so. Evidence: `TestSendReport` against a bare repository in `t.TempDir()` (Go's test temp, removed by the test — not `.agents/scratch/`): second run the same second makes `<dir>-2`; `stray.txt` named, not staged, not in the commit; a behind checkout gets `push rejected … pull --rebase` with its commit one ahead of upstream. The commit uses `git commit -- <paths>`, so anything the operator had staged stays out too, 2026-09-17
- [x] The first push is into an EMPTY repository: a freshly created one has no commits, so the clone warns and leaves no upstream branch, and the first push must set it (`git push -u origin HEAD:main`). Every later run pushes plainly — verify: integration against a local bare repository with no commits, who: AI — expect: the first run creates `main` upstream and succeeds; the second run pushes without `-u`. Evidence: `TestSendReport` starts from `git init --bare -b main` with no commits; the unborn local branch is renamed `main` before the first commit, the first push sets `origin/main` as upstream (asserted), the second run pushes and origin has 2 commits. That the second push omitted `-u` follows from the upstream check and is not separately asserted, 2026-09-17
- [x] Clone-on-first-use, its own task because it ships to four machines and runs exactly once on each — verify: integration, point the constant at a local bare repository and run with the default path absent, who: AI — expect: the directory is created and populated; a second run reuses it and does not re-clone; a clone that fails exits non-zero, names the URL and git's message, and leaves no half-made directory. Evidence: `TestSendReport` runs with the default path absent and the URL a local bare repository: created and populated; later runs reuse it (origin commit count grows by one each). `TestResolveFeedbackFailures`: a failed clone names the URL and `--feedback-repo` and leaves nothing under `~/.config/sh-agent`; clone goes through a temporary sibling renamed on success, 2026-09-17
- [x] `--dry-run`, and the invariant that `report` runs no git command in the harness repo beyond `Inspect` — verify: unit plus a grep of `report.go` for git invocations, who: AI — expect: `--dry-run` against a real feedback checkout leaves `git status` clean and still prints the redaction list; no `exec.Command("git"...)` in `report.go` targets the harness repo. Evidence: `TestSendReport` dry run with the path absent clones nothing and prints the redaction list; dry run against the real checkout leaves `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` byte-identical. `grep -nE 'exec\.Command|gitOut\(|Inspect\(' report.go`: one `Inspect(repo)`, every `gitOut` targets the feedback checkout or its parent for the clone, no `exec.Command`. Added: `--feedback-repo` naming a harness checkout is refused (`TestResolveFeedbackFailures`), 2026-09-17
- [x] `report.json` shape: every field in Interfaces, `null` for the repo-derived ones with no checkout, `redactions: []` when nothing fired — verify: unit, who: AI — expect: the record parses and carries each key; the nothing-to-send case still writes the record and exits 0. Evidence: `TestReportRecord`: every key present, the seven source-derived keys `null` with no checkout and no install, `redactions` is `[]`; with a plain-copy harness installed only `harness_commit` is null, `drift` 0, `skills` 2, `agents` 1. The nothing-to-send path writes and pushes the record in `TestSendReport`'s behind-checkout run. Beyond the spec: `vendor`, `files` and `installed_at` are also null when nothing is installed, 2026-09-17
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: `gofmt -l cmd internal`, `go vet ./...`, `go test -race -count=1 ./...` all clean — evidence: `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-17-delivery-rework-phase-2.md`, PASS: 118 pass, 0 fail, 1 pre-existing skip; govulncheck clean; `report --dry-run` from a scratch home wrote nothing. Not exercised: the real feedback remote (Phase 4). Reviewer and security run over the whole change at Phase 4's Done row, as planned, 2026-09-17

### Phase 3 — The docs, rewritten around the four places

- [x] `deploy/remote.md`: § Downstream mirrors and § Releases-as-delivery retire; a § The four places replaces them — verify: `git grep -nE 'image/harness|deploy/harness|Downstream mirrors|downstream mirrors' -- README.md AGENTS.md context skills agents .agents/docs/deploy ':!skills/mermaid-syntax'` is empty, who: AI — expect: empty.
