title: Plan — sh-agent works everywhere (2026-09-18)
body:
# Plan — sh-agent works everywhere   (2026-09-18)

## Why

The operator, 2026-09-18, own words: "I want us to work until the delivery mechanism sh-agent is flawless. This is dod for this long session." and, on scope: "All features of sh-agent need to work and make sure the harness is installed when you say install. And all other functions of sh-agent need to work. This is the core of the harness. In other sessions we will work on improving the harness but now focus on sh-agent." Three releases this week each found a gap on a real machine that no test here had seen (BUG-076, 077, 078, 079): a stale plain copy installed as if current, a verified binary shadowed on PATH, a shell's hash running the old file. The trail proves paths one at a time; nothing yet says every path is proven.

## Scope

In: every `sh-agent` verb — `install`, `update`, `status`, `report`, `adopt`, `list`, `render`, `diff`, `uninstall`, `version` — on every kind of place — a checkout, a release binary, a plain copy — and the two orderings that bit (first install into an empty home; update over an existing install, including from a binary outside `~/.local/bin`). For each cell: either exercised with its output logged, or refused with a message that names the cause. `install` puts the harness where each CLI reads it, and `status` afterwards reports drift none — proven from a fresh home, not assumed. A full-repository code and security audit of `cmd/sh-agent` and `internal/harness`, every finding fixed or rebutted in writing. The install output names each file it adds, updates or removes (the operator's "more info", option 1, 2026-09-18). A release at the end so binary-only places get all of it.

Out: the harness content itself (`context/`, `skills/`, `agents/`) — other sessions; new verbs; Antigravity-specific behaviour beyond what `install` writes for it; the feedback repository's reading side.

Follow-ups noted, not built: `linux/arm64` execution (no machine; the plan's Phase 4 names it as the remainder); the darwin swapped-signature edge (the Mac, the operator); graduating BUG-078/079's rules into `context/AGENTS.md` (a `/retro` decision); a `status --files` listing; moving the ~220-line `settings.json` editor from `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` into `internal/harness` (audit simplify lens, medium — a structural move with no behaviour change, found in: Phase 2 audit). From the v1.2.3 gate's security row (`reviews/2026-09-18-security-v1.2.2-30f7488.md`), accepted for the tag: an unwritable `~/.config/sh-agent` (0500) passes the tightening and `install` deploys everything then fails at `SaveState` with no manifest — a writability probe beside `TightenConfigDir` that refuses BEFORE any write, with a test; `yamlQuote` should also escape U+0085, U+2028, U+2029 and the C1 range (YAML 1.1 line breaks); the README/`remote.md` `grep -qxF` marker and `release.go`'s marker regex agree but nothing pins them together — a test; a failed `filepath.Abs(home)` is swallowed (only when `Getwd` fails) — refuse instead. found in: Phase 4 gate.

## Surfaces touched

`cmd/sh-agent/main.go` (every verb's wiring, `update` both paths, `pathHint`), `internal/harness/{apply,plan,repo,source,release,report,adopt,state,render,inventory,derive,pathguard}.go` and their tests; `README.md` § Install, § Install without cloning, § Daily commands; `.agents/docs/deploy/{local,remote}.md`; `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md`; `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md`. The audit's recon brief: `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-18-recon-sh-agent-audit.md` (Phase 2's first task writes it).

## Interfaces

- `install` output, one line per file it changes, on every run (`internal/harness/apply.go` `Install`, the per-file `switch`): `add     ~/<rel>` when the previous file does not exist (`errors.Is(readErr, fs.ErrNotExist)`); `update  ~/<rel>` when it exists with different bytes; `update  ~/<rel> (previous file unreadable: <err>)` when `ReadFile` fails for any other reason — today that branch writes over the file anyway (`writeAtomic` renames over it), and this plan keeps that and only names it (D6); `mode    ~/<rel> (0644 -> 0755)` when the bytes are equal and only the permission differs — the `os.Stat` probe runs on every run, `--dry-run` included, and only the `os.Chmod` is gated on `!dryRun` (D8); counted under `unchanged` because no bytes moved (D7); `remove  ~/<rel> (no longer in the source)` when the previous install's manifest names a file the source no longer has, on the real run as on `--dry-run` (today only `--dry-run` prints it); `keep    …` unchanged. `unchanged` files print nothing. The summary line keeps its shape, `N written, N unchanged, N removed, N kept — N files managed`, with `written` = add + update. `--dry-run` prints exactly the same lines and writes nothing (`write`/`remove` today become `add`/`update`/`remove`, so one vocabulary on both runs).
- `update` after a replacement (release path) or a rebuild (checkout path): the BUG-079 note when the process is not the installed file and a PATH entry reaches it by name; silent when nothing was written (D2).
- The verb × place matrix, `.agents/docs/testing/sh-agent-matrix.md`: rows are verbs, columns are checkout / release binary / plain copy, each cell `exercised: <log>` or `refused: "<message>"` or `n/a: <why>`; every cell filled before Done.
- No new flags, no new verbs, no config keys.

## Failure modes

- A cell that cannot be exercised on any machine here (arm64) is written `remainder: <machine needed>` and named in the handoff, never left blank or marked exercised.
- A verb that fails on a place kind refuses with a message naming the cause and the alternative (the BUG-076 rule); a silent no-op is a defect.
- An audit finding the implementer disagrees with is rebutted in the report's `## Outcome` with a checkable reason, never dropped.

## Verification

Tiers: unit (`go test -race`, each verb's package tests) / integration (scratch homes under `.agents/scratch/`, every verb against each place kind built from this checkout: a clone for "checkout", the release binary built with `-ldflags -X main.version=vX.Y.Z` for "release binary", a `git archive` export for "plain copy") / e2e (the operator's Mac and devbox, and this box's real home, for the cells that need a real PATH, a real shell and a published release) / release (`/preflight`).

E2E criteria: (golden) on a machine with no harness, `sh-agent install` from a release binary produces a home where `claude -p` quotes a rule from `context/AGENTS.md` and `agy -p` lists a skill, and `sh-agent status` says drift none; (edge) `sh-agent update` run from a copy outside `~/.local/bin` names that copy, and after `hash -r` the shell runs the installed one. Both hold whatever the output lines are called.

## Phases

- [x] Cold-reader check — three rounds (`reviews/2026-09-18-review-plan-sh-agent-works-everywhere-cold-read-{1,2,3}.md`): round 1 two blocking (the `--project` scope; D6/D7 undecided), round 2 one (D8), round 3 `design ready` with one blocking item that was a test fixture, not a design gap — at the cap the operator chose to proceed with it decided as D9: "Go with 1", 2026-09-18

### Phase 1 — install says what it changed
- [x] `add`/`update`/`mode`/`remove` per-file lines on every run (`internal/harness/apply.go`), `written` = add + update, `--dry-run` uses the same words — verify: unit (`TestInstallNamesEveryChange`: a first install lists every file as `add`; a second with one changed source file lists one `update` and nothing else; a removed source file lists one `remove`; a deployed file `chmod`ed to 0644 lists one `mode` line and stays counted `unchanged`; a deployed file made unreadable (a regular file with mode `0000`, which `ReadFile` refuses for a non-root process and which `writeAtomic`'s rename replaces; the case is skipped when the test runs as root, D9) lists `update … (previous file unreadable: …)` and is written; `--dry-run` lists the same lines and writes nothing; `--dry-run` over a deployed file `chmod`ed to 0644 lists the `mode` line and leaves the mode as it was), who: AI — expect: the seven cases pass and a mutation that drops the lines fails them — docs: `README.md` § Daily commands, `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md`. Evidence: `TestInstallNamesEveryChange` failed on all seven cases before the change and passes after; seven must-fail mutations (`.agents/scratch/phase1-mustfail/mutate.py`) each fail it; README `install` row and `delivery.md` say so, 2026-09-18
- [x] Existing tests that match the old `write`/`remove` dry-run lines updated in the same change — verify: `go test -race ./...`, who: AI — expect: green. Evidence: no test matched the old lines (grep), `go test -race -count=1 ./...` green on the first run after the change, 2026-09-18
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: `go run ./cmd/sh-agent install --home .agents/scratch/x` twice prints one `add` line per managed file (260 at the time of writing; the count is whatever `list` manages) then none, and a touched source file prints one `update` — evidence: `testing/2026-09-18-verify-sh-agent-works-everywhere-phase-1.md` (PASS, 227/0/0; first install 260 `add` = 260 written; second install 0 change lines; a touched skill in a scratch clone → its two vendor copies as `update` plus the rebuilt binary; `--dry-run` after `chmod 666` → one `mode … (0666 -> 0644)`, file left 0666) and `…-phase-1-2.md` over the final range d737282 (PASS, 227; a directory at a destination fails the install by name with no line). Reviews `reviews/2026-09-18-review-b393525-028a43b.md` (APPROVE WITH NITS, the low fixed) and `…-review-028a43b-d737282.md` (APPROVE); docs lens `…-b393525-028a43b-docs.md` APPROVE. Entry `changes/2026-09-18-install-names-every-change.md`. Commits 028a43b, d737282, 2026-09-18

### Phase 2 — audit
- [x] `explorer` recon: every verb × place-kind cell in the code, with file:line where each is handled or refused, and the cells no test covers — verify: brief written, who: AI — expect: `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-18-recon-sh-agent-audit.md` with the matrix skeleton. Evidence: brief written 2026-09-18; no silent cell across ten verbs × three place kinds; four coverage gaps, below
- [x] From the recon: a CLI-level test drives `update` on a plain copy through `main.go`'s wrapping (the `errPlainCopy` refusal is unit-tested only at `Behind`/`Pull`); `status` on a plain copy pins its "update is refused" line; `adopt` on a release binary pins its refusal AND names the alternative (a checkout) as the refusal rule wants; `sync` as a literal verb — verify: unit, who: AI — expect: four tests, each failing without its code path
- [x] From the Phase 1 verifier: a relative `--home` given with `--repo` resolves against the repo directory on a real install (`Reinstall` sets `cmd.Dir = repo`) but against the invoking cwd on `--dry-run`; decide one (absolutize `--home` before anything runs) and pin it — `bug` skill, verify: unit (a relative `--home` lands in the same place on both runs), who: AI — expect: green; record BUG-080
- [x] `/review internal/harness cmd/sh-agent --all` — the paths scope, both directories read whole (`--project` is the whole repository and takes no paths: one scope per run), every lens: code, security, simplify, docs, and `--tests` mapping every source file in the two directories to its covering test — verify: the merged record `reviews/<date>-review-harness-merged.md`, who: AI — expect: every finding with severity and confidence; the verifier's map names every uncovered file
- [x] From the BUG-079 rounds (`reviews/2026-09-18-security-c868ed4-a078848.md` § Outcome): `IsReleaseVersion` rejects a non-canonical spelling (`v1.02.2`, `v01.2.2`) and `UpdateFromRelease` refuses `compareRelease(tag, version) <= 0` — verify: unit (must-fail for both spellings; must-pass for `v1.2.3` over `v1.2.2`), who: AI — expect: green, and the tag reaches no download
- [x] From the same: the BUG-079 note says "remove it" alone when `from` or its directory is not owned by the caller, and prints only for the default home (or names `--home` in the line) — verify: unit, who: AI — expect: a root-owned fixture (skip when not reproducible) gets no `ln -sfn`; `--home` scratch gets no note or a note naming the home
- [x] Findings fixed or rebutted in writing, each with a test that fails without the fix — verify: `## Outcome` on the record, who: AI — expect: no `left` without an owner; up to three review rounds, then the operator. Evidence: `reviews/2026-09-18-review-harness-merged.md` § Outcome (19 items: 15 fixed with tests, 4 left with owners); three review rounds (`reviews/2026-09-18-{review,security}-{160aa16-3209cf3,3209cf3-e7fec88,e7fec88-42840fb}.md`, each with `## Outcome`), the operator consulted at round 2 (option 1, `TightenConfigDir`); 19 must-fail mutations, 2026-09-18
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: the merged record's `## Outcome` complete; suite green — evidence: `testing/2026-09-18-verify-sh-agent-works-everywhere-phase-2{,-2,-3}.md` (PASS 244 → 248 → 250, every live leg quoted), `testing/2026-09-18-verify-harness.md` (the tests lens); entry `changes/2026-09-18-sh-agent-audit.md`; commits 3209cf3, e7fec88, 42840fb and the checkpoint, 2026-09-18

### Phase 3 — the matrix, on this box
- [x] `.agents/docs/testing/sh-agent-matrix.md` — every verb against a checkout clone, a release-stamped binary and a `git archive` plain copy, from fresh scratch homes; each cell `exercised`/`refused`/`n/a` with the command and the line that proves it — verify: integration, who: AI — expect: no blank cell; `install` then `status` reports drift none from a fresh home on each place kind — docs: `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md` (the matrix as a tier). Evidence: 53 cells from `.agents/scratch/matrix/run.sh` at 3209cf3, re-run by the verifier at e7fec88 (`testing/2026-09-18-verify-sh-agent-works-everywhere-phase-3.md`, PASS: every exit and quoted line matches, no blank cell, drift none from each fresh home); `guide.md` § 3c by `documentation`, 2026-09-18
- [x] Every `refused` cell's message names the cause and the alternative; a cell that is neither exercised nor refused is a bug — verify: read, who: AI — expect: zero silent no-ops, or `bug` skill runs. Evidence: the matrix's § Silent cells — none; every refusal quoted names the cause and the alternative (the two that did not, `update` and `adopt` on a plain copy and `adopt` on a release binary, were fixed in Phase 2 before the run), 2026-09-18
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: the matrix complete for this box — evidence: `testing/sh-agent-matrix.md` (53 cells, none blank) and `testing/2026-09-18-verify-sh-agent-works-everywhere-phase-3.md` (PASS at e7fec88), 2026-09-18

### Phase 4 — release
- [x] `/preflight vX.Y.Z` from the operator's own turn (PATCH if only fixes; MINOR if Phase 1's lines count as new behaviour — D3) — verify: the gate, who: user + AI — expect: SHIP, published, consumed from a fresh download — docs: release entry. Evidence: v1.2.3, PATCH per D3; the operator's "approved go go go" on the proposed version and notes; gate `reviews/2026-09-18-preflight-v1.2.3.md` SHIP (verifier PASS 250, reviewer APPROVE, security six lows none reopening, docs lens APPROVE); tag signed and verified before the push; five assets; consumed from a fresh download and installed from the published binary (`testing/2026-09-17-release-binary-e2e.md` § Added 2026-09-18 — v1.2.3); entry `changes/2026-09-18-release-v1.2.3.md`, 2026-09-18
- [x] Mac and devbox `update` to it; `sh-agent version` unqualified — verify: e2e, who: user — expect: the new version, no note or a note that is true. Mac DONE 2026-09-18 21:52: `verified and installed sh-agent-darwin-arm64 v1.2.3`, the `mode (0755 -> 0700)` line, `version` → `v1.2.3`, `type` → the installed path, drift none (`sh-agent-matrix.md` § Real machines); devbox DONE 2026-09-18 19:54Z: the same lines, `type` → `hashed (/home/admin/.local/bin/sh-agent)`, dir `700`
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: the release published and consumed from a fresh download; the Mac and devbox on it — evidence: `reviews/2026-09-18-preflight-v1.2.3.md` (SHIP), `testing/2026-09-17-release-binary-e2e.md` § v1.2.3, `sh-agent-matrix.md` § Real machines (`sh-agent v1.2.3` on the Mac and devbox), 2026-09-18

### Phase 5 — the matrix, on real machines, and close
- [x] Mac and devbox, already on the Phase 4 release: the cells only a real home can settle (unqualified `sh-agent version`, `type sh-agent`, `status` with no `shadowed`, `report` leaving nothing, `claude -p` and `agy -p` reading the installed files) — verify: e2e, who: user (runs) + AI (logs) — expect: pasted output logged in `sh-agent-matrix.md` § Real machines. Evidence: § Real machines carries all three machines — unqualified `version`, `type`, `status` with no `shadowed`, the private dir; `report` leaving nothing was shown on both binary-only places earlier today; `agy -p` on the Mac quoted the fail-closed rule from the installed file (its only CLI); `claude -p` on this box did the same after this morning's update, 2026-09-18
- [-] Mac: the README browser chain once (`V=` the current release) — verify: e2e, who: user — expect: logged; closes the `shasum`/`xattr` legs — moved to `.agents/docs/handoffs/2026-09-18-sh-agent-works-everywhere-done.md` Next Steps (2026-09-18): a `who: user` box not run this session. The Claude-side leg is n/a: the work Mac has no `claude` (`command not found`, 2026-09-18); `agy -p` quoted the fail-closed rule from the installed `AGENTS.md`, the golden criterion for the CLI that machine runs (`sh-agent-matrix.md` § Real machines)
- [x] Remainder named: `linux/arm64` (no machine), the darwin swapped-signature edge (the Mac, when the operator has a minute) — verify: read, who: AI — expect: both in the handoff's Next Steps, neither marked exercised. Evidence: `sh-agent-matrix.md` § Remainder and § Real machines, the e2e log § Not exercised, the closing handoff's Next Steps; the browser chain joins them, 2026-09-18
- [x] Checkpoint and Done — every cell exercised, refused, n/a or remainder; verifier, reviewer over the whole range, security, documentation, bugs, handoff — expect: `ROADMAP.md` "Now" empty — evidence: `sh-agent-matrix.md` (53 cells on this box, three real machines, the remainder named); the v1.2.3 gate ran verifier, reviewer (opus) and security (opus) over the whole range `v1.2.2..30f7488` with the docs lens; `documentation` ×5 and `bugs` ×3 (BUG-078, 079, 080) this plan; handoff `.agents/docs/handoffs/2026-09-18-sh-agent-works-everywhere-done.md`; `ROADMAP.md` "Now" emptied in the same commit, 2026-09-18

## Risks

Assumptions: a `git archive` export behaves as the plain-copy places did (no `.git`; `Reinstall` copies the running binary) — checked by `go run ./cmd/sh-agent status --home <scratch>` on it saying "plain copy", first task of Phase 3; a release-stamped local build behaves as a downloaded release binary for every verb except `update` (which needs `gh` and the real release) — checked by `status` saying `source embedded vX.Y.Z` on it, first task of Phase 3; the fake-`gh` fixture in `internal/harness/release_test.go` can stand in for `update`'s network step in the matrix — checked by that test's existing PASS.

## Decisions

D1 — 2026-09-18 — Scope is every verb on every place kind, `install` proven to install, audit, release; harness content out — by: the operator, "All features of sh-agent need to work … now focus on sh-agent"
D2 — 2026-09-18 — The BUG-079 note fires only after a binary was actually written; an up-to-date or older-release run says nothing — by: the operator, "1" on the note-trigger table (the round-2 security finding: on the older-release branch the running file is the newer one)
D3 — 2026-09-18 — The release version at Phase 5 is decided at the gate from what shipped: per-file `add`/`update`/`remove` lines are output, not a new surface, so PATCH unless the audit adds behaviour — by: implementer; the operator can override at `/preflight`
D4 — 2026-09-18 — Per-file lines print on every run, no `--verbose` flag; `unchanged` never listed — by: the operator, "So, more info is the best option. It should be clear what is installed new or things like that. Go with 1"
D5 — 2026-09-18 — The audit (Phase 2) is in scope — by: the operator, "I want us to work until the delivery mechanism sh-agent is flawless" and "All other functions of sh-agent need to work"; a mechanism no independent reader has audited whole is not known to be flawless, only not known to be broken (cold read round 1, scope note)
D6 — 2026-09-18 — A previous file that exists but cannot be read is written over, as today, and the line says so: `update  ~/<rel> (previous file unreadable: <err>)`; the alternative, refusing the install, would turn a stray unreadable file into a broken place with no path forward — by: implementer, cold read round 1 (`apply.go:33`, the `default` branch takes every non-nil `readErr`)
D7 — 2026-09-18 — A mode-only correction prints `mode    ~/<rel> (<old> -> <new>)` and stays in the `unchanged` count: the contract is "names each file it changed", a permission is a change, and no bytes were written — by: implementer, cold read round 1 (`apply.go:49-55`)
D8 — 2026-09-18 — The mode probe (`os.Stat`, compare `Perm()`) runs on every run so `--dry-run` prints the same `mode` line the real run would; only the `os.Chmod` is inside `!dryRun` — by: implementer, cold read round 2 (`apply.go:49-55` wraps both today)
D10 — 2026-09-18 — Phases 4 and 5 swapped: the real-machine cells need the release that carries Phases 1–3 on the Mac and devbox, so the release is Phase 4 and the real-machine matrix plus Done is Phase 5 — by: implementer, while closing Phase 3 (the original order asked the operator to update to a release that did not exist yet)
D9 — 2026-09-18 — The unreadable-previous-file fixture is a regular file with mode `0000`, skipped as root; a directory in its place cannot serve, because `writeAtomic`'s final `os.Rename` over a directory fails (the Phase 1 review measured `EISDIR`; the verifier's live run printed `file exists`, `EEXIST` — the kernel's choice depends on the directory; either way the rename refuses) and the install refuses rather than writes — and since the Phase 1 review, the per-file line prints AFTER the write, so that refusal leaves no line claiming a change — by: the operator at the cold-read cap, "Go with 1"; residue judged a fixture detail, not a design ambiguity
Open: none
Rejected: `--verbose` for the per-file lines — a flag nobody remembers on the day it matters; `status --files` — answers "what is installed", not "what just changed"; a Follow-up

title: Assessment — the "Agent context audit" prompt, and whether to create `rules/` (2026-09-21)
body:
# Assessment — the "Agent context audit" prompt, and whether to create `rules/`   (2026-09-21)

Status: PROPOSAL, nothing adopted. No plan is active; ROADMAP "Now" stays empty until the operator decides. A first draft of this file was checked by three independent refuters (measurements, fit, rules lenses; workflow `wf_cc624239-e08`, 2026-09-21); every correction they made is applied below and listed at the end.

## Why

The operator, 2026-09-21, own words: "I will give you a prompt, take a look at it and say what you think. Could this help us or are we already optimized? Write down a plan file so we keep your thoughts even if we dont do this." and "Should we create rules? We dont have any."

The prompt is `agent-context-audit-prompt.md` (untracked at the repo root when this was written; Open question 1 says where it should live). It is a read-only audit of every instruction surface against a five-layer loading model (L0 enforcement, L1 always-on, L2 scoped rules, L3 skills, L4 references): defects first, a scorecard (A1–D2), a pruning review, a goldfish test, a target layout, and a proposed adherence experiment. Every statement is to be labelled MEASURED, DOCUMENTED or INFERRED. This file follows that convention.

## Short answer

We are not optimized, and the prompt's "defects first" step found a live defect within the hour:

**Antigravity CLI loads only the first 24,000 bytes of our global context.** The deployed file is 27,114 bytes. The last 3,114 bytes — most of the Environment & Stack bullets and the Installed inventory — are absent from every Antigravity session, on every place, in every release since v1.2.0 (2026-09-17). Nothing in the tests or smoke checks could see it. Severity medium: Antigravity-only, and nearly every cut bullet has a second home in a skill.

Beyond the defect, the always-on context has drifted to 3.2× the size ADR-009 cut it to on 2026-09-03, by paragraph density (67 → 74 lines, 7,349 → 23,194 chars), and the retro loop that grew it has no delete step. The prompt's method — Step 3 defects, Step 4 pruning classes with counts, Step 6 one-row-per-move layout, a goldfish on the always-on files — is the right tool for the consolidation Feature already queued. Its L0 layer, its Cursor/Codex rows, its goldfish over every skill and its adherence experiment do not apply here. `rules/` comes later, as an output of that pruning, after one probe that the split even helps.

## Measured today (2026-09-21, this box, `main` at dbc26dd)

Commands: `wc -l -m -c`, `head -c`, `tail -c +N`, `git show <rev>:context/AGENTS.md | wc -m -c`, `git tag --contains`, an awk pass over each `SKILL.md` frontmatter, `strings` over the Antigravity conversation store, `agy -p` and `claude -p` from the real home with a no-tools question. CLI versions by `agy --version` (1.2.7) and `claude --version` (2.1.278).

| Surface | Lines | Chars | Bytes | Load | Label |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `context/AGENTS.md` (source) | 74 | 23,194 | 23,324 | always, both vendors, via the deployed file | MEASURED |
| `context/dev-setup.md` (source, appended at install) | 13 | 2,935 | 2,947 | always | MEASURED |
| Generated comment + inventory the installer adds (`render.go`) | 7 | — | 134 + 708 | always | MEASURED (deployed − sources = 843) |
| `~/.claude/AGENTS.md` (deployed) | 96 | 26,972 | 27,114 | always, Claude Code, whole file | MEASURED |
| `~/.gemini/config/rules/AGENTS.md` (identical bytes) | 96 | 26,972 | 27,114 | always, Antigravity, **first 24,000 bytes** | MEASURED (see Defect) |
| Project `AGENTS.md` (this repo) | 77 | 11,706 | 11,743 | always, in this checkout | MEASURED |
| `MEMORY.md` (auto memory) | 1 | 164 | 166 | always, Claude Code | MEASURED |
| Always-on total on Claude Code in this repo | 174 | ≈38,842 | ≈39,023 | ≈9.7k tokens at 4 bytes/token | INFERRED (bytes/4) |
| Longest lines in `context/AGENTS.md` | lines 57, 16, 45 | 1,884 / 1,767 / 1,679 | — | — | MEASURED |
| Directive words (never/always/must/only/every) in `context/AGENTS.md` | — | 98 | — | — | MEASURED; discrete-instruction count (the prompt's A3) NOT done |
| Skill descriptions: name+description total, 27 skills | — | 12,312 | — | every turn (each CLI injects its listing) | MEASURED |
| Skill descriptions over 250 chars / over 1,024 / over 1,536 | 25 / 0 / 0 | longest `cloud-run-deploy` 989 | — | — | MEASURED |
| Largest `SKILL.md` | `terraform` 393 lines | — | — | on demand | MEASURED |
| Agent descriptions | 391–551 chars each | — | — | every turn | MEASURED |
| `rules/` | empty (`.gitkeep`) | — | — | — | MEASURED |

Growth of `context/AGENTS.md` (43 commits): ADR-009's cut is 87a862d (2026-09-03, "Trim the context…"): 16,053 chars / 136 lines → 7,349 / 67. Then 9,124 (09-10) → 12,632 (09-14, 71 lines) → 17,806 (09-17) → 21,046 (09-17, 5bc56fb) → 23,194 (09-18, 74 lines). 23,194 / 7,349 = 3.16×. MEASURED. ADR-009 counted tokens too ("about 3.5k fewer per session") and set "under 70 lines"; no size has been checked since, by any unit. DOCUMENTED (`.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` ADR-009; `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-03-verify-context-trim.md`).

The growth engine: the retro skill's harness-target table (`skills/retro/SKILL.md` lines 52–59) routes every "rule gap or restatement" to `context/AGENTS.md` and every stack finding to `context/dev-setup.md`, with no delete or merge action and no `rules/` row; the `bugs` agent graduates recurring rules INTO the context. Nineteen Graduated rows in `bugs/INDEX.md` name `context/AGENTS.md` (BUG-029, 031, 044, 045, 057, 058, 061, 066, 068–072, 078–082, 084); BUG-083 went to this repo's `AGENTS.md` § Testing. DOCUMENTED.

## Defect — Antigravity CLI truncates the deployed context at 24,000 bytes

- **Observation (MEASURED, twice):** the CLI's conversation store (`~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversations/*.db`, read with `strings`) holds the prompt it built: the file wrapped in `<RULE[/home/kesokaj/.gemini/config/rules/AGENTS.md]>` inside `<user_rules>`, cut mid-sentence, then the CLI's own marker, then the closing tag. 2026-09-21 (`48ae34c2-*`, the probe for this file): `<truncated 3114 bytes>`, 27,114 − 3,114 = 24,000. 2026-09-18 22:20 (`3c034e5c-*`, a v1.3.0-era session): `<truncated 2553 bytes>`, 26,553 − 2,553 = 24,000. The marker counts bytes (the tail is 3,102 chars). Asked with no tools for its last heading, `agy -p` answered `## Environment & Stack` and reported the 3,114-byte truncation itself; it quoted the `date +%F` and `rm -r` rules correctly, so the file loads up to the cut. `claude -p` with the same question named `## Installed` and "Skills (27)" (DOCUMENTED: Claude Code loads a file up to 4 MiB in full).
- **What is cut (MEASURED, `tail -c +24001`):** the second half of the GCP-defaults bullet (after "Once given, record them in" — the ask-first half loads), then Backend Go, Frontend TanStack, Machines/Colima, root steps with `sudo -n`, test locally first, build amd64, Artifact Registry naming, Cloud Run first, gcloud auth and Secret Manager, and the whole `## Installed` inventory.
- **The cap:** 24,000 bytes, observed on two sessions three days apart (MEASURED). Whether it is per rules file or per `<user_rules>` block is UNKNOWN: only one rules file exists on this box, and one file cannot tell the two apart. The vendor page fetched today says "Rules files are limited to 12,000 characters each" (DOCUMENTED, https://antigravity.google/docs/rules-workflows/); the CLI's observed number is different, so the page's per-file wording cannot be transferred to the CLI.
- **Since when (MEASURED):** the crossing commit is 5bc56fb itself (2026-09-17 23:09): 134 + 21,158 + 1 + 2,947 + 708 = 24,948 bytes; the commit before it rendered 22,609. `git tag --contains 5bc56fb` → v1.2.0, v1.2.1, v1.2.2, v1.2.3, v1.3.0, v1.4.0. Every release binary since v1.2.0 installs a context Antigravity truncates; the Mac (Antigravity-only) and the devbox lose 2,553 bytes at v1.3.0 and 3,114 at v1.4.0.
- **Why nothing caught it (MEASURED):** no test pins a deployed file's size against a vendor cap (`TestHarnessMap` pins verb names). The four 2026-09-17 real-home smoke checks installed commits that predate 5bc56fb. The one Antigravity context check after it (d278f5a, 2026-09-18) asked for a Hard-rules sentence, which sits at bytes 13,875–22,609 and loads. The 2026-09-03 procedure's other questions — skill count, pruned names, the grilling command — DO sit in the truncated tail (bytes 26,406+), and the CLI answered them from its own skill listing. A tail question is therefore not enough; the question has to be one only the file can answer.
- **Severity: medium**, Antigravity-only. Every cut stack bullet except "never suggest another cloud provider", "remote boxes only on request", the Cloud Run-first line and the names-only inventory has a skill home (amd64/buildx: `docker`, `cloud-run-deploy`, `preflight`; Secret Manager: four skills; `gcp.md` defaults: five; slog and layout: `golang`; Colima: `docker`, `cloud-run-deploy`; `sudo -n`: `docker`) — but a skill loads on description match, a rule in the context loads always, so the loss is of certainty, not of the words. Antigravity use on this box since the crossing: two sessions, one of them the probe. Confidence: high on the cut and its position; medium on what "per file" means.
- **Recorded as BUG-085** (`.agents/docs/bugs/`), status open; the fix is Phase 1 below.

## Where the prompt fits us, and where it does not

Fits — each would change something here:

- **Step 3 "defects first: anything silently truncated".** Found the defect. The harness had the "silence from your own instrumentation" rule and still had no probe that reads the END of what it installs. Its lasting form here is small: a size test that renders the real repo (the `TestHarnessMap` pattern) and a canary question.
- **Step 4 pruning classes with counts** (KEEP / DERIVABLE / VAGUE / COMMON-KNOWLEDGE / MOVE-TO-SCOPED / MOVE-TO-SKILL / DUPLICATE / STALE). Nothing in `retro`, `bugs`, `review` or `preflight` measures or prunes the context; the loop only adds. A pass over the 74 paragraphs of `context/AGENTS.md` and the 13 bullets of `dev-setup.md`, with a count per class and the projected size if only KEEP remained, is the consolidation Feature's first deliverable. The prompt's A3 (discrete instructions, target ≤100) is the adherence lever its own R7 evidence supports; that count has not been done.
- **Step 6 target layout, one row per move** (content | current layer | proposed layer | reason | check fixed | size change). The operator decides row by row, which is how this operator wants to decide.
- **A goldfish on the three always-on files** (Step 5's G1–G3 on `context/AGENTS.md`, `context/dev-setup.md`, this repo's `AGENTS.md`), after the prune, to check that what remains is sufficient.
- **A check with a unit.** ADR-009 set a line ceiling and a token count and neither was ever re-checked. Bytes are what the vendor cap and the cost measure; instruction count is what adherence measures. Pin the first in a test; count the second in the pruning review.

Does not fit — strike or run report-only:

- **L0 / E1 / MOVE-TO-ENFORCEMENT.** REQUIREMENTS R3, ADR-001, ADR-007 and the non-goals: no hooks, gates, CI, or permission edits — researched and rejected 2026-09-03. E1 would list every MUST/NEVER as lacking a backstop; that is the design, on record. (Claude Code's memory page says a PreToolUse hook is the only way to block an action regardless of the model; the operator knows and chose otherwise.)
- **R4 Cursor and R5 Codex rows, and the 32 KiB and 8,000-char ceilings drawn from them.** Two vendors only. The tightest limit across OUR harnesses is Antigravity's 24,000 bytes observed (12,000 chars documented) and Claude Code's 200-line target. K3's 8,000-char listing ceiling is Codex's; Claude Code documents a 1,536-char cut per skill and no listing budget (DOCUMENTED, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills). The prompt's "~1% of the context window, least-used dropped first" is UNVERIFIABLE from that page.
- **A written loading model per vendor (Step 0 as a spec file).** README's "Adding things by hand" table already states the load mode per surface and the per-vendor scoping key. The one missing fact is the cap: one bullet in REQUIREMENTS § Known limits, not a spec.
- **Step 5 over all 27 skills.** Cold-reader checks exist for plans (feature skill Step 3) and handoffs; agent changes get behavioural N-of-N runs (this repo's `AGENTS.md` § Testing, BUG-083). Twenty-seven skills is the prompt's own >15-run territory, and most are vendored or stable.
- **Step 7 adherence experiment (canary, 3 tasks × 2 layouts × N sessions).** The behavioural-run recipe already exists, and the permanent tail probe is one smoke-check question, not an experiment. Early-versus-late adherence across two layouts is the measure→rule→stale loop the operator closed on 2026-09-18 ("no more retro after this"). Struck unless the operator reopens it.
- **D1 "flag AI-generated context files not human-verified".** Every file here is agent-written and operator-reviewed by trail; uninformative for this repo.

Reference limits checked today (the prompt's Step 1, our two vendors only):

- R1 Claude Code memory — CONFIRMED: target under 200 lines per file; a file up to 4 MiB loads in full; imports load at launch and save no context; `AGENTS.md` read natively when no `CLAUDE.md` is present, otherwise via import; `MEMORY.md` first 200 lines or 25 KB. `.claude/rules/` and `~/.claude/rules/`: "Rules without a `paths` field are loaded unconditionally… Path-scoped rules trigger when Claude reads files matching the pattern, not on every tool use"; `~/.claude/rules/` applies to every project; symlinked rules pointing outside the working directory load only after external-import approval, and then only the unscoped ones. (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory)
- R2 Claude Code skills — CONFIRMED 1,536-char cut and the 5,000/25,000-token compaction budget; no listing-budget percentage on the page. `paths` is also a skill frontmatter key. (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills)
- R3 Antigravity — CONFIRMED 12,000 chars per rules file (documented); global rules documented at `~/.gemini/GEMINI.md` or, for the CLI, `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/rules/`; workspace rules `.agents/rules/`; four activation modes (Manual, Always On, Model Decision, Glob). The harness deploys to `~/.gemini/config/rules/`, which CLI 1.2.7 reads: its prompt names the file as `<RULE[/home/kesokaj/.gemini/config/rules/AGENTS.md]>` (MEASURED); no `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/rules/` exists on this box; whether `config/rules` stays the CLI's path in later versions is UNVERIFIED. (https://antigravity.google/docs/rules-workflows/)
- R4, R5: n/a. R6 (Agent Skills spec), R7, R8: not fetched.

## The `rules/` question

`rules/<name>.md` is built, tested (`source_test.go`, `harness_test.go`, `pathguard_test.go`) and documented in README's deployment table: each file lands as `~/.claude/rules/<name>.md` (always-on, or scoped with `paths:`) and `~/.gemini/config/rules/<name>.md` (always-on, or `trigger: glob` + `globs:`). The directory has been empty since 2026-09-03. A rule file with no frontmatter is a valid always-on rule on both CLIs (the deployed `AGENTS.md` has none). MEASURED and DOCUMENTED. No rule file has ever been loaded live on either CLI from this harness; the smoke checks cover none.

What a rule file would and would not do here:

- **It does not fix the defect by itself.** Moving `context/dev-setup.md` to `rules/dev-setup.md` leaves the main file at 24,167 bytes, still over. The inventory is generated by `render.go`, asserted inside `.claude/AGENTS.md` by `TestPlanFromFSSource` and `TestInventoryAndRender`, and read by the smoke check's skill-count question: moving or dropping it is a code change, not a file drop. And with one file observed, the cap may be per `<user_rules>` block, in which case a split moves the cut to whichever file sorts last and fixes nothing. One probe settles it: a second small rule file in the real home with a canary line, `agy -p` asked for the canary and for `AGENTS.md`'s last heading.
- **Its content already has a home.** The tail's stack bullets are in the skills (grep above): their pruning class is DUPLICATE, not MOVE-TO-SCOPED. Deleting the duplicates alone brings the deployed file under 24,000 bytes with no rule file and no code change.
- **Path scoping is Claude Code's deterministic lever, with a caveat.** A `paths:` rule loads when a matching file is READ (DOCUMENTED above), never when the operator says a word. "Ship means /preflight" and "ask for the GCP defaults" must stay always-on or in a skill description. On Antigravity, Model Decision mode is description-triggered, but README exposes only glob for Antigravity and CLI 1.2.7's support for it is UNVERIFIED.
- **Rules do not change the growth engine.** The retro target table and the `bugs` graduation rule route every new rule into the context; a `rules/` row and a delete/merge action in that table are what change the next retro's output, and they belong in the same commit as the first rule file.

Recommendation: later. After the pruning review shows whether any MOVE-TO-SCOPED residue exists, with a smoke check per rule file on both CLIs before any content depends on it, and with the retro table changed in the same commit.

**Probe result (2026-09-21, after the refute pass, operator-approved):** a 45-byte second rules file beside `AGENTS.md` in the real home never appeared in the CLI's prompt (no `<RULE[...]>` block, canary UNKNOWN, string absent from the conversation store), and the AGENTS.md cut grew from `<truncated 3114 bytes>` to `<truncated 3456 bytes>`. MEASURED. The cap is on the whole rules block, not per file (INFERRED from the two numbers): a split buys nothing, pruning is the only fix, and `rules/` on Antigravity is limited to whatever room the context leaves. Recorded in BUG-085.

## Recommendation

One Feature, the consolidation queued since 2026-09-18, run with the prompt's method inside it. Phases, each a checkpoint:

0. **Probe and record.** BUG-085 record (done). REQUIREMENTS § Known limits: one bullet — Antigravity CLI loads 24,000 bytes of a rules file, documented 12,000 chars, per-file or per-block unknown (operator approval, since REQUIREMENTS is immutable without it). The two-file cap probe in the real home, its result written to the bug record and the bullet.
1. **Under the cap, pinned.** A test that renders the real repo's Antigravity rules file and fails above the observed cap minus a margin (Open question 2) — it fails today. Step 4 pruning classes with counts over `context/AGENTS.md` and `context/dev-setup.md`, written to `.agents/docs/plans/`; the operator approves each DUPLICATE, DERIVABLE, COMMON-KNOWLEDGE and incident-narration deletion by number. A canary sentence as the last line of the deployed context, and the real-home smoke check asks for it on both CLIs. Changelog, the BUG-085 status closed, a smoke run on both CLIs.
2. **Target layout.** Step 6 rows for what remains: KEEP stays; MOVE-TO-SKILL goes to the skill that already owns the topic; any MOVE-TO-SCOPED residue becomes the first `rules/` file(s), with the retro table row, the `bugs` graduation rule and a smoke check per rule file in the same commit. ADR for the layout (rule 3 of this repo's `AGENTS.md` does not fire — `rules/` is already on the map — but the structural decision deserves the record).
3. **Sufficiency.** Goldfish G1–G3 on the three always-on files, fresh `reviewer` dispatches given the file alone; the A3 instruction count; fixes go where a goldfish would look.
4. **Release.** `/preflight` a MINOR, since binary-only places get a changed context and the size test; the Mac and devbox update.

Struck from the prompt for this repo: L0/E1, R4/R5, Step 0 as a spec file, Step 5 over skills, Step 7, the scorecard as a deliverable, D1. Not recommended: running the prompt as written in one session.

## Open questions for the operator

1. Where the prompt file lives: `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-21-context-audit-prompt.md` beside this file (recommended: committed, referenced), or `skills/context-audit/SKILL.md` with `disable-model-invocation: true` if it is to be re-run.
2. The margin for the size pin: 22,000 bytes (8% headroom, recommended) or the bare 24,000. Not 12,000 chars — `context/AGENTS.md` alone is 23,194 chars, so that pin turns the Bug into halving the file, which is the Feature.
3. Whether the consolidation Feature queued since 2026-09-18 is this Feature. Recommended: yes.
4. Whether Phase 0's probe runs before the Feature is scoped (ten minutes in the real home) or as its first task. Recommended: before, so the scope confirmation knows whether a split is even on the table.

## Refute pass (2026-09-21)

Three fresh readers, given this file's first draft, the prompt and the repo, told to refute. Verdicts: adopt-in-part ×3; rules later ×3. Corrections applied: "per rules file" was labelled MEASURED on one file's evidence; the crossing is 5bc56fb itself and every tag since v1.2.0, not "this box today"; the 2026-09-17 smoke checks predate the crossing and the procedure's tail questions are answered by the CLI's own listing; the split leaves 24,167 bytes and the inventory is code; a 12,000-char pin contradicts the fix; severity high → medium; ADR-009 ratio 3.5× → 3.16× and 67 → 74 lines; BUG-083 cited to the wrong file and BUG-029/031 omitted; rule 3 of this repo's `AGENTS.md` does not fire on a `context/` → `rules/` move; the Step 0 spec and Step 7 experiment were oversold; the "1,884-char paragraph" reason for rules named a paragraph the split would not touch; the Claude path-rule trigger was unlabelled (now DOCUMENTED: on read). Journal: `~/.claude/projects/-home-kesokaj-workspace-styrman-harness/22858f28-*/subagents/workflows/wf_cc624239-e08/journal.jsonl`.

## Sources

- Vendor pages fetched 2026-09-21 with WebFetch: Antigravity rules and workflows; Claude Code memory; Claude Code skills (URLs above).
- Repo: `DECISIONS.md` ADR-001, ADR-007, ADR-009; `REQUIREMENTS.md` R3, R5, § Known limits; `bugs/INDEX.md` Graduated table; `README.md` map and deployment table; `internal/harness/plan.go`, `render.go`, `inventory.go`; `skills/retro/SKILL.md` target table; `agents/bugs.md`; `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-03-verify-real-home.md`, `sh-agent-matrix.md` § Real machines.
- Runs: `agy -p` and `claude -p` from the real home, 2026-09-21, no tools, four context questions; `strings` over `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversations/{48ae34c2,3c034e5c}-*.db` (dump in `.agents/scratch/agy-conv-strings.txt`).

title: Agent context audit
body:
# Agent context audit

## Role

Audit the instruction surfaces of the agent harness you are running in (or the repo I point you at) against the standard below.

- READ-ONLY. Do not edit, create, move, or delete anything. Propose changes instead.
- Count with commands (`find`, `wc -l`, `wc -m`, `wc -c`, `grep`). Never estimate what you can measure.
- Label every statement MEASURED, DOCUMENTED (cite the source), or INFERRED.
- If a surface doesn't exist, write "n/a". If you cannot determine something, state your assumption and continue.
- Work through the steps in order.

## Target design

Sort content by when it loads, and write for the tightest limit across harnesses.

- **L0 Enforcement.** Anything that must hold every time lives in hooks, permission rules, sandboxing, linters, or CI, not in prose.
- **L1 Always-on.** One root file: build and test commands, conventions that differ from tool defaults, and pitfalls the agent cannot read from the code. With several harnesses, AGENTS.md is canonical, CLAUDE.md is `@AGENTS.md` plus Claude-only lines, and GEMINI.md and .cursor/rules hold only harness-specific deltas. With one harness, use its native root file.
- **L2 Scoped rules.** One topic per file, triggered by glob, path, or description.
- **L3 Skills.** Multi-step procedures and domain knowledge, loaded by description match or explicit invocation. One canonical skills directory; other harness directories link to it.
- **L4 References.** Design docs, READMEs, schemas, API docs, and scripts, loaded only when read and never imported into L1. A design doc holds the problem, the plan, rejected alternatives, and the file-by-file change list.

Two tests decide length. The right length passes both.

- **Pruning (necessity):** keep a line only if removing it would cause the agent to make mistakes.
- **Goldfish (sufficiency):** a fresh agent with zero history can act correctly from the file alone.

Practice: build context in one session, write it down, then execute and review in fresh sessions fed only that document.

## Step 0 - Map the loading model

Identify the harness(es) in use. For each instruction surface, record when it enters context:

- ALWAYS: every session.
- SCOPED: triggered by glob, path, or description.
- ON-DEMAND: read only when referenced or invoked.

Use the harness's docs, config, or source. For a custom harness, read the code that assembles the prompt. Also record: context window; truncation or byte caps; skill-listing budget, if any; what survives compaction; whether fresh-context subagents exist; deterministic controls (hooks, permission rules, sandbox, CI).

## Step 1 - Verify the reference limits

Collected September 2026. With web access, fetch each source and mark each limit CONFIRMED, CHANGED (give the new value), or UNVERIFIABLE; without it, mark all UNVERIFIABLE. Use CHANGED values in Step 3. Apply only the rows for the harnesses found in Step 0; for a custom harness, treat all rows as the portable standard.

- R1 Claude Code memory: CLAUDE.md target <200 lines per file; loads in full up to 4 MiB; @imports load at launch and save no context; AGENTS.md is read only if imported; MEMORY.md loads only its first 200 lines or 25 KB. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory
- R2 Claude Code skills: description + when_to_use cut at 1,536 chars; listing budget ~1% of the context window, least-used descriptions dropped first; after compaction only the first 5,000 tokens per skill return (25,000 combined). https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills
- R3 Antigravity: rules and workflow files capped at 12,000 chars each; global rules in ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md; workspace rules in .agents/rules; activation: Manual, Always On, Model Decision, Glob; skills in .agents/skills and ~/.gemini/config/skills. Check whether a root AGENTS.md is read. https://antigravity.google/docs/rules-workflows/ and https://antigravity.google/docs/skills/
- R4 Cursor: rules <500 lines; .mdc required in .cursor/rules; types: Always Apply, Apply Intelligently, file globs, manual; AGENTS.md at root and nested. https://cursor.com/docs/rules
- R5 Codex: AGENTS.md chain (root to cwd) shares 32 KiB (project_doc_max_bytes), truncated silently; skills list capped at 2% of the context window or 8,000 chars, descriptions shortened first, skills possibly omitted. https://developers.openai.com/codex/guides/agents-md and https://developers.openai.com/codex/skills
- R6 Agent Skills spec: name 1-64 chars (lowercase, digits, single hyphens, not at either end) equal to the directory name; description 1-1,024 chars stating what and when; SKILL.md <500 lines and <5,000 tokens; references one level deep. https://agentskills.io/specification
- R7 Evidence: more simultaneous instructions, lower adherence (arXiv:2507.11538); context files cost 20%+ more without improving success (arXiv:2602.11988); adherence decays within a session; file length 25-500 lines had no effect (arXiv:2605.10039).
- R8 Elephant-Goldfish Model (Rensin, 2026), source of the Step 5 test. https://drensin.medium.com/elephants-goldfish-and-the-new-golden-age-of-software-engineering-c33641a48874

## Step 2 - Inventory

Find every surface:

- Root and home files: AGENTS.md, AGENTS.override.md, CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, GEMINI.md in the repo, parent dirs, ~/.claude, ~/.codex, ~/.gemini, ~/.cursor
- Rules: .claude/rules, .cursor/rules, .cursorrules, .agents/rules, .agent/rules, workflow files
- Skills: {.agents,.agent,.claude,.cursor,.codex}/skills, ~/.agents/skills, ~/.gemini/config/skills, /etc/codex/skills
- Subagent definitions, commands, MEMORY.md, custom system-prompt files
- References: design docs, READMEs, and any doc an instruction file points to

Per file: path, lines, chars, bytes, tokens (bytes / 4, or a real tokenizer), layer, load mode, trigger if scoped. Resolve imports and @mentions and count them where they load.

Per skill, also: name, name equals directory?, description length and its first 80 chars, body lines and tokens, reference depth, frontmatter keys.

Totals:

- (a) ALWAYS-on lines, chars, and tokens
- (b) discrete imperative instructions in ALWAYS-on content (one instruction = one independently checkable directive)
- (c) sum of name + description chars over model-invocable skills
- (d) each total as % of the context window

If the harness has its own accounting (/context, /doctor, /skill-doctor, /status), ask me to run it and reconcile.

## Step 3 - Score against the standard

Score each check PASS, WARN (over target), or FAIL (over ceiling). Targets are judgment calls to tune with Step 7; ceilings are documented limits from Step 1.

List DEFECTS first: anything silently truncated, dropped, or never loaded (wrong extension, wrong directory, dead glob, missing description, over a byte cap).

- A1 Single always-on file: target <=150 lines; ceiling 200 lines or 12,000 chars.
- A2 All always-on content combined: target <=300 lines or ~4,000 tokens; ceiling 32 KiB.
- A3 Discrete always-on instructions: target <=100.
- A4 Scoped rule file: one topic; target <=100 lines; ceiling 500 lines or 12,000 chars; trigger works (glob matches a real file; description present if model-decided).
- K1 Skill name and description meet R6; description in third person, says what AND when, trigger words first; target <=250 chars.
- K2 SKILL.md body: ceiling 500 lines and 5,000 tokens; critical instructions first.
- K3 Skill listing, total (c): ceiling 8,000 chars; also report it against 1% and 2% of the context window. Flag skill pairs a human could not choose between.
- K4 References one level deep from SKILL.md; reference files >100 lines open with a table of contents.
- K5 Multi-harness skills use only spec frontmatter keys: name, description, license, compatibility, metadata, allowed-tools.
- E1 Every rule that must always hold (MUST, NEVER, security, data loss) has a deterministic backstop: hook, permission rule, linter, or CI. List those that don't.
- P1 With several harness surfaces: one source of truth, as in L1. Report duplicated or contradictory text, with both locations.
- P2 With several harnesses: one canonical skills directory, the others link to it. Report drifted copies.
- D1 READMEs and design docs are ON-DEMAND, never imported into ALWAYS-on files. Flag AI-generated READMEs or context files that were not human-verified.
- D2 Work in progress has a written intent and state doc a new session could resume from. Design docs follow L4.

## Step 4 - Pruning review (necessity)

Classify every instruction or paragraph in ALWAYS-on content as exactly one of:

- KEEP: specific, verifiable, not derivable from the repo, relevant to most sessions
- DERIVABLE: layouts, dependency lists, overviews
- VAGUE: cannot be checked
- COMMON-KNOWLEDGE: the model already does this
- MOVE-TO-SCOPED: applies to part of the codebase
- MOVE-TO-SKILL: multi-step procedure
- MOVE-TO-ENFORCEMENT: must hold every time
- DUPLICATE or CONFLICT: quote both locations
- STALE: path, command, or tool no longer exists (verify)

Report counts per class and the projected ALWAYS-on size if only KEEP remained.

## Step 5 - Goldfish test (sufficiency)

Every new session is a goldfish: it knows only what the files put in front of it. Test each ALWAYS-on file, each skill, and any design doc or README I name.

First state how many runs you plan and a rough token cost. Above 15 runs, test the ALWAYS-on files plus the 5 largest and 5 most recently changed skills, and list what you skipped.

For each file, start a fresh subagent with NO conversation history, given only that file plus the files it references. If the harness has none, give me the prompts to run in a new session. Three separate checks:

- G1 Comprehension: "Using only this file and what it references, explain what it is for, how the related system works, and what you must and must not do." Compare with the repo; list every wrong or missing point.
- G2 Critic: "Review this as an expert. List ambiguities, contradictions, faulty assumptions, and missing edge cases." Keep only findings that would change agent behavior.
- G3 Readiness: "Could you do <task> correctly on the first pass with only this? List every question you would need answered." Pick a representative task from recent git history and name it. Each question is a gap in the file.

PASS = no material G1 errors and no blocking G3 questions. Propose each fix in the file where a goldfish would look for it, then re-check it against Step 4. Per file, report tokens, G1 errors, G2 findings kept, G3 questions, and two verdicts: SUFFICIENT (goldfish) and MINIMAL (pruning).

## Step 6 - Target layout

Propose where each piece of content should live, one row per move: content (file:lines) | current layer | proposed layer | reason | check fixed | token change.

Then give:

- projected totals per layer against the Step 3 budgets
- wiring: imports or links to add, duplicate files to retire
- rules to move into L0, naming the hook event, permission rule, linter rule, or CI check
- design docs or READMEs worth adding, and where

## Step 7 - Propose, do not run, an adherence test

One trivial machine-detectable canary rule; three representative tasks, at least one modifying existing code; N fresh headless sessions with the current files versus the proposed layout. Measure canary compliance early versus late in the session, task success, tokens, and skill trigger rates on should-trigger and should-not-trigger prompts. Give exact commands and an estimated cost. Wait for my approval.

## Output

1. Defects
2. Loading-model map
3. Reference-limit verification
4. Inventory with totals
5. Scorecard A1-D2
6. Pruning counts and projected ALWAYS-on size
7. Goldfish results per file
8. Target layout
9. The 10 highest-value changes, each with file:line, check fixed, and expected effect
10. Adherence test plan

Make no edits until I approve specific items.

title: Plan — Context consolidation: under Antigravity's block cap, pinned, canaried, and no regrowth (2026-09-21)
body:
# Plan — Context consolidation: under Antigravity's block cap, pinned, canaried, and no regrowth   (2026-09-21)

## Why

BUG-085 (`.agents/docs/bugs/BUG-085-antigravity-global-context-truncated-24000-bytes.md`): the Antigravity CLI builds one `<user_rules>` block from `~/.gemini/config/rules/*.md` and cuts it at 24,000 bytes; the deployed context is 27,114 bytes, so the stack bullets and the inventory have been missing from every Antigravity session since v1.2.0. The cap is on the whole block (a 45-byte second file was dropped and cost the first 342 bytes; probe of 2026-09-21), so only pruning fixes it. The context has grown to 3.16× the size ADR-009 cut it to, and the retro loop that grew it has no delete step. The operator, 2026-09-21: "Go with your recommendations" — rows 1–8 of the findings table and the five scope gaps in `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-21-context-audit-assessment.md` (the assessment) and the chat of that date; the audit method comes from `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-21-context-audit-prompt.md` (the prompt).

## Scope

In: a canary line the installer emits as the LAST line of the rendered context; a test that renders the real repo and fails above 22,000 bytes; the pruning of `context/AGENTS.md` and `context/dev-setup.md` under that budget using the prompt's Step 4 classes, every deletion approved by the operator by number; the count of discrete instructions (the prompt's A3); a delete/merge row and a size step in the retro skill's target table; a sentence in the `bugs` agent's rules so a recommended home in the context names what pays for it; the canary question in the real-home smoke check on both CLIs; the approved bullet in `REQUIREMENTS.md` § Known limits with its ADR; goldfish G1–G3 on the three always-on files; e2e from the real home on both CLIs; one MINOR release.

Out: any `rules/` file (deferred: the block cap makes a split worthless until the context has room); skill descriptions (deferred); hooks or any enforcement (R3, ADR-007); Cursor/Codex rows; the prompt's Step 7 experiment; goldfish over skills; a runtime warning in `sh-agent status` when the rendered context exceeds the cap.

Follow-ups noted, not built: whether a second rules file loads when the block is under the cap (needs a smaller context; test once Phase 1 lands, before any `rules/` file); the retro table's `rules/` row, which lands in the same commit as the first rule file (cold read round 1); a `status` line for an over-cap context.

## Surfaces touched

Read this session; the assessment carries the measurements, no recon dispatched (D6).

- `internal/harness/render.go:21-54` — `RenderContext` writes Marker, `context/AGENTS.md`, other `context/*.md` in name order, then `RenderInventoryCompact`; the canary goes after the inventory.
- `internal/harness/harness_test.go:165` `TestInventoryAndRender`, `internal/harness/source_test.go:43` `TestPlanFromFSSource` — assert rendered content; gain the canary-last assertion.
- New `internal/harness/size_test.go` — renders the real checkout (`DirSource(filepath.Join("..", ".."))`, `LoadInventory`, `RenderContext`; the pattern of `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go:1346` `TestHarnessMap`, which reads `../../README.md`).
- `context/AGENTS.md` (74 lines, 23,324 bytes), `context/dev-setup.md` (13 lines, 2,947 bytes) — pruned.
- `skills/retro/SKILL.md:53-59` target table and Step 2 — one row and a size step.
- `agents/bugs.md` § Rules (line 76 onward, "If three records share a prevention rule…") — one sentence.
- `REQUIREMENTS.md` § Known limits — one bullet (approved text in Interfaces). `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` — the ADR.
- `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-03-verify-real-home.md:17` context-questions row, `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md` § 5 — the canary question. README § What gets installed where, the row `context/AGENTS.md` + `context/dev-setup.md` + generated inventory (line 190 today) — gains "+ the canary line". This repo's `AGENTS.md` § Testing — the smoke-check sentence names the canary.
- `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-21-context-pruning-review.md` — Phase 1's numbered classification (new). `.agents/docs/reviews/` — goldfish reports (Phase 3).
- `ROADMAP.md` Now → this plan; `TODO.md` stays empty.

## Interfaces

- `render.go`: `const Canary = "Canary: this context ends with the word GANNET."`; `RenderContext` appends `"\n" + Canary + "\n"` after `RenderInventoryCompact(inv)`. The word is fixed and quoted by the smoke check; it is not a rule and is never answerable from a CLI's skill or agent listing.
- `size_test.go`: `const antigravityRulesBlockBytes = 24000` (observed, BUG-085) and `const renderedContextBudgetBytes = 22000` (D2); `TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock` renders the real checkout (`DirSource(filepath.Join("..", ".."))`, `LoadInventory`, `RenderContext`) and measures the whole block Antigravity would build: `len(rendered context) + Σ len(r.Raw) for r in inv.Rules` (every `rules/<name>.md` deploys beside the context into `~/.gemini/config/rules/`, `plan.go:184`). It fails with `Antigravity rules block is N bytes (context C, rules R), budget 22000 (the CLI cuts the block at 24000): cut M bytes` when the sum exceeds `renderedContextBudgetBytes`. It runs in the normal `go test ./...`, from a checkout only; when `context/AGENTS.md` is missing at `../..` the test fails, never skips.
- Pruning review file (`plans/2026-09-21-context-pruning-review.md`): frontmatter; a numbered table `# | file:line | class | proposed action | bytes` over every paragraph and bullet of the two files, class ∈ {KEEP, DERIVABLE, VAGUE, COMMON-KNOWLEDGE, MOVE-TO-SCOPED, MOVE-TO-SKILL, MOVE-TO-ENFORCEMENT (always "n/a: R3"), DUPLICATE, CONFLICT, STALE} — a DUPLICATE or MOVE-TO-SKILL row names the skill or file that holds or will hold the text; counts per class; the A3 count of discrete instructions (one checkable directive = one) per paragraph and in total; projected bytes if only KEEP remained and after the proposed actions. The operator answers go or no per number, or go all; only then are actions applied.
- `skills/retro/SKILL.md` target table, one row added: `| Rule that only retells a fixed bug, or duplicates a skill | delete from AGENTS.md §, or merge into the project skill | delete from context/AGENTS.md; merge into skills/<name>/SKILL.md |`; Step 6 ("Present and apply") gains one sentence in its harness-scope bullet, the only step at which an addition is on disk (D14): "When the applied target is `context/*.md` or `rules/*.md` (one 24,000-byte block on Antigravity, REQUIREMENTS § Known limits), run `go test ./internal/harness -run TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock -count=1` bare after the edit and before the commit; red means the same edit deletes or merges the sentence that pays for the addition, or the proposal is retargeted to the skill that owns the topic." Step 2 gets only the table row; its five items are unchanged. No `rules/` row in this plan (D11).
- `agents/bugs.md` § Rules, one bullet, needing no tool the agent lacks (D10): "The deployed context is size-pinned (REQUIREMENTS § Known limits), so a recommended permanent home in `context/AGENTS.md` or `context/dev-setup.md` names, under Related, the existing sentence the rule would replace or merge into to pay for its bytes; a rule with nothing to replace is recommended to the skill that owns the topic."
- `REQUIREMENTS.md` § Known limits, first bullet, verbatim (approved 2026-09-21): "**Antigravity global rules are one 24,000-byte block.** CLI 1.2.7 builds one block from `~/.gemini/config/rules/*.md` and cuts it at 24,000 bytes with a `<truncated N bytes>` marker; a second file costs the first one room and is dropped without a marker (BUG-085, measured 2026-09-21; the vendor page says 12,000 characters per file). The deployed context is pinned under 22,000 bytes by a test, and `rules/` files share the block."
- Smoke check (`2026-09-03-verify-real-home.md` context row): the question list gains "the canary word (expect GANNET, the last line)"; a FAIL is any answer but GANNET, and on Antigravity the newest `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversations/*.db` must hold no `<truncated` line inside the `<RULE[...AGENTS.md]>` block (`strings <db> | grep -c '^<truncated'` → 0).

## Failure modes

- Size test red: the run prints the rendered bytes, the budget and the bytes to cut; the change does not land. Nothing changes at install time — a binary-only place installs what its tag rendered.
- Canary absent from a CLI's answer: the file is truncated or not loaded; a bug record, never a passed check.
- A pruned rule that a session needed: the Phase 3 goldfish names it as a G1 or G3 gap and it comes back in the shortest form, counted against the budget.
- Approved deletions fall short of the budget: the size test stays red; a second numbered table, never a raised budget (Open row).

## Verification

Tiers: unit (`gofmt -l cmd internal && go vet ./... && go test -race ./...`, the size test, the render test); integration (`go run ./cmd/sh-agent install --home .agents/scratch/x` and `status --home .agents/scratch/x` drift none; the sandbox start of each CLI, guide § 4, log grepped for parse errors); behavioural (`agents/bugs.md`: three `claude -p --agents` runs in a scratch clone, tool order from the transcript, reported n of 3 — this repo's `AGENTS.md` § Testing); e2e (real home, both CLIs, after the box's install has moved to the pushed commit); cloud smoke n/a.

E2E criteria:
- Golden path: from the real home, `agy -p` and `claude -p` asked with no tools "what word does the global context end with?" both answer GANNET, and the Antigravity conversation store for that run has no `<truncated` line in the `<RULE[...AGENTS.md]>` block.
- Edge: with this checkout's `context/AGENTS.md` padded IN PLACE by enough to exceed the budget by at least 100 bytes — the amount computed from the size the passing run printed — (a saved copy in `.agents/scratch/` first), `TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock` run bare fails naming the excess; the file is restored from the copy and `git diff --stat` is empty afterwards (the must-fail mutation protocol of the global hard rules; D12).

## Phases

- [x] Cold-reader check — three rounds (`reviews/2026-09-21-coldread-context-consolidation-r1.md`, `-r2.md`, `-r3.md`), cap reached with one narrow residue; the operator's override: "approved" (2026-09-21), option 1 — proceed with the default G3 task for `context/dev-setup.md` (D15)

### Phase 0 — Record, canary, docs
- [x] `REQUIREMENTS.md` § Known limits bullet (Interfaces text) and its ADR by `changelog`, read against the diff, one commit (ADR-035; committed 2026-09-21, `git diff --stat`: 2 files, 11 insertions) — verify: `git diff --stat` shows the two files, AI — expect: bullet first under Known limits; ADR names BUG-085 and the 22,000 budget — docs: `REQUIREMENTS.md`
- [x] `Canary` in `render.go`, appended last; `TestInventoryAndRender` asserts the rendered context's last line is `Canary` (red first: "ends with … `go-style`\n"; green after the append; full `go test -race ./...` exit 0, 2026-09-21) — verify: unit, `go test -race ./internal/harness -run 'TestInventoryAndRender|TestPlanFromFSSource' -count=1`, AI — expect: red before the render change (assertion fails on the inventory line), green after
- [x] Smoke-check docs: the canary question in `2026-09-03-verify-real-home.md` context row and guide § 5; the README row named in Surfaces; (`grep -l GANNET` over the four files: 4, 2026-09-21) this repo's `AGENTS.md` § Testing — verify: `grep -n GANNET` over the four files, AI — expect: four hits — docs: `README.md`, `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-03-verify-real-home.md`
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: `go test -race ./...` exit 0; scratch-home install then `status` drift none; `tail -1 .agents/scratch/x/.claude/AGENTS.md` is the canary — evidence: `testing/2026-09-21-context-consolidation-phase-0.md` PASS (250 pass, 0 fail; drift none; canary last; 27,163 bytes, over the cap by design until Phase 1), 2026-09-21

### Phase 1 — Pin and prune
- [x] `size_test.go` with `TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock`, run bare first — verify: unit, `go test ./internal/harness -run TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock -count=1`, AI — expect: FAIL naming about 27,160 bytes and 22,000 (2026-09-21: "Antigravity rules block is 27163 bytes (context 27163, rules 0), budget 22000 … cut 5163 bytes", exit 1)
- [x] Pruning review file: every paragraph and bullet of `context/AGENTS.md` and `context/dev-setup.md` classified, A3 count, per-class counts, projected sizes — verify: the file exists with one row per paragraph (row count = paragraph count by `grep -c`), AI — expect: projected size after actions ≤ 22,000 (`plans/2026-09-21-context-pruning-review.md`: 62 rows = 62 non-empty lines; projected 20,013 bytes; A3 214 → 188; three classifiers merged by majority, Workflow `wf_ebd17196-757`, 2026-09-21)
- [x] Operator approval by number — who: user — expect: go or no per row, or go all ("go all", 2026-09-21)
- [x] Apply approved actions: deletions; merges land in the named skill in the same commit; a MOVE-TO-SCOPED row is kept in its shortest form and listed under Follow-ups as a candidate for the first rule file (D13); every restatement of a moved claim found by grep before review (BUG-084 rule); comments and docs that describe moved text updated — verify: unit, the size test bare, AI — expect: PASS printing the rendered bytes (2026-09-21: 44 actions applied by script from the merged JSON; `Antigravity rules block is 20012 bytes (context 20012, rules 0), budget 22000`, PASS; escape in row 31 confirmed by a chr(92) needle; moves landed in review-standards § 2 and golang § Error Handling, cited from bug Step 3 and feature Step 4; INDEX Graduated rows BUG-066/068/069/082 retargeted by `bugs`)
- [x] Integration: scratch-home install and status; sandbox start of each CLI (guide § 4) — verify: integration, AI — expect: drift none; zero parse errors in both logs (2026-09-21: `.agents/scratch/x` and a logged-in sandbox home `.agents/scratch/sandbox-home` both drift none at 20,012 bytes; both CLIs answered six context questions including the canary and the new Bug-bullet wording; Antigravity's store shows the RULE block closing after the canary with no `<truncated` marker; skill load and verifier dispatch passed on both — `testing/2026-09-21-verify-sandbox-pruned-context.md`)
- [x] Review row: `reviewer` over the phase range (diff only) and `/review --docs` over the same range (the context is an interface) — who: AI — expect: findings fixed or rebutted in `## Outcome` (2026-09-21: code lens APPROVE, no findings; docs lens two findings — the self-hosting-suite rule given a home in review-standards § 2, the saved-diff allowance rebutted as a deliberate tightening, D16 — `reviews/2026-09-21-review-worktree-merged.md`)
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: `go test -race ./...` exit 0 with the size test green — evidence: `verifier` log `testing/2026-09-21-context-consolidation-phase-1.md` PASS (16 commands; block 20,012 of 22,000 bytes; drift none; canary last; escape count 1), 2026-09-21

### Phase 2 — Stop the regrowth
- [x] `skills/retro/SKILL.md`: one table row in Step 2 and the size sentence in Step 6 (Interfaces) — verify: integration, scratch-home install and status, sandbox CLI start, AI — expect: drift none, skill listed, no parse error (2026-09-21: `.agents/scratch/x` and the sandbox home drift none; both CLIs quoted the retro description; zero `Failed to parse skill`)
- [x] `agents/bugs.md` § Rules: the one bullet (Interfaces) — verify: behavioural, three `claude -p --agents` runs in a scratch clone where the dispatch describes a third-repeat prevention rule whose obvious home is the context; the record's Related must name the sentence the rule would replace, or the owning skill, which only the new text asks for; tool order read from the transcript, AI — expect: reported as n of 3, with n stated whatever it is (2026-09-21: **3 of 3** in clones of this repo with BUG-086 as the subject — each record recommends widening the existing pipe-into-filter sentence and cites the 22,000-byte pin; a first arrangement in demo-service clones failed twice on its own fixture and could not exercise the rule at all, BUG-087; `testing/2026-09-21-context-consolidation-phase-2-behavioural.md`)
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: `go test -race ./...` exit 0; install and status drift none — evidence: `go test -race -count=1 ./...` exit 0 (2026-09-21, main agent, bare); install and status drift none in `.agents/scratch/x` and the sandbox home; behavioural tally 3 of 3, 2026-09-21

### Phase 3 — Sufficiency (goldfish)

# Pruning review — `context/AGENTS.md` and `context/dev-setup.md`   (2026-09-21)

Phase 1 of `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-21-context-consolidation.md`, the audit prompt's Step 4 applied. Every non-empty line of the two files is a row (62 rows, 26,246 bytes; the rendered context is 27,163 bytes with the 134-byte marker, blank lines, the 708-byte inventory and the 49-byte canary). Three independent classifiers (Workflow `wf_ebd17196-757`: a strict pruner, a fresh-session sufficiency reader, an evidence-first reader) each classified all 62 rows with grep evidence; the table holds the majority class and action, the vote split where they differed, and the sufficiency reader's replacement text where it agreed with the majority (the most conservative of the three), else the evidence reader's. Bytes after are measured on the exact replacement text, newline included.

## Totals

- Rows per class (majority): KEEP 40, DUPLICATE 10, DERIVABLE 8, MOVE-TO-SKILL 3, MOVE-TO-SCOPED 1. MOVE-TO-ENFORCEMENT: none (R3). STALE: none — every path, verb, flag and bug record cited was checked by at least one reader. CONFLICT: none.
- Actions: shorten 34, keep 18, delete 7, move 3.
- Bytes in rows: 26246 → 19096. Projected rendered context: 20013 bytes (budget 22,000; cap 24,000). Projected if only KEEP rows remained unchanged and every other row were deleted: 19834 bytes.
- Discrete instructions (the prompt's A3): 214 before → 188 after by the evidence reader's count (the strict reader counted 230 → 192, the sufficiency reader 227 → 208; the readers split clauses differently, the direction agrees). The target of ≤100 is not met by this pass and is not a gate of this plan.

## Apply-time cautions (from the readers, verified at apply)

- Row 31 keeps the literal escape `\u0041` in its text; the classifiers' own tooling converted it to `A` once. The applier writes the line through a script and greps for the escape afterwards with a needle built from character codes (global hard rule).
- Row 37 moves the four-step must-fail-mutation protocol to `skills/review-standards/SKILL.md` § 2; `skills/bug/SKILL.md` (Step 3, line 43) and `skills/feature/SKILL.md` (line 84) must cite that section in the same commit, or a bug fix loses the protocol. The remainder stays in the context.
- Rows 38 and 40 move the Go-specific `err == nil &&` guard example and the `go:embed` story to `skills/golang/SKILL.md` § Error Handling and `skills/review-standards/SKILL.md` § 2; a one-line language-agnostic rule stays in each.
- Row 58 split three ways (delete / shorten / keep); shown as shorten, the conservative reading.
- Row 49 grows by 61 bytes: it absorbs the root-file conventions from deleted row 50 and the trail pointer.
- Rows 43–48 (the layout block) delete as one unit; the tree is the `init-project` skill's and every directory a session writes to is named elsewhere in the file.
- Row 39 is MOVE-TO-SCOPED by two readers but stays in shortest form (plan D13); row 55's V8 sentence is the other candidate for a first `rules/` file.

title: Plan — Projects use `AGENTS.md` alone: no project `CLAUDE.md` stub (2026-09-21)
body:
# Plan — Projects use `AGENTS.md` alone: no project `CLAUDE.md` stub   (2026-09-21)

## Why

The operator, 2026-09-21: "I saw that claude can use AGENTS.md from version 2.1.277. That would be greats so we use the full AGENTS.md for everything. Go and verify that and If it is true fix it and cut a new minor", then "Your recommendation. Approved." Verified today on this box (Claude Code 2.1.278): a probe project with only `AGENTS.md` (no `CLAUDE.md` in or above it) was read natively on the second session ("The probe word is HERON-4412, from …/AGENTS.md"); the first session after the upgrade read nothing, as the memory page documents. The user level is different: with the `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` stub removed from a sandbox home, the global context did not load (UNKNOWN); the docs and the 2.1.277 changelog entry cover project `AGENTS.md` only. So the project stub goes and the global stub stays.

## Scope

In: `/init-project` no longer writes a project `CLAUDE.md`; its asset is removed; its description, Step 2 loop and bullet say so and name when a stub is still needed by hand (Claude Code before 2.1.277; Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry or a telemetry-disabled session, which fetch no feature flags; the first session after an upgrade reads nothing either way). An update run leaves an existing stub alone (D1). This repo's own `CLAUDE.md` is deleted (D2). `context/AGENTS.md` § Project layout says a project root is `AGENTS.md` alone. ADR-036 supersedes the project half of ADR-005. Release v1.6.0, MINOR (init-project behaviour changes for every user).

Out: the global `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` stub written by `sh-agent install` (`plan.go:89`, `render.go:17`), verified required; removing stubs from existing projects; Antigravity (reads `AGENTS.md` natively already, ADR-005).

Follow-ups noted, not built: none.

## Surfaces touched

- `skills/init-project/SKILL.md:3` (description names "CLAUDE.md import"), `:22` (update rule mentions the `CLAUDE.md` fold), `:42-44` (the template loop lists `CLAUDE.md`), `:48` (the `CLAUDE.md` bullet); `skills/init-project/assets/CLAUDE.md` (deleted).
- `CLAUDE.md` at this repo's root (deleted); `AGENTS.md` § Layout / Key files if they name it (grep).
- `context/AGENTS.md:65` — "Root: `AGENTS.md` (`CLAUDE.md` is the line `@AGENTS.md`; no `GEMINI.md`)".
- `REQUIREMENTS.md` R2 — the sentence "(`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and a project's `CLAUDE.md` are one-line imports)" is the claim this plan reverses; replaced by the operator-approved text in Interfaces (D4), in the same commit as ADR-036 (the immutability rule; BUG-025 was this exact violation).
- `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md:22` — the `init-deploy` row's prompt says "including the .claude symlinks, CLAUDE.md, .gitignore lines"; `CLAUDE.md` is dropped from it and its check gains `! test -e CLAUDE.md`.
