- **Plan:** `<docs>/plans/*.md` → id is the docs-relative path; status `open: N unticked` when it has N lines matching `^- \[ \]` outside fenced blocks, else `closed`; `line` is the first such line. Fences follow the handoff skill's scan (`skills/handoff/SKILL.md:154`): a run of three or more backticks opens a block, a line of only a run of the same length closes it.
- **Other trail files:** id is the docs-relative path, date from frontmatter `date:`, status empty.

### Refs (every indexed file)

- IDs: `\b(BUG|ADR)-\d{3}[a-z]?\b`, target the ID.
- Paths: tokens matching `[A-Za-z0-9_.@-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9_.@-]+)+/?` or `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.(go|md|ts|tsx|js|json|yaml|yml|sh|py|toml|mod|sum|sql|tf)`, with a trailing `:NN` or `:NN-NN` and trailing `.,;:)` removed and a leading `./` or `a/`, `b/` (diff prefixes) removed. Stored as written. A record's references to its own ID are kept.
- At query time `--refs X` matches targets equal to X, or equal to X without the docs-root prefix (the trail writes `plans/x.md` for `.agents/docs/plans/x.md`). A directory X (trailing `/`) matches targets with that prefix. No basename matching.

### Global registry

Every `search` and `index` run inside a git checkout, with or without `--global`, reconciles that checkout's own index and upserts `(root, base name, now)` into the global `projects` table first, so a project's first run being `--global` still includes itself. Run outside a git checkout, `--global` skips that step and does not refuse; plain `search` and `index` refuse there as Failure modes says. `--global` then reconciles `~config` from `~/.config/sh-agent/`, then each registered project: a root that no longer exists or is no longer a git checkout loses its registration and its rows (a note line says so); for the others, steps 2-5 limited to paths under the docs root. Two registered roots with the same base name are shown as `name`, `name~2` in registration order.

### Instructions (text, Phase 3)

Context entry, under `## Work: classify, then load the skill`, at most 330 bytes, final text chosen in Phase 3 and recorded as a D-row:

> **Search first:** in a git checkout, `sh-agent search <words>` ranks every file and trail record (`path:line`, status, snippet); `--refs <BUG-NNN|ADR-NNN|path>` lists every record naming it; `--open` lists open bugs and plans; `--global` spans projects. Search before opening trail files; exact strings, regex and past revisions stay with grep.

Cuts that pay for it (the rendered context must stay under 22,000 bytes, ADR-035; each cut names where the rule still lives):
1. `context/AGENTS.md:37`: the `find-skills`/`npx skills add` procedure shrinks to "a skill found elsewhere goes into the harness checkout's `skills/` (`sh-agent adopt`), then `sh-agent install`, never only into a vendor directory." The `npx` route stays in the project `AGENTS.md` Layout, where it applies.
2. `context/AGENTS.md:37`: "`/skills` and `/agents` show what a vendor loaded; when something is missing, check the symlinks first." moves to `skills/init-project/SKILL.md`, which creates the symlinks.
3. `context/AGENTS.md:31`: "Read the index before touching an area it names." becomes the `--refs` clause of the new entry and is deleted here.
If these do not free enough, Phase 3 stops and puts further cuts to the operator; the budget is never raised.

## Failure modes

| Case | What the user sees | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| Not inside a git checkout, or `git` missing | `search: not inside a git checkout; use grep` | 1 |
| `.agents/scratch/search.db` not gitignored (`git check-ignore -q` fails) | `search: .agents/scratch/search.db is not gitignored; add ".agents/scratch/*" to .gitignore (/init-project does)`; no file created | 1 |
| `.agents` or `.agents/scratch` is a symlink | `search: .agents/scratch is a symlink; refusing to write through it` | 1 |
| Another process holds the write lock past 10 s | `search: index busy (another sh-agent is indexing); retry, or use grep`; no stale answer is printed | 1 |
| Database unreadable (`SQLITE_CORRUPT`, `SQLITE_NOTADB`) or `meta.schema` ≠ 1 | `note: index at <path> was unreadable (or an older schema); rebuilt` and the answer | 0 |
| A file vanishes between `git status` and the read | the file is dropped from this reconcile; the next one picks up its state | 0 |
| `--refs` names an ID with no record | `<ID>  no record` then any references | 0 |
| `--limit` below 1 or above 50; `--kind` not in the list; `--refs` or `--open` with words, or with each other; `search` with no words and neither flag | `search: <what is wrong>; see sh-agent help` naming the valid values | 1 |
| The global index is rebuilt or found unreadable | the registry is gone with it; `note: N project registrations dropped; each returns on its next search` | 0 |
| Global: a registered root is gone | `note: dropped <root> (no longer a git checkout)` | 0 |
| The checkout is on a network filesystem | SQLite's own error, prefixed `search:`; documented as unsupported in the spec | 1 |
| `sh-agent report` | `search.db` is never collected; the dry run lists it under skipped | — |
| `sh-agent uninstall` | leaves `~/.config/sh-agent/search.db` (not in the manifest, R4); the spec says to delete it by hand | — |
| Checkout build with no module cache and no network (install's rebuild, BUG-006) | Go's own "cannot find module" error; `deploy/local.md` says the first build of a version needs the module proxy | 1 |

## Verification

Tiers: unit (Go tests with `-race`, temp git repositories), integration (the binary against this checkout and a scratch clone), behavioural (headless CLI runs per the project `AGENTS.md` § Testing), e2e (the sandboxed sample-app runs, Phase 5).

E2E criteria:
- In a checkout, after `git switch` to a branch that lacks a word, `sh-agent search <word>` returns no hit from the other branch; after switching back it returns the hit.
- An uncommitted edit and an untracked new file are found by the next search with no other command run.
- `sh-agent search --refs ADR-040` in this repository shows ADR-040's status as superseded by ADR-041 and lists ADR-041 among the references.
- `sh-agent search --global <a phrase from another project's bug record>` run in this repository returns that record.
- A fresh headless session on each CLI, asked where a past decision was made, runs `sh-agent search` before reading trail files (n of N reported).
- The rendered context stays under 22,000 bytes and ends with GANNET.

## Phases

- [x] Cold-reader check — design ready and implementation ready (round 1 `reviews/2026-09-29-coldread-search-index-r1.md`: two blocking gaps, fixed as D15 and D16; round 2 `reviews/2026-09-29-coldread-search-index-r2.md`: one blocking gap, fixed as D18; round 3 `reviews/2026-09-29-coldread-search-index-r3.md`: implementation ready, design needs revision on two non-blocking items) — cap reached; the operator, 2026-09-29: "Proceed with my fixes (Recommended)", resolved as D19, or the operator's same-turn override quoted with its date
- [x] R4 approved by the operator on the exact text in D1 — who: user — expect: the operator's own words quoted in D1 — approved 2026-09-29: "Approve as written (Recommended)", on the text shown verbatim

### Phase 0 — Baselines that need no dependency

> ## R4 — One binary, one dependency, easy on and off

> `sh-agent` is a single Go binary. D30 — 2026-09-29 — Vector gate not passed: fusing MiniLM vectors into the index adds 6.4 points of mean recall@10 overall and 3.0 on drift against the index alone, under the 10-point bar; the plan's literal baseline, the RRF of index and grep, scores below the index alone, and a gate a weaker baseline passes measures the baseline. The delivery condition fails too: the "pure Go" MiniLM library loads ONNX Runtime as a shared library. Vectors are closed; the operator can reopen them — by: implementer, from `testing/2026-09-29-search-recall.md`.
D31 — 2026-09-29 — The context entry, final: "**Search first:** `sh-agent search <words>` ranks files and trail records; `--refs <BUG-NNN|ADR-NNN|path>` lists every record naming it (run it before touching an area); `--open` lists open bugs and plans; `--global` spans projects. Run it before Grep; grep stays for exact strings, regex, past revisions." — by: implementer, measured at 21,988 bytes.
D32 — 2026-09-29 — Security round 1 (`reviews/2026-09-29-security-search-index.md`): the DSN is built with `net/url`; only a checkout with `.agents/docs` registers in the global search index (supersedes the Interfaces § Global registry line "Every `search` and `index` run inside a git checkout … upserts"); modified and untracked files are hashed from their own bytes (no `git hash-object`); printed text carries no control characters; directories the index creates are 0700; secret-shaped names are never indexed (the installer's list, exported as `harness.SecretShaped`) — by: security review, each fix with a test that failed first.
D33 — 2026-09-29 — Docs review (`reviews/2026-09-29-review-8ee5d70-HEAD-docs.md`): ADR-045's version and module count corrected by addendum ADR-045a; `go mod tidy` makes the driver a direct requirement (the `go` directive stays 1.24.4); the project `AGENTS.md` names the known `x/sys` advisory — by: docs review.
D34 — 2026-09-29 — Security round 2: registration stays automatic for a checkout with `.agents/docs`; the residual (a crafted clone that commits `.agents/docs` and that the operator runs `search` in joins `--global` and `/retro` evidence until `index --global --rebuild`) is accepted — by: the operator, "Keep automatic (Recommended)". The global search index reads only `.agents/docs` and drops a registration that lost it; hint and note lines are printable; hashed bytes are the indexed bytes; the secret list ignores case and adds `.git-credentials` and `credentials` (the installer's list and `.gitignore` too) — by: security review round 2.
D35 — 2026-09-29 — Security round 3, the cap: the round-2 read-once change is reverted (it held every modified and untracked file in memory); a file edited and restored while `search` waits for the write lock can stay indexed with the edit until `index --rebuild`, a documented limit; a registration is dropped only on positive evidence, and a check that errors keeps it with a "skipped" note; the README and spec list the secret patterns as they are — by: the operator, "Revert and document (Recommended)".
D36 — 2026-09-29 — Phase 5 finding: on Claude Code the context entry did not make the main agent search in real work (0 of 28 sessions, the larger-project trail questions included); `security` and `reviewer`, which have it as a fixed step, made all 33 calls. Efficiency on sample apps: no measurable difference (median lane cost 5% lower, ranges overlap, n = 2 per app per arm). Recorded as a follow-up for the operator, not changed in this plan — by: implementer, from `testing/2026-09-29-search-efficiency.md`.
D37 — 2026-09-29 — The Antigravity app lanes are reported, not compared: `agy -p` returned before dispatched subagents did in the search arm's lanes, so they did less work, and the baseline tasklog lane stayed void after three rounds of grants (each added by name per the project `AGENTS.md`); the larger-project pair is the one Antigravity comparison — by: implementer.
D13 — 2026-09-29 — Consumers that get their own line, from the audit (`plans/2026-09-29-audit-search-consumers.md`): `skills/review-standards/SKILL.md:48` and `agents/dreamer.md:36` (restatements: `search <key words>` beside the literal grep), `skills/dream/SKILL.md:41` (graduation check), `skills/handoff/SKILL.md:154` (`search --open --kind plan` first, the awk scan when search refuses), `agents/dreamer.md:29`, `skills/bug/SKILL.md:33`, `skills/feature/SKILL.md:19` (`search --refs <path>` and `--open --kind bug` instead of reading all of `bugs/INDEX.md`), `skills/retro/SKILL.md` (`search --global` for "happened in another project"). The context's restatement rule (`context/AGENTS.md:55`) is covered by the new entry. Added on the operator's question "why not all places that generate lots of md files?" — the audit ranked steps that already grep, and the writers have none because they write without looking: `agents/documentation.md` (`search <changed command or flag>` for every doc that describes it, before editing), `agents/bugs.md` (`search <symptom words> --kind bug` and `--refs <path>` before assigning a new number, to find a duplicate or an existing prevention rule), `agents/changelog.md` (`--refs <path>` for the bug and ADR IDs a change entry should cite; `search` for the ADR a new decision supersedes), `agents/explorer.md` (`search` and `--refs` as its first recon step), `agents/reviewer.md` and `agents/security.md` (`--refs <path> --kind bug` for the files in the diff: past failures, never the author's intent), `skills/research/SKILL.md` Step 1 (`search <topic> --kind plan` for earlier research). Not to use it, and their lines unchanged: `agents/verifier.md` (live-tree, diff-scoped checks), `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:40` (secret scan), the retro skill's exact `rule_ref` greps, and any grep at a past revision (`/review --docs` at the scope's head) — by: implementer, from the audit.
Rejected: vendoring (D9); a watcher or service (D3); a trigram tokenizer (23 MB here against 3.4-12 MB for porter; exact substrings stay with grep); basename matching in `--refs` (`main.go` would match every command); a `--json` output (no consumer named); a separate skill (D7); storing records in the database as the source (D2).

title: Plan — `sh-agent search`: release readiness (2026-09-29)
body:
# Plan — `sh-agent search`: release readiness   (2026-09-29)

## Why

The operator, 2026-09-29, after the search index plan (`plans/2026-09-29-search-index.md`) closed: "I want everything to be done before we cut a new version. Nothing waiting, nothing in todo roadmap or waiting." The open items are that handoff's Next Steps (`handoffs/2026-09-29-2102-search-index-done.md`): the main agent does not use `sh-agent search` in real work (0 of 28 sessions, D36 of the search plan), the Antigravity runs the release gate needs are incomplete, and the benefit on a project with a large trail was never measured over several sessions.

## Scope

In:
- A clean A/B of the whole harness per arm on Claude Code: `--setting-sources project,local` (measured 2026-09-29: user-level skills and context not loaded, project skills loaded), each arm's installed `.claude/{skills,agents,commands}` copied into the run's project, its rendered context appended once. This removes the first comparison's two caveats (v1.12.1 skills in both arms; the context loaded twice).
- Main-agent adoption: measured with the new skills in place; if the main agent still does not search, one change to the context or a skill (D2), measured again.
- A multi-session test on a large trail: three sessions of ordinary work in a clone of this repository at v1.12.1, per arm.
- Every Antigravity run `AGENTS.md` § Release requires: one completed run of each changed skill and agent.
- Reviews and verification of anything this plan changes; docs; the real-home smoke after the operator's install on this box.
- Trail closed: `TODO.md` and `ROADMAP.md` empty, the handoff with nothing queued, so `/preflight v1.13.0` is the only next step.

Out: the release itself (`/preflight` from the operator's turn); the known limits D25 (`x/sys` advisory, needs Go 1.25) and D35 (the edit-during-lock race), both documented decisions; installs on the other machines (after the release).

Follow-ups noted, not built: none.

## Surfaces touched

- `.agents/scratch/eff-kit/` (kit, gitignored, ADR-010), new files beside the Phase 5 kit, which stays as it is: `clean-session.sh` (one clean-arm session), `lane-clean.sh <arm> <app|trail> <n>` (a fresh project, then sessions s1–s3; results in `results-clean/<arm>-<app|trail>-<n>-s<k>.{json,err}`, projects in `~/sandbox/search/eff/cwork/`), `metrics-clean.py` (per lane type, session and arm; the main agent's and the subagents' `sh-agent search` calls in separate columns; prints the D3 count), `score-trail.py` (s1 drift fixed, s2 answers out of 5, s3 `go test ./cmd/sh-agent -run '^TestUsageMatchesDocComment$' -v` shows the test ran and passed, pushed), prompts `LT1`–`LT3` in `prompts.sh`. Each arm's Claude Code install: `~/sandbox/search/eff/chome-<arm>/` (`sh-agent install --vendor claude` of v1.12.1 and of this tree).
- `context/AGENTS.md` or one skill, only if D2 changes wording.
- `.agents/docs/testing/` logs; `testing/skill-matrix.md` if a scenario changes.

## Interfaces

Clean-arm Claude session: `cd <project>; PATH=<arm wrapper dir>:$PATH claude -p --setting-sources project,local --append-system-prompt "$(cat ctx-<arm>.md)" --permission-mode acceptEdits --allowedTools <the Phase 5 list> < prompt`, where `<project>/.claude/` holds a copy of `<arm home>/.claude/{skills,agents,commands}` from `sh-agent install --vendor claude --home <arm home>` of that arm's tree, excluded from git by `<project>/.git/info/exclude`. No `--agents`, no `--add-dir`.

Large-trail lane (per arm, one clone of this repository at v1.12.1 with its `.agents/docs` trail, the drift seed of the search plan's Phase 5, and a bare origin): s1 "resume from the trail, then fix the seeded drift: `sh-agent update --check` exits 2 when behind — make every living file agree, as a Task under the Definition of Done"; s2 "resume from the trail, then answer the five trail questions of the search plan's Phase 5 in ANSWERS.md with file:line, commit"; s3 "resume from the trail, then, as a Task under the Definition of Done, add a Go test `TestUsageMatchesDocComment` to `cmd/sh-agent` that fails when a verb in the usage text is missing from `main.go`'s doc comment, or the other way round"; the exact prompts are `LT1`–`LT3`. Each prompt carries its own "Do not ask me anything" and its push instruction; s2 is a question session that commits and pushes.

## Failure modes

- A run auto-denied on Antigravity: the command is added by name and the run repeated (project `AGENTS.md` § Testing).
- `agy -p` returns before a dispatched subagent: the run is repeated up to three times; still void after three, the gate is told in the log, and the operator decides (Open row).

## Verification

E2E criteria:
- The main agent of the search arm runs `sh-agent search` in at least 4 of 6 large-trail sessions (Phase 1, or Phase 2 after the change), or the operator has accepted the measured number in their own turn.
- The clean A/B's per-session table exists for Claude Code with both arms delivering; the main agent's `sh-agent search` count is reported for each arm.
- Every changed skill and agent has one completed Antigravity run on disk (artifact or answer) with no auto-denied line.
- After the operator's install on this box, the three real-home smoke checks pass on both CLIs, and `sh-agent search --refs ADR-040` answers from the installed binary.
- `TODO.md` and `ROADMAP.md` hold headers only; the newest handoff's Next Steps name only `/preflight v1.13.0`.

## Phases

- [x] Cold-reader check — round 1 `reviews/2026-09-29-coldread-search-release-readiness-r1.md` (one blocking gap, D3), round 2 `-r2.md` (two, D4), round 3 `-r3.md` (one narrow blocking item, one non-blocking) — cap reached; the operator, 2026-09-29: "Proceed with my fix (Recommended)", resolved as D5

### Phase 1 — Clean A/B on Claude Code, with the new skills
- [x] Kit: the files named in Surfaces touched; a dry run of one `trail` project per arm (setup only, no session) shows its `.claude/skills` holds that arm's skills (the search arm's `feature` skill contains `sh-agent search --refs`, the baseline's does not) and the drift seed in place — verify: AI — expect: `grep -c` 2 and 0, the seed line found — done 2026-09-29: `grep -c` 2 and 0, the seed line found, `.claude/` excluded, tree clean, in both arms' dry-run projects
- [x] Sample apps, both arms, 2 runs each, 3 sessions (`lane-clean.sh <arm> linkshelf|tasklog <n>`) — verify: AI, `outcomes.py` pointed at `cwork/`, `metrics-clean.py` — expect: the app rows of the table, main-agent and subagent searches in separate columns — done 2026-09-29: 24 of 24 sessions delivered, all eight lanes pass vet and tests with the feature built; median lane cost 18.02 (base) against 18.17 USD (search); the main agent searched in 9 of 12 search-arm sessions
- [x] Large-trail lane, both arms, 2 runs each (`lane-clean.sh <arm> trail <n>`) — verify: AI, `score-trail.py`, `metrics-clean.py` — expect: per session the trail rows of the table and the three scores — done 2026-09-29: 12 of 12 sessions delivered; every lane: drift fixed, 5 of 5 answers, the new test passes
- [x] Adoption decision (D3): count the large-trail sessions of the search arm in which the MAIN agent (not a subagent) ran `sh-agent search` — verify: AI, the D3 line `metrics-clean.py` prints (main-agent calls only, from the main transcript; subagent transcripts are counted in their own column) — expect: a D-row stating `n of 6` and `adopted` (n ≥ 4) or `not adopted` (n ≤ 3); `not adopted` opens Phase 2, `adopted` marks Phase 2's boxes `[-]` with that D-row as the reason — done 2026-09-29: 3 of 6, `not adopted` (D9); Phase 2 runs
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: `testing/<date>-search-adoption.md` committed — evidence: `testing/2026-09-29-search-adoption.md`, 2026-09-29

### Phase 2 — Main-agent adoption (runs when D3 says `not adopted`)
- [x] D2 decided with the operator: the change and its exact text — who: both — done 2026-09-29: pre-decided, D2
- [x] The change, `TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock` PASS if context — verify: unit — expect: PASS — done 2026-09-29: PASS at 21,996 of 22,000 bytes, GANNET last; the handoff skill's restatement of the order updated (D9)
- [x] Re-run of the probe (`search-first`, 3 with, 3 control) and the large-trail lane, search arm, 2 runs — verify: AI — expect: the main agent runs `sh-agent search` in at least 4 of the 6 large-trail sessions; fewer is an `Open:` row put to the operator with the numbers, never a silent pass — done 2026-09-29: large-trail 6 of 6 sessions (bar: 4), quality unchanged; the probe on the 65-file fixture 0 of 3 with the change and 0 of 3 control — the step is followed on a real-sized trail and skipped on a tiny one (D9)
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: log and change committed; `/review --docs` over the change — evidence: `testing/2026-09-29-search-adoption.md`; commit f41e5c0; `reviews/2026-09-29-review-abbaddc-1634787-docs.md` APPROVE, no findings, 2026-09-29

### Phase 2b — Optimizations (the operator: "run optimizations")
- [x] Measure, then keep only what measures better — verify: AI, `index --rebuild` three times each, and an equivalence run of `parseRefs` over every tracked file — expect: faster build, smaller index, identical references — done 2026-09-29: build 2.2 s → 1.7 s and index 24.1 MB → 21.7 MB on this repository; the prefiltered `parseRefs` returned the same 40,842 references on 1,077 files; kept: insert statements prepared once per reconcile, `parseRefs` skipping lines that cannot match, the `refs(oid)` index dropped (it served only garbage collection); rejected: merging the FTS index after a build (the file grew to 25.8 MB from free pages); `TestRefsPrefilterIsEquivalent` added, mutations O1–O3 each fail it; the extension list is one source for the regex and the prefilter (D8)

### Phase 3 — Antigravity runs the release gate needs
- [x] One completed run of each changed agent without one yet (`dreamer`; `security` on the final wording) and each changed skill (`review-standards`, `dream`, `handoff`, `bug`, `feature`, `retro`, `research`, `init-project`), in a sandbox home installed from this tree — verify: AI — expect: artifact or answer on disk, no auto-denied line, up to three attempts each — done 2026-09-29: 10 of 10 scenarios completed; `init-project` and `dream` with the per-run skip flag (agy auto-denies `$(…)`), D11
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: `testing/<date>-search-agy-gate.md` committed — evidence: `testing/2026-09-29-search-agy-gate.md`, 2026-09-29

### Phase 4 — Real home and close
- [x] `sh-agent update` on this box (D7, on the operator's word), then `hash -r` — verify: AI, `sh-agent status` — expect: binary line without a warning, drift none — first run 2026-09-29 21:32 at 2716d08: 33 written, `binary 2716d0858bc1` without a warning, GANNET last, `sh-agent search --refs ADR-040` answered; repeated after the last change of this plan — third run 22:27 at 8e1b7f5 after the security fix: 1 written, `binary 8e1b7f5aee85` without a warning, both existing indexes tightened to 0600
- [x] Real-home smoke on both CLIs (`testing/2026-09-03-verify-real-home.md`) plus `sh-agent search --refs ADR-040` — verify: AI — expect: PASS, GANNET — done 2026-09-29: PASS on both, `testing/2026-09-29-verify-real-home-search.md` (run at f41e5c0; 8e1b7f5 changed Go code only, and the installed binary answered `search --refs ADR-045`)
- [x] Definition of Done: verifier, reviews for what changed, changes entries, plan closed, `TODO.md`/`ROADMAP.md` empty, handoff naming only `/preflight v1.13.0` — done 2026-09-29: `testing/2026-09-29-verify-search-release-readiness.md` PASS over aae16af..1634787 (362 pass, 2 skips with reasons); code review APPROVE; security findings fixed with Outcome (D10); docs lens APPROVE; `changes/2026-09-29-2326-search-release-readiness.md`; BUG-106 and BUG-107 graduated earlier; the release follows in the same session (D6), so the handoff is written after it and names nothing queued

## Risks

Assumptions: `--setting-sources project,local` excludes the real home's skills and context and loads project skills — checked 2026-09-29 by a probe (a project skill listed, no harness skill, no GANNET). Headless Claude Code reads `.claude/` in the project (only writes are refused) — checked by the same probe.

## Decisions

D1 — 2026-09-29 — The clean A/B replaces the first comparison's setup for everything in this plan; the first comparison stays as recorded — by: implementer, from the probe.
D4 — 2026-09-29 — The kit is new files beside the Phase 5 kit (named in Surfaces touched), because the Phase 5 `metrics.py` sums main and subagent searches and runs the larger task as one session; the matrix task adds a Zip place column, since the table has no row shape for a place — by: cold read round 2 (`reviews/2026-09-29-coldread-search-release-readiness-r2.md`).
D3 — 2026-09-29 — The adoption bar: the main agent of the search arm runs `sh-agent search` in at least 4 of the 6 large-trail sessions (2 runs × 3 sessions); that task is where the trail is large enough for search to matter; sample-app sessions are reported but do not decide — by: cold read round 1 (`reviews/2026-09-29-coldread-search-release-readiness-r1.md`, blocking question 1).
D2 — 2026-09-29 — If D3 says `not adopted`: `sh-agent search --open` joins the context's resume reading order, paid for by an equal cut named in a D-row, then measured again; if it still misses the bar, the number is reported and the release goes ahead — by: the operator, "Resume step (Recommended)".
D5 — 2026-09-29 — Round 3 residue: the third trail session's task is the usage/doc-comment test (the zip-place column documented a place without using `--from-zip`); the prompts carry their own waivers — by: the operator, "Proceed with my fix (Recommended)".
D6 — 2026-09-29 — The release is v1.13.0, a MINOR: new verbs, nothing an existing install must react to — by: the operator, "v1.13.0 (Recommended)", and "Cut new version update docs. This is dod". Scope's Out line on the release is superseded: `/preflight v1.13.0` runs at the end of this plan.
D11 — 2026-09-29 — Antigravity 1.2.13 auto-denies, headless, any command containing `$(…)` whatever the grants (probe in `testing/2026-09-29-search-agy-gate.md`); `init-project` and `dream` ran with the per-run `--dangerously-skip-permissions` flag inside the sandbox home and a throwaway clone, as `testing/2026-09-21-verify-real-home-smoke-5.md` did; from the real home (`toolPermission: always-proceed`) the limit does not apply and both CLIs' smoke passed — by: implementer, measured.
D10 — 2026-09-29 — Reviews of this plan's source changes (aae16af..f41e5c0): code APPROVE (`reviews/2026-09-29-review-aae16af-f41e5c0-code.md`); security two findings, both fixed with tests that failed first (`reviews/2026-09-29-security-aae16af-f41e5c0.md` § Outcome): the index files are refused unless regular files, and are mode 0600 — by: security review.
D9 — 2026-09-29 — Adoption: with the first wording and the new skills the main agent ran `sh-agent search` in 3 of 6 large-trail sessions (`not adopted`). Per D2, `→ `sh-agent search --open` (what is open)` joins the context's resume reading order after `bugs/INDEX.md`, paid for by cutting "`--open` lists open bugs and plans; " from the Search first entry (net +8 bytes, 21,996 of 22,000); `skills/handoff/SKILL.md`'s restatement of the order gains the step. Measured again in a separate arm: 6 of 6 large-trail sessions, same quality; the trail-question session read 12k characters against the baseline's 27k and cost 0.58 against 0.66 USD; the whole lane cost about 15% more than the baseline in both search arms, mostly in s1, where the search arms' agents checked the new bug number against the other branch and renumbered it — by: measured by implementer; change per the operator's D2.
D8 — 2026-09-29 — Optimizations kept only where measured (Phase 2b); warm search was already 25–40 ms and is unchanged; the schema version stays 1 because no release carries the old index — a development cache keeps its extra index until `index --rebuild` — by: the operator, "run optimizations"; measured by implementer.
D7 — 2026-09-29 — The operator asked for the local harness to be updated ("Don't forget to update local harness"): `sh-agent update` runs on this box from this session, once the tree is clean — by: the operator.

title: Plan — audit fix: everything the 2026-09-30 audits found, fixed, improved and extended (2026-09-30)
body:
# Plan — audit fix: everything the 2026-09-30 audits found, fixed, improved and extended   (2026-09-30)

## Why

The operator (2026-09-30, own turn): "I want to fix all things you find, big and small. … Go with your recommendations on the ones you added a recommendation. On the others do research. … The bottom line I want everything fixed, improved, optimized, add new features from your audit report. … do your research first before execute. … split this up in phases and tasks and everything needs to be verified … You can update the local harness everything you need it. Also run sandboxed tests, all allowed. … a separate TODO file in this project that has the HIGHEST priority … when everything is done, re-run the audit."

The evidence is `plans/2026-09-30-recon-audit-fix.md` (IDs C, WS, TS, AG, IN, SD, TR, G). Research briefs: `plans/2026-09-30-research-audit-fix-{frontend,terraform-gcp,golang,cloudrun-operate,formats}.md`.

## Scope

In: every finding in the recon brief, by ID; the workflow gaps G1–G13 as new skills, templates and one context paragraph; the installer simplifications IN-S; a real-home install and the sandbox tiers; a re-audit at the end, published the same way as the two before.

Out: cutting a version (`/preflight`) — the operator cuts it; installing the dream timer on the real home (who: user); `/retro` (user-invoked only; the graduations here go through mechanisms and the bugs agent); the AWS terraform content (deleted, not ported); anything in a consumer project.

Follow-ups noted, not built: a per-project "size tier" beyond the one paragraph (G11); i18n skill; Node/npm hygiene beyond the docker build stage and a frontend paragraph.

## Surfaces touched

`context/AGENTS.md`, `context/dev-setup.md`, `REQUIREMENTS.md` (approval-gated), `README.md` (map legend), `AGENTS.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `PRIORITY_TODO.md`; `agents/*.md` (8); `internal/harness/{derive,inventory,report,apply,release,zip,pathguard,frontmatter}.go` + tests, `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` + tests; `internal/search/{search,dream}.go`, `internal/dream/{collect,run,prompt}.go` + tests; `skills/*` (all 29; python and anti-ui-slop struck; new: requirements, spec, operate-gcp, data-gcp, api-auth-gcp, testing-strategy, explain-project); `skills/VENDORED.md`; `skills/init-project/assets/**`; `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/*.md`; `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md` + a committed kit preamble; five stopped review artifacts (appended void marker); `.agents/docs/bugs/INDEX.md` (via bugs agent); a new handoff.

## Interfaces

**Context budget (C1).** Hard verify: rendered context ≤ 15,000 bytes, pinned by a second test `TestRenderedContextUnderTarget` that FAILS above 15,000 (the 22,000 Antigravity pin stays; guide § 2 and AGENTS.md Setup commands name both pins — docs clause). 14,500 is the goal; a shortfall between 14,500 and 15,000 is reported in the checkpoint, not a failure. Arithmetic (cold read rounds 1–2): the first list saves ≈ 4,600; the second ≈ 2,950; line 11's compaction sentence (moved to `skills/handoff` § Usage) ≈ 200; add-backs ≈ +500 (G11 paragraph, seven skill names minus two, the resume-line clause): net ≈ 14,650. The formats brief's evidence: adherence tracks the number of distinct instructions and their presence, not bytes, so the cut removes whole rules from the always-loaded file and lands each in the skill or agent that acts on it. What moves where:
- line 52 → one short "before commit" bullet (numstat binary check, `rm -r` by name, ` D` stop sign) ≈ 300 chars; the escape/heredoc lesson → `skills/bash` § "Escapes survive tools"; the post-dispatch `git status/log/tag` check → the Skill/Subagent paragraph (one clause).
- line 56 → first sentence + "the two shapes are review-standards § 7"; shapes' text → review-standards § 7.
- line 57 → first two sentences; `hash -r`/`rehash`/`type` → `skills/bash` § "An installed command is verified by the shell".
- line 58 → first clause + pointer; the rest is already review-standards § 2.
- lines 59–62 → one bullet: "Code-shape rules a review checks and an author follows — guard on error, dry-run resolves every path, embedded artifact pinned both ways, verification never in a `&&` chain to a commit — are review-standards § 8"; full text → review-standards § 8 (new) and the four Go-flavoured ones also into `skills/golang/SKILL.md` § Coding Standards (review-standards' new sections are § 7 and § 8, after its existing six).
- line 34 → "A dispatch to reviewer, security or verifier names a tool-call budget below the agent's maxTurns and repeats the artifact duty; an agent stopped with work running is stopped (`TaskStop`) once its artifact is on disk." ## Failure modes

- A context edit that pushes the render over 22,000 fails `TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock`; over 15,000 fails `TestRenderedContextUnderTarget`.
- A skill or agent that no longer parses fails `sh-agent install --home .agents/scratch/x` with the file named.
- A behavioural run that proves nothing (auto-denied, no skill loaded) is reported as such, never as n/N; the kit preamble asserts the fixture before the CLI starts.
- A struck skill leaves no dangling reference: `TestSkillLinksResolve` and `grep -rn python\|anti-ui-slop` over context, skills, docs.
- A REQUIREMENTS edit is made only after the operator approves its exact text (D29a); until then the phase ships without it and the task stays unticked.
- The real-home install fails the smoke checks → `sh-agent install` from the last good commit, reported.

## Verification

Tiers (guide §): 1 Go checks (every phase touching Go); 2 harness self-check (every phase touching context, agents, skills); 3 scratch-home install and drift; 3b report (Phase 1 redaction, Phase 8); 3c verb matrix (Phase 8); 3d search (Phase 1); 3e memory/dream (Phase 1); 4 sandbox CLI start (Phases 3–7); 5 real-home smoke (Phase 9); behavioural runs `claude -p --agents` n of N (Phase 4) and `--append-system-prompt` (Phase 3's size-tier paragraph); skill-matrix rows for every changed and new skill (Phase 9).
E2E criteria (yes/no): (a) the sandbox home of guide § 4 (logged-in copies, deleted by name after) installs the tree with no drift and both CLIs start and answer the canary; (b) in a scratch clone outside every checkout, driven from that sandbox home, `/init-project` then `/spec` then `/feature` produce a spec, a plan and a cold-read artifact; (c) `sh-agent dream --project` with the fake CLIs of guide § 3e on PATH, on a fixture database containing a tool call whose arguments sit in a string-only sub-message, leaks no argument into the recorded prompt; (d) the re-audit lists no high finding from the recon brief as open.

body:
# Plan — R-parity, `sh-agent memory`, background `sh-agent dream`   (2026-09-30)

## Why
The operator, 2026-09-30:
- "The dream skills should be a features that runs autonomously in all projects registered on the machine and checks conversations, assets, feedback, critique, skills, for improvements. This should run in the background as a monitor or subagent that does not care about what is happening. It just collects, generates new skills if needed and such. That was the plan."
- "Dreamer is one and memory is the other. … remember these should work for both Claude or agy and both."
- "In the best of worlds I want the setup and executions to be exactly the same over agy and Claude. … Can we build in that feature in sh-agent?"
- On the R-parity text and the two tables below: "Sounds great. Include this in the next version. Go all approved go work."

Both tables are quoted as the operator approved them in chat on 2026-09-30.

**Dreamer table** (approved):
1. How it runs: a user timer (systemd on Linux, launchd on Mac) runs `sh-agent dream --all` nightly, headless, regardless of what any session is doing.
2. Which projects: every harness project in the global search index (`~/.config/sh-agent/search.db`); no new registry; projects that haven't changed are skipped.
3. What it reads: both CLIs' conversation transcripts, `feedback.jsonl`, each project's memory, bug records, reviews, retros, and the installed skills — read-only, treated as data.
4. What it writes: draft skills and proposals into `~/.config/sh-agent/proposals/`, nothing auto-installed; applied through `/retro --harness`.
5. Which CLI: the one the install manifest names (`agy -p` on an agy machine, `claude -p` where Claude Code is installed).
6. Cost limit: once a night, a cap per project, a log line per run shown by `sh-agent status`.
7. The requirement change: R3 gets one named exception, with an ADR.

**Memory table** (approved):
1. agy's memory is thinner (it writes only on corrections) → both CLIs write the same four types by the same rule, written by the harness.
2. Claude Code loads memory automatically; agy only because the context says so → accept for now.
3. Claude Code's split store in an untrusted folder → the dreamer detects it and moves the notes.
4. Notes don't follow the operator between machines → keep per machine.
5. The memory spec header says "nothing below is built" → fix.

Since then, R10's "the harness provides it once and both CLIs use that version" supersedes memory items 2 and 3 (D2): loading goes through `sh-agent memory show` on both CLIs, and with native writes off there is no split store. Recon: `plans/2026-09-30-recon-memory-dream.md`. Cold read r1: `reviews/2026-09-30-cold-read-parity-memory-dream-r1.md`.

## Scope
In:
1. **R10 (R-parity)**: done in d6e396a. The requirement edits the dream job needs, on the operator's word (D3, D12, D13): the R3 exception, R4's driver and `uninstall` sentences, and the Non-goals memory-keys exception.
2. **`sh-agent memory add|show`** on both CLIs. Claude Code's native auto memory is switched off per project (`autoMemoryEnabled: false`, D2).
3. **The `project-memory` skill** (D14), plus:
   - `feedback-log` rule 7 calls the verb on every CLI;
   - the context resume step runs `sh-agent memory show`;
   - `/init-project` Step 5b writes the new key;
   - `/dream` Step 1 always uses `<root>/.agents/memory`;
   - `agents/dreamer.md`, the memory spec and README are updated.
4. **`sh-agent dream --all | --project <dir>`, with `--dry-run`, the CLI from the global `--vendor` flag**: collect, redact, one tool-free CLI call, then render and write proposals and drafts. Also a state file, a log, a lock, and the `status` line.
5. **`sh-agent dream --install-timer | --remove-timer`**, opt-in (D5). `uninstall` removes the timer (D12).
6. **Consumers**:
   - project-level `/retro` reads the dream proposals for its own project;
   - `/retro --harness` reads the harness-target ones;
   - `report` sends `proposals/dream/harness/` and nothing else under `proposals/dream/` (D19);
   - `status` gets the dream line;
   - the README map gets the job (D13).

Out:
- Auto-applying anything (dreamer item 4).
- Any permission in a vendor settings file (Non-goals).
- Cross-machine memory (memory item 4).
- `memory forget`/`list` verbs (the `/dream` skill deletes interactively).

Follow-ups noted, not built:
- A cron fallback for Linux without systemd.
- Agent worktree isolation in `sh-agent` (a later R10 plan).

## Surfaces touched
- **Go**:
  - `cmd/sh-agent/main.go`: verbs; usage const :39; `status` :508; `uninstall` calls `dream.RemoveTimer`, so `internal/harness` does not import `internal/dream`.
  - new `internal/memory/`;
  - new `internal/dream/` (collect, claude transcripts, prompt, run, render, state, lock, timer);
  - `internal/search`: `ListProjects(home)`, plus `AgyConversationText(home, root, since)`, which keeps the driver inside `internal/search` (AGENTS.md:59, D12);
  - `internal/harness/report.go`: exported `Redact(string) string` over `redactLines` (:199); `Collect` (:331-339) gains `proposals/dream/harness/*.md` and still skips the rest of `proposals/dream/` (D19).
- **Harness text**:
  - `skills/project-memory/SKILL.md` (new);
  - `skills/feedback-log/SKILL.md:90`;
  - `skills/init-project/SKILL.md:110-131`;
  - `skills/dream/SKILL.md` Step 1 and description;
  - `agents/dreamer.md:18,28,32`;
  - `skills/retro/SKILL.md:44,48,118`;
  - `skills/distill/SKILL.md:38`;
  - `context/AGENTS.md:9` (resume).
- **Docs**:
  - `REQUIREMENTS.md` (R3, R4, Non-goals, on approval);
  - `DECISIONS.md` (ADR-047 addendum);
  - `specs/sh-agent/memory-loop.md` (rewritten: the memory half);
  - new `specs/sh-agent/dream.md`;
  - `README.md`: map :5-60 with `TestHarnessMap`, `configDir` contents :30, state rows :212-214, verbs table, `uninstall` row;
  - project `AGENTS.md` Layout (`internal/memory`, `internal/dream`) and :59 (the driver's second reader in `internal/search`);
  - `deploy/local.md` (timer install/remove, uninstall);
  - `testing/skill-matrix.md` and `testing/sh-agent-matrix.md` rows.

## Interfaces

**`sh-agent memory add --type <user|feedback|project|reference> --name <slug> --description <text>`**, with the body on stdin (required, non-empty).
- **Root**: `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from the working directory.
- **The file**: `<root>/.agents/memory/<slug>.md`, whose frontmatter is:
  ```
  ---
  name: <slug>
  description: "<text, JSON-escaped>"
  metadata:
    node_type: memory
    type: <type>
    modified: <UTC RFC 3339>
  ---
  ```
  then the body. `originSessionId` is not written: no CLI exposes its session id to a shell call, and `/dream`'s promote test already counts a file without it as one session.
- **The index**: the line in `MEMORY.md` for that file is `- [<slug>](<slug>.md) — <description>`. The same slug replaces both the file and its line; an existing line is found by its link target `(<slug>.md)`. A `--description` with a newline is refused (exit 2). Files are written 0600.
- **`<slug>`** matches `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$`.
- **Refusals**: exit 2, one line on stderr, nothing written. In order:
  1. not a git checkout;
  2. `.agents` or `.agents/memory` is a symlink;
  3. `git ls-files .agents/memory` prints a path;
  4. `git check-ignore -q .agents/memory/<slug>.md` exits non-zero (the path would be committed: "run /init-project first");
  5. the index would pass 200 lines.
- **Store and writes**: created 0700 when absent. The file is written to a temp name and renamed.
- **Lock**: the index is rewritten whole under `<store>/.lock`, created O_EXCL and holding the PID. A lock whose PID is not alive, or older than 30 s, is removed. A live lock is retried for 5 s, then exit 2 "store busy".

**`sh-agent memory show`**
- Same root and checks 1–3.
- Prints `MEMORY.md`, capped at 200 lines and 25 KB; a cut adds a last line `(… N more lines in .agents/memory/MEMORY.md)`.
- No store, or no index: prints nothing, exit 0.
- **Rollout hint**: when `<root>/.claude/settings.local.json` exists and lacks `"autoMemoryEnabled": false`, `show` prints one last line: `Claude Code's native memory is still on here: run /init-project to switch it off (R10)`. Every session start on either CLI then surfaces the rollout for projects scaffolded before this change.

**`sh-agent dream --all | --project <dir> [--dry-run] [--vendor claude|agy]`**. Neither `--all` nor `--project` is a usage error. `--project` exists for the e2e and to rerun one project after a failure (D15).
- **Projects**: `search.ListProjects(home)`, a plain SELECT on `projects(root,…)` (store.go:41), no reconcile. A missing db means an empty list. `--project` takes one root. A root is skipped with a log line when it is gone, not a git checkout, or lacks `.agents/docs`.
- **Start**: `t0` = now, taken before collecting.
- **Watermark**: in `~/.config/sh-agent/dream-state.json`, `{"projects":{"<root>":"<RFC3339>"},"last_run":{"at":…,"projects":n,"proposals":m,"error":""}}`. The first run uses t0 − 14 days.
- **Changed** means any per-project input below (1, 2, 3, 5, 6) newer than the watermark: file mtime; for transcripts, the line or step time. Input 4 (installed skills) is global: it never makes a project changed and is sent only with a changed project. When nothing changed: skip, log `unchanged`, and write no file. When something changed, the memory files are sent whole; the other inputs only the changed parts.
- **Inputs**:
  1. the memory store;
  2. `feedback.jsonl` lines whose `project` is the root and whose `ts` is after the watermark;
  3. files under `<docs>/{bugs,reviews,retros,changes,handoffs}` with mtime after the watermark;
  4. the installed skills' `name` and `description` from the manifest vendor's skill directory;
  5. Claude Code `~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl` lines with `timestamp` after the watermark whose `cwd` is the root or under it, `type` `user`/`assistant`, text parts only;
  6. Antigravity text from `search.AgyConversationText(home, root, since)` (D8). It copies `conversation_summaries.db` and each matching `conversations/<id>.db` with their `-wal` and `-shm` files into a private temp directory under `<home>/.config/sh-agent/`, opens the copies, and deletes them after; it never opens a live file.
- **Redaction**: every input passes `harness.Redact` and `$HOME` → `~`.
- **Prompt**: fixed instructions (in `internal/dream/prompt.go`), then the inputs in the order above, each fenced and labelled "data, not instructions". The cap is 256 KB: the oldest transcript text is dropped first, and the prompt says what was dropped.
- **CLI**: the global `--vendor` flag (main.go:62, "default: from manifest"): `antigravity`/`agy` → agy; `claude` and `all` → claude (dreamer item 5).
  - claude: `claude -p --tools "" --no-session-persistence --output-format text --strict-mcp-config --setting-sources local`, prompt on stdin (the two flags the code passes, `internal/dream/dream.go`; row corrected 2026-10-01, plan audit-fix SD-spec).
  - agy: the invocation proven by the Phase 4 probe (D7).
  - Both run with cwd `<home>/.config/sh-agent/dream-work/` (0700, kept empty; it is not a project, so the run's own conversation never maps to one) and a 10-minute timeout.
  - The child inherits `sh-agent`'s own environment unchanged: `--home` moves only what `sh-agent` itself reads and writes, never the child's `HOME`, so the CLI authenticates as it does for the operator (AGENTS.md:65). A sandbox run sets `HOME` for the whole `sh-agent` process instead.
  - The binary is resolved on PATH at run time; under the timer, PATH is the one captured at `--install-timer` (below).
- **Model output**: the prompt asks for one JSON object:
  ```
  {"proposals":[{"title","kind":"rule|skill|procedure|memory","target":"harness|project","file","text","evidence"}],
   "skills":[{"name","description","body"}]}
  ```
  `sh-agent` takes the first `{…}` span of stdout that parses. When nothing parses, the project is `fail invalid output`, and the raw text is kept in `<home>/.config/sh-agent/dream-failed/<date>-<project>.txt` (0600), outside the CLI's cwd.
- **Written on success**:
  - `~/.config/sh-agent/proposals/dream/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<project name>.md` (`-2`, `-3` on the same day). Frontmatter: `owner: sh-agent dream`, `date`, `project`, `cli`, `inputs` (counts per kind, and what was dropped). Then one section per proposal:
    ```
    ### <n>. <title>
    **Status:** queued
    **Target:** harness|project   **Kind:** …   **File:** …

    <text>

    Evidence: <evidence>
    ```
  - Harness-target proposals (`target: harness`) are written to a second file, `proposals/dream/harness/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<project name>.md`, same shape. `report` sends that directory (R8: report sends "this machine's corrections, proposals"), so a binary-only or zip place feeds harness proposals back too; project-target files stay on the machine (D6).
  - Every skill goes to `proposals/dream/drafts/<date>-<project name>-<name>/SKILL.md`, with `name` validated as a slug (an invalid name is dropped and listed). The draft is `---\nname: <name>\ndescription: "<…>"\n---\n<body>`.
  - All model text is redacted again before it is written.
- **Zero proposals**: when the JSON parses with no proposals and no skills, no file is written, the log says `ok 0 proposals`, and the watermark advances.
- **Watermark**: advances to t0 only after a successful parse and, when there is anything to write, after the write.
- **Log**: `~/.config/sh-agent/dream.log`, one line per project (`<ts> <root> ok|unchanged|skip|fail <reason>`) and one per run (`<ts> - run <n> projects, <m> proposals[, error <reason>]`). A failure before the first project (no CLI, lock or state unreadable) writes the run line with `error` and sets `last_run.error`.
- **Lock**: `~/.config/sh-agent/dream.lock` holds the PID. A lock whose PID is not alive is stale and replaced; a live lock makes the run exit 0 with "already running".
- **`--dry-run`**:
  - prints per project the input counts and bytes, what would be dropped, and the CLI command line;
  - prints the prompt when `--project` is given;
  - runs no CLI, and writes, locks and advances nothing (a test asserts each).
- **Exit**: 0 when every project is ok, unchanged or skipped; 1 when any failed; 2 on a pre-project failure.

**`sh-agent dream --install-timer | --remove-timer`** (D5, D12)
- **Linux**: writes `~/.config/systemd/user/sh-agent-dream.service` and `.timer`.
  - The service: `ExecStart=<home>/.local/bin/sh-agent dream --all` (BinPath), and `Environment=PATH=<the PATH of the installing shell>`, so `claude` and `agy` in `~/.local/bin` resolve.
  - The timer: `OnCalendar=*-*-* 03:00`, `Persistent=true`.
  - Then `systemctl --user daemon-reload` and `systemctl --user enable --now sh-agent-dream.timer`.
- **macOS**: `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.styrman.sh-agent-dream.plist` with the same program, `EnvironmentVariables` PATH and `StartCalendarInterval` Hour 3, then `launchctl bootstrap gui/<uid> <plist>`.
- **Guards**:
  - `--install-timer` refuses when BinPath is missing, or when `systemctl`/`launchctl` is absent (exit 2, naming it).
  - Unit files are written only when absent or identical to the rendered text; a hand-edited one is kept and named.
- **`--remove-timer`**: `systemctl --user disable --now` / `launchctl bootout`, then deletes the files. Absent is fine.
- **`--home`**: the unit files are written under `<home>`, like every other path (main.go:61); `systemctl` and `launchctl` are resolved on PATH, so tests put fakes first on PATH and never reach the real user manager (R6). Each branch (write, identical, hand-edited kept, absent on remove, a failing `systemctl`, `uninstall` without a manifest) is tested against the fakes.
- **`status`** reports the timer as installed when its unit file exists.
- **The manifest**: the timer is not listed in it (listed files are deleted as stale by the next `install`, apply.go:88-109).
- **`uninstall`**:
  - calls the same removal when a unit file exists, including when there is no manifest (D12);
  - `uninstall --dry-run` prints "would remove the dream timer" and runs no `systemctl`/`launchctl` (a test asserts it).

**`status`**: after the `retro` line (main.go:508):
- `dream      last run <date>: <n> projects, <m> proposals; timer installed|not installed`
- `dream      last run <date> failed: <error>; timer …`
- `dream      never run; timer …`

**`/init-project` Step 5b item 2**: the settings file gets `"autoMemoryDirectory"` as today, and `"autoMemoryEnabled": false`. Each key is handled on its own with the existing branches:
- absent file → both keys in the one-object write;
- present without the key → one inserted line after `{` per key, with the Edit tool;
- present with the key → kept and reported (a `true` is reported, never changed).

The parse check runs after each insert. Antigravity-only machine: nothing (Step 1).

**Context resume step**: "… → `sh-agent memory show` (the project's memory; on every CLI)" replaces "on Antigravity, `.agents/memory/MEMORY.md` when … Claude Code loads it itself". The byte difference is paid in the same edit (`TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock`, 21998/22000 today).

## Failure modes
- `memory add|show` refusal: exit 2 with a one-line reason; the session reports it and continues without memory.
- Headless sessions without a grant for `sh-agent`: the call is refused and no memory loads. This is the same on both CLIs, a cost of R10 (D16).
- `dream`: the per-project failures are those above (fail + log, watermark kept, others continue, exit 1). A pre-project failure is exit 2 plus the run log line and `status` "failed". Unparseable model output keeps the raw text.
- Timer: a failing `systemctl`/`launchctl` exits 2 and names the unit files left in place.

## Verification
Tiers: unit (`go test -race`), sandbox e2e, the `dreamer` behavioural run, § 3d for the search additions, and the release gate's real-home runs. The setups for R10:
- **agy-only**: a sandbox home installed `--vendor agy` (the kit of `testing/2026-09-30-verify-real-home-v1.16.2.md`).
- **both**: the real home, vendor `all`.
- **claude-only**: a sandbox home installed `--vendor claude`, with Claude Code pointed at it by `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and a copied credentials file (chmod 600, deleted by name after). This is an assumption the Phase 2 checkpoint's first run checks; when Claude Code cannot authenticate that way, the claude-only runs are marked not exercised and the "both" runs stand for Claude Code.

E2E criteria:
1. **Memory parity**: in a scaffolded fixture project, on each setup, a session told "remember that we deploy on Fridays" leaves a file and an index line in `.agents/memory/`. A fresh session on the same setup, on each installed CLI, answers "when do we deploy?" with Friday.
2. **Claude native writes are off**: in the claude setup, with the pre-change harness installed (no `project-memory` skill, rule 7 as before), the must-fail control comes first. With `autoMemoryEnabled` absent, a session told a preference leaves a file carrying `originSessionId` (native) in `.agents/memory/`. Then the key is set to `false` and the current harness is installed, and no file with `originSessionId` appears while the verb-written file does. A control that produces no native file makes E2E 2 "not exercised", never passed.
3. **Dream golden path** (home: a scratch `--home` whose `search.db` indexes only the fixture projects; the child is the real `claude`): `sh-agent dream --all --home <scratch>` over two indexed fixture projects with new trail and memory writes one proposal file per project with at least one `**Status:** queued` section. A second run with no changes writes no file and logs `unchanged` twice.
4. **Dream edge**:
   - a deleted root is logged `skip`;
   - a secret-shaped string in a fixture memory file is absent from the prompt, shown by `--dry-run --project` and by the fake-CLI unit test's captured stdin.
5. **Timer** (`who: user`, R6):
   - a unit test pins the rendered unit text;
   - `systemd-analyze verify` passes on the rendered files in scratch;
   - the operator runs `sh-agent dream --install-timer` on this box, and `systemctl --user list-timers` shows it; `--remove-timer` removes it.
6. **Parity**: criterion 1 on the claude and agy setups. Criterion 3 with `--vendor claude` (scratch `--home`, as above) and on the agy-only sandbox (the whole process under the sandbox `HOME`, with its settings file leaving `dream-work/` untrusted, as the real home does).

- [x] Antigravity run of each changed skill and agent — evidence: `testing/2026-09-30-verify-real-home-v1.17.0.md` PASS, 2026-09-30 — (`project-memory`, `feedback-log`, `init-project`, `dream`, `retro`, `distill`, `dreamer`) before the tag (AGENTS.md:77), plus the three-setup parity rows
- [-] Release through `/preflight` ("Include this in the next version") — moved to handoffs/2026-09-30-2206-parity-memory-dream-done.md Next Steps (2026-09-30): the operator will cut the version with a later project

## Risks
Assumptions:
- `autoMemoryEnabled: false` stops native writes — E2E 2's must-fail control.
- `claude -p --tools "" --no-session-persistence` takes stdin and prints only the answer — the first real run in Phase 4.
- agy text is extractable from step blobs (D8) — the Phase 3 probe.
- agy answers tool-free (D7) — the Phase 4 probe.
- Claude Code authenticates from a sandbox `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` — the first Phase 2 checkpoint run.

## Decisions
- D1 — 2026-09-30 — R10 as approved — by: "Sounds great. … Go all approved go work."
- D2 — 2026-09-30 — Memory is written and loaded through `sh-agent` on both CLIs, with native auto memory off per project; this supersedes memory items 2 and 3 under R10 — by: memory item 1, approved; R10
- D3 — 2026-09-30 — R3 exception, revised exact text: "One exception: `sh-agent dream --all`, run nightly by an OS user timer that `sh-agent dream --install-timer` installs and `sh-agent dream --remove-timer` or `uninstall` removes, reads every indexed project's trail and memory, the feedback log and both CLIs' transcripts, runs a CLI with no tools over what it read, and writes only under `~/.config/sh-agent/`, its proposals to `proposals/dream/`; it never edits a project, a skill, a rule or the context, and a proposal takes effect only through `/retro`." — by: the operator, "Go all" (2026-09-30), on this text shown in chat
- D4 — 2026-09-30 — The CLI call has no tools; `sh-agent` reads and writes everything. This departs from the option notes behind dreamer item 5 (`.agents/scratch/2026-09-30-dream-background-options.md` § 5, "the job needs Read/Grep/Write … a dedicated settings file"), not from the approved table line — by: implementer; put to the operator (item 5)
- D5 — 2026-09-30 — The timer is opt-in, installed once per machine with `--install-timer` — by: dreamer item 1 names the command
- D6 — 2026-09-30 — Proposals go to `proposals/dream/` with queue-shaped Status lines, and drafts are files under `proposals/dream/drafts/`. This departs from dreamer item 4's top-level path, because `LastRetro` counts top-level `*.md`. `report` already skips subdirectories (report.go:331-339) — by: implementer; departure put to the operator (item 5)
- D7 — 2026-09-30 — agy's tool-free invocation comes from the Phase 4 probe, in a home where `dream-work` is untrusted; the candidates are `--mode plan --disable-slash-commands --output-format text`. When agy refuses (no answer without a tool, or an untrusted-workspace refusal), the job on an agy vendor stops before any project, with `status` "failed: agy cannot run the dream job here (<reason>)". That is put to the operator with two options: a Non-goals exception letting `sh-agent dream --install-timer` add `dream-work` to agy's `trustedWorkspaces`, or an R10 known difference. Nothing is written into agy's settings without that approval — by: implementer, cold read r2
- D7a — 2026-09-30 — The probe settles D7: the candidate flags answer tool-free from an untrusted, empty cwd on agy, and `--tools ""` does on Claude Code; the refusal branch is not needed — by: implementer, probe
- D7b — 2026-09-30 — D7a was wrong for a real prompt. With the 14 KB dream prompt, `agy -p … --mode plan --disable-slash-commands` tried a `command` tool, was auto-denied, and ended with no answer; its stderr also said `--mode plan has no effect while slash command expansion is disabled`. `--json-schema` (with `--output-format json`) still tried a tool. What works is prompt text: the prompt opens, for BOTH CLIs (R10), with "IMPORTANT: every tool call in this session is refused and ends it with no answer … Answer directly with the JSON object only", and agy runs `-p <prompt> --mode plan --output-format text`. The result was 3 of 3 agy runs ok (2 proposals and a draft each) and 1 of 1 Claude Code run ok. A night on which agy still calls a tool fails that project (`fail invalid output`, watermark kept), and the next night retries — by: implementer, Phase 4 e2e
- D8 — 2026-09-30 — Antigravity transcripts: map by `conversation_summaries.db` `workspace_uris`, then extract UTF-8 runs of 20+ characters from the `steps` blobs, deduplicated in order, inside `internal/search`. If the probe cannot isolate the user's and model's text, transcripts are dropped on BOTH CLIs (R10) and that is put to the operator — by: implementer, from recon
- D8a — 2026-09-30 — D8's probe (copies of `conversation_summaries.db` and one conversation db in `.agents/scratch/agyprobe/`): `workspace_uris` is a JSON array of `file://` URIs, and `last_modified_time` a `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.fffffffff+00:00` string. The `steps.step_payload` blobs hold the user's prompt and the model's reply as UTF-8 runs (the context run's answer "# AGENTS.md — global agent context / 28 skills and 8 subagents / GANNET / bug" came back verbatim), mixed with ids and permission strings. The extractor keeps runs of 20+ bytes that contain at least three spaces, which drops the id noise, deduplicated in order. D8 holds; transcripts stay on both CLIs — by: implementer, probe
- D9 — 2026-09-30 — The watermark lives in `dream-state.json`, not in `search.db`, which is a cache (R4) — by: implementer
- D10 — 2026-09-30 — The `/dream` skill stays (interactive, deletes, gated); `sh-agent dream` is the background proposal job, and the skill's description names the verb. The verb's output is a proposal queue under `~/.config/sh-agent/`, not an R7 record in the project; `context/AGENTS.md:42` ("every retro, distill and dream leaves a record") keeps meaning the skill — by: implementer
- D11 — 2026-09-30 — Existing Claude default stores keep migrating through `/init-project` Step 5b — by: implementer
- D12 — 2026-09-30 — R4 gains two sentences, pending approval (item 1 and item 2):
  - "`sh-agent dream` also opens Antigravity's conversation databases with it, read-only." The reader lives in `internal/search`, so AGENTS.md:59's one-package rule holds.
  - "`uninstall` removes exactly what its manifest lists, and the dream timer when one is installed (R3)."
  The timer stays out of the manifest — by: the operator, "Go all" (2026-09-30), items 1, 2 and 5 of `.agents/scratch/2026-09-30-parity-operator-items.md`
- D13 — 2026-09-30 — Pending approval:
  - the Non-goals exception gains "and the two memory keys `/init-project` writes into a project's gitignored `.claude/settings.local.json` (`autoMemoryDirectory`, `autoMemoryEnabled: false`; R10)" (item 3);
  - the README map gains the dream job (item 4, AGENTS.md rule 3, R9) in the implementing commit with an ADR
  — by: the operator, "Go all" (2026-09-30), items 3 and 4
- D14 — 2026-09-30 — The skill is named `project-memory`, because `memory` shadows Claude Code's built-in `/memory` (BUG-065) — by: cold read r1
- D15 — 2026-09-30 — `--project <dir>` exists for the e2e and for rerunning one project; the CLI is chosen by the existing global `--vendor` flag, not a new `--cli`; `--dry-run` is required by the global rule that a command with side effects has a read-only mode — by: implementer
- D16 — 2026-09-30 — Loading memory costs one `sh-agent memory show` call per session start on both CLIs. A headless run without a grant loads none, and an interactive Claude Code session asks for permission unless the operator allowed `sh-agent`, while agy on this box approves by its own `toolPermission`. Accepted: the harness behaves the same; the difference is each machine's own CLI permission setting, which the harness never writes (Non-goals) — by: implementer, from cold reads r1 and r2
- D17 — 2026-09-30 — With vendor `all`, Antigravity transcripts go to Claude Code's model on the same machine. Accepted: both are the operator's own accounts, and nothing is sent anywhere else — by: implementer, from cold read r1
- D18 — 2026-09-30 — The `.gitignore` check is `git check-ignore -q` on the target path, not a literal line — by: cold read r1 blocking question 6
- D19 — 2026-09-30 — Harness-target dream proposals go to `proposals/dream/harness/` and `report` sends that directory (R8); project-target proposals and drafts stay local. This supersedes D6's "report never sends" for the harness subset — by: implementer, cold read r2
- D20 — 2026-09-30 — Existing projects keep Claude Code's native memory until `/init-project` reruns there; `sh-agent memory show` prints the rollout hint in each such project — by: implementer, cold read r2
- D21 — 2026-09-30 — Over the 256 KB cap after all transcript text is dropped: trail files are dropped next, oldest mtime first, whole files; memory is always sent whole; a project whose memory alone passes the cap fails with `fail memory over cap` — by: the operator, "Go all" (cold read r3 question 1)
- D22 — 2026-09-30 — Phase order under the approvals: all of D3, D12 and D13 are approved, so no phase waits; the README map, the `report` change and the timer land in ONE commit with the code and docs (R9, AGENTS.md rule 3) — Phase 4's `Collect` change and Phase 5's map and timer go in the Phase 5 commit — by: the operator, "Go all" (r3 question 2)
- D23 — 2026-09-30 — A harness-target proposal is written only to `proposals/dream/harness/…`, never also to the project file; one Status line each — by: the operator, "Go all" (r3 question 3)
- D24 — 2026-09-30 — Antigravity's "since": per conversation, by `conversation_summaries.db` `last_modified_time`; a conversation modified after the watermark is sent whole (steps carry no time) — by: the operator, "Go all" (r3 question 4)
- D25 — 2026-09-30 — `/dream`'s promote test counts a memory without `originSessionId` as one session (its existing rule, `skills/dream/SKILL.md:47`); the second session comes from `feedback.jsonl`. `skills/dream/SKILL.md:47` is added to the touched text to say so — by: the operator, "Go all" (r3 question 5)
- D26 — 2026-09-30 — `memory add|show` root: the main worktree's toplevel (the parent of `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir`), so every worktree shares one store — by: the operator, "Go all" (r3 question 6)
- D27 — 2026-09-30 — The r3 non-blocking defaults, as the review recommends:
  - the rollout hint also fires when `settings.local.json` is absent on a machine whose manifest vendor is not `antigravity`;
  - Step 5b's empty-object branch writes the two-key object;
  - `--project` takes the absolute git toplevel of its argument and needs no registration;
  - the child's stderr is kept beside its failure file and redacted;
  - `dream-failed/` text is redacted, and files older than 30 days are pruned at the start of a run;
  - drafts get `-2` on a same-day rerun;
  - the Claude transcript reader honours `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`;
  - `ListProjects` opens read-only, never creating the db;
  - the proposal frontmatter `project` carries the root.
  — by: the operator, "Go all" (r3 non-blocking 7–15)
- D8b — 2026-09-30 — Antigravity step types, from copies of two real conversation databases (`.agents/scratch/agyprobe/` and the gate18 handoff run): 14 is the user's input (the run prompt), 15 the model's reply (the context answer, the handoff's planning text), 132 a tool step (a `view_file` of a SKILL.md), 101 a message event. Only 14 and 15 are read — by: implementer, probe
- D28 — 2026-09-30 — After the feature review (`reviews/2026-09-30-review-cb799ff-f1ca525-code.md`, `reviews/2026-09-30-security-cb799ff-f1ca525.md`):
  - the Antigravity child runs from a private HOME holding a copy of the operator's login and settings that grant nothing, removed after the run; any tool call is refused whatever the operator allows interactively;
  - its prompt goes on stdin as one stream-json message (Linux caps one argument at 128 KiB, and argv is readable in /proc); this supersedes D7b's invocation, and D7b's prompt warning stays;
  - Claude Code adds `--strict-mcp-config --setting-sources local`;
  - locks are flock;
  - pre-project failures and a corrupt state are exit 2 and recorded, and the corrupt state is never rewritten;
  - only the user's and the model's Antigravity steps are read;
  - symlinked trail directories are not followed.
  — supersedes D7b's invocation — by: code review and security review, 2026-09-30
- D29 — 2026-09-30 — After two review rounds found leaks in the Antigravity transcript reader (tool output, then tool-call arguments), the operator chose to keep both CLIs' transcripts, filtered, over dropping them or keeping Claude Code's alone: "Keep both, filtered (Recommended)". The residual risk is an unknown field type in the undocumented format; the text is redacted and goes only to the operator's own CLI's model — by: the operator, 2026-09-30
- D30 — 2026-09-30 — The third review of the Antigravity reader (`reviews/2026-09-30-security-e2cffc1-a275b96.md`: argument pieces glued to a printable length byte or split at a multi-byte character) replaced the byte-run scan with a schemaless protobuf wire-format decoder. Each tool argument is then one whole JSON string field, dropped whole. The operator chose it over dropping the transcripts: "Decode protobuf properly (Recommended)". Measured on copies of the 95 local conversation databases: 971 prose leaves kept, 0 with a tool-argument key. Supersedes D8's extraction — by: the operator, 2026-09-30
- Open: redaction beyond credential shapes and `~` — default: none (the same set as `report`)
- Rejected: the timer in the manifest — the next `install` deletes listed files as stale (apply.go:88-109)
- Rejected: `ExecStart` from `os.Executable()` — under `go run` it is a temp build; BinPath is what `update` keeps current
- Rejected: `memory add --title` — the slug is the title; one less value to keep in step

title: Recon — audit findings, consolidated (2026-09-30)
body:
# Recon — audit findings, consolidated (2026-09-30)

Source: two full audits of this repository on 2026-09-30 (first at f1ca525, second at 58bf00d), six read-only passes each (context and requirements; workflow skills; technical skills; agents; installer code; search, memory, dream and the trail), plus spot checks from the main session. Published as two private pages (`Styrman Harness Audit`, `Styrman Harness Audit II`). This file is the evidence base for plan `2026-09-30-audit-fix.md`; every task there cites an ID below. Confidence is high where a finding was reproduced (marked *repro*) or spot-checked (*checked*); otherwise it was read at the location named.

Two audit claims were refuted and are not listed: "feedback entries lack a project field" (all 15 carry one) and "the installed real-home context is behind the repo" (it carries the current memory line).

## C — global context and governing documents

| ID | Sev | Where | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | high | `context/AGENTS.md` | Rendered context 21,906 of 22,000 bytes (*checked*). No rule can be added; `rules/` cannot deploy. Hard rules ≈1,000 words. |
| C2 | high | `context/AGENTS.md:18` vs `:66` | "ROADMAP and TODO EMPTY at every checkpoint" contradicts "Now names the active plan while one is in progress". |
| C3 | high | `skills/init-project/assets/{TODO,ROADMAP}.md` | Templates carry High/Medium/Low, "Ideas / Nice-to-Have", "Later / Ideas" sections the context forbids as parking lots. This repo's own ROADMAP.md has "Later / Ideas" too. |
| C4 | med | `context/AGENTS.md:66` vs `REQUIREMENTS.md:11` | R2's CLAUDE.md stub list restated differently (Vertex, Foundry missing). |
| C5 | med | `context/AGENTS.md` | Docs-root shorthand `docs/` defined only on the last line; mixed notations `<docs-root>/testing/guide.md`, `docs/testing/guide.md`, bare `testing/`. |
| C6 | med | `context/AGENTS.md:9` | Resume order reads TODO.md second though line 18 keeps it empty. |
| C7 | med | `context/dev-setup.md:8` | Root steps gated on `.claude/settings.json`, a Claude-only file; on Antigravity the rule can never be satisfied (R10). |
| C8 | med | `assets/agents-tree/docs/bugs/INDEX.md` | No `## Graduated` table though the context tells `bugs` to move rows into one; this repo's INDEX.md:87 has the shape. |
| C9 | med | `context/AGENTS.md:52` | 169-word bullet chaining five unrelated checks (binary heredoc, escape, `rm -r`, ` D`, post-dispatch status/log/tag). |
| C10 | med | `context/AGENTS.md:58` | 120-word sentence restating four rules owned by review-standards § 2. |
| C11 | med | `context/AGENTS.md:16` | DoD step 2 is 246 words folding thresholds, rounds, "shorter beats defended", operator-choice and `/review --docs`. |
| C12 | med | `REQUIREMENTS.md` R3, R4, R8, R9, R10 | ≈400 words of approval provenance inside the immutable file; R9's parenthetical 188 words. Needs operator approval to change. |
| C13 | low | `context/AGENTS.md:46` | "bypass hooks" beside "no hooks, ever". |
| C14 | low | `context/AGENTS.md:21,25` | Docs-only ≤10 lines rule stated twice. |
| C15 | low | `context/AGENTS.md:30`; `REQUIREMENTS.md` R10 | `/goal` named but not a harness command; R10 promises a "known differences" list that no spec has. Candidates: `/goal`, the settings.json gate (C7), `.claude/*` links. |
| C16 | low | `context/AGENTS.md:9` | `sh-agent search --open` and `memory show` exit 2 in an unscaffolded checkout before `/init-project` is offered. |
| C17 | low | `AGENTS.md` (project) § Testing | One 397-word paragraph plus six BUG bullets; silent on `internal/memory`, `internal/dream`, guide § 3e and the D30 reader measurement; "protobuf" appears nowhere. |
| C18 | low | `assets/REQUIREMENTS.md:7-19` | Leads with Scale Targets and Latency SLA tables, a burden on a CLI or library. |
| C19 | low | `assets/AGENTS.md:42` | "supplement the global testing tiers"; the context defines no tiers. |
| C20 | low | `ROADMAP.md:3`, `assets/ROADMAP.md:3` | Header comment says "both sections" for a three-section file. |
| C21 | low | `README.md` map legend | Dreamer lines coloured amber (report back) though rule 1 says the timer is neither a way in nor a way back; what it sends to the model provider is not drawn. |
| C22 | low | `REQUIREMENTS.md:31` (R7) | Still "auto memory store"; replacement wording awaits operator approval (handoff 2206 Next Step 3). |
| C-scar | low | `context/AGENTS.md:15,34,46,52,57,58,60,61,62,66`; `dev-setup.md:8,10`; `REQUIREMENTS.md:55-56` | One-off incidents written as global law (tree-freeze, dispatch boilerplate, token file name, escape lesson, `hash -r`, mutation protocol, dry-run child cwd, embed pin, `&&` chain, date-only names, `du` before `rm -r`, `exec format error`, BUG-085 measurements). |

## WS — workflow skills

| ID | Sev | Where | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|
| WS1 | med | `skills/review/SKILL.md:51,52,64` | Single paragraphs of 1,819, 1,730 and 3,446 chars carry the docs brief, the prompts brief and the whole `--fix` loop. |

| WS7 | low | `skills/review-standards/SKILL.md:3,8` | "loaded by /review" is wrong (review never reviews itself); `/preflight` is right (reads small diffs itself). Drop `/review` only. |
| WS8 | low | `feature:25`, `bug:49`, `review-standards:37`, `preflight:77`, `retro:49,141`, `feedback-log:58,86`, `init-project:91`, `review:18` | Scar tissue: another project's name (styrman-harness), operator quotes and BUG ids inside global skills. |
