title: Research — Google skills import: measurements and decisions (2026-10-01)
body:
# Research — Google skills import: measurements and decisions (2026-10-01)

Request (operator, 2026-10-01): add every skill of github.com/google/agents-cli and of google/skills `skills/cloud` and `skills/developers` to the harness.

## What was measured

- Candidates: 141 skills — agents-cli `skills/` 7 (pin 2c39459), its LangChain extension template 1, google/skills `cloud` 131 and `developers` 2 (pin d5d9052). Apache-2.0 both. 5.7 MB, 778 files (614 md, 74 py, 44 yaml, 20 sh). Descriptions all within 1,024 chars; 67,698 chars together (average 480).
- Harness lint on a scratch tree with all of them: 2 refused for `allowed-tools` (`agent-platform-alert-configuration`, `cloud-run-alert-configuration`); none for an unreadable frontmatter line; 26 files carry an exec bit (the embed test refuses those under `skills/`); one name clash, `gke-basics` (the harness's pinned fork). Rendered context with 173 skills: 19,548 bytes of the 22,000 pin.
- Installed into a sandbox home and asked each CLI what it sees (`~/sandbox/audit-fix/imp-*.out`):
  - **Antigravity 1.2.14 lists 109 of 173 skills.** Two runs agree. It drops the longest descriptions first (kept average 382 chars, dropped 690; about 44,000 characters of name plus description survive). 16 of the harness's own 34 are dropped: `feature`, `review`, `golang`, `spec`, `terraform`, `cloud-run-deploy`, `data-gcp`, `requirements`, `testing-strategy`, `project-memory`, `dream`, `explain-project`, `operate-gcp`, `api-auth-gcp`, `json-api-style`, `mermaid-syntax`.
  - **Claude Code lists all 186 names but descriptions for only the first 41 alphabetically** (through `data-gcp`), about 19,800 characters; every later skill — `feature`, `golang`, `handoff`, `init-project`, `preflight`, `review`, `terraform` — is a bare name with no description, so nothing tells the model when to load it.
  - Today's 34 harness skills use 19,310 of those ~19,800 characters on Claude Code: the harness is already at the budget. The agents-cli seven plus the two developers skills alone add 5,749.
- Conclusion: installing the candidates as global skills breaks skill selection on both CLIs, for the harness's own workflow skills first. Even nine more global skills cost existing descriptions on Claude Code.

## The decisions

1. **Where the 141 live.** (a) Global skill directories, as asked — measured broken on both CLIs. (b) **A vendored catalog plus one router skill (recommended):** the 141 are vendored verbatim in the harness under a new directory that is not a skills directory (`catalog/google/<name>/`), installed to a non-skill location on each machine (`~/.config/sh-agent/catalog/google/`), and one small harness skill routes to them: its description triggers on Google Cloud, Gemini, Agent Platform, ADK and agents-cli tasks; its body tells the agent to find the matching entry in the catalog's index and read that SKILL.md and its references from the local copy. One description in the listing instead of 141; identical on both CLIs (R10); offline and pinned. (c) A curated handful installed globally and the rest fetched live by Google's own `finding-google-skills` from GitHub at use time — unpinned instruction text from the network at runtime, and it still costs budget. (d) Per-project only: the catalog is vendored and a project copies the few skills it needs into its own `.agents/skills/` — no global cost, but nothing is available until someone copies.
2. **What the router reads.** The local pinned copy (recommended: reviewed once, same on every machine, works offline) or Google's live `index.json` (always current, but unreviewed text and a network dependency inside a session).
3. **Budget room for the router.** Claude Code has about 500 characters left. A router description of at most 300 characters fits; recommended to also shorten `cloud-run-deploy`'s description (the longest) by the same amount so the listing keeps headroom, and to add a test that pins the sum of all skill descriptions under the measured budget so the next skill drop cannot silently push one out.
4. **The agents-cli seven and the LangChain template skill.** Into the catalog with the rest (recommended), or installed globally (costs about 3,900 characters and pushes six harness descriptions out of Claude Code's listing). The LangChain skill is a project template's own skill ("use when working in this project"); recommended: catalog it, never global.
5. **`gke-basics`.** Keep the harness fork installed as it is; upstream's current `gke-basics` and its 34 `gke-*` siblings go into the catalog, where names cannot clash. Retiring the fork in favour of the catalog's GKE set is a later, separate choice.
6. **The two `allowed-tools` skills.** In a catalog they are plain files the router reads, not skills a CLI loads, so the key grants nothing; kept verbatim, and the installer's permission-key lint does not apply to the catalog directory. (As global skills they would have to be forked without the key or refused.)
7. **Executable bits.** Stored 0644 (the embed test requires it); the mode is the only local change, recorded once in the catalog manifest; the router tells the agent to run scripts through their interpreter.
8. **Project opt-in.** A later phase: a way to copy a catalog skill into a project's `.agents/skills/` when the project lives on that product (so it loads natively there). Recommended: defer; the router covers the need first.
9. **REQUIREMENTS.** R5 lists the directories the installer maps; a catalog directory is a new kind, so R5 gains one sentence — the exact text needs the operator's yes and an ADR. No delivery path changes; the README map is untouched. Release binaries and the zip grow by about 5.7 MB.
10. **Provenance and refresh.** One manifest for the catalog (repository, path, pin, licence, date, the mode-only local change) instead of 141 rows in `VENDORED.md`, with a test that every catalog entry's files match `git archive <pin>` content (the BUG-111 rule, automated), and a documented refresh: fetch at a new pin, read the diff, re-run the security slice on it.
11. **Release rule.** "One Antigravity run of each changed skill" covers harness skills; catalog entries are data. Recommended: the router runs on both CLIs in the matrix, plus a sample of six catalog entries per release (one per family), not 141.
12. **Security.** A security review slice over the imported content before it lands (instruction-shaped text, `curl | sh`, credentials in samples, scripts that write outside the project), and over the diff at each refresh.
13. **Version.** MINOR after this lands (v2.1.0), together with the eleven gate lows and the timer fix already on `main`.

## Work shape if 1(b) is chosen

Feature skill: plan file with phases — (1) REQUIREMENTS R5 text, ADR; (2) installer: the catalog directory kind, its install destination, manifest test, status and uninstall; (3) vendor the 141 at their pins, index file, manifest; (4) the router skill and budget test, description trims; (5) security slice and reviews; (6) sandbox runs on both CLIs (router picks the right entry for six tasks), docs, matrix; (7) release.

## Second measurement — the catalog nested inside one router skill (2026-10-01)

A scratch tree with one new skill, `skills/google-catalog/`, holding the 141 entries under `catalog/<name>/` (exec bits cleared) and a generated `catalog/INDEX.md` (36,435 bytes, one line per entry): the unchanged installer lists 35 skills, renders 15,155 bytes, installs without a refusal (no secret-shaped or symlinked path among the 778 files). Installed into a sandbox home (`~/sandbox/audit-fix/sbImp2`) and asked on both CLIs (`imp2-*.out`):

- Claude Code lists 48 skills (35 + its 13 built-ins), Antigravity 37 (35 + its 2): every harness skill present on both, `typescript`'s description quoted in full on both, `google-catalog` listed, and neither `gke-storage` nor `bigquery-basics` in either list — a `SKILL.md` two levels below a skill directory is not discovered as a skill by either CLI.
- So the catalog needs no new directory kind, no installer change and no REQUIREMENTS edit: the existing skill deployment carries it, and a skill may read its own files on both CLIs.
- First routing probe ("alerting on Cloud Run error rate, as Terraform"): Claude Code loaded the harness's own `operate-gcp` and its alerts reference — correct precedence, wrong probe; Antigravity was denied a shell command under a per-name grant list (BUG-141's shape). The second probe, three tasks the harness does not cover, is recorded in the plan's Phase 4 log.

title: Plan — lean process: fewer review rounds, cold agents and long sessions (2026-10-07)
body:
# Plan — lean process: fewer review rounds, cold agents and long sessions   (2026-10-07)

## Why
The operator asked whether the harness wastes turns and tokens (2026-10-07). An A/B test (`.agents/scratch/2026-10-07-0842-harness-ab-crm-report.md`; not committed) built the same CRM booking service three ways:

| Arm | Cost | Wall time | Acceptance test | Main turns | Subagents |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| No harness | $0.54 | 2.4 min | 25/25 | | |
| Harness loaded | $1.11 | 5.0 min | 25/25 | | |
| Harness, full process | $8.46 | 30.8 min | 25/25 | 87 | 13 |

- About 80% of the full-process run's wall time was process: three plan cold-reader rounds, a verifier per phase, separate documentation and bugs agents, and review rounds.
- The operator's own transcripts show the same pattern: a release session ran 28 agents, and main threads ran 220 turns, one resumed at a 560k context.

The operator approved recommendations 1–6 and 8 and struck 7 ("go your recommendations", 2026-10-07).

## Scope
**In:**
1. **One cold-reader round.** The plan's cold-reader check runs once. Its residue becomes `Open:` rows with defaults. The check is skipped for a plan with one phase that touches fewer than 5 files.
2. **No verifier per phase.** The main thread runs the full test command bare at each checkpoint. One `verifier` per task, at DoD step 1. Review fixes are re-checked by the main thread's bare test run, not by a new verifier dispatch.
3. **The main thread writes small records itself.** That covers the `changes/` entry, the bug record and docs edits of 30 lines or fewer. `changelog`, `bugs` and `documentation` are dispatched only above that, or when the main thread lacks the evidence.
4. **Review rounds capped at 2,** not 3. Round 2 checks the fixes only: it resumes the same agent where the CLI can (Claude Code), and is otherwise a new dispatch carrying the fix lines only.
5. **One reviewer dispatch covers the code and docs lenses together.** `security` is still separate, on its existing triggers.
6. **A new task starts in a fresh session.** After `/handoff`, the agent recommends a fresh session (`/clear`, or a new `agy` conversation) that resumes from the handoff, and does not take up a new task in a session that has closed one.
8. **A BUG-NNN only for what escaped a gate,** or for a user correction. A defect that review catches before commit is a review finding, recorded in the review's `## Outcome`, not a bug.

**Out:** 7 (a light scaffold): the unscaffolded path in `context/AGENTS.md` § Work already is the light tier.

**Follow-ups noted, not built:**
- the preflight gate's own round count beyond what the review skill sets
- dream and retro cadence

## Surfaces touched
- `context/AGENTS.md` — DoD 1-5, the failure line (:33), the subagent line (:35). Must not grow: 14,727 of 15,000 bytes (cold read Q4); detail moves into the skills.
- `skills/feature/SKILL.md` — Gates (:15), template box (:57, :61), Step 3 (:87-93), Step 4 (:99, :101), Step 6 (:111-113).
- `skills/review/SKILL.md` — Step 3 lens table (code+docs as one dispatch), Step 4 Rounds (:94) and merged record, Step 5 (:100, :108, :110, :112).
- `skills/preflight/SKILL.md` — Step 1.1 (:44 dispatches), Step 2 code review and Step 4 docs lens (:59, :78) as one dispatch, round cap.
- `skills/bug/SKILL.md` — Gates (:15), Step 0 "what counts" (:21), Step 5 (:55).
- `skills/handoff/SKILL.md` — Step 3.2 (:65), Step 7 (:182), cross-reference (:191).
- `skills/operate-gcp/SKILL.md:83` and `skills/init-project/assets/**/bugs/INDEX.md` — the bug trigger list, wherever it is restated.
- `agents/bugs.md` (:3, :20, :78), `agents/changelog.md`, `agents/documentation.md` — triggers and "dispatch once per task" wording.
- `README.md:259` — only if it states a changed rule.
- Every other restatement is found by `bash skills/review/scripts/restatement-grep.sh` before review.

## Interfaces
None: these are prose rules. No code, flag, or binary behaviour changes.

## Failure modes
- **Over-cutting:** a defect that a removed round would have caught ships.
  - Mitigation: the reviewer still runs once per task, and security still runs on its triggers.
  - Measure: re-run the full-process experiment; the acceptance test must stay 25/25.
- **Size pins:** a context edit breaks `TestRenderedContextUnderTarget`, whose ceiling is 15,000 bytes. Mitigation: the context only shrinks or holds its size.

## Verification
- **Unit:**
  - `gofmt -l cmd internal && go vet ./... && go test -race -timeout 30m ./...` passes, size pins included.
  - `go test ./internal/harness -run TestSkillListingBudget` passes when a description changes.
- **Install:** `go run ./cmd/sh-agent install --home .agents/scratch/home-lean` succeeds.
- **Behavioural:** re-run the full-process arm of the A/B kit against the scratch-home install. Expect:
  - the acceptance test at 25/25
  - at most 1 cold-reader round, 1 verifier and 1 reviewer, plus security if triggered
  - cost and wall time below the $8.46 / 30.8 min baseline (one run, n=1)
- **E2E criteria:** a fresh `claude -p` session given only the new harness builds the CRM spec. It records no BUG-NNN for review-caught defects, and dispatches no verifier before the DoD.

## Phases
- [x] Cold-reader check — one round per D1: `reviews/2026-10-07-review-lean-process-plan-cold-read.md` (design needs revision / not ready). Every gap and blocking question is answered by D6-D14 below, none needed the operator, and there is no second report.
### Phase 1 — rule edits
- [x] Edit `context/AGENTS.md` (items 2, 3, 5, 6, 8) — verify: `go test ./internal/harness -run TestRenderedContext -count=1` — expect: PASS
- [x] Edit `skills/feature/SKILL.md` (items 1, 2, 3) — verify: read the diff — expect: no "three-round" or per-phase verifier left
- [x] Edit `skills/review/SKILL.md` and `skills/bug/SKILL.md` (items 4, 8) — verify: grep `three` and `third round` — expect: no cap of three left
- [x] Edit `skills/handoff/SKILL.md` (items 3, 6) and the agent descriptions (item 8) — verify: `go test ./internal/harness -run 'TestAgentDescriptionRules|TestSkillListingBudget|TestLint' -count=1` — expect: PASS
- [x] Restatement grep over the key words of each changed claim — expect: every hit updated or a reason written in this plan. Also updated: `skills/preflight`, `skills/retro`, `skills/operate-gcp`, `agents/changelog.md`, `agents/documentation.md` and three init-project templates. The project `AGENTS.md`'s own `/review --docs` lines are kept: the combined dispatch satisfies them.
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: the full test command passes, run bare — evidence: `go test -race -timeout 30m ./...` exit 0, 6 packages ok (before the review fixes, which touched only markdown; `go test ./internal/harness` passed after them; the context is 14,719 bytes, down from 14,727), 2026-10-07
### Phase 2 — measure
- [x] Scratch-home install, then re-run the full-process A/B arm against it — verify: `accept.py` plus `metrics.py` — expect: 25/25, fewer agents and rounds than the baseline; numbers recorded in the changes entry
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: the measurement recorded — evidence: `lean-full` against `.agents/scratch/home-lean`, 25/25, $7.27 / 29.3 min / 6 agents / 62 main turns, against $8.46 / 30.8 / 13 / 87, with 0 bug records (4 before); numbers in the changes entry, 2026-10-07
### Phase 3 — Done
- [x] One `reviewer` over the range (code and docs lenses), fixes, ADR-054, the `changes/` entry, commit, push, `/handoff` — review `reviews/2026-10-07-review-worktree-code-docs.md`: 2 rounds, approved, with an `## Outcome` section

## Risks
Assumptions:
- Claude Code can resume a finished subagent with `SendMessage`. Checked by this session's own tool list.
- Antigravity has no equivalent, hence the fallback in item 4.

## Decisions
- D1 — 2026-10-07 — This plan gets one cold-reader round, under the rule it introduces — by: the operator's approval "go your recommendations".
- D2 — 2026-10-07 — Item 7 is struck: the unscaffolded path is already the light tier — by: the operator's approval.
- D3 — 2026-10-07 — Item 6 is a fresh-session rule, not a context-size threshold, because the model cannot measure its own context — by: implementer, put to the operator in the scope table.
- D4 — 2026-10-07 — The cutoff for the main thread writing docs itself is 30 changed lines — by: implementer.
- D5 — 2026-10-07 — The cold-reader skip is for a plan with one phase that touches fewer than 5 files — by: implementer.
- D6 — 2026-10-07 — Item 1 (cold read Q1, BUG-042): exactly one report and never a second, so the count stays one a headless run cannot argue past. After that report, every gap and BLOCKING question is either answered in the plan (a D-row by the implementer, or a rebuttal) or, when only the user can settle it (scope or a requirement), becomes the user gate. At that gate print mode ends with the question in the handoff, as today. A skipped check is ticked `[-] Cold-reader check — skipped: one phase, <5 files`. The three-round cap leaves the gates list; "no code until the check is resolved" stays — by: implementer, cold read round 1.
- D7 — 2026-10-07 — Item 5 (Q2): `--code` and `--docs` in one `/review` run go to ONE `reviewer` dispatch with slug `<scope>-code-docs`. Its brief is the code brief followed by the Docs brief under its own heading, and the artifact is `reviews/<date>-review-<scope>-code-docs.md`, recorded as two lenses in the merged record. Preflight's Step 2 code review and Step 4 docs lens become that one dispatch; docs findings stay advisory there — by: implementer.
- D8 — 2026-10-07 — Item 8 (Q3): what is excluded is a defect that the review, tests or verifier of the same uncommitted change find and that is fixed before that change's commit. It is recorded in the review's `## Outcome`, not as a BUG. Everything else on the existing list still counts, and "a review finding that was a real defect" becomes "…on committed work". Every restatement is updated — by: implementer.
- D9 — 2026-10-07 — Size pin (Q4): the context must not grow. DoD 2's docs routing and DoD 4's agent detail move to the review and feature skills, and the measured byte count goes in the changes entry — by: implementer.
- D10 — 2026-10-07 — Item 3 (Q5): the 30-line cutoff applies to docs only. The `changes/` entry and the bug record are always the main thread's, unless it lacks the evidence (then `changelog` or `bugs`) — by: implementer.
- D11 — 2026-10-07 — Item 4 (Q6): the cap of 2 is restated at review :94/:100/:112, bug :15 and feature :15, all updated. Resuming a finished subagent with `SendMessage` is verified in this session (the tool is offered to the main thread); every other CLI falls back to a new dispatch carrying only the fix lines — by: implementer.
- D12 — 2026-10-07 — Item 6 (Q7): recommend, never refuse. "Closed a task" means this session wrote a handoff whose Next Steps queue nothing for the agent. The recommendation goes in the handoff's Step 7 report and as one clause in DoD 5 — by: implementer.
- D13 — 2026-10-07 — Non-blocking findings:
  - The E2E criterion is checked as "the run's `bugs/` holds no record of a defect that its own reviews' `## Outcome` lists as fixed before commit", so it cannot pass vacuously.
  - n=1 is stated with the numbers.
  - The A/B kit stays in `.agents/scratch/ab-kit/` (see D14).
  - The Antigravity run of the changed skills is owed before the next release (AGENTS.md § Release) and goes in the handoff's Next Steps — by: implementer.
- D14 — 2026-10-07 — supersedes D13's kit clause — The A/B kit is not committed. It never sourced `kit-preamble.sh`, so the harness arms' `sh-agent` calls registered the scratch app in the real global search index (BUG-162). It is rebuilt on the preamble, with fixtures under a non-checkout parent, as a follow-up in the handoff's Next Steps — by: implementer.
- Rejected: a numeric context threshold (150k), because the agent cannot observe it.
- Rejected: removing the verifier entirely, because an independent run is the only check that the tree, not the author's shell, passes.

title: Plan — trajectory and agent/sandbox metrics in a local SQLite store (2026-10-08)
body:
# Plan — trajectory and agent/sandbox metrics in a local SQLite store   (2026-10-08)

## Why
The operator (2026-10-08): "I want to use the local sqllite more to gather trajectory data and agent/sandbox metrics from all sessions. Give me suggestions on metrics for agent evaulations." Today the SQLite holds nothing about sessions: `sh-agent dream` reads transcript text and then drops it (`internal/dream/collect.go:435-466`). Tool calls, tokens and timings are never read. The only measurement so far is the one-off A/B kit (`testing/ab-kit/metrics.py`, n=1). Claude transcripts on this box cover only 2026-10-05..10-08, so every day without an ingest loses data for good.

Measured baseline (2026-10-08, Claude transcripts, deduplicated by `tool_use.id`, verbs counted at command position):
- 1,619 tool calls.
- 38 of those (2.3 %) were SQLite-backed verbs. 27 were the reviewer's `search --refs --kind bug`; the main thread made 11 of its 612 Bash calls this way.
- grep/rg-style lookups numbered about 848.
- `memory add|show`: 0.
- `search.db`: 29 MB.

## Scope
**In:**
- `~/.config/sh-agent/metrics.db`, a SQLite **store of record**.
- `sh-agent metrics ingest|show|export`.
- Ingest of Claude Code main and subagent transcripts and Antigravity conversation databases as **shape only**.
- Events joined from git, the trail and `feedback.jsonl`.
- Sandbox kit homes ingested under a label.
- `dream --all` ingests before it dreams.
- The metric catalogue below, computed by `show`.

**Out:**
- Arguments, prose or file paths in any row, except the two path columns D12 names.
- Sending anything through `report`.
- A live dashboard or server: the visual report is a static file (D26).
- Any hook.
- Any change to `context/`. The context has 64 bytes of headroom.

**Follow-ups noted, not built:**
- Redacted arguments, which would enable path-level checks (C-gaps).
- Aggregates in `report` (rejected for now, D27).
- A dated `export` run nightly.

**Consumers:**
1. The operator, running agent evaluations: `show`, `--json`.
2. `/retro` and the nightly dreamer, which get evidence (regressions, correction rate, rule violations) from `show --json` and turn it into proposals. Those proposals reach the harness through the existing loop (Phase 7, D27).
3. The A/B and seed kits: `ingest --source --label` replaces `ab-kit/metrics.py` (Phase 5).
4. `dream --all`, which ingests nightly.
5. The operator reading `sh-agent metrics report`, a self-contained HTML file with charts (Phase 6, D26).
6. Not the agents themselves: no agent queries metrics mid-task, and nothing needs it.

### Metric catalogue (what `show` computes)
- **A. Outcome**
  - A1 DoD closure: a commit plus a handoff in the session window.
  - A2 Verifier status (`## Status:` heading of `testing/*-verify-*.md` in the window).
  - A3 Review findings by severity (`**[high|medium|low / confidence: …]**` lines in `reviews/*.md` in the window).
  - A4 Escaped defects: BUG records dated after a session commit.
  - A5 Corrections: `feedback.jsonl` entries in the window.
  - A6 Sandbox pass rate per label, with pass^k (all k runs of a label pass).
- **B. Efficiency**
  - B1 Tokens: in, out, cache read and cache write; cache-hit ratio. Cost is taken from Claude's `cost-state.totalCostUSD`, with no price table.
  - B2 Wall time and active time (gaps under 5 min), turns, tool calls.
  - B3 Peak context and compactions.
  - B4 Subagents by type, with tool calls and SendMessage resumes.
- **C. Process adherence**
  - C1 search : grep ratio.
  - C2 Forbidden shapes (`git add -A`/`git add .`, `push --force`, `--no-verify`, a `git commit` in the same Bash call as `go test`).
  - C3 The first three Reads by trail kind.
  - C4 Skills loaded.
- **D. Reliability**
  - D1 Tool error rate, permission denials and interrupts.
  - D2 Retry loops: the same `cmd_hash` twice in a row.
  - D3 Subagent tool calls.

## Surfaces touched
- New: `internal/metrics/` (`store.go`, `verb.go`, `claude.go`, `agy.go`, `events.go`, `show.go`, tests, `testdata/`).
- `cmd/sh-agent` (verb wiring) and `internal/dream/run.go` (ingest first).
- `REQUIREMENTS.md` R3, R4 and R7 (Phase 0, after approval).
- `AGENTS.md` (Layout and Rules lines naming the one driver importer).
- `README.md` (verb table, state table rows 217-218, the map's dream→configDir label).
- `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/metrics.md` (new) and `DECISIONS.md` (ADR-055).
- `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md` § 3e, `testing/sh-agent-matrix.md`, `testing/ab-kit/`.

Code to reuse (package seams: D8; import direction `dream → metrics → search`, never back):
- Open rules: `internal/search/store.go:144-171` (`prepareFiles`, 0600/0700, symlink refusal), exported as `search.PrepareDBFiles`; WAL + busy timeout copied as the DSN string.
- Antigravity copy-then-read: `internal/search/dream.go` `copyDB`/`openCopy`, exported as `search.CopyDB`. A new `search.ProtoFields(b []byte) []Field{Path []int; Varint uint64; Bytes []byte}` sits beside `walk` (`:316-403`); `walk` is unchanged.
- Path kind: `internal/search/parse.go:270` `kindOf`, exported as `search.KindOf`.
- Trail record times: `trailDates` moves from `internal/dream/collect.go:207` to `search.TrailDates` (dream calls it there), so `metrics` never imports `dream`.
- The Claude walk is NOT reused: `claudeTranscript` (`collect.go:355-433`) filters by one root and skips `subagents/`. `metrics` owns its own all-projects walker (D9).

## Interfaces
The spec holds every shape: `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/metrics.md` (verbs, flags, the transcript-root rule, `Verb`, the shared tool vocabulary, `show --json` keys, the report, metric definitions, schema, invariants). The D-rows below record why each shape was chosen.

## Failure modes
The spec's `## Failure modes` table.

## Verification
Tiers (each on Claude Code AND Antigravity, D29): unit (`go test -race`, with fixtures for both vendors); an integration run of the binary against a scratch home holding a copy of real transcripts; one Antigravity session run, then `metrics ingest` + `show` (Phase 3).

E2E criteria:
- **Golden path.** `~/.claude/projects` is copied into `.agents/scratch/metrics-home/.claude/projects`; it may hold secrets, and the copy is deleted when the check ends. Then `env -u CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR sh-agent metrics ingest --home .agents/scratch/metrics-home`. `show --json --all-labels` must report `B.tool_calls` and `B.tool_calls_by_tool`, main and subagent sessions included, equal to an independent count over the same copy: unique `tool_use.id` per tool name. The verb count is not compared, because that would need a second normaliser; `Verb` has its own table tests. A second ingest adds 0 rows.
- **Edge case (canary).**
  - `SECRETCANARY123` is placed in every field the ingester reads that must not be stored: a positional argument, a flag value, a Read path, a tool_result body, user text, assistant text, and a Skill `args`.
  - After ingest, the canary is absent from the bytes of `metrics.db`, `-wal` and the export.
  - Must-fail control: with `Verb` patched to keep positionals (on a copy, review-standards § 2), the test goes red.
- **Migration.** A v1 store with rows opens under a schema list one entry longer and keeps every row. A store whose `meta.schema` is above the binary's is refused, and its bytes are unchanged.

## Phases
- [x] Cold-reader check — one report (`reviews/2026-10-08-review-metrics-store-plan-cold-read.md`), every item answered by a D-row, a rebuttal or the user (D7–D24)
### Phase 0 — Requirements, ADR, spec
- [x] Spike: Claude `message.usage`, `tool_result.is_error`, `cost-state` and `subagents/*.meta.json` exist; Antigravity `gen_metadata` holds the model name and a usage-shaped message — verify: read-only probe, AI — expect: field list recorded in D2, D3 — evidence: probe 2026-10-08 (cost-state: one line per session end or resume, cumulative; 0 lines while a session runs)
- [x] Propose the exact R3/R4/R7 text to the operator — verify: operator's approval in their own turn, user — expect: approved text quoted in a D-row — evidence: D21
- [x] ADR-055 (`.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md`) + REQUIREMENTS edit + ROADMAP in one commit — verify: `git show --stat HEAD`, AI — expect: REQUIREMENTS.md, DECISIONS.md and ROADMAP.md in one commit — evidence: 4df050f
- [x] Spec `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/metrics.md` (agreed by the operator, D30) — docs: specs/sh-agent/metrics.md. The R10 rows in `memory-loop.md` § Known differences move to the Phase 3 spike, which produces them.
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: requirements, ADR and spec committed and pushed — evidence: `go test ./internal/harness` exit 0 (REQUIREMENTS text), commits 4df050f + Phase 0 close, 2026-10-08
### Phase 1 — Store
- [x] Exports in `internal/search`: `PrepareDBFiles`, `DSN`, `IsBusy`, `OpenCopy`, `KindOf`, `ProtoFields` (`internal/search/export.go`); `TrailDates` moves in Phase 4 to `internal/trail` (D31); the AGENTS.md and package-comment driver lines updated in the same change (restatement rule) — verify: `go test -race ./internal/search ./internal/dream` — expect: existing tests unchanged and green; a `ProtoFields` table test over a hand-built protobuf
- [x] `internal/metrics/store.go`: Open, migrations, salt, refusal of a newer schema — verify: `go test -race ./internal/metrics -run 'Store|Migrat'`, AI — expect: symlink refusal, newer-schema refusal (bytes unchanged) and v1 row survival pass, and fail with the migration loop removed

## Risks
Assumptions:
- Antigravity's usage-shaped message (fields 2, 3 and 5 under `gen_metadata`) is input, output and cached tokens. Checked by: the first task of Phase 3. If it cannot be confirmed, the token columns stay NULL for agy (R10 known difference).
- Claude Code keeps writing `cost-state` at session end. Checked by: the Phase 2 fixture comes from a current transcript. A running or crashed session has no cost line, so `cost_usd` is NULL and `show` notes it.

## Decisions
- D1 — 2026-10-08 — SQLite is the store of record at `~/.config/sh-agent/metrics.db`, separate from `search.db`; collection is a new verb plus `dream --all`; rows are shape only; nothing goes through `report` — by: operator, plan-mode answers 2026-10-08 ("SQLite as store of record", "New verb + nightly dream", "Shape only", "Local only for now").
- D2 — 2026-10-08 — Claude cost and duration come from the last `cost-state` line of a session (`totalCostUSD`, `totalDuration`; cumulative, written at session end or resume). No price table. Subagent cost is not separate (it is in the parent's total) — by: implementer (spike 2026-10-08: 1–4 lines per ended main session, 0 in a running one, none in subagent files).
- D3 — 2026-10-08 — Antigravity tokens are read from `gen_metadata` by field number (path ending 2 = input, 3 = output, 5 = cached; 4 under the parent = context window 256000), pinned by a fixture and reported as best-effort — by: implementer (spike; no schema published; confirmed or dropped in Phase 3).
- D3a — 2026-10-08 — Refines D3 with the exact paths from the second spike (one 18-generation conversation, read-only copy). One `gen_metadata` row is one model call. Its fields:
  - 1→4→2 input tokens, 1→4→3 output tokens, 1→4→5 cached tokens (absent when 0);
  - 1→19 the model name;
  - 1→9→10→1 the context used and 1→9→10→4 the window (256000), which gives B3 peak context on Antigravity.

  Each generation is stored as a `steps` row of kind `generation` (`ext_id` = `<conversation>:gen:<idx>`). Its time is that of the i-th model reply (step type 15), because the spike's conversation had 18 of each; with no such reply the time is null. Whether input includes the cached tokens is unconfirmed; the spec's known-difference row keeps "best-effort" — by: implementer (spike 2026-10-08).
- D4 — 2026-10-08 — New package `internal/metrics` as the second driver importer — by: implementer.
- D5 — 2026-10-08 — Forward-only migrations; a store is never deleted on a version bump (the opposite of `search/store.go:112-136`), because it is the only copy — by: implementer, from D1.
- D6 — 2026-10-08 — `cmd_hash` is salted with a per-store salt kept in `meta`. It allows equality detection only. It does not stop brute force by someone who can read the file, which is acceptable for a local 0600 file — by: implementer.
- D7 — 2026-10-08 — `ingest` reuses the global `--vendor` (`cmd/sh-agent/main.go` `c.fs.StringVar(&c.vendorFlag, "vendor", …)`). Empty means all — by: cold read round 1 (G2).
- D8 — 2026-10-08 — Seams: `metrics` imports `search` (exported `PrepareDBFiles`, `CopyDB`, `KindOf`, `TrailDates`, `ProtoFields`); `dream` imports `metrics`; `search` imports neither — by: cold read round 1 (G3).
- D9 — 2026-10-08 — Transcript root: `--source` > `--home` > `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (only with neither flag) > the real home. This closes the R6 leak through the environment variable — by: cold read round 1 (G7).

- Rejected: `internal/metrics` code inside `internal/search` — it keeps "one importer" true in wording only, and couples two stores.
- Rejected: decoding agy `step_payload` for anything — it holds tool output (2026-09-30 security decision).

body:
# Recon - project   (2026-10-09)

## Status: COMPLETE

Range reviewed: the whole repository at HEAD (c267990), no diff.

## Question
Inventory and structure map: uniformity, orphaned and dead-code candidates (six deliverables from the dispatch).

## Summary
Layout in AGENTS.md matches disk except: `internal/trail` (3 files, 517 lines) exists and is not named; root files `PRIORITY_TODO.md`, `embed.go`, `embed_test.go`, `init_project_test.go`, `plan_test.go`, `testmain_test.go`, `go.sum`, `README.md`, `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `TODO.md` are not in the Layout block (only README/REQUIREMENTS/embed are named elsewhere). `PRIORITY_TODO.md` (1 line, a header) is almost certainly a leftover: commit 1b8e89b said "PRIORITY_TODO emptied and its rule removed" but the file was kept; nothing outside dated trail records mentions it. No dead files or unused go.mod requirements found; dead-code candidates are ~28 exported identifiers used only in their defining file (could be unexported). Trail is healthy: 166 bug records = 166 INDEX rows, one open bug (BUG-139), no plan with real unticked boxes. `.agents/scratch/` holds ~200 untracked-by-design leftovers (gitignored).

## 1. Inventory
Root (not named in Layout): AGENTS.md (17,396 B, named by definition), README.md (48,625 B), REQUIREMENTS.md (65 lines), ROADMAP.md (10 lines; "Last reviewed: 2026-10-01", Now and Next empty), TODO.md (5 lines, empty), PRIORITY_TODO.md (1 line: "# PRIORITY TODO - audit fix (operator, 2026-09-30)"), embed.go (the `styrman` package, `//go:embed all:context all:skills all:agents all:commands all:rules`), root tests embed_test.go, init_project_test.go, plan_test.go, testmain_test.go (package at repo root, 4 test files), go.mod/go.sum, .gitignore.
Dirs, all named in Layout: context/ (AGENTS.md, dev-setup.md), agents/ (8 files), skills/ (38 entries: 36 skills + VENDORED.md + google-catalog catalog; 885 tracked files), commands/ (only .gitkeep, by design), rules/ (critical-thinking.md + .gitkeep), cmd/sh-agent (7 files, 4,586 lines), internal/ (89 tracked files), .agents/docs (1,523 tracked), .agents/scratch (gitignored, 1 tracked .gitkeep), .agents/skills (symlink to ../skills, tracked as a symlink).
Layout names `internal/{harness,search,memory,dream,metrics}` only; disk also has `internal/trail`. Layout says `.agents/docs/` has "plans, changes, ADRs, reviews, testing, deploy/{local,remote,gcp}.md, bugs/INDEX.md"; disk also has handoffs/, retros/, specs/sh-agent/, architecture/DECISIONS.md (ADR home). Not on disk but named: none found.
.gitignore: `/.claude/` and `/agent/` have no matching path today (fine, they are created by tools); `.agents/memory` and `.claude/settings.local.json` likewise absent. Secret-shaped block is pinned to plan.go secretShaped() per its comment.

## 2. Structure map of the binary (counts: go files / lines incl. tests)
- internal/harness 35 / 14,073; ~70 exported funcs/methods; imported by cmd/sh-agent and the root package tests. Installer, update, report, release, zip, state, lint, derive.
- internal/search 14 / 5,068; ~12 exported; imported by cmd, metrics (agy.go, claude.go), dream (collect.go). Owns SQLite DSN helpers (`search.DSN` used by metrics/store.go:71).
- internal/memory 3 / 762; 6 exported; imported by cmd, dream.
- internal/dream 12 / 3,750; 11 exported; imported by cmd only.
- internal/metrics 21 / 5,009; 16 exported; imported by cmd, dream.
- internal/trail 3 / 517; 6 exported; imported by dream/collect.go, metrics/events.go, memory/memory.go, search/reconcile.go, search/search.go. No SQLite.
Flow: cmd/sh-agent/main.go:84 main() -> verb table (one FlagSet per verb; entries at main.go ~146-200: version, uninstall, report, memory, dream, metrics, search, index, install, sync, status, diff, update, list, render, adopt) -> `run` func or inline closure. install/sync -> runInstall -> harness plan/apply (plan.go, apply.go, derive.go); update -> repo.go/release.go/zip.go; report -> harness/report.go; search/index -> search.Search/Reconcile (git-reconciled SQLite); memory -> memory add/show; dream -> dream.Run (collect via search + memory, run CLI, timer install); metrics -> ingest/show/report via metrics store. (Per-verb leaf tracing below main.go's table was not read line by line.)

## 3. Uniformity
- Errors: `%w` wrapping is concentrated in harness (apply 7, release 7, repo 6, zip 6, report 10, inventory 7); dream, memory, search, metrics wrap sparsely (dream/state.go 1, dream/collect.go 1); metrics and search files show none by this grep. Uneven but not contradictory.
- log/slog: used only in internal/harness/harness_test.go; the CLI prints with fmt to stderr (main.go "sh-agent:" prefix). Global context says Go services use slog JSON; this is a CLI, so divergence is by kind, not a defect. Say so if a plan asks for uniform logging.
- Home resolution: os.UserHomeDir/HOME only in cmd/sh-agent/main.go, internal/harness/pathguard.go, internal/dream/run.go (dream also needs the agy private HOME). No other package reads HOME directly; they take a home argument. Good.
- Atomic writes: os.Rename in harness/apply.go and harness/adopt.go only; os.WriteFile in harness/report.go and dream/run.go (non-atomic). memory and metrics writes not located by this grep (SQLite or other helper); unverified.
- SQLite: sql.Open at internal/metrics/store.go:71 (via search.DSN), internal/search/store.go:187, and internal/search/dream.go:266 (read-only DSN on copies). Matches AGENTS.md (search and metrics are the driver importers; dream goes through search). Close discipline not audited.
- Tests: each of 8 test dirs has its own testmain_test.go (dream uses main_test.go): the root, cmd, harness, metrics, trail, search, memory (dream differs in name). 38 test files use t.TempDir or a home helper.
- Frontmatter: agents all `description:` double-quoted, tools lists (bugs/changelog/documentation: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write; dreamer/explorer/reviewer/security/verifier: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Write), models sonnet x6, haiku (changelog), opus (security); maxTurns 20/30/40/40/40/40/40/45 (bugs, changelog, documentation, dreamer, explorer, reviewer, security, verifier). Skills: no non-catalog SKILL.md uses `disable-model-invocation`; description quoting mixed (some quoted with `"`, some plain; first-char scan was inconclusive).

## 4. Orphan and dead-code candidates
Exported but referenced only in their defining file (no other non-test file): harness Alive, AssetName, BuildRecord, Canary, Collect, Collection, Doc, Keys, LatestRelease, Lint, LoadAgents, LoadDocs, OriginKind, ParseOrigin, ReadSettings, Record, Redaction, ReleaseRepo, ResolveFeedback, RunningElsewhere; search AgyConversation, IsBusy; memory Refusal; metrics Adherence, Efficiency, ErrNewerSchema, Reliability, RenderReport. Many are used by tests (e.g. LoadAgents 9) and some are method names (Collect, Keys, Alive) where the per-name grep over-matches. Treat as "could be unexported", not dead: LatestRelease, LoadDocs, OriginKind, AgyConversation, IsBusy, Refusal have 0 test refs and no cross-file refs - best true candidates (verify with `go vet`/staticcheck-like check before acting).
Files no package imports: none found; every internal package is imported by cmd or another package. go.mod: only `modernc.org/sqlite` direct; indirect set is what sqlite pulls (go-humanize, uuid, isatty etc. not imported by repo code, as expected).
Agents with no dispatcher: none; all 8 appear in context/AGENTS.md (dreamer, explorer once each) and in 4-12 skills.
Skills nothing names (no context mention, no other skill mentions): explain-project, find-skills, google-catalog (router; named in Installed list at install time), harness-audit. They are triggered by description only; likely deliberate.
Scripts: kit-preamble.sh, seed-security/run.sh, ab-kit/{run.sh,accept.py}, agy-rel/run.sh, review/scripts/restatement-grep.sh, google-catalog/scripts/refresh-catalog.sh all have other referrers (basename match, so run.sh counts are inflated: 81 refs is the shared name). accept.py has 7.
Docs: not all untracked-by-link docs checked (see Not checked). `.agents/docs/testing/` has 349 files, most dated records; undated: guide.md, sh-agent-matrix.md, skill-matrix.md, kit-preamble.sh.

## 5. Trail health (tracked files)
architecture 1 (DECISIONS.md), bugs 167 (166 records + INDEX; BUG-001 .. BUG-166), changes 264 (2026-09-03 .. 2026-10-09-1651), deploy 3, handoffs 114 (2026-09-03 .. 2026-10-09-1652), plans 79 (22 recon/research briefs; 2026-09-03 .. 2026-10-08), retros 16 (2026-09-14 .. 2026-09-30; none since), reviews 525, specs 5 (specs/sh-agent), testing 349. Uncommitted: .agents/docs/testing/2026-10-09-verify-project.md (untracked, from another agent, not mine).
Open: `sh-agent search --open` reports 1 open record: BUG-139 (documentation agent roadmap lane held in 5 of 6 runs, open since 2026-10-01). Plans: only 2026-09-15-harness-practices-g01-g26.md matches `- [ ]` (4 hits; the matches at lines 180-183 are a template inside the plan, not work; ROADMAP does not name it). INDEX vs record: 166 records and 166 rows, ids all present; status agreement not conclusively checked (graduated rows use a different column layout, my check was inconclusive).
ROADMAP.md "Last reviewed: 2026-10-01" is 8 days old with Now empty - consistent with no active plan.

## 6. Risks and open questions for a fix plan
- PRIORITY_TODO.md: leftover (1b8e89b says its rule was removed) or deliberate? Deleting it is a root-file change; also check no test pins it.
- Is internal/trail meant to be in AGENTS.md Layout? (It exists since plan 2026-10-08-metrics-store D31.) Adding is a docs-only edit but AGENTS.md is the project rule file.
- Root-level Go tests (init_project_test.go, plan_test.go, embed_test.go, testmain_test.go) sit in package `styrman` beside embed.go: deliberate (they test embedded content) but unnamed in Layout.

Per-verb call chains below main.go's verb table; full exported-surface listing via `go doc`; error-wrapping and atomic-write audit for memory, metrics, search, dream beyond a grep; SQLite Close discipline; skill description quoting per file; INDEX status vs record status (check inconclusive); undated docs under .agents/docs with no inbound link; test naming conventions; vendored catalog contents; staticcheck/deadcode tooling (not run).

title: Review — Google's Elephant-Goldfish Model (egm.dev) against this harness (2026-10-23)
body:
# Review — Google's Elephant-Goldfish Model (egm.dev) against this harness   (2026-10-23)

Research record promoted from scratch on 2026-10-23 (operator: "go all approved"). Its items became plan `2026-10-23-session-sized-work.md` Phases 3–5.

## What was read

- https://egm.dev/ and the repository github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model, shallow clone at `.agents/scratch/egm-review/upstream/`, HEAD `d651fe86c12dccc5272274e002674fb8eec4c547` (2026-10-22, "Fix bootstrap prompt truncation and Claude transcript lookup (#114)").
- GitHub metadata (`gh api`): created 2026-09-13, 218 stars, 19 forks, 17 open issues, 0 releases, 0 tags, pushed 2026-10-23. `plugin.json` version 0.1.0. Apache-2.0. Footer: "not an officially supported Google product".
- Every file under `skills/`, `agents/`, `.claude-plugin/`, `resources/`, `docs/{claude,getting_started,harnesses,faq}.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `AI_POLICY.md`, `plugin.json`.
- Harness side: project `AGENTS.md` rules 1–6, `skills/VENDORED.md`, `internal/harness/inventory.go` (`agentKeys`, `SlashOnly`, permission keys), `derive.go` (`toolMap`), `size_test.go` budgets (run), the 2026-09-15 research record and its G-rows, ADR at `DECISIONS.md:63` (2026-09-03) and ADR-050, `skills/{feature,bug,spec,review,research}/SKILL.md` frontmatter and the feature skill's plan template and cold-reader brief, `agents/reviewer.md`.

## What EGM is

Seven skills (`egm-brainstorm`, `egm-draft`, `egm-review`, `egm-review-loop`, `egm-resolve`, `egm-drift-report`, `egm-bootstrap`), all `disable-model-invocation: true`; nine subagent personas in `agents/` (zoom-out, comprehension, design critic, implementation readiness, codebase details, structural, style, synthesizer, bootstrap orchestrator) plus nine Claude adapters in `.claude-plugin/agents/` (`tools: [Read, Grep, Glob]`, `model: inherit`, `omitClaudeMd: true`, each reading its persona at run time); five document standards (8.4 KB) in `resources/document_standards/`; a design-doc template (`skills/egm_draft/references/design_doc.md`); one `PreToolUse` hook that auto-allows Read/Grep/Glob inside the plugin cache; manifests for Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, ChatGPT. Prose only, no script beyond the hook, no network call. Tests: pytest over YAML scenario files (required/forbidden regexes per turn) and an opt-in live Claude probe.

The skills read `agents/`, `resources/` and `docs/claude.md` at run time through `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` (21 references). `docs/harnesses.md`: "Skill-only installers that copy `skills/` alone break EGM."

## Items

### 1. The install commands are a fourth way in

`claude plugin marketplace add google/elephant-goldfish-model` and `agy plugin install …` put files on a machine through a channel the map does not draw. Project `AGENTS.md` rule 1: three ways in, nothing else; rule 3: a new path is an ADR plus a map change in one commit. Global `AGENTS.md`: a skill found elsewhere goes into the checkout's `skills/`, then `sh-agent install`, never only into a vendor directory. The plugin route would also leave each machine on whatever `main` it fetched, with no pin and no `sh-agent status` line for it.

**Recommendation:** strike the plugin install as a mechanism. Whatever is taken enters through `skills/` and `agents/` here and reaches machines in a tag. (The operator may try the plugin in a sandbox home to see it run; that is a test, not a deployment.)

### 2. Verbatim vendoring is not possible

`VENDORED.md` defines verbatim as an empty `diff -r` against the pin. EGM's skills cannot run as copied: 21 `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` references, personas and standards outside the skill directory, cross-skill calls by file path. In a harness install there is no plugin root; agents are self-contained files in `~/.claude/agents/` and derived for Antigravity. The nine Claude adapters carry `omitClaudeMd` and `license` keys that `agentKeys` refuses; the hook is unnecessary (nothing lives in a plugin cache) and the installer refuses `hooks` anyway.

**Recommendation:** fork, under harness names, or take pieces (item 4). Exception: the five document standards and the design-doc template are plain files with no plugin reference and can travel verbatim as `references/` with the Apache-2.0 `LICENSE` beside them, pinned by commit in `VENDORED.md`.

### 3. Wholesale adoption costs more than it adds

Two shapes were weighed. (a) Harness-native fork: seven personas become seven agents, the standards become references, seven skills (about 95 KB of prose) rewritten for paths, scratch location and interaction rules; then, by the release rule, one Antigravity run per changed skill and agent before a tag: 16 runs, plus both CLIs' smoke. (b) Catalog shape, as `google-catalog`: the whole tree pinned as data under one router skill that substitutes the root; personas read at run time by a general-purpose subagent (EGM's own fallback for hosts without named personas). (b) keeps the text verbatim and the pin honest, but the google-catalog refresh script is bound to its two sources (a new script or a generalisation is code, so a design question), and the reviewers would be whatever general-purpose agent each CLI offers, outside `derive.go`, so not the same on both CLIs.

The method itself is already here. The 2026-09-03 ADR (`DECISIONS.md:63`) names the elephant/goldfish repository as one of its two sources: design-before-code with an artifact-only goldfish, fix-or-rebut with a round cap, the four user gates. The 2026-09-15 research (a different, earlier repository, vshvedov/elephant-goldfish at b8ebb3d) adopted G04 (Decisions section and cold-reader box), G07, G10, G11, G13, G15, G16, G21, G22, G23, G25. The `bug` skill's Step 2 is a goldfish diagnosis; the `feature` skill's Step 3 is a goldfish read of the plan. `rules/critical-thinking.md` (ADR-050) matches EGM's `egm-review` Execution Constraints 3–10 almost sentence for sentence.

**Recommendation:** defer both shapes; adopt the deltas in item 4.

### 4. What is new since 2026-09-15, worth taking

- **Five document standards** (`zoom-out`, `feature-spec`, `implementation-readiness`, `heilmeier`, `re-implementation`; 8.4 KB). The cold-reader brief in `feature` Step 3 asks three questions in one paragraph; the standards give the reviewer a written rubric per question (zoom-out ↔ Scope, implementation-readiness ↔ Readiness, its "Zero-Decision Rule" is the harness's BLOCKING definition stated better). Land as `skills/feature/references/standards/` (verbatim, pinned) and one sentence in the Step 3 brief naming them.
- **The naive-reader lens** (`agents/comprehension.md`: undefined terms, acronyms, comprehension gaps). This is G27 of 2026-09-15, "later", with concrete text now. One clause in the cold-reader brief, no new agent.
- **A spec-vs-code drift lens** (item 6).

Not new, already present or rejected: the Decisions section, the no-code gate, review rounds with a cap, rebuttals needing a checkable reason, the anti-sycophancy rules, recon before the plan.

**Recommendation:** fix (adopt) the first two as one Task on `skills/feature/`; a behavioural run of the cold read on both CLIs is the tier.

### 5. The isolation gap is real and is a design question

EGM reviewers run with `omitClaudeMd: true`: no user, project or local instruction file reaches the goldfish (Claude Code 2.1.271+; this box has 2.1.309). The harness's `reviewer` cold read runs with the global context and rules loaded, because the key is not in `agentKeys` and ADR-056a refuses a restriction one CLI drops: Antigravity has no equivalent, so the derived agent would silently be less isolated than the Claude one. The gap matters most for the cold read of a plan written under the same context the reviewer then reads.

**Recommendation:** operator decides: (a) reopen ADR-056a for keys that only tighten a subagent, marking the Antigravity derivation as the documented gap (a dashed line, rule 4's honesty), or (b) accept the gap and record it in `agents/reviewer.md`. Either is an ADR; (a) is a code change in `inventory.go` and `derive.go`.

### 6. Drift report: a different lens from `--docs`

`/review --docs` is diff-scoped and `--project` lists stale references between docs (G06). EGM's `egm-drift-report` reads every spec under a directory, finds the code it names, and reports logic described but absent, models missing fields, hardcoded values where logic was planned, and architectural divergence; one report file, weekly cadence. The harness has `.agents/docs/specs/` and no sweep that checks them against code.

**Recommendation:** defer to its own Task: a `--drift` lens on `/review` over `<docs-root>/specs/` (and `plans/` with closed boxes), reviewer-dispatched, written to `reviews/`. New flag, so the review skill's docs and matrix rows change; no code.

### 7. Brainstorm swarm and the five-stage review pipeline

`egm-brainstorm` fans out six lenses; `egm-review` runs stages 5→9 with up to seven personas per stage and a synthesizer. The 2026-09-15 research struck these as G38 (three to six dispatches per use, no recorded need) and G37 (uncapped panels against the three-round cap). No incident since then shows the single cold read missing what a panel would catch.

**Recommendation:** strike, unless the operator sets a dispatch budget and names a plan where the cold read missed something a lens would have caught.

### 8. Bootstrap

`egm-bootstrap` writes a `README.md` with sentinel blocks into every directory of a tree, bottom up, and keeps them current. `explain-project` writes one `onboarding.md`; the global rule says comments say why, not what; per-directory generated prose drifts the moment code moves and is exactly what item 6 would then report.

**Recommendation:** strike.

### 9. EGM text that contradicts harness rules (to strip in any fork)

`resources/execution_instructions.md` and the skills' constraint blocks: scratch "under `/tmp/`" (harness: `.agents/scratch/`, never `/tmp`); "ONE QUESTION AT A TIME" and no "(Recommended)" prefix (the operator's protocol is one numbered table with a recommendation per row; `AskUserQuestion` puts the recommended option first); "NO SUMMARIES" (the Definition of Done ends in a report); "SILENT ENFORCEMENT / NO META-TALK: you MUST NOT mention … policies" (a concealment instruction; the harness leads with what is broken and never restates a failure as success). The anti-sycophancy items 3–10 duplicate `critical-thinking.md`.

**Recommendation:** fix in any fork; never vendor these lines. The standards and template (item 4) contain none of them (checked: no `/tmp`, no question rule, no silence rule in `resources/document_standards/` or `references/design_doc.md`).

### 10. Maturity and pin

Forty days old, 0.1.0, no release or tag, 17 open issues, a fix to Claude transcript lookup landed yesterday; Cowork and ChatGPT support carry open verification gaps (#105, #106). `VENDORED.md` requires a full 40-digit commit pin verified by `git archive <pin> <path> | tar -x` then `diff -r`, never a date; a verbatim Apache-2.0 file carries the `LICENSE` with it.

**Recommendation:** pin d651fe86c12dccc5272274e002674fb8eec4c547 for anything taken; re-pin only after reading the diff.

### 11. Budgets and CLI behaviour (no blocker)

Skill listing: 19,274 of 19,500 bytes, 226 bytes of headroom, but `TestSkillListingBudget` skips slash-only skills, so EGM-shaped skills would not count; references do not count. Antigravity block: 17,338 of 22,000; sixteen inventory names fit. Antigravity hides slash-only skills from the model (verified 2026-09-03, `verify-sandbox.md:37`). Claude's `Skill` tool refuses slash-only skills, so a skill that calls another must say "read its SKILL.md and follow it", which EGM already does. `toolMap` maps Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Write, Edit: every EGM adapter tool derives. The harness has no slash-only skill today; the first one flips the inventory's `slashNote` sentence automatically.

### 12. Tests

EGM's unit tests are pytest over frontmatter, links and manifests, plus YAML scenarios with required and forbidden patterns per turn. The harness is Go stdlib only and tests behaviour with run kits (guide § 4). The scenario files are a usable seed for a run kit's assertions, not a tier that can run here.

**Recommendation:** defer; each adopted piece gets one behavioural run per CLI, logged under `testing/`.

## Sources

- https://egm.dev/
- https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model (clone at `.agents/scratch/egm-review/upstream`)
- https://daily.dev/posts/introducing-the-elephant-goldfish-model-plugin-scaling-design-driven-ai-software-development-liy0vmgnv
- https://medium.com/@drensin/elephants-goldfish-and-the-new-golden-age-of-software-engineering-c33641a48874
- `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-15-research-beads-elephant-goldfish-goldfish.md`, `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` (2026-09-03 ADR, ADR-050, ADR-056a)

title: Research — session-sized work: splitting tasks so a session never fills its context (2026-10-23)
body:
# Research — session-sized work: splitting tasks so a session never fills its context   (2026-10-23)

Research record promoted from scratch on 2026-10-23 (operator: "go all approved"). Its items became plan `2026-10-23-session-sized-work.md`.

## Evidence

### This box's sessions (metrics store, copy in `.agents/scratch/egm-review/metrics/copy.db`, read-only; 49 main Claude Code sessions since 2026-09-01, sandbox labels excluded)

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| Peak context per session, median / p75 / p90 / max (tokens) | 573,527 / 822,796 / 943,841 / 967,274 |
| Sessions whose peak passed 200K / 400K / 900K | 38 / 29 / 9 of 49 |
| Sessions with at least one compaction (total compactions) | 13 (16); max 3 in one session |
| Tool calls per session, median / p90 / max | 288 / 646 / 842 |
| Corrections logged per session, no-compaction vs compacted sessions | 0.06 vs 0.08 (3 events in all: under-logged, not a signal) |
| Escaped bugs per session, either bucket | 0.00 |
| Handoffs per session | 0.75 vs 1.15 |

Reading: on 1M-window models the sessions here run at half a million tokens for most of their life and compact at about 967K (the Claude Code default for native-1M models). The local store cannot yet show a quality difference between short and long sessions: it records corrections and escaped bugs, and both are near zero in the window.

### Published evidence

- Chroma, "Context Rot" (July 2025, 18 models incl. five Claude): "model performance consistently degrades with increasing input length"; "even a single distractor reduces performance relative to the baseline"; LongMemEval, 306 prompts: focused prompts of about 300 tokens beat full prompts of about 113K tokens "across all models", the Claude family showing the largest gap.
- Anthropic, "Effective context engineering for AI agents": context is "a finite resource with diminishing marginal returns"; degradation is "a performance gradient rather than a hard cliff"; the three long-horizon levers are compaction, structured note-taking outside the window, and sub-agents that return a condensed summary; "do the simplest thing that works".
- Claude Code docs, Best practices: "Most best practices are based on one constraint: Claude's context window fills up fast, and performance degrades as it fills"; "Use `/clear` frequently between tasks"; after two failed corrections, "`/clear` and start fresh with a more specific prompt"; after a spec is written, "start a fresh session to execute it. The new session has clean context focused entirely on implementation, and you have a written spec to reference."
- Claude Code docs, context window: what survives compaction (CLAUDE.md and rules re-injected; up to five recently modified files re-read; skill bodies capped at 5,000 tokens each, 25,000 total); `/autocompact <tokens>` sets an earlier pass (100K–1M); `/context` shows the live breakdown to the USER; nothing tells the MODEL its own usage.
- Antigravity: `agy --continue` and `agy --conversation <id>` exist (`agy --help`); no compaction control found; community reports describe compaction as aggressive and opaque with no token meter. Unverified beyond those reports.

### What the harness already has

- Global context: checkpoints "before the context gets long or the session may end (`/handoff`)"; Definition of Done step 5 "recommend a fresh session for the next task"; "progress that lives only in chat or a compaction summary is lost".
- `handoff` Step 7: "Start a new session and paste: `Read the handoff at <path> and continue the work.`" and "recommend a fresh session (`/clear` on Claude Code, a new conversation on Antigravity) for the next task". The paste line is generic: it names no phase, no approvals, no check.
- `feature` Step 4: one phase per checkpoint; an in-progress note when "the context may compact, the session may end"; nothing sizes a phase to a session or ends the session at the checkpoint.
- Sub-agents for large reads (explorer at 10+ files, verifier, reviewer): the main thread still runs a median 288 tool calls.
- `/review --resume`: the cold-read test that a fresh session can resume from the trail. This is the quality gate the feature needs and it exists.
- The learning loop already holds this correction once: feedback.jsonl 2026-10-21 19:04 (crew): "Start fresh sessions to keep the context small, and run autonomously with as few questions as possible: standing approvals in the prompt, ask only outside them or for critical failures." Today is its second occurrence; the retro cadence says a repeated correction graduates into a mechanism.

### Resume cost, measured

A fresh session's resume order on this project reads about 124 KB (roughly 30K tokens) before work: `bugs/INDEX.md` 50 KB, the active plan 27 KB, project `AGENTS.md` 18 KB, the rendered global context 16 KB, the handoff 4 KB, three changes 8 KB. Splitting a 600K session into three 200K sessions costs about 90K tokens of re-reads and saves nothing in tokens; the gain is quality, not cost. `INDEX.md` is 40% of the bill and grows with every bug.

## Stress test of the premise

- What the operator is not seeing: the gain they felt comes from two things at once, a fresh window AND the forced write-down of state into a prompt. The harness already forces the write-down (plan, handoff). The unmeasured part is the fresh window. Without a quality signal in the metrics the claim "fewer hallucinations" stays the operator's observation plus the literature; the plan must add the measurement, not assume it.
- Strongest counter-argument: a split mid-phase loses in-flight state the handoff cannot carry; Anthropic's own guidance ("sometimes you should let context accumulate because you're deep in one complex problem") and the resume cost both say split only at checkpoints, never on a token count.
- The model cannot see its context fill. A rule keyed on "when the context is long" is unobservable from inside; a rule keyed on a structural boundary (phase checkpoint, task done) is observable every time. Claude Code gives the OPERATOR a gauge (`/context`, status line); Antigravity gives none that was found.
- Over-splitting: Trivial and Task classes fit one session by definition; the rule is for Feature plans and for sessions that take a second unrelated ask (the "kitchen sink" pattern).
- Cross-CLI: anything that depends on `/clear`, `/autocompact` or a status line is Claude Code only; the structural rule and the kickoff prompt work on both.

## Items

### 1. Add it as its own feature plan, run before the EGM tasks

Different subject from EGM, a design question in it (where the always-on rule lives), and it changes how every later task is run. The EGM items (standards and naive-reader lens into `feature`; the `--drift` lens; the ADR-056a decision) become its first session-sized phases and its first measurement.

### 2. The always-on rule and where it lives

Rule: a session is one Task or one plan phase. At the phase checkpoint (or at Definition of Done step 5) the session writes the handoff with a kickoff prompt and ENDS; the next phase starts in a fresh conversation. A second unrelated ask in a session gets its own kickoff prompt instead of being done in place. Where: `rules/session-sizing.md` (always-on on both CLIs; the Antigravity block has 4,662 bytes of room). The hand-written context has 71 bytes of headroom, so a sentence there means removing one.

### 3. The kickoff prompt

The handoff gains `## Kickoff`: the exact prompt for the next conversation, written for a reader with no context: project path, the plan path and the ONE phase to do, the standing approvals it may act on without asking (the 2026-10-21 correction's words), what must pass before it stops (the phase's Checkpoint evidence; for an unattended run, the `/goal` condition), and the instruction to end with the next kickoff. The handoff's Step 7 report prints it in a fenced block, after "run `/clear` (Claude Code) or start a new conversation (Antigravity), then paste:". File-drop change to `skills/handoff/SKILL.md` only; no `sh-agent` verb.

### 4. Phase sizing in the feature skill

A phase is what one fresh session can finish and verify; the plan's cold reader (Step 3) gets a fourth question: "can each phase be finished by a fresh session that reads only the plan and the files it names?" A number for "finish" is not invented here: the metric in item 5 sets the target and `/retro` tunes the sizing.

### 5. Measure it

The metrics store already holds peak context per session (B3). Add one report row, "main sessions whose peak context passed the target (default 300K)", and the per-session peak in `show --json`, so `/retro` sees the trend; keep corrections and escaped bugs beside it. A small code change in `internal/metrics` (Task). Starting target 300K is a proposal, not a finding; the operator picks it.

### 6. Resume cost

`bugs/INDEX.md` (50 KB) is read in full by every fresh session. Options: resume reads only its open rows (`sh-agent search --open` already exists for plans) or a short `## Open` head the full table follows. A separate Task; it halves the cost of every split.

### 7. Claude Code knobs the operator can set today, outside the harness

`/autocompact 300k` (compaction before the gradient bites instead of at 967K), a status line with context percentage, `/clear` then `claude --resume` when a session must be revisited. Not harness changes (settings are a non-goal); recorded in `deploy/local.md` § Operator steps if the operator adopts them.

### 8. Not proposed

A token-count trigger for the model (unobservable); automatic `/clear` (no CLI exposes it to the model; hooks are refused, ADR-007); a `sh-agent next` verb (the handoff's fenced block does the job without code); per-project compaction instructions in CLAUDE.md (the project root holds `AGENTS.md` alone).

## Sources

- https://www.trychroma.com/research/context-rot
- https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices · https://code.claude.com/docs/en/context-window · https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config · https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs
- https://discuss.ai.google.dev/t/frustrated-with-aggressive-context-compaction-before-plan-execution/167983 · https://agentpedia.codes/blog/managing-context-antigravity-sessions (community, unverified)
- `~/.config/sh-agent/feedback.jsonl` entry 2026-10-21T19:04:11+02:00; `sh-agent metrics show --since 2026-09-01 --json`; `skills/handoff/SKILL.md` Step 7; `skills/feature/SKILL.md` Step 4
