- Assumption 4: a kit run never ingests into the real home: the kit's wrapper pins `--home` on every `fyr` call (`.agents/kit/kit-preamble.sh:241-251`, BUG-107) — checked by the Phase 4 rows' exit scan.
- Most sessions on this box are Claude Code (49 historical main sessions, 1 Antigravity session in the copy); the feed captures only Antigravity sessions (ADR-062), so this box's numbers stay thin until its work runs on Antigravity.

## Decisions

D1 — 2026-10-25 — The checkpoint feed is written in the `handoff` and `retro` skills and named once in the context, run by the agent; the binary triggers nothing — by: implementer (R0 "the moments the context names", R3)
D2 — 2026-10-25 — The handoff skill ingests before it stores the handoff — superseded by D9
D3 — 2026-10-25 — A record's time is the minute stamped in its ID, never `updated` (moved by edits and by the import) — by: implementer
D4 — 2026-10-25 — A migrated project is joined from records only, an unmigrated one from files only, never both for one root; corrections excepted (D11) — by: implementer
D5 — 2026-10-25 — `events.ref` is the record ID for both joins, rewritten by an SQL migration 3 — superseded by D10
D6 — 2026-10-25 — A2 reads every `testing` record with a `## Status:` heading — superseded by D12
D7 — 2026-10-25 — Corrections are read from both the global feedback records and `feedback.jsonl`, deduplicated by `ts` — refined by D11
D8 — 2026-10-25 — C3 counts `fyr record get` by the ID's kind and `fyr record list` as `list`; `fyr search` and `fyr memory show` are not trail reads for C3 — by: implementer
D9 — 2026-10-25 — The handoff skill's last call, after store, commit and push, is `fyr metrics ingest`; a failure is reported in chat, never written into the immutable handoff — supersedes D2 — by: cold read round 1 (E2E 1 could not pass with the ingest before the store)
D10 — 2026-10-25 — The ref rewrite runs in Go inside every join through `brain.ImportedID` (the import's own `slugOf`), idempotent, no schema change; a collision's `-N` suffix is not reproduced, so such a pair stays two events (named in the spec) — supersedes D5 — by: cold read round 1 (SQL `lower()` is not `slugOf`)
D11 — 2026-10-25 — Global feedback records are read for every project root, migrated, unmigrated or gone, matched on the main worktree root (root itself when gone), before the root-gone check as today; `ts` is compared normalised to UTC — refines D7 — by: cold read round 1
D12 — 2026-10-25 — A2 over records counts a `testing` record only when its title matches `^Verif(ication|y)\b` and its body has a `## Status:` heading, so behavioural-run records do not count; the file join keeps its `*-verify-*` name filter — supersedes D6 — by: cold read round 1
D13 — 2026-10-25 — A4 over records reads the bug body as stored; an imported closed bug holds only its title and prevention (`internal/brain/import.go:442-454`), so it gives no A4 event, and the events stored before the migration stay; no change to the bug skill — by: cold read round 1
D14 — 2026-10-25 — `/retro --dry-run` skips the ingest (its read-only promise, `skills/retro/SKILL.md:15`) and says the numbers are from the last ingest — by: cold read round 1
D15 — 2026-10-25 — Record times are read in the machine's local zone; a valid minute is required (`ParseInLocation`); another machine's zone offset is a known limit in the spec — by: cold read round 1
D16 — 2026-10-25 — `recordRead` counts only the program `fyr` (any directory) and `go run ./cmd/fyr`; it skips `--home`/`--repo` and their values and other flags; `get` with no ID word, or an unknown prefix, is `record`; `FEEDBACK` and `PROPOSAL` are in the vocabulary — by: cold read round 1
D17 — 2026-10-25 — First-reads keep today's count shape: the first three steps that carry a kind, now `Read` or `Bash` — by: cold read round 1
D18 — 2026-10-25 — Phase 1 of the first draft is split: the reference rule (Phase 1) and the records join (Phase 2) — by: cold read round 1 (sizing)
D19 — 2026-10-25 — The plan is approved and its scope confirmed as written, S2, S3, D11 and D12 kept; D13's limit and the Antigravity-only feed (Risks) accepted — by: the operator, "Go all approved" (2026-10-25), over the table of the planning session's report
D20 — 2026-10-25 — A `correction` ref an older ingest stored as its entry's `ts` with an offset (`+02:00`) is rewritten to the UTC form inside the join's transaction, as D10 does for file refs, a duplicate deleted; without it the 3 such refs on this box would count twice once D11 normalises — by: implementer (found while writing D11)
D21 — 2026-10-25 — `ForMetrics` loads a migrated checkout even when `brain.db` does not exist yet, creating it, as every record verb and `ForDream` do (Assumption 2); only a root with no `trail.jsonl` and no store gets the empty input with nothing created. Otherwise a fresh clone's sessions would get no trail events — by: implementer (the Interfaces comment said "No brain.db: an empty input" without the migrated case)
Rejected: ingest inside `fyr record add handoff|change` — a behaviour no skill names (R3), slows every record write, and couples `internal/brain` to `internal/metrics`
Rejected: a `created` column in `brain.db` — a schema change to the brain store for a time the ID already carries
Rejected: placing records by `updated` — an edit or the import moves it to a later session
Rejected: an SQL migration for the refs — SQL cannot express `slugOf`, and a schema bump would make older binaries refuse the store for a rewrite they tolerate
Rejected: keeping file-name refs and keying records to them — a record ID cannot be turned back into its file name
Rejected: ingesting before the handoff is stored (D2) — the session's own handoff would miss the join

title: Plan — fyr check: docs freshness and drift (2026-10-25)
body:
# Plan — `fyr check`: docs freshness and drift   (2026-10-25)

Status: approved by the operator 2026-10-25 (D24), with O2, O4 and O6 answered (D25–D27) and O3 and O5 answered (D30, D31); Phase 1, Phase 2 and Phase 3 done 2026-10-25; the Done section (reviewer, security, verifier) next. The cold read (REVIEW-2026-10-25-2036-review-cold-read-of-the-fyr-check-plan, 17 gaps, 4 blocking) is answered by D9–D23, by rebuttals in its `## Outcome`, and by the Open rows. O1, O7 and A3's `Open:` row answered by the operator 2026-10-25 (D35–D37), with D38 for `SPEC-fyr-check`'s code; nothing is open before Phase 3.

## Why

Roadmap item 3 (`ROADMAP.md` Next) asks for: "`fyr check`: docs freshness and drift (docs naming verbs, flags or paths that do not exist; specs older than the code they describe; requirements without an enforcement site)".

ADR-063 § Consequences builds roadmap items 2–4 on the brain store. `REQUIREMENTS.md` R0 says fyr "grows to evaluate projects and catch drift in the binary and its specs, never in the context", and that the CLI asks it for help "when work starts drifting".

Measured, 2026-10-25:

- The recall measurement over records scored 0.025 on drift questions, against 0.269 on words (`HANDOFF-2026-10-25-1742-…`, Agent notes). Search does not find drift; a check can.
- No existing check covers any of the three:
  - `TestHarnessMap` (`cmd/fyr/main_test.go:868`) checks only the verbs in README's map.
  - `TestSkillLinksResolve` (`internal/harness/skill_links_test.go:18`) checks only a skill's own `references/`, `assets/` and `scripts/` links.
  - `restatement-grep.sh` greps only the words it is handed.
  - The `review --docs` brief (`skills/review/SKILL.md:58-66`) is worked by hand.
  - Recon: `PLAN-2026-10-25-2024-recon-fyr-check-2026-10-25`.
- Prototypes of the rules on this checkout, run read-only from scratch scripts (`.agents/scratch/cr2/`, `.agents/scratch/cr/proto.py`), each an approximation and not the implementation:
  - The path rule finds 38 in 254 candidates. One is real drift: `DEPLOY-gcp` line 5 names `skills/init-project/assets/agents-tree/docs/DEPLOY-gcp`, but the template is now `skills/init-project/assets/records/DEPLOY-gcp.md`. The other 37 are another checkout's paths (the kit's fixture: `internal/greet/greet.go`; the old layout: `.agents/docs/`).
  - The verb rule, before D16, finds 8. Five of them are D16's program-word cases (`cmd/fyr` in a layout fence, `~/.config/fyr`). Three are true statements naming a removed verb (`` `fyr report` is gone ``).
  - The spec rule, under D9 and D10, finds 1 of 6 stale: `SPEC-fyr-record`, with 4 code commits since its line was committed. It takes 5.6 s.

Terms:

- The **docs set** is defined in Interfaces § The docs set.
- A **living record** is a `spec`, `guide` or `deploy` record with status `current`; every other kind is history (`skills/review/SKILL.md:59`).
- The **vocabulary** is the verbs, subverbs and flags of the running binary.
- The **kit** is the Antigravity run kit, `.agents/kit/` (`GUIDE-testing` § 4).
- A spec's **commit** is the commit that first carries its current `trail.jsonl` line (D9).

## Scope

In:

- S1. A verb, `fyr check`, read-only over the git checkout of the working directory, with three rules:
  - (a) **docs.** A file of the docs set or a living record names a `fyr` verb, subverb or flag the vocabulary lacks. A file of the docs set or a living record names a path of this checkout, or a `path:line`, that does not exist (D26, superseding D3's path half).
  - (b) **specs.** A current `spec` record names code that has been committed to since the spec's commit, or names no code.
  - (c) **requirements.** A Must or Should item of `REQUIREMENTS.md` has no `enforced by:` site, or one that does not resolve.
- S2. The consumers, each a skill, with the context unchanged (Open O1). Who asked: the feature skill's Step 1 capability rule; the operator decides (Open O7):
  - the `review` skill's docs brief runs `fyr check`. Preflight Step 4 already runs that brief verbatim (`skills/preflight/SKILL.md:72`), so preflight's text does not change (D17);
  - the `requirements` skill runs it after the approved text is written to `REQUIREMENTS.md`.
- S3. The docs a new verb owes:
  - `usage` and README § Daily commands;
  - a new `SPEC-fyr-check` spec record;
  - `SPEC-fyr-record`: `brain.ReadTrail`, a reader of the export that opens no store;
  - `GUIDE-fyr-matrix` rows and `GUIDE-testing` § 3h;
  - `GUIDE-skill-matrix` rows for the two changed skills.
- S4. This repository passes its own check. Every first-run finding is fixed (a doc, a record, a spec naming its package), or it shows that a rule is wrong, which a D-row then corrects.

Consumers, by who would use the capability:

1. `/review --docs`, and through it `/preflight` Step 4. Planned (Phase 3).
2. The `requirements` skill, which traces `enforced by:`. Planned (Phase 3).
3. The main agent "when work starts drifting" (R0). The context names only `fyr record get` (`context/AGENTS.md:13`). Not planned: Open O1.
4. `fyr dream`. Not planned (Follow-ups).
5. The `documentation` agent has no shell, so it gets the output the main thread passes. No task.
6. The operator, by hand: the README row.

Out:

- A removed top-level file or directory. A candidate's first segment must be tracked now, so a doc naming a top-level entry that was deleted is not caught (D11; a Known limit in the spec).
- A project's own CLI verbs: only `fyr` verbs are known.
- Prose outside code spans and fences.
- Any write: no index, no brain store, no fix.
- `REQUIREMENTS.md` edits.
- A commit, hook or CI gate (R3).
- Telling a finding the range introduced from one already there. `check` reports the whole tree; the reviewer sorts the two (D17).

Follow-ups noted, not built:

- Give this repository's `REQUIREMENTS.md` an `enforced by:` line per item, so rule (c) checks it. That is a requirements edit: the operator's approval, an ADR, one commit.
- Add `fyr check` counts to the dream's numbers-only summary.
- `context/AGENTS.md:59` names `scripts/restatement-grep.sh`, a path relative to the skill. `scripts` is not a top-level entry here, so it is no candidate even under D26.

REQUIREMENTS touched, none conflicting:

- R0: the binary catches drift; the context does not grow.
- R3: no gate.
- R4: stdlib only; `check` opens no SQLite.
- R6: tests use scratch roots and `--home`.
- R7: it reads `.agents/trail.jsonl`.
- R10: it reads only the checkout and the binary. A shallow or partial clone skips rule (b) with a note on every place (D13).

## Surfaces touched

- `internal/check` (new): the docs set, a code-span and fence scanner, the three rules, `Run`. It imports `internal/trail` and `internal/brain` (`ReadTrail` only).
- `internal/brain/export.go`: `ReadTrail` wraps `openTrail` (`:69`) and `readRecords` (`:173`).
- `internal/trail`: `NoIndexMarkers`, the two marker names now in `internal/search/reconcile.go:163-164`, which search then reads from here (D20).
- `cmd/fyr/main.go`:
  - the `verbs` table (`:171`), `usage` (`:45-82`), `writesState` (`:345`, default false);
  - `runMetrics` (`:524-531`) and `memoryCmd` (`:906`), whose subverb lists become one variable each (D14).
- `cmd/fyr/record.go`: `recordFlags` (`:24`) is the record vocabulary as it stands.
- `README.md` § Daily commands (`:36-52`). The map does not change, because `check` adds no delivery path (AGENTS.md rules 3–5).
- `skills/review/SKILL.md` (docs brief, `:58-66`) and `skills/requirements/SKILL.md` (`:44`, Step 3's `enforced by` wording, and the step that writes the approved file).
- Records:
  - new: `SPEC-fyr-check`, ADR-064;
  - edits: `SPEC-fyr-record`, `GUIDE-fyr-matrix`, `GUIDE-testing`, `GUIDE-skill-matrix`;
  - Phase 3's first-run fixes in living records.

## Interfaces

### The verb

```
fyr check
```

- No flags of its own. `--home` and `--repo` are accepted, as on every verb, and have no effect.
- A positional word is a usage error, exit 2.
- The root is `trail.Roots(wd)`'s `top`: the linked worktree itself. `ErrNotCheckout` is a refusal (D13).
- It reads that tree, its `.agents/trail.jsonl` and `git`, and writes nothing: no `.agents/scratch/search.db`, no `brain.db`, no state-directory move.

Output (D18). On stdout, in rule order (a), (b), (c), sorted by place and line within each rule:

```
<where>:<line>  <rule>  <text>
note: <text>
check: N findings (docs D, specs S, requirements R); fyr <version>
```

- `<where>` is a repo-relative path or a record ID.
- `<line>` is 1-based in the file or record body. It is omitted when the rule has none (`spec-stale`, `spec-unlinked`).
- `<rule>` is one of `verb`, `subverb`, `flag`, `path`, `line`, `spec-stale`, `spec-unlinked`, `requirement`.
- `cmd/fyr` passes every line through `search.Printable`.

Exit status:

- 0: no findings; notes may be printed.
- 1 with the summary line: findings.
- 1 with no summary line: a refusal, `check: <reason>` on stderr. The refusals are a directory that is not a checkout, and a `trail.jsonl` that does not parse (its line named, as `record` does). Nothing is checked after a refusal.
- 2: a usage error.

### Go

```go
package check

// VerbSpec is one verb of the running binary. Flags are the verb's own and
// the two global ones. Subverbs maps each subverb to the flags it takes, the
// global ones included; nil for a verb without subverbs.
type VerbSpec struct {
	Flags    map[string]bool
	Subverbs map[string]map[string]bool
}

// Vocabulary maps each verb name, "help" included, to its spec.
type Vocabulary map[string]VerbSpec

type Finding struct {
	Where string // repo-relative path or record ID
	Line  int    // 1-based; 0 when the rule has none
	Rule  string // verb subverb flag path line spec-stale spec-unlinked requirement
	Text  string
}

type Report struct {
	Findings []Finding
	Notes    []string
}

// ErrRefused wraps a reason Run checked nothing for.
var ErrRefused = errors.New("check refused")

// Run checks the checkout at root against v. It writes nothing.
func Run(root string, v Vocabulary) (Report, error)
```

```go
package brain

// ReadTrail parses root's .agents/trail.jsonl through the export's path guard
// and line rules, without opening brain.db. ok is false when there is no file.
func ReadTrail(root string) (recs []Record, ok bool, err error)
```

```go
package trail

// NoIndexMarkers are the file names that take a directory out of the search
// index and out of fyr check's docs set (.sh-agent-noindex kept for old trees).
var NoIndexMarkers = []string{".fyr-noindex", ".sh-agent-noindex"}
```

`cmd/fyr` builds the Vocabulary (D14):

- Each verb's flags come from a fresh FlagSet with `--home`, `--repo` and `v.flags(c)`, read with `VisitAll`.
- `record`'s subverbs come from `recordFlags`, with their own flags.
- `metrics` (`ingest show report export`) and `memory` (`add show`) each get one package-level list. Each dispatcher's refusal text is built from that list, with the text unchanged. Their subverbs take the verb's flags.

### The docs set

- **Files**: every tracked `*.md` (`git ls-files`), minus:
  - a directory holding a `trail.NoIndexMarkers` file;
  - the vendored skills and catalogs `skills/VENDORED.md` names when it exists. This is the same exclusion `restatement-grep.sh:46` makes (D5).
- **Records**: the living records from `brain.ReadTrail`. With no `trail.jsonl`: `note: no .agents/trail.jsonl: records, specs not checked`.

### Scanning (D15)

- A fence opens with three or more backticks or tildes at up to three spaces of indent, whatever its info string, and closes with the same character run. A fence left unclosed runs to the end.
- Indented code blocks are not read.
- An inline span is a run of N backticks closed by the next run of exactly N on the same line. A span that does not close on its line is not a span.
- In a fence, a line ending in `\` joins the next. A finding's line is the line where the span or segment starts.

### Rule (a), docs

**Verbs, subverbs and flags.** These are read over every file of the docs set except `ROADMAP.md` and `TODO.md` (D6), and over every living record, inside spans and fences only. For each chunk:

1. Strip `<…>` placeholders.
2. Split at `|`, `&&`, `||`, `(`, `)` and line ends, and in a fence also at `;` (D28).
3. A segment counts when its program word is one of the following (D16). Before reading the program word, skip a `$` prompt and `VAR=value` words.
   - `fyr`;
   - a path ending `/bin/fyr`;
   - `./fyr`;
   - the three words `go run ./cmd/fyr`.
4. Skip `--home` and `--repo` with their value, whether written `--home X` or `--home=X`.
5. The next word W must match `^[a-z][a-z-]*$`. Otherwise the segment is not checked.
6. W not in the vocabulary gives a `verb` finding.
7. If W has subverbs, the next word that does not start with `-` and matches that pattern is S. An S that is not one of them gives a `subverb` finding.
8. Every word in the segment matching `^[\[("']*--([a-z][a-z0-9-]*)` is a flag; text after the name (`=…`, `]`, `,`, `.`, `)`) is ignored. A flag not taken by S (or by W, when W has no subverbs) gives a `flag` finding.

**Paths.** These are read over every file of the docs set except `ROADMAP.md` and `TODO.md`, and over every living record, deployed content (`skills/`, `agents/`, `context/`, `rules/`, `commands/`) included (D26). A deployed file naming another project's path writes it with D12's placeholder.

A candidate is an inline span holding one token with no space, which may end `:N` or `:N-M`. All of these must hold:

- it contains none of `< > * { } $ ~ …`, no `..` and no `://`, and is not absolute;
- the last segment is not a Go identifier: no `.` followed by an upper-case letter, as in `internal/trail.Command` (D11);
- after a leading `./` is stripped, it is a tracked top-level file, or its first segment is a tracked top-level directory;
- `git check-ignore` does not ignore it. A path below a symlinked directory is not asked, and a batch git still refuses is asked one path at a time (D29).

How a candidate is checked (D19):

- Existence is checked through `os.Root` at the checkout, which refuses a path that leaves the root through a symlinked component. A missing candidate gives a `path` finding.
- `:N` (and `:M`) is checked only on a regular file of at most 16 MiB with no NUL byte in its first 8 KiB. A number past the file's last line, or a `:N` on a directory, gives a `line` finding. On any other file, `:N` is not checked.

A path in another checkout is written with a placeholder, which makes it no candidate: `<clone>/internal/greet/greet.go`, `<project>/.agents/docs/` (D12; Open O6).

### Rule (b), specs

For each current `spec` record (D9, D10):

- **Its code**: the path candidates in its body that exist, files or directories, except `*.md` files, `.agents` and `.agents/trail.jsonl`. If none are left, the result is `spec-unlinked`.
- **Its commit**: the oldest commit `git log -G '"id":"<ID>".*"updated":"<updated>"' --format=%H -- .agents/trail.jsonl` lists. That is the commit whose diff added the spec's current line; a later version has a later `updated`. None, because the edit is not committed yet, means the spec is not stale.
- **Stale** when `git rev-list --count <commit>..HEAD -- <code> ':(exclude).agents/trail.jsonl' ':(glob,exclude)**/*.md'` is greater than 0. The finding is `spec-stale`, with the text `N commits to <code> since <short commit>`.
- **Ancestry, not clocks.** A commit that carries both the code and the spec's update is not counted. That is the Definition of Done's normal case.
- **Remedy.** A person who re-reads the spec and finds it true runs `fyr record edit <ID> --status current`. That stamps `updated` (`internal/brain/brain.go:428`); the next commit carries the new line, and the spec is clean.
- **Skipped with a note**: a shallow clone (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository`), a partial clone (`trail.PartialClone`), or `trail.Readable` false. Under any of these the history is not whole (D13).

### Rule (c), requirements

- No `REQUIREMENTS.md` at the root: `note: no REQUIREMENTS.md`.
- **Items** follow the template's shape (`skills/init-project/assets/REQUIREMENTS.md:11-22`): a line `- **<letter><digits>** — …` under `## Must` or `## Should`, and its `<!-- … enforced by: X -->` comment before the next item or heading.
  - A struck item (`— struck`) is skipped.
  - `## Could` is not read.
- **No field.** A file with no `enforced by:` anywhere gives `note: REQUIREMENTS.md has no enforced-by field: not checked` (D8, confirmed by D30).
- **Otherwise these give a `requirement` finding**:
  - an item with no comment;
  - an empty value;
  - a value holding `<`, which is the template's placeholder;
  - a value beginning `not yet enforced:` (a `requirement` finding, D31). Such a value is one part and is never split.
- **Resolving a value** (D22). The value is split at commas. A part resolves when its first token resolves, taken up to whitespace, ` § `, `::` or `#`. The token resolves as one of:
  - an existing path, by the path rule's existence and `:N` checks;
  - `Test\w+`, declared as `func TestX(` in a tracked `*_test.go`;
  - a record ID present in `trail.jsonl`, such as `ADR-063` or `GUIDE-testing`.

  A part whose token does not resolve gives a `requirement` finding naming it.

## Failure modes

| Situation | What the operator sees |
|---|---|
| Not a git checkout | stderr `check: <dir> is not a git checkout`, no summary, exit 1 |
| `trail.jsonl` does not parse | stderr `check: .agents/trail.jsonl:<n>: <reason>`, no summary, exit 1. A half-read trail would give a false clean run. |
| No `trail.jsonl`, no `REQUIREMENTS.md`, a shallow or partial clone, or unreadable history | a `note:` line per skipped part; exit 0 when nothing else is found |
| A doc names a verb of a newer binary than the one running | a `verb` finding; the summary names the running version |
| A spec flagged after a refactor that changed no behaviour | `spec-stale`, cleared by the remedy, never by changing the rule |
| A true statement names a removed verb or another checkout's path | a finding; the statement is reworded (`` the `report` verb is gone ``, D12, D16) |

## Trust boundaries and data handled

- **Record bodies** may come from another machine, through a pulled `trail.jsonl`. `ReadTrail` keeps the export's guard (`export.go:37-69`). Bodies are only matched against patterns, and output passes through `search.Printable`.
- **Path candidates** are resolved inside the checkout only, through `os.Root` (D19). The `:N` read is capped.
- **`git`** runs through `trail.Command` with paths after `--`. The `-G` pattern takes a record ID and an RFC 3339 stamp, regexp-quoted.
- **`security`** is due at Done, because this is input parsing.

## Verification

Tiers:

- Unit tests: `go test -race` over `internal/check`, `internal/brain`, `internal/trail` and `cmd/fyr`.
- The § 1 suite at every checkpoint.
- The `GUIDE-fyr-matrix` rows for `check` (§ 3c).
- One behavioural Antigravity run per changed skill (kit, `GUIDE-testing` § 4), which `AGENTS.md` § Release requires before a tag.

E2E criteria:

1. **Golden path.** At the last checkpoint, `fyr check` in this checkout exits 0. Its summary line begins `check: 0 findings`. `git status --porcelain` and the `--home` directory are unchanged.
2. **Must-fail.** Set up a scratch clone with a scratch `--home`. First record its baseline output. Then make these changes:
   - a README span naming `fyr frobnicate`, and one naming `` `cmd/fyr/main.go:99999` ``;
   - a new current `spec` record naming only the new file `internal/check/e2efixture.go`, committed with that file, and then a second commit to that file;
   - a `REQUIREMENTS.md` holding one template-shape Must item whose `enforced by:` is `TestNoSuchTest`.

   `fyr check` must then exit 1 and print the baseline's findings plus exactly one `verb` (README, its line), one `line` (README, its line), one `spec-stale` (the new record) and one `requirement` (`REQUIREMENTS.md`, its line). The requirements note is gone. The fixture lives at `internal/e2efixture/fixture.go`, not `internal/check/` (D32).
3. **Edge: not the harness.** In a scratch git repository with one commit, no `.agents/` and no `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `fyr check` exits 0 with the two notes. Afterwards the repository has no `.agents/` and its status is unchanged.

## Risks

Assumptions:

- A1: a metadata-only `fyr record edit` stamps `updated`. Checked 2026-10-25 (`internal/brain/brain.go:428`).
- A2: the kit's rows let Antigravity run `fyr check` from the skill text. They grant `command(*)` or `command(fyr)` (`GUIDE-testing` § 4). Checked by the Phase 3 rows.
- A3: the first run was about 45 findings before D26: 38 paths, 3 removed-verb statements, 1 or 2 specs, plus whatever the real scanner adds. D26 adds deployed content's paths (recon: 208 of 337 resolvable tokens there name other projects' paths, though only those anchored on this checkout's top-level entries are candidates). Re-measured read-only at Phase 1's checkpoint with the real rule (a), and again by Phase 3's first task. Phase 1 (2026-10-25, after D28 and D29): 67 findings, 64 `path` and 3 `verb` (the removed `report` verb in `DEPLOY-local` and twice in `SPEC-fyr-delivery`). The paths: `GUIDE-skill-matrix` 24, `SPEC-fyr-search` 7, `skills/VENDORED.md` 8 (upstream paths in its Source column), `DEPLOY-gcp` 1 (the real hit), and the rest deployed content naming a project's `.agents/rules/`, `.agents/agents/` or `.agents/docs/`. So A3's 60 is passed; Phase 3 takes that to the operator as its `Open:` row. Phase 2 (2026-10-25): 70, the same 67 plus 3 specs: `SPEC-fyr-dream` and `SPEC-fyr-metrics` stale (1 commit each), `SPEC-fyr-memory-loop` unlinked; requirements 0 with the no-field note (this `REQUIREMENTS.md` has no `enforced by:`). `SPEC-fyr-check` names the deployed directories (`skills/`, `agents/`, `context/`, `rules/`, `commands/`) in spans, so they are its code and it goes stale on every skill edit: Phase 3 rewords it or a D-row narrows a spec's code. Over 60 findings: those that do not show a rule wrong go to Follow-ups, and an `Open:` row goes to the operator.
- A4: `git log -G` over `trail.jsonl` stays fast. It takes 5.6 s for 6 specs on this box (prototype). Checked again at Phase 2's checkpoint; over 30 s becomes a D-row. Phase 2 (2026-10-25): the whole run, rules (a) to (c) over 7 specs, 8.3 s on this checkout.

Other risks:

- Rule (b) counts any commit to a spec's code, including a refactor; the remedy is a re-read. If it proves noise, a threshold is a later D-row.
- The path rule misses a removed top-level entry (D11) and prose mentions.
- D26 path-checks deployed content: its other-project paths must be reworded with D12's placeholder, which grows Phase 3 and the diff a reviewer reads.

## Decisions

D1 — 2026-10-25 — `fyr check` is read-only. It reads files, `git` and `.agents/trail.jsonl` through `brain.ReadTrail`, and opens no store. So it runs on an unmigrated project and on a project that is not the harness, and changes nothing there — by: implementer (recon risk 5: the store path writes `brain.db` and refuses unmigrated projects)

D2 — 2026-10-25 — Findings exit 1, as `fyr status` does on drift; notes never count. Nothing wires the status to a gate (R3) — by: implementer; Open O2 asks the operator

D3 — 2026-10-25 — The path rule reads only root `*.md` files and living records. The verb and flag rule reads the whole docs set, because a skill naming a `fyr` verb that does not exist is drift on every place — by: implementer (recon: 62% of resolvable path tokens in deployed content are other projects' paths); Open O4 asks the operator — path half superseded by D26

D4 — 2026-10-25 — Subverbs live in one `subverbs` field of the `verbs` table — superseded by D14

D5 — 2026-10-25 — The docs set excludes vendored skills and catalogs, per `skills/VENDORED.md` (as `restatement-grep.sh` does), and noindex directories. A vendored file is never edited, so a finding in one could not be fixed — by: implementer

D6 — 2026-10-25 — `ROADMAP.md` and `TODO.md` are outside rule (a), because they name what is not built yet (`fyr eval`) — by: implementer

D7 — 2026-10-25 — A spec's code is the existing paths its body names — superseded by D10 (cold read finding 2: its claim that two specs name no path was wrong)

D8 — 2026-10-25 — Rule (c) reads only the template's `enforced by:` field. A file without it gives a note — by: implementer; Open O3 asks the operator

D9 — 2026-10-25 — Rule (b) compares by ancestry, not clocks. The spec's commit is the oldest commit whose `trail.jsonl` diff adds its current id+`updated` line (`git log -G`). The spec is stale when `rev-list --count <commit>..HEAD` over its code, with `trail.jsonl` and `*.md` excluded, is greater than 0. An uncommitted spec edit is not stale. This replaces the `updated`-against-commit-time comparison, which marked all 6 specs stale forever because `updated` is stamped before the commit that carries it — by: cold read round 1 (finding 1; prototype: 1 of 6 stale, 5.6 s)

D10 — 2026-10-25 — A spec's code is the existing candidates in its body, minus `*.md` files, `.agents`, `.agents/trail.jsonl` and ignored paths. None left gives `spec-unlinked` — supersedes D7 — by: cold read round 1 (findings 1, 2)

D11 — 2026-10-25 — Path candidates stay anchored on a tracked top-level entry, so a removed top-level entry is not caught (a Known limit in the spec). A last segment holding `.` plus an upper-case letter is a Go identifier, not a path. "Not in `skills/`" means files under `skills/` are not scanned; a token naming `skills/…` elsewhere is a candidate — by: cold read round 1 (finding 4; Phase 1's verify clause now uses a nested path)

D12 — 2026-10-25 — A doc naming a path in another checkout writes it with a placeholder (`<clone>/…`, `<project>/…`), which is no candidate. There is no ignore marker. `SPEC-fyr-check` states the convention — by: cold read round 1 (finding 8); Open O6 asks the operator

D13 — 2026-10-25 — The root is `trail.Roots`' `top`, and `ErrNotCheckout` is the only checkout refusal. Rule (b) is skipped with a note on a shallow clone (`--is-shallow-repository`), a partial clone, or `trail.Readable` false, on any git version. The partial-clone test sets the promisor config in a scratch repo — by: cold read round 1 (findings 5, 9, 10)

D14 — 2026-10-25 — The vocabulary takes `record`'s subverbs and their flags from `recordFlags`, the existing per-subverb table, so `record get --title` is a finding. `metrics` and `memory` get one package-level subverb list each, which builds their unchanged refusal texts; a test pins every list against its dispatcher. No new field on `verb` — supersedes D4 — by: cold read round 1 (finding 6)

D15 — 2026-10-25 — The scanner reads backtick and tilde fences of any info string and single- or multi-backtick spans closed on their line. It does not read indented blocks. In a fence, `\` continuation joins the next line, and a finding is placed at the line where its span or segment starts — by: cold read round 1 (finding 7)

D16 — 2026-10-25 — The program word is `fyr`, a path ending `/bin/fyr`, `./fyr`, or `go run ./cmd/fyr`, so `cmd/fyr` in a layout fence and `~/.config/fyr` do not count. A true statement naming a removed verb is reworded so the verb stands alone (`` the `report` verb ``) — by: implementer (verb prototype: 8 findings, of which 5 were program-word noise)

D17 — 2026-10-25 — The single home of the consumer text is the `review` skill's docs brief, whose reviewer runs `fyr check`. Findings on lines the range changed are docs findings; the rest are listed as pre-existing. Preflight Step 4 runs that brief verbatim, so preflight's text does not change — by: cold read round 1 (finding 11)

D18 — 2026-10-25 — Findings, notes and the summary go to stdout. A refusal goes to stderr with no summary line. Both exit 1, so the summary line tells "checked" from "refused". `cmd/fyr` applies `search.Printable`, so `internal/check` does not import `internal/search` — by: cold read round 1 (finding 13)

D19 — 2026-10-25 — Existence goes through `os.Root` at the checkout, which does not follow a symlinked component out. `:N` is read only on a regular file of at most 16 MiB with no NUL in its first 8 KiB; otherwise `:N` is unchecked — by: cold read round 1 (finding 14)

D20 — 2026-10-25 — Both noindex marker names move to `trail.NoIndexMarkers`, which search and check read — by: cold read round 1 (finding 15)

D21 — 2026-10-25 — E2E 2 is measured against the scratch clone's baseline output, and its spec fixture is a new record naming a file only it names. `spec-stale` has no line — by: cold read round 1 (finding 12)

D22 — 2026-10-25 — An `enforced by:` value splits at commas, and each part resolves by its first token (up to whitespace, ` § `, `::` or `#`) as a path, a declared Go test or a record ID (an ADR or a guide). A `not yet enforced:` value is one part — by: cold read round 1 (finding 3); its verdict is Open O5

D23 — 2026-10-25 — S2 drops the preflight edit (D17), and the `requirements` skill runs the check after the approved file is written: the skill drafts in scratch (`skills/requirements/SKILL.md:42`), so a check right after drafting would read the old file — by: cold read round 1 (findings 3, 16)

D24 — 2026-10-25 — The plan is approved as written, D1–D23, and Phase 1 starts. O1, O3, O5 and O7 stay open until the phase they shape — by: operator (this session, in their own turn)

D25 — 2026-10-25 — Findings exit 1, a refusal exits 1 with no summary line, notes never count (D2 confirmed); answers O2 — by: operator

D26 — 2026-10-25 — The path rule reads the whole docs set, deployed content (`skills/`, `agents/`, `context/`, `rules/`, `commands/`) included, minus `ROADMAP.md`, `TODO.md`, vendored and noindex directories; supersedes D3's path half (the verb rule already read everything). Another project's path in a deployed file is written with D12's placeholder, so Phase 3 rewords those too; A3 is re-measured — answers O4 — by: operator (against the default)

D27 — 2026-10-25 — Another checkout's path is reworded with D12's placeholder; the rule is not narrowed to file-shaped tokens (D12 confirmed) — answers O6 — by: operator

D28 — 2026-10-25 — `;` splits a chunk into segments in a fence only. In a span it is the punctuation of a quoted message: the first real run gave `fyr never` and `fyr reads` from `…; fyr never removes them` in `GUIDE-fyr-matrix` and `DEPLOY-remote`, quoting the binary's own output, which cannot be reworded without making the doc wrong. A second command after `;` in a span is not checked (a Known limit) — by: implementer (Phase 1 first run: 3 of 6 verb findings)

D29 — 2026-10-25 — Implementation details the plan left open, settled in Phase 1: (1) `git check-ignore` dies on a path beyond a symbolic link (`.agents/skills` here), which left every scratch path unignored (10 false findings), so such a path is not asked and a failed batch is asked one path at a time; (2) the trail refusal is the brain's own text, `check: trail.jsonl line <n>: <reason>`, the text `fyr record` refuses with, not the `.agents/trail.jsonl:<n>` form Failure modes sketched; (3) `memory`'s refusal text stays a literal, since it carries each subverb's flags, and only its acceptance reads `memorySubverbs`; `metrics`' two refusal texts are built from its list; (4) every verb and subverb also takes `--help`, which the flag package answers; (5) `check` is registered in `init`, since `runCheck` reads `verbs` and the literal would refer to itself; (6) until Phase 2 every run prints `note: rules (b) specs and (c) requirements are not built yet (plan Phase 2)`, so a count of 0 there is not read as checked — by: implementer

D30 — 2026-10-25 — Rule (c) reads only the `enforced by:` field, and a file without it gives the note (D8 confirmed); no proxy and no flag-every-item — answers O3 — by: operator

D31 — 2026-10-25 — A `not yet enforced:` value is a `requirement` finding (exit 1 under D25), because it is a requirement with no enforcement site, which roadmap item 3 asks to find — answers O5 — by: operator

D32 — 2026-10-25 — E2E 2's spec fixture is `internal/e2efixture/fixture.go`, a directory no spec names. At `internal/check/e2efixture.go`, as first written, its two commits also made `SPEC-fyr-check` stale, correctly, since `internal/check` is that spec's code, and the criterion's "exactly one `spec-stale`" failed on the fixture, not the rule (first run, 2026-10-25: 5 specs against the baseline's 3) — by: implementer (Phase 2 checkpoint)

D33 — 2026-10-25 — Rule (b) details settled in Phase 2: (1) `rev-list` excludes only `**/*.md`; the `.agents/trail.jsonl` exclude is dropped, because the spec's code already drops `.agents` and the trail, so it could never apply (its mutation survived every test); (2) "a commit to `trail.jsonl` alone" is read as no finding and no note: the note is for an incomplete history; (3) code paths go to git as `:(literal)` pathspecs, and the `-G` pattern is a basic regular expression with the ID and stamp escaped (superseded at Done, 2026-10-25: `-G` compiles an extended one, and both are quoted with `regexp.QuoteMeta`; code and security review), `"id"` before `"updated"` as the export writes them (a Known limit); (4) the shallow or partial-clone note prints whether or not the trail holds a spec; (5) the text says `1 commit` in the singular — by: implementer

D34 — 2026-10-25 — Rule (c) details settled in Phase 2: an item runs to the next item or any heading, so a `###` sub-heading ends it; the `enforced by:` value runs to the end of its HTML comment; backticks around a token are dropped; a record ID of any kind or status resolves; a `Test…` token resolves only as `func TestX(` opening a line of a tracked `*_test.go`; a finding sits on the item's line and starts with the item's ID; a `REQUIREMENTS.md` that is a symlink, not a regular file or over 16 MiB gives its own note, never the no-file one — by: implementer

D35 — 2026-10-25 — The context is unchanged: `fyr check` is not named in `context/AGENTS.md`, and the skills are its only callers (the default) — answers O1 — by: operator

D36 — 2026-10-25 — Both consumers stay: the `review` skill's docs brief and the `requirements` skill run `fyr check` (S2, the default) — answers O7 — by: operator

D37 — 2026-10-25 — A3's `Open:` row: Phase 3 fixes all 70 first-run findings, none goes to Follow-ups; another project's path in deployed content is reworded with the `<project>/…` (or `<clone>/…`) placeholder (D26, D27), and `skills/VENDORED.md`'s upstream paths get a form `TestVendoredRowsCarryAPin` still parses — by: operator

D38 — 2026-10-25 — `SPEC-fyr-check` is reworded so its spans no longer name the deployed directories (`skills/`, `agents/`, `context/`, `rules/`, `commands/`) as paths, which made them its code and the spec stale on every skill edit; rule (b) is not narrowed — by: operator

Open O1: R0 says the binary catches drift "never in the context". Does that keep `fyr check` out of the context, leaving the skills as its only callers? Or may the context's drift sentence (`context/AGENTS.md:13`) name it? That would take about 40 of the 195 bytes free. — default: the context is unchanged — answered by D35: unchanged.

Open O2 — answered by D25: exit 1.

Open O3 — answered by D30: the note.

Open O4 — answered by D26: yes, path-check everything.

Open O5 — answered by D31: a `requirement` finding.

Open O6 — answered by D27: reword.

Open O7: S2's consumers (the review docs brief and the `requirements` skill) come from the feature skill's capability rule; your request named only the check. Each changed skill needs an Antigravity run before the next tag (`AGENTS.md` § Release). Keep both, keep one, or none for now? — default: keep both — answered by D36: keep both.

Rejected: going through the brain store (`openForSearch`). It writes `brain.db` and refuses unmigrated projects (D1).
Rejected: a `Code:` line or a new field per spec. It changes the format of every spec for a link the body can carry (D10).
Rejected: comparing `updated` with commit times. It never converges (D9).
Rejected: an ignore marker for intentional paths. It is a second convention beside the placeholder (D12).
Rejected: checking every backticked token everywhere, at about 60% noise (D3) — reversed for path tokens by the operator (D26); verb and flag tokens were already read everywhere.
Rejected: a `--json` flag. No consumer parses it.
Rejected: auto-fixing. `check` reports and a person decides (R3).
Rejected: a `preflight` edit. Step 4 reuses the review brief (D17).

title: Recon — fyr check (2026-10-25)
body:
# Recon — fyr check (docs freshness and drift)

Status: COMPLETE. Scope: Q1-Q8 of the dispatch; ~19 tool calls. Read-only; only this file written (plus helper scripts/output under .agents/scratch/recon/).

## Summary
The verb table is introspectable (one `verbs` map, one FlagSet built per call), but usage text is a hand-written const, so "docs name a verb/flag that does not exist" is mechanically checkable for verbs and, with effort, flags. Three existing checks cover slivers (TestHarnessMap: verbs in the README map; TestSkillLinksResolve: references/assets paths in skills; restatement-grep.sh: manual keyword grep) but none checks arbitrary path mentions, spec age, or requirement enforcement. A naive backticked-path check over the harness's own docs is ~60% false positives (they describe consumer-project paths), so it needs a repo-root-anchored, allow-listed scope. Specs name almost no code paths (0-3 each), so "older than the code" has no link to measure without a new convention. The repo's REQUIREMENTS.md has no "enforced by" field; code cites only R3-R10 in comments.

## Q1 Verb and flag surface
- `var verbs = map[string]verb` at cmd/fyr/main.go:171; `verb{flags func(*ctx), positional, source, run}`. Verb list = its keys (plus `help`).
- run() main.go:237: one fresh `flag.NewFlagSet(cmd)` per invocation, common `--repo` `--home` added (:258-260), then `v.flags(c)` (:262). No static per-verb flag table; to enumerate flags, build a ctx+FlagSet, call `v.flags(c)`, `fs.VisitAll`. Subcommands (record add/get, metrics show...) are NOT in the table: dispatched inside runRecord/runMetrics/runMemory (main.go:532-593 area; cmd/fyr/record.go:19-29 has a per-subcommand allowed-flag map `"import": {"dry-run": true, ...}`).
- Flag-to-subcommand mapping exists only in the flag help strings ("metrics show: ...") and in record.go's map.
- usage is const at main.go:45-82, hand-written; verb lines match `"\n  "+verb+" "`.
- TestHarnessMap, cmd/fyr/main_test.go:868-896: reads ../../README.md, cuts `\n## How it works\n` to next `\n## `, takes the ```mermaid block, `regexp fyr ([a-z]+)`, asserts each verb is in usage via `strings.Contains(usage, "\n  "+m[1]+" ")`. Reusable pattern, but it is a test inside package main, not callable from a verb; a `check` verb in cmd/fyr can reuse `verbs` and `usage` directly.
- Related: cmd/fyr/search_test.go:88 TestUsageMatchesDocComment (usage vs a doc comment); usage_test.go pins exit-2 messages.

## Q2 Existing drift checks
- TestHarnessMap: verbs named in README map only (not flags, not other docs).
- `fyr status` (internal/harness/apply.go:209 `Report.Drift()`): installed files vs repo; not docs vs code.
- skills/review/scripts/restatement-grep.sh (NOT scripts/restatement-grep.sh): `git ls-files` minus records and vendored, greps given words; exit 0 hits/1 none/2 usage. Run by the `review` skill (--docs lens, skills/review/SKILL.md:62) and `review-standards` (SKILL.md:79). Tested by internal/harness/restatement_script_test.go. It needs the words handed in; it discovers nothing.
- `review --docs` / `--project` (skills/review/SKILL.md:62-66): by hand, model-judged accurate/outdated/redundant; ends with `git grep` re-checks.
- skills/preflight/SKILL.md:60 "Step 3: Trail freshness": by-inspection list: newest change describes the diff; no future dates (`fyr record list`); no TEST- removed; CHANGE/ADR never rewritten (git show base:.agents/trail.jsonl); ROADMAP/TODO touched since base (report-only). This is a candidate for `fyr check` (trail checks mechanical).
- skills/harness-audit/references/areas.md:17: asks whether a skill restates a context rule and whether the copy drifted (judgement).
- Tests pinning docs to code: internal/harness/skill_links_test.go:18 TestSkillLinksResolve (backticked `references|assets|examples|scripts/...` and md links in non-vendored skills exist); catalog tests pin CHECKSUMS/INDEX; size_test.go; TestVendoredRowsCarryAPin.
- Coverage vs the three checks: (1) verbs/paths: partially (README map verbs; skill reference paths); flags: none; (2) specs older than code: none; (3) requirement enforcement: none.

## Q3 Path mentions
- internal/search/parse.go:185-231: `pathToken` regexp, `refExtensions` list, `normalizeRef`, `parseRefs(text) []ref{line,target}` extracts `BUG|ADR-NNN` ids and path-shaped tokens (any slash path, or bare name with extension go/md/ts/.../tf) per line. No backtick requirement, no `:line` suffix handling (a `path:12` loses the colon part via TrimRight(":") only when trailing; `a.go:12` matches `a.go` since `:` is outside the class). No existence check there; `--refs` just matches targets against indexed text. A check can reuse parseRefs (unexported; needs export or copy).
- Sample (scripts in .agents/scratch/recon/paths.sh, outputs res.tsv; regex: backticked tokens containing `/`; non-vendored README/AGENTS/context/rules/agents/skills md files; 580 unique (file,path) pairs): 129 exist, 243 placeholder-ish (contain `~`, `<>`, `*`, leading `/`, or `.agents/scratch`), 208 do not exist as written. So among 337 resolvable-looking tokens, ~62% missing, almost all intentional: they are paths in the CONSUMER project (`web/`, `ui/`, `deploy/gcp.md`, `.agents/rules/`, `internal/greet`), Go import paths (`crypto/tls`, `log/slog`, `cloud.google.com/go/cloudsqlconn`), or non-file strings (`linux/amd64`, `distroless/static`).
- Five examples: `crypto/tls` (agents/security/agent.md), `linux/amd64` (skills/cloud-run-deploy/SKILL.md), `web/` (context/dev-setup.md), `internal/greet` (skills/golang/references/testing.md), `src/routeTree.gen.ts` (skills/typescript/references/tsconfig.md).
- One real hit seen: context/AGENTS.md mentions `scripts/restatement-grep.sh`, which does not exist at that path (real path skills/review/scripts/restatement-grep.sh); may be intentional (consumer-relative, or the dispatch and global context use it as shorthand) but is exactly what a check should surface. Also references/go-review.md and references/typescript-review.md named by agents/reviewer/agent.md (resolve inside skills/review-standards/, not the agent).
- Implication: scope must be narrowed: only paths whose first segment is a top-level tracked dir of THIS repo (cmd, internal, skills, agents, context, rules, commands) AND only in harness-own docs, or in a project's own README/specs/ROADMAP rather than in skills that describe other projects.

## Q4 Specs vs code
- Spec records (`fyr record list --kind spec`): SPEC-fyr-record, -search, -metrics, -dream, -memory-loop, -delivery; status `current`. Record JSON in .agents/trail.jsonl has fields `date`, `id`, `kind`, `status`, `title`, `updated` (RFC3339), `body`. `date` is the record's date (SPEC-fyr-metrics: date 2026-10-24, updated 2026-10-25T19:08:58Z; the body title says 2026-10-08) so title date, `date`, `updated` all differ; `updated` is the edit time.
- Spec-to-code links: counting backticked `*.go` paths with a slash per spec: metrics 2, record 1, dream 3, delivery 1, search 0, memory-loop 0; all exist today. Metrics spec ends "Decisions: ADR-055. Plan: PLAN-..."; the link is by prose/ID, not by path list. No frontmatter or field naming the code. So "older than the code it describes" has no mapping; options: (a) a convention (a "Code:" line / extra metadata) -> new design; (b) infer by verb name: spec `fyr metrics` <-> internal/metrics/ (package-per-verb is stable here: internal/{search,memory,dream,metrics,brain,redact,trail}); (c) infer from backticked paths in body.
- Measurement with internal/trail: `trail.Dates(root, docs)` (trail.go:37) gives newest commit time per tracked file under a docs path (also modified set; falls back to mtime on partial clone/no git); `trail.Log(root, args...)` (trail.go:149) runs git safely: `git log -1 --format=%ct -- <paths>` for code. Spec's age = record `updated` (not a file; trail.jsonl is one file so Dates would give only the whole file's time, useless per spec). Caveat: any edit to a spec record (even a typo) refreshes `updated`; and trail.jsonl exports touch lines for all projects' records.

## Q5 Requirements
- This repo's REQUIREMENTS.md: 40 lines, headings `## R0 ... ## R10` (R0 Purpose; R10 at :52), each one prose paragraph ending "(ADR-NNN, ...)", no "enforced by", no tiers. "enforced by" appears in REQUIREMENTS.md once only.
- init-project template (skills/init-project/assets/REQUIREMENTS.md): tiers Must (R1..), Should (S1..), Could (C1..), Non-goals, Known limits; each Must/Should item is `- **R1** — sentence.` followed by an HTML comment `<!-- provenance: <who>, <date>; enforced by: <test | rule | guide path> -->`; Could has no such comment. Struck items stay as "R3 — struck <date>: <why>". skills/requirements/SKILL.md mentions "enforced by" twice (requires listing where enforced and tracing).
- Mechanical meaning of "enforcement site": template shape: parse the `enforced by:` value; check it names an existing path (test, rule, guide) or a test name/function that exists; flag missing/empty/placeholder values. This repo's shape: no field; the only mechanical proxies are (i) the R-id cited in code/tests, (ii) ADR ids cited. A requirement with neither is "without an enforcement site" by proxy, which is weak: prose requirements are enforced by tests that never name them.
- R-id citations in *.go (word-boundary, hits/files): R0 0/0; R1 4/1; R2 1/1; R3 12/8; R4 10/10; R5 1/1; R6 8/6; R7 3/3; R8 7/6; R9 6/4; R10 3/2. R0 has none (it is purpose, not testable). Citations are in comments, not asserted by any test; R-ids also collide with other things (`R4` etc. in unrelated text possible; not verified).
- Parsing REQUIREMENTS.md of this shape is easy (`^## R(\d+) — `); of the template shape needs the bullet+comment pairing.

## Q6 Running on any project
- brain.go:82-92 `unmigrated(top)`: a project with no .agents/trail.jsonl but `.agents/docs/` or `docs/` is refused ("trail is still files ... migrate with fyr record import"). Reads load a changed trail.jsonl first, so even `record get` may write the store (cmd/fyr/main.go writesState: `record` always true => state-dir migration runs). A `check` verb would need to decide: read only files + `trail.jsonl` directly (no store, no writes; add `check` to writesState's false side) or go through brain (inherits refusal and store writes).
- Project root: internal/trail Toplevel/Roots (trail.go:201,235) resolve git toplevel/main worktree.
- `fyr search` in a fresh git repo (.agents/scratch/recon/nonrepo, one commit): refused with "search: .agents/scratch/search.db is not gitignored; add \".agents/scratch/*\" to .gitignore (/init-project does)". So search requires a scaffolded-ish repo; `check` should not write a cache into an unprepared project (stay read-only, or no index).
- Arbitrary project vs this one: no `verbs`/`usage` to compare against (those are fyr's own, available only for this repo's docs or fyr's own checkout; a project's docs naming `fyr foo` can be checked against the running binary's verbs; a project's own CLI is unknowable). Path check works generically via `git ls-files`. Specs: a project may have `spec` records in trail.jsonl; REQUIREMENTS.md template shape. restatement-grep.sh already contains the BUG-138 lesson: harness-only assumptions (skills/VENDORED.md) must not take the script down elsewhere.

## Q7 Consumers and budgets
By-hand freshness/drift/restatement mentions today:
- context/AGENTS.md:13 ("`fyr record get` on the plan ... when work drifts"), :56 (REQUIREMENTS immutable / must not drift), :59 (grep every restatement; `review` runs restatement-grep.sh).
- skills/review/SKILL.md:62-66 (--docs lens, --project), skills/review-standards/SKILL.md:79, agents/reviewer/agent.md:34, agents/documentation/agent.md:58 (deploy guides live; GUIDE-onboarding stale), skills/preflight/SKILL.md:60-70 (Trail freshness, --docs lens), skills/harness-audit/references/areas.md:17, skills/requirements/SKILL.md (enforced-by tracing), skills/retro/SKILL.md:68 (rule gap or restatement), skills/feature/SKILL.md, skills/init-project/assets/records/DEPLOY-gcp.md.
- Budgets: TestRenderedContextUnderTarget (size_test.go:63) pins the render before `## Installed` under 15,000; measured today 14,805 bytes (via `fyr render`, cut at `## Installed`), so ~195 bytes headroom; full render 15,714 vs 22,000 cap (TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock adds rules/*.md, 2,767 more). context/AGENTS.md alone is 12,553, dev-setup.md 2,131. R0 itself says check lives in the binary/specs "never in the context", so consumers must be skills (preflight Step 3, review --docs, harness-audit, requirements) pointing at `fyr check`, not new context text. TestSkillListingBudget: budget 19,500 bytes (size_test.go:97-98); I did not measure current usage. A new verb changes no skill description, but editing a description could trip it.

## Q8 Docs a new verb owes
- cmd/fyr/main.go: `verbs` entry (:171), `usage` const line(s) (:45-82), `writesState` switch (:342-362) if it reads only (default false is fine), TestHarnessMap/usage_test.go as needed (usage format rule `"\n  "+verb+" "`); TestUsageMatchesDocComment (search_test.go:88) pattern for doc comment parity.
- README.md "Daily commands" table (:36-52), and map only if a path/line changes (AGENTS.md rules 3-5: a check adds no delivery path; the map need not change).
- New `SPEC-fyr-check` spec record (`fyr record add spec`); the other specs are the home for verb behaviour (README:54). Guide records: GUIDE-fyr-matrix ("every verb on every kind of place", 2026-10-25) needs rows; GUIDE-testing (§1 ... §3x per package) gets a section; GUIDE-skill-matrix only if skills change.
- Consumers' skills (preflight Step 3, review, harness-audit) if they adopt it; ADR if scope/consumers decision; CHANGE record; ROADMAP Next line (ROADMAP.md:13) moves to Now.

## Conventions
Stdlib-only Go (R4); usage errors exit 2 with reason on the writer, refusals exit 1; exit codes documented in usage; verb run funcs `runX(c *ctx)`; packages internal/<verb>; tests in-package; dated sampled evidence goes to records not files; never write outside .agents/scratch or ~/.config/fyr in dev (R6).

## Risks
1. False positives dominate path checking (see Q3): without a harness-aware allow-list, `fyr check` is noise and gets ignored. Skills/context describe other projects' paths by design.
2. Context headroom ~195 bytes under the 15,000 pin; any new context pointer must be paid by deletion.
3. "Specs older than code" has no spec-to-code mapping and `updated` is edit time; likely noisy (code churns constantly; any commit to internal/<x> would flag the spec). A threshold or "N code commits since" rule is a design choice, not derivable.
4. R-ids are not cited by any test; "no enforcement site" on this repo's prose shape would flag R0/R1/R2/R5 immediately; the verb would be red on day one on its own repo.
5. Read path through brain mutates state (store load, state-dir migration) and refuses unmigrated projects; a docs-check that refuses on projects with stale docs is perverse (the unmigrated ones are the likeliest to have drift).
6. Overlap/duplication with TestSkillLinksResolve and TestHarnessMap: either reuse their logic or end up with three path checkers drifting apart.
7. Flag checking: flags are not extractable from prose reliably (`--home`, `--dry-run` are shared by many verbs; a doc line `fyr search --kind K` needs verb-attributed matching); subcommand flags are not in the table.
8. Rule 6 of AGENTS.md: delivery claims have one home; a check must not restate them.

## Open questions
- Does `fyr check` run only in a checkout of fyr (compare to this binary's verbs) or in any project (generic path/spec/requirement checks with the shape detected)? 
- Exit codes: report-only (like preflight's lag item) or exit 1 on findings (like `status` on drift)? Does it fail preflight?
- What counts as the code a spec describes: a convention to add (metadata line in specs), inferred from verb/package names, or paths in the body?
- Enforcement-site semantics for this repo's prose requirements: accept ADR citations? test comments? or reshape REQUIREMENTS.md (immutable without operator approval, R0 provenance)?
- Is `scripts/restatement-grep.sh` in context/AGENTS.md:59 (and the dispatch) intentionally a shorthand? Real path is skills/review/scripts/restatement-grep.sh.
- Current TestSkillListingBudget total not measured.

## Not examined
Body of the spec records beyond SPEC-fyr-metrics' head; GUIDE-fyr-matrix and GUIDE-testing contents; TestUsageMatchesDocComment internals; how search --refs matches (only parse.go read); Toplevel/Roots edge cases; internal/harness status drift internals beyond Report.Drift; non-markdown docs; AGENTS.md of the project listing other doc-claim sites; whether R-id word hits in *.go refer to requirements (not verified individually); the 208 "missing" list was not classified item by item (only sampled).

title: Plan — harness audit fix (audit of 2026-10-25, fyr at c4885ae) (2026-10-25)
body:
# Plan — harness audit fix (audit of 2026-10-25, fyr at c4885ae)   (2026-10-25)

Status: closed 2026-10-25. Phases 0, 0b, 1, 2, 2c, 3 and 4 done, and Phase 5 partly; the rest dropped by D22 in favour of the brain plan (`plans/2026-10-25-sqlite-trail.md`). The merged checkpoint is D21.

## Why
The operator, in their own turn on 2026-10-25: "When you are done finish with a e2e and full audit of the entire project". The audit found no high, 27 med, 53 low, 17 simplifications and 11 gaps. The evidence is `plans/2026-10-25-recon-harness-audit.md`, and the report is `reviews/2026-10-25-harness-audit.md`.

## Scope
- **In:** every audit ID whose row in § Dispositions reads `fix` — all 27 mediums, the lows (D11: the ones the audit recommended deferring included), the simplifications that shorten a file without moving a rule, and G16 and G17.
- **In, behind an approval:** SD12 (D2, D15): the `REQUIREMENTS.md` R3 edit is proposed in Phase 2b and coded only after the operator approves it in their own turn.
- **Out (`defer`):** C26 (Phase 6 of plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md`), G15 and G18–G25 (D9), WS39 and TS-S1 (D12).
- **Rejected:** AG20 (D12: whole-file rewrites accepted, no wider edit tool); IN22, SD18 and TR15 (the audit's "not a defect, note only").

## Surfaces touched
- `agents/{bugs,changelog,documentation}/agent.md` (AG16–AG19, AG22, AG24), and the docs-root paragraph in all eight if AG23's mechanism is a text one;
- `skills/{feature,bug,review,review-standards,preflight,handoff,retro,distill,explain-project,harness-audit,grilling,research,gcloud-setup,gke-basics,frontend,typescript,data-gcp,bash}`;
- `skills/find-skills` removed and a fork under another name added (TS30, D18); `skills/VENDORED.md`;
- a trailer-check script under one skill's `scripts/` (TR8, D13);
- `cmd/fyr/main.go` (IN15, IN16, IN17, IN18, IN21, IN29 messages; SD12 usage text after approval);
- `internal/harness/{inventory,apply,state,release,zip,source,repo}.go` and their tests; `internal/harness/catalog_test.go` (TR13, TR8's fixture test);
- `internal/dream/{collect,prompt,run}.go`, `internal/memory/memory.go`, `internal/trail/trail.go` and their tests (SD15–SD17, SD-S1, SD-S2); `internal/dream` for SD12 after approval;
- `internal/search/testdata/recall.tsv` (SD13);
- `REQUIREMENTS.md` R3 and `ROADMAP.md` in one commit (SD12, only the exact text the operator approves, with its ADR);
- `context/AGENTS.md` (D1's date line, C28, C36, C-S5, the dream mention after D15's approval; inside the 15,000 and 22,000 pins);
- root `AGENTS.md` (C29's goal struck, C32, C35, C-S1, rule 1's dream sentence after approval), `README.md`, `TODO.md` (C-S5);
- `.agents/docs/deploy/{local,remote}.md`, `.agents/docs/specs/fyr/{delivery,search,dream}.md`, `.agents/docs/testing/{fyr-matrix,guide}.md`, `testing/agy-rel/run.sh` (the new rows);
- `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` (status lines and the numbering note, by the header edit its line 3 allows), `.agents/docs/bugs/{INDEX.md,BUG-139-*,BUG-171-*,BUG-177-*}`.

## Interfaces
- **Lint.** Skill, command and rule frontmatter is checked against an allow list per kind (IN23, D7). The list holds at least every key a skill in the tree carries today. It grows only by a D-row when a vendored skill needs a new key, since a vendored file is never edited. Command and rule names pass `validName` (IN25).
- **`fyr diff`** writes nothing anywhere (IN24, D8, D19). It renders the plan in memory and compares bytes in Go; for a changed file it pipes the plan bytes to the system `diff -u - <dest>` on stdin. No diff algorithm is hand-written.
- **`fyr` exit codes.** An unknown command exits 2 and prints on the caller's writer, like every usage error (IN16). `list -h` exits 0 (IN15).
- **`fyr status`** names a leftover `sh-agent` on PATH (F4 of plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md:33`, TR9), and classes a kept `~/.claude` entry as kept, not stale (IN32).
- **Manifest.** `LoadState` refuses an entry outside the roots fyr manages (`.gemini/config`, `.local/bin/fyr`, the kept `.claude` entries) (IN26).
- **Dream opt-in (SD12, D2, D15).** `dream --all` sends only a project carrying an opt-in marker that git does not carry. The marker is something the operator creates on this machine: for example an entry fyr writes under `~/.config/fyr/`, or an untracked, ignored path. A marker committed in the repository does not count. The marker's form, and any verb or flag it adds, are settled in the `REQUIREMENTS.md` proposal and its ADR.
- **No new verb or flag** beyond what that ADR adds.

## Failure modes
- **An existing skill trips the new allow list** (IN23). The install refuses it and names the file and key. Phase 2 runs the lint over every skill in the tree before making it strict, and lists any key it would refuse.
- **A context edit pushes past a size pin.** The pin test fails; the edit is shortened, and the pin is never raised. With the goal struck (D10), 15,000 bytes is the only ceiling for the hand-written part.
- **The R3 proposal is not approved.** Phase 2b is struck by a D-row. No other phase depends on it (D19).
- **A box needs the network** (TS32's key page, TS35's build, TS36's registry) **and the box has none.** The box is reported BLOCKED with what is missing, never filled from memory.
- **A tag is cut while this plan is open** (plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md` Phase 6). It is cut only at a checkpoint of this plan, never mid-phase, so every changed skill and agent already has its Antigravity run (AGENTS.md § Release).

## Verification
- **Unit, every code phase:** `gofmt -l cmd internal`, `go vet ./...`, `go test -race -timeout 30m ./...`, and govulncheck by full path. They run on `/usr/bin/go` go1.24.4 (D16). govulncheck passes when it reports no advisory beyond the 15 recorded stdlib ones (audit § Measurements) and no finding a module reaches.
- **Install:** a scratch-home install, then `fyr status` from that home shows a `binary` line with no warning.
- **Behavioural, every phase that changes `context/`, `agents/` or `skills/`:** one sandbox start of the CLI, and one Antigravity row per changed agent, rule and workflow skill (kit `testing/agy-rel/run.sh`, preamble `testing/kit-preamble.sh`), reported as n of N.
- **Review, every phase:** `/review --docs` over the phase's range when it changes `context/`, `agents/` or `skills/`; a `reviewer` when the phase's diff reaches 50 lines or 5 files; `security` for Phase 2's lint and manifest changes and Phase 2b's dream change. Findings get `## Outcome`.
- **Verifier:** at each checkpoint, last, on a frozen tree, writing its log under `testing/`.
- **Restatements:** a grep for every changed rule (D1's date rule, SD12's "every indexed project", the trailer rule, the budget wording) over `context/ agents/ skills/ README.md AGENTS.md .agents/docs/specs .agents/docs/deploy`, run before the phase's first review round.
- **E2E (Phase 6):** a re-run of `testing/2026-10-25-verify-fyr-e2e-c4885ae.md` (E2E 1–4 local, and its four Antigravity rows), then `/harness-audit --reaudit`, with every ID `fixed`, `partly` (and what is left), `struck (D<n>)` or `deferred`, checked against § Dispositions.

## Decisions
