Each of the six dispatch sites states its own number (30 for an agent, 15 for a verifier re-run); the context gains no bytes, because its hand-written part is 14,623 bytes, past the 14,500 goal (C29) — by: the operator (2026-10-25). (The site count is corrected by D19.)
D7 — 2026-10-25 — Table row 5 (IN23), permission keys: "Allow list per kind (Recommended)". Skill, command and rule frontmatter outside a per-kind allow list is refused, as agents already are; the phase lints every skill in the tree first and lists any key it would refuse; `security` reviews it — by: the operator (2026-10-25).
D8 — 2026-10-25 — Table row 7 (IN24), `fyr diff`: "Diff in memory (Recommended)". `diff` renders and compares in memory and writes nothing, under the home or the system temp — by: the operator (2026-10-25).
D9 — 2026-10-25 — Table rows 1, 2, 4, 6, 10, 13, 14, 15, 17, 18 and 19: "Approve all as written (Recommended)". Fix 1, 2, 4, 6, 10, 13, 14 (the header edit DECISIONS.md line 3 allows), 15, 18 (G16 and G17 only) and 19; defer 17 (C26, to Phase 6 of plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md`) and G15, G18–G25. Row 15's re-measure waits for go1.27.2 on this box, which the operator restores — by: the operator (2026-10-25). (Row 15's toolchain is superseded by D16, and row 19's reach is settled by D11.)
D10 — 2026-10-25 — Cold read finding 1. It found no box for G16, G17, TR10 (D1) or C29, and no restatement grep for D1. G16 and G17 get a Phase 3 box with the `feature` row. TR10 gets a Phase 5 box with both pins, the `ctx-deploy` and canary rows, and a restatement grep (`skills/handoff/SKILL.md:158` is a known hit). C29, asked of the operator: "Strike the goal (Recommended)". The 14,500 goal leaves root AGENTS.md and `size_test.go`'s comment, and the 15,000 pin is the only ceiling — by: the operator (2026-10-25).
D11 — 2026-10-25 — Cold read finding 2. It found that the lows had no list. § Dispositions now gives one row per audit ID, and Phase 6 checks against it. The operator was asked whether row 19's "fix per area" also covers the lows the audit recommended deferring (C32, C33, WS37, AG21–AG24, IN17, IN18, IN21, IN29, IN32, IN-S2, IN-S3, SD16, SD-S1, TR12, TR13, TS35–TS37). The answer: "Fix them all". Each is in its phase. AG23's mechanism is asked first, in Phase 1. The network-bound ones report BLOCKED rather than guess — by: the operator (2026-10-25).
D12 — 2026-10-25 — Cold read finding 2, the lows the audit left to the operator: "Approve all as listed (Recommended)". WS30: fix (the planning session ends after Step 3). WS39: defer until after the crossing. IN16: fix (an unknown command exits 2 on the writer). IN26: fix (LoadState refuses entries outside the managed roots; `security` reviews it). AG20: strike (whole-file rewrites accepted). SD-S2: fix. TS-S1: defer. IN-S1: fix. TR14: BUG-139 marked accepted — by: the operator (2026-10-25).
D13 — 2026-10-25 — Cold read finding 3: D4's premise is false. `handoff` has no `git log` step, and `preflight:38` is a Step 1 range read, not a check before the push. Asked how the check runs: "Script the skill runs (Recommended)". One script under one skill's `scripts/` exits non-zero on a trailer line in `git log @{u}..HEAD --format=%B`. A new step before the push in `handoff` Step 6 and `preflight` Step 6.4 runs it. A Go test runs it against a fixture that must fail and one that must pass. It is a script a skill runs, the global rule's graduation mechanism, and still not a git hook (R3). BUG-177 graduates to it in Phase 5 — by: the operator (2026-10-25).
D14 — 2026-10-25 — Cold read finding 4, expects that observe nothing.
  - Every box's expect is now a fact a grep, a test or a row can see.
  - AG16's "one Antigravity row each" means an injection row per record agent (`inject-bugs`, `inject-changelog`, `inject-documentation`, the `agents-security` pattern). The existing dispatch rows cannot see the data clause.
  - IN19, asked of the operator: "Re-run under fyr (Recommended)", with rows for the migration, the zip path and D32.
  — by: the operator (2026-10-25) for IN19; the rest by the AI under the standing approval.
D15 — 2026-10-25 — Cold read finding 5. A marker git carries would let a cloned repository opt its reader in. Asked of the operator: "Local only (Recommended)". Phase 2b's R3 proposal names a marker the operator creates on the machine and git does not carry, with the must-refuse test "a committed marker does not count". Any verb or flag it adds is settled in its ADR. The restatements of "every indexed project" are listed in Surfaces and in Phase 2b's box — by: the operator (2026-10-25).
D16 — 2026-10-25 — Cold read finding 6: D9 and Risks contradicted each other on go1.27.2. The link points at the absent `~/sdk/go1.27.1`, not 1.27.2. Asked of the operator: "go1.24.4, recorded (Recommended)". The recall re-measure and every checkpoint run on `/usr/bin/go` go1.24.4, and the spec row names the toolchain. govulncheck passes with no advisory beyond the recorded 15 stdlib ones and no finding a module reaches. SD13's box re-pins q41's gold before measuring. This supersedes D9's "waits for go1.27.2" — by: the operator (2026-10-25).
D17 — 2026-10-25 — Cold read finding 7, the tiers the plan owes. Every phase now ends in a checkpoint, with `/review --docs` wherever `context/`, `agents/` or `skills/` change. Each also gets a reviewer at 50 lines or 5 files, the verifier last, one sandbox start and rows reported as n of N (§ Verification). Phase 6 re-runs the E2E before the re-audit — by: the AI, under the standing approval.
D18 — 2026-10-25 — Cold read finding 8, Phase 4's mechanisms.
  - TS30, asked of the operator: "Fork under a new name (Recommended)", because a `VENDORED.md` note never reaches the model.
  - TS32: the recipe points at Google's install page and prints the key's fingerprint with `gpg --show-keys` to compare against it. No fingerprint is embedded, since one would go stale.
  - TS33 and TS34 are direct edits of the `gke-basics` fork, which is not verbatim (`VENDORED.md:21`), not override notes.
  — by: the operator (2026-10-25) for TS30; the rest by the AI under the standing approval.
D19 — 2026-10-25 — Cold read findings 9–12, by the AI under the standing approval.
  - **Budgets (9).** The budget sites are listed in Phase 3's box from the audit: eleven sentences in six skills, re-grepped first. 30 applies to `preflight`'s release reviewer too. A site whose dispatch is seen cut off gets a higher number by a D-row.
  - **Phase 2 facts (10).** The old unit names and F4 are cited from plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md:21,33`. The allow list grows only by a D-row (§ Interfaces). `diff` compares in Go and pipes to the system `diff` on stdin, with no hand-written diff.
  - **Surfaces and tags (11).** The missing surfaces are listed. A tag waits for a checkpoint of this plan.
  - **Order (12).** Phase 2b runs whenever the operator approves, and no phase depends on it. Interfaces says "no new verb or flag beyond what that ADR adds".
D20 — 2026-10-25 — AG23's mechanism. The operator said "go all approved. finish this projectr now" instead of choosing, so the AI took the text option: one text home with a one-line pointer in each agent. It needs no code change and no ADR. The install-time include stays open as a design question for later — by: the AI, under the operator's go (2026-10-25).
D21 — 2026-10-25 — Execution. Following "finish this projectr now", Phases 1, 2, 2c, 3, 4 and 5 ran in parallel, one worktree each, with fixed names between them (`skills/handoff/scripts/check-trailers.sh`; `handoff` § Usage holds the `agy -p` detail). They were merged in order. The per-phase Checkpoint boxes became one checkpoint over the merged range: `/review --docs`, a reviewer, `security` for Phase 2, then the verifier. Each phase still logs its own Antigravity rows. This follows the global Definition of Done ("once per task over the whole change") and departs from D17's per-phase checkpoints — by: the AI, under the operator's go (2026-10-25).
D22 — 2026-10-25 — Phase 5 stopped after its first commit; its remaining boxes, and Phase 6 (E2E and re-audit), are struck. The operator moved the trail into the brain store (`plans/2026-10-25-sqlite-trail.md`, ADR-063), which removes the docs this phase was fixing — by: the operator ("Finish 1-4, stop 5-6").

title: Recon — harness audit of fyr at c4885ae (2026-10-25)
body:
# Recon — harness audit of fyr at c4885ae   (2026-10-25)

- **What and why.** This is the evidence base of the harness audit the operator asked for on 2026-10-25 ("finish with a e2e and full audit of the entire project"). It covers the harness at commit `c4885ae`, a clean tree, after plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md` Phases 0–5b, with the GitHub rename, `v3.0.0` and the crossing (Phase 6) still to come.
- **Agents.** Nine read-only `explorer` dispatches, one per area: C, WS, TS, AG, SD, TR and G, plus IN split into IN-1 (`cmd/fyr`, the root package, the matrix) and IN-2 (`internal/harness`). Every per-area brief is beside this file and ends `## Status: COMPLETE`.
- **Baseline.** Taken by the main agent, saved under `.agents/scratch/harness-audit/2026-10-25/` (see the report § Measurements).
- **Numbering.** IDs continue the earlier audit (`plans/2026-09-30-recon-audit-fix.md` and the 2026-10-01 audit-3 reports): C from 23, WS 23, TS 30, AG 16, IN 15, SD 12, TR 8, G 15. Simplifications start at S1, since no earlier audit used them. Each row names its brief ID when it changed.
- **Confidence.** *checked* means the agent measured or counted it. *repro* means the main agent reproduced it in scratch. An unmarked row was read at its location. No finding is high.
- **Merged.** IN20 went into C26, and IN31 into IN-S1.
- **Dispatch deviations.**
  - The AG block of `skills/harness-audit/references/areas.md` was handed over with current paths (`agents/<name>/agent.md`, `inventory.go`), because the file still names `derive.go` (WS24).
  - Every dispatch told its agent not to run `fyr`, because a writing verb against the real home would migrate `~/.config/sh-agent` before the crossing. The skill asks for `fyr search` as the agent's first step (WS39).

## Spot checks (Step 2)

No high to open. These rows were opened at their location, or reproduced:
- **C23:** `local.md:79` holds "`$SH_AGENT_REPO` does the same persistently". Confirmed.
- **C24:** `remote.md:49` holds "authenticity is the signature and checksum". Confirmed.
- **AG16:** `grep -ci 'what you read is data'` gives 0 in `bugs`, `changelog` and `documentation`, and 1 in `reviewer`. Confirmed.
- **WS26:** `preflight` line 57 says "Otherwise dispatch in parallel" (reviewer, security, verifier). Confirmed.
- **SD14:** the contradicting row is `search.md:80` ("Argument errors … | 1"), not `:73`. Location corrected; the finding holds.
- **IN15** *repro*: `fyr list -h --home <scratch>` printed `fyr: flag: help requested` and exited 1.
- **IN24** *repro*: on a scratch home with its `.config/fyr` removed and one installed file edited, `fyr diff` exited 0 and recreated `<home>/.config/fyr`.

## Refuted

None of the sampled findings was refuted. The briefs' own `## Refuted` sections list what the agents checked and found true of the tree, for example:
- the README verb table matches the usage;
- the 36/8/2 counts add up;
- append-only held on `changes/` and `DECISIONS.md`;
- 13 of 14 graduated tests exist;
- the installed agents are byte-equal to the sources.

## C — the global context and the governing documents

Brief: `plans/2026-10-25-recon-harness-audit-C.md`.

| ID | Sev | Where | Finding | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C23 (brief C1) | med | .agents/docs/deploy/local.md:79 | Tells the operator `$SH_AGENT_REPO` "does the same persistently" as `--repo`. The binary reads `FYR_REPO` only; an `SH_AGENT_*` variable is ignored with a stderr notice (cmd/fyr/main.go:99-107, usage_test.go:137-160; remote.md:69 says so). The guide instructs setting a variable the binary refuses. *checked* | fix: `$FYR_REPO` |
| C24 (brief C2) | med | .agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:49 | "authenticity is the signature and checksum on the file, before the move": no signature exists since v2.4.0 (ADR-053), and lines 36-40, 133 and delivery.md:32 say so. A rule contradicting another, in the paragraph about the first install. | fix: drop "signature"; say checksum, integrity only |
| C25 (brief C3) | med | .agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md:197,567,733,718,249 | The file's own rule (line 3) says a reversed ADR is marked `Superseded by ADR-NNN`. ADR-025 and ADR-060 (both superseded by ADR-062 per its Consequences) and ADR-052 (superseded by ADR-053, whose header says so) still read `— Accepted`. ADR-061 and ADR-031 ("four procedures", now three) are amended by ADR-062 or by R9, and their headers show nothing (ADR-031 not in ADR-062's visible Consequences; the cut line hid the rest: unverified). A reader scanning headers or `fyr search --refs` status takes the dead ones as live. Only 4 headers say Superseded (181, 231, 383, 586). *checked* by grep | fix: append a status line to the headers, the only permitted edit by line 3's own rule, or an operator choice to leave the history; operator's call |
| C26 (brief C4) | med | README.md:26,28,121,138; .agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:13,29,76; git remote | Every install, update and release command names `github.com/kesokaj/fyr`, `v3.0.0` and `fyr-<os>-<arch>` assets. `origin` is still `kesokaj/styrman-harness`; the newest tag is v2.7.0 and carries `sh-agent` assets only. Until Phase 6 a reader following the README Quick start gets a failing clone. Known and planned (Phase 6); recorded here so the audit does not lose it. *checked* (`git remote -v`, `git tag`) | defer to Phase 6; make the rename, the v3.0.0 tag and these docs one ordered step, and check README `go install ...@v3.0.0` after the tag exists |
| C27 (brief C5) | low | .agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:253 | Operator step: "the three smoke checks on each CLI". One CLI exists since ADR-062. | fix: "on Antigravity" |
| C28 (brief C6) | low | context/AGENTS.md:3 vs :33,57,60 | The header says "No hooks, gates, or scripts stand behind these rules". The context then names a script (`restatement-grep.sh`, exists), tests (size pins, lint tests) and "a mechanism — a test, a script a skill runs" as the graduation path. Not false for hooks and gates, but "scripts" contradicts line 57. | fix: "no hooks or gates" |
| C29 (brief C7) | low | AGENTS.md:26-27 | Says the hand-written context has a "goal 14,500". It is 14,623 (pins.txt), over the goal, under the 15,000 pin (377 B of headroom). A stated goal that is already missed. *checked* | strike the goal, or trim ~125 B; operator's choice |
| C30 (brief C8) | low | .agents/docs/specs/fyr/delivery.md:82 | "Built and shipped" lists `report` among the verbs `fyr` has; the next paragraph (84) says it is gone. The 2,400-word paragraph also duplicates `changes/` and release notes back to v2.0.0, and `TestDeliverySpecCurrent` (cmd/fyr/delivery_test.go) pins this section to the release entry. | fix: remove `report` from the verb list; see C-S2 |
| C31 (brief C9) | low | .agents/docs/specs/fyr/delivery.md:21-26 | The places table keeps a "CLIs" column in which every row says "Antigravity". Dead column. | strike the column |
| C32 (brief C10) | low | AGENTS.md:19; .agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:56; local.md:34; README.md:110 | Rule 6 says what a tag delivers to which kind of place is stated once. `remote.md:56` ("the place changes only when a release is cut") and `local.md:34` restate the per-place claim in prose that is not command documentation. R8/R9, AGENTS rule 1, README "In words", delivery.md:40-44 and remote.md:53-57 list the three ways in in six places in different wordings. rule 6 exempts command docs, so only the "changes only when" clauses count. | defer; trim the two clauses to the pointer |
| C33 (brief C11) | low | .agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md:718,733 | ADR-061 (dated 2026-10-23) sits before ADR-060 (2026-10-24), and ADR-059 is deliberately unused. Numbering is not date-ordered; harmless but a reader looking for the next number needs ADR-062's text. | defer |
| C34 (brief C12) | low | .agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:147-165 | The v2.4.0 "bridge" block (private-key signing, `allowed_signers` with the operator's email and public key, `sh-agent` names, `styrman-harness-v2.4.0.zip`) is dead procedure and the only place in a living deploy guide that tells the operator to run `ssh-keygen -Y sign`. It cannot be run again: it is "v2.4.0 only". It also carries a personal email in a living doc. | strike (history stays in ADR-053 and git) |
| C35 (brief C13) | low | AGENTS.md:88 | Key files row `plans/2026-09-03-rebuild.md` "The rebuild checklist": a seven-week-old closed plan listed as a key file. | strike the row |
| C36 (brief C14) | low | context/AGENTS.md:31 | `agy -p` print-mode paragraph names vendor tool names `WaitMsBeforeAsync`, `manage_subagents`, `manage_task`; it is the only line in the context naming them, and its detail is a skill's job (it already says "else: handoff § Usage"; grep finds `WaitMsBeforeAsync` nowhere else in skills/agents). Vendor behaviour: unverified: needs the Antigravity CLI tool reference. | simplify to the rule plus the pointer once the handoff skill carries the tool names; see C-S4 |
| C-S1 | | AGENTS.md "Rules for working here" (985 words, 40% of the file) | Rules are lists of lint refusals with their test names and BUG numbers (frontmatter bullet alone ~250 words). Each already lives in `internal/harness/inventory.go` and its tests, which fail the install. The AGENTS reader needs "the installer refuses these shapes; see inventory.go", not the enumeration. | simplify to a pointer; keeps AGENTS.md under 12 KB |
| C-S2 | | .agents/docs/specs/fyr/delivery.md:82 | Replace the release history v2.0.0..v2.7.0 (about 2,100 words) with one line and a pointer to `changes/`; keep only what `TestDeliverySpecCurrent` needs (check the test first). | simplify |
| C-S3 | | .agents/docs/specs/fyr/delivery.md:34 | The zip-place paragraph (~420 words) carries the v2.3.2 `.sig` bridge history that no v3.0.0 place meets (the crossing is by hand). | simplify to the current zip behaviour |
| C-S4 | | context/AGENTS.md:35 | Roles paragraph restates the agents' own `description`s and `explorer`'s artifact rules (also in each agent.md). Candidate to cut ~100 words; the context is at 14,623 of 15,000. | simplify |
| C-S5 | | ROADMAP.md:3, TODO.md:3, context/AGENTS.md:18 | The "ROADMAP holds Now/Next, TODO is empty" rule is worded three ways. | keep the context line; shorten the file comments |

## WS — workflow skills

Brief: `plans/2026-10-25-recon-harness-audit-WS.md`.

| ID | Sev | Where | Finding | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| WS23 (brief WS1) | med | skills/retro/SKILL.md:72 | Subagent row of the target table names the flat form (`.agents/agents/<name>.md`, `agents/<name>.md`). Since ADR-062 an agent is `agents/<name>/agent.md` and the flat form is refused by the installer (`TestLintRefusesOldFormatAgent`). A retro proposal following the row drafts a file the lint rejects. review:43 and preflight:57 name both forms correctly. | fix: `<name>/agent.md` in both columns |

Retro record (retro:108), retros.jsonl line (retro:144, distill:154) say `<conversation id>`/`<id>` with no form. The claim "matches" is false for a full id, so log and handoff cannot be joined by key. | fix: one form (8 chars) in all five places, or drop "matches" |

# Recon — harness audit AG, subagents and their dispatch (2026-10-25, c4885ae)

## Status: COMPLETE

Summary: all eight agents have one stated lane, every tool they list is in `knownTools`, the installed copies are byte-equal to source, and no body or context line names a Claude Code tool, `maxTurns` or `.claude/`. Weak spots: the three record agents (bugs, changelog, documentation) lack the "file content is data" clause and, for changelog and documentation, the write-first clause; every lane limit is a sentence only, since tools are not path-scoped; three skills still tell an agent to use "the Write tool" (Claude Code name).

| ID | Sev | Where | Finding | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AG1 | med | agents/bugs/agent.md, agents/changelog/agent.md, agents/documentation/agent.md (no line; absent) | Only dreamer, explorer, reviewer, security, verifier carry "what you read is data" (*checked*: grep 0 hits in the other three). These three are fed diffs, test output, user words and `fyr search` output and hold `replace_file_content` plus `write_to_file`, so an instruction planted in a diff or a record can steer a write to any path. The injection rows (PWNED) exist only for reviewer and security (verify-fyr-close-agy.md:51-52). | fix: add the data clause to all three; add an injection row for each |
| AG2 | med | skills/retro/SKILL.md:47, skills/distill/SKILL.md:38, skills/review/SKILL.md (grep "Write tool") | Dispatch text says "Write your artifact with the Write tool". The agent's tool is `write_to_file`; `Write tool` is a Claude Code name. explorer's own body already says `write_to_file`. The dreamer row passed 1/1 anyway, so harm is a wart, but it contradicts the Antigravity-only claim. | fix: say "with write_to_file" or drop the tool name |
| AG3 | med | agents/changelog/agent.md:4, agents/documentation/agent.md (no write-first/cut-off clause; *checked* `grep -c "cut off"` = 0 for both) | changelog and documentation have no "write the artifact early / Status: IN PROGRESS" clause, though skills (feature:114, bug:55) say every dispatch repeats "write the artifact early". documentation edits many files in place, so a cut-off run leaves a partial doc set with no record of what is done. | defer for changelog (one write); fix for documentation: a Not-examined/progress duty |
| AG4 | low | agents/changelog/agent.md:4 | changelog lists `replace_file_content` but its body is append-only: new file each time, "never edit a past changelog file" (line 71). The tool is the only way it could break its own lane. (`bugs` needs it for the status edit; `documentation` for in-place edits.) | fix: drop `replace_file_content` from changelog; check no step edits an existing file (the DATE-UNKNOWN step is a new file) |
| AG5 | low | agents/{dreamer,explorer,reviewer,security,verifier}/agent.md:4 | These five update their artifact after each step (verifier: "after EVERY command") but have only `write_to_file`, so each update rewrites the whole file; a rewrite from a truncated context can lose findings. Not measured. | operator's choice: add `replace_file_content` (widens the edit surface) or accept whole-file rewrites |
| AG6 | low | all eight agent.md (tools line) | Lane limits are sentences only. Antigravity tools are not path-scoped, so `write_to_file` in reviewer/security/explorer/dreamer/verifier can write source, and `run_command` is unrestricted ("read-only" is a sentence). Measured holds are 1 of 1 per row (explorer: "tree unchanged"; reviewer and security: no PWNED; dreamer: artifact + promoted files). No row tests source-edit refusal for bugs, changelog, documentation or verifier. | defer; record as a known limit in the testing guide; add negative rows when an agent next changes |
| AG7 | low | agents/documentation/agent.md:50, agents/bugs/agent.md:9 | Lane prohibitions for the three record agents (REQUIREMENTS.md immutable, bugs "never modify source") are one sentence each with no hold rate; changelog's append-only rule has one run (dispatch-changelog 1/1, x10). | defer |
| AG8 | low | agents/documentation/agent.md:17-18; agents/bugs/agent.md:12 | Docs-root resolution is repeated in documentation, bugs, reviewer, security, explorer, verifier, dreamer (the same three-way if/elif). Seven copies drift independently. | defer; one copy would need a code or skill change, so the operator's choice |
| AG9 | low | agents/documentation/agent.md:39 vs agents/verifier (testing/guide.md) | Shared seam: both documentation and verifier write `testing/guide.md` ("maintained by both"). It is the one file two agents share; stated in both bodies, so a stated overlap, not a conflict. | none; note only |
| AG-S1 | | skills/{bug:55,feature:112,review:105} | The fact "record agents have no shell, so the dispatch carries `fyr search --refs` output" is restated in three skills plus the bodies. | strike two, point at feature:112 |

## Measurements
- `wc -l agents/*/agent.md`: 91, 90, 63, 80, 76, 98, 83, 83 lines (664).
- `for a in agents/*/agent.md; do cmp -s $a .agents/scratch/harness-audit/2026-10-25/home/.gemini/config/agents/<n>/agent.md; done`: 8 of 8 same.
- Tools per agent (frontmatter): bugs, changelog, documentation = view_file, grep_search, find_by_name, replace_file_content, write_to_file (no shell; each body says "you have no shell"); dreamer, explorer, reviewer, security, verifier = view_file, grep_search, find_by_name, run_command, write_to_file. All within `knownTools` (inventory.go:241); keys within `agentKeys` (inventory.go:236); `model:` set only on changelog (flash) and security (pro).
- Body versus tools: every "run" duty sits on an agent with run_command; every "write" on one with write_to_file; "edit" duties (bugs status, documentation) have replace_file_content. No mismatch found.
- `git grep -n -i -E "maxTurns|TaskStop|subagent_type|\.claude/" -- context agents skills rules commands (not google-catalog)`: 0 hits in agents, context, rules; only gke-basics:22 (`~/.claude/skills/...`, another area) and prompt-audit references (a reference to CLAUDE.md files, legitimate).
- "cut off" clause count per agent: bugs 2, dreamer 1, explorer 1, reviewer 1, security 1, verifier 1, changelog 0, documentation 0.
- "data" clause count: bugs 0, changelog 0, documentation 0; others 1 (verifier 2).
- Dispatch sites found: bug:39 (explorer), distill:38 and retro:47 (dreamer, 30-call budget, write-early), explain-project:12, feature:23 and :90, harness-audit:41 and :88, preflight:44, :59, :60, review:105, handoff:167, testing-strategy:56. Those I read name a budget and "write the artifact early". Not all verified (see below).
- Latest Antigravity rows (testing/2026-10-25-verify-fyr-close-agy.md:48-55): dispatch-bugs 1/1, dispatch-changelog 1/1, dispatch-documentation 2/2, agents-security 1/1, agent-reviewer 1/1, agent-explorer 1/1, agent-verifier 1/1, agent-dreamer 1/1.

## Refuted
- "An agent body still names a Claude Code tool or maxTurns": no (grep above). The explorer's first command is `fyr search` and it says `grep_search`/`find_by_name`/`view_file`.
- "A tool on an agent is unknown to the lint": no, all in knownTools.
- "Two agents share a write lane": only testing/guide.md (AG9), by stated design. changelog (changes/), bugs (bugs/), documentation (specs, deploy, README), reviewer/security (reviews/), verifier (testing/), explorer (plans/ recon), dreamer (retros/) are separate.
- "Installed definitions differ from source": no, cmp same.

## Not examined
- Full text of the dispatch prompts at preflight:44/59/60, handoff:167, feature:23/90, explain-project:12, bug:39 (whether each repeats every duty); only harness-audit:41, retro:47, distill:38, review:105 read.
- Whether Antigravity honours `model: flash|pro` or enforces `tools:` (vendor behaviour; unverified: needs Antigravity docs).
- Bodies of each agent beyond the greps and frontmatter: line-by-line contradiction check inside each definition not done.
- Behavioural hold rates beyond the one latest log; older logs under testing/ not read.
- Security judgement on AG1: the effect is a prompt-injection surface; I did not test it.

- `TODO.md`: empty (header and format comment only). `ROADMAP.md`: Now = one active plan, Next = 2 items (limit 3), Last reviewed 2026-10-25. Compliant. *checked*
- README counts: 36 skills (table groups sum 6+7+5+7+8+3 = 36, equal to `fyr list` and status.txt), 8 agents, 2 rules, 0 commands; `commands/` holds only `.gitkeep` (`git ls-files commands`). README's command table matches the `usage` const in cmd/fyr/main.go:41-69 verb by verb (install/sync, status, diff, update, uninstall, list, render, adopt, search, index, memory, dream, metrics ingest|show|report|export, version). *checked*
- Map: `TestHarnessMap` PASS (harnessmap.txt). Edge count 0-19 recounted from the mermaid source; the `linkStyle` groups (teal 0,1,5,6,7,8; plum 2,3,4; indigo 9-13; amber 14,15,16; olive 17,18,19) match the legend. Dashed lines: harnessRepo/releases to zipPlace and zipPlace to installer (by hand), configDir to retroHarness (one machine), dreamer to provider (not a harness path, ADR-049). Each is still a gap by AGENTS rule 4. The two zip lines "done by hand" and the retro line "same machine only" are current. *checked* by reading
- Pointer targets in context: `review-standards` §2 and §8, `handoff` § Usage, `feature` § Decisions, `bash` § Installed commands, `golang` runtime-data rule, `review` Steps 4-5, `scripts/restatement-grep.sh`, `docs/bugs/INDEX.md` "Graduated" all exist. *checked*
- Tests cited by AGENTS/README/remote.md (14 names, TestHarnessMap, TestDeliverySpecCurrent, TestEmbedHoldsOnlyTrackedFiles, the lint tests, TestSkillListingBudget, TestVendoredRowsCarryAPin, TestAgyCorpusLeaves, TestRedactShapes, ...) all exist (`git grep "func <name>"`). *checked*
- Requirement to implementation: R0 `search`/`memory`/`metrics`/`dream`/`install` verbs exist in usage; R1 `agents/<n>/agent.md` lint (TestLintRefusesOldFormatAgent); R4 no settings write left in non-test code (`git grep settings.json|autoCompactWindow|attribution` finds only internal/dream/run.go:378, a private dream HOME settings file, which is dream's own, not a vendor setting write to the real home: judged, not run); R5 `adopt`; R8/R9 `update --from-zip`, `TestHarnessMap`; R10 no automatic check seen (convention + matrix, `testing/fyr-matrix.md`). Only R2 ("a template AGENTS.md never sits beside source") and R6 (scratch home) have no dedicated test that I found; they are convention. unverified: I did not grep tests for them.

## Refuted

- "The README map has a stale `report` or feedback node": refuted, none (`TestHarnessMap` PASS and my read).
- "README states a command the binary lacks": refuted, table equals usage.
- "TODO.md or ROADMAP.md hold ideas": refuted.
- "The context cites a pointer that no longer exists": refuted for all eight pointers above.
- "Context or rules still name Claude Code or `sh-agent`": refuted for context/, rules/, REQUIREMENTS.md, README.md, ROADMAP.md, AGENTS.md (git grep -i found only delivery.md's quotes and history, the crossing guide and AGENTS.md:67's `styrman`-free text; the hits are dated history or the crossing, by design D8/D32).
- "Requirement R4's `update` refuses dirty checkout on every path is untested": not examined for tests, but delivery.md:42 and remote.md:115 state it consistently; no contradiction found.

## Not examined

- DECISIONS.md body beyond ADR-060, ADR-061 (head), ADR-062 (first 900 chars per paragraph), and the header lines; whether ADR-062 amends ADR-031 is therefore unverified (C3).
- remote.md lines 131-264 read with each line cut at 700 chars; the remaining text of the release procedure and "Access" section (264 onward) not read.
- delivery.md from line 93 to the end (the file is 21 KB; read through § Agents opening).
- `.agents/docs/specs/fyr/{search,memory-loop,dream,metrics}.md` (outside area C).
- Whether each Known limit's vendor facts (24,000-byte block, tool names) still hold: unverified: needs the Antigravity CLI documentation and a run.
- Tests behind R2 and R6; whether `TestDeliverySpecCurrent` constrains which text in delivery.md § Where things stand must stay (needed before C-S2).
- gcp.md: read in full (635 B); it is correct and consistent with the context's GCP rule.

title: Recon — harness-audit G (coverage gaps)
body:
# Recon — harness-audit G (coverage gaps)

## Status: COMPLETE

Walk (feature): requirements -> `requirements` skill (init-project template; `feature` Step 1/2 only cite a REQUIREMENTS item in "Why"); design -> `feature` Steps 1-3 + `spec` + `codebase-design`; plan -> `feature` Step 2 (plan file, ADR shape); implementation -> `feature` Step 4 + `golang`/`typescript`/`frontend`/`bash`/`docker`; tests -> `testing-strategy` + `verifier` + `docs/testing/guide.md` template; review -> `review` + `review-standards` + `reviewer`; security -> `security` agent (no skill; `review --security`); docs -> `documentation` agent; release -> `preflight` + `cloud-run-deploy`; operation -> `operate-gcp` + `data-gcp`; learning -> `feedback-log`, `retro`, `distill`, `dream`, `project-memory`. Bug: `bug` Steps 0-5 + `bugs` agent, then same tail. Every stage has an owner; the gaps below are at the edges.

| ID | Stage | Today | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| G1 | Implementation / tests for non-Go-TS stacks | Language skills exist only for `golang`, `typescript`, `frontend`, `bash`; `testing-strategy` tiers are Go + Playwright + compose. Operator profile is Go + TS, so Python, Rust or mobile work has no conventions, no test tiers. | A short paragraph in `testing-strategy` (or `feature` Step 4) saying "other stack: write the stack's commands into `docs/testing/guide.md` first and the verifier runs those", only if such projects are in scope; otherwise state the non-goal in `context/dev-setup.md`. |
| G2 | Design: requirements check | `requirements` skill exists, but `feature` Step 1/2 never asks "does this conflict with REQUIREMENTS.md / which item does it serve"; only the global hard rule (immutable) and the plan's "Why" line cite it. A feature that contradicts a Must is caught only by the reviewer if told. | One line in `feature` Step 1 (and cold-reader Step 3): list REQUIREMENTS items the scope touches; a conflict is a proposed edit, not a plan row. |
| G3 | Design / security | `security` runs only at DoD step 2 (after code). No threat-model or data-handling step in `feature` Step 2 (plan has Failure modes but no "trust boundaries / data classes / secrets" row). Auth/crypto changes are found late. | Add one row "Trust boundaries and data handled" to the plan template in `feature` Step 2; trigger = same words as the `security` dispatch rule. |
| G4 | Implementation: data / migrations | `feature` Phase order mentions "data model and migrations"; `data-gcp` covers Cloud SQL only. No guidance for local/embedded DB (SQLite, which the harness itself uses), expand/contract migrations, rollback of a migration, or backfill. `operate-gcp` rollback is for Cloud Run revisions, not data. | A reference file under `data-gcp` (or `feature`): migration rules (expand/contract, reversible or backup-first, test on a copy), including the SQLite case. |
| G5 | Project size: script / one-file tool | `init-project` scaffolds the full trail (docs tree, ROADMAP, REQUIREMENTS) for every project; context offers "Unscaffolded project" only as Trivial/Task, no DoD. No "small" tier between the two. | A paragraph in `init-project` naming a minimal scaffold (AGENTS.md + docs/changes + handoffs only) or an explicit "scripts stay unscaffolded" statement. |
| G6 | Docs: onboarding / user-facing docs | `documentation` agent maintains how-it-works docs and `docs/onboarding.md` "when a project has one"; `init-project` assets have no onboarding or CHANGELOG-for-users template. `explain-project` exists for reading, not writing. | Optional template `onboarding.md` in init-project assets, or strike (state that README is the only user doc). |
| G7 | Release: non-Cloud-Run targets | `preflight` + `cloud-run-deploy` cover a service on GCP. A library, CLI binary or a frontend-only static site has no release path in a skill (the harness's own `deploy/remote.md` is project-local). `init-project` has `deploy/{local,remote,gcp}.md` templates only. | A "release shapes" paragraph in `preflight`: binary/tag-only, container, static site (GCS/Firebase not covered), and which gate steps skip. |
| G8 | Operation: other than Cloud Run | `operate-gcp` is Cloud Run only; GKE has `gke-basics` but no runbook; no skill for a local/self-hosted service (the operator's own Linux box) beyond `docker`. | Note in `operate-gcp` scope line pointing at what to use for GKE/local, or a runbook section in `gke-basics`. Low priority (default compute is Cloud Run). |
| G9 | Tests: performance, accessibility, load | `frontend/references/accessibility.md` exists; `testing-strategy` has no perf/benchmark/load tier (grep of `benchmark|load test` finds only mentions in other skills). `verifier` runs only the project's own commands. | One tier row "benchmark / load smoke" in `testing-strategy`, only when a requirement names a number. |
| G10 | Learning: a failure with no number | Context requires a BUG record for anything that "reached a commit, deploy or user"; `bug` Step 0 decides. Works for bugs; for a feature that was rejected or abandoned mid-plan there is no abandon/retire record (plan boxes `[-]` only). | One sentence in `feature` Step 6: abandoned plan -> `[-]` boxes + ROADMAP "Now" cleared + handoff line. Check whether it exists before adding (Step 6 text mentions `[-]`, so probably covered). |
| G11 | Dependency updates | Only `operate-gcp` has "dependency and base-image cadence" (Cloud Run); no stage owns updating Go/npm modules for a non-deployed project; `security` reviews dependency risk only on a diff. | A line in `golang`/`typescript` skills pointing at `govulncheck`/`npm audit` cadence, or move the cadence paragraph into a shared place. |

Claude Code dependence (the last ask): none found in the shipped text. `git grep` of `maxTurns|/goal|TaskStop|AskUserQuestion|TodoWrite|subagent_type|PreToolUse|SessionStart|allowed-tools|.claude/` in `context/ rules/ agents/ skills/` (excluding the vendored catalog) returns only prose in `skills/review-standards/references/prompt-audit/prompt-audit.md` (audits CLAUDE.md files of other projects, legitimate) and an unrelated `gke-basics` line. Context says "No hooks, gates" and uses Antigravity names (`manage_subagents`, `WaitMsBeforeAsync`). Agent tools lists use Antigravity tool names. Remaining soft dependency: the dispatch "tool-call budget" is advisory (no `maxTurns` in agent.md, allow-list in `agentKeys` has no such key), so the cut-off the explorer definition mentions is only the caller's; the budget is prose, not enforced (not a Claude-only feature, but a mechanism gap).

## Measurements
- `ls skills agents rules commands`: 36 skills, 8 agents, 2 rules, `commands/` empty.
- `ls skills/init-project/assets`: AGENTS, README, REQUIREMENTS, ROADMAP, TODO + `agents-tree/` with docs/{specs/TEMPLATE, deploy/{gcp,local,remote}, testing/guide, architecture/DECISIONS, bugs/INDEX} and .gitkeep dirs. No template for plans, handoffs, changes, reviews (those come from skills/agent definitions).
- `git grep -n -E 'maxTurns|/goal\b|TaskStop|AskUserQuestion|TodoWrite|EnterPlanMode|run_in_background|subagent_type|\.claude/|allowed-tools|PreToolUse|SessionStart' -- skills(-catalog) agents rules context`: 5 hits, none a live dependency.
- `git grep -il -E 'python|pytest|rust|cargo|swift|kotlin|android' -- skills(-catalog)`: hits only in VENDORED, api-auth-gcp, bash, feature, feedback-log, find-skills, gke-basics, google-catalog (client libraries, examples); no skill on them.
- `git grep -il -E 'migration|postgres|cloud sql|...'`: data-gcp, docker, cloud-run-deploy, feature, codebase-design mention; only data-gcp has migration substance (Cloud SQL).
- `wc -l`: feature 114, bug 57, preflight 113.

## Refuted
- "A stage depends on a Claude Code hook, `/goal` or Agent-tool parameter": no such live reference (see above).
- "`security` is a skill the feature flow cannot load": it is an agent (`agents/security/agent.md`, model `pro`) reached from DoD step 2 and `review --security`; `skills/security` does not exist and none is referenced as one.
- "Requirements stage has no producer": `requirements` skill plus init-project template exist; the gap is only G2 (consumption in `feature`).

## Not examined
- Full text of `requirements`, `spec`, `testing-strategy`, `review`, `retro`, `dream` skills beyond descriptions/greps; the init-project `testing/guide.md` template body; `rules/session-sizing.md`; whether G10's `[-]` handling already covers abandoned plans; the vendored catalog; whether `docs/onboarding.md` has a template elsewhere. G-rows are judged from descriptions, headings and greps, not full reads; severity not assigned. Used about 8 of 30 tool calls.

title: Recon — harness audit IN-1, cmd/fyr (2026-10-25, c4885ae)
body:
# Recon — harness audit IN-1, cmd/fyr (2026-10-25, c4885ae)

## Status: COMPLETE

Scope: cmd/fyr/main.go read in full (1345 lines); cmd/fyr tests, embed.go, go.mod, root tests, fyr-matrix.md, README command table sampled (see Not examined). No tool was run; baseline outputs under .agents/scratch/harness-audit/2026-10-25/ were read.

| ID | Sev | Where | Finding | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| IN1 | low | cmd/fyr/main.go:242-244, :89-95 | `fyr list -h` (or `--help`) returns `flag.ErrHelp`; `main` prints `fyr: flag: help requested` and exits 1. Help is a successful ask, and the usage block of the FlagSet is on the writer, so the extra stderr line and exit 1 are wrong. No test pins it (grep ErrHelp: one site, no test). | fix: return nil on ErrHelp (or exit 0) and pin it |
| IN2 | low | cmd/fyr/main.go:221-223 | Unknown command returns a plain error (message carries the whole usage block), so it goes to os.Stderr via main, not the caller's writer, and exits 1. Every other usage error exits 2 on the writer (usage_test.go:15-60). `testing/2026-10-25-verify-fyr-rename.md:48` already notes the 2-vs-1 contradiction ("Phase 5 should reconcile"); `TestMainExitStatus` pins 1. | operator's choice: pin 1 and fix the docs that say 2, or move to exit 2 on the writer |
| IN3 | low | cmd/fyr/main.go:754, internal/harness/repo.go:231 | `update --check` / `--dry-run` at a checkout call `harness.Behind`, which runs `git fetch --quiet` (moves remote-tracking refs, may use the network). Usage text (main.go:50) says `--dry-run ... changes nothing`; the fetch is disclosed in the usage ("git fetch") but not as an exception to "changes nothing". Not a data risk. | defer: reword to "changes nothing in the tree or the home" |
| IN4 | low | cmd/fyr/main.go:318-319 | `writesState` lists `adopt` and a plain project-local `search` / `index` as state-writing verbs, so they run the migration. `adopt` writes into the repo, and a local `search` writes `.agents/scratch/search.db` (the home is used only for --global). Over-migrating is harmless and arguably safe (rename is one atomic step, refuses symlinks, leaves both-present alone), but the table contradicts the comment at :313-315 ("writes under the state directory"). Also `dream --install-timer/--remove-timer` migrate though they write no state. | defer: say in the comment that migration is deliberately early for these |
| IN5 | med | .agents/docs/testing/fyr-matrix.md:1-86 | The verb x place matrix is a 2026-09-18 document: cells quote `sh-agent`, 260 files, `--vendor all`, the old repository name `styrman-harness.git`, 27 skills / 7 agents. The header discloses the rename but no cell was re-run under `fyr`; there are no rows for the state-dir migration (install vs status/diff/uninstall --dry-run on a home with only ~/.config/sh-agent), for `update --from-zip`, or for the D32 keep-the-old-~/.claude path, which are what Phase 4b/5b changed. The "Silent cells: None" claim is therefore a claim about the old binary. | fix: re-run the matrix with `fyr` and add the migration rows, or mark the file historical |
| IN6 | low | README.md:162 vs release-v270.txt | README names assets `fyr-linux-amd64`, `fyr-darwin-arm64`, `fyr-linux-arm64`; the newest release (v2.7.0) carries `sh-agent-*` and `styrman-harness-v2.7.0.zip`. Known (Phase 6 not done, first fyr tag is v3.0.0), recorded so the README is not read as true of a published release. | defer: Phase 6 |
| IN7 | low | cmd/fyr/main.go:1320 | `os.RemoveAll(dir)` of the unpacked zip: `dir` is the `MkdirTemp(parent, "zip-*")` result returned by `harness.UnpackZip`, never user text; parent is `~/.config/fyr` or, on a dry run with no state dir, the directory holding the zip (zip.go:~97). A dry run with no state dir therefore creates and removes a `zip-*` directory beside the operator's zip: not "writes nothing" but it is cleaned up (unless the removal fails: a warning only). | defer: document the beside-the-zip scratch in the usage text |
| IN8 | low | cmd/fyr/main.go:129-135 | `ctx` holds 27 fields, of which `dreamProject` and `metricsProject` are two `--project` flags registered by different verbs (fine: one per FlagSet), but `global` is declared twice (search and index) with the same help text. Not a defect; the shared flag is registered by two verbs, which the "one verb per flag" rule tolerates only because the text says "search, index". | strike or defer |

## Measurements

- Verb table: `verbs` map has 15 keys (version, uninstall, memory, dream, metrics, search, index, install, sync, status, diff, update, list, render, adopt) plus `help` / `-h` / `--help` in run(). Usage text covers all 15 (sync as an alias on the install line); README table (lines 40-51) covers all but `help`, with `sync` under install. No verb missing from either. Measured by reading main.go:44-74, :161-217 and README.md:40-51.
- Exported functions with no caller outside tests: none in cmd/fyr (package main, no exports). Not measured for internal/ (other dispatch).
- Duplicate helpers in cmd/fyr: `TestMain` is identical in cmd/fyr/testmain_test.go and testmain_test.go (root), 21 lines each, by necessity (two packages). `reorder` + `hasFlag` are two argument scanners; `hasFlag` is used only to give `--from-zip` on a wrong verb a better message.
- Errors always nil: none seen in main.go; `selfExecutable`, `runVersion` (returns nil by design).
- Writes/deletes in main.go, with guards: `os.RemoveAll(dir)` at :1320 (temp dir from UnpackZip, see IN7); all other filesystem mutation goes through `harness.Install`, `Uninstall`, `MkdirAllTracked`/`RemoveCreated`, `SweepStaleDirs`, `MigrateStateDir` (one `os.Rename`, refuses a symlinked old dir, leaves both-present alone), `dream.*Timer`, `metrics.*`, `memory.Add`, `search.*` — those are the internal half; `os.Lstat`/`os.Stat`/`os.ReadFile` in main.go are reads. main.go itself has one delete and no direct writes.
- Home confinement: `c.home` is made absolute (main.go:268) and every path in main.go is `filepath.Join(home, ...)`; `knownCheckout` refuses a discovered checkout other than the installed one. Whether Install/Uninstall follow links inside the home is the harness half's question (not examined).
- Tests: baseline test.txt exit 0; cover.txt cmd/fyr 90.5% of statements, root package no statements. Only `TestVersionVerb` calls `run()` without `--home` and it is a pure print; no cmd/fyr test touches the real HOME (the `t.Setenv("HOME", ...)` at main_test.go:1096, 1392, 1418 and metrics_test.go:74 point at temp dirs).
- Dependencies: git grep of Go imports outside the module and stdlib finds only `modernc.org/sqlite` (one import line). go.mod requires sqlite plus its indirect set; no `toolchain` directive (matches ADR-029). Which package imports sqlite was not checked in this half.
- Command: `git grep -hn '^\s*"[a-z0-9.]*\.[a-z]*/' -- '*.go'` (path-like strings in the output are test fixtures, not imports).

## Refuted

- "A read-only mode skips a guard the real run resolves": `update --check/--dry-run` runs the same dirty-tree refusal as the real run (main.go:1041, above the checkOnly return); `install --dry-run` resolves `knownCheckout` and `ResolveSource` as the real run does; `uninstall --dry-run` probes the timer and the legacy-timer notice as the real run. Not refuted for internal/harness.Install (other half).
- "The state-dir migration runs in a read-only verb": it does not. `writesState` (main.go:316-328) returns false for `--dry-run`, `update --check`, `status`, `diff`, `list`, `render`, `memory show`, `metrics show|report|export`, `version`, and those print `StateDirNotice` on stderr instead (main.go:333-341). `metrics report` cannot create `~/.config/fyr` ahead of a migration: `existingMetricsStore` Lstats the store first and exits 1 when it is missing, so a report cannot run before a migration has put the store where it expects it (a home with only the old dir gets "no metrics store").
- "`--from-zip` can fall through to a normal update": refused before the FlagSet for other verbs (:229), and for `update` an empty or flag-looking value, `--check` and `--repo` are exit 2 (:283-291); the decision is made on the parsed flag, not the raw args.
- "Refusals do not reach the caller's writer": every usage refusal in main.go that exits 2 prints to `out` (:230, :252, :286, :289, :411, :463, :479 ...). The exceptions are IN1 and IN2.
- "A release can ship an artifact its own verification did not check": not decidable from cmd/fyr; the zip path always hashes the bytes it unpacks and passes them to `VerifyZipSums` first (zip.go:60-66). The release publishing path is the harness / preflight half.

## Not examined

- cmd/fyr/*_test.go bodies beyond usage_test.go:1-80 and crossing_test.go:1-35, and the headers of the test files (counts only: main_test 1500 lines/34 top-level funcs); zip_test.go, migrate_test.go, delivery_test.go, memory/metrics/search tests not read.
- embed.go read (10 lines, the embed pinned both ways by embed_test.go:15,54 by name); embed_test.go, plan_test.go, statedir_test.go, init_project_test.go bodies not read.
- fyr-matrix.md lines 40-86 read truncated to 260 columns.
- README.md read only at the command table and the install sections' grep hits.
- The baseline outputs install.txt, status.txt, diff.txt, uninstall-dry.txt, gofmt.txt, vet.txt, govulncheck.txt were opened only to their first lines (status, uninstall) or not at all.
- All of internal/harness (Install, Uninstall, UnpackZip's link handling, UpdateFromRelease, Reinstall), internal/dream timer writes, which package imports sqlite, whether `fyr dream` with neither --all nor --project errors with exit 2.
- Behaviour was not run; nothing here is measured on a binary.

title: Recon — harness-audit IN-2: internal/harness (2026-10-25, commit c4885ae)
body:
# Recon — harness-audit IN-2: internal/harness (2026-10-25, commit c4885ae)

## Status: COMPLETE

Read in full: apply, state, release, zip, plan, inventory, frontmatter, migrate, sweep, source, repo, adopt, render, pathguard, owned_*. Nothing run (read-only). About 12 tool calls used.

## Summary
The installer holds its stated rules. Every destructive step in apply.go (resync, uninstall) is limited to manifest entries that `LoadState` has already filtered with `filepath.IsLocal`, skips symlinks and paths under a link, and keeps `~/.claude` files. The release path verifies the exact bytes it then installs (SHA256SUMS line, `# fyr vX.Y.Z` marker equal to the tag, canonical tag regex). The zip unpack validates every name, kind, size and duplicate before it writes. I found no high-severity defect. The defects are in the lint's asymmetry (skills, commands and rules use a two-key deny list while agents use an allow list), a "read-only" `Diff` that creates a directory, command and rule names that are never validated, and a few warts.

| ID | Sev | Where | Finding | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| IN1 | med | internal/harness/inventory.go:209, :348 | Skills, commands and rules refuse only the exact keys `allowed-tools` and `hooks` (a case-sensitive deny list), while agents use an allow list (`agentKeys`, :236). Any other permission-shaped key (`permissionMode`, `mcpServers`, `allowedTools`, `Allowed-Tools`, `allowed_tools`) passes in a skill, command or rule, though the AGENTS.md and ADR-056 rationale ("the next vendor key is refused by default") applies equally. Whether Antigravity honours any of them is not known from the code. | defer to operator: either an allow list for skills (name, description, disable-model-invocation, metadata, license...) or fold the key match to lower case with `-`/`_` removed. Security judgement needed. |
| IN2 | med | internal/harness/apply.go:277 (called from Diff) | `Diff` calls `ConfigDir`, which does `MkdirAll(~/.config/fyr, 0700)`, and writes a temp file there. `fyr diff` is meant to be read-only, so on a home with no state dir it creates one. Status does not. It is only reached when a file differs, so it is minor in practice. | fix: use a temp dir under an existing dir, or pipe the plan bytes via `diff -` on stdin and write nothing |
| IN3 | med | internal/harness/inventory.go:336-361 (loadDocs) | Command and rule names come from the file name and are never passed through `validName` or `identLike`, unlike skills and agents. The name is rendered in backticks into the deployed AGENTS.md (`RenderInventoryCompact`:439,446) and used as a path segment (plan.go:113,117). A name with a backtick, a newline or a leading `.` gets into the model's context. Path escape is impossible (glob gives one segment). For a checkout the author is the operator; for a zip install `zipNameSafe` (zip.go:267) allows a newline or backtick in an entry name, so a hand-downloaded zip could inject prose into the context. The zip is unsigned when it has no SHA256SUMS (the "unverified" path). Security judgement needed. | fix: `validName("command"/"rule", ...)` in `loadDocs` |
| IN4 | low | internal/harness/state.go:58-64 | `LoadState` accepts any local manifest entry, not only entries under `.gemini/config`, `.local/bin/fyr` or the old `.claude`. A hand-edited `state.json` listing `.ssh/authorized_keys` makes the next install or uninstall remove it (the manifest is user-owned, so this is the stated trust root, but there is no allowed-root check). A local entry such as `.` also reaches `os.Remove(home)` (fails if non-empty). | defer; add an allowed-prefix filter next to `IsLocal` if wanted. Security judgement needed. |
| IN5 | low | internal/harness/apply.go:225 | `Status` does `os.ReadFile` before looking at `lerr`, so a planned path that is a symlink to a FIFO or a special file blocks, and a symlink target is read before it is classed "foreign". `Diff` checks the link first. Read-only, so no damage. | fix: move the ReadFile after the link check |
| IN6 | low | internal/harness/release.go:36, :224 | The `# fyr vX.Y.Z` marker regexp is `(?m)` and matches on any line; `FindSubmatch` takes the first. A SHA256SUMS with two different markers is not refused. The doc says "at the top". The attacker model is the same as the file's own content, so there is no bypass, but the check is looser than described. | fix or amend the comment: refuse a second distinct marker |
| IN7 | low | internal/harness/release.go:150-155 | After a verified binary is written, a failed `install` returns an error with the new binary in place and the old harness deployed. The message names `install` failing but not that the binary is already replaced (`status` then shows drift). | defer: add a sentence to the error |
| IN8 | low | internal/harness/inventory.go:53-75 | Doc comments are scrambled: the `validName` comment sits over `identLike`, and its tail ("time rather than finding a file written beside their home.") is orphaned over `validName`. Violates "comments say why". | fix |
| IN9 | low | internal/harness/apply.go:51, :133, :139 | Three ways of deciding "not fyr's to remove" are repeated (symlink or underLink or claudeFile): in `saveOnError`, in the resync loop and in Uninstall. | see IN-S1 |
| IN10 | low | internal/harness/apply.go:216-253 | `Status` counts old `.claude` manifest entries still on disk as `stale` (it has no `claudeFile` check), so a home from before ADR-062 shows drift until the next install drops them from the manifest. After D32 that is the only way to clear it. Probably the intended prompt to run install; untested here. | defer; confirm with the operator |
| IN-S1 |  | internal/harness/apply.go:51,133-142,337 | One helper `fyrOwns(home, rel) (kind)` for symlink / underLink / claudeFile would replace three copies of the same condition. | operator's choice |
| IN-S2 |  | internal/harness/{source.go,repo.go,inventory.go} | Exported but used only inside the package (no non-test caller outside it): `AssetName`, `DirSource`, `EmbeddedSource`, `IsRepo`, `Keys`, `LoadAgents`, `LoadSkills`, `ParseStrict`, `ReadCapped`, `RemoveState`, `RenderInventoryCompact`, `RunningElsewhere`, `SaveState`, `SplitList`, `TightenConfigDir`. Not dead, only needlessly exported. `SecretShaped` (plan.go:135) is a one-line wrapper over `secretShaped`, used once outside (internal/search). | defer; low value |
| IN-S3 |  | internal/harness/release.go:327-376 and zip.go | Zip verification (`VerifyZipSums`, `ErrZipNoSums`, `zipNamesIn`) lives in release.go while the unpack lives in zip.go. | defer |

## Measurements
- Exported symbols with no caller outside `internal/harness` (non-test): command `for f in <exported funcs>; grep -rn "harness\.$f" --include=*.go cmd internal | grep -v _test.go`. Result: the 15 listed in IN-S2. None has zero callers, so there is no dead exported code *checked*.
- Destructive and write sites, `grep -n 'os\.\(RemoveAll\|Remove\|Rename\|Chmod\|MkdirAll\|OpenFile\)' internal/harness/*.go` excluding tests; guards read:
  - apply.go:148 (stale `os.Remove`) and :348 (uninstall): manifest entry (IsLocal-filtered, state.go:60), not a Claude file, Lstat is not a symlink, not under a link. *checked*
  - apply.go:472 `pruneEmptyDirs`: only removes empty directories, stops at home, `.claude`, `.gemini`, `.gemini/config`, `.config`, `.local`, `.local/bin`. It does not stop at `.config/fyr`; RemoveState (state.go:136) removes it when empty, which is intended. *checked*
  - apply.go:112/420 `WriteAtomic`: reached only after the symlink and underLink checks. A race between check and write is not guarded (TOCTOU, acceptable on a single-user home).
  - release.go:125 `RemoveAll(dir)`: dir is a fresh `MkdirTemp` under `~/.config/fyr`. :140 write goes through `WriteAtomic(~/.local/bin/fyr)` and does not check for a symlink at the destination (rename replaces the link rather than following it). *checked*
  - sweep.go:35 `RemoveAll`: only direct children of `~/.config/fyr` with prefix `release-` or `zip-`, real directories, older than 1 hour. *checked*
  - zip.go:102 `RemoveAll(tmp)`: its own `MkdirTemp`. :245-254 writes are under `tmp` with names validated by `zipNameSafe`, `O_EXCL`, symlink entries refused. *checked*
  - adopt.go:79/89/101/120 `RemoveAll`: staging and backup under the repo's `.agents/scratch`, name from `validName`, overlap refused with `within`. *checked*
  - repo.go:284 `RemoveAll(build dir)`: repo scratch, per pid.
  - migrate.go:52 one `Rename` of `~/.config/sh-agent` to `~/.config/fyr`, only when the new one is absent and the old is a plain directory. Refuses a symlink. *checked*
- Error values that are always nil: none found in the files read. `StateDirNotice` and `TightenConfigDir` return no error by design.
- Imports: harness imports only the standard library and `github.com/kesokaj/fyr` (the embed package); no SQLite. *checked* by reading the import blocks of all files read.
- Lint, agents: unknown tool names refused (inventory.go:308-312), `knownTools` has six names; tools key absent is allowed (what the CLI then grants is not shown in the code). Agent keys allow-listed; `subagent: true` and `mainAgent: false` forced.
- Test, from baseline: `test.txt` shows `ok internal/harness 92.9s coverage 89.8%`, exit 0.

## Refuted
- "A path can write or delete outside home": refuted for the manifest paths (IsLocal in LoadState, tested by `TestLoadStateDropsNonLocalManifestEntries`, `TestResyncNeverFollowsANonLocalManifestEntry`), for plan paths (`validName` for skills and agents; file names inside a skill come from a WalkDir under the skill dir, symlinks refused), and for the zip (zipNameSafe plus `IsLocal`, trees allow-listed).
- "A release can ship an unchecked artifact": refuted. `downloadRelease` returns the bytes it read; `verifyRelease` hashes those same bytes against the line for the exact asset name; the bytes written by `WriteAtomic` are `data`, not a re-read. The marker must equal the tag; duplicate-conflicting lines for the asset are refused; the file read is capped at 256 MiB. The `.zip` path hashes the buffer it unpacks (zip.go:55-66). Residual: SHA256SUMS comes from the same release as the binary (unsigned, ADR-053, stated).
- "Dry run skips a guard the real run applies": refuted for Install (the same Lstat, underLink and claudeFile checks run before the `dryRun` branch) and Uninstall. Exception: IN2 for Diff, which is not a dry run.
- "A refusal exits zero": every refusal here returns an error; I did not read the exit-code mapping in cmd/fyr (see Not examined).

## Not examined
- Test files (11k lines, mostly harness_test.go and catalog_test.go); only their names were used. Whether tests cover IN1-IN3 and IN10 is unknown.
- `cmd/fyr` (other dispatch): how errors map to exit codes, whether `MigrateStateDir` runs before every writing verb (only one call site seen, main.go:335), and what `diff` and `status` do about `StateDirNotice`.
- pathguard.go semantics only partly relevant (read in full, but its callers are in cmd).
- No `go test`, `go vet` or `govulncheck` run (read-only); coverage figure is the baseline's.
- Which keys Antigravity honours in skill, command and rule frontmatter (IN1), and what a missing `tools:` grants an agent, cannot be told from the code.

title: Recon — harness-audit SD: search, memory, dream (2026-10-25, commit c4885ae)
body:
# Recon — harness-audit SD: search, memory, dream (2026-10-25, commit c4885ae)

## Status: COMPLETE

Read-only; no `fyr`, `go` or `sh-agent` run. 21 of 30 tool calls used. Baseline outputs read from `.agents/scratch/harness-audit/2026-10-25/`.

## Summary

The three packages hold up against the asks. Every git call into a project goes through `trail.Command`. Model output is fenced as data, the model has no tool grants, and its output lands only in `~/.config/fyr/proposals/` for the operator. The dry-run shows the cap works. The real gaps are: (1) any clone with `.agents/docs` that is searched once is registered and goes nightly to the model (a security judgement for the operator); (2) the search spec's measured numbers and one exit code are stale or contradictory; (3) the project name reaches the prompt and the proposals header without the one-line fold every other field gets. `ReplaceOldTimer` and its `on()` probe are sound for the paths I could read; the macOS branch was not run.

## Findings

| ID | Sev | Where | Finding | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SD1 | med | `.agents/docs/specs/fyr/search.md:38`; `internal/dream/run.go:111-124` | A checkout with `.agents/docs` registers itself in the global index on ANY `search` or `index` run inside it. `dream --all` then reads that project's trail (bugs, reviews, retros, changes, handoffs), memory and Antigravity transcripts and sends them, redacted for credential shapes only, to the model. Running `fyr search` once in an untrusted third-party clone therefore queues its text as prompt input and its owner's content as outbound data. The fence and the no-tools run limit injection to "a queued proposal the operator must approve". This is a security judgement (trust boundary) and the code path was read for dream only, not the registration code itself. | Operator's choice: opt-in registration (`fyr index --register`), or say in `dream.md` and the dream skill that registration is automatic. Defer if accepted as designed. |
| SD2 | med | `.agents/docs/specs/fyr/search.md:96` | The recall figure is stale. The spec says 0.633 index against 0.296 for grep (re-measured 2026-10-01). *Checked* `recall.txt` today: index mean all 0.499, grep 0.261 (words 0.577 vs 0.154; drift 0.145; open 0.500). Question q41 ("open plan") scores 0.00 and q33's gold is a date-pinned record. The gold lists decay as plans close, so the "open" arm measures the fixture, not search. | fix: re-pin the open gold, then update the spec row with the dated measurement. |
| SD3 | low | `.agents/docs/specs/fyr/search.md:29` vs `:73` | Contradiction. Line 29 says argument errors exit 2 (BUG-168). The Failure-modes row for argument errors says exit 1. Code returns `usageError` (`internal/search/search.go:99-125`), consistent with 2. | fix: table row to 2. |
| SD4 | low | `internal/dream/prompt.go:43`; `internal/dream/run.go` `render` (`# Dream proposals — %s`); `unique(... day+"-"+c.Name ...)` | `c.Name` (base name of the checkout, from the index or `filepath.Base(root)`) is written into the prompt, the proposals file header and file names with no `oneLine`/`o.line` fold, unlike `Root`, `Title`, `File` and every label. A directory name holding a line break could forge a `### N.` / `**Status:** queued` line in the Status-driven queue (the exact thing `o.line` guards, `run.go` SD3 comment). Needs a hostile directory name, so low. | fix: fold `c.Name` once in `collect`. |
| SD5 | low | `internal/memory/memory.go:64-71` | `Root` is `filepath.Dir(git-common-dir)`. For a submodule (`.git/modules/x`), a `--separate-git-dir` checkout or a bare repo this is not the work-tree top, so the store path points into `.git/…` and the failure is a misleading "not ignored" refusal. Not run. | defer; or derive from `--show-toplevel` of the main worktree. |
| SD6 | low | `internal/trail/trail.go:144-153` vs `search.md:42` | `trail.Log` refuses every partial clone, while search allows one on git >= 2.44. Policy differs by caller. Not read: what `trail.Dates` does when `Log` refuses. If it returns no dates, `collect` falls back to mtime, the case the SD4 comment (`collect.go`) says made a whole trail look new and evict transcripts. | Open question; check `Dates`. |
| SD7 | low | `internal/dream/timer.go:295-311` | `on()` on darwin counts only "Could not find service" as off. A plist that is on disk but not loaded is auto-loaded at next login, so "off" there means "turned off by hand in this session". Sound as a conservative rule. Unmeasured: no macOS here. | none; note only. |
| SD-S1 | | `internal/dream/collect.go:fit` | `fit` calls `prompt(*c)` (a full re-render of ~260 KB) for every dropped input; with 34 drops that is 34 renders per project per night. Compute the size once and subtract each drop. | defer; speed is not a problem at this size. |
| SD-S2 | | `internal/dream/dream.go:dryRun` | A `--project` dry-run prints one `left out:` line per dropped record (34 here). A count with the first few would read better. | operator's choice. |

## Measurements

- `cat .agents/scratch/harness-audit/2026-10-25/search-open.txt`: index current, 1874 files, 0 changed reconciled in 115 ms; 2 open records (plan fyr-agy-only, 6 unticked; BUG-139). `bugs-open.txt` shows BUG-139 as the only open row in `bugs/INDEX.md`, so search and the INDEX agree. No duplicate or missed record seen.
- `recall.txt` (FYR_RECALL=1 TestRecall): index mean all 0.499 over 41; grep 0.261. See SD2.
- `dream-dry.txt`: `memory 5, feedback 0, trail 33, skill 36, metrics 0, transcript 0; 261306 bytes` against the 262144-byte cap (`maxPrompt`, `dream.go:24`). `grep -c 'left out' dream-dry.txt` = 34 (31 trail, 0 transcript, 3 other). The drops run oldest first (2026-10-09 to 2026-10-23), as `fit` says.
- `timer-dry.txt`: `would install the nightly dream timer (fyr dream --all at 03:00); installed now: false`.
- `test.txt`: all packages ok under -race. `cover.txt`: search 84.1%, memory 90.5%, dream 89.2%, redact 97.8%.
- Calls to `git` in the three packages (`git grep -n 'trail.Command'`): `search/reconcile.go:42` (the wrapper, used for `rev-parse`, `ls-files -s/-z/--others`), `search/search.go:147` (`check-ignore`), `memory/memory.go:64,131,289` (`rev-parse --git-common-dir`, `check-ignore`, `ls-files`). All run with `--no-optional-locks`, `core.fsmonitor=false`, `log.showSignature=false`, `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` and the operator's inherited environment (trail.go:137-141). `git status` is never run; `ls-files` runs no clean filter.
- Calls to a service manager (`git grep -n 'exec.Command' internal/dream/timer.go`): `systemctl --user daemon-reload / enable --now / disable --now / is-enabled` and `launchctl bootstrap / bootout / print`, with unit names suffixed by a hash of a non-real home (`namesFor`, `timer.go:70-86`), so a scratch home never touches the real unit. The real home is resolved from the account database, not `$HOME` (BUG-149).
- Prompt entry points: `prompt()` (`prompt.go:43-65`) and `collect` (`collect.go`). Each of memory, feedback, trail, skills, metrics and transcripts is fenced `<<<data kind: label` with `>`/`<` runs of three or more spaced out, and the label folded. `scrub` = `redact.Redact` plus home path to `~` runs on every input and on `Dropped`. `c.Name` is not folded (SD4).
- Refusals against tests (string and name greps of `*_test.go`, coarse): search busy `TestBusyRefusesNotStale`; symlinked scratch `TestRefuseSymlinkedScratch`; symlinked db `TestRefuseSymlinkedDatabase`; not gitignored (search_test.go); partial clone `TestGlobalSkipsUnsafePartialClone`; noindex (search_test.go). Memory: slug, type and newline description (`TestAddRefusals` rows at memory_test.go:153-155), the 200-line cap in Add (:147), symlinks (6 hits), held lock (`TestHeldLockRefusesAfterRetry`), tracked store (`TestShowRefusesTrackedStore`). Dream: already running, the `--all` and `--project` clash, memory over cap, control character in the timer path, denied actions and tool steps, a kept unit with other text (timer_test.go:108-116), a bad skill name (`../escape`, run_test.go:50), no binary (timer_test.go:125), `ReplaceOldTimer` (timer_test.go:481-581), a symlinked memory store (collect_test.go:395-403). Not confirmed by a name match: "a symlinked docs root or record directory is never followed" (`linked`, `collect.go`) has no `symlink` hit in `dream/*_test.go` beyond the store test. I did not look for a differently worded test.

## Refuted

- "A model answer can run a command": the call is `agy --mode plan` with a private HOME and `settings.json` granting nothing (`run.go` `agyHome`); `answer()` returns no answer on any tool step or denied action. Output goes to files under `~/.config/fyr/proposals/` at mode 0600.
- "A model-chosen skill name or path can write outside the proposals dir": `skillName` regexp `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$` gates drafts; `unique` joins fixed prefixes; `File:` is only printed (folded by `o.line`).
- "A repository's git config can make search, memory or dream run a program": covered by `trail.Command` (fsmonitor, signature, lazy fetch); partial clones guarded. Inherited `GIT_*` and `PATH` come from the operator's environment, not the repository. A symlinked `.agents`, `.agents/scratch`, `.agents/memory` and `MEMORY.md` are all refused.
- "A scratch home shares a timer with the real one": `namesFor` hashes any home that is not the account's; `TestReplaceOldTimer` covers the other-home case (timer_test.go:536). The dream's agy login is read from the real `$HOME` by design (`run.go` `agyHome`, the comment states it).
- "`ReplaceOldTimer` can leave no timer": new unit is written and started before `old.remove()`; a refused install keeps the old one with the error (`timer.go:365-367`). `on()` treats a missing manager or a failed probe as on. The one gap is that both fire in 03:00 if the removal fails; the error is returned.

## Not examined

- `internal/search/parse.go`, `store.go`, `export.go`, the middle of `reconcile.go` and `search.go` (ranking, reference parsing, chunking); so "returns a record twice" is only checked by the CLI baseline, not by reading the dedupe code (the spec says one chunk matching both word rounds is counted once).
- `internal/dream/metrics.go`, `state.go`; `internal/redact` and `internal/metrics` beyond the call site. Whether the redactor catches every kind of secret is outside this brief.
- `.agents/docs/specs/fyr/dream.md` (87 lines) and the skills `skills/project-memory`, `skills/dream`, `skills/retro`: not read. How `/retro` consumes the queued proposals (a prompt-injection path from model text to a main-session instruction) is therefore unchecked.
- `trail.Dates` and `trail.DocsRoot` behaviour (SD6); the macOS paths of `timer.go`; `search.AgyConversationText` after line 140 (workspace match, row text extraction).
- Whether the Failure-modes table is complete against the code's error strings: I matched the rows by message only for the few listed under Measurements.

| TR-S1 | | .agents/docs/bugs/INDEX.md:131-188 | One 57-row Graduated table plus the main table with the same IDs, with a 2-3 line prevention cell in the main table. A reader checks one row per bug. | simplify: drop the Prevention text from rows once graduated, keep ID and target |

## Measurements
- `git log --diff-filter=M --numstat v2.7.0..HEAD -- changes DECISIONS.md`: 5 commits, additions only (8,8,5+35,5+37,5+20; 0 deletions). Append-only held. *checked*

- "Append-only was broken": the 5 commits only add lines.
- "A fresh session cannot resume from the newest handoff": the 1111 handoff is complete on Next Steps and Kickoff, within the limits of TR2 and TR8. Not read for gaps in the Phase 5 state.
- No trail text was found telling a later agent to skip a gate or trust a source.
- BUG-177 describes what happened (commit, amend, `c565b27`), not a hope. I did not check the other nine records.

## Not examined
- The ten newest bug records except BUG-177; the earlier two handoffs in full; retros content; `changes/` of v2.6.2..v2.7.0; reviews' `## Outcome` sections; `~/.config/fyr/feedback.jsonl` (outside the checkout, so I cannot say if a correction was logged and never acted on); each graduated row's cited sentence (only the tests were looked up).

body:
# Recon — harness-audit TS (2026-10-25)

## Status: COMPLETE

Scope: technical and vendored skills at c4885ae. Content is on-stack (Go, TanStack Start, GCP); no other cloud is recommended (EKS/AKS appear only in "when NOT to use"). Catalog baseline all PASS. Vendored pins: pin not re-checked.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| TS1 | med | skills/find-skills/SKILL.md:100 | Vendored Step 6 offers `npx skills add <owner/repo@skill> -g -y`: unpinned CLI, `-y` skips the prompt, `-g` writes into the global skill directory. VENDORED.md:~60 says "pin the CLI's version and read its prompt; never `-y`", and the context routes installs through the checkout. Verbatim text contradicts the harness rule (lines 29, 56, 90, 140 also run bare `npx skills`). VENDORED.md's note says the old Step 6 edit "now lives in the context" but the contradicting text still ships. | operator's choice: add a note row in VENDORED.md Notes (like the catalog notes) that the model must not run `-y`/`-g`, or fork under another name; do not edit in place |
| TS2 | med | skills/gcloud-setup/SKILL.md:23,69,95-96,104-105 | Teaches `gcloud config set project/compute/region/zone` (machine-wide state in `~/.config/gcloud`), while the google-catalog router (SKILL.md step 5) forbids `gcloud config set` and demands `--project` per command.
