## Risks

- **A doc that names a moved `path:line`.** The only one in a current spec, guide or deploy record is `SPEC-fyr-check`'s example, handled in Phase 1 (D8). `fyr check` catches any other in tracked Markdown.
- **A spec goes stale on a phase's commit.** A spec's code is every existing path its inline spans name, directories included (`internal/check/specs.go:71-95`). A commit under a named directory therefore stales it even when its `Code:` line does not name the split file. Step 4 of the procedure re-stamps it (D8).
- **Test time.** `cmd/fyr` takes about 13 minutes under `-race` on a one-CPU box, once per phase. The per-step `go test ./cmd/fyr/` runs without `-race`.

## Decisions

D1 — 2026-10-26 — The operator approved the audit's items 1–15 "as plan":
- items 2–8 are this plan's phases;
- item 9 and `TestRefreshCatalogScript` are Follow-ups;
- item 11 (cyclomatic complexity) stays a reading-only limit;
- item 12 adds vendored files to the rule's exemption (done, ADR-066 amended);
- items 13–14 are deferred to the release gate;
- item 15 (`~/.claude/rules/`) is the operator's.

— by: the operator's words "go all approved as plan", 2026-10-26.

D2 — 2026-10-26 — A grouped `var`, `const` or `type` block is one declaration. It moves whole and is never split. Where an audit sends its members to two files, the block stays in the source file:
- `internal/brain/import.go:61-72`;
- `internal/search/reconcile.go:26-31`;
- `internal/dream/run.go`'s `cliTimeout`/`killGrace`/`keepFailed` block, which also settles that audit's contradiction.

A block whose members all go to one file moves there, for example `maxImportBytes`/`maxImportFiles` to `import_guard.go`. `declmove` enforces this: it panics before writing any file when two members name two targets (checked on a scratch copy). — by: cold read round 1 (G1, Q1)

D3 — 2026-10-26 — The proof sees comments, and the move keeps them.
- `declsum` prints one line per declaration and one per comment group.
- `declmove` carries a detached comment with the declaration after it, and keeps the source's whole head up to the end of its imports.

Validated on scratch copies of `internal/harness/catalog_test.go`, whose lines 24–31 are a detached block that documents `CATALOG_DIR` and `CATALOG_WRITE`:
- old move with old sum: EQUAL, despite the block being lost (the gap);
- old move with new sum: DIFF;
- new move with new sum: EQUAL, with the block kept.

No file in scope has a build tag. — by: cold read round 1 (G2, Q2)

D4 — 2026-10-26 — `declmove` names a method `Type.method`, so a method and a type or function of the same name (`Summary.acc` and type `acc` in `internal/metrics/show.go`) go where each is listed. Checked on a scratch copy. — by: cold read round 1 (G8d)

D5 — 2026-10-26 — The audits (INDEX and items 2–8) and the exact sources of both tools are stored as the record `PLAN-2026-10-26-1133-recon-the-code-modularity-audit-and-the-move-too`. A phase never depends on one box's `.agents/scratch/`. — by: cold read round 1 (G8b, G9, G10)

D6 — 2026-10-26 — The old copy for `declsum` is `git show HEAD:<path> > .agents/scratch/modularity/orig/<file>`, taken before the phase's first move. — by: cold read round 1 (G8c, Q7)

D7 — 2026-10-26 — Verification follows the rule's item 5 literally, step by step: after each target file, build, vet, the package's tests and the `declsum` diff. The full `-race` line runs once per phase. — by: cold read round 1 (G7, Q4)

D8 — 2026-10-26 — Specs and `fyr check`.
- A `line` finding is fixed in the move's commit. Phase 1 changes `SPEC-fyr-check`'s example `cmd/fyr/main.go:171` to `cmd/fyr/main.go:1`, the package doc's first line, which stays in `main.go`.
- `spec-stale` can only show after the move's commit. Each such spec is then re-read and re-stamped with `fyr record edit <id> --status current` in a commit of its own, as 44df74a did.
- `fyr check` exit 0 after that commit is the phase's verify.
- The list of specs is `fyr check`'s output, never computed in advance, because a spec's code includes every directory its spans name (`internal/check/specs.go:71-95`).

— by: cold read round 1 (G3, G4, Q3)

D9 — 2026-10-26 — In `TestOneRepositoryName` (`cmd/fyr/main_test.go:1433`), `cmd/fyr/main.go` is replaced, not supplemented, by the file that receives `runAdopt` and its clone URL. The change is made in the move's commit. — by: cold read round 1 (G6, Q6)

D10 — 2026-10-26 — Gold rows 36, 38 and 39 of `cmd/fyr/testdata/recall.tsv` name `cmd/fyr/main.go`. Phase 1 repoints each to the file that `git grep -l -F` finds holding its phrase after the move, in the move's commit. `TestRecall` is a measurement, skipped without `FYR_RECALL=1` (`cmd/fyr/recall_test.go:291`), so no gate would catch a stale row. — by: cold read round 1 (G5, Q5)

D11 — 2026-10-26 — The old Phase 7 is split into Phases 7a–7e, one package (or, for `internal/harness`, one file) per session. Two further rules:
- Phase 7a reads `TestNoTmpInHarnessProse`'s walk before naming new files.
- The `catalog_test.go:N-M` comments in `internal/eval/{procs_linux,guard,creds}_test.go` cite the run kit's own test file, which 8374f9c ported; no phase touches them (a Follow-up).

— by: cold read round 1 (G10, Q8)

D12 — 2026-10-26 — The plan cites R4: imports per package are unchanged by a move. Its Risks no longer name the `fyr eval` plan, which is closed. — by: cold read round 1 (G8a, G9)

## Follow-ups

- **Functions over 50 lines** (audit item 9; `.agents/scratch/funclen.txt`): their own plan, each split a code change with its tests.
- **`TestRefreshCatalogScript`:** the closures into a struct, then the split.
- **A `GUIDE-eval` row for `rules/code-modularity.md`,** for the release gate (AGENTS.md § Release).
- **The three `catalog_test.go:N-M` comments in `internal/eval`:** qualify them as the run kit's file, or cite its test names (D11).

--- owner: main date: 2026-10-27 --- # Plan — the audit's operator choices: registration, child environments, eval, redactor, skills, map (2026-10-27) Status: written 2026-10-27 from the decisions of `HANDOFF-2026-10-27-1042-handoff-2026-10-27-every-audit-session-row-appro` (§ Key Decisions). The cold read is done (`REVIEW-2026-10-27-1117-review-cold-read-of-plan-2026-10-27-audit-choice`, answered by D13–D31 and O1–O2). Approved 2026-10-27 ("go all approved"): O1 and O2 are answered by D32 and D33, and the phases were cut from 11 to 8 sessions by D34–D37 (Phases 2 and 3 merged, Phases 8 and 10 merged, Phase 9 struck, Phase 11 moved to `PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-cleanup`). A value check at d3b0c11 (D38–D43, the operator's "GO ALL APPROVED WITH YOUR RECOMMENDATIONS") then cut it again: Phases 7 and 8 run next; Phases 1, 2, 4 (the dream half) and 5 are held behind O4; Phase 6, Phase 4's git half, row 14, TS39 and G28 are struck. It runs after `/preflight v3.1.0` and after `PLAN-2026-10-27-funclen` is closed (§ Session order). Closed 2026-10-28: absorbed into `PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` (`PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-choices` D47; the ledger's D1, D8). Every box left unticked here is marked `[-]`, superseded by that plan; this record is history, and the ledger is the only list of remaining work. ## Why The 2026-10-27 audit (`REVIEW-2026-10-27-harness-audit`) left 21 rows of work for the operator. They were presented as the closing table of the audit session, summarized in `HANDOFF-2026-10-27-1038-handoff-2026-10-27-funclen-plan-written-full-aud` § Next Steps. The operator answered every row "go all approved" on 2026-10-27. `HANDOFF-2026-10-27-1042-…` records each answer by row number. This plan builds rows 2–4, 6–10 and 13–21 as recorded there: - Row 1 is the funclen plan, and row 5 is the release. - Row 11 (TR18) and row 12 were settled with no work. - Row 17's leftovers, row 18's WS49, row 19's G26, G27, G29, G30 and G33, and row 20 belong to `PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-cleanup`. § Scope repeats every item, so this plan does not depend on the table's scratch copy. Requirements touched: - **R3:** who the nightly dream reads (row 2; O1). - **R4:** the brain and metrics stores that rows 3 and 14 read. - **R7:** `fyr record` (row 18, SD42 and SD47). - **R8:** what leaves the machine. Rows 2 and 4 narrow it; nothing widens it. - **R10:** one behaviour on Linux and macOS. The allow-list must hold on both (D27). ## Terms - **Finding IDs** are the audit's: C context and docs, WS workflow skills, TS tool skills, AG agents, IN the binary and installer, SD the stores and the dream, TR the trail, G coverage gaps; `-S` marks a simplification. Each ID's finding, file:line and evidence is in `REVIEW-2026-10-27-harness-audit` and its recon `PLAN-2026-10-27-recon-harness-audit`. Row 16's IDs are in the re-audit, `REVIEW-2026-10-27-1037-harness-audit-2-fyr-at-9aa2afc-58-of-63-fixed-20`. - **Row N** is the closing table's row, as `HANDOFF-2026-10-27-1042-…` § Key Decisions numbers it. - **who:** the last item of a box's `verify:` clause, `AI`, `user` or `both`. - **Open:** a question only the operator settles, with the implementer's default (`feature` skill § Decisions). - **The funclen plan** is `PLAN-2026-10-27-funclen`; its D-rows are cited as "funclen D". - **A place:** a machine with the harness installed (`SPEC-fyr-delivery` § The model). - **The SD24 test** is the `trail.Command` test that pins the dropped repository variables (`git grep -n SD24 -- internal/trail`). - **BUG-111's procedure:** a vendored pin is written only after `git archive | tar -x` into scratch and `diff -r` against the directory (AGENTS.md § Rules for working here). ## Scope In, by row of the closing table: - **Rows 2–3 (SD19, SD49):** registration becomes opt-in. `fyr index --register` writes a marker under `.git/`. Every cross-project consumer takes only registered roots: the dream's `--all` targets, `fyr search --global`, `brain.ImportGlobal` and the metrics trail join (D3, D15). An explicit `fyr dream --project ` needs no marker (D16). An ADR and the R3 edit (O1). - **Row 4 (SD25):** the dreamer's `agy` gets an allow-listed environment. One real dream run follows (D7, D8). - **Row 4 (IN44):** eval prints each row's `setup` and `check` hashes before it runs. `SPEC-fyr-eval` § Known limits gains a line (D9, D22). - **Row 6 (WS40):** strike `retro` Step 6's from-another-project apply branch, and `distill --global`'s direct write. Both queue a global `proposal`. An ADR. - **Row 7 (AG25):** `harness-audit` stores the explorer's own draft. Its dispatches stop setting the artifact's path, title or frontmatter. - **Row 8 (C37):** relabel the README map's experience node (§ Interfaces). An ADR, the map and the docs, in one commit (AGENTS.md rule 3). - **Row 9 (SD28):** dream news dropped by the cap is offered again. O2: the approved mechanism does not work as worded; D33 settles it. - **Row 13:** eval's own opens under the row's log directory go through an `os.Root`. `trail.Command`'s environment becomes an allow-list (D6, D7, D21). - **Row 14:** metrics scans `agent_name` and `parent_conversation_id` as nullable, with a test. - **Row 15:** the `preflight` row of `GUIDE-eval` tells the agent to wait for or stop its background tasks. - **Row 16, SD60a only:** it lands in Phase 5 (D24). The rest of row 16 moved to the cleanup plan (D36). - **Row 18:** - SD41: Docker PAT, Terraform Cloud and Slack app-level token needles. - SD42: `record add` and `record edit` warn, never refuse. - SD47: accepted, with one sentence in `SPEC-fyr-record` § Load. - IN39: documented as the binary's exception. - TS39: frontend `engines` becomes `>=24`. - TS40: struck with no edit (D11). - **Row 19 (G28):** `context/dev-setup.md` declares stacks other than Go and TypeScript out of scope. - **Row 21:** one line each in `DEPLOY-remote` for the two accepted risks. D34 — 2026-10-27 — Phase 3 merges into Phase 2: the same registered-root filter at one more consumer, plus a two-column scan fix. — by: the operator's "Go all approved", 2026-10-27, over the scope table's row 2. D35 — 2026-10-27 — Phase 9 (row 10, WS45, `grilling` → `stress-test`) is struck: cosmetic, it spent the skill listing's last 102 bytes, and it cost three eval runs. `grilling` stays vendored as is. — by: the operator's "Go all approved", 2026-10-27, over the scope table's row 3. D36 — 2026-10-27 — Phase 11 (row 16 except SD60a, which stays in Phase 5) moves to `PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-cleanup` § Follow-ups, where its Phase 1 triage keeps or strikes each item. The table offered "move or strike"; move is taken, the choice that loses nothing. — by: the operator's "Go all approved", 2026-10-27, over the scope table's row 4; move by implementer. D37 — 2026-10-27 — Phase 10 merges into Phase 8: both are skill and doc edits with `/review --docs`. Phase 10's one-commit rule (AGENTS.md rule 3) holds inside the merged session. Phases 4–7 are not merged, because each is a trust boundary with its own security read. — by: the operator's "Go all approved", 2026-10-27, over the scope table's row 5. D38 — 2026-10-27 — Value check at d3b0c11 (`.agents/scratch/audit-choices-value-check.md`): Phases 1, 2, 4's dream half and 5 improve only `fyr dream`, and the dream has never run on this box (no fyr timer in `systemctl --user list-timers --all`, no `~/.config/systemd/user/fyr*`, no `~/.config/fyr/dream.log`). They are held behind O4, neither built nor struck. Their findings are real: `internal/dream/dream.go:124` takes every `brain.Scopes` entry; `internal/brain/search.go:105` syncs any touched checkout's `trail.jsonl`; `collect.go:153` drops oldest first and `run.go:132` stores `t0`. — by: the operator's "GO ALL APPROVED WITH YOUR RECOMMENDATIONS", 2026-10-27; the hold is the recommendation's own condition, which the operator did not answer. D39 — 2026-10-27 — Phases 7 and 8 run next, in that order. Phase 7: `internal/redact/redact.go` has no Docker, Terraform Cloud or Slack app-level needle, and no `cmd/fyr/record*.go` calls the redactor, while `trail.jsonl` is committed and pushed. Phase 8: `skills/retro/SKILL.md:151` and `skills/distill/SKILL.md:101,133` let another project write the harness checkout, against AGENTS.md rule 1; `README.md:81` omits `brain.db` from the contract map. — by: the same turn. D40 — 2026-10-27 — Phase 4's git half (row 13's trail half) is struck: `internal/trail/trail.go:154` already drops the 11 repository-locating variables (SD24), so an allow-list adds only `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`/`COUNT`, and it risks breaking git for an operator who relies on another variable. `trail.Command` keeps its deny-list. — by: the same turn. D41 — 2026-10-27 — Phase 6 is struck. IN44's hash is printed, never enforced, and useful only to someone who compares it with an old record. The `w.logs` root guards a parent-directory race against an agent that already runs as the operator's own user (`w.sb` sits inside `w.dir`), while `openRegular` keeps `O_NOFOLLOW` and the sole-link check. Row 15's `preflight` prompt line moves to the cleanup plan's preflight-timeout follow-up. — by: the same turn. D42 — 2026-10-27 — Row 14 (NULL `agent_name`/`parent_conversation_id`) is struck as speculative: a copy of this box's `conversation_summaries.db` held 9 rows and 0 NULLs in either column (the copy deleted after the count). — by: the same turn. D43 — 2026-10-27 — TS39 and G28 are struck. Node 22 is LTS until 2027-04, so `>=22.12` excludes nothing that `>=24` fixes. G28's line would spend part of the hand-written context's last 186 bytes on little behaviour. — by: the same turn. D44 — 2026-10-27 — The Docker needle takes `dckr_oat_` beside `dckr_pat_`: Docker's own Hub API spec documents both as one kind, access tokens. The Slack needle's `xapp-` also covers the rotating `xoxe.xapp-` the same Slack page names. Each length is the vendor's shortest documented example, which `TestVendorDocExamples` pins. — by: implementer. D45 — 2026-10-27 — The warning judges a new title too: the title is exported with the body (`internal/brain/export.go`'s wire line). The Phase 7 security review's medium finding (`REVIEW-2026-10-27-2156-security-review-phase-7-of-audit-choices-sd41-ne`). Its lows (the warning's volume, 206 of 1,228 bodies in this repo; naming the needle; the Slack family `xoxe-`/`xoxc-`/`xoxd-`/`xwfp-`; eval and import writing unchecked) go to the ledger's inventory (D47). — by: implementer, answering the review. D46 — 2026-10-27 — O4 answered: the dream phases do not wait for the operator's client machines. Each is verified in a sandbox: a scratch home whose index holds fixture projects only, with the dream run end to end. That run decides keep or strike in the ledger's inventory (D47). It replaces the operator's earlier "Not yet — defer". — by: the operator, 2026-10-27: "On the dream. Make a test in a sandbox so you can verify. DONT WAIT FOR THE CLIENTS". D47 — 2026-10-27 — After Phase 7, every unfinished item in the trail moves to ONE plan record, the ledger: this plan's Phase 8, Done and the held dream phases; `PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-cleanup`; open bugs; follow-ups; handoff Next Steps; and D45's deferred lows. Each item gets a value check at HEAD and names the eval or test that verifies it. Kept items are planned, the rest struck or deferred. The ledger is the only list of remaining work, and this plan closes with a pointer to it. A release (`/preflight`) follows the ledger's last phase. — by: the operator, 2026-10-27 ("1 file that all tasks/phases are in … this is the only truth", "One plan record", "When this is done cut a new version"). Rejected: - Registration by a committed file (`.agents/registered`): a clone carries it, which is SD19 itself. - Filtering only at `register`, or only inside `ListProjects` and `brain.Scopes`: the first misses `brain.Scopes`, and the second cannot log the skip (D3, D15). - A new verb to list former registrations (D17). - A refusal when an eval script's hash changed (D9). - Refusing a record body the redactor would change: the operator chose warn. - Editing `skills/grilling` in place: a vendored skill is never edited (AGENTS.md). - Merging Phases 4–7: each is a trust boundary with its own security read (D37).

# Plan — audit cleanup: the deferred lows, the deferred gaps and the older follow-ups   (2026-10-27)

Status: written 2026-10-27; cold read `REVIEW-2026-10-27-1117-review-cold-read-of-plan-2026-10-27-audit-cleanu` answered (D3, D4). It waits for the operator's approval. It runs last, after `/preflight v3.1.0`, `PLAN-2026-10-27-funclen` and `PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-choices` (that plan's § Session order). Its Phase 1 re-triages every item against the head of that day and puts the table to the operator. The recommendations below are provisional until then. Closed 2026-10-28: absorbed into `PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` (`PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-choices` D47; the ledger's D1, D8). Every box left unticked here is marked `[-]`, superseded by that plan; this record is history, and the ledger is the only list of remaining work.

## Why

The 2026-10-27 audit (`REVIEW-2026-10-27-harness-audit`) and its fix (`PLAN-2026-10-27-harness-audit-fix`, § Scope "Out, `defer`") left deferred items. The closing table of the audit session, given in chat and summarized in `HANDOFF-2026-10-27-1038-handoff-2026-10-27-funclen-plan-written-full-aud` § Next Steps, sorted them into its rows 17–20. This plan's § Scope reproduces every item of those rows, so it does not depend on the scratch copy of that table. The operator approved every row on 2026-10-27 ("go all approved"; `HANDOFF-2026-10-27-1042-handoff-2026-10-27-every-audit-session-row-appro` § Key Decisions):

- **Row 17:** the deferred lows fold into the funclen phases where a file is touched anyway, and the rest go into a post-release plan. O3 below recommends folding none.
- **Row 18:** WS49 deferred.
- **Row 19:** G26, G27, G29, G30 and G33 deferred.
- **Row 20:** re-triaged after the release.

This plan is that post-release plan. The planning session's Kickoff named its scope.

Requirements touched, by item (no wording changes; an item whose fix would need one goes to the operator as a proposed `REQUIREMENTS.md` edit, never a box here):

- R3 (the dream and its timer): SD30, SD34, SD35, SD36, SD-S4.
- R4 (the stores): SD-S6, SD-S7, the metrics file join.
- R8 and R9 (the zip place; ADR-038): IN38.
- REQUIREMENTS § Known limits (the 24,000-byte block): C-S6, C-S7, and any context line.

## Terms

- **ID prefixes** are the audit's areas (`skills/harness-audit/references/areas.md`): C context and docs, WS workflow skills, TS tool skills, AG agents, IN the binary and installer, SD the stores and the dream, TR the trail, G coverage gaps. `-S<n>` marks a simplification. Every ID's finding, file:line and evidence is in the record `PLAN-2026-10-27-recon-harness-audit` (its Final IDs table, then the area briefs).
- **The crossing:** every place having moved from `sh-agent` to `fyr` (ADR-062). BUG-161's rule: removing migration code waits for the operator's word that every place has crossed.
- **who:** the last item of a box's `verify:` clause, `AI`, `user` or `both`.
- **Open:** a question only the operator can settle, with the default the implementer follows (`feature` skill § Decisions).

## Scope

In, each with a provisional recommendation. `fix` says how, `strike` says why, `yours` means only the operator can decide. Phase 1 confirms each one at the head of that day.

**Deferred audit lows (row 17), plus four the row's list missed.** WS51, G32 and TR-S2 are in the fix plan's defer list but not in row 17. SD-S9's recommendation was "none". Each phase is the one that implements the item if Phase 1 keeps it.

| ID | What (audit wording, shortened) | Provisional | Phase |
|---|---|---|---|
| C41 | size headroom: context, skill listing, block | strike: the size tests pin it; re-measure only | — |
| C-S6 | AGENTS.md's Rules section restates the lint | fix: a pointer to `inventory.go` and its `TestLint*` | 6 |
| C-S7 | the context's roles paragraph restates agent artifact rules | fix: trim; it frees context bytes | 6 |
| C-S8 | the ROADMAP comment restates the context | fix: trim | 6 |
| WS51 | `feature`, `codebase-design` and `spec` triggers overlap on "design" | strike: a fix spends listing bytes, and no misfire is recorded | — |
| WS-S5 | the dreamer dispatch is written out in both `retro` and `distill` | fix: one home in `retro`, a pointer from `distill` | 6 |
| WS-S6 | `init-project` Step 5 is "Nothing to set up" | strike: renumbering breaks Step citations | — |
| WS-S7 | `preflight` Step 2 item 2 is one 1.5 KB paragraph | fix: split into bullets, same words | 6 |
| TS43 | `distroless/static-debian12` may be dated | fix if a newer tag is published, checked at the time | 6 |
| TS-S2 | GKE guidance twice (fork and catalog) | strike: the router's precedence row already decides | — |
| AG28 | `GUIDE-eval` has no `inject-*` row (a planted instruction the agent must not follow) for explorer, verifier, dreamer, and no `lane-*` row (the agent stays in its lane) for five agents | fix: the rows, then run them | 6 |
| AG29 | shell-less agents told to `mkdir` | fix: wording, after checking each agent's `tools:` | 6 |
| IN36 | global `--repo` silently ignored by verbs that do not read it | yours: warn on stderr (recommended), or refuse; the D-row lists the verbs (`run_dispatch.go:28-32, 126` has the precedents) and `main.go:73`'s usage line | 2 |
| IN38 | `update --from-zip --dry-run` unpacks beside the zip; a kill leaves it | strike: IN10 put the unpack beside the zip on purpose (`cmd/fyr/update_zip.go:18-22`), a dry run must not create `~/.config/fyr`, and the sweep runs only on a real run (`:100-103`); a `DEPLOY-remote` line names the leftover `zip-*` directory | — |
| IN40 | the loader reads `workflows/`, which the embed and zip do not carry | fix: drop `workflows/` from `loadDocs` (`inventory.go:144`) and `checkManagedTree` (`:48, 69, 100`), so a stray directory is ignored, not refused; the comments at `plan.go:36-37` and `source.go:19`; the 3 fixtures (`pathguard_test.go`, `source_test.go`, `auditfix_test.go`); README and AGENTS.md § Layout if they name it | 2 |
| IN47 | the creds scan skips any file with ELF, Mach-O or Java magic | strike: a SPEC-fyr-eval Known-limits line | 3 |
| IN48 | eval's credential patterns are a second list beside `redact` | fix as a test only: for each eval kind (`internal/eval/creds.go:18-30`), its sample run through `redact.Redact` must change; no new `redact` API, and eval keeps its per-kind counts | 3 |
| IN-S4, IN-S5 | metrics flag ownership hard-coded (`verb_metrics.go:155`) beside the `flags:` table (`ctx_verbs.go:78-90`) | fix: the table wins; the error text and exit code for a flag outside its subverb stay, pinned by the existing tests | 2 |
| IN-S6 | `ctx` holds ~40 flat per-verb fields | strike: a wide refactor for no defect | — |
| IN-S7 | `DirSource`, `OriginString`, `ParseOrigin`, `SaveState` exported, no outside caller | fix for three: unexport `DirSource`, `OriginString` and `ParseOrigin`; `SaveState` stays, because `cmd/fyr` tests call it (`usage_test.go:129`, `zip_update_test.go:90, 106`, `checkout_test.go:24, 126`); `State.Origin` stays | 2 |
| IN-S8 | two git-env policies (eval's `withoutGit`, `trail.Command`) | strike: they serve different children. Eval's `withoutGit` (`internal/eval/guard.go:130`) passes the row's whole environment to the sandbox `fyr` (`row_env.go:33-41`) and drops `GIT_*`; `trail.Command`'s allow-list (audit-choices Phase 3) is for fyr's own git reads | — |
| IN-S9 | three readers of CLI files, one uncapped | fix: one capped reader | 3 |
| SD23 | the global query reads `~/.config/fyr` sources whole each time | strike: 414 files reconcile in 36 ms (the audit's measurement) | — |
| SD30 | the dream prompt's left-out line (`internal/dream/prompt.go:71`) cost 11.6 KB of the 256 KB prompt | fix: name the first N, count the rest | 4 |
| SD34 | the Linux scratch-home timer cannot load (reasoned, not run) | fix or strike from one `fyr dream --install-timer --home .agents/scratch/<name>` run on this Linux box | 4 |
| SD35 | the OAuth copy is left after a killed run until the next run | strike: 0700 and swept by the next run; a Known-limits line | 4 |
| SD36 | the service unit has no `TimeoutStartSec` | fix: one unit line, with the render test | 4 |
| SD37 | `AgyConversationText` creates `~/.config/fyr` during a dry run | strike: its window needs a place that has not crossed the rename (fix plan D14) | — |
| SD44 | a linked worktree of a separate-git-dir checkout gets its own brain scope | strike: a `SPEC-fyr-record` line | 5 |
| SD53 | an undated Antigravity conversation is read only once by metrics ingest | fix if a test over a copied fixture database shows a later update lost, else strike | 5 |
| SD54 | metrics matches a conversation's generation times to its steps by position | fix: match by ID if the source has one, else strike | 5 |
| SD-S3 | two protobuf wire walkers (`internal/search/export.go:84-146`, `internal/search/dream_proto.go:23-98`) | fix: one walker with a leaf callback | 5 |
| SD-S4 | `timer.go`'s legacy migration code | yours: remove once every place has crossed (the operator's word) | 4 |
| SD-S6 | `trail.jsonl` hashed up to three times per write (`internal/brain`) | fix | 5 |
| SD-S7 | `parseTrail` (`internal/brain`) used by one test | fix: move it into the test | 5 |
| SD-S9 | `stepsOf` N+1 | strike: the audit's own "none" | — |
| TR19 | three handoffs recommended against a recorded memory | strike: BUG-186 records it | — |
| TR23 | BUG-186's correction has no feedback record | yours: a global `feedback` record is the real store's | — |
| TR-S2 | handoffs copy carried items instead of linking | strike: the handoff skill's carried-items rule is a separate design | — |
| G32 | operation outside Cloud Run | yours: defer again (recommended), or a line in `operate-gcp` | — |

**Row 18:** WS49 (`preflight` runs the verifier twice). Recommendation: yours. Step 2 could reuse Step 1's log when HEAD is the commit Step 1 verified and the tree is clean, or the item can be struck. Phase 6.

**Row 19:** G26 (migrations beyond Cloud SQL), G27 (a requirement's number has no test tier), G29 (no tier between a full scaffold and unscaffolded), G30 (no release shape for a library, CLI or static site), G33 (no branch or PR policy). Recommendation: yours. Strike each with no edit, the way G28 is declared in `context/dev-setup.md` by audit-choices Phase 8, unless the operator now wants one built. Building one is a new Feature, not a row here.

**Row 20, the older follow-ups no record carries** (TR's Left undone):

| Item | Provisional | Phase |
|---|---|---|
| `uninstall`/`--remove-timer` leave an old-named unit; `status` does not name a leftover `sh-agent` on PATH (CHANGE-2026-10-25-1108) | fix: one `status` warning line; strike the unit part if every place crossed | 2 |
| `fyr check`: it does not check the dream summary's counts, nor the context's skill-relative script paths (TR's Left undone in `PLAN-2026-10-27-recon-harness-audit`) | fix, with Phase 1's D-row naming each check | 3 |
| `fyr eval --parallel N` | strike: no measured need | — |
| pruning old eval sandboxes | yours: a new flag is a design question; recommended a Known-limits line instead | 3 |
| metrics: drop the file join — `joinEvents`' reads of `feedback.jsonl` and of a project trail still in files, beside `brain.ForMetrics` (`internal/metrics/events_join.go:56-68`, `joinRoot`); not audit-choices Phase 2's registration gate | yours: needs the operator's word that every project migrated | 5 |
| AG17's "Write tool" wording (an agent body names a tool by a name its `tools:` list does not hold; the recon's TR section) | fix | 6 |
| funclen's follow-up: 77 long test functions | strike: struck by the operator from funclen (its D1 item 3) | — |
| funclen's follow-up: the documented gofmt command misses the root `*.go` | fix: `gofmt -l cmd internal *.go` (the glob is the root's files only, so `.agents/scratch` stays unwalked, BUG-048) in AGENTS.md, README.md:227, `skills/harness-audit/SKILL.md:36`, `skills/harness-audit/references/areas.md:36`, `agents/verifier/agent.md:28`, `GUIDE-testing` and `DEPLOY-local`; the changed skill and agent owe their `fyr eval` rows (`harness-audit-elsewhere`, `agent-verifier`) | 6 |

Out:

- Everything `PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-choices` builds.
- New behaviour for a G-gap (a new Feature if the operator wants one).
- Any item Phase 1 finds already fixed at its head; it is struck with the commit that fixed it.

Follow-ups noted, not built: none yet.

## Surfaces touched

Provisional, by phase. Phase 1 re-finds every location at its head:

- **Phase 2:** `cmd/fyr`, `internal/harness`.
- **Phase 3:** `internal/eval`, `internal/check`.
- **Phase 4:** `internal/dream`.
- **Phase 5:** `internal/metrics`, `internal/search`, `internal/brain`.
- **Phase 6:** `context/`, `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `skills/` (preflight, retro, distill, frontend or docker for TS43, harness-audit), `agents/`, and the `GUIDE-eval`, `GUIDE-testing` and `DEPLOY-local` records.

The evidence for each ID is in `PLAN-2026-10-27-recon-harness-audit` (its Final IDs table, then the briefs).

## Interfaces

No exported name, CLI verb or output changes, except:

- IN36, if the operator picks warn: `fyr: warning: --repo is ignored by <verb>` on stderr, exit status unchanged.
- IN40: `workflows/` is no longer read, and a stray one is ignored.
- IN-S7: three exported names of `internal/harness` become unexported; `SaveState` stays.
- The row-20 `status` line, if kept: `warning: <path> is an old sh-agent binary on PATH`.

Phase 1 writes, for every item it keeps, one D-row holding: the exact change; the test that fails without it, with its fixture named (a copied fixture database, never the real home, for SD53 and SD54); the doc file that describes it, or `none`; and the R-items above it touches. An item whose D-row cannot be written goes to the operator as `yours`. Later phases build only from those D-rows.

## Failure modes

- **A removal breaks an old place** (SD-S4, the row-20 unit part, the metrics file join): each waits for the operator's word that every place has crossed (BUG-161's rule). Without that word it is not done.
- **A trimmed context sentence loses a rule** (C-S7): `/review --docs` checks that every rule in the trimmed text still has a home.

## Trust boundaries and data handled

Due for `security`: IN48 (credential patterns, Phase 3). Else none: IN-S8 and IN38 are provisionally struck, and a Phase 1 answer that keeps either adds `security` to its phase.

## Verification

Tiers:

- **Unit:** `go test -race` at every checkpoint.
- **Scratch-home install** after a `cmd/` or `internal/` change.
- **Behavioural runs on Antigravity** (`fyr eval <row>`) for each changed skill, agent or the context. `fyr eval` is the one verb that does not take the trail's `--home`: it runs with `--fixture ~/sandbox/fyr-eval/fixture --home ~/sandbox/fyr-eval/home`, both outside every checkout (AGENTS.md § Testing; `GUIDE-testing` § 4).
- **`/review --docs`** over every phase that changes a command's output, a usage line, a spec or a doc, as well as `context/`, `skills/` or `agents/`.
- **Scratch-home install:** `go run ./cmd/fyr install --home .agents/scratch/home`, then `fyr status --home .agents/scratch/home`.

E2E criteria (yes/no):

1. Every item of § Scope ends as fixed (with a test or a doc line), struck with a reason, or answered by the operator. The plan's table says which, with the commit.
2. At Done, `go test -race -timeout 30m ./...` passes and the scratch-home install shows no warning.
3. Every `GUIDE-eval` row named by Phase 6 passes on Antigravity.

## Phases

- [x] Cold-reader check — one report (`REVIEW-2026-10-27-1117-review-cold-read-of-plan-2026-10-27-audit-cleanu`: design needs revision, implementation not ready; G1–G16, 14 questions, 6 blocking), every item answered: IN-S7, IN38, IN-S8, IN48 and the file join by the revised § Scope rows; the eval `--home` (G11), requirements (G14), terms (G16), record IDs (G10) and scratch evidence (G9) by § Terms, § Verification and § Why; the per-item design gaps (G5–G8, G12, G13, G15) by Phase 1's D-row duty in § Interfaces; sizing by D3 (Phase 4 split) — all in D4

Every Kickoff below says: every fyr call carries `--home .agents/scratch/home-trail`, except `fyr eval`, which carries `--fixture ~/sandbox/fyr-eval/fixture --home ~/sandbox/fyr-eval/home` (§ Verification).

### Phase 1 — re-triage (row 20) and the operator's answers
Needs the operator in the session: the Kickoff says ask, then wait.
- [-] Re-check every ID of § Scope at the head of that day, from `PLAN-2026-10-27-recon-harness-audit` and the tree: still present (file:line), already fixed (commit), or changed. — verify: one line per ID in `.agents/scratch/cleanup-triage.md`, AI. — expect: every ID has a state. — superseded by `PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` (2026-10-28): every unfinished item of this plan is a row of its § Inventory, kept, struck or deferred there
- [-] Put one numbered table to the operator (global context § Operator): one row per open item, the recommendation updated by the re-check, plus one row asking whether every place has crossed (§ Terms) for SD-S4, the row-20 unit part and the metrics file join. — verify: the operator's answer in their own turn, user. — expect: an answer per row. — superseded by `PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` (2026-10-28): every unfinished item of this plan is a row of its § Inventory, kept, struck or deferred there
- [-] Record the answers as D-rows (`by:` the operator's words), each kept item's D-row in § Interfaces' form; strike what is struck with its reason; drop a phase left with no item (`[-]`, with why). — verify: `fyr record get PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-cleanup`, AI. — expect: no `Provisional` column entry left without a D-row. — superseded by `PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` (2026-10-28): every unfinished item of this plan is a row of its § Inventory, kept, struck or deferred there
- [-] Checkpoint — expect: the plan updated, ROADMAP Next updated, commit and push, the handoff with Phase 2's Kickoff — evidence: <command and exit status>, <date> — superseded by `PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` (2026-10-28): every unfinished item of this plan is a row of its § Inventory, kept, struck or deferred there
```text
Project: /home/kesokaj/workspace/styrman-harness. Read AGENTS.md, then the newest handoff (fyr record list --kind handoff | head -1, then fyr record get it), then fyr record get PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-cleanup; do Phase 1 — the re-triage. Every fyr call carries --home .agents/scratch/home-trail.
Standing approvals (closed set): reading the tree and the trail; the plan record's edits; ROADMAP Next; commit and push; the closing handoff. Never: code, a test, a skill or doc edit, a REQUIREMENTS.md edit, a release, a real-home install, anything outside this repository. The operator's answers to the table are theirs to give in their own turn: ask, then wait.
Done when: every row is answered and recorded as a D-row. Then write the handoff with Phase 2's Kickoff and end the session.
```

D1 — 2026-10-27 — Scope is the deferred audit lows not folded into funclen, G26, G27, G29, G30, G33, WS49 and row 20's re-triage. WS51, G32, TR-S2 and SD-S9 are added because the fix plan deferred them and row 17's list missed them. — by: the planning session's Kickoff (the operator, 2026-10-27), and implementer for the four.

D3 — 2026-10-27 — Phases follow packages, as the funclen plan does: `cmd/fyr` with `internal/harness`, eval with check, the dream alone, the three stores, then text. — supersedes the first draft's one phase for four packages — by: cold read round 1.

D4 — 2026-10-27 — The cold read (`REVIEW-2026-10-27-1117-review-cold-read-of-plan-2026-10-27-audit-cleanu`) is answered in the plan: IN-S7 keeps `SaveState`; IN38 and IN-S8 are provisionally struck; IN48 is a test only; IN40 ignores a stray `workflows/`; the metrics file join is defined; `fyr eval` takes its own `--home` and `--fixture`; full record IDs; requirements cited per item; § Terms defines the vocabulary; the evidence is the recon record, not scratch; Phase 1 writes each kept item's D-row in § Interfaces' form, with its test, fixture and doc. — by: cold read round 1.

Open: O3 — row 17 said "fold into the funclen phases where a file is touched anyway". `PLAN-2026-10-27-funclen` § Interfaces promises splits that change no behaviour and no exported name, reviewed as extract-function only (its D3, D11, D12). Every row-17 item changes behaviour, an exported name, or a function the split is moving. Folding one in would break that promise and the review it rests on. Recommended: fold none; all go here. — default: fold none. The funclen phases run as written unless the operator says otherwise.

Rejected:

- Building a G-gap here: each is a new Feature (D1).
- One phase for all code, or one for the four stores: too much for one session (D3).

## Follow-ups

From the `/preflight v3.1.0` gate (2026-10-27). Each is a finding left with this plan as its owner in its review record's `## Outcome`. Phase 1 re-triages each with the rest:

- `internal/search/open_unix.go:182`: a conversation file is opened before its type is checked, so a device file is opened before it is refused. Check the type before opening and keep the check after it. Source: `REVIEW-2026-10-27-1556-security-review-v3-1-0-gate-part-c-search-brain`, low.
- `cmd/fyr/eval.go:257`: off Linux, no process check runs before ingest, so on macOS a stray process could swap the sandbox home before ingest. Source: `REVIEW-2026-10-27-1556-security-review-v3-1-0-gate-part-d-cmd-dream-eva`, low. That review's finding 2 also proposes a hardening: scan a lockfile-backed `node_modules` for the real token's exact bytes.
- `internal/trail/dirty.go`: `Dirty` assumes its root is the top level. Resolve the top level inside `Dirty`, or refuse another root. Source: `REVIEW-2026-10-27-1601-security-review-v3-1-0-gate-fixes-round-2-fb335e`, low.
- `internal/harness/dryrun_dir_test.go`: pin that the real run still saves the manifest through `saveOnError` when a directory is in the way. Source: `REVIEW-2026-10-27-1623-review-bug-189-fix-31de61a-worktree-internal-har`, low.
- This plan's Phase 4 Kickoff approves `fyr dream --install-timer`/`--remove-timer` "against a scratch home", which on Linux reaches the real systemd user manager. Reword it before Phase 4 runs. Source: `REVIEW-2026-10-27-1556-security-review-v3-1-0-gate-trail-records-part-2`, low.
- BUG-179's record carries an unguarded restore command (`mv ~/.config/fyr …`). Mark it as history or guard it. Source: `REVIEW-2026-10-27-1556-security-review-v3-1-0-gate-trail-records-part-1`, low.
- `GUIDE-fyr-matrix` is stale. It cites `TestSymlinkedIndexRefused`, which is gone, and its "How the cells were run" line is 2026-10-25 at 3797da5. Update it from `TEST-2026-10-27-1720-verification-v3-1-0-gate-3c-matrix-re-run-v3-0-0`. Owner: documentation. Source: the v3.1.0 gate report, Step 4.
- `GUIDE-testing` § 3d: the warm records-and-files search bound was re-baselined from 250 ms to 400 ms in the v3.1.0 gate on the operator's delegation (2026-10-27). Profile the records half (`fyr search` with hits spends about 200 ms there, against 43 ms for the reconcile and 38-54 ms for `--kind code`) and find why d3db2ae's binary measured 90-177 ms on 2026-10-26 and 272-277 ms on 2026-10-27; tighten the bound again when it is understood. Source: `TEST-2026-10-27-1720-verification-v3-1-0-gate-v1-re-run-v3-0-0-75453d`, `TEST-2026-10-27-1805-verify-v3-1-0-gate-the-main-agent-s-tiers-corpus`.
- BUG-191 (fixed; its graduation open, BUG-183 recurred): graduate the rule "a `GUIDE-eval` row is added with its `TestSuiteHarness` `want` entry, and `go test ./internal/eval` runs before the commit" into a mechanism, so a record edit a Go test pins cannot be committed unknowingly. Then set BUG-183 and BUG-191 to `graduated`. Source: BUG-191.
- Eval rows' checks that write `> "$SB/..."` or read a store through `strings` follow a link the session planted under `$SB`, and `intact()` (`internal/eval/row.go:56`) checks only the three top-level directories. Eight rows write `> "$SB/…"` and about twenty read a store through `strings` (round 2's count; `smoke` was fixed in the gate, and its cell is the worked example: `pwd -P` on each directory, no link, no here-string): read through a variable or a pipe, and refuse a linked `.db`. Source: `REVIEW-2026-10-27-1845-security-review-v3-1-0-gate-records-fc78002-ff4c`, finding 1, low.
- Records repeat private values (DNS suffix, artifact host, host name, session ID) that a security read reports: put "name where a value sits, never the value" into `agents/security/agent.md` (and the handoff skill), with its eval row. Source: the same review, finding 3, low; the v3.1.0 handoff's Agent notes.
- BUG-190 (open): graduate its prevention rule into `agents/verifier/agent.md`, and `agents/security/agent.md` too: never open a file under the operator's real `~/.gemini/` or `~/.config/fyr/` in place, only a copy in `.agents/scratch/`. Add a `GUIDE-eval` row that proves it. The changed agents owe their `fyr eval` rows. Source: BUG-190, `REVIEW-2026-10-27-1809-security-review-v3-1-0-gate-trail-records-31de61`.
- The `smoke` eval row's check can be fooled by the session it checks: a hard link passes every link test; a process left running races the path checks because leftover processes are reaped after the row's check (`internal/eval/run.go:172-174`); and the rule set, skill count and store are taken from what the session left in `$SB`. Refuse a link count above 1, reap or check processes before step 13, and take the expected set from the clone. Source: `REVIEW-2026-10-27-2055-security-review-v3-1-0-gate-records-48ee381-3cd0`, three lows.
- The `preflight` eval row ran 1,076 s against agy's 1,200 s print ceiling (332 s at 4789d3e), and one run in two timed out. Shrink the row's task or raise the row's own timeout. Source: `TEST-2026-10-27-2031-eval-1-of-1-pass-at-a4e3cec`.
- `GUIDE-testing` § 3d's `go build -o .agents/scratch/fyr` lands inside a directory of that name where one exists. Name a file that cannot clash. Source: the v3.1.0 gate report, Step 4.
- `install` searched against the larger `.agents/scratch/home-trail` store takes 422–436 ms, outside § 3d's bound (which names `.agents/scratch/s`). Fold into the § 3d profiling item above. Source: the v3.1.0 gate report.
- Moved from `PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-choices` Phase 11 (its D36, 2026-10-27). These are the re-audit's lows, each stated in `REVIEW-2026-10-27-1037-harness-audit-2-fyr-at-9aa2afc-58-of-63-fixed-20`. Phase 1 re-triages them with the rest:
  - C44: one new ADR. It states that ADR-062 reversed ADR-003's derived agents, and that ADR-062 renamed ADR-006's `sh-agent` binary and `~/.config/sh-agent` to `fyr` and `~/.config/fyr`. It also states what each still holds. ADR-003 and ADR-006 stay unchanged (audit-choices D10).
  - WS52: reword `skills/feature/SKILL.md:17` to name the skills that state their own gates (audit-choices D12).
  - WS54: drop `skills/discover-skills/SKILL.md:12-16`'s two broad "When to use" bullets. WS52 and WS54 owe `fyr eval feature discover-skills`.
  - WS53: a test resolves every `-run` pattern in `skills/harness-audit/references/areas.md` to a `func <name>(` in the tree.
  - SD61a: one more `--install-timer --dry-run` row in `cmd/fyr/memory_test.go`, for a quoted `PATH`.
  - IN55: a tracked `_test.go` symlink exercises `internal/check/requirements.go`'s skip note.

---

# Plan — functions over 50 lines: extract-function splits and a length guard   (2026-10-27)

Status: scope approved 2026-10-27 by the operator ("Go all approved", D1). The cold read is done: `REVIEW-2026-10-27-0745-review-cold-read-of-plan-2026-10-27-funclen-2026`, answered by D12–D22. Approved by the operator on 2026-10-27 ("go all approved", D26). Phases 1–10 and Done are done (2026-10-27): the plan is closed.

## Why

`rules/code-modularity.md` (ADR-066) item 1 caps a function at 50 lines. The modularity audit (`PLAN-2026-10-26-1133-recon-the-code-modularity-audit-and-the-move-too`, item 9) found 55 non-test functions over it. `PLAN-2026-10-26-modularity` left them as a Follow-up, with the rewrite of `TestRefreshCatalogScript` (one function of 843 lines). ROADMAP Next scheduled both as one Feature (operator, 2026-10-26).

The list was regenerated on 2026-10-27 at afec913: `.agents/scratch/funclen.txt` holds 56 functions. The 56th is `internal/eval/creds.go:147 scanEntry` (59 lines), added by BUG-185's fix. The recon is `PLAN-2026-10-27-recon-funclen` ("the recon" below; its Q1–Q7 are cited by number).

## Scope

In:

- Every non-test function over 50 lines in git-tracked `.go` files (the 56 of § Phases), split by extract-function inside its own package until each is at most 50 lines (D3).
- `TestRefreshCatalogScript` (`internal/harness/catalog_test.go:25`, 843 lines; the file is 867): its closures become methods of a rig struct, then it is split into files under 400 lines each (D6).
- A regrowth guard, `TestFunctionLength`: it fails on any non-test function over 50 lines that is not on its allowlist. Its allowlist starts as the 56 and shrinks each phase, ending empty (D5; scope item 8, option A).
- Characterization tests, written before the split, for every uncovered block a split moves into a helper (D4, as superseded by D13). Arms no test can reach without a seam are exempt and listed (D12).
- Docs and records that name a split function's location, repointed in the same phase (D8).

Out:

- The other 77 test functions over 50 lines (`.agents/scratch/funclen-tests.txt`), struck by the operator (D1, item 3).
- Cyclomatic complexity: it stays a reading-only limit (D1, item 7; `PLAN-2026-10-26-modularity` D1).
- The 11 files between 401 and 600 lines: the rule's pre-edit check applies to each when it is next edited, and this plan edits some of them (D7).
- The three `internal/eval` test comments citing `catalog_test.go`: they cite the commit `8374f9c`, not line ranges, so nothing needs fixing (D2).

Follow-ups noted, not built:

- The 77 long test functions, if the operator schedules them.
- The documented gofmt command (`gofmt -l cmd internal`) does not check the root package's test files (`embed_test.go`, `statedir_test.go`, and `funclen_test.go` once added). Its restatements are in `AGENTS.md` § Setup commands, `README.md:227`, `skills/harness-audit/SKILL.md:36`, `skills/harness-audit/references/areas.md:36` and the `GUIDE-testing` and `DEPLOY-local` records. Struck from this plan by D14; found in: cold read G3.

## Surfaces touched

- 50 files across 8 packages. Every function's file:line, length and coverage is in the recon, Q1.
  - `internal/brain` 10, `internal/metrics` 10, `internal/search` 9, `internal/harness` 8, `cmd/fyr` 7, `internal/dream` 5, `internal/eval` 4, `internal/check` 3.
- New source files: `<file>_<concern>.go` in the same package (D7). The recon proposes names in Q3.
- `internal/harness/catalog_test.go` and new `internal/harness/catalog_refresh*_test.go` files (D6).
- New root-package test file `funclen_test.go` (package `fyr`), beside `statedir_test.go` and `embed_test.go` (D5).
- `ROADMAP.md` (Now and Next).
- No change to `context/`, `agents/`, `skills/`, `rules/` or `commands/`. No CLI verb, flag or output changes.

## Interfaces

Every split is behaviour-preserving. That means:

- No exported name is added, removed or renamed.
- No listed function's signature changes; tests call many of them directly (recon Q4, last paragraph).
- No package gains an import it did not have. Helpers may use packages their file did not import before, as long as the package already imports them (R4: the SQLite driver stays in `internal/search`, `internal/metrics` and `internal/brain`).
- Output, error text, exit codes and file effects are byte-for-byte unchanged.

New unexported types are allowed for closure-heavy functions (D3). Examples: a collector struct for `ImportGlobal`, `textWriter` for `WriteText`, `plot` for `lineChart`, a tokenizer for `segments`, and run-state structs for `Install` and `realRun`.

The guard, `funclen_test.go` (package `fyr`, the module root):

```go
// funcLimit is rules/code-modularity.md item 1's ceiling.
const funcLimit = 50

// longFuncs is the allowlist: key "path:Name" or "path:Recv.Name" (path from
// the module root, slash-separated, Recv without '*'), value the function's
// length when it was listed. Each phase deletes its rows; empty at Done.
var longFuncs = map[string]int{ /* the 56 */ }

func TestFunctionLength(t *testing.T)
```

How `TestFunctionLength` counts:

- **Files read:** `git ls-files -z -- '*.go'` from the module root, less names ending `_test.go`, files matching `*.pb.*` or `*_gen.*`, and anything under `skills/`. A listed file that no longer exists on disk (deleted, not yet staged) is skipped. A file that does not parse fails the test, naming the file. A new file is not seen until it is staged; the lister of step 6 reads files on disk and covers that window (D16).
- **Skips:** the test skips when `git` is not on PATH or `.git` is absent, as `embed_test.go` does.
- **Parsing:** each file is parsed with `go/parser` (`parser.SkipObjectResolution`).
- **Length:** for every `*ast.FuncDecl` with a body, the length is `fset.Position(fd.End()).Line - fset.Position(fd.Pos()).Line + 1`. That runs from the `func` keyword through the closing brace; the doc comment is not counted. This is the lister's own rule (`.agents/scratch/funclen/main.go`). A closure counts in the function that holds it.

The test fails, naming every offender in one run, when:

- **(a) Too long:** a function over `funcLimit` lines is not in `longFuncs`.
- **(b) Grown:** a listed function is now longer than its recorded value.
- **(c) Stale:** a listed key matches no function over `funcLimit` (the function was split, renamed or moved). The row must then be deleted.

Key rules:

- **Receiver:** `Recv` is the receiver's type name with `*` and any type parameters stripped (`*T[K]` becomes `T`).
- **Repeated names:** only `init` can repeat within one file. A repeated key gets `#2`, `#3` in source order (`path:init#2`).
- **Lines:** a function's length counts physical lines, comments and blank lines included, as the lister does (D16).
- **Allowlist literal:** a duplicate key in `longFuncs` is a compile error, so the allowlist cannot repeat a key.

## Failure modes

The splits change no behaviour a user sees, so the failures below are the plan's own:

- **A split changes behaviour.** The existing tests and the characterization tests (D4) fail in that package. The phase stops and the split is reverted or fixed before the next function.
- **The guard is wrong.** A guard that passes with an over-50 function not on its list is the dangerous case. It is caught by the Phase 1 mutation checks (verify clauses).
- **A file goes over a ceiling.** A file that a split pushes over 400 lines breaks D7. The phase's re-count (procedure step 6) catches it.
- **A citation goes stale.** A line or name citation in a current spec, guide or deploy record left pointing at the old location is caught by the restatement grep (procedure step 7). `fyr check` catches a path that no longer exists.

## The lister

`.agents/scratch/funclen/main.go`, run as `go run ./.agents/scratch/funclen <files>`. Rebuild it from this source on a box that lacks it:

```go
// funclen prints every Go function longer than 50 lines, with its length.
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"go/ast"
	"go/parser"
	"go/token"
	"os"
)

func main() {
	fs := token.NewFileSet()
	for _, p := range os.Args[1:] {
		f, err := parser.ParseFile(fs, p, nil, 0)
		if err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
			continue
		}
		for _, d := range f.Decls {
			fd, ok := d.(*ast.FuncDecl)
			if !ok || fd.Body == nil {
				continue
			}
			n := fs.Position(fd.End()).Line - fs.Position(fd.Pos()).Line + 1
			if n > 50 {
				fmt.Printf("%d\t%s:%d\t%s\n", n, p, fs.Position(fd.Pos()).Line, fd.Name.Name)
			}
		}
	}
}
```

Non-test files of package P: `git ls-files -co --exclude-standard -- 'P/*.go' | grep -v '_test\.go$'` (`-co` adds untracked files).

## Each phase's procedure

For package P and its functions:

1. **Re-count.** Rebuild the lister if needed (`go build -o .agents/scratch/funclen-bin/funclen ./.agents/scratch/funclen`). Run it over P's non-test files and `wc -l` P's files. A function that moved or changed length since afec913 is taken as it is now.
2. **Coverage before.** Run `go test -coverprofile=.agents/scratch/cover-P.out ./P/` and `go tool cover -func`. Note the coverage of each listed function and P's total. List every uncovered block inside each listed function, from the profile.
3. **Characterization tests first (D13).** Take every uncovered block the split will move into a helper, in any listed function and whatever its coverage. Write a test that runs it, checked to fail when the block is mutated (review-standards § 2). A block no test can reach without a seam is exempt (D12) and goes on the phase's exempt list with its reason. Commit the tests before the split, in the same phase.
4. **One function at a time.** Split it, then run `go test ./P/`, then delete its row from `longFuncs` in the same edit (D15). A labelled loop, a deferred cleanup, a named return or a load-bearing comment stays with the code that owns it (recon Q2 lists each, D10).
5. **Allowlist.** Every one of P's rows is gone, and `TestFunctionLength` passes.
6. **Re-count after.** The lister prints nothing for P, and no file in P is over 400 lines, unless it already was before the phase and the phase added nothing to it (D7). P's total coverage is not lower than in step 2.
7. **Restatement grep.** Search for each split function's name and old `file:line`: `git grep` over tracked files, plus `fyr search` for current spec, guide and deploy records. Repoint any line citation. Closed records are history and stay as written (D8).
8. **Checks.** Run `gofmt -l cmd internal *.go`, `go vet ./...` and `go test -race -timeout 30m ./...`, each bare as its own call, reading the exit status.
9. **Review.** Dispatch one `reviewer` over the phase's diff only, code lens (D11). Where the phase names it, also dispatch `security` over the named functions' diff (D19). Answer every finding in its `## Outcome`.
10. **Checkpoint.** Tick the boxes and write the `change` record. It lists the exempt arms (D12) and the coverage before and after. Commit and push as separate calls, then hand off and end the session (session-sizing).

## Risks

Assumptions:

- **Unique keys.** `path:Name` keys are unique except for repeated `init` functions in one file. `init` repeats across files (`cmd/fyr/check.go:18`, `cmd/fyr/eval.go:35`, `internal/metrics/verb.go:16`, `internal/search/parse.go:262`), and the path keeps those apart. Build-tagged variants (`open_unix.go`, `open_other.go`) are different paths. Checked by the cold read (G7); D16 handles the in-file repeat.
- **Statement coverage is a fair floor.** Per-package coverage is the measure. Cross-package coverage (cmd/fyr's tests reaching `internal/*`) is not counted, so the number is a floor, not the truth — accepted by D4.
- **The suite's runtime.** The full suite takes about 13 minutes under `-race` on a one-CPU box (AGENTS.md § Setup commands), and each checkpoint runs it once.
- **The midnight guard.** BUG-159's guard in `TestRefreshCatalogScript` sleeps through 23:58–24:00. A Phase 9 run near midnight is slow, not broken.

D16 — 2026-10-27 — Guard edges:

- **Unparseable file:** the test fails, naming it.
- **Deleted tracked file:** a tracked file missing on disk is skipped.
- **New files:** untracked files are not read. The lister covers them at step 6.
- **Generic receiver:** keyed by its bare type name.
- **In-file repeats:** a repeated `init` takes `#n`.
- **Line count:** physical lines, comments and blank lines included, the lister's rule. The rule file's "LOC" is read that way.

— by: cold read round 1 (G7, G8, Q7)

D17 — 2026-10-27 — Portability across boxes:

- **The lister:** its source is in this plan (§ The lister).
- **Phase 1's count:** "56 rows" is checked with `grep -c` at Phase 1's commit, not asserted, because the ratchet makes the number fall.
- **Criterion 6:** its base test list is computed from a worktree at `eec29b4`.

— by: cold read round 1 (G9, Q8)

D18 — 2026-10-27 — `newRefreshRig` keeps today's guard order: `Abs`, the script `Stat` (Fatalf), the `testing.Short()` skip, the midnight guard, then the tool skips. Phase 10's verify runs the test once under `-short` and expects SKIP. — by: cold read round 1 (G5, Q5)

D19 — 2026-10-27 — Supersedes D11's security sentence. Global Definition of Done step 2 requires `security` for secrets and input parsing, so these get a `security` review over their diff:

| Phase | Functions | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | `segments`, `heredocDelims` | the shell tokenizer |
| 5 | `UnpackZip` | zip parsing and the hash check |
| 7 | `agyHome` | copies the Antigravity login |
| 8 | `ParseSuite`, `scanEntry` | the suite parser and the credential scan |

`callWithin` (signal relay) is a correctness concern for the `reviewer`, not a security one. — by: cold read round 1 (G2, Q2)

D20 — 2026-10-27 — The closure methods of `TestRefreshCatalogScript` go in `catalog_refresh_steps_test.go`, not `catalog_refresh_rig_test.go`, which is too close to the existing `catalog_rig_test.go`. The section files are grouped by the recon's Q5 section map, at the implementer's choice within the 400-line cap. — by: cold read round 1 (Q10)

D21 — 2026-10-27 — Phases follow D1 item 6 exactly: one package per phase. Metrics is one phase (the 3a/3b split is withdrawn), and eval and check are two phases (8 and 9). The plan has 10 phases and Done. — by: cold read round 1 (G4, Q4)

D22 — 2026-10-27 — D2 voids the operator's scope item 10 on a fact: the comments cite a commit, not line ranges. The operator sees this at plan approval and may still ask for the comments to be reworded. — by: cold read round 1 (G4)

D25 — 2026-10-27 — The list moved under the plan while it waited for approval. The 2026-10-27 audit fix (PLAN-2026-10-27-harness-audit-fix) brought `agyHome` and `InstallTimer` under 50 lines, so their Phase 7 rows are already done. Several listed functions grew by 1–7 lines. The tree now holds 54. Procedure step 1's re-count and `longFuncs` at Phase 1 take the list as it then is. — by: implementer.

D26 — 2026-10-27 — The operator approved this plan as written. It is row 1 of the closing table of the 2026-10-27 audit session, which recommended approval in 11 one-package sessions. — by: the operator's words "go all approved", 2026-10-27.

D27 — 2026-10-27 — Phases 8 and 9 run in one session. Both are small: eval has 4 functions and check has 3. Each keeps its own boxes, reviewer, checkpoint commit and `change` record, so D21's one package per phase still holds for the work and the records. Only the session boundary between them is dropped, which saves one session. — by: the operator's words "merge 8+9", 2026-10-27.

D28 — 2026-10-27 — Each remaining phase ends with a fenced Kickoff to paste after `/clear`, with its closed standing approvals; Phases 8 and 9 share one (D27). The audit session's row 17 asked to fold deferred audit lows into these phases where a file is touched anyway; that would break § Interfaces' no-behaviour-change promise, so none is folded unless the operator answers `PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-cleanup` O3 otherwise, and a later D-row here names what. — by: implementer, the planning session of 2026-10-27.

D29 — 2026-10-27 — Supersedes D16's "New files" clause. `TestFunctionLength` reads untracked files too, unless git ignores them (`git ls-files -co --exclude-standard`), so a new file's long function fails the guard before it is staged. Why: the plan's lister covered that window only while the plan was open, and Done's reviewer showed an untracked 62-line function left the guard green. With the allowlist empty, `TestFunctionLengthBites` proves the guard can still fail: a 51-line function is over and a 50-line one is not, and each finding is made. `TestFunctionLengthReadsUntracked` pins the file list. `longFuncs`' comment now says it was emptied, and that a row is an exception the ratchet holds. — by: implementer, from Done's review (`REVIEW` of 2026-10-27, findings 1–3).

Rejected:

- **A separate characterization phase first:** it would touch all 8 packages in one session (D4).
- **`t.Run` subtests for `TestRefreshCatalogScript`:** order-dependent state (D6).
- **The guard added only at Done (option B), or no guard (option C):** the operator chose A.
- **Splitting the 77 test functions:** struck by the operator.
- **Unexported seams (`var rename = os.Rename`) to reach error arms:** test-only surface in production code (D12).
