title: Plan — the visible dream (2026-10-28)
body:
# Plan — the visible dream (2026-10-28)

## Why

The operator wants to SEE the dream: today `fyr dream` runs `agy` in a private HOME that fyr deletes, so nothing it did is listed anywhere the operator looks, and the nightly 03:00 timer runs when no one is at the machine. Phase 8a of `PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` researched it (that plan's D35) and the operator approved the seven-row proposal on 2026-10-28, "Approve recommendations (Recommended)" (ledger D36; the proposal file `.agents/scratch/ledger/p8a/proposal.md` is gitignored scratch, so the texts that bind are copied into D1 below). Ledger D36 (7) makes the build this plan, under the feature skill, after ledger Phase 9 and before the ledger's Done.

REQUIREMENTS touched: R0 (its last sentence, replaced, D36 1), R3 (its exception, replaced, D36 3), R4 (unchanged: no new dependency; Antigravity's databases stay read from copies; the new reads are `agy`'s own print-mode reports and `/proc`), R6 (the visible branch runs in `--home`'s Antigravity home, never `$HOME` when they differ, D3), R7 (harness state stays in `~/.config/fyr/`; the dream conversation is the CLI's own state in its own store, which R3's new text names: "beside the conversation the CLI itself keeps"), R8 (unchanged: what leaves the machine is the same redacted prompt), R10 (the macOS process check is verified only by the operator's Mac run, ledger A2).

**Terms.** *Visible branch*: `agy` runs with `HOME` set to `--home` (default `$HOME`), so its conversation is written to `<home>/.gemini/antigravity-cli` and `/resume` lists it there. *Private branch*: today's `agyHome` (`internal/dream/agy_home.go:60`), a temporary HOME `~/.config/fyr/dream-agy-home-*` with a copied login and deny-all settings, removed after the run. *dream-work*: `<home>/.config/fyr/dream-work`, the run's empty working directory (`run.go:65`). *The oracle*: `agy -p "/permissions"` and `agy -p "/config"` with `--output-format json`, which print the effective permission state "without starting an agent turn, spending quota or leaving a conversation behind" (agy changelog, version 1.1.12; saved at `.agents/scratch/ledger/p8a/agy-changelog.txt:656`). *Ledger A2*: the operator's macOS `fyr dream --all` run (`PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` § The operator's questions). *AS1–AS5*: this plan's assumptions (§ Risks). *SD15*: the project-name scrub (`SPEC-fyr-dream` step 2). Verify tags: `AI` = the implementing session checks it; `user` = the operator does; `both` = the session prepares, the operator confirms. Every `fyr` command in development carries `--home .agents/scratch/<name>` (AGENTS.md § Rules for working here); a record is edited by `fyr record get <ID>` into scratch, edit, `fyr record edit <ID> --body < file`.

## Scope

In:
1. REQUIREMENTS.md R0 and R3 replaced by D36's sentences, with the ADR, the map, README's prose and the specs, in Phase 1's one commit (D36 7; D16 for how the not-yet-built parts are drawn and worded).
2. The timer fires hourly; an `--all` run first checks for an interactive `agy` session of the operator's uid and exits quietly without one (D36 4; D9).
3. The dream conversation stays in the operator's Antigravity home — the visible branch — only when the oracle shows that home grants no tool without review; otherwise the private branch as today; never `--dangerously-skip-permissions` (D36 2; D11).
4. The prompt's first line reads `dreaming: <project>`; the working directory stays dream-work (D36 5; D14).
5. The dream's own conversations are never read back as a project's input or ingested as a metrics session (D5; needed by 3).
6. A project attempted in the last 24 hours, success or failure, is not attempted again (D10; needed by 2: an hourly timer otherwise retries a failing project 24 times a day, each leaving a conversation).
7. `fyr status` names an installed timer whose unit text is not today's render (D13; needed by 2: a machine that keeps its nightly unit silently stops dreaming).

Out: a pinned conversation title (struck by D36 5); a per-run tool switch or a permission file fyr writes into the operator's home (none documented, ledger D35 4; fyr never edits the operator's settings); parsing `settings.json` or the shared rules file by hand (D11, Rejected); the desktop app or Hub counted as a session (D9); `fyr install` or `update` rewriting an installed timer (D4).

Follow-ups noted, not built: the map's interactive page (ledger item 38, the operator's).

## Surfaces touched

- Requirements and records: `REQUIREMENTS.md` R0 (line 7), R3 (line 19); `ROADMAP.md`; a new ADR (the store assigns the number; `ADR-073` if nothing else lands first) amending `ADR-047a` and `ADR-067`; `SPEC-fyr-dream`; `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § What stays on the machine, the paragraph beginning "Two things leave a machine"; `SPEC-fyr-metrics` (2 schedule lines; the ingest's exclusion); `SPEC-fyr-memory-loop` (1 line), `GUIDE-testing` (1 line, § 3e), `DEPLOY-local` (2 lines) — each "nightly"/"03:00" restatement (`fyr record get <ID> | grep -n -i 'nightly\|03:00'`).
- `README.md`: line 3 ("a nightly consolidation"), line 19 ("in the nightly dream"), line 50 (the `fyr dream --install-timer` row), the map (line 82 the `dreamer` node, lines 102–111 the edges and `linkStyle`), line 114 (legend, "the nightly dreamer"), line 116 ("runs on its own, nightly").
- `AGENTS.md` (this repo): rule 1's "The nightly dream timer" (line 14) and the `internal/dream` layout line (line 52) (D7).
- Skills (prose and one description): `skills/dream/SKILL.md:3` (its DESCRIPTION: "The nightly `fyr dream` job"; `TestSkillListingBudget` and the release rule's Antigravity run of a changed skill apply), `skills/project-memory/SKILL.md:56`, `skills/retro/SKILL.md:48`, `skills/handoff/SKILL.md:178`.
- Code, `internal/dream`: `timer.go` `renderSystemd` (lines 102–128) and `renderLaunchd` (line 158); `run.go` `realRun` (24–73) and `project` (107–143); `agy_home.go` `checkAgy` (20–26), `findLogin` (31–51), `agyHome` (60–102), `agyAuthHint` text (138); `dream.go` `command` and its comment (197–205), `StatusLine` (217); `state.go` (the state shape, D10); `prompt.go` `head` (66); `run_dry.go` (17–26, the "HOME a private copy" text). `timer.go` is 446 lines: new logic goes in new files (`rules/code-modularity.md` item 2).
- Code, `cmd/fyr`: `verb_dream.go` 54, 59, 68; `ctx_verbs.go` 76–77; `help_text.go` 41, 203; `main.go` 18; `dream_arms_test.go:36` (asserts the install message verbatim).
- Code, readers of Antigravity's store: `internal/metrics/agy.go` `agyConversations` (70–99) and `firstWorkspace` (101–113); `internal/search/dream.go` `AgyConversationText` (91) and `listConversations` (132); `internal/search/dream_workspace.go` `newWorkspaces` (31), `judge` (44); `internal/harness` (the shared name, D5).
- Comments naming "nightly": `internal/dream/run_dry.go:33`, `run_files.go:68`, `response.go:74`, `timer.go:3,300,444`, `timer_install.go:32-33`, `internal/memory/memory.go:70`, `internal/search/copy.go:12`, `internal/trail/trail.go:2`.

## Interfaces

**The process check** (new file `internal/dream/agy_process.go`; OS parts split as the implementer sees fit):
```go
// agySession reports whether an interactive agy session runs under uid.
func agySession(goos string, uid int) (bool, error)
var procRoot = "/proc"              // Linux; a test points it at a fake tree
var psArgs = func() ([]byte, error) // macOS: `ps -U <uid> -o args=`; a test replaces it
```
A process counts (D9) when ALL hold: its real uid is `uid` (Linux: the first field of the `Uid:` line of `procRoot/<pid>/status`, readable for every process, never the directory's owner, which is root for a non-dumpable process); its name is `agy` (the base name of `cmdline`'s first argument, or of the `exe` link with a trailing ` (deleted)` removed — `agy update` replaces the binary under a live session); and its arguments hold neither `-p`/`--print` (a headless run: fyr's own child, `fyr eval`, a script) nor, as the first non-flag argument, one of `agy`'s subcommands (the list `agy --help` prints, recorded in Phase 2's first task: `remote-control`, `mcp`, `update` and the rest are not a person at a session). An entry that cannot be read (gone, another user's) is skipped. macOS: the same rules over `psArgs`'s lines. Not counted: the desktop app and the Hub (not `agy` processes).

Where it is asked: first in `realRun` for `--all`, BEFORE `harness.ConfigDir` (which creates the directory, `run.go:25`), the lock, the ingest and every write. No session: print `fyr dream: no agy session of this user; nothing to do` to stdout (the unit's journal), create nothing, exit 0. The check errors: exit 2 with the error on stdout, create nothing (D2). `--project` never asks. `--all --dry-run` prints `agy session: yes` or `agy session: no (a real --all run would stop here)` and continues.

**The cooldown** (D10): `state.json` gains `"attempts": {"<root>": "<RFC 3339>"}`, written when a project's CLI call starts (before `call`), success or failure. `--all` skips a project whose attempt is under 24 h old with `<root> skip attempted <time>`; the dry run prints the same. `--project` ignores it (the operator asked). The watermark (`projects`) is unchanged in meaning. A state file without the key reads as empty (an older fyr's file).

**The timer**: systemd `OnCalendar=hourly`, `Persistent=true`, `TimeoutStartSec=2h` unchanged, both `Description=` lines say hourly; launchd `StartCalendarInterval` with `Minute` 0 and no `Hour`. `verb_dream.go`: "would install the hourly dream timer (fyr dream --all every hour, while an agy session runs)" and "dream timer installed: fyr dream --all runs hourly while an agy session runs". An existing unit with other text is refused by `planTimer` as today (D4). `StatusLine` (D13): a unit on disk whose text differs from `renderSystemd`/`renderLaunchd` for this home and the unit's own frozen `PATH` reads `timer installed, older schedule: fyr dream --remove-timer, then fyr dream --install-timer`. — docs: README row 50, `fyr help dream`, `SPEC-fyr-dream`.

**The branch** (new file `internal/dream/agy_visible.go`):
```go
// visibleHome runs the oracle in home from work and reports whether every
// tool needs review there, and why not when one does not.
func visibleHome(argv0, home, work string, env []string) (ok bool, why string)
```
It runs `agy -p "/permissions" --output-format json` and `agy -p "/config" --output-format json` with `HOME=home`, the working directory `work` and ADR-067's allow-listed `env`, each with a 30-second timeout, and parses their output. `ok` only when ALL hold, else `false` with the first failing reason (D11, D6):
1. The login is there: `<home>/.gemini/antigravity-cli/antigravity-oauth-token` exists, or on macOS `<home>/Library/Keychains` is a directory (`findLogin`'s rule, read under `home`).
2. `work` holds no entry (a project configuration file there, or an `.agents/` manifest, would add to the session; agy changelog 1.2.16 at `agy-changelog.txt:250` loads `.agents/` manifests from every directory up to the project root) — and the oracle's reported workspace or project root, if it reports one, is `work` itself, not an ancestor (a `$HOME` that is a git checkout).
3. The effective review mode the oracle reports is one of the modes Phase 4a's research shows to require review for EVERY tool call, file reads in the workspace aside (agy grants those under the default review mode, changelog 1.1.20 at `:546`; `work` is empty). `always-proceed` and any mode that auto-approves fail.
4. The oracle reports no allow rule from any source (CLI settings, the shared Remote Control rules, project configuration; changelog 1.3.6 at `:404` names the three) and no grant of access outside the workspace (changelog 1.1.14 at `:620`).
5. Both outputs parse into the shape Phase 4a recorded; anything else fails (an `agy` upgrade that changes the report sends the dream private until fyr learns it).

**The run's lifecycle** (D12): `checkAgy` checks only that `agy` is on PATH. For each project, after the cooldown and before the call, `realRun`'s `project` asks `visibleHome(o.Home, dream-work)`. Visible: `env = childEnv(os.Environ(), o.Home)`. Private: the private home is built on the run's first private project (`findLogin` under `$HOME`, then `agyHome`) and reused by later private projects of the run; its cleanup is deferred in `realRun`; a failure to build it fails that project (`<root> fail <reason>`, exit 1 at the end), not the run. The `call`'s env is per project. One `dream.log` line per project before the call: `<root> agy home visible` or `<root> agy home private (<why>)`. The dry run prints the branch per project and runs the oracle (it starts no turn and spends no quota).

**The prompt** (D14): `head` becomes `"dreaming: " + c.Name + "\n\n" + instructions + "\n\nProject: " + c.Name + "\n"` — `c.Name` already scrubbed (SD15). The `Project:` line stays; the tool warning becomes the message's second paragraph, and `SPEC-fyr-dream`'s "the prompt's opening warning" becomes "the prompt's warning". `fit` counts with `len(head(c))`, so `collect_fit_test.go`'s equality holds unchanged.

**dream-work is no project's** (D5, D15): `harness.DreamWork(home string) string` = `filepath.Join(home, harness.StateDir, "dream-work")`; `realRun` uses it. Both readers compare a conversation's workspace against the set {`DreamWork(home)`, its `filepath.EvalSymlinks` form when that resolves}, by equality or prefix + separator. `metrics.agyConversations(src, tmp, exclude []string)` drops a conversation whose `firstWorkspace` matches (no session, no `ingest_state` row); `ingestAgy` passes `o`'s home's set. `search.newWorkspaces(root, exclude []string)` makes `judge` return not-kept with `whyDream = "a fyr dream conversation"` when any workspace matches; `AgyConversationText(home, …)` passes the set, so the dream's input and `activityIn`'s in-use check both skip it. — docs: `SPEC-fyr-metrics`, `SPEC-fyr-dream`.

**The requirement and map texts** are D1's, verbatim; the map edge and the docs' "being built" sentence follow D16.

## Failure modes

| What fails | What the operator sees |
|---|---|
| No interactive `agy` session when the timer fires | Nothing in `dream.log` or `state.json`, no directory created; one journal line; the next hour asks again |
| The process check errors | Exit 2, the error in the journal, nothing written; `systemctl --user status` shows the failed unit |
| The oracle fails, times out, or reports a grant or a shape fyr does not know | The private branch for that project, as today; `dream.log` names why; no conversation in `/resume` |
| The settings change between the oracle and the call | The call runs under the new settings (the window of one project's oracle-to-start); a Known limit in `SPEC-fyr-dream` |
| A project's dream fails (`invalid output`, timeout, auth) | `dream.log` `fail …`, kept in `dream-failed/` as today; not attempted again for 24 h (D10); in the visible branch the failed conversation stays in `/resume` |
| The private home cannot be built for a project | That project fails, the run goes on, exit 1 |
| A machine keeps its nightly unit after the upgrade | `fyr status`: `timer installed, older schedule: …` (D13); `--install-timer` refuses with "exists with other text" until `--remove-timer` |
| Two `agy` processes write the operator's store at once | agy's own design (the desktop app, the Hub, Remote Control and several sessions share it); agy fixed a lock-dropping corruption risk there in 1.2.9 (`:324`); fyr adds nothing (AS5) |
| macOS `ps` missing or its output unparsable | Exit 2 as above; verified only by ledger A2 |

## Trust boundaries and data handled

Untrusted input: project trails, memory, feedback and Antigravity transcripts in the prompt (unchanged). NEW: in the visible branch that prompt runs in the operator's own Antigravity home with the operator's installed context, skills, MCP servers and plugin hooks loaded (ledger D35 4; D8), and the redacted prompt persists in `<home>/.gemini/antigravity-cli` where today it is deleted. The no-tools guarantee becomes the oracle's report (`visibleHome`) instead of isolation. NEW reads: `agy`'s print-mode reports (parsed, untrusted shape: fail closed), `/proc/<pid>/{status,cmdline,exe}` or `ps`. The login is used in place in the visible branch, no longer copied. The child environment stays ADR-067's allow-list with `HOME` = `--home`. This touches secrets, input parsing and a trust boundary: `security` is due at Phase 4b and at Done.

## Verification

Tiers: unit (`go test -race` of `./internal/dream ./internal/metrics ./internal/search ./internal/harness ./cmd/fyr`, each new check with a must-fail mutation, `review-standards` § 2); the repo's full command (`gofmt -l cmd internal && go vet ./... && go test -race -timeout 30m ./...`, bare, its exit status read); the scratch-home install (`fyr status` shows a `binary` line with no warning); the sandbox (Phases 4a and 5: the real `agy` in a sandbox home, never the real one); the operator's checks (`/resume`, the Mac).

E2E criteria:
1. Golden path: with the operator in an interactive `agy` session and a registered project idle for a day with news, the next hourly run leaves one conversation in the home's Antigravity store whose workspace is dream-work and whose first user message starts `dreaming: <project>`, and the project's proposals are `proposal` records as today.
2. Edge: with an allow rule in that home's settings, the same run leaves no new conversation in the home's store, `dream.log` says why, and no `dream-agy-home-*` is left.
3. Edge: with no interactive `agy` session, an `--all` run creates nothing under the home's `.config/fyr/`.
4. The next dream of that project does not carry the earlier dream's text, and `fyr metrics ingest` stores no session whose root is dream-work.

## Phases

- [x] Cold-reader check — one report (`REVIEW-2026-10-28-1517-review-cold-read-of-the-visible-dream-plan-2026`: design needs revision, implementation not ready, 3 BLOCKING), every item answered by a D-row, a rebuttal or the user — evidence: BLOCKING 1–3 → D11, D10, D9; findings → D2, D12–D16, the two rebuttals and the Answered row; the two items only the operator settles (D8, D16) go with the phases question; 2026-10-28
- [x] The operator's approval of the phases, recorded as a D-row — evidence: D17; 2026-10-28

### Phase 1 — the requirements, the ADR, the map and the docs: ONE commit (D36 7; AGENTS.md rules 3 and 6; D16)
- [x] `REQUIREMENTS.md` R0: the sentence "The brain is consulted, never consulting: nothing in `fyr` acts on the CLI between its turns (R3), and the CLI learns only what it asks for." becomes D1's R0 sentence verbatim; R0's citation list gains the new ADR. — verify: `git diff REQUIREMENTS.md`, AI. — expect: that sentence and the citation only. — done: R0's sentence equals D1's verbatim (a substring check), citation ADR-073 added; `git diff` shows that sentence only; 2026-10-28
- [x] `REQUIREMENTS.md` R3: from "One exception:" to "(ADR-047a, ADR-062, ADR-068.)" becomes D1's R3 text verbatim, `ADR-0NN` written as the new ADR's number. — verify: `git diff`, AI. — expect: the exception replaced, nothing else. — done: R3's exception equals D1's verbatim with ADR-073 (a substring check); plus R8's "nightly" dropped by D19; 2026-10-28
- [x] The ADR: `fyr record add adr --title "The visible dream" --home .agents/scratch/home-trail`, in the feature skill's ADR shape: Context (ledger D32 3, D35), Decision (D36 rows 1–5; this plan's D2–D16), Consequences (no-tools holds by the oracle's report in the visible branch, not by isolation; the conversation persists in the operator's store; the hourly cadence, the 24-hour cooldown and the operator's quota; the operator's MCP servers and hooks load in a visible dream, D8; the macOS check by ledger A2); "Amends ADR-047a (the schedule, where the CLI runs) and ADR-067 (HOME is `--home` in the visible branch)". ADR-047a and ADR-067 are not edited. — verify: `fyr record get <ADR>`, AI. — expect: in the store and in `.agents/trail.jsonl`. — done: ADR-073 stored (`fyr record get ADR-073`), in `.agents/trail.jsonl`; 2026-10-28
- [x] README's map: the node `dreamer["fyr dream --all<br/>hourly user timer, while agy runs<br/>a CLI with no tools"]`; the new edge `dreamer -. ## Risks

Assumptions:
- AS1: a live `agy` session is found by `cmdline`/`exe` as D9 says — the binary is ELF on the Linux box (cold read); the subcommand list is recorded by Phase 2's first task; a live session is checked only by V0.
- AS2: `agy -p "/permissions"` and `/config` report the effective review mode, every allow rule by source and the outside-workspace grant, and start no turn and leave no conversation (changelog 1.1.12, `:656`) — checked by Phase 4a's first task; if the reports lack a needed fact, D11's fallback applies.
- AS3: a review mode exists in which every tool call needs review in print mode — checked by Phase 4a's first task (D35 never probed `strict`, and `agy_home.go:94` chose to set `request-review` explicitly rather than trust the default).
- AS4: a headless plan-mode run in a home with the harness context installed answers with the JSON object and makes no tool call (the context's resume order tells a session to run `fyr` commands) — checked by V1; on failure the phase stops and the operator decides.
- AS5: two `agy` processes on one store are safe — agy's design (several sessions, the desktop app, the Hub, Remote Control share it); its 1.2.9 fix (`:324`) shows agy repairs bugs there; fyr does not test it.

Other risks: the operator's quota is spent while they work (D36 4), bounded by D10 to one attempt per project per day; the oracle adds up to three `agy -p` calls per project per run (no turn, no quota, per AS2; the third, `/hooks`, by D26).

## Decisions

D1 — 2026-10-28 — The texts this plan lands, verbatim from the operator's approval (ledger D36; the proposal file). R0's new sentence: "The brain is consulted, never consulting: nothing in `fyr` acts on a CLI session between its turns, and a session learns only what it asks for; the one conversation `fyr` starts is the visible dream (R3), a conversation of its own that no session is sent into." R3's new exception: "One exception: `fyr dream --all`, run hourly by an OS user timer that `fyr dream --install-timer` installs and `fyr dream --remove-timer` or `uninstall` removes, acts only while an Antigravity CLI process of the operator's runs (a process check when the timer fires, no daemon), over the projects the operator registered with `fyr index --register` (a marker inside the checkout's `.git/`, which no clone carries) that are idle for at least a day and have something new since their last dream. It reads those projects' records and memory and the global feedback records and the Antigravity CLI's conversations, and a numbers-only summary of the metrics store (its metric keys and values for each project's window and the window before, never a tool, skill, agent, label or path), first ingests those conversations into the metrics store (R4), and runs the CLI headless in plan mode with no tools over what it read: in the operator's own Antigravity home, from an empty working directory under `~/.config/fyr/`, when that home's settings grant no tool without review, so each project's dream is one conversation the operator can open with `/resume`, and otherwise in a private home that grants none, never with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`. It writes only under `~/.config/fyr/`, its proposals as global `proposal` records, beside the conversation the CLI itself keeps; it never edits a project, a skill, a rule or the context, and a proposal takes effect only through `/retro`. (ADR-047a, ADR-062, ADR-068, ADR-0NN.)" — by: the operator, "Approve recommendations (Recommended)", 2026-10-28 (ledger D36).
D2 — 2026-10-28 — The process check runs for `--all` only, before anything is created; no session exits 0 with one stdout line and creates nothing (D36 4's "exits quietly"); a check that errors exits 2 and creates nothing, failing toward not dreaming. — by: implementer; refined by cold read round 1 (before `ConfigDir`, not only before the lock).
D3 — 2026-10-28 — The visible branch's Antigravity home is `--home` (default `$HOME`), never `$HOME` when they differ: the dream already reads conversations from `--home`'s store (`internal/search/dream.go:92`), and a development run with a scratch `--home` must never write the operator's real store (R6). — by: implementer.
D4 — 2026-10-28 — An installed nightly unit is not rewritten by `install`, `update` or `--install-timer` (which refuses other text, `timer_install.go` `planTimer`); the upgrade is the operator's `--remove-timer`, then `--install-timer`, named by README row 50, `fyr status` (D13) and the closing handoff. Rewriting it from install or update would change the install path (AGENTS.md rule 3). — by: implementer.
D5 — 2026-10-28 — A conversation whose workspace is dream-work is no project's: not ingested into `metrics.db`, not read by any project's dream or in-use check. Without it a registered checkout at or above the config directory would feed each dream its previous one, and metrics would count dream runs as sessions. — by: implementer.
D6 — 2026-10-28 — `visibleHome` fails closed: every failed, unparsable or unknown report sends that project private; it is asked before each project's call. — by: implementer.
D7 — 2026-10-28 — This repo's `AGENTS.md` rule 1 and layout line change in Phase 1's commit with the rest of the docs (the restatement rule), though D36 7's list did not name the file. — by: implementer.
D8 — 2026-10-28 — In the visible branch the operator's MCP servers, plugins and hooks load as in any session they start; the model still has no tool it can use without review (D11). Written as a Consequence in the ADR and a Known limit in `SPEC-fyr-dream`. — by: implementer; put to the operator with the phases.
D9 — 2026-10-28 — "An Antigravity CLI process of the operator's" (R3) is an interactive session: real uid from `/proc/<pid>/status` (a non-dumpable process's directory is root's), name `agy` from `cmdline` or from `exe` with ` (deleted)` removed (`agy update` mid-session), and neither `-p`/`--print` nor a subcommand (`remote-control` is a background daemon and would hold the check true forever; `mcp`, `update` are not a person at a session). — by: cold read round 1 (BLOCKING 3, the reviewer's report `.agents/scratch/agents/reviewer-2026-10-28-1510.md`), decided by the implementer.
D10 — 2026-10-28 — One attempt per project per 24 h under `--all`, success or failure, kept in `state.json` `attempts`: a failed project keeps its watermark (`run.go:130-137`), so under an hourly timer it would otherwise re-run up to 24 times a day, each a call of up to 10 minutes and, in the visible branch, a new conversation in `/resume`. This keeps today's nightly ceiling. — by: cold read round 1 (BLOCKING 2), decided by the implementer.
D11 — 2026-10-28 — The visible check asks `agy` itself: the print-mode reports `/permissions` and `/config` (no turn, no quota, no conversation; changelog 1.1.12) give the effective state over every permission source — CLI settings, the shared Remote Control rules, project configuration, review and cycle modes, the outside-workspace grant — where hand-parsing `settings.json` and `config.json` covered two sources by guess and missed the rest. Fallback, if Phase 4a finds the reports lack a needed fact: the visible branch is not built, the plan records that as a superseding D-row and the operator decides between hand-parsing with every unknown key failing closed and striking the visible branch. — supersedes the first draft's file-parsing rules — by: cold read round 1 (BLOCKING 1), decided by the implementer.
D12 — 2026-10-28 — The run's lifecycle: `checkAgy` checks PATH only; the login check belongs to the branch (visible: under `--home`; private: under `$HOME`); the private home is built lazily on the run's first private project and reused; a failure to build it fails that project, not the run; env per project; no ask "before the first project" beyond the per-project one. — by: cold read round 1 (NON-BLOCKING 4).
D13 — 2026-10-28 — `fyr status` names an installed unit whose text is not today's render, with the two commands to replace it. Without it a machine that does not reinstall keeps a 03:00 unit that, with the session check, almost never dreams, and nothing says so. — by: cold read round 1 (finding on `StatusLine`).
D14 — 2026-10-28 — The prompt opens `dreaming: <name>`, a blank line, then today's instructions with the `Project:` line kept; the tool warning becomes the second paragraph. — by: cold read round 1 (NON-BLOCKING 5).
D15 — 2026-10-28 — The dream-work exclusion matches the path as written and its `EvalSymlinks` form, by equality or prefix; `home` reaches `agyConversations` and `newWorkspaces` as an exclude set; V1 records the URI `agy` actually stores and checks the set matches it. — by: cold read round 1 (NON-BLOCKING 6).
D16 — 2026-10-28 — Phase 1 lands the requirements, ADR, map and docs before the code (the Kickoff's and D36 7's order), so AGENTS.md rule 4 ("nothing is drawn solid before it works for every place") is kept by drawing the new edge DASHED in Phase 1 and turning it solid only when V1 and ledger A2 pass; each edited spec carries one "being built" sentence that Phase 5 removes; no tag is cut while this plan is open. — by: implementer; put to the operator (cold read round 1 finding on Phase 1 timing).
D17 — 2026-10-28 — The operator answered the three questions through the question popup: phases — "Approve all (Recommended)" (Phases 1, 2, 3, 4a, 4b and 5 as written, D9, D10 and D13 included); map timing — "Dashed until built (Recommended)" (D16 as written: the new edge dashed in Phase 1, solid once V1 and ledger A2 pass, a "being built" sentence per edited spec until Phase 5, no tag while this plan is open); MCP and hooks — "Accept, as a Known limit (Recommended)" (D8 as written). — by: the operator, 2026-10-28.
D18 — 2026-10-28 — The cooldown's `attempts` key lives in `~/.config/fyr/dream-state.json` (`internal/dream/state.go:29`); `state.json` in § Interfaces, Scope 6, D10 and the cooldown task means that file — `state.json` is the install manifest. — by: Phase 1 review NIT (`REVIEW` of Phase 1).
D19 — 2026-10-28 — R8's "the nightly dreamer's redacted prompt (R3)" becomes "the dreamer's redacted prompt (R3)" in Phase 1's commit, recorded in ADR-073; the plan's restatement list had missed it. — by: the operator, "Approve drop 'nightly' (Recommended)" (the question popup), 2026-10-28, on the Phase 1 review's BLOCKING finding.
D20 — 2026-10-28 — Beyond D16's spec sentences, README lines 3 and 117 and AGENTS.md rule 1 carry a being-built clause ("nightly until then"), the legend's dashed-line definition and AGENTS.md rule 4 name a line drawn ahead of its approved code (ADR-073), and Phase 5's docs box removes those clauses with the spec sentences. — by: Phase 1 review, NON-BLOCKING findings 1 and 4, decided by the implementer.
D21 — 2026-10-28 — AS1: `agy --help` (agy 1.4.9) lists the subcommands `agent`, `agents`, `changelog`, `help`, `install`, `mcp`, `mic-serve`, `models`, `plugin`, `plugins`, `remote-control`, `update`; `agySubcommands` holds exactly these. Its flags add `--prompt` as an alias of `--print`, so the headless test is `-p`, `--print` or `--prompt`, one dash or two (Go's flag package), with or without `=value`; `--prompt-interactive`/`-i` and `--print-timeout` are other flags. `file` on `~/.local/bin/agy`: ELF 64-bit LSB pie executable, x86-64. — by: implementer, Phase 2.
D22 — 2026-10-28 — Phase 2's departures from § Interfaces, none changing a decision: `psArgs` takes the uid and runs `ps -ww -U <uid> -o args=` (`-ww` so a long command line is not cut); the dry run's line carries the `[dry-run] ` prefix every dry-run line has, and a check that errors exits 2 in a dry run as in the real one; the older-schedule line adds `--home '<home>'` to both commands under a home that is not the real one (the bare commands act on the real home, BUG-149's class); and since the binary now runs hourly, the being-built clauses Phase 1 wrote (README lines 3, 50, 117, AGENTS.md rule 1, `SPEC-fyr-dream`, `SPEC-fyr-delivery`) say what is built and keep only "until its Phase 5 the dream still runs in a private home" (the restatement rule; D20's removal in Phase 5 stands for the rest). — by: implementer, Phase 2.
D23 — 2026-10-28 — Phase 3's departures from § Interfaces, none changing a decision: `harness` also holds the set and its match (`DreamWorkPaths`, `InDreamWork`), so both readers share one predicate; the resolved form comes from the deepest existing ancestor of dream-work, the rest joined back, so a symlinked home or config directory matches after dream-work is removed (review finding 2); the metrics ingest excludes the set of `--home` and, under `--source`, of the sandbox home too, the store it reads (review finding 1 pins it); `judge` names a dream conversation (`a fyr dream conversation`) only when a workspace of it is under the root, else it is left out unnamed as another project's; `listConversations` takes the `*workspaces` instead of the root. — by: implementer, Phase 3.
D24 — 2026-10-28 — Phase 4a's oracle research (AS2, AS3), agy 1.4.9 in a sandbox home with a 0600 copy of the operator's login, from an empty dream-work; every report exit 0, `conversation_summaries.db` 0 rows after all of them (no turn, no conversation). `/config --output-format json` is one object `{"status":"SUCCESS","command":{"name":"config","data":{"config":{…}}}}` with every setting as its effective value: `toolPermission` (no settings, `{}` and an unknown value all read `request-review`; also `strict`, `always-proceed`, `proceed-in-sandbox`, the four the docs name, https://antigravity.google/docs/permissions), `agentMode` (`""` by default and for `"agent"`; `plan`, `accept-edits`, `auto`), `allowNonWorkspaceAccess` (bool), `trustedWorkspaces` (null or a list), `permissions` (null or `{allow, deny, ask}`, and null for a rule it cannot parse). It reports the settings, not the session: `--mode plan` beside an `agentMode` of `auto` still reads `auto`. `/permissions` is `{"permissions":[{"scope":"project"},{"scope":"shared"},{"scope":"global"}]}`, a scope gaining `allow`, `deny` or `ask` lists from the settings, the unparsable rule `ls` included. Review modes that require review for every tool call: `request-review` (reads inside the workspace aside, changelog 1.1.20) and `strict`; `always-proceed` and `proceed-in-sandbox` approve. Not found: a workspace or project-root field in any report, and the files that hold shared or project rules — ten guesses at `~/.gemini/config/config.json`, `~/.gemini/config/projects/*.json` and dream-work's `.agents`/`.gemini`/`.antigravity` reported nothing, so the two scopes are read but not proven to surface (a Known limit). Found instead: from a dream-work under a git checkout agy loads the `.agents/skills` of the checkout and of every directory between (41 skills of this repo; a probe skill in the sandbox home's `.agents`), and not from a sibling directory; `/hooks` reported `[]`. The saved reports are `internal/dream/testdata/oracle/` (14 pairs, no account data). — by: implementer, Phase 4a.
D25 — 2026-10-28 — `visibleHome`'s departures from § Interfaces rule 2, none against a decision: the reports name no workspace (D24), so fyr walks dream-work's ancestors itself, as written and as resolved, and fails on a `.git` (a checkout, whose `.agents` agy loads) or a `.agents` in any of them except the home's own, which loads in every session the operator starts under it (D8's class; this box has a `~/.agents`, so the alternative left the visible branch unreachable here); a `trustedWorkspaces` entry at or above dream-work fails (trust loads a workspace's hooks, changelog 1.1.1 at `:834`), a relative one too; `env` is fyr's environment and `visibleHome` applies `childEnv` with `HOME=home` itself, so no caller can pass the oracle more. Consequence for Phase 5: V1 and V2's `$S/vis` sits inside this checkout, whose `.git` sends every dream private; their sandbox home must be outside every checkout, which the Phase 5 Kickoff's "nothing outside this repository" forbids — the operator's call before Phase 5 (the handoff's Next Steps). — by: implementer, Phase 4a.
D26 — 2026-10-28 — Phase 4b's review of Phases 2–4b (`REVIEW-2026-10-28-1741-security-review-visible-dream-phases-2-4b-oracle`, `REVIEW-2026-10-28-1741-review-visible-dream-phases-2-4b-session-check-c`): (1) a third oracle report, `agy -p /hooks --output-format json`, must be `{"hooks":[]}`, else the project runs private: a pre-tool hook can return a permission decision none of the reports show; this narrows D8 (MCP servers, plugins without hooks and the home's skills still load; a home with a hook never dreams visibly); (2) `/config` is pinned both ways to the 36 keys agy 1.4.9 reported, `permissions` to `allow`/`deny`/`ask`, and `artifactReviewPolicy` to `asks-for-review`, Interfaces rule 5 as written ("anything else fails"), which `readConfig` had kept for five keys only; (3) a run that stops for want of a session sweeps a killed run's copies under the lock when `~/.config/fyr` exists (`sweepIdle`), since the no-session hours otherwise kept a private home's login copy for days; (4) the branch reason in `dream.log` and the dry run is redacted, folded and stripped of control characters, with its paths as written (`logReason`). ADR-073 is not edited; its D8 Consequence reads narrower by this row. — by: the operator for (1), "Require no hooks (Recommended)" (the question popup, 2026-10-28); the implementer for (2)–(4), on the security review's findings 1, 3 and 5.
Rebutted (cold read round 1): "Phase 4 needs the operator's real settings" — D11's oracle research runs in a sandbox home with variants written by the session, never the operator's files (R6).
Rebutted (cold read round 1): "`openRegular` refuses a symlinked `settings.json`" — fyr no longer reads the settings files (D11).
Answered (cold read round 1): the restatement list now holds `skills/dream/SKILL.md:3`, README lines 3 and 19, `dream_arms_test.go:36`, the dry-run and auth-hint texts, and the living records (`SPEC-fyr-memory-loop`, `GUIDE-testing`, `DEPLOY-local`, `SPEC-fyr-metrics`); closed records (bugs, changes, handoffs, ADRs) are never rewritten. Changelog citations now carry versions and the file; AS5 no longer claims line 324 proves safety. Assumptions are AS1–AS5, distinct from ledger A2. Terms, verify tags and the record-edit mechanism are defined in § Why. Phase 4 split into 4a and 4b. Phase 5's user boxes move to the handoff when not done, as the feature skill's Step 6 allows.
Rejected: a hidden `--timer` flag so only the timer's run checks for a session — a second shape for `--all`; a manual `--all` with no session is told so.
Rejected: a `dream.log` line per hourly no-op — 24 lines a day of nothing; the journal has them.
Rejected: `TimeoutStartSec` under an hour — a run of several projects at up to 10 minutes each can exceed it; a `Persistent=` timer does not start an active unit, so a long run only skips an hour.
Rejected: parsing `settings.json` and the shared `config.json` by hand (the first draft) — two sources of at least four, a guessed schema for the second, and no view of review or cycle modes (D11).

| 1 | The release upload waited for approval the ship request had already given | "What are you waiting for? finish it" — feedback log 2026-09-18T23:00:00+02:00 | correction of procedure | `skill:preflight` |
| 2 | A value added to a vocabulary in prose, not in the file's schema/template lines; a claim reversed in one file and left in five others — four review rounds | `bugs/BUG-084-…md`; `reviews/2026-09-18-review-v1.2.3-3b5b71a-code.md` rounds 1–3; `reviews/2026-09-18-preflight-v1.3.0.md` | trail: prevention rule written nowhere general | `AGENTS.md § Hard rules` ("A behaviour change includes the text that DESCRIBES it") |
| 3 | The verifier's definition alone held in 1 of 3 runs, then 1 of 1 after the wording fix; the first two attempts proved nothing (permission gate; `--allowedTools` swallowing the prompt); a scratch `HOME` cannot authenticate either CLI | `bugs/BUG-083-…md`; `changes/2026-09-18-retro-applied.md` § Verification; handoff `2026-09-18-v1.3.0-released.md` § Agent notes | trail: prevention rule; missing knowledge in the project's own testing recipe | `project AGENTS.md § Testing` |

## Proposals

### Proposal 1: Showing the release notes is not a gate
Scope: harness — Target: `skills/preflight/SKILL.md` Step 6, item 1 — Status: applied 2026-09-18 (42fad8f) (harness queue: `~/.config/sh-agent/proposals/2026-09-18-retro.md`)

### Proposal 4: The behavioural-run recipe for an agent or context change says how it is run and what it proves
Scope: project — Target: `AGENTS.md` § Testing — Status: applied 2026-09-18 (42fad8f)
Scope rule: target-in-project — why: this repo's own testing procedure for its own files; the promotion check (`retros.jsonl` targets named `AGENTS.md` from other projects; feedback `rule_ref` `project AGENTS.md § Testing` from other projects) found no hit.

Trigger: BUG-083. The verifier's rewritten rule was tested by `claude -p --agents` in a scratch clone: the first run was blocked at the permission gate (no `--allowedTools`), the second had its prompt swallowed by the variadic `--allowedTools` list, and only then did three runs produce evidence — 1 of 3, then 1 of 1 after the wording fix. A tier-4 CLI start from a scratch `HOME` failed on both CLIs ("Not logged in"; "authentication timed out") because credentials live in the real home. None of this is in the paragraph that prescribes the run.

Current behaviour: § Testing says "`claude -p --agents <json built from the working-tree file>` in a scratch clone of a small repository, several runs, with the agent's artifact carrying something only the new definition writes".

Expected behaviour: the same sentence names the dispatch shape, the permission form and the way the result is reported, and says where a CLI start can authenticate.

diff:
```
-A change to `agents/*.md` also gets a behavioural run: `claude -p --agents <json built from the working-tree file>` in a scratch clone of a small repository, several runs, with the agent's artifact carrying something only the new definition writes, so the run proves which definition ran;
+A change to `agents/*.md` also gets a behavioural run: `claude -p --agents <json built from the working-tree file>` in a scratch clone of a small repository, several runs, with the agent's artifact carrying something only the new definition writes, so the run proves which definition ran — the dispatch text does NOT repeat the changed rule (the definition alone is under test), the prompt goes on stdin because `--allowedTools` is variadic and swallows a trailing argument, `--allowedTools` names the agent's tools or every call is refused at the permission gate and the run proves nothing, the tool-call order is read from the run's subagent transcript under `~/.claude/projects/`, and the result is reported as n of N runs, never "works" (BUG-083);
```
and, after "The real home is never touched.":
```
+A CLI started from a scratch `HOME` cannot authenticate (credentials live in the real home), so the tier-4 CLI start is the sandbox procedure or the real-home smoke checks, never `HOME=<scratch> claude -p`.
```

Rationale: the recipe that took four attempts to get right is written where the next change to `agents/` will read it; applying it graduates BUG-083's prevention rule (`bugs` moves the row).

### Proposal 5: The delivery claim has one home; every other living file points at it
Scope: project — Target: `AGENTS.md` § How the harness works, a new rule 6 — Status: applied 2026-09-18 (42fad8f)
Scope rule: target-in-project — why: this repo's own docs convention; no promotion hit.

Trigger: the v1.3.0 gate. Applying ADR-033's model to README:245 (round 1) exposed the ADR-030 sentence in `AGENTS.md:63` (round 2), which exposed `remote.md:8`, `:91`, `:195` and `delivery.md:7`, `:56` (round 3): one claim, six restatements, each found by the previous fix's pointer. The next delivery ADR does it again.

Current behaviour: rule 3 says a path change lands in ONE commit with the code, the docs and the map; nothing says where the prose claim lives.

Expected behaviour: one home, and every other file a one-line pointer.

diff (after rule 5):
```
+6. **The delivery claim has one home.** What a tag delivers, to which kind of place, and how a place moves forward is stated once, in `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md` § The model; README, this file, the deploy guides and the ADRs point at it in one sentence and never restate it. The v1.3.0 gate spent three review rounds finding the same claim stale in six files after one ADR (ADR-030 → ADR-033); a change to the claim is one file plus the map.
```
Applying it is a docs task: `delivery.md` gets the § The model paragraph (the ADR-033 wording now in `AGENTS.md:63`), and the six sentences become pointers — `documentation` for README/spec/deploy, the main agent for `AGENTS.md`; `/review --docs` over the range.

Rationale: the sweep rule (Proposal 2) catches a stale restatement; this removes the restatements so there is nothing to catch.

## Feedback log entries

- 2026-09-18T23:00:00+02:00 — correction — "What are you waiting for? finish it" — `skill:preflight` (finding 1).

## Not proposed

- `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:77`'s IN PROGRESS qualifier: an accepted gate low, a Task in the handoff, not a rule gap.
- The verifier's `go run … --dry-run` "1 written" observation: the testing guide's tier 3a already prescribes the built binary; dispatch text, not a rule.
- The `sh-agent-update.timer` on this box installing a push thirty seconds later: the map's own dashed line (remote.md § timer), documented; the project rule "no timer as the mechanism" is about delivery, and the timer runs `update`, which is the mechanism. Nothing to change.
- The Mac's `type` path and devbox's `~/.local/bin`: matrix facts, recorded.

name: asking-format
description: "How to put questions and unclear items to the operator — short list for one choice, numbered table for several, full write-ups on request only"

# Vendor format check — context, skills, subagents   (2026-09-03)

Range reviewed: the working tree after the rebuild (e75bf90 plus the rename and GCP-rule changes)

Documentation-based check that what `sh-agent install` deploys is in the shape each vendor documents. The live check on the operator's Mac is a later task.

## Verdict: PASS with three fixes applied

## Sources

| Vendor | Source | What it settled |
|---|---|---|
| Agent Skills spec | https://agentskills.io/specification | `SKILL.md` fields: `name` (1–64, lowercase, hyphens, **must match the directory name**), `description` (1–1024), `license`, `compatibility`, `metadata` (string map), `allowed-tools` (space-separated). Optional `scripts/`, `references/`, `assets/`. Keep `SKILL.md` under 500 lines. |
| Claude Code skills | https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md | User-level `~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`; command name comes from the directory; extra fields `disable-model-invocation`, `user-invocable`, `argument-hint`, `arguments`, `allowed-tools`, `disallowed-tools`, `model`, `effort`, `context`, `agent`, `background`, `hooks`, `paths`, `shell`, `when_to_use`; `metadata` is kept but not acted on; `description` + `when_to_use` are capped at 1,536 characters in the listing; `~/.claude/commands/*.md` still works but is merged into skills. |
| Claude Code subagents | https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.md | User-level `~/.claude/agents/<file>.md`, identity from `name`; `tools` is a comma-separated string; `skills` is a YAML block list; `model` ∈ sonnet/opus/haiku/fable/inherit/full id; `memory` ∈ user/project/local; `isolation: worktree`; `effort` ∈ low…max; `maxTurns` integer; `description` single line. |
| Claude Code memory | https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (via the claude-code-guide agent) | `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` supports `@path` imports, relative to the file, up to 4 hops; user-level imports load without a prompt. |
| Antigravity CLI 1.1.24 | Embedded customization guide and changelog in the `agy` binary (`agy changelog`; `strings` on the binary) | Global customization root `~/.gemini/config/` (skills at `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, agents created by `/agents` there, `skills.json`/`plugins.json`, `mcp_config.json`, `hooks.json`); workspace root `.agents/` with `rules/*.md`, `skills/`, `agents/<name>/agent.md`; workflows deprecated in favour of skills; skills injected by name + description (progressive disclosure); markdown agents support `mainAgent`, `subagent`, `hidden`, `inheritMcp`, `inheritCustomizations`, `commandExecutionPolicy`, `model` (`flash`/`pro`/`inherit`), plus `tools`, `skills`, `rules`, `plugins`, `mcpServers` keys; markdown agents inherit ambient skills and rules by default; `disable-model-invocation` is a recognised skill key. |

## Skills (28)

Checked by script: every `name` equals its directory name and matches `[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`; every description is non-empty and under 1,024 characters; no `SKILL.md` exceeds 500 lines; every frontmatter key is either a spec field or a documented Claude Code field.

- **Fix:** `mermaid-syntax` had a top-level `version: 1.5.0`, which is not a spec field. Moved to `metadata: {version: "1.5.0"}`.
- `bash` and `docker` use `allowed-tools: Bash` (spec field, experimental; Claude honours it, Antigravity ignores unknown fields).
- `audit`, `distill`, `grill-me`, `handoff`, `init-project`, `research`, `retro` use `disable-model-invocation: true` + `argument-hint`; both vendors know the first, Antigravity ignores the second.
- Vendored skills (`anti-ui-slop`, `gke-basics`, `gcloud-auth-verification`, `skill-repair`, `terraform`, `codebase-design`, `grilling`, `grill-me`, `find-skills`) carry `license`/`metadata` per spec; untouched.
- Directory layout: `references/`, `assets/`, `examples/` only. No `scripts/` remain.

## Subagents (6)

- Frontmatter keys used: `name`, `description`, `tools`, `model`, `effort`, `maxTurns`, plus `memory` (changelog, documentation), `skills` (reviewer), `isolation` (verifier). All documented for Claude Code.
- **Fix:** `reviewer` had `skills: review-standards` as a scalar; the docs show a block list. Changed to `skills:\n  - review-standards`. The installer's frontmatter parser was taught YAML block lists so the inventory and derivation read both spellings.
- Descriptions are one line, double-quoted, 317–446 characters, free of unescaped colons.
- Antigravity derivation emits `name`, quoted `description`, `subagent: true`, `mainAgent: false`, `model` (`opus`→`pro`, `haiku`→`flash`, `sonnet` omitted = inherit), `tools` mapped to `view_file`, `grep_search`, `find_by_name`, `run_command`, `write_to_file`, `replace_file_content`; Claude-only keys dropped. `skills` is dropped because markdown agents inherit the global skills.
- The agy binary carries `description` YAML keys, so a frontmatter `description` is read; what its changelog calls "H1-delimited system prompts" could not be pinned down from the binary. The derived body keeps `##` headings only, so the whole body is one prompt. Left for the live check.

## Global context

- Claude Code: `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` = marker line + `@AGENTS.md` → `~/.claude/AGENTS.md`. Documented import form, one hop, user level.
- Antigravity: `~/.gemini/config/rules/AGENTS.md`. The global root is confirmed; the `rules/` subdirectory is the workspace convention (`.agents/rules/*.md`) applied to the global root, and the plugin guide recommends `rules/AGENTS.md` as the consolidated rule file. Left for the live check. If it fails, the alternative is a plugin (`~/.gemini/config/plugins/sh-agent/{plugin.json,rules/AGENTS.md}`), which needs no registration when placed in the global root.
- Content: 104 lines deployed (context + environment + inventory), no vendor-specific instructions except the discovery note.

## What was not checked

- Live loading on either CLI (deliberately deferred by the operator).
- Antigravity IDE paths (out of scope).
- The exact agy tool-name list beyond the six mapped names.

## Verdict: APPROVE

Nothing is broken. This is the round-1 fix commit for the two-lens Phase 7 review (`2026-09-15-review-641eccd-worktree-merged.md`) plus the Phase 7 gate-advisory and init-update work. All five round-1 code/docs fixes (P4–P7, P6) are present, correct, and match the code they describe; the new test can fail; `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `gofmt -l` are clean. The three Go files touched (`apply.go`, `main.go`, `harness_test.go`) carry only string/comment changes — no logic changed, so there is no new flow-tracing surface to break. I re-derived the round-1 fixes independently from the diff rather than trusting the prior report, and confirmed them:

- `internal/harness/apply.go:37` and `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:309` — both now tell the operator to move a hand-written `CLAUDE.md`'s content into a rule file under `rules/` and let `install` write the one-line import; matches `README.md:53` and R2 (`REQUIREMENTS.md`).
- `internal/harness/harness_test.go:257` — new assertion `strings.Contains(out.String(), "move its content into a rule file under rules/")`. This is a real, failable assertion: reverting the `apply.go:37` string change makes it fail (the old string was "add the line `@AGENTS.md` to it yourself"), and it does not duplicate the pre-existing `keep    ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` check above it.
- `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:65,77,81` — Step 4 is advisory (owner/severity/confidence, filed under Follow-ups/Next Steps), Step 5's blocking list has no docs clause ("Step 4's docs gaps never block"), Step 6's "needs none" sentence is gone. Cross-checked against ADR-024 in `DECISIONS.md` and plan rows D46/D49 — consistent, and BUG-026 is recorded `fixed` in `INDEX.md` and its own record.
- `README.md:32`, `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md:12,27` — the `--vendor` default/widening text matches `resolveVendor` (`cmd/sh-agent/main.go:216`) and the `update` command's vendor handling (`:344-350`): `update` passes `--vendor` only when `vendor != VendorAll`, so an install recorded as a single vendor stays that vendor across `update`, and `--vendor all` on `install` only is the widening path the docs describe.
- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:124` / `AGENTS.md:35` — comment says "image or VM build step"; matches `deploy/remote.md`'s new description of the two mirrors' different build steps.

I also re-verified several evidence claims recorded in this range's own review/changes artifacts rather than taking them on faith (the `grep -cF` counts in plan task 7.7 and the changes entry for the gate-docs-advisory work); all reproduce exactly as claimed.

No REQUIREMENTS.md violation, no recorded bug (BUG-INDEX) reintroduced, no hand-rolled auth/crypto, no new dependency.

## Findings

None that meet the correctness/security/rule bar. Two low-confidence observations, not findings (no concrete failure mode, noted for completeness):

- `skills/init-project/SKILL.md` Step 4's new per-file copy loop (`find ... | while read -r f; ... [ -e "$d" ] && continue ...`) replaces the old `cp -R`; I traced its `.gitkeep`-only-into-empty-directory branch and the `[ -e "$d" ]` skip-if-exists branch by hand and both are correct for the cases the accompanying changes entry claims were tested (fresh clone: 18 files + 4 links added; second run: nothing added). This is prose in a skill file, not executed by CI, so I did not run it myself; the changes entry (`…phase7-init-update.md`) says the code reviewer ran it in scratch clones with matching results, which I did not re-verify independently. Low confidence, not a finding.
- The `.gitignore`-in-gofmt-list noise (`gofmt -l .` also lists files under `.agents/scratch/adv-init/...` and `.agents/scratch/lintcheck/main.go`) is pre-existing scratch content, gitignored (`.gitignore:21`), untouched by this diff, and not part of the repo's tracked Go tree. Not a finding.

## Criteria

1. Dead code — pass. # Review — 641eccd-worktree-code   (2026-09-15)

Range reviewed: 641eccd..fe21671 (`git diff 641eccd..fe21671 -- context agents skills README.md AGENTS.md .agents/docs/deploy .agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md`) plus the uncommitted working tree (`git diff fe21671 -- skills .agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md`: `skills/init-project/SKILL.md`, `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md`)

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

The worst problem is in `/preflight` Step 4, the mechanism ADR-023 just settled. A rebutted docs finding is carried forward only from the newest prior gate report's `## Outcome`, and no step writes the carried rebuttal into the next report's `## Outcome`. So one gate report later the finding is raised again and blocks. That is the failure ADR-023 was written to remove ("instead of blocking every later release"). A second defect sits in the same mechanism: the docs reviewer is never told about the rebuttal, so its REQUEST CHANGES verdict can still block. A third: Step 6 still says SHIP "has no findings left", which contradicts Step 4's new `left` gaps. These three findings are the third round on this one mechanism (BUG-026, ADR-023). Under Definition of Done step 2 and BUG-026's prevention rule, take them to the operator before a third patch. Two findings sit outside preflight. README's new `--vendor all` "widens" claim is false for `sh-agent update`. And the binary's two CLAUDE.md messages still give the procedure README just replaced. The working-tree init-project update is sound. Its shell snippets were run in scratch clones and behaved as documented, and the new `init-update` matrix check passes a correct update and fails two wrong ones.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:65` — A rebuttal is carried forward for one gate report only.
  - Step 4 reads "the `## Outcome` of the newest prior `reviews/*-preflight-*` report" and cites a rebutted finding "in the gate report". It does not say the citation goes into that report's `## Outcome`.
  - Step 6 (line 81) fills `## Outcome` only with "one line per finding" of the gate it resolves. A cited finding is by definition not raised, so it gets no line. On SHIP the report "needs none".
  - Failure path: gate N-1 has the rebuttal in its Outcome. Gate N reads it and cites the finding in its body. Gate N+1 reads gate N's Outcome, finds no rebuttal, and raises and blocks the finding again. That happens whenever two NO-SHIPs follow each other, or a SHIP is followed by the next release.
  - Same day, same version: Step 5 writes the same path, `$(date +%F)-preflight-<version>.md`, so the re-run overwrites the report whose Outcome held the rebuttal. Git still has it; the next run does not read git.
  - The "same statement at the same file:line" key also breaks when a fix for another finding shifts lines in the same doc. That key is the operator's ADR-023 wording, so this is noted for the operator, not re-argued.
  - Fix (operator's call, per BUG-026): Step 4 reads the Outcome of every prior preflight report, or each gate report copies carried rebuttals into its own `## Outcome`. The shorter option: a rebutted docs finding gets a doc change so it stops being raised, and the carry-forward mechanism is deleted.
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:65,77` — A rebutted finding can still block through the reviewer's verdict.
  - Step 4 dispatches the docs reviewer "with the docs brief exactly as `/review` Step 3 gives it". That brief (`skills/review/SKILL.md:48`) carries no prior rebuttals, so the reviewer raises the rebutted finding again and sets its verdict from it.
  - Step 5 blocks on "a Step 4 REQUEST CHANGES verdict or high-severity docs finding, not counting a finding a prior gate report rebutted". The exclusion names findings, not the verdict.
  - Result: a rebutted finding that is the only reason for REQUEST CHANGES still blocks every run.
  - Fix: the verdict blocks only when a non-rebutted finding supports it. Or drop the verdict clause and block on high-severity non-rebutted findings alone.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:81` — Step 6 contradicts the new `left` gaps.
  - Stale text: "the SHIP path has no findings left and needs none" (no `## Outcome`).
  - Line 65, changed in this range, now says "every other gap is recorded as `left` with an owner", and ADR-023 says "A low-severity docs gap can ship, recorded with its owner". A SHIP report therefore does have `left` findings.
  - No step says where they go: Step 5's section list has no place for them, and Step 6 says SHIP needs none.
  - An agent following Step 6 on SHIP drops the owners ADR-023 requires. This is the describing-text rule (review-standards §3).
  - Fix: Step 5 names where `left` gaps go on SHIP (for example a `## Outcome` with `left` lines), and line 81 drops "has no findings left".
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `README.md:32` (also `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md:27`, which is scoped to install) — `--vendor all` does not widen through `update`.
  - README says every command accepts `--vendor` and "`--vendor all` widens a single-vendor install to both". That holds for `install`: `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:137` passes an explicit flag through the rebuild.
  - It fails for `update`: `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:348` appends `--vendor` only when `vendor != harness.VendorAll`. The child `install --repo …` then resolves the default from the manifest (`resolveVendor`, main.go:216-224) and reinstalls the old single vendor.
  - Silent failure: `sh-agent update --vendor all` on a claude-only install never installs Antigravity.
  - Checked by reading the code. Not run, because `update` fetches and pulls this repo.
  - Fix: pass `--vendor` whenever `vendorFlag != ""`, as install does, with a test. Or narrow the README sentence to `install`.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/apply.go:37`, `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:309` — The binary contradicts README's new CLAUDE.md procedure.
  - README.md:53 now tells the operator to move a hand-written `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` into `rules/`, remove it, and reinstall, so the file becomes the one-line import R2 requires.
  - The binary still prints the replaced procedure: `install` says "add the line `@AGENTS.md` to it yourself", and `status` says "make sure it contains the line `@AGENTS.md`".
  - Following the binary leaves a CLAUDE.md with content plus an import, which is not the one-line import of REQUIREMENTS.md R2. The operator also gets two conflicting instructions.
  - This is a describing-text miss (review-standards §3; BUG-027's "grep the subject, not the old wording"). The binary is outside the diff's paths but is what README describes.
  - Fix: change both messages to point at the README procedure. No test asserts on either string (grep of `cmd/`, `internal/`).

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. The change is docs and skill text only, with no orphaned file or dangling reference. The `anti-ui-slop` MANIFEST mention was correctly removed: the directory holds only LICENSE and NOTICE.
2. Flow tracing — fail. `--vendor all` traced through `update` → `Reinstall` → child `install` loses the flag (finding 4). Preflight Step 4 → Step 5 → Step 6 → the next Step 4 loses the rebuttal (findings 1, 2).
   - What held: README `--dry-run`, `--force` and repo discovery via parents match `main.go`/`repo.go`. The remote.md mirror paragraph matches both mirrors' `VENDORED.md`, crew's `image/Dockerfile` builder stage, argolis's `032_setup-harness.sh` (run as root) and its 5-minute `devbox-autoupdate.timer`. The Mac log cited in remote.md exists.
   - init-project Steps 3–6, run in `.agents/scratch/review-641eccd/upd` (a clone of the older demo-app scaffold): update added only `.agents/docs/retros/.gitkeep`, and a second run added nothing.
   - The `init-update` matrix check exits 0 after a correct update and 1 for a modified `TODO.md` and for a scaffold-message commit (BUG-024's must-pass rule met).
   - In a fresh repo (`.agents/scratch/review-641eccd-new`) the loops produce exactly the documented tree and four resolving links. A wrong-target link and a real directory are reported as "kept".
3. Standards conformance — fail on describing text (findings 3, 5). The init-project staging and commit wording matches the global hard rules (stage by name, read `--cached --stat`, commit in its own call). `go run ./cmd/sh-agent list` and `install --dry-run --home .agents/scratch/review-641eccd-home` exit 0: the new quoted frontmatter passes the installer's lint, and the dry run wrote no file.
4. Directory layout — pass. No new files. The new matrix row sits in the existing table.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — concern, not a separate finding. The preflight rebuttal carry-forward is the third round of patches on one mechanism (BUG-026). Deleting it (fix the doc so the finding stops recurring) is shorter than defending it. No security-sensitive code.
6. Decoupling — pass. Skill edits stay inside their own files. Preflight reuses the `/review` docs brief by reference, which is also why finding 2 needs a change on the preflight side, not in the brief.

## Not examined
- `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-15-harness-practices-g01-g26.md` (modified in the working tree; outside the dispatched scope).
- The `init-update` matrix row was not run through either CLI. Only its check was exercised, against states built by hand.

- The commit message's verification claims (`go test -race`, `gofmt`, `go vet`, render) were not re-run: no Go file is in scope.
- `sh-agent update` was not executed (it fetches and pulls this repo), so finding 4 is from reading the code.
- Of argolis `032_setup-harness.sh`, only the header was read; crew's `entrypoint.sh` was not read.

title: Review — c192622-22c106c-code, round 2 (2026-09-15)
body:
# Review — c192622-22c106c-code, round 2   (2026-09-15)

Range reviewed: c192622..22c106c, paths `context agents skills README.md AGENTS.md` (`git diff c192622..22c106c -- context agents skills README.md AGENTS.md`), plus the uncommitted round-1 fixes in the working tree (`git diff -- skills agents`: `agents/bugs.md`, `skills/{bug,feature,handoff,init-project,preflight}/SKILL.md`; 6 files, +12/-12). Standards: `skills/review-standards/SKILL.md` § 1–3 as in this repository.

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

Of the seven round-1 fixes, five are correct and complete: F1, F3, F4, F6 and F7. Two of them introduced new defects.

The worst is F2, which rewrote the preflight Step 4 mechanism, the one the round-1 review asked about. Every Step 4 docs finding now blocks the release, and the fix after NO-SHIP is followed by a full `/preflight` re-run. But Step 4 has no coverage rule and ignores prior rebuttals. A finding rebutted in the gate report's `## Outcome`, which Step 6 explicitly allows, is re-raised by the fresh docs reviewer on the re-run. Step 5 then blocks again, and Step 6 allows no override. A release with a correct rebuttal therefore cannot ship. By the context's own rule, this is the second round landing on the same mechanism.

The second defect is F5, the bug-fix clause added to preflight Step 2. It contradicts ADR-022, which is Accepted, and plan row D8. Both say that Step 2's release-diff threshold stays.

Neither new defect breaks the installer, and no frontmatter changed.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:65`, `:77`, `:81` — a rebutted Step 4 docs finding blocks every re-run, and nothing stops it.
  - **The rules involved:**
    - `:65` says each Step 4 finding "blocks the release" and that "`/preflight` runs again".
    - `:77` lists "a Step 4 docs finding" as blocking, with no exception.
    - `:81` lets the task that resolves NO-SHIP findings close one as `rebutted`, and says "Never ship on NO-SHIP — no override."
  - **Why the re-run does not honour a rebuttal:**
    - Step 4 dispatches the docs reviewer "with the docs brief exactly as `/review` Step 3 gives it", over the whole `<base>..HEAD`. The dispatch has no mention of the earlier gate report or its Outcome.
    - Step 2 has a way through: it reuses a prior report whose `Range reviewed:` covers the commits. Step 4 has nothing like that.
  - **Concrete failure:** the docs reviewer raises a false positive. It is rebutted with a checkable reason, as `/review` Step 4 requires. `/preflight` runs again, and the same diff against the same docs gets the same finding, so the result is NO-SHIP again. The only ways out are editing correct docs until the reviewer is satisfied, or abandoning the release.
  - **Introduced by the fix:** before it, the gate fixed docs findings inside the run, so a re-run was rare. Now every Step 4 finding forces a full re-run, and each re-run re-reads text that was already accepted.
  - **Fix, either of these:**
    - At `:77`, exclude a Step 4 finding that an earlier gate report over the same base lists as `rebutted` in its `## Outcome`, and have Step 4 pass those Outcome lines to the docs reviewer.
    - Simpler: give Step 4 Step 2's coverage rule. Cite a prior `*-docs` report whose `Range reviewed:` covers the commits and whose gate Outcome closes every finding, and run the docs lens only over the commits after it.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:50` — the F5 fix contradicts an Accepted ADR and a plan decision.
  - **What the records say:**
    - ADR-022 Consequences (`.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md:179`): "Features and tasks keep the 50-line / 5-file threshold, and so does the release gate's review of the release diff (`skills/preflight/SKILL.md` Step 2), which reads a sub-threshold release diff itself."
    - Plan D8 (`plans/2026-09-15-harness-practices-g01-g26.md:1197`) says the same.
  - **What changed:** `:50` now also dispatches the release reviewer when the range "adds a bug fix". `DECISIONS.md` is unmodified, and no new ADR or D-row records the change.
  - **Concrete failure:** a later reviewer or resume reads the Accepted ADR as the decision. Round 1 of this review did exactly that ("ADR-022's Consequences keep it on purpose"), and so will a future session, which then either reverts `:50` or sees two authorities that disagree.
  - **Not needed in behaviour:** `skills/bug/SKILL.md:53` already reviews every bug fix whatever its size. Step 2's coverage rule then cites that report, so the clause only fires for a fix that skipped its own Definition of Done.
  - **Fix:** prefer the shorter one. Revert `:50` and correct the Phase 5 changes entry's wording in the next `changes/` entry. That was the round-1 docs report's second option, and it agrees with ADR-022 and D8. Otherwise, append an ADR that amends ADR-022 plus a D-row superseding D8.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-15-harness-practices-g01-g26.md` (outside the dispatched paths; trail) — two fixes changed rehearsed plan edits without the D-row that `skills/feature/SKILL.md:85` requires.
  - **Which edits:**
    - The F1 fix changed I-23b's "no" branch (plan `:1023` still holds the removed text).
    - The F2 fix deleted I-21d–g's post-gate fix path (plan `:914`, `:922`, `:930`).
  - **What goes stale:** task 5.4's ticked expect greps for "fix those in skills, agents, rules", "Step 4's docs fixes, the changelog entry" and "plus its records and Step 4's docs fixes". None of those strings exists in the working tree any more.
  - **Where it fails:** Phase 6's Checkpoint must map every I-edit to a matrix row. Mapped from the plan, it would expect behaviour that the tree no longer has, and a resume reading the plan's Decisions finds no record that the mechanism changed.
  - **Fix:** add dated D-rows for both changes (by: review round 1) that name the superseded I-edit text.

### Round-1 fixes verified
- **F1** `skills/init-project/SKILL.md:44` — **fixed.**
  - The harness no longer writes a `CLAUDE.md` that is not a one-line import. On "no" the file is untouched, and the summary says Claude Code will not import `AGENTS.md`.
  - This matches `README.md:53`'s handling of a hand-written global `CLAUDE.md`.
  - Step 7 stages only created paths, so an untouched `CLAUDE.md` is not committed.
  - `git grep "keep the content and add"` over the dispatched paths prints nothing.
- **F3** `skills/init-project/SKILL.md:8`, `:66` — **fixed.**
  - `:8` no longer claims anything about Antigravity.
  - `:66` matches `testing/2026-09-15-verify-g26-precedence.md`: Antigravity CLI 1.2.3 found neither control skill nor control agent (rows 28–29), and project rules were not in the test's table. It also matches `context/AGENTS.md:37` ("may not load on every vendor… `/skills` and `/agents` show what a vendor loaded").
  - No other non-vendored file claims Antigravity loads the project layer (grepped `README.md context agents skills commands rules AGENTS.md`).
- **F4** `skills/handoff/SKILL.md:49` — **fixed.** It agrees with `skills/bug/SKILL.md:49` word for word, with `agents/changelog.md:94`, and with the same skill's `:32` (its Follow-ups are read as open work).
- **F2** `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:65`, `:77`, `:85`, `:90` — **the round-1 defect is gone; a new defect was introduced** (finding 1).
  - Gone: fixes now go through ordinary work with its Definition of Done, and a re-run's Step 2 verification row needs a log that reaches the new HEAD, so nothing unchecked reaches the tag.
  - Nothing else in the dispatched paths still describes in-gate docs fixes.
- **F5** `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:50` — **wording applied, but it conflicts with the decision record** (finding 2).
- **F6** `agents/bugs.md:76` — **fixed.** The five homes equal `context/AGENTS.md:31` and `agents/bugs.md:70`, and ADR-021 (which also lists `context/AGENTS.md` for this repository).
- **F7** `skills/feature/SKILL.md:97`, `skills/bug/SKILL.md:53` — **fixed.** Both use exactly the trigger wording of `context/AGENTS.md:17` and `agents/documentation.md:12`.

### Considered, not findings
- **`:65` "the gate never edits the tree after it has run" versus Step 6 SHIP.** The changelog entry and the version bump are written after the gate. Step 6 names them explicitly and they predate this range, so a reader has no ambiguity that fails.
- **`:50`'s proxy "a `bugs/BUG-*.md` record in the range".** It also matches process-failure records such as BUG-008, BUG-011 and BUG-013, which are not fixes. The cost is an extra review, not a correctness failure. It is moot if `:50` is reverted.
- **Handoff Step 3 (`:64`) versus the table (`:49`).** Step 3 sends "any deferred idea worth keeping" to Next Steps; the table sends deferred work to the plan's Follow-ups when a plan is active. Resume reads both locations (`:32`), so nothing is lost.
- **Base-ref fallback on a re-run in a tagless project (`:44`).** It takes the base before the dots of the newest preflight report, so a NO-SHIP report does not shift the base.
- **Frontmatter.** No uncommitted fix touches frontmatter, so there is no BUG-004 exposure. No file under `cmd/` or `internal/` changed.

## Criteria
1. **Dead code: pass.** Markdown only. The fixes delete the post-gate fix path whole, with no residual references in the dispatched paths (`git grep` for "docs fixes", "still unfixed", "keep the content", "find the same rules" prints nothing there).
2. **Flow tracing: fail.** The preflight re-run after a rebutted Step 4 finding cannot reach SHIP (finding 1). Traced so far:
   - Step 4 fix → ordinary Definition of Done → re-run Step 1, Step 2 coverage and verifier row → Step 5. This holds.
   - The installer copies the changed files verbatim, and no Go test asserts the changed wording (`grep` over `internal cmd`).
3. **Standards conformance: fail.**
   - `:50` contradicts the Accepted ADR-022 and D8 (finding 2).
   - Plan edits changed without D-rows (finding 3).
   - Describing texts for F3, F4, F6 and F7 now agree with their sources (§ 3 last box).
   - gofmt, vet and tests are not applicable, since no Go changed.
4. **Directory layout: pass.** No new, moved or deleted file.
5. **Simplicity (DIY-except-security): pass with a note.** Deleting the in-gate fix path made preflight shorter, which is the right direction. Finding 1's coverage-rule fix keeps it short. Nothing security-related is hand-rolled, and no dependency was added.
6. **Decoupling: pass.** The `documentation` and main-agent routing is stated the same way in `context/AGENTS.md:16`, `skills/review/SKILL.md:60` and `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:65`.

## Not examined
- **Round-1 range not re-read in full.** Round 1 read the whole committed range. In round 2 I re-read in full only the fixed files: `init-project` and `preflight` whole, `handoff` lines 30–80, and `bugs.md`'s range diff. The other committed files in the range were not re-read.
- **Nothing was run.** No CLI start, install, status or Go tests; the change is Markdown only and touches no frontmatter.
- **Round-1 docs report read only by grep.** Only the lines matching preflight, Step 2 and ADR-022 were read. The merged report was read in full.
- **G26 precedence log read in part.** Lines 9–52 were read by grep, plus lines 79–90 in full.
- **Other files outside the dispatched paths.** Beyond the cited lines: the plan (only grepped), `changes/`, the uncommitted `skill-matrix.md` and `ROADMAP.md` edits (seen in the diff, not judged), vendored skills.
- **Whether Claude Code imports `@AGENTS.md` from a `CLAUDE.md` that has other content too.** This bears only on the accuracy of `init-project:44`'s summary sentence.
