| skills/docker/SKILL.md | outdated | `:105` vs `context/dev-setup.md:8`; `:108` vs `:57` |
| skills/docker/references/health-checks.md | accurate | `:40-42` agrees with cloud-run-deploy; `:8` `/healthz` matches `skills/cloud-run-deploy/SKILL.md:90` |
| skills/docker/references/setup.md | outdated | `:12` `web/.output` vs `skills/frontend/SKILL.md:43,59` |
| skills/feature/SKILL.md | outdated | `:19` `docs/bugs/INDEX.md` vs `:11`; `:82` omits `/handoff` vs `context/AGENTS.md:19` |
| skills/feedback/SKILL.md | accurate | `:54` vocabulary matches `skills/retro/SKILL.md:49`; `:81` matches `skills/handoff/SKILL.md:34,103` |
| skills/frontend/SKILL.md | accurate | `:77-99` SPA/SSR model consistent with `context/dev-setup.md:6`; current as of e5833a3 |
| skills/frontend/references/design.md | accurate | `:6` points at "Apps & Dashboards" (`skills/frontend/SKILL.md:101`); `:112` link exists |
| skills/frontend/references/theme-system.md | outdated | `:346` `tailwind.config.ts`, `:217` `index.html` vs `skills/frontend/SKILL.md:34,40,61` |

title: Review — sweep-skills-2 (2026-09-15)
body:
# Review — sweep-skills-2   (2026-09-15)

Range reviewed: working tree, `skills/golang/` read whole — `SKILL.md` (59 lines) and all seven `references/*.md` (5863 lines). This is not a diff (the tree was clean for `skills/golang`). Lens: `--docs --project`. Compared against `context/AGENTS.md`, `context/dev-setup.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `skills/review-standards/references/go-review.md`, `skills/VENDORED.md`, `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md`, `go.mod`, and the other files inside the scope.

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

`SKILL.md` is accurate, but all seven reference files are outdated. They contradict the skill's own coding standards, which the review agents enforce. Worst first:
- `golang-testing.md` teaches a `testing/synctest` call that does not compile. `golang-architecture.md:725` in the same skill says that API was replaced.
- `golang-architecture.md:544` says `Close()` errors need no check. `go-review.md:23` says the opposite, because an unchecked close on a writer can lose the final flush.
- `golang-io-web.md` makes Cobra + Viper the default CLI stack, registered in `init()`, and uses testify in its handler test. This breaks stdlib-first, no-`init()` and no-assertion-library (`SKILL.md:27,40,41`, `context/AGENTS.md:49`).
- `golang-ecosystem.md` sends benchmark "audit trail" files to `/tmp`, against `context/AGENTS.md:53`.
- About 150 pointers name deep-dive guides, `assets/examples/*.go`, `templates/*` and `*.md` debug files that were cut in e5833a3 and no longer exist.

## Classification (--project)

| File | Class | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| `skills/golang/SKILL.md` | accurate | `SKILL.md:49-55` names exactly the 7 files, and each sub-topic it lists exists as a `## Sub-topic:` header. `SKILL.md:40` matches `context/AGENTS.md:49` and `context/dev-setup.md:5`. Its rules are the ones the references contradict (see findings). |
| `references/golang-core.md` | outdated | `:61` `wg.Go()` "Go 1.24+" (it is 1.25). `:230` maps "8-entry buckets and overflow chains" (Swiss tables since 1.24). `:399` sends samber/oops readers to Ecosystem, but oops lives in `golang-samber.md:539`. |
| `references/golang-testing.md` | outdated | `:143,161` synctest shown as "Experimental" with `synctest.Run(func(t *testing.T)`. `:252` `is.NotNil` breaks its own `:28`. `:513-527` lists reference files that do not exist. |
| `references/golang-architecture.md` | outdated | `:544` Close errors unchecked. `:534` and `:612` point at itself for content that is in `golang-structure.md`. `:647,668` `/golang-modernize` does not exist. |
| `references/golang-structure.md` | outdated | `:497` "see the decision table below": the table was replaced by `:561`. `:489` "<10 services" threshold breaks `:561` and `SKILL.md:26`. |
| `references/golang-io-web.md` | outdated | `:413` `assert.New(t)`. `:893` Cobra+Viper default. `:929-1047` twelve `assets/examples/*.go` pointers, but there is no `assets/` directory. |
| `references/golang-ecosystem.md` | outdated | `:792,795,799` use `/tmp`. `:323` says every project MUST have `.golangci.yml`, against `SKILL.md:23`. `:464-496` names debug files that do not exist. `:240` still teaches the tools.go pattern, which `golang-architecture.md:760` supersedes. |
| `references/golang-samber.md` | outdated | `:3` is accurate (stdlib first), but `:192` marks a plain loop "✗ boilerplate, error-prone" and `:722` says `oops.Recover()` "MUST" be used. `:627-638` does not compile. It has 20+ pointers to guides that do not exist. |

No file is wholly redundant.

## Findings

### High

None blocking by `REQUIREMENTS.md`. `REQUIREMENTS.md:17-19` (R4, stdlib only) covers the harness binary, not user projects.

### Medium

- **[medium / confidence: high] divergent** `skills/golang/references/golang-testing.md:143` and `:161`, against `golang-architecture.md:725`.
  - **Wrong:** the file calls `testing/synctest` "Experimental … not yet covered by Go's compatibility guarantee" and shows `synctest.Run(func(t *testing.T) { … })`. `Run` never took a `*testing.T`: in Go 1.24 it was `Run(func())`, and only behind `GOEXPERIMENT=synctest`. The package became stable in Go 1.25 as `synctest.Test(t, func(t *testing.T))`, which `golang-architecture.md:725` itself lists as the replacement. On this stack (`go.mod` 1.24.4, docker skill `golang:1.24`) the sample fails to compile either way.
  - **Should say:** "`testing/synctest` (Go 1.25+; Go 1.24 only with `GOEXPERIMENT=synctest`): `synctest.Test(t, func(t *testing.T) { … })`."
- **[medium / confidence: high] divergent** `skills/golang/references/golang-core.md:61`, against `golang-architecture.md:750`.
  - **Wrong:** core says "Go 1.24+: `wg.Go()`"; architecture says Go 1.25+. `sync.WaitGroup.Go` shipped in Go 1.25. Code written from core fails to build on the stack's pinned 1.24 (`go.mod:3`).
  - **Should say:** "Go 1.25+: `wg.Go()`".
- **[medium / confidence: high] divergent** `skills/golang/references/golang-architecture.md:544`, against `skills/review-standards/references/go-review.md:23` and `skills/golang/SKILL.md:19`.
  - **Wrong:** "`.Close()` errors: acceptable to not check — `defer f.Close()` is fine without error handling." The review checklist requires `Close()` errors to be checked on writers, because a swallowed close loses the final flush. A writer would ship code the reviewer then flags, and the data-loss path is real.
  - **Should say:** "An unchecked `defer Close()` is acceptable on read-only resources. On writers (files written, `gzip`/`bufio` writers) check the `Close()` error."
- **[medium / confidence: high] divergent** `skills/golang/references/golang-io-web.md:413-432`, against `golang-testing.md:28,342` and `SKILL.md:41`.
  - **Wrong:** the "Testing HTTP Handlers" sample uses `is := assert.New(t)` (testify) and `is.NoError`, `is.Equal`, `is.Contains`. The testing reference and SKILL.md say no assertion library by default and hand-written fakes.
  - **Should say:** use stdlib checks (`if err != nil { t.Fatalf(…) }`, `if rec.Code != http.StatusOK { t.Errorf(…) }`) with a hand-written fake.
- **[medium / confidence: high] divergent** `skills/golang/references/golang-io-web.md:893`, against `SKILL.md:27`, `SKILL.md:40`, `context/AGENTS.md:49` and `context/dev-setup.md:5`.
  - **Wrong:**
    - `:893` says "Use Cobra + Viper as the default stack for Go CLI applications"; stdlib `flag` only "for trivial single-purpose tools" (`:897`).
    - `:903-910` adds six third-party packages as the Quick Reference.
    - `:944` registers subcommands "in `init()`", which SKILL.md forbids unless absolutely required.
    - `:963-965` binds everything to Viper's global instance, which is global mutable state (`SKILL.md:26`).
    - The harness's own CLI is stdlib only (`REQUIREMENTS.md:19`).
  - **Should say:** "stdlib `flag` (with a small subcommand switch) is the default. Cobra/Viper is a dependency to justify when a deep subcommand tree or shell completions demand it. Wire subcommands from `main`, not `init()`."
- **[medium / confidence: high] divergent** `skills/golang/references/golang-architecture.md:200` and `golang-samber.md:192`, against `SKILL.md:40`, `SKILL.md:55`, `golang-samber.md:3` and `golang-architecture.md:199`.
  - **Wrong:**
    - `golang-architecture.md:200`: "for filter/group-by/chunk, use `github.com/samber/lo`".
    - `golang-samber.md:139`: "Everything else … requires manual for-loops. `lo` fills this gap".
    - `golang-samber.md:192`: the plain loop is marked "✗ Manual — boilerplate, error-prone".
    - `golang-samber.md:243`: "Compose lo functions … instead of writing nested loops".
    - These make a dependency the default, while SKILL.md says samber only "when stdlib is demonstrably not enough" and `golang-architecture.md:199` quotes "a little copying is better than a little dependency".
  - **Should say:** "write the loop; `lo` only when the stdlib is demonstrably not enough, justified in the change entry". Drop the ✗ label on the loop.
- **[medium / confidence: high] divergent** `skills/golang/references/golang-core.md:373` and `golang-samber.md:722`, against `SKILL.md:18`, `SKILL.md:55` and `golang-samber.md:3`.
  - **Wrong:** `golang-core.md:373` says "Use `samber/oops` for production errors needing stack traces, user/tenant context…" with no stdlib-first qualifier. `golang-samber.md:722` says "`oops.Recover()` MUST be used in goroutine boundaries", an unconditional MUST for a third-party library.
  - **Should say:** "wrap with `fmt.Errorf("…: %w")` and attach variable data as `slog` attributes; `samber/oops` only when that is demonstrably not enough". For `golang-samber.md:722`: "if the project uses oops, recover at goroutine boundaries with `oops.Recover()`".
- **[medium / confidence: high] stale** `skills/golang/references/golang-structure.md:497` (also `:489`, `:493-494`, `:506-507`), against `golang-structure.md:561`, `:600` and `SKILL.md:26`, `:41`.
  - **Wrong:**
    - `:497` "Choose the right DI library for your project size and team — see the decision table below": the table was cut, and `:561` now says "the default answer is no".
    - `:489` "Small projects (< 10 services) SHOULD use manual constructor injection" implies a library above 10 services. `:554` says 15+ and `:600` says under 20, so the file gives three thresholds.
    - `:493-494` (lazy init, singletons/transients) and `:506-507` (centralized container, lazy loading) are leftovers of the cut container material.
  - **Should say:** "Dependencies are wired by hand in `main()`; a DI library is a dependency to justify, default no (see DI Libraries)." Delete the decision-table pointer and the container-lifecycle items.
- **[medium / confidence: high] stale** `skills/golang/references/golang-ecosystem.md:792`, `:795`, `:799`, against `context/AGENTS.md:53`.
  - **Wrong:** benchmark baselines go to `/tmp/report-1.txt`, and "Keep all `/tmp/report-*.txt` files as an audit trail". The global rule is never `/tmp`; scratch lives in `.agents/scratch/`. `/tmp` is also cleared on reboot, so the "audit trail" does not survive.
  - **Should say:** `… | tee .agents/scratch/bench/report-1.txt` and `benchstat .agents/scratch/bench/report-1.txt .agents/scratch/bench/report-2.txt`.
- **[medium / confidence: high] divergent** `skills/golang/references/golang-ecosystem.md:323` (also `:321`, `:376`), against `SKILL.md:23` and `AGENTS.md:15`.
  - **Wrong:** "Every Go project MUST have a `.golangci.yml` — it is the source of truth". SKILL.md makes `go vet` + `staticcheck` the gate. This repo's own gate is `gofmt -l . && go vet ./... && go test -race ./...`, and it has no `.golangci.yml`. `golang-architecture.md:665` also says run golangci-lint. Two sources name different lint gates.
  - **Should say:** one gate, stated in SKILL.md. For example: "`go vet` + `staticcheck`; golangci-lint when the project already configures it".
- **[medium / confidence: medium] divergent** `skills/golang/references/golang-ecosystem.md:105-113` (also `:24`, `:27`, `:32`), against `context/AGENTS.md:13-15` and `context/dev-setup.md:5`.
  - **Wrong:** a second "Definition of Done for Observability" says a feature is not done without Prometheus metrics with PromQL comments, spans on every service method and DB query, Grafana dashboards and alert rules, and PostHog/Segment RUM events. `:24` says "Every HTTP endpoint MUST have latency and error rate metrics"; `:27` says "Set up OpenTelemetry tracing on new projects". This conflicts with the global Definition of Done, and it adds Prometheus, OTel and PostHog as defaults on a stdlib-first, Cloud Run stack.
  - **Should say:** a checklist framed "when the service has a metrics/tracing backend", not a Definition of Done. Or cut it.
- **[medium / confidence: medium] security** `skills/golang/references/golang-ecosystem.md:1030`.
  - **Wrong:** "Register for discoverability — add to Context7, DeepWiki, OpenDeep, zRead. **Even for private libraries.**" This tells an agent to submit private source to third-party indexers, which leaks it (compare `skills/VENDORED.md:24`, "this repository is not published").
  - **Should say:** "Public libraries only; never register a private repository with an external indexer."
- **[medium / confidence: high] stale — files that do not exist, cut in e5833a3.** `find skills/golang -type d` shows only `references/`.
  - **Wrong:**
    - `golang-io-web.md:929, 933, 944, 948, 969, 989, 1010, 1026, 1030, 1039, 1043, 1047` point at `assets/examples/{main,root,serve,flags,args,config,version,exit_codes,output,signal,completion,cli_test}.go`.
    - `golang-ecosystem.md:464-496` points at `compilation.md`, `common-go-bugs.md`, `testing-debug.md`, `diagnostic-tools.md`, `concurrency-debug.md`, `pprof.md`, `performance-debug.md`.
    - `golang-ecosystem.md:995`, `:1019`, `:1060` point at `templates/README.md`, `templates/CHANGELOG.md`, `templates/llms.txt`.
    - An agent told to "copy the template from templates/README.md" finds nothing and may invent its contents.
  - **Should say:** inline the gist or delete the pointer.

### Low

- **[low / confidence: high] stale — named guides that do not exist.** They are written as links but point at nothing, so the reader is sent looking for guides that were never installed. Delete them, or inline one line.
  - `golang-core.md:29, 65, 79, 164-168, 226, 249, 272, 276, 289, 299, 381-385, 486, 508`
  - `golang-testing.md:105, 189, 338, 511, 513-527`
  - `golang-architecture.md:115, 174, 315-323, 562, 582, 616-621, 705, 709`
  - `golang-structure.md:378, 430, 436-439, 443, 447, 514`
  - `golang-io-web.md:496, 618, 747, 828, 839, 861-866`
  - `golang-ecosystem.md:49-65, 257-269, 372, 572-591, 653, 670-688, 745, 784, 826-833, 910, 915, 991, 1013, 1032, 1042, 1054, 1088`
  - `golang-samber.md:42, 110, 112, 180, 273, 275, 304, 344, 379, 405, 471, 528, 784, 892, 909, 945, 947, 1014, 1040, 1079, 1095`
  - `golang-ecosystem.md:271` is an empty `## Cross-References` header.
- **[low / confidence: high] stale — cross-references to the wrong file or to each other.**
  - `golang-architecture.md:534` points at "the Architecture reference" for `var _ Interface = (*Type)(nil)`. Should point at `golang-structure.md` (the pattern is at `:146-154`).
  - `golang-architecture.md:612` points at Architecture for 12-factor. Should point at `golang-structure.md` (`:384`).
  - `golang-core.md:399` points at Ecosystem for the samber/oops API. Should point at `golang-samber.md` (`:539`).
  - `golang-core.md:109` sends graceful shutdown to Architecture, and `golang-architecture.md:634` sends it to Core. It lives only in `golang-io-web.md:355`.
  - `golang-io-web.md:436` and `:461` send "comprehensive HTTP testing" to Testing, and `golang-testing.md:105` sends it to "HTTP Testing" (not in the skill).
  - `golang-io-web.md:872` and `golang-testing.md:390` send database integration tests to each other; neither has them.
  - `golang-io-web.md:654` (gRPC error mapping in Core) and `:655` (bufconn in Testing): neither target has it.
  - `golang-core.md:550` (integer overflow section in Ecosystem): absent.
  - `golang-testing.md:386`, `:392`, `golang-core.md:178`, `:640` and `golang-architecture.md:211`, `:373` send readers to Ecosystem for linter configuration. `golang-ecosystem.md:347-349` has none.
  - `golang-ecosystem.md:901` (Structure, for where doc files belong): absent.
- **[low / confidence: high] stale** `golang-architecture.md:647` and `:668` name an "explicit `/golang-modernize` invocation". There is no such command (`commands/` is empty) and no such skill among the 27. Should say "when the user asks for a full modernization scan".
- **[low / confidence: high] stale** `golang-testing.md:532`, `golang-ecosystem.md:37`, `:596` and `golang-samber.md:119` point to the `samber/cc-skills@promql-cli` skill. It is not in `skills/` and not in `skills/VENDORED.md`. Remove these pointers.
- **[low / confidence: high] divergent** `golang-testing.md:252` `is.NotNil(result)`, against `golang-testing.md:28` and `SKILL.md:41` (no assertion library). The `:251` indentation is also broken. Should say `if result == nil { t.Fatal("Process returned nil") }`.
- **[low / confidence: medium] divergent** `golang-testing.md:27` and `golang-core.md:27`: "Packages with goroutines SHOULD use `goleak.VerifyTestMain`" makes `go.uber.org/goleak` a default. That conflicts with `golang-testing.md:28` and `SKILL.md:40`. Should say "`goleak` is a test dependency to justify; the `-race` run and explicit goroutine joins come first".
- **[low / confidence: high] divergent** `golang-testing.md:201`, `:209`, `:226` use `for i := 0; i < b.N; i++` as the benchmark pattern. The same file at `:440` says `b.N` loops "should migrate to `b.Loop()`", and so does `golang-architecture.md:752`. Use `for b.Loop()`.
- **[low / confidence: high] divergent** `golang-ecosystem.md:240-255` presents the `tools.go` blank-import pattern as current. `golang-architecture.md:760` says "Move tool deps to `go.mod` tool directives (Go 1.24+)", and the stack is on 1.24. Should say `go get -tool <pkg>` and a `tool` directive, with `tools.go` only below Go 1.24.
- **[low / confidence: high] divergent** `golang-ecosystem.md:168` ("Using `go get -u` to upgrade an existing dependency is safe") against `golang-ecosystem.md:223` ("Prefer `go get -u=patch` … minor upgrades may … change behavior"). Should say "`go get -u=patch` is the routine upgrade".
- **[low / confidence: high] divergent** `golang-architecture.md:472` ("init() … across files in **filename alphabetical order**") against `golang-core.md:661` ("`init()` execution order across files is unspecified"). Should say "the spec only encourages lexical filename order; the go tool follows it; never depend on it".
- **[low / confidence: high] divergent** `golang-core.md:628` discards `sql.Open`'s error with `_` in the recommended `sync.Once` example, against `SKILL.md:19` and `golang-core.md:363`. Should use `sync.OnceValues` returning `(*sql.DB, error)`.
- **[low / confidence: high] divergent** `golang-io-web.md:530` uses `log.Printf("method=%s …")` in the recommended gRPC logging interceptor, against `SKILL.md:30` (slog JSON) and `golang-core.md:372`. Should say `slog.InfoContext(ctx, "rpc", "method", info.FullMethod, …)`.
- **[low / confidence: medium-high] outdated** `golang-core.md:230`: "Maps are hash tables with 8-entry buckets and overflow chains". Since Go 1.24 (the stack's version) maps are Swiss tables. Should say "Swiss tables since Go 1.24 (groups of 8 slots, open addressing); buckets with overflow chains before".
- **[low / confidence: high] outdated** `golang-io-web.md:30`: "`ReverseProxy` with `.Rewrite` (Go 1.26+)". `Rewrite` has existed since Go 1.20; 1.26 is only when `Director` was deprecated (`golang-architecture.md:727`). Should say "`.Rewrite` (Go 1.20+)".
- **[low / confidence: high] outdated — code samples that do not compile.**
  - `golang-io-web.md:752-755`: `GetUser(id string)` uses an undefined `ctx`.
  - `golang-io-web.md:770-773`: `err :=` redeclares the named result `err` ("no new variables on left side of :=").
  - `golang-samber.md:627-638`: `return oops…` inside a handler with no result.
  - `golang-samber.md:730`: `With("panic_value", r)` with `r` undefined.
  - `golang-samber.md:609-611`: `r.db.Query(query, id)` without a context and with rows never closed, against `golang-io-web.md:676`, `:678`.
  - `golang-samber.md:667`: interpolates `req.ProductID` into the message of a "good" example, against its own MUST at `:710`.
- **[low / confidence: medium] divergent** CI-oriented guidance against `context/AGENTS.md:45` ("no CI, no hooks, ever"): `golang-ecosystem.md:267` (Dependabot/Renovate auto-merge PRs), `:1010` (CI build-status badge), and `golang-architecture.md:647` (Agent 5 scans the "CI pipeline").
- **[low / confidence: medium] outdated** `golang-ecosystem.md:412` and `:417`: "`run.timeout` (default: 5m)" and "`run.skip-dirs`". These are golangci-lint v1 settings, while the same file targets v2 (`:334`, `:416`). v2 has no default timeout and moved directory exclusion to `linters.exclusions.paths`. Unverified against the current golangci-lint docs.
- **[low / confidence: medium] provenance** `skills/golang/` derives from `samber/cc-skills`: it has that project's Persona/Modes format, `golang-testing.md:532` names `samber/cc-skills@promql-cli`, and `golang-ecosystem.md:33` links samber's alert library. It was imported in 9dcdc4c and cut in e5833a3, but `skills/VENDORED.md` has no source or licence row for it. `VENDORED.md:14-26` records attribution for the other third-party-derived skills. Add a row, or state in `VENDORED.md` that `golang` is a fork. The upstream licence is unverified.

## Unverified

- `golang-architecture.md:653`, `:693-695`: "latest Go is 1.26". Go 1.27 would be due around August 2026. The local toolchain is 1.24.4, so this could not be checked.

title: Review — sweep-skills-3 (2026-09-15)
body:
# Review — sweep-skills-3   (2026-09-15)

Range reviewed: Scope: the named files as they are in the working tree, read whole — not a diff: skills/handoff/, skills/init-project/, skills/json-api-style/, skills/mermaid-syntax/, skills/preflight/, skills/python/, skills/research/, skills/retro/, skills/review/, skills/review-standards/ (HEAD d1ff612 plus the uncommitted edits at skills/retro/SKILL.md:75 and skills/review/SKILL.md:48)

Lens: `--docs`, with the `--project` classification clause applied to the named files. Report only.

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

The worst problem: `skills/retro/SKILL.md` says a retro is never started uninvited and is only *suggested*, and its trigger list leaves out the 14-day cadence. The global context (`context/AGENTS.md:41`) and the binary's own `sh-agent status` hint (`cmd/sh-agent/main.go:271`) both tell the agent to *run* `/retro`, including on that 14-day cadence. An agent following the skill never acts on the hint. Two rule restatements in `/preflight` are also narrower than their sources: the security trigger drops "crypto", and the docs-freshness step re-lists a shorter target set than the `--docs` brief now carries. Both init-project templates for ROADMAP and TODO still include "Ideas" sections, which the Definition of Done forbids. The rest are low-severity stale names and internal contradictions between skills and their reference files. Nothing is broken in the installer code this scope describes.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high] divergent** `skills/retro/SKILL.md:3` ("Never start one uninvited") and `skills/retro/SKILL.md:25-32` ("When to Suggest … two or more … Suggest it naturally") versus `context/AGENTS.md:41` ("Run `/retro` at the end of a session with two or more corrections, and whenever `sh-agent status` shows more than 14 days since the last one") and `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:271` ("past 14 days, run /retro at the end of the next session"). The skill makes it a suggestion and leaves out the 14-day trigger (narrowed). The context and the binary tell the agent to run it. Should say: the skill's trigger section names both conditions from context:41 and uses the same verb as the context ("run", or change both to "suggest").
- **[medium / confidence: high] divergent** `skills/init-project/assets/ROADMAP.md:15-17` (`## Later / Ideas` — "Unscheduled directions worth keeping visible") and `skills/init-project/assets/TODO.md:13` (`## Ideas / Nice-to-Have`) versus `context/AGENTS.md:18` ("at Done both are EMPTY … neither file is a parking lot for ideas"), `skills/handoff/SKILL.md:64`, and each template's own line 3. Every new project is scaffolded with sections that invite the parking the Definition of Done forbids. Related: `agents/documentation.md:30,43` still assigns Next/Later to documentation ("move items between Next and Later"). Should say: no ideas sections, or a comment that they stay empty at Done and that ideas go to the handoff's Next Steps.
- **[medium / confidence: high] narrowed: `context/AGENTS.md:16` → `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:51`** — the security row triggers on "auth, IAM, secrets, input parsing, or dependencies" and leaves out **crypto**. Both the context and `agents/security.md:3` list "auth, crypto, secrets, IAM, input parsing, or dependencies". A release that touches only crypto code gets no security row. Should say: "auth, crypto, secrets, IAM, input parsing, or dependencies".
- **[low / confidence: high] narrowed: `skills/review/SKILL.md:48` → `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:65`** — preflight Step 4 dispatches "the docs brief" but re-lists its targets as README, specs, the testing guide and deploy/ only. It omits the newest `changes/` entry and the old-wording `git grep` over `AGENTS.md`, `.agents/{rules,skills,agents,commands}/` and the paths the project `AGENTS.md` adds (here `context/`, `agents/`, `skills/`), all of which the brief (now uncommitted at review:48) carries. Should say: "the `--docs` brief from `/review` Step 3, verbatim", with no second list.
- **[low / confidence: medium] narrowed: `context/AGENTS.md:16` → `skills/review/SKILL.md:60`** — the `--fix` stop rule keeps "a round's findings land on the mechanism the previous round fixed" but drops the context's second condition, "or a fix introduces the next round's defect". Should say: add that clause.
- **[low / confidence: medium] divergent** `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:87` — "`local.md` when the project is local-only: build for `linux/amd64`, push to Artifact Registry, deploy". The amd64/Artifact Registry steps belong only to `gcp.md` (`context/dev-setup.md:10-11`). The template `skills/init-project/assets/agents-tree/docs/deploy/remote.md:29-33` copies with `scp`, and this repo's `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md:14-23` installs into a home. Should say: follow the chosen guide's own procedure and verify step; amd64 build plus Artifact Registry push only for `gcp.md`.

Should say: "never edited without the user's explicit approval".
- **[low / confidence: high] stale** "Resume Protocol" at `skills/handoff/SKILL.md:34`, `:150`, `:154` and `skills/init-project/SKILL.md:18` (also `agents/changelog.md:84`). Tiers left the global context in 87a862d ("move procedures into feature and bug skills") and are now named in `skills/feature/SKILL.md:48`. - **[low / confidence: high] divergent** `skills/review-standards/SKILL.md:3` ("loaded by the reviewer agent, /review, and /preflight") and `:8` ("Whoever is reviewing (the `reviewer` agent, `/review`, `/preflight`) loads this file and judges the diff") versus `skills/review/SKILL.md:9` ("It never reviews by itself") and `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:48` ("Never self-review"). Only `agents/reviewer.md:6-7` loads the skill. - **[low / confidence: medium] divergent** `skills/handoff/SKILL.md:78` — "Session ID: <conversation-id> … matches the feedback log's session field" versus `skills/feedback/SKILL.md:44` (`"session": "first-8-chars-of-conversation-id"`). A full id never string-matches the log. Should say: "its first 8 characters are the feedback log's session field".
- **[low / confidence: medium] divergent** `skills/review-standards/references/typescript-review.md:29` — "flag `export default` for anything but framework-mandated files" versus `skills/typescript/SKILL.md:40` ("no default exports for shared modules"). The checklist is broader than the idiom authority, and `skills/review-standards/SKILL.md:36` says the language skill wins. Should say: scope the check to shared modules, as the typescript skill does.
- **[low / confidence: high] divergent** `skills/python/references/python-fundamentals.md:12,39` (marked ✅: `from typing import Optional`; `from collections import defaultdict` at :11) contradicts the same file's `:27` ("❌ Do not import individual classes/functions from modules") and `:158` ("Use X | None instead of Optional[X]"), and `skills/python/SKILL.md:35` rule 4. Should say: `import collections` / `import typing`, with no `Optional`.
- **[low / confidence: high] divergent** `skills/python/references/python-fundamentals.md:73` — `logger.error(f"Invalid integer input: {e}")` versus `skills/python/SKILL.md:48` rule 13 and the same file's `:255-259` (lazy `%` formatting in logging calls). - **[low / confidence: high] incorrect example** `skills/python/references/python-fundamentals.md:278` — `with threading.Lock():` creates a new lock on every entry, so nothing is ever excluded. Code copied from the "✅ Locks" example has a data race. Should say: `lock = threading.Lock()` at module or instance scope, then `with lock:`.
- **[low / confidence: medium] divergent** `skills/mermaid-syntax/SKILL.md:29,38,249` ("Always wrap text containing special characters in double quotes", with `? < >` in the list) versus the skill's own unquoted examples: `examples/flowchart-examples.md:46` (`Attempt{Attempts < 3?}`), `:93` (`Q1{Budget > 1000?}`), `:94`, and `references/flowchart-complete.md:324` (`Check{Condition?}`). # Review — sweep-skills-4   (2026-09-15)

Range reviewed: working tree, `skills/typescript/` read whole (`SKILL.md`, 46 lines; the directory holds no other file; last touched by e521826, no uncommitted change) — not a diff. Lens: --docs --project.

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing in `skills/typescript/SKILL.md` is broken on its own: every file it names exists (`frontend`, `golang`, `bash` skills) and its rules agree with each other. The worst problem sits next to it: the `frontend` skill, which this skill hands all TanStack Start work to, calls `vite.config.ts` "The ONLY config file" (`skills/frontend/SKILL.md:34`), while this skill requires a strict `tsconfig` (`skills/typescript/SKILL.md:18-20`) and the frontend's own build runs `tsc -b` (`skills/frontend/SKILL.md:96`), which needs a `tsconfig.json`. An agent that follows the frontend tree literally writes no tsconfig, and then the build fails or skips the strict baseline. The other findings are rules this skill states that the review checklist (`skills/review-standards/references/typescript-review.md`) or the frontend skill repeat with a different meaning. Because of those, a reviewer applying the checklist flags code that follows this skill.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: medium]** divergent — `skills/frontend/SKILL.md:34` vs `skills/typescript/SKILL.md:18-20` (and `skills/frontend/SKILL.md:96`) — the frontend tree says `vite.config.ts  # The ONLY config file`. The typescript skill requires `strict: true` + `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` + `noImplicitOverride`, set in a tsconfig ("One config per package"). The frontend build `vite build && tsc -b` needs a `tsconfig.json` in the package: TypeScript's documented `-b` behaviour, not run here. The line came in with e5833a3 (2026-09-13) and most likely means "the only Vite/Start config, no `app.config.ts`". Read literally, it forbids the tsconfig that the other two lines need. Should say: `vite.config.ts  # the only build config: tanstackStart(), react(), tailwindcss()` and add `tsconfig.json  # strict baseline per the typescript skill` to the tree.
- **[low / confidence: high]** divergent — `skills/typescript/SKILL.md:24` vs `skills/frontend/SKILL.md:95` — the typescript skill says "**No `any`.**" with no exception, and so does the checklist (`typescript-review.md:7`). The frontend skill says "No `any` where a real type is feasible". The typescript description (`:8`) says not to load it for "UI, styling, components", so for component code the looser frontend wording is often the only rule in context. Should say (frontend:95): "Type every prop and API payload. No `any`: use `unknown` and narrow (typescript skill)."
- **[low / confidence: high]** divergent — `skills/typescript/SKILL.md:46` vs `skills/review-standards/references/typescript-review.md:9` — the skill accepts `@ts-expect-error` "(with reason)" and ranks it above `@ts-ignore`. The checklist lists `// @ts-ignore` among "disabling flags" that are findings outright, and flags `@ts-expect-error` "without a linked issue". So a reviewer flags a reasoned `@ts-expect-error` that follows the skill. The checklist names the skill as the language authority (`typescript-review.md:3`, `review-standards/SKILL.md:35-36`), so the checklist should change. Should say: "`// @ts-ignore` anywhere, or `// @ts-expect-error` without a reason comment".
- **[low / confidence: high]** divergent — `skills/typescript/SKILL.md:40` vs `skills/review-standards/references/typescript-review.md:29` — the skill bans default exports only "for shared modules". The checklist flags `export default` "for anything but framework-mandated files (routes)". The checklist's example is also wrong for this stack: TanStack routes use the named `export const Route` (`skills/frontend/SKILL.md:71`), and the framework-mandated default export is `vite.config.ts` (`skills/frontend/SKILL.md:53`). Should say (checklist:29): "flag `export default` in shared modules; framework-mandated files (`vite.config.ts`) are exempt".
- **[low / confidence: medium]** divergent — `skills/typescript/SKILL.md:45` vs `skills/review-standards/references/typescript-review.md:8` — the skill requires a comment on every `as` cast and `!` assertion ("each one needs a comment explaining why the compiler is wrong"). The checklist accepts "a runtime check **or** an adjacent comment". So a cast with a runtime check and no comment passes review but breaks the skill. Pick one wording. The skill is the authority, so the checklist should say "an adjacent comment proving the invariant (a runtime check does not replace it)". The other option is to widen the skill.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** stale verification — `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md:41` — the `typescript` row's pass check is `grep -qi "typescript" "$OUT"`. The prompt asks for "a strictly typed TypeScript function", so any answer with a ```` ```typescript ```` fence or the word TypeScript passes, whether or not the skill loaded. The check cannot fail. Procedure step 3 (`skill-matrix.md` §Procedure 3) reads the transcript for `Skill` tool uses, and that transcript read is the only real signal. Should say: a check that also requires a rule found only in this skill, e.g. `grep -qiE "unknown|noUncheckedIndexedAccess|satisfies" "$OUT"`, plus the transcript `Skill` use recorded as the pass condition.

## Classification (--project)

| File | Class | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| `skills/typescript/SKILL.md` | accurate | `:8-9`, `:14` name `frontend`, `golang`, `bash` and all three exist (`skills/frontend/SKILL.md:1-2`, `skills/golang/`, `skills/bash/SKILL.md:1-3`). The routing matches `context/dev-setup.md:6`, `skills/review-standards/SKILL.md:35` and `agents/reviewer.md:41`. Its rules agree with each other and with `review-standards/SKILL.md:28`, which requires caught errors typed `unknown`, as `:41` does. The divergences above belong to the neighbouring files, which name this skill as the authority. Not redundant: it is the one language-level source, and the checklist defers to it (`typescript-review.md:3`). |

## Unverified

- That `tsc -b` fails without a `tsconfig.json`: this comes from TypeScript's documented build-mode behaviour. No `tsc` was run here.
- Whether `README.md`, `<docs-root>/specs/` (empty), `testing/sh-agent/guide.md` and `deploy/*.md` should mention this skill at all: none of them name it, and none claims to list skills one by one, so the absence is not a finding.
- The newest `changes/` entry (`2026-09-15-research-beads-elephant-goldfish.md`) does not touch TypeScript. There is nothing to compare.

## Criteria

1. Dead code — n/a — docs lens
2. Flow tracing — n/a — docs lens
3. Standards conformance — n/a — docs lens
4. Directory layout — n/a — docs lens
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — n/a — docs lens

## Not examined

- Vendored skills (`skills/VENDORED.md`) were excluded from every search, as the brief requires.
- `.agents/rules`, `.agents/commands` and `.agents/agents` do not exist in this repo, so they were not searched.

## Re-check commands

title: Cold read — `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-16-attribution-write.md`
body:
# Cold read — `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-16-attribution-write.md`

Range reviewed: plan file (`.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-16-attribution-write.md`), against `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` (install case, `attributionHint`, `attributionOff`), `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` (`TestAttributionNote`), `REQUIREMENTS.md`.

## (1) Gaps

- **`REQUIREMENTS.md` Non-goals contradicts the plan, and nothing addresses it — file:line `REQUIREMENTS.md:43`.** The Non-goals section reads: "Editing `settings.json` or any vendor setting: the harness is files in the customization directories, nothing else." The plan's D2/R4 sentence has `install` write a key into `~/.claude/settings.json` — the exact thing this bullet forbids. The plan's "Surfaces touched" list names only `REQUIREMENTS.md` R4, not the Non-goals section, and the operator's recorded approval (Why, D2) covers only "the one-sentence change to R4," not any edit to Non-goals. Per this repo's own hard rule, `REQUIREMENTS.md` is immutable without explicit operator approval for the *exact edit* — the plan has approval for one addition, not for resolving this direct contradiction. Implemented as scoped, the file ships self-contradictory. **BLOCKING.**
- **`ADR-010` is left standing and now false — `DECISIONS.md:81`.** ADR-010's Decision text says "`REQUIREMENTS.md` names editing vendor settings a non-goal" and its Consequences lean on "nothing installed outside the customization directories." The plan adds ADR-025 but does not mark ADR-010 superseded (the file's own convention, e.g. `## ADR-023: … — Superseded by ADR-024`). A reader of DECISIONS.md after this ships finds two ADRs asserting opposite things with no cross-reference. Not in Surfaces touched. **BLOCKING** (same root cause as the Non-goals gap — resolving one likely resolves both, but the plan decides neither).
- **A second, unnamed restatement of "never writes vendor settings" in README — `README.md:16`.** The paragraph the plan clearly intends to fix is line 14 (the attribution note, in the same section named in Surfaces touched). But line 16, in the same `## Install` section, separately says "the installer never touches vendor settings (ADR-010)" about `permissions.additionalDirectories`. This is a second, independent claim that becomes false and cites the same ADR-010 that gap 2 above leaves unresolved. Likely to be caught by an implementer re-reading the whole section, but it is not named, so it is a gap under review-standards §3 (grep the subject noun "vendor settings" across the repo) rather than a certainty. **NON-BLOCKING** (a competent implementer editing "README § Install" would likely see it), but worth calling out since it shares the ADR-010 root cause.
- **`sync` is not mentioned anywhere in the plan, but shares the exact code path.** `main.go:110` is `case "install", "sync":` — one switch arm. `attributionHint` already fires for both today; the plan's Interfaces section says `attributionSet` is "called from the install case for vendor all or claude" and Scope says "In: `install` (vendor all or claude)," never mentioning `sync`. Precedent (attributionHint firing for both) suggests the intent is for `sync` to write the key too, but the plan never says so, and the verification/E2E criteria only exercise `install`. **NON-BLOCKING** — the existing shared switch arm and `attributionHint` precedent give a reasonable implementer a default (treat `sync` the same as `install`), but it should be named so the test matrix covers it explicitly.
- **Detection of "no attribution key" vs. "not a JSON object" is under-specified.** The Interfaces section's insert branch requires "valid JSON object, no `attribution` key"; the fallback ("malformed... write nothing") doesn't explicitly say whether a syntactically-valid-JSON-but-non-object top level (e.g. `[]`, `"x"`, `42`) counts as "malformed." In practice `json.Unmarshal` into a `map[string]json.RawMessage` errors on those inputs, so the natural implementation folds this into "malformed" — but the plan doesn't state the decoding target, so this is asserted rather than checked. **NON-BLOCKING** (a reasonable implementer's natural choice matches the advisory-only spirit of D4).

## (2) Scope

Nothing found beyond what `## Why` and the Decisions ask for. The plan explicitly rejects the two scope expansions a reviewer would otherwise flag (forcing a value over a custom one; removing the key on `uninstall`), each with a D-row. The "new helper vs. extend `attributionOff`" choice (Interfaces, line 26) is explicitly left to the implementer and recorded as such — not silent scope creep.

## (3) Readiness

Questions a first-pass implementer would have to ask (or guess) before/while building:

1. **BLOCKING** — Does the Non-goals bullet in `REQUIREMENTS.md` get edited (and did the operator actually approve that edit), or does the plan's R4 addition ship alongside a bullet that flatly contradicts it?
2. **BLOCKING** — Does ADR-010 get a "Superseded by ADR-025" marker, consistent with how this file already handles superseded decisions (ADR-023)?
3. NON-BLOCKING — Does `sh-agent sync` also get the key written (same switch arm, same vendor gate), or only `sh-agent install`? (Reasonable default: same as `install`, following the `attributionHint` precedent already in the code.)
4. NON-BLOCKING — README's second "vendor settings" claim (line 16, ADR-010 citation) — reasonable implementer catches it while editing the section the plan already names.
5. NON-BLOCKING — New helper function vs. three-state `attributionOff` — plan explicitly defers this to the implementer.

## Verdict

**design needs revision** (two gaps: the Non-goals contradiction and the unresolved ADR-010).
**implementation not ready** (2 BLOCKING questions, both stemming from the same root cause: the plan never proposes the Non-goals edit or the ADR-010 supersession, so it cannot yet claim the operator approved them).

## Not examined

`context/AGENTS.md` full render/line-count claim ("render stays 93 lines") was not independently re-rendered; `deploy/local.md` and `deploy/remote.md` full files were only grepped for the attribution string, not read end to end for other stale restatements; `ADR-025`'s not-yet-written text obviously not reviewed since it doesn't exist yet.

title: Review — attribution-write (2026-09-16)
body:
# Review — attribution-write   (2026-09-16)

Range reviewed: working tree, `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` and `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go`
Blobs read: `main.go` a5b537b78337b42df94f27df9091e8d465e8fa13, `main_test.go` d428d98860017d9b06e980400b003bdf26f3c311

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

The write path is sound for every realistic settings.json (small file, one flat top-level object): the `json.Unmarshal`-into-map gate filters comments, a second top-level value, and BOM-prefixed files into the "malformed, nothing written" branch before the textual-insertion code ever runs, `json.LastIndexByte`/`IndexByte` land on the true outer braces because that gate guarantees a single well-formed object, and the final `json.Valid(result)` is a real safety net, not decoration. `gofmt`, `go vet`, and `go test -race -count=1 ./cmd/sh-agent/` all pass clean. One concrete, verified bug: a top-level JSON `null` (a value D7 explicitly names) gets the wrong message and is untested — worth a one-line fix, not a blocker.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:509-535` (`attributionSet`) — a settings.json containing the single JSON value `null` prints `settings: <path> could not be edited safely (the result would not parse); add the key by hand` instead of the plan's D7 message `is not a JSON object; add the key by hand`. Verified live: `printf 'null\n' > .claude/settings.json && sh-agent install` → the "could not be edited safely" line, file untouched. Cause: `json.Unmarshal(data, &top)` does **not** error on `null` into a `map[string]json.RawMessage` (it leaves `top` nil with `err == nil`), so execution falls past the `json.Valid(data)` / "is not a JSON object" branch (which only fires on `err != nil`) into the textual-insertion path, where `trimmed` has no `{`/`}` and `closing <= opening` (both -1) triggers the generic "could not be edited safely" message. No data loss (nothing is written either way), but it is a plan (D7) conformance miss and the one non-object case with no test coverage — `TestAttributionSet`'s "not an object is left alone" case uses `["x"]`, not `null`. Fix: check `top == nil && err == nil` (or `bytes.Equal(bytes.TrimSpace(data), []byte("null"))`) alongside the `err != nil` branch and route it through the same "is not a JSON object" message.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:592, 596, 601, 606` — `tmp.Close()` (cleanup call inside the write-error branch) and all four `os.Remove(tmpName)` calls on the error-cleanup paths discard their return values outright (not even `_ = `), which the go-review checklist's error-handling bullet flags. Low severity because these are best-effort cleanup after the primary error is already reported to the operator via `out` (a failed `Remove` just leaves a stray `.settings-*.json` temp file, not data corruption), but it is a real gap against the stated rule; worth `_ = os.Remove(tmpName)` for explicitness if the project wants the checklist literally satisfied.

- **[low / confidence: low]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:509` / `readSettings` — `readSettings`'s `io.LimitReader(f, 1<<20)` truncates silently (no error signals truncation). Before this diff that only fed the read-only "off" judgment; now the same truncated bytes can be re-serialized and written back via the temp-file/rename in `attributionSet`. For the narrow, unrealistic case of a settings.json >1 MiB whose top-level object happens to close exactly within the first MiB with further bytes beyond it, the write would silently drop everything past the truncation point. Real settings.json files are tiny, so this is not worth blocking on, but it's a behavior change in what the truncation feeds (read-only → potential overwrite source).

## Criteria

1. Dead code — pass. No orphaned functions; `readSettings` is a genuine shared helper used by both `attributionSet` and `attributionOff`, matching the plan's Open-item default.
2. Flow tracing — pass with the `null` gap above. `attributionSet` is wired into the install case exactly where the plan specifies (vendor all/claude, before `attributionHint`), `attributionOff`'s refactor onto `readSettings` preserves its old three-state contract (verified via `TestAttributionNote`'s directory/FIFO/malformed cases, still passing), and every new subtest can fail (checked by inspection: each asserts either a file-content invariant or a specific output line that the code must actively produce). The two must-fail demonstrations are plan-recorded (2026-09-16, custom_value/off_value and missing_file/other_keys) but not independently re-verified here (would require editing source, which I don't do).
3. Standards conformance — pass on gofmt/vet/test; one low-severity gap on unchecked `Close`/`Remove` returns on cleanup paths (see finding above). Doc-comments on `attributionSet`/`readSettings`/`attributionOff` describe the current behavior accurately.
4. Directory layout — pass. Both changes stay in `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` and its co-located `main_test.go`; no new files.
5. Simplicity / DIY-except-security — pass. Textual insertion instead of decode-reencode is justified in-comment (D3, avoids `encoding/json` key reordering); no new dependency; stdlib only (`bytes`, `encoding/json`, `os`, `io`).
6. Decoupling — pass. `readSettings` is a small, single-purpose helper at the seam both callers need; no cross-package reach-ins; `attributionSet` and `attributionOff` stay independently readable.

## Not examined

- `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `context/AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md`, and the deploy guides — out of scope per the dispatch (limited to `main.go`/`main_test.go`); the plan's Phase 1 doc tasks (R4/ADR-025, context/README/deploy wording) are still unticked in the plan file, consistent with not being in this diff.
- CRLF, BOM, and comment/second-top-level-value inputs were reasoned through against documented `encoding/json` semantics and one BOM/comment case is structurally identical to the already-tested "malformed" cases (both fail `Unmarshal` and `json.Valid` together), but none of the three was run live against the binary — only `null` and the dry-run/vendor-agy/no-write paths were empirically exercised.
- The plan's two must-fail demonstrations (Phase 1, row 4) were not independently reproduced by reverting code, per the reviewer's no-source-edits constraint; taken on the plan's own record.

## Outcome

- Finding 1 (medium) — fixed: a bare `null` (which `json.Unmarshal` leaves as a nil map without an error) now takes the "is not a JSON object; add the key by hand" branch; test `null is left alone`.
- Finding 2 (low) — fixed: the error paths call `abandonTemp`, which reports the write failure and names the temp file if even its removal fails; the one remaining bare `tmp.Close()` sits on a file discarded on the next line and says so in its comment.
- Finding 3 (low) — fixed: `attributionSet` refuses a file larger than 1 MiB before reading ("is larger than 1 MiB, more than this tool will rewrite; add the key by hand"), so the bounded reader can never feed a truncated write; test `a file over the read bound is left alone`.
- Added after the verifier's flag, before this review returned: a symlinked settings.json is never written through (`os.Lstat`, "is a symlink; add the key to its target by hand"); test shown to fail without the guard.
- Round 1 closed 2026-09-16; no second round owed (no mechanism finding).

title: Review — bug-043-guide-wording (2026-09-16)
body:
# Review — bug-043-guide-wording   (2026-09-16)

Range reviewed: working tree, agents/verifier.md
Blob sha (working tree content): 0c97f0b300c2fdc98472ad98d5b0b3cd26ac8842

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

The edited line (line 54) does close the loophole — the duty is now unconditional on `guide.md`'s own absence, with "however many earlier logs `testing/` holds" explicitly overriding the old evidence-of-a-first-time reading. But the file was not read whole before this diff was cut: line 97, in the same file's own **Records** section, still says the guide is written "when the procedure is new or its steps changed" — the exact ambiguous framing BUG-043 fixed, left standing eight lines below its own log entry as a second, contradicting statement of the same duty. An agent that treats Records (the section literally titled "what you write") as authoritative can read "the procedure is new" as false — this project has earlier logs — and skip the guide even though it is absent, reproducing BUG-043 from inside the same file that just fixed it.

## Findings
- **[high / confidence: high]** `agents/verifier.md:97` — "Writes: ... and `<docs-root>/testing/<app>/guide.md` when the procedure is new or its steps changed" contradicts the fixed rule at line 54 ("whenever `$docs_root/testing/<app>/guide.md` does not exist ... however many earlier logs `testing/` holds"). "The procedure is new" is not defined and reads exactly like the pre-fix "first time" trigger that let a run with an older log skip the write. Fix: state the same condition once (file absent, or steps changed) so the two sections cannot diverge — e.g. "and `<docs-root>/testing/<app>/guide.md` when it does not exist or its steps changed".
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `agents/documentation.md:35` and `skills/init-project/SKILL.md:75` — both still describe the verifier's duty as writing the guide "the first time it runs a project's procedure," the pre-fix phrasing. Not part of this diff and not verifier.md itself, so not a contradiction inside the reviewed file, but a describing-text hit: these two locations were not updated alongside the behaviour change and can seed the same misreading in an agent that consults documentation.md or the init-project skill instead of verifier.md directly.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `context/AGENTS.md:17` — "(created by the verifier on first use, maintained by both)" is a shorter parenthetical using "first use," same family of phrasing but terse enough that it reads more like a label than a trigger condition; flagged for completeness, not treated as a live contradiction.

## Checks requested by the dispatch
- Unconditional reading of the diffed line: line 54 alone is unconditional on absence — pass. But line 97 in the same file reintroduces the condition — see high finding above, so the file as a whole still contains a reading under which the guide can be skipped.
- Contradiction with `context/AGENTS.md` step 3 ("created by the verifier on first use, maintained by both"): no direct contradiction — that line is compatible with "write it whenever absent," it just doesn't state the "however many earlier logs" clarification. Not a blocking contradiction.
- Contradiction with `agents/documentation.md`: yes, in spirit — see the describing-text finding above (line 35, "the first time it runs a project's procedure").
- `go run ./cmd/sh-agent list` — ran; output lists all 7 subagents including `verifier`, and 27 skills including `review-standards`. Frontmatter still parses.

## Not examined
`agents/verifier.md` was read in full; grep covered `context/`, `agents/`, `skills/`, `README.md` for "first use", "first time", "guide.md" (README.md had no hits). Did not examine other agent files beyond the described/grep scope, and did not run the verifier live against a sandbox project to observe behaviour end to end — this review is text-only, as scoped by the dispatch.

## Outcome

- Finding 1 (high) — fixed: `agents/verifier.md` § Records now reads "whenever it is absent or its steps changed", matching § What to run.
- Finding 2 (low) — fixed: `agents/documentation.md` § Your lane ("whenever it runs a project's procedure and finds the guide absent") and `skills/init-project/SKILL.md` Step 4 ("the first time it runs the project's procedure and finds it absent").
- Finding 3 (low) — fixed as well: `context/AGENTS.md` step 3 now says "written by the verifier whenever it is absent" (rendered context stays at 93 lines).
- No restatement of the old duty remains (`grep -rnE 'first use|first time it runs|procedure is new' context/ agents/ skills/*/SKILL.md README.md` is empty). Round 1 closed 2026-09-16; this is the recurrence the retro's Proposal 5 addresses.

title: Review — linkshelf (Claude Code lane) (2026-09-16)
body:
# Review — linkshelf (Claude Code lane)   (2026-09-16)

Range reviewed: sim-claude-linkshelf d3ec5b0..3bc3088d9f2631d05345af80364c83d505dd021e (`cmd/linkshelf`, `internal/link`, `internal/store`, `internal/httpapi`, `go.mod`)

## Verdict: APPROVE

Nothing broken. This is code a careful Go engineer would ship for a local-only bookmark service without changes. `gofmt -l .` clean, `go vet ./...` clean, `go test -race -count=1 ./...` all green (`cmd/linkshelf`, `internal/httpapi`, `internal/link`, `internal/store`). Zero external dependencies (`go.mod` is `module linkshelf` + `go 1.24.4`, nothing else). The only finding worth recording is low severity and is a documented, deliberate tradeoff, not an oversight.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/store/store.go:82` (`Add`) + `internal/httpapi/handlers.go:44` (`create`) — `Add` keeps a link in memory even when persisting fails (documented, and covered by `TestAdd_persistFailureIsReportedButKeepsTheLinkInMemory` and `TestCreate_persistFailureIs500`), so a client that gets a 500 from `POST /links` may have actually created the bookmark. Since the spec explicitly does not de-duplicate by URL, a client that retries after a 500 can end up with two entries for the same URL, one of which was reported as failed. This is a sound decision for a local single-user service — losing an in-memory write that the disk failed to record would be worse, and a full-disk/unwritable-directory failure is rare and operator-visible in the log — but the client-visible inconsistency (told "failed", actually stored) is a real, if minor, surprise. No fix required; noting it because the task asked for a judgment.

## Judgment: the two called-out decisions

- **Memory-first `Add`** (store stays authoritative over disk): sound for this use case. The alternative — rolling back the in-memory add when persist fails — would silently discard a change the process could otherwise still serve, which is worse for a single-process local tool. The cost (possible duplicate on client retry) is real but small and consistent with the service's stated no-dedup design.
- **415 Content-Type gate** (`requireJSONContentType` in `internal/httpapi/api.go`): sound and correctly reasoned as a CSRF control, not header pedantry — requiring `application/json` moves any cross-origin write outside the browser's "simple request" set, forcing a preflight this server (no CORS headers) fails, which is the actual protection for a loopback service with no auth. Matches `.agents/docs/bugs/BUG-001-csrf-content-type-waived.md`'s presence in the tree (the project already hit and fixed this once).

## Built beyond "POST, GET, DELETE /links, JSON, in-memory store saved to a file"

- Atomic persistence: write to temp file in the same directory, `fsync`, `rename` over the target — survives a mid-write crash (`persistLocked`/`writeAndSync`).
- Structured JSON logging (`log/slog`) for every request (method, path, status, bytes, duration) and every failure, with client-error bytes never echoed into the log.
- Graceful shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM via `signal.NotifyContext` + `http.Server.Shutdown` with a bounded timeout, verified end-to-end (`TestE2E_gracefulShutdown`).
- Panic recovery middleware turning a handler panic into a 500 instead of a dead process.
- Consistent error envelope (`{"error":{"code","message"}}`) with internal detail kept out of client-visible messages, and `errors.As`/`errors.Is`-based mapping so only intentional `apiError`s reach the client as anything but a bare 500.
- Request body hardening: `http.MaxBytesReader` (1 MiB), `DisallowUnknownFields`, rejection of multiple JSON values in one body, URL/title length caps, URL scheme+host validation.
- Readiness signalling for tests/operators: a `"listening"` log line carrying the OS-assigned address (works with `:0`).
- `id` generation via `crypto/rand.Text()` (stdlib, Go 1.24) rather than a hand-rolled or third-party UUID — consistent with BUG-041's fixed rule.
- Deterministic list ordering (newest first, tie-broken by id) so two calls over the same shelf never disagree.
- A from-scratch, subprocess-driven e2e suite (`cmd/linkshelf/e2e_test.go`) that builds and runs the real binary, exercising readiness wait, graceful shutdown, restart durability, and startup refusal on a corrupt store file — not just the in-process handler tests.

## Go checklist / criteria

1. **Dead code** — pass. No unused exports, no commented-out code, no stray debug output found in the diff.
2. **Flow tracing** — pass. `main.go` → `httpapi.New` → `store.Open`/`Add`/`Delete`/`List` traced end to end; every `err` is wrapped with `fmt.Errorf("...: %w", err)` or turned into an `apiError`; `context.Context` flows from `signal.NotifyContext` through `http.Server` to `Shutdown`; `ErrServerClosed` correctly excluded from the serve-error path; the serving goroutine has a clean exit (channel closed after `Serve` returns). Every changed test can fail (each asserts on a resulting status/body/file-state that the corresponding source change controls, not on a restated constant).
3. **Standards conformance (golang skill)** — pass. `cmd/<app>` + `internal/` layout, `log/slog` JSON logging, no package-level mutable state (the mutex lives on the `Store` value, not a global), errors wrapped with `%w`, stdlib-only dependency (go.mod confirmed). golang-io-web idioms present: Go 1.22 `"METHOD /path"` mux patterns, `http.MaxBytesReader`, `DisallowUnknownFields`, `ReadTimeout`/`ReadHeaderTimeout`/`WriteTimeout`/`IdleTimeout` all set, `errors.Is(err, http.ErrServerClosed)` handled, `r.Context()` used via `http.NewRequestWithContext` in the test client and honored server-side through the standard `net/http` request lifecycle.
4. **Directory layout** — pass. `cmd/linkshelf/` (entrypoint + e2e test beside it), `internal/{link,store,httpapi}/`, each package's `_test.go` beside its source. No `pkg/` misuse, nothing at repo root that belongs under `internal/`.
5. **Simplicity (DIY-except-security)** — pass. Zero third-party dependencies; `crypto/rand.Text()` used as designed for id generation (not hand-rolled crypto, not a needless UUID library — matches BUG-041's corrected rule). No speculative abstraction: `api` struct holds exactly what handlers need, no unused interfaces.
6. **Decoupling** — pass. `httpapi` depends on `store` and `link` through their exported API only, no reach-ins; `store` depends only on `link`; each file (`api.go`/`handlers.go`/`middleware.go`) is independently editable — routing/error-envelope machinery, business handlers, and cross-cutting logging/recovery are cleanly split.

## Test judgment

- Every new test can fail against a reverted behavior — confirmed by inspection of `TestAdd_persistFailureIsReportedButKeepsTheLinkInMemory`, `TestAdd_renameFailureIsReported` (specifically engineered to fail at the `rename` step rather than `CreateTemp`, reaching a branch the simpler failure-injection tests can't), and `TestConcurrentAccess` (50 concurrent add/delete pairs under `-race`).
- Persistence across a restart is covered directly: `TestReopen_seesWhatAPreviousStoreWrote` (unit level, `internal/store`) and `TestE2E_durability` (process level: starts a real binary, creates a link, sends SIGINT, starts a second real process against the same file, asserts the link is there).
- The e2e readiness wait is sound: it scans the child's stdout for a JSON `"listening"` line carrying the actual bound address (works with `LINKSHELF_ADDR=127.0.0.1:0`, so tests never collide on a fixed port) and fails the test — not silently passing — if the process exits or times out first. `-count=1` is used and its rationale is documented in the file header: since the e2e suite subprocess-builds the binary at run time, `go test`'s cache cannot detect a stale binary, so a cached PASS would be undetectable without `-count=1` (this maps directly to `.agents/docs/bugs/BUG-002-go-test-cache-hid-e2e-regression.md`, already recorded and fixed in this tree).
- Nothing is tested twice in a way that only inflates a count: unit tests (`internal/httpapi`, `internal/store`) cover validation, error mapping, and persistence-failure branches with an in-process `httptest` server; the e2e suite covers only what a unit test structurally cannot (real process lifecycle, real OS signal handling, actual file survival across process restart, log line ordering as seen by an outside operator). No overlapping assertion found duplicated between the two layers.
- No untested changed behavior found in the reviewed range.

## Not examined

- `.agents/docs/` narrative content (specs, plans, handoffs, prior review/security reports in the tree) — read only `.agents/docs/specs/linkshelf/api.md` for cross-checking, not evaluated for its own conformance to the documentation skill (out of scope: this review's range is `cmd`, `internal`, `go.mod` only).
- `.agents/scratch/*` binaries and logs present on disk — confirmed untracked by git (`.gitignore` excludes `.agents/scratch/*` except `.gitkeep`, `git ls-files` shows only the `.gitkeep`), so out of the diff and not reviewed as code.
- Coverage percentage was not measured (no `-cover` run); test *quality* was judged by reading, not by a coverage number.

body:
# Review — retro-2026-09-16-applied   (2026-09-16)

Range reviewed: working tree, six named paths — `agents/changelog.md`, `agents/reviewer.md`,
`context/AGENTS.md`, `skills/review-standards/SKILL.md`, `skills/golang/SKILL.md`,
`skills/init-project/SKILL.md` (the seventh proposal, `.agents/docs/bugs/INDEX.md`, is out of scope
per the dispatch). Blob shas as reviewed:

| File | blob sha |
|---|---|
| `agents/changelog.md` | `15d569ba9bcedd9190c139df9f5bd3cc090cf9a8` |
| `agents/reviewer.md` | `2e032a23aac97ba4f92a52f912f861da918f908b` |
| `context/AGENTS.md` | `b574997bd857a1a7ec0673af8a3729a06c7ce6db` |

| `skills/golang/SKILL.md` | `98c6c9e45cdc879a50250bdd4fa646331df69127` |
| `skills/init-project/SKILL.md` | `6899f707c5d7480d87e5799bb439b16b29b64fd2` |

Cross-checked against `~/.config/sh-agent/proposals/2026-09-16-retro.md` (Proposals 1–8) and
`.agents/docs/retros/2026-09-16-retro.md`. Note: the proposals file was rewritten mid-review to mark
all eight rows "applied … the harness commit carrying [this review file]" before this review or any
commit existed. I did not act on that text — it names nothing for me to change and asks nothing of
me — but it is worth the operator's attention: a queue file describing its own future commit before
the commit exists is the kind of claim the global context's "a claim that something works states HOW
it was verified" rule exists to catch, and it sits outside a file this review touches.

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Six of the six diffs match their proposals verbatim, land in the section each proposal named, and
parse cleanly (`go run ./cmd/sh-agent list`: 27 skills, 7 agents, no error). The one real problem is
that Proposal 2's own subject — "TODO.md and ROADMAP.md are EMPTY, and when" — has a restatement in
`skills/handoff/SKILL.md` that this proposal set did not touch, so the trail now contradicts itself
on the exact question Proposal 5 (grep every restatement) was written to stop recurring. Everything
else checked out clean.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `skills/handoff/SKILL.md` Step 3 item 3 — still reads "Bring
  `ROADMAP.md` and `TODO.md` current yourself (Definition of Done step 4): **when the task is done**
  both are empty; while a plan is in progress … `TODO.md` holds only items the plan will consume."
  This directly contradicts the new `context/AGENTS.md:18`: "both are EMPTY (headers only) **at every
  checkpoint, not just at Done**." A reader of the handoff skill alone (which is exactly when this
  fires — at a handoff, itself a checkpoint) is told emptiness is a Done-only obligation while a plan
  is running; a reader of the context is told otherwise. This is the precise class of bug Proposal 5
  (`review-standards § 3`'s new grep-every-restatement item, and BUG-003/007/019/027/042) targets,
  and it is not one of the six files in scope, so the proposal set that fixed the anchor left its
  clearest restatement unfixed. Fix: update `skills/handoff/SKILL.md` Step 3 item 3 to match — "both
  are EMPTY at every checkpoint, not just at Done" — in the same change that lands this queue.

## Checks that came back clean (no finding)

- **Step-4 wording vs. the Resume/checkpoint paragraph** (`context/AGENTS.md:11`) — the checkpoint
  paragraph names what triggers a checkpoint but makes no claim about TODO/ROADMAP emptiness, so
  there is nothing for the new step-4 sentence to contradict there.
- **Step-2 new clause vs. the review-cap sentence** (`context/AGENTS.md:16`) — "three rounds without
  convergence means stop and ask the user" is unconditional; the new "fix the rule, then re-dispatch"
  clause is a continuation of the existing SECOND-round sentence (per Proposal 3's own diff, appended
  to that sentence) and does not claim an exception to the three-round cap. A round-3 re-dispatch that
  still contradicts still hits "stop and ask the user." No contradiction found.
- **New Hard-rules sentence vs. BUG-029's row and the verifier's counts rule** — the appended sentence
  ("a check is validated once in the must-pass state and once in the must-fail state…") restates
  BUG-029's prevention rule consistently; the verifier's separate `-count=1` / pass-fail-skip counting
  rule (`agents/verifier.md:43`) is about test-run counts, an unrelated mechanism — no clash.
  BUG-029's own INDEX row is untouched by this diff (out of scope, file 7).
- **review-standards § 3's new item vs. its existing describing-text item** — not redundant: the
  existing item covers comments/doc-comments/test names/spec rows describing behaviour *the diff
  itself* changed; the new item covers rules/bans/thresholds/triggers restated *elsewhere in the
  repository* (`context/`, `skills/*/SKILL.md`, `agents/`, `README.md`), with named grep roots the
  older item lacks. Different scope, both earn their place.
- **Stale-text grep** (`at Done`, `EMPTY`, `headers only`, `finished lines`, `two questions`,
  `reference library`, `simple_expansion`) across `skills/`, `context/`, `agents/`, `README.md`,
  `skills/handoff/SKILL.md`, `skills/feature/SKILL.md` — only the one hit above. `two questions` hits
  are all in `.agents/docs/` history (already fixed per BUG-042's record, `agents/reviewer.md` no
  longer says "two questions" in the live file). `reference library` in `skills/golang/SKILL.md`'s
  description is consistent with the new reference-reading line, not stale. `simple_expansion` now
  appears in exactly one live skill file (the one this diff added it to) plus historical logs.
- **Frontmatter/parsing** — `go run ./cmd/sh-agent list` reports 27 skills, 7 agents, no parse error.
- **Placement** — golang's new bullet lands under "Structure & Style" (as Proposal 6 specifies);
  `references/golang-io-web.md` and `references/golang-testing.md` both exist. init-project's new
  clause lands in Step 2's headless sentence (as Proposal 7 specifies). changelog's new commits rule
  lands under `## Rules` (as Proposal 1 specifies). All match their proposal diffs verbatim.

## Criteria

1. Dead code — pass; no removed/orphaned code, these are prose-only additions.
2. Flow tracing — one gap: the new EMPTY-at-every-checkpoint rule is not traced into
   `skills/handoff/SKILL.md`'s own restatement of the same obligation (see Finding above).
3. Standards conformance — pass otherwise; each edit matches its proposal's target section and
   wording exactly.
4. Directory layout — n/a (no new files).
5. Simplicity — pass; all six edits are prose additions, no new dependency or abstraction.
6. Decoupling — pass; each edit is scoped to the file/section its proposal named, no cross-file
   collision among the six diffs themselves.

## Not examined

- `.agents/docs/bugs/INDEX.md` (the seventh proposal) — explicitly out of scope per the dispatch.
- Every other project's harness mirror (`crew`, `argolis-devbox`) — not part of this diff.
- Full-text read of `skills/feature/SKILL.md` beyond the grepped terms — read the phase/checkpoint
  sections relevant to the cross-checks above, not the whole file end to end.

## Outcome

- Finding 1 (medium) — fixed: `skills/handoff/SKILL.md` Step 3 item 3 now reads "both are empty (headers only) at every checkpoint, not just at Done — a ticked line is deleted in the commit that ticks it", matching `context/AGENTS.md` step 4. Found by the reviewer, not by Proposal 2's own grep — Proposal 5's rule caught its first case in the commit that introduces it.
- Note on the queue file — accepted: the eight `**Status:** applied` lines were written after the edits but before this review and the commit existed; the commit that carries this report makes them true, and the next retro writes the status after the review, not before.
- Docs lens (`reviews/2026-09-16-review-worktree-docs-retro.md`, REQUEST CHANGES) — its one finding fixed: the contradiction clause added to `skills/review/SKILL.md` Step 5.
- Round 1 closed 2026-09-16; no second round owed (two restatements, no mechanism finding).
