title: Security review — attribution-write (2026-09-16)
body:
# Security review — attribution-write   (2026-09-16)

Range reviewed: working tree, cmd/sh-agent/main.go and main_test.go

## Blobs pinned — and a warning: the tree moved mid-review

| file | blob at HEAD `1254672` | blob I first read (11:10) | blob I finished against (11:16) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` | `27d03a0e3bc564ee1168ee272ba1fb24df61b339` | `672989cff1dfae6ae413bcc08fdd228b072ae7cd` | **`0657c04d311b738a90a0e47e48bc2275cff27cae`** |
| `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` | `fa2196a50afe393015ae6369a799b3556b542562` | `df476099a12753e037f70b4d65d932661b0288cc` | **`1b0a61bea89cb5a5462bf7683543f201d9bdd71b`** |

Both files were rewritten by another writer at `11:15:50` while this review was running, between my read and my first test run.
The `672989c`/`df47609` blobs were only ever hashed, never written to the object database (`git cat-file -p 672989c` -> "Not a valid
object name"), so they are unrecoverable and **the findings below are stated against `0657c04`/`1b0a61b`, the bytes on disk now**. The
bold column is authoritative. If the tree has moved again since, re-pin before acting on this. What changed in that window is recorded
in "Already fixed under me" so the caller can tell which of my observations were overtaken rather than wrong.

Command: `git diff -- cmd/sh-agent/main.go cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go`. The other modified files in the tree (`REQUIREMENTS.md`,
`ROADMAP.md`, `context/AGENTS.md`, the plan and the three cold-read reviews) were out of scope by instruction and were not read.

## Verdict: FINDINGS

Nothing high or medium. The write is careful in the ways that matter: it refuses a symlink outright via `os.Lstat`, refuses a
directory or FIFO via `!IsRegular()`, refuses anything over 1 MiB before reading it, parses the file into a map before touching it,
re-validates the spliced result with `json.Valid` before it lands, writes through a temp file in the same directory, restores the
original permission bits, and renames. I drove twenty crafted inputs through a binary built from the current blob and could not get it
to corrupt a file, write outside `--home`, hang, panic, or echo a byte of anyone's settings. What is left is a cluster of low-severity
items, the sharpest being that the create branch still opens with `os.WriteFile` — `O_WRONLY|O_CREATE|O_TRUNC`, no `O_EXCL`, no
`O_NOFOLLOW` — so the careful `Lstat` gate is advisory rather than enforced: anything that can write into `~/.claude` in the window
between the two syscalls can still redirect the write through a planted symlink, or wedge the install forever with a planted FIFO.
That precondition is an attacker who already owns the operator's config directory, which is why it is low and not medium, and one flag
closes it.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:491-505` — TOCTOU: the `Lstat` gate is not enforced by the write, and a planted
  FIFO hangs the install with no timeout. `os.Lstat` decides the file is absent, then `os.WriteFile` opens
  `O_WRONLY|O_CREATE|O_TRUNC` with neither `O_EXCL` nor `O_NOFOLLOW`. A local process that can create entries in `<home>/.claude`
  during that window can (a) plant a symlink, which `open(2)` follows, putting the write on any path the operator can write — the one
  way this code still creates a file outside `--home`; or (b) plant a FIFO, where `open(2)` for writing blocks until a reader appears,
  and there is no timeout, deadline, or context anywhere on the path, so `sh-agent install` stops with no further output. Both are
  closed by one change with no behaviour cost: `os.OpenFile(path, os.O_WRONLY|os.O_CREATE|os.O_EXCL, 0o644)` instead of
  `os.WriteFile` — losing the race then yields `EEXIST`, which the existing "could not be written (%v)" line already handles, and a
  FIFO or symlink at the path becomes that same error instead of a hang or a redirect. Confirmed by test that a *pre-existing* FIFO or
  directory is refused cleanly (no hang, file untouched); it is only the race window that is open.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:562-583` — no `Sync` before the rename. The temp file is written and `Close`d but
  never fsynced, and `os.Rename` makes the directory entry atomic, not the data behind it. A crash or power loss in the window can
  leave `settings.json` zero-length or partial — and that file carries `permissions.allow`, the list deciding what Claude Code may run
  without asking. Losing it fails *open into prompting*, not into silent grants, so the security direction is safe; it is still the
  operator's security config being replaced without a durability barrier. Remediation: `tmp.Sync()` before `tmp.Close()`.
  `internal/harness/apply.go:240-263` has the identical pattern, so this is a codebase-wide nit rather than a regression — worth fixing
  in both or neither.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:521-524` + `:645` — two lines of the same output contradict each other for a file
  that is valid JSON but not an object. Input `["x"]` produces, in order: `settings: <path> is not a JSON object; add the key by hand`
  (from `attributionSet`, correct) and then `note: <path> is not valid JSON, so the attribution setting could not be checked` (from
  `attributionHint` -> `attributionOff`, incorrect — the file *is* valid JSON, it just does not unmarshal into that struct). Verified by
  running it. An operator reading the second line will go looking for a syntax error that is not there. The cause is `attributionOff`
  collapsing every `json.Unmarshal` failure into `"is not valid JSON"`; it predates this diff, but this diff is what puts the two lines
  side by side. Remediation: have `attributionOff` distinguish a type mismatch from a parse failure, or let `attributionSet` suppress
  the hint once it has already explained the file.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:481-482` (doc comment) — "every other byte of the file stays" is false for a CRLF
  file, and a description that overstates a guarantee is read as one. The splice does `bytes.TrimRight(trimmed[:closing], " \t\r\n")`
  on the body, so the `\r` ending the last member's line is consumed and replaced by `,\n`. Verified: input
  `{\r\n  "model": "x"\r\n}\r\n` comes back as `{\r\n  "model": "x",\n  "attribution": ...\n}\r\n` — valid JSON, other keys intact,
  but one byte of the operator's file changed outside the insertion and the result has mixed line endings. Not exploitable; filed
  because the comment is the contract a later reader will trust. Remediation: say "every other key's bytes stay" and note the line
  ending, or preserve the file's dominant terminator in `insert`.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:10,39` — `install` now writes a file `uninstall` does not remove, while the usage
  text still promises `uninstall [--dry-run]   remove exactly what install wrote, nothing else`. `grep -rn settings.json internal/`
  returns nothing, so `harness.Uninstall` has no knowledge of it and the manifest never lists it. Not a vulnerability; it is a stated
  guarantee that the diff made untrue, and the safest resolution is probably to amend the sentence (leaving an operator's settings
  alone on uninstall is the right behaviour) rather than to start deleting settings files.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:512-514` vs `:585-601` — the 1 MiB guard is checked against `info.Size()` from the
  `Lstat`, but the read that follows is a separate `open`+`io.LimitReader(f, 1<<20)` with no size re-check. A file that grows past
  1 MiB between the two is read truncated, and the truncated buffer is what `json.Valid` blesses and `rename` installs. Reaching it
  needs the file to be rewritten larger mid-install *and* the first megabyte to still parse as a complete JSON document, which for
  strict JSON means the overflow is whitespace. Very narrow — hence low confidence that it is reachable at all. Remediation if it is
  ever worth closing: read `1<<20 + 1` bytes and treat `len(data) > 1<<20` as the same refusal the size gate already prints.
- **[low / confidence: high]** dependencies — `govulncheck ./...` reports the repo's **toolchain** affected by two stdlib advisories.
  Pre-existing, not introduced here, and not reachable from the new code, but `GO-2025-3956` is squarely in this binary's habits:
  `harness.Reinstall` executes whatever `exec.LookPath("go")` returns. Details in Checked. A toolchain bump fixes both.

### Already fixed under me (present in `672989c`, gone in `0657c04`)

Recorded so the caller can tell these were real and are closed, not that I missed them. In the blob I first read, `attributionSet`
gated on `os.Stat`, which follows symlinks. That made two no-race defects: a **dangling** symlink at `<home>/.claude/settings.json`
reported `ErrNotExist`, so the create branch ran and `os.WriteFile` followed the link and created the file *at the link's target*,
outside `<home>`; and a **live** symlink (a settings.json linked into a dotfiles checkout — the pattern this project's own
`/init-project` uses for `.claude/*`) was read through and then `os.Rename` replaced the *link itself* with a regular file, orphaning
the version-controlled copy while printing "other keys untouched". The same blob also had no size gate, so a >1 MiB file was read
truncated and the truncated buffer could be written back, and `null` at top level relied on the `closing <= opening` arm to catch it.
`0657c04` fixes all four: `os.Lstat` with an explicit `ModeSymlink` refusal ordered first in the switch, an `info.Size() > 1<<20`
refusal, an explicit `top == nil` check for bare `null`, and an `abandonTemp` helper that reports a temp file it could not remove. I
re-ran the symlink cases against the current blob: dangling and live symlinks are both refused with
`settings: <path> is a symlink; add the key to its target by hand`, the link survives, and no file appears outside `<home>`.

### Crafted-input matrix — exercised, not reasoned

Black-box against a binary built from `0657c04` into `.agents/scratch/secrev/` (no source created), one scratch `--home` per case,
sha256 of the file compared before and after. Driver: `.agents/scratch/secrev/{drive,rest,links}.sh`.

| input | file after | message |
|---|---|---|
| UTF-8 BOM before `{` | unchanged | advisory: not valid JSON |
| CRLF | key added | correct; see the CRLF finding for the one trimmed byte |
| trailing `// comment` (JSONC) | unchanged | advisory: not valid JSON |
| second top-level value `{"a":1}\n{"b":2}` | unchanged | advisory: not valid JSON |
| bare `null` | unchanged | `is not a JSON object` |
| array `["x"]` | unchanged | `is not a JSON object` + a contradicting hint (finding above) |
| `{}` | key added, no leading comma | correct |
| `{"a":"}}}"}` (braces inside a string) | key added after the real closer | correct |
| existing `attribution` (any value) | unchanged | left to the operator, hint fires |
| directory at the path | n/a | `is not a regular file`, no hang |
| **FIFO** at the path | still a FIFO | `is not a regular file`, **no hang** (60 s timeout unused) |
| symlink, dangling | link intact, no file created anywhere | `is a symlink` |
| symlink, live | link intact, target unmodified | `is a symlink` |
| mode `0o600` | key added, **mode still 0600** | correct |
| mode `0o000` | unchanged | `could not be read` |
| 2 MB file whose first bytes parse | unchanged | `is larger than 1 MiB` |
| 20 000-deep nesting | unchanged, **no panic** | Go's scanner depth cap (10 000) rejects it first |
| `--dry-run`, file absent | not created | `[dry-run] would create …` |
| `--dry-run`, file present | unchanged | `[dry-run] would add …` |
| `--vendor agy`, file present | unchanged | no settings line at all |
| leftover `.settings-*` temp files after all runs | **none** | `find` across every scratch home |

Two structural properties make the splice sound and are worth keeping in the comment: once `json.Unmarshal(data, &top)` succeeds with
a non-nil map, `data` is a valid JSON document whose top-level value is an object, so the last non-whitespace byte *must* be that
object's `}` and the first `{` *must* be its opener — `LastIndexByte`/`IndexByte` cannot mis-target, which is what the `}}}` -in-a-string
case confirms. And `info.Mode().Perm()` masks setuid/setgid/sticky off, so a strangely-moded original cannot propagate those bits.

## Checked

- **Secrets** — none. The only literal written is `"attribution": {"commit": "", "pr": ""}` — two empty strings. No credential, token,
  key, or path to one appears in either file; grep for `token|secret|key|password|credential` over the diff returns only "keys"
  meaning JSON keys.
- **Injection** — no shell, SQL, or template in the new code. The only external input is the bytes of `settings.json`, flowing to
  `json.Unmarshal`, `json.Valid`, `bytes.TrimRight`/`IndexByte`/`LastIndexByte`, and a byte splice — never to `exec`, never as a format
  string. The path is `home` (operator flag) joined with the constants `harness.ClaudeRoot` and `"settings.json"`, so no path element
  is attacker-controlled; the residual path weakness is symlink resolution in the race window, filed above.
- **Authz/authn** — none in scope, but the diff does move a trust boundary and that is the headline for reviewers: `sh-agent install`
  now *mutates* a file it previously only read, and that same file holds Claude Code's `permissions.allow` — the list governing what
  the agent may execute without prompting. The mutation is correctly fenced (map-parse first, key-absent check, `json.Valid` on the
  result, other keys never reserialized, a present `attribution` of any value left alone), and I could not make it alter or drop
  another key in any of the twenty cases above. No finding, but it is the thing to re-review if the splice is ever loosened.
- **Crypto** — nothing hand-rolled and nothing crypto-adjacent: no primitive, token format, session, or protocol is implemented or
  composed here. `os.CreateTemp`'s randomized suffix is the stdlib's own and is not a security control in this design (the rename is).
- **Dependencies** — none added. `go.mod` is `module github.com/kesokaj/styrman-harness` / `go 1.24.4` with **zero** `require` lines,
  matching the repo's stdlib-only rule; the diff's one new import is `bytes`. `govulncheck ./...` ran
  (`/home/kesokaj/.go/bin/govulncheck`, Go 1.24.4) and reports two stdlib advisories, both reachable from pre-existing code and neither
  from the new code: **GO-2026-4602** (`FileInfo` can escape from a `Root` in `os`; found in `os@go1.24.4`, fixed in `os@go1.25.8`;
  trace `internal/harness/inventory.go:164` `os.ReadDir`) and **GO-2025-3956** (unexpected paths returned from `LookPath` in
  `os/exec`; fixed in `os/exec@go1.24.6`; trace `internal/harness/repo.go:140` `exec.LookPath`). It also counted 2 vulnerabilities in
  imported packages and 43 in required modules that the code does not call. `npm audit` not applicable — no JavaScript in this repo.
  `gofmt -l cmd/sh-agent/` clean; `go vet ./...` clean.
- **GCP surface** — untouched. No IAM binding, service account, `--allow-unauthenticated`, Secret Manager reference, or key file
  anywhere in the diff; the change is local-filesystem only.
- **Output hygiene (asked for explicitly)** — no byte of the file, and no byte of a JSON error, can reach stdout. The `Fprintf`
  arguments across the new code are exactly: `path` (operator-supplied), the `fragment` constant, `tmpName`, and `error` values from
  `os.MkdirAll`, `os.WriteFile`, `os.CreateTemp`, `(*File).Write`, `(*File).Close`, `os.Chmod`, `os.Rename` and `os.Remove` — all
  `*fs.PathError`, carrying a syscall name and a path, never content. The one value that *would* carry input bytes, the
  `json.Unmarshal` error, is deliberately discarded (`cmd/sh-agent/main.go:521`), and the `readSettings` refactor preserved that
  property for `attributionOff`, whose `problem` values are the three constants "could not be read", "is not a regular file", "is not
  valid JSON". The only disclosure is one bit — whether the file is valid JSON but not an object. Confirmed by diffing stdout against
  the file contents for every case in the matrix.
- **Temp-file lifetime (asked for explicitly)** — `os.CreateTemp(filepath.Dir(path), ".settings-*.json")`: same directory as the
  target (so the rename is atomic and never crosses a filesystem), mode `0600` at creation, randomized name, dot-prefixed so Claude
  Code's `settings.json` glob will not read it. Removed on all four post-create error returns, now through `abandonTemp`, which also
  prints the temp path if the removal itself fails. `find` over every scratch home after the full matrix: none left behind. The only
  residue path is a SIGINT/SIGTERM or panic between `CreateTemp` and `Rename`, which leaves a `0600` file containing the operator's own
  settings — no disclosure, and `uninstall` will not clean it (see the uninstall finding).

## Not examined

- **The current blob's own diff was not read as a diff.** `672989c` was never stored in git, so I could not `diff` what I first read
  against `0657c04`; I re-read the whole of `attributionSet`/`abandonTemp`/`readSettings` in the current file and re-ran the full
  matrix against a binary built from it, but the *rest* of `main.go` outside those functions was read only in the original diff. If
  the 11:15:50 rewrite touched anything beyond the attribution block, I did not see it.
- `main_test.go` at `1b0a61b` was read only by grep (confirming new `is larger than 1 MiB` and `is a symlink` subtests at lines 575 and
  587); the full current test file was not read line by line, and `go test -race ./...` was **not run** — the tests were inspected, not
  executed. Test gaps I can still name: no test covers a FIFO, a BOM, CRLF, mode `0000`, or a JSONC comment; every one of those is
  covered only by my scratch matrix, which is not committed and will not run again.
- Whether `{"commit": "", "pr": ""}` actually disables Claude Code's trailers, and whether `"pr"` is a key Claude Code reads at all.
  That is the change's entire purpose and it cannot be verified from this repo. A wrong key name would make the write inert while
  still carrying every risk above. Note that `attributionOff` only ever inspects `commit`, so `pr` is unverified on both sides — the
  tool cannot detect its own setting being wrong.
- Whether Claude Code accepts JSONC in `settings.json`. If it does, this code silently skips every commented settings file (verified
  above: a trailing `// comment` makes it refuse), which is a correctness gap, not a security one.
- Two `sh-agent install` processes racing on the same `--home`: last `rename` wins, and the loser's `json.Valid` was computed against a
  stale read. Not exercised; likely benign because both write the same fragment.
- Behaviour when `sh-agent install` runs as root via `sudo`: the file would be created root-owned under root's `$HOME`, and a later
  non-root install would hit `EACCES` and print the advisory line rather than fail. Reasoned from the code, not run.
- A symlinked `.claude` **directory** (as opposed to the settings file) still routes the write to the link's target, because `Lstat`
  only declines to follow the final component. This is pre-existing for the whole installer — `harness.Install` writes every harness
  file through that same directory — so it is out of this diff's blast radius, but it is the remaining answer to "can `--home` produce
  files outside itself": yes, if `<home>/.claude` is itself a link.
- The four out-of-scope modified files. If any of them *describes* what this write does, that prose was not checked against the code —
  and the CRLF finding shows the in-file comment already overstates the guarantee.

## Outcome

- The tree moved under the review (the verifier's symlink flag and the code review's null/size/cleanup findings landed while it ran); the report's own note says it finished against the later blobs, and its "four real defects closed" line is the record of that. This outcome is against the tree after its three findings were applied.
- Finding 1 (low) — fixed: the create path opens with `O_WRONLY|O_CREATE|O_EXCL`, so anything planted at the path after the `Lstat` fails the open instead of being written through or blocked on; the write is followed by `Sync` and a checked `Close`.
- Finding 2 (low) — fixed: `tmp.Sync()` before the rename on the insert path. The same pattern in `internal/harness/apply.go:240-263` is pre-existing and filed as a Follow-up in the plan, not changed here.
- Finding 3 (low) — fixed: a valid non-object file (`["x"]`, `null`) now gets one line, from `attributionHint` ("is not a JSON object, so the attribution setting could not be checked …"); `attributionSet` returns silently for it. A CRLF file keeps its line endings (the insert uses the file's own), test `crlf file keeps its line endings`; the doc comment says "every byte up to the object's last value stays".
- Its 20 crafted inputs left seven files named by their contents in the repository root (the probe wrote to the content string as a path); removed by name, recorded as BUG-044 — the agent's rule is scratch only.
- Round 1 closed 2026-09-16; no second round owed (three low findings, no mechanism finding).

title: Review — cold read of the delivery-rework plan (2026-09-17)
body:
# Review — cold read of the delivery-rework plan   (2026-09-17)

Range reviewed: `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-17-delivery-rework.md` (untracked, at HEAD c7af0de) plus the code surfaces it names: `cmd/sh-agent/main.go`, `internal/harness/{repo,plan,state,apply}.go`, `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.agents/docs/deploy/{local,remote}.md`, `README.md`, `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` (ADR-026), `skills/retro/SKILL.md`.

## Verdict: design needs revision / implementation not ready

The plan is well argued on the *why* and its Decisions table is unusually complete, but three of its load-bearing claims do not survive contact with the code it names. `reorder` (`cmd/sh-agent/main.go:446`) keys value-taking flags off a hardcoded map that the plan's two new value flags are not in, so `sh-agent report --message note --dry-run` silently parses as `-message="--dry-run"` with `--dry-run` unset — the command PUSHES when the operator asked it not to. `state.json` is rebuilt from scratch on every install (`internal/harness/apply.go:106`), so the "recorded feedback-repo path" the plan puts second in its resolution order is erased by the next `sh-agent update`. And `secretShaped` (`internal/harness/plan.go:206`) matches filenames only, against a collection list that is four fixed names and a `*.md` glob — not one of which can ever match it, so the plan's redaction guarantee is a check that cannot fire, and the Risks row "no secrets, and `secretShaped` refuses a credential" is asserted about content the filter never looks at.

## Findings

### 1. Gaps — what must be decided before implementation starts

- **[high / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:446-451` — **misunderstanding of existing code.** `reorder`'s `takesValue` map holds only `-repo/--repo`, `-home/--home`, `-vendor/--vendor`. The plan adds two value-taking flags, `--message TEXT` and `--feedback-repo DIR`, and its Phase-2 task only claims "`reorder` handles `report --dry-run` as it does every other verb (BUG-002)" — `--dry-run` is a boolean and was never the problem. Trace `report --message note --dry-run`: `flags=["--message","--dry-run"]`, `positional=["note"]`, result `["--message","--dry-run","note"]`; `flag` then binds `-message="--dry-run"`, leaves `dryRun` false, and stops at `note`. The operator gets a real commit and push from a command they dry-ran. **Measured**, 2026-09-17, by copying `reorder` verbatim into `.agents/scratch/` (since removed; no source was touched) and parsing with a FlagSet holding the plan's flags:

```
in=[--message note --dry-run]      reorder=[--message --dry-run note] => message="--dry-run"     dry-run=false narg=1
in=[--feedback-repo /p --dry-run]  reorder=[--feedback-repo --dry-run /p] => feedback-repo="--dry-run" dry-run=false narg=1
in=[--dry-run --message note]      reorder=[--dry-run --message note]  => message="note"          dry-run=true  narg=0
in=[--home /h --dry-run]           reorder=[--home /h --dry-run]       => (correct; --home is in takesValue)
```

So the defect is order-dependent and silent: the operator who writes the flag last is safe, the one who writes it first pushes. Fix: the plan must state that `takesValue` gains both new flags, and Phase 2's expect must name a test for `report --message X --dry-run` asserting nothing was written, not just `report --dry-run`.
- **[high / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/apply.go:106` vs `internal/harness/state.go:14-21` — **the recorded feedback-repo path has no writer and no survival.** `State` has no such field today; the plan's Surfaces line names `state.go` "(the recorded feedback-repo path)" but the Interfaces section never says which verb *writes* it (`report` is described as reading it, third in its resolution order), and `apply.go:106` constructs `State{Repo, Commit, InstalledAt, Vendor, Files}` fresh on every install, with `SaveState` marshalling the whole struct. Any field `report` adds is silently dropped on the next `sh-agent install`/`update`, after which `report` falls through to the `~/.config/sh-agent/feedback/` default and clones a *second* checkout. Decide before coding: who writes it, and whether `Install` must preserve unknown/extra state fields (or whether the path belongs in its own file instead, which would keep `State`'s "manifest, and nothing else" contract intact — see the comment at `state.go:11-13`).
- **[high / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/plan.go:200-225` — **`secretShaped` is reachable but cannot fire on this input, and the plan leans on it as its security control.** It is unexported and `report.go` is in the same package, so the plan's reuse compiles. But it matches a *base filename* against `.env*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `*credentials*.json`, `id_rsa`, etc., and the plan's collection set is exactly `feedback.jsonl`, `retros.jsonl`, `state.json` and `proposals/*.md`. None can match any pattern. The Failure-modes row "A collected file matches `secretShaped` → exit 1" is unreachable, and the Phase-2 expect "a `secretShaped` file refused" can only be satisfied by a unit test that injects a filename the real collector would never produce — a test that cannot fail on the shipping path (review-standards §2). The real exposure is *content*: `feedback.jsonl` is the operator's verbatim corrections and `proposals/*.md` are proposed diffs. Decide: either collect a directory (making the name filter meaningful) or drop the claim and state honestly that content is unscanned, and let the Phase-4 security dispatch judge that.
- **[high / confidence: medium]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:108-111` — **`report` cannot run where the plan most wants it to.** Every verb except `version` and `uninstall` passes through `harness.FindRepo`, which returns a hard error (`"harness repo not found: run from inside the checkout, pass --repo, or set SH_AGENT_REPO"`) when no checkout is found. The plan's Failure-modes row says a plain copy works with `"harness_commit": null` — true, a plain copy is still a harness-shaped tree — but the Risks section simultaneously asserts that a styrman-crew project home receives *installed files, not a checkout*. On such a machine there is no harness tree at all and `report` exits 1 before doing anything. Decide: does `report` require a repo (and therefore cannot report from an install-only home), or does it join the early switch and degrade the four repo-derived fields (`harness_commit`, `drift`, `skills`, `agents`)? Two implementers will build different things here.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** Plan `## Failure modes`, row "The feedback checkout is dirty" — **"It is committed along with the run" contradicts the project's own git rule and the plan's own redaction row.** `AGENTS.md`/`context/AGENTS.md` require staging by name and forbid `git add -A` with untracked files present. Committing whatever a second process left in the feedback checkout also routes around the `secretShaped` gate, which only inspects *collected* files. Decide: stage the run directory's files by name, and either refuse a dirty checkout or name it and leave it.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** Plan `## Phases`, Phase 3 first task — **the Verification criterion is written so it cannot catch what the task is for.** The grep is `git grep -n 'styrman-crew\|argolis' .agents/docs/deploy README.md AGENTS.md`. It does not search for the word *mirror*, and it does not search `skills/`. Standing restatements that survive it: `AGENTS.md:64` ("Machines, mirrors, and the signed-tag release procedure (ADR-026)"), `AGENTS.md:38` ("a downstream mirror … BUG-015"), `README.md:53` ("deployed to every install and every downstream mirror"), `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md:27` ("a downstream mirror (BUG-015)"). The Phase-3 AGENTS.md task only covers "the Release section".
- **[high / confidence: high]** `skills/retro/SKILL.md:132` — **a skill instructs an agent to read the section this plan deletes, and the plan declares `skills/` untouched.** The retro skill tells a harness-scope application to "name the downstream mirrors its `deploy/remote.md` lists as the next task in their projects". Phase 3 retires `deploy/remote.md` § Downstream mirrors. The plan's "Not touched, deliberately: `context/`, `skills/`, `agents/`. This is a delivery change, not a behaviour change for any agent" is therefore wrong as stated: this *is* a behaviour change for the retro agent, which will follow a dangling pointer. Either the plan touches that line or it explains why a dead cross-reference is acceptable.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** Plan Phase 1, second task — **R8 is to be "drafted here" and the plan contains no draft.** The global rule for an immutable file is propose the exact edit → approval → ADR → one commit. The operator cannot approve text that does not exist, and a first-pass implementer has nothing to show them. Worse, the plan never reconciles the new behaviour with the *existing* R7, which says harness state "lives in `~/.config/sh-agent/` and nowhere else" — `report` copies that state into a second git repository and pushes it to GitHub. Decide whether R8 permits that or whether R7 needs an amendment too (both are immutable-file edits requiring approval).
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** Plan `## Risks`, row 3 — **"No project source, no secrets" is asserted and contradicted by what is collected.** `feedback.jsonl` entries carry a `project` field by design (`skills/feedback/SKILL.md:13`), `retros.jsonl` lines carry project paths (`skills/retro/SKILL.md:119`), and `proposals/*.md` hold proposed diffs of project rules in full (`skills/retro/SKILL.md:118`). `state.json` adds the absolute repo path and ~260 `$HOME`-relative paths. So `report` ships the names, paths and partial content of every consumer project into a sibling repository — while D5 records the operator's rule that "styrman-harness and the feedback/trajectory should not be directly connected to any other project". The repository is private and the operator's own, so this may well be fine; it is not *checked*, and it is the one place where D5 and the feedback loop pull against each other.
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** Plan `## Interfaces`, the `go` field — **an implementation choice named in the record shape with no decision behind it.** `"go": "go1.27.1"` can be `runtime.Version()` (the toolchain that built the running binary) or `exec` of `go version` (the host toolchain on PATH). These differ on this very box: HEAD's commit message describes a user-level go1.27.1 SDK placed *ahead of* `/usr/bin/go`, and `Reinstall` pins `GOTOOLCHAIN=local` precisely because the two diverge (`internal/harness/repo.go:170-180`). Since the whole point of the field is to know what a machine can build with, the answer matters and the plan does not give it.
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** Plan `## Interfaces`, `host` — **derivation and path-safety unspecified.** `host` becomes a *directory name* in another repository (`reports/<host>/…`). The plan never says it comes from `os.Hostname()`, nor what happens to an empty result, an error, an FQDN with dots, or a name containing a separator. This repo already treats path safety as a live concern (`internal/harness/pathguard_test.go`, and `LoadState`'s `filepath.IsLocal` drop at `state.go:44-50`); a new attacker-free-but-unvalidated path component should still be constrained deliberately.
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** Plan `## Interfaces`, resolution order — **no behaviour defined for a resolved directory that exists but is not the feedback checkout.** "When that directory does not exist it is cloned" covers only absent. An existing `~/.config/sh-agent/feedback/` that is empty, is not a git repo, or is a clone of something else gets no stated handling, and it is the likely state after a half-finished first run. Decide: validate the remote, or refuse a non-git directory by name.
- **[low / confidence: high]** Plan `## Interfaces`, "Writes to `<feedback>/reports/<host>/<date>-<HHMMSS>/`, one directory per run, never overwriting" — **the non-overwriting property has no mechanism.** Two runs in the same second collide. Name the guard (`os.Mkdir` failing on an existing directory, rather than `MkdirAll`) or the disambiguator.
- **[low / confidence: high]** Plan `## Interfaces`, "`--home` and `--repo` behave as they do for every other verb" vs the literal `~/.config/sh-agent/` throughout — the collection root must be `<home>/.config/sh-agent` (as `statePath` at `state.go:23` does) or the Phase-2 tests cannot run under a scratch home, which R6 requires of every development run. Reasonable implementers will get this right; the plan's text says `~` eight times and never once `<home>`.
- **[low / confidence: high]** Plan `## Failure modes`, row 2 — the message `report: nothing to send from <path>` is printed on a path that nevertheless sends the metrics record. The text contradicts the behaviour the same row specifies.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/state.go:66-73` — `RemoveState` drops `~/.config/sh-agent` when empty. A feedback clone living inside it makes that directory permanently non-empty, so `uninstall` now leaves a git checkout with a configured remote behind. R4's "`uninstall` removes exactly what its manifest lists" still holds, but the plan should say the clone is deliberately not uninstalled, and the docs task should say it too.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** Plan `## Surfaces touched` names "the `report` verb, its flags, its help" — `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` states the verb list **twice**: the package doc comment at lines 5-13 and the `usage` const at lines 35-50. Both are restatements of the same rule and both must change. The docs also restate it (`README.md`, `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md`), and `README.md:51`'s state-location table gains a row for the feedback checkout; neither is named in a Phase-3 task.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** Two new environment variables, `$SH_AGENT_FEEDBACK_REPO` and `$SH_AGENT_FEEDBACK_URL`, appear in Interfaces and in no docs task. `README.md` and `local.md:27` document `$SH_AGENT_REPO` today; the new pair needs the same clause. Per the global rule, a new flag or config key is not done until the file describing it says so.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** The clone URL constant is SSH (`git@github.com:…`) while Phase 4 creates the repository with `gh`. The Risks row quotes the operator on "ssh **or** gh". A machine authenticated to `gh` over HTTPS but without an SSH key hits the clone-failure path even though it has working credentials. The env override makes this recoverable, so it is only a documentation-and-default question — but it should be a stated default, not an incidental one.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** Plan `## Verification` names tiers for collection, redaction, record shape and the git side, but no tier for the **four-branch resolution order** (flag → env → state → default), which is the part with the most branches and the one the state-clobbering finding above breaks.

### 2. Scope — what the plan builds that `## Why` did not name

The `## Why` asks for two things: delivery through `sh-agent` only, and "some sort of feedback function from each place installed reporting back to the main". The plan is disciplined about this — the webservice is assessed and struck (D3), versioned bundles are deferred with a full assessment (D6), and the consumers' own changes are explicitly Out. Against that, three items go beyond the request and only two carry a D-row:

- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `--feedback-repo DIR` **plus** `$SH_AGENT_FEEDBACK_REPO` **plus** a path in `state.json` **plus** a hardcoded default is four configuration mechanisms for one value that, by the operator's own framing (one user, one private repository, four machines), never varies. No D-row asks for any of them. This is configuration for a value that does not vary (review-standards §5), and it is also the source of two findings above (the state field with no writer; the untested resolution order). The simplest correct design is the constant plus one override for tests; `$SH_AGENT_FEEDBACK_URL` alone would cover the sandbox/bare-repo integration tier.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `--message TEXT` is not in the request and has no D-row. It is cheap and plausibly useful, but it is the flag that triggers the `reorder` defect, so it is not free.
- **[low / confidence: low]** Collecting `state.json` into the report *and* deriving `files`/`installed_at`/`vendor` from it into `report.json` sends the same operation's data in two shapes. One of them is redundant; the plan does not say which is authoritative for a future reader of the feedback repository.

The feedback repository itself, its name, and one-directory-per-run **are** covered (D4). Retiring the mirrors and the tag channel **are** covered (D1, D2, D5).

### 3. Readiness — questions a first-pass implementer must ask

BLOCKING (two careful implementers would build different things):

1. Does `report` require a harness checkout? `FindRepo` (`main.go:108`) makes it mandatory for every verb but `version`/`uninstall`, yet the plan wants reports from an install-only home. If not mandatory, what do `harness_commit`, `drift`, `skills` and `agents` contain?
2. Who writes the feedback-repo path into `state.json`, and how does it survive `install` rebuilding `State` wholesale at `apply.go:106`?
3. Is the `secretShaped` gate meant to be real? If yes, the collection set must change (a directory walk) — that is a different command from the one specified.
4. What is the exact text of R8, and does R7's "and nowhere else" need amending in the same approval?
5. `go`: the host toolchain (`go version` on PATH) or the binary's build toolchain (`runtime.Version()`)?
6. Does the dirty-feedback-checkout row really mean "commit everything present", against the stage-by-name rule?
7. Is the deleted `deploy/remote.md` § Downstream mirrors, referenced by `skills/retro/SKILL.md:132`, in scope after all — or does the "skills untouched" line stand and the dangling reference with it?

NON-BLOCKING (a default is stated, or a reasonable implementer decides alone):

8. `--message` and `--feedback-repo` must be added to `reorder`'s `takesValue` — mechanical once the defect is known, but no implementer will find it unprompted, so it belongs in the plan. `TestReorder` (`cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go:20-33`) covers only the three registered value flags plus the boolean `--force`, so no existing test fails when the new flags are added; the plan must ask for a new row.
9. `<home>/.config/sh-agent` rather than a literal `~` under `--home`.
10. Whether `report` should call `knownCheckout` as `install`/`update` do (it only reads the repo; probably not).
11. `os.Mkdir` vs `MkdirAll` for the run directory.
12. SSH vs HTTPS for the clone URL default.
13. Whether the new git calls reuse `repo.go`'s `gitOut`/`exec.Command` style. **The answer should be yes and the plan should say so**: `Pull`'s comment (`repo.go:118-127`) records a deliberate, security-reviewed decision that git runs in the operator's own environment, and `gitOut` (`repo.go:190-201`) is the established error-wrapping shape that surfaces git's stderr. `report.go` lands in the same package, so both are reachable; the plan's silence is the only risk of a second style appearing. Note `gitOut`'s parameter is named `repo` and every existing caller means the *harness* checkout — a second repository flowing through it is fine mechanically but wants a comment.

## Criteria

1. **Dead code** — one finding: the `secretShaped` gate as specified is unreachable code on the shipping path, and the Phase-2 test for it cannot fail. Nothing else in the plan is orphaned; no source was changed, so there is no leftover to delete.
2. **Flow tracing** — fail. Three traces break: `reorder` → `flag.Parse` for the two new value flags; `report` writes state → `install` rebuilds state; `report` → `FindRepo` on a home with no checkout. A fourth, `deploy/remote.md` § Downstream mirrors → `skills/retro/SKILL.md:132`, breaks a documented cross-reference.
3. **Standards conformance** — fail. `AGENTS.md:64`, `AGENTS.md:38`, `README.md:53` and `local.md:27` restate the mirror arrangement and are not covered by the Phase-3 task or its grep; the verb list is restated twice inside `main.go` (lines 5-13 and 35-50); the dirty-checkout row conflicts with the stage-by-name git rule the harness itself ships; R8 is unwritten and R7 is unreconciled.

### Does `report.json` leak by listing file, line and pattern?

No, on this design. `pattern` is one of seven constants written in the source, so it discloses nothing the repository does not already publish. `file` and `line` locate the redaction in the copy that ships alongside it, where `[redacted by sh-agent report]` already marks the same spot — the record adds no information the reader cannot see. What it does record is that a given host produced a credential-shaped string on a given date, which is a property of the machine, not of the secret, and is the kind of signal the loop exists to carry. The one caveat is ordering: if a future change ever sends `report.json` without the redacted copy (a dashboard, a summary branch), the pairing that makes this harmless disappears. Worth a sentence in the ADR, not a finding.

### Scope (round 3)

No new unasked-for surface. `--message`, the env var and the `state.json` field stayed gone; the clone constant is one value, not a mechanism. The round-1/round-2 scope note that `state.json` is both shipped verbatim and mined into `report.json` is still unanswered (plan:44,47) — one sentence naming which is authoritative would close it. The Risks section's round-2 defect IS fixed: plan:149 no longer claims "no secrets" and no longer cites `secretShaped`, and plan:150 reconciles the consumer-project names against D5.

### Readiness (round 3)

BLOCKING:
1. Which bytes does a redaction replace — the needle, or a span to a named delimiter? (plan:45)
2. Does Phase 2 task 3 build the refusal or the redaction? (plan:124 vs plan:45)
3. Does a `-----BEGIN` match redact the line or the block through `-----END`? (plan:45)
4. What survives of `remote.md` § Releases once the crew channel is retired? (plan:133 vs D2)

NON-BLOCKING: JSON validity of the redacted `*.jsonl` copies (assert `json.Valid` per line); the empty-repo first push; `--dry-run` and the clone; R8's noun list; and every carried-over item in the low finding above.

### Which of these are real ambiguities

AMBIGUOUS — two careful implementers diverge and the author must decide: the redaction span (1), the PEM block rule (3), and the fate of § Releases (4). Each has at least two defensible answers and the plan picks none.

SAME-WAY — I would resolve these myself and so would any careful implementer, but the plan text must still be corrected because the wrong text is the acceptance criterion: the stale "refuses" expect (2 — plan:45's three sentences of reasoning plainly win over one clause in a task, but that clause is what gets ticked); the missed stale restatements at `remote.md:45,93` and `README.md:53`; JSON-validity assertions on the copies; the empty-repo first push; `--dry-run` not cloning; R8's noun list; and the whole carried-over mechanical list (host, `Mkdir`, `<home>`, `gitOut`, the surviving clone).

### Criteria (round 3)

1. **Dead code** — pass. Nothing orphaned in the plan; the unreachable `secretShaped` gate is gone and its replacement is reachable by construction.
2. **Flow tracing** — one break left in the plan's own text: `## Interfaces` redact → Phase 2 task 3 refuse. The code traces round 1 broke (reorder/`takesValue`, `State` rebuild, `FindRepo`) are all closed and re-verified this round against `main.go:446-450`, `apply.go:106`, `main.go:105`.
3. **Standards conformance** — the grep no longer forces an implementer to edit vendored text or delete a context rule; five restatements outside its needles still go stale (R3-3).
4. **Directory layout** — pass, unchanged: `internal/harness/report.go` beside its peers, tests in the existing files, integration scratch under `.agents/scratch/`.
5. **Simplicity (DIY-except-security)** — no hand-rolled crypto, auth or session handling; the signed-tag channel is removed rather than reimplemented and git/SSH credentials stay the operator's own. The redaction pass is a substring scan over the operator's own data, not a security primitive — it is a heuristic the plan correctly declines to call a guarantee (plan:149). Configuration is down to one flag plus one constant.
6. **Decoupling** — pass. `State` untouched; `report.go` is a new file in the right package with a single seam to `Inspect`.

### Not examined (round 3)

- The operator's live `~/.config/sh-agent/` — not read, as in round 2. Whether the current `feedback.jsonl` already contains a needle hit, and whether a redaction of it would break JSON, is unmeasured; the JSON-validity finding rests on the documented record shapes (`skills/feedback/SKILL.md:40-52`, `skills/retro/SKILL.md:118-122`), not on the live file.
- `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` read at lines 45-53 and 80-93 only; §§ 1-44 and the resync loop's full body still unread, so the Phase-3 blast radius inside that file is assessed from its headings and grep hits, not from a full read.
- `DECISIONS.md` ADR-001..025, 027..029 remain unread across all three rounds; an earlier ADR restating the mirror arrangement may still go unamended. This is the oldest open gap in the review and no round has closed it.
- `internal/harness/harness_test.go` (1499 lines) and `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` read only at the cited call sites.
- No code exists yet; every verdict above is by reading the named files at HEAD c7af0de plus the two greps quoted, both run this session.

title: Cold-reader check — release-binary plan (2026-09-17)
body:
# Cold-reader check — release-binary plan (2026-09-17)

Range reviewed: `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-17-release-binary.md` (plan document, not a diff), plus the code surfaces it names.

## Round 1

### (1) Gaps

- **G1 (BLOCKING-shaped, high) — `go:embed` is compiled into every build, not only release/`go install` builds, but the Failure-modes table and the "cannot happen" claims assume otherwise.** Interfaces § Failure modes row 1 says a missing-source case "cannot happen for a release or `go install` binary; a dev build prints today's `harness repo not found …`". But `embed.go`'s `//go:embed all:context …` at the module root embeds the five directories into *any* binary built from this module, dev included — there is no build tag gating it. Given the plan's own Source-selection order (`--repo` → env → cwd/parent → recorded repo → embedded, install-release-binary.md:50), a `go run ./cmd/sh-agent status` invoked from outside any checkout with no recorded state would silently fall through to the embedded copy in a dev build too — not error as the table claims — and that embedded copy is whatever was on disk when the binary was last compiled, which can be stale relative to the live checkout a developer is iterating on. The plan does not decide whether the embedded fallback should be disabled for dev/untagged builds (e.g. gated on `buildVersion() != ""`) or accepted as dev behaviour. Two implementers will build different things here, and the difference changes what `sh-agent status`/`install` do during ordinary local testing (`.agents/scratch/x`, per this repo's own testing convention). Cite: plan lines 48–52, 75; `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:100-116` (today's unconditional `FindRepo` hard-error, which the embedded fallback removes for every build, not just release ones).

- **G2 (BLOCKING, high) — the `install`/`sync` rebuild-vs-copy branch (`cmd/sh-agent/main.go:117-158`) is not re-specified for `Dir == ""`.** Today, after `FindRepo` returns a directory, `install` calls `knownCheckout(*repoFlag, home, repo)` (main.go:123, :420) and computes `own := harness.IsCheckout(repo)` (main.go:137) before deciding to rebuild via `go build` or install the running binary as-is. `IsCheckout(repo string)` (`internal/harness/repo.go:79`) does `os.Lstat(filepath.Join(repo, ".git"))` — called with `repo == ""` (the plan's sentinel for the embedded source, "Source" ¶, line 48) this resolves to `Lstat(".git")` relative to the process's *current working directory*, not "no checkout." Likewise `knownCheckout` reads `st.Repo` and calls `samePath(st.Repo, repo)` with the same empty-string ambiguity. The plan's "Source selection" and "Source" paragraphs describe which *readers* take a `Source`, but never say how this specific control-flow block — which decides "rebuild from source" vs "install running binary as-is" — treats an embedded source. The natural answer (treat it like `own=false`, "plain copy, install as-is," since embedded is exactly a running binary that already contains its own vendor data) is plausible but is not decided anywhere in the plan, and getting it wrong via the existing `IsCheckout("")` cwd-relative bug is a concrete latent defect, not a style question. Cite: plan §Interfaces "Source"/"Source selection" (lines 48–52), §Surfaces touched (line 33, 36); `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:117-158`, `internal/harness/repo.go:79-82,420-432`.

- **G3 (gap, high) — R8 restates the exact two-channel model the plan changes, but R8 is absent from Scope, Surfaces touched, and the R9 replacement text, and the plan does not decide what happens to it.** R8 ("One delivery channel, and it is `sh-agent`") reads: "a checkout the operator owns … or an unpacked bundle installed with `sh-agent install`. There is no other channel" (`REQUIREMENTS.md:35`). The plan's approved-pending R9 replacement Install bullet (plan line 43) drops the bundle wording entirely and describes only "clones … or downloads a release's `sh-agent` binary" — a genuinely different two-way split (checkout vs. release binary) than R8's (checkout vs. bundle), with the bundle's code path kept but undocumented (scope item 10, plan line 22: "The unpacked bundle leaves the docs and the map; its code path stays"). After this change, R8 and R9 describe two different, mutually inconsistent worlds unless R8 is also edited in the same commit — and REQUIREMENTS.md is immutable without explicit operator approval per project rule. Review-standards criterion 3 calls this out by name: "every other restatement of [a changed rule] is changed with it." Neither Scope, Surfaces touched, nor Phase 1/5 name an R8 edit or ask the operator to approve one. Cite: `REQUIREMENTS.md:33-35`; plan line 22, 26, 37, 41-46.

- **G4 (gap, medium) — the Source-selection fallback order does not say whether an explicitly-named but invalid `--repo`/`$SH_AGENT_REPO` still hard-errors, or falls through to the next candidate.** Today's `FindRepo` comment is explicit: "A path the operator named is used or refused, never silently replaced by one the walk finds" (`internal/harness/repo.go:14-18`), and the code returns an error immediately when `explicit`/env is set but `!IsRepo(named)` (repo.go:24-26). The plan's flat list — "`--repo` → `$SH_AGENT_REPO` → the working directory or a parent → the recorded repo when it is a directory → the embedded files" (line 50) — reads as one uniform fallthrough and does not say the first two candidates keep their hard-error-on-mismatch behaviour while the rest degrade gracefully. A typo'd `--repo` silently landing on embedded (possibly stale, per G1) instead of erroring is exactly the failure mode the original code was written to prevent.

- **G5 (gap, low, documentation clause missing on a command/flag change) — Phase 5's preflight task says "`skills/preflight/SKILL.md` Step 6 … cross-compile the three binaries, `SHA256SUMS`, `SHA256SUMS.sig`, `gh release create vX.Y.Z`" but does not name where in Step 6's existing six numbered sub-steps this lands, nor how `ssh-keygen -Y sign` for `SHA256SUMS.sig` is meant to run non-interactively inside an agent-run `/preflight` (today's Step 6.3 already signs the git tag with the operator's key on a machine holding it; the plan is silent on whether checksum-signing reuses that same already-unlocked-key moment or needs its own). This is exactly a "task changing a … deploy step with no docs clause spelling out the mechanics" case; the plan does name the doc file to edit (satisfying the letter of the "docs clause" checklist) but not the ordering/interaction, which a first-pass implementer restructuring Step 6 would have to guess at.

- Already self-flagged by the plan (noted here only for completeness, not double-counted as a gap): the "Open" line on `go install …@latest` before `v1.1.0` exists states its own default; D5 and the R9/D1 text are explicitly gated on operator approval in Phase 1 task 1.

### (2) Scope

Reviewed against `## Why` (single-binary download to avoid a `.agents/docs` trail beside projects; `report`'s full clone leaking every place's history to every other place). Nothing found that isn't traceable to a D-row or an operator-confirmed scope item:
- Three-platform cross-compile (D10) — operator scope item 5.
- Source selection extending to `status`/`diff`/`list`/`render`, not just `install` — necessary consequence (a binary-only place has no checkout, so these commands would otherwise always error), not an added shape.
- `version` command's version-string logic (D6) — implementer decision needed to make `status`/`update` work at all for a release binary, not a new feature.
- No extra endpoint, no second shape for the same operation, no configuration invented for a value that doesn't vary was found.

### (3) Readiness

Blocking questions (a first-pass implementer must ask, or two implementers diverge):
1. Does the embedded-source fallback apply to dev/untagged builds too, and if so is that acceptable, or must it be disabled for builds without an injected version (G1)?
2. How does the `install`/`sync` rebuild-vs-plain-copy branch (`own`, `knownCheckout`, `IsCheckout`) treat `Source{Dir:""}` — is it forced down the "plain copy, install as-is" path, and is `IsCheckout`/`knownCheckout`/`samePath`'s `repo string` signature changed to avoid the empty-string/cwd ambiguity (G2)?
3. Does R8 get edited in the same commit as R9, and has the operator approved that text too (G3)? Today's R8 and the plan's proposed R9 describe different channel models.
4. Does an explicit but wrong `--repo`/`$SH_AGENT_REPO` still hard-error, or now silently fall through toward embedded (G4)?

Non-blocking (reasonable default available, or ordinary implementer discretion):
- Exact placement of the binary-attach step inside preflight Step 6, and whether checksum-signing shares the tag-signing key moment (G5) — a competent implementer picks the obvious slot (after tag push, before/alongside "Deploy via the project's deploy guide") and documents it.
- Whether the compiled-in allowed-signer line is a `const` or a package `var` overridable by white-box tests for the fake-`gh` integration tests — ordinary Go test-design discretion.
- `go install …@latest` before `v1.1.0` — plan already states its own default.

### Verified against source (not just recon)

- `TestHarnessMap` **does exist** (`cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go:987`), contrary to the recon brief's claim that it doesn't (`2026-09-17-recon-release-binary.md` line 98, "second pass" findings) — recon is stale/wrong on this point but the plan's own citation (line 36, dispatch's line-987 pointer) is correct, so this did not propagate into a plan defect. Flagged only so an implementer reading the recon brief instead of the plan doesn't chase a nonexistent problem.
- 15 `.gitkeep` files confirmed on disk (`find … -name .gitkeep | wc -l` → 15), matching the plan's Verification bullet (line 89) exactly — recon's "13" was wrong, plan's own number is right.
- `report` command already bypasses `FindRepo` today with a comment anticipating exactly this problem (`cmd/sh-agent/main.go:106-109`) — consistent with the plan's design, no issue.
- `REQUIREMENTS.md` R4/R8/R9 read in full; R8 and R9 both carry "(Approved by the operator 2026-09-17 …)" — same day as this plan, both existing texts, R9's *replacement* still pending approval per Phase 1.

## Not examined

- `internal/harness/report.go`/`report_test.go` bodies (`ResolveFeedback`, `verifyFeedback`, `commitAndPush`, the four pinned tests) — read only via the recon brief's summary, not the source directly; the throwaway-clone rewrite's interaction with existing test assertions is taken on the recon's word.
- `internal/harness/state.go`, `apply.go`, `frontmatter.go`, `derive.go`, `adopt.go` — not read; `adopt`'s "requires a checkout and says so" (plan line 50) not verified against `adopt.go`'s actual error paths.
- `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` § Releases full text (only grepped, not read in full) and § The four places — not verified against the plan's D-rows in detail.
- `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` and `main_test.go`'s fixtures beyond `TestHarnessMap` — not read.
- ADR-030/ADR-031/ADR-029 full texts — not read; only their conclusions as summarized in REQUIREMENTS.md/AGENTS.md.
- `internal/harness/harness_test.go` — not opened.

design needs revision (G1, G2, G3, G4 are gaps the plan does not decide)

implementation not ready — 4 BLOCKING questions listed above (G1–G4)

## Round 2

Fresh read of the plan (2026-09-17-release-binary.md, current version with D1–D16) before reading Round 1 again.

### My own read (before re-reading Round 1)

#### (1) Gaps

- **G6 (BLOCKING, high) — `status` and `update` are not re-specified for `Source{Dir:""}` the way `install` was (D13 covers install only).** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` calls `harness.FindRepo` once, shared by `install`, `status`, `diff`, `update`, `list`, `render` (main.go: the single `repo, err := harness.FindRepo(...)` before the `switch cmd`). D14/D15 make `FindRepo` (or its `Source`-returning successor) hand back the embedded source instead of erroring for a release binary with no tree — but two existing functions built on the old two-state world ("real checkout" or "plain copy, git refused") are never revisited:
  - `status(repo, home, vendorFlag, out)` (main.go:262) calls `harness.Inspect(repo)` unconditionally and, when `info.Commit == ""` (true for both a plain copy *and* an embedded source), prints `"repo %s (plain copy, not its own git checkout; update is refused)\n"` (main.go:272). For an embedded install this is doubly wrong: the repo field is empty/`""` so the line reads `repo        (plain copy...)`, and it says *"update is refused"* — directly contradicting the plan's own Update interface bullet (line 44) and its E2E criterion (line 98, `sh-agent update` on the embedded place prints `up to date (v1.1.0)`, i.e. update plainly works there). The plan's only status-side change (line 56, `"source embedded vX.Y.Z"`) adds a line but never says the old plain-copy line is suppressed or reworded for this case.
  - `update(repo, home, checkOnly, ...)` (main.go:364) is pure git: `harness.Behind(repo)`, `harness.Inspect(repo)`, `harness.Pull(repo, out)`, `harness.Reinstall(repo, args, out)`. None of these are meant to run for a binary-only place — the plan's new release-download flow (lines 60–64) is a wholly separate procedure — but nothing in `cmd/sh-agent/main.go`'s dispatch (`case "update":`, main.go ~"if err := knownCheckout(...); return update(repo, home, ...)") is named as the branch point that sends an embedded/binary-only place to the new flow instead of into this function. Falling through unchanged, `harness.Behind("")` → `IsCheckout("")` → `Lstat(".git")` relative to the process's cwd — the exact ambiguity round 1's G2 flagged for `install`, reproduced here for `update` because D13's fix text says "Binary handling **on install**" only.
  - The "Source selection" paragraph itself (line 52) lists the commands it governs as "`install`, `status`, `diff`, `list`, `render`" — **`update` is not in that list**, even though `update` is exactly the command that most needs to know "checkout vs. embedded" to decide which of two completely different procedures to run. Either the list is an oversight or `update`'s branch is decided by some other unstated mechanism.
  Cite: plan lines 44, 52, 56, 60–64, 98; `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:262-275` (`status`), `:364-408` (`update`), `:117-119` (shared `FindRepo` call).

- **G7 (gap, medium) — the plan never states `FindRepo`'s new return type**, only the ordered list of candidates ("Source selection", line 52) and the `Source{FS, Dir}` shape ("Source" ¶, line 50). `internal/harness/repo.go:20` today is `func FindRepo(explicit, home string) (string, error)`. Surfaces touched (line 34) lists `repo.go: FindRepo, IsCheckout, Inspect, Reinstall` as touched but not what `FindRepo` returns afterward (a `Source`? a `(string, bool, error)` triple where the bool means "embedded"?) or whether `IsCheckout`/`Inspect`/`Reinstall`/`Behind`/`Pull` keep taking `repo string` (untouched for the checkout path) while a new, separate embedded branch in `main.go` short-circuits around all of them. This is the same class of gap as round 1's G2, generalized: G2 asked "how does the install rebuild-vs-copy branch treat `Dir==""`", D13 answered it for install specifically, but the underlying question — "what type does the plumbing between `FindRepo` and every caller carry now, and which existing `repo string` functions must never see `Dir==""`" — is still open for the other five(six) call sites.

#### (2) Scope

Nothing found beyond what a D-row or the operator's own scope list traces to; same conclusion as Round 1 (three-platform cross-compile → D10/scope 5; source selection spanning multiple commands is a necessary consequence, not an added shape; `version` logic → D6, needed for `status`/`update` to function at all).

#### (3) Readiness

Blocking (in addition to whatever Round 1 still has open):
1. G6 — what does `status` print for an embedded install in place of "(plain copy...; update is refused)", and what does `update`'s dispatch in `main.go` look like for `Source.Dir==""` — a new `if` before calling the existing git-based `update()`, or does `update()` itself grow a branch? Two implementers asked to "make update work for a binary-only place" independently will not produce the same `status`/`update` code without this decided.
2. G7 — `FindRepo`'s post-change signature/return shape, and confirmation that `IsCheckout`, `Inspect`, `Behind`, `Pull` are never called with an empty/embedded `Dir` from any of the five-or-six command paths, not just `install`.

Non-blocking: none new beyond Round 1's own non-blocking list (G5-equivalent, defaults stated).

design needs revision — G6, G7 are undecided
implementation not ready — 2 new BLOCKING questions (G6, G7), on top of Round 1's set until verified below

---

### Comparing against Round 1's four blocking items

Read Round 1's report after forming the above. Round 1's four blocking items map to the plan's D13–D16:

1. **G2 (install rebuild-vs-copy branch, `IsCheckout("")` ambiguity) — RESOLVED.** D13 and the new "Binary handling on install" paragraph (plan line 54) directly answer it: embedded → copy, never rebuild, `IsCheckout` never called with `""`.
2. **G1 (embedded fallback scope — dev builds vs release only) — RESOLVED.** D14 and "Source selection" (line 52) now gate the embedded fallback to a release binary carrying a `vX.Y.Z` version; a dev build with no tree found keeps today's hard error.
3. **G3 (R8 restates the two-channel model R9 changes, left unedited) — RESOLVED at the design level, pending execution.** The plan now carries a proposed exact R8 replacement (line 48) and a dedicated Phase 1 task ("Operator approves the R8 sentence," line 106, currently unchecked). Not yet approved, but no longer an undecided gap — it is a tracked, gated step.
4. **G4 (explicit but wrong `--repo`/`$SH_AGENT_REPO` — hard error or fall-through?) — RESOLVED.** D15 and "Source selection" (line 52, "never a fall-through (D15)") restore today's hard-error behaviour explicitly.

All four of Round 1's blocking items are resolved in this revision. However, the fix for items 1–2 (the `install`-specific "Binary handling" and "Source selection" paragraphs) was scoped narrowly to `install`, and in closing that gap the plan left the structurally identical problem open for `status` and `update` (G6/G7 above) — the same class of defect, one command over.

### Not examined (Round 2)

- `internal/harness/plan.go`, `inventory.go`, `render.go`, `frontmatter.go`, `derive.go`, `apply.go`, `state.go` bodies — not read; only signatures grepped. The claim that these five/six readers "move from `repo string` to a `Source`" cleanly (plan line 33) is taken on the plan's word, not verified line-by-line against e.g. `checkManagedTree(repo string)` (inventory.go:106) or `frontmatter.go`'s file-reading calls.
- `internal/harness/report.go`, `report_test.go` — not read in this round; Round 1 already flagged this as unexamined and it remains so here.
- `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` § Releases, § The four places — not read in full.
- `skills/preflight/SKILL.md` Step 6 — not read; G5 from Round 1 (preflight step ordering/signing-key-moment) not independently re-checked.
- `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go`, `main_test.go` fixtures — not read beyond what Round 1 already checked (`TestHarnessMap` existence).
- ADR-029/030/031, `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md` — not read.

## Round 3

Fresh read of the plan (2026-09-17-release-binary.md, current version with D1–D17, Phase 1 tasks 1–2 checked) plus `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `internal/harness/{repo,plan,inventory,render,state,report}.go`, `cmd/sh-agent/main.go`, `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` § Releases, `DECISIONS.md` ADR-030/ADR-031 — before re-reading Rounds 1–2.

### My own read (before re-reading Rounds 1–2)

#### (1) Gaps

- **G8 (BLOCKING, high) — the plan's own R9 replacement makes a released tag deliver binaries to binary-only places, but two other restatements of "a tag delivers nothing / every place follows `main`" are left unedited and unnamed.** `AGENTS.md` § How the harness works rule 2 (`AGENTS.md:13`): *"A tag delivers nothing. `/preflight vX.Y.Z` makes a signed release marker; every place follows `main`."* `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` § Releases, first sentence: *"It is a MARKER naming a version, not a way the harness reaches a machine: every place follows `main` with `sh-agent update`, and a tag changes nothing for any of them (ADR-030 D2, withdrawing ADR-026's tag channel)."* `DECISIONS.md` ADR-031 D3 lists "a tag delivers nothing" as one of AGENTS.md's five strict rules. All three are contradicted by the plan's own proposed R9 Release bullet (plan Interfaces: *"publishes that tag's binaries with checksums signed by the same key. Checkout places follow `main`; binary-only places update to the newest release."*) — for a binary-only place the tag is now exactly how the harness reaches the machine; it is no longer true that "a tag changes nothing for any of them." Surfaces touched names only `AGENTS.md` § How the harness works **rule 1** and `remote.md` § Releases (for the cross-compile/signing mechanics), never rule 2's sentence, never ADR-031 (amend or supersede?), never `remote.md`'s opening sentence. Review-standards criterion 3 ("every other restatement of a changed rule is changed with it — grep its subject nouns") and the global context's describing-text rule both name this exact failure mode. Cite: `AGENTS.md:13`; `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` § Releases opening line; `DECISIONS.md` ADR-031 (D3); plan § Interfaces "Release" bullet, § Surfaces touched.
- This is a design-level gap, not an implementation one: it needs a decision (does rule 2 change to something like "a tag delivers a release; a checkout follows `main`, a binary-only place downloads its assets", is ADR-031 amended or superseded by ADR-033, does `remote.md`'s opening sentence get reworded) before Phase 5's docs task can be executed without a second round of doc drift.

- **G9 (gap, low, mostly resolved but one prose omission survives from Round 2's G7) — the "Source selection" paragraph's command list still omits `update`.** Interfaces § "Source selection" reads: *"Source selection (`install`, `status`, `diff`, `list`, `render`): …"* — `update` is not named, exactly as Round 2 flagged for the old `FindRepo`. Functionally this is now covered: the "Per command with an embedded source" table explicitly gives `update`'s behaviour for `src.Dir == ""` (the release flow), so an implementer reading the whole Interfaces section will not miss it. Flagged only because the prose list itself still reads as if `update` takes a different path than `ResolveSource`, which is not true per the table — a wording gap, not a design gap. Non-blocking: the table resolves it.

#### (2) Scope

Checked against `## Why` (a single downloadable binary so a session doesn't inherit `.agents/docs`; `report` no longer mirrors every place's history to every other place). Everything in Scope and the Phase list traces to a D-row or a quoted operator scope item (three platforms → D10/scope 5; throwaway clone → D8/"throwaway clone for 12"; old-clone cleanup → D9/scope 12; the embedded-source reach into `status`/`diff`/`list`/`render`/`adopt` → a necessary consequence of a binary-only place having no checkout, not an added shape). No extra endpoint, no second shape for the same operation, no configuration invented for a value that never varies. Same conclusion as Rounds 1–2: nothing found.

#### (3) Readiness

Blocking:
1. G8 — is `AGENTS.md` rule 2, `remote.md` § Releases' opening sentence, and ADR-031 D3 edited/amended in the same R9 commit, and with what exact replacement text? Two implementers will otherwise ship code where a binary-only place's `update` downloads a release's binary while the project's own strict rules still say, in three places, that a tag delivers nothing.

Non-blocking:
- G9 — `update`'s omission from the "Source selection" prose list; the per-command table already answers it, so an implementer who reads the whole section is not stuck.
- Carried from Round 1 (still non-blocking, unchanged): exact insertion point for checksum-signing inside preflight Step 6 (G5) — a competent implementer places it right after tag verification, reusing the already-unlocked signing key, and documents it.

### Comparing against Rounds 1–2's blocking items

1. **G1 (embedded fallback scope, dev vs release builds) — RESOLVED.** D14 and "Source selection" gate the embedded fallback to a release binary whose version matches `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+$`; a dev build with no tree keeps today's hard error.
2. **G2 (install rebuild-vs-copy branch, `IsCheckout("")` ambiguity) — RESOLVED.** D13 and "Binary handling on install" directly answer it: embedded → copy, never rebuild, `IsCheckout` never called with an empty path.
3. **G3 (R8 restates the channel model R9 changes, left unedited) — RESOLVED at the design level.** The plan carries a proposed exact R8 replacement and a Phase 1 approval task, now checked `[x]` with the operator's quoted approval.
4. **G4 (explicit but wrong `--repo`/`$SH_AGENT_REPO` — hard error or fall-through) — RESOLVED.** D15 and "Source selection" ("never a fall-through (D15)") keep today's hard-error behaviour.
5. **G5 (preflight Step 6 insertion point / signing-key moment) — still open, still non-blocking**, as in Round 1: a reasonable default is available and stated by the reviewer, not the plan, but it was never blocking.
6. **G6 (`status`/`update` not re-specified for `Source{Dir:""}`) — RESOLVED.** The "Per command with an embedded source" table now gives `status`'s replacement line and `update`'s branch to the release flow explicitly.
7. **G7 (`FindRepo`'s post-change return type/signature undefined) — RESOLVED.** `ResolveSource(explicit, home, version string) (Source, error)` is now the stated signature, with git helpers "called only with `src.Dir != \"\"`" and "with an embedded source none is called (D17)".

All seven of Rounds 1–2's blocking items are resolved in this revision. Round 3 finds one new blocking item (G8), one class apart from G1–G7: those were all about the *code* not deciding what an embedded source does; G8 is about the *project's own rule text* (`AGENTS.md`, `remote.md`, ADR-031) asserting something the plan's own design now makes false, in places the plan's Surfaces-touched list does not name.

### Not examined (Round 3)

- `internal/harness/frontmatter.go`, `derive.go`, `apply.go` bodies — not read; only referenced from `plan.go`/`inventory.go`. The claim that all readers "move from `repo string` to a `Source`" cleanly is still not verified line-by-line against these three files (carried forward from Round 2).
- `internal/harness/report.go` was read this round (lines 1–400: redaction, `Collect`, `Record`, `BuildRecord`, `ResolveFeedback` through its start); `commitAndPush`, `verifyFeedback`, and the four clone-pinning tests in `report_test.go` were not read in full — only their names were grepped.
- `internal/harness/main_test.go`/`cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` bodies beyond earlier rounds' `TestHarnessMap` check — not read.
- `skills/preflight/SKILL.md` Step 6 full text — not read (G5 carried forward unverified independently, as in prior rounds).
- `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md`, `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md`, ADR-029/ADR-033(draft doesn't exist yet) — not read.
- `internal/harness/adopt.go` read only its first ~40 lines; confirms it takes a disk `repo string` throughout what was read, consistent with "adopt requires a checkout," but the full file was not read.

design needs revision (G8 is a gap the plan does not decide; G1–G7 from Rounds 1–2 are resolved)

implementation not ready — 1 BLOCKING question (G8)

title: Release gate — v1.1.0 (2026-09-17)
body:
# Release gate — v1.1.0     (2026-09-17)

Range reviewed: v1.0.0..f129aa7

## VERDICT: SHIP

No blocking finding. Nothing in this release is high severity, no reviewer returned REQUEST CHANGES, the verification row passes at the commit being released, no `REQUIREMENTS.md` violation stands, and no project agent shadows a harness review agent (`.agents/agents/` and `.claude/agents/` hold none — checked before any dispatch, BUG-033).

Thirteen findings were raised across five dispatches. All thirteen are FIXED — none was carried into the release as accepted risk — and each fix has a test that fails without it, or, for the three in documentation, a correction read against the code.

## What this release is

The harness can now be installed from one downloaded binary with `context/`, `skills/`, `agents/`, `commands/` and `rules/` built into it, and `sh-agent update` at such a place moves it forward from a signed GitHub release. `sh-agent report` no longer keeps a clone of the private feedback repository on any machine. `sh-agent report` itself is also new since v1.0.0. MINOR, not MAJOR: every v1.0.0 install keeps working, `state.json`'s shape is unchanged, and no flag was removed — an existing place gains behaviour and is required to react to nothing.

## Rows

| Row | Verdict | Artifact |
|---|---|---|
| Verification, release range | PASS — 99 top-level + 85 subtests, 0 fail, 0 skip; `govulncheck` clean; embedded install byte-identical to the checkout install | `testing/2026-09-17-verify-preflight-v1.1.0.md` (v1.0.0..086deab) |
| Verification, after the gate's own fixes | PASS — 101 + 85, 0 fail, 0 skip, reproducing the main agent's count exactly | `testing/2026-09-17-verify-preflight-v1.1.0-fixes.md` (v1.0.0..6ef7434) |
| Code review, release range | APPROVE WITH NITS — 0 high, 0 medium, 5 low | `reviews/2026-09-17-review-preflight-v1.1.0-code.md` |
| Code review, round 2 over the fixes | APPROVE WITH NITS — 0 high, 0 medium, 3 low | `reviews/2026-09-17-review-086deab-6ef7434-code.md` |
| Security, release range | FINDINGS — 2 low, both in the release procedure, none in the code | `reviews/2026-09-17-security-preflight-v1.1.0.md` |
| Docs lens (advisory) | APPROVE — 0 findings | `reviews/2026-09-17-review-preflight-v1.1.0-docs.md` |
| Release rehearsal | every check passed | § Rehearsal below |

Earlier phase coverage cited rather than repeated, each with its own `## Outcome`: `reviews/2026-09-17-review-f7ee817-21ba8dc-code.md`, `-security-f7ee817-21ba8dc.md`, `-security-73f2c36-83f3cf6.md`, `-security-dab2565-4d45155.md`, `-review-edbddca-1a5578b-docs.md`, `-review-6af54f7-015cf2d-code.md`, `-security-6af54f7-015cf2d.md`, `-security-015cf2d-012b4ca.md`. Two dispatches verified independently, rather than taking it from the dispatch, that `24d08a8^{tree}` and `cd0bbcb^{tree}` are the same tree (`da8d57d5`) — so those phase reviews describe exactly what ships — and that no `*.go` file changed between the merge and the gate.

## Findings, worst first

All fixed. Severity and confidence as the reporting dispatch gave them.

1. **[medium/high] no downgrade protection, and the version was not inside the signed bytes** (Phase 4 security). `tag == version` was an equality test and `SHA256SUMS` named only files and hashes, so a genuinely signed OLDER release installed and verified honestly, and one release's signed checksums verified under another release's tag. Fixed: the tag must parse as `vX.Y.Z` before it reaches argv, must be numerically newer, and `SHA256SUMS` must carry `# styrman-harness vX.Y.Z` matching the tag (D26, D27). This is why the release procedure below writes that line — a release cut the old way is correctly uninstallable.
2. **[medium/high] `RemoveKeptClone`'s guard failed open** (Phase 3 security). When it could not count unpushed work — a branch with no upstream — it deleted the clone holding the operator's only copy. Fixed to count over all refs and keep the clone whenever the count cannot be taken; a stash, ignored files and a symlink now keep it too (BUG-069).
3. **[medium/high] `update --check` deleted files** (Phase 3 security). The read-only mode removed the kept clone because the cleanup sat above its returns. Fixed and pinned in both directions (BUG-070).
4. **[medium/high] `go:embed` shipped untracked files** (Phase 2 security). An ignored `rules/.env` was compiled into a build while every other test stayed green, because nothing read the artifact in the other direction. Fixed by pinning the embedded set to `git ls-files`, and by the release guard below (BUG-066, D23).
5. **[low] `report --dry-run` looped forever** on an unreadable `reports/<host>`, treating "cannot read" as "name taken". Fixed; the test hangs without the fix.
