title: Review — harness-code (audit phase, sh-agent-works-everywhere Phase 2) (2026-09-18)
body:
# Review — harness-code (audit phase, sh-agent-works-everywhere Phase 2)   (2026-09-18)

Range reviewed: `internal/harness` and `cmd/sh-agent`, all non-test `.go` files, read whole in the working tree (not a diff), per `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-18-sh-agent-works-everywhere.md` Phase 2. Files read: `internal/harness/{apply,plan,repo,source,release,state,inventory,pathguard,frontmatter,adopt,derive,render,report}.go` and `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` — all 14 non-test `.go` files in scope (≈4,240 lines). No `*_test.go` file read in full (spot-checked with `grep` only, see Not examined).

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

The code is unusually careful — nearly every non-obvious decision carries a dated review comment explaining a prior failure mode it closes. I found no correctness or security defect that reaches a silent no-op or a false success. I found two places where the operator's own stated rule for this audit — "refuses with a message naming the cause **and the alternative**" — is only half met: `update` on a plain copy gives the cause with no next step, and `adopt` on a plain copy succeeds but tells the operator to do something (commit and push) that the place cannot do. Neither is a silent failure; both are message-quality gaps the audit was explicitly commissioned to find.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:461` (`update`) + `internal/harness/repo.go:118-119,153` — `update` on a plain copy (a tree with no `.git`) surfaces the bare `errPlainCopy`: `"sh-agent: not its own git checkout; a plain copy cannot be updated with git"`. This names the cause but not the alternative, unlike every other refusal in this codebase (compare `ResolveSource`'s release-binary refusal, which says "unset it, or build sh-agent from that tree"; `Pull`'s dirty-tree refusal, which says "commit or stash them"). The plan's own Failure-modes rule for this audit is explicit: "refuses with a message naming the cause and the alternative (the BUG-076 rule)". `status` on the same place kind (`main.go:351`) is a little better — "plain copy, not its own git checkout; update is refused" — but still names no alternative (re-clone as a real checkout, or move to a release binary and use `sh-agent update` there). Fix: wrap the error at the `update()` call site (or in `Behind`/`Pull`) with the alternative, the way every sibling refusal in this file does. No CLI-level test exercises this path today (confirmed by grep — only `Behind`/`Pull` unit tests hit `errPlainCopy`; `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` has no plain-copy `update` case), which is also flagged, independently, as a Phase 2 test-gap item in the plan itself.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:245-257` (`adopt` case) — `adopt` does not check whether `repo` is a git checkout before running. On a plain copy (no `.git`) it succeeds and unconditionally prints `"next: review it, run \`sh-agent install\`, then commit and push the repo"` — an instruction the operator cannot follow, because there is no git repository to commit or push in a plain copy. This is the "a wrong message ... is a finding" case the dispatch names: a reported success carries a next step that does not apply to the place kind it ran on. Compare the release-binary path, which correctly refuses adopt outright (`main.go:249-251`, "adopt needs a harness checkout; this install is a release binary") — the plain-copy path has files to adopt into but no git to finish the workflow, and nothing in `Adopt` or its caller says so. Fix: gate the "commit and push" sentence on `harness.IsCheckout(repo)`, or refuse adopt on a plain copy the same way it is refused on a release binary.

- **[note, not a finding / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/source.go:44-51` — `IsReleaseVersion`'s regex `^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$` accepts non-canonical spellings such as `v1.02.2` or `v01.2.2` (leading zeros). This is not exploitable as a downgrade or confusion vector today — `compareRelease`/`releaseParts` uses `strconv.Atoi`, which parses `"02"` as decimal `2`, and the tag string itself is only ever compared for exact-equality against the signed `SHA256SUMS` marker (`release.go:282`), never used as a numeric identity elsewhere. Flagging only because the plan's own Phase 2 checklist already names this exact gap ("`IsReleaseVersion` rejects a non-canonical spelling") as unchecked/pending — this review confirms the current regex still admits it, so the pending item is real and not stale.

## Criteria

1. **Dead code** — pass. No unused exported function, type, or leftover debug output found across the 14 files; every helper (`gitOutC`, `firstLineOfError`, `hostDir`, etc.) has a live caller.
2. **Flow tracing** — pass with the two findings above. Traced `Install`/`Status`/`Diff`/`Uninstall` (apply.go) against `Plan` (plan.go) and `main.go`'s dispatch for every verb × place-kind combination named in the dispatch (checkout / release binary / plain copy). Error paths are wrapped with context almost everywhere (`fmt.Errorf(...: %w, err)`); the two exceptions above are the only bare/under-specified propagations found. `writeAtomic` (apply.go) and the settings-file write (main.go) both sync-then-rename correctly, so a crash mid-write cannot leave a truncated file. Resource lifetimes (temp files, cloned dirs) are closed/removed on every path I traced, including `defer os.RemoveAll` in `cloneThrowaway`/`Reinstall`/`Adopt`'s staging.
3. **Standards conformance** — pass. Go idioms observed throughout: context-wrapped errors, no naked panics, `context` not needed here (no long-running I/O beyond `exec.Command`, which is bounded by the OS). Comments describing security-relevant behavior (secret redaction, symlink refusals, signature verification) are consistent with the code they sit beside — no stale doc-comment found.
4. **Directory layout** — pass. `cmd/sh-agent/` holds only the entrypoint; `internal/harness/` holds all private logic; no stray files.
5. **Simplicity / DIY-except-security** — pass. Release verification uses `ssh-keygen -Y verify` (a vetted external tool, not a hand-rolled signature check) and `crypto/sha256` as designed — both conform to the security exemption. No hand-rolled auth, crypto, or session logic anywhere in scope. Stdlib-only throughout (`go.mod` per `AGENTS.md` carries no dependency), consistent with the project's stated constraint.
6. **Decoupling** — pass. Clean seams: `harness` package owns all filesystem/git/release logic; `main.go` is thin wiring plus two operator-facing pieces of state (`--home`/`--vendor` resolution, `attribution*` for Claude's settings.json) that arguably could live in `internal/harness` but are small and self-contained — not a finding, no second caller exists to justify moving them.

## Not examined

- Test files (`*_test.go`) in both directories were not read in full — only grepped for specific coverage questions (plain-copy `update`, `Adopt` scenarios). The dispatch scoped this review to the non-test `.go` files; test-coverage completeness is Phase 2's separate verifier-mapping task.
- Did not run `go build`/`go vet`/`go test` — this review is a static read, per the hard limits (no network, no `--home` outside `.agents/scratch/`, no tree-changing git commands); I did not invoke any Go tooling since it was not requested and risked no scope violation either way, but no build/vet/test confirmation is claimed here.
- The recon matrix `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-18-recon-sh-agent-audit.md` was named as background by the dispatch and not independently re-verified line-by-line against the source; this review's findings were derived from reading the source itself, not from trusting the recon's claims.
- `linux/arm64` and darwin-specific code paths: none exist in the reviewed files (no `//go:build` tags in scope), so nothing was skipped there — noted for completeness only.

title: Review — harness-docs (2026-09-18)
body:
# Review — harness-docs (2026-09-18)

Range reviewed: `internal/harness` and `cmd/sh-agent`, read whole as they stand in the working tree (docs lens — not a diff), compared against `README.md`, `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md`, `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md`, `.agents/docs/deploy/{local,remote}.md`, and the newest `.agents/docs/changes/` entry (`2026-09-18-install-names-every-change.md`).

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

The docs are unusually well kept — almost every command, flag, and refusal message I checked in `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` and `internal/harness/*.go` is quoted or paraphrased accurately in README § Daily commands, the deploy guides, and the delivery spec, including recent additions (the per-file `add`/`update`/`mode`/`remove` lines, the BUG-078/079 shadow and stale-binary notes, the release verification chain). Two gaps are real, both narrow: `install`'s `keep`/`kept` output for a foreign `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` is undocumented, and README's "so `sh-agent update` works from anywhere" overstates what the checkout-discovery fallback actually does — it can refuse.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/apply.go:35` and `:143` (the `keep    ~/%s (not written by sh-agent; …)` line and the `%d kept` count in `Install`'s summary line) — no living doc names either. README.md:162 (install row of § Daily commands) documents the per-run output as `add` / `update` / `mode` / `remove` plus "counts the unchanged," and `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md:43` repeats the same four-category description ("added, updated …, corrected the mode of, or removed, with the unchanged as a count"). Neither mentions the fifth category: when an unmanaged `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` exists and differs from the harness stub, every install run prints a `keep` line for it and folds it into a separate `kept` count in the summary (`%d written, %d unchanged, %d removed, %d kept — %d files managed`). A reader following the docs and then running `sh-agent install` sees an unexplained line and count. Fix: add `keep` to the README/delivery.md description, or point at the existing "existing ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md … is left alone" paragraph (README.md:196) and note that install now also prints and counts it per run.

- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:546` (`knownCheckout`) — install and update refuse to build from a checkout that was only found by walking up from the working directory (or from the manifest's recorded path) when a *different* checkout is already the one on record; the two refusal messages ("this home was installed from the release binary …, not from a checkout …" and "checkout … is not the installed one (…); pass --repo … to build and install from it") appear nowhere in a living doc. README.md:171 and `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:77` both describe the discovery order ("finds the checkout from `--repo`, then `$SH_AGENT_REPO`, then the working directory or any of its parents, then the path recorded at the last install") and README specifically concludes "so `sh-agent update` works from anywhere" — which is true only when the discovered checkout matches the installed manifest's recorded repo, or `--repo`/`$SH_AGENT_REPO` is set explicitly. On a second-or-later install/update run from an unregistered checkout-shaped directory (an unpacked copy under review, a second clone) the command refuses instead of "working," and no doc says so. Fix: add one line to README § Daily commands (or `remote.md` § First install) naming the refusal and its two messages.

- **[low / confidence: low, unverified]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:301-303` — `report` on a release binary prints `report: --repo is not used here; this release binary reports the harness built into it` when `--repo` is passed; not documented in README's `report` row or `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md` § Report back. Narrow edge case (passing `--repo` to `report` specifically on a release-binary install); I did not check whether this is deliberately left out as too minor to document elsewhere.

## Criteria

Docs lens: criteria 1-6 are the language/code-quality lens and do not apply to this dispatch.

1. Dead code — n/a — docs lens
2. Flow tracing — n/a — docs lens
3. Standards conformance — n/a — docs lens
4. Directory layout — n/a — docs lens
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — n/a — docs lens
6. Decoupling — n/a — docs lens

## Not examined

- `internal/harness/adopt.go`, `frontmatter.go`, `derive.go`, `state.go`, `source.go`, `pathguard.go` (beyond `NoteRunningElsewhere`/`PathShadows`), `report.go`'s full redaction-shape list, and `release.go`'s edge-case messages (`"this binary reports version %q, which is not a release; leaving it alone"`, the stale `release-*` cleanup note) were not individually diffed against every doc line — spot-checked only via grep for their exact wording; I did not find contradictions but did not exhaustively re-read each doc paragraph against each message.
- `README.md` sections beyond § Daily commands, § Install, § Install without cloning, § The loop, and § What gets installed where were not read in full (e.g. § Adding things by hand's full table, anything past line ~220).
- `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` beyond line ~120 (the rest of § Releases, any sections after it) was not read.
- `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md` was read in full and cross-checked against `apply.go`'s dry-run/rebuild messages; no discrepancy found there.
- I did not run any command (per hard limits: no network, no real-`$HOME` install, no `sh-agent report`), so all comparisons are static text-vs-text, not observed output.

title: Review — harness, every lens (2026-09-18)
body:
# Review — harness, every lens     (2026-09-18)

Range reviewed: the named files as they are in the working tree, read whole — not a diff: internal/harness cmd/sh-agent. Tree at 160aa16 (Phase 1 of `plans/2026-09-18-sh-agent-works-everywhere.md` closed). The audit phase of that plan, run as `/review internal/harness cmd/sh-agent --all`: five agents, one per lens, each given the scope text and its brief, reading the same frozen tree. The explorer's matrix (`plans/2026-09-18-recon-sh-agent-audit.md`) is background: no silent cell across ten verbs × three place kinds; four coverage gaps.

## Verdicts

| Lens | Agent | Verdict | Artifact |
|---|---|---|---|
| code | `reviewer` | APPROVE WITH NITS — 1 medium, 1 low | `reviews/2026-09-18-review-harness-code.md` |
| security | `security` (opus) | FINDINGS — 1 medium, 7 low (one low/low) | `reviews/2026-09-18-security-harness.md` |
| simplify | `reviewer` | APPROVE WITH NITS — 1 medium, 3 low | `reviews/2026-09-18-review-harness-simplify.md` |
| docs | `reviewer` | APPROVE WITH NITS — 2 medium, 1 low | `reviews/2026-09-18-review-harness-docs.md` |
| tests | `verifier` | PASS — 2 coverage gaps; 77.1% / 86.9% | `testing/2026-09-18-verify-harness.md` |

No high anywhere. No FAIL. The release verification chain — signature, namespace, in-band version marker, hash over the exact bytes written — was read end to end and found sound (security).

## Findings, worst first

Each carries the lens, severity, confidence, and the disposition the fix round takes; `## Outcome` below records what happened.

1. **[security, medium/high]** `internal/harness/adopt.go:168` `copyTree` keeps group/other write bits (`Perm()|0o600`) where `plan.go:138` strips them (`&0o755|0o600`): an adopted third-party skill lands group-writable in the tree every install ships; git records only the x bit. → **fix**: plan.go's expression; test.
2. **[code, medium/high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:461`, `repo.go:118-119,153` — `update` on a plain copy surfaces `errPlainCopy` with no alternative named, unlike every sibling refusal (the BUG-076 rule). No CLI-level test. → **fix**: name the alternative (a checkout or a release binary; `install` still deploys it as it is); CLI test (recon gap 1).
3. **[docs, medium/high]** `apply.go:35,143` — the `keep` line and the `kept` count are undocumented; README `install` row and `delivery.md` list add/update/mode/remove only. → **fix** (`documentation`).
4. **[docs, medium/medium]** `main.go:546` `knownCheckout` refuses an install/update from a checkout found by walking up from cwd when a different one is on record — undocumented, and README's "works from anywhere" reads as a contradiction. → **fix** (`documentation`): describe the refusal and qualify the claim.
5. **[simplify, medium/medium]** `main.go:676-895` — a ~220-line `settings.json` editor lives in the entrypoint, not `internal/harness`. → **left** (main agent): a move with no behaviour change, during an audit whose purpose is behaviour; a Follow-up of the plan.
6. **[security, low/high]** `release.go:106,116` — `v1.02.2`, `v01.2.2`, `v1.2.02` pass `IsReleaseVersion`, compare equal, reach the download (the signed marker stops substitution); `releaseParts` reads an overflowing component as `v0.0.0`. → **fix**: canonical spelling only, `compareRelease <= 0` refuses, overflow is an error; tests for all four (Phase 2 box).
7. **[security, low/high]** `pathguard.go:112-121` — the BUG-079 note is `--home`-blind: run with `--home <scratch>` it calls the scratch home's binary "the installed binary" and may send the reader to relink their real one at it; and `ln -sfn` is offered before ownership is known. → **fix**: the note prints only for the default home; "remove it" alone when `from` is not the caller's; tests (Phase 2 box).
8. **[code, low/high]** `main.go:245-257` — `adopt` on a plain copy prints "commit and push the repo" with no `.git` present. → **fix**: the message depends on `IsCheckout`; test.
9. **[recon/tests]** `adopt` on a release binary refuses without naming the alternative; `status` on a plain copy's "update is refused" line untested; `sync` never invoked by name; `Diff`'s body 0% (the one `diff` test has no drift). → **fix**: four tests, `adopt`'s message names a checkout.
10. **[verifier, Phase 1]** a relative `--home` with `--repo` resolves against the repo dir on a real install (`Reinstall` sets `cmd.Dir = repo`) and against cwd on `--dry-run`. → **fix** (`bug` skill, BUG-080): absolutize `--home` at entry; test.
11. **[simplify, low/medium]** `main.go:691,732-733` vs `readSettings` — the 1 MiB settings bound enforced two ways; `status` never warns on an oversized file. → **fix**: one bound in `readSettings`.
12. **[simplify, low/high]** the `settings: %s could not be written (%v); add the key by hand` format string ×7. → **fix**: one helper.
13. **[security, low/high]** `report.go:400-402,453-458` — the throwaway clone's parent created `0o755` where `release.go` uses `0o700`. → **fix**: `0o700`.
14. **[security, low/high]** `apply.go:220-237` `Diff` writes the rendered harness to `os.CreateTemp("")` — `/tmp`. → **fix**: the temp file under `~/.config/sh-agent/` (the home's runtime dir), removed after.
15. **[security, low/high]** `inventory.go:394-403` `cell` slices a description by bytes and can cut a rune. → **fix**: rune-aware.
16. **[security, low/low]** `frontmatter.go` `yamlQuote` escapes `\` and `"` only; `DeriveAgy` renders descriptions with it. → **assess**: the installer already refuses multi-line descriptions; if a control character can still reach it, escape it; else rebut.
17. **[security, low/high]** `repo.go:74-82` + `main.go:546-570` — `LoadState` sanitises `Files` but not `Repo`; `knownCheckout` compares `st.Repo` with a repo `st.Repo` itself chose. → **left** (main agent): the manifest is written by `sh-agent` as the user; a prior write as the user is the attacker already holding the user's rights; `knownCheckout`'s purpose (a DIFFERENT checkout found from cwd) still holds when the walk finds one.
18. **[simplify, low/low]** `main.go:557-562` a comment duplicated back to back. → **fix**.
19. **[docs, low/unverified]** `report: --repo is not used here` on a release binary undocumented. → **fix** (`documentation`), one clause.

## Not checked

- No lens ran on a machine other than this one; the Mac and devbox cells are Phase 4's.
- The test files were scanned for secrets, not read (security); the code lens did not read the test files in full.
- `govulncheck` was not run by the agents (no network); this session's last run (`testing/2026-09-18-verify-sh-agent-works-everywhere-phase-1-2.md`) was clean on go1.27.1 with zero third-party requires.
- `report.go`'s redaction list, `release.go`'s edge messages, `adopt.go`, `frontmatter.go`, `derive.go`, `state.go`, `source.go` were grep-checked by the docs lens, not read.
- The simplify lens's medium (5) and security's 17 are left by decision, not verified further.

## Outcome

Written by the main agent after the fix round (batch A: `internal/harness`; batch B: `cmd/sh-agent`), before the round's own review; each fix has a test that failed before it and a must-fail mutation (`.agents/scratch/phase2-mustfail/mutate.py`, 13 of 13 failing as test failures).

1. adopt keeps write bits — **fixed** (internal/harness/adopt.go:175); `TestAdoptStripsGroupAndOtherWrite`.
2. `update` on a plain copy names no alternative — **fixed** in the error itself (internal/harness/repo.go:119); `TestUpdateOnPlainCopyNamesTheAlternative` drives it through the CLI.
3. `keep`/`kept` undocumented — **fixed** by `documentation` (README `install` row, `delivery.md`).
4. `knownCheckout` refusal undocumented — **fixed** by `documentation` (README § Daily commands qualified; `local.md` § Configure).
5. the settings editor in `main.go` — **left**, main agent: a structural move with no behaviour change; the plan's Follow-ups.
6. non-canonical tags — **fixed**: canonical regex and an int-fit check (internal/harness/source.go:54); `compareRelease(tag, version) <= 0` refuses with "is not newer than" (internal/harness/release.go:117); `TestIsReleaseVersionIsCanonical`, `TestNonCanonicalTagNeverReachesTheDownload` (the tag never reaches the download).
7. the BUG-079 note under `--home` and before ownership is known — **fixed**: real home only (internal/harness/pathguard.go:118); "it is not yours to relink" when `from` is not the caller's (internal/harness/pathguard.go:134); `TestNoteRunningElsewhereOnlyForTheRealHome`, `TestOwnedByCaller`.
8. `adopt` on a plain copy says commit and push — **fixed** (cmd/sh-agent/main.go:267); `TestAdoptOnPlainCopySaysWhereToCommit`.
9. the four coverage gaps — **fixed**: `TestAdoptOnReleaseBinaryNamesTheAlternative` (and the message names `git clone`), `TestStatusOnPlainCopyNamesTheRefusal`, `TestSyncIsInstall`, `TestDiffVerbShowsDrift`.
10. relative `--home` — **fixed**, BUG-080 (cmd/sh-agent/main.go:107); `TestRelativeHomeResolvesAgainstTheInvokingDirectory` reproduced the stray directory inside a scratch clone before the fix.
11. two bounds on the settings file — **fixed**: one, in `readSettings` (cmd/sh-agent/main.go:848); `TestStatusWarnsOnOversizedSettings`; `TestAttributionSet`'s expectation follows the shared note.
12. the format string ×7 — **fixed**: `settingsUnwritable` (cmd/sh-agent/main.go:831).
13. throwaway parent `0o755` — **fixed** (internal/harness/report.go:457); `TestThrowawayParentIsPrivate`.
14. `Diff` in `/tmp` — **fixed**: under `~/.config/sh-agent/` (internal/harness/apply.go:227); `TestDiffUsesTheHomeNotTmp` also covers the 0% body.
15. `cell` by bytes — **fixed** (internal/harness/inventory.go:398); `TestCellIsRuneSafe`.
16. `yamlQuote` control characters — **fixed**, escaped as `\uXXXX` (internal/harness/frontmatter.go:180); `TestYamlQuoteEscapesControlCharacters` — whose expected string the file tool converted into the character itself on first write (BUG-057's class, caught by grepping for the escape).
17. `LoadState` and `s.Repo` — **left**, main agent, with the reason narrowed after security's round 2: not "the attacker already has the user's rights" (a `state.json` from a dotfiles sync, a restored backup or a shared `--home` is none of that) but that `knownCheckout`'s comparison is real when the cwd walk finds a checkout, and a recorded path that names no harness is refused by `ResolveSource` before anything is built or run. Sanitising `Repo` further is a Follow-up, not a fix this round makes.
18. the duplicated comment — **fixed**.
19. `report: --repo is not used here` undocumented — **fixed** by `documentation`.

title: Review — harness-simplify (2026-09-18)
body:
# Review — harness-simplify   (2026-09-18)

Range reviewed: internal/harness and cmd/sh-agent (whole-file read, not a diff): all non-test `.go` files in `internal/harness` (adopt.go, apply.go, derive.go, frontmatter.go, inventory.go, pathguard.go, plan.go, release.go, render.go, repo.go, report.go, source.go, state.go) and `cmd/sh-agent/main.go`.

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing here is broken. The codebase is unusually well-defended (every non-obvious choice carries a comment naming the bug or review round that produced it) and I found no dead exported code, no case of two functions silently disagreeing on the same question (the brief's `binOnPath`/`PathShadows` and lexical-vs-`os.SameFile` pairs are already gone — `PathShadows` and `RunningElsewhere` both use `os.SameFile` identity consistently, one call each). The one real issue is `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` carrying a self-contained ~220-line settings.json editor that has nothing to do with CLI orchestration, plus a small cluster of literally-duplicated message strings inside that same code. Everything else is either already minimal or a single-purpose helper with one caller.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:676-895` (`attributionSet`, `attributionHint`, `attributionOff`, `readSettings`, `abandonTemp`) — a self-contained JSON-file editor (read `~/.claude/settings.json`, insert one key, atomic rename) with no dependency on flag parsing or command dispatch. It sits in the 945-line entrypoint file next to install/update/status orchestration, so it and the CLI wiring share one file and one diff for unrelated changes. Every other piece of logic this size in the repo (install, plan, state, release, report) lives under `internal/harness` and is called once from `main.go`; this cluster is the outlier. Shorter version: move these five functions verbatim into a new `internal/harness/attribution.go`, export the two entry points (`AttributionSet`, `AttributionHint`) and call them from `installFiles`/`status` as already written — deletes ~220 lines from `main.go` with no behavior change.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:703,711,716,721,725,784,816` — the exact format string `"settings: %s could not be written (%v); add the key by hand\n"` is repeated verbatim at seven call sites inside `attributionSet`/`abandonTemp`, and `"settings: %s could not be edited safely (the result would not parse); add the key by hand\n"` is repeated at two more (lines 756, 775). A wording change (there have already been several review rounds touching this file) has to be made in up to nine places to stay consistent. Shorter version: one `settingsWriteFailed(out io.Writer, path string, err error)` helper (3 lines) replacing the 7 identical `fmt.Fprintf` calls, and a second one-line helper for the "could not be edited safely" pair — net deletion of roughly a dozen duplicated lines.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:691,732-733` vs `internal/harness` pattern in `readSettings` (main.go:822-843) — the 1 MiB bound on `settings.json` is enforced twice, two different ways: `attributionSet` does its own `os.Lstat` + `info.Size() > 1<<20` check and refuses with a message, then falls through to call `readSettings`, which does its *own* `os.Stat` of the same path and silently truncates via `io.LimitReader(f, 1<<20)` instead of rejecting. `attributionOff` (used by `status`) reaches `readSettings` directly and never gets the oversized-file message `attributionSet` gives — the same file is judged two different ways depending which command reads it. Shorter version: make `readSettings` itself reject a file over the bound (return the "is larger than 1 MiB" problem string) and delete `attributionSet`'s separate Lstat-and-size branch (lines 730-735) along with the duplicate `1<<20` constant; one bound, one message, checked once per read instead of twice.

- **[low / confidence: low]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:557-562` — the comment on `knownCheckout` explaining why a manifest's `EmbeddedPrefix` value is not handed to `samePath` is printed twice, back to back, identically. Harmless (not user-facing text) but is a straightforward accidental duplication; delete one copy.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. Every exported function in `internal/harness` and every unexported helper in both packages has at least one real (non-test) caller; checked by grepping each identifier's call sites. `redactDocument` initially looked uncalled because it is passed by reference (`add("state.json", redactDocument)`), not called by name — confirmed live.
2. Flow tracing — not in this lens
3. Standards conformance — not in this lens
4. Directory layout — not in this lens
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — one finding: the settings.json editor is a correctly-scoped, dependency-free implementation (no library needed for a one-key JSON patch), but its size-bound check is implemented twice with different outcomes (reject vs. silent truncate). No hand-rolled crypto/auth; `crypto/sha256` and `ssh-keygen -Y verify` in `release.go` are used as designed, not DIY.
6. Decoupling — one finding: the attribution/settings-file cluster in `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` is an independent module living in the wrong package, making the entrypoint file a grab-bag of CLI dispatch plus an unrelated file-editing concern. Everything else split cleanly: each `internal/harness` file owns one concern (state, plan, release, report, pathguard) with small interfaces at the seams (`Source`, `File`, `Report`).

## Not examined
- Every `*_test.go` file (out of scope per the dispatch: non-test `.go` files only).
- `go vet ./...` and `gofmt -l` were run and are clean, but no deeper static analysis (staticcheck, golangci-lint) was run — not installed in this sandbox.
- Runtime behavior was not exercised (no `sh-agent install`/`update`/`report` invocation, per the hard limits: no real-`$HOME` install, no network, no `sh-agent report`).
- Criteria 2 (flow tracing), 3 (standards conformance) and 4 (directory layout) were not evaluated at all, per the brief's scope restriction to criteria 1, 5, 6 plus reuse/efficiency.

title: Review — plan-sh-agent-works-everywhere-cold-read-3 (2026-09-18)
body:
# Review — plan-sh-agent-works-everywhere-cold-read-3   (2026-09-18)

Range reviewed: plan file, round 3 — `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-18-sh-agent-works-everywhere.md` (with D8) and `internal/harness/apply.go`

## (1) Gaps

- **BLOCKING (new)** Phase 1 task 1's chosen fixture for "previous file unreadable" (`apply.go:33-62`, D6) is "a directory in its place, which `ReadFile` refuses". I verified with a standalone `os.Rename` probe (regular file → existing directory) that this fails with `EEXIST`/`file exists`, not a silent overwrite. In the default branch, `writeAtomic` ends with `os.Rename(name, dest)` (`apply.go:298`); when `dest` is a directory, that rename errors, and `Install` returns `fmt.Errorf("writing %s: %w", dest, err)` (`apply.go:61`) instead of printing `update ~/<rel> (previous file unreadable: …)` and succeeding. The plan's own claim — "lists `update … (previous file unreadable: …)` and is written" (Phase 1, line 47) — cannot be true for the fixture it names; the install would instead return an error (or, if `writeAtomic` is extended to `RemoveAll` a directory first, that is new behavior the plan never decides). Either the fixture must change (e.g. a regular file that returns a non-`ErrNotExist` read error some other way — permission bits are unreliable as root/CI often bypass them) or `writeAtomic` must gain directory-removal handling the plan doesn't currently authorize. This blocks Phase 1 task 1 as written: two implementers would diverge on whether the test asserts success or an error.
- **Resolved from round 2**: D8 plus the added Phase 1 clause ("`--dry-run` over a deployed file `chmod`ed to 0644 lists the `mode` line and leaves the mode as it was") closes round 2's blocking gap about the `os.Stat` probe being trapped inside `if !dryRun`. Confirmed against `apply.go:49-55`, which today wraps both `Stat` and `Chmod`, matching D8's cited line range.
- **Carried over, still low severity**: Phase 1's checkpoint (line 49) still states "260 at the time of writing" for the add-line count with no re-derivation caveat beyond the parenthetical already there — acceptable as written, not blocking.

## (2) Scope vs Why

No new endpoints, verbs, flags, or config keys found beyond rounds 1-2. D1-D8 each carry an attributed operator quote or an implementer note with citation; nothing in the plan builds beyond the `## Why`/`## Scope` request.

## (3) Readiness

1. **BLOCKING** — Does the "previous file unreadable" test fixture (a directory standing in for the deployed file) actually exercise the `update … (unreadable)` line, or does `os.Rename` over a directory error out first? Verified: it errors first. Not stated; the plan asserts an outcome ("is written") that contradicts what the named fixture produces with today's `writeAtomic`.
2. **NON-BLOCKING** — Exact wording/formatting of the `mode` line's `(0644 -> 0755)` old→new values (octal vs `-rwxr--r--` style) — Verification line 40 makes wording non-binding; a reasonable implementer follows the interface line's literal example.
3. **NON-BLOCKING** — The "260 add lines" checkpoint figure will drift with unrelated content changes; a reasonable implementer re-derives it at run time.

## Verdict

`design needs revision` / `implementation not ready`: one new BLOCKING gap. D8 correctly closed round 2's finding, but Phase 1 task 1's own added test fixture for the D6 "unreadable file" case is internally inconsistent with `apply.go`'s rename-based `writeAtomic` — verified by direct `os.Rename` probe (file over existing directory → `EEXIST`). The plan needs either a working fixture for "read fails but write can proceed" or an explicit decision that this case is instead a refusal/error path.

## Not examined

Did not re-read `main.go`, `plan.go`, `repo.go`, `source.go`, `release.go`, `report.go`, `adopt.go`, `state.go`, `render.go`, `inventory.go`, `derive.go`, `pathguard.go`, `apply_test.go`, or any docs surface (`README.md`, `.agents/docs/deploy/{local,remote}.md`, `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md`, `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md`); Phase 2-5 content beyond re-confirming D8 against `apply.go`. This round re-verified round 2's fix (D8) and probed the one new fixture Phase 1 added since round 2, given the 20-tool-call budget.

title: Review — v1.2.1-f91257c-docs (2026-09-18)

# Review — v1.2.1-f91257c-docs   (2026-09-18)

Range reviewed: v1.2.1..f91257c (git log v1.2.1..f91257c); diff v1.2.1...f91257c

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Docs lens only. The BUG-078 fix (PATH-shadow warnings in `install`/`status`, `--dry-run` printing no PATH claim) is described accurately and consistently in README.md, `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md` and `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` — checked the exact strings against `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` and `internal/harness/pathguard.go` and they match verbatim (`warning: %s comes before %s on PATH...`, `note: %s is not on PATH...`, `shadowed   %s comes first on PATH...`, and the `--dry-run` skip of `pathHint`). The one real gap: `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md`'s real-home smoke-check section was not updated to require the new `shadowed`/`sh-agent version` checks that `local.md` and `remote.md` now both prescribe in their own Verify sections, so the two doc surfaces that describe "how to verify an install" have drifted apart from each other in this range.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md` § "5. Real-home smoke checks" — `local.md` § Verify and `remote.md` § Verify were both changed in this range to require `sh-agent version` unqualified matching what was installed and `sh-agent status` showing no `shadowed` line (BUG-078). `guide.md`'s own real-home checklist (context questions, skill load, agent dispatch) was not touched and still does not name either check, so a session following the testing guide alone would not catch a PATH shadow the deploy guides now explicitly guard against. Not a `dropped:`/`narrowed:` finding under old-wording since `guide.md` never had this wording to begin with — flagging per the dispatch's explicit prompt to check whether it should name the `shadowed` line.
- **[n/a informational]** `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md` has no status-line or install-output table to update — checked, nothing there references the wording this range changed, so no finding there.
- **[n/a informational]** README `## How it works` mermaid map (lines 5-49) is untouched across the whole range v1.2.1..f91257c — confirms AGENTS.md rule 3's map question is answered "no reroute" for the full range, not just the earlier 4cdc0b5..52574a0 slice a prior review checked.

## Old-wording grep (rule: every restatement of a changed sentence)

- `allowed-signers` → `allowed_signers`: `remote.md` corrected its own two occurrences (spelling fix, round 3). Grepped the whole range's living-doc surfaces (`README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.agents/{rules,skills,agents,commands}`, `.agents/docs/specs/`, `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md`, `.agents/docs/deploy/`) for the old `allowed-signers` (hyphenated) spelling post-fix — none found; both deploy docs and README now consistently use `allowed_signers`.
- `install --dry-run` PATH claim: no other living doc restates the old (absent) behaviour incorrectly; only README and remote.md ever described dry-run PATH behaviour, and both are current with the code (checked against `main.go:274-278`).
- No other rule, threshold, or trigger text in this range's diff (checksum/signature verification steps, the `--clobber` requirement, `sh-agent version` ordering) had a prior restatement elsewhere in the repo left stale — these are additions to README/remote.md, not edits of wording that existed elsewhere.

## Criteria

1. Dead code — n/a — docs lens
2. Flow tracing — n/a — docs lens (traced doc claims to `main.go`/`pathguard.go` instead; see Verdict)
3. Standards conformance — n/a — docs lens
4. Directory layout — n/a — docs lens
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — n/a — docs lens
6. Decoupling — n/a — docs lens

## Not examined

- `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` and `internal/harness/pathguard_test.go` were not read line-by-line for stale assertions (only grepped for the message strings, which matched); a full stale-test sweep of these two files was not performed given the tool-call budget.
- ROADMAP.md and the 2026-09-17-release-binary.md plan diff were not compared against their own historical wording for stale restatements.
- The four dated verifier/security logs and review reports added in this range (`reviews/2026-09-18-*`, `testing/2026-09-18-verify-bug078-path-shadow*.md`) were not read for content — excluded by the dispatch's own rule (never grepped in changes/, reviews/, dated logs) and not part of the docs-lens comparison set.

# Review — v1.2.3-3b5b71a-code   (2026-09-18, round 4 — at the operator's call)

Range reviewed: commits v1.2.3..10a9fe2 (`git log v1.2.3..10a9fe2`); diff `git diff v1.2.3...10a9fe2`. Round 1 covered v1.2.3..3b5b71a, round 2 3b5b71a..94bec82, round 3 94bec82..8e1b044; this round re-checks the five round-3 fixes over `git diff 8e1b044..10a9fe2`. New findings this round are scoped to the delivery claim's restatements and the preflight verification row.

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

All five round-3 fixes are correct, and the delivery mechanism is now consistent everywhere the one prescribed grep reaches: no sentence in `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.agents/docs/deploy/*.md` or `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/*.md` still says a tag delivers nothing or that every machine follows `main`. One nit remains inside the mechanism the round touched: `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:52` now permits an `IN PROGRESS` log to be replaced by a fresh dispatch, while `:77` still blocks on "a verifier log whose Status is still IN PROGRESS" without saying which log — read literally, a gate that correctly re-ran a cut-off verifier and got a clean PASS still finds a blocking condition on disk. That is a false NO-SHIP, not a false ship, so it does not block a release; it should be qualified in the same file.

## Findings (round 4)

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:77` vs `:52` — `:52` now distinguishes the two non-PASS cases: a FAIL or BLOCKED log "is carried to Step 5 as it is and blocks there — never replaced by a re-run cited alone", while "only one left IN PROGRESS" sends the gate to a fresh dispatch. `:77` did not gain the matching qualifier and still blocks on "a verifier log whose Status is still IN PROGRESS (a run cut off before it finished; BUG-083)" — unqualified, so the superseded log the gate was just told to replace still satisfies a blocking condition. Fix: at `:77`, say "the verifier log cited for the Verification row, or any FAIL or BLOCKED log in the range" — keeping the FAIL/BLOCKED case deliberately range-wide (that asymmetry is right, and `:52` states it) while letting a replaced IN PROGRESS log go.

## Verification of the round-3 fixes

- **`.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:8`** — "Git is the transport for a checkout place and a signed release download for a binary-only one (§ Releases), both on the operator's own credentials", now citing R8, R9, ADR-030 and ADR-033. Correct and complete: it matches `:128` ("Then the release's binaries, which is how a binary-only place updates (R9, ADR-033)"), `README.md:154`, `deploy/local.md:43`, and `REQUIREMENTS.md` R9; the "no push-based deploy, no CI, no hooks, no service" tail is preserved, so nothing the old sentence guaranteed was dropped.
- **`.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:91`** — "A checkout place never installs from a tag; a binary-only place installs only from one (§ Releases)." Correct, and it keeps the timer paragraph's point intact (the timer is a checkout mechanism, so the first clause is the one that governs there). No longer contradicts `:95`, `AGENTS.md:63` or R9.
- **`.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:195`** — "There is no deploy step after the push: a checkout place picks the commit up, and a binary-only place the release, with `sh-agent update` when the operator runs it." Correct; the "no deploy step" invariant that R9 and ADR-030 D2 protect survives the split.
- **`.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md:7`** — now names R8 and R9, ADR-030 and ADR-033, with a parenthetical for the release binaries. Correct; consistent with `:33` and `:76`, which already carried ADR-033.
- **`.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md:56`** — the withdrawn-channel bullet keeps its history and gains "ADR-033 later restored a narrower channel: the binaries published with a tag, which a binary-only place updates to after verifying their signed checksums — an asset the place fetches, never a push to a machine." Correct, and the "never a push" clause keeps the bullet's original point (the section is "What is deliberately NOT being built", and what is still not built is a push channel) — the addition does not turn the bullet into a contradiction of its own heading.
- **`skills/preflight/SKILL.md:52`** — the FAIL/BLOCKED re-dispatch path that round 3 flagged is closed, with the "never replaced by a re-run cited alone" clause naming the exact failure mode. Correct; see the one nit above for the `:77` half.
- **The prescribed grep** (`grep -nE 'ADR-030|tag' README.md AGENTS.md .agents/docs/deploy/*.md .agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/*.md`) — every hit read. Nothing still says a tag delivers nothing or that every machine follows `main`. The remaining ADR-030-only citations are all historically correct as written: `AGENTS.md:74` (now naming both ADRs), `remote.md:56` (ADR-030 D1, per-machine credentials — untouched by ADR-033), `remote.md:91` (the timer's trust root — untouched), `delivery.md:43` (ADR-030 D4, a dependency the spec is arguing against).
- **G10 check** — the replaced sentences exist nowhere else; no orphaned copy of "a tag is never what a machine installs from", of the old `remote.md:8` transport claim, or of the unconditional Verification row survives anywhere the grep reaches. The `README.md` map (lines 8-45) already draws both paths — `harnessRepo -- "clone once, update pulls" --> checkoutPlace` and `releases -- "update downloads and verifies" --> binaryPlace` — so the project `AGENTS.md` rule 3 (a delivery change whose diff does not touch the map is incomplete) is satisfied by a map that was already correct; the `tags: release markers` node label is paired with a separate `Releases` node and is not the withdrawn claim.

## Criteria (round 4)

1. **Dead code** — pass. Every replaced sentence is gone, not duplicated; no stale copy left beside its replacement.
2. **Flow tracing** — pass. The ADR-033 delivery claim now reaches `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `README.md` (prose and map), `deploy/remote.md`, `deploy/local.md` and `specs/sh-agent/delivery.md` consistently; the verifier Status vocabulary reaches both `/preflight` rows, with the one unqualified reference named above.
3. **Standards conformance** — pass with the one nit. No BUG-004 frontmatter hazard; no agent `description:` touched in this range.
4. **Directory layout** — pass. Each fix landed in the file that owns its claim; trail artifacts under `.agents/docs/` in the right directories.
5. **Simplicity (DIY-except-security)** — pass. No code, no dependency, no security-sensitive surface anywhere in v1.2.3..10a9fe2; `go.mod` untouched.
6. **Decoupling** — pass. The verifier/`preflight` seam and the requirements/docs seam are each consistent in both directions.

## Noted, out of round

- `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:93`, the section heading "Releases — signed tags, as release markers", is now narrower than the section's own first sentence (a tag also carries the binaries). Not a contradiction and not in this round's scope; worth a word if the section is edited again.

## Trail claims checked against the code (rounds 1-3, still valid)

- `BUG-078`/`BUG-079`/`BUG-080`/`BUG-081`/`BUG-082` graduated-to claims all resolve to sentences present in `context/AGENTS.md`; the Graduated rows match; `BUG-083` (`open`) points at the § Work dispatch sentence, which exists and carries the round-2 wording; `BUG-084`'s record file and INDEX row exist (text not read).

## Not examined

- `gofmt -l cmd internal`, `go vet ./...`, `govulncheck`, `go test ./...` — not re-run this round; no Go source changed anywhere in v1.2.3..10a9fe2, and round 2 read a bare green `go test ./...` at 94bec82, whose Go tree is identical to 10a9fe2's.
- No installer run and no CLI start in any round: the changed context, agent, skill and command files were read, not deployed.
- `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` and `specs/sh-agent/delivery.md` were read at the lines the prescribed grep returned plus the diff hunks, not end to end; a contradiction stated without the words `tag` or `ADR-030` would not have been caught.
- `.agents/docs/bugs/BUG-084-*.md`, `reviews/2026-09-18-review-v1.2.3-3b5b71a-docs.md`, and `testing/2026-09-18-verify-preflight-v1.3.0.md` (which grew in this range) — not read.
- Round-1 "Not examined" still stands for the rest of the trail markdown in the range (the retro, three handoffs, two cold-read plans, the changes entry, the worktree-retro review, two testing logs, the works-everywhere plan).

## Outcome

- Finding 1 (`skills/feedback-log/SKILL.md:48` schema line without `redirection`): fixed at `skills/feedback-log/SKILL.md:48`.
- Finding 2 (`agents/verifier.md:71` template Status without `IN PROGRESS`): fixed at `agents/verifier.md:71`.
- Finding 3 (`agents/verifier.md:18` "FIRST command" unsatisfiable before Pre-flight): fixed at `agents/verifier.md:18` ("the FIRST verification command … once the docs root is resolved") and the matching dispatch sentence at `context/AGENTS.md` § Work.
- All three in the pre-gate commit that follows 3b5b71a; recorded as BUG-084 (a value added to a vocabulary in prose but not in the file's own schema/template lines).
- Round 2 (over 3b5b71a..94bec82): all three verified fixed; two findings raised — `/preflight`'s blocking list did not know the new `IN PROGRESS` status, and `AGENTS.md:63` still carried the ADR-030 delivery claim the README fix superseded.
- Round 3 (over 94bec82..8e1b044): both round-2 findings verified fixed at `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:52,77` and `AGENTS.md:63,74`; four findings raised — `remote.md:91` and `:8`, a re-dispatch path introduced at `preflight:52`, and stale ADR framing at `delivery.md:7,56`.
- Round 4 (this review, over 8e1b044..10a9fe2, at the operator's call): all four round-3 findings verified fixed at `remote.md:8,91,195`, `delivery.md:7,56` and `preflight:52`; the prescribed grep over `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `deploy/*.md` and `specs/sh-agent/*.md` finds no surviving "a tag delivers nothing" or "every machine follows `main`" claim. One low nit open: `preflight:77`'s IN PROGRESS clause is unqualified and can block a gate whose cut-off log was correctly replaced. Verdict APPROVE WITH NITS — nothing here blocks a release.

- `.agents/docs/changes/2026-09-18-retro-applied.md` cross-checked against the actual diff (files, bug citations, verification claims about the 1-of-3 behavioural runs): accurate, matches `BUG-083`'s INDEX row and record.

Standards conformance — pass: every restatement of the changed rules (verifier's early-log rule, the two BUG-backed Hard-rules sentences, the feedback-log signal vocabulary) is updated consistently in this range; the one still-stale restatement (reviewer/security/explorer wording) predates this range and was already tracked, not reintroduced.

# Review — worktree-retro-docs (2026-09-18)

Range reviewed: working tree diff via `git diff HEAD -- context/AGENTS.md skills/feedback-log/SKILL.md agents/verifier.md skills/feature/SKILL.md`

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

Docs-lens review (no source, config, or tests in scope). Nothing is factually wrong in the new text, but two restatements of the "write the artifact early" rule were left on the old wording after `agents/verifier.md` replaced it, the new feedback-log triggers 6/7 have no matching `signal` vocabulary value, and two of the four cited events in `context/AGENTS.md`'s Hard rules have no BUG record backing them despite the project's own "every failure gets a number" rule.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `agents/reviewer.md:20` and `agents/security.md:18` — both still read "Write your report file as soon as you have one finding worth recording, then UPDATE it as you go...", the exact phrasing `agents/verifier.md` just replaced with the per-command IN-PROGRESS-log rule. Criterion 3 ("every other restatement of a changed rule is changed with it") applies: these are the same "write the artifact early" rule for sibling read-only agents, now inconsistent with the verifier's stricter version. `agents/explorer.md:17` carries the same old wording too but explorer writes a brief, not a pass/fail log, so it is the weaker case of the three — still worth a decision either way, not a silent skip. `restated: agents/reviewer.md:20, agents/security.md:18 (also agents/explorer.md:17) still say the old thing; agents/verifier.md:18-19 has the new thing.`

- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `skills/feedback-log/SKILL.md:28-29` (new triggers 6 "Redirection" and 7 "A missed filing") vs. the Signal Types table (`skills/feedback-log/SKILL.md:73-78`, values `correction|override|restatement|format|gap`) — neither new trigger maps cleanly to an existing signal value. Trigger 6 ("the user changes what is being built... even when no word of it is 'no'") is closest to `override` but `override` is documented narrowly as "User changed agent's choice to something else" (tool/pattern), not scope/direction. Trigger 7 ("the user asks for something a rule says should already exist... the ask IS the correction") is closest to `gap` ("Agent lacked knowledge it should have had") but the trigger's own text says the agent *did* know the rule and just didn't file it — that's not a knowledge gap. Since `rule_ref`/`signal` values are the controlled vocabulary `/retro` matches on across projects, an entry logged under triggers 6/7 will be coerced into a signal that doesn't describe it, or left ambiguous. Either add `redirection` and a value for trigger 7 to the table, or the SKILL.md states explicitly which existing value each maps to.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `context/AGENTS.md` Hard rules — of the four sentences this scope changes, two cite BUG ids that exist (`BUG-078`, `BUG-079` on the "verified by the shell" sentence; `BUG-080` on the "read-only mode" sentence — both confirmed present in `.agents/docs/bugs/INDEX.md`). The other two cite dated events with no BUG id at all: "(three rounds on one mechanism in styrman-harness, 2026-09-18, each passing a fresh-fixture test)" on the Review bullet, and "(four mutations read as 'fails as it must' on a build error, styrman-harness 2026-09-18)" on the mutation-testing bullet. `git grep` of "fresh-fixture", "fresh fixture", "build error", "mutations", "declared and not used" against `.agents/docs/bugs/INDEX.md` returns nothing — no BUG-NNN record documents either event, unlike the other two sentences in the same diff that do cite one. The project's own rule ("Every failure gets a number... a fix that took more than one attempt, a review finding that was a real defect... Dispatch `bugs`") applies to both: three rounds on one mechanism and four mutations misread as passing are exactly the failure classes that rule names.

## Not a finding (checked, clean)

- `agents/verifier.md` § Write the artifact EARLY: the "roughly two thirds of your budget" sentence survives unchanged in the diff (still present, untouched by the replacement).
- `context/AGENTS.md`'s `## Installed` block and skill/agent counts: unaffected by this scope — no skill, agent, command, or rule was added or removed, only prose edited in place. No update needed, correctly left alone.
- README.md § Install without cloning, `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md` § Verify, `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` (lines ~46-52) all already state the same "verify from the shell that will run it" procedure (`hash -r`/`rehash`, `type sh-agent`, `which -a`) that the new `context/AGENTS.md` sentence describes, each citing BUG-078/BUG-079. Consistent.

## Criteria

1. Dead code — n/a — docs lens
2. Flow tracing — n/a — docs lens
3. Standards conformance — FAIL: rule restated in `agents/reviewer.md` and `agents/security.md` not updated alongside `agents/verifier.md`'s changed wording (see finding above); feedback-log's new triggers not reflected in its own signal vocabulary table.
4. Directory layout — n/a — docs lens
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — n/a — docs lens
6. Decoupling — n/a — docs lens

## Not examined

- `skills/feature/SKILL.md` diff (added clause about a test fixture in a verify clause not producing its claimed condition): checked it has no stale restatement elsewhere via targeted grep of "verify clause" and "test fixture" wording, but did not exhaustively grep every skill under `skills/` for a paraphrase of this specific clause — only the four named-in-brief targets (context/AGENTS.md, feedback-log, verifier.md, feature/SKILL.md sentences) got full grep treatment.
- Did not check `.agents/docs/specs/` or the newest `changes/` entry against this diff in detail beyond the bug-index and deploy/README checks above — no changes/ entry appears to reference this exact diff yet (working tree, uncommitted).
- Did not run any test suite (docs-only scope; none applicable).

## Outcome

- Finding 1 (`agents/reviewer.md:20`, `agents/security.md:18`, `agents/explorer.md:17` keep "one finding worth recording"): left — owner: the next `/retro`. Proposal 6 was the verifier's: its passing commands read as "no finding yet", which is why its rule now names the first command. For a reviewer, security or explorer the finding IS the unit, and whether they want the per-step form is a separate proposal; noted in the handoff.
- Finding 2 (triggers 6 and 7 without a signal value): fixed at `skills/feedback-log/SKILL.md:28-29` (each trigger names its signal) and `:79` (`redirection` row).
- Finding 3 (two sentences citing no BUG id): fixed — the events are recorded as BUG-081 and BUG-082 (`bugs/INDEX.md` Graduated table) and cited at `context/AGENTS.md:26` and `:56`.

title: Security review — fix round for the Phase 2 audit (160aa16..3209cf3)
body:
# Security review — fix round for the Phase 2 audit (160aa16..3209cf3)

Range reviewed: 160aa16..3209cf3 (`git diff 160aa16..3209cf3 -- . ':!.agents/docs'`, plus the four docs in the dispatch)

## Verdict: FINDINGS

Seven of my eight audit findings are closed as written. One is not: the `0o700`
on the throwaway clone's parent is **inert on every machine that has run
`install`**. `SaveState` writes `~/.config/sh-agent/state.json` through
`writeAtomic`, whose `os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(dest), 0o755)` (`apply.go:291`)
creates that directory first, and `os.MkdirAll` returns nil for an existing
directory without touching its mode — measured, twice: a scratch probe
replicating the two calls in order prints `-rwxr-xr-x` after both, and
`~/.config/sh-agent` on the operator's own box is **0755** right now. So
`report.go:457`, `apply.go:224` and the older `release.go:136` all no-op. I also
have to correct my own earlier framing of that finding, and `release.go`'s
comment with it: 0755 grants group and other **r-x, not w**, so nobody can
pre-create `report-<pid>` as a symlink there — the exposure the 0700 actually
closes is READ exposure, and that is the one still open: every local account can
traverse `~/.config/sh-agent` and read the feedback log, the retro proposals, and
the transient clone of the **private** `styrman-harness-feedback` repository
while `report` runs (and after a SIGINT, until the next sweep). Everything else
in the round does what its finding asked, and two of the new tests
(`TestNonCanonicalTagNeverReachesTheDownload`, `TestDiffUsesTheHomeNotTmp`) are
genuine must-fail checks of the behaviour they pin.

## Status of the eight prior findings — checkable statements

1. **`copyTree` mode — CLOSED.** `adopt.go:175` is now
   `writeAtomic(target, data, info.Mode().Perm()&0o755|0o600)`, identical in
   effect to `plan.go:138`: 0666 lands 0644, 0775 lands 0755. Directories in the
   same walk are `MkdirAll(target, 0o755)`. `TestAdoptStripsGroupAndOtherWrite`
   asserts `Perm()&0o022 == 0` on the adopted file (skipped as root, correctly).
3. **Canonical tags + `<= 0` + overflow — CLOSED.** `source.go:46` is
   `^v(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$`, which rejects
   `v1.02.2`, `v01.2.2`, `v1.2.02`; the added `strconv.Atoi` loop rejects
   `v99999999999999999999.0.0` before `releaseParts` could read it as `v0.0.0`.
   `release.go:116` is `compareRelease(tag, version) <= 0` with the message "is
   not newer than". `compareRelease` has exactly **one** production caller
   (`release.go:116`, confirmed by grep across the module) and both its operands
   are gated by `IsReleaseVersion` above it (`:102` for `tag` from the GitHub
   API, `:114` for the running `version`), so `releaseParts`' surviving
   `return [3]int{}` is unreachable from production code. The guard moved to the
   entry rather than to the parse; that is equivalent **here and only here**, and
   a second caller of `compareRelease` would have to repeat the gate. The doc
   comment at `release.go:369-370` ("Both are known to match") says so, which is
   the mitigation.
4. **The BUG-079 note — CLOSED for `--home`, PARTIAL for ownership.**
   `pathguard.go:118` returns unless `filepath.Clean(os.UserHomeDir()) ==
   filepath.Clean(home)`, and `TestNoteRunningElsewhereOnlyForTheRealHome`
   exercises both directions by setting `HOME`. `ownedByCaller` downgrades the
   remedy. Two residuals, findings B and C below.
5. **Throwaway parent `0o700` — NOT CLOSED.** Finding A.
6. **`Diff` out of `/tmp` — CLOSED for `/tmp`; the leak survives.**
   `apply.go:223-227` writes under `filepath.Join(home, ".config", "sh-agent")`,
   and `TestDiffUsesTheHomeNotTmp` proves it by setting `TMPDIR` to a
   non-existent path and requiring `Diff` to succeed — a real must-fail check.
   The `tmp.Write` error path at `:231-233` still returns without
   `os.Remove(tmp.Name())` and without `Close`, so a write failure leaks the file
   and its fd; the remediation that removed the temp file entirely (`diff … -`
   with `cmd.Stdin`) was not taken. Severity drops from "debris in a shared
   directory" to "debris in the operator's own directory at 0600". Finding E.
7. **`yamlQuote` — CLOSED.** `frontmatter.go:167-189` escapes `\`, `"`, `\n`,
   `\t` and every rune `< 0x20` or `== 0x7f` as `\uXXXX`. `\u` + four hex digits
   is a valid double-quoted escape in YAML 1.1 (`ns-esc-16-bit`) and YAML 1.2, so
   the rendered `agent.md` parses; DEL is included. Better than the finding
   asked: the reachable case is not the hypothetical newline (`entries()` splits
   on `\n`, `TrimRight`s `\r` and joins continuations with a space, so `Parse`
   cannot return a value containing a line break) but a **mid-line** control — a
   raw ESC, NUL or DEL inside a vendored skill's `description:`, which `keyLine`'s
   `(.*)` matches, `TrimSpace` preserves, and `Lint` does not refuse. That case
   was live and is now escaped. One residual, finding D.
8. **`cell` — CLOSED.** `inventory.go:396-402` converts to `[]rune` and takes
   `string(r[:max])`; every later index is a byte offset into that already
   rune-aligned prefix, so neither the space cut (ASCII boundary) nor the
   `cut = len(head)` fallback (the whole prefix) can split a rune.
   `TestCellIsRuneSafe` sweeps `max` from 5 to 119 over a multi-byte string and
   checks `utf8.ValidString`.

## The two findings left — do the reasons hold

**17 / `LoadState` does not sanitise `Repo`.** Two halves, two answers.

- *"a prior write as the user is the attacker already holding the user's
  rights"* — **sound for the default home and the default threat model, but it
  claims more than it proves and should be recorded narrower.** `state.json` is
  a file, not a live process; it arrives by any route that populates
  `~/.config`, and two of those are not "the attacker already has your rights":
  (a) a dotfiles repository or a restored backup carrying
  `~/.config/sh-agent/state.json` — a normal way for `~/.config` to be seeded,
  which makes `repo` an input from off the machine; (b) `--home <dir>` where the
  directory is shared or group-writable — and on this very box `~/.config` is
  **0775**, so the user's group is already a wider set than the user. In both,
  the `repo` field selects the directory `Reinstall` runs `go build` in and then
  executes. The disposition (leave it) is defensible — high cost, blast radius is
  the operator's own account — but write the reason as: *"no path writes
  `state.json` except `sh-agent` running as the user; a `state.json` that arrives
  from a backup, a dotfiles sync or a shared `--home` is out of model."* Closing
  it for real is still one `IsCheckout(st.Repo)` call before a build.
- *"`knownCheckout`'s purpose (a DIFFERENT checkout found from cwd) still holds
  when the walk finds one"* — **holds; verified against the resolution order.**
  `ResolveSource` (`repo.go:22-70+`) takes `--repo`, then `$SH_AGENT_REPO`, then
  the cwd walk, and only then the recorded manifest. So whenever the walk (or a
  flag) supplies `repo`, `st.Repo` is an independent value and
  `samePath(st.Repo, repo)` is a real comparison that refuses the mismatch — the
  case the guard exists for. The circularity bites only where nothing else
  supplied a repo and `st.Repo` was itself the selector, which the guard never
  claimed to cover. The claim is accurate as written.

## Findings — new surface from the fixes

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/report.go:457`,
  `internal/harness/apply.go:224`, `internal/harness/release.go:136` — **the
  `0o700` never applies.** `os.MkdirAll` is a no-op returning nil when the
  directory exists, and `~/.config/sh-agent` always exists by the time any of
  these run, created 0755 by `writeAtomic` under `SaveState` during the first
  `install` (`report`, `update` and `diff` all presuppose an install). Measured
  two ways: a scratch probe (`.agents/scratch/security-phase2/mkdirmode.go`,
  gitignored, no harness import, replicating `MkdirAll(dir,0o755)` then
  `MkdirAll(dir,0o700)`) prints `-rwxr-xr-x` for both; and `stat` on the
  operator's own `~/.config/sh-agent` returns **755** today. Why it matters, with
  the threat corrected: 0755 grants group and other r-x, **not w**, so the
  symlink-planting story in `release.go:132-134`'s comment and in my own earlier
  finding is wrong for this directory — nobody else can create an entry in it.
  What 0755 does leave is read access for every local account to
  `feedback.jsonl`, `retros.jsonl`, `proposals/*.md`, `state.json`, and — for the
  duration of `report`, and indefinitely after a SIGINT until the next
  `sweepInterruptedClones` — a working clone of the **private**
  `styrman-harness-feedback` repository holding this machine's reports. On a
  single-user box that is nothing; on the devbox or any host with a second
  account it is a disclosure. Remediation: one `ensureConfigDir(home)` helper —
  `os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o700)`, then when the directory already exists and
  `ownedByCaller` says it is the caller's, `os.Chmod(dir, 0o700)` — called from
  `SaveState` and from the three sites above; stdlib `os` only, no dependency.
  The test to add is the arrangement the current one avoids: `TestThrowawayParentIsPrivate`
  uses a bare `t.TempDir()` home with no prior install, which is the **one**
  arrangement in which the fix works, so it passes while the shipped behaviour
  does not; the new test must `Install` first (as `TestDiffUsesTheHomeNotTmp`
  already does, where the 0700 is provably inert and unasserted) and then assert
  the mode.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/pathguard.go:131` — the note
  decides "yours to relink" from `os.Lstat(from)`, but the operation it advises
  (`ln -sfn <installed> <from>`) is governed by **write permission on
  `filepath.Dir(from)`**, not by the ownership of the file at `from`. The two
  disagree in the case that actually occurs on these machines: a `sh-agent` the
  operator owns sitting in `/usr/local/bin`, a root-owned directory —
  `ownedByCaller` reads true, the note says "point it at the installed binary
  (`ln -sfn`)", and the command fails with EACCES. My audit's remediation said
  "stat `from` **and its directory**"; the directory half was not implemented. On
  the brief's symlink question: `Lstat` is the **right** call of the two — a
  symlink replacement is a directory operation, and on a sticky directory the
  link's own uid is what governs it, so following to the target's owner would be
  strictly worse — but neither `Lstat` nor `Stat` is sufficient without the
  parent. Remediation: also require `filepath.Dir(from)` to be the caller's (or
  writable by them) before offering `ln -sfn`. Advice-only surface; filed because
  a wrong remedy in a security-relevant note is what sends an operator to `sudo`.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/pathguard.go:141-147`
  (`ownedByCaller`) — the brief's root question, answered: for **root** (uid 0) a
  user-owned `from` (uid 1000) reads as *not* the caller's, so root running
  `update` gets "it is not yours to relink — remove it, with the rights that own
  it". The direction is the conservative one and the resulting advice is not
  harmful (root relinking a file inside a user's `~/.local/bin` is not advice to
  give), but the sentence is false as stated for root, who owns everything by
  capability. The realistic shape is `sudo sh-agent update` with `$HOME` left as
  the user's: the real-home gate at `:118` passes, `os.Getuid()` is 0, and every
  file in that home reads as foreign. No security consequence — the note writes
  nothing and touches nothing. Reword to "not owned by the user this process runs
  as". Separately, `os.Getuid()` (real uid) is the weaker of the two for a "can I
  write this" question; sh-agent is not setuid so it does not matter today, and
  `os.Geteuid()` is the one-word change that keeps it not mattering.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/frontmatter.go:178-183` —
  `yamlQuote` escapes C0 and DEL but not the **C1** controls (U+0080–U+009F,
  notably U+0085 NEL) or U+2028/U+2029. In YAML 1.1 — libyaml, PyYAML, what most
  embedded parsers implement — those are line-break characters, so a description
  carrying one renders as a raw break inside the double-quoted scalar. This is
  **not** injection: a double-quoted scalar ends at its closing quote, so the
  worst case is a fold to a space or a parse error, never a second mapping key.
  Filed only because the fix's own rationale ("a raw control character ends a
  double-quoted YAML scalar for a strict parser") applies verbatim to these four
  runes. Remediation: extend the guard to
  `r < 0x20 || (r >= 0x7f && r <= 0x9f) || r == 0x2028 || r == 0x2029`.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/apply.go:220-234` — `Diff`, a
  read-only verb, now **writes into the home**: it creates `~/.config/sh-agent`
  when absent and drops a temp file there. Confined to sh-agent's own directory
  and only on drift, so this is a note rather than a defect against the read-only
  rule (which is scoped to `--check`/`--dry-run`), but `sh-agent diff --home <a
  home you are merely inspecting>` now mutates it. The `tmp.Write` error path at
  `:231` leaks the file and its fd (no `Remove`, no `Close`), and README's new
  `diff` row asserts "removed after" without qualification — a description one
  error path wider than the behaviour. Remediation closes all three at once and
  is the one the audit gave: `exec.Command("diff", "-u", "-L", …, dest, "-")`
  with `cmd.Stdin = bytes.NewReader(f.Data)`, and no temp file at all.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go:1599-1629`
  (`plainCopyOf`, new in this range) — the fixture copies `context/`, `skills/`,
  `agents/`, `commands/` and `rules/` out of this checkout by walking the
  **working tree**, not `git ls-files`, into `t.TempDir()` (i.e. under `$TMPDIR`,
  which this project's rules put off limits for generated files). Today nothing
  leaks: `git status --untracked-files=all` and `git ls-files --others --ignored`
  over those five directories are empty, and a `find` for symlinks and
  secret-shaped names (`.env*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `*.tfvars`, `id_*`,
  `*credential*`) returns nothing — so the copy is all tracked content. The
  mechanism is the one `AGENTS.md` names as sharp ("an artifact built from the
  WORKING TREE rather than from git is pinned to what git tracks — `go:embed`
  compiled a gitignored `.env` into a release binary"): a gitignored credential
  dropped into `skills/` by a vendored skill would be refused by `secretShaped`
  at `install` and at `adopt`, and copied raw by this fixture. Exposure is
  bounded — `t.TempDir()` roots are 0700 — so it is a test-hygiene finding, not a
  shipping one. Remediation: drive the walk from `git ls-files -- <dir>`, or
  reuse `secretShaped` as a skip in the fixture; and point the fixture's root at
  `.agents/scratch/` rather than `$TMPDIR` if the project wants its own rule
  honoured in tests too.

## Checked

- **Secrets:** clean in the diff. No credential, token or key added in any
  changed file; `release.go:40`'s compiled-in **public** signer line is untouched
  by this range. The new test bodies were grepped for PEM headers and
  `ghp_`/`sk-ant-`/`AKIA`/`AIza`/`xoxb-`/`ssh-rsa`/`ssh-ed25519` shapes —
  nothing. Secrets in *output*: the two new message strings (`errPlainCopy`, the
  `adopt` refusal) embed only the public clone URL; the new `settingsUnwritable`
  helper prints `path` and `err` and no file content, exactly as the five sites it
  replaced did; `readSettings`' new size branch returns a fixed sentence and no
  bytes. The `plainCopyOf` fixture is the one secret-adjacent mechanism, above.
- **Injection:** no new shell, no new `exec.Command`, no new argv construction.
  The only argv-relevant change (`release.go:116`, `source.go:46-62`) *narrows*
  what can reach `gh`. `filepath.Abs(home)` at `main.go:106` runs before every
  path join and removes a class of relative-path surprise (BUG-080) rather than
  adding one. `Diff`'s new `filepath.Join(home, ".config", "sh-agent")` uses no
  external input. Path traversal from the manifest is unchanged: still one choke
  point at `LoadState`'s `filepath.IsLocal` filter over `Files` (and still not
  over `Repo` — finding 17, left).
- **Authz/authn:** not a service. The one new authorization-shaped predicate is
  `ownedByCaller`, which gates **no operation** — it only chooses the wording of
  an advisory line. `knownCheckout` is unchanged by this range except for the
  removal of a duplicated comment.
- **Crypto:** nothing hand-rolled and nothing added. The release chain
  (`ssh-keygen -Y verify` over `SHA256SUMS` in a pinned namespace with the signer
  compiled in, then `crypto/sha256` over the asset bytes) is untouched except for
  the version gate, which only tightens it. `yamlQuote` is an encoder, not a
  primitive. No finding.
- **Dependencies:** unchanged and best case — `go.mod` still has **zero**
  third-party requires. The three new imports are stdlib: `syscall`
  (pathguard.go), `strconv`/`strings` (source.go); `fmt` was already imported in
  frontmatter.go. `go vet ./...` exits 0 and `gofmt -l cmd internal` is empty, so
  the range builds. `npm audit`: not applicable, no JavaScript in the repository.
  `govulncheck ./...`: **not run** — it queries `vuln.go.dev` and this dispatch
  forbids network; I did not fake it. Residual is small: zero third-party
  modules, so the only surface is the standard library, and this box runs
  go1.27.1, above both advisories `AGENTS.md` records as fixed in
  go1.24.6/go1.25.8. One command closes it.
- **GCP surface:** none in range — no IAM binding, service account,
  `--allow-unauthenticated`, Secret Manager call, or service-account key file.
  The only remote endpoints are GitHub via `gh` and `git`.
- **Docs in the dispatch** (`README.md`, `deploy/local.md`, `deploy/remote.md`,
  `specs/sh-agent/delivery.md`): read whole for this range. They match the code —
  the canonical-tag rule, the "not newer than" refusal, the `--home` gate on the
  BUG-079 note, the ownership-aware remedy, the `knownCheckout` refusal with its
  exact message, and the `keep` line are each described accurately, and
  `remote.md` now tells the operator never to cut a tag with a leading zero.
  One inaccuracy, named above: README's `diff` row says the temporary copies are
  "removed after" without the `tmp.Write` exception.

## Not examined

- `govulncheck ./...` — not run (network prohibited). Exact command above.
- `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` was **not read line by line**: I read the diff's
  new test functions and the two helpers (`plainCopyOf`, `scratchClone`) in full,
  plus `TestRelativeHomeResolvesAgainstTheInvokingDirectory` and
  `internal/harness/audit_test.go` whole. The ~1590 pre-existing lines of
  `main_test.go` and the unchanged `harness_test.go`, `report_test.go`,
  `pathguard_test.go`, `source_test.go` were scanned for secret material only.
  I make no coverage claim beyond the individual tests I name here; the `--tests`
  lens owns the coverage map.
- No verb was executed against any home, real or scratch, and no install was
  performed. The only thing run was `.agents/scratch/security-phase2/mkdirmode.go`
  — a standalone `package main` with no harness import (the Go tool skips
  dot-prefixed directories, so it is invisible to `./...`), plus read-only `stat`,
  `go vet`, `gofmt -l` and `git` queries. `git status --untracked-files=all`
  confirms the working tree is unchanged apart from review artifacts.
  `sh-agent report` was not run, as the dispatch requires.
- The **runtime** behaviour of the two consumer CLIs is out of scope: the YAML
  claims about `\uXXXX` rest on the YAML 1.1/1.2 specifications and on reading
  `DeriveAgy`, not on feeding a generated `agent.md` to the Antigravity CLI. That
  behavioural run is the project's own testing procedure and belongs to the
  verifier.
- The unchanged parts of `report.go` (the redaction list, `Collect`, the push
  path) and of `release.go` (download, `verifyRelease`, `checksumFor`) were not
  re-read in this range; they were audited on 2026-09-18 in
  `reviews/2026-09-18-security-harness.md` and are untouched here apart from the
  two lines in the diff.
- Nothing in `context/`, `skills/`, `agents/`, `commands/` or `rules/` changed in
  this range, so their content was not audited; for `plainCopyOf` I enumerated
  them only for untracked, ignored, symlinked and secret-shaped entries.

## Outcome

Written by the main agent after round 2 of the Phase 2 fix round, in its commit.

- [low] finding 5 not closed — `MkdirAll(…, 0700)` no-ops on a dir every install had already created 0755 — **fixed**: `ConfigDir(home)` (internal/harness/state.go:76) creates the runtime dir 0700 or tightens an existing one (internal/harness/state.go:86), and every writer of it goes through it: `SaveState` (so every install tightens it), `cloneThrowaway`, `Diff`, the release download. `TestInstallMakesTheConfigDirPrivate` (internal/harness/audit_test.go:200) covers a fresh home and a pre-existing 0755 one; `TestThrowawayParentIsPrivate` now pre-creates the dir 0755 — the arrangement the earlier version of the fix could not pass; mutations for the chmod and for `SaveState` bypassing `ConfigDir` fail them. The operator's own dir tightens on their next `install`/`update`.
- [low] relinking is governed by the directory's owner, and root should read `Geteuid` — **fixed**: the advice is keyed on `os.Stat(filepath.Dir(from))` (internal/harness/pathguard.go:141) and `ownedByCaller` compares with `os.Geteuid()` (internal/harness/owned_unix.go:17); the sentence says "with the rights that own its directory". Not pinned at the note level: no non-root test can make a directory it does not own; `TestOwnedByCaller` pins the predicate with a fake `Stat_t`.
- [low] `Diff`'s write-error leak and README's unqualified "removed after" — **fixed** (the `defer`, internal/harness/apply.go:242); README's clause is now true on every path. `plainCopyOf` copying the working tree rather than `git ls-files` — **left** (main agent): a test fixture under `$TMPDIR`, removed by the test; the five directories hold nothing untracked today, and the embed test (`TestEmbedHoldsOnlyTrackedFiles`) fails the build if that changes.
- finding 17's `left` reason — **narrowed** in the merged record: a `state.json` from a dotfiles sync, a restored backup or a shared `--home` is not an attacker with the user's rights; what holds is that `knownCheckout` compares the cwd-walk result against the manifest (a real comparison), and a `Repo` value that names no harness is refused by `ResolveSource` before anything builds.

title: Security review — BUG-078 PATH shadow warning, round 4 (4cdc0b5..28e4747)
body:
# Security review — BUG-078 PATH shadow warning, round 4 (4cdc0b5..28e4747)

Range reviewed: 4cdc0b5..28e4747

Round 4 is the one bounded extra round granted at the three-round cap. It re-reads the range with attention
