# Cold-read review, round 2 — `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-28-update-from-zip.md`   (2026-09-28)

Range reviewed: plan file `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-28-update-from-zip.md` and the code surfaces it names
(`internal/harness/source.go`, `repo.go`, `apply.go`, `state.go`, `cmd/sh-agent/main.go`, `REQUIREMENTS.md` R8/R9,
`.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` ADR list, `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md`, `README.md`,
`.agents/docs/deploy/{local,remote}.md`). Round-1 report read only after forming my own view, per the dispatch.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: design needs revision (round-1's blocker is fixed; one new blocking gap found, one round-1 non-blocker still open)

Round 1's high-severity finding (the symlink-refusal scope contradiction) is resolved: D6 and the current
"Checks run at two scopes" text in `## Interfaces` § `UnpackZip` explicitly scope the symlink/mode/size checks to
the five extracted trees and keep name-safety/entry-count archive-wide, with `.agents/skills` named as the case it
exists to admit. Round 1's findings 2 and 3 (Origin-vs-Dir precedence in `apply.go`, and `status`'s `LoadState`
reordering) are also now spelled out explicitly in the current `## Interfaces` text. Good revision.

But the plan still has a real hole: nothing in it gives a zip-installed home, running a non-release (development)
build with no local checkout, any way to run `status`, `list`, `render`, `diff`, `install`, or a plain `update`
afterward — every one of those calls `harness.ResolveSource` before reaching the command's own logic, and
`ResolveSource`'s only change is to *skip* a `zip:` manifest value as a directory candidate (repo.go:75), never to
succeed because of it. On a machine with no reachable checkout and a dev-versioned binary, `ResolveSource` falls
through to `"harness repo not found and ..."` and the command errors out before printing anything — including
`status`, whose whole job for this feature is to report the zip install. The plan's own Scope line promises
`--from-zip` "from any binary, release or development build," and its Golden-path E2E criterion sidesteps the gap
by using "a binary built with a canonical release version" (release binaries short-circuit `ResolveSource` via the
embedded-files branch regardless of the zip marker) — so the untested path is exactly the dev-build one the scope
claims to support.

## Findings

- **[high / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/repo.go:22-88` (`ResolveSource`) vs. plan `## Interfaces` §
  `ResolveSource` ("skips it as a candidate") — for a zip-installed home whose binary is NOT a release version (no
  local checkout reachable, no `--repo`/`$SH_AGENT_REPO`), every command that calls `ResolveSource` before its own
  logic (`status` at `main.go:184-185`, `diff`, `install`, `list`, `render`, plain `update`) fails with
  `"harness repo not found and ..."` before doing anything. The plan only removes the `zip:` value from the
  candidate walk (repo.go:75); it adds no success path for this case. This directly contradicts Scope's claim that
  `--from-zip` works "from any binary, release or development build" — a dev build that installs from a zip cannot
  run `status` on itself afterward. The plan's own Golden-path E2E (Phase 3) uses a release-versioned build, which
  masks the gap because the release branch of `ResolveSource` never consults the manifest at all. **Must decide**:
  either `ResolveSource` gains a zip-aware success branch (e.g., a `zip:`-prefixed `st.Repo` on a non-release binary
  returns some usable `Source`, or a dedicated error naming `--from-zip` as the way to reinstall), or the plan
  narrows Scope to "release binaries only" for the parts of the feature that run after the initial `--from-zip`
  call, and says so.
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** Plan `## Phases`, Phase 3, task 2's verify clause: `grep -iE 'two ways|no third'
  over the living docs prints nothing that describes the delivery model` — checked against the current text of the
  four docs the plan itself lists as surfaces to touch, and the pattern misses restatements that don't use the
  literal words "two ways" or "no third": `README.md:182` ("`sh-agent` is the only way the harness reaches a
  machine (R8): a checkout ... or a release binary ...") and `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:61` ("it is no longer
  one of the ways in") both restate the two-ways delivery model without the grepped phrase, and would read as clean
  even if left unedited. This is the exact failure mode `AGENTS.md`'s own describing-text rule warns about (grep
  subject nouns, not old wording) — the fix is a broader pattern (e.g. `-iE 'two ways|one way|only way|no third|
  two alternatives'`) or a manual read of the four listed files rather than trusting this one grep as sufficient
  before the Phase-3 checkpoint.
- **[low / confidence: medium, carried from round 1, still open]** `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md:39`,
  `README.md:182`, `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md:45-55`, `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:61` all describe a
  pre-existing, already-shipped "plain copy (no `.git`) — the unpacked zip" install path: download the repo zip by
  hand, unpack it, run `sh-agent install --repo <dir>` from a dev build. That is materially the same operator
  problem this plan solves (no SSH/`gh`), through a different, already-documented mechanism that leaves the tree on
  disk permanently rather than deleting it. The plan lists these four files as surfaces to touch but never states
  whether the old path is deprecated, kept as a parallel fallback, or how the two should be distinguished in the
  docs. Not fixed since round 1.

## Scope

Everything in `## Scope: In` still traces to a D-row or the operator's "approve as written, go all but number 6."
No unrequested endpoint, flag, or configuration surface found. One scope-adjacent observation, not a violation:
Scope's claim "from any binary, release or development build" is broader than what the plan's own design (see
finding 1) currently supports end-to-end — that's a design gap, not unrequested scope, since the operator's request
implies "works after install too," which the plan doesn't yet deliver for a dev build.

## Readiness

1. **BLOCKING** — How does `status` (and every other `ResolveSource`-calling command) work on a zip-installed home
   running a development build with no local checkout? (Finding 1. Two implementers diverge: one leaves it broken
   as an accepted limitation, the other adds a new `ResolveSource` branch — different code, different docs claim.)
2. **NON-BLOCKING** — Is the Phase-3 `grep -iE 'two ways|no third'` check trusted as sufficient, or does whoever
   runs Phase 3 also manually re-read the four listed doc files? (Finding 2. A careful implementer reads the files
   anyway and catches the missed restatements; the plan's stated verify clause alone would not.)
3. **NON-BLOCKING** — Does the docs update (Phase 3) mention the pre-existing plain-copy/unpacked-zip path at all,
   and how it relates to `--from-zip`? (Round-1 finding 4, still open. A reasonable `documentation` pass can resolve
   this inline without asking first, but it's undecided.)

## Not examined

- `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-28-recon-from-zip.md` (the recon this plan cites) — not read; the plan is expected to
  stand on its own for this check.
- `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md` and `reviews/2026-09-28-review-v1.7.0-381e86d-code.md` findings 1-3 (Phase
  4) — not read in detail; Phase 4 is downstream of the Phase 1-3 design questions this review focused on.
- `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` existing test patterns, to check `TestUpdateFromZip`/`TestStatusAfterZip`/
  `TestKnownCheckoutZip` naming conforms to existing convention — not read.
- `README.md` § How it works (the map) itself, and its dashed/solid line convention (AGENTS.md rule 4) — not opened.
- ADR-034's full text (only the portion quoted in `repo.go`'s comments was read) — the plan's claim that ADR-038
  "supersedes ADR-034 for this one path only" was not verified against ADR-034's full wording.
- `internal/harness/embed.go`, `release.go`, `report.go` — not read in this round; not central to the new findings.

body:
# Cold-read review, round 3 (final) — `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-28-update-from-zip.md`   (2026-09-28)

Range reviewed: plan file `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-28-update-from-zip.md` and the code surfaces it names
(`internal/harness/{source.go,repo.go,apply.go,state.go}`, `cmd/sh-agent/main.go`, `embed.go`, `REQUIREMENTS.md`
R8/R9, `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` ADR-030/ADR-031/ADR-037). Rounds 1 and 2's reports read only after
forming my own view, per the dispatch.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: design needs revision — one new blocking gap; rounds 1 and 2's blockers are fixed

Rounds 1 and 2's high-severity findings are resolved in the current plan text: D6 scopes the symlink/mode/size
checks to the five extracted trees while keeping name-safety archive-wide (round 1's `.agents/skills` contradiction);
D7 explicitly decides that a zip-installed dev build with no checkout gets an improved *error* naming the zip
install, not a working `ResolveSource` success path (round 2's gap); D8 settles the plain-copy-vs-zip-place docs
relationship (round 1 finding 4 / round 2 finding 3); the Phase-3 grep in task 2 now includes `only way the
harness|\bways in\b|one of the ways` and a positive control pinned to the exact two lines (`README.md:182`,
`deploy/remote.md:61`) round 2 found the narrower pattern missing. All four of rounds 1-2's open items are closed.

But the plan still has an unresolved, self-contradicting edit to an immutable, operator-locked requirement: it adds
a fifth bulleted item to R9 without deciding what happens to R9's title and its own "no others" clause, both of
which the operator personally dictated as "vital," "set in stone," "rock solid" (ADR-031).

## (1) Gaps

- **[BLOCKING]** R9 is titled "Four procedures, set in stone" and ADR-031 (D1) records the operator's own words
  fixing "the four procedures... Install, Update, Report back, Release — and no others," calling this "vital,"
  wanting it "set it stone... rock solid." The plan's Interfaces section directs: "R9 **Install/Update** gains:
  '**Zip place:** the operator downloads the repository zip by hand and runs `sh-agent update --from-zip <file>`....'"
  — quoted with the same bold-label-plus-colon format as the four existing bullets (`**Install:**`, `**Update:**`,
  `**Report back:**`, `**Release:**`). Read as written, this inserts a fifth bulleted procedure into a section whose
  own title says four and whose own text says "and no others." The plan:
  - never states whether R9's title becomes "Five procedures" (and if so, on what approval — R9's title is not
    among the "REQUIREMENTS text quoted under Interfaces" the Why section says was approved verbatim, only the R8
    first sentence and the R9 bullet text are; the title and the "no others" clause are not shown as edited anywhere
    in the plan);
  - never states whether ADR-031 (D1: "fixes the four procedures... and no others") is amended or superseded
    alongside ADR-038 — ADR-038's own description ("supersedes ADR-034 for this one path only... amends the 'two
    ways, no third' claim in `delivery.md`") names ADR-034 and `delivery.md` but not ADR-031 or R9 itself;
  - never states an alternative reading where the zip material is folded as prose into the existing `Install:`
    and/or `Update:` bullets instead of becoming a labeled fifth bullet, which would keep R9's count at four and
    avoid the contradiction — the literal quoted text (a standalone bold-labeled paragraph) argues against this
    reading, but the plan doesn't rule it out either.

  `TestHarnessMap` (ADR-031 D4) checks that install/update/report are named on the map and pins verbs, not R9's
  bullet count or its title text — nothing in the test suite would catch a shipped REQUIREMENTS.md whose heading
  says "Four... and no others" sitting above five bullets. Two careful implementers diverge here: one pastes the
  approved bullet in and ships R9 self-contradicting itself (literal execution of the approved text, title left
  untouched since not itself approved); the other treats "set in stone... and no others" as still binding, retitles
  the section and treats that retitling as needing its own explicit operator approval before Phase 3 — which the
  plan's Why section, scoped to "the REQUIREMENTS text quoted under Interfaces," does not currently grant. This must
  be decided — and, per this project's own rule, decided by the operator explicitly, before Phase 3 writes to
  `REQUIREMENTS.md` — not inferred by whoever implements the phase.

- **[non-blocking, low]** `internal/harness/state.go:77`'s `ConfigDir(home)` returns `(string, error)`, not a bare
  string. The plan's "Order of work" step 2 pseudocode, `harness.UnpackZip(file, harness.ConfigDir(home))`, reads as
  passing the two-value call directly — not valid Go against `UnpackZip(zipPath, parent string)`. Trivial for an
  implementer to fix (call it, handle the error) and not a design question; noted so nobody copies it literally.

## (2) Scope

Nothing in `## Scope: In` is unattributed: every item traces to the operator's "approve as written, go all but
number 6," and item 7 (the matrix) is explicitly D5, read from the same turn. No second shape for `update`, no
unrequested endpoint, and no configuration surface for a value that never varies was found — `--from-zip`,
`--home`, `--vendor`, `--dry-run` are all flags every command already accepts, not new surface invented for this
feature. Nothing to flag.

## (3) Readiness

1. **BLOCKING** — Does R9's title stay "Four procedures, set in stone," change to five, or does the zip material
   fold into the existing `Install:`/`Update:` bullets instead of becoming a fifth labeled one — and, either way,
   does ADR-031's D1 ("fixes the four procedures... and no others") get amended alongside ADR-038? (Gap above.
   Two implementers ship different REQUIREMENTS.md text, and one of the two ships a document that visibly
   contradicts its own heading and the operator's own "set in stone... and no others" instruction — on a file this
   project treats as immutable without the operator's explicit approval.)

Everything else checked resolves without a question: D6-D8 close rounds 1-2's blocking and non-blocking items;
`apply.go:117-123`'s `Origin`-before-`Dir` precedence, `status()`'s `LoadState` reordering, and `repo.go:75`'s
`ZipPrefix` skip are all now spelled out explicitly enough for a first-pass implementer to follow without guessing;
`reorder()`'s `takesValue` table needing `--from-zip` is named as a task; the five embedded trees
(`context, skills, agents, commands, rules`) match `embed.go:9`'s `//go:embed` directive exactly — the `workflows`
in `source.go:19`'s doc comment is a stale, pre-existing reference to Antigravity's vendor-side deploy layout, not
a source tree, and outside this plan's scope; ADR-038 is the next free ADR number.

## Not examined

- `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md` and `reviews/2026-09-28-review-v1.7.0-381e86d-code.md` findings 1-3
  (Phase 4) — not read in detail; downstream of the Phase 1-3 design question this round focused on, and rounds 1-2
  didn't flag it either.
- `README.md` § How it works (the map) itself, and its dashed/solid line convention — not opened in any of the
  three rounds.
- `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md`'s full text (only grep hits read across rounds).
- `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` existing test conventions, `zip_test.go` (does not exist yet — new file).
- ADR-034's full text (only the portion quoted in `repo.go`'s comments was read, across all three rounds).

# Preflight — v1.10.0   (2026-09-28)

Range reviewed: v1.9.0..e33a4e1

VERDICT: SHIP

Nothing blocks the release:
- no verifier FAIL, BLOCKED or IN PROGRESS log at the head;
- no high security finding, and the security report names no release-diff path under `## Not examined`;
- no REQUEST CHANGES from a code review;
- no REQUIREMENTS violation: R9's zip-place clause is back to the v1.9.0 text, with the operator's words quoted in its note (ADR-041);
- no project agent shadows a review agent.

**How the range got here:**
- `--unverified` was added (`b1ecab3`, ADR-040), gated as a planned v2.0.0, and hardened (`d3e493b`).
- The operator then reversed it before any tag: "Don't complicate things. Just accept the zip. This is a workaround for environments that can't use the normal way." (`c30b8da`, ADR-041).
- The v2.0.0 gate artifacts (`reviews/2026-09-28-*-v1.9.0-b1ecab3*`, `testing/2026-09-28-verify-v2.0.0-gate*.md`) describe code that does not ship. They are kept as records only.
- This gate ran over `v1.9.0..c30b8da`, and its two test lows were fixed in `e33a4e1`.

## Findings and decisions, worst first

| # | Source | Severity / confidence | Finding | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | security (v1.8.0 → v1.10.0) | medium → accepted | A zip without the full signed pair installs `UNVERIFIED` | **Accepted by the operator (ADR-041):** "Just accept the zip." `UNVERIFIED` in the output and `;unverified` in the manifest disclose it. A zip with the pair is still verified, and refused if the check fails. |
| 2 | security (gate) | low / high | Extra words after `update --from-zip <file>` are ignored silently | **Left, by the operator's decision.** ADR-041 names stray-argument refusals among the hardening the operator stopped. The worst case installs `UNVERIFIED`, the documented behaviour. |
| 3 | security (v1.9.0 gate, carried) | low / high | An older signed release's zip installs `VERIFIED`; there is no downgrade check | **Accepted (ADR-039, ADR-041):** a zip place has no other way to roll back, and the first line names the release. |
| 4 | code (gate) | low / medium | No end-to-end test for a half pair | Fixed in `e33a4e1`: `TestUpdateFromZipHalfPairSaysUnverified`. Must-fail seen. |
| 5 | code (gate) | low / medium | `TestUnpackZipLateRefusalCreatesNoParent` asserted no refusal text | Fixed in `e33a4e1`. Must-fail seen. |

## Reviews

- **Code:** `reviews/2026-09-28-review-v1.9.0-c30b8da-code.md` (opus, APPROVE WITH NITS; `## Outcome`). The `e33a4e1` change adds tests only, and its must-fails are recorded there.
- **Security:** `reviews/2026-09-28-security-v1.9.0-c30b8da.md` (FINDINGS, one low; `## Outcome`).
- **Docs:** `reviews/2026-09-28-review-v1.9.0-c30b8da-docs.md` (APPROVE, no findings).

## Verification

`testing/2026-09-28-verify-v1.10.0-gate-r2.md`, PASS over `v1.9.0..e33a4e1`:
- gofmt and vet are clean;
- `go test -race`: 171 pass, 0 fail, 0 skip;
- govulncheck is clean;
- scratch install: drift none, and GANNET is untruncated on both vendors.

The first gate log (`verify-v1.10.0-gate.md`, PASS at `c30b8da`, 170 pass) says the range added and removed no tests. That is inaccurate: tests were added in `b1ecab3`/`d3e493b` and some were removed in `c30b8da`, netting 170. Its PASS stands.

## Trail freshness

- **Newest change entry:** `changes/2026-09-28-2054-v1.10.0-gate-tests.md`. With `2044-zip-accepts`, `2020-v2.0.0-gate-fixes` and `2010-unverified-flag`, it covers the range.
- **Dates:** none is in the future.
- **Append-only:** `changes/` gained additions only. `DECISIONS.md` gained ADR-040 and ADR-041. Its one changed line is ADR-039's heading, now marked "its one-file refusal superseded by ADR-041"; ADR-040's heading is marked "Superseded by ADR-041".
- **ROADMAP.md** "Now" and **TODO.md** are empty.

## Version

MINOR, v1.10.0. Relative to v1.9.0, a zip with only one of the two files now installs `UNVERIFIED` instead of being refused. Nothing becomes required, and nothing an existing deployment must react to.

## What was not checked

- **macOS:** the zip-place path has not run there.
- **The real release zip:** verifying it with the real key is release step 3b on this host, and the operator smoke check on each machine.
- **The skill matrix and CLI-start sandbox runs:** `context/`, `agents/` and `skills/` did not change in this range.

title: Review — a9717cc-f916e35-code (2026-09-28)
body:
# Review — a9717cc-f916e35-code   (2026-09-28)

Range reviewed: a9717cc..f916e35

Scope: this is round 2 of the v1.7.0 gate, over one commit (f916e35). It fixes three round-1 findings. I read the three non-trail edits in full: `AGENTS.md:66`, `agents/changelog.md:94` and `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:40`. I read two trail files in full: the change entry and the verification log `testing/2026-09-28-verify-v1.7.0-gate-fixes.md`. I checked the fixes against the round-1 reports: `reviews/2026-09-28-review-v1.6.0-a9717cc-code.md` (finding 1) and `reviews/2026-09-28-security-v1.6.0-a9717cc.md` (medium, low). To test whether the new `AGENTS.md` bullet can be followed, I read the gate-fix run's own agy artefacts. They are still on disk in the sandbox home `.agents/scratch/tsn/.gemini/antigravity-cli/`: `log/cli-20260928_153137.log` and `conversations/4b0948d6-….db`, strings only.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

All three fixes close the substance of their findings, and none breaks anything. The sandbox rule no longer hands a sandbox an always-proceed grant over real checkouts. The gate-fix run shows the CLI loaded the narrow list (`toolPermission=request-review`, the ten allow entries) and ran the probe's `ls` and `find` through it. However, the rule as written prescribes `list_dir(*)`, and agy 1.2.8 rejects that entry: "ignoring invalid allow entry "list_dir(*)": unknown action "list_dir"". The run's own log shows the rejection, but the verification log missed it, because the check the rule names reads stderr only. Its phrase "command(<name>) for each read-only command" also let the evidence run grant `find`, `git` and `sed`. Those commands are not read-only: `find -exec` and `sed -i` can run or write anything. The preflight fix adds `sk-ant-` and the two file names, but not the `refresh_token` pattern the security finding asked for, and nothing records why. All three findings are low. None blocks.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: high]** `AGENTS.md:66`: the prescribed read-only list names `list_dir(*)`, which agy 1.2.8 does not accept.
  - **Evidence:** the gate-fix run's log, `.agents/scratch/tsn/.gemini/antigravity-cli/log/cli-20260928_153137.log:157`, reads `W0928 15:31:40.063519 … permission_grant_store.go:431] ignoring invalid allow entry "list_dir(*)": unknown action "list_dir" in grant string: "list_dir(*)"`.
  - **Why the check missed it:** the rule's detection step is "checked for the "auto-denied" stderr line". The verification log's evidence is "stderr empty". But this warning goes to `cli.log`, not stderr. The run passed only because the model listed directories with `command(ls)` and `command(find)`; the transcript shows `ls -la` and `find .agents …` calls. A run whose model reaches for the directory-listing tool would get an auto-denied line, so the stderr check would catch that failure afterwards. It would not catch it beforehand.
  - **Same entry elsewhere:** `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md:14` carries the same entry. That line predates this range.
  - **Fix:** drop `list_dir(*)` from the bullet, or replace it with the action name agy's grant store accepts. That name was not determined here. Also add to the bullet that the run's `cli.log` is grepped for `invalid allow entry` before its output counts. This is the rule's own principle: a run proves its setup.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `AGENTS.md:66`: "`command(<name>)` for each read-only command" grants by command name. The evidence run read that phrase as "commands used for reading" and granted `command(find)`, `command(git)` and `command(sed)` (`cli.log:100`).
  - **How it fails:** under the threat model of the security finding, instruction-shaped text reaching the run is the risk. `find … -exec sh -c '…'` is an arbitrary shell. `sed -i` writes any file the uid can write. `git` can commit, change config or push, and ssh reads `~/.ssh` from the passwd home, not `$HOME`. If agy matches `command(x)` on argv[0], which is inferred and not verified here, the narrow list is close to `command(*)` whenever `find` is on it.
  - **Why low:** it is still far narrower than `always-proceed`, and the trust list is the scratch clone only.
  - **Fix:** say that a `command(<name>)` grant covers every argument. Name only commands that have no write or exec mode, such as `ls`, `cat`, `head`, `wc` and `grep`. If a probe needs `git log`, use an argument-scoped `command(git log)`, if agy supports that form. The security lens should confirm the matching semantics.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:40`: the round-1 security remediation asked for `sk-ant-` **and** `refresh_token` in the fallback scan. Only `sk-ant-` was added. A JSON `"refresh_token": "…"` line does not match the existing `token=`.
  - **What still covers it:** the new stop-by-name on `antigravity-oauth-token` and `.credentials.json` covers those two files under their own names.
  - **The gap:** the content scan, the live control on this gitleaks-less host, still misses a refresh token copied or pasted under any other name. The change entry says the scan "gains `sk-ant-`, `.credentials.json` and `antigravity-oauth-token`", which is accurate, but it does not record the omission as a rebuttal.
  - **Fix:** add `refresh_token` to the pattern list. If it is left out on purpose, record why in the security report's `## Outcome`.

Checked and clean:
- **Code-review finding 1 (`agents/changelog.md:94`): closed.** The Output line now lists "any date-only file name (a dispatch that gave no `HHMM`)", which agrees with rule 1 at `:22`. The verification log says honestly that the control did not fail (2 of 2 either way) and that the fix aligns the file rather than changing behaviour. That is the right reading. `tools:` is unchanged, so `toolMap` is not affected.
- **Security medium (`AGENTS.md:66`): closed in substance.**
  - Remediation 1 is met. The file is written for the run, with a narrow `permissions.allow`, and `trustedWorkspaces` holds the scratch clone only. The log confirms `workspaceDirs=[…/tsn-probe/e2e1/demo]` and `ApplyProjectPermissionGrants: no grants`.
  - Remediation 3 is met. The settings file is deleted with the token; `settings.json` and `antigravity-oauth-token` are both absent from `.agents/scratch/tsn/.gemini/antigravity-cli/` (names listed).
  - Remediation 2 is partly met. The bullet now says the real file "approves every tool". The reconciliation with guide § 5 did not happen, and no Outcome records it. `testing/guide.md:141` still tells a real-home headless check to use "the real settings' `permissions.allow` entries", a list the real file no longer has, according to the security report. That sentence is about the real home, not the sandbox, and predates this range. It is deferred in `handoffs/2026-09-28-open-items.md` per the security report, so it is not a finding against this diff.
- **Sandbox bullet, restatements:** a grep for `antigravity-cli/settings`, `always-proceed`, `trustedWorkspaces`, `toolPermission` and `copied token` found no copy of the old "carries the real home's settings.json" wording in `context/`, `skills/`, `agents/`, `commands/`, `rules/`, `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, the testing guide, the skill matrix, the 2026-09-03 sandbox log or `deploy/`.
- **Preflight restatements:** `ya29` appears in `skills/`, `context/`, `agents/`, `commands/`, `rules/`, `README.md` and `AGENTS.md` only at `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:40`. Step 6 re-runs it by reference, so there is no second list to update.
- **Context size:** `context/` is not touched, so `TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock` is not affected.
- **BUG-092:** the change entry and the verification log agree on the incident: a truncated `sed` range, `cd ""`, and a fake change entry deleted by name. The fixture assertion `check_demo` is said to be validated in both states. I did not re-run it.

## Criteria

1. **Dead code: pass.** The range is prose only, and no text is orphaned.
2. **Flow tracing: pass, with findings 1 and 2.** I traced the settings file from the rule to what the CLI loaded (`cli.log:100`), to what it rejected (`:157`), and to the tool calls the run made (transcript). I traced the changelog reply flag from rule 1 to the Output list. I traced the preflight patterns to Step 6's re-run.
3. **Standards conformance: pass, with finding 3.** No restatement of a changed rule is left standing, and project rules are respected: scratch only, real home untouched. Remediation 2's guide reconciliation is not done, but the guide text it names is pre-existing and deferred.
4. **Directory layout: pass.** The new files are a bug record, a change entry and a testing log, each in its trail directory.
5. **Simplicity (DIY-except-security): pass.** There is no code and no dependency. The security surface is permission configuration, not a hand-rolled primitive.
6. **Decoupling: pass.** Each fix is confined to the file that owns the rule.

## Not examined

- **agy's `command(<name>)` matching semantics:** argv[0] versus the full command line, and whether an argument-scoped form exists. I inferred them and did not test them. No live agy run was made by this review.
- **Probe 2's transcripts** (changelog `claude -p` runs under `~/.claude/projects/`) and the `check_demo` script in `.agents/scratch/tsn-probe/lib.sh`: not read. The 2-of-2 figures come from the verification log.
- **The BUG-092 record body and its INDEX row:** only their presence in the commit was checked.
- **The round-1 reports' `## Outcome` sections:** none exists yet in the three untracked round-1 reports. That is the main agent's step and is outside this range.
- **Go checks:** there is no Go change, so `go test`, `sh-agent install` and `status` were not run here.

# Review — a9717cc-f916e35-docs   (2026-09-28)

Range reviewed: a9717cc..f916e35

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

The three changed statements are each consistent with the living docs the dispatch named. No stale restatement of the old sandbox-settings wording survives (it had exactly one home, `AGENTS.md`, and it is gone from there and appears nowhere else). No stale restatement of the old, shorter secret-shaped-path list survives either — `skills/preflight/SKILL.md` is the only place that enumerated it. The one thing worth a line: the generic Git rule in `context/AGENTS.md` (the single source deployed to every project) was not grown alongside `skills/preflight/SKILL.md`'s project-specific list, so a reader of the generic rule alone would not know a bare CLI token file (no `.json`, no recognizable extension) is also secret-shaped — flagged below as a disagreement, not a blocking defect, since the two lists serve different scopes (every project vs. this repo's own testing artifacts).

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `context/AGENTS.md:45` vs `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:40` — the global Git rule's secret-shaped-path list (`.env*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `*.tfvars`, `*.tfstate`, credential JSON) was not extended when this repo's own commit-staging rule grew to add "a CLI token file (`antigravity-oauth-token`)" as a new category. `antigravity-oauth-token` has no filename pattern matching any entry in the generic list (it is not `credential JSON`, nor `.env*`/`*.pem`/`*.key`/`*.tfvars`/`*.tfstate`) — a project relying only on the global rule's parenthetical would not recognize a bare-token CLI credential file as a stop-the-commit case. Since `context/AGENTS.md` is deployed verbatim to every project, and preflight's own list just demonstrated the generic list is incomplete, either widen the global rule's parenthetical (e.g. add "or a bare CLI token file") or note in `skills/preflight/SKILL.md` that this item is project-specific and not assumed to generalize. Not a blocking defect — the two rules are at different scopes and neither literally contradicts the other — but it is the kind of gap review-standards § 3 asks to surface when a restatement grows in one place and not its sibling.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — n/a — docs lens
2. Flow tracing — n/a — docs lens
3. Standards conformance — n/a — docs lens
4. Directory layout — n/a — docs lens
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — n/a — docs lens
6. Decoupling — n/a — docs lens

## Per-statement disposition

1. **Sandbox settings.json (`AGENTS.md:66`).** Old wording ("carries the real home's `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json`") searched across `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `context/`, `agents/`, `commands/`, `rules/`, `skills/` (minus `VENDORED.md` entries), `.agents/docs/specs/`, `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md`, `.agents/docs/deploy/`. No hit anywhere else — `dropped: AGENTS.md:66 (old)`, cleanly replaced, no orphaned restatement. `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md` § 4 (Sandbox start of each CLI, lines 114–126) describes only the credential-file-copy-and-delete procedure, never the settings.json content, so it neither restates the old claim nor needed updating. `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md:140–142` (§ 5, Real-home smoke checks) says a headless Antigravity check "uses the real settings' `permissions.allow` entries" — this is the real-home case, a different scope from the sandbox-home case the diff changed, and is not stale.

2. **Secret-shaped path list / fallback scan patterns (`skills/preflight/SKILL.md:40`).** Old shorter list (`.env*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `*.tfvars`, `*.tfstate`, credential JSON / `PRIVATE KEY`, `-----BEGIN`, `AKIA`, `AIza`, `ya29.`, `token=`, `password=`) searched the same file set. `context/AGENTS.md:45` still carries the shorter, generic version — see Finding above (flagged as a disagreement, not a stale copy of THIS diff's exact old text, since `context/AGENTS.md` was never touched by this range and the two lists were never identical to begin with — preflight's list has always had `gitleaks`-plus-fallback items the global rule never enumerated). `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md:66` and `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md:53` carry a much larger, already-inclusive needle list (report-redaction shapes) that already included `sk-ant-` before this diff — no staleness there, different mechanism (report redaction vs. commit-time scan). No other file in scope lists these patterns.

3. **changelog.md Output — date-only file name (`agents/changelog.md:94`).** This is consistent with, not contradicted by, `agents/changelog.md:22` ("A dispatch that gives only a date gets a date-only file name, flagged in your reply") — the Output section addition just catches the Output line up to a rule the Instructions section already stated. `skills/init-project/SKILL.md:24,108` and `skills/handoff/SKILL.md:43` independently describe date-only names for a different purpose (counting old entries, not flagging a live dispatch) and are unaffected. No stale or disagreeing restatement found.

title: Review — signed-zip-code, round 2 (2026-09-28)
body:
# Review — signed-zip-code, round 2   (2026-09-28)

Range reviewed: 0b762db..worktree (`git diff 0b762db`: README.md, AGENTS.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, ROADMAP.md, DECISIONS.md ADR-039, deploy/remote.md, specs/sh-agent/delivery.md, cmd/sh-agent/{main.go,zip_test.go}, internal/harness/{release.go,zip.go,zip_test.go}; plus the untracked plan `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-28-signed-zip.md`, read by grep)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

Round 1's three blocking items are fixed. The map, its `linkStyle` indices and the six-asset count are all right, and the VERIFIED path now has a test that fails under the `verifiedTag` mutation (reproduced below). Two problems remain.

1. **Release step 5 runs too late, and only on linux/amd64.** It runs after `gh release upload`, so the binary it checks has already shipped. That contradicts ADR-039's "so a binary built with a stray test signer never ships". It also executes `./sh-agent-linux-amd64` unconditionally, which cannot run on a Mac or an arm64 box that holds the signing key.
2. **Security finding 2 is fixed in code but not pinned.** Re-inserting the exact old move-away hint compiles and leaves every test green. The only negative assertion sits on the checksum-mismatch path, which never carried the hint.

The stale-pair remedy from round-1 finding 4 still gives the wrong advice: it tells the operator to fetch the OLD release's zip.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:171-173` (new step 5) runs after step 4's `gh release create` and `gh release upload` loop (lines 165-169).
  - **Timing:** by the time the check runs, the assets are public. A failure there means a release with a bad signer is already published. ADR-039 Consequences (`DECISIONS.md`, "so a binary built with a stray test signer never ships") and the step's own comment ("never ships") claim the opposite.
  - **Host:** the step executes `./sh-agent-linux-amd64`. This guide lets a release be cut on any machine holding the signing key (§ Releases, line 96; line 215 "before that machine cuts a release"), and the places include two Macs. On darwin/arm64 or linux/arm64 the command fails with an exec format error, and the gate stops only after the publish.
  - **Fix:** move step 5 between step 3 (sign) and step 4 (release create). Run the binary that matches the host, for example `./sh-agent-$(go env GOOS)-$(go env GOARCH)`, since all three share one `-ldflags`. Keep the output going into a file.
  - The rest of step 5 is sound. It writes to `../zipcheck.out`, not a pipe. `--dry-run` runs the same `UnpackZip` check, so it prints the trust line. `SHA256SUMS`/`.sig` sit in the same directory as the zip, which is the cwd. The dry run on the fresh `../zipcheck` home unpacks under the system temp directory (main.go:1057-1060).

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/zip_test.go:694` and `internal/harness/release.go:447-449`: removing security finding 2's hint is not pinned by any test.
  - **Mutation:** in the scratch copy `.agents/scratch/rev2-signed-zip/tree`, the target text occurred exactly once. I made the `verifySignedSums` error return in `VerifyZipSums` `fmt.Errorf("%w (move SHA256SUMS and SHA256SUMS.sig out of %s to install the zip unverified on purpose)", err, dir)`, which is security's quoted round-1 text.
  - **Result:** `go vet` was clean, so the mutation compiled. Every `TestUpdateFromZip*` test and `TestVerifyZipSums` PASSED under `-v`. I restored from the saved copy, and `cmp` confirmed the restore.
  - **Why the test cannot catch it:** the `move SHA256SUMS` needle is checked only after the checksum-mismatch run, and the mismatch error never carried the hint, even in round 1. The paths that did carry it are the bad signature (`TestUpdateFromZipForeignSignatureRefused`, the `foreign key` subtest) and a missing `SHA256SUMS`. Those assert only a positive substring.
  - Per the global DoD, a finding is fixed only when each trigger it names has a test that fails without the fix. Security named two triggers: signature failure and `.sig` without `SHA256SUMS`.
  - **Fix:** assert that no `move` hint appears on the foreign-signature refusal and on a `.sig`-only folder. Neither case exists as a unit test yet; see round-1 low 6.

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/release.go:453-455`: the stale-pair remedy is still wrong. This is round-1 finding 4, only half fixed.
  - **The case:** genuine v1.9.0 `SHA256SUMS`/`.sig` left in `~/Downloads`, next to a newly downloaded `styrman-harness-v1.9.1.zip` (the browser saved the new pair as `SHA256SUMS (1)`). The error reads: `the signed SHA256SUMS beside it are release v1.9.0's and do not list styrman-harness-v1.9.1.zip: no line names styrman-harness-v1.9.1.zip — download that release's own zip, under its own name`.
  - **Why it is wrong:** "that release" is v1.9.0, so the advice is to fetch and install the OLDER release. That is a silent downgrade for an operator, or an agent, that follows tool output. The advice fits only the renamed-zip case, which is the one the unit test covers (`renamed zip`, which asserts `no line names`).
  - **Missing test:** the unit case round 1 asked for, sums signed for tag A beside a zip named for tag B, was not added.
  - **Fix:** name both possibilities, for example "download the SHA256SUMS and SHA256SUMS.sig of the release this zip belongs to, or that release's zip under its own name". Or parse `styrman-harness-(vX.Y.Z).zip` from the file name, and when it names a different version than the sums, say the sums are stale. Add the tag-A/tag-B case.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-28-signed-zip.md:106` (D7) still says "The error names the files, so the operator can move them away to install unverified on purpose". That is the hint security finding 2 removed, and ADR-039 says the messages "never suggest removing the checksums". This is the active plan, which the next session reads on resume, and no later D-entry supersedes it. **Fix:** append a D-entry that withdraws D7's last sentence and cites the security review. Do not edit D7 in place if the log is append-only.

- **[low / confidence: high]** ADR-039 says "The messages name what to download", but the refusals that mean tampering do not. `SHA256SUMS signature does not verify (…)`, `<zip> has no SHA256SUMS`, `<zip> has no SHA256SUMS.sig` and the no-marker error carry no remedy at all. Security finding 2's first remediation bullet ("say the files are not genuine and to download the release's three files again") was not applied. **Fix:** either wrap those errors in `VerifyZipSums` with that sentence, or narrow the ADR's claim.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/release.go:414-425`: the `ErrZipUnsigned` doc comment was split from its declaration. `SwapReleaseSigner` was inserted between them, so `SwapReleaseSigner`'s godoc now opens with "ErrZipUnsigned: no SHA256SUMS … The caller installs it marked UNVERIFIED.", and the exported `ErrZipUnsigned` (line 425) has no doc. This is the describing-text rule. **Fix:** move the two comment lines back above `var ErrZipUnsigned`.

## Round-1 findings — status

1. **Map, high: FIXED.**
   - `README.md:20` relabels the Releases node "platform binaries + release zip + signed SHA256SUMS".
   - `:37` relabels the preflight edge "signed binaries and zip".
   - `:41` adds the dashed `releases -. "release zip + signed SHA256SUMS, by hand; verified" .-> zipPlace`.
   - The unverified `main`-zip line at `:40` is kept.
   - **`linkStyle` checked against the edge order.** There are 21 edges, indices 0-20:
     - 0 edit→ship
     - 1 ship→harnessRepo
     - 2 ship→preflight
     - 3 preflight→harnessRepo
     - 4 preflight→releases
     - 5 harnessRepo→checkoutPlace
     - 6 releases→binaryPlace
     - 7 harnessRepo→zipPlace
     - 8 releases→zipPlace
     - 9-11 the three →installer edges
     - 12 installer→homeFiles
     - 13 homeFiles→sessions
     - 14-20 the report loop
   - Teal `0,1,5,6,7,8`, plum `2,3,4`, indigo `9-13` and amber `14-20` cover every index exactly once. The new edge is teal like its sibling releases→binaryPlace. Every pre-change index shifted by exactly +1 from index 8 on.
   - The rest of finding 1 is fixed too:
     - `AGENTS.md:14` rule 2 now says "binaries and a zip of its tree, with signed checksums";
     - README Release (`:65`) is fixed;
     - remote.md now says "all six" (`:170`) and "the six assets" (`:182`).
   - One gap: `TestHarnessMap` still does not pin labels, so a future relabel drift stays uncaught. That is the existing design, not a finding.
2. **VERIFIED path untested, medium: FIXED AND TESTED.** `TestUpdateFromZipVerifiedAndTampered` (`cmd/sh-agent/zip_test.go:640`) goes through `harness.SwapReleaseSigner`. I reproduced the mutation in a scratch copy: `verifiedTag = tag` occurred once, was replaced with `_ = tag`, compiled, and made the test fail at `zip_test.go:682` ("a verified zip does not say so"). The file was restored from a saved copy and `cmp` matched. The tampered half flips one byte, gets `checksum mismatch`, and asserts an empty home.
3. **Remedy messages, medium: PARTLY FIXED.**
   - No "move the sums away" hint remains in the code (`grep` over `cmd`, `internal`, README, AGENTS, REQUIREMENTS, ADRs, deploy, specs, context, skills, agents).
   - Three gaps remain, each a finding above:
     - the plan's D7 still states the hint;
     - the removal has no test that fails without it;
     - the stale-pair message now gives downgrade advice.

Round-1 lows:
- `AGENTS.md`/README "binaries with signed checksums": fixed.
- R9's one-file wording and the missing `.sig`-only test: not addressed. They are not re-raised, but the `.sig`-only test is now also needed by the second finding.

## Other checks asked for
- **ADR-039's Open bullet** (`DECISIONS.md`, Consequences) records honestly that a zip with nothing beside it still installs with exit 0. It marks this as an operator question requiring an R9 change, and it cites the security medium. This matches the security report's first finding, and nothing in the diff claims otherwise. README's zip section says `main` zips are unsigned. delivery.md now states the verified/unverified split once, and README/AGENTS point to it: rule 6 holds.
- **REQUIREMENTS R9** was edited with a recorded approval ("All approved", ADR-039).
- **Gates:** `gofmt -l cmd internal` is clean, `go vet ./...` is clean, and `go test -race -count=1 ./...` passes for all three packages. No `t.Parallel` is in `cmd/sh-agent`, so the global signer swap does not race.

## Criteria
1. **Dead code: pass.** `SwapReleaseSigner` has a caller (the CLI test), and `ErrZipUnsigned` is used by main.go. Nothing is orphaned.
2. **Flow tracing: pass with gaps.** `updateFromZip` → `UnpackZip(check)` → `VerifyZipSums` → `verifySignedSums`/`checksumFor` is consistent, `ErrZipUnsigned` maps to UNVERIFIED, and every other error refuses before any write. The gaps: one test cannot fail (the second finding), and one remedy message is wrong (the third finding).
3. **Standards conformance: fail (low/medium).** Restatements left standing: the plan's D7, and ADR-039's "messages name what to download". The godoc is split from its identifier. The formatting and vet gates are verified as run.
4. **Directory layout: pass.** Nothing new lands outside the existing files.
5. **Simplicity (DIY-except-security): pass.** Signatures use OpenSSH `ssh-keygen -Y`, checksums use stdlib `sha256`, and there is no new dependency. `SwapReleaseSigner` is an exported test hook in production code. It is reachable only inside this module (`internal/`), and security round 1 already discussed the hook trade-off, so it is not a finding here.
6. **Decoupling: pass.** `UnpackZip` takes a plain `func(sum string) error`, and verification lives in `release.go`.

## Not examined
- The plan file, the cold-read reviews and the E2E/verify logs were read only through grep. I did not check the plan's tick state against the work.
- The BUG-094 record and `INDEX.md` diffs were not read in this round.
- The release procedure was not executed. The step 5 finding comes from reading the guide's step order and host assumptions, not from a run on a Mac.
- macOS was not examined.

# Review — time-sortable-names-code (2026-09-28)

Range reviewed: `17fa89b..e5a49d4`, limited to `-- context agents skills` (5 files, 114 diff lines: `agents/changelog.md`, `context/AGENTS.md`, `skills/handoff/SKILL.md`, `skills/init-project/SKILL.md`, `skills/preflight/SKILL.md`)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

The change (switching `handoffs/` and `changes/` filenames from `YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md` to `YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM-<slug>.md`) is small, self-consistent across the files it touches, and verified: `TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock` still passes (20498/22000 bytes), a scratch `sh-agent install`/`status` cycle shows 0 drift, and the new date-only-name counting regex in `init-project/SKILL.md` was hand-tested and counts correctly. One real cross-reference was missed: `skills/handoff/SKILL.md` Step 3 still tells the agent to capture a single `date +%F` value and "use that date everywhere below," but Step 5 (changed in this diff) now needs a `date +%F-%H%M` stamp — the instruction wasn't updated to match its own consequence.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/handoff/SKILL.md:62` vs `:145` — Step 3.1 says "Run `date +%F` and use that date everywhere below — never a date from memory," but Step 5's save command (changed in this diff, e5a49d4) now computes `$(date +%F-%H%M)`, a different value than what Step 3.1 told the agent to capture and reuse. The frontmatter (`:74`) and heading (`:76`) templates still use plain `YYYY-MM-DD`, so as written there are now two different "the date" values in the same document with no instruction telling the agent which one to capture when, or to derive the filename stamp from the same captured moment rather than a fresh `date` call that could tick over to a new day relative to the frontmatter/heading date in a long-running session. This is the same class of gap the project's own describing-text rule (`context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules, and review-standards §3) is meant to catch: a rule changed in one place (Step 5) whose sibling restatement (Step 3.1) wasn't updated with it. Fix: either have Step 3.1 capture the full `date +%F-%H%M` stamp up front and Step 5 reuse it, or explicitly say Step 5 recomputes a fresh timestamp for the filename only.

- **[none — verified fine]** `skills/init-project/SKILL.md:24` — the new date-only-name counting pipeline (`grep -E '^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}-' | grep -vcE '^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{4}-'`) was hand-tested against a mix of date-only and timed filenames (including a slug that itself starts with 4 digits) and counts correctly (2 of 4 files, the two true date-only names). No finding.

## Criteria

1. **Dead code** — pass. No functions/files orphaned; this is a docs/skill-prose change only.
2. **Flow tracing** — one gap found (the finding above): the handoff skill's own internal cross-reference between "capture the date once" (Step 3) and "the filename now needs a timestamp" (Step 5) wasn't reconciled. Everywhere else the stamp threads correctly: `agents/changelog.md` description → dispatch instruction in `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:86` both say "the stamp from `date +%F-%H%M`"; `agents/changelog.md`'s own fallback logic (no Bash tool available to the agent, confirmed via its unchanged `tools:` line) was correctly adjusted to drop the old "run `date +%F` yourself" fallback (which was never actually executable by this agent) in favor of filesystem-context inference or `DATE-UNKNOWN`.
3. **Standards conformance** — pass except the Finding above. Grepped `YYYY-MM-DD` and `date +%F` across `context/`, `agents/`, `skills/`, `commands/`, `rules/`, `README.md`: all other restatements (reviews/, plans/, testing/, retros/ naming; `date +%F` used for other artifact types) are legitimately out of this change's scope (the commit history / plan names only `handoffs/` and `changes/` as the phase-1/phase-2 target), and none of them claim the old `changes/`/`handoffs/` format.
4. **Directory layout** — n/a, no new files; edits land in the same files that already owned this convention.
5. **Simplicity / DIY-except-security** — pass. Pure shell `date`/`grep`, no new dependency, no crypto/auth surface touched.
6. **Decoupling** — pass. Each file edited independently states the convention for its own agent/skill; no shared helper needed, consistent with this repo's "file drop, never code" rule for skill/agent changes.

## Not examined

- `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-28-time-sortable-trail-names.md` and `ROADMAP.md` — modified in this range per `git status` but excluded by the dispatch's path filter (`-- context agents skills`); not reviewed here.
- `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-28-verify-time-sortable-names-phase-2.md` — untracked, also outside the path filter; not reviewed.
- Behavioural verification (an actual dispatch of `changelog` or `/handoff` exercising the new stamp end-to-end) was not run by this reviewer — only the static file-drop consistency and the `install`/`status` drift check were exercised, per the tool-call budget for this dispatch.

## Outcome

- Finding 1 (`skills/handoff/SKILL.md:62` vs `:145`): fixed. Step 3.1 now reads "Run `date +%F` and use that date everywhere below, and `date +%F-%H%M` for the handoff's file name (Step 5)". It was fixed together with the docs-lens finding 1 (`reviews/2026-09-28-review-time-sortable-names-docs.md`), plan D5.

title: Review — update-from-zip-code (2026-09-28)
body:
# Review — update-from-zip-code   (2026-09-28)

Range reviewed: 1cb2608..worktree (`git diff 1cb2608` plus the untracked `internal/harness/zip.go`, `internal/harness/zip_test.go`, `cmd/sh-agent/zip_test.go`)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

The worst problem is that BUG-093 is only half fixed. `UnpackZip` creates `~/.config/sh-agent` once the NAMES pass, and five refusals come after that point: a symlink, a non-regular mode, a duplicate name, the size limits, and the final `IsRepo`. A zip refused for any of them still leaves an empty `~/.config/sh-agent` on a fresh home. I reproduced this with the CLI for the symlink and duplicate-name cases. The code comments claim the opposite, and no test can see it: the internal refusal tests pass a parent that already exists. Second, an EMPTY `--from-zip` value (`--from-zip "$ZIP"` with the variable unset, or `--from-zip=`) falls through to the normal `update`. On a release binary that downloads and replaces the binary, which is the opposite of what the flag promises, and it does so even with `--dry-run`. I reproduced this in a scratch home. Third, the "--from-zip belongs to update" refusal sits after the `uninstall`/`report`/`version` switch, so `uninstall --from-zip x` uninstalls. gofmt, vet and `go test -race ./...` are clean.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/zip.go:57-63` (parent created) vs `:90-93`, `:95-98`, `:100-101`, `:104-105` (later refusals). This is a recurrence of BUG-093 ("a command that can refuse its input creates nothing before the refusal point").
  - The code calls `os.MkdirAll(parent)` after the name pass. It then refuses on symlink, non-regular mode, duplicate name (the `O_EXCL` failure in `unpackFile`), per-file or total size, and the final `IsRepo`. The deferred cleanup removes only `tmp`, never the parent it created.
  - Reproduced with the scratch binary `.agents/scratch/rv-zip/sh-agent` (`-X main.version=v0.0.1`) and a fresh home for each case. `update --from-zip sym.zip` exits 1 and leaves `home/.config/sh-agent`; `dup.zip` leaves the same.
  - Two comments overclaim and are stale under the describing-text rule: `zip.go:57-58` ("a refused zip leaves nothing behind, not even the directory") and the `updateFromZip` comment in `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` ("so a refused zip writes nothing").
  - Tests that pass for the wrong reason: every refusal case in `TestUnpackZipRefuses`, `TestUnpackZipLimits`, `TestUnpackZipRefusesDuplicateName` and `TestUnpackZipNotHarness` passes `parent := t.TempDir()`, which already exists, and checks only `zip-*`. They cannot observe parent creation. The only fresh-home CLI test, `TestUpdateFromZipRefusedZipWritesNothing`, covers just the name refusal.
  - Fix, two parts:
    - Move the mode and duplicate-name checks into the first pass over `zr.File`. Both are known from the headers.
    - For the checks that need content (size, `IsRepo`), record whether `parent` existed before `MkdirAll` and remove it on error when this call created it.
  - Add fresh-home CLI tests for a symlink, a duplicate name and an oversize file. Each asserts the home is empty.

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:130` (`if *fromZip != ""`). An empty value is treated as "flag absent".
  - `sh-agent update --from-zip "$ZIP"` with `$ZIP` unset, or `--from-zip=`, runs the ordinary `update`. On a release binary that is `UpdateFromRelease`: it downloads the newest release and replaces `~/.local/bin/sh-agent`. That contradicts the stated contract "nothing is fetched and the binary itself is not replaced" (R9 zip-place sub-bullet; README § Install from a zip).
  - Reproduced: `update --from-zip= --home <scratch> --dry-run` printed `downloading sh-agent-linux-amd64 v1.7.0` / `verified and installed …` and wrote `<scratch>/.local/bin/sh-agent`. The real `~/.local/bin/sh-agent` was untouched (mtime 16:03, before the run).
  - Fix: detect the flag was set (`fs.Visit`, name `from-zip`) and refuse an empty value before anything else. Add a test that `update --from-zip=` returns an error and writes nothing.

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:113-122` vs `:130-133`. The `cmd != "update"` refusal runs after the `version`/`uninstall`/`report` switch has already returned.
  - `sh-agent uninstall --from-zip x.zip` uninstalls. Reproduced with `--dry-run`: exit 0, "would remove 258 files and the manifest". `report --from-zip x` sends a report.
  - The comment at `:127` says "Refusals come before anything is read". `TestUpdateFromZipRefusals` covers only `install`, which reaches the check.
  - Fix: move the `*fromZip != "" && cmd != "update"` refusal above the first `switch cmd`. Extend the refusal table with `uninstall` and `report`, and assert the manifest is still there after `uninstall`.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:203-212` (`diff`). `status` now says a zip-installed home's drift is "not compared" because the zip is not kept. `diff` has no zip branch: with a release binary it diffs the installed zip harness against the binary's embedded files and prints every difference between the zip's `main` and the release as drift. No test covers it. Fix: the same `ZipPrefix` check as `status`, print "not compared", return 0.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` `updateFromZip`: interrupted runs leave the unpacked tree behind.
  - The unpack directory is removed only by `defer`. A run killed mid-way, e.g. by SIGPIPE on `update --from-zip f.zip --dry-run | head -2`, leaves the whole unpacked tree in `~/.config/sh-agent/zip-*`. Reproduced: the dry run left `zip-1845427001/…` under an existing config dir.
  - Nothing ever sweeps stale `zip-*` directories. That breaks "a dry run writes nothing" for a realistic invocation.
  - Impact is limited: `report` collects named files only (`report.go:262-287`), so the leftover is not sent.
  - Fix: remove stale `zip-*` under the parent at the start of a non-dry run, or accept it and say so in the docs.

- **[low / confidence: high] pre-existing, outside the range, reached through finding 2.** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:214-236`: `update` on a release binary ignores `--dry-run`. `UpdateFromRelease` receives `*check` only, so `update --dry-run` downloads and replaces the binary. Not introduced by this diff. Recorded because finding 2 makes it reachable from a command line that asked for a dry run.

## Items the dispatch asked about

- **Tests that pass for the wrong reason:** the internal refusal tests' pre-existing parent (finding 1). The others hold:
  - `TestUpdateFromZip` proves the zip, not the embedded files, was installed (`ZIPMARKER` under a release version).
  - `TestUpdateFromZipDryRunWritesNothing` would fail if the D10 `parent = ""` branch were removed, because `MkdirAll` would create `.config`.
  - `TestUnpackZipRefuses` proves each fixture holds its condition before trusting the refusal.
- **Behaviour with no test that fails without it:**
  - Refusals after the name pass on a fresh home (finding 1).
  - The empty value (finding 2).
  - Non-update commands other than `install` (finding 3).
  - `diff` on a zip home (finding 4).
  - The dry-run branch that unpacks under an EXISTING `~/.config/sh-agent`: its cleanup is covered only indirectly, by the shared `defer` that `TestUpdateFromZip` exercises.
- **Read-only mode with a side effect:**
  - A dry run with an existing `~/.config/sh-agent` unpacks the full tree into the home and deletes it afterwards. This is by design (plan D10, README says so) and is cleaned on normal exit. It is not cleaned on a kill (finding 5).
  - `--from-zip=` combined with `--dry-run` downloads and replaces the binary (findings 2 and 6).
- **Error path leaving state:** finding 1. When `Install` fails after unpacking, the tree is removed by the `defer`.
- **Flag handling:**
  - `reorder`'s value table has both `-from-zip` and `--from-zip`.
  - `--from-zip --dry-run` with the file forgotten takes `--dry-run` as the path and fails at `open`, which is safe.
  - The `--check`/`--repo` refusals come before the zip is read (`TestUpdateFromZipRefusals` would fail otherwise).
  - The non-update refusal is misplaced (finding 3), and an empty value is not refused (finding 2).

## Criteria

1. **Dead code: pass.** No unused functions, commented-out blocks or leftover debug output.
2. **Flow tracing: fail.**
   - Findings 1–4.
   - `Source.Origin` goes through `Install` correctly (manifest records `zip:sha256:…`, no commit, verified by `TestInstallRecordsZipOrigin`).
   - `ResolveSource` never treats the marker as a path (decoy test).
   - `knownCheckout` names the zip.
   - `status` reads the manifest first and presence-checks with exit 1 on missing.
   - Every file and reader opened in `zip.go` is closed on every path.
3. **Standards conformance: fail (minor part).**
   - gofmt, vet and `go test -race ./...` are clean (run 2026-09-28).
   - Stdlib only.
   - Errors are wrapped with the zip path.
   - The overclaiming comments in finding 1 and at `main.go:127` break the describing-text rule.
   - The "three ways in" restatement is updated in `AGENTS.md` rule 1, `README.md`, `delivery.md`, `deploy/{local,remote}.md` and `REQUIREMENTS.md` R8/R9 (text marked operator-approved, ADR-038).
4. **Directory layout: pass.** `zip.go` and its test are in `internal/harness`, the CLI test is beside `main.go`.
5. **Simplicity (DIY-except-security): pass.** `archive/zip`, plus `crypto/sha256` used as a checksum, which is stdlib as designed and not hand-rolled. The limits are variables only so tests can lower them.
6. **Decoupling: pass.** The `zip:sha256:` parsing and the 12-character truncation appear in three places (`status`, `knownCheckout`, `ResolveSource`). That is a small duplication with no failure mode today.

## Not examined

- ADR-038's full text in `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md`: only its effect on R8/R9 and the delivery spec was read.
- The BUG-093 record body.
- The plan except § Interfaces, D10 and the phase checkboxes.
- The cold-read reviews and the verify logs.
- README prose beyond the diff hunks.
- `TestHarnessMap` against the new map lines (it passed as part of the suite; its content was not read).
- `internal/harness/release*.go`: finding 6 comes from observed behaviour and the call site only.
- No mutation runs of my own; the verifier log's mutation claims were not re-checked.
- macOS behaviour (a case-insensitive filesystem with two names differing only in case is refused by `O_EXCL`, by reasoning, not run).

Scratch used: `.agents/scratch/rv-zip/` (the scratch binary, crafted zips, scratch homes).

title: Review — update-from-zip-code-r2 (2026-09-28)
body:
# Review — update-from-zip-code-r2   (2026-09-28)

Range reviewed: 1cb2608..worktree (`git diff 1cb2608` plus the untracked `internal/harness/zip.go`, `internal/harness/zip_test.go`, `cmd/sh-agent/zip_test.go`)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

The round-1 findings are fixed inside `UnpackZip` and the flag handling, but BUG-093 is still open one layer up. `updateFromZip` hands the unpacked tree to `installFiles`, and `harness.Plan` refuses zip content there: a skill with no description, a secret-shaped file, an unquoted `#`, an unmapped agent tool. By that point `UnpackZip` has already created `~/.config/sh-agent`. I reproduced it: a zip whose `skills/bash/SKILL.md` has no `description:` exits 1 on a fresh home and leaves `home/.config/sh-agent` behind.

Second, `TestFromZipEmptyValueRefused` has no isolation. If the regression it pins comes back (an empty value read as "no flag"), the red run falls through to a normal `update` from the package directory. `ResolveSource` then finds the operator's real checkout, and `update` runs `git fetch` with the operator's credentials. On a clean tree that is behind, it also runs `git pull --ff-only` and `Reinstall`. That is BUG-094's class: a red test with real side effects.

gofmt, vet and `go test -race ./...` are clean (run 2026-09-28).

## Round-1 findings — status

| # | Round-1 finding | Fixed? | Test that fails without the fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Refusals after `MkdirAll(parent)` leave `~/.config/sh-agent` | Fixed inside `UnpackZip`: `checkZipTrees` validates kinds, duplicates and sizes before `mkdirAllTracked`, and the defer removes the created chain. Still open at the CLI level (new finding 1). | `TestUnpackZipLateRefusalCreatesNoParent` (symlink, duplicate; fresh parent) fails under the round-1 code. Nothing fails if the chain-cleanup loop is removed (finding 4). |
| 2 | Empty `--from-zip` value falls through to `update` | Fixed: `fs.Visit` detects the flag and the empty value is refused (`main.go:119-132`). | `TestFromZipEmptyValueRefused`. Its red path is unsafe (finding 2). |
| 3 | `uninstall`/`report --from-zip` run | Fixed: the refusal block sits before the first `switch`. | `TestFromZipRefusedOnOtherCommands`, 8 commands. It asserts the home stays empty and nothing is printed, with `PATH` emptied, which is correct isolation. |
| 4 | `diff` compares a zip home to the embedded files | Fixed (`main.go` diff case, `ZipPrefix` check). | `TestDiffAfterZip` (release version; would print drift containing ZIPMARKER). |
| 5 | Interrupted runs leave `zip-*` | Fixed for later real runs: `sweepStaleZipDirs` removes entries older than 1 h. A dry run never sweeps, by design. | `TestUpdateFromZipSweepsStaleDirs`. It uses `Chtimes` for the old entry, keeps the fresh one, and asserts that a dry run does not sweep. |
| 6 | `update --dry-run` on a release binary downloads and replaces | Fixed: `dry` sets `*check`, and `ErrNewerRelease` under dry prints and returns nil. | `TestReleaseUpdateDryRunChangesNothing`, with a fake `gh` alone on `PATH`. The checkout path has no test (finding 3). |

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high] BUG-093 recurrence.** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:1064` (`UnpackZip` creates the parent chain) vs `:1075` (`installFiles` → `harness.Plan` refuses the zip's content).
  - `UnpackZip` validates only the archive's shape. Plan's content refusals come after the parent exists: a SKILL.md without a description, a secret-shaped name (`plan.go:120`), an unquoted `#` in frontmatter, an unmapped agent tool. On success `UnpackZip` returns with `~/.config/sh-agent` created. The caller's `defer os.RemoveAll(dir)` removes only the `zip-*` tree.
  - Reproduced with a scratch binary built from the worktree, input `.agents/scratch/rv2-zip/nodesc.zip`. Output: `sh-agent: skill bash: SKILL.md has no description`, exit 1. `find home1` → `home1/.config/sh-agent`.
  - The comment at `main.go:1051-1052`, "UnpackZip creates the parent only after the zip's names pass, so a refused zip writes nothing", is false for this case. It is also stale on "names": validation now covers kinds, duplicates and sizes too. Under the describing-text rule that is part of this finding.
  - No CLI test refuses a zip at the Plan stage on a fresh home.
  - Fix: have `updateFromZip` own the chain. Call a tracked mkdir before `UnpackZip`, so `UnpackZip` always receives an existing parent. When `installFiles` returns an error, remove the `zip-*` tree and then `os.Remove` the created chain, deepest first. `os.Remove` keeps anything a partial install wrote.
  - Add a fresh-home CLI test with a description-less skill that asserts `os.ReadDir(home)` is empty.

- **[medium / confidence: high] Red-path isolation (BUG-094 class).** `cmd/sh-agent/zip_test.go:272-284` (`TestFromZipEmptyValueRefused`).
  - The test sets `SH_AGENT_REPO=""` but neither `PATH` nor the working directory. `version` is the dev build.
  - Under the exact regression it pins (round-1 code: `if *fromZip != ""`), `update --from-zip= --home <tmp>` falls through to the normal `update`. `ResolveSource` walks the cwd (`cmd/sh-agent`) up to the real checkout (`repo.go:65-72`), and `knownCheckout` passes because the scratch home has no manifest. `update` then calls `harness.Behind` → `git fetch --quiet` in the operator's checkout, with their credentials. If the tree is clean and behind, it also runs `Pull` and `Reinstall`.
  - I did not run the mutation, deliberately, because it would fetch. The call chain was traced by reading.
  - The same exposure exists, less likely, if the whole `zipSet` block regressed:
    - `TestUpdateFromZipRefusals` (`:108-126`): the `--repo ../..` row names the real repository root.
    - `TestUpdateFromZip`, `TestStatusAfterZip` and `TestDiffAfterZip` set `version = "v1.2.3"`. A fall-through there reaches `UpdateFromRelease`, which runs the real `gh`.
  - The sibling `TestFromZipRefusedOnOtherCommands` shows the right pattern and cites BUG-094.
  - Fix: in every `--from-zip` CLI test, `t.Setenv("PATH", t.TempDir())` (or a fake-`gh` dir) and `t.Chdir(t.TempDir())`. The zip path needs neither `PATH` nor the cwd: `selfExecutable` is `os.Executable`. Confirm the tests stay green after the change.

- **[low / confidence: high] Checkout-path `--dry-run` untested.** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:232-235, 271-276`.
  - D11 makes `update --dry-run` read-only "on the checkout and release paths". Before this range, the checkout path ignored `--dry-run` entirely: it pulled and reinstalled.
  - No test runs `update --dry-run` against a checkout. `grep` in `main_test.go` finds `--check` and plain `update` only. Removing `*check = true` would leave the checkout path pulling on a dry run with every test green.
  - Fix: extend the existing local-remote checkout test near `main_test.go:1129` with `update --dry-run` on a behind checkout. Assert HEAD is unchanged, the `[dry-run] update would pull` line appears, and exit is 0.

- **[low / confidence: high] Chain cleanup has no test.** `internal/harness/zip.go:84-95` (the created-chain cleanup) and `zip_test.go:336` (`TestUnpackZipLateRefusalCreatesNoParent`).
  - After D11, both cases in that test are refused in `checkZipTrees`, before `mkdirAllTracked` runs. The test proves validation precedes creation, but it never reaches the cleanup loop.
  - The post-creation refusals are the final `IsRepo` (a zip with `context/AGENTS.md` and no `skills/`) and I/O errors. The loop works: I reproduced `noskills.zip` on a fresh home, exit 1 and the home left empty. But deleting the loop fails no test.
  - Fix: add a `noskills` case with a fresh parent (`home/.config/sh-agent`). Or move the `skills/` presence check into validation, so the loop guards only I/O errors.

## Items the dispatch asked about

- **`UnpackZip` validate-then-write, and cleanup of the parent chain.**
  - The split is sound. `readCapped` → hash → parse → name pass → root → `checkZipTrees` (kinds, duplicates, sizes counted by decompressing into `io.Discard`) → `mkdirAllTracked` → write.
  - The named return `err` is what the defer reads. Every error after `mkdirAllTracked` returns through the named result, so the shadowed `err` inside the loop does not bypass it.
  - The chain is removed deepest first with `os.Remove`, which never deletes a non-empty directory.
  - The write phase re-checks sizes and uses `O_EXCL`, as defence in depth.
  - Gaps: findings 1 and 4.
- **`fs.Visit` block before the first `switch`.** Correct.
  - Only home resolution (`os.UserHomeDir`, `filepath.Abs`) runs before it, and neither writes.
  - It covers `--from-zip=`, `--from-zip ""` and both dash forms, since `reorder` lists both.
  - Ordering: other command first, then empty value, then `--check`/`--repo`.
- **`update --dry-run` sets `--check`.**
  - Release path: `shedKeptClone` is skipped (`!*check`). `UpdateFromRelease` receives `check=true`, and `ErrNewerRelease` becomes the message plus exit 0. Tested.
  - Checkout path: `update()` returns before `shedKeptClone`/`Pull`/`Reinstall` under `checkOnly`. `Behind` still runs `git fetch`, which updates remote-tracking refs, the same as `--check` always has. This is not a finding, but "changes nothing" in the comment at `main.go:229-231` holds only for the working tree and the home.
  - Checkout path untested: finding 3.
- **`diff` zip branch.** Correct and tested.
  - `src` is resolved before the zip check, so a DEV build on a zip home with no checkout errors with `ResolveSource`'s zip note rather than "not compared". That is acceptable and states the way out.
- **`sweepStaleZipDirs`.** Correct.
  - It globs only `<home>/.config/sh-agent/zip-*`. `Lstat` plus `IsDir` means a symlink named `zip-x` is not followed.
  - The age comes from mtime, which the unpack never back-dates because `unpackFile` sets no `Chtimes`.
  - It runs only on a real run, before `UnpackZip`. A refused zip may therefore still sweep hour-old debris; that is harmless and removes only this command's own leftovers.
- **`secretShaped`'s `*oauth-token*`.**
  - Consistent with the context's Git rule (`context/AGENTS.md:45`) and preflight.
  - No tracked harness file matches: `git ls-files | grep -i oauth` is empty.
  - `TestSecretShapedCLITokenFiles` fails without the pattern for `antigravity-oauth-token`.
  - The pattern is broad (a future doc named `*oauth-token*.md` would be refused at install and adopt). No such file exists, so this is not a finding.
- **`.gitignore` line.** `git ls-files -ci --exclude-standard` is empty, so no tracked file becomes ignored. Pass.
- **Network or credentials from tests.**
  - On the green path, no test reaches either: the full suite passed, and `TestReleaseUpdateDryRunChangesNothing` and `TestFromZipRefusedOnOtherCommands` isolate `PATH`. No package uses `net/http`.
  - On the red path, `TestFromZipEmptyValueRefused` can, and so can the zip tests that set a release version (finding 2).
  - Whether the main agent's "empty-value" mutation ran a real `git fetch` depends on how it was mutated. Deleting the `case *fromZip == ""` line routes `""` into `UnpackZip` and fails safely. Reverting to the round-1 `!= ""` gate reaches `git fetch`. The dispatch does not say which one was run.

## Criteria

1. **Dead code: pass.** No unused functions, commented-out blocks or debug output.
   - `short()` has two callers (`status`, `knownCheckout`). `repo.go` inlines the same truncation, which is duplication, not dead code.
2. **Flow tracing: fail.** Findings 1 (a refusal after creation, across the `UnpackZip` → `installFiles` hop) and 2 (a red path reaching the network).
   - Errors are wrapped with the zip path.
   - Resources are closed on every path in `zip.go`.
3. **Standards conformance: fail (minor part).**
   - gofmt, vet and `go test -race ./...` are clean.
   - Stdlib only.
   - The stale comment at `main.go:1051-1052` is part of finding 1.
   - Missing tests for changed behaviour: findings 3 and 4.
4. **Directory layout: pass.** Tests sit beside `zip.go` and `main.go`.
5. **Simplicity (DIY-except-security): pass.**
   - `archive/zip`; `crypto/sha256` is used as a checksum, as designed, which is not hand-rolling.
   - `mkdirAllTracked` is small and needed for exact cleanup.
6. **Decoupling: pass.**
   - `zip:sha256:` parsing is repeated in three places (`status`, `knownCheckout`, `ResolveSource`), as in round 1, with no failure mode.

## Not examined

- `internal/harness/zip_test.go` lines 1-130 and 176-335 were skimmed by test name and parent setup only, not read line by line.
- `readCapped`'s body: it is outside `zip.go` and I did not open it. Its behaviour is inferred from `TestUnpackZipRefusesOversizedArchive`'s name.
- `UpdateFromRelease`'s internals: the release dry-run was judged from its call site and its test.
- The docs hunks (README, delivery.md, deploy guides, REQUIREMENTS, DECISIONS/ADR-038, skill-matrix, VENDORED.md): that is the docs review's scope.
- The phase-1/phase-2 verify logs, and the e2e log beyond its Not exercised and D11 rerun sections.
- No mutations of my own. Finding 2's fall-through was traced by reading, not run, because running it would fetch from the real remote.
- macOS.

Scratch used: `.agents/scratch/rv2-zip/` (scratch binary, `nodesc.zip`, `noskills.zip`, homes `home1`, `home2`).
