title: Security review — v1.8.0..52cebd8 (release gate) (2026-09-28)
body:
# Security review — v1.8.0..52cebd8 (release gate)   (2026-09-28)

Range reviewed: v1.8.0..52cebd8

Three commits: e4ae34c, 0b762db, 52cebd8. 36 paths; none binary (`git diff --numstat`, no `-` columns). The tree was at 52cebd8 throughout. The only untracked files were artifacts from other agents running in parallel, plus this file.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS (none blocking; one carried medium stays open by decision)

**The worst problem is the medium carried from both earlier rounds, and it is still open.** Whoever supplies a zip can leave `SHA256SUMS`/`SHA256SUMS.sig` out. The zip then installs with exit 0, marked `UNVERIFIED` in a single stdout line (`internal/harness/release.go:445-447` → `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:1085-1087`).

**Why it does not block this gate.** This is the behaviour R9 approves, word for word. ADR-039 (Consequences, "Open"), the plan's Follow-ups and the change entry all record it honestly. Every path this range adds either verifies or refuses, so the exposure is strictly narrower than the v1.8.0 that shipped.

**Two conditions, which only the gate writer can meet:**
- (a) the v1.9.0 gate report carries it as an open medium, narrowed but not closed;
- (b) the release handoff's Next Steps asks the operator the `--unverified` question. The only handoff in the range (`2026-09-28-1806`) predates this change and asks a different question.

**What I verified fresh:**
- The verification code (read whole: `release.go`, `zip.go`, `updateFromZip`).
- Release step 3b: executed, must-pass and must-fail.
- The pinning of the removed bypass hint: both mutations that survived round 2 now fail named subtests.
- `govulncheck`: clean.
- BUG-094's feedback-repo claim: confirmed.

The findings below are low: one unrecorded trust verdict, one stale comment on the trust anchor, one pre-existing gap in the release procedure, one skill instruction, and the optional archive scope.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high] Carried from round 1 and round 2. OPEN by decision; not blocking under conditions (a) and (b).**
  - **Where:** `internal/harness/release.go:445-447` (`VerifyZipSums` returns `ErrZipUnsigned` when both files are absent) together with `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:1085-1087` (the closure turns that into nil, and the zip unpacks and installs).
  - **The weakness:** trust is decided by whether two files are present, and the party who supplies the zip controls that. Unchanged since round 1.
  - **Remediation (unchanged):** an explicit opt-in, for example `--unverified`, without which a zip with no sums is refused. This is an R9 change, so it is the operator's decision, with an ADR (project rule 3).
  - **If that flag lands:** the accepted downgrade (see the status table) becomes the remaining route for an attacker. Revisit it then: on a release binary, warn when `compareRelease(verifiedTag, buildVersion()) < 0`. Both are existing helpers, so no dependency.

- **[low / confidence: high] The trust verdict is not recorded anywhere that outlives the command's output.** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:1112`.
  - **What happens:** the manifest origin is `zip:sha256:<hex>` whether the zip was VERIFIED or UNVERIFIED. `status` prints `from zip sha256:<hex>` either way: E2E log run 1, README § Install from a zip. `sh-agent report` carries the same value.
  - **Why it matters:** once the one stdout line is gone, neither the operator nor a later session nor a feedback report can tell that an unverified zip became the agents' instructions. That weakens the only control the medium above has, which is disclosure.
  - **Remediation:** record the verdict in the manifest (`verified vX.Y.Z` or `unverified`) and print it in `status`. This is a manifest change, which the plan scoped Out, so it is the operator's call. It can land with the flag in the first finding.

- **[low / confidence: high] Carried from round 1 and round 2, neither fixed nor rebutted: stale comment on the trust anchor.** `internal/harness/release.go:34-35`.
  - **What it says:** `releaseSigner` is "a variable only so a test can substitute a test key's line".
  - **What is true:** the variable is also what `-ldflags -X` replaces at link time. Measured this round: a build with `-X …/internal/harness.releaseSigner=gate@signer …` accepted a scratch key's signature and printed `VERIFIED` (`.agents/scratch/sec-gate-3b/`). The CLI test also reaches it through `SwapReleaseSigner` (`release.go:415-422`).
  - **Why it matters:** a reader auditing the trust anchor learns the wrong thing about how it can be replaced.
  - **Fix:** the comment names `-X`, release step 3b as the guard against it, and `SwapReleaseSigner`.
  - **Optional hardening (round 2):** a test that parses the module's non-test files with stdlib `go/parser` and fails on any reference to `SwapReleaseSigner` besides its declaration. Today there is none (grep), and the linker drops it from the binary (round 2, `go tool nm`).

- **[low / confidence: medium] Pre-existing, not introduced by this range: the binaries and the release zip come from different sources.** `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` § Releases, steps 0-1 (lines 131-144) against step 1b (line 147).
  - **The two sources:**
    - Step 1 builds the binaries from the WORKING TREE, and step 0 re-checks only the five embedded trees.
    - Step 1b archives the TAG's object tree.
  - **The gap:** say a tracked file under `cmd/` or `internal/` changes after line 108's whole-tree clean check, which runs before the tag and the pushes. The change is compiled into every binary and signed into `SHA256SUMS`. Meanwhile the signed tag and the zip describe other code.
    - Step 3b catches this only when the change touches the signer.
    - `TestEmbedHoldsOnlyTrackedFiles` compares file lists, not content, and only for the five trees.
    - Step 1's comment ("from the tag's own tree") is therefore guaranteed for the five trees only.
  - **Why it is low:** the window is minutes inside one `/preflight` turn, and nothing is expected to write source then.
  - **Fix, cheapest first:**
    - repeat line 108's `test -z "$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all)"` in step 0;
    - or build from a `git archive vX.Y.Z` export, so the binaries and the zip share one source and the embed contamination guard becomes unnecessary.
  - **Confidence is medium** because I read only preflight's Step 6 by grep, not in full.

- **[low / confidence: low] The restored `find-skills` tells agents to install third-party skills globally without confirmation.** `skills/find-skills/SKILL.md`, Step 6.
  - **Provenance:** it is verbatim upstream at `435076e`; reviewer confirmed byte-identical via `gh api`.
  - **What it says:** `npx skills add <owner/repo@skill> -g -y`, where "`-g` installs globally … `-y` skips confirmation prompts".
  - **What the context says:** `context/AGENTS.md` § Global vs project says a found skill goes into the checkout's `skills/` and is "never only into a vendor directory".
  - **Why it matters:** a third-party skill is instructions every later session reads. The checkout route keeps a commit and provenance in `VENDORED.md` as the review point. A `-g` install has neither, and `sh-agent install` never removes it (the old local text said so).
  - **What is measured:** the context sentence wins 2 of 2 on Claude Code (`testing/2026-09-28-verify-find-skills-routing.md`). Antigravity is not exercised.
  - **Remediation:**
    - run that log's question once on Antigravity;
    - optionally name `-g` in the context sentence ("not `npx skills add -g`").

    The vendored file stays verbatim, per `skills/VENDORED.md`.

- **[low / confidence: medium] Carried from round 1 and round 2; optional: the release zip carries the whole tracked tree.** `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:147` (step 1b).
  - **What it ships:** the tag's whole tracked tree, including `.agents/docs/`. That tree holds hostnames, machine paths, the operator's email and a report record's contents; the same section's own paragraph lists them.
  - **What is new:** the zip is now a first-class asset that README sends zip places, meaning corporate workstations, to download. It is about 3.1 MB (measured on a 52cebd8 archive), far below the 64 MiB read cap.
  - **Why it stays low:** the content equals GitHub's own source zip for the tag, and the repository is private.
  - **Optional minimisation:** `git archive … vX.Y.Z context skills agents commands rules`. `UnpackZip` accepts it, since `zipRoot` needs only `top/context/AGENTS.md`. Check it against R9's "a zip of its tree" wording.

## Round-1 and round-2 findings — status at 52cebd8

| Earlier finding | Status |
|---|---|
| r1/r2 medium: the sums can be omitted | **Open by decision**: ADR-039 Consequences "Open", plan `## Scope` Follow-ups, change entry `1925`. Conditions (a) and (b) above. |
| r1 medium: bypass hint in refusals | **Fixed and now pinned.** No `VerifyZipSums` message suggests removing the checksums; ADR-039 and plan D7 say so. Round 2's two surviving mutations were re-run in `.agents/scratch/sec-gate-mut/tree`, a `git archive 52cebd8` copy; each compiled (`go vet` exit 0). The narrow hint (sums absent, `.sig` present) fails `TestVerifyZipSums/sig_present,_sums_missing`. The reworded hint on every error fails `sig_missing`, `foreign_key` and `sig_present,_sums_missing`. The copy was restored (`cmp` clean) and is green again. |
| r1/r2 low: downgrade to an older verified release | **Rebutted by decision**: ADR-039 Consequences, "allowed: the operator chooses the zip. The first line names the release". Accepted while the medium is open, because an unsigned zip is a strictly stronger route for an attacker. See the note on the first finding. |
| r1 low: `-X` trust anchor, no built-binary check | **Fixed** by step 3b, executed this round (see Checked). The comment nit remains: third finding. |
| r1 low: "five assets" | **Fixed**: `remote.md` "all six" and "the six assets"; ADR-039 "six assets". |
| r1 low: test coverage | **Fixed**: `TestUpdateFromZipVerifiedAndTampered` covers the VERIFIED branch (reviewer r2 reproduced the `verifiedTag` mutation). `sig present, sums missing` is now a subtest. |
| r1/r2 low: stat errors read as "unsigned" | **Fixed**: `release.go:440-444` treats only `fs.ErrNotExist` as absent. Pinned by `sums unreadable: refused, not unsigned`. `os.Lstat` was not adopted, so a dangling symlink counts as absent. That gives nothing to someone who could delete the file anyway. |
| r2 low: README steers to the unverified path | **Fixed**: the example is now `styrman-harness-vX.Y.Z.zip` with the sums beside it, and the `main` zip is named second as unsigned. |
| r2 low: `SwapReleaseSigner` hardening and stale comment | **Open**: third finding. |
| r1/r2 low: archive scope | **Open, optional**: last finding. |
| r2 condition (c): the plan contradicts ADR-039 | **Met**: `## Scope` now has "Follow-ups, not built: a zip handed over WITHOUT its sums still installs … put to the operator (ADR-039 Open …)". |

## Checked

- **Verification soundness, re-read fresh:**
  - `UnpackZip` reads once, hashes, calls `check(sum)`, then parses that same buffer (`zip.go:52-65`).
  - `VerifyZipSums`:
    - both files absent → `ErrZipUnsigned`;
    - any other stat error → refusal;
    - one file present → refusal naming the missing file;
    - both present → `verifySignedSums`: the signature over the in-memory bytes through stdin, `-I` the compiled-in identity, `-n sh-agent-release`, `allowed_signers` written 0600 into a fresh `os.MkdirTemp` that is never the zip's folder; then the marker is read from the verified bytes; then `checksumFor` by exact base name against the hash of the unpacked buffer.
  - Only `ErrZipUnsigned` becomes nil in the closure. No other error wraps it.
  - `verifyRelease` still compares the marker with its own tag and keeps its messages.
  - A folder the attacker controls can only cause a refusal or a hang (a FIFO named `SHA256SUMS`). Both give nothing beyond omitting the files.
- **Release step 3b, executed** in `.agents/scratch/sec-gate-3b/`. A `git archive 52cebd8` zip and `SHA256SUMS` signed by a scratch `gate@signer` key; the operator's key signed nothing. The exact step 3b command lines were run twice:
  - binary built with `-X` naming the scratch signer: run exit 0, `grep` exit 0, `VERIFIED against the signed SHA256SUMS of release v0.0.2`;
  - binary with the real compiled-in signer (must-fail): run exit 1, `SHA256SUMS signature does not verify`, `grep` exit 1.

  In both runs `../zipcheck` stayed empty (0 entries) and no `sh-agent-verify-*` directory was left in the temp directory (0 before, 0 after).
- **Report sweep** (`report.go:410-439`):
  - names come from `ReadDir` and are filtered on the `report-` prefix, `IsDir` (lstat semantics) and not-a-symlink;
  - a non-numeric suffix is skipped, and a live pid is kept;
  - `TestSweepInterruptedClonesGlobCharsInHome` passes, and the reviewer traced it red against the old glob.

  No new reach outside the home's own config directory.
- **Secrets:** none.
  - Every new file was read whole and every hunk read.
  - A pattern scan of the added lines (private-key armour, `gh*_`, `github_pat_`, `AKIA`, `xox*`, `AIza`, `sk-`, `"private_key"`, `password/secret/token=`) hit only round 2's own list of those patterns.
  - The signer line and email are public-key material that was already committed.
  - The handoff's session ID and release URL are not secrets.
  - Scratch hygiene:
    - no `.credentials.json` anywhere under `.agents/scratch/`;
    - the six `tsn-probe/runs/token-*/antigravity-oauth-token` files are 38-byte fixtures (all six match a fake/test/dummy needle) and differ from the real home's token, compared with `cmp -s` without printing either;
    - the E2E scratch key `e2e-signed/keys/k` is 0600, and gitignored by `.gitignore:40`.
- **Instruction-shaped text:**
  - an injection-phrase scan of the added lines found 0 hits;
  - the trail files carry ordinary plan and review prose;
  - the bypass hint is gone from the plan's D7 and from ADR-039;
  - `find-skills` Step 6 is the fifth finding.
- **Injection:**
  - no new exec surface;
  - `ssh-keygen` paths are option arguments, with no shell;
  - the tag in the VERIFIED line comes only from signed bytes and is limited to `v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+`;
  - `git archive` in step 1b reads the object database, and no `.gitattributes` exists (round 1).
- **Authz/authn:**
  - the trust anchor is unchanged and compiled in;
  - `ssh-keygen` is located from system paths first;
  - `SwapReleaseSigner` has no non-test reference (grep over `cmd` and `internal`).
- **Crypto:** nothing is hand-rolled. It uses OpenSSH `ssh-keygen -Y verify` (SSHSIG) and stdlib `crypto/sha256` as designed.
- **Dependencies:**
  - `go.mod` is untouched;
  - `govulncheck ./...` on go1.27.1: "No vulnerabilities found.", exit 0 (`.agents/scratch/sec-gate-govulncheck.txt`);
  - `npm audit` does not apply: `npm` is present, but no `package.json` is tracked;
  - `npx skills` is unpinned, as before this range.
- **GCP surface:** not touched.
- **Tests I ran:** `go test -race -count=1 -run 'TestVerifyZipSums|TestUnpackZip|TestUpdateFromZip|TestUpdateFromRelease|TestSweepInterruptedClones|TestReleaseSigner|TestVerif|TestHarnessMap|TestSecretShaped' ./...` at 52cebd8: exit 0, with 3 packages `ok`.
- **The BUG-094 claim**, checked read-only with `gh api`:
  - feedback-repo commit `1703cea7dfb2` has one file, `reports/dave/2026-09-28-172114/report.json`, with status `removed`;
  - that path returns 404 at the default branch;
  - the earlier commit `c5d47b2` still holds it in history, and its content is metrics only (BUG-094 record).
- **Not a security matter, for the reviewer:** in the `cmd/sh-agent/zip_test.go` header of `TestUpdateFromZipRefusedRunSweepsNothing`, "nothing, not even a stale leftover." now appears twice.
- **Actions to disclose:**
  - I created `.agents/scratch/sec-gate-3b/` (a scratch key, two builds, two signed release folders, `zipcheck`), `.agents/scratch/sec-gate-mut/` (an archive copy of the tree, a mutation script, logs) and `.agents/scratch/sec-gate-govulncheck.txt`;
  - two read-only `gh api` calls;
  - I edited no live file and ran no git command that changes the working tree (`git archive` to a file or stdout only);
  - `sh-agent` ran only as scratch builds, `--dry-run` into a scratch home.

## Not examined

- **Release-diff paths: none.** All 36 paths were read. New files were read whole: the two change entries, the handoff, the plan, the 7 reviews and the 4 testing logs. Every hunk of every modified file was read. `release.go`, `zip.go`, `updateFromZip`, `sweepInterruptedClones`, `find-skills/SKILL.md` and `remote.md` § Releases lines 94-185 were read in full.
- **Outside the diff, in its blast radius, not read:**
  - `installFiles` and `harness.Plan`: the unchanged install path a zip feeds;
  - `sweepStaleZipDirs` past line 1140;
  - `release_test.go` helpers (`newRelease`, `signRelease`): by name only;
  - `skills/preflight/SKILL.md` Step 6: grep only, which is why the fourth finding is medium confidence;
  - the unchanged remainder of modified docs (README outside its hunks, `DECISIONS.md` before ADR-039, REQUIREMENTS outside R9, `delivery.md` outside § The model).
- **Not run:** the full test suite, `gofmt` and `go vet`, which are the verifier's; the untracked `testing/2026-09-28-verify-v1.9.0-gate.md` belongs to that run.
- **Not exercised:**
  - macOS (`go env GOOS/GOARCH` in step 3b, the `ssh-keygen` location, `$TMPDIR`);
  - the cross-compiled darwin/arm64 and linux/arm64 binaries, which step 3b does not self-verify, as accepted in round 2;
  - the real v1.9.0 zip under the real key, which does not exist yet;
  - the Antigravity leg of the `find-skills` routing question.

## Outcome

1. **Medium, unsigned zip installs UNVERIFIED: left, open by decision.** R9 allows it and ADR-039 records it as Open. It is carried in the v1.9.0 gate report, and the release handoff asks the operator about `--unverified`.
2. **Low, verdict not recorded: fixed.**
   - The manifest records `zip:sha256:<hex>;verified vX.Y.Z` or `;unverified`, and `status` shows `(verified vX.Y.Z)` or `(unverified)`.
   - A manifest written before this change keeps the bare form, which is still read.
   - Tests: `TestStatusAfterZip` covers `(unverified)`, and `TestUpdateFromZipVerifiedAndTampered` covers `(verified v1.2.3)`.
   - Must-fail: dropping both suffixes compiled and failed both tests.
   - `README.md` and `delivery.md` describe the new form.
3. **Low, signer comment: fixed.** The `releaseSigner` comment in `release.go` now says `-ldflags -X` replaces it, so a binary's builder chooses what it trusts. The release binaries are built from the tag with no `-X`.

title: Security review — v1.9.0-c30b8da (release gate) (2026-09-28)
body:
# Security review — v1.9.0-c30b8da (release gate)   (2026-09-28)

Range reviewed: v1.9.0..c30b8da

Four commits, 18 paths, none binary: d60ccdd (handoff), b1ecab3 (`--unverified`), d3e493b (gate fixes), c30b8da (ADR-041, which removes the flag).

- HEAD was c30b8da throughout, and at the start the working tree matched c30b8da (`git diff --quiet c30b8da`).
- Four untracked files appeared during the run. One is this report. The other three are concurrent gate artifacts: `review-v1.9.0-c30b8da-{code,docs}.md` and `testing/2026-09-28-verify-v1.10.0-gate.md`.
- There were no unpushed commits and no new tag.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS (one low, non-blocking; nothing here blocks the gate)

**No path lets a failed verification install anything.** The net code change across the range is one operator: `VerifyZipSums` now treats half the pair as `ErrZipUnsigned` (`&&` → `||`, `internal/harness/release.go:450`). Everything else nets out to v1.9.0, apart from comments, usage text and test assertions:
- the `--unverified` flag, its refusals and the stray-argument refusal were added and then removed;
- the updated usage text is `main.go:44`.

When both files are present, every failure path returns an error that does not wrap the sentinel, so the `check` closure (`cmd/sh-agent/main.go:1091-1101`) passes it on unchanged. `UnpackZip` then returns before it parses or writes anything, and the deferred `RemoveCreated` removes the directories it made (`internal/harness/zip.go:54-67`). The hash that is checked is the hash of the one in-memory buffer that is later parsed and unpacked, so there is no gap between check and use. I confirmed this three ways:
- by reading the code;
- with the edge cases below;
- with three must-fail mutations at c30b8da, each of which compiled and failed named tests (see Checked).

The one finding is a low about input parsing. It sits inside the class of hardening ADR-041 declined, so it is the operator's call.

## Accepted by decision (ADR-041) — recorded, not findings

- **A zip without the full pair installs marked UNVERIFIED.** This covers neither file, `SHA256SUMS` only, and `.sig` only.
  - The output line says `UNVERIFIED`, the manifest records `;unverified`, and `status` prints `(unverified)`.
  - Consequence, stated in ADR-041 itself: deleting the `.sig` beside a tampered release zip turns a refusal into an UNVERIFIED install. The trust line then reads the same as for a `main` zip ("no signed SHA256SUMS beside it"). A stripped signature is therefore disclosed only as generic UNVERIFIED.
  - Compared with v1.9.0 this gives an attacker nothing new: whoever can strip one file could already strip both, which installed UNVERIFIED in v1.9.0. What changes is the operator-error case (a partial download), which used to be refused.
- **Downgrade to an older signed release zip installs, printed as VERIFIED.** This was the prior review's low 2. ADR-041 now accepts it explicitly ("An older release's zip installs; there is no downgrade check"; rejected because "a zip place has no other way to roll back").
- **The prior review's lows 1 and 3 are moot.** The flag they concerned no longer exists. `--unverified` now fails flag parsing ("flag provided but not defined") rather than being read as anything.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:124-135`: stray positional arguments on `update --from-zip` are silently ignored.
  - **What happens:** c30b8da removed the `fs.NArg() != 0` refusal along with `--unverified`. Take `sh-agent update --from-zip ~/Downloads/x.zip SHA256SUMS SHA256SUMS.sig`, where the operator passes the pair as arguments or from another folder:
    - `reorder` sends the two names to positionals, and nothing reads them;
    - `VerifyZipSums` looks only beside the zip;
    - so when the pair is not in the zip's own folder, the zip installs UNVERIFIED with exit 0, while the operator believes they supplied the signature.
  - **Why it is only low:**
    - the first output line and `status` both say UNVERIFIED;
    - the net behaviour equals v1.9.0, which never checked `NArg`;
    - ADR-041's context names "stray-argument refusals" among the hardening the operator stopped.
  - **Remediation, if the operator wants it:** restore the one `case fs.NArg() != 0:` refusal in the `zipSet` switch (stdlib `flag`, no dependency), with a test that `update --from-zip a.zip SHA256SUMS` is refused. Otherwise record the decline in the gate's Outcome.

## Checked

**Failed verification never installs.** I checked this edge case by edge case, reading c30b8da.
- **Pair present, any check fails** (`verifySignedSums`, `checksumFor`, a mismatch, `sshKeygen` missing, a `MkdirTemp` error): the error is built with `fmt.Errorf`/`errors.New` and never wraps `ErrZipUnsigned`, so the zip is refused.
- **A file vanishes between `VerifyZipSums`' stat and `verifySignedSums`' re-stat:** "has no SHA256SUMS(.sig)", a refusal (fails closed).
- **A stat error other than ENOENT** (permission, ELOOP): refused, pinned by `TestVerifyZipSums/sums_unreadable`.
- **The pair is a directory:** the read fails and the zip is refused.
- **`verifiedTag`:** set only on a nil error after `want == sum`. `sum` is the SHA-256 of the buffer that is unpacked. The tag comes from the signed marker `v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+`, so it cannot inject anything into the manifest origin or the output.

**Must-fail mutations**, run in `git archive c30b8da` copies under `.agents/scratch/sec-c30b8da/`. The `-run` set was the zip, `--from-zip`, zip status/diff/known-checkout and `VerifyZipSums` tests.
- **Baseline:** `go test -race -count=1 -v -run '<that set>'`. Both packages ok, 54 PASS lines, 0 SKIP. `/usr/bin/ssh-keygen` is present, so the signature tests ran.
- **Each mutation:** the needle matched exactly once and `go vet` exited 0.
  - **M1**, the closure swallows every error: `TestUpdateFromZipForeignSignatureRefused` and `TestUpdateFromZipVerifiedAndTampered` fail.
  - **M2**, a failed signature is reported as unsigned (`release.go:465`): `TestVerifyZipSums/foreign_key` and `TestUpdateFromZipForeignSignatureRefused` fail.
  - **M3**, a checksum mismatch is reported as unsigned (`release.go:472`): `TestVerifyZipSums/checksum_mismatch`, `…/github_source_archive` and `TestUpdateFromZipVerifiedAndTampered` fail.

**Input parsing.**
- `zip.go` is unchanged in the range but was read whole:
  - one capped read (64 MiB);
  - names are refused when absolute, when they hold a backslash or a `..` element, or when `filepath.IsLocal` rejects them; names are also capped at 1,024 bytes and 32 levels deep;
  - at most 5,000 entries;
  - only the five trees are written;
  - a symlink or a non-regular file inside a tree is refused, and so is a duplicate name;
  - sizes are counted by decompressing: 16 MiB per file, 128 MiB in total;
  - writes use `O_EXCL`.
- `--from-zip` refuses an empty value, a value that starts with `-`, `--check`/`--repo`, and any other command.
- `checksumFor` refuses two different hashes for one name and a malformed hash.
- The stray-argument gap is the finding above.

**Secrets:** none.
- A regex scan over the whole content of all 18 paths at c30b8da looked for private-key armour, `gh[pousr]_`, `github_pat_`, `AKIA`, `xox*`, `AIza`, `sk-`, quoted password/secret/token/api-key assignments and `Bearer`. It had one hit, a false positive: the prior security review's prose naming the `github_pat_` needle.
- Emails found:
  - `f@example.invalid`, a test fixture;
  - `git@github.com`;
  - `ostling.simon@gmail.com`, the signer principal. That is public-key identity, committed since ADR-026 and in the README, in a private repository.
- No IPv4 addresses.
- The handoff carries a session ID, commit hashes and machine descriptors ("work Mac", "devbox"), none of which is secret.

**Instruction-shaped text:** 0 hits for injection phrasing across the 18 paths. One trail note, not a security finding:
- The newest handoff in the range, `handoffs/2026-09-28-1948-v1.9.0-released.md`, still recommends the `--unverified` refusal in Next Steps 1–2, and ADR-041 reversed that.
- Under the "newest handoff wins on conflict" resume rule, a session could re-propose it until a newer handoff supersedes it.
- It points toward stricter behaviour, so there is no security downside. The post-release handoff should say ADR-041 closed those items.

**Authz/authn:** the trust anchor is unchanged. It is the compiled-in signer line, checked by `ssh-keygen -Y verify` with namespace `sh-agent-release`, preferring the system path. There is one residual, which predates this range and is documented at `release.go:41-44`: when neither `/usr/bin` nor `/bin` has `ssh-keygen`, a PATH-planted verifier together with control of the zip's folder could forge a VERIFIED label.

**Crypto:** nothing new and nothing hand-rolled. It is still OpenSSH signature verification plus `crypto/sha256` used as a checksum.

**Dependencies:**
- `go.mod` is untouched in the range.
- `govulncheck ./...` on go1.27.1: "No vulnerabilities found.", exit 0.
- `npm audit`: not run. The range touches no npm files; the prior gate recorded no tracked `package.json`, which I did not re-check.

**GCP surface:** not touched.

**Hygiene on the live tree:** `gofmt -l cmd internal` printed nothing, and `go vet ./...` exited 0.

**Actions to disclose:**
- I created `.agents/scratch/sec-c30b8da/`: folded read copies of the diff's markdown, the per-commit code log, four `git archive` copies (base, m1–m3), and test, vet and govulncheck logs. It is gitignored by `.agents/scratch/*` (confirmed with `git check-ignore -v`).
- I edited no tracked file and ran no git command that changes the working tree.

## Not examined

**Release-diff paths: none.** All 18 paths were read end to end at c30b8da:
- the four Go files in full;
- the markdown (10 new trail files, `DECISIONS.md`, `README.md`, `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `delivery.md`) whole, from `git show c30b8da:<path>` folded at 900 columns so no line was cut.

**Blast radius, outside the diff, not read this run:**
- the install of the unpacked tree: `installFiles` → `harness.Plan`/`Install` (`plan.go`, `apply.go`, `inventory.go`, `frontmatter.go`, `pathguard.go`);
- `state.go` (the manifest write);
- the test helpers `newRelease`/`signRelease` in `release_test.go`.

The content of an UNVERIFIED zip reaching the installer is accepted by decision. Whether crafted in-tree names could misuse `Plan`/`Install` was not re-examined here. It is unchanged since v1.8.0's review.

**Not run:**
- a built-binary run against the real v1.9.0 release zip and pair with the real compiled-in signer; the evidence rests on the CLI and unit tests with a swapped signer, plus M1–M3;
- the full test suite (the verifier's job);
- macOS.

**Not read:**
- `.agents/scratch/fb-cleanup`, the feedback-repository scratch clone the handoff names (gitignored, outside the diff);
- the three concurrent gate artifacts that appeared during this run.

## Outcome

1. **Low, extra words after `update --from-zip` are ignored: left, by the operator's decision.** ADR-041 records that the operator stopped the stray-argument refusal along with `--unverified` ("Don't complicate things. Just accept the zip."). The case in the finding is `--from-zip x.zip SHA256SUMS SHA256SUMS.sig`, with the pair in another folder. It installs marked `UNVERIFIED`, which is the documented behaviour for a zip without its pair beside it.

title: Cold-read — `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-29-search-index.md` (2026-09-29)
body:
# Cold-read — `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-29-search-index.md`   (2026-09-29)

Range reviewed: the plan file `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-29-search-index.md` and the code surfaces it names (`cmd/sh-agent/main.go`, `internal/harness/state.go`, `internal/harness/report.go`, `internal/harness/size_test.go`, `REQUIREMENTS.md` R4, `skills/handoff/SKILL.md:154`, `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md`, `README.md` § How it works). No git diff — this is a design-document read, per the dispatch. The "R4 approved by the operator" gate is treated as approved on D1's text, per the dispatch note.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: design needs revision (2 BLOCKING gaps), implementation not ready

Both blocking gaps are in the FTS5/query design (`internal/search`, Phase 1), the newest and least-checked surface. Everything else the plan touches (main.go's verb switch, `reorder`/`takesValue`, `state.go`, `report.go`'s explicit `Collect` allowlist, the ADR-heading regex against real `DECISIONS.md` text, the handoff skill's fence-scan line, the context-budget arithmetic) was verified against the actual code and text and matches what the plan claims.

## (1) Gaps

- **BLOCKING — `chunks_fts` external-content sync is undecided.** Interfaces § Storage declares `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE chunks_fts USING fts5(heading, body, content='chunks', content_rowid='id', ...)`. An `external content` FTS5 table does **not** update itself when `chunks` is written — SQLite requires either triggers on `chunks` or explicit `INSERT INTO chunks_fts(chunks_fts, rowid, ...) VALUES('delete', ...)`/insert calls issued by the writer, or queries against it can return stale results or fail once the backing row is gone. Reconcile step 5 ("for every oid not in blobs, read the file and insert chunks, records and refs") and the GC clause ("delete blobs … not in any project's view whose last_seen is older than 14 days") never mention writing to `chunks_fts` at all — not on insert, not on the GC delete. Two implementers would genuinely diverge here: one adds triggers in the schema, one issues manual shadow-table writes in Go, a third forgets it and ships a search that returns nothing (or, after the first GC, a corrupt/erroring FTS index once the underlying `chunks` rows it points at are gone). This has to be decided in Interfaces § Storage/Reconcile before `internal/search`'s schema task (Phase 1, first checklist item) starts.
- **BLOCKING (inferable, but unstated) — the query-time join back to the current `files` view is never written down.** Storage's prose says "Everything derived from content is keyed by the git blob ID (`oid`)… `files` is the current view" — implying every branch/commit's content is chunked once into a project-wide, cross-branch cache, and that `search` must restrict hits to oids present in the *current* `files` row for the project. But the Interfaces § Commands / Query description of `search` never states this join explicitly, and it is exactly what the first E2E criterion tests ("after `git switch` to a branch that lacks a word, `search` returns no hit from the other branch"). An implementer who reads only the Commands section and queries `chunks_fts` (a global, non-per-project table with no `project` column) without joining through `chunks.oid = files.oid AND files.project = ?` will produce stale/cross-branch hits and fail that criterion silently in normal use (it only shows up when two branches diverge on a word). Worth one explicit sentence in Query, not left to be inferred from Storage's aside.
- **Non-blocking, but worth a one-line default before Phase 1**: the mapping from a docs-root directory name to a `--kind` value is stated for the one irregular case ("`architecture` → `adr`") but not for the regular ones (`bugs`→`bug`, `changes`→`change`, `handoffs`→`handoff`, `reviews`→`review`, `retros`→`retro`, `specs`→`spec`) — low ambiguity, a reasonable implementer singularizes correctly, but it is technically unstated.
- **Non-blocking**: when an oid (content) is current at more than one path in the same project (duplicate file content, or a rename mid-reconcile), `records`/`refs` are parsed once per oid but the parsing rules are path-dependent (a Bug's ID comes from "the file name's `BUG-NNN`"; a Plan's kind comes from living under `<docs>/plans/`). The plan does not say which path is used when an oid has more than one current path. A rare edge case; a "first path seen this reconcile" default is fine and an implementer would plausibly pick it without asking.

## (2) Scope

Everything under Scope § In traces to a D-row attributing it to the operator's own words or to the research/audit records the operator commissioned (D1–D13). I found no endpoint, output shape, or configuration surface added beyond what a D-row covers:
- The global index, the recall/grep/token baselines, and the vector gate are each tied to specific operator quotes or to the Phase 4 gate the operator explicitly conditioned ("if it gives the agent … more memory", "audit … which services benefit", the eight-row recommendation table).
- `--open` and the metadata graph are the concrete shape of Scope § In bullet 1 ("a metadata graph of the trail … status … cross-references"), not an unrequested addition.
- No config knob is added for a value that plausibly never varies (busy timeout, GC age, per-file cap, snippet length are all fixed constants in the design, not flags).
Scope is clean.

## (3) Readiness

Questions a first-pass implementer would have to ask, or guess at:

1. **BLOCKING** — How does `chunks_fts` stay in sync with `chunks` on insert and on GC delete (triggers vs. manual shadow-table writes)? (Gap 1 above.)
2. **BLOCKING** — Does every `search`/`--refs`/`--open` query join through `files` to restrict hits to the current project's oids, and is that also true for `--global`'s per-project sub-queries? (Gap 2 above.)
3. NON-BLOCKING — directory-name-to-`--kind` mapping for the regular cases (Gap 3): a reasonable implementer singularizes without asking.
4. NON-BLOCKING — which path is used to parse records/refs when an oid has more than one current path (Gap 4): rare, obvious default.
5. NON-BLOCKING — exact `modernc.org/sqlite` DSN syntax for the stated pragmas (the plan writes `journal_mode=WAL, busy_timeout=10000, foreign_keys=off` as intent, not as a literal connection string; the driver takes `_pragma=` query parameters). An implementer translates this without needing to ask.
6. NON-BLOCKING — the Phase 3 byte budget is razor-thin: `go run ./cmd/sh-agent render` on this checkout today measures 21,952 of the 22,000-byte budget, i.e. 48 bytes of headroom before any of the three named cuts are applied. The plan already names this exact contingency ("If these do not free enough, Phase 3 stops and puts further cuts to the operator; the budget is never raised."), so it is not an undecided gap — just flag it as the first thing to measure in Phase 3, since the margin is essentially zero.

I did not find a Verification/E2E criterion that bakes in an implementation choice beyond what Interfaces already commits to, and I did not find a verify-clause fixture that fails to produce the condition it claims (the two candidates I checked — `TestBusyRefusesNotStale`'s "second connection" and `TestConcurrentReconcile`'s "twice as subprocesses" — are both achievable as described: SQLite's file-level locking works across two connections in one process as well as across two processes, so "second connection" doesn't need cross-process to hold a real write lock).

## Criteria

This is a design-document cold-read, not a diff review; the six review-standards criteria apply loosely:
1. Dead code — n/a (no code yet).
2. Flow tracing — fail on the two BLOCKING gaps above (chunks→chunks_fts sync; query→files join); everything else traced (verb switch placement, `Collect`'s explicit allowlist needing a new skip entry, `reorder`/`takesValue`, size-test budget) matches the actual source.
3. Standards conformance — R4's proposed text (D1) correctly threads the "stdlib only" rule change through to the project `AGENTS.md` bullet (Phase 1 task); D9 justifies the one dependency and the no-vendor decision with a measured number, matching the security-exemption/stdlib-first bar. No unaddressed restatement found (checked `REQUIREMENTS.md` R4/R9, project `AGENTS.md`, `README.md` § How it works — R9's four procedures and the map are about delivery paths, not query verbs, so search/index correctly don't need a map change).
4. Directory layout — `internal/search` as a new package, kept out of `internal/harness` so the installer's package doesn't gain the driver, matches the project's Go layout rule and the decoupling concern the plan itself names.
5. Simplicity — pure-Go driver, no vendoring (measured 137 MB, D9), no service/watcher/hook (R3/R8), reconcile-at-query-time (D3) — all justified against the stdlib-first/DIY-except-security bar; no hand-rolled crypto or auth surface in this plan.
6. Decoupling — the oid-keyed, cross-branch content cache decoupled from the per-project `files` view is a reasonable seam, but it is exactly the seam the two BLOCKING gaps sit on: the plan draws the boundary but doesn't finish specifying the maintenance obligation (FTS sync) or the read obligation (current-view join) at that seam.

## Not examined

- The scratch research/audit briefs the plan cites (`plans/2026-09-29-recon-project-index.md`, `plans/2026-09-29-audit-search-consumers.md`, `plans/2026-09-29-research-sqlite-index.md`) were not opened; D-row attributions were taken at the plan's word.
- `agents/*.md` and `skills/*/SKILL.md` files D13 names for one-line additions were not individually opened to confirm the cited line numbers (`skills/review-standards/SKILL.md:48`, `agents/dreamer.md:36,29`, `skills/dream/SKILL.md:41,48`, `skills/bug/SKILL.md:33`, `skills/feature/SKILL.md:19`) — only `skills/handoff/SKILL.md:154` was checked and confirmed accurate.
- `modernc.org/sqlite`'s actual DSN pragma syntax and its FTS5 support surface were not built/run — Risks already flags this as checked only for linux/amd64 (run) and darwin/arm64 (build), with linux/arm64 deferred to the Phase 1 build task; taken as stated.
- Phase 4/5 sandboxed efficiency-run mechanics (cost, kit contents) were read but not evaluated against the actual `.agents/scratch/eff-kit/` (does not exist yet — nothing to check).

title: Cold-read review (round 2) — sh-agent search plan (2026-09-29)
body:
# Cold-read review (round 2) — sh-agent search plan   (2026-09-29)

Range reviewed: `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-29-search-index.md` (design-document cold read, no code yet) plus the code/text surfaces it names: `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` (doc comment, `usage`, the pre-`ResolveSource` verb switch, `reorder`/`takesValue`), `internal/harness/state.go:71-79` (`ConfigDir`), `internal/harness/report.go:225-295` (`Collect`'s explicit per-name allowlist), `REQUIREMENTS.md` R4, project `AGENTS.md` "Stdlib only" bullet, `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` (ADR heading regex against real text, including ADR-035/039/040/042/044's irregular status strings), `skills/handoff/SKILL.md:150-156` (the fence-scan awk), `skills/review-standards/SKILL.md:44-50` and `agents/dreamer.md:25-40` (spot-checked, not exhaustive), and a sample `BUG-*.md` file's frontmatter shape. Diffed the plan itself against git HEAD to see exactly what changed since round 1 (`reviews/2026-09-29-coldread-search-index-r1.md`) — D14, D15, D16, D17 and their corresponding Interfaces edits.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: design needs revision — one new BLOCKING gap found; the two round-1 BLOCKING gaps are genuinely closed.

Round 1's two blocking gaps (FTS5 external-content sync; the query-time join back to the current `files` view) are fixed and I independently re-verified both against the actual Interfaces text, not just against the round-1 report's say-so: the `chunks_ai`/`chunks_ad` triggers are the textbook pattern for an `fts5(..., content='chunks', content_rowid='id')` table, and "Every query reads through `files`" is now spelled out with the exact join for `search`, `--refs` and `--open` alike. Independently reading the plan fresh, I found one new inconsistency in the Interfaces spec itself that neither round 1 nor D14-D17 touched: the `--kind` enum and the global index's own kind assignment disagree.

## (1) Gaps

- **BLOCKING (new) — `--kind`'s accepted values and the global index's actual kind values disagree.** Interfaces § Commands, line 58: "`--kind` one of `bug adr plan change handoff review testing retro spec deploy trail code doc`" — 13 values. Interfaces § Storage's last sentence (line 118): "The global index stores `feedback.jsonl`, `retros.jsonl` and `proposals/*.md` under project `~config`... kind `feedback`, `retro`, `proposal`." Two of those three kinds — `feedback` and `proposal` — are not in the `--kind` enum. `retro` is already covered (docs-root `retros/` also maps to `retro`), so it's fine; `feedback` and `proposal` are not. As written, an implementer validating `--kind` against the documented enum (which Phase 1's query task will do — the enum is exactly what `TestSearchRanksAndCaps`/kind-filter logic needs to check against) has no way to let a user filter `--global --kind feedback` down to just the feedback log, even though rows with that exact kind exist in the database by design. Two implementers diverge concretely here: one silently extends the enum to 15 values so the global kind values are reachable; one implements exactly the documented 13-value enum, in which case `feedback` and `proposal` rows are permanently unfilterable by kind (present in unfiltered/`trail`-adjacent search, invisible to any `--kind` query) — a real behavioural difference, not a style choice. This needs one sentence in Interfaces before the Phase 1 query task and the Phase 2 global-kind task both lock in a `--kind` value list independently.
- **Non-blocking — whether `--global` self-registers the invoking project.** Interfaces § Global registry: "`search` and `index` **without** `--global` upsert `(root, base name, now)` into the global `projects` table after the project reconcile. `--global` reconciles `~config`... then each **registered** project." Taken literally, a project's very first-ever `sh-agent` invocation being `search --global` would reconcile every *other* already-registered project plus `~config`, but never register or reconcile itself (registration only happens on the non-`--global` path) — so a fresh project's own trail would be silently absent from its first global search. In practice this is unlikely to bite: `/init-project` and normal workflow will run a plain `search`/`index` before anyone reaches for `--global`, and the plan's own E2E criterion for `--global` is run from this already-dogfooded repository. A reasonable implementer would most likely make `--global` also perform the local project reconcile+register as a first step (matching user expectation that "global" includes "here"), so I call this non-blocking, but it's worth one explicit sentence given it's cheap to state and the current wording, read strictly, says the opposite.
- Everything else I checked against real repo state matches the plan's claims exactly (not just "R1 said so"): the pre-`ResolveSource` verb switch (`main.go`, `version`/`uninstall`/`report` cases before `harness.ResolveSource`) is exactly where D10 says `search`/`index` will sit; `reorder`'s `takesValue` map and its BUG-002 comment match the plan's flag-ordering claim; `report.go`'s `Collect` is a closed per-name allowlist (`feedback.jsonl`, `retros.jsonl`, `state.json`, `proposals/*.md`) with no wildcard, so "search.db is never collected" is accurate only once an explicit skip entry is added, which is exactly what the Phase 1 task and `TestCollectNeverSendsSearchDB` do; the ADR heading regex correctly parses every irregular status string I tried it against by hand (ADR-035's colon-containing title, ADR-039/042's "superseded... by ADR-041"/"superseded in part by ADR-044" trailing clauses, ADR-044's "amends ADR-042"); the handoff skill's fence-scan awk at `skills/handoff/SKILL.md:154` matches the plan's paraphrase exactly; a real `BUG-*.md` file's frontmatter (`id:`, `status:`, `date:`, `# ` title) matches Records § Bug, and `status: open` (not some other token) is the literal value used by all files carrying it, confirming `--open`'s bug clause. I found no restatement of "no dependencies"/"stdlib only" left unaddressed outside append-only historical ADR/review records (which the project's own layout rule exempts from retroactive edits).

## (2) Scope

Re-confirming round 1's finding, independently: I traced every Scope § In line and every Phase deliverable to a D-row or to a direct quote in `## Why`, and found nothing added beyond what a D-row covers (global index → D5; recall/grep/token baselines and the vector gate → the operator's "go with your recommendations" table via D6/D8; `--open` and the metadata graph → Scope bullet 1, the operator's own words; no speculative config flag for a value that plausibly never varies — busy timeout, GC age, per-file/snippet caps are fixed constants, not flags). Scope is clean.

## (3) Readiness

1. **BLOCKING (new)** — Does `--kind` accept `feedback` and `proposal` (the global index's own kind values), or are those two kinds simply unfilterable? (Gap 1 above.)
2. NON-BLOCKING (new) — Does `--global` also reconcile+register the invoking project on its own, or strictly only already-registered ones? (Gap 2 above.) A reasonable implementer self-registers; state it explicitly.
3. Round-1's two BLOCKING questions (FTS5 sync mechanism; query-time `files` join) are closed by D15/D16 and the corresponding Interfaces text — re-verified independently, not just taken on the round-1 report's word.
4. Round-1's non-blocking questions (kind-mapping table for regular directories, which-path-when-duplicate-oid default, exact DSN syntax) are closed by D14/D17 and the corresponding Interfaces text.

I found no Verification/E2E criterion baking in an unstated implementation choice, and no verify-clause fixture that fails to produce the condition it claims — I specifically re-checked `TestBusyRefusesNotStale` ("a second connection holding `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`") and `TestConcurrentReconcile` ("runs the test binary twice as subprocesses"): both are genuinely achievable as described (SQLite's file-level `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` lock is real across two connections in one process, and `go test -c`'s compiled binary can be exec'd twice as real OS processes).

## Criteria

Design-document cold read, six criteria applied loosely (no code exists yet):
1. Dead code — n/a.
2. Flow tracing — the two round-1 blocking breaks in the `chunks`→`chunks_fts` and query→`files` seams are closed and I re-verified the fix text matches SQLite's actual external-content-table contract; the new `--kind` vs. global-kind-value break (gap 1) is the same class of defect, one level up, between two Interfaces sub-sections that were each internally consistent but never cross-checked against each other.
3. Standards conformance — R4's proposed replacement (D1) and the project `AGENTS.md` "Stdlib only" bullet update trace correctly; D9's 137 MB vendoring measurement supports the no-vendor call under the stdlib-first/DIY-except-security bar; no unaddressed restatement of "no dependencies" found outside append-only historical records.
4. Directory layout — `internal/search` as a new package outside `internal/harness` matches the project's Go layout rule and the plan's own decoupling rationale (installer's package doesn't gain the driver).
5. Simplicity — pure-Go single dependency, no vendoring, no service/watcher/hook, reconcile-at-query-time; no hand-rolled crypto/auth surface anywhere in this plan.
6. Decoupling — the oid-keyed cross-branch cache vs. per-project `files` view seam is now fully specified (round 1's gap); the `--kind` enum vs. global kind-value seam (this round's gap) is the same kind of two-sections-don't-agree issue and should be fixed the same way, in Interfaces, before Phase 1/2 lock in independent enums.

## Not examined

- The scratch research/audit briefs the plan cites (`plans/2026-09-29-recon-project-index.md`, `plans/2026-09-29-audit-search-consumers.md`, `plans/2026-09-29-research-sqlite-index.md`) were not opened this round either; D-row attributions taken at the plan's word, same as round 1.
- Most of D13's individual consumer line citations (`skills/dream/SKILL.md:41,48`, `skills/bug/SKILL.md:33`, `skills/feature/SKILL.md:19`, `skills/retro/SKILL.md`, `agents/dreamer.md:29`) were not opened; I spot-checked `skills/review-standards/SKILL.md:44-50` and `agents/dreamer.md:25-40` only, both plausible but not pinned to the exact cited line number.
- `modernc.org/sqlite`'s actual DSN pragma syntax, FTS5 support, and cross-compile behaviour were not built or run (no module cache / network access from this review) — Risks already states this is checked for linux/amd64 (run) and darwin/arm64 (build) only, linux/arm64 deferred to the Phase 1 build task; taken as stated, not independently re-verified.
- Phase 4/5 mechanics (`.agents/scratch/eff-kit/`) — nothing exists on disk yet to check.
- `internal/harness/size_test.go`'s exact byte budget was not re-measured this round (round 1 measured 21,952/22,000 bytes; D17 notes Phase 3 measures first, which I take as sufficient given the contingency clause was already present and unchanged).

body:
# Cold-read review (round 3) — sh-agent search plan   (2026-09-29)

Range reviewed: `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-29-search-index.md` (design-document cold read, no code yet) plus the code/text surfaces it names: `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` (doc comment, `usage`, `reorder`/`takesValue`), `internal/harness/state.go` (`ConfigDir`), `internal/harness/report.go` (`Collect`'s explicit per-name allowlist), `internal/harness/size_test.go` (the 22,000-byte budget), `REQUIREMENTS.md` R1–R9 (not just R4 — read the whole file this round, since D4 explicitly reasons about a term R7 already uses), a real `BUG-*.md` file's frontmatter, `skills/dream/SKILL.md`, `skills/bug/SKILL.md`, `skills/feature/SKILL.md`, `agents/dreamer.md` (D13's cited consumer lines, spot-checked), `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/` and `.agents/docs/bugs/` directory listings. Also read both prior cold-read rounds (`reviews/2026-09-29-coldread-search-index-r1.md`, `-r2.md`) in full to confirm their findings are actually closed in the current text rather than take the D-rows' word for it.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: design needs revision (two new NON-BLOCKING gaps) — implementation ready (zero BLOCKING questions this round; both prior rounds' BLOCKING gaps stay genuinely closed)

Round 1's two BLOCKING gaps (FTS5 sync, query-time `files` join) and round 2's one BLOCKING gap (`--kind` enum missing `feedback`/`proposal`) are all fixed in the current text and I re-verified each independently: `chunks_fts`'s AFTER INSERT/DELETE triggers are present in the schema (Storage, lines 102-107); "Every query reads through `files`" is spelled out for `search`, `--refs` and `--open` alike (line 116); `--kind`'s line 58 enum now lists `feedback` and `proposal` alongside the other 13 values, matching Storage's kind assignment (line 118); `--global` now self-registers and reconciles the invoking project first (Global registry, line 151), closing round 2's non-blocking item too. I found no BLOCKING gap this round. I found two small NON-BLOCKING gaps neither prior round touched.

## (1) Gaps

- **NON-BLOCKING — R7 and the new feature both use the word "index" for different things, and the plan never touches R7's text.** `REQUIREMENTS.md` R7 (`REQUIREMENTS.md:29`, unchanged by this plan's Surfaces touched list) reads: "The harness's own state (manifest, feedback log, the harness proposal queue, **the cross-project index**) lives in `~/.config/sh-agent/` and nowhere else" — an existing reference to `retros.jsonl` (D4 says so explicitly: "R7 already calls `retros.jsonl` 'the cross-project index'"). The plan's own vocabulary for the new feature is "the global **index**" throughout Scope and Interfaces, its verb is literally `sh-agent index`, and its file is `~/.config/sh-agent/search.db` — landing in the exact directory R7's sentence enumerates, unmentioned by that enumeration. D4 used the R7 collision only to justify the *file name* (`search.db`, not `index.db`); it never revisits R7's prose itself. A reader of `REQUIREMENTS.md` after this ships, with no other context, cannot tell from R7 alone whether "the cross-project index" now means `retros.jsonl`, the new `search.db`, or both — and Surfaces touched names only R4 for `REQUIREMENTS.md` edits, so nothing in the plan closes this. A one-clause fix in Phase 1's R4/D1 task (naming `search.db` in R7's parenthetical, or renaming R7's phrase) settles it; a reasonable implementer would not silently invent a fix on their own since `REQUIREMENTS.md` is immutable without the operator's approval (project `AGENTS.md`) — this has to be an explicit edit, decided before Phase 1's ADR-045/R4/AGENTS.md commit task, not inferred.
- **NON-BLOCKING — `--refs`'s output shape for a directory target is unstated.** Interfaces § Commands says: "For a path, the first line is `<path> tracked|modified|untracked|absent` and then the references" (line 86). Separately, § Refs says a trailing `/` on `--refs X` means X is a directory, matching every ref under that prefix (line 147). A directory has no git blob, so it has no `tracked|modified|untracked|absent` state — the "first line" rule as literally written does not compose with the directory case. Two implementers could diverge: one omits the state line entirely for a directory target and prints only the reference list, one tries to compute a state for the directory itself (and either errors or defaults to something arbitrary). No unit test in Phase 1's `TestRefs` checklist item names a directory-target case, so nothing forces this decision to surface during implementation. A reasonable implementer most likely skips the state line for a directory (the natural reading, since directories were never given a state anywhere else in the spec), so this is non-blocking, but it is worth one clause before `TestRefs` is written.
- Everything else re-checked against real repo state matches the plan's claims exactly: a real `BUG-001` file's frontmatter (`id:`, `status:`, `date:`, `# ` title) matches Records § Bug precisely; the docs-root directory listing (`architecture bugs changes deploy handoffs plans retros reviews specs testing`) matches D17's directory-to-kind table exactly, with no directory left unmapped; `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/` already holds `delivery.md` and `memory-loop.md`, so a new `search.md` there (Phase 3) matches the existing layout convention with no surprise; `report.go`'s `Collect` remains a closed per-name allowlist with no wildcard scan of `~/.config/sh-agent/`, so the Phase 1 task to add an explicit `search.db` skip entry is necessary (not redundant) for the Failure-modes row to actually print it under "skipped"; D13's cited consumer lines (`skills/dream/SKILL.md:41`, `skills/bug/SKILL.md:33`, `skills/feature/SKILL.md:19`, `agents/dreamer.md:29`) each land on the paragraph D13 describes, though `skills/dream/SKILL.md:48` (cited alongside `:41` for "graduation check") is the "doubt resolves to `keep`" sentence rather than the graduation-verdict row itself (that's line 41) — a loose but defensible pairing, not a wrong citation.

## (2) Scope

Re-confirming rounds 1 and 2, independently: every Scope § In line and every Phase deliverable still traces to a D-row or a direct operator quote in `## Why`; the global index → D5, the recall/grep/token baselines and vector gate → D6/D8, `--open` and the metadata graph → Scope bullet 1's own words, the Phase 5 larger-project task → D11 (an implementer inference from the operator's words, attributed, not silent). No config knob for a value that plausibly never varies; no endpoint or output shape without a D-row. Scope is clean.

## (3) Readiness

1. NON-BLOCKING (new) — Does `REQUIREMENTS.md` R7's "the cross-project index" get a clarifying word once `search.db` also lives in `~/.config/sh-agent/`, or does it stay pointed only at `retros.jsonl`? (Gap 1.) State it in the R4/R7 edit task.
2. NON-BLOCKING (new) — For `--refs` on a directory target, is the `<path> tracked|...` first line printed at all? (Gap 2.) A reasonable implementer omits it; state the default.
3. Rounds 1 and 2's BLOCKING questions (FTS5 sync, query-time `files` join, `--kind` vs. global kind values) are closed by D15/D16/D18 and the current Interfaces text — re-verified independently against the schema and prose, not taken on the D-rows' word.
4. Round 1's and round 2's non-blocking questions (kind-mapping table, duplicate-oid path choice, DSN syntax, `--global` self-registration) are closed by D14/D17/D18 and the current text.

No Verification/E2E criterion bakes in an unstated implementation choice; no verify-clause fixture fails to produce the condition it claims (this round re-checked `TestFTSFollowsGC`'s `INSERT INTO chunks_fts(chunks_fts) VALUES('integrity-check')` call, which is the documented way to validate an external-content FTS5 table's shadow-table consistency and genuinely fails if the triggers are wrong — it exercises what it claims to).

## Criteria

Design-document cold read, six criteria applied loosely (no code exists yet):
1. Dead code — n/a.
2. Flow tracing — the chunks↔chunks_fts and query↔files seams (rounds 1-2) and the `--kind`/global-kind-value seam (round 2) stay closed under re-verification; this round's two gaps are lower-stakes cross-references (a REQUIREMENTS.md term, an output-format edge case) rather than a broken data-flow seam.
3. Standards conformance — R4's D1 replacement text is internally consistent; the new gap is R7, a sibling requirement the plan's Surfaces touched list never names, which is exactly the kind of unaddressed restatement the project's own rule on changed-rule restatements flags.
4. Directory layout — `internal/search` outside `internal/harness`, and `specs/sh-agent/search.md` beside the existing `delivery.md`/`memory-loop.md`, both match convention on inspection.
5. Simplicity — pure-Go single dependency, no vendoring, no service; no hand-rolled crypto/auth surface.
6. Decoupling — unchanged from round 2's assessment; no new coupling issue found.

## Not examined

- The scratch research/audit briefs (`plans/2026-09-29-recon-project-index.md`, `plans/2026-09-29-audit-search-consumers.md`, `plans/2026-09-29-research-sqlite-index.md`) were not opened this round either.
- Most of D13's individual consumer-line citations beyond the four spot-checked here (`skills/review-standards/SKILL.md:48`, `skills/handoff/SKILL.md:154`, `skills/retro/SKILL.md`, `agents/bugs.md`, `agents/changelog.md`, `agents/explorer.md`, `agents/reviewer.md`, `agents/security.md`, `skills/research/SKILL.md`) were not opened this round; rounds 1-2 spot-checked a different, disjoint pair.
- `modernc.org/sqlite`'s actual DSN pragma syntax, FTS5 support and cross-compile behaviour were not built or run (no module cache/network access from this review), same limitation both prior rounds stated.
- Phase 4/5 mechanics (`.agents/scratch/eff-kit/`) — nothing exists on disk yet to check.

title: Review — coldread-search-release-readiness-r1 (2026-09-29)
body:
# Review — coldread-search-release-readiness-r1   (2026-09-29)

Range reviewed: `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-29-search-release-readiness.md` (cold-reader check; no diff — a plan document, per dispatch)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: implementation not ready (small number of BLOCKING questions), design needs revision on one point — the plan is otherwise unusually well cross-referenced and its facts (context budget, `--vendor` flag, `.claude` layout, the reused kit, the reused drift seed, the reused waiver text) all checked out against the actual repository state.

## (1) Gaps

- **G1 — Phase 2's trigger condition is undefined, and its own step contradicts it.** Phase 2 header: "only if Phase 1's main-agent count is low." The plan never states a threshold (a number, a fraction, "below N of M") for "low," and Phase 1's own checkpoint has no gate step that decides go/no-go on Phase 2 — the next task after Phase 1's checkpoint is Phase 2's D2 row itself, which assumes the answer is yes. A first-pass implementer with Phase 1 results showing, say, 1 of 6 main-agent searches has no stated rule for whether that counts as "low" (triggering Phase 2, an operator-turn context edit under a 12-byte budget) or "acceptable" (skip Phase 2, go straight to Phase 3). **BLOCKING.**
- **G2 — the clean-arm interface names a permission surface ("the Phase 5 list") by pointer, not value.** `## Interfaces`: `--allowedTools <the Phase 5 list>`. The search-index plan's Phase 5 (`2026-09-29-search-index.md`) was checked and its `--allowedTools` list is recoverable from `eff-kit/`, but the readiness plan never states whether the *same* list applies unchanged to the large-trail lane, which runs a different task (`sh-agent update --check`, editing `testing/sh-agent-matrix.md`) than the sample-app lanes the list was built for. A tool the large-trail tasks need but the sample-app list didn't grant (e.g. a `find`/`wc` used only by the recon-style s2 task) would silently auto-deny mid-run rather than fail the read. NON-BLOCKING — the plan's own failure-mode clause ("a run auto-denied on Antigravity: the command is added by name and the run repeated") covers the failure path when it happens, so a reasonable implementer can discover and patch the list without a design question. Noted because it is the one place the Interfaces section under-specifies a concrete, checkable value.
- **G3 — no docs clause for a Phase 2 context/skill edit.** If D2 changes `context/AGENTS.md` or a skill's wording, project `AGENTS.md` requires `/review --docs` over the change (Phase 2's own checkpoint step names this — good) but the Testing section of project `AGENTS.md` also requires updating `testing/skill-matrix.md` for a changed scenario and this plan's own `## Surfaces touched` list says so too ("`testing/skill-matrix.md` if a scenario changes") — yet no Phase 2 task instructs writing that matrix row. Low risk (the Definition of Done's documentation step would likely catch it), but it is a named surface with no task pointing at it. NON-BLOCKING — a reasonable implementer covers it under Phase 4's "Definition of Done" catch-all step.
- **G4 — the E2E verification criterion for the clean A/B doesn't state a bar.** `## Verification`: "The clean A/B's per-session table exists for Claude Code with both arms delivering; the main agent's `sh-agent search` count is reported for each arm." This is a reporting criterion, not a pass/fail one — it is satisfied by any numbers, including a repeat of the prior 0-of-28 result. Given the plan exists specifically to act on D36 (adoption), the absence of a numeric bar for "adoption achieved" means Phase 1 can complete, Phase 2's own trigger (G1) is undecided, and the plan can reach Phase 3 with D36 still open and no verification clause catching it. This compounds G1 rather than being independent.

## (2) Scope

Nothing found beyond `## Why`. Each phase maps to a named open item: Phase 1 → the two comparison caveats and the "never measured over several sessions" clause; Phase 2 → D36 (main-agent adoption) explicitly; Phase 3 → "the Antigravity runs the release gate needs"; Phase 4 → "trail closed... so `/preflight v1.13.0` is the only next step," matching the operator's quoted request verbatim. The reused kit (`eff-kit/`), reused drift seed, and reused waiver text (`$WAIVE` in `prompts.sh`, confirmed on disk) are all instances of Phase 5 infrastructure from the closed search-index plan being carried forward, not new configuration surface. No extra endpoint, second shape, or unrequested config found.

## (3) Readiness

Blocking questions (would produce different builds):
- **Q1 (= G1).** What count/threshold makes Phase 1's main-agent-search result "low"? Two implementers reading "0 of 28" as the known baseline could reasonably pick "any nonzero triggers Phase 2" or "must clear the same bar the subagents cleared (3 of 3 per session)" — materially different amounts of work (skip Phase 2 vs. edit the 12-byte-tight context under operator sign-off).

Non-blocking (the plan states a workable default, or a competent implementer decides alone without changing the outcome):
- Q2 (= G2): exact `--allowedTools` list for the large-trail lane — recoverable from the existing kit, and the plan's own auto-deny/repeat failure mode absorbs a wrong first guess.
- Q3 (= G3): who writes the `testing/skill-matrix.md` row if D2 fires — covered by the Definition of Done step and `/review --docs`.
- Q4: exact wording of "the drift seed of the search plan's Phase 5" and "same waivers text as the sample apps" — both point at concrete, present artifacts (`testing/2026-09-29-search-efficiency.md`'s `deploy/remote.md` exit-code seed; `eff-kit/prompts.sh`'s `$WAIVE` string), checked and confirmed to exist as described.

Facts checked and found correct (not gaps): the 22,000-byte Antigravity context budget and the plan's implicit "12 bytes free" constraint (`go test -run TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock` → 21988/22000, confirmed); `sh-agent install --vendor claude` exists as a real flag (`cmd/sh-agent/main.go:97`); `ClaudeRoot = ".claude"` confirms the `<home>/.claude/{skills,agents,commands}` layout the Interfaces section assumes; this repository's own `.claude/` is untracked and currently holds no `skills`/`agents`/`commands` symlinks, so the plan's "copy an arm's `.claude/{skills,agents,commands}` into the project" step cannot silently write through a symlink into this repo's real `skills/`/`agents/` trees for the large-trail lane (a real risk had `.claude` been tracked with symlinks, which it is not); Phase 3's eight named skills and seven named agents match exactly the files touched by commit `6ee7bf9` (the only agents/skills commit since `v1.12.1`), including `init-project` (a 2-line addition, confirmed by `git show`) — the list is accurate, not stale or padded; ADR-040 exists in `DECISIONS.md` (superseded by ADR-041, but present as searchable text, which is all the smoke check needs).

design needs revision (G1 is a real gap: a decision gate with no stated threshold sitting in front of an operator-turn edit to a resource that is already 99.9% full). implementation not ready (Q1 is BLOCKING).

title: Cold-reader check — search release readiness (r2) (2026-09-29)
body:
# Cold-reader check — search release readiness (r2)   (2026-09-29)

Range reviewed: `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-29-search-release-readiness.md` (plan document, no diff, per dispatch). A prior round (`reviews/2026-09-29-coldread-search-release-readiness-r1.md`) already ran; this is an independent fresh read, not a rebuttal check — its findings (G1/D3 threshold, now resolved; G2/G3 non-blocking allowedTools/matrix gaps, still open in the same low-risk form) are not repeated except where new evidence changes their status.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: implementation not ready — two new BLOCKING gaps in the Phase 1 kit build that r1 did not reach, both concrete and code-checked against the actual scripts the plan says it reuses.

## (1) Gaps

- **G5 — `metrics.py` does not produce the main-vs-subagent split the plan's own verify clause claims it does. BLOCKING.** Phase 1's D3 task says: "count the large-trail sessions... in which the MAIN agent (not a subagent) ran `sh-agent search` — verify: AI, the transcript split of `metrics.py`." Read `.agents/scratch/eff-kit/metrics.py:47-57`: `scan(main)` and `scan(subs)` are computed into separate dicts `km` (main-transcript tool-call kinds) and `ks` (subagent-transcript kinds) — the split genuinely exists at that point — but line 57 immediately merges them: `sh_search=km.get('sh-agent-search', 0) + ks.get('sh-agent-search', 0)`. Only the summed total is stored per row and printed (line 67: `sum(x['sh_search'] for x in r)`); `km`/`ks` are discarded. As written, the script cannot answer "did the MAIN agent search" — it can only answer "did anything search." This matters concretely: the closed search-index plan's own efficiency data (`testing/2026-09-29-search-efficiency.md`) shows subagent-only counts of 11–22 per session while the main agent's count was 0 in every sample — using the existing combined field for D3 would silently report a high adoption number built entirely from subagent calls, the opposite of what D3 is designed to measure. The plan names no task that changes `metrics.py` to keep `km`/`ks` separate through to the printed/JSON output. Two implementers would build genuinely different things here: one adds a `sh_search_main` field and gates D3 on it (correct); another reuses the existing `sh_search` column as-is (silently wrong, and nothing in the plan's Verification catches the mistake — the E2E criterion just says "the main agent... runs `sh-agent search` in at least 4 of 6," not naming a specific field).
- **G6 — the large-trail lane's three-session shape does not exist in the reused kit; `lane.sh`'s current `large` branch is a single session, and reusing its session labels collides with the sample-app metrics table. BLOCKING.** Plan `## Interfaces`: "Large-trail lane... s1 ... s2 ... s3 ..." — three separate resumed sessions per run. Read `.agents/scratch/eff-kit/lane.sh:10-19`: the `large` branch runs exactly ONE session (`"$sess" "$arm" "$d" "$cli-$arm-large-$n" "$LARGE"`) that both fixes the drift and answers the five questions in one prompt (`prompts.sh:9`, the `LARGE` variable). `score-large.py` scores that single combined session only (checks `ANSWERS.md` content and the drift string in one directory, no per-session split). The readiness plan's s1/s2/s3 shape — and its brand-new s3 task ("add one row to `testing/sh-agent-matrix.md` for `sh-agent version` on a zip place") — has no existing scoring or session-splitting logic to reuse; "Kit: clean-arm mode" (Phase 1's first task) does not name building this. Compounding it: `metrics.py`'s printed table (line 62-67) buckets purely by `sess ∈ {s1,s2,s3,large}` and `arm`, ignoring `app` — if the new large-trail sessions are tagged `s1`/`s2`/`s3` (to match the plan's own naming), they land in the *same* aggregate rows as the sample apps' `s1`/`s2`/`s3` sessions (build-the-app vs. fix-drift-in-a-trail are unrelated tasks), corrupting the median cost/time table the Verification clause requires ("The clean A/B's per-session table exists... with both arms delivering"). Two implementers would tag these differently (e.g., `app=large` with distinct session names) or not notice the collision at all and get a silently merged, meaningless table.
- **G7 — `testing/sh-agent-matrix.md` has no "zip place" column for the s3 task to add a row to. NON-BLOCKING but under-specified.** The matrix's header is `| Verb | Checkout | Plain copy | Release binary |` (`.agents/docs/testing/sh-agent-matrix.md:14`) — three place-kinds, no "zip place" column anywhere in the table, and `version` already has a row with three filled cells. "Add one row... for `sh-agent version` on a zip place" doesn't match the table's actual shape: there is no row to add (version's row exists) and no column to put a zip-place cell into without extending every row's width. A reasonable implementer resolves this by adding a fourth column (the natural fix, matching AGENTS.md's three-ways-in-plus-zip framing) but the plan doesn't say so, and a much lazier implementer could append an orphan row/footnote instead. NON-BLOCKING: the project's testing conventions (one cell per verb × place-kind, "nothing blank") make the column addition the only conforming choice, so a competent implementer decides this alone.
- **G1–G4 (r1, carried forward, status changed):** G1 (Phase 2 trigger threshold) is now **resolved** — D3 states the bar explicitly (n ≥ 4 adopted, n ≤ 3 not adopted) and Phase 1's checkpoint task computes it. G4 (no numeric bar in Verification) is likewise resolved by the same D3 text now present in `## Verification`. G2 (`--allowedTools` list for the large-trail lane) and G3 (no task names writing `testing/skill-matrix.md` for a Phase 2 wording change) are unchanged from r1 — still present, still non-blocking for the same reasons r1 gave (auto-deny/repeat failure mode; Definition of Done catch-all).

## (2) Scope

Nothing found beyond `## Why`, and this agrees with r1: every phase maps to a named open item from the operator's quote or the handoff's Next Steps (D36 adoption, incomplete Antigravity gate runs, unmeasured large-trail benefit, trail-closing). The new large-trail three-session design (G6) is a *scope expansion within* an already-named item ("never measured... over several sessions") — the plan is right to build it, but it is new infrastructure, not a reuse, and should not be described as reused kit without a task that builds it.

## (3) Readiness

Blocking questions (would produce different builds):
- **Q1 (= G5).** Does `metrics.py` need a code change to separate main-agent from subagent `sh-agent search` counts before D3 can be computed, or is the existing combined `sh_search` field intended to be read as "main agent" (it is not — it sums both)? An implementer who doesn't check the script's actual behavior will get D3 wrong silently.
- **Q2 (= G6).** What is the large-trail lane's actual session/tagging structure: is `lane.sh`'s `large` branch rewritten to run three resumed sessions with distinct tags that avoid the sample-app `s1`/`s2`/`s3` buckets in `metrics.py`, and who scores the new s3 (matrix-row) task, since `score-large.py` has no logic for it?
- **Q3 (= G7, weak — leaning non-blocking).** Does the s3 task add a new "Zip place" column to `sh-agent-matrix.md`, or handle the `version`-on-zip-place fact some other way? Two claims about the new dependency are wrong, though: one names the wrong pinned version, and one asserts a `govulncheck` result that no longer holds now that the dependency is in `go.mod`. Neither is a design defect, both are two-word/one-clause fixes.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `AGENTS.md:29,32` — "`govulncheck ./... # clean on go1.25.8+`" and "On a Go older than go1.24.6 or go1.25.8, `govulncheck` reports two standard-library advisories … the fix is upgrading the machine's Go" is no longer true once this range's dependency (`modernc.org/sqlite`, pulling in `golang.org/x/sys` v0.37.0) is in `go.mod`. Verified by running `govulncheck ./...` on `go1.27.1` (above the 1.25.8 floor the doc names): it reports "1 vulnerability in modules you require" (GO-2026-5024 in `x/sys`, per plan D25/`.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-29-search-index.md` D25), not the "0 vulnerabilities" the doc's "clean" claim promises. This advisory is orthogonal to the local Go version — D25 says the fix needs `x/sys` v0.44.0, which needs `go 1.25.0` in the module's `go` directive, ruled out by D21 — so it will keep showing on every machine, including go1.25.8+, until that constraint lifts. `AGENTS.md` was edited in this range (the `go mod download` line was added right above) but the govulncheck lines were not updated to say a third, dependency-pinned advisory is now expected and non-blocking. Fix: add a clause noting the `x/sys` GO-2026-5024 advisory as expected/non-reachable (D25), same treatment as the two stdlib ones.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` ADR-045 — "The pure-Go `modernc.org/sqlite` v1.60.1 was measured here" states the wrong version. `go.mod:16` and `go.sum:22-23` pin `v1.46.1`, matching the plan's own D21 ("`modernc.org/sqlite` is pinned at v1.46.1 … `go get` of v1.60.1 raised this module's `go` directive to 1.26.0 … a Go 1.24 machine … could no longer build"). v1.60.1 was the version *rejected* by D21, not the one shipped; ADR-045's sentence reads as if v1.60.1 is what got pinned. Fix: correct the version number to v1.46.1 in ADR-045's Context paragraph (or add the D21 rejection detail there).

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` ADR-045 — "It adds 7.6 MB to the binary and nine indirect modules" undercounts: `go.mod`'s `require` block lists ten modules besides `modernc.org/sqlite` itself (`dustin/go-humanize`, `google/uuid`, `mattn/go-isatty`, `ncruces/go-strftime`, `remyoudompheng/bigfft`, `golang.org/x/exp`, `golang.org/x/sys`, `modernc.org/libc`, `modernc.org/mathutil`, `modernc.org/memory`), not nine. Minor and doesn't change the decision, but a reader recounting the tree gets ten, not nine.
