- 3 "checkout place runs main's tip unsigned" — left: operator — accepted risk, recorded as an ADR line by `changelog` (R9; a change is a path change under AGENTS.md rule 3).
- 4 "redaction misses token shapes" — fixed at `internal/harness/report.go` (prefixes and regexp needles); rows in `TestReportRedactShapes`.
- 5 "two vendored skills without source or pin" — fixed at `skills/VENDORED.md` (both recorded as forks with the upstream base and pin) and `AGENTS.md` (the vendoring rule names them); `TestVendoredRowsCarryAPin`. Not re-vendored verbatim: both were rewritten locally, and a verbatim copy would change what agents read (an operator choice, below).
- 6 "push errors unscrubbed" — fixed at `internal/harness/report.go` (`pushError`); `TestPushErrorScrubsCredentials`.
- 7 "main.go layout" — left: deferred; both lenses non-blocking.

Round-1 agent findings: reviewer medium "WriteAtomic drops the temp-file-left-behind diagnostic"; security low "gke-basics pin eff85cf is wrong", low "`\b` misses a token after a literal `\n` or `_`; test.pypi.org", low "the release sweep is not tested end to end", low "two read-only globs remain".

## Round 2

- "diagnostic dropped" — fixed at `internal/harness/apply.go` (`abandon`); `TestAbandonNamesATempFileItCouldNotRemove`.
- "gke-basics pin wrong" — fixed at `skills/VENDORED.md:30` (google/skills 6f0b877, SKILL.md the only local change; verified by the verifier with `git archive` + `diff -r`).
- "`\b` misses escaped and underscored tokens; test.pypi.org" — fixed at `internal/harness/report.go` (no leading `\b`; second PyPI prefix); rows in `TestReportRedactShapes`.
- "release sweep untested end to end" — fixed at `internal/harness/release_test.go` (`TestUpdateFromReleaseSweepStaysInHome`).
- "read-only globs at `state.go:137` and `internal/search/reconcile.go:185`" — left: operator — outside this task; the security agent's round 3 confirms neither can do more than read.

Round-2 agent findings: reviewer medium and security low "WriteAtomic now renames before closing and returns a close error for a file already in place" (introduced by the round-1 fix); security low "sk_test_, rk_test_, sk-svcacct-, sk-admin-, workflows webhook, percent-escaped userinfo", low "the sweep's age limit is untested", low "split date wrong".

## Round 3

A round-1 fix caused the round-2 defect (WriteAtomic's ordering). The mechanism's purpose is not in doubt: the original order, close before rename, is the one every caller and the settings writer relied on, so it was restored rather than redesigned, and the two-attempt fix is recorded by `bugs`.

- "rename before close" — fixed at `internal/harness/apply.go` (close, then rename; nil after); `TestWriteAtomicClosesBeforeRename` (a source-level pin, added after the round-3 agents ran, test-only, diff read by the main agent).
- "more token shapes" — fixed at `internal/harness/report.go` (five prefixes, `%` in the url-token class); rows in `TestReportRedactShapes`.
- "age limit untested" — fixed at `internal/harness/release_test.go` (a fresh `release-young` must survive; age zero fails it).
- "split date" — fixed at `skills/VENDORED.md:30` (5d9d054, 2026-06-23).

Round-3 agent findings: reviewer APPROVE, none; verifier PASS, "close-before-rename has no covering test" (closed by the pin test above); security low "upper-case host, 16–19-character userinfo, `hooks.slack.com/triggers/`, `=`-padded token, `sk-None-`" (fourth pass over the deny-list; put to the operator as one choice), low "ordering untested" (closed), low "`deploy/local.md:66` enumerates the old shapes" (to `documentation`).

## Outcome

- 1 fixed — `internal/harness/apply.go` `WriteAtomic`, `cmd/sh-agent/main.go`.
- 2 fixed — `internal/harness/sweep.go`, `release.go`, `main.go`.
- 3 left: operator — accepted risk, ADR by `changelog` (R9; checkout places follow `main` by design).
- 4 fixed — `internal/harness/report.go`; remaining shapes after three rounds left: operator — one choice: (a) generalise to one rule per kind (`(?i)hooks\.slack\.com/`, `://[^/\s:@]{16,}@`, an `sk-None-` prefix), recommended, or (b) accept and record; the redaction is documented as a safety net, not a guarantee (`delivery.md` § report).
- 5 fixed — `skills/VENDORED.md`, `AGENTS.md`; left: operator — whether the two forks should be renamed to satisfy the "differently named skill" rule (recommended: keep the names; the rule's purpose, that a re-fetch never overwrites local text, is now stated in the manifest).
- 6 fixed — `internal/harness/report.go` `pushError`.
- 7 left: operator — `main.go` layout, deferred; both lenses non-blocking. Struck 2026-09-30 on the operator's word ("Go with your recommendations"): the file works, and splitting it is churn.
- Docs: `deploy/local.md:66` and `specs/sh-agent/delivery.md:56` describe the redaction shapes — in flight: `documentation`.
- Operator's choices (2026-09-30, "Go with your recommendations"): finding 4's remainder fixed by one rule per kind (`changes/2026-09-30-0910-redaction-per-kind-rules.md`, `reviews/2026-09-30-security-worktree-redaction.md` § Outcome); finding 5's fork names kept.

title: Review — project-prompts (2026-09-30)
body:
# Review — project-prompts   (2026-09-30)

Range reviewed: the whole repository at HEAD (3478a1c)

## Status: COMPLETE

Lens: `review-standards/references/prompt-audit/prompt-audit.md` (Anthropic prompt-audit reference, Apache-2.0, vendored verbatim per `skills/VENDORED.md`), executed as a `--project`-scope audit over this harness checkout's own prompt surface.

## Step 0 — Scope and target model

**Scope**, from the dispatch: `AGENTS.md` (root), `context/AGENTS.md`, `context/dev-setup.md`, `agents/*.md` (8 files), `skills/*/SKILL.md` less the six vendored skills (`grilling`, `codebase-design`, `find-skills`, `anti-ui-slop`, `gke-basics`, `terraform`, per `skills/VENDORED.md`), `commands/*.md`, `rules/*.md`. No `CLAUDE.md` or `GEMINI.md` exists at the root (by design — root `AGENTS.md` says "no CLAUDE.md, no GEMINI.md"; R2). `commands/` and `rules/` hold only `.gitkeep` — no prompt content there to audit. `.claude/settings.local.json` exists but is a settings file (Step 1 explicitly excludes settings/credential files from reading) — not opened. `.agents/rules/` does not exist in this repo.

**Target models**: this harness explicitly deploys one context to two vendors — Claude Code and the Antigravity CLI (Gemini) — so every instruction file in scope is read by both. No finding in this report rests on one model's documented behaviour alone; per the dispatch, any such finding would be downgraded to `flag`, but none arose.

## Step 1 — Inventory

- `AGENTS.md` (root, 90 lines) — project rules, source of the global context.
- `context/AGENTS.md` (67 lines) — the global context, deployed verbatim to both vendors.
- `context/dev-setup.md` (13 lines) — appended to the context at install.
- `agents/bugs.md`, `agents/changelog.md`, `agents/documentation.md`, `agents/dreamer.md`, `agents/explorer.md`, `agents/reviewer.md`, `agents/security.md`, `agents/verifier.md` — 8 subagent definitions (76–108 lines each), Claude Code format.
- 22 non-vendored `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`: `bash`, `bug`, `cloud-run-deploy`, `distill`, `docker`, `dream`, `feature`, `feedback-log`, `frontend`, `gcloud-setup`, `golang`, `handoff`, `init-project`, `json-api-style`, `mermaid-syntax`, `preflight`, `python`, `research`, `retro`, `review`, `review-standards`, `typescript` (28–281 lines each).
- `commands/`, `rules/` — empty (`.gitkeep` only).
- No request-building code, no tool-schema definitions, no few-shot blocks, no application system-prompt assembly code anywhere in scope: this is a pure agent-configuration surface (Group 4 mostly not applicable, per the dispatch).

## Step 2 — Provenance

Checked `.agents/docs/bugs/INDEX.md` (through BUG-089) and `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` (ADR ids cross-referenced below) for every prohibition and emphatic line that looked like a candidate. Every prohibition/emphasis instance found in scope either (a) carries its own stated reason in the same sentence, or (b) traces to a specific bug row or ADR already cited inline in the text (e.g. BUG-004 frontmatter quoting, BUG-006/015 install-vs-copy, BUG-041 crypto/rand vs. hand-rolled, BUG-085 the GANNET canary and the 24,000-byte cap, ADR-029/030/033/035/038/045/045a — all verified to exist in `DECISIONS.md`). None of the historical dates or bug/ADR citations read as decorative "history narrative" (Group 2 row) — each is load-bearing: it is either the reason a still-active constraint exists, or (in `REQUIREMENTS.md`'s case) the required amendment trail for a file that is immutable without the operator's approval.

## Step 3/4 — Classification and anti-pattern scan

Ran the Group 1 signal greps (§1a–1f of the lens: `MUST|NEVER|ALWAYS|CRITICAL|IMPORTANT` density, `think step by step`/`<scratchpad>`/prefill scaffolds, hedge words, word/turn-count ceilings, grader vocabulary, date-conditionals, anti-formatting rules, trait claims, identity stubs, `Remember,|Again,|As stated above`, retired-model names, reminder cadences) across `context/`, `agents/`, and all 22 non-vendored `SKILL.md` files, then read the full text of `context/AGENTS.md`, `context/dev-setup.md`, root `AGENTS.md`, all 8 `agents/*.md`, and `skills/{bug,feature,preflight}/SKILL.md` in full (the three most likely to carry patch-accretion cruft, per their bug history of repeated gate revisions — BUG-018, BUG-026, BUG-042).

Result: no Group 1 hits. The one non-trivial grep hit (`MUST`/`NEVER` in `mermaid-syntax/SKILL.md:112,175`) is exact-syntax contract text for a fragile operation (Mermaid frontmatter and namespace rules) — keep-list items 3 and 4, not cruft. The `v11.5.0` version note in the same file documents a specific historical Mermaid bug range and its fix; it is tool-contract knowledge, not a stale prompt scaffold, and nothing in the repository contradicts it. No `<scratchpad>`, no assistant-prefill pattern, no forced-tool-choice pattern, no numeric word/turn caps, no grader vocabulary, no anti-formatting rules, no identity-stub role lines, no retired-model names, no reminder-cadence text anywhere in scope.

Every prohibition in `context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules and root `AGENTS.md` carries its own reason in the same sentence (e.g. "Never hand-roll auth, crypto… — vetted libraries only. Calling the standard library's `crypto/*` as designed… is not hand-rolling") — these read as reasoned, current constraints (keep-list item 5), not inherited pressure language from older models. The project's own stated design ("No hooks, gates, or scripts stand behind these rules; they hold because they are read") explains the density of `NEVER`/`ALWAYS` without it being dated-model over-triggering language: each instance is a distinct, reasoned constraint rather than a repeated intensifier.

**Group 2 — stale facts / cross-file contradiction.** Checked every file path and test name that `AGENTS.md` (root) and `context/AGENTS.md` name against the actual tree: `internal/harness/plan.go`, `internal/harness/derive.go`, `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-03-rebuild.md`, `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md`, `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md`, `internal/harness/report.go`, `internal/search/search.go`, `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md`, `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md`, `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-03-verify-sandbox.md`, `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-03-verify-real-home.md`, `.agents/docs/retros/2026-09-18-retro-2.md`, `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/search.md`, `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-29-dreamer-memory-loop.md`, `REQUIREMENTS.md § Known limits` — all present. Named test functions (`TestHarnessMap`, `TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock`, `TestSendReport`, `TestDryRunNeverBuilds`, `TestReadsNeverLeaveCheckout`) all resolve to real files under `internal/`/`cmd/`. All 8 ADR ids cited in the two AGENTS.md files exist in `DECISIONS.md`. No cross-file contradiction found between `context/AGENTS.md`, root `AGENTS.md`, and the 8 agent definitions: the repeated "docs root resolution" and "Records/Scratch/Never" boilerplate across all 8 agent files is identical working redundancy (keep-list item 8), and the ownership split between `changelog` (changes/, DECISIONS.md) and `documentation` (README, specs, testing/deploy guides, ROADMAP Next/Later) is stated consistently in both files with no overlap claimed twice.

**Group 3 — tool descriptions.** Not applicable in the conventional sense: this project defines no custom API tool schemas. The closest analogue, the `tools:` frontmatter lists on the 8 agents, name only Claude Code's built-in tools (`Read`, `Grep`, `Glob`, `Edit`, `Write`, `Bash`) — no worked examples, no scolding cross-references, no fake dialogue embedded in any agent's tool list or body.

**Group 4 — request config / sub-agent roster.** No request-building code in scope (not applicable). Roster check (the one Group-4 item that always applies): compared all 8 agents pairwise for near-duplicate task+toolset pairs. `bugs`, `changelog`, and `documentation` share the identical tool list (`Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write`) but write to disjoint artifact classes (bug records, changelog/ADRs, and how-it-works docs respectively) with no overlapping ownership claimed — not a duplicate roster entry. `explorer` and `dreamer` share `Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Write` but operate over disjoint inputs (codebase recon vs. memory-store/trail consolidation) and produce disjoint artifacts (recon brief vs. retro candidate list) — not a duplicate. `reviewer` and `security` share `Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Write` but have explicitly distinct checklists (six general-correctness criteria vs. six security-specific checks), different trigger conditions (size threshold vs. "touches auth/crypto/secrets/IAM/parsing/dependencies, any size"), and different models/effort (`sonnet`/high vs. `opus`/max) — a deliberate two-lens split named in the Definition of Done, not redundancy. No roster finding.

## Findings

None at high or medium confidence. The surface is clean: every prohibition and emphasis instance found carries its own reason or traces to a bug/ADR record that still applies, no dated scaffolds or scoring/grader vocabulary appear anywhere in scope, every path and test name the instruction files cite resolves in the current tree, and the sub-agent roster has no redundant pair.

Two low-confidence, non-actionable observations (left out of the proposed diff per the lens's own threshold — flagged, not fixed):

- **[flag / confidence: low]** `skills/mermaid-syntax/SKILL.md:159` — "Fix: Upgrade to Mermaid v11.5.0+." This is idiom-dated only in the trivial sense that any pinned library version eventually ages; nothing in the repository contradicts it (it documents a specific historical bug range, not the current recommended version), so it is not a Group-2 stale-fact finding under the lens's own bar (a claim the repository contradicts). No action proposed.
- **[flag / confidence: low]** `feedback-log/SKILL.md:56` and `distill/SKILL.md:156` both reference a 2026-09-13 format cutover for `feedback.jsonl`'s `rule_ref` field ("Entries written before 2026-09-13 use free text and are simply never matched"). This is migration-relative phrasing (Group 1d signal) but is functionally necessary here — it tells the agent how to treat old log rows it may still read — so it is not proposed for removal; noted only because the lens's signal list would flag the phrasing pattern.

## Proposed diff

None. No finding reached the high/medium-confidence, actionable bar (Step 6 of the lens). An audit that finds nothing changes nothing.

## Criteria

1. Dead code — n/a — prompts lens
2. Flow tracing — n/a — prompts lens
3. Standards conformance — n/a — prompts lens
4. Directory layout — n/a — prompts lens
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — n/a — prompts lens
6. Decoupling — n/a — prompts lens

## Not examined

- Full line-by-line reads of 19 of the 22 non-vendored `SKILL.md` files (`bash`, `cloud-run-deploy`, `distill`, `docker`, `dream`, `feedback-log`, `frontend`, `gcloud-setup`, `golang`, `handoff`, `init-project`, `json-api-style`, `mermaid-syntax`, `python`, `research`, `retro`, `review`, `review-standards`, `typescript`): these were covered by the Group 1 signal-grep sweep (§1a–1f patterns) across their full text plus targeted spot-checks of the hits it returned, not by a full sentence-by-sentence read against Step 3's "could the model already know this" test. `bug`, `feature`, and `preflight` were read in full.
- `review-standards/SKILL.md` was not re-read from this repo's copy on disk; its content is known verbatim because it is the file that invoked this audit (this repo is the source `sh-agent` deploys from), so the deployed and checked-out copies are the same file by construction.
- External verification of the Mermaid-version claim (`v11.5.0`) against the currently shipping Mermaid release — out of the repository's own record, so left as a low-confidence flag rather than checked.
- `.claude/settings.local.json` — a settings/credential-adjacent file the lens's Step 1 says not to read; not opened, consistent with the lens.
- No PR or diff range exists for this dispatch (whole-repo `--project` scope was named explicitly), so no "what changed since the last audit" comparison was possible; this is a from-scratch pass, not a delta from a prior prompt-audit report (none exists in `.agents/docs/reviews/` to diff against).

title: Review — project-simplify (2026-09-30)
body:
# Review — project-simplify   (2026-09-30)

Range reviewed: the whole repository at HEAD (3478a1c), no diff.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing broken. The codebase is unusually well-documented for its complexity (nearly every non-obvious branch cites a BUG-/D-/ADR- number for the edge case it guards), `deadcode ./...` finds no genuinely unreachable production code, `go mod tidy -diff` shows no unused module, and the one cross-package dependency between the two internal packages (`internal/search` calling `harness.SecretShaped`) is exactly the kind of small, single-function reuse this lens wants to see rather than a duplicated reimplementation. The one real finding is a duplicated atomic-write sequence that has already needed a manual two-place fix once (evidenced by the code's own comments); the rest are lower-confidence architectural observations, not defects.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/apply.go:309-347` (`writeAtomic`) and `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:908-935` (the settings-file writer inside `attributionSet`) independently implement the same temp-file-then-rename sequence: `CreateTemp` in the destination directory, write, `Sync`, `Chmod`, `Close`, `Rename`, with cleanup on each failing step. This is not a style duplication — the apply.go comment at line 328-332 says the fsync step "was fixed there first" in the settings writer and had to be ported across, i.e. the exact failure mode (a fix landing in one copy and needing manual porting to the other) has already happened once. Shorter fix: extract the shared steps (temp-create, write, sync, chmod, close, rename, cleanup-on-error) into one helper in `internal/harness` that returns a plain `error`; have `attributionSet` call it and translate the returned error into its own `"settings: %s could not be written (%v)"` messages, instead of re-running the five-step sequence inline. This removes ~25 duplicated lines and the two-place-fix hazard.

- **[low / confidence: low]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` (1199 lines) mixes CLI dispatch (`run`) with several self-contained pieces of logic that have no dependency on `flag`, `os.Args`, or CLI output framing and could live in `internal/harness` as independently testable units: the settings-JSON attribution editor (`attributionSet`, `attributionHint`, `attributionOff`, `readSettings`, `settingsUnwritable`, `abandonTemp`, roughly lines 815-1035) and the PATH-shadow reporter (`pathHint`, lines 788-814, which is a thin wrapper over `harness.PathShadows`/`harness.RunningElsewhere`, both already in `internal/harness`). Moving them would shrink the one file two engineers currently share for "install output," "attribution notice," and "update/zip" work, letting those be edited in parallel without touching the same 1199-line file. Not a correctness issue — flagged for the "files independently editable" test in this lens, at low confidence since the current grouping (everything the `install`/`update` commands print) is a defensible single concern too.

## Criteria

1. Dead code — pass. `deadcode ./...` reports one candidate (`internal/harness/release.go:422 SwapReleaseSigner`) but it is called from `cmd/sh-agent/zip_test.go` (a different package's test), so it is a deliberate test seam, not dead code; the tool's non-test build graph simply can't see it. No commented-out code blocks, no unreachable branches, no unused module found (`go mod tidy -diff` empty).
2. Flow tracing — not in this lens
3. Standards conformance — not in this lens
4. Directory layout — not in this lens
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass, with the one reuse finding above counted here too (the duplicated write sequence is the main simplicity gap found); the security-sensitive path-safety code (`zipNameSafe` in `internal/harness/zip.go`) layers a manual absolute/`..`/backslash check in front of `filepath.IsLocal`, which looks redundant at first read but is deliberate defense against Windows-backslash paths that `IsLocal` does not special-case on Unix — not flagged, since this is exactly the kind of belt-and-suspenders the DIY-except-security exemption asks reviewers not to second-guess.
6. Decoupling — pass, with the one low-confidence note above; the `internal/search` → `internal/harness` dependency is a single well-scoped function (`SecretShaped`) called one way only, which is the interface size this criterion wants, not a reach-in.

## Not examined

Markdown surfaces (`context/`, `agents/*.md`, `commands/`, `rules/`, individual `skills/*/SKILL.md` bodies) were surveyed only at the directory/manifest level (skill count against `AGENTS.md`'s "Skills (28)" and `skills/VENDORED.md`'s provenance table, which reconcile); their prose was not read line by line for dead/redundant instructions. `internal/search/store.go`'s SQLite schema-versioning path and `internal/harness/report.go`'s clone/push flow (both flagged in the initial survey as candidates) were read only at the function-signature level, not traced for efficiency; nothing suspicious surfaced in that pass, but a full read could still find something this budget didn't reach. Test files were not reviewed (out of lens: flow tracing/standards, and reuse across test helpers specifically was not checked).

title: Review — v1.13.0-f00d059-code (2026-09-30)
body:
# Review — v1.13.0-f00d059-code   (2026-09-30)

Range reviewed: v1.13.0..f00d059

Source diff: `git diff v1.13.0...f00d059 -- cmd internal skills/VENDORED.md` (12 Go files and VENDORED.md), plus the living docs the range changed that describe the changed behaviour (`.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md`, `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, deploy guides) where they restate it. Trail records (reviews, changes, bugs, handoffs, plans, testing logs) were read only where a finding needed them.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing in the range is broken. `WriteAtomic`, `abandon`, `SweepStaleDirs`, `pushError` and the new needles are correct as written, every regexp compiles under RE2 (package init runs in the targeted tests, which pass at f00d059), and the removed names (`writeAtomic`, `globOrNil`, `sweepStaleZipDirs`, `abandonTemp`) have no reference left in Go code. The worst item is low: two new prefix needles, `sk_test_` and `rk_test_`, are plain substrings, so ordinary snake_case identifiers such as `task_test_`, `disk_test_`, `network_test_`, `framework_test_` or `benchmark_test_` redact a whole feedback record. That is the "bare `sk-` matches every `task-`" case the needle list's own doc comment says is avoided, and no test pins it. The other findings are low too: two new tests assert on source text, which `review-standards` § 2 rejects; the settings-write error branch that changed has no behavioural test; the delivery spec's list of needles omits the Slack-webhook rule. None blocks a PATCH release.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/report.go:48` — `"sk_test_"` and `"rk_test_"` are matched with `strings.Contains` (`needleIn`, report.go:110). They occur inside common identifiers: `ta`+`sk_test_`, `di`+`sk_test_`, `ma`+`sk_test_`, `netwo`+`rk_test_`, `framewo`+`rk_test_`, `benchma`+`rk_test_`, `bookma`+`rk_test_`. A feedback or retro line that names, for example, `network_test_utils.py` or `run_benchmark_test_suite` is replaced whole by the redaction marker. This errs on the safe side (nothing leaks), but the correction is lost from the report, and it contradicts the invariant in the comment at report.go:36-38 ("Nothing shorter than a vendor's own prefix is listed — a bare `sk-` would match every 'task-'"). The benign list in `TestReportRedactShapes` (report_test.go:128-134) does not include such a word, so the behaviour is neither pinned nor refused. Fix: pin these two by length and alphabet, as the OpenAI rule already is: a keyword needle `[sr]k_(test|live)_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}` (Stripe secret and restricted keys carry 24+ characters after the prefix). A preceding-character boundary would not work, because it would reintroduce the missed-after-literal-`\n` case from the security check. Then add `network_test_helpers` and `task_test_data` to the benign list, and lengthen the `sk_test_FAKEVALUE`-style fixtures to a realistic size. The alternative is to accept it and add those words to the pinned over-redaction list. That is an operator choice; I recommend the length pin, because it changes one line per needle.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go:1799` `TestSettingsWriteUsesHarnessWriteAtomic` and `internal/harness/harness_test.go:1905` `TestWriteAtomicClosesBeforeRename` assert on source text (`os.ReadFile("main.go")`, `os.ReadFile("apply.go")` plus `strings.Index`), which `review-standards` § 2 rejects ("tests that assert on source text rather than behaviour"). They are also weaker than they look. The second one takes the FIRST `tmp.Close()` in the function body, so a comment inside `WriteAtomic` that mentions `tmp.Close()` above the rename would make it pass whatever the call order. The first replaced the deleted behavioural test `TestAbandonTempReportsRemoveFailure`. That test's diagnostic now lives in `abandon` and is covered behaviourally by `TestAbandonNamesATempFileItCouldNotRemove`, so what the source test adds is only a design pin. Fix for the first: replace it with the behavioural test in the next finding, which covers the same seam through behaviour. For the second, the order is truly unobservable after a successful return. Either accept it explicitly as a documented structural pin in the report's Outcome, or restrict the search to code lines (skip lines whose trimmed text starts with `//`) so a comment cannot satisfy it.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:907-909` — the settings-write error branch changed from `abandonTemp` to `harness.WriteAtomic` plus `settingsUnwritable`, and no test drives `attributionSet` into it. `grep "could not be written" cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` finds nothing. The earlier logs (`testing/2026-09-16-verify-attribution-write.md:39`) already recorded this gap, and the range leaves it open while changing the branch. Fix (non-root; skip as root, as the neighbouring tests do): a settings file in a directory chmodded `0o500`, `attributionSet` run with `dryRun=false`, then assert that the output contains `could not be written` and `add the key by hand`, and that the file is byte-identical afterwards.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md:56` — the enumerated needle vocabulary ("vendor token prefixes, … token shapes pinned by length and alphabet (a JWT, an OpenAI key, an npm or Hugging Face token), and a bare userinfo token in a URL") has no entry for the new `slack webhook` rule (`(?i)hooks\.slack`, report.go:87). That rule is a host match, not a token prefix or a length-pinned shape. The global context's describing-text rule requires every enumeration to change when a value joins a vocabulary. Fix: add "any Slack webhook URL" to that sentence.
- **[low / confidence: medium, pre-existing, not introduced by the range]** `skills/VENDORED.md:24-31` — the range now states correctly that `gke-basics` and `terraform` are local rewrites that keep their upstream names. That contradicts the project `AGENTS.md` rule "Third-party skills are vendored verbatim … never edit them in place — fork into a differently named skill". Because they stay listed in VENDORED.md, they are also excluded from the `/review --docs` living-docs set ("every skill directory under `skills/` not listed in `skills/VENDORED.md`"), even though they carry harness-specific cross-references written here. Not a blocker for this PATCH. It is a one-line operator choice: rename both forks (recommended: it restores the rule), or amend the rule to name these two as grandfathered forks that `/review --docs` still reads.

## Checks made (no finding)

- `WriteAtomic` (apply.go:309): Write, Chmod, Sync, Close, Rename, and every failure goes through `abandon`. After Close, an error means `dest` is unchanged. `abandon`'s second `Close` on the Close and Rename branches returns `os.ErrClosed` and is ignored, with no double close of the fd. The five callers (`apply.go:79`, `adopt.go:175`, `release.go:170`, `state.go:68`, `main.go:907`) all propagate or report the error. For the settings path, `MkdirAll` is a no-op (the file was just `Stat`ed), `tmp.Chmod(info.Mode().Perm())` matches the old `os.Chmod`, and the temp name changes from `.settings-*.json` to `.sh-agent-*` (harmless).
- `SweepStaleDirs` (sweep.go): ReadDir plus a prefix match, skipping symlinks (by DirEntry type) and non-directories, with an Lstat age check and RemoveAll. Two callers: `release.go:147` (ConfigDir, `release-`) and `main.go:1129` (the zip parent, `zip-`, only after a successful install and never on dry run). With parent `""`, `ReadDir` errors and nothing happens, as before. The release sweep now keeps directories younger than 1 h where it previously removed every match. That is intended (ADR/BUG-109), and a leftover under an hour old only costs disk space until the next run. Both callers have a test that fails on the old code: `TestUpdateFromReleaseSweepStaysInHome`, where the `u[1]` glob removed the sibling and skipped its own home, and `TestUpdateFromZipSweepsStaleDirs`. The zip path now prints a `removed …` line where it was silent before. Nothing asserts on the old silence.
- `pushError` (report.go:946): `scrubCredentials` runs before classification, so a rewrite that puts credentials in the URL cannot hide `! [rejected]`. `errPushRejected` stays wrapped with `%w`. The underlying exec error is no longer wrapped, and no caller uses `errors.As` on it (the only consumers are `errors.Is(err, errPushRejected)` at report.go:768 and 794). `TestPushErrorScrubsCredentials` fails without the scrub.
- Regexps: every pattern in report.go is valid RE2 (they compile at init; the targeted tests ran green: `go test -count=1 ./internal/harness ./cmd/sh-agent -run 'Sweep|WriteAtomic|Abandon|Redact|PushError|Vendored|SettingsWrite|Zip|UpdateFromRelease|Attribution'`, both `ok`; `go vet` clean on both packages). False positives on prose beyond what is pinned:
  - `sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{32,}` fires only on `…sk-` followed by 32+ alphanumerics (a hex digest after `task-`/`disk-`). Rare, and documented.
  - `hf_[A-Za-z0-9]{30,}` (`shelf_`…) and `npm_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}` are rare.
  - `(?i)hooks\.slack` fires on any prose naming a Slack webhook host. That errs on the safe side and is deliberate.
  - `://[^/\s:@]{16,}:?@` also fires on `<https://example.com>,<me@x.com>` and on pathless URLs with a query holding an email (`https://site.example?to=a@b`). These are the same class as the pinned second over-redaction case.
  - Only the `sk_test_`/`rk_test_` substring case above is a new, unpinned class.
- New tests assert what their names claim: `TestAbandonNamesATempFileItCouldNotRemove` (both branches), `TestSweepStaleDirsStaysInParent` (its symlink branch is also excluded by `!e.IsDir()`, so removing the explicit symlink check would not fail it; both checks are redundant, so this is no defect), `TestVendoredRowsCarryAPin` (fails on the old "not recorded when vendored" rows), `TestPushErrorScrubsCredentials`, and `TestUpdateFromReleaseSweepStaysInHome`. The two source-text tests are the exception (finding 2).

## Criteria

1. Dead code — pass. `abandonTemp`, `sweepStaleZipDirs`, `globOrNil`, the `io/fs` import in main.go and the unexported `writeAtomic` are removed with no Go references left. The mentions that remain are in dated trail records only.
2. Flow tracing — pass. `WriteAtomic` (five callers), `abandon`, `SweepStaleDirs` (two callers) and `pushError` (one caller, two consumers of `errPushRejected`) were traced end to end, and errors propagate. The one uncovered changed branch is finding 3.
3. Standards conformance — pass with findings. gofmt and vet are clean (vet run here; gofmt left to the verifier). The source-text tests conflict with `review-standards` § 2 (finding 2). One describing-text gap is in delivery.md (finding 4). Stdlib only.
4. Directory layout — pass. `sweep.go` and `sweep_test.go` sit beside each other in `internal/harness`. The tests live beside their code.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. One shared atomic writer and one shared sweep replace duplicated copies, and there is no new dependency. The redaction needles are pattern matching, not crypto or auth. No hand-rolled primitive.
6. Decoupling — pass. `cmd/sh-agent` consumes two small exported functions (`WriteAtomic`, `SweepStaleDirs`) with plain signatures. No reach-in.

## Not examined

- The trail records added in the range (reviews, changes, bugs BUG-109..112, handoffs, plans, testing logs, DECISIONS.md), beyond the lines cited above. `AGENTS.md`, `README.md` and the deploy-guide one-line edits were checked only for restatements of the changed behaviour, not reviewed as docs (that is `/review --docs`).
- The full test suite and `go test -race`: I ran only the targeted `-run` subset above, which is the verifier's job, not a verdict.
- The upstream provenance claims in `skills/VENDORED.md` (pins `6f0b877`, `2271bc4`) were not checked against the upstream repositories.

## Outcome
- 1 `sk_test_`/`rk_test_` match inside ordinary names — fixed before the tag: a `stripe key` needle `[sr]k_(live|test)_[A-Za-z0-9]{16,}` replaces the four bare prefixes (`report.go`), two benign rows in `TestReportRedactShapes` fail without the length.
- 2 source-text tests — fixed in part: `TestWriteAtomicClosesBeforeRename` now reads code lines only (a comment naming the close no longer passes it), and `TestAttributionSetReportsAnUnwritableSettingsFile` drives the settings-write error branch; rebutted for the rest: both pins cover what no behavioural test can observe (the ordering, documented at `apply.go` `WriteAtomic`; the duplication, whose behaviour `TestWriteAtomic*` and the settings tests cover), which `review-standards` § 2 allows as a named exception when the record says so — this record does.
- 3 `delivery.md:56` leaves out the Slack rule — fixed (Stripe keys and Slack webhook hosts named).
- 5 the two forks keep upstream names — left: operator — "Go with your recommendations" (2026-09-30), the recommendation being to keep the names; `AGENTS.md` and `skills/VENDORED.md` state the exception.

# Review — v1.16.2-a275b96-docs   (2026-09-30)

Range reviewed: v1.16.2..a275b96

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Docs lens only (criteria not applied). The spec (`specs/sh-agent/dream.md`) matches the round-2 code: agy stdin stream-json with a private HOME, the Claude strict flags, `toolPermission`, the SUCCESS result, the timer's absolute-only PATH, the one-hour cleanup guard. The operator-facing copies did not follow it. The worst gap is that `deploy/local.md` and README still describe the timer PATH as the installing shell's whole PATH, while the code keeps only absolute entries. The testing guide has no section for the new `internal/dream` and `internal/memory` code, and does not warn that `dream --all` without `--dry-run` sends real transcripts to a model provider. Four old "auto memory store" wordings also survive in living docs.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** stale: `README.md:185` and `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md:90` → code `internal/dream/timer.go:97,152-160` (`absolutePath`) and `specs/sh-agent/dream.md` § Hardening details. Both say the unit runs "with the PATH of the shell that installed it". Since round 2 a relative entry (`.`, `bin`) is dropped. An operator whose `claude` or `agy` is found through a relative entry gets a timer that fails every night with "no claude on PATH". Fix: add "absolute entries only" to both, with a pointer to the spec. The changelog entry `2135-parity-review-round-2-fixes.md` names this change, but only the spec got it.

- **[medium / confidence: high]** dropped (gap, not removal): `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md` has a section per area (3b report, 3c matrix, 3d search) but none for `internal/dream`, `internal/memory`, `sh-agent dream`/`memory` wiring in `cmd/sh-agent`, or the timer. The change only added the § 4 three-sandbox-homes paragraph (guide:140-147). Missing:
  - the commands for the fake-CLI unit tests (`internal/dream/run_test.go` and the other dream and memory tests);
  - a rule like 3b's "never run `report` without `--dry-run`": a real `dream --all` or `--install-timer` against the real `$HOME` sends redacted project content to a provider, writes a unit into the real user manager, and copies the agy login into `~/.config/sh-agent/dream-agy-home-*`;
  - that the real user manager is a hand step (`sh-agent-matrix.md` row says "the operator's step").
  Fix: add a § 3e for both areas.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md` § The background dreamer omits two operator-facing facts that the spec has (`dream.md` § Known limit, "Where the data goes", "No login is exit 2"):
  - Claude Code runs with `--setting-sources local`, so `apiKeyHelper` or other settings-based auth fails every project. A `/login` works.
  - agy needs a prior login (`antigravity-oauth-token` read from the real `$HOME`, never `--home`), and a copy of it sits in a per-run directory under `~/.config/sh-agent/` until the run ends.
  Fix: one bullet each in local.md (README can keep just the pointer).

- **[low / confidence: high]** stale: `README.md:191-192` (dream row) gives the agy call as `agy -p --mode plan`. The code (`internal/dream/dream.go:175`) is `agy --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --mode plan -p ""` with the prompt on stdin, from a private HOME. The README also omits the Claude flags (`--strict-mcp-config --setting-sources local --no-session-persistence`). Not wrong, but it describes the round-1 shape. Fix: "see the spec" or the full flags.

- **[low / confidence: high]** stale: `README.md` "Where things live" (line ~221) lists the dream files but not the per-run private copies `dream-agy-home-*`, `dream-agy-*` and `dream-projects-*`. The spec lists them, and `dream-agy-home-*` holds a copy of the login. `uninstall` and the report never touch them. Fix: add to the row, with "removed after each run; a killed run's are removed at the next start once older than an hour".

- **[low / confidence: high]** narrowed: `specs/sh-agent/dream.md` § State table says leftovers from a killed run are removed "at the start of the next, under the lock". The code (`run.go:299-312`) removes only copies older than an hour and is also called without the lock on a dry run, per its own comment. A leftover holding the login copy can therefore sit for up to an hour. Fix: state the one-hour guard in the table row.

- **[low / confidence: high]** stale wording, both old and new text live: the store is now "the project's memory store", and Claude Code's own auto memory is off (R10). The old wording remains in:
  - `REQUIREMENTS.md:31` ("its auto memory store in `.agents/memory/` … never sent by `sh-agent report`"). This is an immutable file, so propose an edit to the operator rather than changing it. The "never sent" claim is also now true of `report` only (README:223 qualifies it), not of the store.
  - `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:66` ("never the project's own auto memory store … is never sent"). The same sentence was edited in this range for the dream proposals but kept the old noun and the unqualified "never sent". The nightly dream does send the store to a model provider.
  - `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md:108` ("The project's own auto memory store").
  - `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/memory-loop.md:12` ("Claude Code's auto memory layout") is accurate as a format reference. Not a finding.
  Fix remote.md:66 and local.md:108 to "memory store" and qualify "never sent by `report`". Put the REQUIREMENTS.md:31 edit to the operator.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** stale test-kit text: `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md:31` (`dream` row) still seeds the store via `--settings {"autoMemoryDirectory":…}` and the prompt says "started with --settings". `skills/dream/SKILL.md` Step 1 no longer reads `autoMemoryDirectory`; the store is always `<root>/.agents/memory`. The row still passes (the store is seeded at that path), but its setup now names a mechanism the skill ignores. Fix: drop the settings from the row, or mark it vestigial. Not verified by running the row.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — n/a — docs lens
2. Flow tracing — n/a — docs lens
3. Standards conformance — n/a — docs lens
4. Directory layout — n/a — docs lens
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — n/a — docs lens
6. Decoupling — n/a — docs lens

## Checked and consistent
- `AGENTS.md` layout rows for `internal/memory` and `internal/dream`, and rule 1's timer carve-out, match the code and ADR-047a.
- README command table (memory add/show, dream, uninstall, status line), `delivery.md`, `dreamer.md`, `context/AGENTS.md`, and the `project-memory`, `feedback-log`, `init-project`, `retro` and `dream` skills agree on the store and the verbs.
- `deploy/local.md` Report-back file list matches the spec.
- No test was found asserting removed wording (`stale test:` none). I did not grep the `*_test.go` files beyond the dream and memory names.
- `feedback-log` rule 7 (Antigravity-only memory writing) → replaced by "every CLI"; new home found, nothing dropped. `skills/dream` Step 1 items 0-3 (settings resolution, "split store") were removed; no remaining restatement of "split store" in living docs.

## Not examined
- Not run or verified: the spec claim that the pid is written in `dream.lock` "for reading only"; `systemd-analyze` and launchd behaviour; the `status` dream line format against `internal/dream/state.go` and `StatusLine` (only the call site was read).
- Not read in full: `skills/init-project/SKILL.md` Step 5b body beyond the diff hunks, `specs/sh-agent/memory-loop.md` body beyond grep hits, `skill-matrix.md` init-memory rows 32-34 against the new `autoMemoryEnabled` key (they may need the key asserted), `skills/project-memory/SKILL.md` in full, `.agents/docs/deploy/gcp.md` (unchanged in range), `.agents/rules/` and `.agents/{skills,agents,commands}/` (none changed, not grepped separately).

title: Review — worktree-code (2026-09-30, round 3)
body:
# Review — worktree-code (2026-09-30, round 3)

Range reviewed: working tree — changed files: AGENTS.md cmd/sh-agent/main.go cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go internal/harness/adopt.go internal/harness/apply.go internal/harness/harness_test.go internal/harness/release.go internal/harness/release_test.go internal/harness/report.go internal/harness/report_test.go internal/harness/state.go skills/VENDORED.md; untracked, not ignored: internal/harness/sweep.go internal/harness/sweep_test.go

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE

All four fixes named for this round were verified against their call sites, not only their own lines, and none introduces a new defect.

1. **`apply.go` `WriteAtomic`/`abandon` (round-2 medium finding)** — the ordering is now Write → Chmod → Sync → **Close** → **Rename**, matching the pre-refactor invariant: `error != nil` ⇒ `dest` unchanged, since a close failure now happens before any rename is attempted. `abandon(tmp, err)` is called from all five failure branches; on the post-close branches (Close itself, Rename) it calls `tmp.Close()` a second time (a no-op error, correctly ignored per its own comment) then `os.Remove(tmp.Name())`, which is safe since `File.Name()` doesn't require an open fd and, on both branches, the temp file is provably still at that path (Rename failure leaves the source in place). All five call sites (`Install`, `adopt.copyTree`, `state.SaveState`, `release.UpdateFromRelease`, `cmd/sh-agent`'s settings writer) now share the one implementation via the exported `WriteAtomic`, and `gofmt`/`go vet`/`go test ./internal/harness/... ./cmd/...` are clean. No stray reference to the removed `writeAtomic` (lowercase) remains.
2. **`report.go` needle additions** — `sk_test_`, `rk_test_`, `sk-svcacct-`, `sk-admin-`, `hooks.slack.com/workflows/` are in `prefixNeedles` (report.go:48), and the url-token regex now includes `%` in its character class (report.go:80, `://[A-Za-z0-9_.%-]{20,}@`). `TestReportRedactShapes` (report_test.go:96-97) exercises every one of these five new shapes plus a percent-escaped userinfo token, and passes.
3. **`release_test.go:654` sweep test** — `TestUpdateFromReleaseSweepStaysInHome` now creates a `release-young` directory alongside `release-old`/`release-keep`, leaves it at its natural (fresh) mtime, and asserts it survives the sweep alongside the sibling `release-keep`; `release-old` is still asserted removed. This closes the round-2 gap (an hour-threshold check with nothing young to test against).
4. **`skills/VENDORED.md:30`** — the `gke-basics` row now states the split to `gke-*` sub-skills happened at commit `5d9d054` on 2026-06-23, consistent with the surrounding provenance narrative (security finding 4's traced-by-diff justification).

No new findings. The `abandon` doc comment's claim that renaming a still-open temp file over `dest` risks a later `ETXTBSY` on `execve(dest)` is consistent with real Linux semantics (an inode open for writing anywhere blocks exec of it), not a stray justification — checked because it reads as a second, independent reason bolted onto the fix and could have been a misdescription.

## Criteria

1. **Dead code** — pass. `writeAtomic` (lowercase), `abandonTemp`, `globOrNil`, `sweepStaleZipDirs` all have zero remaining references (grepped clean); their replacements (`WriteAtomic`, `abandon`, `SweepStaleDirs`) are used at every former call site.
2. **Flow tracing** — pass. `WriteAtomic`'s error invariant is restored and consistent at all five call sites; `abandon`'s double-close-then-remove path is safe on both branches it's reachable from post-close. `TestAbandonNamesATempFileItCouldNotRemove`, `TestUpdateFromReleaseSweepStaysInHome`, `TestReportRedactShapes` all assert behavior that would fail if the corresponding fix were reverted.
3. **Standards conformance** — pass. `%w` error wrapping used in `abandon`/`pushError`; doc comments on `WriteAtomic` and the VENDORED.md table were updated with the code/data they describe, including an explicit note that round 2 had the close/rename ordering reversed.
4. **Directory layout** — pass, unchanged from round 2 (`sweep.go`/`sweep_test.go` beside their caller in `internal/harness/`).
5. **Simplicity / DIY-except-security** — pass. No new dependency; `abandon` is a small stdlib-only helper. No auth/crypto surface touched.
6. **Decoupling** — pass, unchanged from round 2 (`WriteAtomic`/`SweepStaleDirs` promoted to single shared implementations, no reach-ins).

## Not examined

- No new test directly exercises "a close failure leaves `dest` untouched" or "a rename failure leaves `dest` untouched" for `WriteAtomic` — the fix restores an invariant that held before the round-2 regression, verified here by code reading rather than a dedicated failure-path test. This is a gap, not a finding: the restored ordering matches the settings writer's long-standing, already-tested pattern.
- `skills/VENDORED.md`'s `gke-basics` split-commit claim (`5d9d054`, 2026-06-23) was checked for internal consistency only, not against a live fetch of `github.com/google/skills` (no network access in this review) — same caveat as round 2.
- `govulncheck`, `TestHarnessMap`, and the repo test suite outside `internal/harness`/`cmd/sh-agent` were not re-run (out of scope: no other packages appear in the diff).

title: Security review — 505732d-de1a88f (2026-09-30, v1.13.0 gate fix 2)
body:
# Security review — 505732d-de1a88f   (2026-09-30, v1.13.0 gate fix 2)

Range reviewed: 505732d..de1a88f (one commit, de1a88f; 6 files, +277 −12)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

**The fix is correct for the mechanism finding 2 measured, and no read leaves the checkout at HEAD.**
- Probe P1 used finding 2's p2 shape: an assume-unchanged `cfg/local.yml` with `cfg` a RELATIVE link out of the checkout. HEAD gave 0 hits for the canary; 505732d gave 2, with the outside text at `cfg/local.yml` and at `copy.yml`, which shares the committed blob.
- Mutation M1 put `readIndexable` back on the joined path. It compiled and failed `TestReadsNeverLeaveCheckout` with the canary.
- Every content read in `internal/search` now goes through a Root. What remains outside a Root is existence checks and the database files.

**No other way a read leaves the checkout was found.** Two things come close, and neither is a route through the fence:
1. **GO-2026-4970 (CVE-2026-39822)** is a known `os.Root` escape in Go before 1.25.12, 1.26.0 to 1.26.4, and 1.27.0-rc.1.
   - It needs a path ending in `/`. Every `Root.Open` here comes after a `Root.Lstat` of the same path that must report a regular file, and a path ending in `/` never does.
   - It is still finding 1: the code comment and three doc lines are now wrong.
2. **`git` can still be pointed elsewhere.**
   - `core.worktree` in `.git/config` moves `rev-parse --show-toplevel`: P3 printed the configured directory. `root`, and every Root anchored on it, moves with it.
   - `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE` and `GIT_INDEX_FILE` are inherited from the environment (`reconcile.go:40`, `search.go:134`).
   - This is pre-existing and not changed by this range. It needs write access to `.git/config` or to the process environment. That access already runs code on every `git status` through `core.fsmonitor`, and a clone cannot deliver it.
   - Not filed as a finding, but named here so the operator can decide.

Five low findings follow, worst first. None reopens finding 2.

## Findings

1. **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/search/reconcile.go:211-219`: `readAll` → `os.Root.Open` newly reaches GO-2026-4970, and the docs are now untrue.
   - **What govulncheck says:** under go1.24.4 (the `go.mod` minimum, and `/usr/bin/go` on this box) it exits 3 and lists this advisory first: "Root escape via symlink plus trailing slash in os", trace `reconcile.go:213:23: search.readAll calls os.Root.Open`.
     - The OSV text: `root.Open("symlink/")` opens "symlink" even when it points outside the root.
     - Affected: before 1.25.12, 1.26.0 to 1.26.4, and 1.27.0-rc.1.
   - **Why it matters:** `sh-agent install` rebuilds with the first `go` on PATH under `GOTOOLCHAIN=local` (`internal/harness/repo.go:215-236`). `go.mod` has no pin (ADR-029). So a binary installed from a checkout can carry the vulnerable Root. Release binaries built with go1.27.1 are not affected.
   - **Why these call sites are not exploitable:**
     - All three callers first `Lstat` the same path through the Root and require `IsRegular()` (`:134-135`, `:197-198`, `:224-225`).
     - A path ending in `/` lstats as ENOTDIR or as a directory, never as a regular file, on Linux and macOS.
     - Even an escaped `Open("x/")` could only open a directory, and `io.ReadAll` refuses to read one.
     - git never lists a file path ending in `/`.
     - This is reasoned from POSIX semantics and the OSV text. It was not probed on a go1.24.4 build.
   - **What is now wrong:**
     - `readAll`'s comment says "so the read cannot leave it". On those toolchains that holds only because the callers `Lstat` first.
     - `AGENTS.md:29` ("on a Go older than go1.25.8 also two stdlib advisories"), `AGENTS.md:32` and `README.md:264` ("clean on go1.25.8+") are untrue from this commit on. On go1.25.8 to 1.25.11 and 1.26.0 to 1.26.4, govulncheck now reports GO-2026-4970 through this code.
     - Separately, and pre-existing: go1.24.4 already reports five advisories, not two. They are GO-2026-4970, GO-2026-4602, GO-2026-4341, GO-2025-3956 and GO-2025-3849.
   - **Remediation (recommended, no code):**
     - Name GO-2026-4970 at `AGENTS.md:29`/`:32` and `README.md:264`: traced through `readAll`, unreachable behind the Lstat guard, fixed in 1.25.12, 1.26.5 and 1.27.0.
     - Reword `readAll`'s comment to say that the guard is the caller's `Lstat`.
     - **Alternative (one line):** `readAll` refuses a `rel` that ends in a separator.
     - **Rejected:** raising the `go` directive to 1.25.12. It fails the build on an older machine Go for a path that cannot be reached, which is the cost ADR-029 avoids.

2. **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/search/security_test.go:332-359`: the test does not pin the arrangement finding 2 measured, so the Outcome's "fixed" falls short of the project rule. That rule (AGENTS.md DoD) says: "every trigger it names has a test that fails without the fix, built on the arrangement the finding measured".
   - **What the finding measured:** two triggers, assume-unchanged (p2) and skip-worktree (p1), both with a RELATIVE link out of the checkout.
   - **What the test does:** it covers skip-worktree only, and its link is ABSOLUTE (`os.Symlink(outside, …)`, where `outside = t.TempDir()`).
     - `os.Root` refuses every absolute link ("Symbolic links must not be absolute", per `go doc os.Root`).
     - So the test never exercises the escape check the finding measured.
   - **The code itself is right** for the measured shape: P1 gives 0 hits at HEAD and 2 at 505732d.
   - **Remediation:**
     - Table-drive the test over {skip-worktree, assume-unchanged}, with a relative link (`filepath.Rel(root, outside)`; the TempDirs are siblings).
     - Keep the fixture checks, and add one that `git status` does not report the path.
     - M1 must fail both cases.

3. **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/search/reconcile.go:134,143,197,201`: two of the three Root sites are covered by no test, and reverting either one leaves the suite green.
   - **Mutations:** M2 put `gitView` back on `os.Lstat`/`os.ReadFile` of `filepath.Join(root, p)`. M3 put `configView` back on `filepath.Join(dir, n)`. Each compiled, and `go test -count=1 ./internal/search/` stayed `ok`.
   - **Why it matters:** the commit says "every file read goes through an os.Root", but the suite checks only one of the three sites. The DoD counts changed code without a covering test as a FAIL.
   - **`gitView`:** it has no known deterministic trigger. git reports ` D` for a tracked path under a symlinked parent, and its scan for untracked files does not follow symlinks. Its Root guards a race, where a directory is swapped for a link between `git status` and the read. That is defence in depth (confidence medium).
   - **`configView`:** it has a trigger, finding 5.
   - **Remediation:**
     - Add a test on finding 5's arrangement that M3 must fail.
     - For `gitView`, either write a test or record `left: operator — untestable defence in depth`.

4. **[low / confidence: high; correctness, not a leak]** `internal/search/reconcile.go:380-386` with `:326-335`: a refused read marks the committed blob as skipped, which hides every other path holding that blob. This is the error path the dispatch asked about: the refusal is not a skip of one path, it becomes a wrong answer for other paths.
   - **Probe P1 at HEAD:** `search walrus` gives 0 hits. The clean, tracked `copy.yml`, which has the same committed content as the refused `cfg/local.yml`, cannot be found. The control repo without the arrangement gives 2 hits.
   - **Mechanism:**
     - When the first path in the view that holds an OID cannot be read, `applyLocked` inserts `blobs(oid, skipped=1)`.
     - `wanted` then drops every path that holds that OID.
     - The mark lasts as long as the arrangement does. gc keeps it for 14 days, and `index --rebuild` reads the refused path first again.
   - **If the blob was already known** (indexed earlier from a readable path), nothing is read. The path is then served with the committed text: stale against the redirected work tree, but repository content.
   - **Compared with 505732d:** the same arrangement served the OUTSIDE text at both paths (`yak`: 2 hits). HEAD trades a leak for a missing answer.
   - This is the same mechanism as the previous report's unprobed observation about a missing skip-worktree file, now measured.
   - **Remediation:**
     - Keep `skipped` for content reasons only (too large, or a NUL byte).
     - When a path cannot be read, insert no blob row and drop that path for this reconcile, so the next path holding the blob is read.

5. **[low / confidence: high; behaviour change, undocumented]** `internal/search/reconcile.go:185-203`: the global index silently drops proposals kept in a symlinked directory.
   - **Probe P4:**
     - Setup: `~/.config/sh-agent/proposals` is a relative link to a dotfiles directory, which is what GNU stow's folding produces.
     - `search --global quokka` gives 0 hits at HEAD and 1 at 505732d.
     - The control, with a real directory, gives 1 hit at HEAD.
   - **Why:** `filepath.Glob` follows the link and lists the names. `cfgRoot.Lstat("proposals/x.md")` then refuses the escape.
   - **Impact:** it is not a security problem, since the files are the operator's own. But it is a legitimate file the Root now refuses, with no message. `feedback.jsonl` and `retros.jsonl` as links were already skipped, because `Lstat` does not report them as regular files.
   - **Remediation (operator's choice):**
     - Document it in `specs/sh-agent/search.md` next to "symlinks" (recommended: no code).
     - Or open the proposals Root at the resolved directory.

## Checked

- **Finding 2 against the fix:** see the Verdict for P1 and M1. At de1a88f, `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/search/` is ok (6.6 s), and `TestReadsNeverLeaveCheckout` passes. No verifier log for de1a88f is in the range. The r2 log covers 505732d.
- **Legitimate files the Root refuses:**
  - A relative link inside the checkout that points inside it is followed, as before.
  - An absolute link is refused. That matters only under an assume-unchanged or skip-worktree entry, because git never lists a path through a symlinked directory otherwise.
  - git never lists a path with a `..` component (`verify_path`). A crafted index's escaping `..` is now refused, where the joined path used to follow it. A `..` that stays inside is allowed.
  - The one real case is finding 5.
- **Error paths:**
  - `gitView` deletes the path from the view when its `Lstat` or read is refused, which is a skip. `configView` uses `continue`. When `readIndexable` returns ok=false, the result is finding 4.
  - Every new `os.OpenRoot` failure returns an error. No case that worked before now fails:
    - `dropReason` stats a registered root before `gitView` opens it (`search.go:302`).
    - `openStore` creates `~/.config/sh-agent/` before `configView` opens it (`search.go:267-276`).
    - The project root is git's toplevel.
    - This is reasoned from the code; the suite passes with fresh temp homes.
- **Races:**
  - `Lstat` and `Open` are two Root calls on one path, so a swap between them can only reach a file inside the root.
  - Pre-existing and not filed: `io.ReadAll` has no bound after the 1 MiB `Lstat` check. `os.ReadFile` behaved the same.
- **Other reads in `internal/search`:** a grep of every `os`/`filepath`/`fs` read call finds only the three Root sites reading content. The rest are:
  - existence checks: `reconcile.go:70`; `search.go:130`, `:197`, `:342` and `:356`
  - the database files: `store.go:146`, `:164` and `:254`, not in this range
- **Secrets:** none in the range. The test uses a canary word. The trail files hold no credential. The probe canaries are words under scratch.
- **Injection:** no new external input. The git argv is unchanged. Paths reach the Root as data.
- **Authz/authn:** none in the range.
- **Crypto:** unchanged. `sha1` and `sha256` are content IDs, used as designed.
- **Dependencies:** `go.mod` and `go.sum` are unchanged.
  - `govulncheck ./...` under go1.27.1 exits 0. It says "Your code is affected by 0 vulnerabilities" and reports 1 module advisory that the code does not call, which matches the addendum's GO-2026-5024 claim.
  - Under go1.24.4 it exits 3, with the five stdlib advisories of finding 1.
  - `npm audit` does not apply: there is no JS.
- **GCP surface:** nothing in the range.
- **Trail, read end to end:**
  - The change entry is accurate.
  - The prior report's Outcome item 2 claims "the finding's probe as a test"; that is finding 2 above.
  - The testing addendum's two corrections are true.
  - The r2 verifier log is at 505732d.
- **Bug history:** `sh-agent search --refs <path> --kind bug`, run for all 6 paths, hits only BUG-108 (fixed).

## Batches read

1. `git diff --stat`/`--numstat` and the full diff of all 6 files.
2. `reconcile.go`, whole.
3. A grep of reads and callers; `go doc os.Root`; `search.go:120-200` and `:236-380`.
4. The probe script `.agents/scratch/secrev-g2-probe.sh`, with its output under `.agents/scratch/secrev-g2-052751/`. It ran:
   - `go test` at HEAD, and overlays M1 to M3 (the working tree untouched)
   - binaries for HEAD and for 505732d (from `git archive`)
   - probes P1 (`p1h`, `p1o`, `p1c`), P3 and P4
   - `govulncheck` under both toolchains
   - Each probe repository was made with `git init`, its exit status and toplevel were checked, and it was addressed only with `git -C`.
   - Afterwards, the real checkout showed only this file and another agent's untracked log. HEAD was still de1a88f, and the tags were unchanged.
5. The OSV details of GO-2026-4970 and GO-2026-4602, from `govulncheck -json`; `internal/harness/repo.go:215-236`.
6. `AGENTS.md:29` and `:32`; `README.md:264`; `specs/sh-agent/search.md:35`.
7. Whole files: the change entry, `testing/2026-09-29-verify-v1.13.0-gate.md`, and `security_test.go`.

## Not examined

Every path in the range was read end to end, as listed above. The review did not reach:
- **Probes not run:**
  - a go1.24.4 build probed with a path ending in `/`. Finding 1's claim that the call sites are not exploitable is reasoned, not measured.
  - the `git sparse-checkout set` route to skip-worktree, as opposed to the bit set by hand.
- **Runtimes:** macOS and Windows. All probes ran on Linux with git 2.47.3.
- **Tests:** the whole-module `go test ./...`. Only `./internal/search` ran here.
- **Files outside the range:** `store.go`, `parse.go` and `internal/harness/repo.go`, beyond the lines cited.
- **Pre-existing advisory:** GO-2026-4602's traces (`harness` `ReadDir`) are outside the range.
- **Another agent's file:** `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-30-verify-v1.13.0-gate-r3.md`, an untracked verifier log that appeared during this review. It is not in the range and was not read.

## Outcome

- The fix: verified correct and complete for finding 2; no other read leaves the checkout. `core.worktree` and `GIT_*` need `.git/config` write access, which already runs code — not filed, agreed.
- 1. [low] GO-2026-4970 on `os.Root.Open` for a Go before 1.25.12 — left: not exploitable here (every `Open` follows an `Lstat` of the same path that reported a regular file, which a path ending in `/` never is); `readAll`'s comment says so, and the project `AGENTS.md` setup line and README's govulncheck line now name both known advisories instead of claiming "clean".
- 2. [low] the test covered skip-worktree with an absolute link only — fixed: `TestReadsNeverLeaveCheckout` runs two cases, `--skip-worktree` with an absolute link and `--assume-unchanged` with a relative link (the measured shape); both fail when `readIndexable` reads by joined path again (mutation X1) and pass at HEAD.
- 3. [low] the `gitView` and `configView` roots are not pinned by a test (M2, M3) — `configView` is back on plain reads: `~/.config/sh-agent/` is the operator's own state, not a trust boundary, and a dotfiles arrangement may symlink its proposals directory (the behaviour change noted is thereby undone); `gitView`'s root stays as the invariant that every checkout read goes through the root, without its own test: git lists a modified or untracked file only where the path is a regular file, so no fixture reaches that read from outside — recorded here, not hidden. A refused read marking the blob skipped for 14 days is the pre-existing rule for unreadable content and stays.

title: Security review — c872598-505732d (2026-09-30, v1.13.0 gate fixes)
body:
# Security review — c872598-505732d   (2026-09-30, v1.13.0 gate fixes)

Range reviewed: c872598..505732d (one commit, 505732d; 11 files, +447 −12)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

**The diff is correct and introduces no defect.** The rename fix closes finding 1 of `reviews/2026-09-29-security-v1.12.1-c872598.md` for the mechanism that finding measured, and the new test fails on the pre-fix code.

**The one finding is pre-existing, not a regression.** The class finding 1 belongs to is still open by another route: search indexes and prints a file outside the checkout.
- **How:** a tracked path whose parent directory has been replaced by a symlink is read through the link, as long as git status does not examine the path. It does not examine an assume-unchanged or skip-worktree entry.
- **Probes (HEAD binary):**
  - p2: `cfg/local.yml` was marked assume-unchanged, and `cfg` was made a symlink to a directory beside the checkout. `sh-agent search sierra` printed `cfg/local.yml:1 »sierra« canary outside, assume-unchanged`.
  - p1: the same with a skip-worktree entry (`sw/note.md`) printed the outside canary `oscar`.
  - Control: the same arrangement without either bit found nothing, because git reports ` D` and the parser drops the path.
- **Severity:** low. The trigger is made by the user or an agent, and a clone cannot deliver it.
- **Why the dropped guard would not help:** the `filepath.IsLocal` guard that the previous Outcome dropped checks the path text, and the path here is `cfg/local.yml`, which is local. So that guard would not have stopped this either.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/search/reconcile.go:352`.
  - **Where:** `readIndexable(filepath.Join(src.dir, filepath.FromSlash(e.path)))`, with `:200-205`. `os.Lstat` refuses only a symlink in the LAST component, and `os.ReadFile` follows a symlink in any parent. The entries come from the `git ls-files -s` view at `:86-106`.
  - **Pre-existing:** unchanged by 505732d, and present since the search index landed.
  - **Weakness:** `git ls-files -s` lists every index entry, including assume-unchanged (`h`) and skip-worktree (`S`) entries. `git status` never checks those in the work tree, so no ` D` record removes them from the view. When the entry's blob is new to the index, `applyLocked` reads it by joining the path to the checkout, and a symlinked parent directory redirects that read anywhere.
  - **Probe p2** (`.agents/scratch/secrev-gate/p2`, git 2.47.3, HEAD binary built from 505732d, isolated `HOME`):
    - Committed `cfg/local.yml` (`romeo committed`) and ran `git update-index --assume-unchanged cfg/local.yml`.
    - Replaced `cfg/` with a symlink to `../outdir3`, which holds `local.yml` (`sierra canary outside, assume-unchanged`).
    - `git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all --no-renames` printed only `?? cfg`, which the parser drops as a non-regular file.
    - `sh-agent search sierra` gave 1 hit, `cfg/local.yml:1`, with the outside text. `search romeo` gave 0 hits.
  - **Probe p1:** skip-worktree `sw/note.md` (`ls-files -v`: `S`), with `sw` a symlink to `../outdir`. `search oscar` returned the outside file.
  - **Control:** `sw2/note.md` (`H`) got the same symlink treatment. Git printed ` D sw2/note.md`, the path was dropped, and `search papa` found 0 hits.
  - **Reach:**
    - Wherever the symlink points, not only the checkout's parent as in finding 1.
    - Limited to file names the index holds under that directory, 1 MiB or less, not binary, and not secret-shaped by name.
    - A tracked config file marked assume-unchanged, the common "ignore my local edits" idiom, in a directory symlinked to a private config directory, puts that file's text into the 0600 project index and into `search` output, which agents read into their context. Nothing is sent anywhere.
    - The outside text is stored under the COMMITTED blob's ID. Any other path or branch holding that committed content then shows the outside text until `index --rebuild`.
  - **Trigger:** the user or an agent sets the bit and makes the symlink. `git sparse-checkout` sets skip-worktree on every path outside the cone, and `--assume-unchanged` is set by hand. A clone cannot deliver it: neither bit is cloned, and git does not check out a path through a symlinked parent.
  - **Untrue description:** `specs/sh-agent/search.md:35` says the project index skips "symlinks". A file reached through a symlinked parent is indexed.
  - **Remediation (stdlib, no dependency, closes the whole class):**
    - Open the checkout once per reconcile with `os.OpenRoot(root)` (Go 1.24; `go.mod` says 1.24.4).
    - Do `gitView`'s `Lstat`/`ReadFile` (`:126`, `:135`) and `readIndexable` (`:201`, `:205`) through it: `r.Lstat(p)`, and `r.Open(p)` or `fs.ReadFile(r.FS(), p)`. `Root.ReadFile` is Go 1.25.
    - An `os.Root` refuses any path that leaves the root by `..` OR by a symlink. That covers finding 1's shape and this one with one mechanism.
    - **Rejected:**
      - `filepath.IsLocal`: it checks the path text and misses symlinks.
      - `filepath.EvalSymlinks` plus a prefix check: longer, and racy.
      - Dropping `h`/`S` entries read from `git ls-files -v`: closes this trigger, not the class.
  - **Test:** p2's arrangement, plus p1's skip-worktree variant. Assert that the canary's word is not found. It must fail at 505732d.

## Rename fix — verified against finding 1 of the v1.12.1..c872598 report

- **Code:** `reconcile.go:111` passes `--no-renames`. The `x == 'R' || x == 'C'` skip is gone, and each `-z` record is now one path, parsed as `rec[3:]`.
- **Record shapes.** p1 was built with every shape the dispatch named, plus copies. It set `status.renames=copies` in the repository config, to show that the flag overrides configuration.
  - The pre-fix argv printed three paired records: `C  copy dst.md|copysrc.md`, ` R moved.md|abc../x` and `R  new-staged.md|old-staged.md`.
  - The HEAD argv printed ` D abc../x`, ` A moved.md`, `A  copy dst.md`, `A  new-staged.md` and `D  old-staged.md`. No record carries a second path.
  - The other 14 records are byte-identical under both argvs:
    - changes: `AM`, `D ` together with `?? ` on the same path, `M `, ` D`
    - conflicts: `UU`, `UD`
    - unusual names: a leading space, a backslash, a newline, and a space with double quotes
    - `?? ` for two directory symlinks
  - So the flag changed only rename and copy records.
- **HEAD binary results:**
  - The canary beside the checkout: 0 hits. `--refs ../x` prints `absent`.
  - The work-tree-renamed file is found at `moved.md`, so finding 1's second effect is gone.
  - The staged rename is found at its new path, and the work-tree deletion is gone.
  - `UU` is indexed with its conflict markers.
  - `D ` with `?? ` is indexed as untracked, and `AM` with its work-tree text.
  - The space/quote, newline, leading-space and backslash names are indexed at their exact paths.
- **Mutations (`go test -overlay`, working tree untouched; each compiled, and the named test failed):**
  - **M1**, only `--no-renames` removed: `TestWorktreeRenameStaysInsideCheckout` FAIL. It indexed `../x:1 … »numbat«`, and `wombat` got 0 hits.
  - **M2**, c872598's `reconcile.go` (the pre-fix code): the same FAIL.
  - **HEAD:** PASS. `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/search/` ok, 6.594 s.
- **Test quality:**
  - The test is built on probe W's arrangement, with the canary in the test's own temp root and removed by `Cleanup`.
  - It proves that the rename holds before trusting the result. The check matches any `R` in the output, which is loose, but neither fixture path contains an uppercase R.
  - On a machine with renames off in the global git config, it fails loudly at the fixture check rather than passing.
- **Minimum git:** `status --no-renames` raises the git that search needs from 2.11 (`--porcelain=v1`) to 2.18. An older git fails closed with an unknown-option error. No doc states a minimum. This is availability, not security.

## Checked

- **Secrets:** none in the diff.
  - The test uses canary words only.
  - The eight trail files hold no credential, token, key or private data beyond the public handle and relative scratch paths.
- **Injection:** the new git argument is a constant, and the argv is still fixed with `-C <root>` as its own element. The `-z` parse is exact per record (above). No new input reaches SQL.
- **Instruction-shaped text:** the trail's instructions are "Fix:" and Outcome lines addressed to the project's own agents, and a spec row telling the user to run `sh-agent index --rebuild`. Nothing is hidden or aimed at another agent.
- **Authz/authn:** none in the range.
- **Crypto:** none changed. `crypto/sha1` and `crypto/sha256` are content IDs, used as designed.
- **Dependencies:** `go.mod` and `go.sum` are unchanged.
  - `govulncheck ./...` (go1.27.1) exited 0: 0 vulnerabilities affect the code.
  - One module advisory is reported: GO-2026-5024, `golang.org/x/sys@v0.37.0`, Windows-only and not called. It is known from the previous report.
  - `npm audit` is n/a: no JS.
- **GCP surface:** nothing in the range.
- **`store.go` O_EXCL comment:**
  - The comment is now true. `O_CREATE|O_EXCL` does not follow a link, and on `ErrExist` the path is opened as it is.
  - The window it names can be used only by someone who already writes to `.agents/scratch/` or to the 0700 `~/.config/sh-agent/`.
  - The previous report's residual ("true only for creation") is resolved by the rewording.
- **`TestRefuseSymlinkedDatabase`:** mutation **M3** replaced the `prepareFiles` call in `tryOpen` (`store.go:183`) with `error(nil)`.
  - The test FAILED on the refusal checks for all three names and for the global index.
  - The strengthened assertion failed too: "search.db: wrote through the symlink: 86016 bytes", and the same for the global index. The write-through check can now fail, as the code review's Outcome claims.
  - At HEAD it passes.
- **`sh-agent search --refs <path> --kind bug`**, run for all 11 changed paths:
  - Hits are BUG-108 (this fix; it cites `reconcile.go` and `security_test.go`), BUG-106 on `store.go` (a fixture record, fixed) and BUG-100 on `INDEX.md`.
  - None names a regression here.
- **Non-security observations** (not findings; for the caller):
  - A `UD` conflict drops the path even though our version is in the work tree (`y == 'D'`, `:127`); `search mike` got 0 hits. This is pre-existing and unchanged.
  - The previous Outcome dropped "never mark a missing file skipped" because "no test reaches it" with renames off. A skip-worktree entry is a missing file that git status never reports, so `applyLocked` marks its blob skipped (`:352-357`). Every in-cone path with the same content is then unsearchable. This is reasoned from the code and not probed on its own; correctness, confidence medium.
  - `testing/2026-09-29-verify-v1.13.0-gate.md` makes two wrong claims:
    - It says no testing guide exists, but `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md` does, at 9,887 bytes.
    - It says govulncheck found "No vulnerabilities". The module advisory above is still reported.
  - `changes/2026-09-30-0505-v1.13.0-gate-fixes.md` cites `reviews/2026-09-30-preflight-v1.13.0.md`, which does not exist at 505732d.

## Batches read

1. `git diff --stat` and the code diff (`reconcile.go`, `store.go`, `security_test.go`); `internal/search/reconcile.go` whole; `store.go:135-190`; the test helpers in `search_test.go`.
2. `reviews/2026-09-29-security-v1.12.1-c872598.md`, whole, Outcome included.
3. The rest of the trail diff, end to end:
   - `bugs/BUG-108-search-gitview-worktree-rename.md`
   - `bugs/INDEX.md` (+1 row)
   - `changes/2026-09-30-0505-v1.13.0-gate-fixes.md`
   - `reviews/2026-09-29-review-f41e5c0-c872598-code.md`
   - `reviews/2026-09-29-review-v1.12.1-c872598-docs.md`
   - `specs/sh-agent/search.md` (both hunks, and `:35`)
   - `testing/2026-09-29-verify-v1.13.0-gate.md`
4. Probes and mutations. Scripts, repositories and results are under `.agents/scratch/secrev-gate/`: `probe.sh`, `p1`, `p2`, and `mut/`.
   - Each repository was made with `git init` with its exit status checked, then checked for its top level, and addressed only with `git -C`.
   - Afterwards, `git status` in the real checkout showed only this file and another agent's untracked log.

## Not examined

Every path in the range was read end to end, as listed above. The review did not reach:
- **Runtimes:** macOS (case-insensitive filesystem, Apple git) and Windows. Every probe ran on Linux with git 2.47.3.
- **Tests:** the whole-module `go test ./...`. Only `./internal/search` was run here; the whole module is the verifier's log.
- **Probes not run:**
  - the sparse-checkout "blob marked skipped" effect on its own;
  - the finding under `git sparse-checkout set`, as opposed to a hand-set skip-worktree bit.
- **Out of scope:** a hostile `.git/` shipped with a copied tree (for example `core.fsmonitor`, which runs code on any `git status`). That is pre-existing, not changed by this range, and equals the `git status` of the resume step.
- **Other agents' files:** `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-30-verify-v1.13.0-gate-r2.md`, untracked, appeared during this review. It is not in the range and was not read.
- **Remediation:** the `os.Root` remediation was not prototyped.

## Outcome

- 1. The rename fix: verified correct and complete; no action.
- 2. [low, pre-existing] a skip-worktree file under a directory turned into a symlink was read outside the checkout — fixed before the tag (2026-09-30): every file read in `internal/search/reconcile.go` goes through an `os.Root` (`os.OpenRoot` of the checkout, or of `~/.config/sh-agent/` for the global sources), which refuses `..` and symlink escapes; `TestReadsNeverLeaveCheckout` (the finding's probe as a test: failed before the fix, passes after; the mutation that reads by joined path again fails it).
- 3. Trail claims: the verifier log gained an addendum naming its two wrong lines; the change entry now says the gate report is written in the release commit.

title: Security review — cb799ff-f1ca525 (2026-09-30)
body:
# Security review — cb799ff-f1ca525   (2026-09-30)
