title: Security review — worktree-p8 (2026-10-01)
body:
# Security review — worktree-p8   (2026-10-01)

Range reviewed: round 2 (this update) — working tree against HEAD 7c2e30a: the same files as round 1 plus the test files that changed, `cmd/sh-agent/{main_test,search_test,memory_test,zip_test}.go` and `internal/harness/{settings_test,phase8_test}.go`, by `git diff HEAD -- <files>` and each new file whole; focus on the round-1 fixes (`AttributionSet`/`underLink`, `reorder` keeping `--`, the stray-argument refusal in `run`, `ReadCapped`, the zip-directory note in `delivery.md`) and the lows left by decision; what was not re-read is under `### Not examined (round 2)`. Round 1: working tree against HEAD 7c2e30a — Phase 8 of the audit-fix plan (installer refactor, verbs unchanged): `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` (verb table, per-verb FlagSets, argument reordering, origin parsing calls, `report` source resolution, dry-run unpack location), `internal/harness/repo.go` (`ResolveSourceLenient`, origin helpers), `internal/harness/settings.go` (new: reads and writes `~/.claude/settings.json` for the attribution setting), `internal/harness/release.go` (signers scratch directory beside the zip, `ReadCapped`), `internal/harness/zip.go` (`UnpackZip` parent, `copyCapped`), `internal/harness/apply.go` (one origin-parse site), `internal/harness/frontmatter.go` and `inventory.go` (`ParseStrict`), `internal/harness/pathguard.go` (`pathCandidates`), `internal/harness/report.go` (comments only), and the untracked `phase8_test.go`, `repo_origin_test.go`, `settings.go`, `settings_test.go`.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

**Round 2 (at the end of this file):** the medium is fixed (measured and mutation-checked). Five lows remain or are new. The worst is that `update`'s `--from-zip` gate still disagrees with the parser when `--` is the value of a value flag. The round-1 text below is unchanged.

Worst first: the new settings writer (`AttributionSet`) checks only the last path component for a symlink, so when `~/.claude` itself is a linked directory (a dotfiles layout) it creates or rewrites `settings.json` in the link's target, outside the home. The installer refuses exactly that for every other file under `~/.claude` (`underLink`, BUG-129's prevention rule), so one install now leaves the vendor files untouched and edits the operator's dotfiles checkout. The rest are low: (a) a new gate/parser disagreement where `update -- --from-zip FILE` runs a normal update; (b) a lone `-` silently disables every flag after it (this was already the case at HEAD), which turns `uninstall - --dry-run` into a real uninstall; (c) the signers scratch now sits beside the zip and is open to a race in a shared folder without the sticky bit; (d) `ReadCapped` cuts the read short instead of refusing; (e) `ParseOrigin` treats any unknown value as a path; (f) a case-insensitive key match in the attribution hint. report.go is confirmed comment-only. `report` reads and sends nothing new. govulncheck reports nothing new.

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/settings.go:29-127` (`AttributionSet`) — `os.Lstat(path)` at :34 checks only the final component. When `~/.claude` is a symlink to another directory, every write goes through it: absent file → `MkdirAll` (:45) and the `O_EXCL` create (:52) land in the target directory; present file → `WriteAtomic` (:122; `CreateTemp` + `Rename` in `filepath.Dir(dest)`) rewrites the target's `settings.json`. The comment at :32 cites "a dotfiles checkout" as the reason for the Lstat, but dotfiles setups usually link the whole directory. `Install` refuses every file under such a `~/.claude` through `underLink(home, rel)` (`apply.go:407`). The BUG-129 prevention rule reads "Lstats the path AND its components … The test links a directory, not only a file". `settings_test.go:229-249` links only the file. In principle an install writes into a repository outside the home that the operator may commit and push from (the inserted bytes are a constant fragment, nothing secret). Remediation: before any branch that writes or reports a would-write, `if underLink(home, filepath.Join(ClaudeRoot, "settings.json"))`, print one line ("is under a symlinked directory; add the key by hand") and return. Add a test that links the `.claude` directory and asserts the target is unchanged, mutation-checked (remove the guard → the test fails).
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:233` with `hasFlag` (:261) and `reorder` (:928, `--` case :940) — a new disagreement between the gate and the parser. `hasFlag` stops at `--`. `reorder` drops the `--` and places what follows after the flags, so `flag.Parse` parses it (measured on a scratch build: `sh-agent version -- --bogus` exits 2, "flag provided but not defined: -bogus"). So `sh-agent update -- --from-zip FILE` sets `c.fromZip` while `hasFlag` reports no `--from-zip`: the zip branch and all its refusals are skipped and a normal `update` runs with the zip silently ignored. On a release binary that downloads the newest release and replaces the binary (signature-verified), the outcome the comment at :234-237 says the refusals exist to stop. On a checkout it fetches, pulls and reinstalls. HEAD decided with `fs.Visit` on the parsed set (`zipSet`), so gate and parser agreed. Only the operator's own argv reaches it. Remediation, minimal: for `update`, decide from the parsed set (`c.fs.Visit`, as HEAD did). Principled: `reorder` keeps `--` in its output and verbs without positional arguments refuse them (next finding), so the `--` form becomes a usage error. Test: `update -- --from-zip <missing>.zip` never reaches `ResolveSource`.
- **[low / confidence: high; already present at HEAD]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:943` (`reorder`) and every verb that never reads `c.fs.Args()` — a lone `-` counts as a flag, and `flag.Parse` stops at it (a one-character argument is a non-flag), so every flag after it is left unparsed and ignored. Only `adopt`, `memory` and `search` look at positional arguments. Measured on a scratch build: `sh-agent version - --bogus` exits 0, and `sh-agent list - --check` exits 0 while `sh-agent list --check` exits 2 (the verb table's IN5 usage error is bypassed). Consequences, from reading the code: `uninstall - --dry-run` removes every installed file; `update - --check` pulls or downloads and reinstalls; `install - --home .agents/scratch/x` installs into the real `$HOME`, which this repo's AGENTS.md forbids during development. HEAD had the same `reorder` loop and one FlagSet. Remediation: in `reorder`, a token is a flag only when it is at least two characters and starts with `-`. Give each `verb` entry its arity and refuse `c.fs.NArg() > 0` with exit 2 in `run` for verbs that take no positional argument. Add a test per read-only mode (`uninstall - --dry-run`, `update - --check`) asserting nothing changes.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/release.go:452-461` (`VerifyZipSums`) — the signers scratch moved from the system temp directory to `os.MkdirTemp(dir, ".sh-agent-verify-*")` beside the zip. Mode 0700 protects the directory's contents but not its name. If the zip's folder is writable by another account and has no sticky bit (e.g. a group-shared 2775 download folder), that account can rename the new directory away and put its own at the same path. The window is between `MkdirTemp` and the `allowed_signers` write (:262) or ssh-keygen's `-f` read (:265); renaming within one parent needs only write permission on the parent. The other account's own allowed_signers line can bind the compiled-in identity to its key, so a SHA256SUMS signed by that key verifies, and the install is printed and recorded as "VERIFIED against the signed SHA256SUMS of release …". The zip place already accepts unsigned zips as UNVERIFIED (ADR-041), so what an attacker gains is a false VERIFIED label, behind a race and an unusual folder mode. HEAD's sticky `/tmp` did not allow the swap. Side effects of the same change: a signed zip in a read-only folder (offline media, the zip place's own use case) is now refused outright (fail-closed, but an availability loss); an interrupted run leaves `.sh-agent-verify-*`, and for a dry run the unpacked `zip-*` tree, in the operator's download folder, where no sweep reaches. The comment at :452-454 ("scratch is the project's or the home's") does not describe the zip's folder, which is neither. Remediation: create the signers scratch, and the dry-run unpack, under the home's `~/.config/sh-agent`. `updateFromZip` already creates and tracks that directory as the unpack parent; pass it to `VerifyZipSums` (the `check` closure has it in scope), and for the dry run create it tracked and remove it afterwards. A considered stdlib alternative, `-f /dev/fd/3` through `exec.Cmd.ExtraFiles`, needs no file at all, but its behaviour with ssh-keygen on both platforms is unverified here.
- **[low / confidence: high; already present at HEAD, now the "one capped read" with a new caller]** `internal/harness/release.go:359-369` (`ReadCapped`) — the cap is a Stat-time check followed by `io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(f, max))`. When a file is longer than its Stat said, that returns the first `max` bytes with a nil error: a FIFO or character device (Stat size 0), a file still growing, or a failed `f.Stat()` (the check is skipped on error). The read is cut short instead of refused. The checksum paths still fail closed: ssh-keygen verifies the same in-memory bytes Go then parses (`verify.Stdin`, :270), and the zip's sum is computed over the bytes it unpacks, so no shorter checksum input can pass. The gap is in the function's stated contract, which `ReadSettings` (new) and future callers rely on; a FIFO named SHA256SUMS also blocks the open. `TestReadCappedRefusesOversize` covers regular files only. Remediation: read `max+1` and refuse `len(data) > max` (the `copyCapped` shape in zip.go), refuse a non-regular file using the opened handle's Stat, and treat a Stat error as an error.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/repo.go:143-152` (`ParseOrigin`) — every value that is neither `embedded:` nor `zip:sha256:` becomes `OriginPath`. That includes `""` (pinned so by `repo_origin_test.go:23`), a relative path, a `zip:` value of another shape, and a value with a newline or terminal escape. HEAD's `ResolveSource` and `runDiff` treated every `zip:` value as a zip; now such a value is a `ResolveSource` candidate checked with `IsRepo` relative to the working directory (BUG-067's shape). `status` (main.go:669, :673) and `knownCheckout` (:880) print `Release`/`Trust` raw. Only a hand-edited or foreign `state.json` carries such values, since sh-agent writes absolute paths (`absSource`) and `zip:sha256:` only (`ZipOrigin`), and the cwd walk is tried first, so exposure is small. Remediation: `OriginPath` only for an absolute path with no control character. Anything else becomes a fourth kind that no reader follows and that `status` reports as unreadable. Print `Release`/`Trust` with `%q` or strip control characters.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/settings.go:179-205` (`attributionOff`) — decodes into a struct, and encoding/json matches struct keys case-insensitively (exact match preferred, last key wins). Given `"attribution": {"commit": "x"}` followed by `"Attribution": {"commit": ""}`, the check returns "off" and prints no hint, while Claude Code (case-sensitive JSON) still adds the trailer. This is an advisory check on an operator-owned file. Remediation: decode through `map[string]json.RawMessage` at both levels (exact keys), as `AttributionSet` already does at the top level.

## Checked
- **Secrets:** none in the diff or the new files. `settings_test.go`'s "SECRET" is a sentinel. `ReadSettings`/`AttributionHint` print only fixed phrases and the path, never file bytes or the JSON error string; the tests pin that the set of problem strings is closed and that no "invalid character" text is echoed.
- **Injection / input parsing:** each verb gets its own FlagSet, and undefined flags are refused (`list --check` exits 2, measured). An empty `--from-zip=` and a flag-shaped value (`--from-zip --dry-run`) are refused. `reorder` now reads which flags take a value from the FlagSet, so a value flag can no longer swallow the next argument (BUG-002's shape). `--home` is made absolute before use (BUG-080). `--repo` goes through `IsRepo` and `absSource`, unchanged. Vendor writes still pass `Lstat` + `underLink` in apply.go (unchanged). Exceptions: the first three findings.
- **report / `ResolveSourceLenient`:** behaves identically to HEAD's inline resolution (release binary → embedded files plus a note when `--repo` is given; development build → `ResolveSource`, or the zero Source with the error as the note). `SendReport`/`BuildRecord` receive the same Source as before. report.go's `git diff HEAD` filtered to non-comment `+`/`-` lines is empty (comment-only change confirmed), so redaction and the `SecretShaped` list apply to the same inputs. Nothing new is read or sent.
- **settings.go write path:** the final-component Lstat refuses a symlinked file. Creation uses `O_EXCL` with mode 0644; nothing secret is written, and this matches Claude Code's own default. Edits go through `WriteAtomic` (CreateTemp 0600 in the same directory → Chmod to the file's own `Perm()` → Sync → Close → Rename), so the mode is preserved and never widened, and a link planted after the Lstat is replaced, not written through. The textual insertion is re-validated with `json.Valid` before the write. The dry run returns before any write (tested). Exception: directory components (first finding).
- **zip.go:** `copyCapped` returns an error past the cap, not a short read; at most max+1 bytes are written before the refusal, and the unpack directory is removed on error, as before. `UnpackZip` hashes and unpacks the same in-memory bytes. The empty-parent dry run unpacks beside the zip (fourth finding).
- **frontmatter.go / inventory.go:** `ParseStrict` lints and parses the same entries, so `LoadSkills`/`LoadAgents`/`LoadDocs` refuse exactly what `Lint` refused before (`TestParseStrict` compares the two errors).
- **pathguard.go:** `pathCandidates` is a pure refactor of the PATH walk; both callers keep their Stat/SameFile identity checks.
- **apply.go:** `OriginString` records the same manifest values as before (round trip pinned by `TestSourceOriginString`). `Inspect` runs only for a tree with no Origin.
- **Crypto:** nothing hand-rolled. The sha256 checksum and `ssh-keygen -Y verify` are unchanged; only the signers-file location moved (fourth finding).
- **Authz/authn:** not applicable (local CLI); no privilege boundary is added or crossed.
- **Dependencies:** go.mod is not in the diff. settings.go imports only stdlib.
- **govulncheck:** `govulncheck ./...` exit 0, "Your code is affected by 0 vulnerabilities". `-show verbose` names one module advisory that is not called: GO-2026-5024, golang.org/x/sys v0.37.0, fixed in v0.44.0 — the known one (AGENTS.md, ADR-045a). Nothing new.
- **npm audit:** not run; the repository has no `package.json`, `web/` or `ui/`.
- **GCP surface:** none in the diff.

## Not examined
- The diffs of `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` and `cmd/sh-agent/search_test.go` (test-only changes), `README.md` and `.agents/docs/testing/sh-agent-matrix.md` (docs).
- Bodies not in the changed hunks: `harness.Install` beyond its origin site, `Plan`, `Uninstall`, `UpdateFromRelease`, `downloadRelease`, `UnpackZip`'s entry loop, `SendReport`/`BuildRecord` beyond their use of the Source, `LoadState` beyond its first 25 lines (`os.ReadFile` with no size cap, unchanged), `MkdirAllTracked`/`RemoveCreated`/`SweepStaleDirs`, and `internal/dream`, `internal/search`, `internal/memory` (reached only through unchanged calls).
- Dynamic verification: only the parsing probe ran (`version`/`list` on a build in `.agents/scratch/sec-p8/`, which supports the third finding and the `--` half of the second). `update -- --from-zip` itself was not executed, because it would `git fetch` the real checkout or download a release. The first, fourth, fifth, sixth and seventh findings are by reading; no race or FIFO was staged.
- `go test`/`go vet` were not run by this review (the verifier's lane).

## Outcome
- [medium] `AttributionSet` writes through a linked `~/.claude` — fixed at `internal/harness/settings.go` (`underLink(home, rel)` before anything else, the same rule every installed path follows; the refusal names the link); test `TestAttributionSetRefusesALinkedClaudeDir`, red before the fix (the file was written into the link target), green after

## Round 2

Probed build: `.agents/scratch/sec-p8r2-bin`, built at 10:26:57 from the tree whose `main.go` sha256 starts `ada60dcb1c01271a`.

### Verdict (round 2): FINDINGS, all low. The medium is fixed.

Worst first: the gate/parser disagreement from round-1 low 2 survives in one shape. `hasFlag` (`cmd/sh-agent/main.go:268-282`) stops at the first literal `--`. The flag package, however, takes a `--` that follows a value flag as that flag's VALUE and keeps parsing. So `sh-agent update --home -- --from-zip FILE` sets `c.fromZip = FILE` while `hasFlag` reports no `--from-zip`. The zip branch and every refusal in it (`main.go:240-254`) are skipped, and a normal `update` runs. This was measured on the scratch build with `HOME` and `PATH` pointed at scratch directories. The probe exits 1 at `git fetch`, stopped only by the empty `PATH`. The control, `update --from-zip FILE`, fails at "reading the archive" instead. `update --vendor -- --from-zip FILE` behaves the same way, and `update --home=-- --from-zip FILE` correctly takes the zip branch. Every other round-1 fix holds under measurement or mutation. Two test gaps, one unsafe test arrangement and one read-only residual are listed below. Nothing new reaches the network, a secret or a privilege boundary.

### Findings (round 2)
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:240` (`if cmd == "update" && hasFlag(rest, "from-zip")`) with `hasFlag` (:268). The gate re-scans argv, and argv disagrees with the parse when `--` is the value of `--home` or `--vendor`. `--repo --` was not probed. What follows is from reading `runUpdate` and `update`:
  - With `--home --`, the normal update runs against the home `<cwd>/--`. On a checkout place that means fetch, the dirty check, pull, rebuild and reinstall there. On a release binary, `UpdateFromRelease` runs with that home; its body was not read.
  - With `--vendor --` on a clean checkout place, the following all run before `installPassArgs` refuses the vendor (`update`, `main.go:788-830`): `git fetch`, the kept-clone shed, and the `git pull` of the real checkout.

  The operator named a zip and got the update that the comment at :241-245 says must not happen. Only the operator's own argv can reach this, and a `--` value is nonsensical, hence low. Remediation, shorter than the current code: decide the update's zip branch from the parse (`c.fs.Visit` for `from-zip`, as HEAD's `zipSet` did). Keep `hasFlag` only for the pre-parse refusal on the other verbs, where a disagreement already fails closed: their FlagSet has no `from-zip`, so `install --home -- --from-zip x` exits 2. Test: `update --home -- --from-zip <missing>.zip` and `update --vendor -- --from-zip <missing>.zip` must end in the zip's own error. Run the test with `PATH` emptied (BUG-094's rule) and mutation-check it.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` `TestVerbRefusesStrayArguments`. `--repo` and `--home` are appended AFTER the stray arguments, and reorder now keeps everything after `--` positional. Suppose the regression this test exists to catch happens: the refusal at `main.go:217` is removed or bypassed. Then the third case runs `update` with neither flag parsed. The home is the operator's real `$HOME`, and the source is the checkout found from the test's working directory. On a dirty tree the dirty check stops it. On a clean tree, such as a verifier run on a commit, it would fetch, pull and reinstall into the real home. That is BUG-094's class: a red test acting on real state. The test sets neither `HOME` nor `PATH`. Remediation: put `--repo`/`--home` before the stray arguments, call `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())`, and set `PATH` to an empty directory, as BUG-094's test does.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/phase8_test.go:124-145` (`TestReadCappedRefusesOversize`). Round-1 low 5 is fixed in code but not covered. Both cases are regular files, where the `Stat` shortcut refuses before the new max+1 read is reached. Measured: in a scratch copy with `io.LimitReader(f, max+1)` reverted to `max`, the package compiles and this test passes. Remediation: add a stream leg. Either `ReadCapped("/dev/zero", 32)` must fail with "more than the 32 bytes" (Linux and macOS both have it; skip on Windows), or a FIFO is fed 33 bytes by a goroutine. Mutation-check the leg against the revert above.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/settings_test.go:265-279` (`TestAttributionSetRefusesALinkedClaudeDir`). The linked target is empty, so only the create branch is exercised. Round 1's medium named two triggers. The second, a target that already holds `settings.json` and is edited through `WriteAtomic`, has no test. The guard sits above both branches today, so the code is right. But if the guard were moved below the `ErrNotExist` case, the edit branch would be unguarded with every test green. Mutation here: with the guard removed, this test fails (it compiled and the named test failed), so it is real for the trigger it covers. Remediation: add a second leg that writes `{}\n` into the target first, then asserts the target is unchanged and holds no new entry afterwards.
- **[low / confidence: high; by reading; residual of round-1 low 3]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` `reorder` (`case strings.HasPrefix(a, "-")`) with `runSearch`. A lone `-` still counts as a flag and stops `flag.Parse`. The stray refusal covers the 13 verbs without positional arguments, and `memory` (`len(args) != 1`) and `adopt` (`NArg() != 1`) refuse by arity. But `search foo - --global` searches the local index for the words `- --global foo`, with `--global` unparsed. Search is read-only, so this is informational. Remediation, as in round 1: a token is a flag only when it is at least two characters long.

### Round-1 findings re-checked
| # | Round 1 | Now | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [medium] `AttributionSet` writes through a linked `~/.claude` | fixed | `settings.go:36-39` calls `underLink` before any Lstat or write. With the guard removed, `TestAttributionSetRefusesALinkedClaudeDir` fails; the real tree passes. A scratch-home install still creates `settings.json` normally. The test covers the create branch only (fourth round-2 finding). |
| 2 | [low] `update -- --from-zip FILE` runs a normal update | fixed for the bare marker; open when `--` is a value flag's value | P1, `update -- --from-zip F --home H`: exit 2, "update takes no arguments", H never created. Control C1 reaches the zip branch. P6 and P6v: first round-2 finding. |
| 3 | [low] a lone `-` disables later flags | fixed for every verb without positional arguments; open for `search` | P2 `list - --check`: exit 2 (control `list --check`: 2). P3 `version - --bogus`: 2. P4 `uninstall - --dry-run --home H` with `HOME=H`, an installed scratch home: exit 2, and the 435 entries keep the same tree hash before and after, so a real uninstall would have shown. P5 `install - --home X` with `HOME` set to a decoy: exit 2, decoy and X stay empty. Real home unchanged: the `~/.claude/skills` listing and the mtimes of `~/.claude`, `~/.claude/skills`, `~/.claude/settings.json` and `~/.local/bin/sh-agent` are identical before and after. |
| 4 | [low] signers scratch beside the zip | open by decision (documented) | `delivery.md` now states that the zip's directory is the operator's own writable folder, never shared or read-only. The code is unchanged (`release.go:461-468`). Three effects remain as described: the swap race in a shared non-sticky folder, the refusal in a read-only folder, and the leftover `.sh-agent-verify-*`/`zip-*` after an interrupted run. The note does not mention the leftovers. `TestVerifyZipSumsWritesNothingUnderTempDir` pins the location and the clean-up on success and on refusal. |
| 5 | [low] `ReadCapped` cuts a stream short | fixed in code; untested (third round-2 finding) | `release.go:368-377` reads max+1 bytes and refuses past the cap, returning no partial data. A FIFO still blocks at `os.Open`, which costs availability only and needs an operator-placed file. |
| 6 | [low] `ParseOrigin` treats an unknown value as a path | open by decision | `repo.go:143-152` unchanged. |
| 7 | [low] the attribution hint matches keys case-insensitively | open by decision | `settings.go:195-205` unchanged. |

No fix introduced a defect beyond the first two round-2 findings:
- The stray refusal runs before the home and the source are resolved (`main.go:217-222`).
- It quotes argv with `%q`, so a control character in an argument is escaped, not echoed.
- The re-emitted `--` marker gives `search foo -- bar` the words `foo bar`, pinned by `TestDoubleDashKeepsFollowingArgumentsPositional`.

### Checked (round 2)
- **Secrets:** none in the changed tests or the fixes. The new refusal echoes only argv, `%q`-quoted.
- **Injection / input parsing:** probes P1-P7 ran on the scratch build from cwd `.agents/scratch/sec-p8r2/cwd`, each with `HOME` and `PATH` pointed at scratch directories. Each comes with a control showing that the branch it was meant to miss is reachable. Results are in the table and the first round-2 finding.
- **Authz/authn:** not applicable (local CLI); unchanged.
- **Crypto:** unchanged; nothing hand-rolled.
- **Dependencies:** `go.mod` and `go.sum` are not in the diff. `govulncheck ./...` exits 0, with no vulnerability in called code and one in a required module that is not called. That is the same count as round 1: GO-2026-5024, golang.org/x/sys, with the module set unchanged; it was not re-listed with `-show verbose` this round. `npm audit`: not applicable (no `package.json`, `web/` or `ui/`).
- **GCP surface:** none.
- **Tests, targeted, on the real tree:** in `internal/harness`, `TestAttributionSet*`, `TestReadCapped*` and `TestVerifyZipSumsWritesNothingUnderTempDir` are ok. In `cmd/sh-agent`, `TestReorder`, `TestReorderSearchFlags`, `TestVerbRefusesAnotherVerbsFlag`, `TestDoubleDashKeepsFollowingArgumentsPositional` and `TestVerbRefusesStrayArguments` PASS.
- **Mutations,** in a scratch copy (`.agents/scratch/sec-p8r2/mut/`, never the real tree):
  - A, the settings guard removed: the named test FAILS.
  - B, `max+1` changed to `max`: `TestReadCappedRefusesOversize` still PASSES.
- **The tree moved during this review.** `main.go` was rewritten at 10:25:06 and `main_test.go` at 10:25:52. This review's first read of `reorder`, before 10:25, saw the earlier marker handling; `reorder` was re-read at 10:28. The probes ran on a build made at 10:26:57. The sha256 prefixes of what this round covers:
  - `main.go`: ada60dcb1c01271a
  - `settings.go`: b191ffaccafdedb1
  - `release.go`: 526825542d4fae56
  - `zip.go`: 52616b108817ca77
  - `repo.go`: 9f19889c90877181

  The verifier log `testing/2026-10-01-verify-audit-fix-phase-8-r2.md` (10:24:09) predates the `main.go` and `main_test.go` writes, so it does not cover this `main.go`.

### Not examined (round 2)

Not re-read: lines 1-94, 535-787 (`installFiles`, `report`, `memoryCmd` beyond its arity check, `resolveVendor`, `status`), 871-924, 966-1054, and the file's tail. Whether the 10:25:06 rewrite touched them was not checked; no snapshot of round 1's tree exists.

title: Review — b549d71-a0a54b4-docs (2026-10-05)
body:
# Review — b549d71-a0a54b4-docs   (2026-10-05)

Range reviewed: b549d71..a0a54b4

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

Docs lens only. Worst first: the release procedure in `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` § Releases is the document `/preflight` runs, and it does not carry the v2.4.0 bridge that ADR-052 decides. Its step 3 signs `SHA256SUMS` with the NEW key from the agent, and step 3's own verify and step 3b use the new line or the host binary. By ADR-052's own reasoning every v2.3.2 place refuses a checksum file signed that way, so an operator following the guide as written ships a v2.4.0 that no v2.3.2 place can update to. The bridge exists only in ADR-052 and a one-sentence note. Also stale: the "new machine" operator step still reads `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`. REQUIREMENTS.md's Antigravity clause and the delivery spec are consistent with their ADR/measurements.

## Findings

- **[high / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:151-165` (step 3 and 3b; ADR-052 in `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md:572-575`) — dropped/narrowed: ADR-052 says v2.4.0's `SHA256SUMS.sig` is signed by the RETIRED key and that step 3b runs a v2.3.2 binary built from the tag, because the v2.4.0 binary "would refuse the bridge signature by design". remote.md step 3 says "signed with the same key as the tag" and signs through the new agent key (`release-signer.pub` = new line), verifies against the new `allowed_signers`, and 3b runs this host's own built (v2.4.0) binary. remote.md:102 tells the reader only WHAT to verify v2.4.0 against, never how to produce it. Run as written for v2.4.0, step 3 yields a signature v2.3.2 places reject, so `sh-agent update` fails everywhere it matters; following ADR-052 instead means leaving the written procedure. Fix: add the bridge variant to step 3 and 3b in remote.md (which key signs, how the retired key is fed to `ssh-keygen -Y sign`, which binary runs 3b, which `allowed_signers` line step 3's verify uses), marked for v2.4.0 only. `TestReleaseSignerMatchesTheDeployGuide` does not catch this (it reads only lines that START with `ostling.simon@gmail.com ssh-`).

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:220` — a statement that no longer matches: "On a new machine, `ssh-keygen -y -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 | ssh-keygen -lf -` must print the fingerprint in § Releases". The key is never at that path now (remote.md:102 says so, and calls that path a login key). The line was not updated with the rest of the signing commands; the replacement check is the `ssh-add -L` line at remote.md:106. Fix: point the new-machine step at the `ssh-add -L` check (or `ssh-add -l` fingerprint compare to `SHA256:BwBzPnfX…`).

- **[low / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:205` — still says the stricter forms include "the private-key-derived fingerprint" and "the operator's key passes". The first check no longer derives from a private key (remote.md:106 reads the agent's public half). It is a dated rehearsal, so only the parenthetical is stale. Fix: say "the agent-held key check" or mark the sentence as the 2026-09-16 rehearsal of the earlier form.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `README.md:99-100` — "The signer line is the one compiled into every sh-agent": untrue after rotation; every sh-agent up to v2.3.2 has the retired line, only v2.4.0 and later have the new one. README:103-104 (new) adds the bridge note, so the two sentences sit side by side and disagree. Fix: "compiled into every sh-agent from v2.4.0".

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `README.md:141-146` (zip/Mac download block, `V=vX.Y.Z`) and `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:23-33` (release-binary install block) — both verify against the NEW line only; the bridge note exists only at README:103-104. A reader of either block with `V=v2.4.0` fails verification with no pointer to the retired key. remote.md:26 says "§ Releases' allowed_signers line", which for v2.4.0 is the wrong key. Fix: a one-line pointer to remote.md § Releases' bridge sentence in each block.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/release_test.go:445-468` and ADR-052 ("`TestReleaseSignerMatchesTheDeployGuide` pins code and guide together") — coverage claim wider than the pin: it matches only lines beginning `ostling.simon@gmail.com ssh-` (one line at remote.md:99). The 9 other copies of the key (README:109, 143; remote.md:32, 106, 109 (signingkey), 122, 156, 159; `printf`-prefixed or key-only lines) are not pinned. I checked by hand: all 10 copies of the new key at a0a54b4 are identical and the old key survives only as the bridge note at remote.md:102. Not covered: future drift in those copies. Not a stale test.

## Checked and consistent

- Release signer line and fingerprint: `release.go` var, remote.md:99 and :102, README:109 and :143, ADR-052 all agree (`SHA256:BwBzPnfX…`); old line absent from living files.
- `AGENTS.md:73` "SSH agent holds the release key (never a default key path; ADR-052)" matches remote.md:102; no other living file says the key is "the operator's ed25519 key" on the Linux box. DECISIONS.md:207-211 (ADR-030, "The Mac cannot cut a release until it holds this key") is a dated record, excluded by brief; the live claim in remote.md is correctly replaced ("any machine whose agent holds it").
- REQUIREMENTS.md:55 (Antigravity second-file clause) matches ADR-051 and the 2026-10-05 rows (16,993 bytes). Restatements: `size_test.go:14-15` ("A second file costs the first one room") and `testing/guide.md:191` (BUG-085) are still true under the new clause. README:242, README:292, AGENTS.md:25 restate only the 24,000/22,000 pins, unchanged.
- `delivery.md:77` ("newest tag v2.4.0") matches the changes/ECR convention of pre-writing the release commit; `git tag -l 'v2.4*'` is empty at this moment, so it is true only once the tag lands (handoff says pending) — noted, not a finding.

## Unverified

- That `ssh-keygen -Y sign -f <public key file>` signs through the agent on the operator's machines with a password-manager agent or hardware key: the changes entry reports a throwaway key on OpenSSH 10.0p2 only. I did not run it.
- That the retired key's private half is still available on this box (`.agents/scratch`) for the v2.4.0 bridge signing, per ADR-052's "Consequences": not looked at (scratch).
- The v2.3.2 binary's refusal of a new-key-signed SHA256SUMS: taken from ADR-052 and `release.go` comments, not re-run.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — n/a — docs lens
2. Flow tracing — n/a — docs lens
3. Standards conformance — n/a — docs lens
4. Directory layout — n/a — docs lens

Restatement-grep.sh output on the broad key-word set (35 KB, saved by the harness) was read only through its first 2 KB; I replaced it with narrower `git grep` at a0a54b4 over README.md, AGENTS.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, context/, agents/, rules/, non-vendored `skills/*/SKILL.md`, `.agents/docs/specs/`, `testing/guide.md`, `deploy/` and the harness tests. Not read in full: `skills/preflight/SKILL.md` Step 6 beyond the lines the grep returned, `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/dream.md` and `memory-loop.md`, plan files. title: Review — signer-rotation-code (2026-10-05)
body:
# Review — signer-rotation-code   (2026-10-05)

Range reviewed: b549d71..a0a54b4

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

The worst problem: the release procedure that `/preflight` runs line by line has no bridge path, even though ADR-052 says v2.4.0 is a bridge release. Run as written for v2.4.0, step 3 signs `SHA256SUMS` with the NEW key. Step 3 then verifies it against the new key, and step 3b checks it with the v2.4.0 binary, which trusts the new key. Every check passes, and the result is a release that no v2.3.2 binary-only place can update to, now or later. The second problem: zip places are stranded after the rotation, and nothing says so. Third, the Operator steps in `remote.md` still tell a new machine to check `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`. The new commands themselves are correct. I ran each one with throwaway keys and it works, and each check fails when it should. The new signer line and its fingerprint are the same everywhere they appear.

## Findings

- **[high / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:106-123,155-163` (§ Releases procedure, steps 0–3b), against `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` ADR-052 bullet 3 and `remote.md:102`. The prose says v2.4.0's `SHA256SUMS.sig` is signed by the retired key. The procedure has no step that does that:
  - The pre-check (`ssh-add -L … grep -qxF '<new key>'`) only checks for the new key.
  - Step 3 writes the new key's public half to `release-signer.pub` and signs with it.
  - Step 3's verify uses the new allowed-signers line.
  - Step 3b runs `./sh-agent-$(go env GOOS)-$(go env GOARCH)`, which is built from the v2.4.0 tag and so carries the new key.

  For v2.4.0, every line exits 0 and certifies a release whose signature every v2.3.2 binary refuses (`release.go` verifies `SHA256SUMS.sig` only against its compiled-in signer). Binary-only places are stranded and need a manual reinstall. `/preflight` follows this block literally ("each command its own call"), so the prose note does not protect the run. ADR-052's "a v2.3.2 binary built from the tag" is also ambiguous: a binary built from the v2.4.0 tag is not a v2.3.2 binary.

  Fix: add an explicit v2.4.0-only bridge block:
  1. Pre-check that the retired key is in the agent.
  2. Sign with the retired key's public half.
  3. Verify against `ostling.simon@gmail.com ssh-ed25519 …BkX…`.
  4. For 3b, use a binary built from `git archive v2.3.2` into `.agents/scratch/` and require the `VERIFIED … release v2.4.0` line.
  5. Add a must-fail check that the v2.4.0 binary refuses the bridge signature.

  Also say where the retired private key is loaded from for this one signing.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` ADR-052 Consequences and `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md:77` (the v2.4.0 sentence). Zip places are left stranded and nothing records it. Per delivery.md § The model (line 32), `update --from-zip` "installs the unpacked tree with the RUNNING binary" and never replaces it, and a release zip whose signed pair does not verify is refused. A zip place on a v2.3.2 binary therefore accepts the v2.4.0 zip (retired key) but keeps a binary that trusts only the retired key. It then refuses every later release zip, which is signed by the new key alone.

  ADR-052 only says "every place should run `sh-agent update` soon", which does not move a zip place's binary. The delivery spec's v2.4.0 sentence (the one home for what a tag delivers, AGENTS.md rule 6) does not mention the rotation at all.

  Fix:
  - Append a note (ADRs are append-only) and add a delivery.md sentence: a zip place must download the v2.4.0 binary by hand.
  - Add the same to the v2.4.0 release notes.
  - Have the operator decide the version number against the rule in `remote.md:207`: "MAJOR for what an existing deployment must react to".
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:220` (§ Operator steps). It still says "On a new machine, `ssh-keygen -y -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 | ssh-keygen -lf -` must print the fingerprint in § Releases before that machine cuts a release". That contradicts `remote.md:102` ("It is never `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`") and the new `ssh-add -L` pre-check. On a correctly set-up machine the check fails, because `id_ed25519` is a login key. Satisfying it means putting the release key at the default path, which is what caused ADR-052 in the first place. This is a restatement the rotation missed.

  Fix: replace it with the `ssh-add -L | cut -d' ' -f1,2 | grep -qxF '<signer>'` check. Related: `remote.md:205` still lists "the private-key-derived fingerprint" among the "stricter forms above", and that check is no longer in the block. Drop the clause or mark it historical.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` ADR-051 Consequences ("the v2.4.0 tag still goes on `caa37d6`") and `.agents/docs/handoffs/2026-10-05-1248-v2.4.0-tag-still-pending.md`. Both are false after a0a54b4. `caa37d6` compiles in the exposed key, and the source change in `release.go` after the gated head `b549d71` means the procedure's `HEAD^ == <gated head>` and records-only `git diff --quiet` checks now need a new gate. The procedure guards against tagging the wrong commit, but ADR-052 does not say that it supersedes that part of ADR-051.

  Fix: one sentence in an appended note saying the v2.4.0 gate is re-run over a range that ends at or after a0a54b4.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:32` (the release-binary download chain) and `README.md:143` (the Mac/browser chain). Both carry only the new signer line and no v2.4.0 note. The bridge comment exists only above README's first chain (`README.md:103-104`). With `V=v2.4.0` both chains fail closed at `ssh-keygen -Y verify`, so this is safe but confusing.

  Fix: point both at the bridge note, or print the retired line beside them.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/release_test.go:449` `TestReleaseSignerMatchesTheDeployGuide` pins only `remote.md` lines that start with `ostling.simon@gmail.com ssh-`. These copies of the key are not pinned:
  - the three new signing lines (`ssh-add -L` check `remote.md:106`, `key::` in `:117`, `release-signer.pub` in `:156`)
  - README's two lines (`README.md:109,143`)

  They are all consistent today. I checked every occurrence: 7 in remote.md, 2 in README, 1 in release.go, 1 in DECISIONS.md, all byte-identical. At the next rotation they can drift unseen. The test's own comment says "two copies of a key are two keys the day one of them is rotated".

  Fix: match the base64 key body anywhere in remote.md and README, not only at line start.

## Verified (how, and on which path)

- **Fingerprints.** `printf '<key>' | ssh-keygen -lf -` gives `SHA256:BwBzPnfXKuKrWP6p10IZgcDG8uwSRXJOFv0Izl+79yQ` for the new key, which matches remote.md:102 and ADR-052. The retired key gives `SHA256:5HpYQJjpG+yE1xXBTOIZPsTkbkgkVnV8z0eG8hBawyU`, which matches the old guide.
- **Signing commands, rehearsed** with two throwaway ed25519 keys and an `ssh-agent` whose socket was under `.agents/scratch/rv-signer` (since deleted), on OpenSSH 10.0p2 and git 2.47.3 on this Linux box:
  - `ssh-add -L | cut -d' ' -f1,2 | grep -qxF '<pub>'`: exit 0 with the key loaded; exit 1 with an empty agent, with only a different key loaded, and with no agent (`SSH_AUTH_SOCK` unset).
  - `git -c gpg.format=ssh -c user.signingkey='key::<pub>' tag -s`: exit 0 with the key in the agent; exit 128 ("Couldn't find key in agent?") with the key absent, and no tag created. `verify-tag` against an allowed-signers line built the procedure's way says `Good "git" signature for ostling.simon@gmail.com`.
  - `ssh-keygen -Y sign -f <pubfile> -n sh-agent-release SHA256SUMS`: exit 0 and writes `.sig` with the key in the agent; exit 255 ("No private key found") and no `.sig` with the key absent.
- **Go change.** `gofmt -l internal/harness/release.go` is empty, `go vet ./internal/harness/` passes, and `go test -count=1 -run 'TestReleaseSignerMatchesTheDeployGuide|TestChecksumFor' ./internal/harness/` is ok. I did not re-run the must-fail mutation that the change entry claims. The test's logic (exact line equality) fails on the old line by inspection.
- **Old-key search.** `git grep` at a0a54b4 for the old key, the old fingerprint and `id_ed25519` found, outside the history records:
  - the bridge note (`remote.md:102`, intended)
  - ADR-026/052 text (append-only history)
  - `remote.md:220` (finding above)
  - unrelated secret-name lists (`plan.go:222`, `harness_test.go`, `.gitignore`, `skills/docker`)

  There are no stale copies in `context/`, `skills/preflight`, or `agents/`.

## Criteria

1. **Dead code: pass.** The diff only swaps a constant's value and adds a comment. Nothing is orphaned.
2. **Flow tracing: fail.** The new signer flows correctly from `releaseSigner` to `verifyRelease` to the guide pin. The release flow does not: the bridge step ADR-052 requires is in no executable step, and the 3b self-check would pass a mis-signed bridge (finding 1). The zip place's binary is never replaced, so it loses the update path (finding 2).
3. **Standards conformance: fail.** The rotation missed restatements at `remote.md:220` and `:205` (finding 3), and the ADR-051 consequence is stale (finding 4). The `release.go` comment is accurate. Go style is clean.
4. **Directory layout: pass.** No new files. The edits sit in the files that own each claim.
5. **Simplicity (DIY-except-security): pass.** Signing and verification stay in `ssh-keygen` and `git` as designed, and nothing is hand-rolled. Signing through the agent by public key removes the private-key path, which is the simpler and safer shape.
6. **Decoupling: pass.** The trust root is still one compiled-in variable, and the test swap seam is unchanged.

## Not examined

- The records in the range, read only through grep:
  - `handoffs/2026-10-05-1242-*`, `handoffs/2026-10-05-1248-*`
  - `reviews/2026-10-05-preflight-v2.4.0.md`, `reviews/2026-10-05-review-v2.3.2-0c0846c-{code,docs}.md`
  - `testing/2026-10-05-verify-v2.3.3-gate{,-rows}.md`
  - `changes/2026-10-05-1238-*`, `changes/2026-10-05-1248-*`
- The untracked `changes/2026-10-05-1317-release-signer-rotation.md`, read for context only (outside the range).
- `reviews/2026-10-05-security-v2.4.0-signer-rotation.md`, not read.
- macOS: OpenSSH and git behaviour for the `key::` signing and the agent-held `-Y sign` was not rehearsed there.
- The real release key and the retired key: neither was used. The rehearsal used throwaway keys only.
- The full test suite: not run. Only the signer pin and checksum tests were run.
- Whether ADR-051's REQUIREMENTS edit also needed a ROADMAP.md change in the same commit: not assessed.

title: Review — signer-rotation-code-r2 (2026-10-05)
body:
# Review — signer-rotation-code-r2   (2026-10-05)

Range reviewed: a0a54b4..41af344

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

The worst problem: bridge step 3b cannot run as written. `git archive v2.3.2` runs from `.agents/scratch/release-v2.4.0`, and from a subdirectory `git archive` archives only that subdirectory of the tree. v2.3.2's tree has no `.agents/scratch/release-v2.4.0`, so the archive is empty: 0 entries, exit 0. `tar` then succeeds with nothing to unpack, and `go build` fails with `stat …/v232src/cmd/sh-agent: directory not found` (rehearsed, below). The failure is closed, so nothing mis-signed ships. But by step 3b the v2.4.0 tag and `main` are already pushed, so `/preflight` stalls with a published tag that has no assets, and the operator has to improvise the fix in the middle of a release.

Second: `remote.md:103` (the signer paragraph, edited in this range) still tells a reader to "verify v2.4.0 against that key", meaning the retired, exposed key. ADR-052a, the install block at `remote.md:28` and README all say a human verifies `SHA256SUMS.current.sig` against the current key.

The rest of the bridge is correct. Bridge step 3, rehearsed with throwaway keys, signs, verifies, cross-refuses and removes the retired key from the agent exactly as written. The new test fails on a third `ssh-ed25519` key. Every finding in round 1 is fixed except the parts listed under Round 1 status below.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:197` (bridge 3b, `mkdir -p ../v232src && git archive v2.3.2 | tar -x -C ../v232src`). The command runs from `.agents/scratch/release-v2.4.0`, the cwd that step 2's `cd` set. `git archive` with no path archives only the cwd's subtree, so the result here is empty.
  - **Rehearsed:** from a subdirectory under `.agents/scratch/`, `git archive v2.3.2 | tar -t | wc -l` printed `0` and git exited 0. The build line as written then printed `stat …/v232src/cmd/sh-agent: directory not found` and exited 1.
  - **Fix:** `git -C "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" archive v2.3.2 | tar -x -C ../v232src`. Rehearsed: the build exits 0, and `../sh-agent-v2.3.2 version` prints `sh-agent v2.3.2`.
  - **Why it matters:** the tag and the pushes come before the binary block, so a 3b that cannot run leaves a pushed tag with no assets ("a marker no place can update to", `delivery.md` § The model).
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:103`, last sentence. It reads: "its `SHA256SUMS.sig` is signed by the retired key, `ssh-ed25519 …BkX…`, so verify v2.4.0 against that key and every later release against the line here." That contradicts four other places:
  - ADR-052a: "`SHA256SUMS.current.sig` by the current key, the one every human check and README's v2.4.0 path verify, because the exposed key alone proves nothing now".
  - `remote.md:28`, the install block's v2.4.0 comment.
  - `README.md:103-104`.
  - `README.md:139-140`.

  A reader of § Releases who follows this sentence checks v2.4.0 against a key the security review calls proof of nothing. This range edited the paragraph (it added the `ssh-add -t 900` text) and left this clause standing.
  - **Fix:** "v2.4.0 also carries `SHA256SUMS.current.sig` by the current key; verify that file against the line here (ADR-052a). Its `SHA256SUMS.sig` by the retired key is for v2.3.2-and-older binaries only."
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/release_test.go:478-503` `TestEveryDocumentedReleaseKeyIsKnown`. These gaps were all measured in a scratch copy of 41af344:
  - **Retired key accepted anywhere.** The test accepts the retired key at any position in either file. I swapped the retired key into the NORMAL step 3's `release-signer.pub` line (`remote.md:157`). Both this test and `TestReleaseSignerMatchesTheDeployGuide` still passed. That is round 1's high failure in reverse: a later release signed with the exposed key, with the tests green.
  - **Non-ed25519 keys missed.** The regexp sees only `ssh-ed25519 ` keys. An appended `sk-ssh-ed25519@openssh.com AAAA…` key, which is the hardware-key form `remote.md:103` recommends for the release key, passed. At a rotation to a hardware key, `strings.Cut(releaseSigner, " ssh-ed25519 ")` also turns the test into a Fatalf, so it does fail loudly there.
  - **Two files only.** It scans only `remote.md` and `README.md`. Today no other living file carries a key: a `git grep` found only `DECISIONS.md`, which is history, and `release.go`.

  ADR-052a's "refuses any key in `remote.md` or README that is neither" is therefore wider than the test, which refuses only ed25519 keys.
  - **Fix:** allow the retired key only between the bridge heading and the closing fence of its block, plus the `remote.md:103` sentence. Widen the regexp to `(?:sk-)?ssh-[a-z0-9-]+(?:@openssh\.com)? (AAAA[0-9A-Za-z+/=]+)`.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:194` (`ssh-add -d retired-signer.pub && rm -f retired-signer.pub   # … delete its private file too`). Nothing in the block or its prose says where the retired private key is loaded from. Round 1 asked for this. The only deletion is a comment with no command. The load is fail-closed: line 189's `ssh-add -L … grep` exits 1 when the key is absent. The deletion is the step that `/preflight`, running commands, skips silently. ADR-052 Consequences names "this box's scratch copy" as a location.
  - **Fix:** name the file, and make the deletion a command (`rm -f <that path>`) followed by a `test ! -e` check.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:201` (`! "./sh-agent-…" update --from-zip … > ../zipcheck-new.out 2>&1`). The negation passes on ANY non-zero exit (a flag error, an unwritable home, a missing file), not only on the signature refusal it claims to prove. Line 203-204 limits the damage, because the same binary must then print VERIFIED with the current signature. A refusal for an unrelated reason would still be read as "refuses the retired key".
  - **Fix:** keep the `!` line, then add `grep -q '<the refusal text release.go prints on a signature mismatch>' ../zipcheck-new.out`.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:177` (`# all six`) and `:216` ("lists the six assets"). For v2.4.0 the bridge prose adds a seventh asset. The upload change itself is stated in the bridge prose (`:181`, "step 4's upload list gains `SHA256SUMS.current.sig`"), but the loop at `:174` and these two counts are not marked. A literal run of step 4 uploads six assets and the listing check reads as satisfied, which leaves README's v2.4.0 path (`--pattern 'SHA256SUMS.current.sig'`) failing for every reader.
  - **Fix:** give the bridge block its own step-4 loop line, or add "(seven for v2.4.0)" to both counts.

## Round 1 status

From `reviews/2026-10-05-review-signer-rotation-code.md`:

1. **[high] No bridge in the procedure: fixed, with defects.** `remote.md:181-205` adds the bridge block. It carries:
   - a retired-key pre-check (`:189`)
   - the retired key's signature (`:190-191`)
   - a verify against the retired line (`:192-193`)
   - a v2.3.2 binary for 3b
   - a must-refuse check on the v2.4.0 binary

   I rehearsed step 3 with throwaway keys. It also adds a current-key signature, which goes past the original ask.

   Defects:
   - The 3b build cannot run as written (finding 1).
   - "Where the retired key is loaded from" is still open (finding 4).
2. **[medium] Zip places stranded: fixed.** The fix is in `delivery.md:32` (the zip edge and the binary-only edge, stated once, in rule 6's one home) and in ADR-052a's Context and Consequences. ADR-052a Consequences records the operator's version decision. The release-notes part could not be checked in this range: notes are built at release time.
3. **[medium] `remote.md:220` `id_ed25519` check: fixed.** It is now `remote.md:249`, "`ssh-add -l` must list the fingerprint …". The `:205` sub-point is also fixed: `remote.md:234` now marks the rehearsal as made "with the key then read from a file (the agent form above replaced it, ADR-052)".
4. **[low] ADR-051 consequence and handoff stale: open.** Nothing in the range says the v2.4.0 gate is re-run over a range ending at or after a0a54b4. The untracked `testing/2026-10-05-1317-verify-v2.4.0-gate.md` suggests a re-gate is under way, but I did not read it.
5. **[low] `remote.md:32` and README `:143` had no bridge pointer: fixed.** The pointers are at `remote.md:28` and `README.md:139-140`. But see finding 2: `remote.md:103` now disagrees with them.
6. **[low] Signer pin matched only lines starting with the email: fixed in part.** `TestEveryDocumentedReleaseKeyIsKnown` now matches every `ssh-ed25519` key in both files. Its gaps are in finding 3.

From `reviews/2026-10-05-review-b549d71-a0a54b4-docs.md`:

1. **[high] Bridge missing in steps 3/3b: fixed, with defects.** Same as code item 1. Step 3's verify line, the signing key and the 3b binary are each now named.
2. **[medium] `remote.md:220`: fixed.** Same as code item 3.
3. **[low] `remote.md:205` "private-key-derived fingerprint": fixed.** Marked historical (`remote.md:234`).
4. **[low] README "compiled into every sh-agent": fixed.** It now reads "from v2.4.0" (`README.md:100`).
5. **[low] README Mac block and `remote.md` install block: fixed.** The pointers are at `README.md:139-140` and `remote.md:28`. `remote.md:26`'s "§ Releases' allowed_signers line" is now right for the v2.4.0 path too, since that path verifies the current key.
6. **[low] Test coverage claim: fixed in part.** See finding 3.

## Agreement check: README, remote.md install block, delivery.md, ADR-052a

- **Agree.** These all say a human verifies v2.4.0 by `SHA256SUMS.current.sig` against the current key:
  - `README.md:103-104` (the gh chain)
  - `README.md:139-140` (the browser chain)
  - `remote.md:28` (the install block)
  - ADR-052a Decision
  - `delivery.md:32` ("verified by hand against the current key's `SHA256SUMS.current.sig` (README § Install without cloning)")
- **Disagrees.** `remote.md:103` says to verify v2.4.0 against the retired key (finding 2). ADR-052's own Consequences says the same ("uses the retired key's line"). As an append-only record, ADR-052a amends it generally ("amends ADR-052") without naming that sentence, which is acceptable.
- **Agree.** The binary-only edge reads the same in `delivery.md:32` and ADR-052a Context, and `README.md:167` agrees that `update` takes only the newest release.
- **Agree.** The bridge block's description of what 3b proves matches ADR-052a Decision line for line. The one exception is "removed from disk" (finding 4).

## Verified (how, and on which path)

- **Bridge step 3, every line as written.** Rehearsed with two throwaway ed25519 keys substituted for the real ones, in an `ssh-agent` whose socket was under `.agents/scratch/`, on this Linux box. Results:
  - Current-key sign plus `mv`: 0.
  - Verify of `.current.sig`: 0.
  - Retired key in agent: 0.
  - Retired sign: 0.
  - Retired verify: 0.
  - `ssh-add -d retired-signer.pub`: 0, "Identity removed". Afterwards the retired-key check exits 1 and the current-key check exits 0.
  - Must-fail cross-check: `.current.sig` against the retired allowed_signers exits 255.

  Scratch removed after the run.
- **Bridge step 3b build.** The as-written and corrected forms were run in `.agents/scratch/` (results in finding 1). Against the v2.3.2 tag:
  - The tag exists locally.
  - v2.3.2 has `--from-zip`, `--dry-run` and `--home` (`cmd/sh-agent/main.go:120,172,204`).
  - It prints the exact `VERIFIED against the signed SHA256SUMS of release ` string (`main.go:1161`).
  - Its `releaseSigner` is the retired key (`release.go:46`).

  So lines 199-200 grep the right text once the build works. I did not run 3b end to end, since a signed v2.4.0 zip needs a real key.
- **`TestEveryDocumentedReleaseKeyIsKnown`.** Run in a `git archive 41af344` copy under `.agents/scratch/`. Must-pass: `ok` with `TestReleaseSignerMatchesTheDeployGuide`. Must-fail: a third `ssh-ed25519 AAAA…` key appended to README fails at `release_test.go:497` with the expected message. The mutated code compiled and the named test failed. The two passing mutations are in finding 3. Each mutation was restored from a saved copy. `gofmt -l` is empty and `go vet ./internal/harness/` passes on the copy.

## Criteria

# Review — v2.3.2-0c0846c-code   (2026-10-05)

Range reviewed: v2.3.2..0c0846c (`git diff v2.3.2...0c0846c`, 8 commits, 32 files; no Go source changed)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing in the range breaks a test, the lint or a size pin. At HEAD 0c0846c the hand-written context is 14,700 bytes against the 15,000 pin, the Antigravity block is 16,907 of 22,000 (context 15,653 plus rules 1,254), and the skill listing is 19,340 of 19,500. The rule file's frontmatter passes every lint test. The worst problem is in the new rule file itself. Its last bullet, "Disagree before complying", is unconditional and contradicts the first bullet's clause that a direct instruction is carried out with its risks reported after the work. That is the same wording behind the Antigravity refusals that round 2 measured: with the old text, Antigravity refused 2 of 3 valid direct-instruction runs. The clause added in 07564fb brought this to 0 of 3, but the contradiction is still in the text and n=3 is thin. Two smaller problems. First, the new approval sentence in the context ("Nothing proposed runs until they approve it") conflicts with the feature skill's "Everything else runs without asking". Second, an edited line in the feature skill still says "numbered list" where ADR-050 chose the table. One verification gap: no one has checked that the nightly `sh-agent dream` Claude child still returns bare JSON now that a reply-shape rule and an always-on rule may load into it.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `rules/critical-thinking.md:14` against `rules/critical-thinking.md:8`. Bullet 1 says "a direct instruction is carried out: its risks go in the reply's table, after the work". Bullet 7 says, with no condition, "Disagree before complying." The two conflict for exactly the case ADR-050 calls P2. `.agents/docs/testing/2026-10-05-verify-critical-thinking-r2.md` records the failure mode: under the old text, Antigravity answered "Disagree with patching `os.ReadFile` alone; resolve … before …" and did not carry out the instruction. That happened in 2 of 3 valid runs across both rounds, and in 1 of 2 runs in round 2 even with the skip-permissions flag. The new clause gives 3 of 3 on Antigravity. But the unconditional bullet that a model can still pick is still in the file, three valid runs is a small sample, and a release place has not received the rule yet. Fix: scope bullet 7 so the file has one rule, not two. For example: "Disagree before complying with a proposal, plan or claim; a direct instruction follows bullet 1." Or remove it, since bullet 1 already says when to disagree. Then re-run Antigravity P2.
- **[medium / confidence: low]** `context/AGENTS.md:5` together with `internal/dream/dream.go:177` and `internal/dream/run.go:133-143`. The nightly Claude child runs `claude -p --tools "" --setting-sources local` with the real `HOME` (only the agy child gets a private `HOME`, `run.go:249-271`). If user memory and `~/.claude/rules/` load under that flag, every reply that "reports, proposes or asks" is now told to open with an explanation line, a recommendation line and a numbered table. That shape would fail `parse()`: the prompt demands "ONE JSON object and nothing else" (`internal/dream/prompt.go:23`). Each project would then log `fail invalid output`. The escape clause "unattended runs and subagents follow their dispatch" probably prevents this. But no log in the range runs `sh-agent dream` after the rule landed, and this machine has no `dream.log`. Low confidence: I did not establish whether `--setting-sources local` suppresses user memory and rules. Fix: one `sh-agent dream` run (or `--dry-run` plus one real project) against a home with the rule installed, before the next tag. Record the result next to the testing guide's § 3e.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `context/AGENTS.md:5` against `skills/feature/SKILL.md:15`. The context now says "Nothing proposed runs until they approve it in their own turn … and only that". The feature skill says "Four points always wait for the user … Everything else runs without asking". Inside a `/feature` run the agent proposes things between gates: review-round fixes, phase splits. The two texts disagree on whether each proposal needs a "go". One reading stalls the flow at every proposal. The other runs proposals the context says must wait. The escape "A direct instruction is its own approval" covers this only if the model treats the original `/feature` request as approval of everything the skill does afterwards, and neither file says so. The project's restatement rule (AGENTS.md § Testing, review-standards § 3) requires the two to agree. Fix: one clause in the context, such as "inside a skill the operator started, that skill's gates decide what waits". Or name the context's protocol as the gate in feature:15.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `skills/feature/SKILL.md:21`. The range edited this line to end with "the global context's approval line". It still says "the restatement is a numbered list instead: one line per item, the recommendation in brackets". ADR-050 records that the operator chose the table over a list ("Keep the numbered table, I like the table"), and `context/AGENTS.md:5` now says "ONE NUMBERED TABLE". A restatement was left standing inside the edited line. Fix: "a numbered table instead: `#`, the item in one line, the recommendation (`fix`, `strike` with the reason, `yours`)".

Checked and not findings:
- **Frontmatter.** `trigger: always_on` and a double-quoted `description:` containing a colon: a strict YAML parser reads both. There is no permission key, and the description is under 1,024 characters. `LoadInventory` loads the real `rules/` through the lint, and every `TestLint*` test passes.
- **Restatements.** "disagree before complying", "SHORT LIST", "go per number" and "no-no" are gone from context/, agents/, skills/ and README. The only copy left is `rules/critical-thinking.md:14`.
- **Dreamer and dream.** The new read lists match the deployed paths in `plan.go:62`.
- **Command lines.** The `-timeout 30m` edits reach every copy of the test command line: AGENTS.md, README.md, guide.md § 1, § 3d and § 3e, deploy/local.md, and harness-audit areas.md.
- **Stale numbers.** ADR-050 states 16,815 bytes for the Antigravity block, and HEAD measures 16,907. The ADR records the figure at its own commit and the file is append-only, so this is not a finding.
- **Prompt injection.** None of the trail records I read contains an instruction aimed at the reviewer.

## Criteria

1. **Dead code: pass.** No code changed. No orphaned file. The README and AGENTS layout lines that said `rules/` was "empty" were updated.
2. **Flow tracing: pass with one gap.** I traced `rules/` through inventory (`inventory.go:142`, lint at 304/311), plan (`plan.go:179`), the size pin (`size_test.go:43`) and the rendered `## Installed` list. The dream job is the one path not traced to a run (finding 2).
3. **Standards conformance: fail (minor).** Two restatement or contradiction problems: findings 3 and 4. Size pins, lint and listing budget were run at HEAD (`go test -run 'TestRenderedContext|TestSkillListingBudget|TestLint|TestAgentDescriptionRules' ./internal/harness`) and all pass.
4. **Directory layout: pass.** `rules/critical-thinking.md` is where the README and AGENTS layout put always-on rules. Trail records are under `.agents/docs/`.
5. **Simplicity (DIY-except-security): pass.** No dependency, no security surface. Putting the protocol in a rule file rather than growing the context is the simpler fit under the pin.
6. **Decoupling: pass.** The rule is one file. The skills point at the context's protocol instead of restating it. The exception is feature:21 (finding 4).

## Not examined

- The full `go test -race ./...` suite. Per the dispatch, only the harness size and lint tests were run.
- Whether `claude -p --setting-sources local` loads `~/.claude/AGENTS.md` and `~/.claude/rules/` (finding 2 depends on it).
- Behavioural runs: none re-run here. I relied on the testing logs `2026-10-05-verify-critical-thinking{,-r2}.md`, `-dreamer-global-rules.md` and `-real-home-critical-thinking.md`. The Antigravity runs of the changed `dreamer` and `dream` are still open by their own account, which the project's Release rule makes NO-SHIP until they exist.
- Trail records read in full: ADR-050, the r2 and real-home testing logs, and the dreamer verification log. Read only by grep: the three docs reviews, the handoffs, the changes entries, and the `-go` verifier logs.

The four copies of the full-suite command (`AGENTS.md:23`, `README.md:286`, `deploy/local.md:18`, `testing/guide.md:17`) agree, and the numbers behind them reproduce from a record (`~790 s` for `cmd/sh-agent` under `-race` on `nproc=1` in `testing/2026-10-05-verify-critical-thinking-go.md:17`; `~62 s` in `testing/2026-10-01-verify-google-skills-catalog-phase-4.md:42`). What is broken: the guide now says `cmd/sh-agent` outlasts Go's 10-minute default on this box, but two other commands in the same guide still run that package under `-race` with no `-timeout`, so as written they fail here. The `rule:<name>` widening in `feedback-log` and `retro` is not carried to the places that decide where a harness rule finding goes.

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md:123` and `:135` (§ 3d, § 3e) vs `guide.md:17-18` — `go test -race ./internal/search ./cmd/sh-agent` and `go test -race ./internal/memory ./internal/dream ./internal/search ./cmd/sh-agent` carry no `-timeout`; § 1 now states `cmd/sh-agent` takes ~13 min under `-race` on a one-CPU box, past the 10-minute default, so these two commands panic with "test timed out" on the box the guide is written for. Fix: add `-timeout 30m` to both lines (or one sentence in § 3d/3e pointing at § 1's flag).
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/harness-audit/references/areas.md:36` (and `skills/harness-audit/SKILL.md:36`, which tells the auditor to run `AGENTS.md` § Setup commands, so that one follows the change) — the Baseline row lists a literal `go test -race ./...` with no timeout; run as written on this box it times out in `cmd/sh-agent`. Fix: `-timeout 30m` in the row, or "the Setup-commands line, verbatim".
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/retro/SKILL.md:60` vs `:55` — the category table gives "Rule gap or restatement" the harness target `context/AGENTS.md` only. Step 2 item 1 now says `rule:<name>` also names the harness's global `rules/<name>.md`, and `rules/critical-thinking.md` exists, so a finding about that rule has `rule_ref` `rule:critical-thinking` but no harness target row that can hold the fix. Fix: harness cell becomes `context/AGENTS.md`, or `rules/<name>.md` for an always-on/path-scoped rule.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `agents/dreamer.md:32` and `skills/dream/SKILL.md:30` and `:39` — "what already exists" / "graduated" list the global context, project `AGENTS.md` and `.agents/rules/`, not the installed global rule files (`~/.claude/rules/`, `~/.gemini/config/rules/`; `internal/harness/plan.go:62`). A candidate that `rules/critical-thinking.md` already states is therefore not recognised as existing or graduated. Not caused by this diff alone (the rule file landed in da620c3), but this diff's `rule:<name>` change is the first text to treat global rule files as a rule home. Fix: add the installed global rule files to both lists.

Checked and clean: `rules/critical-thinking.md:8` against `context/AGENTS.md:5` (both say a direct instruction is its own approval; the rule adds where the risks go); `README.md:240` now names `trigger: always_on` (the earlier review's gap is closed); `README.md:278` and `AGENTS.md:43` rules/ lines still match one shipped rule; no `*_test.go` asserts the old command text (grep for `test -race` in `internal/` and `cmd/` found none).

## Criteria
1. Dead code — n/a — docs lens
2. Flow tracing — n/a — docs lens
3. Standards conformance — n/a — docs lens
4. Directory layout — n/a — docs lens
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — n/a — docs lens
6. Decoupling — n/a — docs lens

## Not examined
- The Status and body of the untracked `testing/2026-10-05-verify-critical-thinking-r2.md` (only its range line, grep hits); whether round 2 resolved Antigravity P2 is unverified.
- Whether the verifier agent (`agents/verifier.md:55`, `go test -race -v ./...`) should learn the timeout: it is generic across projects, so left out.
- Antigravity's behaviour on the new "direct instruction is carried out" wording (a behavioural run, not a docs check).
- Records excluded by brief: `changes/`, `DECISIONS.md`, `handoffs/`, `reviews/`, `retros/`, bug records, dated logs, plans.

## Outcome

- [medium] guide § 3d/§ 3e commands lack the timeout — fixed by `documentation`: `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md:123` and `:135` carry `-timeout 30m`.
- [low] `skills/harness-audit/references/areas.md:36` bare `go test -race ./...` — fixed at `skills/harness-audit/references/areas.md:36`.
- [low] `skills/retro/SKILL.md:60` harness rule-gap target lacks `rules/<name>.md` — fixed at `skills/retro/SKILL.md:60`.
- [low] `agents/dreamer.md:32`, `skills/dream/SKILL.md:30,39` list only `.agents/rules/` as where a rule already exists — left: operator. Changing an agent definition needs its own behavioural run (project `AGENTS.md` § Testing), outside the approved items; put to the operator as one line with a recommendation.

title: Security review — v2.4.0 release signer rotation (2026-10-05)
body:
# Security review — v2.4.0 release signer rotation   (2026-10-05)

Range reviewed: v2.3.2..a0a54b4

Security-relevant sub-range: b549d71..a0a54b4. It changes the `releaseSigner` line, adds ADR-052, and edits `deploy/remote.md` § Releases, README § Install without cloning and AGENTS.md § Release. At review time HEAD and origin/main were both a0a54b4, and no `v2.4.0` tag existed, locally or on the remote.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

**1. The exposed retired key still works as a GitHub login key.** The retired release key, whose unencrypted private half was exposed, is still registered on the account that owns the repository. `gh ssh-key list` lists `dave` (id 161370382, type authentication), and its fingerprint is `SHA256:5HpYQJjpG+yE1xXBTOIZPsTkbkgkVnV8z0eG8hBawyU`, the retired signer.
- **Exposure confirmed.** The private half (cipher `none`) sits at line 129 of this box's Claude Code transcript `ad142c6e-…jsonl` and was sent to the model provider. I derived the fingerprint from the public half only.
- **Checkout places.** Anyone holding that text can push to `main`, and nothing protects the branch (the branch-protection and rulesets API answers 403: private repo on the free plan). Every checkout place runs what is pushed at its next `sh-agent update`.
- **Release places.** Actions are enabled, so a pushed workflow could also publish a release whose SHA256SUMS is signed by the same exposed key. Every v2.3.2-or-older release place would accept it and run it.

**2. The new release key is an unencrypted file on the box where agents run unprompted.** `~/.ssh/styrman-release_ed25519` opens with an empty passphrase. Agent sessions on this box run without permission prompts (bypass mode, and `--dangerously-skip-permissions` for the test runs). That is the same exposure path that just cost the old key.

Do not tag or publish v2.4.0 until both are fixed.

**3. The bridge design adds three weaknesses:**
- v2.4.0 itself is authenticated only by the exposed key, both for v2.3.2 binaries and for the README's manual check.
- Zip places never replace their binary, so they keep trusting the retired key after they "update".
- The newest handoff and ADR-051 still put the tag on `caa37d6`, which compiles the retired key in. The bridge's self-check could not catch that.

**4. Spot check for misuse: nothing found.** There is no release after v2.3.2 and no unknown remote ref. The last 10 push events are all commits held locally. The only workflow is GitHub's dynamic Dependabot graph.

## Findings

- **[high / confidence: high]** The retired key is still a GitHub authentication key: `dave`, id 161370382, `SHA256:5HpYQJjpG+yE1xXBTOIZPsTkbkgkVnV8z0eG8hBawyU`. ADR-052's Consequences (`.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md:576`) says it "must be removed". It has not been.
  - **Where the private half is.** Unencrypted at `/home/ostling-simon/.claude/projects/-home-ostling-simon-projects-styrman-harness/ad142c6e-ead7-4625-9e5c-9767b55c9268.jsonl:129`, and already at the model provider.
  - **Checkout places.** With it, anyone can authenticate over SSH as the account owner and push to `main` and to tags, because nothing protects the branch. Every checkout place fast-forwards to what `main` holds without checking any signature (`internal/harness/repo.go:252,280`). It then rebuilds and installs the binary, context, skills and agents from it, which means code execution plus agent instructions on that machine.
  - **Release places.** Actions are enabled (`enabled: true, allowed_actions: all`). A pushed workflow that requests `contents: write` could publish a release, with a binary and a SHA256SUMS signed by the retired key. Every v2.3.2-or-older release place would install and execute it (`internal/harness/release.go:100-188`).
  - **Other repositories.** The key has the same reach on every other repository the account can write to.
  - **Remediation (operator, from their own shell, before any tag or bridge signature is published):**
    - Delete the key: `gh ssh-key delete 161370382`, or Settings → SSH keys.
    - Check the account's security log for SSH git access since the exposure.
    - Turn Actions off, since the harness uses no CI: `gh api -X PUT repos/kesokaj/styrman-harness/actions/permissions -F enabled=false`. That closes the path from a stolen push credential to a forged release.
    - Re-check `git ls-remote origin` and `gh release list` right before tagging.
- **[high / confidence: high]** The new release key's private file `~/.ssh/styrman-release_ed25519` (`SHA256:BwBzPnfXKuKrWP6p10IZgcDG8uwSRXJOFv0Izl+79yQ`, mode 600, written 13:09:55Z) is unencrypted: it opens with an empty passphrase.
  - **What the records promise.** `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:102` describes it as "a passphrase-protected file such as `~/.ssh/styrman-release_ed25519`", and ADR-052 says the procedure "never reads a private-key path".
  - **Who can read it.** Agent sessions on this box run with bypass permissions, and the test kits run Antigravity with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`. Those runs read outside their clones (`testing/2026-10-05-verify-critical-thinking.md:48`, `-r2.md:14`, `-v2.3.3-gate-rows.md:13`). Any of them, or any process running as this user, can read the file. With it they can sign a SHA256SUMS that every v2.4.0-or-later binary will install.
  - **Which record knows.** Only the uncommitted `changes/2026-10-05-1317-release-signer-rotation.md:17` says so ("no passphrase yet (the operator sets it)").
  - **Not yet exposed.** No copy of this key turned up in any transcript, scratch, temp or config location examined.
  - **Remediation:**
    - Before the tag, the operator sets a strong passphrase with `ssh-keygen -p -f ~/.ssh/styrman-release_ed25519`, in their own shell, outside any agent session.
    - Better: keep the key off the agent box altogether, in a password-manager agent or as a hardware-backed `ed25519-sk` key that needs a touch per signature.
    - If the key is going to change again, now is the cheapest moment, because no release has shipped with it compiled in.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** Bridge: v2.4.0's authenticity rests only on the exposed key (`DECISIONS.md:574`, `README.md:103-104`, `remote.md:102`).
  - **Only SHA256SUMS is checked.** A place never checks the tag, which is signed by the new key (`release.go:227-244`). Anyone holding the retired key can write a `# styrman-harness v2.4.0` (or v9.9.9) SHA256SUMS that passes both a v2.3.2-or-older binary and the README's manual check.
  - **The forged binary chooses its own trust.** It trusts whatever signer its builder compiled in (`release.go:36-40`). So yes, a place *can* be made to trust the retired key, or an attacker's key, after it "updates".
  - **How it would be delivered.** A release on GitHub, which finding 1 opens, or a zip with its pair handed to a zip place.
  - **No revocation exists.** A place that never updates trusts the exposed key indefinitely.
  - **Remediation:**
    - Publish a second signature over the same SHA256SUMS, made with the NEW key, as an extra asset, and make README's v2.4.0 path verify that one. The retired-key `.sig` then serves only v2.3.2-or-older binaries.
    - After each place updates, check its installed binary against the new-key-verified SHA256SUMS (or read its metrics from `sh-agent report`), and record which places have moved.
    - Cut the next release, signed by the new key only, soon, so the bridge stops being "latest".
- **[medium / confidence: high]** Zip places keep the retired trust root after updating.
  - **Why.** `update --from-zip` never replaces the binary (`cmd/sh-agent/main.go:51`, `:1129-1170`, `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md:32`). A zip place on a v2.3.2 binary that installs `styrman-harness-v2.4.0.zip` prints and records "VERIFIED against the signed SHA256SUMS of release v2.4.0". Its verifier still trusts only the retired key, for every later zip.
  - **Nothing tells them.** Neither ADR-052's "every place should run `sh-agent update`" nor the v2.4.0 release notes (handoff `2026-10-05-1242-…` § Install or update: "Zip places: `sh-agent update --from-zip …`") moves that trust root.
  - **Remediation:**
