title: Review — worktree-code-docs (2026-10-07)
body:
# Review — worktree-code-docs   (2026-10-07)

Range reviewed: working tree vs HEAD (4793d5a): context/AGENTS.md, skills/{feature,review,bug,handoff,preflight,retro,operate-gcp}/SKILL.md, agents/{bugs,changelog,documentation}.md (ROADMAP.md and plans/ ignored). Code lens and docs lens in one pass.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE (final, after round 2; round 1 was REQUEST CHANGES)

The worst problem: the new combined `--code --docs` dispatch is specified by two instructions that cannot both be followed. The Docs brief's item 1 marks every review criterion `n/a — docs lens`, but review Step 3 now sends it, under a `## Docs lens` heading, in the same dispatch as the code brief that demands all six criteria. Beyond that, the "failure" definition now contradicts itself, and several living restatements of the changed rules were left stale (operate-gcp, three init-project templates). No contradiction between context/AGENTS.md, bug, feature, review, preflight, handoff and retro on the two-round cap, the 30-line docs rule or the "main agent writes records" rule was found. The size and description pins pass (`go test ./internal/harness -run TestRenderedContext|TestSkillListingBudget|TestAgentDescription|TestLintDescriptionLimit`).

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `skills/review/SKILL.md:52,60` vs `:50` — Step 3 puts the code brief and the Docs brief in ONE dispatch ("the code brief, then the Docs brief under `## Docs lens`"), but Docs brief item 1 says "Keep your report template with every criterion marked `n/a — docs lens`". Read literally the reviewer must both apply the six criteria and mark all six n/a; a second agent contradiction of this kind is what Step 5 calls "the rule is the defect". Fix: word item 1 conditionally ("when the docs lens is the whole dispatch, mark every criterion n/a; in a combined dispatch the criteria belong to the code brief and items 2-7 populate a separate `## Docs lens` section"). Preflight Step 2 (`skills/preflight/SKILL.md:~58`) and context step 2 inherit the same ambiguity.
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `skills/bug/SKILL.md:21`, `agents/bugs.md:3` — the failure list still includes "a test failing for a reason other than the change under test" and "a fix that took more than one attempt", and bugs.md still lists "a failing test that took more than one attempt" as a dispatch trigger, while the same sentences now say a defect the same uncommitted change's review/tests/verifier caught "is not a failure" / "never for a defect ... tests caught". Those items are by nature caught by the change's own tests before commit, so a print-mode run can argue either way (the BUG-042 pattern: a gate that counts nothing checkable). Fix: state the boundary as the one checkable fact (the defect reached a commit, a deploy, or the user), and say explicitly that a multi-attempt fix or foreign test failure inside one uncommitted change is recorded in the review `## Outcome`/changes entry, not as a BUG, or keep them as BUG triggers and carve them out of "Not a failure".
- **[medium / confidence: high]** stale restatements the diff left standing:
  - `skills/operate-gcp/SKILL.md:80` — "Every incident gets a number (the global rule: anything that went wrong)"; the global rule now reads "every failure that escaped its change's own gates" (`context/AGENTS.md:33`).
  - `skills/init-project/assets/agents-tree/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md:5` — "(the changelog agent writes them)"; ADRs are the main agent's (context step 4, `agents/changelog.md:73`). Pre-dates this diff but is exactly the restatement of the changed record-writing claim.
  - `skills/init-project/assets/agents-tree/docs/bugs/INDEX.md:3,10` — "Maintained by the `bugs` agent" / "Rows move here, by the `bugs` agent"; context now says the main agent writes records, `bugs` only when it lacks the evidence (`context/AGENTS.md:33,18`).
  - `skills/init-project/assets/agents-tree/docs/deploy/local.md:8` — "the `documentation` agent keeps it current (Definition of Done step 3)"; step 3 now sends edits up to 30 lines to the main agent.
  These templates are copied into every new project, so the stale claim is propagated.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/feature/SKILL.md:93` vs `:57` — the user gate on the one-report cold read hangs on "a BLOCKING question only the user can settle", a classification the author makes with no checkable count; an unattended run can label everything NON-BLOCKING and write D-rows, which is the self-answer path BUG-042 warned about (the count there was reports, which is now exactly one, so the count itself holds; the escape is the classification). Also line 57 allows `[-]` for "the user's same-turn override quoted with its date" while Step 3 lists only the one-phase/under-5-files skip. Suggest: make the reviewer's BLOCKING marks the input (every BLOCKING item is either answered by the user's words or recorded as an `Open:` row), and list the override in Step 3.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/bug/SKILL.md:55`, `skills/operate-gcp/SKILL.md:83` — a record the main agent writes "in the `bugs` agent definition's format" inherits `owner: bugs` from the template (`agents/bugs.md:30`), misattributing authorship. Say `owner: main` when the main agent writes it.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass; nothing orphaned (the removed "three-round"/"cold-read round 4" wording has no living remnant: grep over context, skills, agents, rules, README found none).
2. Flow tracing — fail on one hop: review Step 3 combined dispatch vs Docs brief item 1. Round cap (context 16, review 100/112, bug 15, feature 15, preflight 78) consistent; `--docs` rides preflight Step 2's dispatch, falls back to a lone docs run.
3. Standards conformance — fail: the stale restatements above; size/description/listing pins pass.
4. Directory layout — pass; no new files in scope.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass; nothing hand-rolled, the change removes dispatches.
6. Decoupling — pass; one home per claim (30-line rule lives in context step 3, restated by pointer in feature/bug/preflight; bugs/changelog/documentation descriptions carry the agent-side half).

## Not examined
Behavioural runs of the changed skills/agents on either CLI (guide § 4); the interactive README map; skills/init-project/SKILL.md body beyond grep hits; `skills/review/SKILL.md` lines outside Steps 3-5; full diff of `skills/handoff` (read, only the two edits). README.md:259 was read and states nothing the diff changed.

## Round 2

Verified the fixes against the working tree; `go test ./internal/harness -count=1` passes (76s).

- Finding 1 (combined dispatch vs Docs brief item 1) — fixed: `skills/review/SKILL.md:60` is now conditional (alone: all criteria n/a; inside `--code --docs`: the code brief fills the criteria, the list is the `## Docs lens` section). No other text restates the old item.
- Finding 2 (failure boundary) — fixed: one fact ("reached a commit, a deploy or the user") is stated identically in `skills/bug/SKILL.md:21`, `agents/bugs.md:3`, `context/AGENTS.md:11,33`, `skills/operate-gcp/SKILL.md:80`; the "in however many attempts" clause resolves the overlap with the "fix took more than one attempt" list item. Residual (not a finding): the list items and the boundary sentence still sit side by side, and the boundary wins by its own wording.
- Finding 3 (stale restatements) — fixed: operate-gcp:80, DECISIONS.md:5, bugs/INDEX.md:3,10, deploy/local.md:8 now agree with context steps 3-4. A repo-wide grep for the old wording ("anything that went wrong", "changelog agent writes", "by the `bugs` agent", "documentation agent keeps") found no living remnant.
- Low `owner:` finding — fixed: `owner: main` stated at `skills/bug/SKILL.md:21,55`; `agents/bugs.md:30` template keeps `owner: bugs` for a dispatched agent, which is correct.
- Low "author-judged BLOCKING" (`skills/feature/SKILL.md:93`) — rebuttal accepted: the cold reader marks BLOCKING, and each user-only item ends as a D-row, rebuttal or `Open:` row a later reader can check. The Step 3 vs line 57 override mismatch is left as a nit.

No defects introduced by the fixes found.

## Outcome

Written by the main agent, 2026-10-07. Round 2 resumed the same agent with `SendMessage` (review Step 5) and approved.

| # | Finding | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The combined `--code --docs` brief contradicted itself | **fixed** at `skills/review/SKILL.md:60`: Docs brief item 1 is now conditional |
| 2 | The failure boundary could be argued either way | **fixed**: one fact, "reached a commit, a deploy or the user", worded the same at `skills/bug/SKILL.md:21`, `agents/bugs.md:3`, `context/AGENTS.md:11,33` and `skills/operate-gcp/SKILL.md:80` |
| 3 | Stale restatements | **fixed**: `skills/operate-gcp/SKILL.md:80`, and in the init-project templates `docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md:5`, `docs/bugs/INDEX.md:3,10` and `docs/deploy/local.md:8` |
| low | A main-written bug record still said `owner: bugs` | **fixed**: `owner: main` at `skills/bug/SKILL.md:21,55` |
| low | The BLOCKING gate is judged by the author | **rebutted**: the cold reader marks an item BLOCKING; the author decides only whether the user alone can settle it, and records every item as a checkable D-row or rebuttal (`skills/feature/SKILL.md:93`). Round 2 accepted this. |
| nit | Step 3 and the checkbox at line 57 differ on the user override | **left**: implementer; the override wording is unchanged from before this change |

title: Review — 2c0f215-166aa39-code-docs (2026-10-08)
body:
# Review — 2c0f215-166aa39-code-docs   (2026-10-08)

Range reviewed: 2c0f215...166aa39 (10 commits, metrics store Phases 0-7; 59 files, +6007/-119). Lens: `--code --docs`.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

No finding blocks. The worst is a correctness hole in the command normaliser: `git -C <dir> add -A` (and any git call with a global option before the subcommand) is stored as `git -C -A`, so the "forbidden shape" counters (`git add -A`, `git add .`, `git push --force`) and the commit/test chaining check silently undercount for the very form this repo's own rules use. Two leftover-copy and one Antigravity staleness issues follow, then small docs gaps. Privacy invariants I probed (no arguments, secrets, prose or paths in the store; numbers-only dream block; HTML escaping; 0600/O_EXCL writes; parameterised SQL) hold. `gofmt -l`, `go vet` and `go test -count=1` for `internal/metrics`, `internal/dream`, `internal/search` pass; the full `-race` suite was not run (see Not examined).

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/metrics/verb.go:225-229` (`verbFrom`) — the subcommand is taken only when `rest[0]` is name-shaped, so git global options before it hide it. Probed by running `Verb`: `git -C /p commit -m x` gives `git -C -m`; `git add -A` gives `git add -A` but `git -C dir add -A` gives `git -C -A`. `show.go:402-421` reads `w[1]` as the subcommand, so `git -C dir add -A`, `git -C dir push --force` and `git -c k=v commit` never count as forbidden and never set `commit` for the "commit chained to test" check. These are the headline process-adherence numbers (`C.forbidden.*`) that `/retro` source 11 and the dream prompt cite. Fix: for `git`, skip `-C <value>`, `-c <value>`, `--git-dir=…`, `--no-pager` etc. before choosing the subcommand (the value is dropped anyway), and add a `TestVerb` row for `git -C x add -A` to `git add -A`.
- **[medium / confidence: low]** `internal/metrics/agy.go:230-231, 213-217` — Antigravity tool steps and generation rows use `ON CONFLICT … DO NOTHING`, unlike Claude's tool rows (`claude.go`, DO UPDATE). A conversation ingested while a tool step is still running (the nightly dream or a manual ingest mid-session; `ingestAgy` re-reads a conversation whenever its mtime moved) freezes that step at `is_error=0`, and a generation row stays at `ts=NULL` forever, so Antigravity `D.tool_error_rate` and per-day charts can be under-counted. I did not confirm that Antigravity writes a non-final status for a running step, hence low confidence. Fix: upsert `is_error`/`ts` for `agyTool` and the generation `ts`, or skip steps whose status is not final, with a re-ingest test (ingest, then add the failure, then ingest again).
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/metrics/agy.go:54`, `internal/dream/metrics.go:49`, `internal/dream/run.go:334` — `metrics-agy-*` holds full copies of Antigravity's conversation databases (prose and tool output), and `dream-metrics-*` a copy of the metrics store, both made under `~/.config/sh-agent/` and removed only by `defer os.RemoveAll`. A SIGINT/SIGKILL or a crash during `metrics ingest` leaves them; `removeCopies` sweeps only `dream-agy-*` and `dream-projects-*`, so these stay forever (0700, but they are transcript content outside any retention rule). Fix: add the two prefixes to `removeCopies` (and have `metrics ingest` sweep `metrics-agy-*` older than an hour at start), with a test beside the existing `removeCopies` one.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:420-440` (`ingest`), `:490-505` (`export`) — `metrics ingest` silently accepts `--json`, `--since`, `--project`, `--all-labels`, `--out`, and `export` accepts all of them, while `show`/`report` do refuse the ingest-only flags (`metricsShowOptions`). README says a flag a verb does not define is a usage error with exit 2; `--json` on `ingest` exits 0 and ignores it. Fix: mirror `metricsShowOptions`' refusals in `ingest` and `export`, with a test.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/metrics/show.go:143-146`, `events.go:46-120` — `--project` and the events join compare `sessions.project_root` (the first line's `cwd`, or the first workspace URI) by equality with the project root, and `docsRootOf(root)` stats `<cwd>/.agents/docs`. A Claude Code session started in a subdirectory or a worktree is therefore absent from the dream's per-project numbers and `/retro` source 11, and gets no handoff/verifier/review/bug events. Spec § `--project` states the exact match, so this is a documented limit, but README's row ("only sessions in this project root") and the retro skill do not warn that a subdirectory start is invisible. Fix: say so in the README row and the retro source, or match by prefix.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `REQUIREMENTS.md:15` (R3 addendum) vs `internal/dream/metrics.go:44-73` — R3 says the dream reads "`sh-agent metrics show --json` for each project's window, numbers only"; the code reads `Summary.Numbers()` from a `Snapshot`, not `show --json` (whose JSON also carries tool, skill, subagent and label names, `show.go:28-110`). The code is the narrower and safer reading, so no leak, but a reader of R3 would believe the whole `show --json` goes to the model. REQUIREMENTS is immutable without the operator: raise it as a proposed wording edit ("the numbers-only form of `metrics show`"); do not edit it.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md:81-97` (`## The background dreamer`) — the operator's deploy guide for the timer does not say that every nightly run now ingests both CLIs into `~/.config/sh-agent/metrics.db` first, that a real run adds `metrics.db`/`dream-metrics-*` to the state, or that `sh-agent metrics` exists at all (README and `specs/sh-agent/dream.md` do). Add one bullet and the `metrics ingest` / `metrics export` backup step (the store is the only copy once a transcript expires). `README.md:84` ("beside the global search index `search.db`, a cache `report` never sends") enumerates the state beside `search.db` without `metrics.db`; I read only its first 200 characters, so treat as unverified.
- **[note / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/testing/2026-10-08-verify-metrics-sandbox.md` — its own status is **FAIL** (skill-matrix `retro` row, Claude Code, 0 of 2) with the control run at 2c0f215 still open. Not a code defect, but a release gate must treat the range as NO-SHIP until the control run exists or the row is re-run; the matrix rows for `metrics *` also show Antigravity/other places "not run" for `export` beyond cmd tests.

## Docs lens

Restatement grep over the changed claims ("one package that imports the driver", "used only by the search index", "never sent", `search.db`, `dream-work`) listed these living files: README.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, `internal/harness/report.go`, `specs/sh-agent/{dream,memory-loop,search,metrics}.md`, `deploy/remote.md`, `testing/guide.md`.
- Updated consistently with the code: AGENTS.md layout rows (`internal/search` "one of the two packages", `internal/metrics`), `internal/search/store.go` and `dream.go` comments, README map label + command table + state table, R3/R4/R7, `memory-loop.md` Known differences (cost, denials, tokens), `dream.md`, `testing/guide.md` § 3g, matrix rows, `ab-kit/run.sh` (`metrics.py` has no remaining reference outside records), `skills/retro/SKILL.md` source 11 (key names match `show --json`'s nested `A`/`B`/`C`/`D` groups and `Numbers()`'s flat keys).
- `specs/sh-agent/search.md:11` still says the search index is "the" derived SQLite index with no mention that a second SQLite file exists; harmless, its claim is only about its own cache. No `stale test:` hits (the moved `trailStatusArgs` test was retargeted to `trail.StatusArgs`). `dropped:` none. `narrowed:` none found.
- Unverified: the browser rendering claims (light/dark/400 px) in the matrix and guide, and the "15 local conversations" sample behind the Antigravity null columns.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. `search/export.go` wrappers each have a caller in `internal/metrics`; the old `trailDates`/`trailStatusArgs` were moved to `internal/trail`, not duplicated; `ab-kit/metrics.py` deleted with no leftover reference.
2. Flow tracing — pass with findings 1-3. Ingest to events to Show to Numbers to dream prompt is connected end to end; errors propagate (`Failed` list, exit 1); a store newer than the binary is refused untouched; `Snapshot` refuses a schema mismatch; the dream treats a metrics failure as non-fatal by design (D16). Tests for ingest idempotence, canary no-content, uninstall-keeps-store and `report` skip list exist and pass.
3. Standards conformance — mostly pass. Stdlib-only apart from the already-allowed driver; every dated trail file has frontmatter; finding 4 (flag refusal) and finding 7 (docs) are the departures; README/AGENTS/R4 restatements are consistent.
4. Directory layout — pass. `internal/metrics`, `internal/trail` (no driver import), tests beside code, spec in `specs/sh-agent/`; `internal/trail` has no test file of its own (covered through `internal/dream`'s `TestTrailDateFromGit`).
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. The hand-written shell tokenizer in `verb.go` is a text normaliser, not a security primitive (its weakness is finding 1); salt and ids come from `crypto/rand`, the command hash is a salted `sha256` checksum, used as designed: no DIY crypto, no new dependency.
6. Decoupling — pass. `metrics` reaches `search` only through the exported wrappers and `trail`; `dream` calls `metrics` through two replaceable variables; `internal/harness` imports neither.

## Not examined
- Full `go test -race -timeout 30m ./...` (about 13 minutes here); I ran `gofmt`, `go vet` and `-count=1` without `-race` on `internal/metrics`, `internal/dream`, `internal/search`, plus the harness-map/uninstall/report tests.
- `internal/metrics/show.go` lines 215-385 and 440-660 (accumulators, DoD closure, retry loops, text writer), `report.go` chart geometry (template and escaping were checked), and every `*_test.go` body beyond names and the verification log: tests were not mutation-checked.
- ADR-055/055a text, the plan, the spec's invariants table and the eight `changes/` entries (read by name and diff stat only); `testing/guide.md` § 3g commands were not run; no real-home ingest (R6).
- `skills/retro/SKILL.md` source 11 behaviour on Antigravity beyond what the verification log reports.

## Outcome

Written by the main agent, 2026-10-08.
1. `verb.go` — git global options hide the subcommand: **fixed** by `skipGitGlobals` in `internal/metrics/verb.go`, under `TestVerbGitGlobalsAndQuotedHeredoc` (red before the fix).
2. `agy.go` — Antigravity tool and generation rows are inserted once and never updated: **fixed**; both upserts are now `DO UPDATE`, under `TestAgyStepUpdatedOnReingest` (red before the fix).
3. Temporary copies are never swept: **fixed** by `sweepCopies` in `internal/metrics/agy.go` and two new prefixes in `internal/dream/run.go` `removeCopies`, under `TestIngestSweepsStaleCopies` and `TestRemoveCopiesSweepsMetricsCopies` (both red before the fix). The same finding is in the security report.
4. `ingest` and `export` accept flags they do not read: **fixed** by `metricsFlagsOutside` in `cmd/sh-agent/main.go`, under seven new `TestMetricsUsageErrorsExit2` cases (red before the fix).
5. `--project` and the events join use an exact `cwd` match: **fixed**. `show` now matches the root or anything under it, with LIKE wildcards escaped. The events join groups sessions by `trail.Toplevel`. Pinned by `TestSubdirectorySessionsBelongToTheProject` (red before the fix). The spec and README rows say so.
6. R3 says `show --json`, but the code sends `Numbers()`: **left: operator** — it is a REQUIREMENTS.md wording edit, proposed in the feature's closing report.
7. `deploy/local.md`'s dreamer section omits the ingest and the backup: **fixed**, with one bullet in `## The background dreamer`.
8. The sandbox log's FAIL row (Claude `retro`, 0 of 2) with no control run: **left: operator**. It is an Open row in the plan, and the range is not called releasable until a control run exists.

title: Review — metrics-store plan, cold read (2026-10-08)
body:
# Review — metrics-store plan, cold read   (2026-10-08)

Range reviewed: `.agents/docs/plans/2026-10-08-metrics-store.md` (a plan file, not a diff), plus the code surfaces it names: `internal/search/store.go`, `internal/search/dream.go`, `internal/search/parse.go`, `internal/dream/{collect,run,dream}.go`, `cmd/sh-agent/main.go`, `internal/harness/{state,report}.go`, `README.md`, `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `testing/ab-kit/{run.sh,metrics.py}`.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: design needs revision / implementation not ready

Worst problem first: the schema in `## Interfaces` cannot compute several catalogue metrics the plan promises (A6 pass^k has no pass/fail source or run identity; C4 skills loaded has no column; C2 `git add .` is undetectable because positional words are dropped; D1 permission denials have no column), while `## Scope` says no paths are stored and the schema stores several. Second, the plan's "Code to reuse" does not survive contact with the code: the helpers are unexported, `proseLeaves` returns prose only, `dream` would have to import `metrics` while `metrics` needs `dream`'s `trailDates` (an import cycle), and `--vendor` is already a global flag on every verb, so redeclaring it panics at start-up. Third, two verify fixtures do not produce the condition they claim (see G8, G9). The 7 BLOCKING questions below must be answered before a first pass.

I could not check the plan's spike claims (`cost-state.totalCostUSD`, `subagents/*.meta.json`) against real transcripts: the probe of `~/.claude/projects` was refused by the permission layer and I did not retry it. They are unverified by me, not disproved. Nothing else in the repo mentions `cost-state` (grep over `.agents/docs`, `internal`, `skills`: only this plan).

## Findings (Gaps, question 1)

- **G1 [high / high]** Schema vs catalogue vs "no paths" (`plan:22-29, 46-67, 86-98`).
  - A6: "pass rate per label, with pass^k" needs a per-run pass/fail and a run identity. The schema has neither (`sessions.label` only; `events.kind` has no `pass`). Pass/fail today lives in `ab-kit/accept.py`, which is not ingested.
  - C4 "Skills loaded" needs the Skill tool's `skill` argument, B4 needs `subagent_type`; no column holds either, and `## Scope` Out says "Arguments... in any row".
  - C2 `git add -A`/`git add .`: `Verb` keeps flag names only and drops positional words, so `git add .` is indistinguishable from `git add file`.
  - D1 "permission denials" and "interrupts": `steps.kind` has `interrupt`, but nothing for denial; how either is detected (text match on tool_result prose) is undecided.
  - "Out: file paths in any row", yet `sessions.project_root`, `sessions.source`, `ingest_state.source` are paths, and `events.ref`/`events.value` are untyped. A5 "corrections" from `feedback.jsonl` and A3/A4 events could hold prose or file:line unless stated. Fix: a D-row listing exactly what each `events` kind stores in `ref`/`value`, and which path-valued columns are permitted (the canary test would also fail if the canary sat in a directory name).
- **G2 [high / high]** `--vendor` is already registered for every verb: `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:~203` (`c.fs.StringVar(&c.vendorFlag, "vendor", ...)`, values `all, antigravity (or agy), claude`, resolved against the manifest by `resolveVendor`). The plan's verb flag `--vendor claude|agy|all` on `ingest` would call `StringVar` twice on one FlagSet, which panics ("flag redefined: vendor"). Decide: reuse the global flag, and say what an empty value means (manifest's vendor, as `resolveVendor`, or all). `ctx` is one flat struct (`main.go:~100-108`), so each new flag is a field there.
- **G3 [high / high]** The reuse list is wrong, and the dependency direction is unspecified.
  - `internal/search`: `tryOpen`, `prepareFiles` (store.go:~144-171), `openCopy`, `copyDB`, `kindOf` (parse.go:270), `proseLeaves`/`walk` are all unexported. The plan says only "exported if needed" for `kindOf`. Two driver-importing packages either duplicate the security-reviewed `prepareFiles` or share a helper; undecided.
  - `walk` (search/dream.go:~316-403) returns text leaves only, discarding field numbers. D3 ("tokens read by field number") and Phase 3 ("type 132 tool name only") need a different decoder returning (field, value); not in the plan or the spike.
  - `claudeTranscript` (dream/collect.go:355-433) lists only `projects/<dir>/*.jsonl` and filters per line by `cwd` under one root; it does not walk `<session>/subagents/*.jsonl` and is not usable for an all-projects ingest. `trailDates` (collect.go:207) is in package `dream`, which `dream/run.go` would make import `metrics`; `metrics` importing `dream` is a cycle. These helpers need a home (an exported package, or `metrics` owns copies).
- **G4 [high / medium]** Reverses a recorded security decision without a security step. `search/dream.go:203-206` reads only step types 14 and 15 and says 132 "holds file and command output ... (security review 2026-09-30)". The plan reads 132 for the tool name. Nothing in the phases dispatches `security` (global DoD: input parsing, secrets; also a transcript parser feeding a persistent store), nor the reviewer, verifier, changes entry or handoff. The step-132 tool-name field was not in the Phase 0 spike (the spike lists only `gen_metadata`).
- **G5 [high / medium]** Idempotency model is inconsistent. `unique(session_id, ext_id)` with `ext_id` = "tool_use.id or message id": a tool_use step and its tool_result share the same `tool_use_id`, so the unique index collides. `steps` PK is `(session_id, seq)`; after "size < offset, re-read from 0" a replaced file reassigns `seq`, so PK conflicts or silently drops rows even with ext_id dedupe. Streaming assistant messages repeat one message id across lines (the reason `ab-kit/metrics.py` dedupes by `m['id']`); which line's `usage` wins is not stated. The unit of `ts`, `started_at`, `ended_at` (s or ms) is not stated. For agy, `ext_id` and the incremental offset of a SQLite source are not defined (`ingest_state.offset` for a DB).
- **G6 [high / high]** Metric definitions that two implementers would compute differently: A1 "commit plus handoff in the session window" (handoff is committed after the session ends in the DoD; window = started_at..ended_at?); A4 "BUG records dated after a session commit" (any bug after any commit is meaningless without a link; bug date is a day, commit time is seconds); "ambiguous" overlap "counted separately" (what does `show` print?); project root choice when `cwd` changes within a session (collect.go filters per line); A2/A3 window for subagent sessions.
- **G7 [high / high]** R6 / sandbox hazard with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. `claudeTranscript` gives the env var priority over `<home>/.claude` (collect.go:358-361). `metrics ingest --home .agents/scratch/metrics-home` and `--source DIR` would read the operator's real transcripts whenever the variable is set. The dream tests defeat this with `os.Unsetenv("CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR")` (`internal/dream/main_test.go:9-16`); the plan's Verification does not, and `--source` makes it a product bug, not a test bug. Decide: `--source`/`--home` ignore the env var, or the env var applies to the real home only. Also the golden path copies real transcripts (may hold secrets) into `.agents/scratch`; say so and delete it after.
- **G8 [medium / high]** Phase 3 verify fixture: "the live DB path is never opened (the test makes it unreadable)". Copy-then-read must `open(2)` the source to copy it; a file at mode 0 fails that with EACCES (and root bypasses it), so the test would fail the copy rather than prove the driver never opened the live path. The existing proof is different: `TestCopyDBNeverOpensSource` (`internal/search/dream_test.go:360-377`) makes the source DIRECTORY read-only (0o500), so SQLite cannot create `-wal`/`-shm` beside the original, and the copy succeeds. Use that.
- **G9 [medium / high]** Verification names implementation choices and under-specifies conditions.
  - Golden path: "an independent Python count" of the SQLite-verb count needs a second implementation of `Verb` (the plan's own baseline says "verbs counted at command position"); a mismatch cannot be told from a normaliser difference. `--json` shows `"A":{…}` with no key names, so "reports the same tool-call count" has no key to read. Whether subagent calls are in the count (baseline 1,619) is not stated.
  - Canary: where it sits is unstated. In a positional word it is dropped; as a flag name (`--SECRETCANARY123`) `Verb` keeps it by design; in `cwd` it lands in `project_root`. The test must place it in each field the ingester reads and prove it can fail (a deliberate leak makes it red) — silence is not evidence.
  - "Migration: a binary carrying a v2 test migration" is an implementation choice (an injectable `migrations`); state the criterion (a v1 store with rows opens under a newer schema list and keeps every row, and a newer store is refused untouched).
- **G10 [medium / high]** `dream` wiring. `Run` splits at `dream.go:69-80`: `realRun` or `dryRun`. The plan says `--all` and `--project` ingest first, without saying a `--dry-run` must not (global rule: read-only mode resolves the same guards and performs no side effect, and its test asserts that). Ingest is store-wide, but `--project DIR` implies one root; undecided. Whether the ingest sits inside `dream.lock` (run.go:~53, taken before `o.targets()`) or before it: undecided, as is whether an ingest failure counts toward `last_run.error`.
- **G11 [medium / high]** Map rule 3 and the delivery files. AGENTS.md rule 3: a change to a path lands "in ONE commit with the code, the docs and the map". The plan puts ADR-055 and the REQUIREMENTS edit in Phase 0, the README map label in Phase 5, the code between. Also: `report` collection is an explicit list and names `search.db*` in `Skipped` so a dry run shows it (`internal/harness/report.go:~424-430`); the plan adds `metrics.db` and `-wal`/`-shm` without a "never sent" test or a `Skipped` line. "Metrics record" already means `report.json` in R8/R9 and `delivery.md:54`; the plan's new `metrics` verb and store reuse the word without a sentence that separates them. `uninstall` (R4: removes exactly what its manifest lists): what it does with `metrics.db`, the only copy (D5), is not decided. The ADR file is `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` (the plan says `DECISIONS.md`; ADR-054 is the last, so 055 is free).
- **G12 [medium / medium]** R10 parity. Antigravity has no subagents, compaction records or cost in the plan's sources; B1 tokens may be Claude-only. R10 says what a CLI's runtime alone controls is listed in `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/memory-loop.md` § Known differences; the plan puts it in the new spec only, and lists none of B3, B4, cost as Claude-only. The Risks claim "checked by ... first task of Phase 3" but Phase 3 has no such task, and Verification's "one Antigravity session run" tier has no phase task either.
- **G13 [medium / medium]** Spike evidence. Phase 0 spike is ticked with "field list recorded in D2, D3", but D2 and D3 are one line each and no probe artifact is named; `cost-state` semantics (cumulative vs per-line, per subagent, reset on resume) are not stated and the repo's existing metric script takes cost from the CLI result JSON, not `cost-state` (`ab-kit/metrics.py:3, 14`). Risks lists "Claude keeps writing cost-state" as an unchecked assumption while D2 treats it as a spike result.
- **G14 [low / high]** Docs clauses. `export` (Phase 1) and `--vendor agy` (Phase 3) change the command surface with no `docs:` clause; the `usage` text at `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:~56` and its tests are not listed. `README.md` verb table row, the state table rows 217-218 and `delivery.md`/`dream.md` appear only in some tasks.
- **G15 [low / medium]** Concurrency and failure edges left open: "the second waits or names the lock" (pick one); an Antigravity copy failure makes the whole source fail while "the others are still ingested" (per source, per conversation?); whether a non-git root or a deleted root still gets session rows; a store written by a newer binary on one place and read by an older `show`.

## Scope (question 2)

Built but not named in `## Why` (the request: use SQLite for trajectory data and agent/sandbox metrics; suggest metrics):
- `metrics export` and its JSONL shape: a second output shape beside `show --json`, no D-row says who asked (the only operator answers quoted in D1 are "SQLite as store of record", "New verb + nightly dream", "Shape only", "Local only for now"). A dated nightly export is already a follow-up, so the verb has no consumer in `## Consumers`. Gap unless a D-row or strike.
- Replacing `ab-kit/metrics.py` and `run.sh` (Phase 5) is a consumer in the plan (Consumers 3) but not in D1; acceptable if the operator approves it as a D-row, since it changes a verification kit.
- `--project`, `--since`, `--all-labels` and `--label` filters on `show`: a plausible reading of "metrics from all sessions"; low risk, but each is surface. `meta.salt` and `cmd_hash` serve D2 (retry loops) only; D6 records the choice.
- The A-group joins (git, trail, feedback) go beyond "trajectory data" but are the "metrics for agent evaluations" the operator asked for suggestions on; the operator approved the plan's shape in plan mode per D1, so I do not count them.

## Readiness (question 3)

BLOCKING (two careful implementers would build different things):
1. Where does pass/fail and run identity for A6 pass^k come from? (G1)
2. How are C2 `git add .`, C4 skill names, B4 subagent type and D1 denials stored given "no arguments"? Which exact columns/`events` payloads, and which path columns are allowed? (G1)
3. `--vendor`: reuse the global flag (and its meaning) or a new name? (G2)
4. Which package owns the shared SQLite open rules, the agy copy, the protobuf field decoder, `kindOf` and `trailDates`, given `dream -> metrics`? (G3)
5. `ext_id`/`seq` rule for tool_use vs tool_result rows, replaced files, streamed message ids, and the units of every timestamp. (G5)
6. Definitions of A1 window, A4 (which bug belongs to which commit), and what "ambiguous" does to the numbers. (G6)
7. Do `--home` / `--source` ignore `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`? (G7)

NON-BLOCKING (a reasonable implementer decides, or a default can be stated):
- Fixture for "never opens the live DB" (use the read-only-directory pattern) (G8); canary placement and JSON key names for the golden path (G9) (a reasonable implementer fixes these, but the plan's own acceptance should name them).
- Dry-run behaviour of dream ingest; lock placement; failure-counting (G10).
- Single-commit rule for the map; `Skipped` line and "never sent" test for `metrics.db`; `uninstall` behaviour (G11) (ask the operator in Phase 0 when proposing R3/R4/R7).
- R10 known-differences location; the missing Phase 3 check task (G12).
- Spike evidence and `cost-state` semantics (G13).
- Docs clauses, usage text (G14).
- Concurrency wording; per-conversation failure (G15).
- `export`: keep or strike (operator decision).
- No `security`, `reviewer`, `verifier`, changes entry or handoff step in the phases (G4).

## Check against REQUIREMENTS.md and AGENTS.md

- R3: the dream exception says it "writes only under `~/.config/sh-agent/`" and runs a CLI over what it read. An ingest step that writes a persistent store from both CLIs' transcripts is a new write the exception text does not name; the plan lists the R3 edit (Phase 0). OK as proposed, pending operator approval.
- R4: "one dependency ... used only by the search index"; D4 makes `internal/metrics` a second importer; the plan lists the R4 edit and the AGENTS.md Layout and Rules lines (`AGENTS.md:45, 63`). Not a violation if approved first; Phase 0 orders it correctly. R4 also says search indexes are caches, never sent: `metrics.db` is a store of record, so the edit must say it is not a cache and is never sent (G11).
- R6: ingest and tests use `--home`, but G7 shows the env-var path to the real transcripts.
- R7 edit listed. R8/R9: the "metrics record" wording collision (G11).
- README map rules 1-6: rule 1 (no new path back): met, nothing goes through `report`, but no test pins it. Rule 3: ADR and the map must share one commit with the code (G11). Rule 4: the dream→configDir label gains `metrics.db`; the plan keeps the line solid, and it works for every place only if the dream timer or `metrics ingest` runs there; the first real ingest is a user task in Phase 2. Rule 5: `TestHarnessMap` is named in Phase 5. Rule 6: the plan does not restate the delivery claim.
- Driver/dependency: no new dependency; the existing driver only. OK.

## Criteria (applied to a plan)

1. Dead code: pass. The plan removes `ab-kit/metrics.py` and adds nothing it leaves unused; `kindOf`'s export is conditional.
2. Flow tracing: fail. Schema vs catalogue (G1), reuse vs code (G3), flag collision (G2), `ext_id` rule (G5), dream dry-run (G10).
3. Standards conformance: fail. Rule 3 single commit (G11); DoD steps absent (G4); R10 parity location (G12); docs clauses (G14).
4. Directory layout: pass. `internal/metrics/` with tests beside code, spec under `specs/sh-agent/`, ADR at `architecture/DECISIONS.md`.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security): mostly pass. Stdlib plus the existing driver; `sha256` with a random salt is stdlib use, not DIY crypto; `export` is a second shape without an operator request (Scope).
6. Decoupling: fail until G3 is decided; `dream -> metrics -> (dream|search internals)` has no stated seam, and two packages would duplicate or reach into each other's unexported code.

## Not examined

- Real Claude/Antigravity transcripts and conversation databases (the probe was refused by the permission layer; the spike's field claims are unverified by me, and the agy step-132 payload and `gen_metadata` field numbers were not read).
- `internal/search/store.go` beyond lines 100-180 and `internal/dream/collect.go` lines 1-195 and 470-end; `internal/dream/state.go`, `timer.go`, the `testing/guide.md` § 3e text, `sh-agent-matrix.md`, `kit-preamble.sh`, `accept.py`, `specs/sh-agent/dream.md`/`search.md`/`memory-loop.md` bodies; `TestHarnessMap`; the remainder of `run.sh` after line 50.
- No code was run.
