title: Security review — 2c0f215-166aa39 (2026-10-08)
body:
# Security review — 2c0f215-166aa39   (2026-10-08)

Range reviewed: 2c0f215..166aa39 (10 commits, metrics store Phases 0-7; 59 files, +6007/-119). Diff: `git diff 2c0f215...166aa39`.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

The worst problem is that metrics ingest now runs `git log` without anyone watching, every night and on every `ingest`, inside every project root any session ever recorded. That covers each Claude Code transcript's `cwd`, each Antigravity workspace URI and each sandbox work dir read with `--source`, and every root already stored is re-run on every later ingest (`events.go:46` selects all main sessions). The call disables `core.fsmonitor` and nothing else. Repo-local config is therefore still trusted, and `log.showSignature=true` combined with `gpg.program` (or `gpg.format=ssh` with `gpg.ssh.program`) names a program that `git log` runs on any signed commit in the window. The earlier security rounds of 2026-10-01 already counted a project's `.git/config` as untrusted. This change widens the set of repos it applies to, from indexed projects to every directory a transcript names. That includes A/B and sandbox work dirs where the agent under test wrote `.git/config` itself (`ab-kit/run.sh:73` runs the ingest automatically). No new dependency was added. Store SQL is parameterised. The HTML report escapes every data string. Report collection is an allowlist, so the metrics store, its exports and its HTML reports are never sent. The dream prompt gets only fixed keys and numbers.

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `internal/metrics/events.go:192` (`commitsIn`), and `internal/trail/trail.go:20` (`Dates`, now also reached from metrics through `events.go`) — `git log` runs in roots taken from transcript data, with repo-local config honoured apart from `core.fsmonitor`. `log.showSignature` together with `gpg.program`/`gpg.ssh.program` in a repo's `.git/config` makes `git log` start the named program for a signed commit dated inside the window (the committer controls the date). git-subtree had to add `--no-show-signature` because this setting overrides custom `--format` output, which is why confidence is medium; no probe was run, by design. The trigger is a repo the operator once opened a CLI in, or a sandbox repo an agent under test controlled, and nobody is prompted. `trail.Dates`'s `git log` passes neither `--no-optional-locks` nor any `-c` override. **Remediation:** pass `--no-show-signature` and `-c log.showSignature=false` to both `log` calls. Better, add one shared helper for every git call into a project (`-c core.fsmonitor=false -c log.showSignature=false -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null`, `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, env `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` left alone). Also consider running joinEvents only for roots that are indexed projects (`search` project list) or under `--source`, not for every directory ever recorded. Add a test that sets `log.showSignature=true` and `gpg.program=<a marker writer>` in a fixture repo and asserts the marker is not written.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/metrics/agy.go:62` (`metrics-agy-*`), `internal/dream/metrics.go:57` (`dream-metrics-*`), `internal/dream/run.go:334` (`removeCopies`) — the new temp dirs under `~/.config/sh-agent/` hold full copies of Antigravity conversation databases (prose, tool arguments) and a full copy of `metrics.db`. They are removed only by `defer os.RemoveAll`. A killed nightly run (timer stop, reboot, OOM) leaves them behind for good. `removeCopies` sweeps only `dream-agy-` and `dream-projects-`, the exact sweep added for this leftover case. That conflicts with R4's "never arguments or prose" for state at rest in `~/.config/sh-agent/` (mode 0700, same user, so it is not exposed to other users). **Remediation:** add both prefixes to `removeCopies`, or call the sweep from `metrics ingest` itself so a run without dream also cleans up. Add a test that plants an old `metrics-agy-x` dir and asserts it is removed.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/metrics/verb.go:339` (`heredocDelims`) — a here-doc opened as `<<\EOF` (backslash-quoted delimiter, valid bash) is not recognised. No delimiter is captured, so the body lines are tokenised as commands, and any body line whose first word matches `programName` (`^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.+-]*$`) is stored as a verb. A bare token line (`sk-…`, `ghp_…`, `AKIA…`) written through such a here-doc would end up in `step_verbs`, against the "no positional word" invariant. **Remediation:** accept a leading `\` before the delimiter word (`<<\EOF`, `<<-\EOF`). Add a Verb test with a token-shaped body line under `<<\EOF` that asserts no verb comes out.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/metrics/claude.go:448` (`hash`) and `internal/metrics/store.go:55` (export includes `meta`) — `cmd_hash` is SHA-256(salt‖0x00‖full command) cut to 64 bits, and the salt is stored in the same database and written into every `metrics export`. Anyone holding the store or an export can therefore confirm a guessed low-entropy command, arguments included, which is weaker than the spec's "never arguments" wording suggests. High-entropy secrets cannot be recovered this way. I do **not** count this as hand-rolled crypto: it is `crypto/sha256` used as an equality fingerprint, and no authenticity or secrecy claim depends on the salt. `crypto/hmac` would be the idiomatic keyed form if one were ever needed. **Remediation:** state in `specs/sh-agent/metrics.md` that the hash confirms guesses and that an export is as sensitive as the store, or hash only the normalised verb plus a coarse argument count if retry-loop detection allows it.

## Checked
- **Secrets:** none in the added code, tests or kit. The metrics store holds no arguments or prose, apart from the verb leak above. `report.Collect` is a named allowlist (feedback, retros, state, proposals, dream harness proposals), so `metrics.db*`, `reports/*.html` and any export under `~/.config/sh-agent/` are never sent. The new Skipped lines are only labels.
- **Injection:** every store query is parameterised. The `show.go:137-152` filters append fixed SQL text and bind values. `exportTable` concatenates only the constant `tables` list. `git` is run with `exec.Command` and an argv, never a shell. The HTML report (`report.go`) uses `html/template` for the page, and every data string inside the hand-built SVG goes through `template.HTMLEscapeString`; CSS classes are constants and there is no script. Antigravity `conversation_id` is checked for `/`, `\`, `.` and `..` before it is used in a path (`agy.go:109`). The dream prompt carries `Numbers()` only: fixed keys and float values.
- **Authz/authn:** no auth surface. Store files are 0600 (`prepareFiles`) in a 0700 dir. Exports and reports are written `O_EXCL|0600`. Symlinked transcripts and DB files are refused (`Lstat` plus `IsRegular`).
- **Crypto:** `crypto/rand` 16-byte salt and `crypto/sha256` fingerprint, used as designed (see the low finding). Nothing hand-rolled.
- **Dependencies:** `go.mod`/`go.sum` are not in the diff; `modernc.org/sqlite` now has a second importer, `internal/metrics`, which R4 as amended allows. `govulncheck` is not installed on this box (not on PATH or in GOPATH/bin), so it was not run. There is no npm ecosystem in scope.
- **GCP surface:** none touched.
- **Bug history:** `sh-agent search --refs <path> --kind bug` returned 0 records for the new `internal/metrics/*` files and `search/export.go`. It found BUG-110/127/074 for `harness/report.go` (redaction, which this change does not touch), BUG-131/134/135 for `dream/collect.go` (BUG-135 is the git flag-order and fsmonitor class the main finding extends), and 14 records for `cmd/sh-agent/main.go`.

## Not examined
- `internal/metrics/show.go`, read only at lines 125-155: the summary maths, the forbidden-shape and retry-loop detection, and what the full `--json` contains (read locally by `/retro`, never sent).
- `internal/metrics/agy.go` lines 150-240 (step decoding) and `search.ProtoFields`/`fields` recursion depth on hostile protobuf input.
- `internal/dream/collect.go` diff (-77 lines, the move of trail dating into `internal/trail`), apart from the extracted `trail.go`.
- All `*_test.go` files in the range; the spec, plan, ADR and testing docs.
- The `git log` + `log.showSignature` behaviour was not reproduced (no probe, to stay defensive); hence medium confidence.
- `govulncheck` (tool absent).

## Round 2

Range reviewed: 166aa39..working tree (uncommitted fixes, `git diff HEAD`, 19 files +302/-22, plus untracked `internal/trail/trail_test.go`, `BUG-164`, `cmd/sh-agent/x.jsonl`), read 2026-10-08.

### Status: COMPLETE

### Verdict: FINDINGS

The four round-1 findings are fixed as named. One residual remains in the same class. The fixes close `log.showSignature`/`gpg.program`, but `trail.Dates` still runs `git status` in every transcript root, and a repo's own config plus in-tree `.gitattributes` can make `git status` run a **clean filter** (`filter.<driver>.clean`/`.process`). Separately, a partial-clone repo can make `log`/`status` run a lazy fetch through the repo's `core.sshCommand` or remote helper. The new `hardened()` comment and the spec say "the root's own config is untrusted", which claims more than three `-c` overrides can deliver. The operator's decision to keep running git in every transcript root, sandboxes included, is recorded. The residual follows from that decision and should be stated as such, not presented as closed.

### Round-1 findings, re-checked
- **git log signature program (medium):** fixed for the named vector. `trail.Log` (`trail.go:60-64`) adds `-c log.showSignature=false` and `--no-show-signature`. `commitsIn` (`events.go:200`) and `Dates` both use it, and `StatusArgs` and the new `Toplevel` use `hardened()`. Every non-test reference to `trail.*` was re-read: `dream/collect.go:75` (Dates), `events.go:63/134/200`, and `collect_test.go:514` (StatusArgs). Nothing exported was left without a caller (`StatusArgs` keeps `Dates` and the test, as before). The marker tests pass: 40 of 40 isolated runs, and 3 parallel runs of trail+metrics+dream. **But** one run of `go test ./internal/trail/ ./internal/metrics/ -run 'Signature|Sweep|Salt|Heredoc|Verb'` FAILED in the fixture, with `gpg failed to sign the data` / `failed to write commit object`. See the flaky-test finding below.
- **leftover copies (low):** fixed. `sweepCopies` (`agy.go:287-303`) runs at every Antigravity ingest, and `removeCopies` (`dream/run.go:334-337`) now also matches `metrics-agy-` and `dream-metrics-`. The one-hour age guard protects a concurrent run's fresh copy.
- **`<<\EOF` here-doc (low):** fixed (`verb.go:378-379`), including `<<-\EOF` and `<< \EOF` (spaces are trimmed first). `skipGitGlobals` also drops `-c k=v` values, which keeps a `-c http.extraHeader=…` value out of the subcommand slot. No new leak found.
- **salt in export (low):** fixed (`store.go:162-168`). A consequence to put on record: an export is the store's "only backup", and a store rebuilt from it would get a new salt (`ensureSalt`), so `cmd_hash` values from before and after a restore never compare (D6). That is acceptable but undocumented; there is no import path today.

### New findings
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `internal/trail/trail.go:38` (`git status` via `StatusArgs`), reached nightly and on every `metrics ingest` from `events.go:134` for every transcript root — `hardened()` does not neutralise **clean filters**. `.gitattributes` (in-tree, or `.git/info/attributes`) assigning `filter=x`, with `filter.x.clean`/`filter.x.process` in `.git/config`, makes `git status` start that program when a tracked file under the docs pathspec has stat data that does not match the index; an agent under test editing its sandbox repo produces exactly that. A **partial clone** (`extensions.partialClone` + promisor remote) is a second gap: when `log --name-only` or `status` needs a missing object, git starts a lazy fetch, which runs the repo's `core.sshCommand` or a remote helper. The comment at `trail.go:50-54` and the spec's "git in project roots" bullet claim the root's config is untrusted, which these gaps contradict. **Remediation:** export `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` on every `trail` git call (git ≥ 2.45; this box has 2.47.3), or pass `--no-lazy-fetch`. Drop `git status` from the metrics path; the events need commit dates, and an uncommitted record can keep its mtime. Alternatively, run `status` only for indexed projects (the dream's own set). Either way, narrow the comment and the spec to name the three settings that are disabled and say that git in a hostile repo is not made safe by them. Add a marker test with a clean filter (must trip a plain `git status` first, as the signature fixture does).
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/trail/trail_test.go` `signedRepo` fixture is **flaky**: it failed 1 of ~53 runs here, under parallel package load, at the fixture's own signed commit. The likely cause is that the fake `gpg` never reads stdin, so git's write of the payload can hit a closed pipe when the script exits first. A fixture that fails intermittently gets skipped or deleted, and then the regression pin is gone. **Remediation:** start the fake with `cat >/dev/null` on the signing path. Also strengthen the precondition: it proves only that `git log -1` (default format) trips the marker, not that the exact `--format=%H %ct` / `--format=%ct --name-only` argv does without the hardening. Run the unhardened argv in the precondition so the green result means what it claims (silence-is-not-evidence rule).
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/x.jsonl` (untracked, 0600, one `meta` schema row): a `metrics export` from the test cases at `cmd/sh-agent/metrics_test.go:96-97` wrote into the package directory, through a relative `x.jsonl` path, during a run before the refusal existed. That breaks the scratch rule, and staging `cmd/sh-agent/` would commit it. Today it holds no sensitive data, but if the refusal regresses, the same cases export a real store's rows into the source tree. **Remediation:** use `filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "x.jsonl")` in those cases and delete the stray file by name (the author's job, not done here).
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/metrics/show.go:149-155` — SQLite `LIKE` is case-insensitive for ASCII by default, so `--project /home/u/Proj` also matches `/home/u/proj/...`, and so does the dream's per-project numbers summary (`dream/metrics.go`, `Project: root`). The escaping of `\`, `%` and `_` is correct, and the query stays parameterised, so this is a correctness and isolation slip, not injection. **Remediation:** `substr(project_root, 1, ?) = ?` with the length of `p + "/"`, or `PRAGMA case_sensitive_like` on the connection. Add a test with a case-variant sibling.

### Checked (round 2)
- Injection: the new LIKE clause escapes and binds its values. `exportTable`'s meta query is a constant. `skipGitGlobals`/`heredocDelims` only remove words. `metricsFlagsOutside` uses `flag.Visit` over a fixed own-flag set (it does not cover `--vendor`/`--home`, which export ignores; this is usage, not security).
- Secrets: none added. The stray `x.jsonl` holds only `{"table":"meta","row":{"key":"schema","value":"2"}}`.
- Crypto, dependencies, GCP: unchanged (no `go.mod` change). `govulncheck` is still unavailable on this box.

### Not examined (round 2)
- `internal/metrics/agy.go` upsert change (`DO UPDATE` on generation and tool steps) beyond reading it: correctness only.
- `internal/dream/run_test.go`, `internal/metrics/{agy,events,store,verb}_test.go`, `cmd/sh-agent/metrics_test.go` beyond the lines cited.
- Docs diffs (`README.md`, `deploy/local.md`, `bugs/INDEX.md`, `BUG-164`), except the spec's metrics bullets.
- The clean-filter and lazy-fetch vectors were not reproduced (defensive review, no probe); hence medium confidence.

## Round 3

Range reviewed: 166aa39..working tree (round-3 fixes, `git diff HEAD`; `internal/trail/trail.go` rewritten, `trail_test.go`, `metrics/show.go`, `cmd/sh-agent/metrics_test.go`, docs), read 2026-10-09.

### Status: COMPLETE

### Verdict: FINDINGS (low only)

Both round-2 findings that were in scope are fixed, and so are the two lows. `git status` is gone from `internal/trail`. Modified records are now detected with `ls-tree` plus `hash-object --no-filters --stdin-paths`, which runs no clean filter, and any mismatch, missing file or git error falls back to mtime, the safe direction. Every call goes through one builder, `command()`, with the hardened options and `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`. One gap remains: `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH` only exists in recent git, roughly 2.44 or 2.45 and later. An older git ignores the variable without complaint, and Apple's Xcode git (2.39.x) is older, so on the operator's macOS machine the lazy-fetch vector stays open unless git comes from Homebrew. The package comment ("none of them starts a program the repository defines") and the spec bullet do not mention that condition.

### Round-2 findings, re-checked
- **clean filter / lazy fetch (medium):** the clean-filter part is fixed: no `status` call remains in `trail`. `hash-object --no-filters` reads raw bytes, and `ls-tree`/`rev-parse`/`log --no-show-signature` start no repo-defined program for the keys reviewed (fsmonitor, signatures, filters, textconv, hooks). On paths: `--stdin-paths` with a path holding a newline or starting with `"` gives a count mismatch or a different hash, both safe. A symlinked final component is refused by `Lstat`. A symlinked intermediate directory only yields an equality bit that stays local. The lazy-fetch part is fixed only on new git (see the first new finding). `TestDatesRunsNoCleanFilter` asserts its own precondition (a plain `git status` trips the marker), and it passes.
- **flaky signature fixture (low):** fixed. The fake gpg drains stdin and the precondition uses the exact argv. `go test ./internal/trail/ -count=15` and a combined trail+metrics+dream run were all green here.
- **stray `x.jsonl` (low):** fixed. The cases at `cmd/sh-agent/metrics_test.go:88-97` now write under the temp home, `cmd/sh-agent/x.jsonl` is gone, and `go test ./cmd/sh-agent/ -run Metrics` left no untracked file (`git status --short --untracked-files=all` shows only the trail records and `trail_test.go`).
- **case-insensitive LIKE (low):** fixed. `show.go` now uses `project_root = ? OR substr(project_root, 1, length(?)) = ?` with `p+"/"`, bound and case-sensitive; `length` and `substr` both count characters, so they agree on non-ASCII paths.
- **References:** `StatusArgs` was removed together with its test (`TestTrailStatusArgs`), and no reference is left (`grep` of `internal`, `cmd`). The exported `Dates`, `Log` and `Toplevel` each have callers (`dream/collect.go:75`, `metrics/events.go:63,134,200`). `command` and `changed` are unexported. Nothing is left exported without a caller.

### New findings
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/trail/trail.go:111` (`command`), and the claims at `trail.go:6-11` and `specs/sh-agent/metrics.md:259`: `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` (and `--no-lazy-fetch`) arrived in git 2.44/2.45. Older git ignores it, so a partial-clone repo (`extensions.partialClone` with a promisor remote and missing objects) can still make `ls-tree` or `log --name-only` fetch through the repo's `core.sshCommand` or remote helper. The operator's macOS machine typically runs Apple git 2.39. `TestCommandsNeverLazyFetch` pins the env entry, not the behaviour, so it passes on a git that ignores it. **Remediation:** before any other call, read `git config --get extensions.partialClone` (a config read starts nothing) and skip the root if it is set; or refuse to run when `git version` is below the floor. State the floor in the spec and the package comment. A behavioural test needs a promisor fixture with a missing tree that asserts no transport ran.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `trail.go:118` (`Toplevel`), used by `events.go:63`: a root's `core.worktree` setting decides what `rev-parse --show-toplevel` prints. A hostile repo can therefore move its sessions' events onto another project's root, where `log` then runs and `trailFiles` are read, so one project's metrics get corrupted by another. No program runs and nothing leaves the machine. **Remediation:** accept a toplevel only when it is an ancestor of the session's `cwd` (`strings.HasPrefix(cwd+"/", top+"/")`), else keep `cwd`.
- **[info / confidence: high, pre-existing, outside the range]** `internal/search/reconcile.go:132` runs `git status --untracked-files=all` with no hardening (no `core.fsmonitor=false`, clean filters live) in the checkout `sh-agent search` is run from. The global context tells every session to run `sh-agent search --refs` before touching an area, in any project. This is the same class as BUG-164, on an interactive path instead of an unattended one. Worth its own bug record. Not part of this range's fixes.
- Correctness note, not security: a repository whose docs carry `eol=crlf` or LFS attributes now reads every such record as modified, so it falls back to mtime (the BUG-131 class for those repos). The safe direction, documented in `Dates`'s comment.

### Checked (round 3)
- Injection: every git call is an argv, with no shell. Stdin for `hash-object` is the path list taken from `ls-tree -z`. `show.go` binds all three values.
- Secrets, crypto, dependencies, GCP: unchanged. `go vet` of trail, metrics, dream and `cmd/sh-agent` is clean. `govulncheck` is still not installed.

### Not examined (round 3)
- `filterRepo` fixture internals and `TestCommandsNeverLazyFetch` beyond the lines cited. Docs diffs other than the spec bullet and BUG-164's round-2 section.
- The lazy-fetch and `core.worktree` behaviours were not reproduced (no probe), and the exact git version that introduced `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH` was not verified against git's release notes on this box.
- The full `go test -race ./...` was not run; only the packages named above were.

## Outcome

Written by the main agent, 2026-10-09.

Round 1:
1. **Medium.** `git log` in transcript roots honours `log.showSignature` + `gpg.program`: **fixed** by `internal/trail` `command`/`Log` (`-c log.showSignature=false`, `--no-show-signature`), under `TestDatesRunsNoSignatureProgram` and `TestLogRunsNoSignatureProgram` (red before the fix). Recorded as BUG-164, an escaped defect: the dreamer has had it since v2.0.0. The remediation part "limit to indexed roots" is **rebutted**: the hardening closes the named vector, and transcript roots are where the operator ran a CLI (sandbox and A/B data by design, plan D11/D24).
2. **Low.** `metrics-agy-*` and `dream-metrics-*` are not swept: **fixed** by `sweepCopies` in `internal/metrics/agy.go` and `removeCopies` in `internal/dream/run.go`, under `TestIngestSweepsStaleCopies` and `TestRemoveCopiesSweepsMetricsCopies`.
3. **Low.** `<<\EOF` here-docs are not recognised: **fixed** in `internal/metrics/verb.go` `heredocDelims`, under `TestVerbGitGlobalsAndQuotedHeredoc`.
4. **Low.** The salt travels in exports: **fixed** in `internal/metrics/store.go` (export leaves out the salt row), under `TestExportOmitsSalt`.

Round 2:
5. **Medium.** `git status` runs clean filters, and a partial clone can lazy-fetch: **fixed**. `status` is gone from `internal/trail`, replaced by `ls-tree` plus `hash-object --no-filters`; the dreamer's read is covered too, on the operator's choice "Fix both in this feature". `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` is set on every call. Pinned by `TestDatesRunsNoCleanFilter` and `TestCommandsNeverLazyFetch`. The spec wording is narrowed.
6. **Low.** The `signedRepo` fixture was flaky: **fixed**. The fake gpg drains stdin and the precondition uses the exact argv (40/40 repeat runs).
7. **Low.** A stray `cmd/sh-agent/x.jsonl` was written: **fixed**. The file was deleted by name, and the test cases use the temp home.
8. **Low.** `LIKE` is case-insensitive: **fixed** with a `substr` prefix comparison in `internal/metrics/show.go`, under `TestSubdirectorySessionsBelongToTheProject` (an upper-case sibling).

Round 3, the operator's extra round:
9. **Low.** `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH` is ignored by git older than 2.44: **fixed**. A partial clone is not read at all (`partialClone` in `internal/trail/trail.go`), under `TestPartialCloneIsNotRead`; the spec says so.
10. **Low.** `Toplevel` follows `core.worktree`: **fixed**. Only a parent of the directory is accepted, under `TestToplevelIsAParent`.
11. **Info, outside the range.** `internal/search/reconcile.go` runs an unhardened `git status`: **left: next task**, recorded as open BUG-165.

No round 4 was run. Round 3 reported lows only; each fix has a test that was red before it, and the verifier runs after the fixes.

title: Security review — dbd776d-3bffdcf (2026-10-09)
body:
# Security review — dbd776d-3bffdcf   (2026-10-09)

Range reviewed: commits dbd776d..3bffdcf (git log dbd776d..3bffdcf); the diff is git diff dbd776d...3bffdcf.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

The worst problem is in the new command-line credential needle (`internal/harness/report.go:151`). It puts `(^|\s)` in front of `sshpass` and the MySQL client names. That anchor fails the same way as the `\b` the project rule bans: the token is missed when a quote, a backtick, a `/` or a `key:` comes right before the command name. I ran a probe in a scratch copy at 3bffdcf (`.agents/scratch/sec-3bffdcf`, a test file inside package `harness`, since removed). With `redactLines(..., jsonl=true)`, `{"text":"sshpass -p FAKEVALUE ssh h"}` and `{"text":"mysql -u root -pFAKEVALUE db"}` both came through **unredacted**. The raw line has a `"` before the command name. The decoded line, printed by `fmt.Fprintln` of a Go map (`report.go:324`), has `text:` before it. `/usr/bin/mysql -uroot -pFAKEVALUE` was also not matched. This text reaches `sh-agent report` (feedback.jsonl, retros.jsonl, proposals) and the dreamer's prompt (`internal/dream/collect.go:157`, `:254`). The mcpServers refusal is correct and is reached on every install path. Its two test rows fail when the refusal is removed: I removed `"mcpServers"` in the scratch copy and `TestLintPermissionKeysByKind` failed on both rows. The usage-error change, the `Lint` removal and the process-group kill open no new hole. The process-group change does leave one gap: a child process can outlive the run (finding 6).

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/report.go:151` — In the `command-line credential` needle, `(^|\s)` before `sshpass` and before `(?:mysql|mariadb|mysqldump|mysqladmin)` hides the token when a non-space character comes right before the command name. Four cases show it. (1) A JSON string value that starts with the command: the raw line has `"sshpass`, and `decoded()` (`report.go:315-325`) prints a map as `map[text:sshpass ...]`. Both were missed in the probe. (2) Markdown inline code, `` `mysql -pX` ``, which is common in prose, trail files and transcripts that the dreamer reads through `harness.Redact`. (3) A full path, `/usr/bin/mysql -pX` (missed in the probe). (4) A literal `\n` before the name in raw text, the case the AGENTS.md rule names. A password typed into such a command reaches the feedback repository or the model provider. This is the BUG-110/BUG-127 failure class. The `-u` and `--user` part is not affected, because the flag always comes after a space. **Remediation:** for `sshpass`, drop the anchor; the word is distinctive. For the MySQL family, use `(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])`, which still spares `mkdir -p`. Add `{"text":"sshpass -p FAKEVALUE ssh h"}` (through the jsonl path), `` `mysql -pFAKEVALUE` `` and `/usr/bin/mysql -pFAKEVALUE` to `shapeSecrets`. Also check the older cookie rule's `(^|\s)(-b|--cookie)` (`report.go:138`) the same way. The same anchor is there, though `-b` normally comes after a space.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/report.go:151-152` — The brief named Docker credentials. The two new needles cover only `curl -u` and `config.json`'s double-quoted `"auth": "<base64>"`. These forms were missed in the probe:
  - `docker login -u user -p FAKEVALUE reg`. `-p` is matched only after `sshpass` or the MySQL clients; `--password` is caught by the existing flag rule.
  - `'auth': '…'` (single-quoted) and YAML `auth: <base64>`.
  - A Kubernetes `.dockerconfigjson: <base64 of the whole config>`. Its inner `"auth"` is never visible as text.

  (`"identitytoken"` and `--docker-password=` are already caught by `secret assignment`.) **Remediation:** this is a new kind, so it is the operator's design question under the BUG-110 rule. Proposed: a `docker login` line carrying `-p`/`--password` as one rule, and `["']?auth["']?\s*[:=]\s*["']?[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{8,}` together with `\.?dockerconfigjson` as the Docker-auth kind. Each needs a near-miss.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/report.go:151` — The `command-line credential` needle has documented gaps beyond finding 1. The probe confirmed each of these as unmatched:
  - `-u` and `--user` forms: the attached `curl -uadmin:FAKEVALUE`, the empty-user `curl -u :TOKEN`, and a digit-first user `curl -u 12345:FAKEVALUE`. The last is excluded on purpose to spare `docker run -u 1000:1000`, but numeric account IDs exist.
  - Other command-line credentials: `redis-cli -a PASS`, `smbclient -U user%PASS`, `htpasswd -b file user PASS`, and the `.npmrc` form `_auth = <base64>`.

  **Remediation:** this is a decision for the operator. Recommended: accept `-u` with the value attached; allow an empty user (`-u :x`); add the `redis-cli -a` and `.npmrc _auth` kinds. Add a near-miss for each.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/report.go:152` — The `credentials key` value alphabet `[A-Za-z0-9+=_.-]{16,}` leaves out `/`. A base64 credential with a `/` in its first 16 characters is not matched. That is about 22% of random base64 values; `credentials: abc/defFAKEVALUE0123456789` was missed in the probe. **Remediation:** allow `/` but refuse a value that starts with `/`, `~` or `./`, or ends in `.json`, so `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=/path` stays a near-miss. Add a slash-bearing shape to `shapeSecrets`.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/inventory.go:261` and `internal/harness/plan.go:156` — The Claude agent file is deployed verbatim (`a.Raw`), and the lint uses a deny-list. Two keys from Claude Code's documented subagent table (`.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-30-research-audit-fix-formats.md:12`) still pass:
  - `memory`: per Claude Code's sub-agents documentation, it enables Read, Write and Edit automatically, which widens an agent's `tools:` allowlist without showing it.
  - `initialPrompt`: it is auto-submitted as the first user turn under `claude --agent`. Text the operator never typed would then arrive as "the operator's own turn", which the global context treats as approval.

  I did not re-verify either effect against a live CLI. Antigravity is not exposed, because `DeriveAgy` (`derive.go:41-62`) writes only an allowlist of keys. **Remediation:** replace the deny-list with an allowlist of agent keys (`name`, `description`, `tools`, `disallowedTools`, `model`, `maxTurns`, `skills`, `effort`, `color`), so a future vendor key is refused by default. Failing that, add `memory` and `initialPrompt` to the refused set.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/dream/run.go:211-217` — Two gaps came with the process-group change:
  - **Ctrl-C:** `Setpgid` takes the CLI out of the terminal's foreground group, and neither `cmd/sh-agent` nor `internal/dream` handles signals (grep for `signal.` found nothing). Ctrl-C on an interactive `sh-agent dream` kills sh-agent but not the CLI. The CLI then runs on as an orphan with the operator's credentials, sending the prompt to the model, with no deadline.
  - **Normal exit:** when the CLI exits before the deadline while a helper (an MCP or language server) keeps the pipes open, `Cancel` is never called. The helper is never killed, and `Run` returns `exec.ErrWaitDelay` after 30 s, so a successful run is reported as a failure. `TestCallReturnsAtTheDeadlineDespiteAGrandchild` covers only the deadline path.

  **Remediation:** after `Run` returns, on every path, send `syscall.Kill(-pid, SIGKILL)` to the group. In `runDream`, use `signal.NotifyContext(SIGINT, SIGTERM)` to drive the same context. Add a test for the early-exit-with-helper case.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/report_test.go:184-197` — Two cases are over-redacted, which is safe, but neither is pinned in the over-redaction list as AGENTS.md requires: `mysql -P3306 -h db` (`(?i)` turns the port flag `-P` into a match) and `docker run -u node:node img`. In this repository's own trail, the three new needles match four lines (`.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-30-security-cb799ff-f1ca525.md:38`, `2026-09-30-security-f1ca525-e2cffc1.md:27`, `2026-10-09-review-project-merged.md:39`, `2026-10-09-security-project.md:25`). These are review records quoting `curl -u user:pass`; they are redacted out of dream prompts, which does no harm. **Remediation:** pin both over-redactions in the test.

## Checked
- **Secrets:** none found. I grepped the added lines of the diff for AWS, GitHub, Google API, Slack, OpenAI-style, PEM and password-assignment shapes; the test fixtures use `FAKEVALUE`. New error output: the strings printed by `IsUsage` are constant (`search.go:98-128`, six `usageError` sites, none echoing the user's value). `(*ctx).vendor` now prints the `NormalizeVendor` error on `c.out`. That error can carry a manifest's `vendor` value, which is not secret and was already printed before, on stderr.
- **Injection:** no new command, SQL or path construction. Dream skills are now read with `harness.Split` and `harness.Parse` (`collect.go:284-290`). Block scalars are folded with spaces, so a hostile `SKILL.md` cannot inject a newline or a fake heading into the dreamer's prompt, which the old key-line reader could not either. The skill file is still read with `Lstat` and regular files only (`collect.go:212-221`). There is no length cap (`Parse` rather than `ParseStrict`), and skills are dropped from the budget last (`collect.go:169`). That was already the case with the old single-line reader, so it is not a new finding.
- **Authz/authn and the lint:** `mcpServers` is refused in `LoadAgents` (`inventory.go:261`). Every install path reaches it: `harness.Plan` → `LoadInventory` → `LoadAgents` (`plan.go:76`). The `--from-zip` path goes through `installFiles` → `harness.Plan` (`main.go:797`), and `status` and `report` also call `LoadInventory`. Mutation check: with the key removed in the scratch copy, the test failed on both new rows; restored, it passed. `Lint` was removed, but every loader already called `ParseStrict` (`inventory.go:190,241,299`), and no other `Lint` caller exists, so no load path lost the lint.
- **Process-group kill:** `Cancel` runs only after a successful `Start`, so `cmd.Process` is never nil there. Linux does not hand out a PID that is still in use as a process-group ID, so `Kill(-pid)` reaches only the CLI's own group: the CLI and the descendants that stayed in it. sh-agent sits in its own group and is never hit. There is a microsecond window between the leader being reaped by `Process.Wait` and `Wait` reading the context result. In that window the kill still targets the original group, or returns ESRCH.
- **`search.IsUsage`:** it matches only the unexported `usageError` (`errors.As`), which only `validate` builds. A database or filesystem error cannot be classified as a usage error.
- **Crypto:** nothing in the diff hand-rolls a primitive or protocol. No finding.
- **Dependencies:** no change to `go.mod`. `/home/ostling-simon/.go/bin/govulncheck ./...`: 0 vulnerabilities the code calls, 0 in imported packages, and 1 in a required module that the code does not call (the known GO-2026-5024 in AGENTS.md; I did not re-list it in verbose mode). There is no npm ecosystem in scope.
- **GCP surface:** the diff touches no IAM, service account, deploy flag or Secret Manager.
- **Bug history:** `sh-agent search --refs <file> --kind bug` for report.go (BUG-110, BUG-127), inventory.go (BUG-143, BUG-036), run.go (BUG-166, BUG-169), collect.go (BUG-164, BUG-131), main.go (BUG-168, BUG-130) and search.go (BUG-168, BUG-125). Findings 1–4 are in the BUG-110/127 class.

## Not examined
- The other 34 files of the commit, beyond their stat line: delivery_test, usage_test, zip_test, the `internal/trail` and `internal/memory` changes, `internal/metrics` (claude.go, events.go), release.go, the `internal/search` export and reconcile changes, and the docs and skill line edits.
- Any live Claude Code run to confirm the `memory` and `initialPrompt` effects. Finding 5 relies on the vendor documentation.
- The pre-existing skill-body dynamic shell injection (`` !`cmd` `` in a `SKILL.md`), and whether the skill lint should refuse it. It is out of the diff.
- Whether `report` sends anything else that is JSON-shaped beyond feedback.jsonl, retros.jsonl, state.json and proposals. I read only `report.go:380-435`.
- `govulncheck -show verbose`, to name the one required-module advisory.

## Round 2

Range reviewed: the round-1 fixes, uncommitted in the working tree, `git diff 3bffdcf` (report.go, report_test.go, dream/run.go, run_test.go, cmd/sh-agent/main.go, usage_test.go, delivery.md, search.md, skills/harness-audit/SKILL.md).

### Status: COMPLETE

### Verdict: FINDINGS (low only)

Round-1 findings 1–4, 6 and 7 are fixed. Finding 5 (agent keys `memory` and `initialPrompt`; allowlist) is still open: the review record says the operator decides, and `inventory.go` did not change. I ran a probe against a scratch overlay: `.agents/scratch/sec-r2` holds `git archive 3bffdcf` with the nine changed files copied over, and the probe file was removed afterwards.
- Every round-1 shape that slipped through is now redacted: the `"text":` JSON line on the jsonl path, `{"cmd":["sshpass","-p",…]}`, the backtick, the full path, `-uadmin:x`, `-u :x`, `-u 12345:x`, `docker login -p`, single-quoted and YAML `auth:`, `.dockerconfigjson`, `_auth =`, `redis-cli -a`, `smbclient -U user%pw`, `htpasswd -b`, and `credentials: abc/def…`.
- The fixes introduced one regression: a short Docker `auth` value is now missed (R2-2).
- The process-group fix closes the Ctrl-C and clean-exit gaps. It leaves SIGHUP and one small signal-drop window (R2-3, R2-4).

### Findings
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/report.go:160` — **Regression.** The `auth key` rule needs 16 base64 characters, not counting the `=` padding, so a short Docker `auth` value that 3bffdcf's `"auth"…{8,}` caught now passes. Probe results:
  - `"auth": "YWRtaW46YWRtaW4="` (`admin:admin`): not matched.
  - `"auth": "YWRtaW46cHcx"` (`admin:pw1`): not matched.
  - `{"t":"{\"auth\":\"YWRtaW46YWRtaW4=\"}"}` on the jsonl path: not redacted.

  A weak default registry password is the likeliest one to be short. **Remediation:** keep the round-1 double-quoted JSON alternation `"auth"\s*:\s*"[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{8,}"` next to the 16-character rule for the other quotings (`"auth": "basic"`, at 5 characters, stays benign). Add the `admin:admin` shape to `shapeSecrets`.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/report.go:159` — The `-u` alternative now has nothing in front of it, so it matches inside any hyphenated word followed by `:` or `%`. It redacts 66 of 120,390 lines in this repository's trail and skills, against 4 at 3bffdcf. Examples:
  - `date -u +%FT%TZ`, a command the trail itself prescribes (`.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md:123`).
  - `anti-ui-slop/SKILL.md:3` (`.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-30-recon-audit-fix.md:81`).
  - `--unverified`:**, `X-User-Id:12345`, `https://…/my-url%20here`, `run-until:5`, `--user-agent:Mozilla`.

  The command alternative also matches any line that names mysql and later has a ` -a`/` -p` with a value (`mysql is down; ran ls -a /tmp`). All of this errs on the safe side and costs only dream inputs, but none of these cases is pinned on the over list. **Remediation:** put a non-word class in front of the flag only, `(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_-])(?:-u|--user|--username)`. Quotes, backticks and spaces still precede the flag there, and the command names keep no anchor. Leave `+` out of the user's first character. Pin `date -u +%FT%TZ` as benign.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/dream/run.go:226-227` — Only SIGINT and SIGTERM are forwarded. If the terminal closes or SSH drops during a hand-run `sh-agent dream`, SIGHUP kills sh-agent by default. The kernel sends SIGHUP only to the foreground group, which the CLI has left, and the shell does not know the CLI's group as a job. The CLI then runs on as an orphan with the operator's credentials and no deadline, which is the round-1 gap again by another signal. SIGQUIT and a SIGKILL or OOM kill of sh-agent leave the CLI running the same way. **Remediation:** add `syscall.SIGHUP` and `syscall.SIGQUIT` to `signal.Notify`. Optionally, on Linux, set `SysProcAttr.Pdeathsig` for the direct child. It fires when the creating OS thread exits, so it needs `runtime.LockOSThread` around `Start`, and it does not reach helpers.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/dream/run.go:239-241` — A signal that arrives after `close(waited)` and before `signal.Stop(sigs)` is buffered in `sigs` and never read. The Ctrl-C is swallowed, and sh-agent goes on to the next project. The window is microseconds. **Remediation:** call `signal.Stop(sigs)` first and then `close(waited)`. After that, drain `sigs` without blocking, and re-raise any signal found (kill the group, `signal.Reset`, `Kill(self)`).

### Checked
- **Kill reach after `Wait`** (`run.go:242`): `Kill(-pid)` runs after the leader is reaped. If helpers are still in the group, Linux allocates no new PID equal to a live process-group ID, so the kill reaches exactly those leftover helpers. If the group is empty, the call returns ESRCH. The only way to hit something else is the PID counter wrapping to exactly this value and the new process making itself a group leader, all within the microseconds between `Wait` returning and the kill. Even then only same-uid processes can be hit (EPERM otherwise). This is information, not a finding.
- **Kill reach on the signal path:** `killGroup` (the CLI's own group) and `Kill(os.Getpid(), sig)` (sh-agent itself). Nothing outside the dream job's children. A helper that called `setsid` is outside the group and survives, by design (the round-1 "left the group" test); WaitDelay only cuts its pipes.
- **Side effects of the signal path:** `signal.Reset` does not clobber any other handler; `signal.` appears nowhere else in `cmd/sh-agent`, `internal/dream` or `report.go`. dream.lock is a `flock` (`run.go:650`), so dying of the re-raised signal releases it.
- **The rest of the run.go fix:** `exec.ErrWaitDelay` is treated as success only after the deadline check, and Go returns it only for a zero exit status. The `Start` error path is equivalent to the old `Run`.
- **Declarations and references:** the needle renamed from `docker auth` to `auth key` has no other reference in Go or the living docs. `call`, `callWithin`, `killGrace` and `cliTimeout` are all still used (`run.go:130,188-189`). `installPassArgs` (`main.go:1113`) is called by update and by `runInstall`'s rebuild; forwarding an explicit `--vendor all` is correct, with no security effect. The fix introduces no new exported identifier.
- **Tests:** `go test ./internal/harness ./internal/dream ./cmd/sh-agent -run 'Redact|TestCall|InstallPass'` passed in the scratch overlay. The interrupt test drives a real SIGINT through a helper process, and it would fail without the handler: the default exit kills only the test binary.
- **Other surfaces:** the `skills/harness-audit/SKILL.md:36` govulncheck path and the `search.md:29` exit-status text are docs only, with no security effect. No secret shape appears in the added lines; the test shapes use `FAKEVALUE`.

### Not examined (round 2)
- The full test suite, `-race`, and the claim that removing the three needles fails 46 assertion lines; I ran only the targeted tests above.
- The "red before" claims for the new dream and usage tests.
- `usage_test.go` beyond its role as a caller of `installPassArgs`.
- The `delivery.md` sentence beyond the removed `mcpServers` mention.
- govulncheck was not re-run, since the fix changes no dependency.

title: Security review — project (2026-10-09)
body:
# Security review — project   (2026-10-09)

Range reviewed: the whole repository at HEAD (c267990), no diff.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

The worst problem: a harness agent file can still carry `mcpServers:`. Claude Code's subagent format documents that key (`.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-30-research-audit-fix-formats.md:12`), and the installer deploys the agent file byte for byte to `~/.claude/agents/` on every machine (`internal/harness/plan.go:156`). That gives a harness agent a way to start a process that the operator's permission mode never gates. The BUG-143 lint refuses only `hooks` and `permissionMode` for agents. The 2026-10-01 gate recorded this gap and left it open (`.agents/docs/changes/2026-10-01-1433-gate-lows-closed.md:18`), and it is still open at HEAD. The rest is low:
- the redaction test does not meet the project's own near-miss rule for every needle;
- a few credential kinds are not covered;
- the systemd unit text is not escaped against operator-supplied quotes and newlines;
- ADR-053's accepted residual risk is restated for the record.

The zip extraction, the release update, the SQL construction, the frontmatter line-grammar lint and the dream job's tool-free invocation held up in this reading.

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/inventory.go:261`: `permissionKey(front, "hooks", "permissionMode")` does not refuse `mcpServers`. An agent can declare an inline stdio MCP server, which is a command line that Claude Code starts when the agent is used. `plan.go:156` ships `a.Raw` unchanged. For Antigravity the risk is lower: `derive.go:47-50` writes only `model` and `tools`, so the key never reaches agy. Starting an MCP server is not a tool call, so the operator's permission mode never sees it. This is the confused-deputy shape BUG-143 closed for skills, reachable by anyone who lands a commit or a hostile zip in the harness tree, and then active on every place. The confidence is medium because whether Claude Code honours an inline `mcpServers` in a user-level agent file was not tested here (the 2026-10-01 review marked the same point low). Remediation: add `mcpServers` to the agent refusal list, and prefer an allow-list of the agent keys the harness uses (`name`, `description`, `tools`, `model`, `skills`, `color`, …) over a deny-list. Pin it with a row in `TestLintPermissionKeysByKind` that fails without the fix.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/report.go:97-100` against `internal/harness/report_test.go:161-176`: AGENTS.md requires "every needle gets a benign near-miss in `TestReportRedactShapes`". `bearer`, `authorization`, `url credentials` and most prefix needles (`AKIA`, `AIza`, `ghp_`, `glpat-`, `xoxb-`, …) have no benign near-miss. Only `ASIA` (as `ASIAN food`) and the regexp needles do. `bearer\s+\S` matches prose such as "the bearer of the token", so a whole line is dropped. That is the safe direction, but the behaviour is unpinned, so a later tightening of it is unreviewed. Remediation: add a benign near-miss per needle, with the over-redacting ones (`the bearer of`) pinned on the `over` list as `ASIAN food` is.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/report.go:59-140`: these credential kinds match no needle, and the same rules are what `sh-agent dream` uses before it sends text to a model provider (`internal/dream/collect.go:160`):
  - CLI credential flags: `curl -u user:pass`, `--user user:pass`, `mysql -p<pw>`, `sshpass -p`.
  - A JSON `"auth": "<base64 user:pass>"` key, the shape of Docker's `config.json`.
  - A `credential`/`credentials` key (`CREDENTIALS=…`).

  Each is a kind, not an instance. Under the project's BUG-110 rule they are a design question for the operator, not a batch to add here. Remediation: decide per kind; if accepted, add one rule per kind with a near-miss each.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/release.go:180-197`, `:349`: the release binary and the `SHA256SUMS` it is checked against come from the same release, fetched by the same `gh release download`. The check proves the download is whole and belongs to that release, not who made it (ADR-053, stated at `:26-31`). Anyone with write access to `kesokaj/styrman-harness` releases (the account or a `contents:write` token) can publish a higher `vX.Y.Z`. `sh-agent update` on every release place then installs it and executes it (`:144`). The same holds for a checkout place's `git pull` followed by `go build` (`repo.go:280`, `:308`). This is the accepted model, recorded so the residual risk is on file, not as a defect against the ADR. If the threat model changes, a vetted signature check is needed (`gh attestation verify`, or `ssh-keygen -Y verify` against an embedded allowed-signers file); never a hand-rolled one.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/dream/timer.go:86-99`: `renderSystemd` escapes `%` and `$` in the binary path, `--home` and PATH. It does not refuse or escape `"`, `\` or a newline. A newline in `--home` or in a PATH entry would add arbitrary directives, such as an extra `ExecStart`, to a user unit that runs nightly. A `"` ends the quoted word early. Every input belongs to the operator (their own `--home` argument and their shell's PATH), so this is self-inflicted unless something else sets PATH. Remediation: refuse control characters, `"` and `\` in all three before writing the unit, with a test per character.
- **[info]** `internal/harness/report.go:351-365`: `Collect` calls `Lstat` and then `os.ReadFile`. This is a small TOCTOU in which a file swapped for a link between the two calls is followed, and the read has no size cap. Both lie inside the operator's own `~/.config/sh-agent`, so there is no trust boundary. `ReadCapped` plus `O_NOFOLLOW` would make it uniform with the rest of the code.
- **[info]** `internal/dream/run.go:303-311`: on macOS the whole `~/Library/Keychains` folder is linked into agy's private HOME. Keychain item ACLs still apply per application. The child runs in plan mode with `request-review` and an empty allow list (`:316`), and any tool step voids the answer (`:228-231`). That is the same exposure as an interactive agy session. No finding.

## Checked
- **Secrets:** no credential in the tree was found in this reading. The installer refuses secret-shaped files in skills (`plan.go:120`, `secretShaped` at `:216`). The report's clone and push errors are scrubbed of URL credentials (`report.go:645-650`). Nothing in `cmd/` or `internal/` uses `log/slog` (grep: 0 calls), so there is no structured log of secrets. The dream job's private HOME and its database copies are 0600/0700 and swept after an hour (`run.go:377-398`).
- **Injection:** SQL is parameterised throughout. The only concatenations are constant table names (`reconcile.go:660`, `metrics/ingest.go:145`) and generated `?` lists (`search.go:77`). The SQLite DSN is escaped through `url.URL` against `?#%` pragma injection (`search/store.go:76`, `dream.go:40`). Release tags are validated before they reach argv (`release.go:86`). Every `git` call in the project root goes through `trail.Command` (prior review). The report refuses `GIT_DIR`-family redirects (`report.go:790`) and pushes to a constant URL.
- **Zip and update:** `update --from-zip` (`zip.go`) hashes and parses one buffer, so verify and unpack see the same bytes and there is no TOCTOU. Entries with `..`, absolute paths, backslashes or non-local names are refused, with depth and length bounds. Symlink and special entries are refused, writes use O_EXCL, sizes are counted by decompressing against per-file, total, entry and archive caps, and only the five trees are written. The release update has no downgrade or sideways move, the version marker binds the SUMS file, ambiguous hash lines are refused, the download goes to a random temp directory, and the binary is replaced by an atomic rename of the hashed bytes. `go build` runs with `GOTOOLCHAIN=local` (`repo.go:319`).
- **Authz (skill and agent lint):** `frontmatter.go` was read for flow maps, `<<` merge keys, `...` and `%` directives, BOMs, `key:value` without a space, tab-led and indented-first lines, and non-newline breaks. Each is refused or is not a top-level key to a YAML reader. Skills refuse `allowed-tools` and `hooks`, and symlinks inside skills are refused (`plan.go:108`). The agent gap is above.
- **Crypto:** only `crypto/sha256` as a checksum, plus `sha256` for a unit-name suffix. Nothing is hand-rolled.
- **Dependencies:** `go.mod` has `modernc.org/sqlite v1.46.1` and its indirect modules, as AGENTS.md permits. govulncheck is NOT on PATH (`which govulncheck` empty, no `~/go/bin`), so it was not run and the accepted-advisory list was not re-confirmed. There is no npm ecosystem. A vendored-skill grep for exfiltration and `| bash` found only catalog entries whose `curl | bash` lines `skills/google-catalog/catalog/MANIFEST.md:62-68` already flags.
- **GCP surface:** this repository deploys nothing to GCP and has no IAM bindings, service accounts or `--allow-unauthenticated`. Not applicable.
- **Dream:** the Claude call has no tools, `--strict-mcp-config`, `--setting-sources local` and no session persistence (`dream.go:181`). Every input is redacted before the prompt (`collect.go:131-134`, transcripts decoded before line redaction). Drafts are written to the proposals folder only and never installed. The lock is a non-blocking flock (`run.go:599-603`).
- **Memory:** the store must be gitignored before a write (`memory.go:131`), and writes are 0600.

## Not examined
- `internal/harness/pathguard.go` (the `--home` guard), `owned_unix.go`, `sweep.go`, `adopt.go`, `source.go`, and `apply.go` beyond its symlink checks.
- `internal/search/reconcile.go`'s `os.Root` use: the GO-2026-4970 Lstat guard was not re-verified. Also not read: `search/parse.go`, `export.go`, and `search/dream.go` beyond its DSN.
- `internal/metrics` readers (`agy.go`, `claude.go`, `ingest.go`) beyond the SQL grep, and the HTML report (`metrics/report.go`), where output escaping is unchecked.
- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` beyond the `--from-zip` wiring, and `report.go`'s `RemoveKeptClone` and `writeAndPush`.
- The release procedure: `skills/preflight/SKILL.md` and `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` § Releases were not read.
- Pins in `skills/VENDORED.md` were not verified (no `git archive` diff), and `go.sum` was not checked.
- govulncheck was not run (not installed).
- The launchd plist renderer beyond its XML escaping.
- No test file was read except parts of `report_test.go`.

title: Security review — v2.6.2-66f3412 (2026-10-09)
body:
# Security review — v2.6.2-66f3412   (2026-10-09)

Range reviewed: commits v2.6.2..66f3412 (git log v2.6.2..66f3412); the diff is git diff v2.6.2...66f3412.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

No finding is high or medium, so nothing here blocks the gate. The worst problem is low, a new dream signal-handling bug (finding 1). The two round-2 findings I raised in `reviews/2026-10-09-security-dbd776d-3bffdcf.md` on the redaction needles are fixed at `6cec23b`; a probe at 66f3412 confirms both. The two on the signal path are fixed as well.

Finding 1 sits in the new signal path in `internal/dream/run.go:227`. `signal.Notify` on SIGHUP or SIGINT re-enables a signal that the parent had set to ignored: `nohup` does this for SIGHUP, and a non-interactive shell's `cmd &` does it for SIGINT. On that signal the CLI's group is killed. `signal.Reset` then restores the inherited ignore (`runtime/signal_unix.go:160-163`, and `sigdisable` restores `fwdSig`), so the re-raised signal does nothing. sh-agent carries on, and the project that was running fails. No data or credential is exposed.

What remains is low and named below:
- **Two needle shapes still pass** (finding 2).
- **Private data on disk:** 23 copies of the operator's Antigravity conversation databases are still in a gitignored scratch directory (finding 3).
- **Two open items left to the operator by their word:** the agent-key allow-list and a `PRIVATE_KEY=` kind (finding 4).

I read all 57 release-diff paths; the trail markdown carries no credential, token, key, or instruction an agent would act on.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/dream/run.go:226-235` — **Notify re-enables a signal the parent ignored.** The goroutine kills the group (`:232`), then calls `signal.Reset(sig)` and `syscall.Kill(os.Getpid(), sig)` (`:234-235`).
  - **What goes wrong:** if sh-agent was started with SIGHUP or SIGINT ignored, `Reset` puts back `SIG_IGN`, so sh-agent does not die. Before this range the CLI shared sh-agent's ignored disposition and kept running. Now a hand-run `nohup sh-agent dream --all &` loses its in-flight project at logout and then continues with the next one.
  - **Not affected:** the systemd timer path.
  - **Impact:** an availability and correctness slip. Nothing leaves the machine.
  - **Fix:** do not register a signal for which `signal.Ignored(sig)` is true at the call. Add a test that starts the helper with SIGHUP ignored and asserts the CLI is not killed.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/report.go:159` — **two shapes still pass the command-line rule.** The `-u`/`--user` flag must now follow whitespace. In a probe at 66f3412, these went unredacted:
  - A quoted attached flag: `curl "-uadmin:FAKEVALUE" h`.
  - A JSON string that starts with the flag, on the jsonl path: `{"text":"-uadmin:FAKEVALUE"}`. The decoded map prints it after `text:`.

  The common forms are redacted: the split JSON array `["curl","-u","admin:…"]`, `["curl","-uadmin:…"]`, and the backtick form. **Fix:** put a `"`, `'` or backtick, or a `:` after a key, in front of the flag as well as whitespace (`(?:^|[\s"'`:])`). Add the two shapes to `shapeSecrets`. Both are rare, which is why this is low.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/testing/2026-10-09-verify-project.md:254` — **private conversation copies left in scratch.** The log records copying the operator's Antigravity conversation databases into scratch.
  - **What I found:** `.agents/scratch/verify-project/corpus/` still holds 23 `*.db` copies. They are mode 0600, dated 2026-10-09 17:17, and gitignored by `.gitignore:42`.
  - **The rule they break:** guide § 3e (in this diff) says the copies "are deleted after", and the log does not record a deletion.

title: Review — v2.6.2-13c5bde-code-docs (2026-10-12)
body:
# Review — v2.6.2-13c5bde-code-docs   (2026-10-12)

Range reviewed: v2.6.2..13c5bde plus the working-tree fixes of round 2

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS (round 2: all three round-1 findings fixed; three new low findings, below)

Nothing in the range is broken in a way that blocks a release. The worst issue is old, not added by this range, but it falls inside the range's own BUG-168 claim. `sh-agent update --vendor <bad>` still exits 1, not 2. On a checkout it also pulls before the vendor is checked, because `runUpdate` never calls `c.vendor()` and the vendor is first resolved in `installPassArgs`, after `harness.Pull`. The other two findings are narrow: a signal can be dropped in a small window in the dream CLI wrapper, and the new `-u` credential needle has a `\b`-style guard in front of it, which the project's needle rule forbids. gofmt and `go vet ./...` are clean. Targeted tests pass for dream (`TestCall*`, timer), harness (`TestReportRedact*`, `TestLint*`, `TestAgent*`) and cmd (`TestDeliverySpecCurrent`, usage). The docs lens found no stale restatement.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:709` and `:1086` (`installPassArgs` called from `runUpdate` and the checkout update path). An unknown `--vendor` on `update` is a usage error, but it still exits 1, and on a checkout it is caught only after `harness.Pull` (main.go:1080-1086). So a usage mistake moves the checkout and then refuses to install. Probe (`.agents/scratch/rv-1012b`): `sh-agent update --from-zip none.zip --vendor bogus` → `sh-agent: unknown vendor "bogus"…`, exit=1; `sh-agent diff --vendor bogus` → `sh-agent diff: unknown vendor…`, exit=2. BUG-168, fixed in this range, set out to make usage errors exit 2 (`(*ctx).vendor` now does), and delivery.md:77 says "usage errors exit 2". The checkout path was not probed by running it, because it would pull the real repository; it was read in the code. Fix: call `c.vendor()` at the top of `runUpdate`, before the dirty check, fetch and pull, and in `updateFromZip`'s caller. Add a usage test asserting exit 2 and an unmoved checkout. The behaviour predates the range; the range's BUG-168 claim is what leaves it uncovered.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/dream/run.go:235-253` (`callWithin`'s signal goroutine). If a signal lands in `sigs`, the 1-buffered channel, just as `cmd.Wait()` returns, and the goroutine has not been scheduled before `close(waited)`, both select cases are ready. Go then picks one at random, so a SIGTERM or SIGINT can be swallowed and `sh-agent dream --all` goes on to the next project. The comment at :249 covers a signal arriving after `signal.Stop` but before `close`, not this case. The window is narrow. Fix: in the `<-waited` case, do a non-blocking receive on `sigs` and handle any pending signal the same way.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/report.go:170` ("command-line credential" needle). The `-u`/`--user` branch is fronted by `(?:^|[^A-Za-z0-9_-])`, which works like `\b`: a letter or `_` right before `-u` hides the flag. In text mode (`Redact`, which serves `proposals/*.md`), the raw line `{"cmd":"curl https://x \\\n-u admin:s3cretpass"}` is NOT redacted. JSONL mode redacts it through `decoded` (probe `.agents/scratch/rv-1012a`: text=false, jsonl=true). The project AGENTS.md rule says "A needle matched against raw text has no `\b` in front — a literal `\n` or an underscore is a word character and hides the token". deploy/local.md:67 already lists text files' JSON escapes as a known gap, and the comment at report.go:150-153 records the operator's 2026-10-12 choice that a missed shape is a known limit. So this is low: the needle's front guard conflicts with the letter of the rule, but the miss is a documented gap. Fix if wanted: allow `\\[nrt]` as an extra left boundary, plus a near-miss pin.

## Criteria
1. **Dead code: pass.** `frontField`/`unquote` (dream) are removed and replaced by `harness.Split`/`Parse`. `search.IsBusy` and `harness.Lint` are removed. `LoadDocs`, `LatestRelease` and `memory.Refusal` are unexported. The `index`/`--rebuild` refusals removed from `search.validate` were confirmed unreachable: `index` is `positional: false` and has no `--refs/--open/--kind` flags, `search` has no `--rebuild` flag (main.go:183-194), and main.go:620-622 are the only callers of `Search`/`Index`. `restatement-grep` finds no living references to the removed symbols.
2. **Flow tracing: pass, with findings 1 and 2.** `ctx.vendor`, the search `usageError`→`IsUsage`→exit 2 path, `metricsSummary` (store closed by defer on every path), `installPassArgs`' new explicit-vendor pass-through and `trail.DocsRoot` were traced end to end. Dream's `callWithin` was traced too: process group, `Cancel`, `WaitDelay`, `ErrWaitDelay` only on a clean exit, and the group killed after Wait. The dream lock is `flock` on an `O_CLOEXEC` fd, so the self-kill re-raise leaves no stale lock. The new tests have must-fail shapes: grandchild deadline, a helper after a clean exit, interrupt, ignored signal, and `TestDeliverySpecCurrent` against the newest release entry.
3. **Standards conformance: pass.** gofmt and vet are clean. Restatements of the changed rules were checked:
   - The agent allow-list (ADR-056) appears in AGENTS.md § Rules and README.md:233.
   - The stub list's one home (ADR-057) is consistent across REQUIREMENTS.md, context/AGENTS.md and skills/init-project/SKILL.md:61. No living doc still says "R2 lists".
   - The timer's control-character refusal has no stale "line break" wording in living docs.
   - The README status row ("installed binary's build") matches main.go:946-960.
4. **Directory layout: pass.** `DocsRoot` is in `internal/trail`, the shared seam. `delivery_test.go` sits beside the verb table it reads.
5. **Simplicity (DIY-except-security): pass.** No new dependency. `readSmall` now uses `io.LimitReader`. No hand-rolled security primitive. The redaction regexps are pattern matching, not crypto.
6. **Decoupling: pass.** Three copies of the docs-root resolver were collapsed into `trail.DocsRoot`. Dream reuses the installer's frontmatter reader from `harness`, which it already imported, instead of a private parser.

## Docs lens
- `restatement-grep.sh` ran over `permissionMode`, `R2 lists`, the old timer wording, `LoadDocs` and `IsBusy`. Hits were only in plans, bugs and reviews (records) and in the code comments that state the new rule. No stale living copy.
- `git grep` at 13c5bde over the living set (README, AGENTS.md, REQUIREMENTS, context, agents, skills, specs, guide, deploy, `*_test.go`) found no old wording for: the stub-list home, the agent `hooks`/`permissionMode` list, the removed `--from-zip`/adopt messages, or `frontField`/`Lint(`/`LatestRelease`.
- `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md:77` still describes the agent permission lint as "`allowed-tools`, `hooks`, `permissionMode`, per kind". That is correct for v2.6.2, which the paragraph describes, but the release commit must restate it as the ADR-056 allow-list (plus `mcpServers`) when the tag moves. This is a release-gate note, not a finding against the range.
- search.md's exit-status row (limit, kind, modes, `--rebuild` to `search`, reason on stdout) matches main.go:617-628 and the flag table. dream.md step 4 (signals watched, an ignored INT/HUP left alone, a 30 s grace, the answer kept) matches run.go:212-262.
- Unverified: dream.md's claims about macOS/launchd behaviour, and Antigravity behaviour for agents carrying newly allow-listed keys (`disallowedTools`, `color`). `DeriveAgy` drops both, so `disallowedTools` does not restrict an agent on Antigravity. No agent sets either key today.

## Not examined
- New test bodies beyond their outlines and comments: `cmd/sh-agent/usage_test.go`, `zip_test.go`, `main_test.go`, `internal/harness/harness_test.go`, `report_test.go`, `internal/dream/run_test.go`, `timer_test.go`, `collect_test.go`, `internal/metrics/events_test.go`, `internal/trail/trail_test.go`. No mutation was run against them.
- The full `go test -race ./...` (excluded by the dispatch) and `govulncheck`.
- The diffs of `skills/review/SKILL.md` and `skills/harness-audit/*`, read only as diff lines.
- The trail records in range (reviews, testing logs, the recon plan, changes, handoffs), treated as records, not reviewed.
- A run of the checkout `update` path, not exercised (it would pull the real checkout).


## Round 2

Scope: `git diff HEAD` on 13c5bde (uncommitted): cmd/sh-agent/main.go, main_test.go, usage_test.go; internal/dream/run.go, run_test.go, timer.go, timer_test.go; internal/harness/report.go, report_test.go; deploy/local.md; BUG-171 record and INDEX row. gofmt clean; `go vet` clean on the three packages; `TestRelayKeepsASignalQueuedAtTheEnd`, `TestInstallTimerChecksTheHomeItself`, `TestReportRedactShapes`, `TestUpdateRefusesABadVendorFirst`, `TestUsageErrorsExit2`, `TestUpdateNeverInstallsDirtyTree` pass.

### Round-1 findings
1. **Finding 1 (update --vendor): fixed.** `run` now validates a non-empty `--vendor` through `c.vendor()` right after the home is made absolute (main.go:270-278). That is before the `--from-zip` dispatch and before any verb runs, so update, status, uninstall and report all exit 2 with the reason. `c.vendor()` with a non-empty flag only normalizes the value and reads no state. The remaining vendor error branches (`ctx.vendor`, `memoryCmd`, `installPassArgs`) are not dead code: they are still reachable when the home's recorded state holds an unknown vendor. `TestUpdateRefusesABadVendorFirst` can fail. With the old code, the checkout case pulls, so HEAD moves and the exit is 1; the dry-run case exits 0; the zip case exits 1. The fixture puts origin one commit ahead, which makes the "HEAD unmoved" assertion meaningful. `behind := advanceOrigin` keeps `TestUpdateNeverInstallsDirtyTree` unchanged in meaning, and the moved helper has both callers.
2. **Finding 2 (queued signal): fixed.** `relay` falls back to a non-blocking receive once `waited` closes, and `callWithin` waits on `relayed` before returning. The test runs 200 iterations with both cases ready: the old single `select` would fail on a coin flip. Its second half asserts that no signal means no call.
3. **Finding 3 (escaped break before `-u`): fixed.** `\\[nrt]` is an extra left boundary. A text-mode probe of `{"cmd":"curl https://x\\n-u admin:…"}` is now redacted (`.agents/scratch/rv-1012c`). There is a must-fail shape and a near-miss (`a literal \\n-u is the user flag`).

Security finding 3 (the timer home): fixed. The check now covers `bin+home+path`. The test's home `base/"x/..` passes the old check because Join cleans the quote out of `bin`, so the test can fail.

### New findings
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/report.go:178` (the new `mongo(?:sh)?|sqlcmd` client branch under `(?i)`). It over-redacts two common benign lines that no test pins, which breaks AGENTS.md: "over-redaction in the safe direction is pinned there" (`TestReportRedactShapes`). Probe `.agents/scratch/rv-1012c`:
  - `docker run --name mongo -p 27017:27017 -d mongo` is redacted, because `mongo` followed later by ` -p <port>` matches.
  - `sqlcmd -S srv -a 4096 -Q q` is redacted, because sqlcmd's `-a` is the packet size and `(?i)` also turns `-[pa]` into `-P`/`-A`.

  The direction is safe, but the rule requires each case pinned as accepted over-redaction, as `mysql -P3306` and `docker run -u 1000:1000` are at report_test.go:200. Fix: add both to that pinned list, or narrow the branch (e.g. require `mongo(?:sh)?` at a command position, or `sqlcmd` with `-P` only).
- **[low / confidence: medium]** Docs lens, stale since 6cec23b (in range, not caught in round 1): `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md:102` and `README.md:198` both say "`--vendor all` widens a single-vendor install to both through `install`; `update` keeps the recorded vendor instead". `installPassArgs` now forwards an explicit `--vendor all` to the install an update runs, and `TestInstallPassArgsForwardsAnExplicitVendor` "explicit all" pins it. So `update --vendor all` also widens. Only an update *without* `--vendor` keeps the recorded vendor. This round's fix edited local.md:102's sentence and left the clause standing. Fix: "`update` without `--vendor` keeps the recorded vendor; with one it passes it on, so `update --vendor all` widens too", in both files.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/dream/run.go` `callWithin`/`relay`: `onSignal` returns right after `syscall.Kill(os.Getpid(), sig)`, and the death that follows is asynchronous to the main goroutine. Now that `callWithin` waits on `relayed`, it returns and `dream --all` can start the next project's CLI, in its own group and so orphaned, in the moment before the process dies. The window is microseconds against a fork/exec, so this is unlikely. Fix if wanted: block after the self-kill (`select {}`), so `relayed` never closes on the signal path.

### Round 2 not examined
- No mutation run (source edits are out of my lane). Must-fail claims rest on reading the old code against each test.
- The full test suite, which the coordinator runs in the background.
- The BUG-171 record body beyond its INDEX row.
- The new `ldap`/`openssl`/`keytool`/`lftp` branches beyond the shapes and near-misses in the test and three probes (`ldapsearch -x -w` with no value stays; `-keypass` with no value stays; `openssl enc -pass pass:x` is redacted).
