title: Security review — dream over records
body:
# Security review — dream over records

owner: security
date: 2026-10-25

Range reviewed: 6348999..716cf85 -- internal/dream internal/brain/dream.go internal/brain/search.go (blast radius followed: brain store open/sync/load and trail.jsonl guards, the global import's feedback bodies, internal/redact, trail.Command/Log/Roots/Readable, search.ListProjects, retro skill's use of proposal records, SPEC-fyr-dream)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

The worst problem: what leaves the machine is NOT unchanged in kind. For a migrated project the dream now sends global `feedback` records' bodies, and the global import stores each feedback record's body as the raw `feedback.jsonl` line (`internal/brain/import.go:954`, `Body: l`). The old path ran every such line through `redact.RedactJSONL` before `scrub` precisely because a secret JSON-escaped on the line (`&sig=` marshalled as `&sig=`) does not match the raw-text needles (SPEC-fyr-dream § Hardening details); the new path (`internal/dream/collect.go:76`) only runs `scrub` (raw `redact.Redact`). Probe in `.agents/scratch/secprobe/main.go`: a marshalled feedback line holding `https://h.example/api?x=1&sig=AbCdEfGhIjKlMnOpQrSt123` comes back from `redact.Redact` byte-for-byte unchanged and from `redact.RedactJSONL` as `{"redacted":"[redacted by fyr]"}`. Second: `activity`'s `git log` skips the partial-clone guard every other object-reading git call uses. Scope isolation itself holds: records, memory and feedback are selected by the scope `trail.Roots` resolves (worktree registration checked), a planted `trail.jsonl` can only carry exported kinds into its own scope with `project=''`, retired memories are excluded (`status = 'closed'`), proposals are not read back into prompts, and labels are validated record IDs.

## Findings

- **[high / confidence: high]** `internal/dream/collect.go:76` (with `internal/brain/import.go:954`) — feedback records reach the prompt with raw-text redaction only. Imported feedback bodies are the verbatim JSONL line, so a secret behind a JSON escape (`&sig=…`, `\/`-escaped URLs, any needle a JSON escape splits) passes `scrub` and is sent to the model provider — the one data flow R3 permits, now weaker than the file path it replaced (`collect.go:291`, `RedactJSONL` first). Trigger: `fyr record import --global` of a `feedback.jsonl` holding a correction that quotes a SAS/Teams URL with `&sig=`, then `fyr dream --project <migrated root> --dry-run` — the prompt carries the signature. Remediation: run each feedback record's body through `redact.RedactJSONL` (as a line) before `add`, exactly as `feedback()` does, or redact at import/`record add` time too; better, make `scrub` the single place and give it the JSON-line pass for every input that is JSON. Test that fails without the fix: in `TestCollectReadsRecords` (or a new `TestCollectRedactsFeedbackRecordsAsJSON`), stub `forDream` to return a Feedback record whose Body is `json.Marshal` of a map holding `...?x=1&sig=AbCdEfGhIjKlMnOpQrSt123`, call `collect`, assert `AbCdEfGhIjKlMnOpQrSt123` is absent from `c.Prompt`.

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/dream/dream.go:160` — `activity` runs `trail.Command(p.Root, "log", "-1", "--format=%ct")` directly instead of `trail.Log`, so it skips `trail.Readable` (`internal/trail/trail.go:149-166`, the policy SPEC-fyr-dream names: "a partial clone is ... read only on a git of 2.44 or later"). On a git older than 2.44 (Apple's bundled git is 2.39) `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH` is ignored, and a checkout whose `.git/config` declares a promisor remote (`extensions.partialClone` or `remote.<r>.promisor=true`) with its HEAD commit object missing makes `git log -1` lazy-fetch through that repository's own config (remote URL, `core.sshCommand`, transport helpers) from the unattended nightly `--all` job. For a migrated project this is now the dream's only object-reading git call (the file path's `trail.Dates` went through the guarded `Log`), so the guard built for exactly this case is bypassed. Trigger: a dream target (file index or brain scope) whose `.git` is planted as above, `fyr dream --all` on git < 2.44. Remediation: `trail.Log(p.Root, "-1", "--format=%ct")` (adds Readable and `--no-show-signature`), treating its error as "no commit known". Test that fails without the fix: in `idle_test.go`, a repo with `git config extensions.partialClone origin` and trail's `lazyFetchSafe` forced false (expose a test hook, or wrap the call in a dream-level var); assert `activity` performs no `git log` (e.g. a `GIT_TRACE` file under the test dir stays free of `log -1`, or an injected command hook is never called).

- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `internal/dream/run.go:524` + `skills/retro/SKILL.md:59` — every dream proposal, project-target included, is now one global `proposal` record, and `/retro --harness` lists "every queued global `proposal` record" with no target filter (before: only `proposals/dream/harness/` reached it). Model-written text derived from project A's private trail now surfaces in the harness checkout's retro, whose records are committed and pushed with the harness; the target is only a body line (`Target: project`), not a field the list can filter on. The same paragraph also says a queued proposal's diff "is reused as drafted", while a dream proposal's must never be — the only discriminator is the `Dream —` title prefix, which any `fyr record add proposal` can also carry. Remediation: keep harness- and project-target dream proposals distinguishable by a field or a distinct title prefix the skill filters on (e.g. `Dream (harness) —`), and have `/retro --harness` list only harness-target ones; update `AGENTS.md` rule 1 (still says harness-target proposals wait under `~/.config/fyr/proposals/dream/harness/`) per rule 3. Test: a `write()` test with one project- and one harness-target proposal asserting the two records are distinguishable by the attribute the skill filters on.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/brain/dream.go:91` + `internal/brain/export.go:257` — `updated` from a checkout's `trail.jsonl` is only checked to parse as RFC 3339: a future value (clock skew on a teammate's box, or planted) makes `in.Last` future, so `activity` reports "in use" every night and the project is never dreamt under `--all`; a non-`Z` offset breaks the string comparisons `updated > ?` and `max(updated)` (records skipped or re-sent). Remediation: normalize `updated` to UTC `Z` on load and clamp `Last` (and the `updated > since` window) to `now`. Test: load a trail.jsonl with `"updated":"2099-01-01T00:00:00Z"` and assert `activity(...)` returns "" a day after the last commit.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/brain/dream.go:12-21`, `:51` — `fyr dream --dry-run` now opens the real `brain.db` read-write: `Scopes` and `ForDream` go through `openStore` (MkdirAll, migrate), and `openForSearch`'s `sync` loads (writes) a changed `trail.jsonl` into the store, creating `brain.db` when it is absent and a target has a trail. `ListProjects` reads a copy for exactly this reason ("a dry run must leave the directory as it was"); SPEC-fyr-dream says a project with no proposals "creates no brain store". Remediation: a read-only open (or a copy, as `ListProjects`) under `--dry-run`, and no `sync` from the dream's reads. Test: `Run` with `DryRun` on a scratch home with no `brain.db` and a migrated target; assert `brain.db` still does not exist.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/dream/dream.go:133-141` — `targets` dedups by the literal root string, while records are keyed by the `trail.Roots` main root: a project the file index registered under a linked-worktree or symlinked path and its brain scope are two targets, so the same records are sent twice a night and two proposal sets stored. Remediation: dedup on `trail.Roots(root)`'s main root. Test: a project registered as its worktree path plus its scope; assert one collect.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/dream/run.go:524-533` — proposals are stored one `Add` at a time; a failure after the first leaves earlier records stored while the watermark does not advance, so the next run stores them again (duplicate queued proposals for `/retro`). Remediation: one transaction for the project's proposals, or advance-on-partial with the stored IDs logged. Test: a `propose` stub failing on the second call, then a second run; assert no duplicate titles.

## Checked
- Secrets: none in the diff; redaction of new inputs checked per kind — memory/trail record text goes through `scrub` (collect.go:150); feedback records do not get the JSON-line pass (finding 1); labels are validated record IDs; proposal title/body pass `o.line`/`o.clean` (scrub) and `normalize`.
- Injection: all SQL in brain/dream.go parameterized; model text in proposals indented, one-line fields folded; prompt fences unchanged (`block`); proposal records are not read back into prompts (kind filter in ForDream).
- Authz / scope isolation: ForDream selects by the `trail.Roots` scope (linked-worktree registration verified, trail.go:252-265); global feedback only `project = scope`; `loadLocked` refuses unexported kinds and inserts `project=''` into the own scope only; `guardExportPath` refuses a symlinked `.agents` or `trail.jsonl` (an Lstat `migrated()` true on a link ends in that refusal, a failed project, not a read). Propose opens a global session, writes only `brain.db` under the home; drafts stay under `proposals/dream/drafts/` with kebab names.
- Git: `activity`'s call goes through `trail.Command` (fsmonitor off, showSignature off, no lock) but not `Readable` (finding 2); `canonicalProject`/`Roots` use `rev-parse` only.
- Crypto: none touched.
- Dependencies: go.mod/go.sum unchanged in the range. govulncheck ran under the shell's go1.24.4 (not the operator's go1.27.2): 15 standard-library advisories reached (toolchain age, e.g. GO-2025-3849 database/sql fixed in 1.24.6), none introduced by this diff; npm not applicable.
- GCP surface: none touched.

## Not examined
- `internal/search/dream.go` `AgyConversationText` beyond its call sites (unchanged; read as before).
- Test files in the range (`collect_test.go`, `idle_test.go`, `run_test.go`) beyond the diff stat; the tests proposed above were not run.
- The feedback-log skill's own `fyr record add feedback` body format (whether non-imported feedback records are JSON too).
- `brain.normalize`, `cleanTitle`, `readBody` internals (relied on their doc comments).
- `internal/brain/search.go` Refs/naming changes beyond reading the diff (search ranking, no data-egress path).
- No `fyr dream --dry-run` was run end to end in a scratch home; finding 1 was verified with a redaction probe only.
- Observation, not a finding of this review: `.agents/trail.jsonl` in the working tree was modified at 17:23:43 (the `PLAN-2026-10-25-sqlite-trail` line) by another process during this review; this review did not touch it.

## Outcome

Each fix has a test that failed with the fix mutated out (main thread, 2026-10-25), except finding 2's, whose guard is tested where it lives.

| # | Finding | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | feedback records redacted as raw text only | FIXED: `redactFeedback` compacts a feedback record's body to one line and runs `redact.RedactJSONL`, as the log's lines are; `TestFeedbackRecordsAreRedactedAsJSON` (the probe's `json.Marshal` shape, `&sig=AbCd…` as `&`; fails with the raw path) |
| 2 | `activity` bypassed the partial-clone guard | FIXED: the commit is read through `trail.Log`, whose refusal on a git older than 2.44 is pinned by `TestPartialCloneIsReadOnlyOnANewGit` in `internal/trail`; no dream-level hook was added, since it would test the indirection, not the guard |
| 3 | project-target proposals listed by `/retro --harness` | FIXED: the title leads with the target (`Dream, project —` / `Dream, harness —`); `/retro` takes its project's `Dream, project` ones, `--harness` everything else; `TestRunWritesProposalsDraftsAndState` asserts both titles; AGENTS.md rule 1 already named records (716cf85) |
| 4 | future or offset `updated` | FIXED: `ForDream` compares parsed times, never text, and a record dated after now never makes a project in use; `TestFutureRecordIsNotUse` |
| 5 | dry run writes the brain store | FIXED: a dry run reads a copy (`brainCopy`: `search.CopyDB` into `~/.config/fyr/dream-brain-*`, swept by `removeCopies`, or the system temp directory when there is no store); `TestDryRunLeavesTheBrainStore` (no store created; an existing one byte-identical; no copy left) |
| 6 | one checkout counted twice | FIXED: targets are keyed by the main worktree root (`projectKey`, links resolved); `TestTargetsDedupeOneCheckout` |
| 7 | proposals stored one at a time | FIXED: `brain.ProposeAll` stores a project's proposals in one transaction, each checked by `checkRecord` first; `TestProposalsStoredTogether` (an oversize second body stores neither) |

title: Review — cold read of the metrics-at-checkpoints plan
body:
# Review — plan-metrics-checkpoints (cold-reader check)   (2026-10-25)

Range reviewed: `.agents/scratch/plan-metrics-checkpoints.md` (identical to record PLAN-2026-10-25-1754-plan-metrics-fed-at-every-checkpoint-joined-to-r), plus the code surfaces it names: `internal/metrics/{events,store,agy,show,writer,verb}.go`, `internal/brain/{dream,search,import,brain,record}.go`, `internal/dream/metrics.go`, `skills/{handoff,retro,feedback-log}/SKILL.md`, `context/AGENTS.md`, `.agents/kit/kit-preamble.sh`, `REQUIREMENTS.md` R3.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

Worst first: E2E criterion 1 cannot pass as written, because D2 puts the ingest BEFORE the handoff is stored, `fyr metrics show` never ingests (only the `ingest` verb at `cmd/fyr/main.go:551` and the dream at `internal/dream/metrics.go:25` do), and the criterion forbids a hand-run ingest, so `dod_closed` stays 0 of 1. E2E criterion 2 contradicts S1 (a migrated project's sessions are meant to gain events). The A4 bug join reads a hex run in the bug record body, but the import keeps only the title and prevention rule of a closed bug (`internal/brain/import.go:442-454`), so escaped bugs stay zero for imported bugs. Several interface contradictions (feedback on an unmigrated project, gone roots, `/retro --dry-run` writing the store) would make two implementers build different things.

## Findings

### (1) Gaps

- **[high / confidence: high]** plan:129 (E2E 1) with plan:105, :174 (D2) — The golden path cannot hold. The handoff skill ingests, THEN stores the handoff (D2: "the session's own handoff is joined by the next ingest"). Criterion 1 requires `dod_closed` closed 1 of 1 "with no `fyr metrics ingest` run by hand". A1 needs a handoff event in the session's window (`SPEC-fyr-metrics` A1); the handoff record does not exist when the only ingest runs; `show` does not ingest. Decide: ingest again after the store (then D2's "failed ingest recorded in the trail" is lost), or the criterion permits one ingest after the handoff, or `dod_closed` is expected 0 of 1 until the next checkpoint (then say so and test a different thing).
- **[high / confidence: high]** plan:130 (E2E 2) vs plan:13, :138 — "the count of handoff, verifier and review events per session does not rise for any session that existed before" contradicts S1: this repo is migrated and its records (HANDOFF-2026-10-25-1742, REVIEW-2026-10-25-1719, TEST-2026-10-25-1738) fall in the windows of the copy's historical sessions, so the new binary ADDS events for them by design. The criterion should pin "no duplicate of an event the old binary stored under a file name" (a project that has both: an unmigrated checkout copy), not "does not rise". As worded it fails on the intended behaviour, or passes only on a fixture that never exercises S1. It also names a way (two binaries on one copy) rather than the outcome.
- **[high / confidence: high]** plan:77, :74 (A4 over records) vs `internal/brain/import.go:442-454` — For a bug that is not open, the import rewrites the body to `# BUG-NNN: title` plus the Prevention section; the file's commit hex runs are discarded. `joinEvents` looking for a hex run in the body finds nothing for every imported closed bug, so A4 (escaped bugs) over records is zero for exactly the backlog the plan is meant to repair; only bugs filed by `fyr record add bug` after the migration can carry a sha. The plan asserts "(as today)" without checking the import. Decide: where the sha lives (a body convention the bug skill must write; a different source), and say A4 history is lost for imported bugs. Also `bugFile` records have no `date` minute, and the `ts` rule "record's `date` at 00:00 local" is only a stored stamp (placement is by the commit), so say that.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** plan:57-58, :65 — `ForMetrics` contract says an unmigrated checkout returns "Migrated false and nothing else", but the join rule says corrections are read from every global feedback record about root PLUS `feedback.jsonl`, for a home "not yet imported". After `fyr record import --global` the home holds feedback records and (per the Why) no file; the project may still be unmigrated (no `trail.jsonl`) — then `Feedback` is empty by contract and A5 is zero, the very blindness Why #1 names. `openForSearch` (`internal/brain/search.go:105-140`) does return an open store when `brain.db` exists without a `trail.jsonl`, so reading the feedback is possible; the plan must say it is read for an unmigrated project too, and then `Migrated` false with `Feedback` set contradicts "nothing else".
- **[medium / confidence: high]** plan:62-63, :33 — Gone project root. `joinEvents` today counts file-log corrections BEFORE the `os.Stat(root)` check (`events.go:100-105` then `:106-109`), so corrections of a vanished checkout still count. `ForMetrics(home, root)` goes through `trail.Roots(o.Dir)` (`brain/search.go:107`) and, with a gone directory and no `Global`, returns `nil, "", nil` (`:109-111`): the record-based corrections of a gone root would be silently dropped, and the plan does not say whether ForMetrics is called before or after the stat. Decide the order and the root-gone result.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** plan:151-153, `skills/retro/SKILL.md:15, :98` — `/retro --dry-run` is "analysis only … nothing written". Step 11 would run `fyr metrics ingest` first, a write to `metrics.db` (and, via the file-wins load, to `brain.db`, A2). The plan gives no dry-run branch; `review-standards` § 8 requires a read-only mode to keep new side effects below its early return, with a test. Decide: skip the ingest in `--dry-run` (and say the numbers may be stale), or declare it an allowed write.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** plan:81, :86-88 (migration 3) vs `internal/brain/import.go:314-321` — The migration computes `lower(stem)`, but the import ID is `slugOf(stem)`: every run of characters outside `[a-z0-9._-]` becomes `-`, leading/trailing `-._` are trimmed, the slug is cut at 120 bytes, and a collision adds `-N`. A file with a space, `+`, uppercase-with-symbol, trailing `.` or a long name rewrites to an ID the import never gives, so the "no duplicates after migration" promise (S2, D5) fails for those; and Phase 1's A1 check ("`<PREFIX>-` + the lowercased stem — expect: the rule matches") will find it does NOT match as written. Decide: accept the residual (say which names), or make the migration/ref function the same `slugOf` (Go, not SQL) and note SQL can't express it.
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** plan:67 — "record time … read in the machine's local zone". A record's ID minute is the local time of whoever added it (`brain.go:258`, `time.Now()`), and a `trail.jsonl` pulled from git is written on another machine (the plan's own Trust section, :119). Across zones the minute lands hours off, in the wrong session's window; a DST fold/gap has no decision either. Also the minute is unvalidated: `HANDOFF-2026-09-03-2459-…` or a slug starting `…-2024-…` parses as a time. Decide the zone rule (or accept and name the error), and the HHMM validity check. (Imported feedback IDs carry the line's own offset, `import.go:953`, so FEEDBACK IDs differ again; the plan correctly reads the body `ts` for those.)
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** plan:72, :178 (D6) — A2 now counts every `testing` record with a `## Status:` heading. The plan itself stores Antigravity matrix results and verifier logs as `testing` records (:153-154, "stored as a `testing` record"); a behavioural-run record with a Status line becomes a `verifier` event in the session whose window covers it, inflating A2 and changing the spec's definition (`SPEC-fyr-metrics` A2 is the `*-verify-*` log). D6 states the divergence for the filename filter only, not this effect. Decide whether the spec's A2 changes for migrated projects only (then the same session's verifier counts differ across the migration), or a title/kind marker narrows it.
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** plan:96-101 — Under-specified `recordRead`: (a) "the first command segment whose program is `fyr`, or `go run ./cmd/fyr`" — does `./.agents/scratch/fyr-bin`, `$HOME/.local/bin/fyr`, `env FOO=1 fyr`, or a global flag before the verb (`fyr --home X record get`) count? The kit's wrapper puts `--home` AFTER the verb (`kit-preamble.sh:248`), which is the only shape tested; (b) `Verb` returns a verb string, not words — `recordRead` needs the tokenizer's segments (`verb.go:107` `segments(stripHeredocs(cmd))`), so say it takes the words of each segment and which function supplies them; (c) "first ID word" after `get`: `fyr record get --global X`, `fyr record get -h`, flags before the ID. (d) show.go:461 counts "first three steps with a kind", not "first three Reads"; plan:101 reads "a main session's first three steps that are a Read with a target_kind, or a Bash with a non-empty target_kind" — those are different counts (the current loop skips steps without a kind and counts the first three that have one); state which, the fixture at :146 only fits the second.
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** plan:98, :146 — Phase 2's expect `fyr record get FOO-1` → `record`: the prefix table lists 13 prefixes but `prefixes` (`brain/record.go:28-33`) also has `FEEDBACK`, `PROPOSAL` (global-only), and a `GUIDE-` ID has an extra case (`GUIDE-…` vs kind `guide`). Say whether FEEDBACK/PROPOSAL are in the vocabulary; `target_kind` is then a closed set and `show`'s `first_reads` keys must accept `list`/`record` (is that key set validated anywhere? Not read).
- **[low / confidence: medium]** plan:33, :48, :63 — "the D16 test", "D21 of the brain plan", "the file wins", "`openForSearch`" are cited without the plan or file that defines them (D-rows of `PLAN-2026-10-25-sqlite-trail`). `Migrated` for a linked worktree: the session root is `trail.Toplevel(root)` (a worktree) while the scope is the main worktree (`Record.Scope`, `record.go:15`; `ForDream` filters by `project = scope`), and the plan says "feedback … whose project is root". State which of root / scope is used for each filter.
- **[low / confidence: high]** plan:134-165 — The name `A1`–`A5` is used for two different things: the spec's metrics (A1 DoD, A5 corrections; plan:7, :74-75) and Risks assumptions A1–A4 (plan:137, :150, :165-168). "Check assumption A1 (Risks)" is the only disambiguator. Also `E2E`, `kit`, `Open:`, `1 of 1` (`Closed` shape) are used undefined; `--all-labels --project <clone>` (plan:129) are real flags (`cmd/fyr/metrics_test.go:169-177`), `verifier.PASS` key was not verified against `show --json`.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** plan:137, :165 — Assumption A1 ("verify … the import's ID function") is stated as checked in Risks but is the first task of Phase 1 (unticked); migration 3 shape and Phase 1's `TestMigration3` fixture (`x.md`, `HANDOFF-x`) assume it holds. I checked it: it does not hold exactly (see the slug finding above), so the checkbox's "else a D-row changes migration 3" branch is already taken.

### (2) Scope — what the plan builds that `## Why` did not ask for

The Why names two gaps: the blind join on a migrated project, and nothing feeding the store at a checkpoint. Items not traceable to either with a D-row "by: operator":
- **C3 / S3 (first reads via `fyr record get|list`)** — named in the Why's gap 1 (last sentence) but no D-row says the operator asked for it; all D-rows are `by: implementer`. It is the larger `agy.go`/`show.go`/transcript-parsing surface and the only new input-parsing of command lines (security review due). Gap unless approved.
- **S2's forward migration** and the ID-form `ref` for BOTH joins, a second shape for the same operation: the file join keeps running for unmigrated projects but now emits record-style IDs (`HANDOFF-…` from `x.md`). The simpler alternative — leave file-join refs alone and key the records join to the same name — is not weighed. D5 states the choice; none says the operator asked.
- **D7 dual corrections (record + `feedback.jsonl`, dedup by `ts` string)** — a second source and a dedup rule for a window (a home between `import --global` and the next feedback write) the operator may not care about; also `ts` string equality across `Z` vs `+00:00` forms is not addressed.
- **D6 (A2 on every testing record)** is a metric-definition change nobody asked for (see the finding above).
- Cost-free, accepted: the retro and handoff skill edits (S4) are the request.
Each is a gap unless the operator's approval of this plan is the D-row (the Open line at :181 says that is the default; say it for each).

### (3) Readiness — questions an implementer would have to ask

1. BLOCKING — E2E 1: where does the ingest that sees the handoff run? (finding 1)
2. BLOCKING — E2E 2: what exactly must not rise, given S1 adds events? (finding 2)
3. BLOCKING — A4 over records: where does the commit sha come from for imported closed bugs? (finding 3)
4. BLOCKING — Feedback for an unmigrated project in a home that was imported: read or not? Does `Migrated` false really return no `Feedback`? (finding 4)
5. BLOCKING — `/retro --dry-run`: does Step 11 ingest? (finding on dry run)
6. BLOCKING — Migration 3 against `slugOf`: SQL `lower(stem)` or Go-side rewrite; what happens to non-matching names? (slug finding)
7. NON-BLOCKING — Gone root: ForMetrics before or after `os.Stat(root)`? Default implied: after, like the commits; but corrections of a gone root then regress; an implementer would choose to keep the file-log path for it.
8. NON-BLOCKING — Zone/HHMM validity (local zone is stated; validity is a decision an implementer makes alone, but cross-machine error should be named).
9. NON-BLOCKING — recordRead program shapes (`fyr-bin`, global flag before verb) — decided by an implementer; the fixture list at :145 pins the happy shapes.
10. NON-BLOCKING — "first three steps" vs "first three reads with a kind" in `show` (the fixture at :146 pins it).
11. NON-BLOCKING — FEEDBACK/PROPOSAL in the `get` vocabulary.
12. NON-BLOCKING — D6's A2 inflation by Antigravity-run testing records.
13. NON-BLOCKING — The summary line wording the handoff copies into Environment State (what `Result.Line()` prints is in `internal/metrics/ingest.go`, not read here).

### (4) Sizing — could a fresh session finish and verify each phase from the plan alone?

- **Phase 1** — No. It holds four code surfaces (`ForMetrics`, the join, migration 3, the shared ref) and a spec edit; its expectations depend on unresolved items 3, 4, 6 above, and its checkpoint carries E2E 2, which as written cannot be evaluated (finding 2). Split the migration + ref rule from the records join, or resolve the findings first.
- **Phase 2** — Yes, once the "first three" semantics (Q10) and the program shapes (Q9) are fixed; self-contained and testable from fixtures.
- **Phase 3** — Not as written: E2E 1 cannot pass (finding 1), and the checkpoint requires it. The Antigravity rows depend on the kit (`GUIDE-testing` § 4, not read here), so a fresh session needs the kit's row syntax from that guide; the plan cites it, which is enough once finding 1 is resolved. A3 (timing a 24 MB store + 17 MB directory) is cheap and well specified.
- Docs clauses: spec, skills, guides and the context are named; `fyr metrics` help text/`README` § How it works were not checked for a restatement of "ingest runs only inside the dream or by hand" (plan:8), which becomes false; grep `ingest` in README, `SPEC-fyr-delivery`, `DEPLOY-*`, `skills/retro`, `skills/dream` for it. (Not run.)

## Criteria

1. Dead code — n/a for a plan. Migration 3's `DELETE` after `UPDATE OR IGNORE` is correct only when the rewritten key equals the key the join writes (slug finding).
2. Flow tracing — fail: E2E 1 (ingest order), the feedback path (ForMetrics contract vs join rule), gone-root ordering.
3. Standards conformance — fail: `review-standards` § 8 read-only mode (`/retro --dry-run`); a changed claim ("ingest runs only inside the dream or by hand", plan:8) has restatements not listed; R0/R3/R4/R6/R7 cited and R3's "writes only under `~/.config/fyr/`" is respected (the ingest writes `metrics.db`, and `brain.db` for the file-wins load).
4. Directory layout — pass: new code lands in `internal/brain/dream.go`, `internal/metrics/*`; no new files named.
5. Simplicity — mixed: two ref shapes and a dual correction source (D5, D7) buy migration-window cases; the doc does not show who asked. No auth/crypto/hand-rolled primitive.
6. Decoupling — pass: `brain` does not import `metrics` (rejected inline in the plan); `ForMetrics` returns data only.

## Not examined

`internal/metrics/ingest.go` (`Result.Line`), `internal/metrics/show.go` outside lines 440-490 (the `Closed`/`first_reads` JSON shapes), `search.KindOf`, the kit's row syntax in `GUIDE-testing` § 4 and `GUIDE-skill-matrix`, `SPEC-fyr-record` § Import, README/other restatements of "ingest only in the dream", `REQUIREMENTS.md` R0/R4/R6/R7 text beyond R3 and the R4 heading, `skills/handoff/SKILL.md` outside lines 140-160, whether the timing assumption A3 holds. No mutation or run of any test. Tool-call budget (30) was spent on reading; no prior bug records were searched (`fyr search --refs` not run for the plan's surfaces; BUG-179 forbids fyr without `--home` and the search was not needed for a plan).

Answered in the plan (PLAN-2026-10-25-1754-plan-metrics-fed-at-every-checkpoint-joined-to-r), 2026-10-25, by the main thread; checked against the code before answering (`internal/brain/import.go:313-321` slugOf, `:442-454` closed-bug trim):

# Review — 811442c-33c652a-code-docs   (2026-10-25)

Range reviewed: 811442c..33c652a (git log 811442c..33c652a; git diff 811442c...33c652a), repo /home/kesokaj/workspace/styrman-harness, branch main. Code lens and docs lens in one dispatch.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing in the range breaks a REQUIREMENTS.md rule or reintroduces a recorded bug. `go vet`, `gofmt -l` and `go test -count=1 ./internal/metrics ./internal/brain` pass on the tree at 33c652a, and so do the harness lint and size tests I ran. The join, the ref rewrite and `recordRead` hold up on reading: ref rewrites are idempotent, a record read failure keeps the stored events, and only a closed set of kind names leaves `recordRead` (R4). Two low-severity nits follow, neither blocking.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/metrics/events.go:96-101` (with `store.go:74`, `search/store.go:72-79`) — `joinEvents` begins a deferred transaction whose first statement is now a SELECT (`rewriteFileRefs`, then `rewriteCorrectionRefs`); before this range the first statement was the `put` INSERT. The DSN has no `_txlock=immediate`. If another ingest (the nightly dream, or a second session's handoff ingest, which this range makes routine) commits between that read and the first write, SQLite returns SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT at once and the 10 s busy timeout is not used. The ingest then exits 1 with "database is locked". The next run recovers because the join is idempotent, so this is a spurious failure, not data loss. Fix: begin the join with a write (open the tx `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, or run the two rewrites after a no-op write), and add a test with two connections if the race can be made to occur. I did not reproduce it.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/feature/SKILL.md:107` and `rules/session-sizing.md:8` — both restate the phase-end sequence ("`change` record, commit, push, then the handoff", "That is the checkpoint"). The context's phase-end line (`context/AGENTS.md:11`) now adds `fyr metrics ingest` after push, and these two copies were left unchanged (review-standards § 7: every restatement of a changed rule is changed with it). The sequences do not contradict, because the handoff's last call is the ingest (`skills/handoff/SKILL.md:178`). But the context line puts the ingest before the handoff and the handoff runs it again, so a phase end ingests twice, and `feature` still says the checkpoint has no ingest. Fix: name the ingest in both copies, or drop it from the context's phase-end line and leave it to the handoff.

## Docs lens

Compared with README.md, `SPEC-fyr-metrics` (new C3, A2-A5, "One reference per trail item", "When ingest runs", the failure rows), `GUIDE-testing` § 3g, `GUIDE-skill-matrix` (handoff, retro and the new metrics-feed row), `skills/handoff`, `skills/retro`, `cmd/fyr/main.go` usage and `.agents/kit/agy-rel/run.sh`. The restatement-grep on "metrics ingest" listed README.md:49, context/AGENTS.md:11, cmd/fyr/main.go (usage), and the two skills. All agree with the code, apart from the nit above.

- stale test: none found. The assertions changed in `events_test.go` trace to the ref and ID change in `events.go`.
- dropped: none. The retro skill's old "No metrics store yet (`fyr metrics ingest` never ran)" is replaced, not lost (`skills/retro/SKILL.md:57`).
- narrowed: none.
- Known limit the spec states and that is not a finding: an old file named `HANDOFF-x.md` keeps its file-name ref (`events.go` `rewriteFileRefs`, SPEC "One reference per trail item"); a `-N` collision suffix is not reproduced.
- The retro row of `GUIDE-skill-matrix` changed beyond the metrics feed: it was rewritten from the files check to a record check. That is consistent with the trail being records (R7). I did not run it.
- Unverified: the kit runs ("kit 3 of 3 PASS, must-fail FAIL"), the "12 of 12 mutations caught" claim, the E2E runs, the measured 0.2 s ingest. I did not read `TEST-2026-10-25-1943` or the four `change` records. I did not check that `.agents/trail.jsonl` matches the store.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. `ImportedID`, `KindOfID`, `refKinds`, `findings`, `rekey`, `programAt` and `ForMetrics` each have callers. The `read` closure in `ForDream` is now a one-line wrapper over `store.records`, which is harmless.
2. Flow tracing — pass with the nit in finding 1. Callers are traced from `ingest` through `joinEvents`, `ForMetrics`, `joinRecords` and the ref rewrites. A migrated project never also reads files, a records read error keeps the stored events, and `rekey` deletes the old row only when the update changed nothing. The new tests can fail: the fixture sets a non-UTC `time.Local`, and `TestJoinRecordsBrokenTrail` and `TestCorrections` cover the error and the gone, unmigrated and migrated cases.
3. Standards conformance — pass, except the restatement nit (finding 2). The comments and the spec rows I read match the code.
4. Directory layout — pass. New code sits in `internal/metrics` and `internal/brain` with tests beside it.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. Stdlib only, no new dependency. `ForMetrics` and `ImportedID` are small. No auth or crypto code is touched.
6. Decoupling — pass. `metrics` imports `brain` through two exported functions (`ForMetrics`, `ImportedID`/`KindOfID`) and not through brain's internals. `ForDream` and `ForMetrics` share `store.records`. Ingest now loads each migrated root's `trail.jsonl` into `brain.db` through `openForSearch`, which writes only under `~/.config/fyr/` (R3, R4), changes no project file and so dirties no tree after the handoff commit.

## Not examined
- Record bodies in `.agents/trail.jsonl` beyond the guides and the metrics spec: the four `change` records, the three handoffs, the plan, `TEST-2026-10-25-1943`.
- `internal/metrics/events_test.go`, `agy_test.go`, `brain/import_test.go` and `brain/metrics_test.go` were read only in part or not at all (`records_test.go` was read in full).
- The full `go test -race ./...` suite (I ran only the metrics, brain, harness lint and size packages), `govulncheck`, and any Antigravity run of the changed `handoff` and `retro` skills.
- I made no call on the preflight NO-SHIP rule for an unrun skill (AGENTS.md § Release); that is the caller's gate.

## Outcome

Main agent, 2026-10-25. Round 2 skipped: the one fix has a test that fails without it, the verifier runs after the fixes, and the security review of the same range reported nothing of medium or higher (review skill Step 4).

1. Deferred join transaction (`events.go:96-101`) — fixed: the metrics store opens every transaction `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` (`internal/metrics/store.go:74-77`, `_txlock=immediate`; every transaction there writes: `agy.go:183`, `store.go:109`, `events.go:91`). Test: `TestTxTakesWriteLockAtBegin` (`internal/metrics/store_test.go:232`): with the store's transaction open after a read, a second connection with no busy timeout cannot write. It FAILED before the fix ("a second connection wrote while the store's transaction was open") and passes after. A concurrent ingest now waits up to the 10 s busy timeout (`internal/search/store.go:33`) instead of failing at once.
2. Phase-end restatements (`skills/feature/SKILL.md:107`, `rules/session-sizing.md:8`) — rebutted as a contradiction: both copies end the phase with the handoff, whose last call is `fyr metrics ingest` (`skills/handoff/SKILL.md:178`), so every copy produces the ingest; the context naming it at `context/AGENTS.md:11` is plan D1 ("named once in the context"). The second ingest of a phase end is idempotent (events keyed `(session, kind, ref)`, `ON CONFLICT … DO UPDATE`, `internal/metrics/events.go`) and took 198 ms warm (`TEST-2026-10-25-1943-behavioural-runs-metrics-phase-4-the-checkpoint`). Left: operator — whether to reword `context/AGENTS.md:11` to name the ingest as the handoff's last call, dropping the double ingest; a context edit owes an Antigravity run, outside this session's approvals.

# Security review — 811442c-33c652a   (2026-10-25)

Range reviewed: commits 811442c..33c652a (git log 811442c..33c652a); the diff is git diff 811442c...33c652a

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

Nothing high or medium. The worst problem is that `fyr metrics ingest` is no longer read-only towards the brain store. `brain.ForMetrics` calls `openForSearch`, which runs `session.sync` → `loadLocked`. So every ingest loads `.agents/trail.jsonl` into `~/.config/fyr/brain.db` for every project root that any recorded Antigravity session ran in. That includes roots where the operator never ran a `fyr` verb. The phase also starts this ingest at every handoff, every `/retro` and every phase end, not only nightly. A scope loaded this way becomes a `brain.Scopes` target of `fyr dream --all`. The dream ingests before it picks targets (`internal/dream/run.go:91-92`). So a checkout's committed trail, which another party may have written, can reach the dreamer's off-machine prompt in the same run that loaded it. The load's own guards still hold: symlinked or non-regular `.agents` and `trail.jsonl` are refused, the open is non-blocking with a 256 MiB cap, the scope is pinned to the checkout, and unexported kinds are refused. The dreamer is redacted, has no tools, and its proposals take effect only through `/retro`. A session that follows the context's resume order (`fyr record list --open`) loads the same file anyway. That keeps the severity low. Everything R4 limits in the metrics store still holds: no arguments, prose or paths beyond what was stored before.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/brain/dream.go:140` (`ForMetrics` → `openForSearch` → `sync`/`loadLocked`), called from `internal/metrics/events.go:120` — the metrics join now **writes** to the brain store. For each `project_root` in the metrics sessions, a changed `.agents/trail.jsonl` is loaded into a brain scope (`internal/brain/export.go` `loadLocked`, file wins, D21). That scope then joins `brain.Scopes` (`internal/brain/dream.go:15-37`) and becomes a `--all` dream target (`internal/dream/dream.go:146-163`). The ingest also runs before targets are chosen (`internal/dream/run.go:91-92`). Net effect: an ingest whose only job is to record session shapes widens the set of checkouts whose (redacted) trail text leaves the machine in the dreamer's prompt. It also brings third-party prompt-injection text into the dreamer, whose proposals are data and are re-derived at `/retro` step 9. No `R3`/`R4`/`SPEC-fyr-metrics` line says metrics ingest may create brain scopes. Remediation: make `ForMetrics` read-only. Either query the scope's rows without the file-wins load, or load only when the scope already exists in `meta`. If neither suits the join's "file wins" intent, record the load as a decision in SPEC-fyr-metrics § The join. Add a test that ingest over a root with a `trail.jsonl` and no brain scope creates no scope (`brain.Scopes` unchanged).
- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/metrics/events.go:91-120` — `ForMetrics` opens brain.db and can take its write transaction (`st.tx(loadLocked)`) while the metrics.db write transaction from `s.db.Begin()` is open. That happens once per root. Now that ingest runs at every handoff and `/retro` as well as nightly, a concurrent ingest, dream or `fyr record` write can stall behind the nested locks until the busy timeout. Availability only, no integrity or confidentiality effect. Remediation: collect every root's `MetricsInput` before `Begin()`.
- **[low / confidence: high]** (environment, not the diff) The `go` on this box is `/usr/bin/go` go1.24.4. `~/.local/bin/go` is a dangling symlink to `~/sdk/go1.27.1/bin/go`, and `~/sdk` is empty. AGENTS.md § Setup commands says go1.27.2. Against go1.24.4, `govulncheck ./...` reports 15 stdlib advisories that the code reaches: html/template ×8, os ×3 (incl. GO-2026-4970), net/url ×3, os/exec GO-2025-3956, database/sql GO-2025-3849. A binary built here ships them. Remediation: restore the user-level SDK and re-run govulncheck. Update the AGENTS.md line if the version changed.

## Checked

- **Secrets** — the 19-file diff has no credentials. The one secret-shaped value in the `.agents/trail.jsonl` diff is `AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE`, AWS's documented example key (a redactor fixture reference). The other hits are prose ("OAuth token … deleted"). No `.env`, key or token files.
- **Injection** — new SQL is parameterized (`records`, `ForMetrics`, `rekey`, `rewrite*Refs`). The only interpolated SQL is the fixed `recordCols`/WHERE literals from the caller and the static `GLOB '*.md'`. `recordRead`/`recordWords`/`programAt` parse untrusted conversation command lines: every slice index is bounds-guarded (`len(words) >= 3`, `programAt` returns only `i < len(words)`), so a hostile line cannot panic, and only a fixed vocabulary leaves (a `prefixes` kind, `record`, `list`). R4 holds. `KindOfID` prefixes do not overlap (`internal/brain/record.go:29-32`). The regexes (`recordStamp`, `verifyTitle`, `hexRun`, `finding`) are RE2 and linear.
- **Trust boundaries / git** — every new git call goes through `trail.Roots`/`trail.Command`, which disables fsmonitor, optional locks, gpg via `log.showSignature` and lazy fetch. A `bug` event's value is a SHA only when `matchCommit` finds it in the session's own commits. A record body yields only patterns (status line, severity counts, ts). Feedback records yield only an RFC 3339 ts, normalized to UTC.
- **R4 (metrics store contents)** — event refs are now record IDs. For a migrated project they come from a `parseLine`-validated `trail.jsonl` (bounded slug). Before, the ref was the trail file's base name, so the store gains no new prose or path class. `show.go`'s first-reads change counts only kinds.
- **Authz/authn** — not applicable (local CLI, no auth surface touched). `ForMetrics` reads global feedback only for `canonicalProject(root)`, so it does not cross project scopes.
- **Crypto** — none added or changed. Nothing hand-rolled.
- **Dependencies** — `go.mod`/`go.sum` unchanged in the range. New imports are internal only (`internal/brain` from `internal/metrics`; `path`, `database/sql` stdlib). govulncheck ran with go1.24.4 (see finding 3): 15 stdlib advisories reached and none in third-party modules. It also reports 5 imported-package and 42 required-module advisories that the code does not call. No npm ecosystem.
- **GCP surface** — none in the range.
- **Skills/context/kit** — the handoff skill adds `fyr metrics ingest` after the push, as the last call, never fatal. The retro skill adds an ingest at step 11, skipped under `--dry-run`. The context adds an ingest at the phase-end checkpoint. The kit adds a `metrics-feed` row to the same widened-permission case as `handoff`. None of these adds a permission key, a new command shape beyond a `fyr` verb, or an instruction to trust tool output. Retro step 9 still treats dream text as data.
- **Past bugs** — `fyr search --refs` per changed file. Only BUG-181 (`internal/metrics/agy.go` zero-time `ended_at`, open, not security) and BUG-096 (retro step numbers, fixed). Neither touches the diff.

## Not examined

- The bodies of the new and changed tests (`internal/metrics/agy_test.go`, `events_test.go`, `records_test.go`, `internal/brain/import_test.go` beyond the diff) were not read line by line, and `go test` was not run: the verifier's lane.
- The `.agents/trail.jsonl` diff: only scanned for secret shapes, not read as content. `ROADMAP.md` and `README.md` were not reviewed for security relevance beyond the ingest row.
- `internal/dream/run.go` `realRun`: only lines 91-92 (ingest, then targets) were read, not how the dream's redaction handles a scope loaded this way. The redactor (`internal/redact`) was not re-reviewed.
- govulncheck could not run on the documented go1.27.x toolchain (the SDK is missing), so the stdlib advisory picture for the intended toolchain is unverified.
- `brain.readRecords`/`parseLine` (ID and line validation of a loaded trail) were relied on from their comments and earlier reviews, not re-read.

## Outcome

Main agent, 2026-10-25. No finding of medium or higher, so no round 2 (review skill Step 4); the verifier runs after the reviewer's fix (`internal/metrics/store.go:74-77`).

1. `ForMetrics` writes `brain.db` through the file-wins load — rebutted: a recorded trade-off, not a defect. `SPEC-fyr-metrics` § Data, "Trail from files or records, never both" already says the read goes "through the file-wins load (`brain.ForMetrics`, which may write `brain.db` as the dream's read does)", and the plan records it as D21 and Assumption 2 ("accepted") in `PLAN-2026-10-25-1754-plan-metrics-fed-at-every-checkpoint-joined-to-r`. The scope it adds is one a session in that checkout loads anyway: the context's resume order starts with `fyr record list --open` (`context/AGENTS.md:9`), which loads `.agents/trail.jsonl` the same way (`openForSearch` → `sync`, `internal/brain/search.go:128-133`). The guards this report lists in its verdict still hold. A read-only `ForMetrics` (no load, or load only an existing scope) would change D21's case, where a fresh clone's sessions get trail events. That is a design change, so it goes to the operator as a choice and is not made here.
2. Brain write lock taken inside the metrics transaction — rebutted: no lock cycle exists. Only `cmd/fyr/main.go` and `internal/dream` import `internal/metrics`, and the dream runs its ingest before it opens any brain store (`internal/dream/run.go:91`, `ingestFirst`, then `targets`/`collect`). `internal/brain` imports nothing of `internal/metrics` (`grep` of the import path: none). So no path holds `brain.db` while waiting on `metrics.db`. A concurrent `fyr record` write is waited out under the 10 s busy timeout (`internal/search/store.go:33`), the bounded stall the report already rates availability-only.
3. Stdlib advisories under go1.24.4 — left: operator. This is the box's environment and the range does not cause it: `~/.local/bin/go` points to a missing `~/sdk/go1.27.1`, so `/usr/bin/go` go1.24.4 builds. Restoring the user-level SDK (`DEPLOY-local` § Operator steps) and re-running `govulncheck` is the operator's step; it also blocks a release cut from this box.

title: Review — cold read of the fyr check plan
body:
# Review — plan-fyr-check cold reader   (2026-10-25)

Range reviewed: `.agents/scratch/plan-fyr-check.md` (PLAN-2026-10-25-2024-plan-fyr-check-docs-freshness-and-drift-2026-10), plus the code surfaces it names. No diff exists; this is the cold-reader check.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

design needs revision / implementation not ready. 17 gaps, 4 BLOCKING questions.

Worst first: rule (b) cannot converge on this repository. The comparison is a commit time against the record's `updated`, and `updated` is stamped before the commit that carries it. Any spec whose code set contains `.agents/trail.jsonl` is stale forever, because every `fyr record edit` rewrites that file and its commit is later than the stamp. I prototyped the plan's candidate rule over `.agents/trail.jsonl` (script in `.agents/scratch/cr/proto.py`, run read-only). All 6 current specs come out `stale`. 4 of the 6 name `.agents/trail.jsonl` and 3 name `AGENTS.md` or a bare `.agents`. So S4 and E2E 1 (`check: 0 findings`) are unreachable for those specs by the plan's own remedy. D7 also states a fact the prototype contradicts. The second worst: rule (c) rejects the values the `requirements` skill writes, and the skill runs the check right after writing them.

Measurements are from the working tree at 3d2fc66 (git 2.47.3). The prototype is an approximation of the plan's rule, not the implementation.

## Findings

1. **[high / confidence: high] Rule (b), plan lines 188-193 and D7 (BLOCKING).** Two defects.
   - The `updated` stamp comes before the commit that holds the code and the trail. The Definition of Done edits the spec (`updated` = T1), then commits code and `trail.jsonl` (T2 > T1), so the newest commit to the spec's paths is newer than `updated`. The remedy (`fyr record edit --status current`) restamps at T3, but the edit rewrites `trail.jsonl`, which needs another commit. That is clean only if the spec does not name `trail.jsonl`.
   - Evidence in this tree: SPEC-fyr-metrics is stale by 225 s against the last handoff commit 3d2fc66, because that commit touched `.agents/trail.jsonl` and `internal/*` paths it names. SPEC-fyr-search, SPEC-fyr-memory-loop and SPEC-fyr-metrics all name `.agents/trail.jsonl`.
   - Needed decisions: what counts as a spec's code (exclude `trail.jsonl`, `AGENTS.md`, bare `.agents` and `*.md`?), and the basis of the comparison (the commit that last changed the spec's line in `trail.jsonl`, a tolerance, or the HEAD that holds `updated`).

2. **[high / confidence: high] D7 is factually wrong (BLOCKING).** D7 says `SPEC-fyr-search` and `SPEC-fyr-memory-loop` "name none". Under the plan's own candidate rule they do:
   - SPEC-fyr-search names `.agents`, `.agents/scratch`, `.agents/trail.jsonl`, `AGENTS.md` and `skills/google-catalog/catalog/`.
   - SPEC-fyr-memory-loop names `.agents/trail.jsonl`, `AGENTS.md` and `agents/dreamer/agent.md`.
   - So `spec-unlinked` does not fire. A spec can pass rule (b) by naming `AGENTS.md`, and the "code" set is mostly non-code.
   - Also, `SPEC-fyr-search` names `.agents/docs`, `.agents/docs/plans/x.md` and `internal/trail.Command`, which the rule reports as missing paths. That is noise.

3. **[high / confidence: high] Rule (c) vs the `requirements` skill (BLOCKING).** `skills/requirements/SKILL.md:44` has the skill write "enforced by" as a test, rule, guide or ADR, "or `not yet enforced: <what would>`". The template's last comment adds "the test or dashboard that measures it". Plan lines 206-209 resolve only a path, a Go `Test\w+` name or a record ID, split at commas.
   - Findings the plan would give on legitimate values: `not yet enforced: …` (and a comma inside it), a prose rule, `GUIDE-testing § 4`, `path § section`, `web/e2e/x.spec.ts`, pytest `file::test`, a dashboard.
   - S2 has the skill run the check immediately after writing exactly those lines.
   - The plan must say what `not yet enforced:` is (finding, note or valid) and what a non-Go project's value looks like.

4. **[medium / confidence: high] Path rule vs its verify clause (BLOCKING).**
   - A candidate needs a tracked top-level file, or a first segment that is a tracked top-level directory (plan lines 178-182). A doc naming a *removed* top-level file or directory is therefore never a candidate. That is the central drift case. Yet the Phase 1 verify (line 255) expects "`path` for a missing top-level path", which the rule cannot produce. Only a nested missing path (`internal/gone.go`) can.
   - The same clause expects "no candidate for … anything in `skills/`". README and the records name `skills/review/SKILL.md:58-66`, which the rule makes a candidate. If the clause means "skills files are not scanned", it must say so, because the sentence as written fixes a different test.
   - `S1(a)` says a docs-set file names a missing repo path; D3 limits that to root `*.md` and records.

5. **[medium / confidence: high] `trail.Toplevel` is the wrong function (non-blocking).** It returns the cleaned dir, with no error, when `dir` is not a checkout (`internal/trail/trail.go:201-217`). `trail.Readable` (`:164`) tests only for a partial clone on an old git. Neither detects "not a git checkout". `trail.Roots` (`:235`) does, via `ErrNotCheckout`, and handles submodules, `core.worktree` and bare repositories. The failure table (plan lines 213-216) names the wrong functions. Default: use `Roots`' `top`.

6. **[medium / confidence: high] D4 "one home" is false (non-blocking).** The subverb names also live in these places, none of which the plan lists:
   - `recordFlags` (`cmd/fyr/record.go:24`) is a second table of the record subverbs, with per-subverb flags. `runRecord` prints the const `recordUsage` for an unknown word (`record.go:41-48`), not a list from a field.
   - `memoryCmd` hard-codes `add` and `show` plus a usage string (`cmd/fyr/main.go:906`).
   - `runMetrics` hard-codes the usage string and the switch (`main.go:524-531`).
   - "Each dispatcher's switch reads the field" cannot be done for a `switch`, and the refusal texts are existing, tested behaviour. Decide: derive `recordFlags` from the field, and whether the vocabulary keeps the per-verb union (so `fyr record get --title` passes, a false negative) or the per-subverb table.

7. **[medium / confidence: medium] Markdown scanning is undefined (non-blocking).** There is no markdown parser (R4 stdlib only), so the implementer hand-writes one. Undecided points:
   - double-backtick spans (the plan's own E2E text uses them), multi-line spans, `~~~` and indented fences, indented code blocks;
   - non-shell fences (`go`, `json`) that contain the word `fyr`;
   - flag tokenisation with trailing punctuation (`--dry-run]`, `--all,`, a quoted `"--x"`), line-continuation `\`, and the line number of a wrapped span.
   These change the first-run finding set.

8. **[medium / confidence: medium] No escape hatch for intentional references; A3 is measurable now (non-blocking).** S4 demands zero findings, but living docs legitimately name legacy or runtime paths such as `.agents/docs/` (what `record import` migrates), `.agents/rules/`, and historical verbs. In this tree rule (a) reaches `.agents/docs` and `.agents/docs/` in SPEC-fyr-delivery, SPEC-fyr-record and SPEC-fyr-search. Fixing them means rewording true statements. A3 says "not checked"; a read-only count would settle it before the plan is approved. Decide the policy: reword, or allow a marker.

9. **[medium / confidence: medium] Shallow clones (non-blocking).** `trail.PartialClone` (`trail.go:177-198`) tests only promisor config. In a `--depth N` clone the boundary commit "touches" every path, so every spec is `spec-stale` at the tip's time. R10 says the verb behaves the same on every place. Default: detect `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` and skip rule (b) with a note.

10. **[low / confidence: high] Partial-clone path is inconsistent and depends on the git version (non-blocking).** The failure table says an unreadable git (`Readable` false) is exit 1. Rule (b) says a partial clone is a skipped rule with a note. Only a partial clone on git >= 2.44 reaches the note. `lazyFetchSafe` is an unexported variable in `trail`, so a `check` test cannot take either side. The Phase 2 test "a partial clone gives the note" holds on this box (git 2.47.3) and fails on an old git. State which cases are which.

11. **[medium / confidence: medium] Range vs working tree for the consumers (non-blocking).** `/review --docs` and preflight Step 4 work over `<base>..<head>`. `fyr check` reads the working tree and reports the whole repository. It cannot separate a finding the range introduced from one that was already there. Preflight Step 4 already runs the review skill's docs brief verbatim (`skills/preflight/SKILL.md:72`). The plan edits both texts, which creates a second restatement. Decide the single home, and who runs the check (reviewer via `run_command`, or the main thread).

12. **[medium / confidence: high] E2E 2 is not reproducible as written (non-blocking).**
    - "Exactly one `spec-stale`": a commit to `AGENTS.md`, `internal/brain` or `.agents/trail.jsonl` makes several specs stale. The criterion must name a file only one spec names.
    - "Each naming its file or record and line": `spec-stale` has no line (line 101 says omitted when none).
    - E2E 1 says "prints `check: 0 findings`", but the summary line has a suffix; state "begins with".

13. **[low / confidence: medium] Output channels and a lump exit code (non-blocking).**
    - Findings go to `c.out` (stdout, the verb convention); refusals go to stderr; both exit 1, so a skill cannot tell "findings" from "refused". Say stdout vs stderr per case.
    - `search.Printable` lives in `internal/search` (the SQLite importer); the plan says `internal/check` imports only `trail` and `brain`. State that `cmd/fyr` applies it.

14. **[low / confidence: medium] Symlink claim is wrong for path components (non-blocking).** Plan line 225: "`os.Lstat` follows no symlink out". `Lstat` does not follow the *last* component only. A tracked symlinked directory inside a tree (`internal/link -> /etc`) makes `internal/link/passwd` a candidate whose existence is tested outside root. The `:N` check must open and read the file: say regular files only, a size cap, and how a binary file counts. This is for the `security` review the plan already schedules.

15. **[low / confidence: high] noindex honours two names (non-blocking).** `internal/search/reconcile.go:151-160` honours `.sh-agent-noindex` as well as `.fyr-noindex`, as "a privacy control the operator placed". The plan names one. `isNoIndexMarker` is unexported, so `check` either duplicates it (a second home) or search exports it.

16. **[medium / confidence: medium] Scope the `## Why` did not name.** The request (ROADMAP item 3, R0) names the check only.
    - The three consumer-skill edits (S2), their `GUIDE-skill-matrix` rows and the three Antigravity runs have no D-row saying who asked. Under `AGENTS.md` § Release each changed skill needs an Antigravity run before a tag, so S2 widens the release gate.
    - The `note:` output class and `line` as a separate rule follow from E2E 3 and the interfaces; no other extras (`--json` and auto-fix are rejected).
    - Ask the operator for a D-row on S2 (O1 covers only the context).

17. **[low / confidence: medium] Docs clauses missing (non-blocking).**
    - The subverb task changes the `record`, `metrics` and `memory` refusal texts and has no docs clause. Check `usage` and `recordUsage`.
    - `SPEC-fyr-record` (R7, the export/load reader) is not in S3, though `brain.ReadTrail` is a new reader of `trail.jsonl`.
    - S3 lists README § Daily commands but not the `requirements` skill's own description of `enforced by`, which must agree with whatever Finding 3 decides.

## Questions I would have to ask

| # | Question | Mark |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 | Rule (b): what counts as a spec's code, and what is compared with `updated` so that a spec updated in the same session as its code is not stale forever? (Findings 1, 2) | BLOCKING |
| Q2 | Rule (c): what is `not yet enforced: …`, a prose rule, a section-suffixed path, a non-Go test or a dashboard? Finding, note or valid? (Finding 3) | BLOCKING |
| Q3 | Path rule: how does a removed top-level file or directory become a candidate, and does "no candidate in `skills/`" mean files or tokens? (Finding 4) | BLOCKING |
| Q4 | D7: which paths make a spec "linked" when `AGENTS.md`, `.agents` and `trail.jsonl` exist? (Finding 2) | BLOCKING |
| Q5 | Which function detects "not a git checkout" (`Roots`)? | NON-BLOCKING (default `Roots`) |
| Q6 | Flags per verb or per subverb, and does `recordFlags` derive from the field? | NON-BLOCKING (plan says per verb) |
| Q7 | Markdown scanning: CommonMark fences, double-backtick spans, token punctuation? | NON-BLOCKING (a reasonable implementer decides) |
| Q8 | Policy for intentionally missing paths in living docs (reword or marker)? | NON-BLOCKING (A3 fallback exists) |
| Q9 | Shallow clone and the partial-clone/old-git split? | NON-BLOCKING |
| Q10 | Range vs working tree; single home for the consumer text; who runs it? | NON-BLOCKING |
| Q11 | Stdout/stderr split; refusal vs finding exit code? | NON-BLOCKING |
| Q12 | Symlinked path components, regular-file-only line counts, size cap? | NON-BLOCKING |
| Q13 | Honour `.sh-agent-noindex` too; share or duplicate the marker test? | NON-BLOCKING |
| Q14 | Operator: who asked for S2 and its release-gating Antigravity rows? | NON-BLOCKING (default in the plan) |
| Q15 | E2E 2 fixture: which file, so exactly one spec is stale? | NON-BLOCKING |

## Criteria (plan lens)

1. Dead code — n/a for a plan; the one candidate is `recordFlags`/`recordUsage` left as a second table (Finding 6).
2. Flow tracing — fail: `trail.Toplevel` and `Readable` do not detect a non-checkout (Finding 5); `updated` vs commit time does not converge (Finding 1).
3. Standards conformance — fail: D4's "one home" is false (Finding 6); verify clauses contradict the rule (Finding 4); a restatement of the docs lens in two skills (Finding 11).
4. Directory layout — pass: `internal/check` beside `trail`/`brain`, `ReadTrail` in `internal/brain/export.go`.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass: stdlib only, no new dependency, nothing in auth or crypto; the hand-written markdown scanner is the cost of R4 (Finding 7).
6. Decoupling — mostly pass: `check` is a leaf; `Printable` and the noindex marker are the two reach-ins (Findings 13, 15).

## Not examined

- `internal/check` does not exist; nothing was run against an implementation.
- ADR-063, SPEC-fyr-record, GUIDE-fyr-matrix and GUIDE-skill-matrix bodies were not read (only GUIDE-testing's headings). No `fyr record get` of SPEC-fyr-record. `skills/requirements/SKILL.md` was read at lines 26 and 44 only.
- BUG records were not read one by one. `fyr search --refs … --kind bug` for `cmd/fyr/main.go`, `internal/brain/export.go`, `README.md` and the three skills found BUG-007, BUG-048, BUG-105, BUG-161 and BUG-023; none concerns this plan's surfaces.
- `TestHarnessMap` (`cmd/fyr/main_test.go:868`) and `TestSkillLinksResolve` were not opened. The `context/AGENTS.md` headroom figure ("195 bytes") was not re-measured; `wc -c` gives 12,553 for `context/AGENTS.md` and 2,131 for `dev-setup.md`, and the size-pin arithmetic (render header, inventory) was not followed.
- The prototype in `.agents/scratch/cr/proto.py` covers only rule (b)'s candidate and staleness arithmetic over `trail.jsonl`; it does not model rule (a) tokenisation.

## Outcome

Answered 2026-10-25 in the plan (PLAN-2026-10-25-2024-plan-fyr-check-docs-freshness-and-drift-2026-10), round 1. Every finding is fixed by a D-row, rebutted, or put to the operator as an Open row. No round 2: the plan goes to the operator for approval.

1. **Fixed by D9.** Rule (b) now compares by ancestry. The spec's commit is the oldest commit whose `trail.jsonl` diff adds its current id+`updated` line (`git log -G`); the spec is stale when `rev-list --count <commit>..HEAD` over its code is greater than 0, with `trail.jsonl` and `*.md` excluded. A prototype (`.agents/scratch/cr2/specs.py`) finds 1 of 6 specs stale (`SPEC-fyr-record`, 4 commits) in 5.6 s.
2. **Fixed by D10, which supersedes D7.** A spec's code excludes `*.md`, `.agents`, `.agents/trail.jsonl` and ignored paths. D7's factual claim was wrong and is struck.
3. **Fixed by D22 and D23; O5 is put to the operator.**
   - A value splits at commas, and each part resolves by its first token (up to whitespace, ` § `, `::` or `#`) as a path, a Go test or a record ID. So `GUIDE-testing § 4`, `path § section`, `file::test` and `ADR-NNN` all resolve.
   - `not yet enforced:` is one part. Its verdict is Open O5; the default is a finding.
   - The skill runs the check after the approved file is written, because it drafts in scratch.
4. **Fixed by D11.** The rule stays anchored on a tracked top-level entry. A removed top-level entry becomes a Known limit, and Phase 1's verify clause now uses a nested path. "Not in skills/" is defined as files not scanned. S1(a) is reworded to D3's scope.
5. **Fixed by D13.** The root comes from `trail.Roots`, and `ErrNotCheckout` is the refusal.
6. **Fixed by D14, which supersedes D4.** `recordFlags` is the record vocabulary, with per-subverb flags. `metrics` and `memory` get one list each, which builds their unchanged refusal texts, pinned by a test.
7. **Fixed by D15**, which states the scanning grammar.
8. **Fixed by D12; O6 is put to the operator.** Another checkout's path is written with a placeholder, and there is no marker. A3 is measured now: about 45 first-run findings (38 paths, 1 real; 3 removed-verb statements; 1–2 specs).
9. **Fixed by D13.** A shallow clone skips rule (b) with a note.
10. **Fixed by D13.** A partial clone, a shallow clone and `Readable` false each give a note on any git version. The partial-clone test sets the promisor config itself.
11. **Fixed by D17.** The single home is the review docs brief; preflight Step 4 reuses it unchanged. The reviewer runs the check and lists findings outside the range as pre-existing.
12. **Fixed by D21.** E2E 2 is measured against the clone's baseline, with a new spec record naming a file only it names. `spec-stale` has no line. E2E 1 reads "begins".
13. **Fixed by D18.** Findings go to stdout, refusals to stderr, and the summary line tells checked from refused. `cmd/fyr` applies `Printable`.
14. **Fixed by D19.** Paths are resolved through `os.Root`, and `:N` only on regular files, capped.
15. **Fixed by D20.** `trail.NoIndexMarkers` holds both names.
16. **Rebutted in part; O7 is put to the operator.** The consumer tasks come from the feature skill's Step 1 capability rule ("the plan gets a task per consumer or a line saying why not"). D17 and D23 cut them to two skills, and O7 asks the operator to keep or cut them. `note:` and `line` follow from the interfaces; they are no extra surface.
17. **Fixed.**
    - The `ReadTrail` task carries `docs: SPEC-fyr-record`.
    - The vocabulary task carries `docs: none`, because its refusal texts are unchanged and pinned.
    - The requirements skill task names its `enforced by` grammar.

title: Review — 17064af-93282df-code-docs (2026-10-25): fyr check feature, code and docs lens
body:
---
owner: reviewer
date: 2026-10-25
---
# Review — 17064af-93282df-code-docs   (2026-10-25)

Range reviewed: Scope: commits 17064af..93282df (git log 17064af..93282df); the diff is git diff 17064af...93282df.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing blocking. The worst problem is latent and low: `breQuote` in `internal/check/specs.go` escapes for a POSIX basic regex, but `git log -G` compiles an extended one, so a spec ID or `updated` stamp holding `+ ? ( ) { } |` would not match its own trail line. Rule (b) then silently treats the spec as having no commit and never reports it stale. The export's own stamps (`...Z`) and the ID grammar (`[a-z0-9._-]`) cannot produce such characters today, so this only bites a hand-edited trail.jsonl. Two other low items are a README row that drops a carve-out and a silent `continue` in rule (b). The new package is otherwise sound. I ran `go vet` clean and `go test` green on `internal/check`, `internal/trail`, `internal/brain` and the `cmd/fyr` check, vocabulary, usage and HarnessMap tests. `go run ./cmd/fyr check` reports 0 findings. Its note says rule (c) is not run here, because this repository's `REQUIREMENTS.md` has no `enforced by:` field.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/check/specs.go:111-120` (`breQuote`, used by `specCommit` at :99) — the comment says git's `-G` default is a POSIX basic regex. It is extended (`REG_EXTENDED`). I checked this in a scratch repo (`.agents/scratch/rv/g`): with only `\ . [ ] * ^ $` escaped, the pattern `"updated":"2026-10-25T10:00:00+02:00"` matched 0 commits, and `\+` matched 1. An unescaped `(x)` in an ID matched a different ID's line (2 commits instead of 1). Consequence: `specCommit` returns "" and `specsRule` `continue`s, so the spec is never stale, with no note. Fix: also escape `+ ? ( ) { } |` and correct the comment; add a `TestSpecRule*` case with a `+hh:mm` stamp.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/check/specs.go:46-48` — if `git rev-list` fails (for example the argument list is too long for a spec whose spans name very many paths), the spec is skipped with no finding and no note. A run that could not check reads as clean, which contradicts the spec's own rule that the summary line tells a run that checked from one that refused. Fix: append a `note:` per skipped spec, or fail the run.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `README.md:51` — the `fyr check` row says every Must and Should item whose `enforced by:` is "missing" is a finding. It omits the carve-out in `SPEC-fyr-check` (the Rule (c) section and the situations table, plan D30) and in `cmd/fyr/main.go` usage: a `REQUIREMENTS.md` with no `enforced by:` anywhere is not checked, only noted. This repository is that case (`note: REQUIREMENTS.md has no enforced-by field: not checked`), so the row over-promises what `fyr check` says about this repository's requirements. Fix: add "(a file with no `enforced by:` field at all is noted, not checked)".

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. Every new function and var has a caller. One trivial leftover: the `m[1] != "Skill"` test in `docsFiles` can never be true, because the regex is lowercase-only, and I did not count it as a finding.
2. Flow tracing — pass with the two low items above. `check.Run` → `brain.ReadTrail` → `trail.Roots`/`Command`/`Log` all pass their errors up; a refusal is `ErrRefused`, mapped to exit 1 with no summary. The `search/reconcile.go` marker move to `trail.IsNoIndexMarker` keeps behaviour: it builds and the search tests pass. The tests can fail: `TestCheckVerb` asserts the checkout and `--home` are unchanged; `TestVocabularySubverbListsMatchDispatchers` pins the lists against the dispatchers.
3. Standards conformance — pass. Stdlib only, no new driver import; the `os.Root` guard against symlink escape is used and tested (`TestDocsRuleSymlinkOutOfRoot`); `search.Printable` is applied to every output line; the Go 1.24 `os.Root` limits are handled by hand in `readFile`. The Docs brief renumbering (3 to 4 and so on, `--project` item 7 to 8) is consistent: the restatements I found (`review/SKILL.md:52`, `GUIDE-testing` "item 3" as `fyr check`, `SPEC-fyr-check`) agree. The `<project>/.agents/...` rewording in the skills and agents matches the spec's placeholder rule. Not verified: whether `GUIDE-skill-matrix` and `GUIDE-fyr-matrix` carry an older item number. I searched only the current spec, guide and deploy records for "Docs brief" and "item 7", and found no stale ones.
4. Directory layout — pass. `internal/check` has no SQLite import, `cmd/fyr/check.go` sits beside `main.go`, tests sit beside their code, and AGENTS.md's Layout lists `internal/check` and the widened `internal/trail` line.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. Stdlib only, no new dependency. `git` is used for ignore and history rather than a re-implementation. No auth or crypto involved.
6. Decoupling — pass. The `trail.NoIndexMarkers` move removes the search-to-check coupling; `brain.ReadTrail` is a narrow read seam; the vocabulary is built from the verbs' own FlagSets and `metricsSubverbs`/`memorySubverbs`, so it cannot drift silently from the dispatchers (and the tests pin them).

## Docs lens
1. Restatement of the changed claims: `restatement-grep.sh` was not run. I used `git grep` and a scan of the current spec, guide and deploy records for "Docs brief", "item 3" and "item 7" instead.
2. Findings: see the README row finding above. `SPEC-fyr-check` matches the code on each point I compared: flags ignored, positional word gives exit 2, the situations table, the item grammar, resolving, and the known limits. The `-G` "id before updated" limit is documented.
3. `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `ROADMAP.md` and `context/AGENTS.md` (the last a placeholder reword only, context otherwise unchanged by D35) are consistent with the code. The `main.go` usage block for `check` matches the spec.
4. Unverified: the Antigravity behavioural runs the change record cites (TEST-2026-10-25-2312) and the matrix rows `review-docs-check` and `requirements-check`. I read the kit's `run.sh` change (a `gi mv` base commit for `review-docs-check`) but did not run it. `go test -race ./...` was not run in full.

## Not examined
- A full `go test -race -timeout 30m ./...` and `govulncheck` (the verifier's job).
- `internal/check/*_test.go` bodies beyond the names, `specs_test.go:39-72` and `cmd/fyr/check_test.go:1-200`.
- The `GUIDE-fyr-matrix`, `GUIDE-skill-matrix` and `GUIDE-testing` records beyond the "item 3" hit.
- The `.agents/trail.jsonl` record diffs (36 lines changed): only spot-read through `record get SPEC-fyr-check`.
- `skills/api-auth-gcp`, `dream`, `feedback-log`, `golang/references/testing.md` and `retro`: their diffs are `<project>/…` placeholder rewordings, checked by the summary of `fyr check` reporting 0, not read line by line.
- The restatement-grep script itself (see Docs lens item 1).

## Outcome

Written by the main agent, 2026-10-25. Round 2 for this lens was skipped (review skill Step 4): every code fix has a test that fails without it, the verifier runs after the fixes, and the security agent's round 2 covered the same code.

1. `specs.go:111-120` `breQuote` (BRE, not ERE) — fixed: `specCommit` quotes the id and the stamp with `regexp.QuoteMeta` (`internal/check/specs.go`, specCommit), `breQuote` removed; `TestSpecRuleOffsetStamp` (`internal/check/hardening_test.go`), a `+02:00` stamp, fails with the stamp unquoted (must-fail run 2026-10-25).
2. `specs.go:46-48` silent `continue` when `git rev-list` fails — fixed: `specsRule` returns `<ID>: git rev-list failed: spec not checked`, and the same for `git log` in `specCommit`, as notes (`internal/check/specs.go`, `check.go` Run); `TestSpecRuleGitFailureIsANote`, two cases, each made by removing one loose object the call needs and proven to make that git call fail first, fails with the note lines removed.
3. `README.md:51` drops the no-`enforced by:` carve-out — fixed: the row now says a file with no `enforced by:` field at all is noted, not checked (`README.md:51`).

title: Security — 17064af-93282df (2026-10-25): fyr check feature, two rounds
body:
---
owner: security
date: 2026-10-25
---
# Security review — 17064af-93282df   (2026-10-25)

Range reviewed: commits 17064af..93282df (git log 17064af..93282df); the diff is git diff 17064af...93282df.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

The worst problem: `fyr check`'s rule (b) runs `git log -G … -- .agents/trail.jsonl` with textconv left on, which is git log's default. A checkout's own tracked `.gitattributes`, combined with a `diff.<driver>.textconv` from the repository's config or the user's, therefore runs an external program from a verb that ADR-064 and SPEC-fyr-check call read-only. It is the same class of hole `trail.Command` already closes for `core.fsmonitor` and for the partial-clone `core.sshCommand` case. The range now has `skills/review` (Docs brief item 3) and `skills/requirements` (Steps 3 and 5) run `fyr check` on whatever checkout is under review. Everything else is low: a regex dialect mismatch that makes rule (b) skip a spec silently instead of failing loud, a super-linear inline-span scanner, and a Lstat-then-blocking-Open race. Separately, the box's Go toolchain has regressed to go1.24.4: 15 standard-library advisories are reachable, and two of them run through the new `internal/check` `os.Root` calls.

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/check/specs.go:99`, via `internal/trail/trail.go:168-172`: `specCommit` calls `trail.Log(k.top, "-G", pat, "--format=%H", "--", ".agents/trail.jsonl")`.
  - **Weakness.** `git log` turns textconv on by default, and pickaxe `-G` runs the textconv filter on both blobs of every commit that touched the path.
  - **How it was verified.** A scratch probe repository (since deleted) on git 2.47.3, with the harmless identity filter `cat`: a tracked `.gitattributes` line `.agents/trail.jsonl diff=probe`, `diff.probe.textconv=cat` in the probe's config, then the exact argv `trail.Log` builds (`--no-optional-locks -c core.fsmonitor=false -c log.showSignature=false -C <dir> log --no-show-signature -G <pat> --format=%H -- .agents/trail.jsonl`). `GIT_TRACE=1` showed `run_command: cat /tmp/git-blob-…/trail.jsonl` three times.
  - **How a checkout reaches it.** The attribute is tracked content, so it travels with any clone, pull or zip. The driver definition can come from three places:
    - the repository's own `.git/config`, for a copied tree or the hostile-config model `trail.Command` already defends against;
    - a driver the user's global or system config already defines, aimed by the checkout at attacker-controlled blob content;
    - `include.path`, `includeIf`, or a `GIT_CONFIG_*` setting.
  - **Impact.** Every `fyr check` runs a program the checkout chose. That includes runs the review and requirements skills now make on foreign checkouts (`--project`).
  - **Remediation.**
    - Pass `--no-textconv` and `--no-ext-diff` on this call.
    - Better: put them in `trail.Log` itself, so a later `-G`, `-S` or `-p` caller cannot inherit the hole. Today's other `Log` callers (`trail.go:58` `--name-only`, `dream.go:193`, `metrics/events.go:404`) do no content diff.
    - Pin it with a test: a fixture repository whose textconv driver writes a marker under the test's temp dir, then assert the marker is absent after `check.Run`.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** Environment, in the blast radius (not caused by this diff). `go version` on this box is go1.24.4 (`/usr/bin/go`). `~/.local/bin/go` is a dangling symlink to `~/sdk/go1.27.1/bin/go`, which no longer exists. That contradicts AGENTS.md § Setup commands, which says "the Linux box runs a user-level go1.27.2 SDK".
