  - Kind, ID, status, date shape, the title (`normalize`: controls to `?`, `oneLine`, 512-byte trim) and the body (controls to `?`, at most 1 MiB) all agree.
  - `Updated` does not (finding 1).
  - Duplicate IDs are refused before the write.
- **Terminal:** every `printImport` line, every refusal (`recordErr`) and every `memoryCmd` error goes through `search.Printable`, and `MemoryShow` lines do too. The one gap is shell syntax rather than terminal control (finding 4).
- **Authz/authn:** n/a beyond scope resolution, which is `trail.Roots` and unchanged in this range.
- **Crypto:** none touched.
- **Dependencies:**
  - `go.mod` and `go.sum` are unchanged in the range.
  - `govulncheck` (`~/.go/bin/govulncheck ./...`) ran on **go1.24.4**, because `/usr/bin/go` is first and `~/.local/bin/go` dangles, the same box state as the previous review. It reports the same 15 reachable stdlib advisories (GO-2025-3849, GO-2026-4970, …), all fixed by a newer Go, plus 5 package and 42 module advisories not reached. The range adds none.
  - No npm surface.
- **GCP surface:** none in this range.

## Not examined

- `internal/brain/import_test.go`, `cmd/fyr/record_test.go` and `cmd/fyr/memory_test.go`: I listed the test names but did not read the bodies.
- `internal/harness/catalog_test.go` and `internal/search/search_test.go` diffs: not read. The `reconcile.go` change, which excludes `.agents/trail.jsonl` from the file index, was read and holds.
- The memory/time bound (finding 6) was not measured.
- The TOCTOU windows (finding 7) are argued from the code; I did not race them.
- Finding 8's three triggers are argued from the code, not run.
- `fyr dream`'s continued reads of the old `.agents/memory` files after migration, if any, are out of this range.
- govulncheck on a Go ≥ 1.25.12: none is installed on this box.

Scratch used: `.agents/scratch/sec-import/`. It holds a build of ddaa522, the probe repos `p1`, `p2`, `p4` and `p5` (each init verified with `rev-parse --absolute-git-dir`, with `GIT_*` unset), `victim/`, and the scratch homes `home1` to `home5`. No source, test or config file was changed.

## Outcome

All eight fixed; each has a test that failed with its fix mutated out (2026-10-25, mutation runs in the main thread).

| # | Finding | Outcome | Test (mutation that failed it) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | impossible date exported, bricking other homes | FIXED: `docDate` and the ADR heading take a date only when it is a real day (`realDay`), else the stem's, else the import's day; every record goes through `checkRecord` — the load's own `parseLine` for exported kinds — before anything is written, in a dry run too, and again in `insertNew` | `TestImportBadDateLoads` (realDay accepting any shape) |
| 2 | global import follows a symlinked `.agents` | FIXED: `readMemoryStore` calls `guardExportPath(root)` first; the project import passes the scope root through the same function | `TestImportGlobalRefusesASymlinkedAgents` (guard removed) |
| 3 | files left as files listed for `git rm` | FIXED: `Remove` holds only trail files; a file outside the trail's directories is a problem and stays; the spec says so in one place | `TestImportLeavesUnknownFilesOffTheRemoveList` (red before the fix) |
| 4 | remove lists printed unquoted | FIXED: `brain.ShellQuote` prints each path as one shell word | `TestShellQuote` (quoting off) |
| 5 | `memory add` skips the title rules | FIXED: the description goes through `cleanTitle` (a refusal, exit 2 as `fyr memory` always had); `memory show` cuts each line at 640 bytes | `TestMemoryAddTitleRules`, `TestMemoryShowBoundsEachLine` (each check off) |
| 6 | no total read cap | FIXED: one `budget` per import, 256 MiB and 50,000 files over the docs tree, the referencing files (now `git ls-files`, tracked only) and the memory store | `TestImportCapsTotalRead` (budget check off) |
| 7 | Lstat-then-ReadFile | FIXED: `readRegular` (`openNonBlocking`: `O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK`, fstat regular, size cap, `LimitReader`) for every read, the logs included | `TestReadRegular` (regular-file check off; symlink and FIFO cases) |
| 8 | one bad global entry aborts the import | FIXED: logs read line by line with an over-long line reported by number; each record checked and reported, not fatal; slugs cut at 120 to leave room for `-N`; a source with a problem is not listed for removal | `TestImportGlobalBadEntriesAreProblems` (long-line check off; failed-source filter off) |

title: Security review — brain-import-round2 (2026-10-25)
body:
# Security review — brain-import-round2   (2026-10-25)

Range reviewed: ddaa522..963467c -- internal cmd (round 2, over the fixes only), against the Outcome tables of `2026-10-25-security-brain-import.md` and `2026-10-25-review-brain-phase2-import.md`

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

The fixes close the round-1 triggers they name. Mutation runs on a scratch copy confirm that the date, symlinked-`.agents`, tracked-store and remove-list fixes are each pinned by a failing test. Five low findings remain, and none is high or medium. Worst: `ImportGlobal`'s `-N` collision suffix is never checked against IDs already used. A source whose record collides is skipped silently, reported as imported, and still listed for `rm`. That breaks the fix's own contract ("a source with a problem is not listed for removal"), and `~/.config/fyr` is not in git, so following the list loses the entry for good. Next: the finding-8 fix bounds `json.Indent`'s result only after computing it, which leaves an unbounded memory amplification. The finding-7 fix guards only the last path component. Three of the claimed caps and checks have no test that fails without them.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/brain/import.go:885-890` (`add`'s `used[r.ID]++` suffix), `:700-708` (`filterStored`), `:1017-1021` (`Sources`): a suffixed ID can equal a real one, and the loser is listed for removal.
  Reproduced on a scratch copy (`.agents/scratch/sec-r2/src`, probe test `zz_probe_test.go`). Proposals `FOO.md`, `foo-2.md` and `foo.md` become `PROPOSAL-foo`, `PROPOSAL-foo-2` and `PROPOSAL-foo-2` again, because the suffixed ID is never checked in `used`. `insertNew` stores the first `PROPOSAL-foo-2` and skips the second as "taken". `filterStored` matches by key, so it keeps **both** in `res.Records` (3 records, `Skipped=1`, no problem). `proposals/foo.md` is in `res.Sources`, under "remove by name once the records are checked". Its text ("lower / C") is in no record.
  Feedback lines can collide the same way: the same minute, titles "fix", "fix" and "fix 2".
  Related, and the same root cause: the project `Import` lists every trail file for `git rm` even when its record was skipped because the scope already held a different record under that ID. Git history keeps those files, so that case is integrity only (confidence: medium).
  Remediation: suffix with `for n := 2; used[id] > 0; n++` until the ID is free, and record the final ID in `used`. In `insertNew`, treat an in-batch duplicate key as an error to report. `filterStored` should follow the record that was actually stored (index, not key). A source whose record was skipped for a reason other than "already stored from this same source" gets `failed`.
  Test that fails without the fix: the probe's three-proposal fixture. Assert three distinct stored IDs, or `foo.md` reported as a problem and absent from `Sources`.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/brain/import.go:938-942`: `json.Indent` runs unbounded, and the `pretty.Len() > maxBody` check comes after the work.
  Measured on the scratch copy: one 20,048-byte feedback line (`[` nested 9,999 deep, under encoding/json's 10,000 depth limit, so `Unmarshal` accepts it) indents to 200,000,057 bytes. That cost 1,337 MB of allocation and 0.44 s.
  `maxLine` (export.go:29, about 6 MiB) lets one line carry about 300 such arrays side by side. The Indent output then grows to roughly 60 GB in a single call, which means an OOM kill of `fyr record import --global`. This is computed, not run, so as not to OOM the box.
  The file is written by the operator's own sessions (`feedback-log`), so the trigger is a prompt-injected or buggy session. Hence low.
  The test's "nested" line (300,000 deep) is refused by `Unmarshal`'s depth limit and never reaches this branch. Removing `|| pretty.Len() > maxBody` passes every test (mutation m3).
  Remediation: indent only a line whose upper bound `len(l) * (1 + 2*maxDepth)` fits `maxBody`, with `maxDepth` found by one scan of the line; otherwise store the raw line. Or always store the raw line.
  Test that fails without the fix: a feedback line of depth 9,999. Assert it is stored with the raw line as its body, and under a small allocation bound (`testing.AllocsPerRun` or `MemStats` delta).

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/brain/import.go:103-127` (`readRegular`), `:755-791` (`readMemoryStore`: `Lstat`, then `ReadDir(store)`, then `readRegular(store/name)`), `:220-235` (`readDocs`): finding 7's fix protects only the final path component.
  `O_NOFOLLOW` applies to the last component only. A directory (`.agents`, `.agents/memory`, `.agents/docs/plans`) swapped for a link after `guardExportPath` or `Lstat` has run is still followed. For the memory store, that imports another directory's memories into this scope and lists them for `rm`.
  The precondition is the one round 1 accepted for #7: a concurrent writer to the checkout. `TestReadRegular` pins only the final-component case.
  Remediation: `os.OpenRoot(top)` (Go 1.24, go.mod `go 1.24.4`), then read everything through the `*os.Root`, which refuses a link that escapes on any component. Note GO-2026-4970 (`os.Root.Open`, fixed in go1.25.12). The box's toolchain is go1.24.4 (see Checked), so upgrade it before relying on Root.
  Test that fails without the fix: swap `.agents/memory` for a link between `readMemoryStore`'s `Lstat` and its `ReadDir` (a test hook), and assert no record and a problem line.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/brain/import.go:129-140` (`ShellQuote`), `cmd/fyr/record.go:155-158`: the quoting is for the shell, but the list is for `git rm`, where a quoted word is still a glob pathspec and still an option.
  `'-rf'`, which `TestShellQuote` asserts and the doc comment claims as protection, still reaches git as an option. `*`, `?` and `[` inside quotes are git pathspec wildcards.
  `search.Printable` runs **after** quoting and turns a control character into `?`. A quoted `a\nb.md` therefore prints as `'a?b.md'`, a git wildcard that also matches `aXb.md`.
  `shellPlain` also admits a leading `=`, which zsh's EQUALS option expands.
  None of this is reachable today: every printed path starts with the docs root and a trail directory, every file under a trail directory is already on the list, and the docs root is the operator's own argument.
  Remediation: print `git rm --` with `GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1` (or `:(literal)` per path). Better, refuse at import a tracked trail path outside `[A-Za-z0-9._/-]`, which also removes the post-quote `?` rewrite. Drop `=` from the first-character class.
  Test that fails without the fix: `printImport` output for a tracked `plans/a?b.md` beside `plans/aXb.md` names only the first, literally.

- **[low / confidence: high]** Test gaps in the Outcome's claims. Each of these mutations passed every test on the scratch copy:
  - m3: the Indent cap removed (above).
  - m7: `checkRecord` removed from `readMemoryStore`, import.go:825. That check is load-bearing for a memory file near 1 MiB: the `"type: …\n\n"` prefix pushes the body over `maxBody`, and without the check `insertNew` fails the whole global transaction, which is round-1 #8's class.
  - m8: the file-count half of `budget.take` (`b.files < 0`) removed. `TestImportCapsTotalRead` lowers bytes only, although Outcome #6 names both caps.
  - Reading only: `TestImportGlobalBadEntriesAreProblems`' two 140-character proposals import as `PROPOSAL-ppp…` and `PROPOSAL-dream-ppp…`, which never collide, so the "room for `-N`" change (slug 120) is untested.
  Remediation: one test per gap, each validated by its mutation.

## Round-1 rows checked

Security report:
- #1 FIXED, verified. `realDay` combines `time.Parse` with `dateRe`. `checkRecord` runs the exported kinds through `parseLine` itself, in the dry run and again in `insertNew`. Removing `realDay` from `splitADRs` alone fails `TestImportBadDateLoads` through the `checkRecord` refusal (m6).
- #2 FIXED, verified. Removing the guard fails `TestImportGlobalRefusesASymlinkedAgents` (m1; `git ls-files` does not stop a symlinked path by accident, m1b). The linked-worktree trigger is closed because `readMemoryStore(scope)` guards the scope.
- #3 FIXED (`leftAlone` filter); residual in finding 1.
- #4 FIXED for the shell; residual in finding 4.
- #5 FIXED. Each case of `TestMemoryAddTitleRules` is independent, because a taken name is an UPDATE, not a refusal. The 640-byte line bound holds; the 25 KB total cap still fits about 40 maximum-length lines, which is by design.
- #6 FIXED for bytes; files untested (finding 5).
- #7 FIXED for the final component; residual in finding 3.
- #8 FIXED for long lines, failed sources and slug room; residual in findings 1, 2 and 5.

Reviewer report:
- `keep` keyed on `rel` (`TestImportCustomDocsRoot`), stored keys by scope (`TestImportStoresSameIDInTwoScopes`), and the dry run's `checkRecord` (runs before `return res`): confirmed by reading.
- The tracked-store refusal is confirmed by reading and `TestImportRefusesCommittedMemory`.
- The removed `loadLocked` constraint branch is safe. The load refuses a duplicate ID first (export.go:202), and `validID` binds each exported kind to its own prefix, never MEMORY-, FEEDBACK- or PROPOSAL-.

## Checked

- Secrets: none added in the range (grep of added lines); messages carry paths only.
- Injection: `ShellQuote` and `Printable` order (finding 4). `git` is called with fixed argv and `--` (`ls-files`); no shell is involved.
- Authz/authn: not applicable. The trust boundary is another project's checkout, covered by `guardExportPath` and the tracked-store refusal.
- Crypto: none touched.
- Dependencies: go.mod and go.sum unchanged in the range. `govulncheck ./...` reports 15 standard-library advisories, all of go1.24.4: both `/usr/bin/go` **and** `~/.local/bin/go` report go1.24.4 on this box, contrary to AGENTS.md's go1.27.2 note. They include GO-2026-6604 (`os`, fixed 1.26.9), newer than AGENTS.md's known list. These are toolchain issues, not this diff; upgrade the box's Go.
- GCP surface: none touched.

## Not examined

- `internal/memory/memory.go` and `memory_test.go` deletions were not read line by line, beyond the claim that `Root`/`Store` remain.
- `cmd/fyr/record.go` outside `printImport`.
- Callers outside the diff, per the dispatch.
- The 60 GB Indent figure is computed, not run.
- govulncheck under go1.27.2: no such toolchain was found on PATH.

## Outcome

Round 2 is the last round (context § Definition of Done step 2); the fixes below were read by the main agent, each with a test that failed with its fix mutated out.

| # | Finding | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `-N` suffix lands on an existing ID | FIXED: the suffix is tried until it names no ID the import already gave; `TestImportGlobalSuffixNeverCollides` (FOO.md, foo-2.md, foo.md → three records; fails with a single-try suffix) |
| 2 | `json.Indent` before its cap | FIXED: the line is stored as written, never indented; `TestImportGlobalStoresTheLineAsWritten` (failed before: the body was the 261-byte indented form of a 72-byte line) |
| 3 | a directory swapped for a link between check and read | REBUTTED: it needs a process writing the checkout (or `~/.config/fyr`) concurrently as the operator's own user, who can already read and write every file the import could be steered to; the same precondition as the store review's finding 3, rebutted there. `os.Root.Rename`-free reading through `os.Root` is possible on Go 1.24 but carries GO-2026-4970 before Go 1.25.12; revisit with the module's go line |
| — | `ShellQuote` words read as options or globs by `git rm` | FIXED: the list's heading says `git rm --literal-pathspecs --`; `TestRecordImport` asserts it |
| — | test gaps | FIXED: `TestImportCapsFileCount` (fails with the file half removed); the 120-character room is pinned by `TestImportGlobalBadEntriesAreProblems`, whose two names now agree past the cut (fails with 128); the Indent cap is gone with finding 2; the `checkRecord` call in `readMemoryStore` was unreachable after `normalize` and is removed (`insertNew` still checks every record) |
| — | toolchain go1.24.4 | LEFT: the operator's step, in the handoff (`~/.local/bin/go` dangles) |

title: Security review — brain-store (2026-10-25)
body:
# Security review — brain-store   (2026-10-25)

Range reviewed: 9e302f1..8bd25ed -- internal/brain cmd/fyr internal/trail internal/search (plus the helpers called: internal/harness WriteAtomic, internal/search printable/cleanSnippet/ftsQuery/dsn/prepareFiles, internal/trail Command/Roots)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

The worst problem: a cloned repository's committed `.agents/trail.jsonl` can exhaust memory in any `fyr record` verb, and in `fyr search <words>`, run inside the clone. `readTrail` reads up to 1 GiB into memory. Then `parseTrail` runs `bytes.Split`, which allocates a 24-byte slice header for every line before it skips blank ones. Measured on this box: a file of 100 MiB of newlines peaked at 2.5 GiB RSS, and that file packs to 101 KiB in git. At the 1 GiB cap the peak is about 25 GiB, which would trigger the OOM killer on most machines. Titles have no length limit, so a single valid record can also carry a title of hundreds of MiB. Our test with a 200 MiB title peaked at 2.5 GiB and left a 200 MiB `brain.db`. That row stays in the store of record and is printed by every `list` and `search`. The export path, the memory/feedback/proposal boundary (R8, D14) and the terminal filter held up under every trigger I tried. What remains is low severity: a check-then-use window on the export and load path (needs a concurrent local writer), match marks that stored text can spoof, and labels that blur where a record came from.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/brain/export.go:24` (`maxTrail = 1 << 30`), `internal/brain/export.go:127` (`bytes.Split(data, []byte("\n"))`), `internal/brain/export.go:79` (whole-file `io.ReadAll`): a planted trail.jsonl can exhaust memory.
  Trigger: commit `.agents/trail.jsonl` containing N MiB of `\n` (or a single line of N MiB). Any `fyr record list|get|add|edit` or `fyr search <words>` in that checkout (a read path, `sync`, `brain.go:132`; `Search`, `search.go:62`) then reads the whole file and splits it.
  Measured with a build of 8bd25ed in `.agents/scratch/sec-brain/`: 100 MiB of newlines gave peak RSS 2,533 MiB in 2.0 s. The git pack of that commit is 100.92 KiB. The cap allows ten times that size. A file of blank lines is also a *valid* empty trail, so the rows are deleted and nothing is refused.
  Why it is reachable: the threat model (a cloned repository is untrusted) and the context, which runs `search` at every session start in any project. The `maxTrail` comment's premise ("low enough that a planted file cannot exhaust memory") does not hold, because the parse amplifies the input about 12–25×.
  Remediation:
  - Stream the parse: `bufio.Reader` line by line, or `bufio.Scanner` with `Buffer(…, maxLine)`, where `maxLine` is about `6*maxBody + 4 KiB` (the JSON `\u` escape worst case). Hash through `io.TeeReader` into `sha256.New()`, so no whole-file copy and no slice-of-lines is ever built.
  - Reject an over-long line before `json.Decode`.
  - Lower `maxTrail` to what a real trail can reach (tens of MiB), or count records (`maxRecords`).
  - stdlib only, no dependency.
  Test that fails without the fix: `TestLoadBoundedMemory` writes 64 MiB of `\n` (and, separately, one 64 MiB line) into a fixture trail. It runs `List` and asserts that `runtime.MemStats.TotalAlloc` grew by less than, say, 4× the file size, or that a line over `maxLine` is refused with its line number before decode.

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/brain/export.go:166` (parseTrail title check) and `internal/brain/record.go:193` (`cleanTitle`): a title has no length limit, so it slips past the 1 MiB rule the body follows.
  Trigger: a trail line with a valid bug record and a 200 MiB `"title"`. Measured: `fyr record list` exits 0, peak RSS 2,560 MiB, and `brain.db` grows to 200 MiB. The title is FTS-indexed and printed in full by every `record list`, `list --all` and `search` hit.
  The store is a store of record and is never pruned (store.go:6), so the row stays after the clone is deleted. It also keeps appearing in `--global` searches and `list --all` from every other project.
  Remediation: cap the title in `cleanTitle` and in `parseTrail` (for example 512 bytes or 200 runes) and refuse longer ones with the line number. Optionally truncate it in `FormatLine` as `CleanSnippet` does.
  Test that fails without the fix: `TestLoadRefusals` gets a case `"long title"` with `strings.Repeat("a", 1<<20)` as title, expecting a refusal naming `line 1`. `TestBodyLimits` (or a new `TestTitleLimit`) gets `Add` with a title over the cap, expecting a usage error.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/brain/export.go:287-291` (guard, then `harness.WriteAtomic`), `internal/harness/apply.go:422-451`: there is a window between the check and the use on the export write.
  `guardExportPath` checks `.agents` and `trail.jsonl` with `Lstat`. `WriteAtomic` then runs `MkdirAll(.agents)`, `CreateTemp(.agents)` and `Rename` by path. If `.agents` is swapped for a symlink in between, the temp file and the rename land in the link's target, replacing a `trail.jsonl` anywhere the user can write. When `.agents` is absent at guard time, `MkdirAll` happily follows a symlink created afterwards.
  The content is this scope's exported rows only (memory is still excluded), and the attacker needs to write to the checkout concurrently. The code comment accepts this risk, and the search index has the same pattern.
  Remediation: open the checkout with `os.OpenRoot(top)` and do the mkdir, temp create and rename through the `os.Root` methods, which refuse a link that escapes the root. Go 1.24 has `OpenRoot`/`Root.OpenFile`/`Root.Mkdir`; `Root.Rename` needs Go 1.25+, so check that against the module's `go 1.24.4` line. Or open `.agents` with `O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW` and keep the fd for `CreateTemp`/rename (needs `unix.Renameat`, which is x/sys; the stdlib route is `os.Root`). Note GO-2026-4970 (os.Root.Open) on a Go older than 1.25.12.
  Test that fails without the fix: a hook variable in `exportLocked`, run between guard and write, that replaces `.agents` with a symlink to a second temp dir. Assert that `Add` refuses and that nothing appears in the second dir.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/brain/open_unix.go:15`: the load opens trail.jsonl without `O_NOFOLLOW`.
  The comment on `guardExportPath` (export.go:30-31) says the load must never read through a link, but the open only checks `Stat().Mode().IsRegular()`, which follows the link. If `trail.jsonl` is swapped for a symlink to any regular file the user can read, between the `Lstat` and the open, that file is read and parsed. Parse errors quote only a line number and one character, and a successful parse needs a valid trail, so I see no content leak. The claim in the comment is stronger than the code.
  Remediation: `os.O_RDONLY|syscall.O_NONBLOCK|syscall.O_NOFOLLOW` (stdlib `syscall`, unix only).
  Test that fails without the fix: a hook between `guardExportPath` and `openNonBlocking` that swaps in a symlink to a valid trail elsewhere. Expect a refusal (ELOOP), not a load.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/search/search.go:658-660` (`cleanSnippet`, called from `internal/brain/search.go:110`): stored text can spoof the match marks.
  FTS5 marks matches with `char(1)`/`char(2)`. `cleanSnippet` turns *every* \x01/\x02 into `»`/`«` before `printable`, and neither `parseTrail` nor `readBody` refuses those bytes.
  Confirmed: a loaded title and body holding `\x01mark\x02` printed `»mark«` in `fyr search zebra`, a search that did not match "mark". It is cosmetic, but it lets a crafted record fake what "matched" in output an agent reads.
  Remediation: refuse C0 controls other than `\t` and `\n` in titles and bodies, in `readBody`, `cleanTitle` and `parseTrail`. Or have `cleanSnippet` map stored \x01/\x02 to `?` first and then use marks that cannot occur in stored text.
  Test that fails without the fix: a `TestLoadRefusals` case with `\u0001` in the body, expecting `line 1`. Or a `TestSearchRecords` case asserting that a hit's snippet has no `»` around an unmatched word.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/brain/search.go:126-134` (`label`), `internal/brain/brain.go:132-146` (any read loads): search output does not say clearly where a record came from.
  Running `fyr search <words>` (or any `record` read) in an untrusted clone loads its trail into the machine-wide store permanently. With `--global` from any other project, those records print under `filepath.Base(scope)+":"`, so a clone at `~/x/styrman-harness` prints exactly like the real project.
  In a linked worktree of a trusted repository that has an untrusted branch checked out, the load replaces the *trusted scope's* exported rows with the branch's file. Until the main worktree next runs a verb, cross-project views attribute the branch's records to the trusted repository. This follows D21 and the shared scope. The security cost is misattributed text in output an agent reads.
  Remediation: print the full scope path in `search --global` labels, or disambiguate basenames that collide. Consider a `record forget --scope` (Phase 2) so a deleted clone's rows can be removed.
  Test that fails without the fix: two scopes with the same basename, one record each. `Search(Global)` labels must differ.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/brain/record.go:39-42`: the export filter `unexportedSQL` and the Go map `unexported` are two hand-kept copies of the R8/D14 boundary.
  Only `memory` is pinned by a test (brain_test.go:481-493). A future kind added to the map but not to the SQL string would be exported to a project's committed file.
  Remediation: build the SQL `IN` list from the map at init, or add a test that, for every key of `unexported`, inserts a row of that kind directly into a project scope and asserts that `exportLocked` leaves it out.
  Test: as described in the remediation; it fails today only if the copies drift, which is the point.

- **[low / confidence: low]** `cmd/fyr/main.go:100` and `internal/brain/export.go:64-80`: errors that are not refusals print without the filter.
  A non-refusal error from the brain package (an `os` error from `Lstat`/`open`/`WriteAtomic`, which carries the checkout path) prints raw as `fyr: <err>` on stderr. Refusals and `recordHits` go through `Printable`. A checkout path holding escape bytes (possible from a hand-extracted archive, not from `git clone`) would reach the terminal.
  Remediation: in `runRecord`'s `recordErr`, pass the default branch through `Printable` as well.
  Test: a `record list` run in a checkout whose directory name contains `\x1b`, with `.agents` unreadable (0000), asserting no ESC byte in the output.

## Checked

- **Secrets:** none in the diff. No secret is logged. The store directory is 0700 and the files 0600 (`PrepareDBFiles`), with symlinked or non-regular companions refused.
- **Injection:**
  - All SQL is parameterized. The only concatenations are the constants `unexportedSQL`, `openSQL` and `recordCols`.
  - FTS input is quoted by `FTSQuery`.
  - No record ID or title reaches a path or a shell.
  - git runs through `trail.Command`, with fsmonitor disabled and `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH` set.
- **Parsing (`parseTrail`):**
  - Each line is decoded as one object with `DisallowUnknownFields`, all seven keys required and trailing values refused.
  - Kind, ID, status and date are checked against bounded regexps, the body is capped at 1 MiB and must hold no NUL, and duplicates are refused.
  - Exported kinds cannot carry a `MEMORY-` ID, and memory, feedback and proposal kinds are refused, so a file cannot insert, overwrite or delete memory rows. The DELETE excludes the unexported kinds, and the `isConstraint` branch is unreachable.
  - The global scope `''` cannot be targeted from a file, because the scope comes from `trail.Roots`, not from the file.
  - `export_sha` is the SHA-256 of the exact bytes parsed, under BEGIN IMMEDIATE, so I found no desync that loses a write. A commit failure after the rename is healed by the next load (file wins).
  - Gaps: memory amplification and the title length (findings 1–2).
- **Terminal:** confirmed empirically. A loaded record with ESC/CSI/OSC-8, BEL, U+202E, U+2028, C1 U+009B, U+200B and a tag character printed every one of them as `?` in `record list`, `record get`, `list --all` and `search` hits and snippets. `get` keeps tabs, and CR prints as `?`. The only leak is the \x01/\x02 mark spoof (finding 5).
- **Authz/authn:**
  - The scope is resolved by `trail.Roots`: a linked worktree must be registered by the common dir, and the toplevel must be the working directory or a parent of it.
  - `feedback`/`proposal` are refused in a project and `memory` in the global scope.
  - `get`/`edit` are confined to the session's scope.
- **Crypto:** `crypto/sha256` is used as a change-detection checksum, which is stdlib used as designed. No hand-rolled primitive.
- **Dependencies:**
  - No new module; `modernc.org/sqlite` was already allowed for `internal/brain` by AGENTS.md (ADR-063).
  - `govulncheck` (`~/.go/bin/govulncheck ./...`) ran on **go1.24.4**, not the go1.27.2 that AGENTS.md documents. `~/.local/bin/go` is a dangling symlink to `~/sdk/go1.27.1`, which does not exist, so the shell falls back to `/usr/bin/go`.
  - Findings on go1.24.4: 15 standard-library advisories that the code reaches. One is GO-2025-3849 (database/sql `Rows.Scan`, a path the brain store uses) and one is GO-2026-4970 (os.Root.Open). All are fixed by upgrading the box's Go, not by code.
  - Not reached: 5 package and 42 module advisories.
  - There is no web/npm surface in this range.
- **GCP surface:** none in this range.

## Not examined

- The `internal/search` file-search path beyond the helpers named, and `search.Validate`.
- `internal/brain/brain_test.go` and `cmd/fyr/record_test.go`: grepped, not read.
- Phase 2 verbs (`record import`, the memory alias), which do not exist yet.
- The non-unix `openNonBlocking`: read, not run.
- The race findings (3, 4) are argued from the code; I did not reproduce them with a racing writer.
- The ~25 GiB figure at the 1 GiB cap is extrapolated from the 100 MiB measurement, not run.
- govulncheck was not run on a Go ≥ 1.25.12, because none is installed on this box.
- The `trail.Roots` core.worktree-to-a-parent case for a checkout delivered as an archive with its own `.git`: earlier audits covered it, and I did not re-review it.

Scratch used: `.agents/scratch/sec-brain/` (a probe repo verified with `rev-parse --absolute-git-dir`, a fyr build, an RSS script, a scratch `--home`); no source, test or config was changed.

## Outcome

Every finding fixed but 3, which is rebutted; each fix has a test that fails without it (run red first, 2026-10-25).

| # | Finding | Outcome | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | trail.jsonl read whole, `bytes.Split` amplifies | FIXED: the load streams (`readRecords` over a 64 KiB `bufio.Reader`, `ReadSlice`; blank lines cost nothing), the hash is streamed (`hashTrail`, `io.TeeReader` for the parse pass), a line over `maxLine` (6 MiB + 64 KiB) is refused before decode, the cap is 256 MiB and enforced while reading (`capped`), the export compares hashes instead of re-reading the file | `TestLoadBoundedMemory` (32 MiB of `\n`: 1,151 MiB allocated before, under 16 MiB after), `TestLoadRefusesAnOverlongLine`, `TestLoadRefusesAnOversizeFile` |
| 2 | no title cap | FIXED: 512 bytes in `cleanTitle` (usage error) and the load (refusal with its line); the import trims to it | `TestTitleLimit` |
| 3 | guard-then-`WriteAtomic` window on the export | REBUTTED: the race needs a process that can write the checkout concurrently, i.e. the operator's own user, who can already write any file the export could reach; what is written is this scope's own exported rows (memory, feedback and proposal never, finding 7). The search index carries the same accepted pattern. `os.Root.Rename` needs Go 1.25 and the module line is 1.24.4. Revisit when the module's `go` line reaches 1.25. | n/a |
| 4 | load opened without `O_NOFOLLOW` | FIXED: `O_RDONLY|O_NONBLOCK|O_NOFOLLOW` | `TestOpenNonBlockingRefusesASymlink` (fixture proven a symlink first) |
| 5 | `\x01`/`\x02` spoof match marks | FIXED: a C0 control other than tab and newline (and DEL) is refused in a body (`readBody`), a title (`cleanTitle`) and the load (`parseLine`); the import maps them to `?` | `TestControlCharactersRefused`; `TestRecordGetIsPrintable` now asserts the ESC refusal and keeps the output filter for C1, U+2028 and bidi |
| 6 | `--global` labels show the base name | FIXED: another project's hits are labelled with the full scope root. `record forget` not added: out of the plan's scope | `TestGlobalLabelsTellScopesApart` |
| 7 | `unexported` map and SQL kept by hand | FIXED: `unexportedSQL` is built from the map | `TestEveryUnexportedKindStaysOut` (mutation: SQL cut to one kind, the test failed on the leaked proposal row; restored, green) |
| 8 | non-refusal errors print unfiltered | FIXED: `recordErr` passes every other error through `Printable` | `TestRecordErrFiltersOtherErrors` |

Spec `specs/fyr/record.md` and `specs/fyr/search.md` updated in the same change. The govulncheck note (go1.24.4 because `~/.local/bin/go` dangles) is the operator's step already in the handoff's Next Steps.

title: Security review — v2.7.0-HEAD (2026-10-25)
body:
# Security review — v2.7.0-HEAD   (2026-10-25)

Range reviewed: commits v2.7.0..HEAD (git log v2.7.0..HEAD); the diff is git diff v2.7.0...HEAD

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

Worst so far: the first `fyr install` on a place that ran v2.7.0 deletes every file the old manifest lists under `~/.claude` (AGENTS.md, the CLAUDE.md stub, skills, agents, rules) with no check that the file still holds what sh-agent wrote. `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` is Claude Code's user-memory file, which Claude Code itself appends to; anything added there since the last v2.7.0 install is removed for good.

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/apply.go:126-147` (resync loop, reached by the ADR-062 shed described at `apply.go:20-24`) — stale manifest entries are removed with `os.Remove` after only an Lstat/symlink check; no content check. v2.7.0 dropped a foreign CLAUDE.md from the manifest (`KeepForeign`/`IsOurs`, removed in this range), but a stub that was ours at the last install and edited afterwards (Claude Code `#` / `/memory` writes to `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`) is still listed and is deleted. Also covers a hand-edited `~/.claude/AGENTS.md` or skill file. `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:89` documents the removal but not that edits are lost. Remediation: for the files under `.claude/`, remove only when the bytes still match what a v2.7.0 install wrote (for CLAUDE.md, the exact stub; for AGENTS.md, the old generated marker on line 1), otherwise keep and name the file with a `keep` line; or move them to a dated backup directory under the state dir instead of deleting. Add a test for an edited CLAUDE.md stub.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/dream/timer.go:315-332` with `cmd/fyr/main.go:825` — `ReplaceOldTimer` decides an old timer exists by FILE presence only, then `InstallTimer` runs `systemctl --user enable --now fyr-dream.timer` (or `launchctl bootstrap`). An operator who stopped the old timer with `systemctl --user disable --now sh-agent-dream.timer` (or `launchctl bootout`) but left the unit files has it switched back on by `fyr install`, and the nightly job then sends that machine's redacted project content to the model provider again — the one off-machine flow (R3's exception) re-enabled without the operator's word. Remediation: on Linux replace only when `systemctl --user is-enabled sh-agent-dream.timer` says enabled (on macOS when `launchctl print gui/<uid>/<label>` finds it loaded); otherwise remove the old files and print that no fyr timer was installed, with the `--install-timer` command.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `.gitignore` (lines removed in this range: `/.claude/`, `.claude/settings.local.json`) — the repo no longer ignores Claude Code's per-repo local settings, which can carry permission grants and env values. A `.claude/settings.local.json` exists in this checkout today; it is ignored only by this box's global `~/.config/git/ignore`, not on another machine. The global git rule (stage by name) makes a commit unlikely, not impossible. Remediation: keep the two ignore lines while any machine may still run Claude Code in this tree, or delete the file.

## Checked
- Release fetch/verify (`internal/harness/release.go`): only names changed — repo `github.com/kesokaj/fyr`, asset `fyr-<os>-<arch>`, marker `# fyr vX.Y.Z`. Tag validated as vX.Y.Z before argv, no sideways/backwards, capped reads, marker tag must equal the release tag, exact asset line with a 64-hex hash, duplicate-hash refusal, `WriteAtomic` of `~/.local/bin/fyr` only after the checksum. Unsigned by design (ADR-053), unchanged. Note (not a finding): the marker regexp's `\s*` after `#` also spans a newline (RE2 `\s` includes `\n`), pre-existing and harmless since the file comes from the same release.
- State-dir migration (`internal/harness/migrate.go`, `cmd/fyr/main.go:300-340`): one `os.Rename`, only when `~/.config/fyr` is absent and `~/.config/sh-agent` is a real directory; a symlinked old dir is refused, both present leaves both untouched; read-only verbs and dry runs only print a notice and read nothing. Verbs that migrate: install, sync, uninstall, adopt, index, search, dream (not dry run), update (not dry run, not --check), `memory add`, `metrics ingest`. Race between two fyr processes (03:00 timer plus a manual verb) ends in a rename error (ENOENT/ENOTEMPTY) or a rename onto an empty dir, not a crossed or deleted state; only the same account can write under `~/.config`. The moved dir keeps its old mode; install's `TightenConfigDir` still corrects it.
- Resync sweep containment (`apply.go`, `state.go:52-63`): manifest entries pass `filepath.IsLocal` at load; a symlink, or a path under a linked directory, is skipped; `pruneEmptyDirs` stops at home, `.claude`, `.gemini`, the agy root, `.config`, `.local`, `.local/bin`. Nothing can delete outside the home. The Lstat-then-Remove window is pre-existing and needs the same account.
- Dream timer (`internal/dream/timer.go`): new names `fyr-dream` / `com.fyr.dream`, per-home hash suffix kept, the quote/backslash/control-character refusal kept, an existing fyr unit with other text is refused, the old unit is removed only after the fyr one is installed. Bare legacy names under a non-real home are listed, never touched.
- Redactor move: the needle tables and `decoded` in `internal/redact/redact.go` are the same as v2.7.0 `internal/harness/report.go` apart from comments, the marker text and the dropped `File` field (diffed in `.agents/scratch/`). Every dream input (memory, feedback, trail, skills, metrics, agy transcripts) and every Dropped line goes through `scrub` → `redact.Redact`; feedback lines through `RedactJSONL` too.
- Off-machine flows: outbound process calls in the range are `gh release view/download` (fetch), `git pull --ff-only` (fetch), `go build`, and `agy` (the dream prompt on stdin, HOME a private copy). No `net/http` or `net` import in non-test code. The report path (git push to the feedback repository) is gone, along with `report.go`. Nothing else leaves the machine.
- Env rename: `FYR_REPO` and `FYR_CHILD` read; no non-test code reads `SH_AGENT_*`; `oldEnvNotices` names a set `SH_AGENT_*` and prints only the variable NAME, never its value.
- Secrets: added lines matching secret shapes are test fixtures (FAKEVALUE, AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE, fake PEM bodies); no secret-shaped path in the range.
- Crypto: `crypto/sha256` used for checksums and unit-name suffixes as designed; nothing hand-rolled.
- Dependencies: `go.mod` changes only the module path; no new module. `govulncheck ./...` (`/home/kesokaj/.go/bin/govulncheck`, go1.24.4): 15 reachable findings, all standard library (os, html/template, net/url, os/exec, database/sql on go1.24.4) — the known old-toolchain class, fixed by upgrading the machine's Go; no reachable module finding. No npm ecosystem in the range.
- Agent lint (`internal/harness/inventory.go`): the allow-list shrinks to `name, description, subagent, mainAgent, model, tools`; tools must be in `knownTools`; `agent.md` is read with `readRegular` (a symlinked file is refused) and a symlinked `agents/<name>` entry is refused as a non-directory; only `agent.md` deploys, so no other file in an agent directory reaches a home.
- Zip path: `internal/harness/zip.go` is unchanged in the range and carries no old-name literal; it does not use `readSums`, so the marker change does not reach it.
- Metrics: the new `internal/metrics/writer.go` writes SQL rows through parameterised `?` placeholders; no file creation, process or network call.
- GCP surface: none in the range.

## Not examined
- `cmd/fyr/main.go` beyond the migration dispatch (lines 290-340), `oldEnvNotices` and `installFiles`; the other verbs' wiring was not re-read.
- `internal/search` changes (`reconcile.go`, `search.go`, `store.go`, `dream.go` `inWorkspace`), `internal/memory/memory.go`, `internal/metrics` (`ingest.go`, `show.go`, `report.go`, `agy.go`) beyond the grep for outbound calls and file writes; `internal/dream/collect.go` beyond `collect`, `scrub` and `feedback`.
- Markdown content changed in the range (`context/AGENTS.md`, `agents/*/agent.md`, `skills/*`, `rules/session-sizing.md`) was not read for instructions that widen what an agent may do; `skills/google-catalog/scripts/refresh-catalog.sh` (4 lines) not read.
- Tests (`*_test.go`) were read only for `TestResyncShedsOldClaudeFiles` and `TestInstallStatusResyncUninstall`; no test was run. No mutation check of any finding.
- No live check of the GitHub side: whether `github.com/kesokaj/fyr` exists and is owned by the operator, and how a v2.7.0 binary's `update` behaves once the repository is renamed (the redirect and the `sh-agent-*` asset name), was not verified.
- `.claude/settings.local.json` in this checkout was not opened (only its ignore status checked).

## Round 2

Status: COMPLETE. Range: the uncommitted working tree over 881389a (`git diff`): fixes for round 1's findings plus the rename edits the coordinator named (repository URL, `FYR_RECALL`/`FYR_CORPUS` docs, agent body tool names).

Verdict: FINDINGS. The timer fix is correct for the case it targets and its test fails without it. One new low-severity defect: the probe reads any failure to ask as "turned off". Round 1's finding 1 is rebutted with evidence and documented; finding 3 is still open.

### Outcome of round 1's findings
- **Finding 1 (resync deletes edited `~/.claude` files): rebutted, accepted risk.** The fix is documentation only (`.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` § crossing: "No content is compared ..."). The rebuttal holds. In v2.7.0, `IsOurs` was `strings.HasPrefix(data, Marker)` (`git show v2.7.0:internal/harness/plan.go`), and `~/.claude/AGENTS.md` and the skills were never `KeepForeign`. So any listed file that kept the generated first line, which includes a stub Claude Code memory was appended to, would have been overwritten by the next v2.7.0 install. A file that lost that line was dropped from the manifest and stays. The loss is not new in this range. No code change; closed.
- **Finding 2 (old timer re-enabled): fixed.** `internal/dream/timer.go` `timerUnit.on()` runs `systemctl --user is-enabled --quiet <old>.timer` / `launchctl print gui/<uid>/<old label>` before anything else. A unit reported as off only has its files removed, and no fyr unit is written or started. With no manager on PATH the probe says on, so `InstallTimer` refuses and the old unit stays, as before. Verified as follows. The one caller (`cmd/fyr/main.go:825`) handles all four (old, replaced, dry-run) combinations, and the turned-off lines come before the replaced lines in the switch. No other reference to the old one-result signature remains (`grep ReplaceOldTimer` over the tree). `go test -run 'TestReplaceOldTimer|TestOneRepositoryName|TestReleaseBinaryWithoutCheckout' ./internal/dream/ ./cmd/fyr/` passes. A mutation in a scratch copy (`.agents/scratch/mut-r2`, `on()` forced to `return true`) makes `TestReplaceOldTimer/old_unit_turned_off:_its_files_go,_no_fyr_timer` fail. The probe runs on a dry run too; it is read-only, and the test pins that it is the only call.
- **Finding 3 (`.gitignore` dropped `/.claude/` and `.claude/settings.local.json`): open.** It is not in this round's diff (`git diff --stat -- .gitignore` is empty) and not rebutted. It needs a fix or a rebuttal in the report's Outcome.

### New findings
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/dream/timer.go:296-300` (`timerUnit.on`). `exec.Command(...).Run() == nil` takes every non-zero exit as "turned off". But `systemctl --user is-enabled` also exits non-zero when it cannot reach the user manager: an SSH session with no `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` or user bus, a container, a box without lingering. `launchctl print` likewise fails for reasons other than "not loaded". In that case an ENABLED old timer has its files removed by `remove()`, whose `disable --now` fails the same way. The `timers.target.wants/sh-agent-dream.timer` link is then left dangling, and install prints "which was turned off", which is false. This fails in the safe direction for data leaving the machine: nothing is sent, the nightly dream just stops. It is an integrity and honesty defect, not an exposure. Remediation: read the state rather than the exit code. Run `systemctl --user is-enabled` without `--quiet`; take only `disabled` (and `masked`) as off, `enabled` as on, and anything else, including an empty stdout or a bus error on stderr, as "cannot tell", which keeps the old unit and names it. For launchd, take only "Could not find service" (exit 113) as off. Add a fake manager that exits 1 with a bus error and assert the old files stay.
- Not a finding: an old unit that is enabled but stopped (`systemctl --user stop` only) counts as on and is replaced with `enable --now`. That starts it now rather than at the next login, the same consent the enabled state already records.

### Checked in round 2
- The rename edits: `cmd/fyr/main.go` adopt message and `internal/harness/repo.go` `errPlainCopy` now give `git@github.com:kesokaj/fyr.git`, pinned by `TestOneRepositoryName` against `harness.ReleaseRepo`. These are text only, with no new input path. Whether the GitHub repository `kesokaj/fyr` exists was not checked (no network call made).
- Agent bodies (`agents/{explorer,documentation,dreamer}/agent.md`): the tool names now written in the bodies (`grep_search`, `find_by_name`, `view_file`, `write_to_file`) are all in each agent's `tools:` list and in `knownTools`. `documentation` still has no `run_command`, which matches its "you have no shell". No body change widens what an agent may do.
- `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` and `local.md`: text only; the timer bullet matches the code's messages.

### Not examined in round 2
- `README.md`, `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md` and `skills/harness-audit/references/areas.md` diffs (the URL and `FYR_RECALL`/`FYR_CORPUS` doc edits): not read line by line; the test pins README's URL only.
- The full test suite and `-race` were not run, only the three named tests. The launchd probe was exercised only through the fake manager; no real `systemctl`/`launchctl` run.

## Outcome

Written by the main agent, 2026-10-25, in the Phase 5 commit of plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md`. Round 2 ran (a medium was reported) and is recorded above.

1. Resync deletes edited `~/.claude` files (medium) — **rebutted**: not a new loss. In v2.7.0, `IsOurs` is a prefix check on the marker line (`git show v2.7.0:internal/harness/plan.go`, line 202). An edited stub that kept its first line was overwritten by every v2.7.0 install (`git show v2.7.0:internal/harness/apply.go`, line 71). One without that line was kept and never listed in the manifest, so the resync never sees it. `deploy/remote.md` § What `fyr install` does at the crossing now says that no content is compared. Round 2 accepted the rebuttal.
2. Old timer re-enabled (low) — **fixed**: `internal/dream/timer.go` (`timerUnit.on`, `ReplaceOldTimer`, which now returns whether it replaced) and the `cmd/fyr/main.go` install messages. The test case "old unit turned off: its files go, no fyr timer" covers linux (`disabled`, `masked`) and darwin. Forcing `on()` to true fails it. Round 2 accepted the fix.
3. `.gitignore` lost the `.claude` lines (low) — **left: operator** — "Keep removed (Recommended)", the operator's answer in this session, 2026-10-25. Stage-by-name (global git rule) keeps the file out of a commit.
4. Round 2, the probe reads any failure as "off" (low) — **fixed**: `on()` returns false only when the manager's answer says off (`disabled` or `masked` from `systemctl --user is-enabled`, `Could not find service` from `launchctl print`). A missing manager, or any other failure, counts as on, and the replacement runs as it did before the probe. The new case "probe cannot tell: replaced as on" fails under the mutation that reads any failure as off. The operator chose "Fix, no round 3" at the cap (this session, 2026-10-25), and the verifier runs after the fix.

title: Security review — worktree (2026-10-25)
body:
# Security review — worktree   (2026-10-25)

Range reviewed: working tree — changed files: .agents/docs/deploy/remote.md cmd/fyr/crossing_test.go internal/harness/apply.go internal/harness/harness_test.go; untracked, not ignored: none; read the diff with git diff HEAD -- <files> and read each untracked file whole.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

Two low findings, no high or medium. The change makes it less likely that fyr deletes files: Install's resync and Uninstall now skip every old-manifest entry under `~/.claude/`, where they used to remove it. The worst gap is that the guard (`claudeFile`, `internal/harness/apply.go:371-377`) checks the prefix on the raw manifest string, while removal acts on `filepath.Join(home, rel)`, and Join cleans the path. So an entry that is not in canonical form but resolves into `~/.claude` misses the guard and is still removed. That breaks D32's promise ("fyr never removes them"). It is not a privilege boundary: only the user can write the manifest (`~/.config/fyr/state.json`), and that user can already delete those files. `LoadState`'s `filepath.IsLocal` filter (`internal/harness/state.go:58-64`) still keeps every removal inside the home, so the old containment boundary is unchanged.

**Is the boundary covered?** Yes, on the paths the brief named, for well-formed manifests: `TestResyncKeepsOldClaudeFiles` (uninstall --dry-run over the old manifest, install, a second install, a real uninstall) and `TestCrossingFromV270` (byte-for-byte keep, the symlinked entry, the keep line, sh-agent removed). Both pass under `-race`. Not covered: non-canonical entries (F1), the `saveOnError` path holding `.claude` entries (F2), a symlinked `~/.claude` directory, and a directory-valued entry.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/apply.go:372` — `claudeFile` runs `strings.HasPrefix(filepath.ToSlash(rel), ".claude/")` on the uncleaned entry, but `Install` (`:137`) and `Uninstall` (`:333`) remove `filepath.Join(home, rel)`, which is cleaned. Entries that resolve into `~/.claude` but do not start with `.claude/` pass `filepath.IsLocal` and miss the guard, so the resync or uninstall removes the file:
  - `./.claude/AGENTS.md`
  - `.gemini/../.claude/CLAUDE.md`
  - `.Claude/...` on macOS's case-insensitive filesystem

  The reverse case, `.claude/../.local/bin/x`, is kept: the safe direction, but still a mismatch. fyr's own writer stores canonical `f.Rel`, so this needs a hand-edited or foreign manifest. That is why the severity is low; the cost is the D32 data-preservation guarantee, not escalation. Remediation:
  - Test the first element of `filepath.Clean(rel)`, compared with `strings.EqualFold` on darwin; or canonicalise entries once in `LoadState` next to the `IsLocal` filter.
  - Add a test case per shape above, red before the fix.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/apply.go:41-61` (`saveOnError`) — when a write fails, or when the sh-agent removal fails at `:147`, the manifest is saved as a union of every old entry still on disk, and that union includes the `.claude` entries. So "they leave its manifest" (`apply.go:24-25`, `remote.md:89`) does not hold on the error path, and `Status` (`:241-249`) keeps reporting them as `stale`. Removal stays safe: both removers check `claudeFile` first. This is a correctness and documentation gap, not exploitable. Remediation: skip `claudeFile` entries when building the union, and add a test with a forced write failure over a manifest that holds `.claude` entries.

## Checked
- **Secrets:** none in the diff, the tests or the doc. Output lines print only counts and relative paths.
- **Injection / path:** manifest entries are the only input. `LoadState` drops non-local entries, and removal uses `Lstat` and refuses symlinks and paths under a link (`underLink`). The one gap is canonical form in the new guard (F1). A TOCTOU between `Lstat` and `Remove` already existed, inside a single-user home; not raised.
- **Authz/authn:** not applicable. A local CLI acting on the invoking user's home.
- **Crypto:** none touched, nothing hand-rolled.
- **Dependencies:** no new module; only a stdlib `strings` import was added.
  - govulncheck ran with the shell's go1.24.4 (`/usr/bin/go`); the go1.27.2 SDK at `~/.local/bin/go` that AGENTS.md names is not on this box.
  - It reports 15 stdlib advisories the code reaches. All come from the old toolchain (e.g. GO-2025-3849, fixed in go1.24.6). None comes from this diff, and the fix is upgrading the machine's Go, never pinning it in go.mod (ADR-029).
  - It also reports 5 in imported packages and 42 in required modules that the code does not reach.
  - npm audit: no npm ecosystem in scope.
- **GCP surface:** not touched.
- **Past bugs:** BUG-128 (early return skips the manifest) and BUG-129 (installer follows symlinks) are respected. The new guard sits before the symlink check, and a symlinked `.claude` entry is kept either way.

## Not examined
- Mutation check: I did not confirm that the new tests fail with the `claudeFile` guard removed, because the review never edits source.
- The full `go test -race ./...` suite: only the two changed tests ran (`TestResyncKeepsOldClaudeFiles`, `TestCrossingFromV270`, plus the `TestInstall*`/`TestUninstall*` names matched).
- govulncheck under go1.27.2: not available on this box.
- `cmd/fyr/main.go` status and drift output for the kept entries in the error-path state of F2.
- The migration code that moves `~/.config/sh-agent`: not changed and not re-read.

## Outcome

Written by the main agent, 2026-10-25, in the Phase 5b commit of plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md` (D32).

1. `claudeFile` tests the raw entry, not the cleaned path it removes (low) — **fixed**: `internal/harness/apply.go` `claudeFile` cleans the entry and compares its first element without case. `TestResyncKeepsOldClaudeFiles` now holds the entries `./.claude/rules/unclean-a.md` and `.gemini/../.claude/rules/unclean-b.md`, and it failed with both files deleted before the fix.
2. `saveOnError` puts the old `.claude` entries back into the manifest (low) — **fixed**: the union now skips `claudeFile` entries. `TestInstallFailureKeepsClaudeFilesOutOfTheManifest` fails with the guard removed (mutation run) and passes with it.

Round 2 skipped: no finding was medium or higher, every fix has a test that fails without it, and the verifier runs after the fixes (`review` Step 4). Not covered, as the report says: a symlinked `~/.claude` directory, which the existing `underLink` rule already keeps.

title: Review — cold read of the fyr eval plan (2026-10-26)
body:
# Review — cold read of the fyr eval plan (2026-10-26)

Range reviewed: `PLAN-2026-10-26-0659-plan-fyr-eval-the-antigravity-run-kit-as-a-verb` (a plan record, no diff), read with its recon `PLAN-2026-10-26-0659-recon-fyr-eval-2026-10-26` and the surfaces it names: `.agents/kit/agy-rel/run.sh`, `.agents/kit/kit-preamble.sh`, `cmd/fyr/main.go` (verbs, run, writesState), `internal/harness/repo.go` (ResolveSource), `internal/metrics/ingest.go`, `internal/brain/{brain,export}.go`, `internal/trail/trail.go` (Roots), `internal/dream/run.go` (callWithin), `REQUIREMENTS.md` R0, R3, R6, R8, R10 and Non-goals, `GUIDE-skill-matrix`.

Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: design needs revision; implementation not ready

Worst first: the plan's own default case cannot pass. The default fixture is the harness checkout, step 4 and the sandbox wrapper load that checkout's trail into `SB/.config/fyr/brain.db`, and that trail holds the literal `-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----` (checked: 2 hits in `.agents/scratch/home-trail/.config/fyr/brain.db`, a store loaded from this repo). Safety check d, ported with the preamble's content patterns, would FAIL every row on it. The kit avoided this on purpose (`run.sh:177-181`). Beyond that, the install step (G1) has no decided cwd or tree, the same-group process kill in step 10 disables the leftover-process check the plan claims to port (G3), and Phase 2 cannot run its own E2E under D3 (G7).

Counts: 17 gaps (G1-G17), 5 scope items (S1-S5), 14 questions (Q1-Q14), 6 BLOCKING.

## Gaps

- **G1 [high] Install source, cwd and env are undecided (step 7, D9).** For a development build, `ResolveSource` takes `--repo`, then `$FYR_REPO`, then the working directory and its parents, then the home's recorded path (`internal/harness/repo.go:58-91`). For a release binary it takes the embedded harness and REFUSES `--repo` and `$FYR_REPO` (`repo.go:36-48`). Step 7 names no cwd, no default for `Options.Repo`, and no env for the subprocess. If cwd is the clone (the natural reading of the other steps), a demo fixture holds no harness and every row fails `install`. If cwd is the project root, "runnable on any project" holds only for harness checkouts. The kit's default was the checkout holding the kit (`run.sh:28,208`, `INSTALL_FROM`); D9 says `--repo` "replaces" it but not what the default is. A dev build also installs the dirty working tree (rebuilt by `Reinstall`, `repo.go:287-305`), while the fixture is HEAD and the record names only HEAD (the Testing record section), so the harness under test is not the commit the record names. An inherited `FYR_REPO` or `FYR_CHILD` in eval's env reaches the install unless the plan sets it.
- **G2 [high] Check d fails every row on the default fixture.** Evidence above. The preamble's pattern `-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----` (`kit-preamble.sh:130`) reads `brain.db` (not ELF or Mach-O, so not skipped). The plan ports "the same name, path and content patterns" and says nothing about the store the plan's own steps 4 and 7 put in SB. The kit kept the harness trail out of KIT_HOME for this (`run.sh:177-181`: the matrix was printed from a store under RUN). Decide: exclude `SB/.config/fyr/*.db` from the scan, or keep the harness trail out of SB, or run default-fixture rows from a trail without those strings. Also the `resume` row (D14, default fixture) hits it first.
- **G3 [high] The step 10 group kill removes the leftover-process detection (BUG-163), and the verify fixture does not produce the condition.** The `callWithin` pattern the plan mirrors calls `killGroup()` unconditionally after `cmd.Wait()` (`internal/dream/run.go`, the `killGroup()` before the deadline check). So a server the agent starts in agy's process group is SIGKILLed before step 15 and the row passes; only a child that left the group (`setsid`, `Setpgid` of its own) is seen by check e. The kit failed the row for any leftover (`kit-preamble.sh:179-215`, run under `timeout --foreground`, no group kill). The Verification fixture "the fake can ... leave a sleeping child behind" is refused by this path unless the child calls `setsid`: the plain `sleep &` child is killed at step 10 and check e's test would pass with check e removed. Decide: record "group members killed" as a failure reason (restores the kit's verdict), or accept the narrower check and say so in the spec; either way the fixture must name `setsid`.
- **G4 [high] "Ported as they are" is false for rows whose prompt or setup is shell.** `prompt` is a literal cell, but `dispatch-changelog` builds it with `$(date +%F-%H%M)` (`run.sh:78`), `inject-changelog` likewise (`:132`), `agent-dreamer` interpolates `$M` (`:120`), and the `retro` and `agent-dreamer` seeds use `$KIT_CLONE` and `$KIT_HOME` (`:107,114,201`). The `setup` and `check` environment lists `SB`, `OUT`, `OUT2`, `FIXDIR` and not a clone variable (`$PWD` would work but is not named). The plan must decide whether prompts are expanded by bash, or setup writes the prompt to a file, or those rows are rewritten at port time. Phase 2's `--list` verify ("same agent and wide flags") does not exercise any of it.
- **G5 [medium] The cell grammar does not parse the rows it ports.** `GUIDE-skill-matrix` has five columns (id, base, extra, prompt, check), not seven. Its `retro` and `handoff` check cells are a backticked check followed by prose, "(changed 2026-10-25: ...)" (the matrix rows 36 and 38). `run.sh:190-192` strips the note ("handed whole to bash, the backticks ran the check as a command substitution"). The plan's rule is "one surrounding pair of backticks is stripped" with no note handling, so the check becomes the whole cell. The `extra` column (`--add-dir`) disappears with no D-row (`run.sh` never passed it, so this is a drop, not a regression, but it is unrecorded).
- **G6 [medium] The `resume` row is not a setup cell (D14).** Step 4 runs `record list --home SB` before setup, which creates `brain.db`; D14's `rm -f "$SB/.config/fyr/brain.db"*` runs at step 5; then step 7's install (and the wrapper) may recreate it. The kit asserted the absence after install (`run.sh:217`) and kept `records-before.txt` empty by skipping the list (`:53-54`). Neither the assertion nor the empty-file behaviour is in Steps 1-17. D14 also pins the check to "the plan that is open at the time of the port"; that row fails when the plan closes.
- **G7 [high] Phase 2 cannot run its E2E under D3.** D3 refuses when `GUIDE-eval` differs from HEAD. The harness's `GUIDE-eval` is created in Phase 2 and Phase 2 is "one commit" (rule 3), but its `fyr eval --list`, E2E 1, 2 and 3 run inside Phase 2 before that commit. Every `fyr eval` in the phase exits 2 with "uncommitted changes". Also unspecified: whether `--list` runs the HEAD comparison; and the case where `trail.jsonl` or the record is absent from HEAD (no commits, untracked export, a new record), where `git show HEAD:` fails: not in the Failure-modes table, the message "has uncommitted changes" would be wrong for it.
- **G8 [medium] `brain.ParseTrail(io.Reader)` wrapping `readRecords` drops the size cap.** The cap and the refusal text come from `ReadTrail` (`export.go:102-113`, `capped{left: maxTrail}`); `readRecords` (`export.go:190`) only bounds one line. `git show HEAD:.agents/trail.jsonl` is unbounded, and the verify clause "same records and the same refusals as `ReadTrail`" cannot hold for an over-size file. `parseTrail([]byte)` already exists (`export.go:183`); say which one the new function wraps and cap the reader.
- **G9 [medium] Guard order contradicts the failure table and E2E 3.** Steps 1-2 create the sandbox directory and clone; guards a-c run at step 6. The table and E2E 3 say a home inside a checkout is refused "before row 1" with "nothing created". Check b is "`git rev-parse --git-dir` in the clone's parent", which needs that parent to exist; for a refusal before creation it must walk to the nearest existing ancestor, which the plan does not say. Check a "after resolving symlinks" has the same dependency on directories not yet made. Refusal precedence among the exit-2 rows (not a checkout, no `GUIDE-eval`, HEAD differs, BUG-106, token, `agy`) is unstated; E2E 3 expects the BUG-106 message and would get D3's message on a dirty tree.
- **G10 [medium] Ingest placement is stated twice, differently.** Steps 1-17 list step 17 (ingest) per row and say its error "makes the invocation exit 1"; the Code shape and Phase 1 put ingest in `cmd/fyr` after `Run` returns, in row order. They agree on the effect but not on who owns it, and a `Run` that returns an error mid-way (SIGINT, row 2 of 3) leaves rows 1 and 3 unstated: does cmd ingest rows 1-2, and with what outcome for row 2 (`interrupted` is a FAIL, D6 says ingest as `fail`)?
- **G11 [medium] R0, R3 and Non-goals are read, not decided.** The plan's REQUIREMENTS list says R0 holds because eval drives "a separate sandboxed CLI". R3's exception for the dreamer says it "runs the CLI with no tools"; eval runs it with tools and with `command(*)` plus `trustedWorkspaces` grants for `wide` rows. REQUIREMENTS Non-goals: "Editing any vendor setting: the harness is files in the customization directories, nothing else (ADR-062)"; eval writes `settings.json` `permissions.allow` (an Antigravity vendor setting) into a sandbox HOME. AGENTS.md says no permission key and cites ADR-056/056a ("the operator's permission mode decides what runs unprompted"). None of these is listed or answered; D4 edits R8 only. The operator's approval covers an R8 text, not these readings. Put each in ADR-065 and in the approval request.
- **G12 [medium] Trust model of the suite is unstated.** `setup` and `check` are bash from the project's committed `GUIDE-eval`, run as the operator's uid with absolute paths to the real home reachable; `--fixture` is any repo. D3 pins the commit, not the trust. A cloned project's suite is code execution on `fyr eval`. The spec should say so (and the security reviewer in Done should be told it is by design, not found).
- **G13 [medium] D11's justification points the wrong way.** "A superset cannot turn a PASS into a FAIL": the agent check FAILS a row when the count is 0 (`run.sh:245-247`). Widening the search to `*.db-wal` can only turn a FAIL into a PASS (a false pass), the unsafe direction. A1 (Phase 1) compares only the `.db` files of two kept sandboxes (no `-wal` there, checked), so the WAL addition is untested. Either drop the WAL or show a run where only the WAL holds the bytes.
- **G14 [medium] E2E 1 is not deterministic and names the kit's workflow.** "The same three rows through run.sh on the same commit give the same verdicts": one flaky agent run makes the criterion fail with no tie-break. `run.sh` refuses a row whose `runs/<row>` exists (`:33`), and `~/sandbox/agy-rel/homes` already holds prior runs of these rows (`lane-reviewer-p1`, `project-memory-5`); the kit needs `AGY_TAG`, which the plan puts Out of eval and does not mention for the comparison run. The metrics half ("K >= 1") checks that ingest ran, not the `outcome`/pass^k claim in S3.
- **G15 [low] Kit behaviours dropped without a D-row (D5 asks for them).** `KIT_ASSERT_GREP` and `KIT_ASSERT_COMMIT` (SHA-only hardening, BUG-157; `kit-preamble.sh:60-84`; recon O8 raised it and nothing answers it), `KIT_BIN`, the before/after listing of the real config, the preamble's three-line proof output. `STYRMAN_SKIP_CRED_PULL=1` rides in the env allowlist (`run.sh:221`) and nothing in this repository reads it (grep: only `run.sh`); the plan cites "the allowlist of `run.sh:220-222`" without naming its variables, so a first pass cannot write the spec's list.
- **G16 [low] Docs clauses.** `uninstall` leaves `<home>/.config/fyr/eval/` (conversation databases, setup output) by omission; R4's "easy on and off" and the `uninstall` usage text are not in any task's `docs:` clause. `brain.ParseTrail` (a new exported function) has no spec row (`SPEC-fyr-record`). `internal/check/check_test.go:179,283` and `internal/check/specs_test.go:92` use `.agents/kit/*.sh` as fixtures and are not in Phase 3's `fyr search --refs .agents/kit/` scope (a test fixture string, but the claimed "no tracked file names `.agents/kit/`" would be false).
- **G17 [low] Exit codes and duplicates.** `fyr eval a a` makes the second sandbox collide ("exists", exit 2) after row 1 ran, against "exit 2 for a refusal before any row ran". macOS O1's default (`ps -axww -E ... HOME=<SB>`) is asserted for a platform nobody has run, and R10 (one behaviour on both OSs) is met by a printed gap line; that is acknowledged in Open O1 and left for the operator.

## Scope (built beyond the request in `## Why`)

The request: the kit as a verb, runnable on any project, results stored as records, compared over time. D1 names items by number; I could not read `.agents/scratch/eval-scope/scope-2026-10-26-0638.md`, so each item below is a gap unless the operator's list covers it.

- **S1** `--list` (a second command shape; no D-row says who asked).
- **S2** `--fixture DIR` (a second source of "the project"; the Why says "any project", which cwd already gives; no D-row).
- **S3** The step 3 migration of an old `.agents/docs` fixture clone into the shipped binary: it exists for the demo fixture and for the sqlite-trail transition (A4, O2), a one-time change that Phase 3 itself retires by rewriting rows. Shipping it in every release binary is a surface for one fixture.
- **S4** The `grants` column with `wide: <reason>` and the fixed named allow list (`run.sh:212`) as code; the Why does not name per-row permission modes. (Kit had it; ported, but unowned by a D-row for the shipped binary.)
- **S5** `Options.Now`, `Self`, `RealHome` seams are test seams, fine; the macOS `procs_other.go` implementation is built on an unverified default (G17). Candidate to ship Linux-only with a printed gap until verified, and write `procs_other.go` after the Mac check.

## Questions (a first-pass implementer would have to ask)

- **Q1 BLOCKING** (G1) In which directory and with which `--repo`, env, and `FYR_*` variables does `<self> install --home SB` run? What is `Options.Repo`'s default?
- **Q2 BLOCKING** (G2) Does check d scan `SB/.config/fyr/*.db`? If so, how does a default-fixture row ever pass?
- **Q3 BLOCKING** (G3) After the group kill at step 10, is a same-group straggler a failure (as BUG-163 required) or silently killed? Which syscall does the test fixture use to leave a child behind?
- **Q4 BLOCKING** (G4) Is a `prompt` cell expanded (bash, `$(date)`, `$M`) or literal? Which variable names do `setup` and `prompt` see for the clone?
- **Q5 BLOCKING** (G7) When is `GUIDE-eval` committed relative to Phase 2's one commit, and does `--list` take the HEAD comparison? What happens when the record is absent from HEAD?
- **Q6 BLOCKING** (G6) How does `resume` start from a home with no `brain.db` when step 4 loads one and install may recreate it? Where does the post-install absence assertion (`run.sh:217`) live?
- **Q7 NON-BLOCKING** (G9) Are guards a-c a pre-flight before row 1 (default I would take: yes, and E2E 3 requires it), and in which order do the exit-2 refusals fire?
- **Q8 NON-BLOCKING** (G5) Does the cell grammar keep a trailing note after the backticked check, or are the two matrix rows with notes edited at port time?
- **Q9 NON-BLOCKING** (G10) Does cmd ingest the rows that finished when `Run` returns an error or an interrupt, and with what outcome for the interrupted one?
- **Q10 NON-BLOCKING** (G8) `ParseTrail` wraps `readRecords` or `parseTrail`, and does it cap the reader like `ReadTrail`?
- **Q11 NON-BLOCKING** (G13) Is `*.db-wal` in or out of the agent search?
- **Q12 NON-BLOCKING** (G15) Which environment variables are in the allowlist, and are `KIT_ASSERT_*` and `STYRMAN_SKIP_CRED_PULL` dropped on purpose?
- **Q13 NON-BLOCKING** (G11) Does the operator's approval of D4 also cover R3, Non-goals and ADR-056 readings (ADR-065 text)?
- **Q14 NON-BLOCKING** (S1-S3) Did the operator ask for `--list`, `--fixture` and the in-binary migration?

## Criteria applied to the plan

1. Dead code: not applicable to a plan; one note, `STYRMAN_SKIP_CRED_PULL` is carried into new code with no reader in the repository (G15).
2. Flow tracing: fails. G1, G2, G3, G6, G7, G10 are broken connections between steps, tests and stated outcomes.
3. Standards conformance: fails on describing text and requirements: G11 (R0/R3/Non-goals), G16 (restatements of `.agents/kit/`), and the `review-standards` §8 rule that a test sets up its condition (G3).
4. Directory layout: pass; `internal/eval` and `cmd/fyr/eval.go` match AGENTS.md § Layout. The new package must also be added to the Layout list (the plan's AGENTS.md edits name rules 1, 4, :56, :76, Release, not the `internal/eval` line).
5. Simplicity: one item, S3 (migration in the binary), plus S1/S2 unowned flags. No new dependency (D10) and no hand-rolled auth or crypto; the credential scan is pattern matching, and the token is linked, not read.
6. Decoupling: mostly sound (eval does not import SQLite, ingest sits in cmd). `ParseTrail` in `brain` and the exported-for-eval surface are small. `fakeAgy` is in `internal/dream`'s test file (unexported), so `internal/eval` copies it; fine, state it.

## Not examined

- `.agents/scratch/eval-scope/scope-2026-10-26-0638.md` (D1's item list; not read, so S1-S5 may be covered there).
- `internal/harness/catalog_test.go:1667-2170` (the kit tests the plan ports) and `:656-664`: only the glob and the first test header were seen; I did not check the ported cases against the plan's Phase 1 list.
- `skills/google-catalog`, `SPEC-fyr-delivery`, `GUIDE-testing`, `GUIDE-fyr-matrix`, ADR-063, the BUG records named in Why: not read; line citations to README (`:59`, `:103-110`), AGENTS.md (`:56`, `:76`) and `skills/review/SKILL.md:64` were checked and match.
- `internal/metrics` pass^k semantics (`PassK`) beyond `ingest.go:65-115`; `metrics show --label` output was not run.
- Real `agy` behaviour (`--mode accept-edits`, `--print-timeout`) and macOS `ps -E`: not run (dispatch forbids `agy`; no Mac).
