title: Review — cold read of the code-modularity plan (2026-10-26)
body:
# Review — cold read of the code-modularity plan (2026-10-26)

Range reviewed: record PLAN-2026-10-26-modularity (read in full from `.agents/scratch/agents/plan-modularity-coldread.md`). Surfaces read: `rules/code-modularity.md`; ADR-066; all audits under `.agents/scratch/modularity/` (INDEX, main, brain-import, search-search, search-reconcile, metrics-show, dream-run, tests); scratch tools `.agents/scratch/declmove/main.go`, `.agents/scratch/declsum/main.go`; `cmd/fyr/main_test.go:1433` (`TestOneRepositoryName`), `cmd/fyr/search_test.go:88` (`TestUsageMatchesDocComment`), `cmd/fyr/recall_test.go` (part); source heads of the six files to split (import blocks, var/const groups, method names, detached comments checked with grep/awk); spec `Code:` spans for all current specs; `fyr check` run read-only (0 findings today); bug list.

Status: COMPLETE

Counts: G1-G9 (9 gaps), S1-S2 (2 scope items), Q1-Q9 (9 questions: 3 BLOCKING, 6 NON-BLOCKING).

## 1. Gaps

- **G1 (high).** The plan's move tool cannot do what the blueprints ask, and the plan's own stop rule fires on the first use. `declmove` keys a declaration by name and panics `decl %v split across targets` when one declaration's names map to two targets (`.agents/scratch/declmove/main.go`, the loop that sets `t`). Three blueprints split a grouped block:
  - Phase 2: `internal/brain/import.go:61-72` is ONE `var (...)` holding `bugFile…indexRow` (→ `import_classify.go`), `pathRef`, `idRef` (→ `import_docs.go`) and `slugBad` (→ classify). `maxImportBytes`/`maxImportFiles` at 78-81 is a second block, and the audit sends it to `import_guard.go`.
  - Phase 4: `internal/search/reconcile.go:26-` is ONE `const (maxFileBytes, binarySniff, gcAge, touchEvery)` under one doc comment; the audit sends the first two to `config_view.go` and keeps the last two in `reconcile.go`.
  - Phase 6: `internal/dream/run.go:26-30` is ONE `const (cliTimeout, killGrace, keepFailed)`. The audit contradicts itself: "run.go (stays) A consts" against "agy_exec.go … plus cliTimeout, killGrace" and "run_files.go … keepFailed".
  
  Plan Scope says "whole-declaration moves" and "a declaration the compiler wants elsewhere means stop and ask", but the compiler does not want these elsewhere; the blueprint does. No D-row decides between (a) keeping the whole block in one file, which deviates from the audit's file contents, and (b) hand-splitting the group, which breaks byte-for-byte and makes `declsum` unequal (it hashes per GenDecl). Phases 2, 4 and 6 cannot start without this.
- **G2 (high).** The proof does not cover what the tool can lose. `declmove` copies only a declaration plus its attached doc comment; a comment not attached as `Doc` is dropped silently from both source and target. `declsum` hashes only declarations, so the sets still match. Verified instance: `internal/harness/catalog_test.go:24-31`, a detached block that documents `CATALOG_DIR` and `CATALOG_WRITE=1`, which `skills/google-catalog/scripts/refresh-catalog.sh:318` depends on. My awk scan found no other top-level detached block in the 16 files. The claim "byte for byte … equal sets" is therefore false assurance for Phase 7. Also not hashed: the package clause, build tags, the import block (source head is kept only in the source file; targets get a bare `package X`), and file mode.
- **G3 (high).** A living spec carries a path:line that the Phase 1 split breaks, against the plan's claim that the audits found none. `SPEC-fyr-check` (status current) cites `cmd/fyr/main.go:171` as the example of a `path:N` reference. `main.go` shrinks to about 127 lines, so `fyr check` rule `line` (`internal/check/docs.go:183`, "has N lines") will report it. The Phase 1 clause "any spec it flags re-read and re-stamped" covers `spec-stale`, not a `line` finding that needs the spec's text edited. The main audit never read the spec bodies (its "Not determined").
- **G4 (medium).** The `fyr check` verify cannot produce the condition it claims. `spec-stale` counts commits to a spec's `Code:` span after the spec's own commit (`SPEC-fyr-check` § rule (b)). Phase Verify runs before the phase commit, so the count is 0 and `fyr check` exits 0 even where the commit will make a spec stale. The plan also names no spec. Facts from the `Code:` lines: `SPEC-fyr-record` is `internal/brain` (a directory, tests included) → stale after Phases 2 and 7; `SPEC-fyr-eval` is `internal/eval/` → stale after Phase 7; `SPEC-fyr-check` names `cmd/fyr/check.go` only (Phase 1 does not touch it); the dream, metrics, search and delivery specs have no `Code:` line. The plan's Risks line ("a spec whose `Code:` span names a split file") has the trigger wrong: it is any commit under a named directory. Ordering (code commit, THEN re-read and `fyr record edit --status current`, then a commit that carries the new line) is not stated, and the re-stamp commit is not in any Checkpoint.
- **G5 (medium).** The recall corpus is not in the plan, though the audit saw it. `cmd/fyr/testdata/recall.tsv:36,38,39` name `cmd/fyr/main.go` as gold for "every file that says …" drift questions, and `recall_test.go` computes gold with `git grep -F`. The phrase "No vendor setting is read or written" is at `main.go:883`, inside `runInstall`'s cluster H, so it moves to `verb_install.go` and gold row 39 (and possibly 38) goes wrong. I did not check the recall threshold, so I cannot say whether the test fails or only lowers a score. Phase 1 has no clause for it; the audit left it "unverified". Phase 4 touches `internal/search/testdata/recall.tsv` territory only if gold names the split files (not checked).
- **G6 (medium).** `TestOneRepositoryName` wording is wrong. The plan says the file list "gains" the file that receives the clone URL. The test (`main_test.go:1433-1454`) requires each listed file to contain `git@github.com:<name>.git`. The only URL in `cmd/fyr` non-test code is in `runAdopt` (`main.go:866`, cluster H → `verb_install.go`); `usage` does not contain it. Leaving `cmd/fyr/main.go` in the list makes the test fail (`does not give the clone URL`). The entry must be replaced, as the audit says; "gains" would leave a red test. The plan should also say the replace is in the same commit as the move.
- **G7 (medium).** The plan departs from the rule it executes without a decision. `rules/code-modularity.md` item 5 says "extract one file at a time, running build, typecheck, and test verification after each step". The plan verifies once per phase, so Phase 1 is 12 files, Phase 7 is about 55 new files across six packages, with `cmd/fyr` at about 13 minutes under `-race`. Each audit gives a per-step order with a gate after each step; the plan drops it with no D-row. D1 approves the audit "as plan", so the audits' orders are arguably in force, but the plan's own Verify text says otherwise.
- **G8 (low).** Stale-claim and unchecked assumptions. (a) Risks says the "open `fyr eval` plan's `internal/dream/run.go:192-262`"; that plan is `closed` now (record list). (b) The plan says "A box without the scratch tools rebuilds them from this description, about 100 lines of `go/ast`"; the description omits the behaviour that matters (name-keyed lookup, attached doc comments only, whole import block copied, source head kept only in the source, last `import` decl wins, writes targets before source so a panic after the first target leaves a half-done tree with no rollback). Two rebuilds would differ. (c) "old copy" for `declsum` is never defined (declmove edits in place; the copy must be taken first, e.g. `git show HEAD:path` into scratch). (d) Method names are keyed bare, so a func and a method of the same name (e.g. `acc` the type and `(s *Summary) acc` in metrics, `close`, `kind`, `label`, `status`) go to the same target; the plan does not say this is accepted or checked per file.
- **G9 (low).** Terms used without definition or citation: "Item 1 … 7 source files and 10 test files over the ceilings" (only the audit's INDEX defines the numbering and it is box-local, `.agents/scratch/`, not in the trail; a fresh session on another box has nothing); "declmove/declsum" (scratch, box-local, gitignored); "audit item 9, `funclen.txt`" (scratch); "`GUIDE-testing`", "`BUG-164/165`", "`BUG-166`" (records, cited by id, findable); "Checkpoint" (defined in AGENTS.md). The plan cites no `REQUIREMENTS.md` item. The moves touch `internal/search`, `internal/metrics` and `internal/brain`, the three SQLite-importing packages (R4, AGENTS.md); a pure move changes no import, so no requirement is at risk, but the plan should say "R4 untouched: imports per package unchanged" or a reader must check.

## 2. Scope

- **S1.** Phase 6's handoff item ("a real macOS `fyr dream --all` owed before the next release") is not requested in `## Why`, but D-rows do not cover it. It follows BUG-166's prevention rule (any change to `agyHome`), which is a project rule, so it is justified by citation; I record it as acceptable. Note it fires for a pure move only by the literal rule; the plan should say it is the conservative reading.
- **S2.** Phase 7's `catalog_test.go` is NOT a pure move even without `TestRefreshCatalogScript`: the audit's blueprint for it (`catalog_rig_test.go`, `catalog_data_test.go`, `pipelint_test.go`, `scripts_pipe_test.go`) is moves, but the plan says "`catalog_test.go` less `TestRefreshCatalogScript`" and then expects the file to stay at ~840 lines. That is consistent, but the plan builds nothing beyond a split of `Why`. No extra endpoint, flag, config or second shape is introduced. No other scope creep found.

## 3. Readiness — questions an implementer would have to ask

- **Q1 (BLOCKING).** Phases 2, 4, 6: a `var (...)`/`const (...)` group the blueprint splits (G1). Keep whole in one file, or hand-split and extend the proof? Which file receives `cliTimeout`/`killGrace`/`keepFailed` (the dream audit contradicts itself)?
- **Q2 (BLOCKING).** Detached comments (G2): where does `catalog_test.go:24-31` go, and does `declsum` get extended (or a second check added, e.g. compare the comment-stripped concatenation of old and new files plus a count of comment groups) so the proof can see it?
- **Q3 (BLOCKING).** `SPEC-fyr-check`'s `cmd/fyr/main.go:171` example (G3): change the spec's example reference (a spec edit, with a re-stamp) or keep a 171-line `main.go`? Also: when in the phase is `fyr check` run, and which commit carries the re-stamp (G4)?
- **Q4 (NON-BLOCKING).** Per-step gate or per-phase gate (G7). Default readable from D1: the audits' order, gate after each step; the implementer can decide, but should say so in the change record.
- **Q5 (NON-BLOCKING).** `recall.tsv` gold rows after Phase 1 (G5): the test will show what fails; the fix is to repoint gold to the file that now holds the phrase. A reasonable implementer decides alone.
- **Q6 (NON-BLOCKING).** `TestOneRepositoryName`: replace, not add (G6). The failing test makes it obvious.
- **Q7 (NON-BLOCKING).** Source of the "old copy" for `declsum` (G8c). Reasonable default: `git show HEAD:<path>`.
- **Q8 (NON-BLOCKING).** Phase 7: `internal/eval/{procs_linux,guard,creds}_test.go` comments cite `catalog_test.go:2107-2127`, `:2140-2170`, `:1719-1748`; the file is 1,662 lines, so these are already wrong, and the moved tests' new file is not named in the plan. The audit says to re-grep; the plan does not. Also unresolved from the tests audit: whether `TestNoTmpInHarnessProse` scans `*_test.go` (not read; `harness_test.go:1041`, `1056` walks directories). A reasonable implementer greps both.
- **Q9 (NON-BLOCKING).** `TestUsageMatchesDocComment` reads `main.go` text; `main.go` keeps the package doc and `usage` (Phase 1 states this), so nothing to ask. Listed to show it was checked: the test lives in `cmd/fyr/search_test.go:88`, not `main_test.go`, which the plan does not say.

## 4. Sizing

- **Phase 7 cannot be finished and verified by a fresh session from this plan alone.** It spans ten files in six packages (`internal/harness`, `cmd/fyr`, `internal/dream`, `internal/search`, `internal/brain`, `internal/eval`), about 55 new files, and the plan gives no per-file clusters: the only blueprint is `.agents/scratch/modularity/audit-tests.md` on this box, which is not a record. Cross-file helper dependencies are open (audit: "which helpers cross clusters … compile errors will show"; `fixture` from `collect_test.go` used by `run_test.go`; `isolate`/`checkoutRoot` across `zip_test.go` and `main_test.go`), and every verify pass is `cmd/fyr` under `-race` (~13 min on one CPU). `rules/session-sizing.md` exists in the repo; this phase should be one phase per package. This counts as gap G10 below.
- Phase 1 (12 files, 11 audit steps, `-race` each) is borderline for one sitting but is unambiguous apart from G3/G5/G6.
- Phases 2–6 are each one package and sized for a sitting once G1 is decided.
- **G10 (medium).** Phase 7 sizing, as above; plus every phase depends on box-local scratch material (`.agents/scratch/modularity/`, the two tools), absent on a fresh clone because `.agents/scratch/` is gitignored. A fresh session on another box has no audit and no tools.

Counts: gaps 10 (G1–G10), scope 2 (S1–S2), questions 9 (3 BLOCKING: Q1–Q3).

## Criteria applied to the plan

1. Dead code: pass for the plan as written (no new dead code); the plan leaves `TestRefreshCatalogScript` and over-50-line functions as Follow-ups. One thing to delete: the plan's stale clause about the open eval plan (G8a).
2. Flow tracing: FAIL. G1 (tool vs blueprint), G2 (proof blind to comments), G3/G4 (`fyr check` ordering and a living path:line), G5 (recall gold), G6 (test list wording).
3. Standards conformance: partial. Departs from rule item 5's per-step verification with no D-row (G7); restatements of the old locations (the three `catalog_test.go:NNNN` comments in `internal/eval`, SPEC-fyr-check's example, recall gold) are not all named (G3, G5, Q8). REQUIREMENTS.md not cited (G9, no violation found).
4. Directory layout: pass. Targets are siblings in the same package, named by concern; no `utils`/`helpers`/`common`/`misc`; `verb_*.go` follows the `check.go`/`eval.go`/`record.go` precedent.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security): pass. A scratch go/ast tool and stdlib only; no dependency; no auth or crypto surface. The security-relevant `git` runner and `os.Root` reads (BUG-164/165) move byte for byte, but the plan relies on the same blind `declsum` (G2) and gives that phase a plain reviewer, not `security`; a pure move is arguably not a security change, so low.
6. Decoupling: pass. Moves inside a package change no interface; the audits record shared vars (`stderr`, `stdin`, `version`, `propose`, `writeState`, `maxImportBytes`) that stay package-level and test-assignable; no visibility widened, which matches rule item 4.

## Verdict

design needs revision. implementation not ready.

## Not examined

- Function bodies of the split files beyond heads, var/const groups and method lists; whether any extracted declaration references a package-level `init` ordering (none found by grep: no `func init` in the 16 files).
- Whether `recall_test.go`'s threshold makes the stale gold in G5 a failure or a lower score.
- `internal/dream` / `internal/metrics` / `internal/search` const and var groups other than the ones named in G1 (search.go consts at about 26-46, metrics' `activeGap/historical/DefaultContextTarget`): not checked for grouping with other names.
- `TestNoTmpInHarnessProse` scanning scope; `skills/harness-audit/references/areas.md`, README and AGENTS.md citations of test names (audit-tests lists them; I did not re-grep).
- `rules/session-sizing.md` text (named, not read); ADR-066 beyond its first lines; `GUIDE-testing`, `GUIDE-eval`, `SPEC-fyr-dream` bodies.
- The audits' line numbers and LOC estimates (taken as given); whether any split target would still exceed 400 lines after imports.
- Did not execute `declmove`/`declsum` (reading only; creating files was outside the brief).

## Outcome

Answered 2026-10-26 by the main thread (cold read round 1), every item in `PLAN-2026-10-26-modularity` § Decisions (D2–D12) or below. Each claim was checked before it was answered: G1, G2, G3, G5, G6 and Q8's line numbers re-read in the tree; the tool fixes validated on scratch copies in `.agents/scratch/coldread-proof/` in a must-fail and a must-pass state.

- **G1 / Q1 (BLOCKING)** — fixed, D2: a grouped `var`/`const`/`type` block moves whole and is never split; where an audit sends its members to two files it stays in the source file. Checked: `declmove` moves the whole group when one member is listed, and panics before writing any file when two members name two targets (scratch copy of `internal/dream/run.go`). This also settles the dream audit's contradiction: the `cliTimeout`/`killGrace`/`keepFailed` block stays in `run.go`.
- **G2 / Q2 (BLOCKING)** — fixed, D3. Confirmed the gap: on a scratch copy of `internal/harness/catalog_test.go`, the old `declmove` dropped the detached block at lines 24–31 and the old `declsum` still reported EQUAL. Fix: `declsum` now also hashes every comment group. `declmove` now carries a detached comment with the declaration after it, and keeps the source's whole head up to the end of its imports. Re-run: old move with new sum gives DIFF (one `comment` line missing); new move with new sum gives EQUAL with the comment kept, and gofmt is clean. Build tags: none of the files in scope has one (grep).
- **G3 / Q3 (BLOCKING)** — fixed, D8: Phase 1 edits `SPEC-fyr-check`'s example `cmd/fyr/main.go:171` to `cmd/fyr/main.go:1`. Confirmed: it is the only `path:N` into a split file in a current spec, guide or deploy record (jq over `.agents/trail.jsonl`).
- **G4** — fixed, D8: `fyr check` runs after the move's commit. Each `spec-stale` finding is re-read, then re-stamped with `fyr record edit <id> --status current`, in its own commit, as 44df74a did, and `fyr check` exits 0 after it. Correction to the report: a spec's code is every existing path any inline span names, directories included (`internal/check/specs.go:71-95`), not only its `Code:` line. So `fyr check`'s output is the list; no list is computed in advance.
- **G5 / Q5** — fixed, D10. `TestRecall` is a measurement, skipped unless `FYR_RECALL=1` (`cmd/fyr/recall_test.go:291`), so the stale gold lowers a score and fails no gate. Phase 1 repoints gold rows 36, 38 and 39 in the move's commit.
- **G6 / Q6** — fixed, D9: in `TestOneRepositoryName`, `cmd/fyr/main.go` is replaced, not supplemented, by the file that receives `runAdopt`, in the move's commit. The Phase 1 text is corrected.
- **G7 / Q4** — fixed, D7: the rule's item 5 is followed literally. After each target file: build, vet, the package's tests, and the `declsum` diff. The full `-race` line runs once at the phase's end.
- **G8** — (a) the plan's Risks clause about the open `fyr eval` plan is struck (that plan is closed). (b) fixed, D5: the tools' exact sources are in the recon record. (c) fixed, D6: the old copy is `git show HEAD:<path>`. (d) fixed, D4: a method is named `Type.method`. Checked: `Summary.acc` moved alone, and type `acc` stayed.
- **G9** — fixed, D5 and D12: "audit item N" and the tools are defined by the recon record. The plan cites R4: imports per package are unchanged, so no package gains the SQLite driver.
- **G10** — fixed, D5 and D11: the audits and tools are the record `PLAN-2026-10-26-1133-recon-the-code-modularity-audit-and-the-move-too`, so no phase needs this box's scratch. Phase 7 is now Phases 7a–7e, one package (or one file) per session.
- **S1** — accepted as written: Phase 6's macOS `fyr dream --all` follows BUG-166's prevention rule. The plan now says it is the conservative reading for a pure move.
- **S2** — no scope beyond `## Why`, per the report; no change.
- **Q8** — rebutted in part. The three `catalog_test.go:N-M` comments in `internal/eval/{procs_linux,guard,creds}_test.go` cite the run kit's own test file, which 8374f9c ported. They do not cite `internal/harness/catalog_test.go`, and no move touches them. Qualifying them is a Follow-up. Answered by D11: Phase 7a reads `TestNoTmpInHarnessProse`'s walk (`internal/harness/harness_test.go:1034`) before it names any new file.

title: Review — e45124e..47453ad, code and docs lenses (2026-10-26)
body:
# Review — e45124e..47453ad, code and docs lenses (2026-10-26)

Range reviewed: e45124e..47453ad (`git diff e45124e...47453ad -- cmd internal skills`, 109 files; 11 code commits 1f1be8c, 824b231, 9f5c6f7, 50bee5a, c464a77, 2d131dc, 4c07410, 2cde2ca, 16b7f07, 93c86d1, a2ee541; the other commits touch only .agents/trail.jsonl, AGENTS.md, ROADMAP.md). HEAD is the range head, so `fyr check` below is verified for this range.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing is broken. The range is what it claims: whole-declaration moves between files of one package, plus three small edits. I did not rely on declsum alone. I re-ran a second, independent check, a per-commit multiset of every source line (blank, `package` and import lines dropped) of each modified file at `<c>^` against that file plus the files the commit added. It is empty for all 11 commits except the one `TestOneRepositoryName` line, so declsum's coverage holds for the bytes between declarations. `gofmt -l cmd internal` prints nothing, and `go vet ./...` is clean, which compiles every moved test. The worst items are one empty `import ()` left in a new file and one living guide section that still names the pre-split catalog test file as its trigger.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/metrics/show_types.go:3` — the new file carries an empty `import ()` block (the only one among the 91 added Go files; `git grep -n '^import ()' 47453ad`). It compiles and gofmt leaves it, but it is residue of the split and dead text. Fix: delete the line.
- **[low / confidence: high]** GUIDE-testing § 3f heading (record `GUIDE-testing`) — "change under `skills/google-catalog/`, to `internal/harness/catalog_test.go`, or to the listing budget" names `catalog_test.go` as the trigger for the catalog verification section. After 2cde2ca that file holds only `TestRefreshCatalogScript`. The tests the section lists (`TestCatalogMatchesChecksums`, `…IndexMatchesEntries`, `…FilesAreCarryable`, `TestCatalogInstallsClean`) live in `catalog_data_test.go`, `scripts_pipe_test.go`, `pipelint_test.go` and `catalog_rig_test.go`. A reader scoping "did I change catalog_test.go?" misses a change to those files. This is `narrowed: GUIDE-testing § 3f → the four new files`. The re-stamp passes (specs only) did not cover guides. Fix: name the file set (`internal/harness/catalog_*_test.go`, `scripts_pipe_test.go`, `pipelint_test.go`).
- **[low / confidence: medium]** Record `BUG-155`, line 7 — "Graduated to: `TestScriptsHaveNoEarlyExitPipe` in `internal/harness/catalog_test.go`", now in `internal/harness/scripts_pipe_test.go:14`. A graduated bug's mechanism address is stale. Bug records are outside the docs lens's grep, and `fyr check` does not read them (0 findings), so nothing flags it. Fix: edit the Graduated line when the bug record is next updated.
- **[low / confidence: high, pre-existing, outside the verdict]** `internal/eval/creds_test.go:31`, `internal/eval/guard_test.go:38` and `internal/eval/procs_linux_test.go:45` cite `catalog_test.go:1719-1748`, `:2140-2170` and `:2107-2127`. `catalog_test.go` had 1,662 lines at e45124e, so these were already past the end of the file before the range, and the range did not change them. The range makes them worse, because the named file now holds 867 lines of one function. The citations should name the real files.
- **[low / confidence: high, declared exception]** `internal/harness/catalog_test.go` is 867 lines, over the 600-line test ceiling in `rules/code-modularity.md`. Plan D11 declares it (`TestRefreshCatalogScript` stays byte for byte; ROADMAP/plan Phase 7b row). Recorded only, not a finding against the range.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass with one nit: the empty `import ()` at `show_types.go:3`. No orphaned declarations (declsum and the line-multiset check both show no line lost or gained). The 7b widening of the `refresh-catalog.sh` grep removed a dead pattern, not added one.
2. Flow tracing — pass. 91 added Go files all declare the package of their directory (checked with a script). No `//go:build` line sits in any moved source or added file, so no constraint was dropped or duplicated; the build-tagged files in the tree (`open_unix.go`, `owned_unix.go` and so on) are not in the range. Test names are verbatim. The helper-process tests (`TestHelperIndex`, `TestHelperAdd`, `TestHelperCall`) moved beside their callers inside one package, so their `-test.run=` names resolve. `refresh-catalog.sh:320` (`catalog_[a-z_]*test\.go`) matches the file that now emits the three named tests' failures, `catalog_data_test.go`, and the rig in `catalog_rig_test.go`; the line keeps `|| true`.
3. Standards conformance — pass. gofmt and vet clean. The nonmove list is complete: `cmd/fyr/main_test.go` (one line in `TestOneRepositoryName`, `main.go` to `verb_install.go`), `cmd/fyr/testdata/recall.tsv` (rows 38 and 39), `refresh-catalog.sh:320`. The rest of `recall.tsv` is untouched, so gold rows still naming `cmd/fyr/main.go` (e.g. row 35) keep whatever recall they had. `TestRecall` was not run by me. `AGENTS.md:93` (`internal/search/search.go` row) still holds, since `Index` and `Search` stay in `search.go`.
4. Directory layout — pass. Files sit beside their package, split by concern (`<entity>_<concern>.go`), tests beside the code. No `utils`/`helpers`/`common` files. The choice to keep each source's rig instead of a `*rig_test.go` was an operator decision (commit messages).
5. Simplicity — pass. No dependency changed, no new code; no security-sensitive code touched (no auth, crypto or secrets in the diff). Stdlib-only rule unaffected.
6. Decoupling — pass. Packages and visibility unchanged (declsum compares declarations byte for byte, so no name was exported to split a file). Splitting the 600+ line files makes adjacent edits independent. Only `catalog_test.go` stays over the ceiling, by plan.

## Docs lens
- `fyr check` at the checkout root (working tree = 47453ad, the range head, so verified): `check: 0 findings (docs 0, specs 0, requirements 0)`. Notes quoted: "note: REQUIREMENTS.md has no enforced-by field: not checked"; and a stderr line "fyr: both ~/.config/sh-agent and ~/.config/fyr exist; fyr reads ~/.config/fyr and leaves ~/.config/sh-agent as it is — merge or remove it by hand" (machine state, not a finding of the scope).
- `restatement-grep.sh -i -- catalog_test writer.log verb_install` listed only: the changed `flags_test.go:177`, `recall.tsv:39`, `refresh-catalog.sh:319-320`, and the three stale eval-test comments above.
- Old-file-name grep in the living docs (`README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `context/`, `agents/`, `rules/`, `skills/` less the vendored catalog and VENDORED.md, and the `spec`/`guide`/`deploy` records): no living doc, spec or deploy record names `cmd/fyr/main.go` for a moved declaration, `import.go`, `reconcile.go`, `show.go`, `dream/run.go`, or any split test file as a location. `SPEC-fyr-check` names `cmd/fyr/main.go:1`, which exists (112 lines). Hits in `agents/documentation`, `init-project`, `golang` and `docker` skills are generic `cmd/<app>/main.go` examples.
- Stale: GUIDE-testing § 3f (see Findings), `narrowed`. No `dropped:` and no `stale test:` found: `TestOneRepositoryName` in `flags_test.go:177` reads the new file, and `refresh-catalog.sh:320` is updated.
- No interface, command, flag or deploy step changed in the range, so README, DEPLOY-* and the map are not affected (map pin `TestHarnessMap` moved to `harnessmap_test.go` verbatim).
- Unverified: GUIDE-eval rows beyond a text search for old file names (no hit); running any test (the verifier's step, not this dispatch).

## Not examined
- I did not run `go test` for any package (vet compiled the tests; the verifier is the next step), and did not run `TestRecall`.
- I did not re-read the 30,298-line diff by eye; coverage came from declsum's recorded proof, my own per-commit line-multiset check, and package/build-tag/import/placement checks by script. I did not re-run `proof.sh`. Import-block correctness of each new file is verified only by `go vet` compiling the packages (an unused or missing import would fail the build), not file by file.
- Function-length (50 LOC) and complexity limits of the moved bodies: not measured; bodies are byte-identical to the originals.
- Plan D-rows other than D11 and the operator decisions quoted in commit messages: taken from those messages, not from the operator's turns.

## Outcome

Main agent, 2026-10-26, one round (no fix touched source, so round 2 has nothing to re-check).

- `internal/metrics/show_types.go:3`, the empty `import ()`: **rebutted**. Not a defect, because an empty import declaration is valid Go (the spec's ImportDecl allows zero ImportSpecs) and `gofmt -l cmd internal` and `go vet ./...` are clean (this report's Criteria 3). A deletion would be a fix with no test that fails without it, which this task's rule forbids. The line goes the next time the rule's pre-edit check touches the file. Operator's choice, 2026-10-26: "Rebut, leave it".
- GUIDE-testing § 3f heading, `narrowed`: **fixed**. The heading's trigger now reads `internal/harness/catalog_*test.go`, `scripts_pipe_test.go` or `pipelint_test.go`. That is a record edit in `.agents/trail.jsonl`, in the commit that carries this Outcome, and the operator approved it on 2026-10-26 ("Edit both"). No test reads guide prose; `fyr check` reads it for paths, and the glob names files that exist.
- BUG-155 Graduated line: **fixed**. It now names `internal/harness/scripts_pipe_test.go`, where `TestScriptsHaveNoEarlyExitPipe` is at line 14. Same commit, same approval.
- `internal/eval/{creds,guard,procs_linux}_test.go` citations of `catalog_test.go:N-M`: **left**, owned by the plan's Follow-up "The three `catalog_test.go:N-M` comments in `internal/eval`" (D11). Pre-existing, outside the range.
- `internal/harness/catalog_test.go` at 867 lines: **rebutted**. It is a declared exception (plan D11 and Phase 7b: `TestRefreshCatalogScript` stays whole), and its split is the plan's Follow-up.

# Review round 2 — fyr v3.0.0 gate, round-1 fixes, code and docs (2026-10-26)

Range reviewed: e53a7cb^..e53a7cb

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

All five fixes close the triggers their findings name. Each new test fails when its fix is mutated out: four mutations in a scratch copy, each compiled and failed a named test (see the table below). None of the fixes adds a code defect. The rebuttal holds: `normalize` calls `oneLine`, and `oneLine` returns "untitled" for an empty or whitespace-only title (`internal/brain/import_classify.go:218-222`). So a memory file with no `description` passes `checkRecord`, and the new test pins that (`no-desc (project) — untitled`). The one finding is a docs restatement. `GUIDE-testing` still states check d without the new outside-link exception. Separately, the working tree moved during this review: an uncommitted `.agents/trail.jsonl` edit, not part of this range and not made by me, makes `TestSuiteHarness` fail (see Observations).

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: high]** `.agents/trail.jsonl:386` (record `GUIDE-testing`, status current). It restates check d as "a dangling link or a link to a directory fails unless the baseline held it with the same target". Since this commit, that sentence is false in one case. A directory link the baseline held with the same target still fails when it resolves outside the scanned directory (`internal/eval/creds.go:86`, `:187`; SPEC-fyr-eval check d was updated in this commit). Fix: add "and a directory link that resolves outside the scanned directory always fails" to the guide, or reduce it to a pointer to SPEC-fyr-eval § Safety checks. Two other copies are dated records, not living docs, and are fine as they are: CHANGE-2026-10-26-1112 (line 363) and PLAN-2026-10-26-0659 (line 537, closed).

## Per-fix judgement (round-1 finding -> fix)
| Round-1 finding | Closes every trigger? | Test fails without fix? | New defect? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reviewer 1 / security 1: memory import, checkRecord removed (`import_memory.go:97-104`) | Yes. Body pushed past maxBody: caught, and pinned by `huge.md`. Empty date/updated: caught by checkRecord's date case (not testable without failing `e.Info`; not covered by a test). Empty description: the rebuttal is CONFIRMED, it becomes "untitled". `ImportGlobal` (`import_global.go:161-166`) shares `readMemoryStore` and appends its problems without aborting, so the global trigger is closed by the same line. It has no test of its own. | M1 (block removed, 1 occurrence): `TestImportSkipsAMemoryTheStoreRefuses` FAIL at import_test.go:503, "MEMORY-huge: the body is over 1 MiB". | None. A skipped file is left out of `files`, so it is not on the remove list (asserted). |
| Reviewer 2: a future record hides activity (`brain/dream.go:70`, `:94`) | Yes. `after()` and `Last` are both bounded by `now`. `activityIn` passes `now` (`dream/dream.go:201`), and its own redundant guard was removed, which is correct now that ForDream filters. `collectIn` passes `time.Now()` (`collect.go:75`). The only callers are these two, through the `forDream` var (`collect.go:355`), and it compiles. | M2a (Last bound): FAIL at fordream_test.go:25. M2b (after() bound): FAIL at fordream_test.go:28. | None. A future record becomes news once its time has passed, which is the intent. |
| Security 2: a baseline directory link that leads outside is skipped (`eval/creds.go:86,96-108,187`) | Yes. An outside directory link that the baseline held now counts. If `EvalSymlinks` fails on the root or the link, the link counts as outside (fail closed). A dangling link written through becomes a file that is read, or a directory link that is outside, so both are caught. | M3 (`&& !f.outside` removed): `TestCredsBaselineLinkOutsideCounts` FAIL at creds_test.go:252. Its must-pass partner is `TestCredsLinkProblems`: an inside `dirlink -> sub` is still skipped. | Not stricter than real runs: the fixture `~/sandbox/fyr-eval/fixture` holds no symlink (`find -type l`: none), and the eval package creates only the token link, after the baseline, and unlinks it before the scan. |
| Security 5: a relative worktree gitdir (`trail/trail.go:285-291`) | Yes. `memory.Root` resolves through `trail.Roots` (`memory.go:37`), and no other code reads `gitdir`. The fix joins against `gitDir`, which git reports as a realpath: checked in scratch through a symlinked path, `--absolute-git-dir` printed the real path. That matches git's `relative_path` between realpaths, so the lexical Join is exact, on macOS too. | M4 (join removed): `TestRootIsTheWorkTreeTop/linked_worktree_registered_by_a_relative_path` FAIL at memory_test.go:108. | None. `named` is computed before the `err` check, but `err != nil` still short-circuits. |
| Reviewer 3: TestRecall path (`areas.md:43`) | Yes. `TestRecall` is at `cmd/fyr/recall_test.go:290`, gated on `FYR_RECALL`. No other living doc names `./internal/search -run TestRecall`. The three hits are dated records. | n/a (docs) | None. |

Mutation protocol: tree = `git archive e53a7cb` into `.agents/scratch/r2mut`. For each mutation the target occurred exactly once. The file was restored from a saved `.orig` copy, and afterwards every file was confirmed byte-identical with `git show e53a7cb:<path> | cmp`. Every mutant compiled.

## Observations (not findings against this range)
- The working tree changed during this review: `.agents/trail.jsonl` has an uncommitted edit of the GUIDE-eval and GUIDE-skill-matrix records (updated 19:21:58Z and 19:22:07Z, which is after e53a7cb), porting matrix rows into GUIDE-eval. With that edit, `go test ./internal/eval` in the checkout fails `TestSuiteHarness` at suite_test.go:160 with "56 rows, want 29". At e53a7cb (the scratch copy) the test passes. Whoever owns that edit must update the pinned row count before a verifier run, and the gated head is not the working tree.
- In the scratch copy, `TestRunRealFyrBaseline` fails with "the install did not name the checkout as its source". That is an artifact of the copy (`git archive`, so not a checkout), and the test passes in the real tree.
- Checks run at e53a7cb: `gofmt -l` (empty) and `go vet` on brain, dream, eval, memory and trail. `go test` on the same packages: brain, dream, memory and trail pass; eval as above.

## Criteria
1. Dead code: pass. The removed `!in.Last.After(now)` in activityIn is now redundant, and taking it out was correct. No dead code was left behind.
2. Flow tracing: pass. The signature change reaches both callers through the `forDream` var. `readMemoryStore`'s problems reach both `Import` and `ImportGlobal`. Check d's `outside` flag is set in `scanCreds` and read in `newCreds`. `trail.Roots` is the only reader of `gitdir`.
3. Standards conformance: pass with one finding. The SPEC-fyr-eval check d text was updated in this commit (verified in the trail diff), but its restatement in GUIDE-testing was not. SPEC-fyr-record ("a memory file it cannot take is a `problem` and stays") is now true again.
4. Directory layout: pass. `fordream_test.go` sits beside `dream.go` in `internal/brain`.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security): pass. Stdlib only (`filepath.EvalSymlinks`, `filepath.Rel`), and no auth or crypto code.
6. Decoupling: pass. No new cross-package reach. The `now` parameter keeps the clock with the caller.

## Not examined
- No full `go test -race ./...`, govulncheck or `fyr status`. Only the five changed packages were vetted and tested.
- `ImportGlobal` has no test of its own for a refused memory file. The fix was judged by reading the shared `readMemoryStore` path.
- The checkRecord trigger "a day no clock gave" (`e.Info` failing) has no test. It was judged by reading the code.
- There is no Antigravity or `fyr eval` run. The relative-paths fix was not exercised with a real git 2.48 `--relative-paths` worktree, because this box has git 2.47.3 and the test hand-writes the relative gitdir file.

## Outcome
