# Review — fyr v3.0.0 release gate, code + docs (2026-10-26)

Range reviewed: 0a1bd0c, f28e8bc, 76327b8, b54395d, a5c70e0, 927c69f, e2435b5, 52259a5, 5593cb8, f8cc874 (each as its own diff, `git show <c> -- . ':!.agents/trail.jsonl'`; head 19c2d2a)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

The worst problem: 76327b8 removed a per-file `checkRecord` from `readMemoryStore` and called it "unreachable", but it can be reached. An old memory file with no `description` now gets past the problems list, and it makes `fyr record import` fail as a whole (in `ImportGlobal`, every project's import), which breaks SPEC-fyr-record's "nothing stops the import". Second: the clock-skew guard b54395d added to the dream's idle check switches off the record signal for the whole project as soon as one record is dated in the future. The rest of the range holds up. The 52259a5 split claim is confirmed mechanically. 927c69f's `spans` rewrite gives the same results as the old loop. The ERE quoting for `-G` is correct (git compiles pickaxe `-G` with REG_EXTENDED). The held `os.Root` and the reordered `unlink` in 5593cb8 do what their comments say. The timer probe in f8cc874 fails closed toward the old behaviour. `gofmt -l cmd internal` printed nothing, and `go vet` passed on eval, brain, check and dream.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/brain/import_memory.go:96-98` (the change is 76327b8's, in `internal/brain/import.go` then). The removed `checkRecord` can be reached. The title is `meta["description"]` with no fallback, so a memory file whose frontmatter has no `description` (or an empty one) normalizes to `Title: ""`, and `checkRecord` refuses that (`import_guard.go:87`). Before 76327b8 such a file was a `problem` and stayed where it was. Now `Import` lists it as a record in a dry run, and its path goes on the remove list. The real run then aborts the whole transaction in `insertNew` (`import.go:186`), with a plain error rather than a refusal. `ImportGlobal` (`import_global.go:161` -> `:191`) fails the whole global import over one such file in any indexed project. That contradicts SPEC-fyr-record: "a project's memory store it cannot take is reported and skipped; nothing stops the import". A second trigger: a file of close to `maxBody` with no frontmatter goes over `maxBody` once `"type: project\n\n"` is put in front. Fix: put the per-file `checkRecord` back, or fall back to the file stem for an empty title and cap the body after the prefix. Add a test with a description-less memory file, for `Import` and for `ImportGlobal`, that fails without the fix.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/brain/dream.go` `ForDream` (the `in.Last` loop) together with `internal/dream/dream.go` `activityIn` (`!in.Last.After(now)`), from b54395d. `in.Last` is the maximum over every record, future ones included. So a single record whose `updated` is in the future (clock skew on the machine that wrote a committed `trail.jsonl` line, or the planted line the comment names) makes `!in.Last.After(now)` false. The project's real record activity in the last 24 h is then never seen: a project whose only recent use is a `fyr memory add` or a record edit with no commit is judged idle and dreamed while in use, against D22. Future records also pass `after()` (it has no upper bound), so they are sent again in every dream, and they keep the project "changed" for good. Fix: leave records dated after `now` out of `Last` (pass `now` into `ForDream`, or filter in `activityIn`), and bound `after()` by `now`. Add a test with one future record and one record 1 h old that expects "in use".
- **[low / confidence: high]** `skills/harness-audit/references/areas.md:43`. The SD baseline runs `FYR_RECALL=1 go test ./internal/search -run TestRecall -v`, but `TestRecall` now lives in `cmd/fyr/recall_test.go:290`; it moved in 9001831, which is outside this range, but f8cc874 edited this same line. As written, the command prints `ok ... [no tests to run]`, a silent pass that measures nothing. Fix: `FYR_RECALL=1 go test ./cmd/fyr -run TestRecall -v`.

Already recorded, not a finding: 76327b8 printed `git rm --literal-pathspecs --`, which git refuses (reproduced in scratch: `error: unknown option 'literal-pathspecs'`, rc 129). This is BUG-180, fixed in 9001831; at HEAD, `cmd/fyr/record.go:156` and SPEC-fyr-record say `git --literal-pathspecs rm --`.

## Criteria
1. Dead code: pass. `breQuote`, the old `Propose`, the bare `sandboxRoot` and the `capped` pre-read check were all removed along with their callers. Nothing commented out or left orphaned.
2. Flow tracing: fail (finding 1). One guard was removed on a reasoning error, and the failure now surfaces at a later hop (`insertNew`) that aborts every record. Otherwise: `specsRule`'s new notes reach `Run`; `ReplaceOldTimer`'s new return value is handled in all four `installFiles` cases; `ProposeAll` gets one transaction for each project; the dry-run brain copy goes through `collectIn` and `activityIn`; `removeCopies` sweeps `dream-brain-*`.
3. Standards conformance: pass with finding 3. The restatements of the rules list (`AGENTS.md` layout row) and of the eval help line were updated. The `fyr record` spec, the help text and the timer behaviour in DEPLOY-remote match the code. Errors are wrapped or noted; the `fyr check` git failures were silent before and are now notes.
4. Directory layout: pass. `plain_{unix,other}.go`, `open_{unix,other}.go` and the `row_*.go` split follow the package-scoped split rule, and the `.agents/kit/` move left no live reference behind.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security): pass. No new dependency. `O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK`, `os.Root` and `regexp.QuoteMeta` are stdlib used as designed, and no auth or crypto code was touched.
6. Decoupling: pass. `search.CopyDB` is a thin export for dream's copy, `trail.Log` stays the single git-log seam (dream now uses it too), and `brain.Proposal` is small.

52259a5 split claim: CONFIRMED. I sorted the non-blank lines of `run.go` before the commit, with `package`, `import` and lone quoted import lines dropped (655 lines), and the same lines of `run.go` plus `row*.go` after (655 lines); `diff` is empty.

## Docs
- README (f8cc874): the clone URL and the map node were renamed to `fyr`. No living doc outside test fixtures still names `kesokaj/styrman-harness`; `cmd/fyr/flags_test.go:188` pins that.
- AGENTS.md (927c69f, e2435b5): the govulncheck note now covers `internal/check`'s trailing-slash strip, and the layout row lists `code-modularity.md` (ADR-066). No other enumeration of the rules needed changing (grep for `session-sizing` over README, context, skills and agents).
- README `fyr check` row (927c69f): the added "noted, not checked" clause matches the help text.
- agents/explorer, dreamer, documentation (f8cc874): tool names switched to Antigravity's (`grep_search`, `find_by_name`, `view_file`, `write_to_file`), consistent with agy-only.
- skills/retro (b54395d): sources 9 and `--harness` filter on the `Dream, project —` and `Dream, harness —` title prefixes that `run.go` writes. Not checked: whether SPEC-fyr-dream says draft-skill proposals belong to the harness (they are now titled `Dream, harness —`, which hides them from a project `/retro`, whose source 9 still calls them skill candidates).
- skills/init-project Step 5 Root (0a1bd0c): that wording is superseded at HEAD (memory moved to the brain store).
- The DEPLOY-remote record describes the turned-off-timer behaviour as the code does it (`is-enabled` disabled/masked, `launchctl print` cannot find it, a manager that cannot be asked counts as on).
- Finding 3 is the one stale living doc.

## Not examined
- The test bodies of `row_replaced_test.go`, `creds_test.go`, `guard_test.go`, `idle_test.go`, `timer_test.go`, `timer_legacy_test.go`, `cmd/fyr/main_test.go`, `hardening_test.go`, `fifo_unix_test.go`, `trail_test.go` and `store_test.go` were read only as far as the diffs showed them. I checked no mutation or must-fail claim for these tests.
- The full race suite, `go vet ./...` over every package, and govulncheck were not run: vet covered four packages only.
- The record files f8cc874 adds under `.agents/docs/` (reviews, testing logs, the change entry, the plan diff, `deploy/local.md`, `testing/guide.md`) and the review records in 0a1bd0c, f28e8bc and 76327b8 were not read.
- SPEC-fyr-dream, SPEC-fyr-eval and SPEC-fyr-check were not read against the code; only SPEC-fyr-record and DEPLOY-remote were, in excerpts.
- Antigravity behaviour of the changed agents and skills was not checked (a release-gate item per AGENTS.md § Release).

## Outcome
- Finding 1 (memory import): fixed in e53a7cb. The per-file `checkRecord` is back as a problem line. The empty-description trigger is rebutted: `normalize` titles it "untitled", which `TestImportSkipsAMemoryTheStoreRefuses` pins. The real trigger, a body pushed past maxBody (security finding 1), fails that test without the fix.
- Finding 2 (a future record hides activity): fixed in e53a7cb. `ForDream(home, root, since, now)` bounds both `after()` and `Last` by now. `TestForDreamIgnoresARecordFromTheFuture` fails on either bound removed.
- Finding 3 (TestRecall path): fixed in e53a7cb (`skills/harness-audit/references/areas.md`).
- Round 2 (`REVIEW-…-r2`, APPROVE WITH NITS) confirmed each fix by mutation.

title: Security review round 2 — v3.0.0 gate fixes e53a7cb (2026-10-26)
body:
---
owner: security
date: 2026-10-26
---
# Security review — v3.0.0 gate, round 2 over the round-1 fixes   (2026-10-26)

Range reviewed: e53a7cb^..e53a7cb (every path in the diff; answers `.agents/scratch/agents/security-2026-10-26-2010.md`)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS (2 low, no medium or high)

The three fixes hold, and so do both rebuttals.

- **Fix 5 (relative worktree gitdir).** I probed it on git 2.47.3. A planted checkout cannot borrow another project's store through the new relative branch. A probe called the real `trail.Roots` on two directories:
  - A genuine worktree whose `gitdir` is relative: accepted, `main=$S/victim`.
  - A planted checkout at `att/a/victim-wt`: refused, "is not a worktree the repository at … registers". Its `.git` file names the victim's registered worktree git dir through a symlinked prefix (`att/a/b/c/lnk -> victim/.git/worktrees`). The prefix is chosen so that a lexical join of `../../../../victim-wt/.git` lands on the planted directory.
  - It is refused because git prints `--absolute-git-dir` as a realpath (`…/victim/.git/worktrees/victim-wt`), not the lexical path. The join then follows the victim's real directories.
- **The weakness that remains (finding 1).** The anti-forgery property now rests on that git behaviour, and the code does not enforce it. Nothing in the tests pins it either.
- **Fixes 1 and 2:** correct. Each new test fails against the parent's code and passes at HEAD; the run is listed under Checked.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/trail/trail.go:285-291` (`Roots`, the new relative branch). `named = filepath.Join(gitDir, named)` is a lexical join on `gitDir` as git printed it.
  - The other two comparisons in this block go through `sameDir` (EvalSymlinks on both sides). This one joins before resolving.
  - So a relative `gitdir`'s `..` steps are applied to whatever path string git hands back.
  - On git 2.47.3 that string is a realpath, so the probe above is refused. If any git, or a `GIT_*` environment `trail.Command` lets through, reported the git dir lexically (the path as written in the planted `.git` file), an attacker could pick a symlink prefix. That prefix would steer the victim's relative `gitdir` onto the planted checkout. This is exactly the forged-commondir borrow the check exists to stop.
  - Precondition: the victim repository has a worktree registered with relative paths (git 2.48+ `worktree.useRelativePaths`), plus a same-user planted checkout.
  - Not reproduced on this box's git.
  - Fix:
    - resolve first (`rg, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(gitDir)`; refuse on error) and join `named` onto `rg`;
    - add a negative subtest to `TestRootIsTheWorkTreeTop` with the probe's layout: a symlinked worktrees prefix and a relative gitdir, with the planted checkout refused. The new subtest only covers the accepting side.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/dream/dream.go:374-380` (`brainCopy`; what is left of round-1 finding 3).
  - The rebuttal holds for the case it names: `dream` is in `writesState` only when not `--dry-run` (`cmd/fyr/run_dispatch.go:122-123`). So a dry run on a home with only `~/.config/sh-agent` does not migrate. Creating `~/.config/fyr` there would trip `bothStateDirs` (`internal/harness/migrate.go:30,49`), and the migration would then leave the old state stranded.
  - The code goes further than the rebuttal needs. It keys on `brain.db` existing, not on `~/.config/fyr` existing. A home where `~/.config/fyr` already exists (metrics, dream state) but holds no brain store yet still gets its copy under `os.TempDir()`, and a killed run leaves it there unswept.
  - Content: a copy built from the project's committed `trail.jsonl`, in a 0700 directory. Same-user exposure only.
  - Fix, optional: use `filepath.Dir(brain.Path(home))` as the parent whenever that directory already exists (Lstat, a directory, not a link), and fall back to temp only when it is absent.

Round-1 finding 4: the rebuttal is accepted.
- The fail-open is documented in `DEPLOY-remote` ("a manager that cannot be asked counts as on").
- It is limited to an old unit whose manager cannot be asked. In that state, the `enable` that would turn the fyr unit on usually fails too.
- It is a documented operator trade-off, not a finding.

## Checked
- **Fix 1** (`internal/brain/import_memory.go:97-104`).
  - `checkRecord` runs once per file in `readMemoryStore`. Both callers (`import.go:117`, the project import and its dry run; `import_global.go:161`) get the problem line and skip the file. So the dry-run claim holds again, and one file no longer rolls back the batch.
  - The error text quotes the ID, date and updated fields with `%q` and never echoes the title or body, so no terminal control text gets through.
  - Mutation: `TestImportSkipsAMemoryTheStoreRefuses` fails on the parent's code ("import built a record the load would refuse: MEMORY-huge") and passes at HEAD.
- **Fix 2** (`internal/eval/creds.go:84-108,187`).
  - `outside` is set only for a directory link.
  - `resolvesUnder` fails closed when either EvalSymlinks errors.
  - A link to the root itself resolves to "." and is skipped, which is correct because the root is walked. A link to an ancestor resolves to ".." and counts.
  - Retargeting an intermediate directory into a link creates a new problem path, which counts.
  - Mutation: `TestCredsBaselineLinkOutsideCounts` fails on the parent ("passes: []") and passes at HEAD. `TestCredsLinkProblems` still passes.
- **Fix 5** (`internal/trail/trail.go:284-293`).
  - The order holds: a read error still refuses, because `err` is checked after the join.
  - `memory.Root` delegates to `trail.Roots` (`internal/memory/memory.go:36-37`).
  - The scratch probe (`.agents/scratch/sec-r2/probe`, `.agents/scratch/sec-r2/rootsprobe`) gave the result in the Verdict.
  - Mutation: the relative subtest fails on the parent ("is not a worktree … registers") and passes at HEAD.
- **Dream "future record" fix** (`internal/brain/dream.go`, `internal/dream/collect.go`, `internal/dream/dream.go`). Records updated after `now` are left out of both the news and `Last`. `activityIn`'s dropped `!in.Last.After(now)` is now implied by the new filter, so behaviour is unchanged. `TestForDreamIgnoresARecordFromTheFuture` passes.
- **Secrets / instruction-shaped text.**
  - Every added line was read.
  - The one changed line in `.agents/trail.jsonl` (record SPEC-fyr-eval) changes `updated` and one sentence of check d, which now describes the outside-link rule. I diffed it field by field, via `.agents/scratch/sec-r2/trail-lines.txt`. It holds no credentials, no private data and no text addressed to a reviewer.
  - `skills/harness-audit/references/areas.md`: a test-path correction only.
- **Injection:** no new exec or SQL surface. The only path inputs are git output and the scanned tree, covered above.
- **Authz/authn:** not in the scope. The trust boundary is the project-scope check, which is covered under fix 5.
- **Crypto:** nothing touched, nothing hand-rolled.
- **Dependencies:**
  - `go.mod` and `go.sum` are unchanged in the range.
  - `govulncheck ./...` on go1.27.3 found 0 vulnerabilities that the code reaches, plus 1 in a required module that is not called (the known GO-2026-5024 class, ADR-045a).
  - `npm audit` does not apply (no JS).
- **GCP surface:** none.

## Not examined
- Git 2.48+ was not available (the box has 2.47.3). I hand-wrote the relative `gitdir`, as the new test does. I did not observe whether a 2.48+ `git worktree add --relative-paths` also writes a relative `commondir`, or whether it changes how `--absolute-git-dir` is printed.
- No full `go test -race ./...`. Only the targeted tests ran, at HEAD and against the parent: `internal/brain`, `eval`, `memory`, `trail`, `dream`.
- `sh-agent search --refs <path> --kind bug` / `fyr search --refs` was not run for the changed files. The bug history was taken only from the round-1 report.
- `ImportGlobal`'s problem line for a memory file names `.agents/memory/<f>` without the project's scope. This is usability only, not followed up.
- No live `fyr eval`, `fyr dream --dry-run` or service-manager run.
- The working tree is not clean at hand-back. `.agents/trail.jsonl` shows ` M`, with the file's mtime at 20:22:07: two records, `GUIDE-eval` and `GUIDE-skill-matrix`, have `updated` 19:21:58Z and 19:22:07Z.
  - This review did not write it. My commands were reads, `go test` on temp directories, `git archive` into scratch and a `trail.Roots` probe, and none of them writes the checkout's trail.
  - It looks like a concurrent writer, probably a `fyr record` run by another session.
  - Those changes were not reviewed. The caller should identify the writer before committing.

## Outcome
- Finding 1 (EvalSymlinks before the join): rebutted. git prints `--absolute-git-dir` with links resolved, and this review's own probe showed the planted case refused, so no trigger reaches the join. Code with no failing test is not added (DoD step 2).
- Finding 2 (copy when ~/.config/fyr exists without brain.db): fixed in 74ecdda, `TestBrainCopyStaysUnderTheStateDir`.
- The trail.jsonl edits it saw were the main agent's GUIDE-eval and GUIDE-skill-matrix rows, committed in 74ecdda.

title: Security review — v3.0.0 gate, the ten uncovered commits (2026-10-26)
body:
---
owner: security
date: 2026-10-26
---
# Security review — v3.0.0 release gate, scoped commits   (2026-10-26)

Range reviewed: 0a1bd0c, f28e8bc, 76327b8, b54395d, a5c70e0, 927c69f, e2435b5, 52259a5, 5593cb8, f8cc874 (head 19c2d2a). Each commit was read as its own diff (`git show <c> -- . ':!.agents/trail.jsonl'`), and then the code those diffs call.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS (5 low, no medium or high)

Nothing in the scoped diffs opens a path out of the machine, a cross-project read or a sandbox escape. The fixes they claim do hold:
- `memory.Root` and `trail.Roots` now check that a linked worktree is registered.
- `openPlain` and `openRegular` judge the file they actually opened.
- `trail.Log` passes `--no-textconv`.
- The eval sandbox holds an `os.Root` handle, and `unlink` runs before `intact()`.
- Feedback records are redacted as JSON lines.
- The timer probe keeps a timer the operator turned off turned off.

The worst finding is a reverted guard. 76327b8 removed the `checkRecord` call per memory file in `readMemoryStore`. The round-2 security review in that same commit had shown the call was load-bearing (its mutation m7). Without it, one oversized memory file is reported as importable in a dry run, and the real run then aborts the whole import transaction. The global import is hit too. It fails closed, so nothing is bypassed. It is an integrity regression in the import's own guard, and the spec claim "checked … in a dry run too" is now false for memory records.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/brain/import_memory.go:~103-107` (76327b8; the call was at import.go:825) — the `checkRecord` → `problem` step was removed, on the claim "Every field is valid by here".
  - Why the claim is false: the body is `"type: <t>\n\n" + body`, built after `readRegular(..., maxBody)` (import_guard.go:52-60). A memory file within about 16 bytes of 1 MiB therefore builds a body over `maxBody`, and `normalize` does not cap bodies. `day` and `updated` stay "" when `modified:` does not parse and `e.Info()` fails.
  - Effect: `Import` (import.go:136-140) and `ImportGlobal` (import_global.go:161-175) append these records with no check. A dry run reports success and lists the file for removal. The real run's `insertNew` re-check (import.go:187) returns an error and rolls back every record in the batch. In the global case that means every project, plus feedback, retros and proposals.
  - Precondition: a same-user write to an untracked `.agents/memory/` file of any indexed project.
  - Fix: restore the per-file `checkRecord(r)` in `readMemoryStore` as a `problem` ("…; not imported"). Add a test with a memory file of `maxBody` bytes that asserts a `problem` line and a successful import of the rest. It must fail with the check removed.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/eval/creds.go:165-168` (`newCreds`, 5593cb8) — a link problem that the baseline held with the same `Readlink` target is now skipped.
  - When the target resolves inside the sandbox it is walked under its own path, so the skip is harmless.
  - When a fixture-tracked link points outside the sandbox (an absolute target, or `../..` past the clone), the agent can write a credential through it, and check e never sees it. Before this commit, such a link always failed closed.
  - Fix: skip only when `filepath.EvalSymlinks(link)` stays inside `w.dir` (where the scan already covers it). Otherwise keep it as a problem. Add a test with a tracked absolute link to a temp directory that the fake agy writes a key into.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/dream/dream.go:~372-381` (`brainCopy`, b54395d) — when there is no live store yet, the dry run's copy home is `os.MkdirTemp("")`, the system temp directory.
  - `forDream` then creates a `brain.db` there and loads the project's `trail.jsonl` into it.
  - The directory is 0700 and is removed by a `defer`. A killed run leaves it behind, and `removeCopies` sweeps only `~/.config/fyr` (run.go:455-458), so nothing reclaims it.
  - It also breaks the project's never-`/tmp` rule.
  - Fix: always create the copy under `filepath.Dir(brain.Path(home))`, making it 0700 when it is missing, so the existing sweep covers it.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/dream/timer.go:294-313` (`timerUnit.on`, f8cc874) — the probe decides on a privacy question (whether the nightly job sends content to the model provider again), and it fails open.
  - Any probe failure other than `disabled`, `masked` or "Could not find service" counts as on, and the old unit is replaced with `enable --now`.
  - In the common indeterminate case (no user bus), `enable` fails the same way and the old unit is kept, so the real exposure is narrow.
  - States not covered: a launchd label the operator disabled with `launchctl disable` while it is still loaded.
  - Fix, optional: when the probe is indeterminate, keep the old unit untouched, install nothing and print the `--install-timer` command, rather than replacing it.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/memory/memory.go:~88-99` and `internal/trail/trail.go:275-288` (0a1bd0c) — the registration check compares `filepath.Dir(<gitDir>/gitdir)` with `top` directly.
  - git 2.48+ with `worktree.useRelativePaths` writes a relative `gitdir`, and `EvalSymlinks` resolves that against fyr's own working directory. Legitimate relative worktrees are therefore refused.
  - This fails closed and cannot be exploited; it is an availability defect.
  - Fix: when the content is relative, resolve it against `gitDir` before comparing. Add a test that uses `git worktree add --relative-paths` when the git version allows it.

## Checked
- **Secrets:** I scanned every added line of all ten diffs for PRIVATE KEY, AKIA, AIza, ya29., sk-ant-, gho_, ghp_, refresh_token and password=.
  - The one hit is f8cc874's review text naming test fixtures (AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE). That is not a credential.
  - I re-ran the scan with an instruction-shape grep ("ignore previous", "disregard", "skip the check", key= shapes) over every added Markdown line, including the tails of lines over 400 characters (scratch `.agents/scratch/sec-2010/tails.txt`): 0 hits.
  - The trail Markdown (reviews, changes, testing logs, plan, deploy guides, spec) holds no credentials or private data beyond this box's paths and user name. No text there is addressed to a reviewer as an instruction.
- **Injection / parsing:**
  - `-G` is a separate argv element quoted with `regexp.QuoteMeta`, which suits git's extended regular expressions. `trail.Log` is the only caller that passes a content diff (check/specs.go:107).
  - `cmd/fyr/eval.go:191` uses `trail.Command("show", "HEAD:…")` with no textconv, since there is no `--textconv` and the blob is shown raw.
  - `spans()` is now linear.
  - `capped` never reads more than one byte past the cap.
  - The import's `-N` suffix loop terminates, and the feedback body is the raw line, so it can no longer be amplified by indentation.
  - The `git rm --literal-pathspecs --` text closes the glob and option readings.
- **Redaction:** `redactFeedback` runs `json.Compact` and then `RedactJSONL`, which tries the raw needles first and then the decoded line. A body that is not JSON falls back to the raw needles. `TestFeedbackRecordsAreRedactedAsJSON` pins the `&sig=` case.
- **Path / symlink handling:**
  - `openPlain` uses O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK and then fstat.
  - `check.openRegular` opens with O_NONBLOCK through `os.Root` and then fstats.
  - `splitLine` strips every trailing slash (GO-2026-4970).
  - In eval, the held `os.Root` (taken at prepare, after guard a) is used for the token unlink, which now runs whether or not the sandbox is intact. A second session runs only when `intact()` holds. Planted output files fail the row as replaced. `scanCreds` no longer follows a linked root. Oversized files are a problem.
  - `outsideCheckout` now matches only git's discovery-failure text, with `GIT_*` stripped and `GIT_DISCOVERY_ACROSS_FILESYSTEM=1`. It fails closed.
- **Eval split (52259a5):** I sorted removed lines against added lines. The only differences are blank, `package` and `import` lines, so it is a pure move.
- **Dream:** ForDream compares parsed times. `activityIn` ignores future-dated records. `ProposeAll` writes one transaction with `checkRecord`. The title prefix is code-set, so model text cannot choose "project" or "harness". `targets()` deduplicates by `trail.Roots`. A dry run reads a copy of the store.
- **Metrics (a5c70e0):** `_txlock=immediate` is appended to the DSN. Locking only; no new input surface.
- **Authz / authn:** not in scope. The trust boundaries are a project checkout and the eval sandbox, both covered above.
- **Crypto:** none touched. Nothing hand-rolled.
- **Dependencies:** go.mod and go.sum are not in the scoped diffs. `/home/kesokaj/.go/bin/govulncheck ./...` on go1.27.3 reports "Your code is affected by 0 vulnerabilities", plus 1 advisory in a required module that the code does not call (the known GO-2026-5024 class, ADR-045a). `npm audit` does not apply (no JS ecosystem).
- **GCP surface:** none.
- **Rules / skills (e2435b5, 5593cb8, b54395d `skills/retro`):** `rules/code-modularity.md` holds only process text and grants no permissions. The retro routing by title prefix keeps dream text marked as data.

## Not examined
- `.agents/trail.jsonl` in every commit: excluded by the dispatch.
- The two renamed kit scripts in f28e8bc (`.agents/kit/agy-rel/run.sh`, `.agents/kit/kit-preamble.sh`): the stat shows pure renames with 0 changed lines. Their content was not re-read in this review.
- I ran no probe or mutation for any finding. Finding 1 rests on reading the code plus the round-2 review's recorded mutation m7. Findings 2 to 5 are from reading the code only.
- I did not run `fyr search --refs <path> --kind bug` for the changed files. The bug history was consulted only through the review records in the range.
- `search.copyDB`'s file modes were not read. The copy sits in a 0700 directory either way.
- No real `systemctl` or `launchctl`, and no live `fyr eval` run.

## Outcome
- Finding 1 (memory import check): fixed in e53a7cb, with the test above.
- Finding 2 (baseline directory link outside the sandbox): fixed in e53a7cb. `TestCredsBaselineLinkOutsideCounts` fails without it, and SPEC-fyr-eval check d and GUIDE-testing say so. The 35 eval rows ran under the new rule, 35 of 35 PASS (TEST-2026-10-26-2131 and -2135).
- Finding 3 (dry-run copy in the system temp dir): rebutted in round 1 (creating ~/.config/fyr from a dry run beside ~/.config/sh-agent would turn the crossing's migration into the both-exist case), then fixed in round 2's narrower form (74ecdda): under ~/.config/fyr whenever that directory exists, never created. `TestBrainCopyStaysUnderTheStateDir` fails without it.
- Finding 4 (timer probe fails open): rebutted. A manager that cannot be asked counts as on, by design and as documented (DEPLOY-remote § Crossing to fyr). In the common indeterminate case `enable` fails the same way and the old unit stays. Security round 2 accepted this.
- Finding 5 (relative worktree gitdir): fixed in e53a7cb. The `linked worktree registered by a relative path` subtest fails without it.

title: Review — BUG-181 fix 3db3c77 (2026-10-26)
body:
# Review — bug-181   (2026-10-26)

Range reviewed: 3db3c77 (one commit on `followups`; the `.agents/trail.jsonl` hunk read only for BUG-181 and SPEC-fyr-metrics text)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing broken. The fix lands in `agyTime`, the one parser both callers share (`internal/metrics/agy.go:114`, `internal/search/dream.go:133`), so the zero time is no time in both. Migration 3 only appends (R4 holds: no rebuild, migrations 1 and 2 untouched). It is safe from schema 1 and from schema 2. `go vet` and `go test -count=1 ./internal/metrics ./internal/search` pass. Every new test failed under a mutation made in a scratch copy. Remaining items are low-severity and about the "class" claim in the Prevention paragraph, not about the fix.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/metrics/events.go:232-233` — BUG-181's Prevention rule says every time column's guard has a test with Go's zero time as input. This site has no guard. `time.ParseInLocation("2006-01-02", r.Date, ...)` on a record dated `0001-01-01` stores `events.ts` as a negative value. The same shape appears at `events.go:283-287` (`recordTime`, a year-0001 stamp in a record ID) and `events.go:460-464` (`correctionRef`, a feedback `ts` of `0001-01-01T00:00:00Z`). Those inputs are fyr's own trail and feedback records, not "another program's store", so this is not a regression and not the BUG-181 class as written. Still, the Prevention text overstates coverage. Either narrow the sentence to Antigravity's store or add the guard. No failure observed today.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/metrics/agy.go:201,32 (writer.step)` — step `ts` is `int64(varint)*1000`. A varint of 2^63 or more wraps to a negative `steps.ts`. `sessions.started_at` and `ended_at` are protected by `if ts > 0` (agy.go:216), but `steps.ts` is not, and `writer.step` stores it unguarded. A zero step timestamp is stored as 0, not NULL. This is a different column from the three the commit repairs, and migration 3 does not touch `steps.ts`. It is speculative (needs a corrupt or hostile Antigravity db). I list it only because the Prevention text claims the class is closed.

- **[low / confidence: high]** Working-tree note — `git status` in the worktree listed ` M internal/eval/{creds,guard,procs_linux}_test.go` at one point, and `git diff --stat` was empty a few calls later. That looks like a stat-dirty index rather than a content change, and nothing in this commit touches them. I made no edit there.

## Checks requested

1. **Every site of the class (a time read from another program's store guarded only by `!= 0`).** Within the two stores fyr reads from Antigravity there are two paths for the summary time. Both go through `agyTime`: the metrics ingest (`agy.go:114`, then `NULLIF(?, 0)` at agy.go:189 and the `ingest_state` write at agy.go:246) and the dream list (`dream.go:133`, where the zero time was already excluded by `!t.After(since)`). `agyTime` also covers the `[]byte` branch (recursion through `string`), the `time.Time` branch and both layouts. A zero time in a non-UTC offset (`0001-01-01 00:00:00+01:00`) has a negative Unix value, so it is also rejected. Step timestamps are a separate source (see finding 2). There are no other `agyTime` callers (`search.AgyTime` is a thin export, export.go:32).

2. **Migration 3 safety.**
   - From schema 1: migrations 2 and 3 both run in the existing transaction. The three UPDATEs name only columns and tables created by migration 1, so they work. Multi-statement `tx.Exec` is already used by migration 1. `TestMigrationOneToCurrent` still passes.
   - From schema 2: run by `TestMigrationRepairsZeroTimes`.
   - Idempotent: a store already at 3 never re-runs it, and a re-run would be a no-op anyway.
   - Real negative values that are not the zero time: the predicate is `< 0`, so any pre-1970 value is nulled, not only -62135596800000. That is intended ("a time before 1970 is no time") and matches the new `agyTime` rule. No legitimate source in this tool produces a negative time. Claude transcript times come from `ts` fields in transcripts; a negative `ended_at` has no other origin than this bug. A real session with steps already has a positive `ended_at`/`started_at`, since `MIN`/`MAX` with step times replaced the negative value. A row with `started_at` NULL and a real `ended_at` is left alone.
   - `ingest_state.mtime` set to 0: the next ingest reads `c.modified = 0`, finds `mtime == c.modified` (agy.go:83) and skips, so the conversation is not re-read. The session row is left NULL, as the test asserts.
   - Behavioural note, not a defect: a zero-time or unparseable-time conversation is re-ingested only when its summary time changes. That was already true before the fix (unparseable gave 0), and Antigravity updates `last_modified_time` when steps are added.

3. **Readers of `started_at` / `ended_at` / `ingest_state.mtime` relying on the old values.** `show.go:44-45` uses `COALESCE(started_at, ended_at, 0)` for the window filter, so a NULL now yields 0, which sorts before every window (excluded), where the negative value was excluded too: same outcome, no relied-on value. `events.go:59-60` requires both columns NOT NULL, so such a session is skipped, which is correct. `agy.go:197` and 217 use `COALESCE(...,0)`, so NULL is handled. The only `mtime` reader is `agy.go:83`. No reader depends on the negative value.

4. **Do the new tests fail without their part of the fix?** I ran each mutation in a scratch copy from `git archive HEAD` (each target text occurred exactly once; each mutated tree compiled and a named test failed), then deleted the copy.
   - Reverting `agyTime` (both `return t, t.Unix() >= 0` and `return agyTime(parsed)`): `TestAgyTime` fails on all three new inputs (`time.Time{}`, the text zero time, 1969) and `TestAgyZeroTimeIsNoTime` fails with `ended_at -62135596800000, mtime -62135596800000; want NULL and 0`.
   - Replacing each of the three migration UPDATEs with `SELECT 1;`, one at a time: `TestMigrationRepairsZeroTimes` fails each time (`0,7,0` for either session-column mutation, `1,7,-62135596800000` for the mtime mutation).
   - The tests prove their conditions: `TestAgyZeroTimeIsNoTime` scans the session row (a missing row would be `ErrNoRows` and fatal) and the ingest_state row. `TestMigrationRepairsZeroTimes` includes an untouched positive row (`ok`, ended 7). Gap: `s.db.Exec` errors in that test setup are ignored, but a failed insert would make the final assertion fail, so it is not a false pass. Not covered: a negative non-zero-time value (e.g. -1) in the migration test, the `[]byte` branch of `agyTime`, and a non-UTC zero time.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. Nothing left behind.
2. Flow tracing — pass. Both `agyTime` callers, the insert guard, the `ingest_state` write and the skip check at agy.go:83 agree on 0 as "no time".
3. Standards conformance — pass with nits. Describing text is updated (SPEC-fyr-metrics § Data, the `agyTime` doc comment, the migration comment, the test comments). The Prevention paragraph's "every time column" claim is broader than what the commit covers (findings 1 and 2).
4. Directory layout — pass. Tests sit beside the code; no new files.
5. Simplicity — pass. Stdlib and SQL only; no dependency; nothing in the DIY-except-security area.
6. Decoupling — pass. The fix sits in the shared parser, so the two packages cannot drift.

## Not examined
- The full `go test ./...` (including the long `cmd/fyr` run) was not run; only `go vet` and `go test` on `internal/metrics` and `internal/search`. `gofmt -l` was not run.
- `govulncheck` not run.
- The BUG-181 repro against a real store copy (`.agents/scratch/m2/metrics.db`) was not repeated; I relied on the tests and the record.
- The `.agents/trail.jsonl` hunk was read only for BUG-181 and the SPEC-fyr-metrics § Data sentence. I did not diff the rest of the SPEC record or check other restatements of the "Every time is stored..." rule beyond a grep for schema-number mentions (none stale).
- No `fyr` command was run.

## Outcome

- Low, `internal/metrics/events.go:232-233` (and 283-287, 460-464): rebutted as a code change. Those parses read fyr's own trail and feedback records, not another program's store, which is the class BUG-181 names. Fixed in the record: BUG-181's prevention now scopes its test clause to time columns fed from another program's store.
- Low, `steps.ts` with no `> 0` guard (`writer.go:32`, `agy.go:201`): left. A negative value needs a varint over 2^63/1000 seconds, which means a corrupt Antigravity database; no store copy holds one. Owner: main, reopened if one appears.

title: Review — followups 3db3c77..28f3cb4, code and docs (2026-10-26)
body:
# Review — followups (2026-10-26)

Range reviewed: 3db3c77..HEAD, code and docs lenses. HEAD moved during the review: it was 28e0fcb (7 commits) when read, then 28f3cb4 (BUG-183, a test-and-record commit) landed on top; findings below say which state each was seen in. Final-state `go test` of check, metrics and eval packages: ok; `gofmt -l cmd internal` empty; `go vet` clean on the three packages. Not run: full `go test -race ./...`.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES (one docs finding, small)

`fyr check` on the final HEAD reports 2 findings, and one of them is the range's own new text: the new GUIDE-eval bullet (line 24) names `internal/greet/greet.go` in backticks, a fixture path that does not exist in this checkout, so the project's drift check fails on it. Everything else in the range is sound: the new check rule, the metrics vocabulary test and the doc edits agree with the code. One of the new eval check cells can pass without the behaviour it names (low).

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** GUIDE-eval record, line 24 (the new `rule-code-modularity` bullet) — `internal/greet/greet.go` is in backticks, and `./fyr check --home <scratch>` on HEAD prints `GUIDE-eval:24  path  \`internal/greet/greet.go\`: internal/greet/greet.go does not exist`. The file lives in the eval fixture (`~/sandbox/fyr-eval/fixture`), not here. Before this range `fyr check` was clean on that record, so the range turned the docs check red. Fix: drop the backticks or name it as the fixture's file (a bare `greet.go` outside a spec's Verification section is not read, SPEC-fyr-check § Known limits), then re-run `fyr check`.

- **[low / confidence: high]** SPEC-fyr-eval (`spec-stale`, same `fyr check` run) — "1 commit to cmd/fyr/eval.go internal/eval cmd/fyr since e0069cbb3cf6": the commit is 28f3cb4 (suite_test.go gained the four `want` rows). Re-read the spec and re-stamp; the spec names no row count, so no text should need to change (grep for `rule-`, `56`, `60 rows` in SPEC-fyr-eval/GUIDE-eval found none).

- **[low / confidence: high]** e139789 (GUIDE-eval row `rule-code-modularity`) — as committed, `go test ./internal/eval` failed: `TestSuiteHarness: suite_test.go:169: 60 rows, want 56` (I saw it at 28e0fcb). Fixed by 28f3cb4 (BUG-183), so the final tree is green; recorded here only because that commit alone is not bisect-safe, and e139789's message says the check was "validated in three states" without a `go test`. BUG-183's prevention rule already covers it.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** GUIDE-eval `rule-code-modularity` check cell — `f=$(grep -l "^func Shout" internal/greet/*.go) && [ "$f" != internal/greet/greet.go ]` passes when `Shout` is defined in a `_test.go` file, or when two files match (`$f` is then multi-line and unequal). I reproduced the first in a scratch clone of the fixture: setup grows greet.go to 432 lines (so the premise holds); the check fails before any work (exit 1), passes with `Shout` in `extra_test.go` (exit 0), passes with `shout.go` (exit 0). The behaviour it names ("the new function lands in a new non-test file") is therefore not what the cell proves. Fix: `grep -l ... $(ls internal/greet/*.go | grep -v _test.go)` and require exactly one match. Also: the lead's brief said two new rows; this range adds one (the three `build-*` rows came in f12f499, before the base).

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/check/verification.go:57-69` — section bounds are line-prefix tests that ignore fences: a `## ` line inside a code fence in the Verification section (a shell comment, a Markdown example) ends the section early, so later names go unchecked; a fenced `## Verification` starts it early. Only false negatives, and no current record is affected (I scanned all 8 current specs: 3 have a `## Verification` heading, none has a fenced `## ` line in it, none uses CRLF). `### Verification` is correctly neither a start nor an end; CRLF is harmless (`\r` sits at line ends, the prefixes and the span regexp are unaffected). No test covers a fenced heading; adding one case to `TestVerificationFileNames` would pin it, or reuse `scan`'s fence state.

## Checked and fine

- The new rule on real records: no false positive on any current spec (final `fyr check` shows no `path` finding in a Verification section; SPEC-fyr-metrics now names `agy_tools_test.go`, which exists). SPEC-fyr-check's own examples (`agy_test.go`, `tools_test.go`, `foo.go` at line 94/124) sit outside a `## Verification` section and are not read. Only SPEC-fyr-dream, -eval and -metrics have that heading; SPEC-fyr-check, -search, -record, -delivery and -memory-loop have none, so the rule does not read them (as the spec says).
- Test: `TestVerificationFileNames` can fail without the rule: it expects exactly `SPEC-a:10 path`, and without `verificationFindings` the finding is absent; it also pins outside-section, fenced, retired-spec, directory-bearing and `:N` names, and the `## After` bound. I did not run a mutation (no edits allowed), so "fails without the rule" rests on reading.
- `internal/metrics/agy_tools_test.go`: want table is independent of `agyTools` and matches it and the SPEC-fyr-metrics vocabulary table (10 Antigravity names plus one unmapped); a dropped or changed mapping would fail; passes.
- SPEC-fyr-dream's BUG-181 sentence matches `agyTime` (`internal/search/dream.go:155`, `t.Unix() >= 0`, and the caller at :133 skips `!ok`). BUG-179's `migrate.go:48` cite is the `case cur:` line, correct; `obsolete` is a valid status (`internal/brain/record.go:129`). BUG-181's prevention rewording is consistent. GUIDE-testing § 3d target split and ROADMAP "Next" are text-only and agree with the commit messages; the 35-39 / 90-177 ms figures were not re-measured.
- `internal/eval` comment edits: names cited (`TestKitPreambleRefusesLeftoverCredentials`, `TestKitPreambleKillsLeftoverProcesses` at 8374f9c) were not re-resolved against that commit (see below).

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass; nothing left behind.
2. Flow tracing — pass; `verificationFindings` is wired in `Run` after the docs rule and runs with or without a trail/history note; test can fail.
3. Standards conformance — fail on the docs side only: GUIDE-eval:24 trips `fyr check`; SPEC-fyr-eval is stale by the tool's own rule.
4. Directory layout — pass; new Go files sit beside their package (`internal/check/verification*.go`, `internal/metrics/agy_tools_test.go`).
5. Simplicity — pass; stdlib only, no dependency, no security-sensitive code.
6. Decoupling — pass; the rule takes `[]brain.Record` and the tracked list through the existing checker.

## Not examined
- Full `go test -race ./...` and `govulncheck` (only check, metrics and eval packages were tested).
- The three internal/eval comment edits' cited test names at 8374f9c (not resolved with `git show`).
- `fyr eval` behavioural runs of the new row (forbidden here); I reproduced its setup and check by hand in a scratch clone, not the CLI's behaviour.
- The 28f3cb4 BUG-183 record and REVIEW-2026-10-26-2339 record bodies beyond their headlines; SPEC-fyr-search and the `REVIEW-…bug-181` record text.
- Timing claims in GUIDE-testing § 3d.

## Outcome

Round 1 fixes are in 7774710; `fyr check` on it: 0 findings.
- [medium] GUIDE-eval:24 named the fixture's file as a path of this checkout: fixed, written `<clone>/internal/greet/greet.go`.
- [low] SPEC-fyr-eval stale after 28f3cb4: re-read (it names no row count) and re-stamped.
- [low] e139789 not bisect-safe: recorded as BUG-183 (fixed in 28f3cb4); not rewritten, since history is never rewritten.
- [low] the modularity check passed on a `Shout` in a `_test.go` file: fixed (`grep -v "_test\.go$"`, `[ -n "$f" ]`); validated in four states: none 1, new file 0, in greet.go 1, only in a _test.go file 1.
- [low] fenced `## ` lines bounded the Verification section: fixed in `internal/check/verification.go` with scan's fence rule; `TestVerificationFileNames` gained a fenced `## ` line and a name after the fence, and fails when the fence skip is removed (mutation run, restored, package green).

title: Preflight — v3.0.0 (2026-10-26): SHIP
body:
# Preflight — v3.0.0   (2026-10-26)

Range reviewed: v2.7.0..1acfc6c

Owner: main. Requested by the operator in their own turn this session: "You run these things. Just go ffs", answering a table whose item 1 was `/preflight v3.0.0`. Version: MAJOR, because the installed command changes name from `sh-agent` to `fyr` (DEPLOY-remote § Releases; plan `PLAN-2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only` Phase 6).

## Failures and what cleared them (FAIL-first)

- **[cleared] Reviewer round 1: REQUEST CHANGES** (`REVIEW-2026-10-26-2142-review-v3-0-0-gate-the-ten-uncovered-commits-cod`; 1 medium, 2 low; confidence high, high and medium).
  - All three were fixed in e53a7cb, each with a test that fails without its fix.
  - The medium's empty-description trigger was rebutted: `normalize` titles it "untitled", and the test pins that. Its real trigger, a body pushed past maxBody, is fixed.
  - Round 2 (`REVIEW-2026-10-26-2142-review-round-2-v3-0-0-gate-fixes-e53a7cb-code-an`): APPROVE WITH NITS, 1 low (GUIDE-testing's link clause), fixed in 74ecdda. Each fix was confirmed by mutation.
- **[cleared] Security round 1: 5 low, none medium or high** (`REVIEW-2026-10-26-2142-security-review-v3-0-0-gate-the-ten-uncovered-co`).
  - Fixed in e53a7cb: findings 1, 2 and 5.
  - Finding 3: rebutted, then fixed in its narrower form in 74ecdda.
  - Finding 4: rebutted, with the behaviour as documented.
  - Round 2 (`REVIEW-2026-10-26-2142-security-review-round-2-v3-0-0-gate-fixes-e53a7c`): 2 low. One was fixed in 74ecdda; the other was rebutted, since git resolves the git dir and the security agent's own probe refused the planted case. Both rebuttals were accepted.
- **[cleared] Verifier FAIL at d341d8f** (`TEST-2026-10-26-2142-verify-v3-0-0-gate-v2-7-0-d341d8f-fail-on-fyr-ch`): `fyr check` gave 7 findings.
  - Cause: today's fixes left SPEC-fyr-dream's text and five spec stamps behind, and the GUIDE-eval note named a path.
  - Fix: d15d0a2 corrected SPEC-fyr-dream (where the dry-run copy goes, and the future-record bound), re-stamped five specs after reading each against e53a7cb and 74ecdda, and reworded the note.
  - Re-run: `TEST-2026-10-26-2146-…-d15d0a2-pass-re-run-af` PASS, then the logs at 1acfc6c below.
- **[cleared] Eval 34 of 35 at 74ecdda** (`TEST-2026-10-26-2131-eval-34-of-35-pass-at-74ecdda`): the `docker` row failed with an auto-denial.
  - Cause: the row's wording, not the skill. The skill had the agent run a read-only `docker buildx imagetools inspect`, which named grants do not cover, and headless Antigravity stopped.
  - Fix: c92219f's row says to run no docker command.
  - Re-run: `TEST-2026-10-26-2135-eval-1-of-1-pass-at-c92219f` PASS.
- **[found and fixed during the gate, low / high] GUIDE-testing § 3d** ran `go test ./internal/search -run TestRecall`, which runs no test (TestRecall moved to cmd/fyr in 9001831). Fixed in 1acfc6c; the § 3d run below uses the new path.

## Step 1 — the release diff

`git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` was clean at the start. Base: v2.7.0 (`git describe --tags --abbrev=0`). The range is 200+ commits, 1,908 files and +34k/−126k lines (the rename, the Claude Code removal, the record trail, fyr check, fyr eval, metrics and the modularity splits). The gate's own fix commits are e53a7cb, 74ecdda, c92219f, d15d0a2 and 1acfc6c, each reviewed as above or a record-and-guide change read by the main agent.

## Step 2 — review, security, verification

- **Security:** the range touches input parsing, paths, the eval sandbox's credential scan, the release fetch path and dependencies, so a security review is owed. It is covered by `REVIEW-2026-10-25-security-v2.7.0-head` and the segment reviews of the same ranges (each COMPLETE), and for the ten uncovered commits by the two rounds above. The round-1 report's `## Not examined` names two kit scripts in f28e8bc that are pure renames with zero changed lines, so no changed line in the release diff went unread. No high finding.
- **Verification**:
  1. Verifier logs reaching HEAD (1acfc6c is HEAD; after it only records changed), all PASS:

  2. What the release changed was run: the plan's tiers are unit, § 3, § 3a, § 3d, § 3g, behavioural runs on Antigravity for every changed skill and agent, the crossing on a scratch place, and the real places after the tag.

Together: one run on Antigravity of every changed skill, agent and rule since its last change, the google-catalog router's `catalog-no-leak`, `catalog-route-1..6` and `catalog-precedence` among them.
     - The crossing on a scratch place: `TEST-2026-10-25-verify-fyr-crossing-local` (Phase 4b).

title: Review — BUG-184 and BUG-185 fixes, working tree on 9242be3 (2026-10-27)
body:
---
owner: reviewer
date: 2026-10-27
---
# Review — bug184-185   (2026-10-27)

Range reviewed: uncommitted working tree on main, diff /home/kesokaj/workspace/styrman-harness/.agents/scratch/agents/diff-bug184-185.patch (read together with internal/eval/creds.go, internal/metrics/agy.go, agy_tools.go and their tests)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

The metrics change (BUG-184) is correct and its test fails without each part of the fix. The credential-scan change (BUG-185) weakens the fail-closed scan more than its comment and its spec line say. Inside a locked node_modules a symlink to a regular file outside the tree, an unreadable (mode 000) file and an oversized file are all now silent, and each was a finding before. The spec records the operator's choice only for "content written there, not seen". No finding is a requirements violation. `go test` for TestCredsLockedModules, TestAgyPathKeys and TestAgyToolVocabulary passes (-count=1). Not run: the full suite, vet and govulncheck. `sh-agent` is not on PATH, so the past-bug search was not run.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/eval/creds.go:161` — With `read` false, `scanEntry` returns before any content read. A file symlink inside a locked `node_modules` that points at a credential file outside the tree (for example `node_modules/x/cfg -> $HOME/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json`) is not a directory link and not dangling, so neither link case fires. The name check sees only the link's own name. Before the change `os.ReadFile` followed the link, so the content scan flagged the credential. Now it passes. This is the BUG-087..123 class (a sandbox that exposes real credentials), and the spec's "checked by name, path and link, never read" does not warn that a link to a file is not caught. Fix: when `!read` and `link` is true, return a finding (or at least read it when `resolvesUnder` is false). Alternatively, skip reading only for non-links. No test covers a link under a locked tree.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/eval/creds.go:141-142` — The comment says "a name, a link and an unreadable file are checked either way". That is wrong. An unreadable file (mode 000, where `os.Stat` succeeds but `ReadFile` fails) and a file over `maxScan` were detected only by the read path, which `read=false` now skips. Under a locked tree both are silently clean; they failed closed before. Either fix the comment and the spec line, or keep the size check (`st.Size() > maxScan`) outside the `read` gate. The mutation "`!read` also skips the size and unreadable problems" is not exercised by any test.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/eval/creds.go:106-116` — The lock condition is a regular file named like a lockfile beside `node_modules`, and the agent under test can create that file. Writing `package-lock.json` makes any later `node_modules` content invisible to the content scan. The operator's choice (2026-10-27, in SPEC-fyr-eval) accepts that content written there is not seen, so I report only that the scan can be disabled by the thing it watches. The baseline does not matter: `locked` is computed per scan, so a lockfile that appears after the baseline still locks the tree. Optional hardening is to require the lockfile in the baseline too, or to leave `node_modules` unlocked when the lockfile is new. The reverse also holds: a monorepo with the lockfile at the root and `packages/*/node_modules` gets no relief (a functional gap, not a security one).

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/eval/creds_test.go:95-118` — Mutations the test would not catch:
  - `strings.HasPrefix(p, d)` with `d` lacking the trailing separator (so a sibling `node_modules_x` is treated as locked). The test has no sibling with a similar prefix.
  - The lockfile list cut to the three tested names (`package-lock.json`, `yarn.lock`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`). `npm-shrinkwrap.json`, `bun.lock` and `bun.lockb` are untested.
  - `Lstat` changed to `Stat`, or `IsRegular()` dropped, in `lockedModules`. A symlinked or directory-shaped lockfile is untested.
  - Any change to symlink, oversize or unreadable handling under the lock. The test has no such rows.

  The test does fail without the fix: the `web/node_modules/prettier/plugins/flow.js` AKIA string would be reported. It also checks that `ui/yarn.lock`, `loose/node_modules` and a plain file named `node_modules` are still read.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/metrics/agy_tools_test.go:255-312` — The test does not catch the mutation that drops the `tool == "Read"` guard on the skill match (a `write_file` of a SKILL.md would store a skill). That guard predates the diff. It also asserts only the trail kind, not the tool name for the new names. TestAgyToolVocabulary covers the names, and the map mutation (`write_file` -> `Edit`) is caught there. I count this as covered.

## Checks asked for

- Does each new test fail without its fix?
  - TestAgyPathKeys: yes for three mutations. Remove the `read_file` map entry and row 1 gets no skill. Remove `Path` and rows 1-4 get no kind. Remove `TargetFile` and rows 5-7 get no kind. Its control row (`view_file`) proves the fixture path is a trail kind, so the equality is not vacuous. I did not run the mutations; I reasoned from the code.
  - TestAgyToolVocabulary: the three new names and the unmapped `manage_subagents` are asserted.
  - TestCredsLockedModules: yes, as described above.
- Same-class sites missed:
  - Other argument keys: `grep_search`, `list_dir` and `find_by_name` take directory or search keys, but only Read, Write and Edit are classified, so no gap there. Go's `json.Unmarshal` matches keys case-insensitively, so a lower-case `path` also lands in `Path`. The conversation DBs on this box show `Path`, `AbsolutePath` and `TargetFile` values that all start with `/`. `targetKind` would class a relative path as "outside" (`filepath.Rel` errors), which holds for `AbsolutePath` today and would silently mislabel a relative `Path`. None seen in the local corpus.
  - Other path consumers: `internal/search/dream.go` reads argument pieces by a string-only rule, not by key name. Its tests name `AbsolutePath` and `TargetFile` only as redaction canaries, so the new `Path` key leaks nothing. Not run against a `Path` canary.
  - Other walks: `scanCreds` is the only caller of `scanEntry` (`row_prepare.go:158` for the baseline, `row_after.go:97` for the check). The baseline and after scans use the same locking function, so they agree.
- Fail-closed properties of the walk:
  - Kept: directory links and dangling links still flag (the checks sit before the `read` gate); `credNames` and `credPaths` are still checked in a locked tree (the test pins `id_rsa`); walk errors on an unreadable directory still flag (the `locked` append happens before the error callback); a symlinked `node_modules` is not walked (`d.IsDir()` is false for links); `scanCreds` still refuses a link as `dir`.
  - Lost: a link to a regular file, an unreadable file, and an oversized file under a locked `node_modules` (findings 1 and 2).

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. The moved `agyTools`, `skillPath` and `agyArgs` leave no stale copies in `agy.go`; the `regexp` import was removed with them.
2. Flow tracing — pass for metrics; the eval scan has the gap in finding 1. Callers of `scanEntry` were all updated.
3. Standards conformance — `scanEntry`'s comment contradicts the `read` gate (finding 2). The `SPEC-fyr-metrics` and `SPEC-fyr-eval` rows in the working-tree `.agents/trail.jsonl` already carry both changes (the path keys, the lockfile rule and the operator-choice note), though the "checked by name, path and link" wording needs the finding 1 caveat.
4. Directory layout — pass. `agy_tools.go` sits beside `agy.go` and is named for its domain, in line with the modularity rule.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. Stdlib only, no new dependency, no auth or crypto code.
6. Decoupling — pass. The tool-vocabulary split into its own file keeps the two seams independent.

## Not examined
- The `.agents/trail.jsonl` spec text beyond the matching rows (only grepped).
- The full test suite, `go vet`, gofmt and govulncheck were not run; only the three named tests (pass).
- No mutation was actually run; all mutation claims are from reading the code.
- `sh-agent search --refs ... --kind bug` and `.agents/docs/bugs/INDEX.md` (no docs root in this project).
- `internal/search/dream.go` in detail beyond the grep above.

## Outcome

- 1 (a file link out of the tree inside a locked node_modules is silent): fixed. `scanCreds` reads a link that does not resolve under the root even inside an install. `TestCredsLockedModules` case `.bin/outside`; the mutation `|| link && false` turns it red.
- 2 (unreadable and oversized files silent; comment overclaims): unreadable is fixed by an `os.Open` under the lock (case `locked.js`, mode 000; mutation caught). Oversized is rebutted: a file under an install is never read, so its size says nothing, and a framework's native binary (Next's SWC, over 64 MiB) would fail every such row. The comment and `SPEC-fyr-eval` check d now say so.
- 3 (test gaps): fixed. The test covers `node_modules.bak` (trailing separator), a symlinked lockfile (`Lstat`), all six lockfile names, links inside and out, and a mode-000 file. Each of those mutations was run and caught (seven in all, restored from a saved copy, diff re-read). An agent-created lockfile hiding a tree is the operator's accepted trade, recorded in `SPEC-fyr-eval` § Known limits.
- Round two over the fixes: not dispatched. The main thread read the fix diff, and each fix is pinned by a mutation that fails without it.

title: Security review — BUG-184 and BUG-185 fixes, working tree on 9242be3 (2026-10-27)
body:
---
owner: security
date: 2026-10-27
---
# Security review — bug184-185   (2026-10-27)

Range reviewed: HEAD 9242be3..working tree (uncommitted on main), as given in .agents/scratch/agents/diff-bug184-185.patch: internal/eval/creds.go, internal/eval/creds_test.go, internal/metrics/agy.go, internal/metrics/agy_tools.go (new), internal/metrics/agy_tools_test.go; and the blast radius: the scan's callers (internal/eval/row_prepare.go:158, row_after.go:95-100), the token it guards (internal/eval/run.go:63, row_session.go:23), the metrics writer (internal/metrics/writer.go targetKind, identifier, nameShape) and search.KindOf (internal/search/parse.go:272).

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

The worst problem is a planned one: check d (the BUG-160 credential scan) no longer reads any file under a `node_modules` that has a lockfile beside it. The scan is there because the live Antigravity OAuth token is symlinked into the sandbox home for the run (`run.go:63`, `row_session.go:23`), and every sandbox is kept on disk afterwards. The token's content copied under that subtree with a name the name patterns miss (say `cp …/antigravity-oauth-token app/node_modules/x/t.json`) now passes. Before, it failed on `refresh_token`/`ya29.`. The condition is easy to meet. Any `npm install` meets it, and that is the normal case in the build-* rows. It is also met by a lockfile of any content, even `{}` or empty, next to a `node_modules` directory anywhere under the sandbox directory, the sandbox HOME included. So one `touch package-lock.json; mkdir node_modules` exempts a whole subtree. SPEC-fyr-eval (trail.jsonl, working tree) records this as the operator's choice of 2026-10-27, so it is an accepted risk, not a hidden one. It is still a real loss of coverage, and the exemption is wider than the problem it fixes (one AKIA-shaped string in prettier). The second finding is smaller. Inside the exempt tree an unreadable (mode 000) file and a file over 64 MiB no longer fail closed. That contradicts both the code comment and the spec sentence, which say they always fail. The metrics change is clean: the new keys feed the same two derivations, so nothing new from tool arguments is stored.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/eval/creds.go:84-86,89,106-116,161` — **What can now get past the scan.** It is any credential *content* written under `<dir>/node_modules/` when a regular file with a lockfile name sits in `<dir>`, at any depth of the sandbox directory (clone, CLI output, logs, sandbox HOME). It must be stored under a name that `credNames`/`credPaths` miss. Before this diff such content was read and failed the row: `gh*_`, PEM key headers, `sk-ant-`, `ya29.`, `"refresh_token"`, AKIA. **How easy the condition is to meet.** (a) Routinely. Every package install creates exactly this pair. npx can also create its own `package-lock.json` + `node_modules` pair under the sandbox HOME's `.npm/_npx/<hash>/` (medium confidence). (b) Trivially on purpose. `lockedModules` checks only that a lockfile name exists as a regular file (`Lstat`+`IsRegular`). It never checks the lockfile's content or that the `node_modules` came from it; the test itself uses `{}`. **Accidental scenarios** (low likelihood, not zero): build tools write caches from the project's own code under `node_modules/.cache/` (babel-loader, terser, eslint) and `node_modules/.vite/`. Values inlined at build time from the environment or a `.env` land there. The `.env` itself is still read, but a copy in the cache is not. **Adversarial agent:** a pattern scan never stopped one (base64 already got past it), so the gain for an adversary is small. The loss is mainly to accidental-leak detection, which is what BUG-160 is about. **Remediation, narrowest first:** (1) Still read dot-directories directly under a locked `node_modules` (`.cache`, `.vite`, `.pnpm` excepted). They hold build output from the project, not third-party code. (2) Compare against the secret itself instead of skipping. When the row links the token, take the token's own `access_token`/`refresh_token` values once, in memory, never logged. Count exact-substring hits in every file, `node_modules` included. That gives zero false positives from third-party code and keeps the BUG-160 guarantee for the one live secret the sandbox holds. (3) At least require a lockfile that is not empty and that existed in the baseline, or that the package manager wrote: a `package-lock.json` whose `lockfileVersion` parses. This raises the bar against a hand-made `{}`. Each option is a design choice for the operator; (2) is the strongest.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/eval/creds.go:141-142,161` — In a locked tree, `!read` returns before the size check and before `os.ReadFile`. A file over `maxScan` therefore no longer produces "larger than … not read", and neither does a file that `os.Stat` can see but `ReadFile` cannot open (mode 000 in a searchable directory) produce "unreadable". Both were fail-closed findings before. The comment "an unreadable file [is] checked either way" is true only for a `Stat` failure. SPEC-fyr-eval's "an unreadable file, or one over 64 MiB (not read), always fails" is now false for this subtree. In practice the effect is small, since the content would be skipped anyway. Fix: either make the comment and the spec sentence name the exception, or keep the oversize/unreadable problems in locked trees (the walk already pays for the `Stat`; checking readability costs one open).

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/eval/creds.go:84,106-111` — When the scan root's own base name is `node_modules`, `lockedModules` checks for a lockfile in the root's *parent*, outside the scanned tree, and can exempt the whole scan. `w.dir` is `<home>/.config/fyr/eval/<stamp>/<row>/`, so this needs a suite row whose id is `node_modules` *and* a lockfile-named file in `<stamp>/`. It is not reachable today in practice. Fix: skip `lockedModules` when `p == root`.

- **[informational / confidence: high]** Path-prefix matching (`underAny`, creds.go:118-125): no confusion found. Entries are `p + Separator`, and `p` comes from `WalkDir`, which joins and cleans children from the same root. So `node_modules2/` or `node_modules-x/` siblings do not match, and nested `node_modules` are covered by the outer prefix. **Symlinks:** `WalkDir` does not descend directory links. A `node_modules` that is a link is not a directory entry and becomes a `dirLink` problem (fail closed), and a lockfile that is a link fails `IsRegular` (not exempt). Both go the safe way. **Case:** `d.Name() != "node_modules"` is case-sensitive, so `Node_Modules` is read, which is safe. On a case-insensitive filesystem (macOS APFS default) a `Package-Lock.json` satisfies the `Lstat`. Since the lockfile proves nothing anyway (finding 1), this adds no new exposure. **Hardlinks:** a hard link to a credential file placed under a locked tree with a harmless name is no longer read. That is a case of finding 1, not a separate path.

- **[informational / confidence: medium]** `internal/eval/row_after.go:93-103` (outside the diff, existing behaviour) — The comment says the scan runs "after the leftover processes are gone". Leftover processes get only SIGTERM before it (`leftoverProcs`) and SIGKILL after it (`:101-103`). A process that ignores SIGTERM can still write, or create a lockfile, while the scan walks. This is a time-of-check-to-time-of-use (TOCTOU) window. The diff makes it a little more useful, because a late `package-lock.json` exempts a subtree. Fix: SIGKILL the process groups before the after-scan.

## Metrics change (question 3)

Nothing new is stored. `agyArgs` gains `Path` and `TargetFile` (agy_tools.go:25-30). `path()` returns the first non-empty one, which feeds exactly the two existing derivations in `agyTool` (agy.go:243-252). (a) `skill`: the regexp group `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+` before `/SKILL.md`, then `identifier`, and only for `Read`. (b) `target_kind`: `targetKind`, a bounded vocabulary of `outside`, `trail`, a trail kind, `code` or `doc` (writer.go:39-48, parse.go:272-294). Neither the raw path nor any other argument key is written. `CommandLine` handling is unchanged (salted hash plus verbs). The new tool names (`read_file`, `write_file`, `edit_file`) only add rows to the constant map. A small existing exposure now also reachable through `read_file`: a directory named like a token under `/skills/` that holds a SKILL.md would be stored as the `skill` value (up to 64 name-shaped characters). This is negligible, since the name has to sit at that exact path shape.

## Checked
- Secrets: none in the diff. The added lines of the working-tree diff of `.agents/trail.jsonl` (2 records, SPEC-fyr-eval and SPEC-fyr-metrics) were grepped for the scan's own credential shapes: no match. The fixture keys in creds_test.go are the test's existing `awsKey`/`ghToken` constants.
- Injection: none; no shell, SQL or template is built from new input (the metrics INSERT stays parameterised).
- Authz/authn: no change. The scan guards the symlinked OAuth token (run.go:63), and the weakening that matters is finding 1.
- Crypto: none added. `w.hash` uses the stdlib `crypto/sha256` with a salt, not hand-rolled, and the diff does not touch it.
- Dependencies: none added (go.mod/go.sum unchanged). `govulncheck ./...` on go1.27.3: no vulnerabilities in reached code, 1 in required modules not called (the known GO-2026-5024 per AGENTS.md; not re-listed verbose). `npm audit`: not applicable, no JS ecosystem in this repo.
- GCP surface: not touched.
- Tests: `go test -count=1 -run 'Creds|Agy' ./internal/eval ./internal/metrics` passes. These are the scoped tests only, not the full suite.

## Not examined
- The full `go test -race ./...` suite; only the two touched packages' Creds/Agy tests were run.
- Whether npx really writes `package-lock.json` beside `node_modules` under `.npm/_npx/<hash>/` (medium confidence from memory, not verified on this box).
- The full SPEC-fyr-eval and SPEC-fyr-metrics records in `.agents/trail.jsonl`. Only the sentences on the node_modules exemption and the fail-closed rule were read.
- Antigravity's real argument keys for each tool (the test's key map is taken on the diff's word); no conversation database was read.

title: Review — cold read of PLAN-2026-10-27-funclen (2026-10-27)

owner: reviewer
date: 2026-10-27
