title: Review — funclen-p2 internal/brain (2026-10-27)
body:
# Review — funclen-phase2-brain   (2026-10-27)

Range reviewed: 91e9d01..working tree (internal/brain, funclen_test.go), diff .agents/scratch/funclen-p2/phase2.diff, code lens only

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

The refactor is behaviour-preserving as far as I can trace it: no regression found in any extracted function. The worst problem is in the claims about untested blocks. Two of the four "reachable only through a seam or a driver failure" claims are false, and both blocks sit in front of a destructive or trust decision. `importTarget`'s trail.Dirty error is reachable from a repo with no commits. `memoryEntries`' git ls-files error is reachable by corrupting `.git/index`. Both take a few lines of fixture, no seam, and no test pins them. Nothing else is wrong.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/brain/import.go` (`importTarget`, the `trail.Dirty` error branch) — claimed unreachable without a seam. It is reachable with no seam. In a `git init` repo with no commit and an uncommitted `.agents/docs/plans/p.md`, a non-dry `Import` returns `checking for uncommitted changes: git ls-tree: exit status 128`. A `.git/index` of garbage on a committed repo gives `... git ls-files: exit status 128`. Both ran against the 91e9d01 code in a scratch copy. This is the guard in front of the import, and it must fail closed when its check cannot run (review-standards § 8, first rule). The code does fail closed. No test proves it, so a later "fix" that treats a Dirty error as clean would pass the suite. Fix: add a test, an unborn repo with a docs file and `dryRun=false`, asserting a non-nil error that is not a refusal, plus `res == nil`. The garbage-index case also works as a second row.

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/brain/import_memory.go` (`memoryEntries`, `git ls-files` error branch) — the claim is false for the same reason. With `.agents/memory/` present and `.git/index` overwritten with garbage, `readMemoryStore` returns `git ls-files .agents/memory: exit status 128` (verified at 91e9d01). The check decides whether tracked, committed memory gets imported and listed for removal, so this is a fail-closed guard in front of a destructive action. The same § 8 test rule applies. Fix: a test that calls `readMemoryStore` on that fixture and asserts the error, and that `recs`, `files` and `problems` are all nil.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/brain/search.go` (`ownHits`, the `st.db.Query` error branch) — the claim is half true. The Query error needs no driver failure. A closed store reaches it: `st, _ := openStore(home); st.close(); ownHits(st, Options{Global: true}, "", "BUG-001", "", 10)` returns `brain: sql: database is closed` (verified on the new code). `ownHits` is a package-level function, so a direct call in a test works. A mutation that drops the `brain:` wrap survived the whole new suite, which confirms the branch is untested. The `Scan` error is correctly judged unreachable: every selected column is `NOT NULL` (store.go:38-49) or an integer rowid, so only a driver failure produces it. Fix: add the closed-store test. The `Scan` branch can stay uncovered, with the gap named.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/brain/import_memory.go` (`memoryEntries`, the non-not-exist `Lstat` branch) — the claim holds. `guardExportPath` runs first and Lstats `.agents` and then `.agents/trail.jsonl`, in the same directory, so anything that makes `Lstat(.agents/memory)` fail with a non-ENOENT error (EACCES, ENOTDIR) already fails the guard. Only a race between the guard and the Lstat reaches it. No finding; this is the judgement the dispatch asked for.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/brain/import_arms_test.go` `TestImportStoreErrors` and `import_global_arms_test.go` `TestImportGlobalStoreErrors` — each takes about 10 s (measured: 10.08 s and 10.04 s) although the test sets `openWait = 100ms`. The override does not govern the failing path. The error comes from the SQLite busy timeout, not `openWait`. The test passes and does assert a real error with `res == nil`, so it is not vacuous. The `openWait` override is dead and the comment "or is busy" does not say which step fails. Cost is about 20 s of suite time under `-race`. Fix: find the step that waits (likely insertNew's BEGIN IMMEDIATE) and shorten the real wait, or drop the dead override.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/brain/brain_input.go`, `checkAdd` — the comment "a plan's is derived from the body below" was moved with the code. In `checkAdd` nothing follows; the body is read in `Add`. This is a stale restatement of position. Fix: "from the body, read after these checks".

## What I verified, by contract item

1. **Behaviour preserved.** Compared old and new by line, function by function.
   - `Add`, `Edit`, `List`: the same checks in the same order. `editFields` still reads stdin before `openSession`, as the original did. `listQuery` is textually the same SQL and argument order.
   - `Search`: `searchQuery` uses `scopeFilter` and `kindFilter`, which are identical to the old inline `if !o.Global` and `kind != "" && kind != "trail"` blocks. The argument order `[q, project?, kind?, date]` is preserved.
   - `Refs`: `ownHits` has the same query, error wrap and `Scan` path. The new `defer orows.Close()` still runs before the second query, because it fires when `ownHits` returns. `seen` and `hits` carry over. `f, args :=` is legal because `f` is now new in `Refs`.
   - `Import`: order is unchanged (target, `readDocs`, `classify`, `outsideText`, `keep`, `removeList`, `Dropped`, `readMemoryStore`, `projectRecords`, `dryRun`, `storeImported`). `importTarget` returns on the same errors with the same text. `storeImported` keeps `defer s.close()`, `insertNew(recs, true)`, `Skipped` and `filterStored`.
   - `ImportGlobal`: the same order (feedback, retros, proposals, memories, `Sources`, `dryRun`, store with scope `""`, `top` `""`, `export=false`). `readProposal` is a method value passed to `WalkDir`, with the same `SkipAll` and the same nil returns.
   - `classify`: `newestHandoff` is now set for any candidate of kind `handoff`, where before it was set in the `dirKinds` branch only. No other branch produces kind `handoff` (`guides` gives `guide`, bugs give `bug`, `splitADRs` gives `adr`), so it is equivalent. `fileStem(c.path)` is the same base-name comparison as before.
   - `readMemoryStore` / `memoryRecord`: the problem texts are byte-identical once recomposed (`rel + ": " + problem + "; not imported"`). The only oddity: an empty `checkRecord` message would read as success. No such message exists.
   - `readDocs`: `placeholder` and `readDoc` are the same code and the same order.
   - Exported API: `go doc -all` of the old and new package is identical.
   - Imports: no non-test file gains an import; only new test files add imports, and `brain_input.go` imports only `strings`.
   - `go build` and `go vet` of `internal/brain` are clean, and `gofmt -l` is empty.
2. **50-line ceiling.** An AST count (func keyword to closing brace) over every non-test file of the package gives a maximum of 49 (`Refs`), then `Search` 48 and `MemoryAdd` 47. Nothing is above 50. The new test file functions pass 50 once (`TestReadMemoryStoreArms`, 53). The funclen guard reads non-test files only.
3. **funclen_test.go.** The diff deletes exactly 10 `longFuncs` rows, all `internal/brain/...`. Nothing else moved.
4. **New tests are not vacuous.**
   - All new tests pass against 91e9d01 (copied into a scratch nested module). That is the characterization claim, and it holds.
   - Nine mutations of the new code were compiled and run. Eight were killed by the named new test: `checkList`'s All+Global, SKILL.md titling, the `user_quote` fallback, the `SkipAll` cap, INDEX status, the testing matrix guide, the not-a-directory store refusal, and the `readDoc` cap wrap. The ninth, dropping `ownHits`' `brain:` wrap, survived, which confirms finding 3. A tenth, targeting `usage("--status needs a value")`, never ran because the text sits in `editFields` in a different form (count 0, skipped).
   - Weak but real: the `"ADR ids"` row of `TestClassifyRefusals` asserts only that distinct IDs raise no error. It is misnamed for a collision test.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. Nothing orphaned; `placeholder`, `readDoc`, `fileStem`, `uniqueIDs` and the rest each have a caller.
2. Flow tracing — pass for the source, with the two missing tests above. Error values, nil results and order match 91e9d01.
3. Standards conformance — pass with a nit. Two guard error paths untested (findings 1 and 2, § 8); one stale position word (finding 6).
4. Directory layout — pass. `brain_input.go` and the `*_arms_test.go` files sit beside the code; no dumping-ground names.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. Stdlib only; no new dependency; nothing security-primitive.
6. Decoupling — pass. `globalImport` and the `check*` helpers sharpen the seams. Files stay under 450 lines.

## Not examined
- A full `go test` of the package or repo (the background run is the caller's). I ran only the new tests, at 91e9d01 in a scratch copy, and nine mutations.
- Existing tests that cover the unchanged arms were not individually re-read.
- Docs, specs and `.agents/trail.jsonl` (code lens only). `SPEC-fyr-record` may name the old function structure; not checked.
- Disclosure: my scratch work used `.agents/scratch/rv/`, which already existed and holds other files dated Oct 25-26. I ran `rm -rf .agents/scratch/rv/old` there without first checking that no `old` directory existed. None is listed now, and I cannot say whether one was removed. It is gitignored scratch. I deleted my own `oldpkg`, `newpkg`, `mut`, `mut.sh`, `flen` and `flen.go`; everything else in `rv/` was left in place.

## Outcome

Each fix below was checked in the must-fail state: the named mutation of the fixed arm, applied to the split code, fails the new test (`.agents/scratch/funclen-p2/mutations-review*.tsv`, all killed).

1. **Fixed.** `TestImportFailsClosedWhenTheDirtyCheckFails` (import_arms_test.go) covers two cases: an unborn repo, and a corrupt `.git/index`. In both, the import returns the dirty check's error, not a refusal, and a nil result. Mutation: returning success from the error branch fails the test. The arm comes off the exempt list.
2. **Fixed.** `TestReadMemoryStoreFailsClosedOnACorruptIndex` (import_arms_test.go) pins the `git ls-files` error, with no records, files or problems returned. Mutation: `if err != nil && false` on the `ls-files` check fails the test. The arm comes off the exempt list.
3. **Fixed.** `TestOwnHitsQueryError` (record_args_test.go) calls `ownHits` on a closed store and expects a `brain: ` error and no hits. Mutation: dropping the wrap fails the test. The `Scan` error stays on the exempt list. It is reachable only through a driver failure, as the review agrees.
4. **Agreed, no change.** The `memoryEntries` `Lstat` arm stays exempt, for the reason the review confirmed.
5. **Fixed in part.** The dead `openWait` override was removed from both store-error tests. Each comment now says the busy write waits out the driver's 10-second busy timeout, which no test variable shortens. The 10 s per test stays. Shortening it would need a seam (D12) or a different store DSN, and `TestAddRefusesABusyStore` pays the same cost today.
6. **Fixed.** `checkAdd`'s comment now reads "from the body, which Add reads after these checks".
- **The weak test row (fixed).** The `TestClassifyRefusals` row "ADR ids" is renamed "distinct IDs".

No second review round: the fixes are three tests, two comments and a row rename. The main thread read their diff.

title: Review — funclen-p3 internal/metrics (2026-10-27)
body:
# Review — funclen-phase3-metrics   (2026-10-27)

Range reviewed: d39c9cf..working tree, paths internal/metrics and funclen_test.go (diff .agents/scratch/funclen-p3/phase3.diff; commit 2fd7609 adds three test files, the rest is uncommitted)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing in the ten splits changes behaviour: I read every moved block against the old code (order of effects, shadowed `err`, named results, switch case order in `segments`, `finish` column loop order, `ingestAgyConversation` call order, float expressions in the line chart) and found no difference. Requirement 7 holds exactly. The weakest point is requirement 6: the new tests execute every previously uncovered block the splits move (except the exempt one), but several of those blocks are executed without their result being asserted, so "pins" is true of coverage and not of every value (findings 1 and 2). Neither is a regression introduced by the splits.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/metrics/verb_tokenize.go:35` — `scanDollar`'s `$(` arm (`t.flushSeg(); t.parenDepth++; return i + 1`) was uncovered before 2fd7609 (old verb.go:214) and is now executed, but mutating `return i + 1` to `return i` (the `(` rescanned and counted twice) leaves the whole package green. Likewise survived: `\`-newline continuation (`if rs[i] != '\n'` -> `true`), `;;` with `caseDepth` (`if t.caseDepth > 0` -> `true`), `#` comment (`!t.inWord` dropped), closeParen's `t.parenDepth--` removed, and the escaped-quote guard `q == '"'`. Of these, the `$(` arm was a previously uncovered moved block, so the claim that the tests "pin" it holds only as execution. The effect of the double count on `Verb` output may be nil for most inputs (could not tell whether the mutants are equivalent; I did not run them against the old code). Fix if wanted: one `Verb`/`segments` case with `$(` followed by `)` and a command after it, asserting the segments. Not blocking: the split itself is faithful.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/metrics/events_join.go:75,80` — the notes `"project root gone: "+root` and `"no git history: "+root` are asserted by no test, before or after the split (`grep` over `*_test.go` and over d39c9cf finds neither string). Mutating either return to `return notes, nil` survives. The blocks are covered (they were not in the uncovered set), so this is a gap that predates the diff, but the diff moved both blocks from `continue` in a loop to an early `return` in a new function, so it is exactly the shape of change a test should pin. By reading, both notes are returned correctly and `joinEvents` appends `rootNotes` (the `records not read` note in records_test.go:170 pins that hop).
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/metrics/report_chart.go` (`lineRows`, `plot.x`, `lines`, `placeEndLabels`) — lineChart's split is covered but its drawing logic is barely asserted: mutants `p.days < 2` -> `< 1`, `len(pts) > 1` -> `> 0`, `if drawn` -> `if !drawn`, the 13px nudge threshold, the `"n/a"` cell, and the end-label sort direction all survived the package tests. Pre-existing weak coverage of lineChart; I checked the new code against the old by reading (same expressions, `plot.iw`/`ih` are float64 as the old `iw*float64(i)` required) and found it equivalent. Mentioned because requirement 6 reads "pins".

No high or medium findings.

## Item 6: the exempt block

`fileTimes.at`'s final `return 0` (events_join.go:129): the exemption holds. `at` is called only from `joinFiles` and `joinFileBugs`, always with a `rel` that came from `trailFiles`, which keeps a path only when `os.Lstat` says regular file; `filepath.Join(root, rel)` rebuilds exactly the matched path. A regular file is not a symlink, so `os.Stat` fails only if the file disappears between the two calls, a race. Reaching it without a seam would be flaky. The mtime-fallback branch just above it (old events.go:174-175) was also uncovered at d39c9cf and is now covered. Coverage (go test -coverprofile, d39c9cf vs 2fd7609 vs working tree, uncovered-block text compared) shows: of every block uncovered at d39c9cf and moved into a helper, the only one still uncovered is that `return 0`; no new uncovered block exists in any helper file (agy_conversation.go, events_join.go except line 129, report_chart.go, verb_tokenize.go, show*.go helpers). The uncovered blocks that remain in joinEvents (fbNote, Begin, the two rewrite* errors), Show, ingestAgyConversation and finish are the ones that did not move. Mutants that DID die on moved code include: put errors for all six kinds, mainWindows scan/slack, `len(ids) > 1`, `!in.Migrated`, agyTool failed flag, model update, `agentType`, RetryLoops, `reads < 3`, `!r.main`, replay-skip, SearchGrepRatio in finishColumn and Numbers, `v == historical`, quotedDelim `k <= 0`, unquotedDelim `end == 0`, project filter args.

## Criteria

1. Dead code — pass. No helper unreferenced (vet clean, all new helpers called); no commented-out code; removed closures (`owners`, `at`, `pf`, `pi`, `n`) have no leftovers.
2. Flow tracing — pass. Callers unchanged; errors propagate as before (`joinRoot` returns `nil, err`, joinEvents ignores notes on error as before); `joinEvents` note order preserved; `Summary.finish` keeps per-column order (finishContext, then finishColumn) and the ambiguous-note placement after the Daily sort; `ingestAgyConversation` still runs session, steps, gens, ingest_state in that order (the `agySteps` argument is evaluated before `agyGens` runs). `add`'s old `continue`s became returns at the same loop-body tail. `acc()` reordering is side-effect independent. Tests added in 2fd7609 are behavioural (triggers and fixtures, no source reading); the mutation sampling above is the caveat.
3. Standards conformance — pass. gofmt and go vet clean; `TestFunctionLength` passes (no function over 50 lines, no listed row stale); no import added to the package; no exported name added/removed (the only exported-surface file changes are inside bodies); new type names (`stepRun`, `plot`, `endLabel`, `textWriter`, `fileTimes`, `agyStep`) are unexported; D10: the deferred cleanup stays in `ingestAgyConversation`, the "security review of v2.6.0" comment moved with `quotedDelim`, the SD55 comment stays with `printable`, the records-read comment moved with the code to `joinRoot`; D12: no package-level function variable or hook added (the test trigger `refuseKind` is schema-level). Several new helpers lack doc comments (`textWriter.row/head`, `countCol`, `addStep`, `addTokens`, `addTool`, `textEfficiency/Adherence/Reliability`); not a finding under the project's rules.
4. Directory layout — pass. New files `agy_conversation.go`, `events_join.go`, `report_chart.go`, `verb_tokenize.go` sit beside their sources, named for a concern (no utils/helpers); files that were over 400 before (events.go 484, report.go 445) end at 358 and 377, verb.go (399) at 340, agy.go at 306, show_add.go grew 242 -> 269; none ends over 400.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. Stdlib only, no dependency, no security-sensitive primitive involved.
6. Decoupling — pass. The helpers stay unexported in the package; `joinRoot` takes the put callback as before; no cross-package reach added; the tokenizer, chart and join helpers are separate files, so adjacent work does not collide in one file.

Requirement 7: `longFuncs` lost exactly the ten internal/metrics rows (verified by diffing the sorted row lists: ten lines removed, all other rows and every non-row line identical apart from gofmt alignment).

## Not examined

- `.agents/trail.jsonl` (modified in the tree, outside the dispatched paths).
- Mutation sampling is partial: about 60 mutants of the new code ran (one file, one mutant at a time, in a copy of the 2fd7609 tree with the working-tree internal/metrics overlaid, never in the working tree); the killed/survived lists above are all that ran. Not run: the same surviving mutants against the 2fd7609 code, so I cannot say whether any survivor was already unpinned before the split (equivalence of survivors is unjudged); mutants for textWriter's row/head formatting, `Show`'s since/until window, and agyTool/verbs (untouched code). Two mutants with `||` in the target text were not run (the harness splits on `|`).
- `go test -race ./...` and the full suite: the coordinator's run; I ran only `go test ./internal/metrics/` (pass), `TestFunctionLength` (pass), gofmt and vet.
- The docs lens was not requested; a grep for file/function names of the split code in living docs found no stale reference, but the specs held in trail records were not searched.

Scratch I created (kept, nothing else removed): .agents/scratch/agents/rv-p3-* (cmp.py, cmp2.py, cover*.out, mut.sh, muts*.txt, mut3.out, save.go) and the directories .agents/scratch/rv-p3-base (d39c9cf extract), .agents/scratch/rv-p3-old (2fd7609 extract), .agents/scratch/rv-p3-new (2fd7609 plus the working-tree metrics package, mutation copy; restored identical to the working tree after the last run). Two stray background wait loops I started were killed.

## Outcome

Written by the main thread, 2026-10-27. All three findings fixed with tests; no source changed after the review (every non-test file in internal/metrics `cmp`-identical to the reviewer's copy `.agents/scratch/rv-p3-new/`). Each new case was checked to fail under its mutant: 15 mutants, 15 killed (`.agents/scratch/funclen-p3/mutations-review.txt`, output `mutations-review.out`). No second round: the fixes are tests only, and the main thread read their diff.

1. **Fixed.** `TestVerbTokenizerArms` gains six cases, one per survivor named: `$(` counted once (`return i + 1` → `return i`), `)` closing its subshell (`parenDepth--` removed), backslash-newline (`if rs[i] != '\n'` → true), `;;` outside a case (`caseDepth > 0` → true), `#` inside a word (`!t.inWord` dropped), a backslash in single quotes (`q == '"'` dropped). Each kills its mutant, so none of the six was equivalent.
2. **Fixed.** `TestJoinEventsRootNotes`: a session root that is gone and one that is not git each give their note and no event; dropping either note fails it (2 of 2).
3. **Fixed.** `TestLineChartDrawing` (new `report_chart_test.go`): the one-day centred marker and no line, the "n/a" cell and no end label for an empty series, the polyline points, the end-label sort and the 13px nudge. Killed: `days < 1`, `len(pts) > 0`, `!drawn`, the threshold at 8, the sort reversed, the "n/a" cell blanked, the nudge at 12 (7 of 7).

Item 6 (the exempt `fileTimes.at` `return 0`) is confirmed, as the review judged.

title: Security review — funclen-p3 tokenizer (2026-10-27)
body:
# Security review — funclen-p3-tokenizer   (2026-10-27)

Range reviewed: 2fd7609..working tree (uncommitted): internal/metrics/verb.go (`segments`), internal/metrics/verb_tokenize.go (new: `runeAt`, `scanQuoted`, `scanDollar`, `scanOperator`, `closeParen`), internal/metrics/verb_heredoc.go (`heredocDelims`, new `quotedDelim`, `unquotedDelim`); plus the tests 2fd7609 added in internal/metrics/verb_arms_test.go.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: CLEAR

No input found on which the new `segments`, `heredocDelims`, `stripHeredocs` or `Verb` returns anything different from 2fd7609. The new code does not widen what reaches a verb. Read arm by arm, the split keeps the old switch's order: the quote and escape arms come first, then `${`, `$((` and `$(`, then the old arms 6-15 in their original order inside `scanOperator`. `r == '\'' || r == '"' || r == '\\' && i+1 < len(rs)` groups as the old two arms did, because `&&` binds tighter than `||`. A `$` with neither `{` nor `(` after it, and a backslash as the last rune, still fall through to the default arm and are written as word runes, as before. Every helper returns the index the old code left in `i`, and the loop's `i++` is unchanged. `closeParen` is the old `)` arm word for word. In `heredocDelims`, the old early `return ds, true` sites now come back as `unparsed=true` with the same `ds`. The quoted branch's old `continue` and the unquoted branch's fall-through both lead to the next loop iteration with the same `line`. The named result `unparsed` is assigned on every iteration, but it is only returned on paths where it is true or on the `j < 0` path, which returns a literal `false`. So no stale value can leak out.

## Findings
- none

## Checked
- **Behaviour preservation (the stated requirement):** a differential harness in `.agents/scratch/sec-p3-fuzz/`, its own module, with no change to the tree. The old code came from `git show 2fd7609:`, the new code was copied from the tree, and the package names were renamed. It compared `segments`, `heredocDelims`, `stripHeredocs` and `Verb` on:
  - 3,000,000 random strings from a shell-metacharacter rune alphabet (including non-ASCII and U+FFFD);
  - 1,000,000 random byte strings, including invalid UTF-8;
  - 3,000,000 token-level strings (`case`/`in`/`esac`, `;;`, `a|b)`, `$(`, `${`, `$((`, `<<`, `<<-`, `<<<`, quoted, unquoted and backslash-quoted delimiters, terminator lines, `2>&1`, `&>`, backticks, line continuations);
  - a coverage-guided `go test -fuzz` run of 240 s: 27,768,802 executions, 635 corpus entries.
  
  Result: zero divergences. The harness was validated in the must-fail state too: a deliberately different input pair is detected (`TestControl`, `TestControlDelims`), and 5 mutations of the new copy were tried. Four were killed: `&` followed by `>` changed to `<`, `k <= 0` changed to `k < 0`, `wantPattern` dropped from `closeParen`, and the `;;` arm disabled. The fifth, `end > 0` changed to `end >= 0` in `unquotedDelim`, is an equivalent mutant: `end == 0` with a quote at `line[0]` returns unparsed either way. One further mutation did not apply and is not counted.
- **Diff integrity:** `.agents/scratch/funclen-p3/phase3-tokenizer.diff` lines 1-288 match `git diff 2fd7609` of the working tree byte for byte. `verb_test.go` and `verb_arms_test.go` are unchanged since 2fd7609. `go test -run 'Verb|Heredoc|Segment|Tokeniz' ./internal/metrics/`: 12 tests PASS.
- **Secrets:** none in the changed files.
- **Injection:** nothing in the change runs, builds a query from or opens a path with the tokenizer's input. The content-to-store boundary is the tokenizer itself, and it is unchanged (see above).
- **Authz/authn:** not touched.
- **Crypto:** not touched; nothing hand-rolled.
- **Dependencies:** none added; the new file imports nothing. `govulncheck ./...` (go1.27.3): your code is affected by 0 vulnerabilities. It also reported 1 advisory in a required module that the code does not call (the known GO-2026-5024 per AGENTS.md; not confirmed with `-show verbose`).
- **GCP surface:** not touched.
- **Past failures:** `fyr search --refs <file> --kind bug` returned no bug records for verb.go, verb_heredoc.go or verb_tokenize.go. The review records found (SD56, SD61b) concern code this diff does not change.

## Not examined
- The rest of the `Verb` pipeline beyond the tokenizer (`segmentVerb`, `programAt`, `verbFrom`, `flagName`, `wrapper`, `isAssignment`; verb.go 200-340): not changed in this range, but they were exercised through `Verb` in the differential.
- Whether 2fd7609's tokenizer itself lets content through (a pre-existing weakness): out of scope for a behaviour-preservation review. The differential shows only that old and new agree.
- The other modified files in the tree (agy.go, events.go, numbers.go, report.go, show*.go, verb_heredoc.go's `stripHeredocs` body above line 52 beyond what the differential exercised, funclen_test.go, the new agy_conversation.go, events_join.go, report_chart.go): not part of this dispatch.
- The random and fuzz inputs are long but not exhaustive: equivalence is shown on the inputs tried plus the static reading, not proven.

title: Review — funclen-p4 internal/search (2026-10-27)
body:
# Review — funclen-phase4 internal/search   (2026-10-27)

Range reviewed: 1a228b5..working tree, `internal/search/` and `funclen_test.go` (diff `.agents/scratch/funclen-p4/phase4.diff`, incl. untracked `internal/search/dream_proto.go`; commit 5294170 adds the four `*_arms_test.go`).

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

No behaviour change found in any non-test source edit: I compared every split against `git show 1a228b5:<path>` line by line. The one claim that is wrong is the stated reason for the `refRows` `rows.Err()` exemption (claim 3): the query plan does not sort everything before the first row. The conclusion (no cheap test) may still hold. Three coverage gaps are low severity. `go test ./internal/search/`, `go vet` and `gofmt -l` are clean.

## Findings
- **[low-medium / confidence: high on the plan, medium on reachability]** `internal/search/search_refs.go:~140` (`refRows`, `rows.Err()` arm) and the exemption record D12 — the premise "ORDER BY, so SQLite evaluates every row before the first is returned" is false for this query. `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` on the real schema (modernc driver, same module) gives, for all three WHERE shapes (ID, dir, path):
  `SEARCH f USING INDEX sqlite_autoindex_files_1 (project=?)` / `SEARCH r ...` (or `SCAN r` for the dir/LIKE shape) / `USE TEMP B-TREE FOR LAST TERM OF ORDER BY`.
  "LAST TERM" is a partial sort: `f.project, f.path` come in index order from the outer loop, and only `r.line` is sorted, per (project, path) group. Rows therefore stream group by group, and an error after the first group (I/O error, page corruption) surfaces at `rows.Next()`/`rows.Err()`, not at `Query`. The arm is reachable in principle. It is probably still not reachable by a data-only fixture, since I found no row-dependent error in that SELECT, so the exemption may stand. Fix: restate the exemption's reason in D12 as "a mid-stream error needs I/O failure or corruption; no data-only trigger found", or cover the arm with a corrupted-page fixture. Do not leave the ORDER BY claim on record. `find()` has the same `rows.Err()` shape (search_query.go:~70); I did not check whether its arm is covered.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/search/dream_proto.go` `skipScalar`, 64-bit arm (`return msg[8:], true`) — a mutation to `msg[7:]` survives the whole package. `TestWalkFixedAndVarintFields` pins the "short 64-bit" refusal but has no case that steps over a whole 64-bit field to the prose behind it, while the 32-bit arm has one ("32-bit then prose") and the varint arm is killed by `TestProseLeaves`. The test's header ("steps over a whole 32-bit field") is honest about 32-bit only. Fix: add a "64-bit then prose" case.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/search/reconcile.go` `applyLocked`, the two post-write statements (`UPDATE blobs SET last_seen ...`, `INSERT INTO meta ... touched:`) — error arms swallowed by mutation survive (M5b, M5c). They moved only by position (they stayed in `applyLocked`, now after `writeFiles`). `TestApplyLockedWriteErrors` covers the blob, chunk and files statements, not these two or the `gc` error. If the Phase 4 note says applyLocked's arms are pinned, name these two as not covered (review-standards § 7, coverage claims name the gap).
- **[info / confidence: high]** Claim 1, timing: `indexBlobs` now closes the inserter's three prepared statements and the os.Root when it returns, before `writeFiles`, the two `UPDATE`/`INSERT` and `gc`. Before, the deferred closes ran at `applyLocked`'s return, after all of them. Inside `indexBlobs` the order is unchanged (inserter, then root, LIFO). The earlier close is safe: statements on the store's single connection hold no lock, and none is used after `indexBlobs`. The claim "closing order unchanged" is true per function but not across the old function. State it as "earlier, harmless" in the change record.
- **[info / confidence: high, pre-existing]** `internal/search/git_view.go` `keptEntries`: `delete(view, p) // an unmerged path appears once` is redundant, because `trackedView`'s `dup` guard already makes `order` unique (mutation M22 survives; removing the `dup` guard is killed by `TestGitViewUnmergedPath`). Existing code, not changed by this diff, so not a finding for this range. It is dead and carries a misleading comment.

## Claim verification
1. Behaviour-preserving extract-function: **verified** by line-by-line comparison against 1a228b5. Checked:
   - `applyLocked`/`indexBlobs`/`writeFiles`: same statements, same order, same error returns. The only difference is the early close above.
   - `refs`: `refsWhere` is pure and computed before the first-line output as before; `recordLine` and `pathLine` close their rows before any nested query (`pathLine` uses `QueryRow`, then `sameName`). `refRows` closes its rows on every path (Scan error, `rows.Err()`, success) before `groupRefs` calls `recordAt`.
   - `AgyConversationText`: the single deferred cleanup (RemoveAll, then `removeIfEmpty` only when created) is untouched. `listConversations` closes rows then db on every path, as before, and the db is closed before any `conversationText` call.
   - `walk`: after `key>>3 == 0` and the key varint, the wire-type dispatch is equivalent. Wire 2 goes to `lengthDelimited` with the same length check, the same nested-first-then-text rule and the same advance. Wires 0, 1 and 5 go to `skipScalar` with identical length checks. Wires 3, 4, 6 and 7 still return false, and `leaves` is flushed only on a whole parse.
   - `prepareProject`: `st.close()` on the gitView and apply errors, `sc.close()` on the register error, and none on `guardProject`/`removeDB`/`openStore` errors, exactly as before. `prepare` still returns `nil, err` without closing, as before.
   - `reconcileGlobal`: `reconcileRegistered`'s three skip/drop notes and error wrapping are identical. `globalDocsRoot` equals the old literal.
   - `find`/`snippets`: `hits[first:]` indexed by `ids` is the old `hits[i+first]`.
   - `gitView` and `indexStats`: `parseIndexStats` returns the same map and `ifi.ModTime()` stays in `indexStats`.
   No exported identifier changed. The import set is unchanged: dream.go dropped `encoding/binary` and `unicode/utf8`, and `dream_proto.go` took them; json and strings stay in both. Same package, so the package's import set is the same.
2. New tests: I ran 37 mutations on a scratch copy of the module, each applied once to a uniquely-matched block and the file restored from the saved original. Of 36 that compiled, 30 were killed by the named tests (see below). The kills are by error-text or output assertions on the targeted block, not side effects. Survivors: M5b and M5c (finding 3), M21b (finding 2), M22 (equivalent mutant, pre-existing). M23 first failed to build (no evidence), and its rewrite was killed.
   - Killed: M1-M5 by `TestApplyLockedWriteErrors`, M6 by `TestReconcileGlobalRebuildRemoveError`, M7 by `...RegistrationReadErrors`, M8 by `...DropError`, M9 and M9b by `...ProjectErrors`, M10 and M12b by `TestPrepareRebuildRemovesProjectDB`, M11 and M12 by `TestPrepareProjectErrors`, M13 by `TestRefsDirDocsRelative`, M14-M16b by `TestRefsReadErrors`, M17 by `TestFindSnippetError`, M18 and M19 by `TestAgyConversationListErrors`, M20 and M20b (cleanup order and removal) by it and `TestAgyConversationText`, M21 by `TestWalkFixedAndVarintFields`, M21c by `TestProseLeaves`, M21d and M21e by the walk test (as a slice-bounds panic: it fails, but by crash, not an assertion), M22c by `TestGitViewUnmergedPath`, M23 by `TestGitViewTrustsIndexStat`, M24 and M25 by `TestGitViewUnreadableFiles`.
   - Test setup conditions hold: `TestAgyConversationListErrors` checks the state directory is gone, which fails for M20/M20b. `TestGitViewUnmergedPath` verifies the three stages before asserting.
3. `refRows` exemption: **refuted as worded** (finding 1).
4. Length and size: `go run ./.agents/scratch/funclen internal/search/*.go` lists only three test functions over 50 lines (`TestAgyConversationText`, `TestCopyDBRetriesOnce`, `TestGitViewRunsNoCleanFilter`, all pre-existing and tests, which `funclen_test.go` excludes). No non-test function exceeds 50. The largest non-test file is `git_view.go` at 308 lines. Test files stay under 600 (`dream_test.go` 437). `funclen_test.go`: nine `internal/search` rows removed, the rest only gofmt realignment.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass for the diff. No leftover scaffolding; the old `walk` block is gone from dream.go (moved, not duplicated). One pre-existing redundant `delete` noted above.
2. Flow tracing — pass. Callers and error paths verified above; rows and statements closed before any nested query on every path; the old order changed only in the harmless early close. Findings 1-3 are test-evidence gaps.
3. Standards conformance — pass. gofmt and vet clean; stdlib only. The describing comments moved with their code. The exemption text in D12 is the stale restatement (finding 1).
4. Directory layout — pass. `dream_proto.go` sits beside `dream.go`, named for its concern; the tests beside the code.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. No new dependency; no auth or crypto touched.
6. Decoupling — pass. Helpers are unexported, with no new cross-package edges.

## Not examined
- The full `go test ./...` and `-race` suite (a full run was in progress; I ran only `./internal/search/`, once clean and then 37 mutation runs in a scratch copy, since removed).
- `rows.Err()` coverage in `find()` (search_query.go) and `registrations()` (global.go), which never checks `rows.Err()` (the old code did not either).
- The plan file, change records and D12/D13 text (I was given the code lens only).
- Restatements of the changed line counts outside `internal/search/` and `funclen_test.go` (I grepped `.go` and `.md` for stale `dream.go:walk` citations: none found outside records, which are immutable).

## Outcome

- **Finding 1, accepted: the reason was wrong, and the arm stays exempt.**
  - The change record's exemption no longer says "every row is evaluated before the first is returned".
  - It now says: the plan is a partial sort (`USE TEMP B-TREE FOR LAST TERM OF ORDER BY`), so rows stream one file at a time, and a mid-stream error needs an I/O failure or a corrupted page. No data-only trigger exists.
  - Checked with a probe test, not committed (`.agents/scratch/funclen-p4/zz_rowserr_test.go.txt`). The first file's only reference matched the exact target, and a later file's reference forced the over-long LIKE. The error still came from `Query`: `refRows`' loop and `rows.Err` arm show 0 coverage, because every refs row is evaluated in the first file's inner scan, before the sorter emits anything.
  - The exemption list in the plan's D12 names no Phase 4 arm; the phase's exempt list is in its change record, which carries the corrected reason.
- **Finding 2, fixed:** `TestWalkFixedAndVarintFields` gains "64-bit then prose". The `msg[8:]` → `msg[7:]` mutant is killed.
- **Finding 3, fixed:** `TestApplyLockedWriteErrors` gains the last-seen update (a trigger on `UPDATE blobs`) and the touched mark (a trigger on `INSERT meta`). Swallowing either error is killed.
- **Finding 3, not covered:** the `gc` error stays uncovered. It never moved: it is `applyLocked`'s last statement.
- **The two info points:** the early close by `indexBlobs` is stated in the change record as earlier and harmless. The redundant `delete(view, p)` in `keptEntries` predates the range and stays: a behaviour-preserving phase removes nothing.
- **No second round:** the fixes are tests only, and the main thread read their diff. Three of three mutants were killed (`mutations-review.out`).

title: Review — funclen P5 internal/harness (2026-10-27)
body:
# Review — funclen-phase5 internal/harness   (2026-10-27)

Range reviewed: ab10666..working tree (commit d2078f4 + uncommitted), `git diff ab10666 -- internal funclen_test.go` as saved in .agents/scratch/funclen-p5/phase5.diff (1853 lines, 15 files)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE

Nothing broken found. Every split function (Adopt, Install, loadSkills, loadAgents, Plan, UpdateFromRelease, ResolveSource, UnpackZip) was compared line by line against its ab10666 version: returned values, error text, output lines and their order, order of checks, file effects, and defer timing are unchanged. The 26 new tests each name an arm that exists on disk, and each test I mutated failed under the mutation that breaks its arm.

## Findings
None.

## Evidence

Behaviour comparison (read against `git show ab10666:<path>` and the code on disk):
- Install -> installRun: the `saveOnError` closure became a method over r.old/r.manifest. Nothing reads the old local `old` after the loop, so mutating r.old.Files is equivalent. The keep-symlink `continue` became `return nil` before the manifest append, same as before. The dry-run `dirInTheWay` check, the "line prints after the write" order, the resync `dryRun` continue, and the `+status-unknown` / `+dirty` order are preserved. tightenConfigDir still runs before the loop.
- Adopt -> findSkill/adoptDest/stageAdopt/swapIn: the check order is the same (find, Abs, validName, Abs dest, overlap, Stat dest, scratch mkdir, remove staging, copy, backup stat/remove/rename, rename in). All error texts are identical. The "NO defer" comment now sits before the swapIn call, where "every failure path below" is still true.
- UpdateFromRelease -> newerRelease/installRelease: `if err != nil || tag == "" { return err }` is equivalent. The up-to-date, not-a-release, not-newer, and checkOnly arms return the same text and the same ErrNewerRelease. The mkdir -> WriteAtomic -> "verified and installed" -> exec order is unchanged.
- UnpackZip -> planZip/writeZipPlan: the named result `err` is still set by `return "", "", err`, so the cleanup defer, registered after the plan and before the writes, fires the same way. Entry-count, name, root and tree checks are in the same order.
- loadSkills/loadAgents -> readSkill/parseSkill/readAgent/checkAgent: the check order is the same. The duplicate-name check still runs last. The `.DS_Store` skip and the flat-agent refusal stay in the loader. `readSkill` returns `ok=false` with a nil error only for a non-directory or a missing SKILL.md.
- Plan -> skillFiles/skillFile: the "skill %s: %w" wrap still covers a failed walk. A failed walk still returns nil files. The mode mask is unchanged.
- ResolveSource -> releaseSource/sourceCandidates: the candidate order and the zipNote text are unchanged. The big comment moved with the code it describes.
- Comments: each moved comment describes the code beside it. Grep for restatements (saveOnError, loadSkills/loadAgents, Adopt's/Install's/UnpackZip's) found no stale copy outside the trail records, which are never rewritten.
- funclen_test.go: 25 rows -> 17; exactly the 8 split functions' rows are gone. TestFunctionLength passes.

Checks run: `gofmt -l cmd internal *.go` is clean. `go vet ./internal/harness .` is clean. `go test -count=1 -run 'TestFunctionLength' .` is ok. The harness targeted tests (Adopt|Install|Plan|UnpackZip|UpdateFromRelease|LoadSkills|LoadAgents|ResolveSource) are ok. The full -race suite was not run (the caller said one was running).

Mutation probing, in a copy under .agents/scratch/funclen-p5-mut/src (the real tree was never written; `git status` identical before and after). Each mutation text occurred exactly once and the file was restored from a saved copy. Every row below compiled and the named test failed (KILLED):
- adoptDest validName removed -> TestAdoptRefusesAnInvalidName
- adoptDest non-ENOENT stat arm removed -> TestAdoptDestStatError

The change record says so. The test file's wording ("need getcwd to fail") stands.

title: Security review — funclen P5 UnpackZip (2026-10-27)
body:
# Security review — unpackzip-split   (2026-10-27)

Range reviewed: ab10666..working tree, `internal/harness/zip.go` and `internal/harness/zip_arms_test.go` (`.agents/scratch/funclen-p5/unpackzip.diff`), with the caller `cmd/fyr/update_zip.go` and the helpers `readCapped` (`internal/harness/release.go:290`) and `isRepo` (`internal/harness/repo.go:188`) as blast radius

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: CLEAR

Nothing is broken. The change is a pure extract-function. The parse-and-check block moves word for word into `planZip` (`zip.go:100-118`), and the write loop plus the `isRepo` check move word for word into `writeZipPlan` (`zip.go:122-144`). Only the return arity changes. All checks still run before the first write, in the same order as at ab10666: the capped read (`zip.go:55`), the sha256 over that same buffer (`:59`), the caller's `check(sum)` (`:63-67`), then `planZip`. `planZip` runs `zip.NewReader` on the same `data`, then the entry count, `zipNameSafe` on every entry, `zipRoot`, and `checkZipTrees` (kinds, symlinks, duplicates, per-file cap by decompressing, total cap). All of that comes before `os.MkdirTemp` (`:80`). The cleanup defer (`:84-90`) still reads the named `err`. The only error return after it is `return "", "", err` at `:92`, where `err` is a block-scoped shadow. Go assigns return operands to the named results before deferred calls run, so the defer sees the error and removes `tmp`. A bare `return` with a shadowed `err` would not compile, so this refactor cannot silently drop the cleanup. Nothing can be written outside the unpack directory: `dest` is still `filepath.Join(tmp, FromSlash(rel))`, every name has passed `zipNameSafe` (which includes `filepath.IsLocal`), symlink entries are refused, and the `O_EXCL` create is unchanged. The per-file cap (`copyCapped` in both `entrySize` and `unpackFile`) and the total cap (checked in `checkZipTrees` and counted again in `writeZipPlan`) behave as before.

## Findings
- None at any severity.
- Informational, pre-existing and unchanged by this diff, not a finding: a panic inside `writeZipPlan` would leave `tmp` behind, because the defer checks `err`, not `recover()`. That was the same at ab10666, and `archive/zip` and `os` do not panic on hostile input as designed.

## Checked
- **Ordering and cleanup, verified by mutation** on a copy of the module at `.agents/scratch/probe-sec-zip` (the real tree was not touched; restored copy byte-identical to `internal/harness/zip.go`). Baseline: `go test -run Zip ./internal/harness/` ok (19 PASS), `TestUpdateFromZipVerifiedAndTampered` ok.
  - M1, cleanup defer removed: killed by `TestUnpackZipDirOverFile`, `TestUnpackZipFileOverDir` and `TestUnpackZipNoSkillsTree` (all through `noZipDirs`).
  - M2, `planZip` moved after `MkdirTemp`: killed by `TestUnpackZipLateRefusalCreatesNoParent`.
  - M3, `check(sum)` moved after `planZip`: survives the `internal/harness` tests, but is killed by `cmd/fyr` `TestUpdateFromZipVerifiedAndTampered`, for the right reason (`unexpected EOF, want checksum mismatch`). The check-before-parse order is therefore pinned only at the `cmd/fyr` level, and that test is the one guarding it.
  - M5, `isRepo` refusal removed: killed by `TestUnpackZipNoSkillsTree`.
  - M6, `zipNameSafe` result ignored: killed by `TestUnpackZipRefuses` and `TestUnpackZipRefusesDeepOrLongNames`.
- **Secrets:** none in the diff or the new test file.
- **Injection / path traversal:** the write path is unchanged. The name checks, the five-tree filter, the symlink and non-regular refusals and the `O_EXCL` create all hold (see above).
- **Authz/authn:** not applicable; this is a local CLI that unpacks the operator's own file.
- **Crypto:** `crypto/sha256` is used as designed, as a checksum over the read buffer. Nothing is hand-rolled. ADR-039's signature path was later superseded (ADR-041, ADR-053: integrity-only `SHA256SUMS`). The caller (`cmd/fyr/update_zip.go:51-62`, unchanged since ab10666) still passes the `VerifyZipSums` check into `UnpackZip`.
- **Dependencies:** none added. `govulncheck ./...` on go1.27.3: 0 vulnerabilities affecting the code, 1 in required modules that the code does not call (the known GO-2026-5024 in golang.org/x/sys, AGENTS.md).
- **Helpers:** `readCapped` and `isRepo` have identical bodies at ab10666 and in the working tree.
- **npm audit:** not applicable; no JS ecosystem in this range.
- **GCP surface:** not applicable; the range touches no IAM, deploy or secret configuration.
- **Past bugs:** `fyr search --refs <path> --kind bug` for `zip.go`, `zip_arms_test.go` and `update_zip.go` returned 0 references (home `.agents/scratch/home-trail`).

## Not examined
- The other files in the working-tree diff since ab10666 (`adopt.go`, `apply.go`, `apply_steps.go`, `inventory.go`, `inventory_load.go`, `plan.go`, `release.go`, `repo.go`, `funclen_test.go`): outside this dispatch's scope. Only `readCapped` and `isRepo` were checked for changes.
- The full `-race` suite was not run, per the dispatch. Only `-run Zip` in `internal/harness` and `-run 'Zip|zip|Sums|Checksum'` in `cmd/fyr` were run, without `-race`.
- `checkZipTrees`, `zipNameSafe` and `zipRoot` were read but not re-audited from scratch, because the diff leaves them unchanged.

## Outcome

- No findings. M3's note, that check-before-parse was pinned only by `cmd/fyr`'s `TestUpdateFromZipVerifiedAndTampered`, is closed in the package: `TestUnpackZipChecksBeforeParsing` (internal/harness/zip_arms_test.go) passes a non-zip with a check that refuses and requires the check's error. The mutant that moves `check(sum)` after `planZip` fails it.
- The panic-leaves-`tmp` note is pre-existing and unchanged; not acted on.

title: Review — index busy on first open, BUG fix (2026-10-27)
body:
# Review — busy-open retry (search, metrics)   (2026-10-27)

Range reviewed: uncommitted working tree vs HEAD 7e60915 (.agents/scratch/bug-busy/fix.diff): internal/search/store.go, internal/search/open_test.go, internal/metrics/store.go, internal/metrics/store_test.go

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing is broken. Both retry loops are bounded, return the right error, close the failed handle on every attempt, and keep the existing mapping (search: errBusy; metrics: the wrapped SQLite error). Both new tests set up their condition (they assert journal_mode == "delete" and a held BEGIN IMMEDIATE) and fail without the fix: I copied the tree to scratch, reverted store.go in search and metrics only, and both TestFirstOpenWaitsForALock tests failed in about 0.4 ms (5 runs each) with "index busy" and "database is locked (5) (SQLITE_BUSY)"; with the fix they pass at 0.31 s. `go test` on internal/search and internal/metrics passes; go vet and gofmt are clean. The scratch copy is deleted.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/search/store.go:187-196`, `internal/metrics/store.go:83-92` — the wait is not bounded by one timeout. The deadline is checked only after an attempt returns, and each attempt can itself wait busy_timeout (DSN sets 10 s) in ensureSchema's BEGIN IMMEDIATE or metrics' migrate. A holder that keeps the write lock for the full 10 s leaves an attempt that ends just before the deadline, followed by another attempt of up to 10 s: about 20 s per open, and about 40 s in search's rebuild path (openStore calls tryOpenWaiting twice). The brain store loop has the same shape (`internal/brain/store.go:90-99`), so this is consistent with existing code. The failure is only a slower refusal, and the comment "as long as that timeout" slightly understates it. No fix required; if wanted, compare the deadline before sleeping.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/search/store.go:90-92` — new exported `IsBusy` wraps `isBusy`, and `internal/brain/store.go:200` keeps its own copy of the same predicate. Not wrong; brain could use `search.IsBusy` later. Not a requirement.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. Nothing unused; `IsBusy` has one caller (metrics/store.go:87). `open` and `openWait` are used.
2. Flow tracing — pass. Callers of metrics.Open (cmd/fyr/verb_metrics.go:62,160, eval.go:239, internal/dream/metrics.go:20) still get the same error type on timeout; a busy error wrapped with %w is found by errors.As in sqliteCode (confirmed by the retry succeeding in the metrics test). A failed attempt closes its db (tryOpen, migrate paths). `s, err` is returned as nil, err on failure. Existing busy tests (TestBusyRefusesNotStale, TestUnchangedSearchTakesNoWriteLock) open an index already in WAL mode, so the retry does not change them; they pass. Stale-schema and unreadable errors are not busy and are not retried.
3. Standards conformance — pass. Functions are under 50 lines and files are well under the ceiling (store.go 279/233; tests 211/305). Comments say why. I grepped docs for "busy" and found no restatement of the open behaviour that is now stale.
4. Directory layout — pass.
5. Simplicity — pass. Stdlib only, no new dependency; matches the brain loop.
6. Decoupling — pass with a nit (above): the metrics store depends on search through one exported predicate, as it already does for DSN and PrepareDBFiles.

## Not examined
The full -race suite (excluded by the dispatch), cmd/fyr and internal/dream tests that call metrics.Open, and a real two-process race (TestConcurrentReconcile's 1-in-9 flake): I did not loop it to show it no longer fails.

## Outcome

- Finding 1 (low), rebutted: the retry checks its deadline after each attempt, so a refusal takes about 10 s in the ordinary case: the first attempt waits the busy timeout and the loop then stops. The longer path, about 20 s (40 s across the rebuild's second open), needs nearly 10 s of immediate deadlock answers followed by one full wait. The brain store's open has the same bound, and SPEC-fyr-search's "past 10 s" still holds. No change.
- Finding 2 (low), rebutted: `search.IsBusy` serves the metrics store, which had no busy predicate. Brain's own copy predates this fix; folding it in would be an adjacent refactor the bug skill excludes. No change.
- The flake loop the reviewer did not run was run by the main thread: `TestConcurrentReconcile`, 3 rounds × 3 parallel × 100 under 12 busy loops, 900 of 900 PASS with the fix (the unfixed build: 2 failures in 900 the same way).

body:
# Review — funclen-p8   (2026-10-27)

Range reviewed: 5ff256e..working tree (commit ad4c954 plus the uncommitted edits to creds.go, row_prepare.go, row_session.go, suite.go, suite_test.go, funclen_test.go); `git diff 5ff256e -- internal/eval funclen_test.go`, saved at .agents/scratch/funclen-p8/phase8.diff

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

No behaviour change found. I compared the four split functions with their 5ff256e versions line by line. Return values, reasons and their order, notes, the error that wins when a row has several faults, defer and close timing, and the SIGTERM/SIGKILL/timeout handling are the same. `go vet` is clean and the new tests pass. The weakness is test strength, not the code. No test kills a change in how `waitAgy` signals: a mutant that sends the cancel-path SIGTERM or SIGKILL to agy alone instead of the group survives, and so does one that sends the timeout kill to the group. This gap was already there at 5ff256e, but the phase exists to pin arms before splitting. One moved comment is garbled.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/eval/row_session.go:99-109` (`waitAgy`) — the group semantics the dispatch names have no test that can fail. I mutated a scratch copy of the package (`.agents/scratch/probe-p8`, since deleted), skipping `TestRunRealFyrBaseline` and `TestSuiteHarness`, which also fail in the copy. The unmutated copy was green. Each mutant below was green too, so no test failed when agy-alone and group handling were swapped:
  - M1: cancel-path `syscall.Kill(-pgid, SIGTERM)` replaced by `cmd.Process.Signal(SIGTERM)`.
  - M2: `syscall.Kill(-pgid, SIGKILL)` replaced by `cmd.Process.Kill()`.
  - M3: the timeout `cmd.Process.Kill()` replaced by `syscall.Kill(-pgid, SIGKILL)`, so the timeout would kill the group and take down what agy started.
  - The new `TestAgySessionArms` deaf agy does `exec sleep`, so it has no child. It kills the stopGrace timer arm only (M4, which drops the SIGKILL and swaps the grace timer for 24h, fails it as intended). It cannot see group versus self.
  - Failure scenario: a later edit makes the timeout kill the group, and BUG-170-style leftovers that check e needs are killed. Everything stays green.
  - Fix: give the deaf script a background child (`sleep 300 &` before the `exec`) and assert that child is dead after a cancel and alive after a timeout (`agyTimeout` is already a variable). The header's "Exempt" list does not name this gap, and the file does not claim to cover it.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/eval/row_prepare.go:96-97` — the comment on `openSandbox` reads "resolves the three paths guard a approved". It is garbled where it was moved. Reword it so it says what the code does: it resolves dir, app and sb into `w.resolved` for the later replaced-sandbox check, and holds SB open as `w.root`. This is a describing-text defect that the global rules count as a finding.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. Nothing is left over. `pgid` passed to `waitAgy` equals `cmd.Process.Pid`, which is redundant but used. The four `longFuncs` rows are removed in `funclen_test.go`, and `TestFunctionLength` passes.
2. Flow tracing — pass.
   - `prepare`: the `||` short-circuit keeps the old step order (clone, sandbox, records, then realBefore, setup, install, settings, credsBefore). I moved `realBefore` after setup in a scratch mutant and `TestRunSetupThatTouchesTheRealConfig` failed, so that ordering is pinned.
   - `ParseSuite`: `parseRow` runs the prefix, column and id checks, then the duplicate check, then `checkRow`. The 5ff256e order is kept, and the new "a duplicate before its own faults" case pins it.
   - `agyOutputs`: it closes `out` itself when the error file fails to open. The old code closed it by defer after `w.replaced`, which nothing can observe.
   - `credKinds`: the body is unchanged.
3. Standards conformance — pass apart from the garbled comment above.
   - gofmt and vet are clean.
   - I grepped `row_prepare.go`, `row_session.go`, `ParseSuite`, `scanEntry` and `row.prepare` across the md files, skills and context, and for any `file.go:NN` citation outside the trail. No stale citation.
   - The duplicate "Step N:" comments inside `cloneApp`, `recordsBefore`, `installHarness` and `writeSettings` are harmless.
4. Directory layout — pass. `prepare_arms_test.go` sits beside the code it covers. All files are under 260 lines and all functions under 50.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. No new dependency and no hand-rolled security primitive.
6. Decoupling — pass. The helpers are unexported methods or functions in the same files, with no widened visibility.

New tests, each checked against its comment:
- `TestPrepareRefusesItsPlace` asserts the reason and the distinguishing note ("is the real home; refusing", "(BUG-106)"), so it fails if either arm breaks.
- `TestPrepareStepWritesRefused`: the "wrapper dir" case is not an install failure in disguise, because the fake `self` only creates `.local/bin`. The four cases map to distinct reasons (setup, install, install, settings).
- `TestPrepareRecordsBaselineRefused` skips under root and restores the mode by cleanup that runs before the TempDir removal.
- `TestAgySessionArms`: the first half pins the replaced arm through the error-file open. It is reached by `EISDIR` on the directory rather than the "not a regular file" message, but it is the same branch. The second half passes and fails as it says (M4).
- Exempt claims, checked against the code: "the clone that is not its own toplevel" and the `EvalSymlinks`/`OpenRoot` failures on directories just made are only reachable by a race. The settings read-back is reachable only if the eval `--home` path contains "toolPermission" (the row id cannot hold capitals). The last `-1` is true for `*os.File` outputs. The "git clone fails" arm is not exempt; it is covered by `run_verdicts_test.go:227`.

## Not examined
- The full `-race` suite (not run, per the dispatch). I ran `go vet` for `./internal/eval` and the root package, and the single-package tests for `TestPrepare*`, `TestAgySessionArms`, `TestSuite*` and `TestFunctionLength`. A scratch copy of the package also ran in full minus two env-dependent tests.
- `.agents/trail.jsonl` (the uncommitted change) and the plan and ROADMAP text. I read only the Go diff.
- `internal/eval` files outside the diff other than `row.go`'s `openRegular`, `row_env.go`'s `agyEnv` and `fakeagy_test.go`'s `fakeSelf`.
- The remaining `longFuncs` rows and whether the plan's "left" counts match them.

## Outcome

- Finding 1 (low), fixed with a test: `TestAgyProcessGroup` (prepare_arms_test.go) gives agy a background child and checks its fate in three cases: an agy that dies of SIGTERM on the run's end loses its child to the group signal; an agy and child that ignore SIGTERM are both killed by the group SIGKILL after stopGrace; at the timeout agy alone is killed and the child lives. The reviewer's three mutants (SIGTERM to agy alone, SIGKILL to agy alone, the timeout kill to the group) are each killed by it (3 of 3). The gap predated this phase.
- Finding 2 (low), fixed: `openSandbox`'s comment now reads "makes SB's CLI directory, records where the row directory, the clone and SB resolve, as the guards approved them, and holds SB open."
- No second round: the fixes are a test and a comment.

# Security review — funclen-p8-eval-suite-creds   (2026-10-27)

Range reviewed: 5ff256e..working tree on ad4c954, limited to internal/eval/suite.go, internal/eval/suite_test.go and internal/eval/creds.go (the dispatch's `.agents/scratch/funclen-p8/sec.diff`, the same text as `git diff 5ff256e -- <those three>`)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: CLEAR

Nothing is broken. Both changes only extract functions. `ParseSuite` now runs `suiteStart`, then `parseRow`, then the duplicate-id check, then `checkRow`. That is the same set of checks in the same order as at 5ff256e, with the same messages. The duplicate check still runs before the prompt, check, agent, grants and placeholder checks, so a row with several faults still reports the same first error. `scanEntry` hands the pattern counting to `credKinds` and keeps the same empty-map check, so it returns the same `(credFinding, bool)`. I checked the equivalence by reading both versions line by line and with a differential test whose ability to fail I confirmed with mutations (below). No dependency, no input surface, no trust boundary and no check was added, dropped or reordered.

## Findings
- none

## Checked
- **Equivalence of ParseSuite (the main question):** I read 5ff256e:internal/eval/suite.go:43-121 side by side with the current suite.go:44-146. Every statement moved over unchanged: the `| \`` prefix, the 7-column count, `leadingID` plus `validID`, the cell mapping (`codeCell` for setup and check, `textCell` for the rest), duplicate id (still before the content checks), empty prompt, empty check, `validAgent`, grants `named` or `wide: <non-blank>`, and placeholders over Prompt and Prompt2. The CR trim, the stop at the first line without a leading `|`, the separator skip and the "has no rows" error stay in `ParseSuite`. The new `err` variables shadow the outer one only inside their own scope, which changes nothing. The only caller is cmd/fyr/eval.go:232, and its signature is unchanged.
- **Differential probe** (`.agents/scratch/funclen-p8-secprobe/`, a standalone module holding the 5ff256e and the current copies of suite.go and creds.go). Results:
  - 300,000 generated bodies: old and new output identical, rows plus error string compared with `%#v`. 144 were accepted and the rest refused, and every refusal class was hit: no table, second table, no rows, row prefix, columns, id, duplicate (41), no prompt, no check, agent, grants, unknown placeholder.
  - The real GUIDE-eval body (60 rows), plus each of its 92 lines with each of 33 suffixes appended: identical.
  - `go test -fuzz FuzzParse` for 90 s (156k execs): no difference.
  - **scanEntry:** 6,014 (path, read) pairs gave identical results. The files covered random mixes of every `credText` kind, real and example AKIA keys, near-misses and ELF and Mach-O magic, plus a credential name (`id_rsa`), a mode-000 file, a directory link, a dangling link, a file link and a fifo. The oversized branch (`maxScan` lowered to 1) was identical with read on and off.
  - **The probe can fail:** each of three mutants of the current copy made it fail. They were: duplicate check moved after `checkRow`, `r.Check == ""` weakened, and the AWS example key counted. The copies were then restored and checked byte-identical to the working tree.
- **Real package:** `gofmt -l internal/eval` printed nothing. `go vet ./internal/eval/` passed. `go test -count=1 -run 'Suite|Cred|Scan' ./internal/eval/` passed (not under -race, because the dispatch said a full race run is already going). The new refusal case "a duplicate before its own faults" pins the dup-before-content order, which mutant 1 showed matters.
- **Past bugs** (`fyr search --refs <path> --kind bug`): suite.go has none. creds.go has BUG-160 (the scan's origin) and BUG-185 (node_modules lockfile handling in `scanCreds`, not touched here). suite_test.go has BUG-183 (pinned row count, not touched here).
- **Secrets:** none in the diff. The test strings are table fixtures, not credentials.
- **Injection:** no new input path. Setup and check cells still go through `codeCell`. The prompt-placeholder refusal (D21) is unchanged.
- **Authz/authn:** none touched. The grants gate (`named` or `wide: <reason>`) is unchanged and still before any row is accepted.
- **Crypto:** none touched, so no hand-rolled primitive.
- **Dependencies:** none added. `govulncheck ./...` (GOPATH/bin, by full path): "Your code is affected by 0 vulnerabilities". It reports 1 advisory in a required module that the code does not reach, consistent with GO-2026-5024 as recorded in AGENTS.md.
- **GCP surface:** none touched.
- **Process note:** the first probe run's `t.TempDir()` used the default /tmp (Go removed it after the run). Later runs set TMPDIR to the probe's own `tmp/`. All probe files are under `.agents/scratch/funclen-p8-secprobe/`.

## Not examined
- The other uncommitted changes in the same working tree, which are outside this dispatch's diff: internal/eval/row_prepare.go (+62/-?), internal/eval/row_session.go, internal/eval/prepare_arms_test.go, funclen_test.go and .agents/trail.jsonl. row_prepare.go builds the sandbox, so it is security-relevant. It needs its own review before the change is called reviewed.
- `scanCreds` (creds.go:60-120), `newCreds` and the helpers `splitCells`, `textCell`, `codeCell` and `known`: these did not change, and I exercised them only through the probe, without re-reviewing them on their own.
- A `-race` run of the package, deferred to the run already going.

## Outcome

- No findings. The main thread's own differential of `ParseSuite` (200,000 generated suites, old against new, equal; failed under the duplicate-check order mutant) agrees with this review. That order is now also pinned in the committed suite by `TestSuiteRefusals`' "a duplicate before its own faults" case, killed by the order mutant (1 of 1).

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing is broken. The new test makes the same sequence of script and git invocations as the old one, with the same arguments, working directories, HOME and source overrides. It also asserts the same strings, and the guard order, skips and cleanup order match. The only findings are one low-severity comment that now sits away from the code it names and one verified non-issue (the `defer` that moved). Both are below.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/catalog_refresh_guard_test.go:92-94` — the comment in `guardFooting` says "Two ways the guard itself could lose its footing … a parent directory it cannot enter … and no HOME to compare against". Only the first way is under it. The second ("no HOME") is `homeAndPin` at `:244-252`, which has no comment. The old file had the same split (about 300 lines apart), so this is not a regression, and nothing fails. ## Equivalence evidence
1. **Invocation trace.**
   - I copied the repo into scratch twice: once with the old `catalog_test.go` restored, once with the new six files.
   - In each copy I ran `TestRefreshCatalogScript` with `bash` and `git` shims first on PATH.
   - The shims logged cwd, argv, HOME, `CATALOG_AGENTS_CLI_REPO`, `CATALOG_GOOGLE_SKILLS_REPO` and `GIT_TRACE` for every call, then exec'd the real binary.

   - I extracted every `strings.Contains` and `HasPrefix` needle, every `t.Error`, `Fatal`, `Skip` and `Log` format string, the `Geteuid` and `Getuid` conditions and the `refuse(` labels from both versions.

3. **Captured values.**
   - `dest`, `work`, `pinA`, `pinG`, `agents`, `gskills`, `script`, `repo` and `tmp` are rig fields set once in `newRefreshRig`. No method assigns them.
   - `good` is set in `happyPath` (`catalog_refresh_run_test.go:75-76`) before any reader: `missingEntry`, `bystander`, `fetchByRole`, `refuse` and so on.

4. **Order.**
   - The 21 calls in `TestRefreshCatalogScript` follow the old section order.
   - Guards in `newRefreshRig` run in the old order: `Abs`, `Stat(script)` Fatal, `-short` Skip, midnight wait, then `LookPath` for bash, git and go.
   - Only then are `t.TempDir()` and the fixtures made.
   - `t.Skip` and `t.Fatal` inside helpers and `mutate` closures act on the same `t`, as before.
5. **Cleanup and defer.**
   - `t.Cleanup` for the locked directory is registered in `guardFooting` on the same `t`, so the LIFO order against `TempDir` is unchanged.

   - `go test -count=1 -run TestRefreshCatalogScript -v ./internal/harness/` passes (40 s), and the name is unchanged in `-list`.

The `eval` comments citing `catalog_test.go` cite commit 8374f9c, so they still resolve (plan D2). The 77 long test functions are struck out of scope (plan D1). Remaining restatements: none found. 5. Simplicity — pass. This is a rig struct with methods, stdlib only, nothing hand-rolled.
6. Decoupling — pass. The sections share state only through the rig's fields, which the plan's D6 states. The sections are order-dependent, and the type comment says so.

## Not examined
