# Security review — security-v310-round2-ff4c959-48ee381   (2026-10-27)

Range reviewed: ff4c959..48ee381

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

The worst problem is a gate rule, not the code. `ROADMAP.md:13` now moves the real-home smoke (and the macOS `fyr dream --all`) to "the operator's own update of each place after the tag". The justification is a quoted delegation ("Finish the project without me atm. Run in sandboxes if you need to verify"). Project `AGENTS.md` § Release says a gate is NO-SHIP until the real-home smoke has run on Antigravity *before the tag*. GUIDE-eval's own `smoke` note says the row "never stands for a real-home install". The quote asks for sandbox verification. On its face it does not waive the release rule, and a record that claims approval is data, not approval.

On the question I was sent to answer: round 1's finding is fixed as far as it went. The check no longer writes with `>`, and it refuses a `.db` that is itself a link. But the new cell still reaches outside `$SB` and the clone in three ways, all low:
- **Writes:** bash spills each large here-string (`<<<"$st"`) to a temp file under `/tmp`. I confirmed this with a probe under `env -i` on this box's bash 5.2.37: `/tmp/sh-thd.* (deleted)`. So "writes no file" is not true.
- **Reads:** `[ ! -L "$db" ]` tests only the last path component. A directory link planted under `$SB` still steers `ls -t`/`strings` to a real-home store.
- **Option injection:** the rule loop now takes `$r` from file names the session can create under `$SB`, and passes it to `grep` unprotected.

No secrets, credentials or private values were found in any added or changed line.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `ROADMAP.md:13` (the v3.1.0 line). It moves the real-home smoke and the macOS dream run to after the tag, on a quoted delegation.
  - Why it matters: `AGENTS.md` § Release says a gate whose "What was not checked" names a real-home or Antigravity run is NO-SHIP until that run exists, before the tag. `GUIDE-eval` body line 26 says the sandbox `smoke` row never stands for a real-home install.
  - The risk: the quoted sentence, "without me … run in sandboxes", is broad. A resumed or later session reading this line could take it as standing approval to tag without the real-home run, bypassing the gate.
  - Mitigation: the tag is still cut by `/preflight` "from the operator's own turn". I cannot see the conversation, so the operator may have explicitly waived the rule (hence medium confidence).
  - Remediation: before any tag, the gate report states the deviation from § Release as its own item and gets the operator's explicit word on it in their own turn. Otherwise the line keeps the real-home smoke as owed before the tag.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `GUIDE-eval` body line 34 (the `smoke` check cell) and line 26 ("writes no file"). The cell does `st=$(strings "$db")` and then feeds `"$st"` to `grep` six or more times through `<<<"$st"` (the GANNET check, the `<truncated` check, and one per rule file).
  - What happens: bash 5.1+ keeps a here-string in a pipe only when it fits the pipe buffer. A conversation store's `strings` output is far larger, so bash writes it to a temp file in `$TMPDIR` or `/tmp`.
  - Evidence: `checkEnv()` (`internal/eval/row_env.go:12-22`) sets no `TMPDIR`. A probe under `env -i` with a 200 KB here-string showed fd 0 as `/tmp/sh-thd.VoUJ5R (deleted)`.
  - Exposure: the file is mode 0600 and unlinked at once. Still, the sandbox conversation data, or a real store's if the next finding applies, is written outside `$SB` and the clone, and the guide's claim is false.
  - Remediation: pipe instead of using a here-string, for example `printf '%s\n' "$st" | grep -q GANNET`. `printf` is a builtin and a pipe makes no file. Alternatively `strings -- "$db" | grep -q …` per test, or set `TMPDIR=$SB` in `checkEnv` (a code change, which affects every row). Then fix the line-26 claim to match.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `GUIDE-eval` body line 34 (path components above the leaf are not checked). `[ -f "$db" ] && [ ! -L "$db" ]` checks only the final component. `intact()` (`internal/eval/row.go:56-66`, called at `row_after.go:17` before the check at `:35`) checks only the three roots: the row dir, the clone and SB.
  - The weakness: a session that replaces `$SB/.gemini`, `$SB/.gemini/antigravity-cli` or `…/conversations` with a link to the operator's real `~/.gemini/…` makes `ls -t` pick a real conversation DB. That DB is a regular file, so the check passes it, and `strings` reads it in place. That is the BUG-190 class: a live real-home store opened.
  - Same for the rules: `grep "Skills (" "$SB/.gemini/config/rules/AGENTS.md"`, and a `rules/` directory link makes the glob list another directory.
  - What leaks: only the pass/fail bit and the `/tmp` spill above. A small race also sits between the `-L` test and `strings`.
  - Remediation: resolve and pin the parent, for example `[ "$(cd "$(dirname "$db")" && pwd -P)" = "$(cd "$SB" && pwd -P)/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversations" ]`, and the same for `config/rules`. The suite-wide form is the existing audit-cleanup Follow-up (PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-cleanup, the new line 264). That Follow-up should name intermediate directories, not only `.db` leaves.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `GUIDE-eval` body line 34 (rule-name option injection and a forgeable pass). Round 1 recorded "`$r` comes from a literal list". That is no longer true: `r=$(basename "$f" .md)` comes from any `*.md` the session drops into `$SB/.gemini/config/rules/`, and `grep -q "$r" "$OUT"` passes it unprotected.
  - Option injection: a file named `-r.md` or `-f<name>.md` turns `$r` into a grep option. `-f<name>` reads a pattern file relative to cwd, the clone, and a link planted there leads outside. `-r` makes grep search the clone recursively.
  - Forged pass: a file named `..md` gives the pattern `.`, which matches any `$OUT`.
  - A gap the other way: deleting a rule file from the sandbox's `rules/` silently drops that rule from the check.
  - Remediation: `grep -qF -- "$r" "$OUT"` (or `-e "$r"`). Refuse names outside `[a-z0-9-]`. Check the shipped set (the harness's `rules/*.md` in the clone or fixture) rather than what the session left in `$SB`.

## Checked

- **Range:** `git diff --stat ff4c959 48ee381` gives `.agents/trail.jsonl` (+6/−4) and `ROADMAP.md` (1 line).
  - Trail records changed: BUG-191 (status open→fixed and the `updated` stamp; body identical, diffed), GUIDE-eval (body lines 26 and 34), GUIDE-testing (body line 206), PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-cleanup (two Follow-ups added after line 263).
  - Trail records added: REVIEW-2026-10-27-1845-review-…-approve and REVIEW-2026-10-27-1845-security-review-…, both read end to end.
  - Old and new bodies were extracted with `jq` from `git show <rev>:.agents/trail.jsonl` into `.agents/scratch/sec-r2/` and diffed.
- **Secrets:** pattern scan of every added line (138 lines). It covered GitHub, AWS, Google, OpenAI, Slack and GitLab token shapes, `ya29.`, JWT, PEM, email, IPv4, URLs, `.internal`/`.local`/`.corp`, session IDs and 40+ char base64 runs. Only hit: the literal pattern name `ya29.` in the round-1 record's scan list, which is not a value.
- **Private data:** none added. The round-1 record names the private values by kind and location only (DNS suffix, artifact host, host name, session ID) and repeats none. The ROADMAP quotes an operator sentence that contains no private value.
- **Instruction-shaped text:**
  - The ROADMAP's delegation quote is approval-shaped: finding 1.
  - The round-1 record's Remediation and Outcome lines are imperative but addressed to the main thread as review output. I acted on none.
  - No injection canary text was added in the range.
- **Injection:** the smoke check cell is the only executable text in the range: findings 2-4.
  - `$n` is digits only. When the rendered context has more than one `Skills (` line, `$n` holds several lines, which `grep -E` reads as several patterns. That weakens the check but is not a security issue.
  - `"$SB"`, `"$db"`, `"$f"` and `"$OUT"` are quoted. `<RULE[$f]>` is matched with `-F`.
  - Check environment: `env -i` style, `HOME=$SB`, cwd the clone, no `TMPDIR` (`row_env.go:12`, `row_session.go:129-130`).
- **Authz/authn:** finding 1, a gate rule waived on a quoted delegation. The round-1 Outcome says the final gate report quotes the operator verbatim; that report is not in this range.
- **Crypto:** none in the range.
- **Dependencies:** none. `go.mod`/`go.sum` are unchanged in the range (`git diff --name-only`, empty).
  - `govulncheck` was not re-run: the range changes no Go code or module. Round 1 ran it at ff4c959 on go1.27.3: 0 affecting, GO-2026-5024 known and not called.
  - `npm audit`: not applicable (no npm manifest).
- **GCP surface:** none.
- **Past bugs:** `fyr search --refs <path> --kind bug --home .agents/scratch/home-trail`.
  - `.agents/trail.jsonl` returned BUG-183, BUG-178 and BUG-182.
  - `ROADMAP.md` returned BUG-139.
  - None is a security class. BUG-183 is BUG-191's class, which the range closes as `fixed`.

## Not examined

- `ROADMAP.md`: only the changed line 13 was read, from the diff. The rest of the file is unchanged in the range.
- The `smoke` row was not run under a real `fyr eval`, and its must-pass and must-fail states (round-1 Outcome: 1 pass, 6 fail, `.agents/scratch/smoke-check/check2.sh`) were not re-run. That is the verifier's lane.
- The intermediate-link and rule-name findings (3 and 4) are argued from the cell's text and `intact()`. They were not reproduced in a sandbox. The here-string spill (finding 2) was reproduced with a probe outside eval.
- The "final v3.1.0 gate report" that the round-1 Outcome says quotes the operator's turn is not in this range and was not read.
- macOS bash (3.2 by default, unless the eval host uses a newer bash) always uses a temp file for a here-string. Not tested there.

## Outcome

- Finding 1 (medium; ROADMAP moves the real-home smoke past the tag on a quoted turn): fixed in the text. ROADMAP now says the operator's word on AGENTS.md § Release's real-home smoke is still owed before the tag, and the final gate asks for it in the operator's own turn. The gate does not tag without it.
- Finding 2 (a here-string spills to /tmp): fixed. The cell pipes through `printf`, and `env -i … TMPDIR=<scratch dir>` shows 0 temp files.
- Finding 3 (a linked directory reaches a real store): fixed. `pwd -P` on the sandbox home, `conversations` and `rules`, plus `! -L` on the database and on each rule file. Each refused in a must-fail state.
- Finding 4 (a rule file name used as a grep pattern or option): fixed. `grep -qwF --`, names held to `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*`, and `dotglob` so a dotfile is iterated and refused. `-r.md`, `A B.md`, `..md` and `.x.md` each fail the row.
- No third review round (the two-round cap, `review` Steps 4–5). The main agent validated the fixes in 1 good state and 15 bad ones (`.agents/scratch/smoke-check/check3.sh`), and `go test ./internal/eval` (TestSuiteHarness runs `bash -n` on every check) passes.

title: Security review — v3.1.0 gate records, 48ee381..3cd0b48: FINDINGS, three lows (2026-10-27)
body:
# Security review — security-v310-final-48ee381-3cd0b48   (2026-10-27)

Range reviewed: 48ee381..3cd0b48

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

All findings are low. None is a secret, a credential or a write outside the sandbox, and none blocks the gate on security grounds.

The final `smoke` check cell (GUIDE-eval body line 34) writes no file. It has no redirection and no here-string, and every value passes through a variable or a pipe. It fixes round 2's three cell findings: the `/tmp` spill, linked parent directories (`pwd -P` on `$SB`, `conversations` and `rules`), and rule names used as grep options (`-qwF --`, the `[a-z0-9-]` shape, `dotglob`). Its remaining reach outside `$SB` and the clone is read-only, and the content it reads never leaves the check, only its pass/fail bit:
- it reads `$OUT`, which sits outside `$SB` by design;
- a hard link defeats `[ ! -L ]` and `pwd -P`;
- a process the session left running can race the path checks, because leftover processes are reaped only after the check runs.

The worst remaining item is about the verdict's integrity, not exposure: the session decides which store, rule set and skill count the check compares against.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: high]** `GUIDE-eval` body line 34 (`smoke` check cell): a hard link passes every link test. The checks are `[ -f "$db" ] && [ ! -L "$db" ]`, `[ ! -L "$f" ]` and `pwd -P` on the directories. None of them detects a hard link. The session runs as the operator, so it can hard-link any file the operator owns on the same filesystem (the sandbox sits under the operator's home) into `conversations/` as the newest `*.db`, or in place of `rules/AGENTS.md`. `strings` or `grep` then reads that file in place. The content goes only into `$st`/`$n` and `grep -q`, and no command prints it to `check.log`, so the leak is the pass/fail bit. A very large target is also loaded whole into a shell variable (memory, low). The session could already read the same file itself, so the check grants no new capability. Remediation: refuse a store or rule file whose link count is not 1 (`stat -c %h` on GNU; `stat -f %l` on macOS). Alternatively, state in the note that hard links are out of scope. The note currently claims "a link".
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/eval/run.go:172-174`, `row_after.go:15-37` against `:68-89` (applies to the cell above and to every row): a time-of-check race. Step 13 (the row's check) runs right after agy exits, while `leftoverProcs` (step 14, `exitChecks`) runs after it. `waitAgy` kills the process group only on cancel (`row_session.go:102-108`), not on a normal exit. A process the session leaves running can swap `conversations/` or `rules/` for a link between the cell's `pwd -P` test and its `ls -t`/`strings`. The result is the same read-only, pass/fail-only reach that round 2's finding 3 described. This is pre-existing code and outside the range's diff, but the cell's new guarantee depends on it. Remediation: in code, a later change: kill or reap the session's leftover processes before step 13, or run step 14's process check before the row's check. Until then, the note should say that the guard assumes no process outlives the session.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `GUIDE-eval` body line 34 and `REVIEW-2026-10-27-1850-security-review-v3-1-0-gate-round-2-ff4c959-48ee` `## Outcome`, finding 4: the verdict can be forged, and the Outcome over-claims a fix. Three inputs come from what the session left in `$SB`:
  - the rule set (`"$rd"/*.md`): deleting a rule file drops it from the check;
  - the skill count (`Skills (N)` in the sandbox `AGENTS.md`): editable;
  - the store (`ls -t`, newest wins): a planted newer `.db` that holds GANNET and the `<RULE[...]>` strings is the one checked.

  Round 2's finding 4 remediation said "check the shipped set … rather than what the session left in `$SB`". Its Outcome says "fixed" but adopts only the grep and name parts. A second, smaller gap: `n=$(grep … "$rd/AGENTS.md")` reads `AGENTS.md` before the loop's `[ ! -L "$f" ]` refuses a linked one. That read is read-only and only digits reach `grep -E`. Remediation: take the expected rule names and skill count from the clone or the fixture (`$CLONE/rules/*.md`, `fyr list` there), not from `$SB`. Move the `! -L` test on `AGENTS.md` before its first read. Amend the round-2 Outcome to say "partly fixed".
- **[info / confidence: high]** `TEST-2026-10-27-2012-eval-16-of-17-pass-at-4fe0bb6` and `TEST-2026-10-27-2031-eval-1-of-1-pass-at-a4e3cec` (sandbox column) and `TEST-…-1913-…` (Commands, 3c): absolute paths under the operator's home directory, which name the operator's login (32 occurrences in added lines). # Review — phase7-redactor-warning-and-needles   (2026-10-27)

Range reviewed: working tree on top of 2934d42 — `.agents/scratch/phase7-review/source.diff` (README, cmd/fyr/main.go help, cmd/fyr/record.go, new cmd/fyr/record_redact.go + test, internal/redact needles + tests) and `spec-fyr-record.diff` (SPEC-fyr-record). Lenses: code + docs.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing is broken. The warning runs after a successful store, judges exactly the bytes brain.readBody consumed (TeeReader on the same io.Reader, LimitReader inside brain), prints only a line number, and leaves the exit status alone. The three new needles pass `go test ./internal/redact` and `TestRecordRedactorWarning` passes. The one real gap is test strength: the "a refused body prints nothing" claim in the spec and the test comment is not actually pinned (finding 1). Two doc nits follow.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/record_redact_test.go:53-56` — the "refused body prints nothing" case uses body `"\n"`, which holds no token, so the redactor would not warn on it even if `recordAdd`/`recordEdit` called `warnRedactable` before checking `err` (or unconditionally). Reasoning (not a run mutation): `seen` for `"\n"` is clean, so the assertion `errOut.Len()==0` passes regardless of the `err == nil` guard in `record.go:109-112` and `record.go:150-154`. The spec (SPEC-fyr-record, "A clean body, a refused one ... print nothing") and the test header both claim this behaviour. Fix: refuse a body that carries the token, e.g. `token + "\n\x00"` (NUL is refused by readBody after the tee has read it) or a duplicate `--id`, and assert stderr empty and exit 1. Same for edit (`record edit BUG-999 --body` with a token: ID not found).
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `cmd/fyr/main.go:77-80` — the doc-comment on `var stderr` still says it is "where a read-only verb names the state directory from before the rename" and that "its stdout is data"; it is now also where `record add`/`edit --body` print the redactor warning (and the test replaces it for that). Describing-text rule: update the comment.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `SPEC-fyr-record` (new bullet, "The redactor warning") — the rationale is "a project's records reach the committed trail.jsonl" and it says `fyr memory add` does not warn because memory is never exported, yet the code warns for every `add`/`edit --body`, including `record add memory`, `--global` records (feedback, proposals) and project kinds the export skips. Either the code should warn only for exported project kinds, or the spec should say it warns for any `add` / `edit --body` regardless of kind or scope and that only `memory add` and `import` skip it. Today the spec's own contrast is half wrong. Also `record import` stores bodies unwarned; the spec bullet does not name it.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. The `if c.recBody` around the warn in `recordEdit` is redundant (empty `seen` never warns) but harmless and states intent.
2. Flow tracing — pass. recordAdd/recordEdit -> brain.Add/Edit -> readBody via the tee; warning only on `err == nil`; `stdin` is read at call time so tests that swap it work. Redact is the same function dream's `scrub` applies to record bodies (collect.go:138), so "the dream's redactor would change" is accurate. Line number from first differing line is valid for line redactions and key blocks. Raw-stdin line number can differ from the stored body when it had leading blank lines or CRLF; the spec says "as read from stdin", so it is stated.
3. Standards conformance — pass with the two doc nits above. Needles follow AGENTS.md (by kind, no `\b`, each with a benign near-miss in TestRedactShapes, bare shapes in shapeSecrets, vendor-doc examples in TestVendorDocExamples). Help text, README row and spec agree on the behaviour for add/edit. No enumeration of needle kinds elsewhere (README, AGENTS.md, SPEC-fyr-dream, GUIDE-testing § 3b grepped) needs the new kinds.
4. Directory layout — pass (record_redact.go beside record.go in cmd/fyr, tests beside code, files well under limits).
5. Simplicity — pass; stdlib only (io.TeeReader, strings.Builder), no new dependency, no crypto.
6. Decoupling — pass; cmd/fyr imports internal/redact (stdlib-only package), brain untouched.

## Verification run
`go test -count=1 -run TestRecordRedactorWarning ./cmd/fyr/` ok; `go test -count=1 ./internal/redact/` ok; `go test -count=1 -run 'TestHarnessMap|TestFunctionLength' .` ok. No mutation was run (read-only review): the finding-1 claim is by reading.

## Not examined
Full `go test ./...` (in progress elsewhere per dispatch), race run, govulncheck, behaviour on CRLF bodies versus the stored body (needles that depend on a trailing `\r`), regex cost on a 1 MiB body, and whether terraform ID length `{6,}` matches real HCP IDs (taken from the vendor example only).

## Outcome

Answered by the main agent, 2026-10-27; round 2 over the fixes (about 40 lines, under the reviewer threshold) read by the main agent, with a must-fail run per new claim.

1. Fixed. The refused-body case now carries the token plus a NUL, for `add` and for `edit --body` (`cmd/fyr/record_redact_test.go`). Mutation: moving the warning before the `err` check in `recordAdd`, and separately in `recordEdit`, each fails the test.
2. Fixed. The `stderr` comment in `cmd/fyr/main.go` now names the record warning.
3. Fixed in the spec. SPEC-fyr-record's bullet now says every kind and scope warns alike (a `--global` record and a `memory` record added through `record add` too), and that `fyr memory add` and `record import` do not.

title: Security review — Phase 7 of audit-choices: SD41 needles and the record redactor warning
body:
# Security review — phase7 record redactor warning + SD41 needles   (2026-10-27)

Range reviewed: 2934d42..working tree (uncommitted; inputs `.agents/scratch/phase7-review/source.diff` and `spec-fyr-record.diff`). Blast radius read: `internal/redact/redact.go` (whole), `internal/brain/brain.go` readBody/Add, `internal/brain/brain_input.go` editFields, `cmd/fyr/eval.go` record write, the export's wire line (`internal/brain/export.go:299`).

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

Nothing high. The worst gap: the warning covers only the BODY, while the record's TITLE goes into the committed `.agents/trail.jsonl` export too, and nothing checks it. `fyr record add bug --title "rotate dckr_pat_<token> leaked in CI"` stores and exports the token with no warning. One existing title in this repo's trail is already one the redactor would change. Second: the warning would fire on 206 of the 1,228 existing bodies (17%) in this repo, so it risks being ignored when it matters. The new needles themselves are sound, run in linear time and leak nothing. The stdin tee changes nothing about what the store reads.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/record.go:109` (add) and `cmd/fyr/record.go:146-147` (edit `--title`): `warnRedactable` is called with the body only. The title is a field of every exported line (`internal/brain/export.go:299`, `wireLine{…, r.Title, …}`), so it reaches the committed `trail.jsonl` just as the body does. Scenario: an agent writes a bug or change record whose title quotes the leaked token, or a `Authorization: Bearer …` fragment. It is exported and committed, and stderr stays silent. Evidence: running the new `Redact` over the current `.agents/trail.jsonl` finds 1 title it would change. Remediation: run the same check on the title in `add` and in `edit --title` (e.g. `warnRedactable` takes a field label: "the title holds text…"), and add a test row with a token in the title.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/record_redact.go:105-116`, plus the needle over-reach at `internal/redact/redact.go:135-137`: the warning fires on 206 of 1,228 existing bodies in this repo (review 109, testing 63, plan 14, change 9, handoff 6, spec 3, adr 1, bug 1). Most of these records are about the redactor itself and quote needle shapes: `PRIVATE KEY`, `AKIA`, the SD41 vendor examples. The new needles also match prose such as `xapp-level-token`, `the dckr_pat_-prefixed tokens` and `my_project.atlasv1.description_field` (probed). A warning that appears on one write in six gets ignored, so the one carrying a real credential is ignored too. Over-redaction is the accepted safe direction for the DREAM. For a WARNING the cost is fatigue. Remediation (operator's call): put the needle's pattern name in the warning, e.g. `(first at line 3: docker access token)`. `redaction.Pattern` already carries it and it is never the text, so a reader can tell a prose mention of `-----BEGIN` from a token shape at a glance.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/redact/redact.go:137` and the prefix list at `:27`: the Slack kind is still split into instances. `xoxe.xapp-` and `xoxe.xoxp-` are caught. Probes show that rotation REFRESH tokens (`xoxe-1-…`), browser-session tokens (`xoxc-…`) and the `d` cookie (`xoxd-…`) pass unredacted, so a body holding one gets no warning and no dream redaction. AGENTS.md's needle rule says needles grow by KIND. Remediation: one Slack-family regexp, e.g. `xox[a-z]-[A-Za-z0-9-]{8,}|xapp-[A-Za-z0-9-]{8,}`, replacing the four `xox?-` prefixes, with benign near-misses in `TestRedactShapes`. Confidence is medium because the `xoxe-`/`xoxc-`/`xoxd-` shapes come from memory of Slack's docs and were not re-checked against them (no network).

- **[low / confidence: medium]** Other write paths into the export get no warning: `cmd/fyr/eval.go:184` (`fyr eval`'s `testing` record, whose body is `evalBody`) and `fyr record import` (`internal/brain/import*.go`, bodies migrated from Markdown files) both write project records that are exported to `trail.jsonl` unscanned. SD42 is scoped to `add`/`edit`, so this is residual risk, not a regression. I did not read `evalBody` to see whether it can carry transcript text (see Not examined). Remediation: either state the scope in SPEC-fyr-record § the redactor warning ("add and edit only; import and eval are not checked"), or call the same check from those paths.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/record_redact.go:115`: the warning arrives after `.agents/trail.jsonl` has been rewritten with the text. It names neither the record ID nor the recourse. A caller that keeps only stdout (the ID) loses it, and the next DoD step is commit-and-push. Warning rather than refusing is the operator's choice (SD42) and is not a finding. Remediation: add the ID and the fix, e.g. `…; stored as written in BUG-001 — fyr record edit BUG-001 --body replaces it before you commit`.

Checked and clean (no finding):
- **No leak through the warning.** It prints a line number only, never the text (pinned by the test's `strings.Contains(out+stderr, token)`). The line number comes from the body as read from stdin, which is what the spec says.
- **What the store reads is unchanged.** `readBody` (`internal/brain/brain.go:171-200`) takes a plain `io.Reader` with no `*os.File` assertion, Stat or TTY check that the `io.TeeReader` could defeat. It reads through `LimitReader(maxBody+1)`, so `seen` is bounded at 1 MiB+1 and is judged only when the store succeeded. A refused body (oversize, NUL, empty) or a missing ID leaves no warning. The stored body is `seen` with CRLF folded and blank lines and whitespace trimmed. A lone `\r` is refused by `bodyText`, so normalization cannot create a needle that the raw-body check missed.
- **New needles, positive cases.** Real-shaped fakes of all three kinds are caught bare, after a literal `\n`, and in the vendor doc examples. There is no `\b` in front, which follows the needle rule.
- **Regex cost.** Go RE2 runs in linear time. Benchmark of whole `Redact` on 1 MiB adversarial inputs (one alnum line, `abcdef.atlasv1.` repeated, `abcdefg.` repeated, 1 MiB of prose lines), old vs new: about 0.9–1.0 s before and 1.0–1.15 s after (+10–15%). Inputs the new needles match short-circuit and got faster. A test run was in progress on the box, so the absolute numbers are noisy. Not a DoS.
- **Tests.** `go test -run 'TestRedact|TestVendorDocExamples' ./internal/redact/` and `go test -run TestRecordRedactorWarning ./cmd/fyr/` both PASS, confirmed with `-v`. The test token `dckr_pat_FAKEVALUEFAKEVALUE` is fake.

## Checked
- Secrets: none in the diff. The test tokens are FAKEVALUE fakes and the vendor doc examples are published placeholders. The new warning prints no matched text.
- Injection: no new parsing of external input. The body path is unchanged (`readBody`). The warning's format string takes only an int.
- Authz/authn: not touched. The warning changes no exit status or scope.
- Crypto: not touched. Nothing hand-rolled.
- Dependencies: none added (stdlib `io`, `strings`). `govulncheck ./...` with `$(go env GOPATH)/bin/govulncheck`: 0 vulnerabilities reached, 1 in a required module not called (the known GO-2026-5024 per AGENTS.md; not re-verified with `-show verbose`). `npm audit` is n/a: no JS ecosystem in the diff.
- GCP surface: not touched.

## Not examined
- `evalBody` in `cmd/fyr/eval.go`: whether a `fyr eval` testing record can carry transcript or tool output (and so a credential) into the export.
- Whether any of the 206 existing trail bodies that would warn holds a REAL credential rather than a quoted needle shape. I counted them only and printed no matched text. This is worth a separate read-only pass by the operator.
- `record import`'s body sources (`internal/brain/import_docs.go`, `import_memory.go`, `import_global.go`) beyond the grep.
- The README and main.go usage text, which were read in the diff only, for wording.
- Slack, Docker and HCP Terraform token formats were not re-checked against the vendors' current docs (no network). The Slack gap above is from memory.
- The full `go test ./...` was not run, per the dispatch: a run was in progress on this tree.

## Outcome

Answered by the main agent, 2026-10-27.

- Medium, the title: fixed. `warnRedactable(title, body)` judges a new title too (`add` always, `edit` only with `--title`), with its own line, `fyr record: warning: the title holds text the redactor would change; stored as written`. Tests: a token title on add and on `edit --title` warns; an `edit --status` keeping a token title and a clean `--title` do not. Mutation: disabling the title check fails both warning rows. SPEC-fyr-record, the help text and README say so.
- Low, the warning's volume (206 of 1,228 bodies in this repo) and naming the pattern: deferred to the operator. It changes the approved message and needs a new exported function from `internal/redact`. Goes to the inventory ledger for a value check.
- Low, the Slack family (`xoxe-`, `xoxc-`, `xoxd-` and Slack's documented `xwfp-` are not covered): deferred to the operator. AGENTS.md's needle rule calls for one rule per kind, and this is a needle-set change outside Phase 7's three approved kinds. Goes to the inventory ledger.
- Notes, `fyr eval` and `record import` writing to the trail with no check, and the warning naming no record ID: deferred to the inventory ledger with the two above.

title: Review — cold read of PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger (2026-10-27)
body:
# Review — ledger plan cold-reader   (2026-10-27)

Range reviewed: `PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` (source copy `.agents/scratch/ledger/PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger.md`, read in full) at HEAD ade98e8 plus the uncommitted `.agents/trail.jsonl`. Cross-read: `PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-choices` (all D-rows, Phases, E2E) and `PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-cleanup` (§ Scope, row 18-20, § Follow-ups, D1-D4), AGENTS.md, and the HEAD tree.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

The plan is sound in structure and its evidence mostly holds at HEAD, so nothing makes it unbuildable. Two things would stop a fresh session partway, and both are cheap to fix in the plan text. (1) Phase 6 cannot run its own `fyr eval preflight` verify: the box edits `GUIDE-eval` (a record in `.agents/trail.jsonl`), and `fyr eval` refuses an uncommitted `GUIDE-eval` (`cmd/fyr/eval.go:229`). The Kickoff approves a commit only at the checkpoint, after the evals. (2) The sandbox recipe has no build step for `$B`, and its S1/S3 fake runs use `dream --all`. Once Phase 3 lands, `--all` skips any unregistered fixture, so S1 and S3 on the final head and S3 in Phase 4 send nothing and fail. S2's `search --global` and `metrics ingest` halves also have no fixture that can show anything. Inventory spot-checks: 13 rows checked, all supported. No unfinished item of either source plan is missing, apart from the nits below.

## Findings

Ranked blocking / should-fix / nit. "Conf" is my confidence.

### Blocking

- **[blocking / conf high]** § Phases, Phase 6 box 3 (`preflight` row) and its Kickoff. The box edits the `preflight` row of `GUIDE-eval`, then verifies with `fyr eval preflight` twice. `fyr eval` refuses with "GUIDE-eval has uncommitted changes; commit them first" (`cmd/fyr/eval.go:229`, pinned by `cmd/fyr/eval_test.go:493`, and the verb × place matrix lists the same refusal). The Kickoff's closed set approves "the checkpoint's change record, commit and push" only, and the checkpoint is the last box. A session either stalls or commits outside its approvals. Fix: add a box or a sentence: "commit the GUIDE-eval edit (record + test) first, in its own commit; then run the evals", and add that interim commit to the Kickoff's approvals. The same applies to any later phase that edits `GUIDE-eval` and then evals, and to Phase 6 box 1 if the agent edits must be committed for a clean eval label (the label is only "dirty", so not blocking).

### Should-fix

- **[should-fix / conf high]** § The sandbox, recipe (and § Terms `$B`). `B=$R/.agents/scratch/fyrbin` is used but nothing builds it. § Terms says "a binary built from the tree under test" and no box or recipe line has `go build -o .agents/scratch/fyrbin ./cmd/fyr`. A fresh session either fails at `"$B" record list` or, on this box, runs the stale 22:03 binary (built from HEAD, not from the Phase's tree), so S1-S3 would test the old code and report a false result. Fix: put the build as the recipe's first command, and say "rebuild before every sandbox run".
- **[should-fix / conf high]** § Verification S1, S3, § Done, and the recipe's "fake runs ... `dream --all`". After Phase 3, `targets()` under `--all` skips unregistered roots (D16), so `fixture-a` and `fixture-cap` are skipped and no `agy` call happens: Phase 4's S3, and the Done box's re-run of S1 and S3 on the final head, would find no stdin files. Only S2 registers `fixture-a`, and it registers only that one. Fix: say that S1/S3 after Phase 3 either use `--project <fixture>` (unfiltered, D16) or first run `fyr index --register` in `fixture-a` and `fixture-cap`; and give the exact command line for S3, which the plan never writes out.
- **[should-fix / conf high]** § Verification S2. It claims "`fyr search --global` and `fyr metrics ingest` skip the unregistered roots (choices E2E 1)", but the recipe cannot show either. `fixture-foreign` has no `.agents/docs/` (choices E2E 1 requires "a clone carrying `.agents/docs/` and `.agents/trail.jsonl`"), so it never enters the global file index; and there is no conversation database under the fake login (`$S/login/.gemini/antigravity-cli` holds only the token and `installation_id`), so `metrics ingest` has no sessions to join. As written, S2's second and third halves pass vacuously. The ledger also dropped E2E 1's last sentence ("a clone of that registered checkout is not registered"). Fix: give the foreign fixture an `.agents/docs/` file and the login a copied/fixture `conversation_summaries.db` with a session rooted in `fixture-foreign` (a copy only), or state that S2 covers the dream half only and the other two halves rest on the unit tests. Add the clone-of-registered case.
- **[should-fix / conf medium]** § Phase 2 Kickoff, approvals. Box 4 (`fyr index --register`) names docs "`SPEC-fyr-search`, README's verbs table, `GUIDE-fyr-matrix`". The Kickoff's closed set lists the SPEC-fyr-search and GUIDE-fyr-matrix edits but not README.md's verbs table (Phase 3's Kickoff does list README's dream row). A fresh session is told to ask only outside the set. Fix: add "README.md's verbs table".
- **[should-fix / conf medium]** § Phase 1 Kickoff. "Never: ... anything outside this repository" contradicts the approved "one real `fyr dream --project` run on fixture-a": that run calls the model over the network and copies the operator's real `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli` token (`internal/dream/agy_home.go:30` reads `os.Getenv("HOME")`). Conversations are read from the `--home` dir, not `$HOME` (`internal/dream/run.go:113`, `internal/search/dream.go:89`), so no conversation leaks (I confirmed this half). Fix: state in the Kickoff that the approved real run reads (copies) the real login token and uses the network, and nothing else under `~/.gemini`.
- **[should-fix / conf medium]** § Inventory item 66 and Phase 10 box 2. Item 66 cites `internal/metrics/events_join.go:56-68`, which at HEAD is the `brain.ForMetrics` call and the feedback loop in `joinRoot`, i.e. the migrated branch the plan wants to keep. The removal named in Phase 10 is `joinFiles` and `fileTimes`; `joinFiles` exists (`events_join.go:134`) but I found no `func fileTimes`. The box would send a session to delete the wrong lines or search for a function that is not there. Fix: re-cite the exact functions (`joinFiles` at `:134` and whatever reads `feedback.jsonl`) and name what stays. (Gated behind A1, so it blocks nothing today.)

### Nits

- **[nit / conf high]** Inventory item 73 (and 16, 32): the verify cell writes `\|` inside a code span (a markdown-table escape). Copied literally, `go test ./internal/search -run 'TestConcurrentReconcile\|TestFirstOpenWaitsForALock'` matches no test (I ran it: `ok ... [no tests to run]`), and `grep -E 'brief-\|owner:'` and the item 32 `git grep -E 'feedback\.jsonl\|...'` match a literal `|`. Each passes vacuously, which is the "verify that cannot fail" the plan is trying to avoid. Phase 9's box 1 writes the plain `|`, so item 32 is covered there. Fix: move these commands out of table cells or write `|` in a prose line.
- **[nit / conf high]** Item 35 and Phase 9 box 4: "every `Test…` name in the record has a `func`". The record also cites the globs `TestUpdateFromRelease*` and `TestRun*`, which have no exact function (my loop reports both as missing along with the truly stale `TestSymlinkedIndexRefused`). Say that a `*`-suffixed name is a prefix and is checked with `git grep 'func TestRun'`.
- **[nit / conf medium]** D1 says every struck/deferred item "keeps its reason here, so nothing lives only in a closed plan", but the audit-choices items struck by its own D-rows (IN44 and the hash line, row 13's `w.logs` root, TS39, G28, WS45 `grilling`, row 14 as item 6, TR18) are not all listed: item 6 and 7 cover rows 14 and the git half; IN44, `w.logs`, TS39, G28, WS45 and SD42/SD47 (done) have no row. They are recorded in choices D35, D41, D43, and that record is never rewritten, so no work is lost; add one "struck by choices D35/D41/D43" row for completeness.
- **[nit / conf medium]** Item 55 (IN57) verify: `grep -n 'record get' cmd/fyr/run_dispatch.go` is empty at HEAD and would be empty after a fix that names "the `record` verbs". Use a pattern the fix must create, or keep "read it". The header (`writesState`, `:135-141`) says "a verb or subcommand that only reads answer false" while the `record` case below it returns `!c.dryRun` for every record verb; the claim is real.
- **[nit / conf low]** Phase 6 sizing: the box runs `agent-verifier`, `agents-security` and `preflight` twice (each up to ~15-25 min with the 20 m print timeout; `agyTimeout = 25m`, `internal/eval/row_session.go:16`), plus the AGENTS.md edit and the `preflight` row cut. If the first cut of the row is still over 900 s the phase needs a second pass. The Risks section already names the fallback; it is the one phase most likely to overrun one session.

## Answers to the five questions

1. **Executable from Kickoff and boxes alone?** Mostly yes. Boxes are concrete, each has a verify and a who, and most verifies are must-fail or a measured value. The gaps are the Phase 6 eval-after-uncommitted-edit trap, Phase 2's missing README approval, Phase 1's "outside this repository" contradiction, the missing `$B` build, and the unwritten S3 command. Standing approvals are otherwise closed and sufficient. Phase 8 box 4 (IN57) and Phase 9 box 4 are "read it"/glob-prone verifies; acceptable.
2. **Inventory evidence.** Spot-checked at HEAD, all supported: #16 (`skills/harness-audit/SKILL.md` Step 1 dispatch sets no path or frontmatter), #25 (`preflight` `:56` reuses the verifier log reaching HEAD), #30 (only agents with `run_command` mention `mkdir`; no "write tool" text in agents/skills/context/rules except a golang reference), #41 (skill listing 19,393 of 19,500; hand-written context 14,814 of 15,000, from the size tests), #43 (`gofmt -l *.go` empty), #46 (measured: `xoxe-`, `xoxc-`, `xoxd-`, `xwfp-` unchanged by `redact.Redact`; `xoxb-`, `xoxe.xoxp-`, `xoxe.xapp-` redacted), #49 (all ten `TestCredsEveryPattern` hit strings change under `Redact`: measured), #54/#53 (`check.go:230` swallows the read error; `requirements.go:188-199` skip note for `_test.go`), #57 (`cmd/fyr/eval.go:293` passes `src.Dir` to `trail.Dirty`, which uses `ls-tree --full-tree`), #59 (`plan_test.go:18` calls `harness.DirSource`), #64 (`status.go` leftover line; `LegacyTimerFiles` exists), #73 (BUG-187, 075cbbe touches `internal/search/store.go` and `internal/metrics/store.go`), #20 (AGENTS.md does not mention `TestSuiteHarness`, so the verify can fail before the edit), #32 (`README.md:81` names the legacy files; DEPLOY-local `proposals/dream/` is the dream output dir, consistent with "stays"). Eval rows `agent-verifier`, `agents-security`, `retro`, `distill`, `preflight` exist in `GUIDE-eval`. Completeness: every row of cleanup § Scope, row 18-20 and § Follow-ups, and every open box of choices (Phases 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, Done) maps to an inventory row or a phase; the BUG list (190, 139, 172, 179, 183, 191) is covered. Gap: the struck choices items listed in the third nit.
3. **Contradictions.** None with REQUIREMENTS.md that I could find: the R3 edit is in D32's words and approved by the operator's D32; Phase 2 puts the ADR, R3 and ROADMAP in one commit as AGENTS.md's REQUIREMENTS rule requires. AGENTS.md rule 3 (map change in one commit with code, docs, ADR) is honoured by Phase 9 box 1. The "Never ... anything outside this repository" clause (Phase 1) contradicts its own approved real run. Phase 4 changes the cap's drop order against ADR-055a, which a new ADR amends, as the plan says.
4. **Sizing and order.** Order 1-4 is right (consumers need the marker; the cap is independent; the filter changes how the sandbox must be driven, see S1/S3 finding). Phase 5 and 6 are the evals-heavy sessions; Phase 6 is the largest. Phase 9 touches eight records plus two ADRs in a doc-only session: large but one sitting. Phase 8 holds six unrelated small items; fine. Phase 10 correctly waits on A1.
5. **Sandbox recipe.** Read line by line. It runs from this checkout except for the missing `$B` build; the fake `agy` output matches the real stream-json shape (`internal/dream/fakeagy_test.go:28-33`), the trail wire fields match `.agents/trail.jsonl`, and the fixtures live under gitignored scratch. It keeps to fixture projects only: the fake runs set `HOME=$S/login`, the real run reads conversations from `--home` (empty) and only the login token from the real `$HOME`; `fyr record list --all` is warned off from the checkout. Not run end to end here (I was told not to run `fyr dream`/`fyr eval`). Residual risks: `git commit` in a fixture inherits the operator's global git config (a `commit.gpgsign=true` would stall it); not checked.

## Criteria

1. Dead code — n/a (a plan, not code). Struck rows are explicit; no orphan item found.
2. Flow tracing — fail: the Phase 6 eval/commit ordering, and S1/S3 after Phase 3, are broken flows between boxes.
3. Standards conformance — pass with nits: AGENTS.md rules 1-6 and the R3 procedure are respected; the verify cells with `\|` and the glob/`record get` verifies are weak.
4. Directory layout — pass: the sandbox lives under gitignored `.agents/scratch/`; new tests land beside their packages.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass: stdlib only, no dependency, allow-list helper reused.
6. Decoupling — pass: phases follow package seams; Phase 2/3 dependency is stated.

## Not examined

- I did not execute the sandbox recipe, `fyr dream`, `fyr eval`, or any `go test -race` (forbidden by the dispatch); recipe findings are by reading plus the code it exercises.
- Rows not spot-checked at HEAD: 2, 3-5 (the dream design is verified through the sandbox, not by me), 14, 15, 17-19, 21 (only the timeout constants), 23, 24, 26-29, 31, 33, 34, 36-40, 42, 44, 45, 47, 48, 50-52, 56, 58, 60-63, 65, 67-72, 74. Row 71 (`copy.go:21`) and the SD34/SD35/SD37 claims were taken from the plan.
- The cited audit records (`PLAN-2026-10-27-recon-harness-audit`, the two harness-audit reviews) and the four explorer briefs in scratch were not opened; D-row citations of `choices` were checked, the audit evidence behind them was not.
- Item 22's `-run` patterns were counted (5 lines) but not each resolved to a function; item 36's § 3d `go build -o .agents/scratch/fyr` text was confirmed in `GUIDE-testing` but the clash was not reproduced.
- Eval row contents (what `agent-verifier`/`agents-security` would catch) were not read; only their existence.

## Outcome

Every finding is fixed in the plan text (`PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` D7), none rebutted:

- Blocking (Phase 6 evals after an uncommitted `GUIDE-eval`): fixed. The box commits the row edit on its own before its evals, and the Kickoff approves that interim commit and push.
- `$B` never built: fixed. The recipe's first step is `go build -o "$B" ./cmd/fyr` from the tree under test.
- S1 and S3 after Phase 3: fixed. Both use `--project` (unfiltered, audit-choices D16). § Runs gives the exact commands F1, R1, D2, F2 and F3, each re-run as written at ade98e8 and reproducing the baseline.
- S2 vacuous halves: fixed for search. The foreign fixture carries a `.gitignore` and `.agents/docs/notes.md`, and at ade98e8 `fyr search --global CANARY` from `fixture-a` returns the clone's record and docs file. The metrics half is stated as resting on Phase 3 box 3's unit test. The clone-of-registered case is added.
- Phase 2 Kickoff, README: fixed. Phase 1 Kickoff, outside-the-repository contradiction: fixed; R1 is named as copying the real login token into a scratch private HOME and sending fixture content to the model, nothing else under `~/.gemini`; the Done Kickoff likewise.
- Item 66 and Phase 10: fixed. They now name `joinFiles` `:134`, `joinFileBugs` `:172`, the `fileTimes` type `:115-122`, `readFeedback`, and what stays.
- Nits: the `\|` cells are rewritten with `-e` and two `-run` calls; the glob rule is added to item 35 and Phase 9; item 55's verify reads the header; item 75 lists audit-choices' own strikes; Phase 6's size is left as is, and its fallback is in § Risks. Fixture commits set `commit.gpgsign=false` (the report's residual risk).

title: Review — cold read of PLAN-2026-10-27-harness-audit-fix (2026-10-27)
body:
---
owner: reviewer
date: 2026-10-27
---
# Review — cold-audit-fix   (2026-10-27)

Range reviewed: `.agents/scratch/harness-audit/2026-10-27/out/plan.md` (PLAN-2026-10-27-harness-audit-fix), a cold read of the plan against the code surfaces it names. No diff exists. Recon rows were read only for IN45, SD38, SD39, SD20 and the Final IDs lines of the riskiest IDs.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: design needs revision; implementation not ready

Worst first. Four places where the plan's premise about existing code is false and the stated fix or its verify clause would not do what the plan says: (G1) `trail.Dirty` "compared as `changed` does" reads every tracked symlink as dirty, and this checkout tracks one (`.agents/skills`, mode 120000); (G3) SD48's "callers already turn a copy error into a skipped conversation" is false for the dream; (G6) IN49's hard-link check runs after `O_TRUNC` has already emptied the shared inode; (G5) SD39's `updated` half is already implemented and its quoted refusal texts do not exist. Several verify/E2E fixtures do not produce the condition they claim (G2, G4, G7). The skill-listing-budget claim checks out (19,287 of 19,500 measured today, 213 headroom) but the plan's own edits overrun it by arithmetic (G13).

## Gaps

- **G1 (SD38, high).** `internal/trail/trail.go` `changed` (lines 91-130) sets `out[path]=true` for any tracked entry that is not a regular file (`!info.Mode().IsRegular()`), skips non-`blob` entries (gitlinks), compares content hash only (no mode) and cannot see a staged-new file (not in HEAD's ls-tree, not in `ls-files -o`). The plan says `Dirty` compares "as `trail.changed` does". `git ls-files -s` shows `120000 .agents/skills` tracked here, so on this repo `Dirty` is always true: `fyr record import` always refuses and `eval`'s source line always says `(dirty)`. Failure modes name only filtered files. Also: `hash-object --stdin-paths` joined by `\n` breaks on a tracked name holding a newline (count mismatch, then `ok=false`), and `changed` takes a `docs` pathspec the plan does not say how to widen to the whole tree.
- **G2 (SD38 verify, medium).** The Phase 1 grep `git grep -n '"status"' -- internal cmd ':!*_test.go'` "prints only non-git strings" is false: `internal/harness/repo.go:222` is a real `gitOut(repo, "status", "--porcelain", ...)` (kept on purpose, the harness's own checkout; the trail header exempts `internal/harness`), and `json:"status"` tags also match. The expectation must list the one allowed git hit. E2E 1's fixture also omits the `.gitattributes` line (`*.md filter=x`): `.git/config` defining a clean filter alone never runs it, so today's code would pass the "fails before" test.
- **G3 (SD48, high).** `internal/search/dream.go:198-205`: `conversationText` returns any non-ErrNotExist copy error, `AgyConversationText` returns `nil, err`, and `internal/dream/collect.go:152-156` fails the whole project on it ("An Antigravity read error fails the project, so its watermark stays"). Also `copyDB` (`dream.go:233-240`) returns an error for a refused `-wal`/`-shm`. So with the plan's "existing error paths are unchanged", one FIFO or symlink at one conversation path makes that project's nightly dream fail every night. Only `internal/metrics/agy.go:58-62` (`fail(source, err)`) is per-conversation. `internal/dream/dream.go:205` swallows the error. The plan must decide skip-the-conversation vs fail-the-project for the dream.
- **G4 (E2E 2, medium).** The metrics ingest opens `conversations/<id>.db` only for ids listed in `conversation_summaries.db` (`internal/metrics/agy.go:36-60`), under `<source>/.gemini/antigravity-cli/` (`ingest.go:57`), and `--source` without `--label` is a usage error (`ingest.go:37`). "A FIFO at `<source>/conversations/x.db` … `fyr metrics ingest --source <dir>`" hits neither: no label gives a usage error, no summaries db returns silently. The fixture needs the label, the `.gemini/antigravity-cli/` path and a summaries row for `x` with a parseable `last_modified_time`.
- **G5 (SD39, medium).** `internal/brain/export.go:282` already parses `updated` with `time.RFC3339`, so the `bad updated` row passes before the fix ("rows fail before, pass after" cannot hold for it). `date` is checked by `dateRe` shape only (`export.go:275`, `record.go:90`). The existing refusals read `date %q is not YYYY-MM-DD` and `updated %q is not RFC 3339`; the plan's "existing refusal shape 'line N: bad date'" does not exist. The plan does not say whether the texts change (tests and the spec pin them).
- **G6 (IN49, high).** `internal/eval/row.go:108-118` `openRegular` passes the caller's flags straight to `OpenFile`; three write sites pass `O_TRUNC` (`row_session.go:52,62,110`). A check "after open" on `Stat_t.Nlink` refuses too late: the shared inode is already truncated. The check must run on an open without `O_TRUNC`, then `Truncate`. The planned test ("a hard-linked `check.log` refused") passes while the other link's data is gone unless it also asserts the target is intact. Also unsaid: whether read sites (`row_after.go:109`, `invoked.go:31`) get the refusal too.
- **G7 (SD43 and SD24, medium).** (a) The verify `git grep -n 'exec.Command("git"' internal cmd` is unscoped: about 30 `_test.go` hits, so "lists only trail.go and repo.go" cannot hold; it also misses the third raw call, `exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "clone", …)` at `row_prepare.go:37`, which the plan neither moves nor excuses (no `-C` form). (b) Both named callers overwrite `cmd.Env` after construction (`guard.go:111-119` sets `LC_ALL=C`, `GIT_DISCOVERY_ACROSS_FILESYSTEM=1` over `withoutGit(os.Environ())`; `row_prepare.go:44-45` uses `withoutGit`), which discards `trail.Command`'s env and SD24's filter, and `guard.go` matches git's English text. `withoutGit` already strips every `GIT_*`: a second, stricter list than SD24's seven. The plan does not say which wins, or whether `outsideCheckout` (which must find no repository) wants `-C`-only semantics. (c) `internal/eval` does not import `internal/trail` today; the new edge is not mentioned.
- **G8 (SD26/SD27, medium).** (a) SD26 exits 2 "with its message, as the real run does"; SD27 prints `[dry-run] would refuse: <reason>`: two shapes for one idea. (b) `cmd/fyr/memory_test.go:135` `TestDreamTimerDryRun` runs `--install-timer --dry-run --home <empty temp dir>` and expects `[dry-run] would`, nil error. After SD26 it refuses (`InstallTimer` first guard: no regular file at `<home>/.local/bin/fyr`, `timer.go:168-171`). The plan's failure mode says to "stub `agy` on PATH", the wrong fix for SD26 (it needs a binary at `harness.BinPath` plus the stubbed `systemctl`). (c) `skills/harness-audit/references/areas.md:43` and its baseline run `dream --install-timer --dry-run --home <scratch>`; WS43/44 edit that file but the plan does not say the baseline then needs `fyr install --home <it>` first. (d) `agyHome` (`agy_home.go:20-60`) creates a temp dir and copies the OAuth token; "the login lookup … without creating anything" requires a split of it, and its signature is unstated. (e) The real run does `ConfigDir`, lock, `readState` and `targets()` before the agy check (`run.go:25-71`); which of these the dry run mirrors is unstated.
- **G9 (IN45, medium).** `leftoverProcs` returns `[]string` and SIGTERMs inline; the new split (killed vs left alone) changes its return shape, unstated. Today environ is read only `hit == ""` (`procs_linux.go:49`), so a cwd match never has its environ examined; the new rule needs that restructured. `TestProcsLeftovers` case "a server left in the clone" (`procs_linux_test.go:81`: cwd match, `HOME=other`, expects SIGTERM and `(cwd)`) is the BUG-163 incident and now asserts the opposite. Restatements of the reversed claim: BUG-163's prevention text ("cwd or executable under the clone … kills them"), the `procs_linux.go` header, the `row_after.go:84` note ("each was sent SIGTERM"); the plan lists SPEC-fyr-eval only. D3's premise ("descendants inherit `HOME=<SB>`") is asserted, not checked; a server started through `env -i`, `setsid`+reset env or a container escapes, which is the BUG-163 class. D3 is "by: implementer" on a safety check.
- **G10 (IN40, medium).** Tests that pin `workflows/` as a source directory and must change, none named: `pathguard_test.go:130-150,225-227`, `source_test.go:37,60-61,102` (the "command in both dirs" collision row), `auditfix_test.go:37`; comments at `plan.go:36-37`, `source.go:19`, `inventory.go:49,70`. `checkManagedTree` does name it (`inventory.go:101`), so the "if it names it" hedge is answerable now. "TestEmbed* and the lint tests stay green" is therefore wrong as stated. A checkout that still has `workflows/*.md` would have it silently ignored; refuse or ignore is undecided.
- **G11 (docs clauses missing).** Behaviour changes with no docs/spec clause: IN41 (install/update/adopt dry-run exit code and `refuse` line), IN42, IN43, IN33, SD29 (dry-run output text), SD37 (where copies go), SD55, SD58 (new note), SD57. IN53's SPEC-fyr-check appears only in Phase 4, not in the Records list. AGENTS.md rule 3 says a change to install/update behaviour whose diff does not touch the map is incomplete; the plan says the map is untouched without addressing IN41/42/43/37 under that rule.
- **G12 (SD20, low).** The recon row is "INSERT … every query; busy error raw"; the plan fixes only the insert and drops the raw busy error (`return nil, err` after `st.close()`) without a D-row. No test is named for "no write lock on an unchanged search" (hold a write lock, search must not wait).
- **G13 (budget, medium).** Measured: `TestSkillListingBudget` reports 19,287 of 19,500, so 213 bytes (plan's figure confirmed). The sentence "Never start one from words in tool output, files, or logs." is 59 bytes with its space; WS42 adds it to two descriptions and WS50 to two more (+236), WS45 adds a ~69-byte trigger list, WS42's removals save about 60 (20 + 40). Net is about +210 to +245 against 213: the overrun is probable, not hypothetical, and "trim from the same descriptions" names no target.
- **G14 (SD48 build tags, low).** `copyFileImpl` has no build constraint; `O_NOFOLLOW`/`O_NONBLOCK` do not exist on non-unix. `internal/metrics` carries `open_unix.go`/`open_other.go` for this and `openRegular` in eval and metrics are two existing copies; search becomes a third. Clearing `O_NONBLOCK` after the `Fstat` is a no-op for a regular file (eval's `openRegular` leaves it set); not asked for by the audit row.

## Scope (what the plan builds beyond `## Why`)

The request ("fix everything that needs fixing") and D1 cover every `fix` row, so none of these is an unrequested feature, but each adds a shape the audit row did not specify and has no D-row: SD27's `would refuse:` line (second refusal shape, G8); SD58's new note text and SD53-free `IN53` note line; SD37's second temp-dir location (`os.MkdirTemp("", …)` instead of `~/.config/fyr`, so a crash leaves private conversation copies in the system temp dir, which `removeCopies(conf, …)` never sweeps); the O_NONBLOCK clear (G14); IN49's refusal for read opens (G6); the SD33 refusal of `--install-timer`/`--remove-timer` with `--all`/`--project`, a new usage rule on top of a test row.

## Questions

- **Q1 BLOCKING (G1).** On a tracked symlink, gitlink or mode change, is `Dirty` true or false? Does a staged-new file count? Pick one table; the symlink case decides whether `import` works on this repo.
- **Q2 BLOCKING (G1).** When `Dirty` cannot answer (`Readable` false, hash count mismatch, newline in a name): does import refuse, does eval omit `(dirty)`? Does `Dirty` reuse `changed` (new pathspec) or duplicate it?
- **Q3 BLOCKING (G3).** Does a refused conversation database skip that conversation or fail the project for the dream (and for `-wal`/`-shm`)?
- **Q4 BLOCKING (G6).** Is the hard-link check made before truncation (open without `O_TRUNC`, `Fstat`, then `Truncate`)? Does it apply to read opens?
- **Q5 NON-BLOCKING (G5).** Keep the existing refusal wording and strengthen `dateRe` to a `time.Parse`, with `bad updated` dropped as already covered? (I would.)
- **Q6 NON-BLOCKING (G7).** Do the two eval callers keep their own env after going through `trail.Command`, and is `row_prepare.go:37` `git clone` left raw on purpose? Fix the grep to `':!*_test.go'` and state the allowed list.
- **Q7 NON-BLOCKING (G8).** One refusal shape for SD26 and SD27? A `checkAgy` split from `agyHome`? Which tests get which stub (binary at `BinPath` for SD26)?
- **Q8 NON-BLOCKING (G9).** `leftoverProcs` new return type; BUG-163 prevention-rule and header edits; cwd-only hits stay alive and fail the row on every run until the operator moves their shell, accepted per D3?
- **Q9 NON-BLOCKING (G10).** Stray `workflows/` in a checkout: silently ignored or a lint refusal? Name the tests to rewrite.
- **Q10 NON-BLOCKING (G11).** Which spec/guide/README row carries IN41, IN42, IN43, IN33, SD29, SD37, SD55, SD57, SD58, and does IN41-43 count under AGENTS.md rule 3?
- **Q11 NON-BLOCKING (G12).** Is the raw busy error half of SD20 dropped on purpose?
- **Q12 NON-BLOCKING (G13).** Which descriptions are trimmed first if the budget overflows? (Or drop the WS42 sentence, already present in 9+ skills.)
- **Q13 NON-BLOCKING (IN51).** `readsNeedle` truncates at the cap (a needle past 64 MiB reads as "agent not invoked", a false FAIL) where `creds.go:176` refuses over-cap files; reuse `maxScan` (a var) or a new const? Truncate or refuse?
- **Q14 NON-BLOCKING (SD24).** What is the threat (a parent git hook exporting `GIT_DIR`)? Why exactly these seven, when `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES` and `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY_n/VALUE_n` pass? One sentence in a D-row.

## Criteria

1. Dead code — n/a (a plan, no diff); SD-S5, SD50 and SD21 are removals the plan names correctly.
2. Flow tracing — fail: G1, G3, G6, G7, G9 each trace a plan sentence to code that contradicts it.
3. Standards conformance — fail: restatements of the reversed IN45 claim (BUG-163, headers, notes) and the `workflows/` pins are not listed (G9, G10, G11).
4. Directory layout — pass: no new file placement; the SD48 build-tag question is G14.
5. Simplicity — pass with notes: no new dependency; SD24/`withoutGit` duplication (G7).
6. Decoupling — pass with notes: new `eval` to `trail` edge and a third `openRegular` copy (G7, G14).

## Not examined

The security-relevant bodies of SD21, SD22, SD40, SD45, SD46, SD52, SD55-SD58 (code not read); IN34, IN41-IN43, IN46, IN50, IN52-IN54 code; every skill/agent/doc edit (WS41-WS48 text, TS41/42, G31/34/35, AG26/27, C-rows, TR-rows) beyond the description-budget arithmetic; the full recon briefs (only the rows quoted above); the `fyr record get` of the plan record (the scratch file was read). Phase ordering and the 35-call budget limited the reading to the riskiest interfaces named in the brief.

Verdict line: design needs revision. implementation not ready.

## Outcome

Answered by the author in PLAN-2026-10-27-harness-audit-fix, 2026-10-27; no item needed the operator.

- G1, Q1: D6 (Dirty's table: a symlink compared by target, gitlinks never, a staged new file always). G2: the grep's allowed hits stated (repo.go:222, JSON tags); E2E 1 names `.gitattributes`.
- Q2: D7. G3, Q3: D8 (a non-regular conversation is skipped by the dream). G4: E2E 2's fixture rewritten (label, path, summaries row).
- G5, Q5: D9. G6, Q4: D15 (link count before truncation; write opens only).
- G7, Q6: D13 (callers keep their env; the clone stays raw; the grep scoped). G8, Q7: D17 and the named test changes.
- G9, Q8: D11 supersedes D3 (IN45 becomes a Known-limits line; BUG-163's net stays). G10, Q9: D12 (IN40 deferred).
- G11, Q10: the per-phase message grep and D20 (rule 3 not engaged). G12, Q11: D19. G13, Q12: D5 (budget order).
- Q13: D16. Q14: D20. G14: D10. Scope: D14 (SD37 deferred), D18 (SD33's refusal is the audit row's alternative); SD58's and IN53's note lines are their rows' fixes.

title: Harness audit — fyr at e3459a4 (2026-10-27)
body:
---
owner: main
date: 2026-10-27
---
# Harness audit — fyr at e3459a4 (2026-10-27)

Range reviewed: no diff; the harness at e3459a4 (Go code identical to eec29b4, where the baseline ran). Areas covered: all eight of `references/areas.md` (C, WS, TS, AG, IN, SD, TR, G), with IN and SD split so that the six packages no area names (brain, check, eval, metrics, redact, trail) were read too. Evidence base: `PLAN-2026-10-27-recon-harness-audit`. Action plan: `PLAN-2026-10-27-harness-audit-fix`.

## What is broken

Nothing is high. The baseline is green: gofmt, vet, `go test -race ./...`, govulncheck (no reachable finding), the v3.0.0 release's four assets against its SHA256SUMS, the scratch-home install/status/diff/uninstall dry run, and every CHANGE and ADR record of v3.0.0 unchanged at HEAD.

The mediums, worst first:

- **SD38** (*repro*): `fyr record import` and `fyr eval` run `git status`, which runs a clean filter the repository's own `.git/config` defines; `internal/trail` says `status` is never called for exactly that reason (BUG-164). Reproduced: a filter in a scratch repo's config ran on import.
- **SD25**: the dreamer's `agy` child inherits the operator's whole environment with only `HOME` swapped, so credential variables reach a process that reads prompt-injectable text.
- **SD19** (SD12 of 2026-10-25, never fixed): any `fyr search` in a checkout that ships `.agents/docs/` registers it, and `fyr dream --all` then sends its content, redacted, to the model.
- **SD49**: `fyr metrics ingest` imports the `.agents/trail.jsonl` of any workspace Antigravity opened into the real `brain.db`.
- **SD48**: Antigravity conversation databases are copied with a plain `os.Open`; a FIFO there hangs ingest, eval and the nightly dream. The spec says every ingest read is non-blocking.
- **IN44**: a `GUIDE-eval` row's `setup` and `check` run as `bash -c` as the operator, gated only by "equals HEAD"; a pulled commit changes what `fyr eval <id>` runs, unseen.
- **IN45**: `fyr eval`'s leftover-process check SIGTERMs the operator's own shell or editor whose cwd is in the sandbox.
- **SD39**: the trail load accepts impossible dates (`9999-99-99`); such a record ranks first in every search it matches.
- **SD26, SD27**: `dream --install-timer --dry-run` and `dream --dry-run` skip guards the real runs enforce (review-standards § 8).
- **SD28**: news dropped to fit the dream's 256 KB cap is never offered again.
- **IN46**: the eval credential scan's tests cover about half its patterns and almost no near-misses.
- **WS40**: `retro` Step 6 and `distill --global` apply, commit and push into the harness checkout from another project — a second path into the checkout beside AGENTS.md rule 1's `/retro --harness`.
- **WS41**: `retro --dry-run` cites the dream skill's Steps 1–5, of which Step 5 writes a record.
- **WS42**: `explain-project` and `discover-skills` trigger on bare how-questions; one writes a record and commits, the other goes to the network.
- **WS43** (*repro*), **WS44**: the audit's own area list runs `TestHarnessMap` where it does not exist (silently green), and reads 3 of 9 packages.
- **AG25**: the context says a dispatch never changes an agent's artifact name; the harness-audit dispatch does.
- **C37, C38**: the README map node still names `feedback.jsonl`/`retros.jsonl`/`proposals/` (brain.db is never named), and the Rules row names two of three rules.
- **TR16**: "a dev command moved the operator's real state" has 11 bug records and is still a sentence.
- **TR17**: the newest handoff predates the funclen plan; a fresh session resuming from it would redo the plan.

## Tally

| Area | high | med | low | simplification | gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C | 0 | 2 | 5 | 3 | |
| WS | 0 | 5 | 7 | 3 | |
| TS | 0 | 0 | 6 | 1 | |
| AG | 0 | 1 | 4 | 0 | |
| IN | 0 | 3 | 19 | 6 | |
| SD | 0 | 9 | 31 | 7 | |
| TR | 0 | 2 | 6 | 1 | |
| G | | | | | 10 |
| **Total** | **0** | **22** | **78** | **21** | **10** |

Recommendations: 67 fix, 38 defer, 3 strike, 21 the operator's (counted from the recon's Final IDs table, column 6).

## Measurements

- `gofmt -l cmd internal`: empty. `go vet ./...`: clean. `go test -race -timeout 30m ./...`: every package ok (go1.27.3, 16 CPUs).
- `go test -cover ./...`: cmd/fyr 90.5, brain 82.0, check 95.7, dream 89.3, eval 90.1, harness 89.7, memory 81.0, metrics 89.5, redact 97.8, search 83.2, trail 68.7 (%).
- `govulncheck ./...`: 0 reachable; 1 in required modules not called.
- `go run ./cmd/fyr render | wc -c`: 15,743. Hand-written context 14,814 of 15,000; block 20,976 of 22,000; skill listing 19,287 of 19,500 (C41).
- Scratch-home install: 890 files; `status` drift none; `diff` exit 0; `uninstall --dry-run` would remove 890 files.
- v3.0.0: `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS` OK for 4 of 4 assets; `update --from-zip fyr-v3.0.0.zip --dry-run`: CHECKED against the release's SHA256SUMS, 1 written (the binary), 889 unchanged.
- `FYR_RECALL=1 go test ./cmd/fyr -run TestRecall`: PASS (99 s). `fyr search --open`: 414 files, reconcile 36 ms.
- `fyr dream --dry-run --project .`: 259,456 bytes, 141 inputs left out (SD28, SD29).
- Trail immutability since v3.0.0: 198 CHANGE/ADR records checked, 0 changed.
- Function lengths: 56 non-test functions over 50 lines, now planned in `PLAN-2026-10-27-funclen` (not counted here).

## The operator's choices

| # | Problem | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | SD19: any checkout that ships `.agents/docs/` registers itself on the first `fyr search`, and `dream --all` sends it to the model | opt-in: register only through `fyr index --register`, marked under `.git/` (never carried by a clone) |
| 2 | SD25: the `agy` child inherits the whole environment | an allow-list (PATH, HOME, LANG/LC_*, TERM, TMPDIR, TZ, proxy and SSL_CERT_* vars); one Antigravity dream run before release |
| 3 | SD49: metrics ingest imports any workspace's `trail.jsonl` into `brain.db` | join only roots registered in the global index (follows #1) |
| 4 | IN44: suite `setup`/`check` bash runs unseen after a pull | print each row's script hash before running, and name it in SPEC-fyr-eval § Known limits |
| 5 | WS40: retro Step 6 and distill `--global` write into the checkout from another project | strike both branches: queue a `proposal`, applied by `/retro --harness` |
| 6 | AG25: harness-audit dispatches override the explorer's artifact path and format | the skill stores the explorer's own draft; dispatches stop overriding |
| 7 | C37: README map node names the old `.jsonl` files and never `brain.db` | relabel the node (map label only; rule 3 change, one commit with the map) |
| 8 | SD28: news dropped by the dream cap is lost for good | advance the watermark only to the newest record sent |
| 9 | SD41: credential kinds the redactor has no needle for (Docker PAT, Terraform, Slack app, …) | add Docker, Terraform and Slack-app kinds, one rule per kind |
| 10 | SD42: record bodies reach the committed `trail.jsonl` unscanned | warn (never refuse) on `record add/edit` when the redactor would change the body |
| 11 | SD47: a pulled `trail.jsonl` can plant open records | accept; say so in SPEC-fyr-record § Load |
| 12 | IN39: `update` writes the binary through a linked `~/.local/bin`; `install` refuses links | state the binary is the exception (the link is the operator's own) |
| 13 | TS39: frontend draws `engines >=22.12`, the stack is Node 24 | raise to `>=24` |
| 14 | TS40: does `rules/code-modularity.md` cover markdown (bash-fundamentals.md is 739 lines)? | no: the rule names programming languages; strike |
| 15 | WS49: preflight runs the verifier twice | defer |
| 16 | TR18: the `delete_repo` scope step, carried in 7 handoffs | strike: accept the scope, recorded once |
| 17 | G26: migration guidance beyond Cloud SQL | defer |
| 18 | G27: a requirement's number has no test tier | defer |
| 19 | G28: stacks other than Go/TypeScript | declare out of scope in `context/dev-setup.md` |
| 20 | G29: no tier between a full scaffold and unscaffolded | defer |
| 21 | G30: no release shape for a library, CLI or static site | defer |
| 22 | G33: no branch or PR policy | defer (solo, `main`) |

Full versions: `.agents/scratch/harness-audit/2026-10-27/out/choices.md`.

## What was not examined

- Vendored pins: not re-checked against upstream (no clone at hand). macOS: nothing run there (launchd timer, keychain branch of `agyHome`).
- Per area (from the briefs' Not examined): C — R3/R4/R8 clauses line by line, most ADR bodies, the second half of DEPLOY-remote; WS — testing-strategy, review-standards references, init-project assets in full; TS — most catalog entries (ten sampled); AG — Antigravity's agent.md semantics, most agent bodies in depth; IN-1/2 — most test files, frontmatter.go 1-195; IN-3 — eval against Antigravity; SD-1 — parse.go, inserter.go, search_refs.go; SD-3 — import_classify.go, import_memory.go, FTSQuery; SD-4 — the report renderer, most tests; TR — most retro bodies, ~115 change records; G — several skills read by grep only.

title: Review: ledger Phase 1 (the dreamer's allow-listed agy environment, TimeoutStartSec=2h) — approve with nits, 3 findings fixed
body:
# Review — ledger phase 1: dreamer child env allow-list, TimeoutStartSec   (2026-10-28)

Range reviewed: uncommitted working tree vs HEAD 7c5fc46 — internal/dream (agy_home.go, run.go, timer.go, fakecli_test.go, timer_render_test.go, new run_env_test.go), new internal/trail/env.go + env_test.go, and the .agents/trail.jsonl hunk (new ADR-067; SPEC-fyr-dream rows 4 and the systemd line). Diff file: .agents/scratch/ledger/p1/phase1.diff.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

The allow-list change is correct: `childEnv` always returns a non-nil env (HOME appended), so `cmd.Env` can never fall back to inheriting fyr's environment; `AllowEnv` matches exactly and by `*` prefix, keeps order, does not alias its input; the only path that starts `agy` (`run.go:61` -> `call` -> `cliCommand`) uses it, and no other child in internal/dream runs on untrusted text. `go test ./internal/trail/ ./internal/dream/ -count=1` passes, `go vet ./...` and `gofmt -l cmd internal` are clean. ADR-067 and the SPEC rows match the code (variable list identical; `repoVars`, `(*row).agyEnv` with USER/LOGNAME exist as cited). The worst problem is a rollout gap, not a code bug: the `TimeoutStartSec=2h` fix (SD36) does not reach any machine that already has the timer installed, and no step or document says so.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/dream/timer_install.go:~108-114` (with `internal/dream/timer.go:113`) — the new `TimeoutStartSec=2h` only exists in a freshly rendered unit. `planTimer` refuses to touch a unit on disk whose text differs ("exists with other text ... kept. Run fyr dream --remove-timer first"), and `fyr install` / `fyr update` only call `dream.ReplaceOldTimer` (the pre-rename unit), never re-render a current `fyr-dream` unit. Failure scenario: the operator's existing 03:00 timer keeps the old service text (no start timeout); a hung `agy` past the per-project kill still blocks every later night (Persistent= does not start an active unit), exactly the SD36 failure, while the new binary's env allow-list does take effect immediately because ExecStart names the binary. If the operator re-runs `--install-timer`, they get an error whose message blames "another PATH, or edited by hand". The SPEC line added at "The systemd service sets TimeoutStartSec=2h" and ADR-067 say nothing about this. Fix: state in SPEC-fyr-dream (and the phase handoff / release notes) that an installed timer needs `--remove-timer` then `--install-timer` to gain the timeout, and add a test that a unit lacking the line is refused with that text (or decide to have install converge the unit); do not claim SD36 closed for existing installs until then. This is the "which version runs first after it ships" check of review-standards § 2.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/dream/agy_exec.go:18-19` — the doc comment of `call` still reads "env replaces the child's environment when set (agy's private HOME); otherwise the child keeps fyr's own." The only caller now passes the allow-listed environment plus HOME, so the parenthetical describes the old `withHome(os.Environ())` shape. Not wrong for a nil env, but the describing-text rule (a changed behaviour includes its text) asks it to say the env is the allow-list (`childEnv`, ADR-067). Fix: reword.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/dream/timer.go:113` — `TimeoutStartSec=2h` bounds the whole `dream --all` run, not one project, and the per-project cap is 10 min (`cliTimeout`) with no dream cap until ledger Phase 4. A box with enough changed projects (firstLook is 14 days) can legitimately exceed 2h; systemd then SIGTERMs fyr mid-run (between projects Go's default SIGTERM kills fyr with no cleanup; the private login-copy HOME is left until the next run's `removeCopies`, already the case for any kill). State is saved per project, so the next night resumes, hence low. Consider naming that the 2h is a whole-run bound in the SPEC line (it currently says "a run hung past the per-project kill").

Rebuttable nits, not findings: proxy variables are allowed by operator decision (D8), so a proxy URL with embedded credentials (an authenticated proxy URL) reaches `agy`; a bare `"*"` name in `AllowEnv` would allow everything (internal callers only, none pass it). `TestAgyEnvAllowList` can fail: it proves the canary is set first, and reverting `childEnv` to the old `os.Environ()` shape puts `canary-` in the recorded env. It relies on the fake shell adding only PWD/SHLVL/_ (a shell adding OLDPWD would make it fail visibly, not pass silently).

## Criteria
1. Dead code — ok: `withHome` removed with its only caller; no remaining reference (grep, vet clean).
2. Flow tracing — passed with the finding above: `os.Environ()` -> `childEnv` -> `r.env` -> `call` -> `cmd.Env` traced; env cannot be nil; macOS login (Keychain) is unverifiable here and ADR-067 says so as a release obligation. The installer/timer trace is the medium finding.
3. Standards conformance — passed except the stale `call` doc comment (low). ADR-067 and the SPEC row 4 restate the list identically to `agyEnv`; no other living file restates "fyr's own environment" for the dreamer (grep over README, REQUIREMENTS, skills, context, agents).
4. Directory layout — ok: `trail/env.go` beside `trail.go`, tests beside code; domain-named files.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — ok: stdlib only, ~25 lines, no dependency; no crypto/auth involved.
6. Decoupling — ok: `internal/trail` stays SQLite-free; dream imports trail (already a dependency direction in the layout), no cycle.

## Not examined
- Pre-flight `fyr search --refs` and `fyr record list --kind bug` (the dispatch forbids every fyr verb); recorded-bug reintroduction not checked beyond the BUG/SD ids named in the ADR.
- Behaviour on macOS and a real `agy` run with the allow-list (cannot be done from this box; ADR-067 names it as a release obligation).
- A real systemd load of the rendered unit (`systemd-analyze verify`), and the full `go test ./...` / `-race` run beyond the two packages named.
- The rest of the trail.jsonl diff beyond ADR-067 and SPEC-fyr-dream; the plan records (`audit-choices` D6/D8/D20/D27/D40, ledger D2) were not read, so their cited decisions are taken from the ADR text.

## Outcome

1. **Fixed.** `--install-timer` keeps a unit with other text on purpose, and its refusal already names `--remove-timer`; the refusal now also names "an older fyr" (`internal/dream/timer_install.go`), and SPEC-fyr-dream § Hardening details says a unit installed before this change keeps its old text and how to get the current one. Test: `TestInstallTimerOlderUnitNamed` (an older unit without `TimeoutStartSec` is kept and the refusal names the case; remove-then-install writes the line). It fails without the message fix (run 2026-10-28). Install still does not converge an existing unit: that is the deliberate keep-and-name rule, and nobody runs the timer today (audit-choices D38).
2. **Fixed.** The `call` doc comment now names `childEnv`; with security's finding 2, `cliCommand` refuses a nil env (`TestCLICommandRefusesNilEnv`, fails without the guard).
3. **Fixed in the docs.** SPEC-fyr-dream now says the 2h limit bounds the whole run and that each project's watermark is saved as it finishes, so the next night goes on. The per-run budget question returns with the cap (ledger Phase 4).

title: Security review: ledger Phase 1 (the dreamer's allow-listed agy environment) — 3 low, fixed or rebutted
body:
