Docs lens: spec2 step 3, step 6, the table row and the ADR agree with the code on drop order, the three wordings (`dropped to fit...`, `too big for the...`, `dropped to fit...; not sent again`) and the label tie-break. Grep for stale "oldest first" restatements again found none outside the unrelated retro skill.

## Not examined (round 2)
- `-race` suite (run elsewhere); a full gocyclo measurement; the effect of identical labels (all feedback inputs are labelled `feedback.jsonl`) on tie order beyond input order, which is stable but was not tested with real feedback files.

## Outcome

- Round 1, finding 1 (high, the stall on ties): fixed. A drop holds `Through` back only while an input strictly older than it is kept; an input of the oldest time left is named `(dropped to fit the <n> KB cap; not sent again)`; `newer` breaks a same-kind tie by label. Tests that fail without the fix: `TestFitTieGroupNeverStalls`, `TestFitTieAboveOlderNeverStalls` (through `sendRuns`, which fails a run whose watermark does not move) and `TestFitUntimedDatedHoldsNothing`; the label-order mutation fails `TestFitTieGroupNeverStalls`. The loss of a split group's tail is accepted in ADR-069 and ledger D17 (a time-and-label cursor, not built).
- Round 1, finding 2 (low, the false "too big" name): fixed, the oldest-time wording above, in code, `TestFitLastDatedDoesNotHoldWatermark`, SPEC-fyr-dream and ADR-069.
- Round 1, finding 3 (low, "may be sent again"): fixed in SPEC-fyr-dream step 6 and ADR-069's consequences.
- Round 2, the complexity of `datedVictim` (low): fixed. The two newest-of scans go through `newerOf`, which leaves `datedVictim` at about 9. The mutation that this exposed (the too-big pick ignoring order) survived the tests, so `TestFitTooBigNewestFirst` was added, and it now fails under that mutation.
- ADR-069 was amended before its first commit. It had been stored this session and was never published.

title: Review — cold read of ledger Phase 4a (fyr help for a person) (2026-10-28)
body:
# Review — ledger Phase 4a cold read (fyr help for a person)   (2026-10-28)

Range reviewed: the plan record PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger (.agents/scratch/ledger/p4a/plan.body): items 81, 82, § Interfaces "Phase 4a", § Each phase's checkpoint, "### Phase 4a" boxes, D18-D20, "Rejected (Phase 4a)"; against cmd/fyr (main.go, run_dispatch.go, ctx_verbs.go, check.go, record.go, eval.go, verb_*.go, tests), internal/check/docs.go, README.md 36-56. Code read at HEAD 94c9db1 (working tree has only .agents/trail.jsonl modified).

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES (design needs revision; implementation not ready)

The worst problem: the plan says "every existing test that greps `usage: fyr <verb>` or `usage` passes unchanged" and that the unknown-verb path stops printing the page, but at least two existing tests pin exactly what the plan removes, and the plan lists neither for change. Beyond that, the usage-error box names no mechanism for 33 `exitCode(2)` sites (some of which are not usage errors), and does not say that Go's default `flag` usage printing must be switched off. Item 82 is already done and checks out.

## Findings (gaps)

1. **[high / high] Tests the plan says "pass unchanged" that cannot.**
   - `cmd/fyr/auditfix_test.go:41` (TestUnknownCommandExits2OnTheWriter) requires `"Commands:"` in an unknown-command output. D19 (4) and the usage-error box say an unknown verb never prints the page. The test must change; the box's must-fail ("the old error path fails the unknown-verb row") would be proved by a row in help_test.go, while this test goes red unmentioned.
   - `cmd/fyr/check_test.go:88-91` pins `memory frob` to the EXACT string `"usage: fyr memory add --type T --name SLUG --description TEXT (body on stdin) | fyr memory show\n"` (equality, line 89). The new error adds `run 'fyr help memory' for its flags`, and "one line per subverb" makes the synopsis two lines. Line 94 relies on `got == memoryUsage` to prove a subverb "reaches its case". Both must be rewritten (e.g. prefix/contains plus a different probe); the plan says nothing.
   - `cmd/fyr/record_arms_test.go:47` requires `strings.HasPrefix(out, "usage: ")` for four record cases (`edit`, `list x`, `import a b`, `import a --global`). The usage-error box says each case is asserted with "all three parts" including the reason line, but these four have NO reason line today (record.go:83 prints `recordUsage` first). Decide: for a case with no reason, the output starts with the synopsis (keeps this test), and the "three parts" table must say so.
   - `cmd/fyr/usage_test.go:106` (`list -h` expects `-home` in stdout) will pass only because the last page line `Every command takes --home DIR ...` contains `-home` as a substring of `--home`. Pass by accident; name it.
   - `cmd/fyr/metrics_test.go:196-204` requires metrics' usage-error output to name `--until` (report) and `--context-target`. The metrics synopsis text must carry every flag of every subverb; test (c) checks only the `Flags:` section, so a synopsis dropping them is not caught by the new tests but is by this old one. Today's metrics bare-verb message is `fyr metrics: ingest | show | report | export FILE` (verb_metrics.go:44), not `usage: fyr metrics`: the "begins `usage: fyr <verb>`" claim (§ Interfaces) is a change, not a keep.

2. **[high / high] Usage-error mechanism is undecided; scope edge wrong.** 33 `exitCode(2)` sites exist (grep `exitCode(2)` in cmd/fyr, non-test). The box lists categories (unknown flag, stray argument, missing/unknown subverb, missing positional) but § Interfaces says "every usage error". Not decided: (a) whether `search --limit 99`, `metrics show --context-target 0`, `--from-zip belongs to update` (run_dispatch.go:33), `--from-zip needs a file` (:124), `index --register --global` (verb_index_register.go:26), `dream --install-timer and --remove-timer, not both` (verb_dream.go:21), `eval --list takes no row` get the synopsis tail; (b) a central wrapper cannot be used: `exitCode(2)` is also `update --check` "behind" (update_checkout.go:33, :80) and eval's "refusal before any row ran" (eval.go:95) — neither is a usage error and neither must print a synopsis; (c) the mechanism: per-site edits across ~8 files, or a `usageErr(c, reason)` helper. Two implementers build different things. BLOCKING.

3. **[medium / high] Go's default flag usage must be suppressed and the plan never says so.** `go run ./cmd/fyr list --no-such-flag` today prints `flag provided but not defined: -no-such-flag` then `Usage of list:` plus the `-home string ...` defaults (run_dispatch.go:68-72 comment "the flag package has named the flag"; newCtx ctx_verbs.go:129 `SetOutput(out)` with no `SetUsage`). The plan's usage error (reason, synopsis, hint) needs `c.fs.SetUsage(func(){})` (or equivalent) in `newCtx`, and the same applies to `-h`, where the FlagSet prints the defaults before `Parse` returns `ErrHelp` — the verb page must replace that, not follow it. Also `newCtx` is called by `vocabulary()` with `io.Discard` (check.go:50) and by tests; the SetUsage change must hold there. BLOCKING-adjacent; I mark it NON-BLOCKING only because the intent is clear, but the failing probe (`Usage of list:` still printed above the synopsis) is the first thing a test would catch.

4. **[medium / high] Restatements of "see fyr help" / "the order `fyr help` lists them" not in the plan.** `internal/search/search.go:54,62,78,80` (four usage errors ending `; see fyr help`), `internal/search/parse.go:249` ("in the order `fyr help` lists them" — the kinds list), `cmd/fyr/ctx_verbs.go:93` (`record --status` usage: "(per kind; see fyr help)"), `skills/harness-audit/references/areas.md:37` ("the verb table against the usage text"). After the change the short page lists no kinds or statuses; `fyr help search` / `fyr help record` do (if the fact audit puts them there). The consumers list in § Interfaces ("Consumers moved in the same commit") names none of these. `internal/search` is a different package from cmd/fyr; changing its error strings has its own tests (grep `see fyr help` in internal/search/*_test.go was not run). Decide: point them to `fyr help search` or drop the clause.

5. **[medium / high] The mock is cited but not in the plan.** § Interfaces: "The mock is D19 (1)". D19 (1) holds only prose. The title line, the per-verb phrases, group heading format, column width, the verb-page flag line format and whether a flagless verb prints `Flags:` (list, status, diff, render, version, check have none; test (c) "names exactly the FlagSet minus home and repo" is ambiguous for the empty set) are not written anywhere a fresh reader can open. A first pass can be built, but the final operator box ("reads `fyr`, `fyr help record`, `fyr record drop`") then decides the text, with no baseline. NON-BLOCKING (implementer writes it), but a named gap.

6. **[medium / medium] `--<name> <ARG>` source undefined.** The flags are "generated from the FlagSet". `flag.UnquoteUsage` yields `string`/`int` for flags whose usage has no backtick (none do today; ctx_verbs.go usage strings). So `<ARG>` is either `<string>` (useless) or needs hand text per flag, or backticks added to ~25 usage strings, which the plan allows ("may be shortened") but does not state. Also bool flags: print no `<ARG>`. Decide.

7. **[medium / high] `help` routing edge cases unstated.** run_dispatch.go:16 routes `help`/`-h`/`--help` only as `args[0]`, ignoring the rest (`fyr -h foo` prints the page today). Undecided: `fyr -h record` / `fyr --help record`; `fyr help record --home X` (the global flags are advertised on the last line of every page, yet `help <verb> <more>` is an exit-2 usage error, and help is routed before any FlagSet, so `--home X` counts as `<more>`); `fyr help help`; `fyr help sync -h`. `fyr update -h --from-zip x`: `reorder` + Parse returns ErrHelp first, fine. What help's own usage-error prints (test (e) asserts only exit 2) is not given. NON-BLOCKING each; two implementers differ on `help record --home X`.

8. **[medium / medium] Verb/subverb page coverage vs the `check` vocabulary.** `vocabulary()` (check.go:47) already has `help` with flags home/repo/help and no Subverbs, and docs.go:55 only validates subverbs when `Subverbs != nil`, so `fyr help record` in a doc should produce no finding; the plan says the vocabulary changes ("`fyr help <verb>` in a doc is a known form"). I found no change needed, so the plan asserts a vocabulary edit it may not need; the box's check is the right gate (the two `fyr check` outputs diffed). Say "if needed". Also `fyr check`'s README scan reads the new README:56 text; a new doc sentence with `fyr help <verb>`: `<verb>` is not a `wordRe` word? Not verified.

9. **[medium / medium] Test gaps: the ten-line cap and the synopsis prefix are pinned by nothing.** Tests (a)-(f) check width, verb set, flag set, byte-identical output, exit codes and the sync alias. Not tested: at most 10 description lines (D19 2), every synopsis begins `usage: fyr <verb>` (the claim § Interfaces relies on for existing tests), the page's last line, the group headings, that a usage error's synopsis equals the verb page's first lines ("one source"). The plan claims none as covered, but names them as requirements; add a test or drop the claim.

10. **[medium / medium] Fact audit sizing and wording.** D20's "every sentence of today's `usage` const" is ~70 very long lines (main.go:35-~110), most of them multi-fact (the `update` line has ~8 facts; `index --register` ~10; `dream --all` ~8; `eval` ~10). Moving a fact into a spec means `fyr record edit <SPEC> --body` on up to 10 records; each edit must keep the spec's tests/checks (`fyr check` verifies specs' code paths and requirement `enforced by:` — editing a spec record changes its "carrying commit" and may trip the spec-staleness rule in check, which the box doesn't mention). Also D20 sends the facts of install/update/uninstall/adopt/status/diff/list/render/version to "README § Daily commands, or DEPLOY-remote": but README's table is one row each, ~1-3 sentences, and AGENTS.md rule 6 of this repo forbids restating the delivery claim outside `SPEC-fyr-delivery`; `update`'s and `--from-zip`'s facts are exactly what rule 6 says has one home. The audit must route those to the spec/DEPLOY-remote, not README prose; the plan does not mention rule 6. Also `check` has a spec (SPEC-fyr-check), `eval` (SPEC-fyr-eval), `search` (SPEC-fyr-search), `memory` (SPEC-fyr-memory?) - D20 lists only verbs with no spec; whether `index`, `list`, `version` have specs is unchecked.

11. **[low / high] REQUIREMENTS not cited.** R10 (one behaviour on every place): the pages live in the binary so a release binary, zip and checkout print the same; the plan states this reasoning in D19 (3) but cites no R-item. R4 (stdlib only) is only echoed by "stdlib only". No requirement is violated. Cite R10 and R4 in D19.

12. **[low / medium] Undefined terms.** "IN15"/"IN16" (finding IDs, defined only by § Terms' reference to the audit's records; a naive reader gets "IN binary and installer" but not the rows), "the writer" (the `out io.Writer` handed to `run`; stdout in production, which is why usage errors go to stdout), "D14 of fyr-check", "short page"/"verb page" (defined in § Interfaces, fine), "hint line". "Go's default" for `-h` is explained only in Rejected.

## Scope (question 2)

What the request (item 81: "fyr help is written for a model, not a person") did not name, and who asked for it:
- `fyr help <verb>` / `<verb> -h|--help` as a second surface: D19 (2), operator-approved ("Go all approved"). OK.
- Usage-error rewrite (synopsis + hint): D19 (4), approved. OK. But the extent ("every usage error") is the plan's, not the approval's (the table row said what it prints, not for which sites).
- The fact audit and moving facts into specs (D20): "by: implementer, from D19 (3)'s risk" — not asked for by the operator; it is protective and arguably required, but it is scope: editing SPEC/README/DEPLOY records beyond cmd/fyr. Flagged as unrequested.
- Hard 79-column limit with a width test (D19 1, operator-approved).
- A FlagSet-generated flag list with `--home/--repo` excluded: derived, no second shape.
- `fyr check` vocabulary edit: asserted, perhaps unnecessary (finding 8).
Nothing configurable was added.

## Readiness (question 3): questions I would have to ask

1. BLOCKING — Which of the 33 exit-2 sites get the synopsis, and by what mechanism (finding 2)? How are `update --check` and `eval`'s refusal exit 2 kept free of it?
2. BLOCKING — For usage errors with no reason today (record/memory/adopt/eval bare verbs, metrics bare verb), is a reason line invented? The `record_arms_test.go:47` HasPrefix `usage: ` says no; the box's "all three parts" says yes (finding 1).
3. BLOCKING — Who edits `auditfix_test.go:41` and `check_test.go:88-94`, and to what (they contradict the plan's "pass unchanged")? An implementer who obeys "unchanged" is stuck; one who edits chooses freely.
4. NON-BLOCKING — Default usage printing off via SetUsage (finding 3): a reasonable implementer does it.
5. NON-BLOCKING — The `<ARG>` source and flagless-verb `Flags:` rendering (finding 6, 5).
6. NON-BLOCKING — `help record --home X`, `fyr -h record`, `help help` (finding 7).
7. NON-BLOCKING — Whether the `internal/search` `; see fyr help` strings change (finding 4); the plan's "restatements in the same commit" rule makes this one a required edit, so an implementer who greps finds it; one who does not ships a stale pointer.
8. NON-BLOCKING — The static page text itself (title line, phrases, group look): the operator box reviews it.
9. NON-BLOCKING — Whether the fact audit's moved facts may edit `SPEC-fyr-*` records and keep `fyr check`'s spec rules quiet (finding 10).

## Sizing (question 4)

One session can build the pages (help_text.go as data, help.go routing and rendering, about 150-250 lines of code, plus 14 verb pages of ~15 lines each; all fine against the 600-line and 50-line-function caps if the text is data and the renderer is split into small functions). It cannot reliably also: complete a per-sentence audit of ~70 multi-fact lines with up to ten record edits, reroute 33 usage-error sites over ~8 files, rewrite 5-6 existing tests, run the full race suite (13 min on a one-CPU box) twice with a review round, and hold an operator reading. That is two sessions' work if the usage-error scope is "every usage error", one if limited to the four listed categories at the dispatch points in run_dispatch.go/parse plus the six subverb sites. This counts as a gap; suggest splitting the fact audit (docs) from the code, or fixing the usage-error scope to the listed sites.

## Item 82 (check)

Plan evidence: the `DEPLOY-remote` edit is `grep -cw sh-agent`, probed on four lines (4 vs 2). Consistent with the stored record claim; I did not re-fetch the record body (not examined).

## Criteria

1. Dead code — n/a (plan review). One risk: the consts `recordUsage`, the memory/adopt/eval usage strings, and `usage` must all be deleted in the same commit ("one source"); the plan names only `usage`.
2. Flow tracing — fail: finding 1-3 (callers/tests not updated; exit-2 sites; default flag usage).
3. Standards conformance — fail: restatements of "see fyr help" and the harness-audit reference not listed (finding 4); AGENTS.md rule 6 not cited for update/zip facts (finding 10).
4. Directory layout — pass: `cmd/fyr/help.go`, `help_text.go`, `help_test.go` beside the code.
5. Simplicity — pass: stdlib only, no new dependency; text in the binary is justified by D19 (3).
6. Decoupling — pass with a note: help_text.go (text) vs help.go (rendering) is a clean seam; the synopsis needs a single source consumed by `run_dispatch.go`, `record.go`, `verb_*.go`, `eval.go` (five edit sites), which should go through one `usageErr` helper to avoid the fan-out.

## Not examined

- The stored record body vs `.agents/scratch/ledger/p4a/plan.body` (taken as identical per the dispatch).
- Other phases' boxes, § Verification, the sandbox recipe.
- `internal/search` tests that pin `; see fyr help` (not grepped).
- Whether `SPEC-fyr-*` records exist for index, list, version; and `fyr check`'s spec-staleness rule's effect on edited specs (not run).
- `wordRe` behaviour on `<verb>` in README text (docs.go regex not read in full).
- A full reading of the 14 per-verb error paths in verb_metrics.go, verb_search_memory.go, verb_dream.go beyond the grep'd lines.
- The `DEPLOY-remote` record body (item 82's edit).

design needs revision
implementation not ready

## Outcome

Answered in PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger, round 1 of 1 (the cold read is one report):
- Findings 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 — fixed in the plan: D21 (1)–(11), § Interfaces "Phase 4b" rewritten (the mock, the verb page, help's own arguments, the usage-error sites and helper, the restatements, the existing tests that change), Phase 4a's boxes and the new Phase 4b.
- Finding 4 — fixed for `internal/search/search.go:54,62,78,80`, `parse.go:249`, `ctx_verbs.go:93`; rebutted for `skills/harness-audit/references/areas.md:37` (D21 4: the short page is still the usage text and lists every verb).
- Finding 10 (sizing) — fixed by D22: the fact audit is Phase 4a's own session, the code is Phase 4b; rule 6 is cited in the audit box.
- Finding 12 — rebutted in part: IN15/IN16 are defined by the plan's § Terms (Finding IDs); "the writer" is now defined.
- Readiness questions 1–3 (BLOCKING): answered by D21 (2) and (1). Questions 4–9: answered by D21 (3), (5)–(8) and D22.
- Item 82: the stored DEPLOY-remote line is `systemctl --user list-timers | grep -cw sh-agent   # 0 (macOS: launchctl list | grep -cw sh-agent)`, read back with `fyr record get`.

Blocking findings open: none. The operator's approval of the boxes is pending.

title: Review — ledger Phase 4b, the help pages (fyr help): approve with nits, 4 low, 2 fixed, 2 rebutted
body:
# Review — ledger-phase4b-help   (2026-10-28)

Range reviewed: working tree vs HEAD 74de149 (17 modified files, plus new cmd/fyr/help.go, help_text.go, help_test.go); diff .agents/scratch/ledger/p4b/phase4b.diff; read against PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger § Interfaces "Phase 4b", Phase 4b boxes and D19-D21.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing is broken. The help routing (`fyr`, `fyr help [verb]`, `-h`, `--help`, `fyr <verb> -h|--help`, `fyr -h <verb>`) behaves as the plan says, and I ran it by hand on a binary built from the tree: help exits 0 on the writer, every usage error exits 2 with reason, synopsis and hint, and the flag package's own `Usage of` text never appears. `gofmt -l`, `go vet ./cmd/fyr`, `go test ./cmd/fyr` (whole package, no -race, 14 s), `go test ./internal/search` and the root `TestFunctionLength` all pass. `fyr check` on the tree reports 10 findings (docs 5, specs 5), the same count as `.agents/scratch/ledger/p4a/check-after.txt`; I did not diff the lines. The facts I checked in the pages are true of the code. Remaining items are two stale restatements and two small inconsistencies, all low.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: high]** `SPEC-fyr-search` record, failure-mode table row "Argument errors (…)" (line 79 of the record body) — still gives the message as `search: <what is wrong>; see fyr help`. The diff changes all four messages to `; see fyr help search` (`internal/search/search.go:54,62,78,80`). A current spec is a restatement the AGENTS rule "a behaviour change includes the text that describes it" requires changed in the same change. Fix: `fyr record edit SPEC-fyr-search --body` with `; see fyr help search`.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `skills/harness-audit/references/areas.md:37` — tells the auditor to compare "the verb table against the usage text and the README". There is no usage text any more: the sources are `shortPage` and `pages` in `cmd/fyr/help_text.go`. Fix: name them, or "the short page".
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/dream/dream.go:107` — a bare `fyr dream` still prints the old one-line `usage: fyr dream --all | --project <dir> [--dry-run] | --install-timer | --remove-timer` with no hint line. Every other bare verb now prints the page's synopsis and `run 'fyr help dream' for its flags`, and `help dream` shows a four-line synopsis. It is outside D21 (2)'s list (so not a plan violation) and exits 2 as before; the inconsistency is the only issue. `cmd/fyr/verb_dream.go:18-27` (the other dream usage errors) has the same gap. Fix: route the three sites through `usageErr(c.out, "dream", ...)` in `runDream`, or record the omission in D21.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/run_dispatch.go:21` — `fyr -help` is "unknown command", while `fyr help -help` and `fyr <verb> -help` print help (`runHelp` strips `-help`, and the flag package accepts it). The `fyr -h|--help` forms the plan names work. Fix: add `-help` to the condition, or leave it and drop `-help` from `runHelp`'s filter (`help.go:111`).

Observations, not findings: the record page lost the kind list and the "feedback and proposal are --global only" note (the Phase 4a audit marks it "stated" in SPEC-fyr-record § Kinds, and `fyr record add x` prints the kinds). Several flag usage lines repeat their placeholder (`--out FILE` / "the HTML file FILE to write"); cosmetic.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. `usage`, `recordUsage` and the literal usage lines are deleted. `pageOf`, `verbHelp`, `flagLines`, `wrapWords`, `usageErr`, `runHelp` all have callers. `metricsSubverbs` is still used by the unknown-subcommand message, so its trimmed comment is accurate.
2. Flow tracing — pass. `run` → `runHelp` or `c.parse` (`ErrHelp` → `verbHelp`, flag error → `usageErr`) → verb. `recordFlagsSet` now returns the usage error and `runRecord` returns it unchanged. `sync` maps to install's page at every site (`pageOf`). `verbs`/`pages` have no init cycle (the build succeeds). `-h` is answered before `resolveHome`, `migrateStateDir` and `ResolveSource`, so help writes nothing. I ran bare `record`, `record add`, `dream`, `search`, `list extra`, `help --home`, `help -- install`, and `-h` on install, update, metrics, eval and check.
3. Standards conformance — pass with the findings above. Stdlib only. Functions are all under 50 lines; the files are 129, 262 and 281 lines. The plan's restatement list is done (search messages, `parse.go:249`, the `--status` usage, main.go doc comment, README:56); the two stale copies above are outside that list. README:56's sentence is true: `fyr`/`fyr help` print the short page, `fyr help <verb>`/`fyr <verb> --help` the verb page, and an unknown flag exits 2 with the verb's synopsis.
4. Directory layout — pass. `help.go`, `help_text.go` and `help_test.go` sit beside `run_dispatch.go` in `cmd/fyr`, as the plan says.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. No dependency, no security surface; the only new input is a verb name looked up in `verbs`.
6. Decoupling — pass. Pages are data in `help_text.go`; flag lines come from the verb's own FlagSet, so a flag is described once. One copy remains: the `--kind` list in search's usage string, pinned against `internal/search` by `TestHelpSearchKindsMatchSearch`.

Tests: they pin what they claim and I found none that passes vacuously. Width, verbs against the table, flags against the FlagSet, byte-identical forms, help's arguments, one row per usage-error site (reason, synopsis equal to the page's first lines, hint, exit 2, no `Usage of`), the left-out sites printing no hint, and the unknown verb printing no short page. Changed assertions in `auditfix_test.go`, `check_test.go`, `usage_test.go` and `record_test.go` each trace to the behaviour change. I did not run the plan's must-fail mutations. Coverage not claimed or pinned: the prose in `about` is checked for length only, never against behaviour, and `-help` at top level is untested.

## Not examined
- The plan's must-fail mutations (not re-run by me); `go test -race` over the whole repo (ran the package without -race); `govulncheck`.
- Line-level diff of `fyr check` output against the p4a baseline (count and category totals only).
- Claims in the pages that were carried over unchanged from the old usage text (update, record, dream, index, eval and check details): checked only where they were reworded or cheap to verify (status shadow note, uninstall, adopt, update --check, install paths, search flags).
- Historical plan/recon records mentioning the old `usage` const: left alone as history.

## Outcome

1. `SPEC-fyr-search` row "Argument errors": **fixed.** The operator approved the one-cell edit in their own turn (plan D25). The cell now reads `; see fyr help search`, the rest of the body is byte-identical, and the edit lands in the same commit as `internal/search/search.go`.
2. `skills/harness-audit/references/areas.md:37`: **rebutted** (D21 (4), which the operator approved in D23). The short page is still fyr's usage text and lists every verb, so the line stays true. Skill edits are also outside this phase's approvals.
3. `fyr dream`'s usage errors (`internal/dream/dream.go:107`, `cmd/fyr/verb_dream.go:18-27`): **rebutted for this phase, raised to the operator.**
   - D21 (2) is a closed list of sites. The dream timer pair is named there as a value check that already says what is wrong.
   - The bare `fyr dream` line is an old-style usage line. Whether it moves to `usageErr` is the operator's call, in the closing table.
4. `fyr -help` at the top level: **fixed.** `run` now routes `-help` like `-h` and `--help`. `TestHelpArguments` has the row `-help record`, which fails without the fix (checked) and passes with it.

Observations:
- The record page has no kind list. `fyr record add x` prints the kinds, and `SPEC-fyr-record` § Kinds holds them, so this is accepted.
- Repeated placeholders are cosmetic and left alone.

No second round. The two fixes are 8 lines of code plus their test rows, each read by the author and pinned by a must-fail check.

title: Review — ledger Phase 5: retro and distill queue proposals (ADR-070), code and docs lenses

# Review — ledger-phase5 (2026-10-28)

Range reviewed: uncommitted diff over 9738ac7 (`.agents/scratch/ledger/p5/phase5.diff`): `skills/retro/SKILL.md`, `skills/distill/SKILL.md`, ADR-070 (one line in `.agents/trail.jsonl`; `git diff --stat` confirms exactly +1 line there, nothing else touched).

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing is broken. The diff does what ADR-070 says: retro Step 6 no longer lets another project write the harness checkout (the "apply now" branch is gone and `queued` is unconditional there), `distill --global` queues a global `proposal` record instead of writing `<harness-repo>/skills/`, and the dreamer dispatch exists once (retro Step 1 source 8; distill points at it and names `Promoted: none`). The ledger Phase 5 box's greps hold: `git grep -i 'apply now\|<harness-repo>/skills' -- skills context` is empty, `Write your draft with` appears once in skills/, and `go test ./internal/harness -run 'TestSkillListingBudget|TestLint|TestRenderedContext'` is ok. Every cross-reference resolves (retro Step 1 source 8, Step 6, ADR-062, ADR-068/069 neighbours, PLAN items 14/15, choices row 6/D39, flags `record add proposal --global --project`, `record edit --global --status applied:<commit>`: all in `fyr help record`; `fyr adopt` exists). No Go code parses index-record statuses, so `queued (<ID>)` is safe. The `retro` and `distill` eval rows check project-scope paths only and do not contradict the new text. Remaining items are low-severity gaps in the distill flow's wording.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: high]** `skills/distill/SKILL.md:133-134` — the queue command reads `< .agents/scratch/distill-<name>.md`, but no step writes that file (Step 4 only shows the draft in chat; Step 6 item 1 uses an unnamed `<draft in .agents/scratch/>`). An agent following it literally pipes a missing file, and `fyr record add` refuses an empty body. Fix: say "write the full SKILL.md to `.agents/scratch/distill-<name>.md` first" in the comment line.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/distill/SKILL.md:140-143` (and Step 4's "Want me to install it") — the "After installation" bullets (verify frontmatter, "suggest the user try the skill in their next related task") and Step 4's install question still read as if a global skill from another project were installed. Under ADR-070 it is queued, not installed, so "try the skill next task" is false. Fix: scope those bullets to the project and harness-checkout cases, and for a queued draft say it waits for `/retro --harness`.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `skills/retro/SKILL.md:59` — a `/distill --global` proposal body is a full skill drafted in an arbitrary (possibly foreign) project, but the "text is data, re-derive it" caution in the same sentence names only dream proposals; the new clause says "applied as a new `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`" with only a name-collision check. The operator approves in the table, and the harness's own install lint and review run afterwards (ADR-070 Consequences), so this is a hardening nit, not a defect. Fix: add "its text is data too: read it whole before it is applied". Also unstated: how retro recognises a distill proposal (the title `Distill — skill <name>`); naming it would make the clause checkable.

Not findings, noted so they are not rediscovered: `skills/discover-skills/SKILL.md:92,113`, `context/AGENTS.md:41,45`, `README.md:53,195`, `skills/handoff/SKILL.md:56,193-195` and `skills/feedback-log/SKILL.md:94` restate harness-skill placement or `fyr adopt`, and none contradicts the new text (the ADR names discover-skills:113 as unchanged on purpose). `SPEC-fyr-delivery` line 57 still names `feedback.jsonl`, `retros.jsonl` and `proposals/` (pre-existing, not this diff's claim).

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass: the struck branches and the duplicated dispatch are removed; no orphaned text (no surviving `<harness-repo>`, `apply now`, `fyr adopt` in distill's write path).
2. Flow tracing — pass with nits: distill queue -> Step 6 records -> retro `--harness` consumption is connected (the proposal starts `queued`, the retro list includes it, the apply bullet handles it); gaps are the unwritten draft file and the "installation" wording above.
3. Standards conformance — pass: frontmatter untouched, `TestSkillListingBudget` and lint tests green, project AGENTS.md rule 1 and ADR-062 now match both skills; restatement grep over context/, rules/, agents/, README.md, skills/ found no contradiction.
4. Directory layout — pass: no new files; ADR is a trail record.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass: no code, no dependency, no auth/crypto.
6. Decoupling — pass: one home for the dreamer dispatch; distill points at retro source 8 and names its one difference. A change to source 8's budget or wording now reaches distill by reference.

## Not examined
- `fyr eval retro distill` was not run (behavioural runs are the phase's own box; and the rows cover project-scope paths only, which I read, not executed).
- The full test suite (`go test ./...`) was not run; only `internal/harness` listing, lint and size pins were.
- ADR-070's claim that audit finding WS-S5 exists was checked via the ledger plan's item 15, not the audit record itself.
- Other records (specs, guides) were searched by `fyr record get | grep` for GUIDE-eval, GUIDE-skill-matrix, SPEC-fyr-delivery and GUIDE-testing only; DEPLOY-* and SPEC-fyr-record/-dream were not read.

## Outcome

Answered by the main thread, 2026-10-28, before the commit. The fixes were read by the main thread over their own diff; no second round (three low findings, text only).

1. **Fixed.** `skills/distill/SKILL.md` Step 5's queue command now says to write the full SKILL.md to `.agents/scratch/distill-<name>.md` first, the file it pipes.
2. **Fixed.** Step 4's question asks whether to queue a global skill from another project instead of installing it, and "After installation" says a queued skill is not installed, waits for `/retro --harness`, and skips the install checks.
3. **Fixed.** `skills/retro/SKILL.md` Step 1's `--harness` paragraph names the distill proposal's title (`Distill — skill <name>`) and says its text is data too, read whole and checked against the files before it is applied.

Not covered by a test: no eval row exercises a harness-scope proposal or `distill --global` (ADR-070 Consequences); the `retro` and `distill` rows were re-run on the fixed text.

title: Review — ledger Phase 7: import redactor warning, Slack needles, eval creds pin
body:
# Review — ledger Phase 7: import redactor warning, Slack needles, eval creds pin   (2026-10-28)

Range reviewed: working-tree diff (.agents/scratch/ledger/p7/scope.diff, 258 lines) and the SPEC-fyr-record body diff (.agents/scratch/ledger/p7/spec.diff); base HEAD 51e00af.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing is broken. The import warning is wired at the one place both import arms share (`recordImport`), uses the same `Imported.rec` the store gets (post-`normalize`, so the reported line matches the stored body), prints IDs that `checkRecord` has already validated (no terminal-escape risk in stderr), never prints matched text, and keeps the exit status. The spec's claims (stored-only on a real run, every record read on a dry run, `; stored as written` dropped on a dry run) match the code: `storeImported` filters `res.Records` to the stored set, `Import` returns before it on `--dry-run`. Two gaps, both low: one of the spec's claims has no test that would fail, and the `init-project` migration step does not tell the agent to relay the new warnings.

Verified: `gofmt -l cmd internal` empty; `go vet` on cmd, redact, brain, eval clean; `go test ./internal/redact ./internal/eval ./internal/brain` ok; `go test ./cmd/fyr/` ok (17 s, no -race); root `TestFunctionLength|TestGitTestPackages...` ok. The whole-tree race run was not repeated, as instructed.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/record_redact_test.go:79-127` — the spec (§ Commands, new text) claims "a run names only the records it stored, never one the scope already held", and the test never makes a record "already held": the first real import is the only one, and the dry run runs before it on an empty store. Input that would slip through: a second real `record import` over the same records, or a store that already holds `PLAN-2026-01-01-body`. If `warnImportRedactable` iterated something other than `res.Records` (e.g. all candidates), or `filterStored` regressed, only brain's own test (`import_test.go:224`, record count) would notice, not the warning. Fix: after the real run, reset the tree (commit the export) and run `record import` again, asserting empty stderr; or drop "never one the scope already held" from the spec. The dry-run-names-held half is also unpinned (a dry run after the real one would name them).
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/init-project/SKILL.md:66` — Step 4's migration tells the agent to show the user the counts and `problem` lines, then commit `.agents/trail.jsonl` alone. Import is the one path that moves old text into the committed export in bulk, and its new warnings (and the `--dry-run` ones) are where the user learns a record holds a credential-shaped string. The step does not mention them, so an agent following it can commit without relaying a warning. Fix: add "and every `fyr record import: warning:` line on stderr (a record the redactor would change; edit it before committing)". Not a restatement of a reversed claim (nothing there says import does not warn), so it is a docs gap, not a contradiction.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/redact/redact_test.go:169-170` — the plan box requires "each needle disabled alone fails TestRedactShapes"; I did not mutate (read-only duty). By reading, `xoxe-1-FAKEVALUE` and `xwfp-FAKEVALUE` match no other needle, so deleting either needle fails the `shapeSecrets` loop; the checkpoint should cite the actual must-fail run.

Not findings, checked: `xoxc-`/`xoxd-` are not added although ledger item 46 names them; the plan box permits it ("a shape Slack does not document is not added; the box says which"), and the diff's comment says so (`internal/redact/redact.go:28-32`). The prior security review (`REVIEW-2026-10-27-2156`) did probe them as unredacted, so the operator should know two of the four named shapes stay unredacted; the checkpoint box must say so. `xoxe-`/`xwfp-` are prefixes, matched case-sensitively with no `\b`, each with a near-miss with the dash removed: conforms to AGENTS.md's needle rules. The new `redact.Redact(c.hit) == c.hit` assertion in `internal/eval/creds_table_test.go:46` can fail (it asserts a property that eval's own list does not guarantee) and passes for all ten kinds today.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. `Imported.Text()` has one caller (`warnImportRedactable`); `firstRedacted` is shared by both warn functions. Nothing orphaned.
2. Flow tracing — pass. `recordImport` -> `brain.Import`/`ImportGlobal` -> `res.Records` (stored-only on a real run, all on a dry run) -> `warnImportRedactable`; project, memory and global arms all populate `Imported.rec`. Error path: no warning when the import returns an error. The only untested hop is the held-record claim (finding 1).
3. Standards conformance — pass with one docs gap (finding 2). Restatement grep over `README.md:46`, `context/`, `skills/*/SKILL.md`, `agents/`, `cmd/fyr/help_text.go:139` and `fyr search`: the only text saying a warning is absent for import was the spec line, now changed; README's sentence is about `add` and stays true; the help page is updated. `SPEC-fyr-record` § Exit status unchanged and correct (exit stays 0). Needle shapes follow the by-kind and near-miss rules. Standing function-length pin passes.
4. Directory layout — pass. Helper in `cmd/fyr/record_redact.go` (65 lines) beside `warnRedactable`; test in its existing test file (128 lines).
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. Stdlib only, no new dependency; reuses `redact.Redact`; no crypto/auth code.
6. Decoupling — pass. brain exposes only `Imported.Text()` and "never judges text"; the redactor stays in `cmd/fyr`; `internal/eval` test imports `internal/redact` (test-only, the dependency direction AGENTS.md allows; eval imports no SQLite driver).

## Not examined
- Mutation runs (must-fail checks of each new needle, of the import warning) — read-only duty; assessed by reading only.
- Whole-tree `go test -race ./...` and `govulncheck` (one run already in progress, per the dispatch).
- The live `.agents/trail.jsonl` diff (excluded by the dispatch; only the spec body diff was read) and Slack's web documentation for the token shapes (not fetched).
- Behaviour of `ImportGlobal` and memory-store arms with a redactable body: read, not run.

## Outcome

1. **Fixed.** `TestRecordImportWarnsOnRedactable` now commits the export and runs `record import --dry-run` (asserting the same three warnings without `; stored as written`), then a real `record import` (asserting exit 0, `3 already stored` and empty stderr). Must-fail: with `storeImported`'s `res.Records = filterStored(...)` dropped, the re-import assertion fails with the three warnings on stderr; restored, it passes.
2. **Deferred to the operator.** The `init-project` Step 4 sentence is a skill edit, outside Phase 7's closed approvals (and a skill change owes an Antigravity run); named in the handoff as a proposed box.
3. **Rebutted: already done.** The must-fail ran before the review: with `"xoxe-"` removed alone, `TestRedactShapes` (text and jsonl rows), `TestVendorDocExamples` (`xoxe-1-Your-Refresh-Token`) and `TestRedactText` fail; with `"xwfp-"` removed alone, `TestRedactShapes` and `TestRedactText` fail; both restored, `go test ./internal/redact/` ok. Slack documents no workflow-token example, so `xwfp-` has no `TestVendorDocExamples` row. `xoxc-` and `xoxd-` stay unredacted (Slack documents neither); the Phase 7 box and the change record say so.

Blast radius followed into internal/brain/import.go (projectRecords, storeImported, filterStored), import_classify.go (ImportedID, slugOf), import_global.go (feedback ID from slugify(title)), import_guard.go (checkRecord), record.go (validID, slugify), memory.go (memorySlug), cmd/fyr/record.go (printImport).

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

Worst first: the new import warning never looks at the record ID, and an import ID is built from the file name (project import) or from the title (global feedback import). So a credential in a trail file's NAME gives an imported record whose ID holds it, and the warning prints nothing for that record. That is a false "clean". The ID is the record's key, it goes into the committed `.agents/trail.jsonl`, and `record edit` cannot change it. I reproduced this with a probe dry run (below). No new output path prints credential text that `printImport` did not already print on stdout. The one partial exception is the global-feedback case, where the ID the warning prints holds the slugged, lowercased title it is warning about. That exception was found by reading the code and was not run end to end. The new Slack needles are sound and cover every prefix the two Slack pages document. `xoxc-`, `xoxd-`, `xoxr-` and `xoxo-` are still missed. A dry run cannot be made to mislead beyond what the spec states.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/record_redact.go:37-48` (`warnImportRedactable`): checks `r.Text()` (title, body) only, never `r.ID`. Project-import IDs are `ImportedID(kind, stem)` = prefix + `slugOf(stem)` (`internal/brain/import_classify.go:24-27`): the file name, lowercased, `_` folded to `-`, up to 120 chars. Verified with a probe repository (`.agents/scratch/sec-probe-repo`, fake token): `plans/2026-01-01-xoxb-1111-2222-fakevaluefake.md` with a clean title and body imports as `PLAN-2026-01-01-xoxb-1111-2222-fakevaluefake`. The dry run printed that ID on stdout and wrote NO warning line for it on stderr. The sibling record with the token in its title did get warned. A scratch program confirmed `redact.Redact` changes that ID string. So the redactor would scrub the ID before a dream prompt, while the operator is told nothing and commits it in `trail.jsonl` as an immutable key. The same gap was already in `record add --id` (`cmd/fyr/record.go`, `warnRedactable` gets title and body only); this diff carries it into import. Remediation: run `redact.Redact` on the ID as well, in import and add/`--id`. A warning cannot name such a record by its ID without printing the text, so the safer shape is a refusal (or, at import, a problem line naming the source by its position, not its path, which holds the same text). Pin it with a test whose fixture puts the token only in the file name. This is an operator design question, because the operator chose warn-over-refuse for text.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `cmd/fyr/record_redact.go:42-46` with `internal/brain/import_global.go:136`: a global `feedback` record's ID is `FEEDBACK-<stamp>-` + `slugify(title)`, where the title is the user's quoted correction (`import_global.go:126-131`). When that title holds a token that survives lowercasing and slugging (for example an `xoxb-` token), the new stderr line `… warning: <ID>: the title holds text the redactor would change` prints up to 48 characters of that token text inside the ID. The text is not new exposure, because `printImport` (`cmd/fyr/record.go:200`) already prints the same ID on stdout. But it contradicts the stated contract "naming the record by its ID and never its text": spec.diff § The redactor warning, `cmd/fyr/help_text.go:139-140`, the doc comment at `record_redact.go:32-35`, and the test header at `record_redact_test.go:73-77`. The test passes only because its fixtures are project files, whose IDs come from file names. This was found by reading the code; I did not run a global import. Remediation: same as the finding above; until then, reword the claim so it does not promise the ID is free of the text.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/redact/redact.go:28-33`: the Slack needles. Against docs.slack.dev/authentication/tokens and /using-token-rotation (fetched into `.agents/scratch/sec-slack-docs/`), every documented prefix is now covered: `xoxb-`, `xoxp-` (which includes CLI service tokens, which the page calls user tokens), `xapp-`, `xoxe.xapp-`/`xoxe.xoxb-`/`xoxe.xoxp-` (through the inner prefix or the xapp rule), `xoxe-1-` refresh and `xwfp-`. A probe confirmed each is redacted, and the near-misses (`xoxe tokens rotate`, `xwfp tokens expire`) stay. Still missed, confirmed by the probe on bare tokens in prose: `xoxc-` (browser session token), `xoxd-` (its `d` cookie value), `xoxr-` (legacy workspace-app refresh) and `xoxo-` (legacy family). `xoxc-` and `xoxd-` are full-account session credentials and are the Slack values most often pasted from devtools. The keyword rules catch them only in assignment or `Cookie:` form. "Slack documents neither" (ledger item 46) decides the question by documentation, but the redactor exists to stop credentials leaving the machine. Remediation, per the AGENTS.md "grow by kind" rule: one kind regex, e.g. `xox[a-z]-[A-Za-z0-9%-]{8,}`, without `\b`, plus a near-miss in `TestRedactShapes`, replacing the per-letter prefix list. This is the operator's call because it reverses a recorded choice. Also noted, safe direction: the prefix needle redacts prose that names `xoxe-` (probe), like the other prefixes.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `cmd/fyr/record_redact.go:52-65` (`firstRedacted` as used by import): the "first at line <n>" for import counts lines of the STORED body, after `normalize` and the import's own extraction. The operator opens the source file. For a file with frontmatter, or an ADR split out of a shared file, the stored line can differ from the source line, so the pointer can send someone hunting for a credential to the wrong line. The spec text for import does not say which body the line counts, while the add text does ("as read from stdin"). I did not verify this on a frontmatter file. Remediation: say "line <n> of the stored body" in the spec and the help text, or map the line back to the source.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/eval/creds_table_test.go:45-49`: the IN48 comment says the two credential lists "cannot drift apart unseen". Only one direction is pinned: every eval hit must be redacted. A redactor needle with no eval row, such as this diff's `xoxe-`/`xwfp-` or any Slack token, drifts unseen, because the eval scan refuses no Slack shape (`internal/eval/creds.go`). This test-header claim overstates its coverage. Remediation: reword to "every eval refusal is also redacted", or add the reverse pin if the operator wants the lists equal.

Questions from the dispatch:
- Does a new output path print credential text? Only through an ID derived from that text: the global-feedback case (finding 2, also on stdout already). IDs are bounded by `validID`/`slugTail`/`memorySlug` grammar, so printing `r.ID` without `search.Printable` adds no terminal-control injection.
- Are the needles sound, and is anything documented still missed? Sound, and nothing documented on the two pages is missed. The undocumented families in finding 3 are missed.
- Can the warning mislead between dry run and real run? Not beyond what the spec states. A dry run warns on every record it read, including those already held, and drops "; stored as written". A real run warns only on records `storeImported`/`filterStored` (`internal/brain/import.go:185-210`) actually inserted, and the test covers both. Remaining edges: a real run after a dry run silently drops already-held records that the dry run named; this is documented. A record already held from a pre-warning import is never re-warned. The false-clean on IDs is finding 1.

## Checked
- Secrets: no real credential in the diff. Fixtures are `FAKEVALUE`-shaped (`record_redact_test.go:85`, `redact_test.go:169-179`). Every probe used fake values.
- Injection: the new stderr lines format a validated ID, a constant and an int. No shell, SQL or path use is added. `ShellQuote`/`Printable` on stdout are unchanged.
- Authz/authn: none touched.
- Crypto: none touched. Nothing hand-rolled.
- Dependencies: none added (`internal/redact` imported into the `internal/eval` test and into `cmd/fyr`, both in-module). `govulncheck ./...` on go1.27.3: no reached vulnerabilities. One module advisory, GO-2026-5024, which is on the known list, so nothing NEW. npm is not applicable (no JS in the range).
- GCP surface: none touched.
- Tests run (package-scoped, no -race tree run): `go test ./internal/redact ./internal/eval -run 'TestCreds|TestRedact|TestVendor|Needle|TestShape'` passed; `go test ./cmd/fyr -run 'TestRecordImportWarnsOnRedactable|TestRecordRedactorWarning'` passed (verbose run confirmed the import test ran).
- Probes (scratch only, `--home .agents/scratch/home-trail`, dry run, which writes nothing): the binary built to `.agents/scratch/sec-probe/fyr`, the probe repo at `.agents/scratch/sec-probe-repo` (git init checked with `rev-parse --absolute-git-dir`, `GIT_*` unset), and the redactor probe at `.agents/scratch/sec-probe/main.go`.

## Not examined
- A real (non-dry-run) global import of `feedback` logs. Finding 2 rests on reading the code only.
- How `import_docs.go`/`import_classify.go` build the stored body for frontmatter files, so the line-number offset in finding 4 is unverified.
- The exact `slugTail` regexp text (`internal/brain/record.go`). I relied on its use in `validID` and on the slug functions.
- Whether `fyr dream` redacts record IDs as well as bodies. The ID and stdout paths of the other verbs (`list`, `get`, `search`) were not re-reviewed.
- Slack pages beyond the two named: the full legacy token list and the App Manifest/config-token page.
- `.agents/trail.jsonl` changes (excluded from the range by the dispatch).

## Outcome

1. **Fixed (import); `add --id` left for the operator.** `warnImportRedactable` now runs `redact.Redact` on each ID. An ID the redactor would change gets its own line, `fyr record import: warning: record <n> in the list above: the ID holds text the redactor would change[; stored as written]`, and that record's title and body lines name it the same way, so stderr never repeats the ID. The import still stores it (warn over refuse, the operator's SD42 choice); a refusal is the operator's call. Test: `TestRecordImportWarnsOnRedactable` gains `plans/2026-01-01-xoxb-fakevalue.md` (clean title and body, token only in the file name) and asserts the `record 4` line in the dry run and the real run, and that stderr holds no `xoxb-`. Must-fail: with the ID check turned off, the test fails; restored, it passes. The same gap in `record add --id` predates this diff; it goes to the operator in the handoff.
2. **Rebutted as a stated limit.** The ID is already printed on stdout by `printImport`, so nothing new is exposed. `SPEC-fyr-record` now states the limit for log-imported global `feedback` and `retro` IDs (`slugify`: lowercased, every other run of characters turned to `-`, at most 48 characters). The help line no longer says "by ID", and the test header says what it pins.
3. **Left for the operator.** The `xox[a-z]-` kind rule reverses ledger item 46 ("a shape Slack does not document is not added"). It is proposed in the handoff, with `xoxc-`, `xoxd-`, `xoxr-` and `xoxo-` named as still unredacted.
4. **Fixed (docs).** `SPEC-fyr-record` says `<n>` is a line of the body as stored, which can differ from the source file's line.
5. **Fixed (comment).** The IN48 comment says one direction only, and that a needle with no eval kind (Slack's) is not pinned there.

title: Security review round 2 — ledger-p7-redact-import-warning fixes
body:
# Security review round 2 — ledger-p7-redact-import-warning fixes   (2026-10-28)

Range reviewed: fixes only. These are the round-1 diff compared with the current diff (`.agents/scratch/ledger/p7/fixes.diff`), the live `cmd/fyr/record_redact.go` (`warnImportRedactable`, lines 32-57) and `cmd/fyr/record_redact_test.go` (`TestRecordImportWarnsOnRedactable`), and the spec text `.agents/scratch/ledger/p7/spec.diff`. I checked them against `printImport`/`recordImport` (`cmd/fyr/record.go:165-223`), `slugify` (`internal/brain/record.go:209-218`, `nonSlug` at :91), `slugOf` (`internal/brain/import_classify.go:26-33`), `internal/brain/import_global.go` (log kinds :34, `add` :70-88, the feedback/retro ID :125-138), `storeImported` (`internal/brain/import.go:185-199`) and `search.printable` (`internal/search/search_query.go:134`). Round 1 is in `.agents/scratch/agents/security-2026-10-28-1144.md`.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

Round 1's finding 1 is closed as stated. No stderr line now prints an ID that the redactor would change. Every ID the warning prints has passed `redact.Redact(r.ID) == r.ID` (`record_redact.go:45-49`), and it never prints a title, a body or a path. The "record <n> in the list above" naming is also unambiguous. The open problem is a weaker version of the same false clean. The redactor runs on the ID after slugging, not on the file name the ID came from. Lowercasing, and turning `=`, `_` and `:` into `-`, takes some credentials out of the redactor's reach. Examples are a case-sensitive key prefix, or a keyword assignment such as `api_key=<hex>`. A probe confirmed this. A tracked file named `2026-01-01-api_key=<32 hex>.md` with a clean title and body gets no warning line at all, because its ID `PLAN-2026-01-01-api-key-<32 hex>` passes the redactor unchanged. The same mechanism gives the documented global-feedback limit, and it is worse than the spec's wording suggests. In 4 of 5 probed credential-shaped titles, the slugged ID passes the redactor, so the title-warning line prints, on stderr, an ID holding the lowercased secret. For an AWS key ID or a hex key that text can be recovered exactly, and the warning line labels it as the sensitive one. Finding 2's spec statement is accurate to `slugify`, apart from three omissions that do not matter for security (listed below).

## Findings

- **[low-medium / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/record_redact.go:45-49`. The ID check runs `redact.Redact` on the slugged ID, not on what the ID was made from. `slugOf` (`import_classify.go:26-33`) lowercases the name and turns every character outside `[a-z0-9._-]` into `-`. `slugify` (`record.go:209-218`) turns every run outside `[a-z0-9]` into `-`. Probe (`.agents/scratch/sec-probe-r2/main.go`, fake values, the slug regexps copied from the source):
  - Project stems. `<date>-AKIA<example>` and `<date>-api_key=<32 hex>`: the redactor changes the stem, but the ID passes unchanged. Result: no ID line, and with a clean title and body, no warning at all. A `ghp_` stem is still caught (`ghp-…` matches).
  - Global feedback titles. `AKIA…`, `ghp_<36>`, `api_key=<hex>` and `password: <value>`: the title is redacted, the ID is not. Only the `xoxb-` title's ID is caught.

  The result is (a) a false clean for a credential in a file name whenever the needle depends on case or on context, and (b) for global feedback, a stderr line `FEEDBACK-…-<lowercased secret>: the title holds text the redactor would change`, which singles that ID out. Exposure is not new: `printImport` already prints the ID and the raw `r.Path` on stdout (`record.go:200`). But the fix's goal of naming such a record by position only holds when the slug happens to keep the needle's shape.

  Remediation: switch to position naming on what the ID came from, not on the ID itself. The simplest shape that cannot drift: name a record by its position whenever ANY of its lines fire. Otherwise, also test `r.Path` (`Imported.Path`, already in hand), and test the title for a log-sourced feedback or retro record whose ID is its slug. Pin it with two fixtures, a stem `…api_key=<fake hex>…` and a global feedback title with an `AKIA`-shaped example value, each asserting that the stderr line holds no part of the value. The round-1 refuse-vs-warn question stays with the operator.
- **[low / confidence: high]** Spec (spec.diff, § The redactor warning) compared with the code:
  - The ID line is described as a project-import matter ("A project record's ID comes from its file name, so …"). The code applies it to every record, including `--global` feedback, retro, proposal and memory. A global `proposal` ID also comes from its file name (`import_global.go:183`).
  - The spec's "known limit" sentence also reads as if a title warning always shows the slug. When the slug is caught, the record is named by position instead. The finding above shows the uncaught case is the common one for credential shapes, so the limit is understated rather than wrong.
  - Minor, not security: a lower-case sentence start, "finding 2). a run names only".

  Remediation: say "a record's ID" (not "a project record's"), and state that the check runs on the ID as stored, after slugging.

## Questions from the dispatch

- **Is finding 1 closed? Does any stderr path print an ID or text the redactor would change?** No such path exists. The three `Fprintf` calls print `name`, a constant, an int and `tail`. `name` is `r.ID` only when the redactor leaves it unchanged, and otherwise it is the position string. A title, body or path is never printed. It is closed for the trigger it names (an ID the redactor would change, which the test pins with an `xoxb-` file name, plus a `strings.Contains(…, "xoxb-")` guard). The broader trigger, a file name holding a credential, is only partly closed (the finding above).
- **Is "record <n> in the list above" unambiguous against `printImport`?** Yes, in all four modes. `recordImport` (`record.go:177-179`) calls `printImport(c, res)` and then `warnImportRedactable(res, c.dryRun)` on the same `res.Records` slice, already final. In a real run, project or `--global`, `storeImported` has already replaced `res.Records` with the stored records (`import.go:197-198`, called from `import.go` and `import_global.go:48`), so both functions walk the filtered list. In a dry run both walk the unfiltered list (the test's held-records dry run confirms 4 of 4). `printImport` prints exactly one line starting with `record  ` per element, in slice order, after one header line that starts with `import`. Problem lines start with `problem  `. Removal, memory and source paths go through `ShellQuote`. `printable` maps every byte below 0x20, newline included, plus the Unicode line and paragraph separators and format characters, to `?`. So a path cannot split a record line or forge another one. The n-th `record  ` line is element n (`i+1`, 1-based). One caveat that does not affect security: "above" assumes stdout and stderr share a terminal. When stdout is redirected, the count still holds against the redirected file.
- **Is finding 2's spec statement accurate to `slugify` and `import_global.go`?** It is accurate where it speaks. Feedback and retro are the only log kinds (`import_global.go:34`). Both take `ID = <prefix>-<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>-slugify(title)` (`:136`). For feedback the title is `corrected`, falling back to `user_quote`. For retro it is `"retro " + base(project)`. `slugify` lowercases, turns each run of characters outside `[a-z0-9]` into `-`, and cuts at 48 bytes. The spec leaves out three things: the leading and trailing `-` trim, the `record` fallback for an empty slug, and the `-N` collision suffix that `add` appends after the 48 (`import_global.go:75-80`). None of these changes the security reading. The spec's coverage and understatement are covered in the second finding.

## Checked

- Secrets: the probe and the test fixtures use fake values only (the `FAKEVALUE` shape, the AWS documentation example key ID shape, a repeated `Ab1` filler, sequential hex). No value is recorded here.
- Injection: the new stderr strings take a validated ID, a constant, an int or a position. `printImport` stdout goes through `printable`, unchanged.
- Authz/authn, crypto, GCP: not touched by the fixes.
- Dependencies: none added by the fixes. `govulncheck` was not re-run: the fixes change no imports (round 1's run stands).
- Tests: `go test ./cmd/fyr -run 'TestRecordImportWarnsOnRedactable|TestRecordRedactorWarning' -count=1` passed (package-scoped; no whole-tree `-race` run).
- Probe: `.agents/scratch/sec-probe-r2/main.go`, run with `go run`. It writes nothing outside scratch and touches no fyr home.

## Not examined

- No end-to-end `fyr record import --global` run against a scratch home. The global-feedback behaviour above rests on the copied `slugify` regexp in the probe and on reading `import_global.go`, not on running the binary.
- The full needle list was not walked to say which other needles the slug defeats. Five title shapes and three stem shapes were probed.
- The memory-record IDs (`memorySlug`) under the ID check were not probed.
- `.agents/trail.jsonl`, and everything outside the fixes, per the dispatch.

## Outcome

1. **Fixed.** `warnImportRedactable` judges the source path as well as the ID (`the ID or the source path holds text the redactor would change`), and names a record by its place in the printed list whenever its ID, path or title trips the redactor. So a slug that hides a secret (an `api_key=<hex>` or `AKIA…` file name, a global log line's title) no longer gives a false clean, and no ID derived from a flagged title reaches stderr. Test: `TestRecordImportWarnsOnRedactable` adds `plans/2026-01-01-api_key=0123456789abcdef.md` (token only in the path, which the slug hides from the ID check) and expects the title record by position. It asserts that stderr holds neither `xoxb-` nor the hex. Must-fail: with the path check removed, it fails; with the title dropped from the naming rule, it fails; restored, it passes.
2. **Fixed (docs).** `SPEC-fyr-record` says project and `--global` records are judged alike. The narrow "known limit" sentence is replaced by the path-and-title rule above.

Not done: no end-to-end `--global` import run. The global path walks the same `res.Records` and the same function; the test's fixtures are project files.

title: Review — ledger Phase 7a: Slack handling removed from the redactor
body:
# Review — ledger Phase 7a, Slack handling removed from the redactor   (2026-10-28)

Range reviewed: working tree vs HEAD (296cc0d): .agents/scratch/ledger/p7a/diff.patch (6 files) and the SPEC-fyr-delivery body edit (.agents/trail.jsonl line 995; .agents/scratch/ledger/p7a/spec-delivery.diff)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE

Nothing is broken. The diff removes exactly the Slack rules that PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger D32 1 orders removed (prefix needles xoxb/xoxp/xoxa/xoxs/xoxe/xwfp, keyword needles "slack webhook" and "slack app token", their comments, rows and near-misses, the Slack mention in the IN48 comment). The operator accepted the resulting risk in D32 1 (a bare Slack token or webhook URL now reaches the dream's model unless another rule catches it); the SPEC edit says so honestly. No living doc was found that still claims Slack coverage. No finding rises to a correctness, security-beyond-the-accepted-risk, or requirement level.

## Findings
None.

Observations (not findings):
- Accepted-risk reversal (D32 1): a bare `xoxb-…`, `xapp-…` or `https://hooks.slack.com/services/…` no longer redacts; only a generic rule (assignment, Authorization header) takes its line. Operator-approved in D32 1; REQUIREMENTS.md contains no Slack/vendor-prefix requirement (grep of "redact" in REQUIREMENTS.md names none).
- The Phase 7a box's own security checkpoint ("`security` over the diff, told the reversal is the operator's call") is the plan's next gate, not this review's.

## Evidence
- `go test ./internal/redact/ ./internal/eval/` ok (eval ran 17.7 s, redact cached); `go test ./cmd/fyr -run 'TestRecordImportWarnsOnRedactable|Redact'` ok.
- Plan's own expect: `git grep -niE "xox|xwfp|xapp|hooks\.slack|slack" -- '*.go' '*.md'` (catalog excluded) names only `internal/metrics` `closeSlack` and ROADMAP.md:9 (the plan description, "Slack handling removed from the redactor (7a, D32)", which is a status line, not a coverage claim). README.md, AGENTS.md, context/, skills/, agents/, cmd/fyr/help_text.go: no Slack mention.
- Records read with `fyr record get --home .agents/scratch/home-trail` and grepped for slack|xox|xwfp|xapp: SPEC-fyr-eval, -record, -search, -check, -dream, -memory-loop, GUIDE-eval, -fyr-matrix, -testing, -skill-matrix, DEPLOY-remote, DEPLOY-local: no Slack mention. SPEC-fyr-delivery is the only one that named it; edited.
- trail.jsonl diff verified by parsing: 1284 lines before and after, exactly one line differs (SPEC-fyr-delivery: `updated`, `body`), and the body diff is the one paragraph in the .diff. The "spec-stale" drift (fyr check) was started but not read (see Not examined).
- Test integrity: record_redact_test swaps `xoxb-fakevalue` for `whsec_fakevalue` in the file name and the leak list. `whsec_` is a surviving prefix needle (redact.go:28-31, near-miss "a whsec is a webhook secret" kept), lowercase file name vs the uppercased slug ID keeps the "ID or source path" branch exercised, and the test passes with the exact expected stderr, so the comment (slugging can hide the ID, the path is judged) still holds. creds_table_test comment reworded to match (no Slack-specific wording). redact_test comments ("Round 3, one rule per kind...", "The security check of that rule: an empty password", "SD41 ... Docker ... and HCP Terraform", redact.go "Two kinds the 2026-10-27 audit named") were all edited with the removed rows and now match their remaining rows. needles_test near-miss map lost exactly the six prefix entries whose needles were removed; `TestEveryNeedleHasAShapeAndANearMiss` passes both ways.
- SPEC-fyr-delivery new sentence "Slack tokens and webhook URLs have no needle of their own... (PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger D32 1)" is true against the code and cites a D-row that exists (line 608 of the plan).

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. No Slack remnants in .go; removed rows/near-misses leave no orphan map entries (test enforces).
2. Flow tracing — pass. Only needle lists shrink; no caller or signature changes; import-warning test and eval creds pin (IN48, one-directional) still hold and run green.
3. Standards conformance — pass. Describing-text grep done across living files and spec/guide/deploy records; restatements consistent. AGENTS.md needle-by-kind rule unaffected.
4. Directory layout — pass. No new files.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. Pure removal; no new dependency; no auth/crypto code.
6. Decoupling — pass. No boundary changes.

## Not examined
- `go run ./cmd/fyr check --home .agents/scratch/home-trail` (drift check of docs/specs) was started but exceeded 120 s and I did not read its result before writing this; the manual grep of every spec/guide/deploy record stands in for it.
- The full `go test -race ./...` (already running elsewhere); `gofmt`/`go vet` not run.
- Historical review/change/plan/ADR records that mention Slack (left as written by the plan's rule).
- Behaviour of `Redact` on live Slack strings was not run directly; judged from the needle list and test results.
- Phase 7a's remaining boxes (security checkpoint, change record, testing record).

## Outcome

- No findings to answer. The "not examined" items: gofmt, vet and the full `-race` suite ran bare on the main thread, on the tree after the security fixes (`.agents/scratch/ledger/p7a/race-2.txt`). The bare-Slack probe ran on the main thread: bare `xoxb-`, `xoxe-1-…`, `xapp-…` and a `hooks.slack.com` URL pass `redact.Redact` unchanged, while `SLACK_TOKEN=xoxb-…` and `Authorization: Bearer xoxb-…` are redacted. `fyr check` was not run for this phase.

title: Security review — ledger-p7a-slack-removal
body:
# Security review — ledger-p7a-slack-removal   (2026-10-28)

Range reviewed: HEAD (296cc0d)..working tree, i.e. `.agents/scratch/ledger/p7a/diff.patch` (6 files: internal/redact/{redact.go,redact_test.go,needles_test.go}, cmd/fyr/record_redact_test.go, internal/eval/creds_table_test.go) plus the SPEC-fyr-delivery body edit (`.agents/scratch/ledger/p7a/spec-delivery.diff`; the `.agents/trail.jsonl` diff is that one record, `body` and `updated` only, one paragraph changed)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: CLEAR

As the operator scoped it (D32 1 removes all Slack handling, with the risk accepted), the change is clean. The removal is complete. Nothing outside Slack was removed. Every remaining prefix needle is still bound by `TestEveryNeedleHasAShapeAndANearMiss`. The generic rules still take Slack tokens written as keyed assignments or Authorization/Bearer headers. The swapped `whsec_` needle drives the same ID-or-path warning branch `xoxb-` did. Nothing in the diff is broken. There are two low findings. The worse one is the spec's new sentence: it puts webhook URLs under "an assignment", but the conventional `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL=https://hooks.slack.com/...` line is NOT caught. That key holds no pass/secret/token/api-key word, so the sentence over-reads in the unsafe direction. The other is a pre-existing gap the diff did not cause: keyword needles have no structural binding, and the `jwt` rule can be deleted with the suite still green.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: high]** SPEC-fyr-delivery, new sentence ("Slack tokens and webhook URLs have no needle of their own … one goes only when a generic rule, an assignment or an authorization header, takes its line"). The sentence is accurate for tokens and over-reads for webhook URLs. A webhook's secret is its URL path. Its usual key names (`SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL=`, `webhook: "…"`, `slack: {webhook: …}`) hold none of the words `secretRe` needs, so the line passes unredacted. Probe on a scratch copy: `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL=https://hooks.slack.com/services/…` gives no needle. `SLACK_WEBHOOK_TOKEN=` and `webhook_secret=` are caught. The paragraph does define "assignments" earlier as password/secret/token/api-key ones, so a careful reader can work it out, but a casual one takes the webhook case as covered. Remediation: make the sentence precise, for example: "…an assignment whose key names a password, secret, token or API key, or an authorization header, takes its line; a webhook URL, whose secret is its path, goes only under such a key (`SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL=` is not one)". Token keys also missed, for the same record: `SLACK_BOT=`, `SLACK_OAUTH=`, `slack_creds=` (shown below).
- **[low / confidence: high, pre-existing, not introduced by this diff]** `internal/redact/redact.go:94` (`jwt`). Disabling this keyword needle leaves `go test ./internal/redact/` green, both at HEAD and in the tree: it was disabled in scratch copies of each, and the other 22 keyword needles each fail the suite when disabled. Every JWT row in `shapeSecrets` is also matched by `jwt short` (:112). But `jwt short` needs 8+ characters after the second dot, and `jwt` does not. So an unsigned `alg:none` JWT (`eyJ….eyJ….`, trailing dot) or one with a short signature is caught by `jwt` alone, and deleting it loses that with no test failing. More generally, `TestEveryNeedleHasAShapeAndANearMiss` binds prefix needles only; keyword needles have no structural binding. Remediation (operator's call, not part of 7a): add a `shapeSecrets` row only `jwt` catches (an unsigned JWT ending in `.`), or extend the binding test to keyword needles (a positive row per pattern, judged by the pattern `needleIn` returns).
- **[info / confidence: high]** `internal/redact/redact_test.go` (new line ~159) `// The security check of that rule: an empty password.` "That rule" was the Slack webhook rule. The one remaining row (`https://FAKEVALUEFAKEVALUE:@host/r`) belongs to `url token`. The comment now points at a rule that no longer exists. Cosmetic: suggest "The security check of the url token rule: an empty password."

## Checked
- **Removal complete, nothing else lost:**
  - `git grep -i -E 'slack|xox[a-z]|xapp|xwfp'` over the tracked tree (trail excluded) finds only `internal/metrics` `closeSlack`.
  - README, AGENTS.md, context, skills and agents carry no Slack claim. Among current/open trail records, only the SPEC-fyr-delivery sentence above mentions Slack.
  - A literal-by-literal diff of HEAD vs the tree for all five Go files: every removed string or backtick literal matches the Slack pattern, and nothing was added except the two `whsec_` literals in record_redact_test.go. That is 22 literals removed in redact_test.go, 12 in needles_test.go and 17 in redact.go.
  - The kept non-Slack rows that shared lines with removed ones are still present: `%2F…@host`, `FAKEVALUE1234567@host`, `…==@host`, `sk-None-`, `…:@host`.
- **Needle binding:** these mutations ran on a scratch copy.
  - Re-adding `"xoxb-"` to `prefixNeedles` fails ("no near-miss").
  - Dropping `"whsec_"` fails the binding test and `TestRedactShapes`.
  - Disabling each of the 23 keyword needles in turn fails the suite for 22 of them; `jwt` is the exception (finding 2).
  - Baseline: green.
- **Generic rules on Slack tokens (scratch probe, `needleIn`):**
  - Caught: `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN=`, `slack_token:`, JSON `"token":`, `SLACK_API_KEY=`, `SLACK_SECRET=` and `--token` (secret assignment); `Authorization: Bearer`, `Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer …")` and a curl `-H` (bearer); `credentials:` (credentials key).
  - Not caught: a bare `xoxb-`/`xoxe-`/`xapp-`/`xoxe.xoxb-` token, `token <tok>` (space with no flag), `SLACK_BOT=`, `SLACK_OAUTH=`, `slack_creds=`, a bare webhook URL and `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL=` (finding 1).
  - This matches D32 1's accepted risk.
- **record_redact_test.go swap:**
  - `slugBad` (`internal/brain/import.go:48`) keeps `_` and `slugOf` lowercases, so the ID is `PLAN-2026-01-01-whsec_fakevalue`. The probe shows both the ID and the path trip `whsec_`, as both did with `xoxb-`.
  - Path order is unchanged: `w…` still sorts fifth after `a/b/c/t`, as `x…` did, so "record 5" still holds.
  - The leak check on `whsec_` still sees the ID if it were printed.
  - `TestRecordImportWarnsOnRedactable` ran (`-v -count=1`) and passes.
  - Pre-existing, unchanged: no row trips the ID alone without the path, so the test cannot tell which half of `idHot` fired.
- **Tests:** `go test -count=1 ./internal/redact/ ./internal/eval/` gives ok/ok; `go test -count=1 -run TestRecordImportWarnsOnRedactable ./cmd/fyr/` gives PASS. The full `-race` suite was not run, per the dispatch.
- **Secrets:** none added. Every token in the tests is a FAKEVALUE or fakevalue placeholder.
- **Injection / authz-authn:** no surface changed. The redactor is a pure text filter, and the diff only shrinks its needle lists.
- **Crypto:** none touched, nothing hand-rolled.
- **Dependencies:** `go.mod`/`go.sum` unchanged. `govulncheck ./...` (go1.27.3) reports 0 vulnerabilities affecting the code and 1 in a required module that the code does not call (the documented GO-2026-5024). `npm audit` does not apply: no JS in the diff.
- **GCP surface:** none touched.
- **Past bugs:** `fyr search --refs <path> --kind bug --home .agents/scratch/home-trail` returned 0 references for each of the five changed files. That scratch store may not hold the full trail, so this is weak evidence. BUG-110 (needles grow by kind) is known from AGENTS.md and was respected.

## Not examined
- The full `go test -race ./...` run, which the dispatch excluded.
- The `fyr dream` call sites beyond `redact.Redact`/`RedactJSONL` themselves: the diff does not change how they are called, only the needle lists.
- The historical trail records (closed plans, reviews) that still mention Slack needles. They are records of their time and are not rewritten by rule.
- An Antigravity behavioural run: not applicable, because no skill, agent or context file changed.

## Outcome

1. Fixed. SPEC-fyr-delivery's sentence now says a line goes only when a generic rule takes it, "an assignment to a name holding a password, secret, token or api-key word, or an authorization header", and names `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL=https://hooks.slack.com/…` as staying. That matches the probe this report ran.
2. Deferred to the operator: it predates this diff and is outside Phase 7a's boxes. Two options: a `shapeSecrets` row only `jwt` catches (an unsigned JWT ending in `.`), or extending the binding test to keyword needles. Either one becomes a ledger box on the operator's word. It is named in this phase's handoff.
3. Fixed. The comment now reads "The security check of the url-token rule: an empty password." (`internal/redact/redact_test.go`).
