# Round 2 — Review — phase9 round 2   (2026-10-28)

Range reviewed: the fixes since round 1, `.agents/scratch/p9/round2-interdiff.txt` (code `.agents/scratch/p9/d37-code-r2.diff`, files `.agents/scratch/p9/phase9-files-r2.diff`) against the working tree on HEAD 62de102, plus the records SPEC-fyr-eval, GUIDE-fyr-matrix and BUG-192 as `fyr record get` shows them.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

One new, blocking defect came in with the fixes. `go test .` (the root package, part of `go test ./...`) now FAILS: `TestStateDirHasOneHome` (`statedir_test.go:63`) flags `cmd/fyr/eval_home_test.go:51` and `:57`. The two new subtest NAMES `".config/fyr linked"` and `".config/fyr linked to the old state"` contain the quoted literal `".config/fyr`, which that test forbids anywhere in a `.go` file. The AGENTS.md Setup command (`go test -race … ./...`) is therefore red. Fix: rename the two subtests (for example `"state dir linked"`, `"state dir linked to the old one"`); no logic changes. I confirmed the failure by running `go test . -count=1`. Every round-1 finding, reviewer and security, is otherwise fixed, and each code fix has a test that fails without it (mutations below). `go test ./cmd/fyr -run 'Eval|Help|Register' -count=1` passes, `go test ./internal/harness` passes, `TestFunctionLength` passes, and gofmt and vet are clean.

## Findings
- **[high / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/eval_home_test.go:51,57` — The subtest names `".config/fyr linked"` and `".config/fyr linked to the old state"` trip `TestStateDirHasOneHome` (`statedir_test.go:63`, needle `".config/fyr`): "names the state directory as a literal; use harness.StateDir". The root package test fails, so `go test ./...` is red and the Definition of Done's step 1 cannot pass. The statedir test scans every `.go` file for a quote followed by `.config/fyr`, string content included. Fix: rename the two map keys so they do not contain a quote immediately followed by `.config/fyr` (the other subtest names `".config linked"` is fine). The later `r.t.Run` output, `-run` patterns and the SPEC/matrix text do not name these subtests, so no restatement follows.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/eval_home_test.go` (`treeOf`) — The size and mtime added to the snapshot are not pinned: mutation M12 (revert the `Fprintf` to path and type only) leaves every test green. The migration and ingest tests detect creates and moves, which the path alone shows; nothing in the suite rewrites an existing real-home file. So the stated purpose, "rewritten there", is untested. Either say so in the comment or add a case that rewrites an existing real-home file. No behaviour is at risk today.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/init-project/SKILL.md:66` — The new sentence says a warning on "the ID or the source path" is fixed "by renaming that source file and committing". For a global-log record the ID comes from the log line's title and the path is the log file, not a record file (`internal/brain/import_global.go:87`, `import.go:16`), so there is no file to rename. Rare; add "or, for a global log line, the title in that log" or leave it. Everything else in the sentence is true: the dry run prints the same warnings (`warnImportRedactable(res, dryRun)`, `record_redact.go:49-63`), `record edit` takes only `status`, `title`, `body` and `global` (`record.go:21`), and the position index `i+1` is the order `printImport` lists the records in (`record.go:195`).

## Round-1 findings, one by one

Reviewer:
1. README `fyr eval` row stale — FIXED. `README.md:52` now reads `fyr eval --home DIR <row>...`, names `<home>/.config/fyr/eval/`, and says a missing `--home`, the real home, a home reaching the real state through a link and a `--home` inside a checkout are refused with exit 2 before anything is written. It agrees with `help_text.go:229-246` and SPEC-fyr-eval line 23. `REQUIREMENTS.md:68` left as it was, as advised (immutable).
2. Matrix row for the new refusals — FIXED. GUIDE-fyr-matrix § eval has the new row (record line 109): "test, not run live: `TestEvalRefusesItsHome` … `TestEvalRechecksItsHomeBeforeWriting`". It cites the unit tests and claims no live run. Honest.
3. "before any other check" wording — FIXED. SPEC line 23 now says "after the usage errors and before every refusal that reads the tree and before the state-dir migration"; `cmd/fyr/eval.go:42-46` says the same. The behaviour matches: `eval.go:53-57` (usage errors) then the `evalHomeRefused` call, `writesState` in `run_dispatch.go:174-177`. The comment's line is long and a little ragged; not a finding.
4. init-project sentence — FIXED except the global-log-line edge above (low).
5. BUG-192 "Until one lands" — FIXED. The Prevention text now says the first candidate landed in Phase 9 and points at § Graduated, which names `context/AGENTS.md` § Git and `check-trailers.sh`.

Security:
1. TOCTOU, refusal did not stop the writes — HOLDS. `eval.go:262-265` (`ingestRow`) refuses before `metrics.Open`; `eval.go:185-189` (`recordEval`) refuses before `brain.Add` and returns exit 1 with `eval: record: not written`. `registerClone` still checks first as well (`eval_register.go:34`). The remaining window (a link made between a re-check and the open) is named in SPEC-fyr-eval line 160, so the doc claim is not stronger than the code. Test: `TestEvalRechecksItsHomeBeforeWriting`; mutations M6 (ingestRow check off) and M7 (recordEval check off) each fail it.
2. String identity instead of device/inode — HOLDS. `eval_home.go:104-112` (`sameFile`) uses `os.Stat` plus `os.SameFile` when both exist, the cleaned string otherwise. Mutation M2 (string compare only) fails five subtests, including `a store hard-linked`, which is the case string comparison cannot see. A case variant and a bind mount are claimed in the SPEC and the comment but not exercised directly (the hard link proves the same mechanism). `internal/eval/guard.go` `checkRoots`, which the security report said "suits" the same change, was left alone: not a finding, `--home` no longer reaches it unchecked.
3. sh-agent and per-store links — HOLDS. `eval_home.go:91-95` adds the pair against `real/OldStateDir` and the three store files. M3 and M4 each fail `TestEvalRefusesItsHome`.
4. Dangling link — HOLDS. `dangling` (`eval_home.go:114-121`) is tested for every pair's first path. M1 fails the `a dangling link` subtest.
5. HOME vs the account's home — HOLDS. `realHomes` (`eval_home.go:54-63`) adds the passwd home through `user.LookupId`, never `Current` (which falls back to HOME); a package var is the test seam, restored in `t.Cleanup`. M5 fails the `the account's home, HOME elsewhere` subtest. On a system where the lookup fails, the check falls back to `$HOME` only, which is the round-1 behaviour.
6. Test coverage — HOLDS, with the M12 gap above. Added: `.config/fyr` linked, `..`-and-slash spelling, old state, store link, hard link, dangling, account home, `--list` without `--home` (`TestEvalListNeedsNoHome`; mutation M10 fails it), and the proof that the snapshot can see a migration (`TestEvalHomeSnapshotSeesAMigration`). The "state directory absent before the run" precondition moved into the planted-old-dir setup; M8 (writesState ignoring the refusal) and M9 (runEval refusal off) each fail `TestEvalRefusesItsHome`.

## Mutation record (scratch copy only, `.agents/scratch/p9r2/`)
Each mutant: target text counted once in the file, applied to a fresh copy of the tree under `.agents/scratch/p9r2/m`, `go vet` first, then `go test ./cmd/fyr -run 'Eval|Register' -count=1`. M2 and M5 first failed to build ("declared and not used"); they were re-written to compile and re-run, and only the compiled results are cited.

| Mutant | Result |
|---|---|
| M1 dangling off | FAIL TestEvalRefusesItsHome |
| M2 string-only compare | FAIL TestEvalRefusesItsHome (5 subtests incl. hard link), TestEvalRechecks…, TestRegisterCloneRefusals |
| M3 old-state pair off | FAIL TestEvalRefusesItsHome |
| M4 store pairs off | FAIL TestEvalRefusesItsHome |
| M5 account home off | FAIL TestEvalRefusesItsHome |
| M6 ingestRow re-check off | FAIL TestEvalRechecksItsHomeBeforeWriting |
| M7 recordEval re-check off | FAIL TestEvalRechecksItsHomeBeforeWriting |
| M8 writesState ignores the refusal | FAIL TestEvalRefusesItsHome |
| M9 runEval refusal off | FAIL TestEvalRefusesItsHome |
| M10 `--list` not exempt | FAIL TestEvalListNeedsNoHome |
| M11 first (home == real) pair off | PASS — equivalent: the `.config` pair catches the same home, so not a gap |
| M12 treeOf without size/mtime | PASS — unpinned (finding above) |

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. `firstOf` has a caller; `accountHomeDir` is a test seam with one test caller; no commented-out code.
2. Flow tracing — pass apart from the blocker. start check → `writesState` (no migration) → `runEval` → per-row `registerClone` → `ingestRow` before open → `recordEval` before `brain.Add`; the error text reaches the output through `search.Printable`. SPEC failure row 133 ("`eval: <row> ingest: not ingested: …` for each row, then `eval: record: not written: …`, exit 1") matches `eval.go:174-189`. The fix tests fail without their fixes (table above).
3. Standards conformance — FAIL on `TestStateDirHasOneHome` (finding 1). `TestFunctionLength` passes; function bodies are short (`sharesHome` about 18 lines). No stale restatement found: README row, help text, SPEC line 23, the matrix row and the `eval.go` comment agree; a scan of current guide, spec and deploy records for `fyr eval` found no usage line without `--home` that should have it.
4. Directory layout — pass. `eval_home.go` and its test sit beside `eval.go` in `cmd/fyr`; `eval.go` is 382 lines, the new files 121 and 206.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. Stdlib only (`os`, `os/user`, `os.SameFile`); nothing hand-rolled in auth or crypto.
6. Decoupling — pass. One helper, `sharesRealState`, is shared by `registerClone`, `writesState`, `runEval`, `ingestRow` and `recordEval`; the account-home seam is a package var, restored by the test.

## Not examined
- The full `go test -race ./...` (about 13 minutes under `-race` on a one-CPU box): I ran `go test .`, `./internal/harness` and `./cmd/fyr -run 'Eval|Help|Register|Record|Import|StateDir|Migrat'` (all but the root package pass), not the whole tree.
- macOS behaviour (case-insensitive APFS, `user.LookupId` without cgo) and bind mounts: reasoned from `os.SameFile` semantics, not reproduced.
- `internal/eval/guard.go` `checkRoots` (string-based, unchanged by the fixes).
- The records other than the three named in the dispatch; `.agents/trail.jsonl` content beyond a scan of current guide/spec/deploy bodies for `fyr eval`.
- A live `fyr eval` run (the matrix row says none was made).

## Outcome

Round 1 (main thread, 2026-10-28):
1. README.md:52 (medium) — fixed, on the operator's word through the question popup ("Edit the row (Recommended)"), since README was approved for the map node only: `fyr eval --home DIR <row>...`, sandboxes under `<home>/.config/fyr/eval/`, the refusal sentence.
2. GUIDE-fyr-matrix row (low) — fixed: a row for the `--home` refusals citing `TestEvalRefusesItsHome` and `TestEvalRechecksItsHomeBeforeWriting`, marked "test, not run live".
3. "before any other check" (low) — fixed in SPEC-fyr-eval's `--home` row and the `runEval` comment: after the usage errors, before every refusal that reads the tree.
4. init-project position-named records (low) — fixed: the sentence says how to find a record named by its place, and that an ID or source-path warning is fixed by renaming the source before the real import, since the dry run prints the same warnings.
5. BUG-192 stale prevention sentence (low) — fixed: it now points at § Graduated.

Round 2:
1. Subtest names broke `TestStateDirHasOneHome` (high) — fixed: renamed to "the state directory linked" and "the state directory linked to the old one"; `go test . -run TestStateDirHasOneHome` PASS.
2. treeOf's size and mtime unpinned (low) — fixed: `TestEvalHomeSnapshotSeesAMigration` now also asserts a same-size rewrite changes the snapshot.
3. init-project rename does not fit a global log line (low) — rebutted: Step 4 runs the project import (`fyr record import`), whose every record comes from a file; a global log line is `import --global`, which Step 4 does not run.

No third round (review Steps 4–5 cap it at two); the round-2 fixes were read by the main thread and mutation-checked (the entry loop and the ingest order each fail their test when removed).

title: Security review — ledger Phase 9 D37: fyr eval refuses a missing or real --home (2 rounds)
body:
# Security review — phase9-d37 (2026-10-28)

Range reviewed: working tree vs HEAD 62de102, `git diff -- cmd/fyr` as saved in `.agents/scratch/p9/d37-code.diff` (eval.go, eval_home.go [new], eval_home_test.go [new], eval_register.go, help_text.go, run_dispatch.go); blast radius read: `cmd/fyr/run_dispatch.go` (run, resolveHome, writesState, migrateStateDir), `cmd/fyr/update_checkout.go` samePath, `cmd/fyr/eval.go` (runEval, evalSetup, recordEval, ingestRow), `cmd/fyr/eval_register.go`, `cmd/fyr/eval_register_test.go` TestRegisterCloneRefusals, `internal/eval/run.go` (SandboxRoot, Preflight, Run), `internal/eval/guard.go` (checkRoots, fingerprint), `internal/harness/migrate.go`, `internal/metrics/store.go` Path, `internal/brain/store.go` Path.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

The change does what it says on the cases it names: a missing `--home`, the real home (and its relative, trailing-slash and `..` spellings, since resolveHome cleans with filepath.Abs first), and a home whose `.config` or `.config/fyr` resolves to the real one are refused with exit 2. No state is written and no migration runs before the refusal, because writesState asks the same helper and `eval` resolves no install source in run(). The weak point is how the check is built. `sharesRealState` compares paths **by string after EvalSymlinks**, and **falls back to raw string equality whenever either side does not resolve**. So it misses every route to the same directory that is not a symlink: a case variant of the home on macOS's case-insensitive APFS, and a bind mount. It also misses a dangling link, and the real home's old state directory. The worst problem is not new in this diff but is in its blast radius. The check runs per row, inside registerClone, after the agent's `command(*)` session. When it then fires, the refusal is only *reported*: `ingestRow` still opens `home/.config/fyr/metrics.db` and `recordEval` still runs `brain.Add` on `home/.config/fyr/brain.db`. So a `--home/.config` replaced by a link during a row sends that row's metrics and the testing record into the real stores. None of these is an exploit by an outsider. The operator controls `--home`, and the in-sandbox agent can already write the real home directly with its own permissions. They are guard-completeness gaps against the mistakes and swaps the guard says it stops.

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `cmd/fyr/eval.go:269-286` (ingestRow), `cmd/fyr/eval.go:189` (recordEval brain.Add): this is a TOCTOU, and the refusal does not stop the writes. sharesRealState is checked at start (`eval.go:58`, `run_dispatch.go:177`) and again per row in registerClone (`eval_register.go:34`). The rows run an agent with `command(*)` for minutes under `--home/.config/fyr/eval/...`. If `--home/.config` or `--home/.config/fyr` becomes a link to the real one meanwhile, registerClone returns its "shares its state directory" error, but `metrics.Open(metrics.Path(home))` and `metrics.Ingest` run anyway, and `brain.Add(Home: c.home)` writes the testing record with no re-check at all. The real-home fingerprint (`internal/eval/guard.go:153`) is taken before the ingest and does not watch `--home`, so nothing notices. This was already so before the diff; the diff's comment says the refused case writes nothing, which holds only for the start check. Remediation: in ingestRow, refuse (return before `metrics.Open`) when `sharesRealState(home)` is true, not after the ingest; re-check right before `brain.Add` in recordEval; better still, refuse at the start any symlink at `home`, `home/.config` and `home/.config/fyr` (`os.Lstat`), and re-check that the components are unchanged (Lstat plus `os.SameFile` against the first snapshot) before each store opens.
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `cmd/fyr/update_checkout.go:137-144` samePath, used by `cmd/fyr/eval_home.go:37-46`: identity is checked by comparing paths as strings, not by device and inode. On macOS, where the default APFS is case-insensitive, `--home /Users/KESOKAJ` is the real home. EvalSymlinks returns it as spelled, so it is not refused, and the run writes sandboxes, metrics and the testing record into the real `~/.config/fyr`. A bind mount of the home or of `~/.config` (Linux) gets past it the same way. I did not reproduce this: the box is Linux and a bind mount needs root. The case behaviour of EvalSymlinks on darwin is my reading of Go, so confidence is medium. Remediation: when both sides exist, compare with `os.Stat` plus `os.SameFile` (stdlib; it compares dev and ino, which catches case variants, bind mounts and links alike). Keep the string fallback only for paths that do not exist. The same check suits `checkRoots` (`internal/eval/guard.go:77`).
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/eval_home.go:41-46`: only `.config` and `.config/fyr` are compared, so `--home/.config/fyr` linked to the real `~/.config/sh-agent` (exactly what MigrateStateDir's own error text advises, `internal/harness/migrate.go:45`) is not refused. Probe result 3: `refused=false`. eval then writes into the real pre-rename state directory, which the real home's next writing verb migrates into `~/.config/fyr`. A per-file link such as `--home/.config/fyr/brain.db` pointing at the real brain.db is not refused either (probe 4). Remediation: also compare against `real/.config/sh-agent`. Better, refuse any symlink at `home/.config/fyr` and its store files (`brain.db`, `metrics.db`), or resolve them and refuse anything that lands inside the real home's `.config/fyr` or `.config/sh-agent`.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/update_checkout.go:140-141`: with a dangling link, samePath falls back to string equality. Example: `--home/.config/fyr` points at the real `~/.config/fyr` before that exists, and the check passes (probe 1). Today a later `os.MkdirAll` through the dangling link fails with EEXIST (probe 1), so this fails closed by accident, not by design: a writer that opened the leaf with O_CREATE, or created the target first, would get through. Remediation: when a path does not resolve, use `os.Readlink` on the deepest component that exists, or refuse any symlink component under `home` (as above).
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/eval_home.go:33`: the "real home" is `os.UserHomeDir()`, which is `$HOME`. If `HOME` points elsewhere, for example inside an eval sandbox (where HOME is the sandbox home), under `sudo -E`, or with a scrubbed environment, then `--home <account's real home>` is not refused (probe 5: `refused=false`). The rest of eval (`eval.go:131`, the token and the fingerprint) uses the same notion, so the guard is consistent but narrow. Remediation: also refuse the account's passwd home, `user.Current().HomeDir` from stdlib `os/user` (no dependency needed). Refuse when `--home` matches either that or `$HOME`.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/eval_home_test.go`: coverage is narrower than the code and the help text claim. Covered: missing, the real home, `.config` linked. Not covered: `.config/fyr` linked, which is the loop's second step (the claimed "at any level"); `--list` running without `--home`; relative, trailing-slash and `..` spellings of the real home (correct by resolveHome, but unpinned); a dangling link. TestRegisterCloneRefusals also links only `.config`. treeOf records path and type only, so the claim "nothing is written under the real home" would miss a write that *modifies* an existing file; it catches only creates, removes and moves. I did not run a mutation to confirm that each runEval branch fails the test (budget). Remediation: add a `.config/fyr`-link case and a `--list` case; include size and mtime, or a content hash, in treeOf.

## Checked
- Secrets: none in the diff; refusal messages name the home path only, no credential.
- Injection: `--home` reaches only filepath.Join and EvalSymlinks; refusal output goes through `search.Printable` (`eval.go:97`). No shell or SQL is built from it. The `..` and trailing-slash forms are cleaned by resolveHome (`run_dispatch.go:111`); probe 6 confirms that even raw forms are refused.
- Authz/authn: no auth surface. The refusal is ordered before migrateStateDir (writesState), ResolveSource, Preflight and any MkdirAll; `eval` has `source: false`, so run() resolves nothing before runEval. Ingest/record TOCTOU above.
- Crypto: none touched, none hand-rolled.
- Dependencies: none added. `govulncheck ./...` (full GOPATH path): 0 vulnerabilities reached, 1 in required modules not called (the known GO-2026-5024, per AGENTS.md). npm is not applicable here (no web/ in the diff).
- GCP surface: none touched.
- Tests: `go test ./cmd/fyr -run 'TestEvalRefusesItsHome|TestRegisterCloneRefusals' -count=1 -v`: PASS, all 3 subtests and the register test.
- Probe: copies of samePath and sharesRealState in `.agents/scratch/sec-d37-probe/` (writes only under its own `w/`); results 1-6 are cited above.
- Past bugs: `fyr search --home .agents/scratch/sec-d37-home --refs <path> --kind bug` for every changed file: only BUG-188 (trail.Dirty, unrelated). The search ran against a fresh scratch home, so it sees only this checkout's export, not records held only in the operator's brain.db.

## Not examined
- macOS behaviour (case-insensitive APFS) and bind mounts: reasoned, not reproduced.
- I made no mutation test of the new runEval and writesState branches.
- `internal/eval/row*.go`: I did not read it all for any other write under `--home` between the row and the ingest. `metrics.Ingest` and `brain.Add` internals were not read beyond their `Path` functions.
- `newEvalRig` (the test rig) was not read, so its premise that `r.real` is `$HOME` is inferred from the test's assertions.
- `trail.Register` was not read.
- The non-`cmd/fyr` parts of the working tree (`AGENTS.md`, `context/AGENTS.md`, `skills/init-project/SKILL.md`, `.agents/trail.jsonl`) are outside this dispatch.

---

# Round 2 — Security review — phase9-d37 round 2   (2026-10-28)

Range reviewed: working tree vs HEAD 62de102, `git diff -- cmd/fyr` as saved in `.agents/scratch/p9/d37-code-r2.diff` (eval.go, eval_home.go [new], eval_home_test.go [new], eval_register.go, help_text.go, run_dispatch.go). This round covers the fixes to the round-1 findings in `.agents/scratch/agents/security-2026-10-28-phase9-d37.md`. Blast radius read: `internal/eval/run.go` (Run, runRow step 1), `internal/eval/guard.go` checkRoots, `internal/trail/register.go` Register, `internal/trail/register_key.go` readKey/ensureKey, the WAL pragmas in `internal/search/store.go`, `internal/metrics/store.go` and `internal/brain/store.go`, and the build tags of Go 1.27.3's `os/user`.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

The fixes are real, and four of the six round-1 findings are closed. Paths are now compared by file identity (`os.SameFile`). The old `sh-agent` directory, the three store files and dangling links are checked. The account's passwd home is checked alongside `$HOME`. ingestRow checks again before any store opens, and recordEval checks again before `brain.Add`. All ten refusal subtests and the re-check test pass, and a scratch probe confirms both the hard-link refusal and the dangling-link refusal. No new problem is worse than low. The worst remaining gap is that the check is built from a list. It names `.config`, `.config/fyr` and three store files, so anything else under the state directory gets through. Probe, all `refused=false`: a link at `--home/.config/fyr/eval` to the real `~/.config/fyr/eval`, a link at `brain.db-wal` (the stores run in WAL mode), and a **hard link at `registration.key`**. The key is the one registerClone's own comment says must never be the real one, because the clone would be sealed with it. Also, rows 2..n of a run make their sandboxes under `--home` with no check between rows, so a link planted by row 1 is followed when those sandboxes are created. None of this lets an outsider in: the in-row agent already holds the operator's own permissions. These are gaps in completeness against the swaps the guard says it catches.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/eval_home.go:32` and `:83-101`: the list of checked paths is incomplete. It holds `home`, `.config`, `.config/fyr` (against the real `fyr` and `sh-agent`) and `brain.db`/`metrics.db`/`search.db`. Probe `.agents/scratch/sec-d37-r2-probe` cases A-C show three layouts that are not refused:
  - (A) `.config/fyr/eval` symlinked to the real `~/.config/fyr/eval`. Sandboxes and the linked login land in the real state directory, and checkRoots (`internal/eval/guard.go:62`) refuses only the real home or a parent of it, not a path inside it.
  - (B) `brain.db-wal`/`-shm` linked to the real ones. All three stores are opened with `journal_mode(WAL)`, so SQLite opens those side files by name.
  - (C) `registration.key` hard-linked to the real key. `readKey`'s openRegular refuses a symlink but not a hard link, and `Register` then seals the clone with the real home's key, which is exactly what `cmd/fyr/eval_register.go:25-27` says must not happen.

  The help text promises a refusal when `--home` "reaches its state directory through a link", which is broader than this. Remediation: stop listing names. Walk `home/.config/fyr` (Lstat, no follow) and refuse when any entry is a symlink, or when any regular file has `Nlink > 1` and is the same file (`os.SameFile`) as an entry under either real state directory. At minimum, add `eval`, `registration.key` and the `-wal`/`-shm` suffixes of each store.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/eval/run.go:123-125` and `:157`: nothing is re-checked between rows. All rows run inside `eval.Run` before recordEval ingests any of them, and each row's step 1 runs `MkdirAll(SandboxRoot(o.Home)/stamp)` with no `sharesRealState`. If row 1 links `--home/.config`, row 2's sandbox is made, and its agent runs, under the real `~/.config/fyr/eval/`. Only the stores are protected now (by the ingest and record re-checks), not the sandbox tree. Remediation: pass a check callback in `eval.Options`, or call `sharesRealState(o.Home)` before each `runRow`, and stop the run with every later row unrun.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/eval.go:264` vs `:280-281`, and `:187` vs `:193`: the re-check does not bind to what is opened. Between the check and the open, `metrics.Open` and `brain.Add` resolve the path afresh. On Linux, rows that left processes are skipped before the open, which shrinks the window. It stays open on other systems (procsChecked false) and against a process that escaped the process group. Remediation: re-check after the open as well (open, `sharesRealState`, close without writing if shared), or open the state directory once via `os.Root` and compare it to the start snapshot with `os.SameFile`.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/eval_home_test.go:160-171` (TestEvalRechecksItsHomeBeforeWriting): the ingest half does not pin the order it claims. It calls ingestRow with an empty `Dir`. Without the re-check, `realDirs` would return nil before any open, so the assertion "the real metrics store was not opened" holds either way. Only the `err == nil` check fails without the fix. A re-check moved after `metrics.Ingest` would still pass. Remediation: give the row a sandbox with `home/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversations` as real directories, so that without the check the code would reach `metrics.Open`. The recordEval half is sound: without the fix, `brain.Add` would create `real/.config/fyr/brain.db`, and treeOf sees it.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `cmd/fyr/eval_home.go:67-73` (accountHomeDir): `LookupId` without cgo. Go 1.27.3's `os/user/lookup_unix.go` is `(!cgo && !darwin) || osusergo`, so a `CGO_ENABLED=0` Linux binary reads `/etc/passwd` only. For an account that lives only in LDAP or sssd, it errors, the account home is silently dropped, and the guard falls back to `$HOME` alone (fails open, the same as round 1). On darwin, `cgo_lookup_syscall.go` (`!osusergo && darwin`) goes through libc without cgo, so macOS release binaries are fine. With cgo and NSS, a network directory can make each call block. Remediation: note the fallback in the doc comment. Optionally print a one-line warning when `LookupId` errors, rather than skipping it silently.
- **[info / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/eval_home.go:25`, `:95`: the refusal message is misleading. A dangling link to an unrelated place is refused, which is the safe direction (probe G), but the message says `--home X is the real home Y, or shares its state directory`, naming a real home it may have nothing to do with. Remediation: give the dangling case its own reason ("a link under --home does not resolve").

## Outcome
- R1-1 (TOCTOU, the refusal did not stop the writes): **narrowed**. ingestRow (`eval.go:264`) refuses before any store opens, and recordEval (`eval.go:187`) refuses before `brain.Add`. Three gaps remain, all in the findings above: the check-to-open window, the missing re-check between rows, and an ingest test that does not pin the order.
- R1-2 (identity compared by string): **closed** for paths that exist. `sameFile` uses `os.Stat` plus `os.SameFile` (dev+ino), which covers case variants on APFS, bind mounts and hard links (the test "a store hard-linked"; probe H). The string fallback is kept only when a side does not exist. checkRoots (`guard.go:62-93`) still compares resolved strings, as noted in round 1. It is not changed by this diff.
- R1-3 (`sh-agent` and per-file links): **closed for what was named**, and the same class remains. The `sh-agent` link and the store-file links are refused, but `eval/`, `-wal`/`-shm` and `registration.key` are not (first finding).
- R1-4 (dangling link): **closed**. `dangling()` refuses any symlink whose target does not resolve (test "a dangling link"; probe G). This is fail-safe: an unrelated dangling link is also refused, which errs in the safe direction (only the message is off, see the info finding).
- R1-5 (`$HOME` only): **closed** where the account database answers. `LookupId` is used, never `Current`, so a changed HOME does not move the check (test "the account's home, HOME elsewhere"). It falls back to `$HOME` alone when LookupId fails (the cgo finding).
- R1-6 (test coverage): **closed** except for the ingest order. There are now cases for `.config/fyr` linked, the old state, a store linked, a store hard-linked, a dangling link, the `..` spelling, the account home, `--list` without `--home`, and a migration snapshot. treeOf now records size and mtime.

## Checked
- Secrets: none added; the refusal messages name paths only.
- Injection: no new sink. `--home` reaches only Stat, Lstat and Join. Output goes through `search.Printable` (`eval.go:188`).
- Authz/authn: no auth surface. Order: writesState asks `evalHomeRefused`, so a refused home is never migrated, and runEval refuses before Getwd and ResolveSource. False positives, from the probe: a legitimate fresh home (E), a home whose `.config` links to an unrelated directory (D), and a home inside the real home (F, the guide's `~/sandbox/...` layout) are all accepted. No panic path: StateDir splits into constants, and `firstOf` guards an empty slice.
- Crypto: none touched in this diff. `seal`/`ensureKey` were read only for the key-path question, not reviewed as crypto.
- Dependencies: none added; `os/user` is stdlib. `govulncheck ./...` (full GOPATH path, go1.27.3): 0 vulnerabilities reached, 1 in a required module not called (the known GO-2026-5024). npm is not applicable.
- GCP surface: none.
- Cost: about 37-46 µs per `sharesRealState` call on this box (probe, 1000 calls, with and without cgo, with LookupId). It runs about 2 + 2×rows + 1 times per invocation, which is negligible next to minute-long rows.
- Tests: `go test ./cmd/fyr -run 'TestEvalRefusesItsHome|TestEvalRechecks|TestEvalListNeedsNoHome|TestEvalHomeSnapshot|TestRegisterCloneRefusals' -count=1 -v`: PASS, all 10 subtests of TestEvalRefusesItsHome with none skipped, plus the other 4 tests. No `t.Parallel` in `cmd/fyr` tests, so the package-level `accountHomeDir` seam has no race.
- Probe: `.agents/scratch/sec-d37-r2-probe/` holds copies of the working-tree functions and writes only under its `w/`. Results are A/B/C/D/E/F refused=false and G/H refused=true.

## Not examined
- No mutation of the source per branch (I may not edit source). The ingest-order gap above was found by reading, not by a mutated run.
- macOS and bind mounts were not run: SameFile's dev+ino semantics there are reasoned, not reproduced.
- `metrics.Ingest` and `brain.Add` internals: I did not read whether they open any other file under the state directory (beyond the WAL side files).
- `internal/eval` row steps 2-15 (prepare, session, afterSession): not re-read for other writes under `--home`.
- `openRegular` (`internal/trail`): its body was not read. That it refuses symlinks is taken from readKey's doc comment. Probe C covers the hard-link case independently.
- The non-`cmd/fyr` files in the working tree are outside this dispatch.

## Outcome (main thread)

Round 1, all six fixed or narrowed in `cmd/fyr/eval_home.go`, `cmd/fyr/eval.go` and `cmd/fyr/eval_home_test.go`, each fix pinned by a subtest that fails without it (mutation record in the round-2 reviewer report):
1. Writes after the refusal (medium) — narrowed: `ingestRow` refuses before any store opens and `recordEval` before `brain.Add`; the window between a re-check and the open stays, written into SPEC-fyr-eval § Known limits.
2. String identity (medium) — fixed: `os.SameFile` when both paths exist (pinned by the hard-linked store case; case variants and bind mounts reasoned, not reproduced on this box).
3. `.config/fyr` to the old state dir, a store link, a dangling link (low) — fixed: the old `~/.config/sh-agent`, every entry in the state dir, and any dangling link are refused.
4. Dangling fallback (low) — fixed with 3.
5. `$HOME` only (low) — fixed: the account's home from `user.LookupId` too (seam `accountHomeDir`, pinned).
6. Test coverage (low) — fixed: `.config/fyr` level, `--list` without `--home`, `..` spelling, dangling link, mtime and size in the snapshot.

Round 2:
1. Fixed name list (low) — fixed: every entry directly in `<home>/.config/fyr` is compared with the real entry of the same name (stores, `-wal`/`-shm`, `registration.key`, `eval/`); pinned by the hard-linked key case, which fails with the loop removed.
2. No re-check between rows; the re-check does not bind the opened store (low) — accepted and written into SPEC-fyr-eval § Known limits: the rows loop is `internal/eval.Run`, outside the D37 box's `cmd/fyr` scope, and a following row's ingest and the record are refused.
3. The ingest half of the re-check test did not pin the order (low) — fixed: the sandbox now has the directories the ingest reads, and with the check removed the real metrics store is opened (the test fails).
4. `LookupId` without cgo (low) — accepted, written into SPEC-fyr-eval § Known limits.
5. The message for a dangling link says "or shares its state directory" (info) — accepted: the refusal is right and the message names the path.

title: Review — cold read of the visible-dream plan (2026-10-28)
body:
# Review — plan-visible-dream cold read   (2026-10-28)

Range reviewed: `.agents/scratch/plan-visible-dream.md` (cold-reader check) and the code surfaces it names: `internal/dream/{run,agy_home,dream,prompt,run_dry,timer,run_files}.go`, `internal/metrics/agy.go`, `internal/search/{dream,dream_workspace}.go`, `cmd/fyr/{verb_dream,ctx_verbs,help_text,main}.go`, `REQUIREMENTS.md` R0/R3/R7, `README.md` map, `.agents/scratch/ledger/p8a/{agy-changelog.txt,proposal.md,d35.md}`.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: design needs revision / implementation not ready

Worst first: the plan's central safety claim (R3 "no tools" holds in the visible branch because a settings check passes) rests on a check whose rule set is a guess. D35 says `toolPermission: strict` was never probed and "what plan mode permits is not documented" (`d35.md:5-6`), yet `visibleHome` accepts `strict` and an unset key, and A4 only checks that the model happened not to call a tool. The check ignores `trustedWorkspaces` (the private branch writes it, `agy_home.go:96`), the changelog's "setting that allows access outside your workspace" and "cycle mode" (`agy-changelog.txt:620`), and the workspace-read grant (`:546`). It also does not use the read-only oracle the changelog documents (`agy -p "/permissions"`, `:656`). Second, hourly cadence plus a no-cooldown retry multiplies failed dreams and visible conversations. Third, "an agy process" is undefined for the `remote-control` daemon, `mcp`, `update` and an exe replaced mid-session. Several citations and restatement lists are wrong (below).

## Findings (gaps)

- **[high / confidence: medium]** Plan § The branch rules 2-3, Risks A4 — the guarantee "no tool without review" is asserted, not verified. Gaps: (a) `strict` and "unset = request-review" are unprobed (`d35.md:6`); the private branch's own comment says "explicit, never agy's default (security review round 2)" (`agy_home.go:94-95`), so the plan relies on exactly the default the harness chose not to trust. (b) `trustedWorkspaces`, the outside-workspace access setting, the cycle-mode and `always-proceed` mode (`changelog:534,620`) are not read by `visibleHome`. (c) Plan mode behaviour in print mode is "not documented" (D35 4), and V2 only tests an allow rule. (d) The changelog documents `agy -p "/permissions"` as a non-interactive read-only report (`:656`); the plan does not consider or reject it as the effective-permission oracle, which would replace hand-parsing two files plus an unknown project file. Needs a probe-and-record task or a D-row (cite `proposal.md:11`, which already warns a new permission source "would bypass the check").
- **[high / confidence: medium]** Failure modes table — the hourly retry. A project whose dream fails (`invalid output`, timeout, auth) does not advance its watermark (`run.go:130-137`), so it re-runs every hour while agy is open (previously once a night), each run up to `cliTimeout` 10 min of the operator's quota and, in the visible branch, each leaves another conversation in `/resume`. The plan has no cooldown, no cap and no growth statement for the operator's store ("Today it is deleted"). It only rejects a no-op log line.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** § The process check — "a process named `agy`" is undefined for: `agy remote-control` is "a background daemon (start, status, stop)" (`agy --help`), and `mcp`/`mic-serve`/`update` are also `agy` processes; a daemon makes the check permanently true, defeating D36 4's purpose. A binary replaced by `agy update` mid-session reads as `/path/agy (deleted)` from `readlink`, base name `agy (deleted)`, so a live session is missed. `/proc/<pid>` is owned by root for non-dumpable processes. Local A1 evidence: `~/.local/bin/agy` is a plain ELF (so `exe` works); no agy was running to test.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** § Surfaces, wrong or incomplete restatement list: (a) `skills/dream/SKILL.md:3` is a skill DESCRIPTION naming "The nightly `fyr dream` job", missing from the plan, whose skills sentence says "prose only, no description" and whose grep (Phase 2) omits `skills/dream`. A description change brings `TestSkillListingBudget` and the AGENTS.md release rule (a changed skill needs an Antigravity run). (b) `README.md` also says "nightly" at line 3 ("a nightly consolidation") and in the line-19 table row ("in the nightly dream"); the plan names only 50, 82, 114, 116. (c) `cmd/fyr/dream_arms_test.go:36` asserts the old install message verbatim; not named. (d) `run_dry.go:26` prints "HOME a private copy with no grants" and `agyAuthHint`'s text (`agy_home.go:138`) says "dream job's private HOME": both wrong in the visible branch. (e) Records restating the schedule (`GUIDE-testing` § 3e, `DEPLOY-local`, `GUIDE-eval`) were not searched; Phase 2's grep covers files only.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** Citations: the plan cites "agy changelog 1.4.9 lines 175, 252, 324, 166" with no file. They sit under versions 1.3.4, 1.2.16, 1.2.9, 1.3.4 in `.agents/scratch/ledger/p8a/agy-changelog.txt` (gitignored scratch). Line 324 is a FIX for corruption from dropped file locks, offered in A5 as "two agy processes on one store are safe"; it proves no such guarantee. Line 166 (browser Settings modal) is the only evidence for rule 4's "project-level settings file in the working directory"; line 404 ("CLI, shared, and project configuration files") is closer, but the project file's location is unknown, and rule 4 checks only `dream-work`, not ancestors (changelog `:250` loads `.agents/` manifests from every directory between cwd and the project root).
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** § The branch, `realRun`/`project` lifecycle: `r.env` is one field set once (`run.go:64`) and `agyHome` is created once with a deferred cleanup (`run.go:59-63`). The plan says the branch is re-decided per call and "private: today's path unchanged" and "visible: no login copy". Unspecified: lazy creation and cleanup of the private home when the branch flips mid-run; per-call env; that `checkAgy` (`run.go:56`, `run_dry.go:17`) demands a `$HOME` login before any branch is chosen, contradicting "a visible branch with no `$HOME` login is fine"; whether a private-branch build failure fails the project or the run (`r.fail` is run-level, exit 2); and what "asks once before the first project" adds beyond the per-call ask.
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** D5 path equality: `firstWorkspace` returns `filepath.Clean` of the URI path (`metrics/agy.go:100`), `judge` compares cleaned strings. The plan compares to `filepath.Join(home, StateDir, "dream-work")` with no `EvalSymlinks`/macOS `/private` rule, so agy recording a resolved path defeats the exclusion; the unit fixtures write whichever string the test chooses and cannot show it. Only V1/V3 on a real agy can; make V3 explicitly compare the stored URI. Also `agyConversations(src,tmp)` (`metrics/agy.go:68`) and `newWorkspaces(root)` (`search/dream.go:142`) take no `home`; the plumbing is unstated.
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** Phase 4's first task (A2/A3) reads KEY NAMES from the operator's real files. If the operator has no allow rule, the key shape of an allow rule cannot be learned that way, so rule 3 stays unconfirmed. It also touches the real home (R6, cited by the plan only for `--home`). Needs a source for the shape (agy docs, a scratch home with a rule added through `agy`), not the operator's files.
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** Phase 1 lands R0/R3, README map (solid olive edge) and specs saying "hourly" and "visible" before Phases 2-4 build them. AGENTS.md rule 4 says nothing is drawn solid before it works for every place (macOS is unverified until A2), and no sentence forbids a tag/preflight between Phase 1 and Phase 5; `fyr check` (SPEC-fyr-check) may report doc-vs-binary drift in that window, yet Phase 1 expects "no new finding".
- **[low / confidence: high]** Naming collision: "A2" is Assumption A2 (rules-file key) AND "ledger A2" (the operator's Mac run, REQUIREMENTS line "R10 ... verified only by the operator's A2 run", Phase 5). A reader cannot tell which.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `openRegular(p, follow=false)` refuses a symlinked final component only; a dotfiles-managed `settings.json` symlink (the repo already reads `~/.config/fyr` "through a dotfiles link", `open_unix.go:15-17`) sends the visible branch private forever, silently. State that this is the intent. Rule 1's macOS `Library/Keychains` is a directory, not an `openRegular` read.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** § Interfaces process check and E2E 3 vs `realRun`: `harness.ConfigDir` (`run.go:25`) does `MkdirAll` before the lock, so "writes nothing under `~/.config/fyr/`" needs the check before line 25, not merely before the lock; Phase 2's test lists an existing directory and would not see it. `lock` leaves `dream.lock` behind, so the lock mutation is observable (checked).
- **[low / confidence: medium]** § Prompt first line: today `head` is `instructions + "\n\nProject: <name>\n"` (`prompt.go:66`). The plan says `dreaming: <name>`, a blank line, then `instructions`; unstated whether the `Project:` line stays and that the `IMPORTANT: every tool call...` warning (`prompt.go:11`) is no longer the first line of the message (`fit`/`collect_fit_test.go` equality, SPEC wording "prompt's opening warning").
- **[low / confidence: medium]** REQUIREMENTS: R7 ("harness state in `~/.config/fyr/` and nowhere else") is touched (conversations now persist in `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli`) and not cited; R3's new text ("beside the conversation the CLI itself keeps") probably covers it, but the plan should say so. R9 is not touched (D4 is consistent).
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `fyr status` (`StatusLine`, `dream.go:217`) says "timer installed" for a stale nightly unit; the only upgrade notice is README and a handoff. An unreinstalled user silently stops dreaming (nightly at 03:00 with no agy). No `status` hint is planned.
- **[low / confidence: low]** Undefined or uncited terms: `AI` and `user` as verify tags; `SD15`, `D32 3`, `D35`, `D36`, `Remote Control`, `ledger item 38`, `ADR-0NN` vs `ADR-073`; "the ledger's recipe (`PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` § The sandbox, recipe)" is by record ID only; the proposal file lives in gitignored scratch (D1 copies the text, good).
- **[low / confidence: medium]** Spec records: Phase 1 edits `SPEC-fyr-dream`, `SPEC-fyr-delivery`, `SPEC-fyr-metrics` but names no mechanism (`fyr record edit`) and no re-stamp (recent handoffs mention "SPEC-fyr-metrics re-stamped").

## (2) Scope
Beyond D36: the per-call re-check of settings (D6, implementer), the `--all --dry-run` "agy process:" line (D2 covers the check, not the dry-run line), the D5 exclusion in `metrics` and `search` (D-row by implementer, justified as needed by the visible branch, but its author is "implementer", not the operator), and `harness.DreamWork`. None is configuration or a second endpoint; the dry-run line and D5 are the ones to confirm with the operator (D8 is already put to them). No gap for config knobs.

## (3) Readiness — questions an implementer must ask
1. BLOCKING: which permission keys/values make a home "visible" (`strict`, unset, `trustedWorkspaces`, outside-workspace and cycle-mode settings, project file location), and may `agy -p /permissions` be the oracle? Two careful implementers will build different guards.
2. BLOCKING: retry policy for a failed project under an hourly timer (cooldown, per-day cap, or accept 24 runs/conversations a day).
3. BLOCKING: what counts as "an agy process" (the remote-control daemon, `agy update`, a `(deleted)` exe, non-dumpable processes) and what `agyRunning` returns for them.
4. NON-BLOCKING: private-home lifecycle across per-call branch flips, `checkAgy` split, and failure level (project vs run). Default implied: lazy, per project; confirm.
5. NON-BLOCKING: whether the `Project:` line stays under `dreaming:`.
6. NON-BLOCKING: symlink handling for D5's `dream-work` path, and how `home` reaches `agyConversations` and `newWorkspaces`.
7. NON-BLOCKING: the full restatement list (skills/dream description, README lines 3 and 19, `dream_arms_test.go`, dry-run text, auth hint, records).
8. NON-BLOCKING: whether a release may be cut between Phase 1 and Phase 5.

## (4) Sizing
Phase 4 cannot be finished from the plan alone: its first task needs the operator's real settings keys and an unresolved choice of source (see the A2 finding), and it bundles research, a security-sensitive guard, a `realRun` restructure and the prompt change plus `reviewer` and `security`; split it (research and guard, then wiring). Phase 5 holds user-only boxes (operator's `/resume` look, the Mac), so a fresh session cannot close it; the plan routes them to the handoff, which is acceptable but means "plan closed" is not reachable in one session. Phases 1-3 are each finishable. Phase 2's A1 can only be completed on a machine with a running agy (none here).

## Criteria
1. Dead code — n/a (plan, no diff); the plan's `psList`/`procRoot` seams are test-justified.
2. Flow tracing — fail: `r.env`/`agyHome`/`checkAgy` lifecycle, ConfigDir-before-check, home plumbing into `metrics`/`search`.
3. Standards conformance — fail: restatement list incomplete (skills/dream description, README 3 and 19, test, dry-run and auth-hint strings, records); R7 uncited; AGENTS.md rule 4 vs a solid map edge before code.
4. Directory layout — pass: new files `agy_process.go`, `agy_visible.go`, `harness.DreamWork` sit where the packages already keep their kind; `timer.go` 446 lines is correctly kept from growing.
5. Simplicity — pass with a question: file parsing re-implements permission resolution agy offers via `/permissions`; no new dependency; nothing hand-rolled auth/crypto.
6. Decoupling — pass: harness/search/metrics already import harness (`go list -deps`), so `DreamWork` creates no cycle.

## Not examined
Records `GUIDE-testing`, `DEPLOY-local`, `GUIDE-eval`, `SPEC-fyr-*` bodies (not fetched; the restatement search over records was not run); `SPEC-fyr-check` behaviour on the Phase 1 window; `internal/dream/fakeagy_test.go` beyond its HOME handling; `timer_install.go` `planTimer`; `internal/dream/collect_fit*.go`; D35's full capture; macOS behaviour; no `agy` process available to test A1.

title: Review — visible-dream Phase 1: requirements, ADR-073, map and docs (docs lens)
body:
# Review — visible-dream Phase 1 docs   (2026-10-28)

Range reviewed: `.agents/scratch/vd1/review-input.diff` — the uncommitted working tree over HEAD 31d02d0: REQUIREMENTS.md, README.md, AGENTS.md, ROADMAP.md, and the bodies of SPEC-fyr-dream, SPEC-fyr-delivery and the new ADR-073 (read from `--home .agents/scratch/home-trail`). Lens: code + docs together. The diff has no code, so the code lens is the cross-check of the docs against `internal/dream` and `cmd/fyr`.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

One blocking item: REQUIREMENTS.md R7 (line 39) still says "the nightly dreamer's redacted prompt (R3)" while R3 now says hourly. This is a restatement of a changed requirement left standing, in the file that is immutable without the operator's approval, so the fix is a proposed one-word edit for the operator. Everything else is non-blocking. The map is sound: 23 edges (0-22), every `linkStyle` index still points at the right edge, the new edge is dashed and olive, and `TestHarnessMap` passes. The remaining findings are present-tense "hourly" claims with no qualifier while the binary still runs nightly, a few spec paragraph and row defects, and living docs that still say "nightly" and are true of today's binary (the plan schedules them for Phases 2, 3 and 5). `fyr check` shows nothing this diff introduced.

## Findings

### BLOCKING
- **[high / confidence: high]** `REQUIREMENTS.md:39` (R7) — "two things leave it … the nightly dreamer's redacted prompt (R3)". R3 (line 19) now says the timer is hourly and acts only while an `agy` session runs. The plan's own restatement list (Surfaces, plan line 29) names only R0 line 7 and R3 line 19, and Phase 1's check "that sentence and the citation only" would have hidden the miss. `git grep -i nightly -- REQUIREMENTS.md` returns this one line. Fix: propose to the operator "the dreamer's redacted prompt (R3)" (drop "nightly"), get approval, and land it in the same commit. Do not edit it without approval.

### NON-BLOCKING
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `README.md:3`, `:19`, `:82` (dreamer node), `:115` (legend), `:117` (In words), `AGENTS.md:14` (rule 1), `AGENTS.md:52` — each states "hourly, while an `agy` session of yours runs" as fact. The binary still installs and runs the nightly 03:00 timer: `internal/dream/timer.go:121` (`OnCalendar=*-*-* 03:00`), `cmd/fyr/verb_dream.go:68` prints "runs nightly at 03:00", `cmd/fyr/help_text.go:41,203`. Only README row 50 (`:50`, "until its Phase 5 the binary still runs nightly and privately"), the legend's dashed-line clause and the two specs carry a qualifier. A checkout place that follows `main` gets README and AGENTS.md saying hourly beside source that is nightly. Plan D16 limits the "being built" sentence to the edited specs, so this follows the approved plan, but a reader of the intro paragraph or the map node gets a false present-tense claim. Fix: one clause in `README.md:3` and in `:117`, or accept this explicitly in the Phase 1 outcome. AGENTS.md rule 4 says nothing is drawn solid before it works; a node label is not a line, so it is not violated, but the label overstates.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** SPEC-fyr-dream § What it does, the paragraph beginning "**The cooldown (ADR-073).**" — the original paragraph "It looks at every project in the global search index … Otherwise, when anything changed since the project's watermark:" was glued onto the end of the cooldown paragraph. Its subject "It" now reads as the cooldown, and the whole target-selection, registration and in-use text sits under the cooldown label. The following numbered list ("Collect", "Ask") still hangs off it. Fix: break after "`--project` ignores it: the operator asked." and restore a subject ("`fyr dream --all` looks at every project …").
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** SPEC-fyr-dream § Failure modes row 1 and step 4 — the diff removes "no Antigravity login" from the exit-2-before-any-project row, removes "login" from the dry run's checks, and says a missing login fails the project (`fail <reason>`, exit 1). The code still does the old thing: `internal/dream/agy_home.go:30-48` (`checkAgy` calls `findLogin`) exits 2 before any project and in a dry run. The top-of-section "Being built … until Phase 5" sentence is the only qualifier. A reader of the Failure modes table gets behaviour the binary does not have. Fix: say in that row (or in a "Being built" note on the table) that the login check moves in Phase 4b, or keep the old row until then.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `AGENTS.md:15-17` (rules 3 and 4) and `README.md:115` (legend, "A dashed line is a gap: done by hand, or limited to one machine") — the new dashed `dreamer` → `sessions` line means "drawn before it is built". Rule 3 says a path change lands "in ONE commit with the code"; this commit has the map line and no code. Rule 4 defines dashed as done by hand or one machine, and its only exception is the provider lines that never turn solid. The authority is plan D16/D17 and ADR-073 (the operator approved), but neither rule nor the legend's last sentence says that a line may be dashed because it is not built yet. Fix: one clause in rule 4 and the legend ("or drawn before the code that makes it true, until its plan closes").
- **[low / confidence: high]** Not in the diff, restating what it reverses; each is true of today's binary, and the plan assigns them to later phases (plan lines 36 and 152). Listed so none is lost:
  - `DEPLOY-local` (record lines 58 and 64: "nightly at 03:00", "not found at 03:00")
  - `SPEC-fyr-metrics` (lines 12 and 73)
  - `SPEC-fyr-memory-loop` (line 4)
  - `GUIDE-testing` (line 143, § 3e)
  - `skills/dream/SKILL.md:3` (the description), `skills/handoff/SKILL.md:178`, `skills/project-memory/SKILL.md:8,56`, `skills/retro/SKILL.md:48`
  - code and strings: `cmd/fyr/ctx_verbs.go:76-77`, `cmd/fyr/help_text.go:41,203`, `cmd/fyr/main.go:18`, `cmd/fyr/verb_dream.go:54,59,68`, `internal/dream/timer.go:3,101,109,118,121,165,300,444`, and the comments the plan lists.
  - The diff's own sentence says "until its Phase 5 the binary still runs nightly", which covers them. None carries its own marker. `SPEC-fyr-delivery` line 83 ("with the nightly timer", under "Built and shipped v3.1.0") is accurate and must stay as is.

### NIT
- `ROADMAP.md:9` says "Phase 1 is done" while the plan's Phase 1 checkpoint box (review, commit, change record, handoff) is still open and nothing is committed. It is true only once this commit lands.
- Plan D10 (not in the diff) names the cooldown file "`state.json` `attempts`". The spec and ADR-073 say `dream-state.json`, which is right: `state.json` is the install manifest (README map, `configDir` node). Fix the plan text before Phase 2, or the implementer may put the field in the wrong file.
- `README.md:40` (`fyr status` row) does not mention the "older schedule" line that SPEC-fyr-dream § Consumers now lists. It is future behaviour, so fix it with Phase 2.
- `fyr check` shows 7 findings; the plan expected "no finding beyond the 6" the Phase 9 handoff lists. The 7th (`SPEC-fyr-check spec-stale`, "1 commit … since 72e8ace") comes from commit 1fe6d12, which is before this diff. See Criteria 5 below.

## Answers to the five asks

1. **Map.** Edges in order: 0 edit-ship, 1 ship-repo, 2 ship-preflight, 3 preflight-repo, 4 preflight-releases, 5 repo-checkout, 6 releases-binary, 7 repo-zip, 8 releases-zip, 9-11 place-installer, 12 installer-homeFiles, 13 homeFiles-sessions, 14 sessions-configDir, 15 config-retroHarness, 16 retroHarness-edit, 17 sessions-dreamer, 18 dreamer-configDir, 19 dreamer-provider (dashed), **20 dreamer-sessions (new, dashed)**, 21 evalRun-configDir, 22 evalRun-provider (dashed). `linkStyle` 0,1,5,6,7,8 teal; 2,3,4 plum; 9-13 indigo; 14-16 amber; 17-22 olive. That is 23 edges, none uncovered, and it matches the old split with the two eval edges shifted from 20,21 to 21,22. Line styles match the legend: the two provider lines dashed ("only things that leave the machine"), the new line dashed "until … builds it". Rule 1 (the dream timer is neither a way in nor a way back) is unchanged apart from "hourly" and ADR-073. Rule 4 is satisfied in effect (new line dashed, not solid), but its wording does not cover this dashed meaning (see non-blocking finding 4). Rule 6 is not touched: README's new text says nothing about what a tag delivers. `go test -count=1 -run TestHarnessMap ./cmd/fyr` passes. The test does not check `linkStyle` indices, so they were checked by hand above.
2. **Restatements.** R7 `REQUIREMENTS.md:39` is the one miss with no plan owner (blocking). The README, AGENTS.md and R0/R3 copies are in the diff. The rest are listed above; the plan places them in Phases 2 (code comments, strings), 3 (`SPEC-fyr-metrics`) and 5 (skills, `SPEC-fyr-memory-loop`, `GUIDE-testing`, `DEPLOY-local`). `context/`, `agents/` and `rules/` hold no "nightly" or schedule claim. `git grep` hits in `skills/api-auth-gcp`, `data-gcp` and `operate-gcp` are unrelated.
3. **Internal consistency.** Cadence is hourly (R3, README, ADR, spec `OnCalendar=hourly`/`Persistent=true`, plist Minute 0). Session check is the same in R3, ADR-073, the spec and README row 50 (uid, name `agy`, no `-p`, no subcommand, exit 0 or exit 2, `--project` never asks). Cooldown is 24 h, success or failure, `--all` only, `--project` ignores it, and the spec and ADR agree. The branches match: visible = `--home` plus oracle, private = login copy from `$HOME`. The state file is `dream-state.json` `attempts`, in the spec, the ADR and the file table (the plan's D10 says `state.json`, a NIT). The R3 text equals plan D1 verbatim; R0 equals it too. One spec defect is the glued paragraph. Existing behaviour checked against the code: `dream-work` (`run.go:65`), `agyHome`/`findLogin` described correctly for the private branch, `TimeoutStartSec=2h` present. Not yet in the code, as the spec says: `attempts`, the oracle, the hourly unit.
4. **Accuracy.** Stated as built without a qualifier: the README and AGENTS.md "hourly" claims (finding 1) and the Failure modes login rows (finding 3). The other new behaviour (session check, cooldown, oracle, `agy home visible` lines, `attempts`, older-schedule status) is either under a "Being built" sentence (the two specs, README row 50, the legend's dashed-line clause) or in ADR-073's Consequences ("until Phase 5 the binary still runs nightly"). Nothing was found in the code that contradicts a claim about existing behaviour.
5. **`go run ./cmd/fyr check --home .agents/scratch/home-trail`** (read-only): 7 findings, exit 1: 5 `.agents/docs` path findings (`GUIDE-fyr-matrix:50,50,51`, `SPEC-fyr-search:26,37`) and 2 spec-stale (`SPEC-fyr-check`, `SPEC-fyr-search`). None names SPEC-fyr-dream, SPEC-fyr-delivery or ADR-073, and none is introduced by the diff. The extra `SPEC-fyr-check` stale finding comes from 1fe6d12, which touched `cmd/fyr` after that spec's last update (`git log 72e8ace..HEAD -- internal/check cmd/fyr …` returns only 1fe6d12). The ledger handoff's count of 6 at that commit appears to have missed it; I did not re-run `fyr check` at 1fe6d12 to confirm.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass: no code in the diff. The comments naming "nightly" in code are Phase 2's.
2. Flow tracing — pass with notes: map edges and `linkStyle` consistent; spec, ADR and requirements agree on the session check, cooldown, branches and state file. Spec paragraph glued (non-blocking); plan D10 names the wrong state file (NIT).
3. Standards conformance — fail: R7 still says "nightly" (blocking); present-tense hourly claims in README and AGENTS.md; rules 3 and 4 and the legend do not cover a dashed line drawn before the code.
4. Directory layout — pass: only existing files and trail records changed; scratch files are under `.agents/scratch/`.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass: no code or dependency. The design relies on agy's own `/permissions` and `/config` reports and hand-parses no settings (ADR-073). No auth or crypto is hand-rolled.
6. Decoupling — pass: this is a docs change. The only coupling note is the oracle-to-call window, which is recorded as a Known limit.

## Not examined
- Did not run the full `go test ./...` or `govulncheck`; only `TestHarnessMap` (`cmd/fyr`) and `fyr check`.
- Did not re-run `fyr check` at 1fe6d12, so the 6-versus-7 difference is inferred from `git log`.
- Did not check the oracle, session check and cooldown behaviour against agy 1.4.9 or the plan's AS1-AS5; they are not built, and the diff only describes them.
- Did not read ADR-047a, ADR-067 or the ledger's D32-D36 for fidelity of the quoted operator words (the quotes match the plan's D1; I did not read the ledger).
- Did not read `skills/` files other than by `git grep` hits, nor `GUIDE-eval`, and did not run any behavioural eval.

## Outcome

README line 3 and the "In words" paragraph carry a being-built clause, AGENTS.md rule 1 says "hourly once … is built, nightly until then", and the layout line drops the word. The map node keeps "hourly": the label names the line the dashed edge draws. Plan D20.

# Review — visible-dream phase 2   (2026-10-28)

Range reviewed: .agents/scratch/vd2/phase2.diff (working tree vs HEAD b7a763a), lenses code + docs

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

Four existing tests fail deterministically on this tree because the diff changed behaviour they pin and did not change them: `TestStatusLine`, `TestRunWritesProposalsDraftsAndState`, `TestTwoRunsSendEveryCappedInput` (all `internal/dream`) and `TestHelpPageShape` (`cmd/fyr`). I ran `go test ./internal/dream -count=1` and `go test ./cmd/fyr -run 'Dream|Status|Help|Usage|HarnessMap' -count=1`. The new code itself reads correctly: the session check, the cooldown, the timer renders and the older-schedule status line all agree with `SPEC-fyr-dream` and the help text. No requirement is violated. The new tests (`AgySession*`, `Cooldown`, `TimerStale`, `StatusLineOlderSchedule`, `RunAllNeedsASession`, `DryRunSessionLine`) pass.

## Findings

BLOCKING

- **[high / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/help_text.go:~199-210` (the `dream` page's `about`) — `TestHelpPageShape` fails with "dream's description is 14 lines, want 1 to 10" (`cmd/fyr/help_test.go:179`). The diff grew the description past the page-shape limit. Fix: tighten the text to 10 lines or fewer. Keep the three new claims: the session check, the 24-hour limit and `--project` ignoring both, and the older-timer sentence.

- **[high / confidence: high]** `internal/dream/answer_test.go:~91-102` (`TestStatusLine`) — the test writes a timer file containing `"x"` and expects `...; timer installed`. `StatusLine` now calls `timerStale`, which treats any unit text that is not this fyr's render as an older schedule. Actual output: `...timer installed, older schedule: fyr dream --remove-timer --home '<tmp>', then fyr dream --install-timer --home '<tmp>'`. The test needs a real render (the `installed()` helper in `timer_stale_test.go`) for the "timer installed" case, or the changed expectation. The diff touches only a comment in this file, so the assertion was never updated for the behaviour change.

- **[high / confidence: high]** `internal/dream/run_test.go:79` (`TestRunWritesProposalsDraftsAndState`) — it fails with "unchanged not logged". The second same-day run now stops at the cooldown (`skip attempted <time>`, `run.go:356`) before the unchanged check, so the log line `<root> unchanged` is never written. The assertion should move the clock past 24 hours, or assert on `skip attempted`. As written it cannot pass.

- **[high / confidence: high]** `internal/dream/collect_fit_test.go:~140-160` (`TestTwoRunsSendEveryCappedInput`) — run 2, one minute after run 1, is skipped by the cooldown, so "run 2 made no call". This test pins the ADR-069 behaviour that a capped run's remaining news goes out on the next run. Under `--all` that next run is now 24 hours later, which matches the nightly ceiling but not the test. Fix: advance `o.Now` by more than 24 hours between the two runs, so the test still proves that two runs send all nine inputs. The test must still fail without the cap logic.

  The four failures show the diff was never run against the full `internal/dream` and `cmd/fyr` suites. The plan's Phase 2 checkpoint requires the full command to exit 0, and the background run on this tree will report the same four.

NON-BLOCKING

- **[low / confidence: high]** `skills/project-memory/SKILL.md:8,56`, `skills/retro/SKILL.md:48`, `skills/handoff/SKILL.md:178` — they still say "the nightly dream job" / "nightly dream" after the schedule changed in code. The plan defers them to Phase 5 (plan Phase 5 docs box). They are false from this commit until then. Accept only if the Phase 5 box stays open and its handoff names them.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `README.md` `fyr status` row and the `fyr status` line — an older nightly unit is named ("older schedule"), but nothing says it now almost never dreams. At 03:00 it finds no interactive `agy` session and exits 0 with one journal line. The plan's D13 states this; the user-facing text does not. Consider adding "it rarely dreams at 03:00" to the status or README text. Optional.

NIT

- Comments about the dream's old schedule remain at `internal/dream/collect_fit.go:21` ("every night"), `collect_fit_test.go:195,250` and `dryrun_test.go:17` ("a project a night"). The plan's grep is for "nightly" only, so its box passes literally.
- `state.Attempts` is never pruned for removed projects; a negligible growth.
- `ROADMAP.md` is modified in the working tree (Phase 2 done) but is not in the supplied diff. Check it is in the commit.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. No unreferenced exports; `procRoot` and `psArgs` are test seams with real users.
2. Flow tracing — fail only through the four stale tests. The code path itself traces end to end:
   - `Run` defaults `Session`, then `realRun` or `dryRun` asks it first, before `ConfigDir` and the lock.
   - The dry run resolves the session, the skip order and the cooldown as the real run does, and `--project` never asks.
   - `ask` stores the attempt before the call, so a killed run still counts it.
   - `readState` tolerates an older file.
   - `timerStale` round-trips the unit's frozen `PATH` through `renderSystemd` and `renderLaunchd`, including the `%%` and XML unescaping.
   - `planTimer` still refuses a unit with other text, as the help and spec claim.
   - `interactive()` agrees with `agy --help` on this box: `--prompt` is an alias of `--print`, `-i` is `--prompt-interactive`, and the subcommand list matches.
3. Standards conformance — fail on the four tests above. Describing text otherwise agrees across README, AGENTS.md rule 1, the help page, flag descriptions, the `verb_dream.go` strings, the spec (session check, cooldown, status line, state file, failure modes) and R3. Skills restatements are NON-BLOCKING above. `gofmt -l` and `go vet` are clean for `internal/dream` and `cmd/fyr`. Cited must-fail mutations were not presented; none checked.
4. Directory layout — pass. New files are beside their code in `internal/dream`, split by concern (`agy_process`, `timer_stale`) and under the file-size limits.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. Stdlib only, no new dependency, no auth or crypto. The process check is a plain `/proc` and `ps` read.
6. Decoupling — pass. `Options.Session` is a one-function seam, `Options.attempted` is a method, and the state change is additive with `omitempty`.

## Not examined
- A macOS run of the `ps -ww -U <uid>` path (`ps` output and `-U <numeric uid>` acceptance), and whether `agy remote-control start` spawns a child with a non-subcommand argv. Both are unverifiable here; the spec names the Mac gap.
- The full `-race` suite and `cmd/fyr`'s remaining tests (slow; the author's background run covers them). I ran only the focused sets named above.
- The `.agents/trail.jsonl` hunk beyond reading `SPEC-fyr-dream` and the plan through `fyr record get` (`--home .agents/scratch/home-trail`). `SPEC-fyr-delivery`, `SPEC-fyr-metrics` and the ADR were not read.
- Must-fail mutation evidence for the new tests (the plan asks for it), and the Phase 2 checkpoint's scratch-home install and `fyr status` `binary` line.
- `fyr check` was run once: its 7 findings are unrelated to dream (missing `.agents/docs` in records, two stale specs).

## Outcome

- BLOCKING 1 (`TestHelpPageShape`): fixed — the `dream` page's description is 10 lines again; it keeps the session check, the 24-hour limit and the hourly timer, and drops the older-timer sentence (the `fyr status` line and README row 50 carry it).
- BLOCKING 2a (`TestStatusLine`): fixed — the test now writes today's render (`installed()`); a unit with other text is `TestStatusLineOlderSchedule`'s.
- BLOCKING 2b (`TestRunWritesProposalsDraftsAndState`): fixed — the second run comes `cooldown + 1m` later, so it still proves an unchanged project calls nothing.
- BLOCKING 2c (`TestTwoRunsSendEveryCappedInput`): fixed — the second run comes a day later; the test still sends all nine inputs across two runs (ADR-069). The cap logic is unchanged and the test was not weakened.
- All four were also caught by the author's full run (`.agents/scratch/vd2/full.log`, exit 1) before the report came back. The fixes were checked by the full command's exit 0, not by a second reviewer round: they are test and help-text edits only.
- The full run also failed `TestFunctionLength` (`realRun` 60 lines, `dryRun` 61), which the review did not name. Fixed by extracting `noSession`, `prepareAgy`, `drySession` and `drySkip`; the twelve mutations still fail their tests after the split.
- NON-BLOCKING (skills say "nightly"): deferred to Phase 5's docs box, which names those four skills; `skills/dream/SKILL.md:3` is a description change that owes an Antigravity run. The handoff names them.
- NON-BLOCKING (the status line does not say an old unit rarely dreams): not taken. The line names the two commands that fix the unit, and `SPEC-fyr-dream` § Failure modes carries the reason.
- NIT (schedule comments outside "nightly"): fixed — `collect_fit.go:21`, `collect_fit_test.go` (two comments), `dryrun_test.go:17`.
- NIT (`attempts` never pruned): rebutted — one timestamp per registered root, the same growth as `projects`.
- NIT (ROADMAP not in the diff): it is in the commit.
- Must-fail evidence (not examined by the review): `.agents/scratch/vd2/mutate.py`, 12 mutations, each FAILs its tests; re-run after the function split.

# Review — visible-dream Phase 3: the dream's own conversations are no project's (D5, D15)   (2026-10-28)

Range reviewed: working tree against HEAD for `internal/` (`.agents/scratch/vd3/diff.patch`, 11 files, read in full), plus `ROADMAP.md` and the three spec records in `.agents/trail.jsonl` (SPEC-fyr-metrics, SPEC-fyr-dream, SPEC-fyr-delivery, compared with HEAD; the `.after` bodies equal the working-tree records). Checked against the plan's § Interfaces "dream-work is no project's", D5 and D15 as read from the plan record, not against a summary.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing is broken. The code does what the plan's paragraph and D5/D15 say. `r.work` equals the old `filepath.Join(r.conf, "dream-work")`, because `ConfigDir(home)` is `home/StateDir`. `harness` imports no fyr package except the root embed, so there is no cycle. Home is made absolute in `cmd/fyr/run_dispatch.go:111`, so a relative `--home` cannot defeat the match. I ran must-fail mutations through `go test -overlay`, which leaves the tree untouched. Each fix-bearing branch fails a named test when removed, except one: the `--source` half of `Options.dreamWork` (finding 1). The spec docs describe the code.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/metrics/ingest.go:70` — The `o.Source` union in `Options.dreamWork` has no test. I mutated line 70 to `if false && o.Source != ""` (it compiled) and `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/metrics` stayed green, 10.1 s. `TestDreamWorkNotIngested` (`agy_dream_test.go`) uses `Options{Home: home}` only. SPEC-fyr-metrics line 54 claims "for `--home` and for `--source` alike", and the eval path (`cmd/fyr/eval.go:287`, `Home: home, Source: sb`) is the real use. A regression there would ingest a sandbox dream's conversation as a session, with no test failing. Fix: add a second ingest in the same test with `Options{Home: other, Source: home}` and the same expectation, then re-run the mutation. Not blocking: the plan's Phase 3 item asks only for the home case and the code exceeds it. The claim of coverage is the gap.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/dream_work.go:20-31` — `DreamWorkPaths` resolves the home only when `dream-work` itself is missing. If `~/.config/fyr` is a symlink and `dream-work` is absent, the resolved form is lost: `EvalSymlinks(home)` stops at the home, not at the `.config/fyr` link. The directory is created by `prepareAgy` before every run, so this is reachable only after someone deletes it by hand. Concrete scenario: the operator removes `dream-work` and an older dream conversation, stored under the `.config/fyr` target, is read as a project's. No change needed; the doc comment says what it does and `TestDreamWorkPaths` pins that. Recorded as a known limit.
- **[nit / confidence: high]** `internal/metrics/agy_dream_test.go:38,53` — `db, _ := sql.Open(...)` and an unchecked `rows.Scan` make a failure surface as a nil-pointer panic or a wrong count instead of a clear message. The M1 and M3 mutations still fail on the counts, so the test can fail. Cosmetic.
- **[nit / confidence: high]** `ROADMAP.md:9` — "Phases 1–3 are done" is written before the Phase 3 Checkpoint box is ticked (plan record: still `[ ]`). It is true once the commit lands; tick the plan's boxes in the same checkpoint.

## Verification (what was run, and how)
- Baseline: `go test -race -count=1 -run DreamWork` over `internal/metrics`, `internal/search`, `internal/harness` and `internal/dream` passed. `go vet` of the four packages is clean, and `gofmt -l internal` printed nothing.
- M1: metrics exclusion disabled (`&& false &&`, compiled). `TestDreamWorkNotIngested` FAILED: "Sessions:3 … want 1". The fixture's dream conversations do ingest when unexcluded, so the condition holds.
- M2: `judge`'s dream test disabled. `TestDreamWorkNotAProjectsConversation` FAILED (all three conversations returned, none left out), and `TestDreamWorkNotInUse` FAILED ("in use by the dream's own conversation"). The positive control in the dream test passes unmutated.
- M3: symlink form dropped from `DreamWorkPaths`. `TestDreamWorkPaths`, the metrics test (2 sessions) and the search test FAILED.
- M4: the `Source` union disabled at line 70 only. Everything stayed green (finding 1). My first attempt also hit `agyRoot` at line 59, which made it inconclusive, so I redid it at line 70 alone.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. Every new function has a caller, `harness.DreamWork`, `DreamWorkPaths` and `InDreamWork` included. No commented-out code and no leftover scaffolding.
2. Flow tracing — pass. `AgyConversationText` is called from `collect.go:97` and `dream.go:171`, both with `home`. `ingestAgy` → `agyConversations` takes the exclude set. Every `newWorkspaces` caller is updated, including `dream_workspace_test.go`. `listConversations` is called from one place. Error paths are unchanged. `whyDream` is named only when a workspace is under the root, as the doc comments, the spec and the test say. A dream conversation under no root stays unnamed.
3. Standards conformance — pass. Longest changed function: `judge`, about 40 lines. No changed file is near 400 lines (`dream.go` 291, `agy.go` 313). Restatements grepped (`dream-work`, `DreamWork`, `newWorkspaces`, `listConversations`, `agyConversations`): the SPEC-fyr-metrics, SPEC-fyr-dream (header, line 30, the file table, the privacy paragraph) and SPEC-fyr-delivery wording agrees with the code, as do ADR-073 and R3. The plan's "ingestAgy passes o's home's set" is exceeded by the `--source` union, and SPEC-fyr-metrics says so. The two metrics test comments are accurate. No `whyX` enumeration elsewhere needed the new value. Gap: finding 1.
4. Directory layout — pass. `dream_work.go` sits beside `state.go` (`StateDir`, `ConfigDir`) in `internal/harness`, the shared-name home the plan names (D5). Tests sit beside their code.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. Stdlib only, no new dependency, nothing security-primitive hand-rolled; this is path comparison.
6. Decoupling — pass. `search` and `metrics` already imported `harness`, and `harness` imports no fyr package but the root embed, so no new edge and no cycle. The exclusion is one predicate (`InDreamWork`) over one set (`DreamWorkPaths`), shared by both readers.

## Not examined
- The full `go test -race ./...` (running in the background by the caller, per the dispatch), `TestFunctionLength` and `TestHarnessMap` results, and `govulncheck`.
- Behaviour against a real `agy` store: whether `agy` stores the path as written or resolved is the plan's V1 check, which is not part of this diff.
- Case-insensitive filesystems (macOS default): a stored workspace differing from `DreamWork(home)` only by case would not match. Not tested, and no evidence either way.
- ADR-073 and the plan's other phases, read only where they restate this behaviour. `SPEC-fyr-delivery`'s change is the phase-label edit only.

## Outcome

- Finding 1 (low, the `--source` union untested): fixed. `TestDreamWorkNotIngested` now ingests twice, `{Home: home}` and `{Home: <other>, Source: home, Label: "eval=dream-work"}`, through `dreamWorkIngest`; the mutation `if false && o.Source != ""` now FAILS it (`.agents/scratch/vd3/mutate.py`, "source union off").
