- Finding 2 (low, a symlinked config directory with dream-work removed): fixed rather than recorded as a limit. `DreamWorkPaths` resolves the deepest existing ancestor and joins the rest back (`resolveExisting`); `TestDreamWorkPaths` gains the case (`.config/fyr` a link elsewhere, dream-work absent, the absence proven first); the mutation "ancestor walk off" FAILS it.
- Nit (`agy_dream_test.go` unchecked `sql.Open` and `rows.Scan`): fixed, both checked.
- Nit (ROADMAP says Phases 1–3 done before the boxes are ticked): answered by the checkpoint — the plan's Phase 3 boxes are ticked in the same checkpoint, before the commit.
- Found by the full command, not the review: `TestStateDirHasOneHome` failed on the new test's literal `".config", "fyr"`; the test now builds the path from `StateDir`.
- Not examined, carried: case-insensitive filesystems (macOS) — a stored workspace differing only by case would not match; no evidence either way, left to the Mac run (ledger A2) and V1.

title: Review — visible dream Phase 4a: the oracle and visibleHome
body:
# Review — visible dream Phase 4a (visibleHome)   (2026-10-28)

Range reviewed: working tree vs HEAD e6248b0: internal/dream/agy_home.go (loginIn split), new internal/dream/agy_visible.go (278 lines), agy_visible_test.go (260), testdata/oracle/*.json (28 files), ROADMAP.md, and the two edited trail records (SPEC-fyr-dream, PLAN-2026-10-28-1510 ...) — the plan's § Interfaces "The branch" and D11, D24, D25 read as the contract.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing is broken that changes a verdict on the oracle's fail-closed logic: every unknown shape, missing field, unknown permission key, missing global scope, non-review mode, accept-edits/auto agent mode, outside-workspace grant, allow rule in any scope, and trusted workspace at or above dream-work returns "not visible" (read line by line against D24 and the saved reports; `go test -count=1 -run VisibleHome ./internal/dream` passes, gofmt/vet clean, `TestFunctionLength` passes). The worst problem is the oracle child's process-group handling: it copies `callWithin`'s Setpgid and kill-whole-group, but not the signal relay that the BUG-169 fix review added to that same code, so an interrupted fyr leaves the oracle's agy and its language server running in an orphaned group. It is low-to-medium (a headless report exits on its own) and nothing calls `visibleHome` yet, so it can be fixed in Phase 4b.

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `internal/dream/agy_visible.go:110-120` (`oracle`) — gives the child its own process group (`Setpgid`) and kills the group on deadline and after exit, but, unlike `callWithin` (`agy_exec.go:42-60`, `watchedSignals`/`relay`), relays no SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP/SIGQUIT to it. `agy_exec.go:35-39` records why: "Ctrl-C stopped reaching a CLI outside fyr's own group (the fix's review)". Same failure here: Ctrl-C of `fyr dream --dry-run` (plan: the dry run runs the oracle) or a service stop during one of the two 30 s oracle calls per project kills fyr and leaves `agy -p /config` and the language server it starts alive in a group nobody kills. Fix: run the oracle through the same group/relay mechanism (share a helper with `callWithin` rather than a second copy), or drop `Setpgid` and kill only `cmd.Process`; decide before Phase 4b wires it in. The duplicated mechanism is also what let the relay be dropped.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/dream/agy_visible_test.go:228-243` (`TestVisibleHomeTimeout`) and `agy_visible.go:100-103,115-118` — the comment claims "killed whole" (the process group) and the code accepts `exec.ErrWaitDelay` as success, but the only test kills a direct child (`exec sleep 30`). Nothing fails if `Setpgid`/`Cancel` is removed (the context kill of the direct child still passes) or if the `ErrWaitDelay` branch is wrong. `call_test.go:178` shows the grandchild-holds-the-pipe fixture for `callWithin`. Add the same two cases (a grandchild keeping stdout past the exit: accepted or bounded by `oracleGrace`; a grandchild alive after the deadline: gone), or cut the claim from the comment. The coverage claim in the plan ("20 mutations ... the timeout") names the timeout only, not these.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/dream/agy_visible.go:211-249` (`configGrants`) — cyclomatic complexity about 13 (error check, field loop, `!ok ||`, four switch cases plus `&&`, trust double loop plus `if`) against the 10 limit in `rules/code-modularity.md` item 1. Length is fine (40 lines) and `TestFunctionLength` does not check complexity. Fix: split the trust loop into a helper (`trustCovers(trusted, work)`) and the field decode into another; `permissionsGrant` sits at about 10, so keep it from growing.

## Checked and found sound (not findings)
- Spec text vs code: SPEC-fyr-dream step "Visible branch" (30 s each, `HOME`/dream-work/allow-listed env, login rule, empty dream-work, no `.git` or foreign `.agents` above it as written and resolved, `toolPermission` request-review/strict, `agentMode` empty/plan, allow in project/shared/global and `/config.permissions`, `allowNonWorkspaceAccess`, trusted at or above, unknown key fails) matches `agy_visible.go`. Known limits (oracle-to-call window; shared/project scopes read not proven; loads the operator's own hooks/MCP/skills) match D24/D25/D8. The "Being built (Phases 4a-5)" sentence and ROADMAP "not yet called" are honest. D25 records the departure from § Interfaces rule 2 (fyr's own walk instead of a reported workspace), so the plan text left unamended in rule 2 is covered.
- Saved oracle reports hold no account data (grepped for user name, `@`, tokens, `/home/`): clean.
- Counts in the plan's done-note (14 pairs, 16 shapes, 7 work cases) match the test file.
- `agentMode: null` and `allowNonWorkspaceAccess: null` read as zero values and pass (default-equivalent); a missing key fails. Not a hole: null is agy's own spelling for unset.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass with a note: `visibleHome` has no caller outside tests until Phase 4b; this is the plan's stated staging (plan, spec line 8, ROADMAP), not an orphan. `exists`/`covers`/`workForms` have no duplicate elsewhere in the package.
2. Flow tracing — one finding (signal relay, above). Error paths return reasons that the caller can log; every failure is "not visible" (fail closed); the guard keeps the safe branch when a check errors (`workAlone` returns the reason on ReadDir error). Timeout check precedes the error check so a late report is dropped, which is the safe direction.
3. Standards conformance — one low finding (complexity). Spec restatements checked, no stale copy found. Not independently re-run: the 20 recorded mutations (`.agents/scratch/vd4a/mutate.py` exists; I did not execute it).
4. Directory layout — pass: new logic in a new file beside `agy_home.go`, tests beside it, fixtures in `testdata/`; `timer.go` untouched (the plan's 446-line note).
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass on dependencies (stdlib only, no auth/crypto implemented; the oracle consumes agy's own report). The duplicate process-group code is the one simplicity point (finding 1).
6. Decoupling — pass: `loginIn` is the only edit to an existing function and `findLogin` behaves as before (`childEnv` reused, not re-listed); `visibleHome` takes `argv0, home, work, env` and touches no run state.

## Not examined
- The 20 recorded mutations were not re-run (read-only review; script not executed).
- The full test suite (another run is in progress), `-race`, and `govulncheck`.
- Behaviour of the real `agy` (1.4.9 reports are taken from the saved testdata and D24, not re-run); the macOS `Library/Keychains` branch of `loginIn` through `visibleHome` (no test via this path; `findLogin` tests not re-read).
- Whether agy loads `AGENTS.md`/`GEMINI.md`-style context files from ancestors of dream-work (fyr's walk checks only `.git` and `.agents`); D24 does not say, so no concrete failure is claimed.
- Phase 4b and 5 code (not in the range).

## Outcome

- Finding 1 (medium), fixed: `runGroup` (`internal/dream/agy_exec.go`) is the one group-and-relay mechanism, taken out of `callWithin` unchanged; `oracle` and `callWithin` both run through it, so the oracle gets the signal relay, the deadline kill and the kill after Wait. Tests: `TestVisibleHomeGroup` (below) and the existing `TestCall*` signal tests over the shared code; mutations "oracle outside a group" (`cmd.Run()` in place of `runGroup`) and "group not killed after Wait" each FAIL them.
- Finding 2 (low), fixed: `TestVisibleHomeGroup` — `hold`, a helper that keeps stdout while agy hangs (timed out, the helper gone), and `leave`, a helper that keeps stdout past a clean exit (the answer accepted after `oracleGrace`, the helper gone); both bounded in time. Each trigger fails without the fix (the two mutations above).
- Finding 3 (low), fixed: `configGrants` split into `readConfig` (the field decode) and `trustCovers` (the trust loop); each is under 10.
- Not taken: a second review round. The fixes are a helper moved verbatim, a test and a split; the main thread read them, and the 22-mutation run covers each.

title: Review: visible dream Phases 2-4b (session check, cooldown, timer, dream-work exclusion, oracle, the branch)
body:
# Review — visible-dream phases 2-4b   (2026-10-28)

Range reviewed: .agents/scratch/vd4b/diff-phases-2-4b.patch (git diff b7a763a + working tree + the 3 untracked files internal/dream/prompt_test.go, run_branch.go, run_branch_test.go; .agents/trail.jsonl excluded)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

I found nothing broken in the code. The oracle verdict (internal/dream/agy_visible.go), the per-project branch (run_branch.go), the session check, the cooldown, the timer render and stale detection, and the dream-work exclusion in search and metrics all fail closed. Each has a test that would fail without it. The R3 clauses I checked hold: operator home only when no tool is granted without review, empty working directory under ~/.config/fyr/, no `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, a process check only for `--all`. The remaining findings are documentation that misdescribes the code or still says "nightly". The most visible is five "nightly dream" restatements left in four skill files.

Verification run: `go test -count=1 ./internal/dream -run 'VisibleHome|Branch|Cooldown|Prompt|Session|TimerStale|StatusLine|DreamWork|Oracle|AgySession'` passed. The DreamWork tests in internal/metrics, internal/search and internal/harness passed. `TestFunctionLength` and `TestHarnessMap` (root package) passed. `gofmt -l cmd internal` was empty, and `go vet` on the four changed packages was clean. I did not run the whole-repo suite, as instructed.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: high]** `skills/project-memory/SKILL.md:8`, `skills/project-memory/SKILL.md:56`, `skills/retro/SKILL.md:48`, `skills/handoff/SKILL.md:178`, `skills/dream/SKILL.md:3` — five living restatements still call the job "nightly" ("the nightly dream job", "the nightly `fyr dream` job only proposes", "waiting for the nightly dream"). The diff makes the timer hourly while an agy session runs (timer.go `OnCalendar=hourly`, README:50) and rewrites every other "nightly" in code comments, help text and README. These skills are read by the model, and "nightly" now misleads. Fix: "the `fyr dream` timer's job" or similar in all five places, in the same change.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/dream/prompt.go:66-67` vs `internal/dream/collect.go:56` — `head`'s comment says the name on the prompt's first line is "one line, scrubbed", but collect.go only runs `oneLine(p.Name)` (fold and fence-escape, no `scrub`/redact). The name is now also the conversation title in the operator's `/resume` list. A directory named like a credential would pass through unredacted. Fix: `oneLine(scrub(p.Name, home))` at collect.go:56, or drop "scrubbed" from the comment.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `README.md:50` (and `REQUIREMENTS.md` R3) say the visible branch is taken "when its settings grant no tool without review". The code (agy_visible.go `visibleHome`/`workAlone`) also requires a login under `--home`, an empty dream-work, no `.git` above it (a dotfiles repo at `$HOME` is enough) and no foreign `.agents` above it. All of these fall to the private home. The failure mode is safe (private), but an operator with a git checkout at `$HOME` never gets the `/resume` conversation, and the README does not say why. The dream.log "agy home private (...)" line does name the reason. Fix: one clause in README:50 naming these conditions. R3 is immutable, so only the operator can change it.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `README.md:114` — "dashed until PLAN-2026-10-28-1510-... builds it", while README:50 and README:117 now say "all of this is built; its Phase 5 has yet to run this end to end", and AGENTS.md rule 4 turns a line solid on the end-to-end run, not on the build. Fix: "until its end-to-end run passes".

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. I found no unreferenced additions. `activity` still has a caller, and `agyAuthHint`'s new `where` argument is used at both call sites. `timerStale`, `servicePATH` and `plistPATH` all have callers.
2. Flow tracing — pass. Traced `Run` → `realRun` → `noSession` → `prepareAgy` → `project` → `branchFor` → `visibleHome`/`agyHome` → `ask` → `call`; and `dryRun` → `dryBranch` → `visibleHome`. `runGroup` keeps the old step order (Start, signal relay, Wait, Stop, close, relay drained, final group kill); the Start error is now wrapped by `cliResult` as before. The oracle propagates timeout, exit and shape errors as a private-branch reason, never as a grant. The dry run asks the oracle as the real run does and honestly says "not asked" when dream-work does not exist yet. The attempt is stored before the call, the watermark after the write. The test fakes never write into the working directory, so I could not check whether a real agy call leaves files in dream-work (see Not examined).
3. Standards conformance — fail on docs only (the four findings above). Code: errors are wrapped and handled, the oracle and the call get a bounded context and a killed group, and the child environment is the allow-list. The §8 shapes hold: a guard failing to run keeps toward private, and a read-only mode makes no dream-work or private home (`TestDryRunBranchLine`).
4. Directory layout — pass. New files sit beside their package. `internal/search` and `internal/metrics` now import `internal/harness` for `DreamWork`. It compiles with no cycle and `harness` does not import SQLite, so this is a note, not a finding.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. Stdlib only, no new dependency. The auth login is copied or used in place; nothing is hand-rolled.
6. Decoupling — pass. The oracle, branch, process check, timer staleness and dream-work path logic are in separate files. The workspace exclusion is passed in as data (`newWorkspaces(root, exclude)`).

## Not examined
- Behaviour against a real `agy`: the saved oracle reports under testdata/oracle were read only as inputs, and the plan's Phase 5 end-to-end run has not happened. In particular, whether a real call leaves anything in dream-work. If it does, `workAlone` returns "dream-work is not empty" and every later project in the run (and later runs) takes the private branch. That is fail-closed, but no test pins it.
- A trusted workspace written as a symlink that resolves above dream-work: `covers` compares the entry as written, not resolved. I judged it speculative, with no concrete failure shown.
- `ROADMAP.md`, the testdata/oracle JSON bodies, internal/dream/timer_*_test.go and agy_process_test.go beyond the diff hunks. The records under `.agents/trail.jsonl` were not read.
- Pre-flight `fyr search --refs` for the changed files returned no recorded bugs for internal/dream/run.go. I did not run it for the other changed files, and I did not read `fyr record list --kind bug`.

## Outcome

1. Skills still say "nightly": deferred, as the plan already assigns them. Phase 5's docs box owns `skills/dream`, `project-memory`, `retro` and `handoff`. `project-memory/SKILL.md:8` is not on the box's list, so the Phase 4b handoff names it for Phase 5.
2. The `head` comment said "scrubbed": fixed. `prompt.go` now says the name is folded to one line (SD15), and `SPEC-fyr-dream` step 4 says "folded to one line as in step 2". The name was already sent on the `Project:` line, so nothing new is exposed. `TestPromptFirstLine` pins the fold on the first line.
3. README row 50's condition was too loose: fixed. It now names agy's reports, no hook loaded (D26), and nothing above the empty working directory (no git checkout or other `.agents`). R3 is not changed: fyr's added conditions only send more dreams private, which R3's "otherwise in a private home" already covers.
4. README's "dashed until … builds it": fixed. It now reads "until the end-to-end run of … passes", as AGENTS.md rule 4 says.

Not examined by the review, and still open: whether a real `agy` call leaves files in dream-work, which would send later projects private. That direction fails closed. The Phase 4b handoff adds it to Phase 5's V1 check.

title: Security review: visible dream Phases 2-4b (oracle, branch, session check, child env, sweep)
body:
# Security review — visible dream phases 2-4b   (2026-10-28)

Range reviewed: b7a763a..f607129 plus the uncommitted working tree and the three untracked files (patch `.agents/scratch/vd4b/diff-phases-2-4b.patch`, `.agents/trail.jsonl` excluded)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

The worst problem is that `visibleHome` can fail open. `readConfig` (`internal/dream/agy_visible.go:228-245`) reads five keys out of agy's `/config` report and ignores every other key. That goes against the plan's Interfaces rule 5 ("anything else fails (an `agy` upgrade that changes the report sends the dream private until fyr learns it)") and against D6. `/permissions` fails closed on an unknown key; `/config` does not. Today no setting grants a tool past the five checked keys, so nothing is exploitable now. But agy keeps adding approval settings (the `proceed-in-sandbox` mode, a widened `always-proceed`, `auto`, honouring "auto-execution" in headless runs at changelog `:789`). Once an upgrade adds one under a new key, fyr will run a prompt built from untrusted project text in the operator's own home, with that grant in force, and log "agy home visible". Second: the oracle never asks `/hooks`, even though agy answers it in print mode. agy's pre-tool hooks return a permission decision, so a hook or plugin can approve a call the oracle never sees. No finding allows a tool grant against the current agy 1.4.9 settings; both are gaps in the fail-closed rule the design depends on.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/dream/agy_visible.go:228-245` (`readConfig`), `:253-268` (`configGrants`): `/config` keys other than `toolPermission`, `agentMode`, `allowNonWorkspaceAccess`, `trustedWorkspaces` and `permissions` are never looked at, and `permissions` is decoded into `{Allow []string}` alone, so an unknown sub-key under it is ignored too. All 14 saved reports in `internal/dream/testdata/oracle/*.config.json` carry the same 36 keys. A new or renamed key in an agy upgrade therefore gives no signal, and if it approves tools the dream runs visible. `artifactReviewPolicy` is also unchecked: changelog `:207`/`:789` say a non-review value lets plans "proceed automatically" in plan mode and headless runs honour it. Tool calls still wait for review in that case, so this part is low on its own. Remediation: pin the recorded key set (any key added to or missing from the 36 → private branch, with the key named); fail on an unknown sub-key of `permissions`; treat `artifactReviewPolicy` other than `asks-for-review` as a reason to go private; add a `TestVisibleHomeShapes` row for "an extra /config key" and for "an unknown permissions sub-key", each checked once in the must-fail state.
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `internal/dream/agy_visible.go:42-65` (`visibleHome`): the oracle checks settings and permission rules but not hooks or plugins. The agy changelog shows pre-tool hooks returning decisions (`.agents/scratch/ledger/p8a/agy-changelog.txt:859` "decision strings returned by pre-tool hooks", `:443` approval prompts that a hook flags). It also shows hooks receiving `lastUserInput`, which is the untrusted prompt (`:33`), and `/hooks` answering in print mode with no turn (`:656`; plan D24 recorded `/hooks` → `[]`). Plan D8 accepts that the operator's hooks and plugins load, but its premise ("the model still has no tool it can use without review") has not been shown for a hook that returns allow. With the operator's global `~/.gemini/config/hooks.json`, or a plugin's hooks, in the visible home, a tool call driven by injected project text could be approved without review. Confidence is medium because the decision semantics come from the changelog, not from a sandbox run. Remediation: add a third oracle call, `agy -p /hooks --output-format json`, and send the dream private unless it reports none (or none on a pre-tool event). Alternatively, show in a sandbox home that a pre-tool hook answering allow is not honoured in a headless `--mode plan` run, and record that as a D-row with the test it got.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/dream/run.go:26` vs `:49`, `:62`; `internal/dream/agy_exec.go:59-64`: a run killed by a signal re-raises it in `runGroup`, so `defer r.removePrivate()` never runs. That leaves `~/.config/fyr/dream-agy-home-*`, holding a 0600 copy of `antigravity-oauth-token`, plus the unredacted database copies. The cleanup that catches them (`removeCopies`) now runs only after `noSession`. The hourly timer's usual case, no agy session, returns before that, so the token copy stays on disk until the next run that finds a session, possibly for days. Systemd's `TimeoutStartSec` SIGTERM takes this path. Remediation: call the private home's cleanup in the signal path before the re-raise, and/or run `removeCopies` before the session check when the config directory already exists (read it with `os.ReadDir`, without `ConfigDir`, so the no-op still creates nothing).
- **[low / confidence: medium]** Design residual (R3 `/resume`): a visible dream leaves a conversation in the operator's store whose first message is redacted but untrusted project text (prompt-injection payloads included). The oracle's verdict holds only at dream time. When the operator later `/resume`s it, the settings in force then apply (possibly `always-proceed`), and any injected instruction in that context reaches a session that has tools. Remediation: confirm that `SPEC-fyr-dream` § Known limits states this, and consider a closing line in the prompt or the conversation's first line ("dreaming: <name>", `internal/dream/prompt.go:68-70`) saying the conversation holds untrusted data.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/dream/run_branch.go:42`, `:75`; `internal/dream/prompt.go:38-40`: `why` can quote a rule from the operator's settings (`ruleGrants` `agy_visible.go:211`, `configGrants` `:265`). It is passed through `redact` and `oneLine`, but `oneLine` folds only whitespace: ESC and other C0/C1 control characters reach `dream.log` and dry-run stdout, and `c.Name` reaches agy's `/resume` title the same way. A credential written inside an allow rule that matches no redact needle is copied into `dream.log` (0600). The source in every case is the operator's own settings or registration, so the impact is terminal-escape noise or a second 0600 copy. Remediation: strip `unicode.IsControl` characters in the log path; consider logging only the rule's kind and scope rather than its text.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/dream/agy_visible.go:285-291` (`covers`): the check is a byte-for-byte prefix compare. On a case-insensitive APFS volume, a `trustedWorkspaces` entry that differs from dream-work only in case is not seen as covering it. `workAlone`'s refusal of any `.agents`/`.git` above dream-work limits what trust could load. Remediation: on darwin, compare with `strings.EqualFold` on each path part (toward private), or treat any trusted entry under the home as covering.

## Checked

- Secrets: no credential in code, tests or the 28 oracle fixtures (they hold setting values, no account data). The child env stays ADR-067's allow-list (`agy_exec.go:151-162`); the oracle gets the same `childEnv` (`agy_visible.go:49`), so a caller cannot widen it. In the visible branch the login is used in place, with no copy. The private home is `MkdirTemp` (0700), with the token copied `O_EXCL` 0600 through `openRegular`. Oracle stderr is discarded, and its error text carries the exit status or a JSON syntax error, never the output. A leftover copy after a signal is finding 3.
- Injection: the prompt reaches agy on stdin as one stream-json message, and its first line, `dreaming: <name>` (`prompt.go:68-70`), means user text never begins with `/` (no slash-command injection). The name and log `why` go through `oneLine` (control characters: finding 5). Unit render: the change is to schedule and text only; `timerStale`'s `servicePATH`/`plistPATH` are display-only (they feed `StatusLine`, which `shellQuote`s the home). Oracle JSON is agy's own serialisation. `oracleData` refuses a trailing second document, a wrong command name, a non-SUCCESS status and null data.
- Authz/authn (the branch decision): `/permissions` fails closed on an unknown key, a nameless scope, a non-list rule set and a missing global scope; `toolPermission` and `agentMode` are allow-lists, an unknown mode reads back as request-review (fixture `bogus-mode`), and a relative or non-path trusted entry fails toward private. `workAlone` checks emptiness and walks both the written and resolved forms for `.git`/`.agents` (a symlinked dream-work into a checkout → private). It runs per project. Gaps: findings 1, 2, 6. Accepted known limits, not re-raised: the oracle-to-call window, and the shared/project permission scopes "read but not proven to surface" (plan D24). Session check (`agy_process.go`): reads the real uid from `status`, counts only same-uid processes, and fails toward not dreaming on errors or odd argv. A same-uid process can fake `agy` in its argv, but no boundary depends on that. `--dangerously-skip-permissions` is absent from `command()` (`dream.go:230-232`).
- Dream-conversation filtering: `internal/search/dream_workspace.go` `judge` drops a conversation with any workspace inside `DreamWorkPaths(home)` and fails closed on non-file URIs. `internal/metrics/agy.go:100` drops one by its first workspace, which is the attribution key there. `DreamWorkPaths` resolves the deepest existing ancestor (symlinked home). No fail-open found.
- Crypto: no crypto code added or changed; nothing hand-rolled.
- Dependencies: none added (`go.mod` untouched in the range). `govulncheck` not run, as the dispatch said it was not needed; `npm audit`: no JS ecosystem in this change.
- GCP surface: none touched (no IAM, service account, Cloud Run or Secret Manager change).
- Tests: `go test -count=1 ./internal/dream -run 'VisibleHome|RunBranch|DryRunBranch'` → `ok` (3.4 s). No test covers an extra `/config` key or `/hooks`.

## Not examined

- No real `agy` run: the hook-decision semantics (finding 2) and the `artifactReviewPolicy` effect come from the changelog, not a sandbox.
- macOS path not exercised (`psArgs`, Keychain link, launchd render); read only.
- Not read in full: `internal/dream/timer_install.go` beyond its diff, `internal/dream/timer.go` outside the diff hunks, `internal/metrics/agy.go`'s `firstWorkspace` body, `internal/search/dream.go`'s `listConversations` loop after the hunk, and `internal/dream/collect*.go` beyond `scrub`/`oneLine`/`Name`.
- Test files skimmed by name only (`agy_process_test.go`, `run_session_test.go`, `run_cooldown_test.go`, `timer_*_test.go`, `dream_work_test.go`, `prompt_test.go`, `run_branch_test.go`), with no mutation checks.
- Docs hunks (README, ROADMAP, AGENTS.md, help_text.go) not reviewed for security claims.
- `SPEC-fyr-dream` § Known limits not read (finding 4 asks for it to be checked).

## Outcome

1. `/config` read only five keys (medium): fixed. `readConfig` pins the key set both ways to the 36 keys agy 1.4.9 reported (`configKeys`): a key added or gone sends the project private, with the key named. `permissions` accepts only `allow`, `deny` and `ask`. `artifactReviewPolicy` must be `asks-for-review`, the one value seen. New `TestVisibleHomeShapes` rows: "harmless key missing", "key added", "permissions key added", "artifact policy"; "field missing" now reads `no toolPermission`. Mutations (`.agents/scratch/vd4b/mutate2.py`): the unknown-key check, the missing-key check, the permissions-key check and the policy check, each removed, each FAIL.
2. No `/hooks` check (medium): fixed by the operator's choice, "Require no hooks (Recommended)" (plan D26, which narrows D8). `visibleHome` runs a third oracle, `agy -p /hooks --output-format json`. `hooksAny` takes only `{"hooks":[]}`, the one report the sandbox saw (now `internal/dream/testdata/oracle/hooks.json`). Any hook, a `null`, an extra key, or no report sends the project private. New rows: "a hook", "hooks of another shape", "hooks key added", "hooks not reported". Mutations: the call removed, the count ignored, the shape loosened, each FAIL. `SPEC-fyr-dream` step 4 and § Known limits say so.
3. A killed run's private home outlived the no-session hours (low): fixed. A run that stops for want of a session now calls `sweepIdle`. It sweeps only in a `~/.config/fyr` that already exists, and only under `dream.lock`, so it creates no directory and never touches a live run's copies; it removes only what is over an hour old, as `removeCopies` does. The sweep was not moved ahead of the lock: a run longer than an hour (the unit allows two) would then lose its live private home to a second run. `TestNoSessionSweepsKilledRun` covers a stale home removed, a young one kept, no log or state written, and nothing removed while another holds the lock. Mutations: no sweep, the lock ignored, each FAIL. The re-raise path itself is unchanged; the sweep bounds a leftover to about an hour plus the next hourly fire.
4. A resumed dream carries untrusted text (low): documented. A new `SPEC-fyr-dream` Known limit, "A resumed dream is a session like any other". No code change.
5. Control characters in the log reason (low): fixed. `logReason` redacts, folds and drops `unicode.IsControl` characters for the `dream.log` branch line and the dry run's line. Paths now stay as written, where they were shown as `~`: a scratch `--home` shown as `~` read as the operator's own home. `TestLogReason` pins it; mutations (no strip, no redact) FAIL. The project name in the `/resume` title is left folded (SD15) and not stripped: it is the operator's own checkout name, and it already reached the model on the `Project:` line.
6. Case-insensitive `covers` on macOS (low, confidence low): rebutted. A trusted workspace loads that workspace's own `.agents`, and `workAlone` already refuses any `.git` or `.agents` above dream-work except the home's, while dream-work itself must be empty. So trust there adds nothing loadable, whatever its case. The macOS path is verified only by ledger A2.

title: `fyr check` — docs freshness and drift
body:
# `fyr check` — docs freshness and drift

Status: rule (a), docs, built 2026-10-25 (plan `PLAN-2026-10-25-2024-plan-fyr-check-docs-freshness-and-drift-2026-10` Phase 1, ADR-064); rules (b), specs, and (c), requirements, built 2026-10-25 (Phase 2); its callers since Phase 3 (2026-10-25) are the `review` skill's docs brief, and through it `/preflight` Step 4, and the `requirements` skill once an approved `REQUIREMENTS.md` is written; the context does not name it (plan D35, D36). Code: `internal/check`, `cmd/fyr/check.go`; `brain.ReadTrail` in `internal/brain/export.go`; `trail.NoIndexMarkers` in `internal/trail/trail.go`.

## The verb

```
fyr check
```

- No flags of its own. `--home` and `--repo` are accepted, as on every verb, and have no effect. A positional word is a usage error, exit 2.
- The root is the git toplevel of the working directory (`trail.Roots`' top: a linked worktree is checked as itself).
- It reads that tree (through `git ls-files`, `git check-ignore` and an `os.Root` at the checkout), its `.agents/trail.jsonl` (through `brain.ReadTrail`, which opens no store) and the running binary's own verb table. It writes nothing: no `.agents/scratch/search.db`, no `brain.db`, no state-directory move. So it runs on a project that was never migrated and on one that is not the harness.

## Output

On stdout, in rule order (a), (b), (c), each sorted by place, then line, then rule name:

```
<where>:<line>  <rule>  <text>
note: <text>
check: N findings (docs D, specs S, requirements R); fyr <version>
```

- `<where>` is a repo-relative path or a record ID; `<line>` is 1-based in the file or the record body, and is left out (with its colon) when the rule has none.
- `<rule>` is one of `verb`, `subverb`, `flag`, `path`, `line` (rule (a)); `spec-stale`, `spec-unlinked` (rule (b)); `requirement` (rule (c)).
- Every line passes through `search.Printable`, so a record body cannot drive the terminal.

Exit status: 0 with no findings (notes may be printed); 1 with findings and the summary line; 1 with no summary line and `check: <reason>` on stderr for a refusal; 2 for a usage error. The summary line tells a run that checked from one that refused. Nothing wires the status to a gate (R3).

| Situation | What the operator sees |
|---|---|
| Not a git checkout | stderr `check: <dir> is not a git checkout`, no summary, exit 1 |
| `trail.jsonl` does not parse | stderr `check: trail.jsonl line <n>: <reason>`, the same text `fyr record` refuses with; no summary, exit 1: a half-read trail would give a false clean run |
| `trail.jsonl` is a symlink, or `.agents` is | stderr `check: … is a symlink: the trail must be the project's own file`, exit 1 |
| No `trail.jsonl` | `note: no .agents/trail.jsonl: records, specs not checked`; exit 0 when nothing else is found |
| A shallow clone, or a partial clone | `note: a shallow clone: specs not checked` or `note: a partial clone: specs not checked`; rule (b) does not run, because its count is only true over the whole history |
| A git call of rule (b) fails for one spec | `note: <ID>: git log failed: spec not checked` or `note: <ID>: git rev-list failed: spec not checked`; the other specs are checked |
| No `REQUIREMENTS.md` at the root | `note: no REQUIREMENTS.md: requirements not checked` |
| `REQUIREMENTS.md` is a symlink, not a regular file, or over 16 MiB | `note: REQUIREMENTS.md is not a regular file of at most 16 MiB: requirements not checked` |
| A `REQUIREMENTS.md` with no `enforced by:` anywhere | `note: REQUIREMENTS.md has no enforced-by field: not checked` (plan D8, D30) |
| A tracked doc or `_test.go` the check cannot read (a link, unreadable, over 16 MiB) | `note: N tracked files skipped (unreadable, a link or over 16 MiB), first <path>`: one note, never a silent skip (IN53 of the 2026-10-27 audit); an unreadable `skills/VENDORED.md` is such a doc, and the vendored skills it would have named are then checked as the project's own (IN56) |
| A doc names a verb of a newer binary than the one running | a `verb` finding; the summary names the running version |
| A true statement names a removed verb, or another checkout's path | a finding; the statement is reworded (below) |

## The docs set

- **Files:** every tracked `*.md` (`git ls-files`), minus every file under a directory that holds a noindex marker (`.fyr-noindex`, or `.sh-agent-noindex` from before the rename; tracked or not, the same names search honours), and minus the vendored skills and catalogs `skills/VENDORED.md` names: a table row whose first cell is a lowercase name or path (the same rows `restatement-grep.sh` reads, forks included), each taken as `skills/<cell>/`.
- **Records:** the living records of `.agents/trail.jsonl`: `spec`, `guide` and `deploy` records with status `current`. Every other kind, and a retired record, is history and is not read.
- `ROADMAP.md` and `TODO.md` at the root are outside rule (a): they name what is not built yet.

## Scanning

Only code is read; prose is not.

- A **fence** opens with three or more backticks or tildes at up to three spaces of indent, whatever its info string (a backtick fence's info string holds no backtick), and closes with a run of the same character at least as long and nothing after it. A fence left open runs to the end. Inside a fence, a line ending in `\` joins the next, and the joined line is placed at its first line.
- An **inline span** is a run of N backticks closed by the next run of exactly N on the same line; a run with no closer is text. Its content is trimmed.
- An **indented code block** (four columns or more after a blank line, not a list item) is not read; a nested list item indented four columns is prose and its spans are read.

## Rule (a), docs

### Verbs, subverbs and flags

Over every file of the docs set and every living record, inside spans and fences:

1. `<…>` placeholders are removed.
2. A chunk splits into segments at `|`, `&&`, `||`, `(`, `)` and line ends, and in a fence also at `;`. In a span `;` is the punctuation of a quoted message, as in an install line that says fyr never removes a file (plan D28).
3. A segment counts when its program word, after a `$` prompt and `VAR=value` words, is `fyr`, a path ending `/bin/fyr`, `./fyr`, or the three words `go run ./cmd/fyr`. So `cmd/fyr` in a layout fence and `~/.config/fyr` are not commands.
4. `--home` and `--repo` are skipped with their value (`--home X` or `--home=X`).
5. The next word W must match `^[a-z][a-z-]*$`; otherwise the segment is not checked.
6. A W the binary lacks is a `verb` finding.
7. When W has subverbs, the first later word that does not start with `-` is S if it matches the same pattern; an S that is not one of them is a `subverb` finding.
8. Every word matching `^[\[("']*--([a-z][a-z0-9-]*)` is a flag (text after the name is ignored). One that S (or W, when there is no S) does not take is a `flag` finding.

The vocabulary is the running binary's: each verb's flags are the ones its own FlagSet declares, plus `--home`, `--repo` and `--help`. `record`'s subverbs take the flags `recordFlags` lists for each (so `--title` on `record get` is a finding); `metrics` (`ingest show report export`) and `memory` (`add show`) take the verb's flags on every subverb. `help` is a verb.

### Paths

Over every file of the docs set and every living record, deployed content (the skills, agents, context, rules and commands directories) included (plan D26), in inline spans only. A candidate is a span holding one token with no space, which may end `:N` or `:N-M`, when all of these hold:

- it holds none of `< > * { } $ ~ …`, no `..`, no `://`, and is not absolute;
- the last segment is not a Go identifier: no `.` followed by an upper-case letter, as in `internal/trail.Command`;
- with a leading `./` and every trailing `/` removed (a trailing slash after a symlink would leave the `os.Root` on a Go before 1.25.12, GO-2026-4970), it is a tracked top-level file, or its first segment is a tracked top-level directory;
- `git check-ignore` does not ignore it. A path below a symlinked directory is not asked (git refuses such a path and would drop the whole batch); if the batch still fails, each path is asked alone.

How a candidate is checked:

- Existence goes through an `os.Root` at the checkout, which resolves a symlink inside the checkout and refuses one that leaves it. A missing candidate is a `path` finding (`… does not exist`); one that leaves the checkout is a `path` finding too (`… does not resolve inside this checkout`), and nothing outside is read.
- `:N` (and `:M`) is checked only on a regular file, not a symlink, of at most 16 MiB with no NUL byte in its first 8 KiB: a number past the file's last line is a `line` finding. `:N` on a directory is a `line` finding. On any other file `:N` is not checked.

**Another checkout's path** is written with a placeholder, which makes it no candidate: `<clone>/internal/greet/greet.go`, `<project>/.agents/rules/`. There is no ignore marker (plan D12, D27). A statement about a removed verb names the verb alone, so the program word does not precede it: the `report` verb is gone.

### Verification file names

In a `spec` record with status `current`, inside its `## Verification` section (from that heading to the next level-two heading; a heading line inside a fence neither starts nor ends it), an inline span outside a fence that holds one bare Go file name, with no directory (`agy_test.go`, which may end `:N` or `:N-M`), must be the base name of a tracked file; when none is, the span is a `path` finding (`` `tools_test.go`: no tracked file is named tools_test.go ``). The `:N` is not checked, since a base name may match several files. The path rule cannot see such a name, which is anchored on no top-level entry, and a spec's table named a test file that was never written (`internal/check/verification.go`, `-run TestVerificationFileNames`).

## Rule (b), specs

For each `spec` record with status `current` (plan D9, D10):

- **Its code** is the path candidates its inline spans name (the path rule's candidates, above) that exist and git does not ignore, files or directories, minus `*.md` files, `.agents` and `.agents/trail.jsonl`. A spec with none left is a `spec-unlinked` finding.
- **Its commit** is the oldest commit `git log -G` finds whose `.agents/trail.jsonl` diff holds the spec's current line, matched on its `"id"` and its `"updated"` stamp, both quoted for the extended regular expression `-G` compiles (a `+02:00` offset is literal). `git log` runs through `trail.Log`, with `--no-textconv`, so no textconv driver the checkout's `.gitattributes` names is started. A spec whose current line is not committed yet has no commit and is not stale.
- **Stale** when `git rev-list --count <commit>..HEAD` over its code, every `*.md` below it excluded, is above 0. The finding is `spec-stale`, with no line: `N commits to <code> since <commit>`.
- **Ancestry, not clocks.** A commit that carries both the code and the spec's new line is the spec's commit and is not counted: the Definition of Done's normal case. A later commit that only moves the line inside `trail.jsonl` does not reset the count.
- **The remedy** is a re-read. A spec found still true is re-stamped with `fyr record edit <ID> --status current`, which sets `updated`; the next commit carries the new line, and the spec is clean. The rule is never changed to clear a refactor.
- Rule (b) does not run on a shallow clone (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository`) or a partial clone (`trail.PartialClone`, or `trail.Readable` false); a note says which (plan D13).
- A `git log` or `git rev-list` of rule (b) that fails for one spec leaves `note: <ID>: git log failed: spec not checked` (or `git rev-list failed`), never a silent pass; the other specs are still checked.

## Rule (c), requirements

Over `REQUIREMENTS.md` at the root, in the init-project template's shape (`skills/init-project/assets/REQUIREMENTS.md`):

- **Items** are lines `- **<letter><digits>** — …` under a `## Must` or `## Should` heading. An item runs to the next item or heading (a `###` sub-heading ends it too). A struck item (`— struck …`) is skipped; `## Could` and every other section are not read.
- **The field** is `enforced by:` inside an HTML comment of the item, its value running to the comment's end. A file holding no `enforced by:` anywhere is not checked; a note says so (plan D30).
- **A `requirement` finding**, placed on the item's line and naming the item, for: no comment holding the field; an empty value; a value holding `<`, the template's placeholder; a value beginning `not yet enforced:`, a requirement with no enforcement site (plan D31); a part that does not resolve.
- **Resolving** (plan D22). The value splits at commas. Each part's first token, taken up to whitespace, `::` or `#` (so ` § note` and `::case` are the reader's), with backticks around it dropped, resolves as:
  - `Test…` (`^Test\w+$`): a `func TestX(` opening a line of a tracked `*_test.go`;
  - a record ID present in `.agents/trail.jsonl`, of any kind or status (`ADR-063`, `GUIDE-testing`);
  - otherwise a path of the checkout, relative, that git tracks (a file, or a directory holding a tracked file), with the path rule's existence and `:N` checks (`cmd/fyr/main.go:1`, `README.md`). An ignored or untracked local file does not resolve (IN54 of the 2026-10-27 audit).

## Known limits

- A removed top-level file or directory is not caught: a candidate must be anchored on a tracked top-level entry now (plan D11).
- Prose is not read: a path or a command named outside code is not checked.
- A bare file name is read only as a Go file in a current spec's Verification section, and only for existence: elsewhere a bare name is often an example (`foo.go`), and a bare name of another extension is not checked.
- Only `fyr` verbs are known; a project's own CLI is not checked.
- A command whose program word is not one of the four forms (`sudo fyr`, a quoted program, `$(go env GOPATH)/bin/fyr` split at its parenthesis) is not checked (plan D16).
- In a span, a second command after `;` is not checked (D28).
- `metrics` and `memory` subverbs are given the whole verb's flags, so a flag one subverb refuses and another takes is not a finding.
- Rule (b) counts any commit to a spec's code, a refactor that changed no behaviour included; the remedy is a re-read, not a threshold. A directory named in a spec's span is code, so a spec whose span names the skills directory goes stale on every skill edit; a spec names such a directory in prose, not in a span (plan D38).
- Rule (b) matches a spec's line on `"id"` before `"updated"`, the order the export writes; a hand-written line in another key order has no commit and is never stale.
- Rule (c) reads only the template's `enforced by:` field: a requirement enforced but not saying so in that field is not seen.

title: Delivery, and what stays on the machine — what this harness is building toward
body:
# Delivery, and what stays on the machine — what this harness is building toward

The picture in one place, because the operator is discarding the agent's memory and the trail has to carry everything on its own. Written 2026-09-17, the zip place added 2026-09-28. What is DECIDED lives in `REQUIREMENTS.md` R7, R8 and R9, ADR-030, ADR-033, ADR-038 and ADR-062 (§ The model below is their one-paragraph statement); what is PLANNED lives in `PLAN-2026-09-17-delivery-rework`; this document is the narrative that makes both readable to someone arriving cold.

## The problem, in the operator's words

> "I want the delivery to be around the fyr only. Nothing else. I'm the sole user of this harness and decide everything but I install it on multiple places and when I decide to update the repo I want a smart way to push any updates to places where I use it."

And the loop back, asked for on 2026-09-17 and withdrawn on 2026-10-24 (ADR-062):

> "Some sort of feedback function from each place installed reporting back to the main is good for a feedback loop so we can take experiences from each installed place to use to make the harness better."

> "… remove the report back to styrman-harness-feedback repo. This should be removed also."

## The four places

Every place runs the Antigravity CLI only (ADR-062).

| Where | How it is driven |
|---|---|
| Work Mac | The operator runs `fyr update` |
| Home Mac | The operator runs `fyr update` |
| A Linux project host | The operator runs `fyr update` |
| A second Linux project host | The operator runs `fyr update` |

The normal flow is deliberately dull: the operator edits this repository, is happy with it, then goes to each place and runs one command. There is no push, no timer that has to work, no service that has to be up. A timer is a convenience some machines add; it is not the mechanism.

## The model

The one statement of what a tag delivers, to which kind of place, and how a place moves forward; every other living file points here (project `AGENTS.md` § How the harness works, rule 6). A **checkout place** follows `main`: `fyr update` fetches, refuses a dirty checkout, fast-forwards, rebuilds the binary from the checkout and reinstalls; a tag changes nothing for it. A **binary-only place** moves only when a new `vX.Y.Z` tag is published: `fyr update` downloads the newest release's binary (a canonical `vX.Y.Z` tag, newer than the running one), checks the binary against the release's `SHA256SUMS` (integrity only: no key signs a release, and who made it rests on the operator's GitHub credential and HTTPS, as for a checkout place; ADR-053), replaces `~/.local/bin/fyr` and installs the harness embedded in it. A tag is therefore a release marker that also carries the binaries a binary-only place updates to; nothing is ever pushed to any machine, and a tag without its assets is a marker no place can update to (R8, R9; ADR-033, superseding ADR-030 D2).

A **zip place** fetches nothing and holds no tag: the operator downloads the repository zip by hand — a browser, `git archive`, whatever reaches GitHub — and runs `fyr update --from-zip <file>`, which unpacks it into a temporary directory under `~/.config/fyr/` (beside the zip when that directory does not exist yet, as on a first dry run), refuses any entry that would leave that directory, installs the unpacked tree with the RUNNING binary, and deletes the directory; nothing is kept on disk but the manifest's `zip:sha256:<hex>` marker, which also records whether the zip was verified. It moves forward only when the operator repeats the download and `--from-zip` — there is no tag to follow and no release to poll — and nothing in the zip replaces the binary — the running binary is installed as every install installs it — so a zip whose harness needs a newer binary needs that binary downloaded by hand too. A release zip is checked against the release's `SHA256SUMS` when it sits beside it, and refused on any mismatch, while a zip without it — a zip of `main`, which has nothing to verify, or a release zip downloaded alone — is installed marked `UNVERIFIED`, because the zip place is the fallback for a machine that cannot take the normal way in (ADR-039, ADR-041) (R8, R9's zip-place sub-bullet; ADR-038). This differs from the existing plain-copy fallback below in what is kept: a plain copy is a tree someone unpacked and left on disk, installed by a binary BUILT FROM that same tree; a zip place keeps no tree at all — the archive is unpacked, installed with the binary already running, and removed, so there is nothing left to build from or diff against (ADR-038 D8, superseding ADR-034 for this one path: a release binary now installs a tree on disk when the operator names it with `--from-zip`, never a recorded or discovered one).

**The crossing to `fyr` (v3.0.0).** v3.0.0 publishes `fyr` assets only, under the one marker `# fyr vX.Y.Z` in `SHA256SUMS`, so a place on v2.7.0 or earlier does not move forward by its own `update`: an old binary finds no asset it asks for, a checkout's old build path no longer exists, and nothing is replaced. Each place is reinstalled by hand once, by `DEPLOY-remote` § Crossing to fyr; after that it moves forward as its kind always did.

## How a machine gets the harness

Three ways, and no fourth:

1. **A checkout the operator owns**, kept current with `fyr update` (§ The model). This is the normal path. The dirty-checkout refusal runs before the `--check` and `--dry-run` returns: on a checkout with uncommitted changes both print the real run's refusal and exit 1; a clean one exits 2 when behind and 0 when current.
2. **A release binary**, installed with `fyr install` and moved forward by `fyr update` (§ The model). One downloaded file carrying `context/`, `skills/`, `agents/`, `commands/` and `rules/` inside it, for a place that only USES the harness: the operator wanted no trail of this repository (then a docs tree, now `.agents/trail.jsonl`) sitting beside their other projects, where a session opened there could mistake it for the project's own. What `update` does there is § The model. That place changes only when a release is cut (ADR-033).
3. **A zip place**, moved forward by the operator repeating a download and `fyr update --from-zip <file>` (§ The model). For a machine that can hold neither the operator's SSH key nor run `gh` — a corporate workstation, say — and so can reach neither of the other two (ADR-038).

A plain copy with no `.git` still installs, and `update` refuses it with a message naming `install` still deploying it as it is and the alternatives above; it is no longer one of the ways in: it is the fallback for a machine that can reach none of them, and it differs from a zip place in what is kept — a plain copy is a tree someone unpacked and left on disk, while a zip place keeps no tree (§ The model).

Authentication is the operator's own SSH key and `gh` login, present on every machine because they log in as themselves. That is why no deploy keys, tokens or per-machine credentials exist anywhere in this design — they would restrict nothing and add key management. The accepted cost is theirs, stated plainly: "if I don't login in with ssh or gh I can't get updates." A release download needs that same credential, because the repository is private; a zip download needs it too, for the same reason; the plain copy is the fallback when that bites.

## What keeps consumers from changing the harness

Part shape, part credential. Only the four checkouts are repositories, and they belong to the operator. Everything downstream of them receives installed FILES: `fyr install` writes the context, skills, agents, commands and rules into a home and never creates a checkout there. But a checkout is not what changing the harness takes — a credential that can push to this repository is, and anything that reaches the operator's SSH key or `gh` login can clone and push, after which every place's `update` deploys it. So a home seeded for agents is read-only only when it reaches no such credential: no forwarded ssh-agent, no `gh` token, no readable key. The shape is provable here; the credential half is each host's to hold (security review 2026-09-17, finding 5).

State the shape as a property of `fyr install`, provable from this repository. Do not rest it on how any particular consumer seeds its homes — that was done once, in ADR-030 D4, and it is a dependency pointing the wrong way: if that consumer changes its entrypoint, a claim in this repository's decision record silently becomes false and nothing here would catch it. What `install` did is on its output, every run: one line per file it added, updated (including a previous file it could not read, written over as before), corrected the mode of, removed, or kept (a managed path already holds a file fyr did not write, left alone and counted separately), with the unchanged as a count; `--dry-run` prints the same lines and writes nothing (2026-09-18, the operator's "more info").

## What stays on the machine

Nothing comes back. A place's experience — the brain store (`brain.db`: every project's trail records and the global `feedback`, `retro` and `proposal` records), the search index (`search.db`), the metrics store (`metrics.db`) and the install manifest (`state.json`) — stays in `~/.config/fyr/` on the machine that wrote it (R7, ADR-062, ADR-071). The logs a place kept before the brain store (`feedback.jsonl`, `retros.jsonl`, `proposals/*.md`) are read into it by `fyr record import --global`, which lists them for the operator to remove; they are not where experience lives. The `report` verb and the `styrman-harness-feedback` repository it pushed to are gone; no verb and no code path replaces them, and no export bundle was built (plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md` D4). A harness-target proposal — a global `proposal` record that `/retro` or the dreamer queued — reaches this repository only by the operator's own hands: `/retro --harness`, run in a harness checkout on the machine whose queue it reads.

Being built by `PLAN-2026-10-28-1510-plan-the-visible-dream-2026-10-28` (Phase 5): its Phase 5 has yet to run the visible branch end to end against the real `agy`. Two things leave a machine, both to the model of the CLI the machine already uses (R8). The first is the dreamer's prompt: `fyr dream` sends each registered project's memory, trail, feedback and transcripts, redacted (`--all`, which the timer runs, takes only the projects registered with `fyr index --register`, ADR-068; `--project <root>`, typed by the operator, takes the root it names), to the model of the CLI the machine already uses, with no tools, headless in plan mode; in the operator's own Antigravity home when its settings grant no tool without review, where the conversation stays (R3's exception, ADR-047a, ADR-049, ADR-073; `SPEC-fyr-dream`). Its redaction (`internal/redact`) is structural, with no JSON walk, and it is a safety net, not a guarantee. The credential needles — vendor token prefixes, and case-insensitive password, secret, token and api-key assignments, `Bearer` and authorization headers written `Authorization: …` (colon form, a quoted header name included; a header set by a call such as `Header.Set("Authorization", …)` is an unlisted shape), URL credentials (including an empty user), token shapes pinned by length and alphabet (a JWT, an OpenAI or Stripe key, an npm or Hugging Face token), and a bare userinfo token in a URL — LOCATE a secret and never define how much is removed: a whole text line, a whole JSONL record, or a whole `-----BEGIN`-to-`-----END` block goes. This is the design the operator chose at the report path's cold-read cap, and the reasoning outlived that path: `AKIA` is a prefix, so replacing the matched token strips the marker and ships the key; a private key's header matches while its body carries no needle at all. Any span shorter than a structural unit leaks while reporting success. Slack tokens and webhook URLs have no needle of their own, by the operator's choice (`PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` D32 1): one goes only when a generic rule takes its line, an assignment to a name holding a password, secret, token or api-key word, or an authorization header, so `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL=https://hooks.slack.com/…` stays.

The second is `fyr eval`'s runs, which only the operator starts: each sandbox's prompts, and the files its agent reads in a clone of the fixture, go to that model unredacted, as in any session of that CLI, because the point is an agent working on the fixture as any session does (ADR-065; `SPEC-fyr-eval`). What eval writes stays on the machine: the sandboxes under `~/.config/fyr/eval/`, the `testing` record and the metrics rows.

`~/.config/fyr/` is created 0700 and every install tightens it to 0700 when it is looser and the directory is the caller's own and not a symlink (either case gets a `note:` instead); the other verbs that write there create it 0700 when absent but leave an existing one's mode alone.

## What is deliberately NOT being built

- **A webservice**, for delivery or for feedback. Git already carries delivery, and nothing comes back. A service adds hosting, per-machine authentication and an attack surface, for one user, against R3, R4 and local-by-default.
- **A way back**, by any transport: the report path was removed on 2026-10-24 (ADR-062), and an export bundle was rejected as a new transport nobody asked for (plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md` D4).
- **A signed-tag delivery channel.** ADR-026 designed one on 2026-09-16 to give a consumer host a trust root; ADR-030 withdrew it the next day because the operator authenticates as themselves everywhere, so it solved a problem that was not there. Tags survive as release markers — `v1.0.0` stands, and the versioning rule and the tag recipe stay in `DEPLOY-remote` (unsigned since v2.4.0, ADR-053); what a tag delivers today is § The model.
- **Vendored mirrors.** Two projects kept a `.git`-less copy refreshed by hand, which is why a mirror refresh kept appearing as a task in three repositories at once. They retire. Each consumer's own session does that work in its own repository.
- **Per-machine keys of any kind**, for the reason above.

## The rule that keeps this repository independent

> "styrman-harness and the feedback/trajectory should not be directly connected to any other project, if any other project wants to use the harness they need the fyr, that's it."

This repository names no consumer project in its living docs and depends on none. Knowing a consumer exists is fine; depending on its internals is not. The test is simple: **would the harness still be correct if every consumer vanished tomorrow?** If a document here needs another repository to be true, it is wrong, whatever it says.

This is easy to get wrong when several of those repositories sit side by side on one disk, because reading them costs nothing. It was got wrong once already, on 2026-09-17, in the same paragraph that stated the rule.

## Where things stand

**Built and shipped** (newest tag v3.1.0, 2026-10-27; v3.0.0, 2026-10-26, was the first to ship the binary as `fyr`; every tag through v2.7.0 shipped it as `sh-agent`, renamed in plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md` Phase 4a): `fyr` with install, sync, status, diff, update (checkout, release binary, `--from-zip`), uninstall, list, render, adopt, version, search and index (`SPEC-fyr-search`), memory and dream (`SPEC-fyr-memory-loop`, `SPEC-fyr-dream`) with the nightly timer, its unit named per home, and metrics (`SPEC-fyr-metrics`), with record (`SPEC-fyr-record`, ADR-063), check (`SPEC-fyr-check`, ADR-064) and eval (`SPEC-fyr-eval`, ADR-065) from v3.0.0; the context, 36 skills, 8 agents and 3 always-on rules as `fyr list` prints them for the tag (ADR-066 added the third); `update` refusing a dirty checkout on every path; the installer refusing secret-shaped files, symlinked destinations, duplicate skill names and the frontmatter shapes its lint names (`internal/harness/inventory.go` and its tests); one FlagSet per verb, usage errors exit 2. What each release added, v2.0.0 through v3.1.0, is its release entry under `changes/` (`*-release-v*.md`) and its release notes.

**The loop back is removed** (ADR-062, 2026-10-24): the `report` verb ran from 2026-09-17 (`TEST-2026-09-17-delivery-rework-e2e`) through v2.7.0; `main` has no `report` verb and no code that sends anything off the machine but the dreamer's redacted prompt and the operator's `fyr eval` runs (§ What stays on the machine). A place on v2.7.0 still has the verb until its crossing (`DEPLOY-remote` § Crossing to fyr; plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md` Phase 6), and the operator deletes `styrman-harness-feedback` in that phase.

**Open, defaulting to no:** whether this repository becomes public. Only that would let a machine bootstrap with no credential at all, and it is a question about content rather than packaging.

**Built, 2026-09-17:** what was here as "a follow-up with its own plan — versioned release bundles" is now the release binary above (ADR-033, `PLAN-2026-09-17-release-binary`). It needed no CI: the binary cross-compiles locally in `/preflight`, which writes the checksums (signed with the tag's key until v2.3.2; unsigned since v2.4.0, ADR-053). It does not remove the credential requirement while the repository is private.

## Agents

An agent is authored as `agents/<name>/agent.md` in Antigravity's format, and `fyr install` copies it unchanged to `~/.gemini/config/agents/<name>/agent.md`; nothing is derived (ADR-062, plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md` D3). The files are the derivation's output at its last commit, `a2e6a5a`, byte for byte (D17). The lint in `internal/harness/inventory.go` holds what the derivation guaranteed: the keys are `name`, `description`, `subagent`, `mainAgent`, `model` and `tools` (`agentKeys`; an old-format key such as `maxTurns` or `effort` is refused); `subagent: true` and `mainAgent: false`; every tool is one of `knownTools` (an unknown name fails the install, since an unrecognised name hangs the subagent); a flat `agents/<name>.md`, the format before ADR-062, is refused with the file named. A model is `pro` or `flash`, or omitted for the CLI's default. There is no `skills:` key: on 2026-10-01 a probe showed an Antigravity subagent reaches a global skill by the path its body names, with or without the vendor's `skills:` key (3 of 3 and 2 of 2 runs; plan audit-fix D5b), and there is no turn limit: the dispatch names the tool-call budget, and the main agent stops an agent whose artifact is on disk.

title: `fyr dream` — the background dreamer
body:
# `fyr dream` — the background dreamer

Status: built 2026-09-30 (plan `PLAN-2026-09-30-parity-memory-dream`). R3's named exception, R4's dream clause, R10 (ADR-047, ADR-047a, ADR-073). The memory half of the learning loop is `SPEC-fyr-memory-loop`.

## What it does

Being built by `PLAN-2026-10-28-1510-plan-the-visible-dream-2026-10-28` (Phase 5): the hourly timer, the session check, the cooldown and the status line are built (its Phase 2), the dream's own conversations are kept out of every reader (its Phase 3), and the branch per project and the first line are built (its Phases 4a and 4b); until its Phase 5 runs the visible branch against the real `agy`, that branch is checked only against agy's saved reports.

Before anything else, a real run (not `--dry-run`) runs `fyr metrics ingest` over every Antigravity session, store-wide whatever `--project` names, inside `dream.lock`. It logs the ingest's summary line to `dream.log`. A failure is logged as `metrics ingest failed: …` and changes neither the exit status nor `last_run.error` (plan `2026-10-08-metrics-store` D16; spec `SPEC-fyr-metrics`). A dry run prints `[dry-run] would ingest metrics into <path>` and writes nothing.

**The metrics block (R3's addendum, ADR-055a).** Each project's prompt carries a `metrics` input: `metrics.Summary.Numbers()` for the project's window (its watermark to now) and for the window of the same length before it, as JSON.
- **Numbers only.** Every key is the metrics package's own name (no tool, skill, agent, label or path), and a metric a CLI cannot produce is absent.
- **Read from a copy.** It is read from a copy of `metrics.db` (`metrics.Snapshot`). A store at another schema is named under "Left out", and no store or no session gives no block.
- **Context, never news.** It never marks a project changed and is dropped first when the prompt is over the cap.
- **How the instructions treat it.** A worsened metric is evidence only when the other inputs show its cause.

`fyr dream --all`, run hourly by a user timer (`--install-timer`) while an interactive `agy` session of the operator's runs, or by hand with `--all` or `--project <dir>`.

**The session check (ADR-073).** A real `--all` run first asks whether an interactive `agy` session of the operator's uid runs, before it creates `~/.config/fyr`, takes the lock, ingests or writes anything. A process counts when its real uid is the operator's (Linux: the first field of the `Uid:` line of `/proc/<pid>/status`, never the directory's owner; macOS: `ps -ww -U <uid> -o args=`, whose arguments are split at spaces, so an `agy` under a path holding one is not counted), its name is `agy` (the base name of its first argument, or of its `exe` link with a trailing ` (deleted)` removed, since `agy update` replaces the binary under a live session), and its arguments hold neither `-p`, `--print` nor its alias `--prompt`, with one dash or two and with or without `=value` (a headless run: the dream's own child, `fyr eval`, a script) nor, as the first non-flag argument, an `agy` subcommand (`remote-control`, `mcp`, `update` and the rest of the list `agy --help` prints); an entry that cannot be read is skipped, and the desktop app and the Hub are not `agy` processes. With none, the run prints `fyr dream: no agy session of this user; nothing to do` on stdout (the unit's journal), creates nothing and exits 0; a check that errors exits 2 with the error on stdout and creates nothing. `--project` never asks. `--all --dry-run` prints `[dry-run] agy session: yes` or `[dry-run] agy session: no (a real --all run would stop here)` first and goes on; a check that errors exits 2 there too.

**The cooldown (ADR-073).** Under `--all` a project whose CLI call started in the last 24 hours, success or failure, is skipped as `<root> skip attempted <time>`, in a dry run too, so an hourly timer tries a failing project once a day, as the nightly one did. `--project` ignores it: the operator asked.

`fyr dream` looks at every project in the global search index, `~/.config/fyr/search.db` `projects` (read from a copy, never opened live; a project whose trail is still files), and at every project scope of the brain store, `brain.db` (a project whose trail is records: such a checkout no longer registers in the file index; brain plan Phase 4). Under `--all` it takes from these two lists only the checkouts the operator registered under this home with `fyr index --register` (`trail.Registered(<home>/.config/fyr, root)`, a marker in the git common directory sealed to the checkout's main path and this home's key; ADR-068, ADR-068a): every other root is logged once per run as `<root> skip not registered (fyr index --register)`, in a dry run too (`[dry-run] <root>: skip (not registered (fyr index --register))`), so `fyr dream --dry-run --all` lists the projects to register (audit-choices D17); a root that is gone or no git checkout says so instead, since registering cannot help it; a clone or a copy of a registered checkout is not registered. `--project <dir>` takes the named checkout with no marker: naming it is the operator's opt-in (audit-choices D16). A project is skipped with a log line when its root is gone, it is not a git checkout, or it has neither `.agents/trail.jsonl` nor its docs root. Under `--all` (the timer's run) it is also skipped while it is in use (D22): a commit (read through `trail.Log`, which refuses a partial clone on a git older than 2.44), a record update in its scope (never one dated after now), or an Antigravity conversation in its workspace within the last 24 hours (`skip in use (<what, when>)`); `--project` dreams at once. One checkout reached by two paths (a worktree, a symlink) is one target. A dry run reads a copy of `brain.db` (under `~/.config/fyr/dream-brain-*`, swept like the other copies, whenever `~/.config/fyr` exists; with none, in the system's temporary directory, since a dry run never creates `~/.config/fyr`, which beside an old `~/.config/sh-agent` would stop the crossing's migration), so it creates, migrates and loads nothing. Otherwise, when anything changed since the project's watermark:

1. **Collect** (`internal/dream/collect.go`), in prompt order:
   - its memory: for a project whose trail is records, every `memory` record that is not retired (labelled by ID); for one still on files, the memory store `<root>/.agents/memory/`, whole, when the trust checks pass (otherwise it is named as left out);
   - its feedback: the global `feedback` records about it (each body, the old log's JSON line, redacted as a JSON line like the log's), and `feedback.jsonl` lines for this root where that old log still exists;
   - its trail: for a project of records, its `bug`, `review`, `retro`, `change` and `handoff` records (the checkout's `trail.jsonl` loaded first when it changed); for one still on files, its `bugs/`, `reviews/`, `retros/`, `changes/`, `handoffs/` files;
   - the installed skills' names and descriptions, read from `~/.gemini/config/skills` (global: never a change on their own);
   - Antigravity conversations that are the root's own, by `last_modified_time` (whole conversations, from copies of the databases; `internal/search/dream.go`): every URI in `workspace_uris` is a file URI under the root (a remote or unparsable one counts as outside), and the nearest directory of each still on disk resolves (`trail.Roots`) to the root's main worktree root (`internal/search/dream_workspace.go`, ledger item 77). A conversation under the root that fails this, one in a checkout nested inside it (a vendored clone, a submodule), one that also names a workspace outside the root, or one whose checkout cannot be read, is never sent: it is named among the left-out inputs by its ID and why, `transcript antigravity <id> (its workspace is a nested checkout, not this project)`, never by its path. A conversation with a workspace in dream-work, as written or with its symlinks followed (`harness.DreamWorkPaths`), is the dream's own and never the root's, even when the root holds the config directory (a checkout at `$HOME`): it is never sent, it is named `transcript antigravity <id> (a fyr dream conversation)` when a workspace of it is under the root, and the in-use check skips it (ADR-073). Known limit: a nested checkout deleted after its session is judged by the directory above it and reads as the root's own; one dated before 1970, Go's zero time among them, has no time and is not collected (BUG-181).

   Everything but memory and skills is taken only when newer than the watermark (a record by its `updated`, never one dated after now); a project's first dream reads the last 14 days. A tracked, unmodified trail file counts as changed at the time of its newest commit (`git log`), an untracked or modified file at its mtime. "Modified" compares the working file's raw bytes (`git hash-object --no-filters`) with HEAD's blob (`git ls-tree`); `git status` is never run, because it runs the repository's clean filters, so a file the repository filters reads as modified and keeps its mtime. Every git call into a project root goes through `internal/trail` (no index lock, no fsmonitor, no signature check, `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`; BUG-164); a partial clone is dated this way only on a git of 2.44 or later, and on an older git its trail keeps its mtimes (`trail.Readable`, SD17); so does a trail holding a tracked name git cannot hash by path, one with a newline or opening with `"` (BUG-188). A copy of an Antigravity database that is torn (the live one was being written) is copied and opened once more after a second; the live database is never opened. Only the user's (step_type 14) and the model's (15) Antigravity steps are read, never tool output; an Antigravity read error fails the project, so its watermark stays. A symlinked docs root or record directory is not followed and is named as left out.
2. **Scrub**: an input's fence runs (`>>>`, `<<<`) and its label's newlines are escaped in the prompt, and the project's name (the checkout's base name) is folded the same way once, for the prompt, the proposals header and the file names (SD15); every input, and its label (a trail file's name can hold a secret's shape, SD31 of the 2026-10-27 audit), passes the redactor in `internal/redact`, each feedback entry first as a JSON line through `harness.RedactJSONL` and the home path becomes `~`; `project:` and "left out" lines are written with `~` for the home too.
3. **Cap**: at 256 KB. The metrics summary is dropped first; then the dated kinds (transcripts, trail and feedback) together, newest first, two inputs of the same time in that order; then skills (ADR-069, amending ADR-055a). What a capped run sends is the oldest news, and the run's `Through` is set just before the oldest dated input it dropped, so step 6 stops the watermark there and the next run offers the dropped inputs again. A drop holds the watermark back only while an input strictly older than it is kept. A dated input larger than what the cap leaves after the prompt's head, memory and the skills is dropped first and holds nothing back (audit-choices D33); so does one of the oldest time left — the last dated input when the left-out line leaves no room, or part of a group of one time (records from one commit) bigger than the room — since a time watermark cannot split such a group, and holding it there would drop the same part every night. Two inputs of one time and kind drop the later label first. The metrics summary and the skills are undated and hold nothing back. A project whose memory alone passes the cap fails. The prompt names what was left out, each as `<kind> <label> (dropped to fit the 256 KB cap)`, `<kind> <label> (too big for the 256 KB cap beside memory and skills)` for one too big, or `<kind> <label> (dropped to fit the 256 KB cap; not sent again)` for one of the oldest time left: the cap is on the whole prompt, not on one input (SD29); a dry run prints one `left out:` line for each of the first five and counts the rest (SD-S2). The size is counted from the prompt's parts once and kept by arithmetic as inputs drop, so a project's prompt is rendered once (SD-S1).
4. **Ask**: one CLI call with NO tools, headless in plan mode, from the empty `~/.config/fyr/dream-work/`, 10-minute timeout, the child getting an allow-listed environment: `PATH`, `LANG`, the locale category names (`LC_ALL`, `LC_CTYPE`, `LC_TIME` and the other ten, never any other `LC_` name), `TERM`, `TMPDIR`, `TZ`, the proxy variables in both cases, `SSL_CERT_FILE` and `SSL_CERT_DIR` from fyr's own, then `HOME` set to the home of the branch below, and nothing else, so no other variable, a credential exported in the operator's shell among them, reaches the process that reads the prompt; a listed variable passes as it is, so a proxy URL with a password in it does reach `agy` (ADR-067; a name joins only after a run shows agy needs it, by the operator, and a login that needs a dropped variable fails with the `not logged in` or `invalid output` hint); the CLI runs in its own process group, which is killed whole at the deadline, on SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP or SIGQUIT (then fyr dies of the signal as before; an interrupt or hangup fyr started with ignored, under `nohup` or as a background job, stays ignored and leaves the CLI alone), and once the CLI itself has exited; a helper it started that keeps the output pipes open past a clean exit is cut loose 30 s later and the answer is kept (BUG-169 and its review).
   - The CLI is `agy`: `agy --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --mode plan -p ""`, the prompt on stdin as one stream-json message and the answer read from the final `result` event's `response`; a result naming `denied_actions` is no answer. The prompt's first line is `dreaming: <project>` (the name folded to one line as in step 2), then a blank line and the instructions with their `Project:` line. agy has no no-tools flag: plan mode, a home whose settings grant no tool without review and the prompt's warning (its second paragraph: every tool call is refused and ends the run with no answer) keep it from calling one (D7b). The home is chosen per project, just before its call, and `dream.log` names it first: `<root> agy home visible` or `<root> agy home private (<why>)`, the reason redacted, folded to one line and stripped of control characters, its paths as written. A dry run asks the oracle too and prints, per project it would dream over, `[dry-run] <root>: agy home visible (HOME <home>)`, `agy home private (<why>): a copy of the login, with no grants`, the same with `, would fail: <reason>` when the private home could not be built, or, before any real run has made dream-work, `agy home not asked: no dream-work yet; a real run makes it, then asks the oracle` (a dry run makes nothing).
