   - **Visible branch** (ADR-073): the operator's own Antigravity home, `--home` (by default `$HOME`, never `$HOME` when they differ, R6), so the conversation is written to `<home>/.gemini/antigravity-cli` beside the operator's own and `/resume` lists it. It is taken only when `agy -p "/permissions" --output-format json`, `agy -p "/config" --output-format json` and `agy -p "/hooks" --output-format json` (the oracle: run with that `HOME`, from dream-work, with the same environment, 30 s each; they start no turn, spend no quota and leave no conversation) show, with fyr's own checks of the home and dream-work, all of (`visibleHome`, `internal/dream/agy_visible.go`; the fields are what agy 1.4.9 reported in the plan's D24 sandbox runs): the login in that home (`antigravity-oauth-token` under `<home>/.gemini/antigravity-cli`, or on macOS a `<home>/Library/Keychains` directory); dream-work empty, and no directory above it, as written or as it resolves, holding a `.git` or a `.agents` other than the home's own (agy loads the `.agents/` of every directory from its working directory up, and the reports name no workspace or project root, so fyr walks it); `/config`'s `toolPermission` `request-review` or `strict`, its `agentMode` empty or `plan` and its `artifactReviewPolicy` `asks-for-review`; no allow rule in any scope `/permissions` lists (project, shared, global; deny and ask rules grant nothing) nor in `/config`'s `permissions`, `allowNonWorkspaceAccess` false, and no `trustedWorkspaces` entry at or above dream-work; `/hooks` an empty list (a pre-tool hook can return a permission decision none of the reports show, so a home with any hook, a plugin's included, runs private; the plan's D26); and each report one JSON object with status `SUCCESS`, each field of the type seen, `/config` holding exactly the 36 keys agy 1.4.9 reported (a key added or gone is an unknown shape, so an agy upgrade that adds a setting sends the dream private until fyr learns it) and its `permissions` no key but `allow`, `deny` and `ask`. Anything else — a report that fails, times out, does not parse, lacks a field, or holds a key fyr does not know in a scope — sends that project to the private branch. fyr never writes the operator's settings; in this branch the no-tools guarantee is the oracle's report, not isolation.
   - **Private branch**: a private HOME, `~/.config/fyr/dream-agy-home-*`, holding a copy of the operator's `antigravity-oauth-token` and `installation_id` (taken from `$HOME`, never `--home`) and a settings file that grants nothing; on macOS, where agy keeps the login in the Keychain and finds it only through `$HOME/Library/Keychains`, that folder is linked into the private HOME (never copied) and the token file is copied only when it exists (BUG-166); the dream job's agy then uses the operator's real Keychain, so a login refresh it makes is the interactive agy's too, unlike Linux, where it only ever touches a copy. It is built on the run's first private project, reused by the run's later private projects, and removed after the run; a failure to build it (no login — no token file, and on macOS no `~/Library/Keychains` either) fails that project with `fail <reason>`, not the run, and the run exits 1. An agy that asks for a browser login (a locked Keychain, an expired login) fails the project, and the log line appends `agy is not logged in inside the dream job's private HOME`, or in the visible branch `inside the operator's Antigravity home (--home)`.
   - A `HOME` that is not an absolute path cannot give the private branch a login: a project that needs it fails, exit 1.

   `--vendor` is a usage error (exit 2). "No `agy` on PATH" is the failure before the first project.
5. **Write**: the first `{…}` of the answer that decodes as `{"proposals":[…],"skills":[…]}`, scrubbed again. Unknown keys are ignored; the fields used are validated.
   - Each proposal is one global `proposal` record (`brain.Propose`; D15): title `Dream, project — <title>` or `Dream, harness — <title>` by its target (so `/retro` and `/retro --harness` each take theirs from the title), `project` the root, status `queued`; a project's proposals are stored in one transaction (`brain.ProposeAll`), all or none; its body names the project, the day, the CLI and the input counts (and what was left out), then `Target: project|harness   Kind: …   File: …`, the model's text indented by four spaces (so it reads as quoted data, never as a field or heading of the record) and `Evidence: …`. Title and body are normalized first (a control character as `?`, the title cut to one line of 512 bytes).
   - `proposals/dream/drafts/<date>-<project>-<name>/SKILL.md`: each draft skill with a kebab-case name, files as before; one more `proposal` record, `Dream, harness — draft skills for <project>`, names each draft's path and each dropped (invalid) name.

   One-line fields (title, kind, file, evidence) have line breaks folded. A project with zero proposals and no draft stores no record (and creates no brain store).
6. **Advance** the watermark, only after a successful parse and write: to the cap's `Through` when step 3 dropped a dated input that holds it back and that instant is before the run's start, else to the run's start. Every dated input older than the new watermark was sent, or named as too big or not sent again; one of the same time as the oldest held back may be sent twice, and a re-sent input may give a duplicate global `proposal`, which `/retro` drops by hand (D33).

**Where the data goes:** to the model of `agy`, the one CLI the run uses and the only one whose transcripts are read. In the visible branch the redacted prompt and the answer also stay in the operator's Antigravity store, as a conversation of its own; a conversation whose workspace is dream-work (as written or through its symlinks) is no project's: it is never ingested into the metrics store and never read by any project's dream or in-use check. From Antigravity, only the user's input and the model's replies are read (step types 14 and 15), and each step's payload is decoded as protobuf by its wire format, with no schema (D30): a length-delimited field that is printable UTF-8 is a text leaf, anything else is tried as a nested message. A leaf is sent only when it has three spaces or more and is not JSON, so a tool call's arguments (a command, a file written), which are one whole JSON string field, never reach the prompt. On the 95 conversation databases of the Linux box, 971 prose leaves were kept and none carried a tool-argument key.
**Hardening details:**
- The private branch's agy settings are `{"toolPermission":"request-review","permissions":{"allow":[]},"trustedWorkspaces":[]}`.
- A stream result whose status is not `SUCCESS`, or that names `denied_actions`, is no answer.
- Each `feedback.jsonl` entry is redacted as a JSON line (`redact.RedactJSONL` in `internal/redact`, which matches the decoded line) before the raw `scrub`, because a secret JSON-escaped on the line (`&sig=…` written as `\u0026sig=…` by `json.Marshal`) does not match the raw-text needles.
- The timer freezes only the absolute entries of the installing shell's PATH.
- The systemd service sets `TimeoutStartSec=2h`: a oneshot has no start timeout by default, and a `Persistent=` timer does not start a unit that is still active, so a run hung past the per-project kill is ended and the next scheduled run starts (SD36; ledger D2). launchd has no start timeout, and the plist sets none. A unit installed by an older fyr lacks the line and is kept as it is, since `--install-timer` never overwrites a unit with other text: `fyr dream --remove-timer`, then `--install-timer`, writes the current one. The limit bounds the whole run, not one project; each project's watermark is saved as it finishes, so the next run goes on from there. The schedule is `OnCalendar=hourly` (`Persistent=true`), and in the plist a `StartCalendarInterval` with `Minute` 0 and no `Hour`; a unit an older fyr installed with the nightly schedule (`OnCalendar=*-*-* 03:00`, `Hour` 3) is kept as it is, for the same reason, and `fyr status` names it: `timer installed, older schedule: fyr dream --remove-timer, then fyr dream --install-timer`.
- The timer's unit name is per home (`dream.UnitFor(home)`): the real home (the account's home from the account database, `os/user` by uid, never `HOME`, which a sandbox run overrides; path cleaned; an account the database does not list — on Linux a release binary reads only `/etc/passwd`, so LDAP, SSSD and systemd-homed accounts and a container's bare uid — has no real home, and every home there gets the suffix) gets the bare `fyr-dream` (systemd) and `com.fyr.dream` (launchd label; plist `com.fyr.dream.plist`); any other `--home` gets `-<first 8 hex of sha256 of the cleaned home path>` appended to both. Install, remove, the installed check and the unit-file paths all derive the name from the same home, and the unit's command is `dream --all --home <that home>`, so a scratch timer dreams over its own home's index, never the real one. A symlinked spelling of the real home counts as the real home (`os.SameFile`). Why: the user service manager is shared by every home of the user, so a scratch `--install-timer`, `--remove-timer` or `uninstall` must never reach the operator's own timer (R6; BUG-144). Before v3.0.0 the names were `sh-agent-dream` and `com.styrman.sh-agent-dream`, suffixed per home the same way: `fyr install` replaces this home's unit under the old name (`dream.ReplaceOldTimer`) after the files and the binary are written, installing the new unit first (with the installing shell's PATH, as `--install-timer` does) and only then stopping the old one (`systemctl --user disable --now <old>.timer`, `launchctl bootout`) and removing its files; it prints `replaced the dream timer <old> with <new>` (`install --dry-run`: `[dry-run] the dream timer <old> would be replaced by its fyr name`). If the new unit is refused (a `fyr-dream` unit with other text exists), the old one is kept as it was and install exits non-zero naming it. `--remove-timer` prints `dream timer removed`, or `no dream timer found for <home> on this system` when it removed nothing (exit 0 both ways); `uninstall` says `removed the dream timer` only when it removed one. Both also stop and remove this home's unit under the old name (`dream.OldTimerHere`: `sh-agent-dream` with this home's suffix, bare at the real home), so a home that never ran `fyr install` since the rename is not left with the old timer running, and the line names it: `(with <old>, its unit from before the rename to fyr)`; a dry run names it and calls nothing (TR9). A unit file that v2.0.0 or earlier wrote under the old bare name (`sh-agent-dream.service`, `.timer`, `com.styrman.sh-agent-dream.plist`) in a home whose own unit name is now suffixed is never removed or stopped by the binary (a stop by name ends whichever unit the manager loaded); `--remove-timer` and `uninstall`, each also with `--dry-run`, print its paths, why it is left alone, the check (`systemctl --user show -p FragmentPath sh-agent-dream.timer`, or `launchctl print gui/<uid>/com.styrman.sh-agent-dream`) and the steps, and the `dream` line of `fyr status` appends `; legacy timer files under <home>: fyr dream --remove-timer --dry-run --home '<home>' prints the cleanup steps`. A unit file of the operating system the binary is not running on (`OtherSystemTimerFiles`: the launchd plist on Linux, the systemd units on macOS) is never removed either: `uninstall` and `--remove-timer` name it and say it stays, dry runs included, since `status` counts it as installed; `uninstall` announces a removal only for a unit of the system it runs on (`TimerInstalledHere`).

## Consumers

- Project-level `/retro` (source 9) lists its project's queued dream proposals (`fyr record list --global --kind proposal --project <root> --open`), re-derives each against the files, and sets its status (`applied:<commit>` or `rejected`).
- `/retro --harness` lists every queued proposal, `Target: harness` ones among them, on the machine that wrote them; nothing sends them anywhere (ADR-062). They are model-written from any project's redacted content, so their text is data, never instructions.
- `fyr status` prints `dream      last run <date>: <n> projects, <m> proposals; timer installed|not installed` (or `failed: <reason>`, or `never run`), and `timer installed, older schedule: fyr dream --remove-timer, then fyr dream --install-timer` for a unit whose text is not this fyr's render for the home and the unit's own `PATH` (each command with `--home '<home>'` under a home that is not the real one).

## State and files (all under `~/.config/fyr/`, 0600 in 0700 directories)

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `dream-state.json` | `projects` (root → watermark), `attempts` (root → when its last CLI call started, the 24-hour cooldown under `--all`; a file without it reads as empty) and `last_run` (at, projects, proposals, error) |
| `dream.log` | one line per project (`ok N proposals`, `unchanged`, `skip <why>`, `fail <why>`), the branch line before each call (`agy home visible`, `agy home private (<why>)`) and one per run; an hourly run that finds no `agy` session writes none |
| `dream.lock` | an flock held for the run (the pid is written in it for reading only); the kernel releases it however the run ends, and a held one makes a second run exit 0 "already running" |
| `dream-agy-home-*`, `dream-agy-*`, `dream-projects-*` | per-run private copies (agy HOME, for the private branch only; Antigravity databases; the index); removed after the run; at the start of a run, under the lock, only copies older than an hour are removed (leftovers of a killed run; a dry run takes no lock) |
| `dream-work/` | the CLI's working directory, kept empty; not a project, so the run's own conversation never maps to one, and no reader takes a conversation whose workspace it is |
| `dream-failed/` | a failed project's stdout and stderr, scrubbed; files older than 30 days are pruned at the start of a run |
| `brain.db` | the proposal records above |
| `proposals/dream/drafts/` | the draft skills above |

Outside `~/.config/fyr/`, in the visible branch only: each project's dream conversation, in `<home>/.gemini/antigravity-cli`, kept by agy as its own state beside the operator's conversations (R3: "beside the conversation the CLI itself keeps"); fyr writes nothing there itself.

## Failure modes

| Situation | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Any failure before the first project: usage, no `agy` on PATH, an unreadable index | exit 2 with a run log line and `last_run.error`; `status` says `failed`. A usage error writes nothing, exits 2 and prints on stdout (not stderr) its reason, dream's synopsis and `run 'fyr help dream' for its flags`, as every verb's usage error does (ledger item 86); `fyr dream` with neither `--all` nor `--project` has no reason line, only the synopsis and the hint. A `--dry-run` makes the same `agy` check and exits 2 with the same message, writing nothing (SD27 of the 2026-10-27 audit); no login under `$HOME` or a relative `HOME` is the private branch's, a project's `would fail` on its branch line (the plan's D12) |
| `dream-state.json` is corrupt | exit 2, and the file is NOT rewritten |
| `--dry-run` with `--install-timer` or `--remove-timer` | both take `--dry-run`: writes nothing, calls no manager. `--install-timer --dry-run` makes every refusal the install makes (no binary at `<home>/.local/bin/fyr`, a quote, backslash or control character in a path, no service manager on PATH, a unit on disk with other text, an OS with no user timer) and exits 2 with its message (SD26) |
| `--install-timer` or `--remove-timer` with `--all` or `--project` | a usage error: `fyr dream: --install-timer and --remove-timer take no --all or --project`, exit 2 (SD33) |
| No interactive `agy` session of this user when an `--all` run starts | one line on stdout (the unit's journal), nothing in `dream.log` or `dream-state.json`, no directory created; exit 0; the next hour asks again |
| The session check errors (an unreadable `/proc`; on macOS `ps` missing or its output unparsable) | exit 2, the error on stdout, nothing created; `systemctl --user status` shows the failed unit |
| The oracle fails, times out, or reports a grant or a shape fyr does not know | that project runs in the private branch; `dream.log` names why; no conversation in `/resume` |
| The private home cannot be built for a project (no login under `$HOME`, a relative `HOME`) | that project fails, `<root> fail <reason>`, before its call, so it is not counted as attempted; the run goes on; exit 1 |
| The CLI exits non-zero or times out | the project fails, its output goes to `dream-failed/`, its watermark stays; the others run; exit 1; under `--all` it is not attempted again for 24 hours; in the visible branch the failed conversation stays in `/resume` |
| A machine keeps its nightly unit after the upgrade | `fyr status` names the older schedule; `--install-timer` refuses the unit's other text until `--remove-timer` |
| Two `agy` processes write the operator's store at once (the dream and a session) | agy's own design: the desktop app, the Hub, Remote Control and several sessions share that store; fyr adds nothing |
| The answer has no decodable JSON | the same, logged `fail invalid output` |
| An agy stdout line over 16 MiB | the same, logged `fail output line too long or unreadable` |
| The docs root or a record directory is a symlink | not followed; named as left out |
| A symlinked `.agents` or `trail.jsonl` in a project of records | the brain store refuses it; the project fails, its watermark stays |
| The store is a symlink, or git tracks it | memory is left out and named in the prompt and the proposal frontmatter; the rest is sent |
| Memory alone over 256 KB | the project fails with `memory over cap` |
| Dated inputs over the cap | the newest are dropped and named, and the watermark stops just before the oldest of them, so the next run sends them; one too big to fit beside memory and the skills is named `too big for the 256 KB cap beside memory and skills`, and the part of a group of one time that does not fit `not sent again`; neither is sent (ADR-069) |
| `feedback.jsonl` is not a regular file, or holds a line over 4 MiB | read up to there; the prompt and the dry run name `feedback.jsonl: …` as left out; never a block on a FIFO, never a silent drop (SD59b of the 2026-10-27 re-audit) |
| No indexed project and no project scope | nothing to do; exit 0 |
| An indexed project or project scope that is not registered under this home (`--all`) | `skip not registered (fyr index --register)`, nothing of it read or sent, not counted in `- run <n> projects`; exit 0 |
| Every project in use within the day | each skipped `in use`; exit 0 |
| A second run while one runs | exit 0, "already running" |

## Known limits

- **The oracle-to-call window** (ADR-073). The visible branch's settings are read just before each project's call; a setting changed between the report and the call applies to that call, for the one project.
- **The shared and project rule scopes are read, not proven** (the plan's D24). `/permissions` lists a `shared` and a `project` scope beside `global`, and fyr refuses an allow rule in any of them, but the sandbox runs could not put a rule in either (their files are not documented), so that agy reports them there is agy's word; a global allow rule was reported.
- **A visible dream loads what the operator's sessions load** (ADR-073, the plan's D8, accepted by the operator; narrowed by D26). The operator's MCP servers and plugins, and the skills of a `.agents` in their home, start as in any session they open under it; a home with any hook, a plugin's included, is not taken (a hook can approve a tool), so the model still has no tool it may use without review.
- **A resumed dream is a session like any other** (security review of Phases 2–4b). The conversation's first message is the redacted but untrusted prompt; the oracle's verdict held when the dream ran, and the operator who opens it with `/resume` continues it under the settings in force then, with whatever tools those grant, so a directive planted in a project's text reaches a session that may act on it. The prompt marks every input as data, never instructions.
- **Only an `agy` process counts as a session.** The desktop app and the Hub are not `agy` processes, so working only there does not let the timer dream. The macOS check is verified only by the operator's Mac run (`PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` A2).
- **A scratch timer on Linux is files only** (audit SD34, `PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` item 9). `--install-timer` with a `--home` that is not the real one writes its units under `<home>/.config/systemd/user`, which the user manager does not search, so `systemctl --user enable --now fyr-dream-<hash>.timer` cannot load them and the files stay; the `systemctl --user daemon-reload` before it still runs on the real, shared user manager. § State and files' "a scratch timer dreams over its own home's index" holds on macOS, where `launchctl bootstrap` takes the plist's own path, and on Linux only with that directory linked into the real one. Reasoned from systemd's search path, not run: the run would reach the operator's real user manager.
- **A killed run leaves its copies until the next run** (audit SD35, item 10). The private HOME (`dream-agy-home-*`, holding the copy of the Antigravity login token) and the read copies (`dream-agy-*`, `dream-projects-*`, `dream-brain-*`, `dream-metrics-*`, `metrics-agy-*`) are removed when a run ends; a run killed by SIGKILL or a power loss leaves them, in 0700 `~/.config/fyr`, until the next run sweeps every one older than an hour. With the timer removed, nothing sweeps them. Same account, so no new reader.

## Verification

Unit tests use a fake CLI on PATH that records its arguments, working directory and stdin (`internal/dream/fakecli_test.go`, used by `internal/dream/run_test.go` and `internal/dream/run_agy_test.go`), so the tool-free flags, the cwd, the absence of a planted secret in the prompt, the file shapes and the watermark rule are pinned; `internal/dream/collect_fit_test.go` pins the cap's drop order, its wording and `Through`, and `TestTwoRunsSendEveryCappedInput` the two-run case. The D7 probe (plan) ran both real CLIs tool-free from an untrusted, empty directory. The end-to-end rows are in `GUIDE-skill-matrix` and `GUIDE-fyr-matrix`.

title: `fyr eval` — behavioural rows against the Antigravity CLI
body:
# `fyr eval` — behavioural rows against the Antigravity CLI Owner: main. Decided by ADR-065; built by `PLAN-2026-10-26-0659-plan-fyr-eval-the-antigravity-run-kit-as-a-verb` (the D-rows cited below are that plan's). Code: `cmd/fyr/eval.go`, `internal/eval/`. ## Purpose The operator runs a project's behavioural scenarios ("rows") against the real Antigravity CLI, each in its own throwaway sandbox, with the safety checks the old run kit's preamble made around every run, and keeps the result: one `testing` record per invocation and one labelled metrics row per session, so runs compare over time. It is the release rule's "one run of each changed skill and agent on Antigravity" as a verb, usable in any project that commits a suite. It is not a gate (nothing runs it but the operator, R3), not a compare verb (D7), and not parallel. ## Interfaces ### The verb ``` fyr eval --home DIR [--fixture DIR] ... fyr eval --list ``` | Flag | Meaning | |---|---| | `--fixture DIR` | the git repository each row clones; default the project root. It is only ever cloned, never written. | | `--list` | print the suite, one line per row: ` `; takes no row; runs nothing and reads the working export without the HEAD comparison (D19) | | `--home DIR` | required for a run (`--list` takes none): fyr's home, where the sandboxes, the brain store the record goes to, and the metrics store live. Refused, exit 2, after the usage errors and before every refusal that reads the tree and before the state-dir migration, so a refused run writes nothing (ledger D37): a missing `--home`; a real home, which is `$HOME` and the account's home from the account database; and a home that reaches a real home's state, compared by file identity (`os.SameFile`, so a symlink, a hard link, a bind mount or a case variant of the path all count) at ``, `/.config`, `/.config/fyr` (also against the old `~/.config/sh-agent`) and every entry directly in it (the stores, their `-wal` and `-shm` files, `registration.key`, `eval/`), each against the real entry of the same name, or through a dangling link at any of them. Asked again before each row's ingest and before the record is written, since a row's agent could link the home meanwhile | | `--repo DIR` | the harness each sandbox gets, resolved as `fyr install` resolves it (D16): `--repo`, `$FYR_REPO`, the working directory and its parents, then the home's last install; a release binary installs its embedded harness and refuses `--repo` | The project root is the top level of the working directory's git checkout. A sandbox is `/.config/fyr/eval///`, `` being `%F-%H%M%S` taken once per invocation; it holds `app/` (the clone), `home/` (the HOME the CLI runs with), `out.txt`, `out2.txt`, `err.txt`, and the logs `install.log`, `setup.log` and `check.log`. Sandboxes are kept; `fyr uninstall` leaves them, since they are not in its manifest. Output, one line per row as it finishes, then the record: ``` eval: PASS|FAIL[ (; )] agy exit s eval:

of PASS; record TEST-… ``` Exit 0 when every row passed, 1 when any failed (or an ingest or the record failed), 2 for a refusal before any row ran. Every printed id and path goes through the printable filter of `fyr search`. Refusals and usage lines go to stdout with the row lines, unlike `fyr check`, which prints its refusal on stderr (IN34 of the 2026-10-27 audit). ### The suite: `GUIDE-eval` A `guide` record of the project, read from `.agents/trail.jsonl` at the project root (never from the brain store). Any prose may surround exactly one Markdown table with this header: ``` | id | setup | prompt | prompt2 | check | agent | grants | ``` - A row line starts with ``| ` ``; cells split on unescaped `|`, and `\|` is a literal `|`. One surrounding pair of backticks is stripped; a `setup` or `check` cell that starts with a backticked span followed by more text keeps only the span (D23). - `id`: the first backticked token of the first cell, one path element of `a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_`, `-`. - `setup`: bash run in the clone before the CLI starts; may be empty. - `prompt` (required) and `prompt2` (optional, a second session on the same home after the first exits 0): literal text with four placeholders eval substitutes itself, never through a shell: `{{CLONE}}`, `{{SB}}`, `{{FIXDIR}}`, `{{STAMP}}` (`%F-%H%M` at the row's start) (D21). - `check`: bash, required; exit 0 is a pass. - `agent`: empty, or an agent the conversation store must show invoked. - `grants`: `named` (the fixed allow list) or `wide: ` (`command(*)`; the reason is printed). `setup` and `check` run in the clone with exactly: `PATH` (eval's own), `HOME` and `SB` (the sandbox home), `OUT`, `OUT2` (the two stdout files), `FIXDIR` (the fixture), `CLONE` (the clone); `setup` also gets the git identity `fixture` / `f@localhost`. ### One row, in order 1. Make the sandbox directory; an existing one fails the row. 2. Clone the fixture (`--no-hardlinks`, every `GIT_*` variable removed); the clone must be its own top level; guards a and b on the real paths. 3. Write `SB/records-before.txt` from `fyr record list --home SB` in the clone. 4. Fingerprint the real config (check c), before `setup`, so a setup that writes it fails the row (IN50 of the 2026-10-27 audit). 5. Run `setup`. 6. `fyr install --home SB` with the resolved source; a wrapper `SB/bin/fyr` pins `--home SB` on every fyr call the agent makes and refuses a `--home` of the agent's own (fyr's flags are last-wins). 7. Write the sandbox's `settings.json`: the grants, and `trustedWorkspaces` holding only the clone. 8. Take the credential baseline of the sandbox directory (check d). 9. Link the operator's login token into SB. 10. Run `agy -p "The project root is the current directory, ; ignore any other checkout. " --mode accept-edits --print-timeout 20m` in the clone, with an allowlisted environment, stdin `/dev/null`, in its own process group; at 25 minutes only agy itself is killed. `prompt2` follows when the first exit was 0 and the sandbox is still intact (below). 11. Remove the token link and `settings.json` by name, through an `os.Root` on SB opened at step 2 and held to step 14 (it follows the directory through a rename, and refuses a link leading out of it); warn when the link was replaced or the real token is no longer a regular file. 12. Count `auto-denied` in `err.txt` and `invalid allow entry` in the newest CLI log. 13. Run `check`; then check f. A conversation database over 64 MiB is not read; the row notes it (`: over 64 MiB, not read`) and check f counts it as not found (IN51). 14. Exit checks c, d and e; then SIGKILL to agy's process group. 15. Verdict: PASS only when the check exited 0, the named agent was invoked, both counts are 0 and every exit check passed. The agy exit status is printed and is not a verdict condition. A failure in steps 1–8 fails the row with its reason and skips 9–13; step 14 still runs. The agent can write in the sandbox directory, so before `prompt2`, after step 11 and again before check d the sandbox directory, the clone and SB must still resolve to the paths guard a approved: otherwise the row FAILs `sandbox replaced`, and nothing is removed, run, scanned or ingested through them; check e matches the approved paths, never a fresh resolution, whether or not the clone still exists. A file eval reads or writes in the sandbox (`err.txt`, `out.txt`, the logs, a conversation database) is opened without following a link and without blocking, and anything but a regular file is refused; a file eval writes that is refused fails the row `sandbox replaced`. Then `cmd/fyr` ingests each started row's sandbox home into the metrics store with label `eval=` and outcome `pass` or `fail`, after the verdict and in row order (D6, D22), and writes the record. ### Safety checks - a. Refused roots: after resolving links, the clone and the sandbox home are absolute, and neither is `/`, the real home or a parent of it, or the install source's tree or a parent of it. - b. Outside every checkout: `git rev-parse --git-dir` fails with git's own discovery failure, `not a git repository (or any of the parent directories)`, in the nearest existing ancestor of the sandbox root (before anything is created) and in the clone's parent. It fails closed: git runs in the C locale with discovery across mounts, and any other error, a `.git` file whose gitdir is gone included, counts as inside. A `--home` inside a checkout is refused (BUG-106). - c. Real config unchanged: the real home's `~/.config/fyr` (minus `eval/`), `~/.config/sh-agent`, `~/.gemini/config` and `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json`, fingerprinted by relative path, type, mode, size, content hash and link target, before install and at step 14; the differing paths are printed, never content. - d. No new credentials in the sandbox directory (the clone, the CLI's output, the logs and SB): the kit's name, path and content patterns, scanned at step 8 as a baseline and at step 14; a path absent from the baseline, or whose matched patterns or match count grew, fails the row. A dangling link or a link to a directory fails unless the baseline held it with the same target (a directory link the fixture tracks is the fixture's), and a directory link that resolves outside the scanned directory always fails, since nothing walks what it leads to; an unreadable file, or one over 64 MiB (not read), always fails (D17, D32, D37). A `node_modules` directory beside a regular lockfile (`package-lock.json`, `npm-shrinkwrap.json`, `yarn.lock`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `bun.lock`, `bun.lockb`) is a package manager's install: its files are checked by name, path, link and readability, never read, because third-party code carries credential-shaped strings of its own; a link inside it that resolves outside the scanned directory is read as anywhere else, and a file over 64 MiB inside it does not fail, since it is not read (BUG-185). The scan root itself is never such an install. The scan never follows the sandbox directory itself when it is a link. Only paths are printed. - e. No processes left (Linux, `/proc`): a process of the same uid whose cwd or exe lies under the clone or SB as guard a approved them, or whose environment holds exactly `HOME=`, is named, sent SIGTERM, and fails the row. - f. Agent invoked: some `SB/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversations/*.db` holds the bytes `"TypeName":""` (D11, D24). ### The testing record Kind `testing`, status `closed`, in the evaluated project's scope of ``'s brain store (so it is exported to the project's `.agents/trail.jsonl`). Title `Eval —

of PASS at `. Body: the fyr version, the project and fixture HEADs, the install source (a tree, marked `(dirty)` when `git status --porcelain` there is non-empty, or `embedded `), the first line of `agy --version`, a line naming the skipped process check off Linux, and a table `row | verdict | reasons | agy exit | seconds | sandbox`. No output of the CLI or a check goes in it. ### Code shape ```go package eval type Row struct{ ID, Setup, Prompt, Prompt2, Check, Agent, Grants string } func ParseSuite(body string) ([]Row, error) func SelectRows(suite []Row, names []string) ([]Row, error) func Expand(prompt string, vars map[string]string) string func Preflight(o Options) error // checkout, then guards a and b on the sandbox root func Run(ctx context.Context, o Options, rows []Row) ([]Result, error) ``` `brain.ParseTrail(io.Reader)` parses an export that is not a file in the checkout (HEAD's, from `git show`) under the same cap and line rules as `brain.ReadTrail`. ## Data - Sandboxes: written only by eval, under the sandbox root, never pruned. - `GUIDE-eval`: written by the operator with `fyr record`; eval only reads it. - The `testing` record: written once per invocation by `cmd/fyr` after every row. - Metrics rows: before the ingest, eval registers the row's clone under the eval home (`trail.Register(/.config/fyr, )`, ledger item 76), so the metrics join reads the clone's trail and the row's `eval=` sessions get their handoff, testing, review and bug events; the operator's run of `fyr eval` is the consent, the marker lives in the clone's own git directory and dies with the sandbox, and its seal names the eval home's key. A clone that is a link, or whose git directory or top level resolves outside it (a `.git` file the agent pointed at another repository), is not registered, since the marker would be written there; nor is one when `--home` resolves to the real home or shares its state directory through a link (the seal would take the real key and the join would load the agent's trail into the real brain store). Then its sessions are still ingested, without record events, and the ingest fails with `the clone was not registered, so its sessions have no record events: `. On a system where check e does not run (`ProcsChecked` false, every one but Linux) no clone is registered, since a process left running could swap the git directory between the check and the write: its sessions are ingested without record events, a known limit there and not a failed ingest. A row that stopped before its clone registers nothing. Then `metrics.Ingest` with `Source` the sandbox home; the store stamps a label's outcome first-write-wins, so eval ingests only after the verdict. - Invariant: nothing a row's agent does writes the real home outside the sandbox root; check c fails the row when something did. eval itself, after the rows, writes `--home`'s metrics store and, through the join, its brain store: `--home` is required and never the real home (ledger D37), so neither store is the operator's. ## Failure modes | When | The operator sees | Exit | |---|---|---| | no row and no `--list`; `--list` with a row; an unknown flag | the usage or the flag error | 2 | | no `--home`; `--home` the real home, or reaching its state directory through a link | `eval: --home is required: …` / `eval: --home is the real home , or shares its state directory; pass a separate home` | 2 | | not a checkout; `--fixture` not a git repository; no install source | `eval: ` | 2 | | the sandbox root inside a checkout | `eval: the sandbox root is inside a git checkout (BUG-106); use a --home outside every checkout` | 2 | | no `GUIDE-eval` in the export; the table does not parse | `eval: `, naming the line | 2 | | `GUIDE-eval` absent from HEAD's export | `eval: GUIDE-eval is not committed; commit it first` | 2 | | `GUIDE-eval` differs from HEAD's | `eval: GUIDE-eval has uncommitted changes; commit them first` | 2 | | a row name unknown or repeated | `eval: no row "" in GUIDE-eval` / `eval: row is named twice` | 2 | | no login token, or it is a link | `eval: no Antigravity login at ` | 2 | | `agy` not on PATH | `eval: agy not found on PATH` | 2 | | a sandbox directory exists, or clone, records list, setup, install or settings fail | that row FAILs with the step's reason; the next row runs | 1 | | the check fails; the agent not invoked; a denial or an invalid grant | that row FAILs with the reason | 1 | | a process left, the real config changed, a new credential | that row FAILs with the reason, even when its check passed | 1 | | agy times out | agy is killed; the check and the exit checks still run; `agy exit -1` | per the check | | SIGINT, SIGTERM or SIGHUP | relayed to agy's group; the row FAILs `interrupted`; later rows do not run; the started ones are ingested and recorded | 1 | | SIGINT, SIGTERM or SIGHUP before the first row starts | `eval: interrupted before the first row; no record written`; nothing ran, so no sandbox, ingest or record | 1 | | an ingest fails | `eval: ingest: `; the verdict stands | 1 | | `--home` came to share the real state during the run | `eval: ingest: not ingested: …` for each row, then `eval: record: not written: …`; no store under the real home is opened | 1 | | the record cannot be written | every row line, then `eval: record: ` | 1 | ## Non-goals - Redacting what a sandbox sends: an agent works on the fixture as any session does (R8, ADR-065). - Running rows in parallel, pruning old sandboxes, a compare or history verb. - Running unasked: no gate, no timer (R3). - Isolation from the operator's machine: the token is linked, the CLI's credential broker and `~/.ssh` stay reachable; the checks detect what a run leaves behind, they do not prevent it. ## Known limits - pass^k counts sessions: a `prompt2` row adds two sessions per run under one label (D12). - When the harness itself is the fixture, a row whose agent writes records can make SQLite copy a page holding a quoted key header (this harness's trail quotes some) into the sandbox's `brain.db` or its WAL; check d then sees a count grow with no new credential, a false FAIL in the safe direction (D33). - Check d does not read the files of a `node_modules` beside a lockfile: a credential's content written there, under a name the name patterns do not match, is not seen (BUG-185; the operator's choice, 2026-10-27, so an app build that installs packages can pass). - A write to a path check c watches by any other process during a row, the operator's own concurrent session included, fails the row `real config changed`, as with the old kit (D33). The real token and the CLI's conversations are not watched: a sandboxed session refreshes the token through its link, and the operator's own sessions write the conversations. - `named` grants are not a containment boundary: `bash`, `python3`, `go`, `git` and `ln` each run anything as the operator's uid, and `HOME=SB` is only a variable, so the agent can reach the real home by absolute path. The checks detect what a run leaves in the paths they watch; they prevent nothing. Containment (a user namespace) would be a requirements change (security review of 2026-10-26). - A check reads what the agent could write (the sandbox's `fyr` and its stores, the clone): a PASS is evidence of a cooperative agent's behaviour, not proof against one that forges its evidence (security review of 2026-10-26). - fyr killed by SIGKILL or the OOM killer leaves the token link in that sandbox and agy running; nothing sweeps old sandboxes. - A process that escapes check e (another cwd, another `HOME`, its own session) can still replace the sandbox after step 14. The ingest refuses a link at the sandbox home or on its way down to `conversations`, and skips a row that left processes (`processes left`), so a replacement it can see is not read (IN35 and the security review of its fix). - Check e sends SIGTERM to every process of the operator's uid whose cwd lies under the clone or the sandbox: an operator shell, editor or `tail -f` sitting there while a row runs is killed, and the row FAILs `processes left`. Keep them out of the sandbox during a run (IN45 of the 2026-10-27 audit). - Eval's own writes (`out.txt`, `out2.txt`, `err.txt`, `setup.log`, `check.log`) refuse a name whose file has another hard link, or that changed between the open and the check, before anything is truncated; a directory swapped in above those names is not guarded (IN49; a Follow-up of the 2026-10-27 audit fix). - Check b's discovery across mounts has no test: it needs a mount. - A process that escapes check e and replaces an ancestor of the sandbox directory between check e and check d's intact test is not tested: it is a timing window; the directory itself replaced by a link is caught by the scan, which never follows it. - Trust: `setup` and `check` are bash from the project's committed suite and run as the operator's uid with the real home reachable; the suite is always the project root's, never the fixture's, so running `fyr eval` trusts the project as much as running its tests (D30). - Check d skips every file that starts with an executable's magic (ELF, either Mach-O byte order, or `CAFEBABE`, which a Java class and a universal Mach-O share): a credential written into such a file, or into any file given that four-byte prefix, is not seen (audit IN47). - Sandboxes are never pruned: every row of every run leaves its directory under `/.config/fyr/eval//` (the clone, the HOME the CLI ran with, `out.txt`, `err.txt` and the logs, none redacted), so the eval home grows with each run until the operator removes old stamps by hand. - The `--home` re-checks before each ingest and the record narrow, never close, the window: a link made between a re-check and the store's open still sends that store's write through it. Nothing re-checks between rows, so a link a row's agent makes under `/.config/fyr` puts the next row's sandbox where it leads; that row's ingest and the record are then refused, but the sandbox is written (security review of D37, round 2). - The account's home comes from the account database; without cgo on Linux that is `/etc/passwd` alone, so for an LDAP, SSSD or systemd-homed account only `$HOME` is compared. - Off Linux there is no `/proc`: check e prints that it did not run and the record says so; the final process-group kill still runs (plan O1). ## Open questions - None open. A `ps`-based check e for macOS is a follow-up, built after it is tried on the Mac (plan O1). ## Verification - `go test -race ./internal/eval/`: the suite grammar and refusals (`TestSuite*`), each safety check with its kit cases (`TestGuard*`, `TestCreds*`, `TestProcs*`, `TestInvoked`), and `Run` against a fake agy (`TestRun*`), each check mutation-checked. - `go test -race ./cmd/fyr/ -run Eval`: the verb's refusals, golden path, failing row, two-session row, ingest and record failures, interrupt, and `--list` (`TestEvalVerb*`); the `--home` refusals, nothing written under the real home, no migration (`TestEvalRefusesItsHome`). - `go test -race ./internal/brain/ -run ParseTrail`: `ParseTrail` equals `ReadTrail` on the same bytes, with the same refusals. - End to end, on a box with the CLI and a login: `fyr eval --fixture project-memory feature lane-reviewer --home `, then `fyr record get ` and `fyr metrics show --label eval=project-memory --json` (`GUIDE-fyr-matrix` § eval).

title: The memory loop — one store, and the `dreamer` agent
body:
# The memory loop — one store, and the `dreamer` agent

Status: built 2026-09-29 (plan `PLAN-2026-09-29-dreamer-memory-loop`); writing and loading moved to `fyr memory` on 2026-09-30 (R10, plan `PLAN-2026-09-30-parity-memory-dream`). The nightly background job is `SPEC-fyr-dream`. Code: `internal/brain/memory.go` (the store behind `fyr memory`) and `internal/memory` (the project root, and the old `.agents/memory/` store `fyr dream` still reads); the agent is `agents/dreamer/agent.md`.

## The store

- **Where:** `memory` records in the brain store, `~/.config/fyr/brain.db`, in the project's scope (the main worktree's root, so every worktree shares one; `SPEC-fyr-record` § Memory). Never exported to `.agents/trail.jsonl`, never committed, local to the machine (brain plan D14, ADR-063). Since brain plan Phase 2 (2026-10-25) it replaces the old per-checkout `.agents/memory/` directory, which `fyr record import` (project) and `import --global` (every registered project, ADR-068: an indexed project without `fyr index --register` is not read) migrate.
- **Shape:** one record per memory, ID `MEMORY-<name>`, the description as its title, the body `type: <user|feedback|project|reference>`, a blank line, then the text.
- **Who writes:** `fyr memory add --type T --name SLUG --description TEXT` (body on stdin; the same name replaces), called by the `project-memory` skill and by `feedback-log` rule 7. Serialised by the store's write transaction.
- **Who reads:** every session runs `fyr memory show` at the end of the resume order; it prints one line per memory, capped at 200 lines and 25 KB. `fyr record get MEMORY-<name>` prints one in full. `/dream` consolidates them; the `dreamer` agent reads them.
- **Lost:** with `brain.db`. Memory has no second copy, as before (R4, R7).

## The `dreamer` agent

- **What it is:** the consolidation judgement of the learning loop, run by an author-independent reader: given the store and the trail, what should become a rule, a skill or a procedure, and what should be left alone. It proposes; it never applies.
- **Definition:** `agents/dreamer/agent.md` — tools `view_file, grep_search, find_by_name, run_command, write_to_file`; no `model` key (the CLI's default); installed as written like every agent (`delivery.md` § Agents).
- **Dispatch text (the contract):** `Project: <root>. Since: <date of the newest retro record titled "Retro —", or "all">. Promoted: <the memories /dream flagged promote, or none>.` plus the standard draft and budget sentences. Never the conversation. The dreamer does not re-derive `/dream`'s verdicts: the promoted memories are its rule-candidate inputs, one candidate row per memory.
- **Reads:** the memory (`fyr memory show`, each with `fyr record get MEMORY-<name>`); the trail since the date — the three newest `handoff` records, the `bug` records and their prevention rules, the `change` records; what already exists — the global context, the global rule files (`~/.gemini/config/rules/*.md`), the project `AGENTS.md` and `<project>/.agents/rules/`, the installed skills' descriptions (`fyr list` or the skill directories), so a candidate is never something a rule already says.
- **Candidate tests:** a **rule** for each file on the dispatch's `Promoted:` line (given, never re-judged: `/dream` owns the two-memory test), for a bug whose prevention rule is recorded nowhere loaded and that recurs (two bugs, or a bug and a memory on the same fact), and for a memory of any type that a trail record restates (a handoff or `change` record on the same fact) when no loaded rule holds it; a **skill** when a memory or the trail shows a procedure of three or more steps done more than once (`/distill`'s bar); a **procedure** (a `references/` page for an existing skill) when the steps belong to a skill that exists; **none** otherwise, listed under "Left alone" with the reason.
- **Writes:** one draft, `.agents/scratch/agents/dreamer-<stamp>.md`, written early with `Status: IN PROGRESS` and finished with `COMPLETE`: Scope, Summary, a Candidates table (`#`, kind, target file, the exact rule text or the draft's path, evidence as `file:line` and record IDs), "Left alone", "Not examined"; the caller stores it as a `retro` record (brain plan D12). Drafts for skills go under `.agents/scratch/dreamer/<date>/<name>/SKILL.md`. No other file, ever; no edit to source, config, rules, skills or memory.
- **Consumers:** `/retro` dispatches it (Step 1 source 8) and turns rule candidates into proposals through its own Step 2 (target, scope, promotion check) — the one place that decides where a rule lives; `/distill` dispatches it first and takes its skill and procedure candidates as candidates. No global index record of its own; the retro or distill record cites its record's ID.

## Error handling

| Situation | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| No store, or an empty one | `/dream` and the `dreamer` say so in one line; the resume clause reads nothing |
| `~/.config/fyr/` denied to the session | the reader says so; the `dreamer` artifact still writes into the project trail |
| Agent cut at its turn limit | a partial artifact with `Status: IN PROGRESS` (its early-write rule); the caller says so |
| `git clean -fdx`, a fresh clone, a deleted checkout | the memory stays: it is in `~/.config/fyr/brain.db`, keyed by the checkout's root, not in the checkout |
| `brain.db` lost | the memory is lost with it; there is no second copy (R4) |
| an old `.agents/memory` that is a symlink, or one git tracks anything under | `fyr record import` refuses it; `fyr dream` reads the old directory (with the same refusals) only in a project whose trail is still files, and a project of records' memory records otherwise (brain plan Phase 4) |

## Known differences (R10)

Retired (plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md` Phase 2): the harness targets one CLI, so there is no difference between CLIs to list. REQUIREMENTS.md R10 no longer cites this section; the limits of the one CLI (compaction window, cost, denials) are in REQUIREMENTS.md § Known limits.

title: Spec — fyr: the metrics store (2026-10-08)
body:
# Spec — fyr: the metrics store   (2026-10-08)

## Purpose

`fyr metrics` keeps the **shape** of every Antigravity session in `~/.config/fyr/metrics.db`. Shape means:
- the tools each session called;
- the normalised command verbs;
- tokens, timings and errors;
- events joined from git and the trail.

The operator queries the store for agent evaluations (`show`, `report`). The nightly dreamer and `/retro` read it as evidence for proposals; every checkpoint feeds it (§ When ingest runs).

It is not:
- a transcript archive: it holds no arguments and no prose;
- a cache: it is the only copy once a transcript expires (R4);
- sent anywhere: it stays on the machine (ADR-062).

Decisions: ADR-055. Plan: `PLAN-2026-10-08-metrics-store`.

## Interfaces

### Verbs

The verbs reuse the global `--home` flag. `--vendor` does not exist (a usage error, exit 2): `ingest` reads Antigravity only (ADR-062, plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md` D7).

```
fyr metrics ingest [--home H] [--source DIR --label KEY=VALUE [--outcome pass|fail]]
fyr metrics show   [--home H] [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--until YYYY-MM-DD] [--project DIR] [--label KEY=VALUE | --all-labels] [--context-target N] [--json]
fyr metrics report [--home H] [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--until YYYY-MM-DD] [--project DIR] [--label KEY=VALUE | --all-labels] [--context-target N] [--out FILE]
fyr metrics export [--home H] FILE
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--source` | directory | none | A sandbox home: `DIR/.gemini/antigravity-cli`. Requires `--label`. |
| `--label` | `KEY=VALUE` | none | On `ingest`: stamped on every session added from `--source`. On `show`/`report`: shows only that label. |
| `--outcome` | `pass`, `fail` | none | The run's acceptance result, supplied by the kit or by `fyr eval`, which calls the same ingest in-process for each sandbox after its verdict, with `--label eval=<row>` (`SPEC-fyr-eval`), used for pass^k. Given after the run (a second ingest of the same `--source` and `--label`), it stamps every session of the label that has no outcome yet, even when no transcript changed; an earlier run keeps the outcome it was stamped with. |
| `--all-labels` | bool | false | Include labelled (sandbox) sessions. Without it, and without `--label`, they are excluded. |
| `--since` | date | 30 days ago | Start of the window. |
| `--until` | date | now | End of the window, exclusive (`show`, `report`). `--since A --until B` and `--since B` never overlap; `/retro` reads the window before its own this way. A session belongs to the window it starts in, `[since, until)`, and is counted whole there, so adjacent windows never share one. |
| `--project` | directory | all | Only sessions whose `project_root` is this directory or under it (a session started in a subdirectory is the project's; a sibling that only shares the name's prefix is not). |
| `--context-target` | token count above 0 | 300000 | The peak context a main session should stay under (`show`, `report`). B3 counts the main sessions whose peak passed it; the value is a flag, not a pin, so `/retro` can tune phase sizing against it without a rebuild (plan `2026-10-23-session-sized-work.md` D4, D15). |
| `--json` | bool | false | Print the `## Output` object instead of tables. |
| `--out` | file | `~/.config/fyr/reports/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>-metrics.html` | Where the report is written. An existing file is refused. |

### Where transcripts are read from

The first rule that applies wins:
1. `--source DIR`
2. `--home H` → `H/.gemini/antigravity-cli`
3. the real home

Ingest reads only the Antigravity CLI's directory; there is no other source. A conversation whose first workspace is the dream's working directory, `<home>/.config/fyr/dream-work` as written or with its symlinks followed (`harness.DreamWorkPaths`), for `--home` and for `--source` alike, is the dream's own (ADR-073): it is not a session and gets no `ingest_state` row (`internal/metrics/agy.go`).

### `ingest` output and exit status

On success it prints this line and exits 0:

```
metrics: N sessions, M steps, K events added; F sources failed
```

- Exit 1 when F > 0. Each failed source is named on its own line, and every other source is still ingested.
- Exit 2 on a usage error.

### When ingest runs

At the moments the context names (R0), run by the agent; nothing inside `fyr` triggers it (no ingest from `fyr record add`, R3):
- the `handoff` skill's last call, after the handoff is stored, committed and pushed; its summary line, or its error and exit status, goes in the chat report;
- `/retro` step 11, before its two `show` calls; skipped under `--dry-run`, which writes nothing and says the numbers are from the last ingest;
- the phase-end checkpoint in the global context (Checkpoint box, `change` record, commit, push, `fyr metrics ingest`);
- every real `fyr dream` run, nightly (`SPEC-fyr-dream`);
- the operator, by hand.

Each run is incremental (per-source offsets in `ingest_state`) and joins every session's events again, so a missed or failed run is made up by the next one. Measured on copies of one box's store (24 MB `metrics.db`, 17 MB Antigravity directory, 2026-10-25): 0.2 s.

### Normalised verb

`Verb(cmd string) []string` reduces a command line to its shape: one string per command in it, `program [subcommand] [flag names…]`.

**What is removed before splitting:**
- here-document bodies (`<<EOF`, `<<-EOF`, `<<'EOF'`);
- comments;
- the insides of quotes, `${…}` and `$((…))`, which stay part of their word and are never split.

**Where it splits:** at `;`, `&&`, `||`, `|`, `&`, newlines, `(`, `$(`, backticks, `{` and `}`. A redirection such as `2>&1` or `&>f` is part of a word, not a separator.

**What is skipped in front of the program:**
- shell keywords that lead a command (`if then else elif do while until !`);
- the wrappers `sudo env command time nohup exec`, with their own flags and those flags' values (`env -u NAME`);
- `VAR=value` words;
- leading redirections and their targets.

**Segments that yield no verb:**
- a segment opened by `for`, `case`, `select` or `function`, or closed by `done`, `fi`, `esac` or `in`;
- a case pattern, i.e. the words before its `)`.

**The program:**
- It is the basename of the first remaining word. For `go run <target>`, see the `go run` rule below.
- It must match `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.+-]*$`; any other word in command position (a glob, an expansion, a quoted path) yields no verb.
- A subcommand is kept only from a fixed allowlist per tool (`subcommands` in `internal/metrics/verb.go`): git, go, gh, docker, gcloud, kubectl, npm, terraform and fyr. An unlisted word is dropped and the verb is the program alone, because that position can hold a short secret (`gh hunter2pass`). npx's package is never kept. git's global options (`-C dir`, `-c k=v`) are skipped before the subcommand. After fyr's subcommand, one more word is kept when it is one of `ingest show report export add` (operator, 2026-10-09: allowlists).

**Flag names:**
- A long flag `--name[=v]` is kept as `--name` only when the name is lowercase letters, digits and dashes, at most 24 characters (`--sk_live_…`, `--Authorization` are dropped).
- For `go gofmt govulncheck find`, `-name[=v]` is kept as `-name` only when the name is lowercase letters and digits, at most 24 characters.
- A short group of at most three letters is kept whole (`-la`, `-rnw`).
- Any other short flag keeps its first letter only (`-c1-200`, `-psecret`, `-xzvf` become `-c`, `-p`, `-x`), because a short option can carry its value glued on.
- A dash followed by a digit (`-20`) is a value and is dropped.

**Never kept:** positional words, except a bare `.` after `git add`.

**Here-documents:**
- A delimiter is read literally, as bash does. A quoted one runs to its closing quote (`<<'END!'`, `<<"$D"`). An unquoted one is the whole word up to a shell metacharacter (`<<END!`, `<<$END`). The body ends only at a line equal to it.
- A here-doc with no delimiter word cannot be matched, so nothing after its line is read.

**`go run`:** the target counts as the program only when it is a tool the subcommand allowlist knows (`go run ./cmd/fyr search` is `fyr search`). Any other target is content, and the verb is `go run` plus its flag names.

A program name longer than 32 characters is content and is dropped.

**Transcript lines:** a line is read in bounded chunks. A line over 16 MB is consumed and skipped, never held in memory whole. An unterminated tail over that size is passed over rather than re-read on every ingest.

**Tool names** follow the identifier rule below; one that fails it is stored as `unnamed`. Everything `metrics ingest` prints (paths, project roots, errors) goes through search's BUG-152 filter: control, format (bidi overrides, zero-width marks), line-separator and paragraph-separator characters become `?`, by Unicode class, because a `--source` sandbox writes those values. `show`'s text output prints a key holding any of them as `?`. Every file ingest reads (a transcript, a trail record, a `.meta.json`) is opened without blocking and checked on the opened file to be a regular file, so a FIFO swapped in after an earlier check neither hangs the ingest nor is read.

**Identifiers:** a skill name, a model or an agent type is stored only when it matches `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.:@/-]{0,63}$`; otherwise it is left empty. So no escape bytes or prose reach the store or the terminal. A subagent's `.meta.json` is read only as a regular file of 64 KB or less.

**Known limit:** a shell construct the tokenizer does not model can still put one identifier-shaped word in command position. That is never more than a single name-shaped word, never a path, a value or prose. Verbs reflect the normaliser of the binary that ingested them; the command itself is never stored, so older rows are not re-normalised.

### Shared tool vocabulary

Antigravity tool names map to a common name. Unknown names are kept as `agy:<name>`. The Claude Code column maps nothing new: it names the tools of the historical rows an older ingest stored, which are kept and read, never written.

| Common | Claude Code (historical) | Antigravity |
|---|---|---|
| Bash | `Bash` | `run_command` |
| Read | `Read` | `view_file`, `read_file` |
| Write | `Write` | `write_to_file`, `write_file` |
| Edit | `Edit` | `replace_file_content`, `multi_replace_file_content`, `edit_file` |
| Grep | `Grep` | `grep_search` |
| Glob | `Glob` | `find_by_name` |
| LS | (none) | `list_dir` |
| Agent | `Agent` | `invoke_subagent` |
| SendMessage | `SendMessage` | `send_message` |

The Antigravity names come from the spike over the local conversation databases (plan D35); `read_file`, `write_file` and `edit_file` are agy 1.4.7's, found in the eval conversations of 2026-10-26 (BUG-184). `manage_subagents` and any other name not in this table are kept as `agy:<name>`.

**Where the shape is read:** Antigravity: the tool name is at `steps.metadata` 4→2 and the arguments JSON at 4→3, which gives `CommandLine` and the path, under the key its tool sends: `AbsolutePath` (`view_file`), `Path` (`read_file`, `write_file`, `edit_file`) or `TargetFile` (`write_to_file`, `replace_file_content`, `multi_replace_file_content`). The step time is at `metadata` 1→1, in seconds. An error is status 7. A subagent is its own conversation; `conversation_summaries.agent_name` and `parent_conversation_id` give its type and parent. Usage, the model and the context are in `gen_metadata`: 1→4→2/3/5, 1→19 and 1→9→10→1.

A **skill load** is a read of `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (only `<name>` is stored). A historical Claude Code row's `Skill` call stays as stored.

### Output (`show --json`)

Keys are snake_case. Every metric is keyed by vendor, and `columns` lists the vendors present: `["agy"]`, or `["agy","claude"]` when the window holds sessions with vendor `claude` that an older ingest stored (historical rows: kept, never written again, plan D7). The `claude` keys appear only then; the example below shows that case. A metric the CLI cannot produce is `null` and is named in `notes`, never shown as 0. The shape is the Go type `metrics.Summary`:

```json
{
  "window": {"since": "2026-09-08", "until": "2026-10-08"},
  "columns": ["agy", "claude"],
  "sessions": {"claude": 16, "agy": 11},
  "subagents": {"claude": {"reviewer": 9}, "agy": {"explorer": 2}},
  "A": {"dod_closed": {"claude": {"closed": 3, "ambiguous": 1, "of": 16}},
        "verifier": {"PASS": 22, "FAIL": 3}, "review_findings": {"high": 8, "medium": 38, "low": 60},
        "escaped_bugs": 0, "corrections": 0, "pass_k": {"arm=lean": {"k": 3, "passed": 3, "pass_k": 1}}},
  "B": {"tool_calls": {"claude": 1899}, "tool_calls_by_tool": {"claude": {"Bash": 1300}},
        "turns": {"claude": 127}, "tokens": {"claude": {"in": 0, "out": 0, "cache_read": 0, "cache_write": 0}},
        "cost_usd": {"claude": 135.24, "agy": null}, "wall_min": {}, "active_min": {},
        "peak_context": {"claude": 412000, "agy": 42000}, "compactions": {"claude": 0, "agy": null},
        "context_target": 300000, "sessions_over_context_target": {"claude": 5, "agy": 0},
        "session_peaks": {"claude": [{"session": "a1b2…", "date": "2026-10-07", "peak": 412000}], "agy": [{"session": "c3d4…", "date": "2026-10-06", "peak": 42000}]}},
  "C": {"sqlite_verbs": {"claude": 42}, "grep_calls": {"claude": 1545}, "search_grep_ratio": {"claude": 0.027},
        "forbidden": {"git add -A": 4, "git add .": 0, "git push --force": 0, "--no-verify": 0, "commit chained to test": 1},
        "first_reads": {"plan": 3}, "skills": {"claude": {"golang": 3}}},
  "D": {"tool_error_rate": {"claude": 0.023}, "denials": {"claude": 10, "agy": null},
        "interrupts": {"claude": 2, "agy": null}, "retry_loops": {}, "subagent_tool_calls": {"claude": {"reviewer": 391}}},
  "daily": [{"date": "2026-10-07", "sessions": {}, "tool_calls": {}, "tokens": {}, "cost_usd": {},
             "sqlite_verbs": {}, "grep_calls": {}, "errors": {}}],
  "notes": ["agy: cost is not exposed by the CLI", "agy: denials, interrupts and compactions are not recorded by the CLI"]
}
```

The values above illustrate the shape. They are not fixtures. In text, `show` prints one `agy` column, plus `claude (historical)` as a second one only when the window holds such rows. `daily` holds one entry per UTC day with activity, keyed by the step's own time, so an idle day has none and a session that ran past the window's end can add a later day (SD52 of the 2026-10-27 audit); the report's trend charts read it. `session_peaks` lists main sessions only, largest peak first, one list per vendor that has a session with a context value in the window; `sessions_over_context_target` counts the entries of that list past `context_target` and is `null`, named in `notes`, for a vendor with no such session (never 0). A session's id and start day are the only identifiers carried: no project path, no content (plan D6, D16).

### Report (`metrics report`)

`metrics report` writes one HTML file, mode 0600. An existing file is refused. The default path is `~/.config/fyr/reports/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>-metrics.html`.

**How it is built:**
- `html/template` with SVG drawn in Go;
- no `<script>`, no URL to any host, no `@import` or `url(`;
- light and dark through `prefers-color-scheme`.

**Colours.** Colour follows the CLI and never its rank: Antigravity keeps categorical slot 2, orange (`#eb6834` / `#d95926`); the historical column, "Claude Code (historical)" in the report, is slot 1, blue (`#2a78d6` light / `#3987e5` dark), drawn only when the window holds historical rows. That pair is the dataviz reference palette's first two slots, validated in both modes. Colours are set by CSS classes, because html/template sanitises a CSS variable in a `style` attribute.

**Hover and identity.** Hover values are SVG `<title>` elements, which browsers show without script. Identity never rests on colour alone: the legend names each CLI drawn, each line is labelled where it ends, and every chart has its numbers as a table.

**Charts:**
- tool calls, tokens, cost, the search:grep ratio and tool errors per day, one line per CLI;
- tool calls by tool (the ten most used);
- subagent tool calls by type;
- runs passed of k per sandbox label;
- the summary table, where the row `sessions over context target (<N>)` reads `k of n`: k the main sessions whose peak passed the target, n the main sessions in the window with a peak at all; `n/a` for a vendor with none.

**Missing values.** A value a CLI cannot produce is not drawn:
- no Antigravity cost line;
- no search:grep point on a day with no grep call.

Tables show those values as `n/a`.

**Consistency.** Every number in the report comes from the same `Summary` as `show --json` over the same window and filters.

**Known limit:** at 400 px the SVG scales down, and tick labels get small (about 6 px) but stay legible. The tables give the same numbers at full size.

### Metric definitions

| Id | Metric | Definition |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | DoD closure | A main session's window is `[started_at, ended_at + 30 min]`. The session is closed when the window holds at least one commit in its project AND a handoff: a handoff file whose `TrailDates` time falls in it, or in a migrated project a `handoff` record whose record time does (§ Invariants, Trail from files or records). |
| A2 | Verifier status | The `## Status:` heading of `testing/*-verify-*.md` files in the window, or of `testing` records whose title matches `^Verif(ication\|y)\b` (the verifier's own title), so a behavioural-run record does not count. Main sessions only. |
| A3 | Review findings | `**[high\|medium\|low / confidence: …]**` lines in `reviews/*.md` files or `review` records in the window. Main sessions only. |
| A4 | Escaped bugs | A `bugs/BUG-*.md` file or a `bug` record whose text contains a hex prefix of 7 or more characters of one of the session's commits. An imported closed bug holds only its title and prevention rule, so it gives none; events stored before the migration stay. |
| A5 | Corrections | Feedback entries in the window whose project is the session's root: global `feedback` records about the root's main worktree, for every root (migrated, unmigrated or gone), and `feedback.jsonl` lines. An entry is keyed by its `ts` in UTC, so one held by both counts once; a body that is not JSON or has no RFC 3339 `ts` is skipped. |
| A6 | pass^k | Per label, 1 when all k `--outcome` runs passed. k and the pass count are shown. |
| — | Replayed history | A resumed or forked Claude session copies earlier messages into a new transcript. `show` counts a tool step, an assistant message or a generation once per CLI and label by its id, under the first session in the query's window that holds it, so replayed tool calls, tokens, verbs and errors are not counted twice. User turns, interrupts and compactions are not deduplicated, and a replay whose original session lies outside the window still counts once inside it. The label is part of the key, so a sandbox run that reuses real ids never hides a real session's steps under `--all-labels`. |
| B1 | Tokens and cost | Antigravity: `gen_metadata` usage; cost is not exposed. Historical Claude rows keep what an older ingest stored (usage per message id, cost from the session's last `cost-state` line). |
| B2 | Time and volume | Wall time = `ended_at - started_at` of main sessions. Active time = the sum of gaps under 5 min between a main session's steps. A subagent runs inside its parent's time and is counted in neither. Also turns (typed user turns) and tool calls (main and subagent). |
| B3 | Context | Peak context = max(input + cache read + cache write) of one message (Claude); the `gen_metadata` context of one generation (Antigravity). Also the number of compactions. Also the sessions whose peak passed the context target, default 300K, and each main session's peak: the peak follows the replayed-history rule above, so a fork's copy of an earlier session's messages counts under the session that first had them, and a subagent's peak belongs to no session (it runs inside its parent's time). |
| B4 | Subagents | Count by type, the tool calls of each, and SendMessage resumes. |
| C1 | Search vs grep | `fyr search\|index` verb segments divided by `grep`/`rg` segments plus Grep tool calls. |
| C2 | Forbidden shapes | `git add -A`, `git add .`, `git push --force\|-f`, `--no-verify`, and `git commit` in the same Bash call as `go test`. |
| C3 | First reads | The trail kind of a main session's first three steps that carry one: a Read target's kind, or a Bash step that is a record verb — `fyr record get <ID>` as the ID's kind (`record` when the prefix is unknown or no ID follows), `fyr record list` as `list`. Only the first segment whose program is `fyr` (any directory) or `go run ./cmd/fyr` is read, past `--home`/`--repo` and their values and other flags; `fyr search` and `fyr memory show` are not trail reads. Bash steps ingested before this rule carry no kind. |
| C4 | Skills | Skill loads per session. |
| D1 | Errors | Tool error rate, denials and interrupts. |
| D2 | Retry loops | The same `cmd_hash` in two consecutive tool steps. |
| D3 | Subagent volume | Tool calls per subagent session. |

## Data

`~/.config/fyr/metrics.db` has mode 0600 in a 0700 directory. A database or companion file that is a symlink, or any other non-regular file, is refused, as in the search index. The directory itself may be a symlink. It uses WAL with a 10 s busy timeout, and every transaction takes the write lock when it begins (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`), so an ingest that meets another waits for it instead of failing at its first write. A new store opened by two processes at once is retried for the same 10 s, because SQLite answers that race with an immediate `SQLITE_BUSY` (BUG-187). Every time is stored as unix milliseconds, UTC. Writer: `internal/metrics` only.

```sql
meta(key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT)            -- 'schema', 'salt' (32 random hex)
sessions(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, vendor TEXT, project_root TEXT, parent_id TEXT, agent_type TEXT,
         model TEXT, label TEXT, outcome TEXT, started_at INTEGER, ended_at INTEGER,
         cost_usd REAL, duration_ms INTEGER)
steps(session_id TEXT, ext_id TEXT, ts INTEGER, kind TEXT, tool TEXT, skill TEXT, target_kind TEXT,
      is_error INTEGER, denied INTEGER, tok_in INTEGER, tok_out INTEGER, cache_read INTEGER,
      cache_write INTEGER, cmd_hash TEXT, context INTEGER,   -- context: migration 2
      PRIMARY KEY(session_id, ext_id))
step_verbs(session_id TEXT, ext_id TEXT, n INTEGER, verb TEXT, PRIMARY KEY(session_id, ext_id, n))
events(session_id TEXT, ts INTEGER, kind TEXT, ref TEXT, value TEXT, PRIMARY KEY(session_id, kind, ref))
ingest_state(source TEXT PRIMARY KEY, size INTEGER, mtime INTEGER, offset INTEGER)
```

### Invariants

- **Identity.**
  - Antigravity: `ext_id` = `<conversation id>:<step idx>`.
  - Rows with vendor `claude` (`ext_id` = message id, `tool_use.id` or a line `uuid`) come from an older ingest. They are kept and read, never written: no code path inserts one, and nothing deletes them (plan D7).
  - Re-ingesting anything adds no rows.
- **Time columns.** `sessions.started_at` and `ended_at` hold unix milliseconds of a real time or are NULL; `ingest_state.mtime` is 0 when the source gave none. A time read from another program's store that is before 1970, Go's zero time among them, is no time: `ended_at` stays NULL (migration 3 repaired the rows stored before, BUG-181).
- **Path columns.** Only `sessions.project_root` and `ingest_state.source` may hold a path. No column holds an argument or prose.
- **Identifiers.** `steps.skill`, `sessions.agent_type` and the `git add .` verb are the only identifiers taken from a tool's input. A Bash step's `target_kind` is a kind from a closed set (the record kinds, `list`, `record`), never the ID or any other word of the command.
- **`events` payloads.**

  | kind | ref | value |
  |---|---|---|
  | `commit` | full SHA | `''` or `ambiguous` |
  | `handoff` | the item's ID | `''` |
  | `verifier` | the item's ID | the status word |
  | `review` | the item's ID | `high=N,medium=N,low=N` |
  | `bug` | `BUG-NNN` | the linked SHA |
  | `correction` | the entry's `ts` in UTC, RFC 3339 (`2026-10-21T12:39:54Z`) | `''` |

- **One reference per trail item.** A `handoff`, `verifier` or `review` event's ref is the trail item's record ID; for a file it is the ID `fyr record import` gives that file (`brain.ImportedID`: the kind's prefix, a dash, the file's stem slugged), so a project's migration adds no second event for the same item. Each ingest first rewrites, inside the join's transaction, every such ref an older ingest stored as a file name (`*.md`) to that ID form; a row whose ID form the session already holds is a duplicate and is deleted. A ref already in ID form is left alone, even one ending in `.md` (a file `notes.md.md` imports as `HANDOFF-notes.md`), so a second ingest changes nothing. No schema change. Known limits: a `-N` suffix a collision added to an ID is not reproduced, so such a file and its record stay two events; an old file whose name is itself ID-shaped (`HANDOFF-x.md`) keeps its file-name ref. A `correction` ref an older ingest stored with another offset (`+02:00`) is rewritten to its UTC form the same way.
- **Trail from files or records, never both.** A migrated project (its checkout holds `.agents/trail.jsonl`) is joined from its `handoff`, `testing`, `review` and `bug` records, of every status, in the scope of its main worktree root, read through the file-wins load (`brain.ForMetrics`, which may write `brain.db` as the dream's read does), but only when the operator registered the checkout under this home with `fyr index --register` (`trail.Registered`; ADR-068, audit-choices SD49): an unregistered checkout holding `.agents/trail.jsonl` reads as unmigrated, so its `trail.jsonl` never becomes a brain scope that `fyr dream --all` and `search --global` would then read, and its sessions, commits and corrections are still joined. An `fyr eval` sandbox's clone is registered under the eval home by `fyr eval` itself before the row's ingest (ledger item 76, `SPEC-fyr-eval` § State), so its `eval=<row>` sessions get their record events and its trail becomes a scope of the eval home's brain store, never the real home's; a clone eval refuses to register (its git directory outside it) is joined as unmigrated. An unmigrated one is joined from its docs root's files. Corrections are read from both sources for every root (A5). A record's **time** is the minute stamped in its ID (`^[A-Z]+-(YYYY-MM-DD)-(HHMM)(-|$)`, read in the machine's zone; an impossible minute such as `2459` is none), never `updated`, which an edit or the import moves. A `handoff`, `verifier` or `review` record belongs to every main session whose window overlaps that minute `[stamp, stamp + 60 s)`; a record with no time gives none of these. A `bug` record belongs to the session owning the commit it cites, with `ts` its `date` at 00:00 local. Only these patterns are taken from a body, never its text. Known limit: a record added on a machine in another time zone is placed off by the zones' difference.

- **`cmd_hash`** = `hex(sha256(salt || command))[:16]`. It supports equality checks only.
- **Fixed markers.**
  - `denied`: an Antigravity step status the spike names (none observed; the CLI does not record denials). Historical Claude rows keep the marker an older ingest set.
  - `interrupt`: a user line starting `[Request interrupted by user`.
  - `compaction`: not recorded by Antigravity; historical Claude rows keep the compact-boundary count an older ingest stored.
- **Antigravity sources.** Antigravity databases are read only from copies. `step_payload` is never read; tool names and command lines come from `steps.metadata`.
- **Export.** `export` writes every row but the `salt`: with it, an export would let anyone confirm a guessed command against `cmd_hash`.
- **git in project roots.** Every git call into a session's project root goes through `internal/trail`: `--no-optional-locks -c core.fsmonitor=false -c log.showSignature=false`, `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`, and `--no-show-signature --no-textconv` on `log` (`trail.Log`; `--no-textconv` since the security review of 2026-10-25, so a content diff starts no textconv driver the checkout picks). Only commands that read objects and files run there (`log`, `ls-tree`, `ls-files`, `hash-object --no-filters`, `rev-parse`, `check-ignore`, `config --get`), never `status`, which runs the repository's clean filters (BUG-164). This closes the program-starting config keys those commands honour (signature programs, clean filters, fsmonitor, a lazy fetch's ssh command); it does not make the repository's config trusted. A partial clone (`extensions.partialClone` set, or any remote marked `promisor`) is read only when this machine's git is 2.44 or later, which honours `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH` (`trail.Readable`, the policy search applies; SD17). With an older git it is not read at all: its sessions get no commit or trail events, and its trail files keep their mtimes in the dreamer. A toplevel is accepted only when it is the session's directory or a parent of it, so a repository's `core.worktree` cannot file a session under another project.
