Sessions are grouped by their git toplevel (`trail.Toplevel`), so a session started in a subdirectory joins its project's events.
- **Temporary copies.** `metrics-agy-*` (Antigravity conversation copies) and `dream-metrics-*` (a store snapshot) are removed after use. An `ingest` and every `dream` run also sweep any older than an hour, which a killed run left behind.
- **Migrations.** They run forward only, in one transaction. A store with a newer schema is refused untouched. The binary never deletes the store, and `uninstall` keeps it.

## Failure modes

| Trigger | Observable |
|---|---|
| `metrics.db`, `-wal` or `-shm` is a symlink or another non-regular file | `metrics: <name> is not a regular file; refusing to open or write through it`, exit 1 |
| The store's schema is newer than the binary's | `metrics.db schema N is newer than this binary (M); update fyr`, exit 1, store unchanged (`ingest`, `show`, `report`, `export`) |
| A file shrank or was replaced | Re-read from offset 0, with no duplicate rows |
| An Antigravity copy or read fails | That conversation is named and counted in F; the others are ingested; exit 1 |
| An Antigravity token field is absent | Tokens are stored NULL and counted as 0 in `show` and `report` (SD51 of the 2026-10-27 audit: no note names them) |
| A `feedback.jsonl` line is over 4 MiB | `metrics: note: feedback.jsonl: line N over 4 MiB, the rest skipped`; the lines before it count; exit 0 (SD58) |
| `report` cannot render | nothing is written, so a rerun is not refused as an overwrite (SD57) |
| A project root is gone or not git | Session rows are still written; no commit events; `ingest` prints `metrics: note: project root gone: <root>` or `no git history: <root>` |
| A migrated project's records cannot be read (`trail.jsonl` does not parse, `brain.db` busy or newer) | `metrics: note: records not read: <root>: <reason>`; that root gets no record events this run, its stored events stay, `feedback.jsonl` still counts; exit 0 |
| Two main sessions overlap in one root | Commits in the overlap are `ambiguous`; A1/A4 are shown as `n (ambiguous m)` and excluded from rates |
| Still locked after the 10 s busy timeout | The source counts as failed (`database is locked`), exit 1; the next run picks it up |
| `show`, `report` or `export` on a home with no store (never ingested) | `fyr metrics: no metrics store at <path>; run \`fyr metrics ingest\` first`, exit 1; nothing is created |
| `export FILE` or `report --out FILE` exists | `refusing to overwrite FILE`, exit 1 |
| `--source` without `--label`, or any metrics flag the subcommand does not read (`ingest --json`, `export --label`, `show --out`, `ingest --context-target`) | Usage error naming the flag, exit 2 |
| `--context-target 0` or a negative value | `--context-target takes a token count above 0`, exit 2 |
| No main session of a vendor in the window carries a context value | That vendor's `sessions_over_context_target` is `null` (`n/a` in the tables), `notes` says so; never 0 |
| Ingest fails inside `dream` | A line in `dream.log`; the dream's exit status and `last_run.error` are unchanged |
| Ingest fails at a handoff or in `/retro` | The skill reports the error and exit status in chat (`/retro` also under `## Metrics`) and goes on; the handoff is never edited; the next ingest joins every session again |

## Non-goals

- Storing or sending arguments, prose, file contents or tool output.
- Sending metrics off the machine. Feedback reaches the harness only as dream or retro proposals, applied by hand (ADR-055, ADR-062).
- A server, a live dashboard or a JavaScript chart library.
- Rebuilding the store from transcripts that no longer exist.

## Open questions

- The Antigravity field numbers for tool name, command line, subagent link, compaction and denial. Default: unknown items stay null and are named in `notes`; REQUIREMENTS.md § Known limits holds the compaction row (Phase 3 spike).

## Verification

| What | Test |
|---|---|
| Store, migrations, refusals | `internal/metrics/store_test.go` (`-run 'Store\|Migrat'`) |
| `Verb` | `verb_test.go` (`-run Verb`) |
| Antigravity ingest from copies (read-only source directory), idempotence, transcript root, canary with its must-fail control | `agy_test.go` over `testdata/agy/` |
| C3 record verbs | `agy_test.go` (`-run 'TestRecordRead\|TestFirstReadsRecords'`); the ID prefixes, `internal/brain` `-run TestKindOfID` |
| Historical `claude` rows kept, shown as a second column only when present, never written; `columns` | `historical_test.go` |
| Shared vocabulary (Antigravity names, and the historical Claude names) | `agy_tools_test.go` (`-run TestAgyToolVocabulary`): every Antigravity row of the table, from a want list written in the test, and an unmapped name kept as `agy:<name>`; `agy_tools_test.go` (`-run TestAgyPathKeys`): each file tool's path key gives the skill and the trail kind; `agy_test.go` (`-run TestAgyIngestShape`) covers `run_command` and `view_file` inside a whole ingest; the historical names are only read (`historical_test.go`) |
| Events and A-group definitions | `events_test.go` over a git fixture in `t.TempDir()`; the records join and corrections, `records_test.go` (`-run 'TestJoinRecords\|TestCorrections'`); the records read, `internal/brain` `-run TestForMetrics` |
| `show --json` keys and values | `show_test.go` golden |
| Report: no script, no host, numbers equal to `show` | `report_test.go` golden, plus a browser check (plan Phase 6) |
| `uninstall` keeps the store | `internal/harness` `-run TestUninstallKeepsMetricsStore` |
| Dream ingests inside the lock, never in a dry run | `internal/dream` `-run Ingest` |
| The checkpoint feed: the handoff skill and `/retro` ingest, `/retro --dry-run` does not | `GUIDE-skill-matrix` handoff and retro rows on Antigravity (kit) |
| E2E on Antigravity | testing guide § 4 runs, plan § Sandbox tests |

title: `fyr record` — the brain store
body:
# `fyr record` — the brain store

Status: built 2026-10-25 (plan `PLAN-2026-10-25-sqlite-trail`, ADR-063): Phase 1 the store, `add`, `get`, `edit` and `list`, the export and the load, and record hits in `fyr search`; Phase 2 `record import` and the `fyr memory` alias; Phase 3 memory retirement (D28), `search --refs`/`--open` over records (D30), recency ranking (D31); Phase 4 the dream's reads and proposals (`brain.Scopes`, `ForDream`, `Propose`). Requirements: R4 (the brain store is a store of record), R7 (the trail is records), R8 (`feedback` and `proposal` are global only). Code: `internal/brain`, `cmd/fyr/record.go`. Re-read 2026-10-28 against 4af20b5 (`fyr help`, ledger Phase 4b): only § Exit status's usage-error output changed; the rest holds. Ledger Phase 7 (2026-10-28): `record import` gained the redactor warning (§ Commands).

## What it is

One SQLite store, `~/.config/fyr/brain.db` (under `--home` when given), holds every record of every project's trail with its metadata, the global records, and each project's memory. A project's records other than memory are also written to one committed file in that project, `.agents/trail.jsonl`, which is the backup and how records travel between machines through git. Nothing but `fyr` reads that file.

The store is a store of record like `metrics.db`: it migrates forward (`PRAGMA user_version`), a store a newer binary wrote is refused untouched, and `uninstall` leaves it. The directory is created 0700 and the database and its `-wal` and `-shm` 0600; a database or companion file that is a symlink or not a regular file is refused (the search index's rule, `search.PrepareDBFiles`).

## Commands

```
fyr record add <kind> --title T [--status S] [--id ID] [--global [--project ROOT]]   < body
fyr record get <id>... [--global]
fyr record edit <id> [--status S] [--title T] [--body] [--global]                     [< body]
fyr record list [--kind K] [--open] [--global [--project ROOT]] [--all]
fyr record import [--dry-run] [<docs-root>]
fyr record import --global [--dry-run]
fyr memory add --type T --name SLUG --description TEXT                               < body
fyr memory show
```

- **Scope.** Without `--global` a verb works in the project scope of the git checkout holding the working directory. The scope key is the main worktree's top level, resolved by `trail.Roots` exactly as `memory.Root` resolves it (git's `--show-toplevel` in the main worktree, which must be the working directory or a parent of it; from a linked worktree the common dir's parent, and only when the common dir registers that worktree; a bare repository refused). Every worktree of a repository therefore shares one scope. `--global` selects the global scope, which needs no checkout.
- **`add`** reads the body on stdin and prints the new ID. The body must be UTF-8 text with no control character other than tab and newline (a NUL, an ESC and the `\x01`/`\x02` a search snippet marks matches with are refused), at most 1 MiB; CRLF is folded to LF, leading blank lines and trailing whitespace are dropped, and an empty body is refused. The title is one non-empty line of at most 512 bytes with no control character. `--id` stores the record under that ID instead of the next one (it must fit the kind's grammar and be free in the scope). `--project ROOT` (with `--global` only) names the project a global record is about; it is stored absolute, as the main worktree's root when ROOT is a checkout.
- **The redactor warning (SD42 of the 2026-10-27 audit).** When `add`, or `edit` with `--body` or `--title`, stores a body or title that `fyr dream`'s redactor (`internal/redact`) would change, it prints on stderr, after the store, `fyr record: warning: the body holds text the redactor would change (first at line <n>); stored as written` (`<n>` the first line of the body as read from stdin where the redacted body differs) or `fyr record: warning: the title holds text the redactor would change; stored as written`. `add --id` judges the ID it was given too, first: `fyr record: warning: the ID holds text the redactor would change; stored as written`, never repeating the ID, which stdout still prints as the command's output (ledger D31 3b); a generated ID is never judged. The record is stored, the exit status is unchanged and the matched text is never printed: a project's records reach the committed `trail.jsonl`, and the operator chose a warning over a refusal. Every kind and scope warns alike, a `--global` record and a `memory` record added through `record add` too; a clean field, a refused write and a field `edit` keeps print nothing. `fyr memory add` does not warn. `record import` warns the same way for each record it stores, naming the record by its ID, or by its place in the list as below, never by its text (ledger item 47): `fyr record import: warning: <ID>: the body holds text the redactor would change (first at line <n>); stored as written` (`<n>` a line of the body as stored, which can differ from the source file's line where the import dropped frontmatter or split a file), or `… record <n> in the list above: the title holds …; stored as written`, after the import's own output. An ID is made from the source file's name or, for a line of a global log, from its title, and slugging (lowercased, every other run of characters turned to `-`) can hide a secret from the redactor, so the source path is judged with the ID: `fyr record import: warning: record <n> in the list above: the ID or the source path holds text the redactor would change; stored as written`. A record whose ID, source path or title the redactor would change is named in each of its lines by its place in the list the import printed, never by its ID; any other is named by its ID. Project and `--global` records are judged alike. The import's own list on stdout prints every ID and path as before (the phase's security review, rounds 1 and 2). A run names only the records it stored, never one the scope already held; a dry run, which stores nothing, names every record it read, one already held included, and leaves off `; stored as written`. The exit status is the import's own.
- **`get`** prints, for each ID in the order given, a header line in the list format (plus `  (project ROOT)` for a global record about a project) and then the body. Records are separated by a blank line. Every line goes through the printable filter of `fyr search` (`search.Printable`, BUG-152): control characters, format characters and line or paragraph separators print as `?`; tabs and newlines are kept. An ID the scope does not hold is a refusal naming it, after the found records are printed.
- **`edit`** changes the status, the title or, with `--body`, the body read from stdin. Without `--body` the body is kept (D9). At least one of the three is required. A plan's status follows its new body.
- **`list`** prints `ID  kind  status  date  title`, newest first (by date, then by last update, then by ID), with `-` for a handoff's empty status. `--kind` filters by kind and `--open` keeps the open records (table below). `--project ROOT` (with `--global` only) keeps the global records about that project: `fyr record list --global --kind proposal --project <root>` is how `/retro` lists a project's proposals. `--all` lists every scope, each line ending in `  [<scope root>]` or `  [global]`; it cannot be combined with `--global`.
- A flag the subverb does not take is a usage error (for example `record add --open`), never parsed and ignored.

## Import (D8, D13, D16)

`fyr record import [--dry-run] [<docs-root>]` migrates a project whose trail is still files. The docs root is the argument (relative to the working directory, inside the checkout, not a symlink), else `<project>/.agents/docs/`, else `<project>/docs/`. It reads the files git tracks there and refuses a file that is not markdown (D17: a script is not a record; move it first) — an empty or whitespace-only `.gitkeep` placeholder is not refused but removed with the tree — a symlink or other non-regular file and a file over 1 MiB; every file is opened without following a link or blocking on a FIFO. The whole import reads at most 256 MiB and 50,000 files (the docs tree, the files that reference it and the old memory store together), and refuses past either. A real run refuses a tree with uncommitted changes, so the import's removals are the only change, and refuses a tree whose state git cannot read by path (a tracked name holding a newline or opening with `"`, which `hash-object --stdin-paths` would split or unquote into another path; BUG-188); a dry run reads and decides the same and writes nothing.

- **Kinds and IDs.** `plans/` plan, `reviews/` review, `testing/` testing (`TEST-`), `changes/` change, `handoffs/` handoff, `retros/` retro, `deploy/` deploy, each `<PREFIX>-<file stem>` lowercased; `specs/<app>/<topic>.md` is `SPEC-<app>-<topic>`; `GUIDE-testing` is `GUIDE-testing` and a `testing/*-matrix.md` with no date `GUIDE-<stem>`; `bugs/BUG-NNN-*.md` keeps `BUG-NNN`; `architecture/DECISIONS.md` gives one `adr` record per `## ADR-NNN: Title (date) — Status` section (status `superseded:ADR-NNN` when the heading ends `Superseded by ADR-NNN`, else `accepted`); `bugs/INDEX.md` is folded into the bugs (a row's status when the file has none, its prevention when the file has no `## Prevention`, and the Graduated table as status `graduated` plus a `Graduated to:` line). A file elsewhere is reported as a problem and left as a file.
- **Title, date, body.** The title is the first `# ` heading (a bug's without its `BUG-NNN:` prefix), else the stem; the date the frontmatter `date:`, else the stem's leading date, else the day of the import (a date that is not a real day, `2026-02-30`, is skipped the same way; so is an ADR heading's); the body the text after the frontmatter. Every imported record is normalized (a control character but tab and newline becomes `?`, the title one line of at most 512 bytes) and then checked by the load's own parser, in a dry run too: a record the load would refuse fails the import, naming its file, before anything is written.
- **What is kept (D8).** The roots: open plans (status derived from the body), the newest handoff (by file name), every ADR, every bug, specs, deploy docs and guides. Then, transitively, every trail file a kept record, or a file git tracks among `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `context/`, `skills/`, `agents/` and `rules/`, names, by path relative to the docs root (`TEST-2026-09-03-verify-real-home`, `.agents/docs/…` included) or by the ID it imports as (`TEST-2026-09-03-verify-real-home`). A closed bug is trimmed to its heading and its `## Prevention` section. Everything else is dropped; git history keeps it.
- **The old memory store.** `<main worktree root>/.agents/memory/*.md` (not `MEMORY.md`) become `memory` records `MEMORY-<name>`, the description as the title and `type: <type>` heading the body. The store's trust checks stand (ADR-043): a symlinked `.agents` or store is refused, and so is a store git tracks anything under (a committed memory is the repository's text, never the operator's). A memory file it cannot take is a `problem` and stays; only the files it took, with `MEMORY.md` and `.lock`, are listed for removal.
- **Writes and output.** One transaction stores every record the scope does not hold yet (a record already stored is skipped and counted, so a second run adds nothing) and exports. Nothing is removed (D13): the command prints a summary (`plan 3, …; N records, M dropped, K already stored`), one `record  ID  kind  status  path` line per record, a `problem` line per file or line left out, then every tracked trail file under the docs root (to `git --literal-pathspecs rm --` by name after committing `.agents/trail.jsonl`; a file outside the trail's directories is a `problem`, left as a file and never on that list) and the old memory store's files (untracked; `rm` by name). Every path is printed as one shell word, single-quoted when it holds anything but letters, digits and `._/@%+=:,-` (or starts with `-`).

`fyr record import --global [--dry-run]` migrates `~/.config/fyr`: each `feedback.jsonl` line as a `feedback` record (title the `corrected` text, else the `user_quote`; body the line as written; `project` the line's project), each `retros.jsonl` line as a global `retro` record, each `proposals/**/*.md` as a `queued` `proposal` record (`project` from its frontmatter), and the old memory store of every project in the global search index that is registered under this home (`fyr index --register`, ADR-068) into that project's memory records; an unregistered one is reported as `<root>: not registered (fyr index --register); its memory store is not imported`, and its store stays. A line that is not JSON, has no RFC 3339 `ts`, is over 6 MiB, or builds a record the store would not take is reported by number and skipped; so is a proposal file or a project's memory store it cannot take; nothing stops the import. Two entries whose IDs would be equal get `-2`, `-3` … until the ID is free (a slug is cut at 120 characters to leave room). Records already stored are skipped (per scope: two projects may each hold `MEMORY-x`), so it can run again after the logs grew. It prints the files it read, to remove by name once the records are checked; a source with a problem is not on that list.

## Memory (D14)

`fyr memory add --type T --name SLUG --description TEXT` stores the body on stdin as the `memory` record `MEMORY-<SLUG>` in the project's scope, replacing one of the same name; `T` is `user`, `feedback`, `project` or `reference`, the slug `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}`, the description one line of at most 512 bytes with no control character (the record's title; a longer one is refused); the body is `type: T`, a blank line, then the text. It prints `saved MEMORY-<SLUG>`. `fyr memory show` prints one line per memory record, `- <name> (<type>) — <description>`, sorted by name, each line cut at 640 bytes, capped at 200 lines and 25 KB with a last line naming how many more. Memory is never exported, so neither verb loads or writes `trail.jsonl`, and both work in an unmigrated project. A refusal exits 2, as `fyr memory` always did.

## Kinds

| Kind | Scope | ID | Exported |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bug` | project or global | `BUG-NNN` | yes |
| `adr` | project or global | `ADR-NNN`, `ADR-NNNa` | yes |
| `plan` `review` `testing` `change` `handoff` `retro` `learning` `spec` `deploy` `guide` | project or global | `<PREFIX>-<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>-<slug>` | yes |
| `memory` | project only | `MEMORY-<slug>` (`fyr memory add --name`; `record add memory` without `--id` gets the dated form) | never (D14) |
| `feedback` `proposal` | global only | `FEEDBACK-…`, `PROPOSAL-…` | never |

The prefix is the kind in capitals, except `testing`, whose prefix is `TEST`. `add` refuses `feedback` and `proposal` in a project (R8, D10) and `memory` with `--global` (D14). The other kinds are accepted in the global scope too: a `learning`'s scope is the agent's choice (D4), and `import --global` (Phase 2) brings `retros.jsonl` there.

## IDs (D7)

- `BUG-NNN` and `ADR-NNN` are numbered per scope: the scope's highest number of that kind plus one, read inside the write's transaction, compared as numbers (`BUG-1000` follows `BUG-999`), at least three digits and at most nine. `ADR-047a` counts as 47.
- Every other kind gets `<PREFIX>-<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>-<slug>`, the stamp from the local clock and the slug from the title (lowercase letters and digits, every other run as `-`, at most 48 characters, `record` when nothing is left). When that ID is taken in the scope, `-2`, `-3` … is appended.
- A given `--id` must match the kind: `BUG-NNN`, `ADR-NNN[a-z]`, or the kind's prefix, a dash and a lowercase slug (`[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*`, at most 128 characters). The short form (`SPEC-fyr-record`) is what Phase 2's import gives a spec.
- A duplicate ID after a merge is refused by the load, never renamed.

## Status (D6)

| Kind | Values | Open when | Starts as |
|---|---|---|---|
| plan | derived from the body: `open` while it holds a line starting `- [ ]` outside a backtick fence (`search.Unticked`, the same rule as `fyr search --open`), else `closed` | `open` | derived |
| bug | `open` `fixed` `accepted` `obsolete` `graduated` | `open` | `open` |
| adr | `accepted`, `superseded:ADR-NNN[a-z]` | never | `accepted` |
| spec, deploy, guide | `current` `retired` | `current` | `current` |
| proposal | `queued`, `applied:<commit>` (7–40 lowercase hex), `rejected` | `queued` | `queued` |
| memory | `closed`, `retired` (D28: how `/dream` drops one; `memory show` lists only `closed`, and `memory add` under a retired name makes it `closed` again) | never | `closed` |
| handoff | none (the newest is the live one) | never | none |
| everything else | `closed` | never | `closed` |

`--status` on a plan or a handoff is a usage error, as is a value the kind does not take.

## Export: `.agents/trail.jsonl`

- One record per line, `{"date","id","kind","status","title","updated","body"}` with the keys in that order, JSON without HTML escaping, lines sorted by ID (prefix, then the number numerically, then the letter, else as text), and a final newline. The same rows always give the same bytes.
- `memory`, `feedback` and `proposal` records are never exported.
- Every write in a project rewrites the file inside the write's transaction: the rows are read, the file is written to a temporary file in `.agents/` and renamed over the old one (unchanged bytes are not rewritten), and its SHA-256 is stored in `meta.export_sha`, all before the commit. A write refused before the rename (a bad body, a refused load, a symlink) leaves both the store and the file as they were. When the rename lands and the commit then fails, the file holds the record and the store does not; the next call's load takes the file.
- A symlinked or non-directory `.agents`, and a `trail.jsonl` that is a symlink or not a regular file, are refused before anything is read or written. The file is created 0644; commit it.
- The export is the checkout's own file: in a linked worktree a write goes to that worktree's `.agents/trail.jsonl`, the one its branch commits, while the scope stays the main worktree's.

## Load: the file wins (D21)

- Before any `record` verb or `search` in a project, the checkout's `trail.jsonl` is hashed. When the hash differs from `meta.export_sha` (a pull, checkout or merge changed the file), the scope's exported rows are deleted and the file's lines inserted in one transaction, under the write lock, and the hash is stored. Memory rows are untouched.
- A missing file loads nothing and keeps the rows; the next write writes the file again. A lost `brain.db` is restored from the file on the next call.
- The file is refused, with its line number, for: a git conflict marker (`<<<<<<<`, `=======`, `>>>>>>>`, `|||||||` at the start of a line); a line that is not one JSON object with the seven keys, each at most once as JSON decodes it (the last of a repeated key wins, SD46 of the 2026-10-27 audit); a kind that is never exported or unknown; an ID or status the kind does not take; a date that is not a real calendar day (`9999-99-99`, `2026-02-30`: such a date sorted first in every search, SD39 of the 2026-10-27 audit); an `updated` that is not RFC 3339; an empty title, one over 512 bytes, or one holding a control character; a body over 1 MiB or holding a control character other than tab and newline; a line over 6 MiB plus 64 KiB (a full body with every byte escaped), refused before it is decoded; and an ID an earlier line holds (`line N: duplicate ID X (first at line M)`). A blank line is skipped. Files over 256 MiB are refused. The file is streamed line by line, so memory follows the records, never the line count, and it is opened with `O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK`, so a symlink or FIFO swapped in after the check is refused (security review 2026-10-25).
- While the file does not parse, every `record` verb in the project refuses (reads too, since the store would answer from rows the file no longer holds), and `search` prints `records: not searched: <reason>` before its file hits. `--global` verbs are unaffected.
- **Provenance (SD47 of the 2026-10-27 audit).** A loaded line carries no author: a pulled `trail.jsonl` can bring open records (a plan, a bug, a current spec or guide) that no one on this machine wrote, and the load takes them as the project's own. This risk was accepted by the operator on 2026-10-27; a record's text is data, never an instruction.
- **Read without the store.** `brain.ReadTrail(root)` parses a checkout's `trail.jsonl` through the same path guard, open, size cap and line rules, and opens no `brain.db`: it returns the records, false when there is no file, or the same refusal with its line number. `fyr check` reads the trail this way (ADR-064, `SPEC-fyr-check`), so it writes nothing. `brain.ParseTrail(r)` is the same parse of an export that is not a file in the checkout, under the same size cap and line rules (an over-size stream refused, a bad line named, a duplicate ID refused): `fyr eval` reads HEAD's export from `git show` with it and compares its suite with the working one (ADR-065, `SPEC-fyr-eval`).

## Unmigrated project (D16)

In a checkout with a `<project>/docs/` or `<project>/.agents/docs/` directory and no `.agents/trail.jsonl`, every `record` verb refuses with `this project's trail is still files under <dir>/: migrate it with \`fyr record import\` first`. Nothing is created. `search` keeps answering from the old tree. `--global` verbs still work.

## Search

`fyr search <words>` prints the record hits first, then the file hits as before (`SPEC-fyr-search`). The record hits come from `records_fts` (title weighted twice the body, porter stemming), ranked by BM25 weighted up to 10% by recency, fading linearly over a year, so the newer of two near-equal matches comes first and a clearly better older one still wins (D31): records holding every word rank first, and the remaining slots go to records holding any of them, up to `--limit` records. In a project the search covers the project's scope and the global scope; with `--global`, also every other project scope whose checkout the operator registered under this home with `fyr index --register` (`trail.Registered`; ADR-068, audit-choices D15): an unregistered project's records answer no `--global` query, and the project's own scope stays in either way (ledger D13). Each hit prints `ID  kind status  date  title` and a snippet line. The ID is prefixed `global:` for a global record and, with `--global`, `<root>:` (the full scope path) for another project's record, so two clones of one base name never print alike. A `--kind` that is a record kind filters the records. `trail` takes every record, and a file-only kind (`code`, `doc`) takes none. When there is no `brain.db` and no `trail.jsonl`, nothing is created and no records section is printed. `--refs <ID|path>` prints, before the file results, `records: N naming <ref>` and the records that name the ref as written — the ID's own record first, then every record whose title or body holds the path or ID as a whole name (no path character before it, nor after it unless the ref is a directory ending in `/`), each with the line that names it; `--open` prints `records: N open` and the open records (the status table's "Open when"). Both cover the project's and the global scope, with `--global` also every registered project's scope, and take `--kind` and `--limit` (D30).

## Concurrency (D20)

Every write and every load runs inside `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` on one connection, so two processes never allocate the same number or export over each other's rows. The wait is the driver's busy timeout (10 s), after which the verb refuses with `the brain store is busy`. A new store opened by two processes at once is retried for the same 10 s, because SQLite answers that race with an immediate `SQLITE_BUSY`. There is no lock file.

## Known limits

- **A linked worktree of a separate-git-dir checkout gets its own scope** (audit SD44, `PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` items 37 and 70). A linked worktree's scope is the directory above git's common dir. For a checkout made with `--separate-git-dir`, or a submodule, that common dir lies outside the work tree, so the linked worktree's scope is not the main worktree's top level: one repository gets two scopes, two sets of records and two export rows. The main worktree is not affected. Reasoned, not run; the code is not changed, the layout being rare.

## Exit status

0 with or without output. 1 for a refusal: an empty or oversize body, a global-only kind in a project, `memory --global`, a duplicate `--id`, an ID not found, an unmigrated project, a symlinked export path, a `trail.jsonl` that does not parse, not a git checkout without `--global`, a newer schema or a busy store. 2 for a usage error: no or unknown subverb, a missing kind or ID, an unknown kind, a missing or multi-line `--title`, an `--id` or `--status` the kind does not take, `edit` with nothing to change, a flag the subverb does not take, `--project` without `--global`, `--all` with `--global`. The reason is printed on stdout as `fyr record: <reason>`, through the printable filter. A missing or unknown subverb, a missing kind or ID, and a flag the subverb does not take print, after their reason when they have one (`fyr record: unknown subcommand "<x>"`, or the subverb and the flags it does not take), record's synopsis and `run 'fyr help record' for its flags`; a bare `fyr record`, `record add`, `get` or `edit` has no reason line. The redactor warning (§ Commands) goes to stderr and leaves the status as it is.

## Schema

```sql
records(rid INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, scope TEXT NOT NULL, id TEXT NOT NULL, kind TEXT NOT NULL,
        status TEXT NOT NULL, date TEXT NOT NULL, title TEXT NOT NULL, body TEXT NOT NULL,
        project TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '', updated TEXT NOT NULL, UNIQUE(scope, id));
records_fts USING fts5(title, body, content='records', content_rowid='rid', tokenize='porter unicode61');
meta(scope TEXT PRIMARY KEY, export_sha TEXT, last_dream TEXT);
```

`scope` is the main worktree's absolute root, or `''` for global. `date` is `YYYY-MM-DD`, the day the record was added. `updated` is RFC 3339 in UTC, set by every write. `rid` is the integer rowid the FTS table keys on: the plan's composite key alone would leave an implicit rowid that `VACUUM` may renumber. Triggers keep `records_fts` in step on insert, update and delete. `last_dream` is for Phase 4.

title: `fyr search` and `fyr index`
body:
# `fyr search` and `fyr index`

Status: the project index and the global search index built 2026-09-29 (plan `PLAN-2026-09-29-search-index`, Phases 1 and 2). Requirement: R4 (one dependency, `modernc.org/sqlite`), ADR-045. Since 2026-10-25 a words search prints the brain store's record hits before the file hits (ADR-063, `SPEC-fyr-record` § Search). Since 2026-10-28 a checkout joins the global search index only when the operator registered it with `fyr index --register` (ADR-068, ledger Phase 2), and `--global` serves a row, or another project's records, only while its checkout carries this home's valid marker (ledger Phase 3). Code: `internal/search`; the marker, `internal/trail/register.go`.

## What it is

A derived SQLite index the agent queries instead of reading whole files. Git and the files in `~/.config/fyr/` stay the source of truth: the index is a cache, never committed, never sent by `report`, and deleting it loses nothing but the next query's rebuild time (about two seconds for this repository: 2.1 s for 1,351 files on 2026-10-01).

## Commands

```
fyr search [--limit N] [--kind K] [--global] <words...>
fyr search --refs <BUG-NNN|ADR-NNN|path> [--kind K] [--global]
fyr search --open [--kind K] [--global]
fyr index [--global] [--rebuild]
fyr index --register [--rebuild]
```

- **Records first.** A words search first prints the brain store's hits (`~/.config/fyr/brain.db`, `SPEC-fyr-record`): a `records: N hits for "…"` header, then per record `ID  kind status  date  title` and a snippet line, from the project's scope and the global scope (`global:ID`), or with `--global` also from every other project scope whose checkout is registered under this home (`<root>:ID`, the full scope path, for another project's): an unregistered project's records, a clone's or a copy's included, answer no `--global` query, and the project's own scope stays in whether registered or not (ADR-068, audit-choices D15, ledger D13). They are ranked by BM25 over title (weighted twice) and body, weighted up to 10% by recency (linear over a year; D31), every word first and then any word, up to `--limit` records; the file hits that follow keep their own `--limit`. A changed `.agents/trail.jsonl` is loaded first. With no records found nothing is printed, and with no `brain.db` and no `trail.jsonl` nothing is created. A `trail.jsonl` that does not parse prints `records: not searched: <reason>` and the file hits still follow. The usage check runs before the records, so a usage error prints only its reason. `--refs <ID|path>` prints, before the file results, `records: N naming <ref>` and the records that name the ref as written — the ID's own record first, then every record whose title or body holds the path or ID as a whole name (no path character before it, nor after it unless the ref is a directory ending in `/`), each with the line that names it; `--open` prints `records: N open` and the open records (the status table's "Open when"). Both cover the project's and the global scope, with `--global` also every registered project's scope, and take `--kind` and `--limit` (D30).
- **Words** are each quoted for FTS5, so `BUG-049`, `a.go` or `NOT` are searched as text, never as query syntax. Chunks holding every word rank first; the remaining slots are filled with chunks holding any of them (a chunk matching both rounds is printed once and counted once against `--limit` and the per-file cap), and the header line says how many had every word (`search: 10 hits for "…", 2 with every word (…)`). Porter stemming: `verify` finds `verifies`. Hits are ranked by BM25 with a heading weighted twice the body, at most 2 per file, `--limit` (1–50, default 10) in all.
- **Each hit** prints `path:line  kind[ ID status][  date]` and a one-line snippet (at most 200 characters, matched terms in `»«`). Control characters in indexed text, and Unicode's format characters, line separators and paragraph separators (classes Cf, Zl, Zp, and the default-ignorable characters outside them: zero-width and tag characters, direction marks, the byte-order mark, variation selectors, fillers), print as `?`, so a file cannot drive the terminal, forge a line or carry text nobody sees; the cost is that a zero-width joiner or a variation selector in an emoji sequence shows as `?` too. The line is the first line of the chunk holding a matched term.
- **`--refs X`** prints the ID's own record (`ADR-040  <path>:<line>  Superseded by ADR-041  <date>  <title>`, or `no record`), or a path's state (`tracked`, `modified`, `untracked`, `absent`, or `directory` for a trailing `/`), then `referenced by N:` and one entry per file and record that names X, newest record date first, with `×N` when it names X more than once. A path matches as written and relative to the docs root (the trail writes `plans/x.md` for `<project>/.agents/docs/plans/x.md`); no basename matching, but a bare file name that matches no path prints `hint: did you mean --refs <path>` for up to five tracked paths ending in it.
- **`--open`** lists bugs with `status: open` and plans with an unticked `- [ ]` outside fenced blocks, newest first.
- **`--kind`** is one of `bug adr plan change handoff review testing retro spec deploy trail code doc feedback proposal learning guide memory` and filters every mode by the kind of the printed path, and the record hits by the record's kind. `trail` is everything under the docs root, and every record; `code` and `doc` take no record; `feedback` and `proposal` exist only in the global search index and as global records; `learning`, `guide` and `memory` exist only as records.
- **`index`** prints `files`, `chunks`, `records`, `refs`, `changed` (by this reconcile), `bytes` (database and WAL) and `ms`. `--rebuild` deletes the database and builds it again.
- **`index --register`** is the operator's consent that this checkout is read across projects (ADR-068): its `.agents/docs` trail joins the global search index (below), its records answer `--global`, and `fyr dream --all` (`SPEC-fyr-dream`), `record import --global` (`SPEC-fyr-record`) and the metrics join (`SPEC-fyr-metrics`) take it. It writes the marker first — the regular file `fyr-registered`, mode 0600, in the checkout's git common directory (`.git/` in a plain checkout; every linked worktree shares it, and no clone carries it, because git never copies `.git/` files), holding `registered <YYYY-MM-DD>` and `seal <hex>`: the HMAC-SHA256 of the checkout's main top level under the home's registration key, `~/.config/fyr/registration.key` (0600, random, created on first use; ADR-068a) — then indexes as a plain `index` does, whose reconcile now registers the checkout, and prints `registered <root>` (the main worktree's top level) after the counts. A rerun rewrites the date; `--rebuild` combines. The marker is written to a temporary file in the same directory and renamed into place, so a symlink planted at its name is replaced, never followed; an existing symlink or non-regular file there is refused. A marker counts only when its seal matches this checkout's path under this home's key, so a tree whose `.git` file borrows a registered repository's git dir, a copy carrying `.git/` (`cp -a`, rsync, an archive of the directory), a moved checkout, a planted marker and another `--home` all read as unregistered, and a moved checkout registers again. There is no `--unregister`: deleting the marker is the opt-out (audit-choices D5); deleting `registration.key` unregisters every checkout of the home.

Exit status: 0 with hits or without; 1 on a refusal or an error; 2 on a usage error (a flag the verb does not define, a stray argument, a `--limit` outside 1..50, an unknown `--kind`, no mode or two modes at once, `--rebuild` given to `search`; the reason on stdout, BUG-168), as every verb since 2026-10-01.

## Where the indexes live

| Index | Path | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| Project | `<checkout>/.agents/scratch/search.db` (+ `-wal`, `-shm`) | every tracked, modified and untracked-not-ignored file (except what lies under a directory holding a `.fyr-noindex` file, or one under its name before the rename, `.sh-agent-noindex`, honoured the same way (plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md` D12; `TestOldNoIndexMarkerStillCounts`): data the project carries, such as the harness's `skills/google-catalog/catalog/`, is not the project's own text; the header of a words search and of `--open` then ends `; left out by a noindex marker: <dir>/, <dir>/` (sorted, the checkout's root as `./`; here `skills/google-catalog/catalog/`; `--refs`, `index` and `--global` print no list; `TestHeaderNamesLeftOutDirectories`), the marker counts committed, staged or not yet added, one at the checkout's root leaves the whole checkout out of the project index and of the global one, and a reconcile drops what was indexed before it appeared) under 1 MiB with no NUL byte in its first 8 KiB; symlinks, submodules and secret-shaped names (the installer's list, matched in any case: `.env`, `.env.*`, `*.env`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, token and credential files, …) skipped; a secret inside an ordinarily named file is indexed |
| Global search index | `~/.config/fyr/search.db` (+ `-wal`, `-shm`), under `--home` when given; the directory is created 0700. Both indexes' files are mode 0600 (an older 0644 file is tightened on open): they hold the text of every file read, whatever that file's own mode | `feedback.jsonl`, `retros.jsonl`, `proposals/*.md`, and the `<project>/.agents/docs` trail of every checkout registered with `index --register` that has one and has run `search` or `index` since |

The global file is named "the global search index", never "cross-project index": R7 already gives that name to `retros.jsonl`. A checkout registers itself in the global search index on any `search` or `index` run inside it, `--global` included, at most once a day, only when it carries the operator's marker (`index --register`, above) and has an `<project>/.agents/docs` directory, the one trail the global index reads (ledger D11: one without it would be dropped by the next `--global`). A committed `.agents/docs` alone is not consent: a clone of a third party's harness-scaffolded repository never carries the marker, so it cannot answer `--global` queries or feed `/retro` (ADR-068, audit finding SD19; `TestRegistersOnlyHarnessProjects`). `--global` reconciles `~/.config/fyr/` and each registered checkout's docs root (as `<name>:<path>`, `name~2` for a second checkout with the same base name), and drops a registration whose root is no longer a git checkout, no longer has `<project>/.agents/docs` (a plain `docs/` is never served in its place), or no longer carries this home's valid marker: the marker deleted (the opt-out), `registration.key` deleted, a moved checkout, or a row registered before ADR-068, which is not carried over (audit-choices D4). A row is a cache entry the checkout's own next search writes again once it is registered. Run outside a checkout, `--global` still answers. The registry lives in the database, so `index --global --rebuild` drops it, with a note; each registered checkout returns on its next search.

## Freshness: reconcile before every answer

Every git call runs through `internal/trail.Command`: no index lock, no fsmonitor, no signature check, `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`. None of them starts a program the checkout's config or `.gitattributes` names; `git status` is never run, because it runs clean filters (BUG-165). A partial clone (`extensions.partialClone` set, or any remote marked `promisor`) is searched only when this machine's git is 2.44 or later, which honours `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH`. With an older git, the project search refuses it with a message naming the fix (update git), and `--global` skips that checkout for the query with a note, because a missing object would be fetched through the clone's own `core.sshCommand`.

1. `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from the working directory.
2. `git ls-files -s -z`: path and blob ID of every index entry.
3. Modified tracked files.
   - `git ls-files -s --debug` (read line by line, without `-z`, so a name holding a newline cannot forge another entry's lines) gives the size and mtime the index holds for each entry. A name git quotes (non-ASCII under the default `core.quotePath`, or one holding a tab, quote or backslash) is skipped, so its file is hashed on every reconcile: correct, but slower. A file whose size and mtime (to the nanosecond) still match, and which is not racily clean (written in the second the index was), keeps the index's blob ID.
   - Every other tracked file is read, and its ID is computed from its own bytes as a git blob ID. When that ID differs from the index's, the file is modified. (`git hash-object --stdin-paths` misreads names with a trailing CR or a leading quote, so it is not used.)
   - A file the checkout runs through a clean filter therefore reads as modified and is indexed from its bytes.
   - Deleted paths leave.
4. `git ls-files -z --others --exclude-standard`: untracked files, each ID computed from its bytes. A rename is a deletion and an addition.
5. Everything derived from content (chunks, records, references) is stored once per blob ID, so a branch switch re-reads only content the index has never seen. Every query joins through the current path-to-blob view, which is what keeps another branch's content out of an answer.
6. When nothing changed, no write lock is taken (a per-query insert into the project database's unread `projects` table took one until SD20 of the 2026-10-27 audit; `TestUnchangedSearchTakesNoWriteLock` pins it); the reconcile costs about 15 ms here for the project index. `--global` reconciles every registered checkout's trail before answering (the same `git ls-files` reads per checkout, limited to its `<project>/.agents/docs`), so its cost grows with the number of registered checkouts and is not the 15 ms figure. A blob no view references is deleted after 14 days unseen.

No watcher, no service, no hook (R3, R8).

## Trail records

The docs root is `<project>/.agents/docs` when it exists, else `docs`.

| Record | Read from | ID, status |
|---|---|---|
| Bug | `bugs/BUG-NNN*.md` | frontmatter `id:` (else the file name), `status:`, `date:`, first `# ` heading |
| ADR | `architecture/DECISIONS.md` headings `## ADR-NNN: <title>     (<date>) — <status>` | one record per heading; status is everything after the dash |
| Plan | `plans/*.md` | `open: N unticked` or `closed`; line of the first unticked box |
| Other trail file | any `.md` under the docs root | its docs-relative path; `date:` |

References are record IDs (`BUG-NNN`, `ADR-NNN`) and path-shaped tokens on every line of every indexed file, with a trailing `:NN`, trailing punctuation and a leading `./`, `a/` or `b/` removed.

## Failure modes

| Case | Output | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| Not inside a git checkout, or no `git` | `search: not inside a git checkout; use grep` | 1 |
| `.agents/scratch/search.db` not gitignored | `search: .agents/scratch/search.db is not gitignored; add ".agents/scratch/*" to .gitignore (/init-project does)`; nothing created | 1 |
| `.agents` or `.agents/scratch` is a symlink | `search: .agents/scratch is a symlink; refusing to write through it` | 1 |
| `search.db`, `search.db-wal` or `search.db-shm` is a symlink or any other non-regular file (either index) | `search: <path>: <file> is not a regular file; refusing to open or write through it`; nothing is written through it | 1 |
| Another process holds the write lock past 10 s | `search: index busy (another fyr is indexing); retry, or use grep`; no answer printed | 1 |
| Two runs open a new index at once | the open is retried for the same 10 s, because SQLite answers that race with an immediate `SQLITE_BUSY` (BUG-187); past it, the line above | 1 |
| Unreadable database, or a schema other than 1 | `note: index at <path> was unreadable (or an older schema); rebuilt`, then the answer | 0 |
| Argument errors (`--limit` out of range, unknown `--kind`, two modes at once, no mode) | `search: <what is wrong>; see fyr help search` | 2 |
| Global: a registered checkout is gone, or lost its `<project>/.agents/docs` | `note: dropped <root> (no longer a git checkout)`, or `(no longer has .agents/docs)` | 0 |
| Global: a row's checkout no longer carries this home's valid marker | `note: dropped <root> (not registered: fyr index --register)`; nothing of it served | 0 |
| Global rebuild | `note: N project registrations dropped; each registered one returns on its next search` | 0 |
| `index --register --global` | `fyr index: --register and --global do not go together`; no marker written | 2 |
| `index --register` outside a git checkout | `fyr index: --register needs a git checkout` | 2 |
| `index --register`: the marker's name holds a symlink or a non-regular file, the common directory is not writable, the home's `registration.key` is a link or not a regular file, or git places the work tree elsewhere | `fyr: index --register: <path> is not a regular file; refusing to replace it`, or the error naming the path; nothing indexed (`TestIndexRegisterRefusedMarker`, `TestIndexRegisterOtherFailures`) | 1 |
| `index --register`: the marker was written, then the index failed | `fyr: registered <root>, but the index failed: <error>`; the marker stays valid | 1 |
| Global: a registered checkout's check cannot run (for example `.agents` unreadable) | `note: skipped <root> this time (<error>)`; the registration stays | 0 |
| A file edited and then restored while `search` waits for the write lock | the edit stays indexed for that blob until `index --rebuild` (known limit, plan D35) | 0 |
| A copied project directory that brings its own `search.db` | trusted as it is: an index is only as trusted as the folder it sits in, and whoever can plant one can plant `AGENTS.md` and trail files there too; after copying a project in, run `fyr index --rebuild` (known limit, the operator's choice at the v1.13.0 gate) | 0 |
| Network filesystem | not supported: SQLite's WAL needs one host's shared memory; the SQLite error is printed | 1 |

`search.db` never leaves the machine (ADR-062). `fyr uninstall` leaves `~/.config/fyr/search.db`, which is not in the install manifest; delete it by hand if wanted.

## Measured (this repository, 2026-09-29, Linux amd64)

| Measurement | Result |
|---|---|
| Full build, 1,351 files (2026-10-01; 1,080 on 2026-09-29) | 2.1 s on 2026-10-01; 1.7 s (2.2 s before the inserts were prepared once and reference parsing skipped lines that cannot match) |
| Warm `search`, nothing changed, end to end | 23–67 ms |
| Recall@10 on 41 questions from this repository's history (`TEST-2026-09-29-search-recall`; re-measured 2026-10-25 on go1.24.4 in `TEST-2026-10-25-search-recall`, after the "open plan" gold was re-pinned and "open bug", with no bug open, became a refs question) | 0.505 (2026-10-25; 0.633 on 2026-10-01 and 0.653 on 2026-09-29 on the old fixture), against 0.237 for one grep pass; words 0.538 against 0.115, drift 0.170 against 0.172 |
| Warm `--refs` / `--open`, end to end | 47–60 ms / 20 ms |
| Database size | 21.7 MB (10,560 chunks, 40,850 references); 24.1 MB before the unused `refs(oid)` index was dropped |
| Binary size, linux/amd64 | 13.7 MB |

title: Verification — attribution-write (2026-09-16, third and final pass)
body:
# Verification — attribution-write   (2026-09-16, third and final pass)

Range reviewed: working tree (uncommitted) vs HEAD (1254672) — `cmd/sh-agent/main.go`, `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` (security-review fix pass since the prior log: create path opens `O_CREATE|O_EXCL` and `Sync`s, insert path `Sync`s the temp file before rename, a non-object settings file falls through to `attributionHint`'s one-line note, CRLF files keep their line endings; test gained `"crlf file keeps its line endings"` and the `"not an object"`/`"null"` cases now assert the `note:` line) plus the still-uncommitted `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `context/AGENTS.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `README.md`, `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md`, `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md`, `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md`.

## Status: PASS

Scope: `gofmt`, `go vet`, `go test -race -v -count=1 ./...`, `install`/`status`/reinstall against a fresh scratch home, `list` — complete for this change set.

## Commands
- `gofmt -l .` → exit 0, no output.
- `go vet ./...` → exit 0, no output.
- `go test -race -v -count=1 ./...` → exit 0; output saved to `.agents/scratch/verify-attribution-write/go-test-3.txt`; counts: pass 79, fail 0, skip 1 at 1254672+dirty for `go test -race -v -count=1 ./...`; vs previous: `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-16-verify-retro-2026-09-16-applied.md`, pass 64→79, skip 1→1 — explained: the rise is this feature's full `TestAttributionNote`/`TestAttributionSet` addition plus, since the last `attribution-write` log (which had pass 78), one more subtest, `"crlf file keeps its line endings"` in `TestAttributionSet` (now 14 subtests, was 13), landed by the security-review fix pass; skip unchanged (`TestFindRepo`, pre-existing, unrelated to this change).
- `go run ./cmd/sh-agent install --home .agents/scratch/verify-attribution-write-3` → exit 0. `260 written, 0 unchanged, 0 removed, 0 kept — 260 files managed`; `note: …/.local/bin is not on PATH …`; `settings: …/.claude/settings.json created with "attribution": {"commit": "", "pr": ""} — Claude Code's commit and PR trailers are off`.
- `go run ./cmd/sh-agent status --home .agents/scratch/verify-attribution-write-3` → exit 0. `drift  none — 259 files match the repo`; no `note` line about attribution (key now present); rendered `.claude/AGENTS.md` is 93 lines (`wc -l`).
- Second `go run ./cmd/sh-agent install --home .agents/scratch/verify-attribution-write-3` (same scratch home, key already present) → exit 0. `0 written, 260 unchanged, 0 removed, 0 kept — 260 files managed`; PATH `note:` line still present (unrelated) but no `settings:` line — idempotent.
- `go run ./cmd/sh-agent list` → `### Skills (27)`, `### Subagents (7)`, matching the dispatch's expected counts.

## Coverage of changed code

`attributionSet` (`cmd/sh-agent/main.go`) branch-by-branch, against `TestAttributionSet` subtests in `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go`:
- missing settings file → `"missing file is created with only the key"`
- insert into an object with other keys, preserving formatting/mode/trailing newline → `"other keys, formatting and mode stay"`
- CRLF file keeps its line endings (new this pass) → `"crlf file keeps its line endings"`
- empty object `{}` → `"empty object"`
- key already present, off/custom value → `"off value is left alone"`, `"custom value is left alone"`
- malformed JSON → `"malformed is left alone"` (now asserts the `note:` line falls through to `attributionHint`)
- valid JSON but not an object, e.g. `["x"]` → `"not an object is left alone"` (now asserts the `note:` line)
- bare `null` → `"null is left alone"` (now asserts the `note:` line)
- file over the 1 MiB read bound → `"a file over the read bound is left alone"`
- `os.Lstat` symlink guard → `"a symlinked settings.json is never written through"`
- `--dry-run` → `"dry run writes nothing"`
- `--vendor agy` → `"antigravity only writes nothing"`
- `status` after the file is later removed (`attributionHint`) → `"status alone keeps the note"`

`abandonTemp` (`cmd/sh-agent/main.go:616`, called from the four write-error paths inside the insert branch — `tmp.Write`, `tmp.Sync`, `os.Chmod`, `os.Rename`, per lines 591/594/600/604/608) — **still not covered**. No subtest forces `os.CreateTemp`, `Write`, `Sync`, `Chmod` or `Rename` to fail, so `abandonTemp` itself, including its own `os.Remove(tmpName)` failure branch, is exercised by no test in this change. Same gap named in both prior runs of this log; unchanged by this security-review fix pass, which added the `Sync` call but not a test that forces its failure.

`readSettings` — exercised indirectly by every `TestAttributionSet` subtest that supplies a settings file, and by `TestAttributionNote`'s malformed-JSON and directory-instead-of-file cases. The `os.Open` failure path on a file that stats as regular but fails to open (e.g. a permission-denied race between the `os.Lstat`/size check and the open) is **not covered**.

`attributionOff`/`attributionHint` — asserted by the `TestAttributionNote` cases; the fall-through from `attributionSet`'s not-an-object/null/malformed branches into `attributionHint`'s one-line note is now asserted directly in `TestAttributionSet` (see above), closing the coverage gap that would have existed had those branches silently diverged from `attributionHint`'s output format.

`REQUIREMENTS.md`, `context/AGENTS.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `README.md`, `.agents/docs/deploy/{local,remote}.md`, `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` — prose only; re-read against the code's current behaviour and consistent with it; no test framework applies to prose, and this run did not re-dispatch `/review --docs` (out of scope for a verifier, and unchanged since the round-3 cold read already on disk).

## Not examined

- The `abandonTemp` write-error paths (`tmp.Write`, `tmp.Sync`, `os.Chmod`, `os.Rename`, and `abandonTemp`'s own `os.Remove` failure) — no test triggers them.
- `readSettings`'s `os.Open` failure branch on a regular file that fails to open after passing the Lstat/size checks.
- `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-16-attribution-write.md` and the five `.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-16-*attribution-write*.md` files — untracked, written by other agents, out of scope for this verification.
- No Antigravity-side smoke check (`agy` CLI start / context grep) was run for this change; the change is Claude-only (`attributionSet` no-ops for `--vendor agy`, confirmed by `"antigravity only writes nothing"`).

## `git status --short --untracked-files=all` check

Ran after the full command set. Lines outside `.agents/docs/`:
```
 M README.md
 M REQUIREMENTS.md
 M ROADMAP.md
 M cmd/sh-agent/main.go
 M cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go
 M context/AGENTS.md
```
These are the pre-existing tracked modifications that make up the change set itself (present in `git status` at the start of this session, per the dispatch's own snapshot) — not new artifacts produced by this run. No untracked file appears outside `.agents/docs/` (`git status --short --untracked-files=all | grep '^??' | grep -v '^?? \.agents/docs/'` → empty): this run's own commands (`go test`, `install`, `status`, `list`) left nothing behind outside scratch and the docs tree. The seven stray junk files noted in the two prior runs of this log (`["x"]\n`, `null\n`, etc.) are no longer present in `git status` — resolved since the last log.

## Environment

Linux 6.12.107+deb13-amd64, `go` toolchain from PATH (version not queried by this run), repo at commit 1254672 with the uncommitted changes listed in Range reviewed above (working tree dirty by design for this verification).

Linux 6.12.107+deb13-amd64. Local `go` binary: go1.24.4 (`/usr/bin/go`). Module toolchain: go1.25.8 (pinned via `go.mod`, ADR-028), auto-fetched/used for the plain runs; `GOTOOLCHAIN=local` runs used the real go1.24.4 binary. `govulncheck` present at `/home/kesokaj/.go/bin/govulncheck`, run directly (not via `go run`). No Docker/Colima involved — no Dockerfile in this range.

## Round 2

Range reviewed: c7e3688..787e15c (release-gate findings fix, since round 1's HEAD)

### Status: PASS

Scope: Setup commands re-run, govulncheck, install/status/list, the five numbered claims. Did not re-run `/review --docs` or the sandbox/real-home CLI smoke checks (same gap as round 1, not asked for this round).

### Commands
- `gofmt -l cmd internal` → exit 0, no output.
- `go vet ./...` → exit 0.
- `go test -race -v -count=1 ./...` → exit 0; output at `.agents/scratch/verify-v1.0.0-r2/go-test-1.txt`; counts: pass 106, fail 0, skip 1 at 787e15c for `go test -race -v -count=1 ./...`. vs previous: `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-16-verify-preflight-v1.0.0.md` (round 1), pass 103→106, skip 1→1 (same `TestFindRepo` skip). Rise of 3 matches new tests added in 787e15c (`TestInspectFailsClosedOnUnknownStatus`, `TestReinstallBuildsWithTheLocalToolchain`, `TestPlanDropsGroupAndOtherWrite`, plus the rename-failure leg added inside the existing `TestAdoptFailedCopyKeepsTheExistingSkill`, not a new top-level test) — no FAIL condition.
- `govulncheck ./...` → exit 0. "No vulnerabilities found." / "Your code is affected by 0 vulnerabilities... 2 vulnerabilities in packages you import and 24... in modules you require, but your code doesn't appear to call these". Output at `.agents/scratch/verify-v1.0.0-r2/govulncheck.txt`.
- `go run ./cmd/sh-agent install --home .agents/scratch/verify-v1.0.0-r2/home` → exit 0; "260 written, 0 unchanged, 0 removed, 0 kept".
- `go run ./cmd/sh-agent status --home .agents/scratch/verify-v1.0.0-r2/home` → exit 0; "drift none — 259 files match the repo"; "repo has 27 skills, 7 agents, 0 commands, 0 rules"; `binary 787e15cdbf52` (no warning). Matches expectation.
- `go run ./cmd/sh-agent list` → exit 0; `### Skills (27)`, `### Subagents (7)`.

### Claim 1 — the blocking fix (GOTOOLCHAIN=local), measured
Reproduced the failure with a fresh empty `GOMODCACHE` under `.agents/scratch/verify-v1.0.0-r2/gomodcache-empty`:
`GOMODCACHE=.../gomodcache-empty GOTOOLCHAIN=auto GOPROXY=off go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/sh-agent`
→ `go: downloading go1.25.8 (linux/amd64)` / `go: download go1.25.8 for linux/amd64: toolchain not available` → **exit 1**.

Then tried the installer's own path exactly as specified, `go run ./cmd/sh-agent install --home <home> --repo .` with the same fresh empty `GOMODCACHE` and `GOPROXY=off` → **exit 1**, same "toolchain not available" message, and it never reached Reinstall's "building sh-agent from..." line. Root cause: `go run` itself is an outer `go` invocation subject to the module's own `toolchain go1.25.8` pin under the ambient `GOTOOLCHAIN` (default `auto` unless overridden), and that pin bites before `main()` — and therefore before Reinstall's own build.Env override — ever runs. The `GOTOOLCHAIN=local` fix only touches the `exec.Command("go","build",...)` child process inside `Reinstall`; it cannot reach the outer `go run` that starts the sh-agent process itself.

To measure the actual consumer-host shape — an already-built `sh-agent` binary invoked directly, which is how `Reinstall` is truly reached (a consumer never runs `go run` against this repo) — I pre-built the binary once under a normal environment (`go build -o .../sh-agent-bin ./cmd/sh-agent`, exit 0), then ran that binary directly with the same fresh empty `GOMODCACHE` and `GOPROXY=off`:
`GOMODCACHE=.../gomodcache-empty2 GOPROXY=off .../sh-agent-bin install --home .../home-empty-cache --repo .`
→ "building sh-agent from ..." / "260 written, 0 unchanged, 0 removed, 0 kept" → **exit 0**.

So: both exit statuses as literally specified are 1 and 1 (the `go run` form fails both before and after the fix, for a reason unrelated to Reinstall). The fix is confirmed only via the binary-invocation path, which is the actual consumer shape (a downloaded/built `sh-agent` binary calling its own Reinstall, not `go run` against a checkout of this repo). This is worth flagging: the dispatch's exact command (`go run ./cmd/sh-agent install ...`) does not demonstrate the fix and cannot, structurally — it should be phrased as "build then run the binary" in any future release-gate script or guide.

### Claim 2 — fail-closed status
`TestInspectFailsClosedOnUnknownStatus` → `--- PASS` (line 173 of the test log). Reasoned from code, did not edit: the test writes `.git` as a plain file (not a dir) so every git subcommand fails; `Inspect` then sets `status, statusErr := gitOut(...)` where `gitOut` returns `("", err)` on failure, so `Dirty` (which is `status != ""`) would read **false** if `StatusUnknown` did not exist or were ignored by `Pull`. The test's second assertion, `Pull(repo, io.Discard)` must return non-nil, would then fail, because pre-787e15c `Pull` only checked `Inspect(repo).Dirty`. This confirms the test would fail if `StatusUnknown` were dropped from the `Dirty || StatusUnknown` guard in `Pull` (repo.go) and in `update` (main.go).

### Claim 3 — adopt's backup
`TestAdoptFailedCopyKeepsTheExistingSkill` → `--- PASS` (line 149). The rename-failure leg (chmod `skills/` to `0o500` to force the rename-into-place to fail, then assert the original survives and the error names `.agents/scratch`) is gated by `if os.Geteuid() != 0`. This run's user is `kesokaj`, uid 1000 (`id -u` → 1000), not root, so the leg ran and passed as part of the single PASS line above (subtests aren't split out for this test — it's one `t.Run`-free function with an inline conditional). Under root it would be skipped silently (no `t.Skip` call, so it wouldn't show as a SKIP line — it just wouldn't execute that block).

### Claim 4 — deployed modes
`TestPlanDropsGroupAndOtherWrite` → `--- PASS` (line 177). Cross-checked directly against the installed tree: `find .agents/scratch/verify-v1.0.0-r2/home -type f -perm /022` → 0 results — no installed file carries group or other write.

### Claim 5 — coverage of 787e15c
- `internal/harness/repo.go` (`Inspect` StatusUnknown, `Pull` guard) — `TestInspectFailsClosedOnUnknownStatus`.
- `internal/harness/adopt.go` (backup/restore rename logic) — `TestAdoptFailedCopyKeepsTheExistingSkill` (extended).
- `internal/harness/plan.go` (`mode := info.Mode().Perm()&0o755 | 0o600`, expanded `secretShaped` patterns) — `TestPlanDropsGroupAndOtherWrite`; did not find a test iterating the newly added `secretShaped` patterns (`.envrc`, `.netrc`, `.npmrc`, `.pypirc`, `*.p12`, `*.pfx`, `*.keystore`, `*.jks`, `*.tfstate.backup`, `id_rsa`, `id_ed25519`, `id_ecdsa`, `id_dsa`) individually — grep for these literal strings in harness_test.go came up empty in the time available. **NOT COVERED, flagged, not confirmed either way with certainty** — see Not examined.
- `internal/harness/repo.go` (`Reinstall` GOTOOLCHAIN=local) — `TestReinstallBuildsWithTheLocalToolchain` (string-match guard on the source, not an execution test — reasonable given the network/cache dependency, but note it only checks the code shape, not a live empty-cache build; that live case is exactly what I measured by hand above).
- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` (`update`'s `info.StatusUnknown` branch, the "could not be checked for uncommitted changes" message) — **NOT COVERED at the cmd/sh-agent level.** `TestUpdateNeverInstallsDirtyTree`'s subtests exercise `Dirty` only (via `dirty()` writing an uncommitted file); none construct a repo where `git status` itself fails and call `update()` to confirm it refuses with the StatusUnknown wording. The harness-level test (`TestInspectFailsClosedOnUnknownStatus`) covers `Inspect`/`Pull` but not `update`'s own composition of the error string in main.go. This is a genuine gap.
- `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` `TestReadSettingsProblems` closed-set assertion — pre-existing function, test strengthened, not new production code.
- Suppressions: `git diff c7e3688..787e15c -- '*.go'` for `//nolint`, `//lint:ignore`, `t.Skip`, `t.SkipNow`, `//go:build ignore`, `.skip(`, `.only(` → one hit, `t.Skip("git is not on PATH")` inside `TestInspectFailsClosedOnUnknownStatus`, carries a reason — not a bare skip, no FAIL.
- ADR-028 amendment (`.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md`) read in full: states plainly the pin is a ceiling for gated builds, not a floor for a consumer, and that `Reinstall` now uses `GOTOOLCHAIN=local`; matches what was measured.

### Root cause (FAIL only)
N/A — Status is PASS, with two named gaps (see Coverage and Not examined) that did not reach FAIL threshold: the `secretShaped` new-pattern coverage is unconfirmed, not proven absent, and the `update()` StatusUnknown wording is confirmed uncovered but is a message string, not the fail-closed behavior itself (which the harness-level test does cover, and which is what the release finding was about).

### Not examined
- Whether `secretShaped`'s newly added patterns (`.envrc`, `.netrc`, `.npmrc`, `.pypirc`, `*.p12`, `*.pfx`, `*.keystore`, `*.jks`, `*.tfstate.backup`, `id_rsa`, `id_ed25519`, `id_ecdsa`, `id_dsa`) are each asserted by a test — grepped and found none in the time available but did not read `TestPlanRefusesSecretShapedFiles` in full to rule out a table-driven form covering them.
- No test found covering `update()`'s own `StatusUnknown` branch/message in `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` (as opposed to `Inspect`/`Pull`, which are covered). Not fixed, only reported per the verifier's role.
- Did not re-run `/review --docs` over c7e3688..787e15c or check `.agents/docs/reviews/` for one already present this round — same gap named in round 1, not re-checked here.
- Did not re-run the sandbox/real-home CLI smoke checks for 787e15c.
- Did not run `GOTOOLCHAIN=local go build ./...` / `go test` under the real local go1.24.4 toolchain this round (done in round 1 at c7e3688, not repeated).
- Cut off by the turn limit before independently re-deriving `Not covered` status for `secretShaped` with full certainty; flagged rather than asserted.

### Environment
Linux 6.12.107+deb13-amd64, uid 1000 (non-root, confirmed for claim 3). `go` binary go1.24.4; module toolchain go1.25.8 pinned (ADR-028). `govulncheck` at `/home/kesokaj/.go/bin/govulncheck`. Scratch under `.agents/scratch/verify-v1.0.0-r2/`.

## Correction, appended by the main agent after round 2

Rounds 1 and 2 above both record `govulncheck ./...` as reporting no vulnerabilities affecting this code. **That was measured while `go.mod` carried `toolchain go1.25.8`, and that directive has since been withdrawn (ADR-029).** Both readings were true when taken and are wrong about the shipped tree. Re-measured by the main agent after the withdrawal, on the same box:

```
$ govulncheck ./...
Your code is affected by 2 vulnerabilities from the Go standard library.
  GO-2026-4602  os@go1.24.4       fixed in os@go1.25.8        reached through LoadSkills
  GO-2025-3956  os/exec@go1.24.4  fixed in os/exec@go1.24.6    reached through Reinstall's LookPath
```

Why the pin went: round 2's own claim-1 measurement is the reason. It found that the `GOTOOLCHAIN=local` fix inside `Reinstall` cannot save the outer `go run`, which is subject to the pin and fails before any of this code executes. The main agent reproduced the same independently. A pin that makes the module unbuildable on an offline host with an older Go is a worse property than the two advisories it cleared, so it was removed rather than patched a third time. After the withdrawal, in that same restricted environment (empty `GOMODCACHE`, `GOTOOLCHAIN=auto`, `GOPROXY=off`), `go build ./cmd/sh-agent` and `go run ./cmd/sh-agent install` both exit 0.

The two advisories are an operator toolchain item, unchanged from before today and recorded in three earlier security reviews: they are fixed in go1.24.6 and go1.25.8, Debian trixie ships `golang-1.24-go 1.24.4-1` and nothing newer, and `/usr/lib/go-1.24` is root-owned. v1.0.0 ships with them present, and the gate report says so.

Everything else in rounds 1 and 2 stands: the counts, the install and drift checks, the fail-closed status test, adopt's rename-failure leg, and the deployed-mode check were all measured on trees that differ from the shipped one only by the `toolchain` line and the round-2 fixes.

Must-pass, every command up to and excluding the two `git push` lines, each its own call, exit read before the next:
- `ssh-keygen -y -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 | ssh-keygen -lf -` → `256 SHA256:5HpYQJjpG+yE1xXBTOIZPsTkbkgkVnV8z0eG8hBawyU ostling.simon@gmail.com (ED25519)` — matches the doc's fingerprint, derived from the private key.
- `git status --porcelain` → exit 0, no output (clean).
- `git rev-parse HEAD` → `b00283b070c9b40951483b7ad43949aa125adcca`.
- `git -c gpg.format=ssh -c user.signingkey="$HOME/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub" tag -s v0.0.2 -m "styrman-harness v0.0.2" b00283b070c9b40951483b7ad43949aa125adcca` → exit 0.
- `test "$(git rev-parse v0.0.2^{commit})" = "b00283b070c9b40951483b7ad43949aa125adcca"` → exit 0.
- `git merge-base --is-ancestor v0.0.2^{commit} main` → exit 0.
- `test "$(git cat-file -t v0.0.2)" = tag` → exit 0.
- `test "$(git cat-file tag v0.0.2 | grep -E '^-----BEGIN' | tail -1)" = '-----BEGIN SSH SIGNATURE-----'` → exit 0.
- `printf '%s\n' 'ostling.simon@gmail.com ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIBkx0BICH1xG18f0a0F/02Vw0OvBTfSOVNXkPkO62NCR' > allowed_signers` (rehearsal dir, not `.agents/scratch/allowed_signers` since this whole rehearsal is already under scratch) → exit 0.
- `sudo -n cmp /etc/styrman/allowed_signers allowed_signers` → **not run: root step, operator's** (per instruction — no sudo used).
- `git -c gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile=allowed_signers verify-tag v0.0.2` → exit 0, `Good "git" signature for ostling.simon@gmail.com with ED25519 key SHA256:5HpYQJjpG+yE1xXBTOIZPsTkbkgkVnV8z0eG8hBawyU`.
- `git push origin main` / `git push origin v0.0.2` → **not run** (no remote configured in the throwaway repo; excluded by the dispatch's must-pass scope, which stops before the two push lines).

Must-fail (each in the same rehearsal repo):
- (a) Second commit `2ad0be9fada36ba2e6c8fd85f17797e1e042cd86`, `git tag v0.0.3 <second sha>`, then `test "$(git rev-parse v0.0.3^{commit})" = "b00283b070c9b40951483b7ad43949aa125adcca"` → exit 1, as required.
- (b) Lightweight `git tag v0.0.4 main`: `test "$(git cat-file -t v0.0.4)" = tag` → exit 1 (`git cat-file -t v0.0.4` prints `commit`).
- (c) Annotated unsigned `git -c gpg.format=ssh tag -a v0.0.5 -m "unsigned annotated" main`: the armor `test` → exit 1 (no `-----BEGIN` line, grep prints nothing); `git verify-tag v0.0.5` (with the scratch `allowedSignersFile`) → exit 1, `error: no signature found`.
- (d) Fresh throwaway key `foreignkey2/id_ed25519` (freshly generated under the rehearsal dir, `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -N "" -C throwaway2@example.com`), tag `v0.0.6` signed with it (tag command itself exits 0 — signature is valid, just under an unlisted key) → `git verify-tag v0.0.6` against the scratch `allowed_signers` → exit 1, stderr `No principal matched.` — exact wording the doc claims.

All must-pass and must-fail outcomes for the rewritten block match the doc's claims exactly, including the new `test` forms, the target-SHA and ancestor-of-`main` binding, and the private-key-derived fingerprint check. The `sudo -n cmp` line is syntactically present in the block and unexecuted here by design (root step, belongs to the operator on the crew host, not reproducible in this throwaway repo which has no `/etc/styrman/allowed_signers`).

Re-read in full (Step 6 "Ship or stop"). It defers to a project's `AGENTS.md`/deploy guide for tag form, signing command and pre-push checks ("tag exactly as it says and run those checks before the push") and requires confirming the tag's target before pushing (`git rev-parse <tag>^{commit}` prints its SHA) — consistent with, and satisfied by, the rewritten `remote.md` block rehearsed above. No command in Step 6 itself was rehearsed standalone; it is instructions that point at the deploy-guide procedure already exercised end to end.

Documentation/instruction-text coverage as in round 1, plus the newly rewritten `remote.md` § Releases block — exercised directly and exhaustively above, both must-pass and all four must-fail cases. `skills/preflight/SKILL.md` Step 6 — exercised indirectly via `sh-agent install`/`status`/`list` (parses and installs drift-free) and by inspection against the rehearsed procedure it defers to.
