title: E2E — v1.1.0 published and consumed from GitHub (2026-09-17)
body:
# E2E — v1.1.0 published and consumed from GitHub (2026-09-17)

Range reviewed: v1.1.0 (tag cb26d2b, release commit 42698d2)

## What ran

The release was cut by `/preflight v1.1.0` from the operator's own turn, on the Linux box (`dave`), following `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` § Releases. This log covers the part no rehearsal could reach: the real GitHub release, downloaded and consumed by the shipping code.

1. **Publish.** `gh release create v1.1.0 --verify-tag` with the three binaries, `SHA256SUMS` and `SHA256SUMS.sig` failed TWICE with `HTTP 500: Error creating asset temp dir` from `uploads.github.com`, a server-side error; both attempts rolled back, leaving no release (confirmed with `gh api repos/.../releases`, which listed none) and the tag intact. The release was then created without assets, which succeeded, and the five assets uploaded one at a time with `gh release upload --clobber` and up to three attempts each — every one succeeded on its first attempt. Final state: five assets, `SHA256SUMS` 287 bytes, `SHA256SUMS.sig` 310, the binaries 6.7–7.0 MB.
2. **Download and verify as a consumer.** `gh release download v1.1.0 --pattern …` into a scratch directory, then the checks a place runs: `ssh-keygen -Y verify -n sh-agent-release` over the DOWNLOADED `SHA256SUMS` → `Good "sh-agent-release" signature for ostling.simon@gmail.com with ED25519 key SHA256:5HpYQJjpG+yE1xXBTOIZPsTkbkgkVnV8z0eG8hBawyU`; `sha256sum -c --ignore-missing` → `OK`; first line `# styrman-harness v1.1.0`, the marker `update` requires; `./sh-agent-linux-amd64 version` → `sh-agent v1.1.0`.
3. **Golden path, install.** Run from `/` with `SH_AGENT_REPO` unset, into a scratch home: `release binary v1.1.0: installing the harness built into it and the running binary`, 260 files written. `status` → `source     embedded v1.1.0 (release binary; update downloads the newest release)`, `installed … from release v1.1.0 (vendor: all, 260 files …)`, `binary     v1.1.0`, `drift      none — 259 files match the repo`, exit 0.
4. **Golden path, update.** `update --check` against the real GitHub → `up to date (v1.1.0)`, exit 0.

## What this settles

- **The published release is installable by the shipping code**, which the rehearsal could only show for locally built assets.
- **D21 holds in the wild.** A release binary built with `-trimpath` at a clean tag reports `v1.1.0` for its own version — `status`'s `binary v1.1.0` line proves the module-version read works for a real release, not just in the unit test.
- **D26's marker survives the round trip** through GitHub's asset storage and is read back as the code requires.
- **The repository stayed private** throughout: `gh repo view --json visibility` reports `PRIVATE` after publishing, and the operator asked about exactly this. A release in a private repository is visible only to accounts that can already read it, and asset download needs authentication — which is what README § Install without cloning relies on.

## Not exercised

- **Every work Mac leg of the plan's e2e criteria.** This ran on the Linux box only. Owed on the work Mac: the README `gh` one-liner, `sh-agent install`, `status` showing `source embedded v1.1.0`, `sh-agent report` leaving no `feedback` or `report-*` directory, and the edge case (`update` with no newer release, and a swapped signature file refused).
- **`darwin/arm64` and `linux/arm64` were built and published but never run** — no machine of either kind was available here.
- **`go install github.com/kesokaj/styrman-harness/cmd/sh-agent@v1.1.0`** — untested; the tag now exists, so it can be.
- **A real `sh-agent report` from this published install.** The operator authorised exactly one real report today (D25) and it ran earlier from the checkout; a second was not authorised, so the golden path's report leg is owed on the work Mac.
- **`update` actually replacing a binary from a real release.** `--check` reached GitHub and compared versions, but no newer release exists to update TO. The replacement path is covered against local assets by the rehearsal (`.agents/scratch/v110-rehearsal/`) and by the unit tests.

## Added 2026-09-18 — everything the Linux box can still settle

Run after the release, on `main` at c7a6116 (the tag's content plus the kept-clone message fix), all in `.agents/scratch/`:

- **`go install` from the tag works, and its version comes from build info.** `GOPATH=<scratch> GOPRIVATE='github.com/kesokaj/*' go install github.com/kesokaj/styrman-harness/cmd/sh-agent@v1.1.0` → exit 0 once git was told to fetch over SSH; the binary reports `sh-agent v1.1.0`, and `go version -m` shows `mod … v1.1.0` with NO `-ldflags` setting — so this is the `debug.ReadBuildInfo().Main.Version` branch of D6/D21, which nothing before could exercise. Installing from it, run from `/` with `SH_AGENT_REPO` unset: 260 files, `source embedded v1.1.0`, drift none. **This closes the last assumption in the plan's Risks.**
- **The README's first install path runs verbatim.** `gh release download --repo kesokaj/styrman-harness --pattern 'sh-agent-linux-amd64' --dir …` then `mv`/`chmod` → `sh-agent v1.1.0`, and it installs 260 files. The only deviation from the README was `--dir` pointing at scratch instead of `~/.local/bin`, so the operator's installed binary was left alone.
- **The README's `go install` path did NOT run verbatim** — recorded as BUG-075 and fixed in the same task. As shipped in v1.1.0 it failed with `could not read Username for 'https://github.com': terminal prompts disabled`: the comment said "over SSH" but the command gave git no way to use SSH. README now carries the working form.
- **All three published binaries verify.** `gh release download v1.1.0` with no pattern fetched all five assets; `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS` → `OK` for `sh-agent-linux-amd64`, `sh-agent-darwin-arm64` and `sh-agent-linux-arm64`; `ssh-keygen -Y verify` over the file as published → good signature. `file` reports the darwin asset as `Mach-O 64-bit arm64` and the linux/arm64 asset as `ELF 64-bit LSB … ARM aarch64`, so the cross-compilation produced the right architectures even though neither can be executed here.
- **`sh-agent update` on the real home** (the operator asked): `up to date with upstream`, the old kept feedback clone correctly KEPT, 260 files unchanged. The clone was then measured — local `HEAD` `e973bac`, remote `main` `09586ff`, tracking ref stale at `71f749e`, and after a fetch `git log --oneline HEAD --not FETCH_HEAD` empty — so it holds nothing unique and is the operator's to delete. The misleading wording that prompted the check is BUG-074, fixed.

### Still only the Mac can settle these

- Running a `darwin/arm64` binary at all: the README one-liner, `sh-agent install`, `status` showing `source embedded v1.1.0`, and the macOS `xattr` quarantine note, which no Linux box can exercise.
- `sh-agent report` from a release-binary install, leaving no `feedback` or `report-*` directory behind.
- The edge case: `sh-agent update` with a swapped signature file refusing and leaving the binary untouched, run against the real release rather than a fixture.
- Whether both CLIs start cleanly from a home installed by a release binary, which needs the sandbox home that no longer exists here.

## Added 2026-09-18 — v1.2.0, and the first real cross-release update

v1.2.0 was cut with the CORRECTED procedure (create the release with notes alone, then one upload per asset). It published first time, with no rollback — the shape v1.1.0's two `HTTP 500`s taught.

- **Published and verified as a consumer:** `gh release download v1.2.0` (all five assets), `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS` → OK for all three binaries, `ssh-keygen -Y verify` over the file as published → good signature, `./sh-agent-linux-amd64 version` → `sh-agent v1.2.0`.
- **The cross-release update path, which could not exist until now.** A scratch place was installed from the v1.1.0 binary (`source embedded v1.1.0`), then `sh-agent update` ran against the real GitHub: `downloading sh-agent-linux-amd64 v1.2.0`, `verified and installed`, the new binary's install, and `4 written, 256 unchanged`. The binary's hash changed, and `status` now reports `source embedded v1.2.0`, `binary v1.2.0`, drift none.
- **Those four files are the point of the release:** `context/AGENTS.md` and `skills/preflight/SKILL.md`, one copy per vendor. A binary-only place picking up new rules is exactly what the release binary was built for, and this is the first time it has happened end to end.
- **The embed-contamination guard ran twice**, as the corrected guide says: once among the pre-tag checks and once immediately before the builds.

### Still only the Mac can settle these

Unchanged from the section above, now owed against v1.2.0 rather than v1.1.0: running any `darwin/arm64` binary at all, the macOS `xattr` quarantine note, `report` from a release-binary install leaving nothing behind, the swapped-signature edge case, and a clean start of both CLIs from a home installed by a release binary.

## Added 2026-09-18 — the work Mac, on v1.2.0 (the operator's own runs)

Host `spgo-mac.roam.internal`, darwin/arm64, Antigravity only. Run by the operator from `/tmp`, i.e. with no harness checkout anywhere near — the shape the whole feature exists for. **This is the first time a `darwin/arm64` binary has been executed at all.**

- **Download and run.** `gh release download v1.2.0 --pattern 'sh-agent-darwin-arm64' --dir ~/.local/bin`, `mv`, `chmod +x` → `sh-agent v1.2.0`, 6709378 bytes, byte-identical in size to the published asset. No `xattr` step needed: a `gh` download is not quarantined, as README says.
- **Install.** `sh-agent install --vendor antigravity` → `release binary v1.2.0: installing the harness built into it and the running binary`, `2 written, 128 unchanged, 0 removed, 0 kept — 130 files managed`. 130 is one vendor's half of 260, and the 2 written are `context/AGENTS.md` and `skills/preflight/SKILL.md` — exactly v1.2.0's delta over what that home already had.
- **Status.** `source     embedded v1.2.0 (release binary; update downloads the newest release)`, `installed … from release v1.2.0 (vendor: antigravity, 130 files …)`, `binary     v1.2.0`, `drift      none — 129 files match the repo`.
- **Report, the first ever from a release-binary install.** `--dry-run` named the throwaway clone (`report-7033`, blob-less, limited to `reports/spgo-mac.roam.internal/`) and the note `harness is the release binary v1.2.0, not a checkout: harness_commit is null, harness_version is set`. The real run sent `reports/spgo-mac.roam.internal/2026-09-18-103648 (c4b13a8)`. Verified independently from the Linux box by cloning the feedback repository: that commit exists and its `report.json` reads `{"host":"spgo-mac.roam.internal","os":"darwin","arch":"arm64","vendor":"antigravity","files":130,"harness_commit":null,"harness_version":"v1.2.0","drift":0,"skills":27,"agents":7,"go":"go1.27.1"}` — the `harness_version` shape existed only in fixtures until now. The push took about 1m 9s.
- **Nothing kept.** `ls -la ~/.config/sh-agent/` afterwards: `state.json` and no `report-*` directory. The throwaway was created and removed on a second machine.
- **`update --check`** → `up to date (v1.2.0)`, exit 0.
- **`adopt`** → `adopt needs a harness checkout; this install is a release binary`. (A typo, `adpot`, first printed the usage text, which incidentally confirmed v1.2.0's updated `update` and `report` descriptions shipped.)
- **CLI start.** `agy -p 'List three skills you have.'` from a scratch directory answered cleanly, naming `golang`, `typescript` and `cloud-run-deploy` with paths under `~/.gemini/config/skills/` — the files the binary carried. This is the tier the Linux box could not run, because its sandbox home no longer exists.

### What the Mac exposed

`ls ~/.config/sh-agent/` also showed `feedback/`, dated 2026-09-17 — the full clone earlier versions kept. `report` ignores it by design, but `update` is supposed to remove it, and the plan says so for BOTH kinds of place (§ Old kept clone cleanup). Only the checkout path called `RemoveKeptClone`; the release-binary branch returned before reaching it. So a binary-only place would have kept holding every other machine's reports — the exact complaint this feature began with, surviving in the one place it was meant to fix. Fixed the same day with a test that fails without the call; it reaches that Mac in the next release.

### Still not exercised anywhere

- The signature edge case on darwin (a swapped `SHA256SUMS.sig` refused). Proven on Linux against the real releases; not run on the Mac.
- The Claude Code side on that Mac: it was installed `--vendor antigravity` only, so `~/.claude` there holds nothing from v1.2.0 and `claude` was not started from it.
- `linux/arm64`: built and published for both releases, never executed on any machine.

## Added 2026-09-18 — v1.2.1 on two machines the operator ran himself

Both runs are from the operator's own shell, on machines with no harness checkout in play. Between them they close every leg that had been owed since v1.1.0 except three, named at the end.

### devbox (Debian, linux/amd64) — first release-binary install on this machine

- **Download verified before anything was moved.** `gh release download v1.2.1` (binary, `SHA256SUMS`, `SHA256SUMS.sig`) into a fresh `mktemp -d`; `ssh-keygen -Y verify -n sh-agent-release` → `Good "sh-agent-release" signature for ostling.simon@gmail.com with ED25519 key SHA256:5HpYQJjpG+yE1xXBTOIZPsTkbkgkVnV8z0eG8hBawyU`; `sha256sum -c` → `sh-agent-linux-amd64: OK`; `./sh-agent-linux-amd64 version` → `sh-agent v1.2.1`, run from the download directory before the install.
- **The install was then lost to PATH shadowing** — recorded as BUG-078, and the reason this section exists. `/usr/local/bin/sh-agent` held the verified v1.2.1 binary (7052333 bytes, and `/usr/local/bin/sh-agent version` printed `v1.2.1` when called by absolute path), but `which -a sh-agent` found `/home/admin/.local/bin/sh-agent` (PATH 1) and `/opt/devbox/bin/sh-agent` (PATH 5) ahead of it at PATH 11. Unqualified `sh-agent` therefore ran a `(devel)` build, which resolved the stale plain copy at `/opt/devbox/deploy/harness` and installed THAT — reporting `drift none` the whole time, because drift is measured against whatever source the running binary resolved.
- **Proof the content was stale, and proof it stopped being so.** With the shadowed binary, `claude -p 'Quote the rule about a guard in front of a destructive action.'` quoted the `rm -r` bullet — the fail-closed guard rule at `context/AGENTS.md:58` was not in that tree. After `/opt/devbox/bin/sh-agent` was pointed at `/usr/local/bin/sh-agent`, `grep -c 'A guard in front of a destructive' ~/.claude/AGENTS.md` → `1`.
- **Install, once the right binary ran.** `sh-agent install --vendor=all` → `release binary v1.2.1: installing the harness built into it and the running binary`, `29 written, 231 unchanged, 2 removed, 0 kept — 260 files managed`. The 2 removed are files the stale tree had and v1.2.1 does not.
- **Status.** `source embedded v1.2.1 (release binary; update downloads the newest release)`, `installed 2026-09-18T10:26:00Z from release v1.2.1 (vendor: all, 260 files …)`, `binary v1.2.1`, `drift none — 259 files match the repo`.
- **Report, from a release binary, `--vendor all`.** `report: harness is the release binary v1.2.1, not a checkout: harness_commit is null, harness_version is set`; `skipped feedback.jsonl (absent)`; sent `reports/devbox/2026-09-18-102654 (1aefa0e)` — 9 files, 1627 insertions, six queued retro proposals among them.
- **Nothing kept.** `ls -la ~/.config/sh-agent/` afterwards: `proposals/`, `retros.jsonl`, `state.json`. No `feedback/`, no `report-*`. First time this has been shown on a `--vendor all` release-binary place.

### The work Mac (darwin/arm64) — the kept clone, shed for real

- **`sh-agent update` on v1.2.1** → `removed the kept feedback clone /Users/spgo/.config/sh-agent/feedback (report no longer keeps one)`, then `up to date (v1.2.1)`. This is the fix for what § What the Mac exposed found on 2026-09-18: the release-binary branch of `update` returned before `RemoveKeptClone`. The clone that machine had held since 2026-09-17 is gone.
- The preceding `update` on that Mac, which fetched v1.2.1 itself, could not have shed it: `git show v1.2.0:cmd/sh-agent/main.go | grep -c shedKeptClone` → `0`, against `4` for v1.2.1. `update` replaces the binary and then runs the NEW binary's `install`, never its `update`, so the shedding waited for a second `update` — worth knowing for any future cleanup that ships this way.
- **`ls -la ~/.config/sh-agent/`** → `state.json` alone.
- **`report`** → sent `reports/spgo-mac.roam.internal/2026-09-18-122933 (789e2d9)`, two files, with the same release-binary metrics note. `feedback.jsonl`, `retros.jsonl` and `proposals/` were all absent and each was named as skipped.

### What these two runs settle

- A `darwin/arm64` binary and a `linux/amd64` release binary both run, install, report and update on machines with no checkout.
- `update` sheds the old kept clone on a release-binary place — the last piece of "report keeps nothing on the machine".
- A release delivers context rules to a binary-only place: the fail-closed guard rule, graduated on 2026-09-17, is now on both machines and was quoted back from neither before this.

### Still not exercised anywhere

- The swapped-signature edge case on darwin (a tampered `SHA256SUMS.sig` refused, binary untouched). Proven on Linux against the real releases; never run on the Mac.
- `linux/arm64`: built and published for all three releases, never executed on any machine.
- The Claude Code side of the work Mac: still installed `--vendor antigravity` only, so `~/.claude` there holds nothing from any release and `claude` has not been started from it. devbox covers the Claude side on Linux.
- `sh-agent update` has never run on devbox: that machine reached v1.2.1 by download and `install`, not by updating from an earlier release.

## Added 2026-09-18 — v1.2.2 published and consumed

v1.2.2 (release commit f3ec5dc on gated head f91257c, tag signed and verified before the push) was cut by `/preflight v1.2.2` from the operator's own turn and published with the create-then-upload-per-asset shape: five assets, each first attempt. Gate: `.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-18-preflight-v1.2.2.md`.

- **Published and verified as a consumer**, from a fresh scratch directory: `gh release download v1.2.2` (all five assets) → `ssh-keygen -Y verify` over `SHA256SUMS` as published → `Good "sh-agent-release" signature`; `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS` → OK for all three binaries; `./sh-agent-linux-amd64 version` → `sh-agent v1.2.2`; and the new binding the docs now ask for, `test "$(./sh-agent-linux-amd64 version)" = "sh-agent $(sed -n 's/^# styrman-harness //p' SHA256SUMS)"` → exit 0. The downloaded `linux/amd64` binary is byte-identical to the one built here (`cmp`).
- **Repository visibility** after the upload: `PRIVATE`.

### Not exercised

- `sh-agent update` from v1.2.1 to v1.2.2 on any place: the operator's Mac and devbox are the binary-only places, and both updates are theirs to run (the handoff's Next Steps). The cross-release update path itself is proven for v1.1.0 → v1.2.0 (Linux, scratch) and v1.2.0 → v1.2.1 (the Mac).
- `darwin/arm64` and `linux/arm64` v1.2.2 binaries: built, checksummed, signed and published; not executed.
- The README browser chain on a Mac, including its `shasum -a 256 -c - --ignore-missing` form.

### Added 2026-09-18 — the v1.2.1 → v1.2.2 update, on all three machines (the operator's runs)

- **Work Mac (darwin/arm64):** `sh-agent update` → `downloading sh-agent-darwin-arm64 v1.2.2`, `verified and installed sh-agent-darwin-arm64 v1.2.2`, the new binary's install `0 written, 130 unchanged` — correct, v1.2.2 changed no embedded file; `sh-agent version` → `sh-agent v1.2.2`; `install --vendor antigravity` → `0 written, 130 unchanged`. Clean.
- **devbox (linux/amd64):** `sh-agent update` → `downloading sh-agent-linux-amd64 v1.2.2`, `verified and installed …`, `0 written, 260 unchanged`; then **`sh-agent version` → `sh-agent v1.2.1`**. `which -a` showed `~/.local/bin` first and `/usr/local/bin` last, so PATH order was right and the BUG-078 guard correctly printed nothing. The `update` had been run BY `/usr/local/bin/sh-agent` (v1.2.1), which `UpdateFromRelease` never replaces — it writes `~/.local/bin/sh-agent` — and bash's command hash kept pointing at `/usr/local/bin`; after `sudo rm` of that file the shell said `-bash: /usr/local/bin/sh-agent: No such file or directory`, which is the hash table, not PATH. `source .bashrc` reset it: `sh-agent version` → `v1.2.2`, `install --vendor all` → `0 written, 260 unchanged`, `status` → `source embedded v1.2.2`, `binary v1.2.2`, drift none, no `shadowed` line. **The documented unqualified `sh-agent version` check is what caught it.** Recorded as BUG-079.
- **This Linux box (checkout place):** `sh-agent update` → `up to date with upstream (790550c)`, rebuilt from the checkout, `0 written, 260 unchanged`; `sh-agent version` → `sh-agent 790550c1f7a6`; `status` → `binary 790550c1f7a6`, drift none, no `shadowed` line. The kept feedback clone here is still declined by `update` (two commits it cannot prove pushed), as intended.

Still not exercised: the README browser chain on the Mac; `linux/arm64`; the swapped-signature edge on darwin.

## Added 2026-09-18 — v1.2.3 published and consumed

v1.2.3 (release commit 91fcf13 on gated head 30f7488; gate `.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-18-preflight-v1.2.3.md`, SHIP) was cut by `/preflight v1.2.3` on the operator's "approved go go go" and published create-then-upload-per-asset: five assets, each first attempt; repository `PRIVATE` after.

- **Published and verified as a consumer**, from a fresh directory, with the by-hand chain's own checks as README now writes them: `ssh-keygen -Y verify` → good signature; `grep -qxF "# styrman-harness v1.2.3" SHA256SUMS` → 0; `sha256sum -c` → OK ×3; `./sh-agent-linux-amd64 version` = `sh-agent v1.2.3`; byte-identical to the build.
- **The published binary installed into a scratch home**: `release binary v1.2.3: installing the harness built into it and the running binary`, `260 written`; `status` → `source embedded v1.2.3`, `binary v1.2.3`, drift none; `~/.config/sh-agent` created `700`.

### The v1.2.2 → v1.2.3 update, on all three machines (the operator's runs, 2026-09-18)

Logged cell by cell in `sh-agent-matrix.md` § Real machines: this box (checkout place), the work Mac (darwin/arm64 release binary), devbox (linux/amd64 release binary). Each printed the `mode ~/.config/sh-agent (0755 -> 0700)` line on its first run, `version` unqualified reported the new version, `type` named the installed path, `status` drift none with no `shadowed` line, and the runtime dir was `700` after. The `darwin/arm64` binary has now run on the Mac; `linux/arm64` still has not run anywhere.

### Not exercised

- The README browser chain on the Mac (`shasum -a 256 -c - --ignore-missing`, Gatekeeper, `xattr`) — the operator's, when convenient.
- `linux/arm64`: built, signed, published for every release since v1.1.0; never executed.
- The darwin swapped-signature edge case of `update`: proven on Linux against the real releases; not run on the Mac.

title: Verification — release-binary Phase 2 checkpoint (2026-09-17)
body:
# Verification — release-binary Phase 2 checkpoint (2026-09-17)

Range reviewed: working tree at HEAD 21ba8dc (branch release-binary, clean at dispatch time; 3
untracked docs artifacts appeared during this run from concurrently dispatched agents —
`.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-17-review-f7ee817-21ba8dc-code.md`,
`.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-17-security-f7ee817-21ba8dc.md`, and this log itself — no tracked
file was modified by this run)

Followed `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md` § 1 and § 3, plus the plan's own Phase 2 task-4
integration tier (`.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-17-release-binary.md`).

## Status: PASS

Scope: complete for the five command groups named in the dispatch (Go checks, race test with
counts, checkout-source scratch-home install/status, release-shaped embedded-source
install/status/update, file-set comparison). guide.md exists and needed no update. Not run:
guide.md § 2 (harness self-check: `list`, `render`), § 3a (plain-copy/mirror tier — this change
does not touch `IsCheckout`/rebuild logic), § 3b (`report` — untouched by Phase 2), § 4/§ 5
(sandbox/real-home CLI smoke checks — out of scope for this diff-free working-tree check),
skill-matrix. Phase 2's own remaining checkpoint items (branch commit/push) are not this
verifier's job.

## Commands

- `gofmt -l cmd internal *.go` → exit 0, no output (clean)
- `go vet ./...` → exit 0, no output
- `go test -race -count=1 -v ./...` → exit 0; output saved to
  `.agents/scratch/verify-phase2/go-test.txt`; counts: pass 81, fail 0, skip 0 at 21ba8dc for
  `go test -race -count=1 -v ./...`; package summary: `ok github.com/kesokaj/styrman-harness
  1.086s`, `ok .../cmd/sh-agent 3.555s`, `ok .../internal/harness 1.816s`. vs previous: none
  found in `testing/` with a counts line for this exact command (earlier logs in this repo predate
  the counts-line convention or cover different commands) — writing this as the first baseline.
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...` (non-verbose, per dispatch item 3) → exit 0, all three packages
  `ok`.
- `go run ./cmd/sh-agent install --home .agents/scratch/verify-phase2-home` → exit 0; "260
  written, 0 unchanged, 0 removed, 0 kept — 260 files managed".
- `go run ./cmd/sh-agent status --home .agents/scratch/verify-phase2-home` → exit 0; `repo
  /home/kesokaj/workspace/styrman-harness (release-binary @ 21ba8dc, uncommitted changes)`;
  `drift none — 259 files match the repo`. Note: "uncommitted changes" reflects the untracked
  docs artifacts named above (present when this status ran), not a modified tracked file — `git
  status --short` at every point in this run showed only untracked additions, never a modified
  tracked path.
- `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -ldflags "-X main.version=v0.0.0" -o
  .agents/scratch/verify-phase2-bin/sh-agent ./cmd/sh-agent` → exit 0.
- From `/`, `SH_AGENT_REPO` unset, using the built binary:
  - `install --home .agents/scratch/verify-phase2-embed` → exit 0; first line "release binary
    v0.0.0: installing the harness built into it and the running binary"; "260 written, 0
    unchanged, 0 removed, 0 kept — 260 files managed".
  - `status --home .agents/scratch/verify-phase2-embed` → exit 0; `source     embedded v0.0.0
    (release binary; update downloads the newest release)`; `installed ... from release v0.0.0`;
    `drift none — 259 files match the repo`.
  - `update --home .agents/scratch/verify-phase2-embed` → exit 1 (expected refusal): "this install
    is the release binary v0.0.0 and has no checkout; download a newer release by hand (README §
    Install without cloning)".
- File-set comparison: `find .../.claude .../.gemini -type f` (paths relativized), sorted, diffed
  between `verify-phase2-home` (checkout source) and `verify-phase2-embed` (embedded/release
  source) → empty diff, exit 0. The two installs produce an identical file set under both vendor
  directories.

## Root cause

N/A — no failures.

## Coverage of changed code

Phase 2's changed surfaces (per the plan's task 4 evidence: `internal/harness/source.go`
`ResolveSource`, `EmbeddedSource`, `IsReleaseVersion`, `EmbeddedPrefix`; `Install` taking a
`Source`; `BuildRecord`'s `harness_version`; `main.go`'s `version`, per-command embedded-source
behaviour, `releaseFromInfo`) are exercised by `TestResolveSource`,
`TestResolveSourceRefusesNamedNonRepo`, `TestEmbeddedInstallStateAndRecord`,
`TestReleaseBinaryWithoutCheckout`, `TestReleaseFromInfo` (all present and passing in this run's
`go test` output) and independently reproduced end-to-end here via the release-shaped build. No
changed file in this working tree lacks a corresponding test — `git diff` against `main` was not
re-examined here since the plan's own task evidence already lists the tests and mutation
must-fails for each; this run's job was to reproduce the integration tier fresh, which it did.

Suppressions added: none observed in the files touched by Phase 2 (no new `//nolint`,
`t.Skip`, `@ts-ignore`, etc. encountered while reading test output or running commands); a full
diff-line grep for suppressions was not performed in this run (see Not examined).

## Not examined

- guide.md § 2 (`sh-agent list`, `sh-agent render | wc -l`) — not run this pass.
- guide.md § 3a (plain-copy/read-only mirror tier) — Phase 2 does not touch `IsCheckout`/rebuild
  logic; the plan's own task-4 evidence already covers the checkout-vs-embedded comparison this
  tier would otherwise add.
- guide.md § 3b (`report` dry-run and report-specific tests) — `report.go` is untouched until
  Phase 3.
- guide.md § 4/§ 5 (sandbox CLI starts, real-home smoke checks) — no change to `context/`,
  `agents/`, or `skills/` content in this range; out of scope for a Phase 2 code checkpoint.
- A line-by-line `git diff main...release-binary` suppression grep (added `t.Skip`, `//nolint`,
  etc.) was not performed; only the working tree's current test output and the plan's own stated
  mutation-tested evidence were read.
- `govulncheck ./...` (named in `AGENTS.md` § Setup commands) was not run in this pass.
- Whether `.agents/scratch/verify-phase2-home` vs `-embed` differ under directories other than
  `.claude`/`.gemini` (e.g. `.config/sh-agent/state.json` content) was not diffed byte-for-byte
  beyond the file-name/path comparison above; `state.json`'s `"repo"` field difference
  (`/home/.../styrman-harness` vs `embedded:v0.0.0`) is expected per D20/D17 and was seen directly
  in each `status` output, not diffed as files.

# Verification — one real `sh-agent report` from this box (2026-09-17)

## Why this run happened

Phase 3 of `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-17-release-binary.md` rests on an assumption no local test can settle: that GitHub serves a `--filter=blob:none` partial clone over SSH and accepts a push from a `--depth 1` clone. The operator authorised exactly one real run for it in their own turn ("Yes, when Phase 3's code is ready"), recorded as plan decision D25. It ran after the local-bare-repository tests passed.

## What ran

Working tree: branch `release-binary` at 0eec14a, clean. Binary: `go run ./cmd/sh-agent` from that tree. Real home, real feedback repository (`git@github.com:kesokaj/styrman-harness-feedback.git`). Host `dave`.

1. `go run ./cmd/sh-agent report --dry-run` → exit 0. Named the throwaway clone (`/home/kesokaj/.config/sh-agent/report-102687`, "blob-less and limited to reports/dave/, and remove it after the push") and the five files it would write: `feedback.jsonl`, `retros.jsonl`, `state.json`, `proposals/2026-09-17-retro.md`, `report.json`. No redaction fired, so nothing was reported as caught — and by the dry run's own documented limit, that is not evidence that nothing needed catching.
2. `go run ./cmd/sh-agent report` → exit 0. Staged stat: five files, 430 insertions. Output: `report: sent reports/dave/2026-09-17-200615 (09586ff)`.

## Result

- **The partial clone works over SSH.** The clone step (`--filter=blob:none --no-checkout --depth 1`) succeeded against GitHub, and `git sparse-checkout set --no-cone reports/dave/` then `checkout` produced a working tree holding this host's directory only.
- **A push from a shallow, blob-less clone is accepted.** `push -u <url> HEAD:main` landed as `09586ff`.
- **Nothing was kept.** `ls -d ~/.config/sh-agent/report-*` → none. `~/.config/sh-agent/` holds `feedback.jsonl`, `retros.jsonl`, `state.json`, `proposals/` and the old `feedback` clone, which this run correctly ignored.
- **Timing:** the push stalled about four minutes with the SSH session established and bytes queued in its send buffer (`ss -tnp` showed `ESTAB` to GitHub, the process polling), then completed with exit 0. Slow, not refused; the first attempt exceeded a 120-second foreground timeout and was watched in the background.

## Not exercised by this run

- That the real clone never held another machine's report CONTENT. The tests check this through a hook before removal (`TestSendReportThrowawayClone`, with `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`); the real clone was removed as designed, so it cannot be inspected after the fact. What this run shows is that the server accepted the filter, not what the clone contained.
- The rejected-push retry against the real remote: no other place pushed during this run. Covered locally by `TestSendReportRetriesRejectedPush`.
- `RemoveKeptClone` against this box's real `~/.config/sh-agent/feedback`. It is still there on purpose: removing it is `sh-agent update`'s job in the operator's own home, not this session's.
- Everything Phase 4 and Phase 5 own.

body:
# Verification — sh-agent-works-everywhere-phase-1

Range reviewed: b393525..028a43b

## Status: PASS

Scope: complete — Go checks, named tests, govulncheck, and all phase-1 checkpoint legs (first install, second install, touched-source-file update, --dry-run mode probe) ran. `testing/guide.md` exists (dated 2026-09-17), no steps changed, so it was not rewritten.

## Commands

- `gofmt -l cmd internal` → exit 0, no output.
- `go vet ./...` → exit 0.
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...` → exit 0, all packages `ok`.
- `go test -race -count=1 -v ./...` → exit 0; counts: pass 227, fail 0, skip 0 at 028a43b for `go test -race -count=1 -v ./...`; vs previous: `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-18-verify-bug079-stale-running-binary-3.md` (pass 226, fail 0, skip 0) → pass 226→227, skip 0→0. The +1 is `TestInstallNamesEveryChange`, the test this range adds; matches the expected 227.
- `go test -race -count=1 -v -run 'TestInstallNamesEveryChange|TestInstallCorrectsTheModeOfAnUnchangedFile|TestInstallStatusResyncUninstall' ./internal/harness/` → all three `--- PASS`.
- `govulncheck ./...` → "No vulnerabilities found." (go1.27.1 on PATH; matches guide's go1.25.8+ expectation).

## Phase-1 checkpoint (plan `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-18-sh-agent-works-everywhere.md` Phase 1)

All runs used `.agents/scratch/` homes; no git command touched this working tree; the clone was made with `git clone -q "$(pwd)" .agents/scratch/verify-phase-1-clone` and left untouched except one appended line to a copy of `skills/bash/SKILL.md` (chosen because `rules/` and `commands/` in this checkout hold only `.gitkeep` — no deployed file exists there to touch; noted as a deviation from the dispatch's suggested `rules/go-style.md`, which does not exist).

1. **First install** (`.agents/scratch/verify-phase-1`): summary line `260 written, 0 unchanged, 0 removed, 0 kept — 260 files managed`. `grep -c '^add '` on the captured output = 260, exactly matching the summary's `260 written`.

2. **Second install**, same home: summary `0 written, 260 unchanged, 0 removed, 0 kept — 260 files managed`; `grep -E '^(add|update|remove|mode) '` on the output = 0 lines (no `update ~/.local/bin/sh-agent` this run — `go run` rebuilt the binary but produced byte-identical output, so no line was printed, which is the documented "may appear" case not firing here).

3. **Touched source file** (via `--repo` into a second scratch home, `.agents/scratch/verify-phase-1-home2`): after appending one line to the clone's `skills/bash/SKILL.md` and re-installing with `--repo`, the only change lines were:
   ```
   update  ~/.claude/skills/bash/SKILL.md
   update  ~/.gemini/config/skills/bash/SKILL.md
   update  ~/.local/bin/sh-agent
   ```
   Exactly the two vendor-deployed copies of the touched file as `update`, plus `update ~/.local/bin/sh-agent` — expected here because the binary embeds `skills/` via `go:embed`, so a changed skill file changes the rebuilt binary's bytes. Nothing else changed (257 unchanged, 3 written, 260 files managed).

   Test-setup note (not a product defect): `internal/harness/repo.go` `Reinstall` runs the rebuilt binary's install with `cmd.Dir = repo` (the `--repo` path), so a *relative* `--home` argument passed alongside `--repo` resolves against the repo directory, not the invoking shell's cwd, on the real-install path — but resolves against the invoking shell's cwd on the `--dry-run` path (which never calls `Reinstall`, since it only prints that the binary "would be" rebuilt). This asymmetry meant my first attempt at the dry-run leg landed in a different (empty) home than the one populated by the prior real installs, silently reporting a fresh `add`-everything run against an unpopulated directory. Worked around by using an absolute `--home` path for the dry-run leg, which resolves identically on both paths. This is a real inconsistency in relative-`--home` resolution when combined with `--repo`, outside the diff under review (`apply.go`'s change-line printing); flagging it rather than filing it, since it is not part of this range's coverage obligation. Recommend a follow-up bug record if the operator wants `--home` resolution audited.

4. **`chmod 666` + `--dry-run`** (absolute home, same touched-clone repo): before: `666`. Dry-run output:
   ```
   [dry-run] the binary would be rebuilt from <repo>
   mode    ~/.claude/skills/bash/SKILL.md (0666 -> 0644)
   update  ~/.local/bin/sh-agent
   [dry-run] 1 written, 259 unchanged, 0 removed, 0 kept — 260 files managed
   ```

# Verification — does Claude Code read `AGENTS.md` natively, at which scope   (2026-09-21)

Range reviewed: no code; the vendor behaviour behind `plans/2026-09-21-project-agents-md-native.md`. Claude Code 2.1.278 on this box (`claude --version`); the documented threshold is v2.1.277 (memory page § AGENTS.md and the 2.1.277 changelog entry, both fetched 2026-09-21).

## Status: PASS — the plan's premise holds at project scope; the global stub is required

Every probe: `claude -p '<question>' --max-turns 1`, no tools, the answer read from the output. Credential copies for a probe home were `chmod 600` and deleted after the run (guide § 4); every probe directory was deleted after.

| # | Arrangement | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Real home; `~/workspace/agentsmd-probe-project` with `AGENTS.md` only (probe word HERON-4412); no `CLAUDE.md` in or above it | run 1: "No `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` from the project directory appears in my context" — the documented first-session-after-upgrade case; run 2: "The probe word is HERON-4412, from …/AGENTS.md" — **read natively** |
| 2 | Same directory with the harness stub `CLAUDE.md` = `@AGENTS.md` | "HERON-4412, from the project's AGENTS.md (loaded via the @AGENTS.md line)" — the import form still works |
| 3 | Probe home OUTSIDE `/home` (the session scratchpad under `/tmp`), `~/.claude/AGENTS.md` only, no `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`; project `AGENTS.md` under that home | runs 1 and 2: both files loaded — probe word right, global context ends with GANNET, first heading `# AGENTS.md — global agent context`, both paths named — the global file is read as an ancestor `.claude/AGENTS.md` |
| 4 | Arrangement 3 plus a project `CLAUDE.md` with content | only the project `CLAUDE.md` given; "No global context ending in GANNET" — **the global context is dropped** (CLAUDE.md-only mode) |
| 5 | Arrangement 3 with the one-line `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` stub restored | global context loads (GANNET, heading) — the user-level stub is exempt from the check |

Invalid arrangements, recorded so they are not repeated (BUG-087's rule): a probe home under `/home/kesokaj` (`~/workspace/sbhome`, or `.agents/scratch/sandbox-home`) — the real `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` is then an ancestor `.claude/CLAUDE.md` of the probe project, Claude switches to CLAUDE.md-only mode, and its `@AGENTS.md` import (external to the project) is not expanded headless; every such run reported `/home/kesokaj/.claude/CLAUDE.md` as its only context whatever `HOME` said.

## Conclusion

Project scope: a project needs only `AGENTS.md` on Claude Code 2.1.277+ where feature flags are fetched (not Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry, not telemetry disabled), from the second session after an upgrade. Global scope: `~/.claude/AGENTS.md` alone loads only as an ancestor file and is lost the moment a project carries a `CLAUDE.md` or sits outside the home directory; the one-line `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` stub stays (plan D3, D5).

## Not exercised

Antigravity (unchanged: reads `AGENTS.md` natively at both levels, ADR-005); Claude Code before 2.1.277; the devbox.

# Verification — time-sortable names, E2E 1: agy cold resume   (2026-09-28)

Range: `9a17e0a` (pushed HEAD). Plan: `plans/2026-09-28-time-sortable-trail-names.md`, Phase 3.

## Status: PASS (with a weak control)

The criterion held in every run. The must-fail control did not fail, so this E2E shows that the rule works, not that it was necessary in this setup. See below.

## The condition, proven before the runs

Two fresh clones:
- **This repo at `9a17e0a`:**
  - by name, `ls handoffs | tail -1` is `2026-09-28-research-okf.md` (the oldest of today's);
  - every file has one mtime (clone time);
  - the true newest by `git log` is `2026-09-28-1450-time-sortable-names.md`.
- **A clean demo** (no harness source), holding `2026-09-28-zz-older-session.md`, committed first, "Next: write the tests", and `2026-09-28-1500-newer-session.md`, committed second, "Next: deploy feature A to staging":
  - name-sort last is the older file;
  - one mtime;
  - `git log` newest is `1500`.

## Runs (agy 1.2.8, `-p --mode plan`, same cold-resume question)

| Run | Context | Project | Handoff cited | Result | Tool calls |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| new ×2 | new (sandbox home `.agents/scratch/tsn`, harness at `9a17e0a`) | this repo | `2026-09-28-1450-time-sortable-names.md` | 2 of 2 right | 9, 11 |
| new ×2 | new | demo | `2026-09-28-1500-newer-session.md`, "Deploy feature A to staging" | 2 of 2 right | 7, 7 |
| control ×2 | old (real home, v1.6.0) | demo | `2026-09-28-1500-newer-session.md` | 2 of 2 right | 9, 9 |

**How each version decided.** The control listed the directory, read both handoffs, and broke the tie with `git log -n 5 --stat`. The new-context runs read both and needed no `git log`. With two same-day files, reading both is cheap, so the rule's gain here is two calls, not a different answer. The expensive case is the one this plan's `## Why` measured before the change: 8 of 17 calls, and the wrong handoff opened first.

## What went wrong on the way (BUG-091)

- **First attempt, new context:** both runs produced no output. Headless agy auto-denied the first shell command, because the sandbox home had no `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json`. The real home's file was copied in: permissions and trusted workspaces, no secret.
- **First attempt, control:** it ran on the harness clone and answered right by citing the new rule, which it read from `context/AGENTS.md` in the clone's tree. A control for a context change cannot run inside the harness repo, which is why the demo project was added.

## Not exercised

- Claude Code for E2E 1 (Phase 2 covered its context runs).
- The real home after `sh-agent update`: the operator's smoke check, in the handoff.

The credential copy was `chmod 600` and deleted by name after each batch; `ls` confirmed it was gone. Both clones were unmodified afterwards (`git status` empty).

# Verification — `update --from-zip` E2E with a real GitHub zip   (2026-09-28)

Range reviewed: 1cb2608..worktree. Plan: `plans/2026-09-28-update-from-zip.md`, Phase 3, E2E criteria 1–3.

## Status: PASS (after one fix, BUG-093)

## Setup, proven before the runs

- **The zip:** `gh api repos/kesokaj/styrman-harness/zipball/main` into `.agents/scratch/e2e-zip/main.zip`. It has 936 entries under ONE top folder, `kesokaj-styrman-harness-1cb26085…`, and `context/AGENTS.md` sits directly under that folder. It also holds this repository's tracked symlink `.agents/skills` as a symlink entry, which is the D6 case. All of this was checked with Python's `zipfile` before any run.
- **The binary:** `go build -ldflags "-X main.version=v0.0.1"`, which reports `sh-agent v0.0.1`, a release version. Its own source is therefore the embedded files, so a context that matches the zip can only have come from `--from-zip`.

## Runs

| # | Criterion | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Golden path: `update --from-zip main.zip --home home` | exit 0. It printed `zip … (sha256 0d66ecfc…): installing its harness with the running binary v0.0.1; the binary itself is not replaced`, installed 258 files, and left no `zip-*` directory under `home/.config/sh-agent/`. `status`: `source … this home was installed from a zip …`, `installed … from zip sha256:0d66ecfc8bda`, `drift not compared — … 258 of 258 manifest files present`, exit 0. The installed `~/.claude/AGENTS.md` is byte-identical (`cmp`) to the same zip's context rendered separately (`go run ./cmd/sh-agent render --repo <unzipped>`), and to the Antigravity copy. It ends with GANNET. |
| 2 | A zip with an `…/x/../../escape` entry (the fixture was checked to hold it) | exit 1, with `entry "…/x/../../escape" would escape the unpack directory: a .. element`. No `escape` file anywhere. **First run: the home held 2 entries**, an empty `.config/sh-agent`, because `ConfigDir` created it before the zip was checked (BUG-093). After the fix: **0 entries**. |
| 3 | Dry run | On a fresh home: exit 0, with a `[dry-run] zip …` line and **0 entries** in the home. On the populated home from run 1: a hash of every file and a list of every path, taken before and after, are **identical**, and no `zip-*` directory was left. |

## Fix made during the E2E

`UnpackZip` now creates the parent directory itself, after every name check has passed, and `updateFromZip` no longer calls `ConfigDir` first. The new test `TestUpdateFromZipRefusedZipWritesNothing` failed before the fix ("a refused zip left 1 entries under the home") and passes after it. The full race suite is green.

## Not exercised

- A zip downloaded through the browser's "Download ZIP" button. It has the same one-top-folder layout, with `styrman-harness-main/` as the folder name, and the unit test `TestUnpackZipGitHubTopFolder` covers that name.
- Antigravity reading the installed files. The install writes the same files as `install`, and those files are compared byte for byte above.
- macOS.

## Rerun after the review fixes (D11)

The binary was rebuilt from the working tree after the review round. The fixes it carries: `UnpackZip` validates before writing and returns the sum of the bytes it read; the `--from-zip` refusals run before any command; `update --dry-run` is read-only; `diff` has a zip branch; stale `zip-*` directories are swept.

| # | Result |
|---|---|
| 1 | exit 0. The first line carries `sha256 0d66ecfc…, UNVERIFIED — a zip carries no signature; …`. `status` shows `from zip sha256:0d66ecfc8bda` and `258 of 258 manifest files present`. The installed context is still byte-identical to the zip's render, and no `zip-*` directory is left. `diff`: `not compared — this home was installed from a zip that is not kept`. |
| 2 | Slip zip: exit 1, with **0** entries in a fresh home. |
| 3 | Dry run: a fresh home keeps **0** entries, and the populated home's hash list is identical before and after. |

## Rerun after round 2 (D13)

The binary was rebuilt again. E2E 1: exit 0, and the context is still byte-identical to the zip's render. E2E 2: exit 1, 0 entries. E2E 3: exit 0, 0 entries.

## Rerun after round 3

Final code (the sweep runs after a successful install; flag-like values are refused): E2E 1 exit 0, context identical; E2E 2 exit 1, 0 entries; E2E 3 exit 0, 0 entries.

   - `TestReleaseUpdateDryRunChangesNothing` — does not call `isolate(t)`; instead sets `PATH` (line 374) to a temp dir (`bin`) containing only a hand-written stub `gh` script (lines 368-374) that logs its args and prints a fake version, never touching the network. No real `git`/`gh` reachable. Network-safe by construction.
   - `TestCheckoutUpdateDryRunChangesNothing` (line 468) — does **NOT** call `isolate(t)` and does **NOT** restrict `PATH`; it uses the real `git` binary from the ambient PATH (via `exec.Command` in the test body, lines 480-493, and inside `run([]string{"update", "--dry-run", "--repo", repo, ...}, ...)`). This is the one test in the file that can reach a real `git`/`gh` binary. However every git operation it performs targets only `t.TempDir()`-local paths: `gitFixture` (main_test.go:704) creates `origin` as a local `--bare` repo under `t.TempDir()` and clones/pushes only between local paths, with `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`/`GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` set to prevent picking up the operator's real git config; no remote URL, `http(s)://`, or SSH host ever appears. The command under test is invoked with `--repo <local path>`, which is the "checkout" mode, not the release/`gh` path, so `gh` (network-capable) is never invoked either. Conclusion: reachable git binary, but no reachable network — root cause of safety is the all-local fixture, not a PATH restriction. Named here per the dispatch's request to name any test that "can" reach git/gh; this one technically can reach the `git` binary but not any network endpoint.

# Verification — v1.7.0 gate fixes, behavioural evidence   (2026-09-28)

Range reviewed: a9717cc..worktree. These are the three one-line fixes the v1.7.0 gate asked for:
- security medium: `AGENTS.md` § Testing, the sandbox agy `settings.json`;
- security low: `skills/preflight/SKILL.md`'s fallback secret scan;
- code-review low: `agents/changelog.md` Output.

## Status: PASS (one control did not fail; see below)

## 1. The sandbox-settings rule, run before it was written

The sandbox home `.agents/scratch/tsn` got a `settings.json` written for the run:
- `permissions.allow`: `read_file(*)`, `list_dir(*)`, and `command(<x>)` for ls, find, git, cat, grep, head, sed and wc;
- `trustedWorkspaces`: the demo clone only;
- no `toolPermission` key.

agy 1.2.8 then made a cold resume on the clean demo (`.agents/scratch/tsn-probe/e2e1/demo`):
- **1 of 1** right: `2026-09-28-1500-newer-session.md`, "Deploy feature A to staging";
- stderr empty, so no "auto-denied" line;
- the token and the settings file were deleted by name afterwards (`ls` shows neither).

The copy of the real home's settings used earlier today was deleted from the sandbox home when the security review named it.

## 2. The changelog Output line (reply flags a date-only name)

`claude -p --agents` ran `changelog-probe`, with a dispatch giving "Date: 2026-09-28" and no HHMM, and the tools of the agent's own `tools:` list.

| Definition | Date-only name written | Reply flags it |
|---|---|---|
| new (working tree) | 2 of 2 | **2 of 2** ("Date-only file name (no HHMM provided in dispatch)") |
| HEAD `a9717cc` (control) | 2 of 2 | 2 of 2 |

**The control did not fail.** HEAD's rule 1 already said "flagged in your reply", and the Output section was the only place that left it out. The fix makes the file agree with itself; it does not change measured behaviour. Every file was written by the subagent inside its own demo repo (`parent_tool_use_id` set, paths under `runs/flag-*`).

## What went wrong on the way (BUG-092)

The first run of probe 2 was invalid. The script pulled `demo()` out of `run.sh` with `sed -n '/^demo()/,/^}/p'`, and that range stopped at the embedded Go code's closing brace. The function came out truncated, `d` was empty, `cd ""` stayed in the harness checkout, and all four runs executed inside `styrman-harness` itself. One control run wrote a fake `changes/2026-09-28-add-healthz-endpoint.md` into this repository. It was untracked, read, and deleted by name.

The fixture now lives in `.agents/scratch/tsn-probe/lib.sh`, with a `check_demo` assertion (own repo root, the endpoint, the commit) that runs before every CLI start. The assertion was validated firing on an empty path and on a non-root directory, and passing on a good fixture.

## Not exercised

- Antigravity for probe 2.
- A second run of probe 1.
- The fallback secret-scan fix (a skill prose change: the pattern list), which is covered by the verifier's install and parse check only.

# Behavioural run — `dream` skill, Phase 1   (2026-09-29)

Range reviewed: working tree over d8e69bf (`skills/dream/SKILL.md`, new).

## Status: PASS — 3 of 3 skill runs on every seed; 0 of 3 clean controls on the skill's vocabulary

## What was under test

`skills/dream/SKILL.md` as written in the working tree, loaded as a project skill through a symlink `.claude/skills/dream` in a fixture repository (`.agents/scratch/dream-probe/fixture`, commit a6cd45c), run headless: `claude -p` with the prompt `/dream --dry-run` plus one line naming the `--settings` file, `--settings <run>/settings.json` holding `{"autoMemoryDirectory": "<absolute run dir>/mem"}`, `--permission-mode acceptEdits`, `--add-dir` on the harness `skills/dream` (so the symlink resolves) and on the run's store, `--allowedTools` = Skill, Read, Grep, Glob and read-only Bash prefixes, no Write. Real home for credentials (Claude Code 2.1.284); real home untouched. Kit: `.agents/scratch/dream-probe/run.sh`, `mem-template/`.

## Fixture store (six memory files plus `MEMORY.md`, copied fresh per run; every seed asserted by `grep`, `test`, `stat` and a session-id comparison before the runs)

| Seed | File(s) | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| Rule sits verbatim in the clone's `AGENTS.md` | `run-tests-before-claim.md` (feedback) | `graduated` |
| Names `cmd/nothing/main.go` and `deploy.sh --region`, neither exists | `entry-point.md` (project) | `broken` |
| One fact in two files, `originSessionId` 2222… and 3333…, no rule holds it ("listings sorted by name", grepped absent from the global context and the clone) | `listings-by-name.md`, `sort-listings.md` (feedback) | `merge`, flagged `promote` |
| Work still open in the newest handoff (v2 migration, issue #12) | `v2-migration.md` (project) | `keep` |
| Cites `.agents/rules/commit-style.md`, which is mode 000 in the clone (the check cannot run) | `commit-subjects.md` (feedback) | `keep`, why names the unreadable file |
| Index line for a file that does not exist | `MEMORY.md` → `old-deploy-notes.md` | `index` row |

## Round 1 (runs 1–3, controls c1–c3): two setup defects, both mine

- The merge pair restated the asking rule that the harness's global context already holds; every run correctly marked both files `graduated` citing `~/.claude/AGENTS.md:6`. Correct behaviour, wrong seed. Reseeded with a fact no loaded rule holds.
- The controls deleted the skill symlink but kept `--add-dir` on the harness skill directory and left the deletion visible in `git status`; all three controls read `skills/dream/SKILL.md` from the harness and followed it (transcripts: a `Read` of that path in each). Control rebuilt: the removal committed in the clone, no harness `--add-dir`.
- Everything else in round 1 was already 3 of 3: store line, `graduated`, `broken`, `keep`, guard `keep`, `index`, nothing written.

## Round 2 (runs 4–6 with the skill, controls c4–c6 without it)

| Run | Store line names the run's store | `graduated` | `broken` | `merge` on the pair | `promote` on the pair | `keep` | guard `keep` | `index` row | Store unchanged | Clone tree clean | Load marker in first user message |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | yes (6 memory files) | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| 5 | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| 6 | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| c4 | no | no | no | (by-hand "merge" noted) | no | (noted) | no | (noted) | yes | yes | no |
| c5 | no | no | no | (by-hand "merge" noted) | no | no | (noted) | (noted) | yes | yes | no |
| c6 | no | no | no | (by-hand "merge" noted) | no | no | no | no | yes | yes | no |

Each control began "`/dream` isn't installed in this session" and then read the store by hand; none printed the store line, none used the verdicts `graduated`, `broken` or `promote`, none applied the guard rule. So the definition, not the prompt, produces the audit.

The load marker: in a `claude -p` run the slash command is expanded into the first user message (`<command-name>/dream</command-name>` followed by the skill body); no run used the `Skill` tool. Present in 3 of 3 skill runs, absent in 3 of 3 controls (plan D13).

Tool calls, executed and refused counted separately (from `~/.claude/projects/-home-kesokaj-workspace-styrman-harness--agents-scratch-dream-probe-runs-<n>-clone/`):

| Run | Turns | Refused by the permission gate | OS or exit errors |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 18 | 4 (compound Bash commands needing approval; `ls ~/.config/sh-agent` blocked by Claude Code) | 2 (EACCES on the mode-000 guard file — the guard seed working) |
| 5 | 21 | 3 | 1 (EACCES) |
| 6 | 28 | 5 | 1 (EACCES) |
| c4–c6 | 14–17 | 1–2 | 0–1 |

- `/retro` reading the verdicts (Phase 2).
- The real home's own store (`asking-format.md` graduation): Phase 2.

## Status: PASS — every Phase 1 expectation met, with one vendor limit recorded (the headless `.claude/` write guard) and six void runs explained

## Kits

`.agents/scratch/memory-probe/`: `fixture/` (an older scaffold: no `retros/`, no `.claude/settings.local.json`, `.claude/skills/init-project` linked to the working tree), `fixture-absent/` (the same plus a committed `{}` settings file), `mem-template/` (two memories and an index, copied into the default per-project path under the real home before a seeded run), `run-init.sh`, `run-remember.sh`, `run-split.sh`; the split fixture is `dream-probe/fixture` with the working-tree `dream` linked. All runs `claude -p`, real home for credentials, prompt on stdin, `--permission-mode acceptEdits`, read-only Bash prefixes plus `mv`, `mkdir`, `cp`, `ln`, `python3` for the init runs. Every seed asserted by the kit before the CLI started (slug computed by the same rule the skill states; the default path emptied first).

## `/init-project` update path with a seeded default store (i1–i3)

| Run | Turns | Store created at `~/.config/sh-agent/memory/<slug>/` | Both files and the index moved, default path empty | `.gitignore` gains `.claude/settings.local.json` | `retros/` created | `.claude/settings.local.json` written | Exact content reported instead |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| i1 | 44 | yes | yes | yes | yes | no (headless guard) | yes |
| i2 | 48 | yes | yes | yes | yes | no | yes |
| i3 | 49 | yes | yes | yes | yes | no | yes |

Claude Code refuses writes under the project's `.claude/` in a headless session (`testing/2026-09-03-verify-sandbox.md` § Vendor behaviour); the skill's Step 5 guard, extended to Step 5b, fired in 3 of 3: the run reported the one-line file for the user. The store, the migration and the `.gitignore` line do not depend on it. Interactive runs are one approval; the E2E in this checkout (Phase 2) is where the write itself is seen. The transcripts read the linked working-tree skill (14 mentions of Step 5b in i1; the installed copy has none), so these runs measured the edit.

## `/init-project` with no default store and a `{}` settings file (a1, a2)

| Run | Turns | `no memory files at <old>` printed | Store created, empty | Settings file | `.before` copy | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| a1 | 46 | yes | yes | stayed `{}` (write refused), one-key content reported | — | — |
| a2 | 53 | yes | yes | stayed `{}` (write refused), one-key content reported | written | said the file is tracked by git and named `git rm --cached` — now a clause of Step 5b |

## The setting honoured headless (m1, m2)

The kit wrote `.claude/settings.local.json` with the key (the operator's part in a real project) and asked Claude Code to remember a fact.

| Run | Turns | Memory file written in the new store | Anything in the default path |
|---|---|---|---|
| m1 | 4 | yes (`demo-deploy-cadence.md` plus the `MEMORY.md` line) | nothing |
| m2 | 4 | yes (`demo-deploy-schedule.md` plus the line) | nothing |

So Claude Code 2.1.284 honours `autoMemoryDirectory` from a project's local settings file in a headless run of a scratch clone; the trust refusal did not occur here.

## `/dream` split-store stop (s1–s12) and the regression run

- **s1–s3, s4–s6, s7–s9: void.** The real home was installed from commit 4426e58 at 14:03 (the operator's action), which put a `dream` skill of the Phase 1 shape under `~/.claude/skills/`; the `/dream` command resolved to that user-level copy, shadowing the project link to the working tree, so nine runs measured text without the split check. Their first lines kept the installed format; the transcripts show the runs listing the default project directory rather than counting its memory files. Recorded as plan D15 and a bug record; the kits now pass `--setting-sources project,local`.
- **s10–s12, valid:**

| Run | Turns | First line carries both counts | `split store — merge before running` | Verdict table absent | Settings store unchanged | Default store unchanged | Clone tree clean |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| s10 | 7 | yes (6; default path: 2) | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| s11 | 6 | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| s12 | 5 | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |

- **Regression, `dream-probe` run 8** (no default store, `--setting-sources project,local`): the first line carries the store and `default path …: could not be counted` (the directory was outside the run's allowed directories), the verdict table and the `promote` flag as in Phase 1 of the dream plan, no split line, store unchanged. The skill now says that phrase takes the count's place when the count cannot run.

## Context clause and capture rule

- `context/AGENTS.md` § Resume gained the Antigravity clause; `TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock` PASS at 21,787 of 22,000 bytes (bare run).
- `skills/feedback-log/SKILL.md` rule 7 names every frontmatter field the spec lists (`name`, `description`, `metadata.node_type`, `type`, `originSessionId`, `modified`) and the index line; read against `specs/sh-agent/memory-loop.md` § The store.

## Not exercised

- The settings write itself (refused headless in every run): Phase 2's E2E in this checkout, interactive.
- Antigravity: the resume clause and the capture rule have not run on agy (plan D7); the operator's real-home smoke.
- A settings file with other keys (the insert-one-line branch): the fixtures had none or `{}`; the branch is stated, not run.
- The hint list when the slug does not match (D9): the absent runs printed the message; no mismatched-slug fixture was built.
- The `~/.config/sh-agent/memory/` directory's mode: created by the runs under the operator's 0700 `~/.config/sh-agent/`; not measured.

## Cost

Ten init and remember runs about $8.20 (the init runs are long, 44–53 turns at about $1.10 each); twelve split runs about $5.10, nine of them void; one regression run.

## Cleanup

The stores the runs created under the real home were removed by name pattern after the log was written: `~/.config/sh-agent/memory/*probe-runs*` (seven directories) and `~/.claude/projects/*probe-runs*/memory` — the second pattern also matched the empty auto-created `memory/` directories of earlier sessions' scratch probes (tsn, retro, prompts); the survey at the start of this session listed every one of them with zero files, so nothing was lost, but the pattern was wider than the seeds it was meant for.

## Kits

## The `dreamer` on the seeded store and trail (d1–d3 first definition; d4–d6 after the `Since`-bounded reading of bug rows and the same-day suffix)

| d1 | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| d2 | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| d3 | yes | yes | yes | **no** | yes | yes |
| d4 | yes | yes | yes | **no** | yes | yes |
| d5 | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| d6 | yes | yes | yes | yes (draft `SKILL.md` under `.agents/scratch/dreamer/`) | yes | yes |

The skill candidate is the soft column: 4 of 6. The two misses read the two release records but did not count them as one procedure done twice. The definition was not reworded a third time for it (the second rewording bounded the bug rows and named `changes/` entries as procedure evidence); the rate is reported as it is, and the matrix row's check keeps the column, so a future run that misses it fails the row. Cost about $0.18 per run (the main agent's part; the subagent's tokens are inside).

## `/retro --dry-run` dispatching the dreamer (t1–t2 first wording; t3–t4 after the dry-run clause)

| Run | `## Memory` with the store line | Memory pair as findings with `rule_ref null` | `dreamer` dispatched (Agent tool, transcript) | Dreamer artifact written and cited | Tree clean |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| t2 | yes | yes | **no**, same reason | no | yes |
| t3 | yes | yes | yes (one dispatch, `subagent_type: dreamer`) | yes, `retros/2026-09-29-dreamer.md` | yes |
| t4 | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |

The first wording let the run read `--dry-run`'s "nothing written" as covering the dreamer's artifact; source 8 now says the dry run still dispatches, an agent's artifact being trail, not a change. 2 of 2 after the clause.

## E2E in this checkout

1. **Criterion 1, the store:** Step 5b run by hand here (this session is the interactive one): `.claude/settings.local.json` written and parsing (the whole `.claude/` is gitignored in this repo; the Step 6 line added anyway), the store created at `~/.config/sh-agent/memory/-home-kesokaj-workspace-styrman-harness/`, the two real memories and the index moved, the default path empty; `/dream`'s first line by hand: `store: <that path> (2 memory files; default path ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory: 0)`, both files indexed. Met.
2. **Criterion 2, the dreamer on the real trail:** first run (`retros/2026-09-29-dreamer.md`) COMPLETE with zero candidates — it read a sample of the bug index and never opened BUG-096; the definition then gained the `Since`-bounded reading of every index row. Second run (`retros/2026-09-29-dreamer-2.md`) COMPLETE with one rule candidate: "read the neighbours before inserting rule text", evidence the read-neighbours memory plus BUG-095 and BUG-096, the grep over every loaded rule cited as empty, a target named. Met on the rerun; both artifacts kept.

## Not exercised

- Antigravity: no run of the dreamer (derived `agent.md` present with every tool mapped), the resume clause or the capture rule; the operator's real-home smoke.

The stores these runs created under the real home (`~/.config/sh-agent/memory/*probe-runs*`) are removed after this log, by that name pattern only.

## After the security round (`reviews/2026-09-29-security-memory-loop.md`)

One more seeded `/init-project` run (i4) against the fixed Step 5b: the headless `.claude/` guard refused the settings write as before, and this time the run printed `migration skipped: the setting is not in place`, left both memory files and the index in the default store, reported the one-line settings content, and created the new store empty with mode 700 (`mkdir -m 700`, since a separate `chmod` was refused — the step now says so). Before the fix, runs i1–i3 moved the files despite the refused write; this run shows the guard. The empty-slug stop was checked by hand: outside a repository the slug command prints an empty string, which the step now refuses before creating anything.

## After the store moved inside the project (D17) and the round-2 security fixes — every probe rerun against the final text

All kits now pass `--setting-sources project,local` (the init kit had lacked it: runs i5 and a3 loaded the installed `init-project` and said so themselves — "the installed copy took precedence over the project's link … a probe meant to test Step 5b needs `--setting-sources project,local`" — and declined to mix the copies; recorded, not counted).

| Probe | Runs | Result |

| `/init-project`, no default store, a tracked `{}` settings file (a4) | 1 | Step 5b's trust check first: content reported, nothing written into the tracked file, nothing moved, store created, both `.gitignore` lines — the tracked-file case of security finding 1, 1 of 1 (the matrix row now seeds an untracked `{}` so the `no memory files at` branch is what it tests) |
| `/dream` split store (s13–s15: settings store at the clone's `.agents/memory/`, the default path seeded) | 3 | first line with both counts, `split store — merge before running`, no table, both stores unchanged — 3 of 3 |
| `/dream` with a foreign `--settings` value (run 9, the kit not yet repointed: value `<run>/mem`) | 1 | refused as neither of the two exact paths, fell back to the default path, wrote nothing — the round-2 root bound working, 1 of 1 |
| `/dream` regression, store at the clone's `.agents/memory/` (run 10) | 1 | store line names it (6 memory files, default path 0), verdicts and the `promote` flag as before, no split, store unchanged — 1 of 1 |
| `dreamer` (d7–d9, store at the clone's `.agents/memory/`, `Promoted:` the pair) | 3 | artifact COMPLETE, the pair, the recurring bug rows and the project memory left alone 3 of 3; the skill candidate 2 of 3 (6 of 9 over all rounds); no refusal — the exact-path rule accepted the store |
| `/retro --dry-run` dispatching the dreamer (t5, t6) | 2 | dispatched, artifact cited, the pair as findings — 2 of 2 |
| E2E criterion 2 on this checkout's real store (`retros/2026-09-29-dreamer-3.md`) | 1 | COMPLETE, two rule candidates: read the neighbours (memory + BUG-095 + BUG-096) and "a project-supplied setting naming a filesystem destination is untrusted when its file is tracked" (BUG-101 + BUG-102) — met |

E2E criterion 1 after the move: this checkout's store is `.agents/memory/` (three files, mode 700, gitignored), `.claude/settings.local.json` holds its absolute path, the default path is empty, and the dream first line by hand reads `store: <root>/.agents/memory (2 memory files; default path …: 0)`.

title: Behavioural runs — preflight writes its verdict last (BUG-105) (2026-09-29)
body:
# Behavioural runs — preflight writes its verdict last (BUG-105)   (2026-09-29)

Change under test: `skills/preflight/SKILL.md` Step 5 gained "Write the verdict line LAST, when every other section is final: read each item under 'What was not checked' against every blocking condition below, the project's own included, and an item a condition names makes the verdict NO-SHIP whatever the rows above say (BUG-105)."

## Status: PASS — with the rule the verdict is written last in 6 of 6 reports; without it, in 0 of 6

## Setup

Claude Code 2.1.284, headless, `--setting-sources project,local`. The arm's skills were copied into the clone's `.claude/skills/`; the agents were passed with `--agents` (the working-tree definitions); the arm's rendered context was appended. Arms: the working tree (with the rule) and the install made before the change (without it). Clones sat under `~/sandbox/search/pf/`, outside every checkout.

Fixture: the `tasklog` sample project, tagged `v0.1.0`, plus one commit adding a project skill `.agents/skills/notes/` and a `## Release` section to its `AGENTS.md`: "a gate whose 'What was not checked' names an Antigravity run of a skill or agent the release range changed is NO-SHIP until that run exists." The run script asserted the tag and the rule's sentence before each start. Prompt: `/preflight v0.2.0`, no remote, never tag, run nothing on Antigravity.

Two variants, three runs per arm each:

- **Plain:** no run of the `notes` skill is recorded anywhere.
- **Wrong CLI (BUG-105's own case):** a testing log records a Claude Code run of the skill, PASS 3 of 3, and no Antigravity run.

## Results

| Variant | Arm | Verdict NO-SHIP, the missing Antigravity run named | Verdict line after "What was not checked" |
|---|---|---|---|
| Plain | with the rule | 3 of 3 | 3 of 3 (lines 45 to 57 of the report) |
| Plain | without | 3 of 3 | 0 of 3 (lines 9 to 11) |
| Wrong CLI | with the rule | 3 of 3 | 3 of 3 (lines 50 to 57) |
| Wrong CLI | without | 3 of 3 | 0 of 3 (lines 11 to 13) |

Both texts reached the right verdict on both fixtures, so the verdict itself does not tell the arms apart here. The ordering does: with the rule the verdict is the last thing written, after the unchecked items are final.

**Antigravity 1.2.13** (sandbox home installed from the working tree, the plain fixture): completed on the first attempt with no skip flag; `VERDICT: NO-SHIP`, the missing run named, the verdict line (41) after the section (16).

## A void batch

The first four runs put the arm's agents into the clone's `.claude/agents/`. Preflight's own check for project agents that shadow the review agents stopped all four before any review, in both arms, so they measured the shadow check and not the rule. The agents were then passed with `--agents`.

## What was not exercised

- A release range in which the old text writes SHIP against its own unchecked items, as v1.12.1's gate did; both fixtures here state the rule plainly enough that either text obeys it.
- Interactive sessions.
